METHODS: PWH were enrolled in Ethiopia, Mozambique, and South Africa and randomized to (i) 1 course of weekly rifapentine-isoniazid for 3 months (3HP), (ii) weekly rifapentine-isoniazid for 3 months given annually for 2 years (p3HP), or (iii) daily isoniazid for 6 months (6H). QFT-Plus testing was performed at baseline, month 12, and month 24. Quantitative and qualitative results, and serial changes (conversions and reversions) were assessed.

RESULTS: From baseline to month 12, 13.0% (196/1502) of participants converted, with no differences between 3HP (13.1%) and 6H (12.9%). From month 12 to month 24, conversion occurred in 4.0% of participants receiving a second course of 3HP (p3HP arm), and in 9.4% of those not receiving a second course (3HP) (P = .110). Overall reversions occurred in 19.0% (178/935) of participants. Reversion rates were similar across study arms and timepoints. The risk of developing TB during the study period was higher among individuals who were QFT-Plus positive at baseline (adjusted hazard ratio, 1.66 [95% confidence interval, 1.41-1.89], P = .034).

CONCLUSIONS: QFT-Plus conversions and reversions occurred frequently in PWH and did not differ by TPT regimen or between those who did and did not receive a second course of TPT. The high rate of QFT positivity, along with the large proportion of conversions despite TPT, highlights the complexity of interpreting serial interferon-gamma release assay results in PWH in high-transmission scenarios.

articles.title: Beauty Abroad, Burden at Home: Complications and National Health Service Impact of Cosmetic Tourism-Insights From the British Association of Aesthetic Plastic Surgeons National Database.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Cosmetic surgery tourism has increased rapidly, with growing numbers of UK patients returning with complications requiring National Health Service (NHS) care. Limited regulation and inconsistent perioperative standards contribute to preventable harm.

OBJECTIVES: The aim of this study was to characterize the nature, severity, and causes of complications from overseas cosmetic surgery and estimate the resulting burden on the NHS.

METHODS: A national retrospective study analyzed all 198 cases reported to the British Association of Aesthetic Plastic Surgeons (BAAPS) Cosmetic Tourism Complications Database between September 2022 and September 2024. Demographic, procedural, and clinical data were examined, and complications were graded using the BAAPS 5-stage classification.

RESULTS: Patients were predominantly female (93%) with a mean age of 39 years; 76% had surgery in Turkey. Abdominoplasty (45%) was the most common procedure, followed by breast and liposuction surgeries. Frequent complications included wound dehiscence (37%), infection (28%), seroma (24%), and tissue necrosis (20%). Nearly half (48%) required operative management under general anesthesia, 28% minor procedures, and 4% intensive care; 1 death occurred from pulmonary embolism. Thematic analysis identified inadequate aftercare (21%), poor preoperative optimization (12%), and premature air travel (5%) as recurrent contributory factors. Estimated NHS treatment costs (£5883-£9328 per patient) equated to £1.2 to £1.8 million over 2 years.

CONCLUSIONS: Cosmetic surgery tourism poses a substantial clinical and financial challenge for the NHS. A multilevel harm-reduction strategy-encompassing patient education, complication insurance, international accreditation, and data surveillance-is essential to improve safety and reduce preventable harm.

articles.title: Response to the Letter Regarding "If Becker Muscular Dystrophy Initially Manifests with Heart Disease and Rhabdomyolysis, Neurological Work-up Is Imperative".

Nationwide Retrospective Analysis of Early Complications After Adult Spinal Deformity Surgery: Insights From the Japanese Spinal Instrumentation Society Database Registry.
articles.abstract:
STUDY DESIGN: Retrospective nationwide registry-based observational study.

OBJECTIVE: To determine the incidence of and factors associated with early complications following surgery for adult spinal deformity (ASD).

SUMMARY OF BACKGROUND DATA: Complications after ASD surgery contribute to morbidity, mortality, and health care costs. Prior studies were limited by small sample sizes and incomplete surgical information. The Japanese Spinal Instrumentation Society database (JSIS-DB) includes detailed instrumentation data, enabling a robust secondary analysis of perioperative factors.

MATERIALS AND METHODS: We analyzed JSIS-DB data from patients undergoing ASD surgery involving the fusion of three or more vertebrae between 2018 and 2022. Demographics, comorbidities, and surgical variables [fusion length, osteotomy, interbody fusion type, minimally invasive surgery (MIS), staged procedures, navigation, and neuromonitoring] were assessed. The primary endpoint was ultra-early perioperative complications within two weeks, classified as major (mortality, massive bleeding, neurological, cardiopulmonary, or infectious events) or minor (dural injury, delirium, or urinary tract infection). Multivariable logistic regression was used to identify the associated factors.

RESULTS: Among 3193 patients (mean age 60.8 yr), the overall complication rate was 28.5%, including 25.4% with major complications and 0.1% with mortality. Increased risk was associated with operative time >5 hours [adjusted odds ratio (aOR) 4.40; 95% CI: 3.60-5.47], fusion >5 levels (aOR: 1.51; 95% CI: 1.20-1.91), posterior/transforaminal interbody fusion (PLIF/TLIF) (aOR: 1.47; 95% CI: 1.20-1.79), and three-column osteotomy (3CO) (aOR: 3.50; 95% CI: 2.21-5.53). Reduced risk was associated with adult idiopathic scoliosis (aOR: 0.48; 95% CI: 0.37-0.63), staged surgery (aOR: 0.24; 95% CI: 0.18-0.32), lateral lumbar interbody fusion (LLIF) (aOR: 0.74; 95% CI: 0.58-0.95), and MIS (aOR: 0.65; 95% CI: 0.49-0.86). Respiratory complications, massive bleeding, neurological deficits, surgical site infections, and proximal junctional kyphosis were associated with prolonged hospitalization (>30 d).

CONCLUSIONS: This nationwide registry analysis demonstrated that prolonged operative time, long fusion, PLIF/TLIF, and 3CO increase the early complication risk after ASD surgery, whereas staged surgery, LLIF, and MIS are protective.

LEVEL OF EVIDENCE: Level III-retrospective cohort study.

articles.title: Phlegmonous Gastritis in Chemotherapy-related Neutropenia with Endoscopic Findings that Prompted Early Therapeutic Intervention.
articles.abstract: Phlegmonous gastritis is a rare and potentially fatal infection of the gastric wall that is often difficult to diagnose due to non-specific symptoms. We report the case of a 56-year-old man with chemotherapy-related neutropenia and immunosuppression, who presented with shock and epigastric pain. Computed tomography revealed diffuse gastric wall thickening, and esophagogastroduodenoscopy revealed extensive mucosal injury, prompting the administration of empiric antimicrobial therapy. He responded well to conservative treatment, with clinical and endoscopic improvements. This case underscores that early clinical suspicion based on endoscopic findings combined with timely therapeutic intervention may be lifesaving in immunocompromised patients.

articles.title: Embolic Ischemic Stroke Associated with Maintenance Intravenous Immunoglobulin Therapy.
articles.abstract: We describe the case of a 51-year-old man who experienced an embolic ischemic stroke during long-term maintenance of intravenous immunoglobulin (IVIG) therapy for chronic inflammatory demyelinating polyradiculoneuropathy (CIDP). At 43 years of age, he was diagnosed with CIDP and had tolerated IVIG well. Immediately after completing the 112th infusion, he exhibited acute right-hand clumsiness. Brain magnetic resonance imaging revealed an acute embolic infarction, and neither risk factors for ischemic stroke nor alternative embolic sources were identified. Although IVIG is generally considered safe, this case highlights that embolic stroke may occur even in relatively younger, low-risk patients during uneventful maintenance IVIG therapy, warranting continued vigilance.

articles.title: Trends and Factors Associated with LDL-C Treatment Target Attainment Rates among Patients with Secondary Prevention Setting of Atherosclerotic Cardiovascular Disease: Assessments from Japanese Health Checkup Data.
articles.abstract: Objective According to the latest Japanese Guidelines for the Prevention of Atherosclerotic Disease, the target for secondary prevention of low-density lipoprotein cholesterol (LDL-C) is <100 mg/dL in patients with coronary artery disease and <70 mg/dL in patients with acute coronary syndrome, familial hypercholesterolemia, diabetes, or atherothrombotic cerebral infarction. However, it is still unclear if the LDL-C treatment target attainment rates are in an upward trend and what are the factors associated with target attainment. This study aimed to investigate the trends and factors associated with LDL-C treatment target attainment. Methods Using the Health Checkup data in Kanazawa City in 2008, 2012, 2017, and 2022 (n = 38,146-51,969), we analyzed the trends of secondary prevention of LDL-C treatment target attainment rates using the Cochran-Armitage trend test and the factors associated with target attainment by a logistic regression analysis from the 2022 health examination. Results We found that the attainment rates showed a significant upward trend over time (p<0.001), and we also found that a male sex (odds ratio: 2.64, 95% confidence interval: 1.72-4.06, p<0.001) and several lifestyle factors, such as walking or any equivalent amount of physical activity for more than one hour a day, were significantly associated with LDL-C target attainment. Conclusion The LDL-C treatment target attainment rates tended to increase over time, and several factors were associated with LDL-C target attainment.

articles.title: Efficacy of Stromal Vascular Fraction for Scar Prevention: A Multicenter, Double-Blinded, Randomized Controlled Trial.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Addressing postoperative scarring remains a significant challenge across all surgical procedures, often leading to long-term aesthetic deficits. Traditional methods for scar management have shown limited efficacy, prompting exploration into innovative approaches such as the application of stromal vascular fraction (SVF).

OBJECTIVES: The efficacy of intraoperative SVF injection in modulating scar formation was assessed by evaluating postoperative scar quality in patients undergoing free tissue transfer.

METHODS: This multicenter, double-blinded, placebo-controlled, randomized study assessed the efficacy of intraoperative SVF injections in mitigating scar formation in patients undergoing free tissue transfer. A total of 45 patients were enrolled from 3 institutions, undergoing either breast reconstruction with abdominal flaps or soft tissue reconstruction with anterolateral thigh flaps. The donor site incision was split in half, with one side receiving SVF injections and the other saline injections, assigned randomly. Scar quality was evaluated using the Vancouver Scar Scale (VSS) and Patient Scar Assessment Questionnaire (PSAQ), along with objective measures of pigmentation using an analyzing device.

RESULTS: The primary analysis endpoint at 6 months after surgery showed a statistically significant improvement in VSS scores in the SVF group compared to the saline group. However, these differences were not maintained at the 9-month follow-up. PSAQ results indicated improved satisfaction with scar appearance at 6 and 9 months in the SVF group, despite no significant changes in erythema and melanin levels.

CONCLUSIONS: Intraoperative SVF infection can improve postoperative scar appearance in patients undergoing free tissue transfer. This study supports further exploration of SVF as a potential tool for enhancing aesthetic outcomes in scar management.

LEVEL OF EVIDENCE: 2 (THERAPEUTIC): For image description, please refer to the figure legend and surrounding text.

articles.title: Patient Comorbidities Drive 90-Day Emergency Department Revisits and Readmissions After Trimalleolar Ankle Fracture Open Reduction and Internal Fixation: A National Database Analysis.
articles.journal: The Journal of the American Academy of Orthopaedic Surgeons
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Trimalleolar ankle fractures are associated with high complication rates and unplanned healthcare utilization. This study aimed to (1) characterize the demographic and clinical profile of patients requiring 90-day readmission; (2) identify risk factors for 90-day emergency department (ED) utilization; and (3) determine comorbidities most strongly linked to 90-day readmissions following trimalleolar open reduction and internal fixation (ORIF).

METHODS: Using the PearlDiver Mariner database from 2010 to 2021, patients undergoing trimalleolar ankle fracture ORIF were identified through current procedural terminology codes 27822 and 27823. Ninety-day postoperative ED visits and hospital readmissions were evaluated. Patients with ED utilization (N = 636) were compared with controls without ED visits (N = 79,956). Logistic regression was used to identify demographic and comorbidity risk factors for both ED utilization and readmission, with statistical significance set at P < 0.05.

RESULTS: ED utilization was higher among older patients (peak 70 to 74 years, P < 0.001). Comorbidities markedly associated with 90-day ED revisits included congestive heart failure (CHF) [odds ratio (OR) 1.55, P = 0.001], fluid and electrolyte disorders (OR 1.35, P = 0.001), pathologic weight loss (OR 1.34, P = 0.012), hypertension (OR 1.26, P = 0.043), and peripheral vascular disease (PVD) (OR 1.25, P = 0.038). Risk factors for 90-day readmission included fluid and electrolyte disorders (OR 1.98, P < 0.001), coagulopathy (OR 1.44, P < 0.001), CHF (OR 1.35, P < 0.001), PVD (OR 1.33, P < 0.001), and pathologic weight loss (OR 1.44, P < 0.001).

CONCLUSION: Postoperative ED visits and readmissions following trimalleolar ORIF are driven largely by patient comorbidities. Older, medically complex patients represent a high-risk group, and targeted perioperative optimization may reduce complications and unplanned healthcare utilization.

articles.title: Optimizing Autologous Fat Grafting: A Systematic Review of Enhancement Strategies and Graft Survival.
articles.abstract: Autologous fat grafting has become an important tool in reconstructive and aesthetic surgery, particularly for breast reconstruction and soft tissue augmentation. Despite its promise, long-term outcomes remain unpredictable. To address this, research has increasingly focused on optimizing graft survival by enriching the lipoaspirate with additional substances. A systematic search of PubMed (National Institutes of Health, Bethesda, MD) and Web of Science (Clarivate, Philadelphia, PA) identified studies on enhancement methods of autologous fat grafting in both animal models and clinical settings, published up to February 2025. In vitro trials, case reports, and studies comparing techniques without specific enhancement of the lipoaspirate were excluded. Twenty-seven studies fulfilled the criteria, including 15 animal studies and 12 clinical studies, most of which investigated applications in breast reconstruction and augmentation. The included studies showed substantial heterogeneity in enhancement strategies, case numbers, follow-up duration, and outcome measures. The most frequently examined approaches involved enrichment with stromal vascular fraction (SVF) and/or adipose-derived stem cells (ADSCs). Both methods demonstrated favourable results in many trials, though statistical significance was not always achieved. Other strategies included the use of Vitamin D3, Botulinum toxin A, platelet-rich plasma (PRP), and less frequently studied agents such as N-acetylcysteine and Salvia miltiorrhiza. Overall, enrichment of lipoaspirate appears to enhance graft survival, with SVF/ADSC-based methods and PRP emerging as the most promising approaches. Nevertheless, marked variability in protocols and outcome measures hampers comparability between studies. Larger randomized controlled trials employing standardized methodologies are essential to confirm clinical feasibility and provide a basis for evidence-based guidelines. Level of Evidence: 3 (Therapeutic)  For image description, please refer to the figure legend and surrounding text.

articles.title: Impact of Nontobacco Nicotine Dependence on Outcomes Following Anterior Lumbar Interbody Fusion.
articles.abstract:
STUDY DESIGN: Retrospective cohort study.

OBJECTIVE: To compare rates of health care utilization, complications, opioid use, and revision surgery following anterior lumbar interbody fusion (ALIF) in patients with versus without nontobacco nicotine dependence (NTND).

SUMMARY OF BACKGROUND DATA: The prevalence of NTND is rising in the United States due to products such as nicotine e-cigarettes, pouches, gums, and lozenges. Studies have shown that tobacco use can contribute to adverse outcomes following spinal fusion surgery, including pseudarthrosis. However, literature focusing specifically on NTND is sparse.

METHODS: The TriNetX database was queried to identify patients over 18 years old who underwent primary ALIF. Patients were stratified into two cohorts based on their history of NTND. Patients underwent propensity score matching in a 1:1 ratio based on demographics and relevant comorbidities. Covariate balance was confirmed by standardized mean differences ≤ 0.1. The following outcomes were collected: (1) medical complications and health care utilization within 90 days, (2) opioid use within 2 years, and (3) surgical complications and revision surgery within 2 years.

RESULTS: Within 90 days, patients with NTND (n=2296), compared with those without (n=2296), had higher rates of emergency department visits ( P =0.001), outpatient encounters ( P =0.001), pneumonia ( P =0.007), ventilator support ( P =0.019), and sepsis ( P =0.015). Patients with NTND received significantly more opioid prescriptions at all time points (all P ≤0.001). More patients with NTND were prFescribed opioids at all time points (all P ≤0.001) except at one week. Lastly, patients with NTND had higher rates of postlaminectomy syndrome (all P <0.001), pseudarthrosis (all P <0.001), and revision surgery (all P <0.05) at all time points within 2 years.

CONCLUSION: Patients with NTND have higher rates of health care utilization, complications, opioid use, and revision surgery following ALIF. Patients should be screened and counseled in a multidisciplinary fashion to ensure the best possible outcome after surgery.

LEVEL OF EVIDENCE: Level IV.

articles.title: Comparison of Early Postoperative Outcomes and Reimbursement Metrics in Obese Versus Nonobese Patients Undergoing Secondary Reconstruction for Achilles Tendinopathy.
articles.journal: The Journal of the American Academy of Orthopaedic Surgeons
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: This study aims to evaluate whether obesity affects early postoperative outcomes or reimbursement metrics following surgical intervention for Achilles tendinopathy.

METHODS: A retrospective analysis was done using the National Surgical Quality Improvement Program database (2013 to 2022). Patients undergoing secondary Achilles reconstruction were identified through Current Procedural Terminology and International Classification of Diseases 9th/10th codes and were categorized as obese (body mass index ≥ 30) or nonobese (body mass index < 30). Demographic variables, comorbidities, 30-day postoperative complications, including mortality, readmission, revision surgery, wound complications, thromboembolic events, respiratory complications, infectious complications, renal complications, cardiac complications, and transfusion. The number of concurrent procedures and work relative value unit (wRVU)-based compensation metrics were compared between the two groups. An analysis of covariance was done to adjust the effect of patient demographics, preoperative comorbidities, and perioperative complications on the valuation of compensation metrics.

RESULTS: Six hundred eighty-eight patients met inclusion criteria: 505 (73.4%) were obese and 183 (26.6%) were nonobese. Obese patients had markedly higher rates of comorbidities, including diabetes and hypertension. No notable differences were found between the two groups in any of the early postoperative complication rates we investigated. The number of concurrent procedures per case was markedly higher in the obese group: 1.2 vs. 1.0, P = 0.015. Regarding compensation metrics, wRVU/hr, and reimbursement ($/hr) were comparable between the groups after analysis of covariance: 14.6 wRVU/hr and 473.82 $/hr for the obese group versus 13.5 and 435.2 for the nonobese group, P = 0.131, respectively.

CONCLUSION: Our findings suggest that secondary reconstruction for Achilles tendinopathy can be done safely in obese patients without increasing short-term postoperative complication rates. Compensation metrics remained comparable between the obese and nonobese groups, indicating that the increased preoperative burden and surgical demands in obese patients may not be matched by a proportional increase in reimbursement.

LEVEL OF EVIDENCE: Level III.

articles.title: Comparison of Two-Screw Versus Four-Screw Internal Fixation on Fusion Speed in Anterior Cervical Discectomy and Fusion : A Prospective Randomized Controlled Trial.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND CONTEXT: The insertion process of the new two-screw internal fixation is simpler than that of four-screw internal fixation for anterior cervical discectomy and fusion (ACDF). However, it is unclear whether there is a difference in fusion rate.

PURPOSE: This study aimed to compare the time required to achieve osseous fusion and the clinical efficacy of four-screw versus two-screw internal fixation.

STUDY DESIGN: A prospective randomized controlled trial.

PATIENT SAMPLE: From October 2021 to April 2023, 80 patients diagnosed with single-level cervical spondylosis were recruited and randomly allocated into a four-screw or two-screw group.

OUTCOME MEASURES: The primary end point was the fusion rate six months postoperatively. Secondary outcomes included the prevalence of complications and patient-reported outcome measures (PROMs), including the Japanese Orthopaedic Association score, Neck Disability Index, and visual analog scale scores for arm and neck pain.

METHODS: Patients were randomized to receive four-screw internal fixation (n=40) or two-screw internal fixation (n=40).

RESULTS: A total of 77 patients completed the trial and were included in the analysis. No significant differences were observed between groups at baseline. The fusion rate in the two-screw group was significantly higher than that in the four-screw group (69.2% vs . 42.1%, P =0.022) at six months postoperatively. No significant difference was found in the fusion rates at 3 and 12 months postoperatively between groups. Overall, PROMs significantly improved after surgery in both groups and did not differ significantly between groups at any follow-up time point. The prevalence of complications was not significantly different between groups.

CONCLUSIONS: Two-screw internal fixation can achieve osseous fusion faster than four-screw internal fixation in ACDF. Two-screw internal fixation seems to achieve the same PROMs and safety as four-screw internal fixation.

articles.title: Prognostic value of liver scoring systems in predicting early outcomes after pericardiectomy: a single-center retrospective study.
articles.journal: Monaldi archives for chest disease = Archivio Monaldi per le malattie del torace
articles.abstract: Pericardiectomy for constrictive pericarditis remains a high-risk operation, and early outcomes are inadequately predicted by conventional cardiac risk models despite the high prevalence of chronic hepatic congestion in this population. We performed a retrospective observational analysis of 104 consecutive patients undergoing isolated pericardiectomy between 2010 and 2024 to determine whether established hepatic scoring systems [Child-Pugh, Model for End-Stage Liver Disease (MELD) and Model for End-Stage Liver Disease-Sodium (MELD-Na)] predict early mortality and major postoperative morbidity. Preoperative clinical and biochemical variables were used to derive the hepatic scores. The primary endpoint was 30-day mortality; the secondary endpoint was new postoperative renal-replacement therapy. Thirty-day mortality was 4.8% (5/104). Patients were classified as Child-Pugh A in 66 (63.5%), B in 35 (33.7%), and C in 3 (2.9%), with corresponding mortalities of 1.5%, 2.9%, and 100% (p<0.01 for trend). Discrimination for 30-day mortality was strong for Child-Pugh [area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) 0.89, 95% confidence interval 0.73-1.00], MELD (0.85, 0.60-0.98), and MELD-Na (0.83, 0.55-0.97), whereas EuroSCORE II showed no meaningful predictive ability (AUC≈0.51). Hepatic dysfunction quantified by Child-Pugh and MELD-based scores is a strong predictor of early mortality after pericardiectomy and outperforms conventional cardiac risk models in this cohort. Incorporation of structured hepatic assessment into preoperative risk stratification may improve perioperative planning and patient counseling; however, the small number of Child-Pugh C patients and the retrospective single-center design necessitate validation in larger prospective cohorts.

articles.title: Letter to the Editor: Association Between Fluid Overload and Pressure Injuries in ICU Patients With Sepsis: A Retrospective Cohort Study.
EXPRESS: Programmed Oscillatory Oxygen Therapy: Reframing Oxygen as a Dynamic Signal for Restoring Cerebrovascular Regulation After Ischemic Stroke.
articles.journal: Journal of cerebral blood flow and metabolism : official journal of the International Society of Cerebral Blood Flow and Metabolism
articles.abstract: Successful recanalization after ischemic stroke does not always restore adequate microvascular perfusion within previously ischemic tissue, partly because persistent microcirculatory dysfunction, impaired neurovascular coupling, and perfusion-metabolism mismatch continue to disrupt cerebral blood flow regulation. Conventional continuous oxygen therapy primarily increases systemic oxygen availability, but may be insufficient to restore impaired cerebrovascular responsiveness, while excessive or prolonged oxygen exposure may increase oxidative stress and attenuate adaptive oxygen-sensitive pathways. In this Review, we propose programmed oscillatory oxygen therapy (POOT) as a treatment-design framework for dynamic oxygen modulation after ischemic stroke. Rather than treating oxygen solely as a metabolic substrate, POOT reframes oxygen as a dynamic biological signal that may engage hypoxia-inducible factor, reactive oxygen species, nitric oxide, and related oxygen-sensitive pathways to support cerebral blood flow regulation and neurovascular coupling. Unlike fixed intermittent hypoxia, intermittent hyperoxia, or hypoxia-hyperoxia training protocols, POOT is proposed as a parameter-explicit and potentially feedback-informed framework targeting post-recanalization microvascular dysfunction. This framework integrates response window, oxygen intensity, cycle structure, treatment frequency and duration, and physiological feedback, providing a conceptual basis for advancing oxygen therapy toward more individualized and precision-oriented modulation after ischemic stroke.

articles.title: EXPRESS: Perfusion Extent and Hypoperfusion Severity Determine Diaschisis Patterns in Acute Ischemic Stroke: A CT Perfusion Study.
articles.journal: Journal of cerebral blood flow and metabolism : official journal of the International Society of Cerebral Blood Flow and Metabolism
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Diaschisis reflects remote functional suppression following focal ischemia and large-scale network disruption. We investigate the prevalence, overlap, and determinants of multiple diaschisis subtypes using acute CTP.

METHODS: We retrospectively analyzed 659 patients with hyperacute large-vessel occlusion stroke. Diaschisis was primarily assessed on CBV maps and classified into Crossed Cerebellar (CCD), Ipsilateral Thalamic (ITD), Ipsilateral Hippocampal (IHD), and CCD+ITD. Tmax-based assessment was exploratory. Multivariable logistic regression evaluated severe hypoperfusion extent (Tmax>6s), hypoperfusion intensity ratio (HIR), and ischemic core volume (CBF<30%).

RESULTS: CCD was the most common subtype, followed by ITD and CCD+ITD, whereas IHD was rare. Greater severe hypoperfusion extent was independently associated with CCD, ITD, and CCD+ITD, while higher HIR was additionally associated with ITD, and CCD+ITD. Ischemic core volume was not independently associated with diaschisis. CCD was independently associated with left hemispheric stroke, while combined CCD+ITD was associated with female sex. Exploratory Tmax-based analyses showed broadly similar associations. Subtype overlap suggested involvement of multiple interconnected network nodes.

CONCLUSION: Hyperacute diaschisis reflects ischemia-driven network dysfunction primarily related to severe hypoperfusion extent, with hypoperfusion severity contributing to specific subtypes. These findings support CBV-based CTP assessment for investigating large-scale network vulnerability, while Tmax-based may provide complementary information for future diaschisis research.

articles.title: EXPRESS: Neutral lipids in Thrombectomy-retrieved clots: Histological link to Stroke Severity, Etiology and 3-Months Functional Outcome.
articles.journal: Journal of cerebral blood flow and metabolism : official journal of the International Society of Cerebral Blood Flow and Metabolism
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND/HYPOTHESIS: Analysis of stroke thrombi collected during catheter-based recanalization offers a promising approach to refine etiological classification and guide treatment, as it provides pathophysiological insights through clot structure and composition. Despite the established role of lipids in large artery atherosclerotic stroke, their presence in stroke thrombi has not yet been studied histologically.

METHODS: In a prospective single-center cohort, neutral lipids were analysed by Oil Red O staining in 145 consecutively collected clots between 07/2020 and 08/2022, and lipid content was subsequently quantified using Orbit Image analysis. Clinical, laboratory and neuroradiological data were recorded. Functional outcome was assessed by modified Rankin Scale at 3 months.

RESULTS: Of 135 evaluable clots, 25 (19%) contained neutral lipids, present as lipid droplets, scattered deposits or foam-cell like configurations. Lipid-positive thrombi contained more fibrin, and patients with lipid-positive thrombi had greater stroke severity and worse functional outcome. Lipid positivity was independently associated with undetermined rather than cardioembolic stroke etiology after adjustment for fibrin content.

CONCLUSIONS: This is the first study to histologically identify neutral lipids within clots retrieved from acute ischemic stroke patients. Thrombus lipid content was associated with worse functional outcomes and may provide additional information on the underlying etiology of otherwise undetermined stroke.

articles.title: Pre-Procedural Prediction of Left Ventricular Ejection Fraction Normalization After Transcatheter Aortic Valve Implantation.
articles.journal: Catheterization and cardiovascular interventions : official journal of the Society for Cardiac Angiography & Interventions
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Transcatheter aortic valve implantation (TAVI) is an established therapy for severe aortic stenosis. Among patients with left ventricular (LV) systolic dysfunction, recovery of LV function after TAVI is heterogeneous, and reliable tools for pre-procedural risk stratification and patient counseling remain limited.

AIMS: We sought to identify simple pre-procedural predictors of complete LV functional recovery after TAVI and to develop a clinically applicable risk score to support patient counseling and post-procedural management.

METHODS: We retrospectively analyzed patients with severe aortic stenosis and baseline LV ejection fraction (LVEF) < 40% enrolled in a large multicenter registry in Japan. The primary outcome was complete LVEF normalization (LVEF > 50%) at 1 year after TAVI. Independent predictors were identified using multivariable logistic regression in a derivation cohort, and an exploratory weighted score was constructed. The score was preliminarily assessed in a separate single-center cohort.

RESULTS: The derivation cohort comprised 177 patients (median age 84 years; 44% women), of whom 94 (53%) achieved LVEF normalization. Lower body mass index (odds ratio [OR] 0.86, 95% confidence interval [CI] 0.77-0.95; p = 0.004), higher aortic valve peak velocity (OR 2.45, 95% CI 1.40-4.29; p = 0.002), and smaller LV end-diastolic diameter (OR 0.93, 95% CI 0.88-0.98; p = 0.020) were independently associated with LVEF normalization. The derived score stratified patients into low-, intermediate-, and high-probability groups (15%, 45%, and 71%, respectively; p < 0.001), with consistent discrimination in the validation cohort.

CONCLUSIONS: A simple exploratory score incorporating body mass index, transvalvular peak velocity, and LV size was associated with the probability of complete LV functional recovery after TAVI. This pre-procedural tool may facilitate patient counseling, expectation-setting, and identification of patients who may require closer heart failure follow-up after TAVI. It should not be used to determine eligibility for TAVI.

articles.title: Morphofunctional indices and ontogeny of long bones of the limbs in the frogs.
articles.abstract: Anuran limbs offer a valuable model for exploring how selective pressures, developmental constraints, and morphological evolution interact. While previous research has largely focused on total limb length, little is known about ontogenetic changes in the proportions of individual limb bones. This study introduces a novel approach using morphofunctional indices to investigate the functional roles of frog limbs, linking morphology to habitat use and locomotion. We present morphological and ontogenetic data from anurans in northwestern Argentina, emphasizing functionally relevant bone indices. Measurements were taken of 18 long bone dimensions (humerus, radioulna, femur, tibiofibula, tarsals) across 79 specimens at metamorphic, juvenile, and adult stages. Eight morphofunctional indices were calculated, including five newly proposed ones. Indices such as radioulna robustness, groove position, femur and tibiofibula robustness, and tarsal fusion differed among ecological and locomotor groups. Terrestrial hopper-walkers such as Rhinella arenarum and Rhinella spinulosa have more robust hind limb bones and shorter, less-fused tarsals than jumpers like Boana riojana. These traits may be functionally associated with short-distance jumping and shock absorption. We also observed a slenderness-robustness gradient across species, reflecting locomotor strategies. Stylopodial elements show negative allometry, while zeugopodial elements exhibit positive allometry, indicating increased precision and flexibility in limb function throughout development.

articles.title: Real-World Clinical Outcomes Following Initiation of the iLet® Bionic Pancreas in Youth with Type 1 Diabetes.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The iLet® Bionic Pancreas replaces carbohydrate counting and manual bolus calculations with simplified qualitative meal announcements. Its performance among diverse patients with high baseline glycated hemoglobin (HbA1c) is not well characterized.

METHODS: Retrospective, single-center cohort study of 71 patients aged 6-21 years with type 1 diabetes (T1D) who initiated the iLet Bionic Pancreas (2023-2025). Primary outcomes were changes in HbA1c and time in range (TIR; 70-180 mg/dL [3.9-10.0 mmol/L]) from baseline to 3 months. Secondary outcomes included glycemic metrics through 12 months, hypoglycemia, and meal-announcement behavior.

RESULTS: Mean age was 13.2 ± 3.5 years; 40.8% Black and 38.0% Medicaid-insured. Baseline HbA1c was 9.4 ± 2.1% (79 ± 23 mmol/mol) and TIR was 30.1 ± 19.0%. At 3 months, HbA1c decreased by 1.8 ± 1.7% (-20 ± 19 mmol/mol) and TIR increased by 22.4 ± 22.5 percentage points (both P < 0.0001) without increased hypoglycemia. Improvements were greatest among participants with baseline HbA1c ≥ 9.5% (≥80 mmol/mol) (ΔHbA1c = -3.0% [-32 mmol/mol]; ΔTIR = +31.2 percentage points). Among participants with paired 12-month data, HbA1c decreased from 9.6%-7.6% and TIR increased from 27.7 to 55.8% (both P < 0.0001). Mean meal announcements were 2.9/d at 3 months and 2.1/d at 12 months (P = 0.722) and were not associated with HbA1c or TIR at 3 months.

CONCLUSIONS: In this real-world pediatric cohort, iLet initiation was associated with substantial glycemic improvement without increased hypoglycemia, particularly among participants with high baseline HbA1c. Favorable outcomes were observed among participants contributing paired 12-month data.

articles.title: Understanding Workplace Violence in Healthcare: Insights from an Eight-Year Case Study in a Swiss Hospital Network.
articles.journal: International journal for quality in health care : journal of the International Society for Quality in Health Care
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Workplace violence against healthcare workers is a growing concern worldwide, with consequences for staff well-being, care quality, and patient safety. However, longitudinal evidence from hospital networks remains limited, and few studies have used statistical process control-informed visual methods to monitor trends over time. This study examined whether reported aggression trends showed distinct temporal patterns across a Swiss public hospital network and whether such patterns could generate hypotheses regarding potentially associated organizational and contextual factors.

METHODS: We conducted a retrospective observational study of reported aggressions toward healthcare staff across the Ente Ospedaliero Cantonale (EOC), the public hospital network of southern Switzerland, over an eight-year period (2017-2024). Data were extracted from the network's internal quality and occupational safety reporting platform. Two standardized indicators were calculated annually for each hospital: aggressions per 1,000 inpatient days and aggressions per 1,000 discharges. Individual control charts with boundaries at ± 1, ±2, and ±3 standard deviations were used to examine temporal patterns, complemented by exploratory simple linear regression to estimate overall linear trends across the full network, the network excluding Locarno Hospital (ODL), and ODL alone.

RESULTS: Across the network, reported aggressions showed an overall upward pattern, with the highest levels recorded in 2024. When standardized by inpatient activity and discharges, both indicators showed increasing trajectories at network level. In contrast, at ODL aggression rates increased from 2018 to 2021, followed by consecutive annual decreases through 2024. Aggressions per 1,000 inpatient days decreased from 1.32 in 2021 to 0.78 in 2024. This temporal pattern differed from the continuing upward pattern observed across the rest of the network. Exploratory linear regression over the full 2017-2024 period did not show statistically significant overall linear trends at ODL. Most reported incidents in 2022-2024 were perpetrated by patients, nursing staff were the most affected professional group, and geriatric units accounted for the largest proportion of reports.

CONCLUSIONS: This study extends previous single-hospital evidence by adopting a network-level perspective, a longer observation period, and statistical process control-informed visual methods. The findings suggest that aggression trends may not be uniform across comparable hospital settings. Although causal inference is not possible, the distinct temporal pattern observed at ODL generates hypotheses regarding organizational and contextual factors potentially associated with differences in workplace violence trajectories and warrants further investigation. Continuous monitoring using standardized indicators may support organizational learning, benchmarking, and targeted prevention.

articles.title: Implementation of a multi-disciplinary hemodialysis access clinic improves time to surgical evaluation and access case volume.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Delays in hemodialysis access creation contribute to prolonged tunneled dialysis catheter dependence and morbidity. In March 2025, our institution implemented a multidisciplinary accelerated hemodialysis access clinic with weekly reserved appointments, same-day duplex vein mapping, and streamlined nephrology-to-surgery referral. We evaluated its effect on access volume, timing to surgical evaluation, and catheter dependence.

METHODS: We performed a retrospective chart review of adults undergoing hemodialysis access procedures at a tertiary academic center from March 17, 2024 to March 13, 2026. Access volume was compared before and after implementation. Patient-level timing metrics were compared between patients evaluated in standard vascular surgery clinic versus multidisciplinary accelerated clinic.

RESULTS: Mean monthly access volume increased from 3.08 ± 2.15 to 8.58 ± 3.00 cases after implementation, an increase of 5.5 cases per month (p < 0.001). Annual access volume increased from 37 to 103 cases (p < 0.001). Among 53 patients, 29 were evaluated in the standard clinic and 24 in the multidisciplinary clinic. Referral-to-clinic time decreased from 63.6 ± 47.7 to 41.0 ± 35.9 days (p = 0.01). Clinic-to-operation time did not differ significantly (21.8 ± 18.5 vs 27.1 ± 17.2 days; p = 0.14). Overall referral-to-operation time decreased from 85.4 ± 51.5 to 68.2 ± 43.9 days but did not reach significance (p = 0.07). Catheter dependence was lower in the multidisciplinary cohort (29% vs 48%; OR 0.36, 95% CI 0.11-1.16). Same-day vein mapping was performed more frequently in the accelerated clinic cohort than in the standard clinic cohort (100% vs 51.7%, p < 0.001).

CONCLUSIONS: A multidisciplinary accelerated hemodialysis access clinic increased procedural volume and shortened time to surgical evaluation. However, total time to access creation was not significantly reduced, suggesting that downstream operative capacity may remain an important barrier.

articles.title: Comparison of arteriovenous fistula patency in lipoprotein apheresis and haemodialysis: A matched case-control study.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Arteriovenous fistulas constitute an effective vascular access option for haemodialysis, demonstrating high patency rates and lower infection risk compared with synthetic accesses. Treatment algorithms and patient characteristics differ between haemodialysis and apheresis therapy, and fistula outcomes in patients receiving lipoprotein apheresis have not yet been systematically evaluated.

METHODS: This single-centre, retrospective cohort study compared arteriovenous fistula outcomes in 29 patients receiving lipoprotein apheresis with those of 87 frequency-matched patients on haemodialysis. Matching criteria included age, sex, fistula configuration and diabetes mellitus status. Primary and secondary patency rates and associated risk factors were assessed over a 24-month follow-up period using Kaplan-Meier and Cox regression analysis.

RESULTS: The study included patients with radiocephalic (n = 72) or brachiocephalic (n = 44) arteriovenous fistulas. Indications for apheresis were elevated lipoprotein(a) levels (n = 26) and dyslipoproteinemia (n = 3). Mean age was comparable between groups (61.4 vs 61.2 years), as was the proportion of male patients (58.6% vs 60.9%). Diabetes mellitus was present in 58.6% of apheresis patients and 49.4% of haemodialysis patients. Two-year primary patency rates were comparable between groups (49.2% vs 50.8%), while secondary patency was lower in the apheresis group (59.9% vs 71.1%). In the apheresis cohort, diabetes was associated with reduced primary (HR, 4.034; 95 % CI, 1.10-14.80; p = 0.035) and secondary patency (HR, 9.807; 95 % CI, 1.24-77.59; p = 0.030). Apheresis before fistula creation demonstrated improved secondary patency (HR, 0.198; 95% CI, 0.04-0.94; p = 0.042). In haemodialysis patients, hyperlipoproteinemia was associated with reduced secondary patency (HR, 2.28; 95% CI, 1.01-5.14; p = 0.046).

CONCLUSIONS: Arteriovenous fistula patency in patients undergoing apheresis was comparable to haemodialysis patients despite elevated lipoprotein levels. Diabetes was associated with reduced fistula patency in lipoprotein apheresis. The findings support arteriovenous fistulas as long-term access option and highlight the importance of individualised access planning.

articles.title: Prenatal Diagnosis of Pulmonary Arteriovenous Malformation With 3D/4D STIC Fetal Echocardiography.
articles.abstract: Pulmonary arteriovenous malformation (PAVM) is a rare congenital vascular anomaly characterized by direct communication between the pulmonary artery and vein, resulting in a right-to-left shunt. Prenatal diagnosis remains uncommon. We report a fetal PAVM diagnosed at 21 weeks' gestation on fetal echocardiography. Color Doppler with graphic flow imaging demonstrated turbulent swirling flow within the right pulmonary vein, while spectral Doppler showed an arterialized pulmonary venous waveform. High-definition color Doppler and 3D/4D spatiotemporal image correlation (STIC) rendering confirmed a fistulous communication between the right pulmonary artery and vein. Prenatal recognition of PAVM is essential for serial surveillance, parental counseling, multidisciplinary perinatal planning, and early neonatal intervention.

articles.title: Editorial for "Association of Cardiac MRI-Derived Epicardial Adipose Tissue Index With Adverse Clinical Outcomes in Heart Failure With Preserved Ejection Fraction".
articles.journal: Journal of magnetic resonance imaging : JMRI

articles.title: Short-Term Complications of Transcatheter Aortic Valve Replacement: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis (PROLONG-TAVR).
articles.journal: Catheterization and cardiovascular interventions : official journal of the Society for Cardiac Angiography & Interventions
articles.abstract: To estimate the cumulative incidence of short-term complications across different transcatheter heart valve (THV) prostheses used for transcatheter aortic valve replacement (TAVR). We performed a systematic review and meta-analysis in accordance with PRISMA and a prospectively registered PROSPERO protocol. Observational studies published from 2002 through May 2024 that included patients with severe aortic stenosis undergoing predominantly transfemoral TAVR and reported prosthesis-specific complications were eligible. Although the original protocol intended to evaluate both short- and long-term complications, long-term outcomes were too sparse and inconsistently reported for robust pooled analyses; therefore, the present analysis focuses on short-term complications. Pooled cumulative incidences were calculated using random-effects models. We included 242 studies comprising 181,187 patients. SAPIEN 3 had the lowest incidence of moderate-to-severe paravalvular leak (PVL) (1.04%, 95% CI 0.69-1.55) and stroke (1.87%, 95% CI 1.64-2.14), whereas ACURATE neo2 had the lowest incidence of permanent pacemaker implantation (PPI) (7.7%, 95% CI 5.82-10.11). Evolut PRO and SAPIEN 3 showed among the lowest rates of major vascular complications (3.56%, 95% CI 2.77-4.57 and 3.87%, 95% CI 3.22-4.66, respectively) and major or life-threatening bleeding (2.96%, 95% CI 2.09-4.17 and 4.8%, 95% CI 4.04-5.69, respectively). Short-term complications have decreased with newer-generation THV prostheses. PVL remains more frequent with self-expanding valves, whereas PPI is the most frequent complication and is generally less frequent with balloon-expandable valves and ACURATE neo2. Stroke rates have changed little across newer generations, and annular rupture, coronary artery obstruction, and valve embolization remain rare (< 1%).

articles.title: International recommendations for child to adult care transition in rare neurological diseases: A scoping review and Delphi consensus study.
A Mitochondria-Targeted and pH-Responsive Fe3+-Astragalin Nanoplatform Reprograms Metabolism to Protect Against Acute Kidney Injury.
articles.abstract: Acute kidney injury (AKI) is a life-threatening clinical syndrome characterized by abrupt renal dysfunction, excessive oxidative stress, inflammatory activation, and profound metabolic disturbances, yet effective therapeutic strategies remain limited. Herein, we developed an ultrasmall pH-responsive nanoplatform (FeAst) through the self-assembly of Fe3+ and the natural flavonoid Astragalin (Ast) for injury-responsive renal delivery and metabolic intervention. The Fe3+-phenolic coordination network endows FeAst with excellent biocompatibility, intrinsic reactive oxygen species (ROS)-scavenging capacity, and mitochondria-targeting capability. Importantly, FeAst preferentially accumulated in injured kidneys, enabling targeted renal delivery. Moreover, the mildly acidic microenvironment associated with AKI triggered partial dissociation of the coordination network, enabling localized Ast release and sustained therapeutic activity. Across multiple experimental models of kidney injury, FeAst markedly improved renal function, alleviated tubular injury, suppressed inflammatory responses, and restored redox homeostasis. Mechanistically, FeAst preserved mitochondrial integrity, re-established glutathione-dependent antioxidant defense, suppressed ferroptosis-related processes by reducing lipid peroxidation and restoring ferroptosis defense systems, and reprogrammed TCA cycle-associated energy metabolism. Moreover, FeAst activated PPAR signaling and suppressed p38 MAPK/NF-κB-mediated inflammatory responses, thereby enhancing cellular bioenergetics and resistance to oxidative stress. Collectively, this injury-responsive nanoplatform integrates selective renal accumulation, controlled drug release, and metabolic reprogramming to provide a promising strategy for precision kidney injury therapy.

articles.title: A Machine Learning Model Based on Ultrasound and Serological Markers for Predicting Postoperative Stenosis of Rex Shunt Procedure in Children With Extrahepatic Portal Venous Obstruction.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: To evaluate the value of combining ultrasound parameters with serological markers for predicting postoperative Rex shunt stenosis in children with extrahepatic portal venous obstruction (EHPVO).

METHODS: The training cohort and temporal validation cohort consisted of 114 and 38 children with EHPVO after Rex shunt procedure, respectively. The study variables included clinical characteristics, ultrasound parameters, and serological markers. Five machine learning models were developed to predict postoperative stenosis after the Rex shunt procedure at different follow-up periods, with performance evaluated using the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUROC).

RESULTS: In the temporal validation cohort, the optimal Logistic regression model integrating ultrasound parameters and serological markers achieved AUROCs of 0.61 (95% CI: 0.38-0.84) at 1 month, 0.67 (95% CI: 0.45-0.90) at 3 months, and 0.82 (95% CI: 0.67-0.98) at 6 months for predicting stenosis.

CONCLUSIONS: A model combining serological markers and ultrasound parameters serves as a promising exploratory prototype for predicting Rex shunt stenosis in children with EHPVO, pending further independent multicenter validation.

articles.title: Pulsed Field Versus Radiofrequency Ablation of Atrial Fibrillation: Esophageal Lesions and Suspected Gastroparesis.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Esophageal mucosal injury and gastroparesis are clinically important complications of radiofrequency ablation (RFA) of atrial fibrillation (AF). Pulsed-field ablation (PFA) is a non-thermal modality that may spare these complications due to its myocardial tissue selectivity.

OBJECTIVES: We aimed to compare the incidence of endoscopically detected esophageal lesions (EDELs) and suspected gastroparesis between RFA and PFA as the primary endpoints. Secondary endpoints included perioperative complications, procedural parameters, and 365-day clinical outcomes.

METHODS: Between July 2023 and July 2025, patients undergoing a first-time AF ablation with RFA or PFA were enrolled. RFA was performed using either a QDOT MICRO catheter (Biosense Webster, Inc., Irvine, CA, USA) or a TactiFlex Ablation Catheter, Sensor Enabled (Abbott, Abbott Park, IL, USA), while PFA was performed using the FARAPULSE system or the PulseSelect system. All patients underwent upper gastrointestinal endoscopy on the day after ablation. An EDEL was defined as esophageal erythema, erosion, ulcer, or atrio-esophageal fistula. Suspected gastroparesis was defined as gastric food residue after > 12 h of overnight fasting. Clinical follow-up was performed with 12-lead or Holter electrocardiography.

RESULTS: A total of 84 patients were included (RFA: n = 43; PFA: n = 41). Esophageal erosion was observed in 2 patients in the RFA group (4.7%) and in none in the PFA group (p = 0.49). Suspected gastroparesis occurred in 15 patients treated with RFA (34.9%) and in none treated with PFA (P<0.001). All patients were asymptomatic during endoscopy. No other procedural complications were observed in either group. The total procedure time was significantly shorter with PFA (158.5 ± 40.8 vs. 193.8 ± 38.3 min, p < 0.001), while the fluoroscopy time was longer. At 365 days, atrial arrhythmia recurrence rates were comparable between the two groups (p = 0.47).

CONCLUSIONS: In this single-center cohort, PFA was associated with a significantly lower incidence of suspected gastroparesis than RFA, and no EDELs were observed in the PFA group. PFA may reduce gastrointestinal injury associated with AF ablation. Further studies are needed to confirm these findings and clarify their clinical significance.

articles.title: Comparative Outcomes of Left Anterior Thoracotomy Versus Resternotomy for Pulmonic Valve Replacement After Tetralogy of Fallot Repair.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Redo pulmonary valve replacement (PVR) in patients with prior tetralogy of Fallot (TOF) repair is surgically challenging. This study aimed to compare the clinical outcomes of the left anterior minithoracotomy (LAT) approach with the traditional resternotomy approach for PVR.

METHODS: A retrospective analysis was conducted on 38 TOF patients who underwent redo PVR, categorized into LAT (n = 20) and resternotomy (n = 18) groups. Patients requiring concomitant valvular surgeries or repair of residual intracardiac shunts were excluded. We compared demographics, operative details, and postoperative outcomes.

RESULTS: Baseline demographics were comparable between groups, except for a higher proportion of males in the LAT group (75% vs 38.9%, P = 0.047). The LAT approach demonstrated nonsignificant favorable trends, including shorter operative times (157.05 ± 49.42 vs 178.06 ± 58.69 min, P = 0.239) and shorter postoperative hospital stays (4.75 ± 1.21 vs 6.17 ± 4.38 days, P = 0.173). Vasoactive-inotropic scores were significantly lower in the LAT group both immediately postoperatively (0.05 ± 0.22 vs 4.36 ± 6.95, P = 0.009) and on postoperative day 1 (0 vs 2.17 ± 4.52, P = 0.039). Postoperative complications, such as atrial fibrillation and pleural effusion, were similar between groups. There was no mortality in either group.

CONCLUSIONS: The LAT approach for PVR after TOF repair is a safe alternative to resternotomy. Comprehensive preoperative imaging evaluation is crucial for determining the optimal incision site. Further studies with larger cohorts are needed to confirm the potential benefits of this approach.

articles.title: Chrysanthemum Morifolium-Derived Nanovesicles Reduce Lactate-Associated Histone Lactylation and Modulate Microglia-Mediated Neuroinflammation in Sepsis-Associated Encephalopathy.
articles.abstract: Sepsis-associated encephalopathy (SAE)-a complication of the central nervous system in patients with sepsis-markedly diminishes cognitive functions and is linked to hippocampal neuritis-induced injury. Plant exosome-like nanovesicles can transport proteins, lipids, and molecular compounds between neural cells and the periphery, thereby modulating target cells. This study examined the therapeutic potential of Chrysanthemum morifolium-derived exosome-like nanovesicles (CRELNVs) in an animal model of lipopolysaccharide-induced SAE, revealing their ability to effectively cross the blood-brain barrier, be internalized by microglia, and alleviate nerve injury and memory impairment by reducing lactate levels in microglia at the hippocampus. CRELNVs decreased lactylation levels in microglia, thus promoting the conversion of microglial cells from the detrimental M1 metabolic phenotype to the protective M2 one. Mechanistically, our finding suggest CRELNVs reduced proinflammatory cytokine release is associated with the inhibition of NF-κB activation. Thus, CRELNVs were concluded to exert their protective effects by modulating the H3K18la/NF-κB axis and regulate microglia-mediated neuroinflammation by responding to the hippocampal neuritis-induced injury in SAE.

articles.title: Corticosteroid Exposure in Autoimmune Hepatitis: Early Toxicity, Cumulative Burden and Associations With Long-Term Patient-Reported Outcomes.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Autoimmune hepatitis (AIH) requires corticosteroid-based induction therapy, but prolonged exposure is common in practice.

AIMS: This study quantified corticosteroid utilization patterns and associations with adverse outcomes from a patient perspective.

METHODS: A cross-sectional patient-reported survey recruited AIHA network members with physician-confirmed AIH (N = 563). Corticosteroid exposure was quantified using annual duration thresholds (≥ 90 days/year at ≥ 5 mg/day prednisone-equivalent). Early side effects (within 6 months; n = 491) and long-term metabolic complications (≥ 2 years disease duration; n = 385) were assessed using multivariable logistic regression adjusting for age, sex and disease duration.

RESULTS: Among 563 participants (median age 53 years; 87.4% female), all participants received a corticosteroid at diagnosis (77.6% prednisone; 11.4% budesonide). Side effects within 6 months were near-universal (96.6%; median 5 symptoms) and greater with predniso(lo)ne than budesonide (5.82 vs. 3.55 symptoms; p < 0.001); 51.2% of predniso(lo)ne-initiated patients developed a new metabolic condition within 6 months. Long-term complications affected 75.9% of the chronically exposed cohort, including weight gain > 5% (47.0%), osteoporosis (30.4%) and hypertension (18.1%). Each additional cumulative year of extensive exposure was independently associated with the composite adverse outcome (adjusted OR 1.11, 95% CI 1.02-1.22; p = 0.014), osteoporosis, Type 2 diabetes, weight gain and cataracts, with significant dose-response gradients (p-trend ≤ 0.008). Patients with > 5 cumulative years had 4-fold higher odds of the composite outcome versus patients in the None exposure group (OR 4.21, 95% CI 1.51-11.71).

CONCLUSIONS: Corticosteroid exposure in AIH is associated with dose-dependent toxicity from the first months of treatment. Reduced induction dosing and budesonide represent potential steroid-minimization strategies in appropriate patients, warranting prospective evaluation.

articles.title: UEFA consensus guidelines on anterior cruciate ligament (ACL) injury in Women's football - part one: risk factors and prevention.
articles.abstract: Anterior cruciate ligament (ACL) injuries are among the most burdensome injuries in women's football, carrying significant consequences for players and the football community. To develop practical, evidence-based guidelines for ACL injury prevention, UEFA convened a multidisciplinary expert panel of 31 doctors, sports scientists, physiotherapists, and a player. Using the RAND-UCLA Appropriateness Method, 101 evidence statements were synthesised from existing literature and subjected to a modified Delphi process with three rounds of confidential voting. Consensus was reached on 88 statements. Through online and in-person discussions, this evidence was integrated with expert and clinical and practical judgement to produce actionable recommendations tailored to women's football. The guidelines conclude that ACL injuries in women's football typically occur in non-contact situations during high-intensity movements such as cutting, pressing, or landing, and may be influenced by a combination of modifiable and non-modifiable risk factors. Proposed modifiable factors include deficits in neuromuscular control, strength, and movement quality, which can be addressed through multicomponent prevention strategies. These programmes were identified as the most effective, incorporating plyometric, strength, and proximal control exercises performed two to three times per week for 15 to 20 minutes, with evidence showing they can reduce non-contact ACL injuries when adherence is high. Successful implementation requires context-specific tailoring, embedding programmes into routine training, and addressing barriers such as limited resources, time constraints, and lack of coach education. The guidelines recommend enhancing buy-in through co-creation with coaches and players, integrating prevention into existing practice, and strengthening organisational and policy support to sustain long-term adoption.

articles.title: Uefa consensus guidelines on anterior cruciate ligament (ACL) injury in women's football - Part Two: rehabilitation, return to play, and players' perceptions.
articles.abstract: Anterior cruciate ligament (ACL) injuries remain a major challenge to player health and performance in women's football. They are associated with lengthy rehabilitation, a high risk of re-injury, and potential long-term knee issues that can impact both career longevity and quality of life. Building on Part One of the UEFA consensus, which addressed risk factors and prevention, Part Two addresses the continuum of care after ACL injury, from rehabilitation to return to play (RTP) and beyond. A multidisciplinary panel of 26 experts in sports medicine, physiotherapy, orthopaedics, and performance science developed evidence-informed statements using a modified RAND-UCLA Appropriateness Method. Through three Delphi rounds, 180 statements were assessed and refined, resulting in consensus on 170 (94%). The panel supported a player-centred, criterion-based approach where progression relies on clinical and functional milestones rather than fixed timelines. Key recommendations emphasise restoring quadriceps strength as a central milestone, integrating neuromuscular and psychological readiness assessments, and adopting phased RTP protocols that gradually re-expose players to the physical and cognitive demands of the game. Psychological and social factors (fear of re-injury, motivation, communication, and support networks) are recognised as vital influences on recovery. These guidelines offer practical, evidence-based advice for medical and performance staff working in women's football. By combining scientific research with expert consensus, they support a holistic, collaborative approach to ACL rehabilitation aimed at protecting player health, lowering re-injury risk, and enabling a confident, sustained return to performance.

articles.title: Economic Evaluation of Prolonged Hypothermic Oxygenated Machine Perfusion Enabling Daytime Liver Transplantation.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Short-duration (1-2 h) dual hypothermic oxygenated machine perfusion (DHOPE) reduces ischemia-reperfusion injury-related complications. Prolonged DHOPE preservation (DHOPE-PRO) may facilitate logistics. We assessed the economic impact of DHOPE-PRO versus conventional short-duration DHOPE, hypothesizing that DHOPE-PRO would not be associated with increased one-year transplantation-related costs.

METHODS: This post hoc economic evaluation of the prospective DHOPE-PRO trial (NL8740) included adult recipients of livers donated after brain death. All transplantation-related medical expenses up to one year post-transplant were collected. The cost of resource use was calculated using 2022 full hospital prices indexed to 2024. Time-driven variable costing was applied to perfusion, surgery, and intensive care costs. The primary outcome was total one-year transplantation-related cost.

RESULTS: Of 24 patients, 12 received a liver after DHOPE and 12 after DHOPE-PRO. Median one-year total costs were €83 583 [interquartile range (IQR) 78 400-104 158] for DHOPE and €78 582 [IQR 73123-92 855] for DHOPE-PRO (p = 0.347). Perfusion costs were higher with DHOPE-PRO (€23 926 [IQR 22711-24 697] versus €17 306 [IQR 16928-17 594]; p < 0.001), while surgery costs were lower (€18 560 [IQR 17806-20 747] versus €21 303 [IQR 19535-25 418]; p = 0.033). Costs related to other medical activities did not differ between groups.

CONCLUSION: In this exploratory single-center economic evaluation, DHOPE-PRO enabled daytime liver transplantation without evidence of increased one-year transplantation-related costs compared with short-duration DHOPE. Higher perfusion-related costs were accompanied by lower surgery-related costs in this cohort. These findings warrant confirmation in larger studies.

TRIAL REGISTRATION: Netherlands Trial Registry number: NL8740.

articles.title: Immediate effects of spinal manipulation, exercise therapy, and open-label placebo on lifting performance and pain in individuals with chronic non-specific back pain: a motion laboratory-based crossover randomized controlled trial.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Chronic non-specific back pain (CBP) is a leading cause of disability worldwide and is commonly associated with limitations in movements such as lifting. Although spinal manipulation (SMT) and exercise therapy (ET) are recommended treatments for CBP, their effects on objectively measured movement performance remain insufficiently explored. Open-label placebo (OLP) has gained attention for engaging placebo-related mechanisms ethically. This study aimed to investigate the immediate effects of SMT, ET, and OLP on lifting performance and pain in individuals with CBP, and to evaluate the add-on effects of OLP.

METHODS: A motion laboratory-based crossover randomized controlled trial included 50 individuals with CBP. Participants were recruited between April and July 2025 and attended a single laboratory session between September and October 2025. Participants performed lifting tasks using light and heavy loads before and after SMT, ET, and OLP interventions in randomized order. Three-dimensional motion capture was used to assess temporal, spatial, and spatiotemporal aspects of lifting performance. Subjective outcomes included pain intensity, perceived effectiveness, willingness to undergo each treatment, and treatment preference. Data were analyzed using linear mixed-effects models and functional data analysis.

RESULTS: Overall lifting performance changed to a small degree following the interventions. No significant between-group differences were observed at the primary endpoint. Significant within-group changes were observed following SMT, including altered intersegmental coordination during the light lift, characterized by a greater relative contribution of back movement early in the lifting phase, reduced thorax-pelvis tilt during the heavy lift, and reduced pain. OLP was associated with reduced thorax-pelvis tilt and increased hip and knee flexion during the light lift. Subjective evaluations did not consistently correspond to objective biomechanical changes.

CONCLUSION: SMT, ET, and OLP demonstrated limited immediate effects on overall lifting performance in individuals with CBP. However, some within-group changes in thorax-pelvis movement and intersegmental coordination suggest that certain aspects of movement quality may respond to short-term interventions even when conventional biomechanical outcomes remain largely unchanged. The findings suggest the value of integrating subjective and objective outcomes, while advanced biomechanical analyses may provide insight into subtle movement changes in CBP.

TRIAL REGISTRATION: The trial is registered at ClinicalTrials.gov (ID NCT06891625).

articles.title: Correction: Dyslipidemia is associated with abdominal fat depots but not with bone mineral density and muscle fat infiltration.

Correction: Protocol for a randomized controlled trial comparing saturated and unsaturated fat sources of a ketogenic diet (KETO-IM) investigating cardiovascular, inflammatory and immune function outcomes in adults living with overweight and prediabetes or type 2 diabetes in Edmonton, Canada.
Correction: Characteristics of plantar pressure during walking in stroke patients with hemiplegia of different brunnstrom stages: a study based on five-region smart insoles.
Neuroimmune-oligovascular signaling shapes oligodendrocyte precursor cell fate and repair after ischemic stroke.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Ischemic stroke causes neuronal and oligodendroglial injury, axonal and myelin damage, and neurovascular unit dysfunction. Oligodendrocyte precursor cells (OPCs) are lifelong progenitors that generate oligodendrocytes while receiving and transmitting signals within neural, immune, and vascular microenvironments. This review examines how neuroimmune-oligovascular communication and intracellular signaling shape OPC survival, recruitment, state transitions, differentiation, and remyelination after ischemic stroke.

MAIN BODY: We first define OPC lineage identity, functional heterogeneity, and signaling interfaces with neurons, microglia/macrophages, astrocytes, endothelial cells, and pericytes. We then examine how excitotoxic, metabolic, redox, inflammatory, vascular, extracellular-matrix, and regulated cell-death signals converge on OPCs across lesion compartments and disease phases. Severe core ischemia depletes the progenitor pool, whereas partially perfused peri-infarct tissue permits reactive proliferation and migration. During the subacute phase, intercellular signals within the post-ischemic niche influence whether recruited OPCs adopt inflammatory, angiogenic, differentiation-competent, or arrested states. Long-term repair ultimately depends on lineage completion and stable myelin formation rather than OPC accumulation alone. The strongest causal evidence supports signaling from the surrounding niche as a regulator of OPC differentiation and demonstrates that OPC-derived myelin repair contributes to neuronal preservation and functional recovery. By contrast, evidence that endogenous OPCs themselves substantially regulate post-stroke inflammation, angiogenesis, blood-brain barrier integrity, or synaptic reconstruction remains less complete and often derives from culture, conditioned-medium, pharmacological, or transplantation paradigms. Therapeutic strategies are therefore organized according to the signaling and lineage bottleneck they target, including acute OPC preservation, niche remodeling, lineage completion, oligovascular reconstruction, and cell-based interventions.

CONCLUSIONS: OPC fate after ischemic stroke is determined by the interaction of cell-intrinsic signaling competence with temporally and spatially changing neuroimmune-oligovascular cues. Translation will require lineage-resolved causal studies, human spatial and longitudinal validation, signaling-linked target-engagement measures, and treatment strategies matched to lesion phase, compartment, and repair bottleneck. A cell-communication framework may therefore provide a more mechanistically testable basis for OPC-centered white-matter repair after stroke.

articles.title: Routine versus postoperative CRP/CT guided selective diverting ileostomy after laparoscopic low anterior resection for rectal cancer: a comparative randomized controlled trial.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Diverting ileostomy is routinely used to protect the anastomosis after laparoscopic low anterior resection (LAR) for rectal cancer, but it exposes most patients to stoma-related morbidity even though only a minority develop a true anastomotic leak. This trial evaluated whether a postoperative C-reactive protein (CRP) and computed tomography (CT) guided selective ileostomy strategy could reduce the rate of ileostomy formation compared with routine diversion.

METHODS: In this RCT, 200 patients with stage II or III middle or lower third rectal cancer undergoing laparoscopic LAR were randomized 1:1 to a CRP/CT-guided selective ileostomy group (n = 100) or a routine diverting ileostomy group (n = 100). In the CRP/CT group, serum CRP was measured daily from postoperative day 1; a threshold of 114 mg/L on day 3 or a rise greater than 15 mg/L per day triggered confirmatory contrast-enhanced CT, with ileostomy formed only if findings were suspicious for leak. The primary outcome was the stoma-free status throughout the 12-month follow-up.

RESULTS: Baseline demographic and tumor characteristics were similar between groups (all p > 0.05). Ileostomy formation was markedly lower in the CRP/CT group than the routine group (22.0% vs. 100.0%, p < 0.001). Anastomotic leak rates did not differ (0% vs. 1.0%, p = 1.000), nor did overall complication rates (31.0% vs. 32.0%, p = 0.879). Operative time (148.4 ± 14.0 vs. 166.6 ± 13.1 min, p < 0.001) and intraoperative blood loss (168.9 ± 28.2 vs. 197.3 ± 39.7 mL, p < 0.001) were significantly lower in the CRP/CT group. Stoma-related complications were far less frequent with the selective strategy (3.0% vs. 30.0%, p < 0.001). The CRP/CT group reported significantly better global health status, physical functioning, and emotional functioning scores (all p < 0.001).

CONCLUSION: A postoperative CRP/CT-guided selective ileostomy strategy reduces the need for diverting ileostomy after laparoscopic low anterior resection for rectal cancer while improving operative outcomes and quality of life; however, confirmed leakage was infrequent in both groups. This approach may serve as an alternative to routine diversion in appropriately monitored surgical units.

TRIAL REGISTRATION: This trial was retrospectively registered at ClinicalTrials.gov (Identifier: NCT07722533) on July 17, 2026.

articles.title: Association of Cardiac MRI-Derived Epicardial Adipose Tissue Index With Adverse Clinical Outcomes in Heart Failure With Preserved Ejection Fraction.
articles.journal: Journal of magnetic resonance imaging : JMRI
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The clinical relevance of the epicardial adipose tissue index (EATI) is increasingly recognized, but its association with clinical outcomes in patients with heart failure with preserved ejection fraction (HFpEF) remains inadequately investigated.

PURPOSE: To evaluate the association between cardiac MRI-derived EATI and major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE) in patients with HFpEF.

STUDY TYPE: Retrospective.

POPULATION: Two hundred sixty-five patients with HFpEF (135 male; mean age 55 years).

FIELD STRENGTH/SEQUENCE: 1.5 T/balanced steady-state free precession.

ASSESSMENT: EATI was quantified on cardiac MRI cine images. MACE was defined as cardiac death or readmission for heart failure.

STATISTICAL TESTS: Welch t-test or Mann-Whitney U test, Cox proportional hazards regression, Kaplan-Meier analysis with log-rank test, and global χ2 model comparison. A p value < 0.05 was considered significant.

RESULTS: During a median follow-up of 33 months (22-65), 42 patients experienced MACE. EATI was significantly higher in the MACE group than in the no-MACE group (33.65 ± 13.91 vs. 26.13 ± 11.28 mL/m2, Z = -3.52, effect size r = -0.22). EATI was independently associated with MACE (multivariable HR = 1.04 [95% CI: 1.01-1.06]). Kaplan-Meier survival analysis confirmed that patients with low EATI had significantly higher event-free survival rate. A model combining EATI with other clinical and conventional imaging risk factors (χ2 = 42.3) showed significantly improved model discrimination for identifying patients at risk of MACE compared with models with clinical variables (χ2 = 26.0) or clinical and conventional imaging variables (χ2 = 34.3).

DATA CONCLUSION: Cardiac MRI-derived EATI was independently associated with MACE in patients with HFpEF and showed favorable discriminatory performance compared with clinical and conventional imaging risk factors.

EVIDENCE LEVEL: 3.

TECHNICAL EFFICACY: Stage 5.

articles.title: The GLP-1R/GCGR Dual Agonist Mazdutide Attenuates Liver Steatosis and Decreases Circulating Cholesterol Levels in Mice With Metabolic Dysfunction-Associated Steatotic Liver Disease.
Assessment of Dental Students' and Recent Graduates' Knowledge of Artificial Intelligence Applications in Dentistry.
articles.journal: European journal of dental education : official journal of the Association for Dental Education in Europe
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Artificial intelligence (AI) is transforming dentistry by enhancing diagnostic accuracy, clinical efficiency and personalized treatment planning. This study evaluates the awareness and perceptions of AI applications among dental students and recent graduates to support AI integration in dental education and practice.

MATERIALS AND METHODS: This cross-sectional study included third, fourth and fifth-year students, along with dentists who graduated within the past 5 years. A total of 452 participants completed a 26-item online survey via Google Forms between July 1 and September 1, 2024. The survey comprised demographic data and AI awareness assessment. Data were analysed using SPSS (version 21, IBM, Chicago, USA), with reliability analyses and descriptive statistics conducted. Fisher-Freeman-Halton Exact Test was used for group comparisons (p < 0.05).

RESULTS: Participants were evenly distributed by academic year, predominantly female and aged 20-30. No significant differences were found between educational levels and gender. Most participants acknowledged AI's transformative potential but did not view it as an immediate threat. Fourth-year students disagreed with 'I see AI as a partner, not a competitor' (p < 0.05). Similarly, recent graduates strongly opposed concerns regarding AI replacing dentists, while fourth-year students expressed higher agreement (p < 0.05). Most participants supported integrating AI education into undergraduate curricula.

CONCLUSION: This study highlights dental students' and recent graduates' perceptions of AI in dentistry. While AI's potential is widely recognized, its presence in dental curricula remains limited. These findings emphasize the need for comprehensive educational programmes to facilitate AI integration in dental practice.

articles.title: CausalCellInfer: Prioritizing Cell-Type-Specific Disease Associations From Genetically Predicted Transcriptomes in Biobank Cohorts.
articles.abstract: Integrating single-cell RNA sequencing(scRNA-seq) with the phenotypic depth of population-scale biobanks is essential for elucidating the cellular basis of complex diseases.
