However, this is hindered by limited scRNA-seq sample size and the lack of cellular resolution in biobanks. We present CausalCellInfer, a scalable computational framework bringing cellular resolution to bulk and genotype-imputed transcriptomes. CausalCellInfer employs an invariant causal prediction-inspired method(scRNA-seq-based invariant generalized covariance measure, scI-GCM) to select environment-stable marker genes, a parsimonious deep neural network for cell-fraction deconvolution, and regularized matrix completion to reconstruct cell-type-specific (CTS) expression profiles. This design is optimized for biobank-scale data with technical heterogeneity and limited gene overlap. Validated across simulated data, pseudo-bulk and real peripheral blood mononuclear cell (PBMC) datasets, CausalCellInfer demonstrated superior accuracy and efficiency over existing methods. Applied to ∼500 000 UK Biobank (UKBB) participants across 29 traits, it captured known pathological shifts, such as reduced pancreatic β-cell proportions in type 2 diabetes, and identified novel biological signals, including disrupted excitatory neuron-oligodendrocyte interactions in depression. Inferred CTS differential expression patterns showed significant concordance with independent single-cell studies and were enriched for Open Targets disease genes. Overall, CausalCellInfer bridges single-cell insights and population-scale genomics, enabling systematic discovery of putative disease mechanisms at cellular resolution.

articles.title: GLP-1 Receptor Agonist Therapy Is Associated With Lower Risk of Lower Extremity Amputation in Adults With Type 2 Diabetes and Foot Ulcer Without Coded Peripheral Arterial Disease: A Hypothesis-Generating Real-World Cohort Study.
articles.abstract:
AIMS: To compare lower extremity amputation (LEA) risk in adults with Type 2 diabetes and diabetic foot ulcer (DFU) treated with glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists (GLP-1 RAs) versus other glucose-lowering therapy, and to test whether coded peripheral arterial disease (PAD) modifies this association and replicates across comparator classes.

MATERIALS AND METHODS: This new-user, active-comparator retrospective cohort study used the TriNetX Global Collaborative Network (queried 11 July 2026). Adults with Type 2 diabetes and DFU were propensity-score matched 1:1 on 22 covariates, giving 21 325 pairs for the primary comparison. Effect modification by coded PAD (ICD-10 I70.2) was examined in independently matched subgroups. Six sensitivity analyses were pre-specified: 30- and 180-day landmarks, all-cause mortality, background-therapy balancing, limb-severity adjustment and a broadened PAD definition.

RESULTS: GLP-1 RA use was associated with lower 5-year LEA risk than all non-GLP-1 RA therapy (hazard ratio [HR]: 0.60, 95% CI: 0.54-0.67). The association was confined to the no-PAD stratum (HR: 0.21, 0.13-0.33) and absent where PAD was coded (HR: 0.97, 0.78-1.20); ratio of hazard ratios 0.21 (0.13-0.36; p < 0.001). All-cause mortality was also lower (HR: 0.48, 0.45-0.50). The insulin no-PAD estimate persisted under background-therapy balancing (0.14), limb-severity adjustment (0.16) and 30- and 180-day landmarks (0.28, 0.33). Broadening the PAD definition attenuated the no-PAD association without abolishing it (HR: 0.34, 0.17-0.65).

CONCLUSIONS: In Type 2 diabetes with DFU, GLP-1 RA use was associated with lower LEA risk, surviving six pre-specified sensitivity analyses. These observational findings are hypothesis-generating and require prospective confirmation.

articles.title: The samplr package: A tool for modeling human cognition with sampling algorithms.
articles.abstract: Many models of cognition have sampling as a central component. Researchers have used them to explain human performance across a wide range of tasks involving perception, probability reasoning, and choice. One family of these models takes inspiration from sampling approaches developed in statistics, either by adjusting samples with prior beliefs or by implementing a sampling algorithm that overcomes the difficulty of independent samples at the expense of autocorrelation. While these models have been successful in modeling human behavior, their adoption has been slowed by the technical difficulties in applying them. Here, we introduce the samplr package, which includes a variety of these algorithms and cognitive models built upon them. We show how models in this package can match qualitative patterns found in human data, and walk readers through examples of how to compare these models quantitatively to human data. This tool aims to make these methods accessible to many more researchers.

articles.title: Temporal patterns of the association between Achilles tendon thickening and clinical outcomes after percutaneous coronary intervention in acute and chronic coronary syndromes.
articles.abstract: Although Achilles tendon thickening (ATT) is associated with adverse outcomes after percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI), whether its prognostic impact differs over time between acute (ACS) and chronic coronary syndromes (CCS) remains unclear. We retrospectively analyzed 1,362 patients who underwent successful PCI and assessment of ATT using soft X-ray radiography. ATT was defined as Achilles tendon thickness ≥8.0 in men and ≥7.5 mm in women. MACE, including death, myocardial infarction, stent thrombosis, stroke, and target vessel revascularization, were investigated for up to 3 years. To evaluate temporal differences, we conducted the Kaplan-Meier method with landmark analysis and time-segmented Cox proportional hazards analyses dividing follow-up into ≤ 1 year and 1-3 years after PCI. ATT was observed in 228 patients (16.7%), who had a significantly higher incidence of MACE compared to patients without ATT. In ACS patients (n = 387), ATT was independently associated with an increased risk of MACE within 1 year, but not beyond 1 year. Conversely, in CCS patients (n = 975), ATT was not associated with early events, but was significantly associated with increased MACE risk during 1-3 years after PCI. Similar trends were observed after excluding familial hypercholesterolemia. These findings suggest different temporal patterns in the association between ATT and MACE after PCI in patients with ACS and CCS, which may provide additional insights into risk stratification during follow-up.

articles.title: Performance Analysis of Laplacian Re-Decomposition-Based PET-MRI Fusion for Quantitative Imaging Biomarkers in Alzheimer's Disease Classification.
articles.journal: Journal of imaging informatics in medicine
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Alzheimer's disease (AD) and mild cognitive impairment (MCI) represent critical stages along the continuum of cognitive decline. This study investigates the Laplacian Re-decomposition (LRD) method for fusing positron emission tomography (PET) and magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) to develop a quantitative imaging biomarker for the classification of AD.

MATERIAL AND METHOD: Data from the Alzheimer's Disease Neuroimaging Initiative (ADNI) database were used in this study. T1, T2, T2-FLAIR, and T2*-weighted MRI sequences, together with [18F]FDG-PET images, were preprocessed and fused using the LRD algorithm. Hippocampal and frontal lobe WM segmentation, performed via U-Net, enabled relative signal contrast (RSC) calculation as a quantitative biomarker for each modality and fused image. Fusion and segmentation performance were assessed using standard metrics. RSC statistically compared between diagnostic groups after adjustment for demographic confounds, and evaluated for classification performance using ROC/AUC analysis.

RESULTS: The mean Dice coefficient achieved by the trained U-Net for hippocampus and frontal lobe WM segmentation were 0.93 and 0.95, respectively. ROC analysis revealed that the RSC extracted from T1-weighted images fused with PET outperformed other modalities for AD vs. Cognitively normal (CN) classification (AUC = 0.88, accuracy = 0.90). Also, T2-weighted images fused with PET, using RSC as a quantitative biomarker, achieved the best classification performance for AD vs. MCI (AUC = 0.81, accuracy = 0.81) and MCI vs. CN (AUC = 0.84, accuracy = 0.88) classification.

CONCLUSION: Our findings indicate that RSC extracted from LRD-fused images achieves competitive classification performance, supporting its potential as a quantitative biomarker for AD.

articles.title: Habitat Radiomics and Machine Learning for Preoperative Three-class Classification of Pediatric Acute Appendicitis: A Dual-center Study with External Validation.
articles.journal: Journal of imaging informatics in medicine
articles.abstract: Accurate preoperative differentiation of pediatric acute appendicitis subtypes is relevant to treatment planning. We developed and externally validated a machine-learning framework combining habitat-based computed tomography (CT) radiomics with clinical variables for three-class classification (simple, complex, and appendiceal abscess). This retrospective dual-center study included 317 children undergoing appendectomy at Institution A (training n = 222, internal validation n = 95) and 174 children at Institution B (external validation). K-means + + habitat segmentation (k = 3) of preoperative noncontrast CT volumes of interest yielded 1218 radiomic features; ten features selected on the training cohort were combined with 20 preoperative clinical variables. Eight classifiers were compared using macro-averaged one-versus-rest area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC), accuracy, and macro-F1, with bootstrap confidence intervals (CIs), DeLong tests, calibration statistics, and decision curve analysis. In external validation, naive Bayes achieved the highest macro-AUC (0.946, 95% CI 0.910-0.974), accuracy 0.776 (0.713-0.833), and macro-F1 0.766 (0.674-0.837), significantly exceeding all seven comparators among the configurations evaluated (p < 0.001); the internal validation macro-AUC was 0.940 (0.893-0.977). Per-class external AUCs were 0.920 (simple), 0.948 (complex), and 0.971 (abscess). Calibration slopes (0.23-0.30) indicated that probability outputs require recalibration before probabilistic use. In a five-arm ablation of the input feature blocks, the fusion model combining clinical variables with habitat radiomics performed best (external macro-AUC 0.971), ahead of habitat radiomics alone (0.952), clinical variables plus conventional whole-VOI radiomics (0.776), clinical variables alone (0.763) and conventional whole-VOI radiomics alone (0.582). Habitat radiomics combined with machine learning provided accurate, externally validated three-class classification of pediatric acute appendicitis in children undergoing appendectomy. Naive Bayes offered the most balanced subtype discrimination. The model is a subtype-stratification aid rather than a stand-alone diagnostic or treatment-selection tool.

articles.title: Evaluation of microplastic pollution in industrial wastewater and their biodegradation using a novel indigenous bacterial isolate.
articles.abstract: Microplastics (MPs) are an emerging environment pollutant that widely distributed across various environmental matrices and pose significant risks to marine biota, invertebrates and humans. Industrial wastewater sample was collected from the Urkura industrial area, Raipur, Chhattisgarh, India to evaluate the presence as well as biodegradation of microplastics. Microplastics were extracted and characterized for size, shape and colour using stereo and fluorescence microscopy, while polymer composition was identified using Fourier Transform Infrared Spectroscopy (FTIR) and Raman Spectroscopy (RS). The analysis revealed (PE) as the predominant polymer, mainly occurring in fibre and fragment forms. Other polymers including polypropylene (PP), polystyrene (PS), low density polyethylene (LDPE) and polyethylene terephthalate (PET) were also identified. Quantitative analysis revealed a mean concentration of 64±1 particles/L (64000 particles/m3). The microplastics exhibited different colors including blue, black, red, violet, brown, grey, green, orange, and transparent, with particle sizes from 50 µm to 5000 µm. A novel bacterial strain, Bacillus paralicheniformis strain PWDS (NR_137421.1), was isolated from soil sample obtained from a plastic dumping area located in Raipur. Biodegradation was carried out for 30 days and process parameters such as pH, temperature, inoculum volume and shaking speed were optimized. The bacterial strain showed a maximum degradation efficiency of about 8.4±0.4%. The study highlights presence of microplastics in wastewater and the efficiency of microbial approaches for effective microplastic bioremediation and environmental sustainability.

articles.title: Clinical and radiological characteristics of MOG antibody-associated disease (MOGAD): a comparative study between pediatric and adult cohorts.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Myelin oligodendrocyte glycoprotein antibody-associated disease (MOGAD) is a distinct inflammatory demyelinating disorder As being first national study of pediatric and adult Turkish MOGAD patients so we aimed to report the clinical presentations, radiological findings, and relapse characteristics between pediatric and adult patients with MOGAD.

, MATERIALS AND METHODS: In this retrospective study, 26 patients (10 pediatric [≤ 17 years] and 16 adult [> 17 years]) who tested positive for MOG antibodies were included. Demographic data, precipitating factors, Expanded Disability Status Scale (EDSS) scores, cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) findings, and magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) features were analyzed.

RESULTS: The mean age was 10.8 years for children and 32.5 years for adults. Precipitating factors, primarily upper respiratory infections, were more frequent in children (70% vs. 12.5%). Pediatric patients predominantly presented with polysymptomatic onset, including pyramidal signs (60%) and encephalopathy (30%), whereas adults most commonly presented with optic neuritis (62.5%). Although adults had higher mean EDSS scores during relapse compared to children (4.31 vs. 3.55), final follow-up EDSS scores were low for both groups (0.78 vs. 0.5). Relapses were recorded only in the adult group (mean rate 1.93). Radiologically, children showed significantly higher rates of brainstem (34.6% vs. 7.6%) and cortical involvement. Spinal MRI revealed the "H-sign" in both groups, but conus involvement was more prevalent in children (75% vs. 7.6%).

CONCLUSION: MOGAD exhibits age-dependent clinical and radiological phenotypes. While pediatric cases often follow a post-infectious, polysymptomatic, and monophasic course, adult cases frequently present as optic neuritis with a higher tendency for relapse. Despite significant acute disability, functional recovery at the last visit was favorable in both populations over a mean follow-up of 24.1 ± 8.2 months in children and 33.6 ± 36.7 months in adults.

articles.title: Hospitalized primary headache in children after emergency department evaluation: a retrospective cohort study.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: To characterize the clinical features, diagnostic evaluation, management, and final diagnoses of children hospitalized for headache following emergency department (ED) evaluation, and to explore factors associated with treatment refractoriness.

METHODS: We conducted a retrospective cohort study of children aged 4-17 years presenting to a tertiary pediatric ED with headache as the primary complaint who required hospitalization between January 2019 and June 2024. Patients whose headache was clearly attributed to trauma, fever, or a previously identified systemic or neurological disorder were excluded. Final headache diagnoses were established during hospitalization by the pediatric neurology team, using ICHD-3 criteria when applicable. Data included demographics, clinical presentation, diagnostic testing, treatments, and discharge diagnoses. Descriptive analyses were performed, with exploratory comparisons between patients requiring ≤ 2 versus > 2 sequential pharmacologic interventions.

RESULTS: Among 3,646 ED visits for headache, 162 (4.4%) resulted in hospitalization; 30 children (18.5% of admissions) had a final diagnosis of primary headache and constituted the study cohort. Mean age was 12.7 years, and 70.0% were female. Although frontal location and pressure-type pain were the most common presentation features, 76.7% of patients were ultimately diagnosed with migraine or probable migraine. Acute neurological abnormalities were documented in 10.0% of patients. Cranial CT was performed in 63.3% and brain MRI in 23.3%, with no acute intracranial abnormality or secondary cause explaining the headache identified. Intravenous metamizole (dipyrone) was the most frequently used first-line acute therapy, and 70.0% of patients required a second sequential pharmacologic intervention. Among patients diagnosed with migraine or probable migraine, 21.7% met criteria for status migrainosus. No clinical variables were significantly associated with treatment refractoriness.

CONCLUSIONS: Hospitalization for primary headache after pediatric ED evaluation was uncommon but identified a clinically severe subgroup, predominantly with migraine-spectrum disorders and frequently requiring escalation of acute treatment. Despite frequent neuroimaging, no acute intracranial abnormality or secondary cause explaining the headache was identified. These findings suggest that more selective imaging strategies may be appropriate in children with a reassuring clinical presentation, although prospective studies are needed to better define predictors of hospitalization, treatment refractoriness, and optimal acute management.

articles.title: Physiological Effects and Clinical Limitations of Impella-Bridge Strategy for Post-Infarction Ventricular Septal Rupture.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Post-infarction ventricular septal rupture (VSR) remains a life-threatening mechanical complication of acute myocardial infarction. We evaluated the feasibility of an Impella-bridge strategy for scheduled VSR repair.

METHODS: We retrospectively analyzed 10 consecutive patients with post-infarction VSR who were transferred to our institution and managed with Impella support. Outcomes included achievement of scheduled repair and serial changes in hemodynamic parameters and organ dysfunction during the bridging period.

RESULTS: The median age was 74 years. All patients received Impella 2.5 or CP support after transfer; veno-arterial extracorporeal life support was added in four patients, and Impella support was upgraded in one patient. The median duration from Impella initiation to VSR repair was 8 (7, 10) days. Scheduled repair was achieved in nine patients (90%). Mean pulmonary artery pressure, central venous pressure, plasma B-type natriuretic peptide levels, and lactate decreased over time before repair, whereas non-CNS SOFA scores increased during bridging.

CONCLUSIONS: In patients with post-infarction VSR, an Impella-bridge strategy may help achieve scheduled VSR repair with improved hemodynamic stabilization; however, SOFA-defined abnormalities, organ support requirements, and device-related complications were observed during the bridging period. Further studies are needed to define patient selection, management strategies, and the optimal timing of repair for this strategy.

articles.title: Volumetric discordance between ¹⁸F-FET-PET/MRI and MRI-based radiotherapy target volumes in high-grade glioma: a prospective pilot study (FETSMaRT).
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: High-grade gliomas carry a poor prognosis, and MRI-based radiotherapy (RT) planning may inadequately capture metabolically active tumor infiltration. ¹⁸F-fluoroethyl-tyrosine (FET) PET provides superior tumor delineation, yet prospective North American evidence supporting integration with RT planning remains limited.

METHODS: FETSMaRT enrolled 30 patients with WHO grade 3 or 4 high-grade glioma receiving post-operative RT. FET-PET/MRI was acquired before RT with the radiation oncologist blinded to PET, enabling retrospective quantification of discordance between MRI-based and FET-PET/MRI-derived gross tumor (GTV), clinical target (CTV), and planning target (PTV) volumes. In the glioblastoma subgroup (n = 23), Kaplan-Meier and Cox analyses related GTV and CTV discordance to time to progression.

RESULTS: Median age was 60 years; 77% had glioblastoma and 60% MGMT promoter methylation. GTV discordance occurred in 17/30 patients (56.7%) and CTV discordance in 15/30 (50.0%). FET-PET/MRI-derived volumes significantly exceeded MRI-based volumes for GTV (43.6 vs. 38.6 cc; p < 0.0001), CTV (119.2 vs. 110.8 cc; p = 0.0045), and PTV (171.1 vs. 159.6 cc; p = 0.0003). Larger GTV∆ and CTV∆ change values were associated with numerically shorter median time to progression, but neither association was statistically significant. Radiation treatment failures were predominantly central (60.0%).

CONCLUSION: FET-PET/MRI-derived target volumes were significantly larger than MRI-based volumes, confirming systematic underestimation of metabolically active tumor extent by anatomical MRI. While not meeting significance in this pilot study, directional CTV and GTV discordance suggests a possible association with progression; the hypothesis generating exploratory pilot data nonetheless justify a prospective trial of FET-PET-guided RT in high-grade glioma. NCT06499831.

articles.title: Stroke-induced astrocyte memories promote glioma progression.
Impact of VI-RADS quality score on VI-RADS diagnostic performance for muscle invasion: the role of tumor size and reader experience.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: To evaluate the inter-reader agreement of the Vesical Imaging Reporting and Data System (VI-RADS) quality scoring system and to assess its impact on the diagnostic performance for detecting muscle invasion.

MATERIALS AND METHODS: This retrospective study included 587 patients who underwent multiparametric bladder MRI before surgery. Three radiologists (two specialists and one non-genitourinary radiologist) independently assessed VI-RADS category and quality scores. Inter-reader agreement was evaluated using weighted kappa statistics. Associations between image quality, VI-RADS categorization, and tumor characteristics were analyzed using multivariable models. Diagnostic performance for muscle invasion was assessed at predefined VI-RADS thresholds and compared across quality groups and tumor size subgroups.

RESULTS: A total of 7/587 (1.2%), 284/587 (48.4%), and 296/587 (50.4%) scans were VI-RADS quality score 0, 1, and 2, respectively. Inter-reader agreement for the final quality score was substantial (k = 0.628-0.702). Higher VI-RADS quality scores were associated with increased T2-weighted image VI-RADS scores (odds ratio [OR], 2.95; 95% confidence interval, 1.17-7.43; p = 0.021). In tumors < 3 cm, particularly for the less experienced reader, higher image quality was associated with increased positive predictive value (PPV) and accuracy at the VI-RADS ≥ 3 threshold (PPV: 51.0% vs 22.7%, p = 0.004; accuracy: 81.6% vs 71.7%, p = 0.023). No significant differences in diagnostic performance were observed across VI-RADS thresholds in tumors ≥ 3 cm.

CONCLUSION: The VI-RADS quality scoring system demonstrated good inter-reader agreement. Optimal image quality improved diagnostic performance in small tumors and for the less experienced reader; however, because only one less experienced reader was included, this finding requires external validation.

KEY POINTS: Question Does image quality, assessed by the VI-RADS quality score, influence diagnostic performance of VI-RADS for detecting muscle invasion in bladder cancer? Findings Higher image quality improved PPV and accuracy of VI-RADS, particularly in tumors < 3 cm and for the less experienced reader, while having limited impact in larger tumors. Clinical relevance Ensuring optimal MRI image quality enhances the reliability of VI-RADS interpretation, particularly in small tumors and non-specialized settings, and supports standardized imaging as a prerequisite for accurate bladder cancer staging.

articles.title: Does Patient-Centered Communication by Physicians Facilitate Cardiometabolic Disease Self-management Among Community Health Center Patients? A Nationwide Study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Cardiometabolic self-management through lifestyle behavior change is critical for patients with cardiometabolic risk conditions (obesity, high blood pressure, type 2 diabetes (T2DM) and/or dyslipidemia) to avoid life-threatening complications.

OBJECTIVE: To examine whether patient-centered communication (PCC) by community health center (CHC) physicians may facilitate patients with cardiometabolic conditions to implement disease self-management behaviors in daily life.

RESEARCH DESIGN: We used secondary data from the 2022 Health Services and Resources Administration-Research Triangle International-designed, nationally representative sample survey of CHC patients (response rate 85.0%). We assessed the association of patients' adoption of cardiometabolic self-management behaviors in five domains (weight management, dietary change, physical activity, reducing sedentariness, and smoking reduction) with ratings of their physician's PCC during primary care visits.

PARTICIPANTS: 2,942 adults aged 18-74 years, with cardiometabolic condition(s) completing a primary care visit.

MEASURES: Outcome: Cardiometabolic self-management (SM) score, sum of patient's weighted fraction scores of behaviors in five domains, multiplied by 100 to obtain a whole integer-based, ratio-scale score. Key independent variable: Patient-rated physician PCC aggregated from scores on five adapted Consumer Assessment of Healthcare Providers and Systems survey questions (CAHPS) during primary care visits (Likert scale 0-3).

RESULTS: Among 2,942 study-eligible patients (25.3% with T2DM, 62.8% obesity, 60.1% hypertension, 50.9% dyslipidemia), the mean cardiometabolic SM score was 246.3 (±82, median 250, possible score range, -30 to 470). The mean PCC score (validated by exploratory factor analysis) was 17.7 (±3.3, median 20, possible range 0-20). A unit increase in PCC was associated with 1.8-point increase in patients' SM score (SE 0.5, p<0.001), after adjusting for demographic variables, chronic conditions, and patient-reported measures of their enabling environment for physical activity, food security, and physical/mental health disability.

CONCLUSIONS: Physicians' PCC as measured by the CAHPS survey may promote better self-management of cardiometabolic conditions by CHC patients who often have low health literacy.

articles.title: Estimation of glomerular filtration rate by standard renal CT imaging.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: To develop and evaluate a method to predict glomerular filtration rate (GFR) from clinical renal CT.

MATERIALS AND METHODS: Medical records of adult living kidney donors operated between 2013 and 2022 and patients considered for neoadjuvant cisplatin prior to cystectomy between 2019 and 2024 were retrospectively reviewed. Inclusion criteria were (1) renal CT obtained at 100 or 120 kVp before and 5-15 min after contrast administration, and (2) iohexol clearance test within 2 months of imaging. The iohexol clearance test was performed on the same day as the cystatin C and creatinine measurements. Estimated GFR values included cystatin C-based eGFR (eGFRcystatin C), creatinine-based eGFR using the Cockcroft-Gault formula (eGFRCockcroft-Gault), and eGFR using the Revised Lund-Malmö formula (eGFRLMR18), which is based on both creatinine and cystatin C. Manual and automatic segmentations of the renal pelvis and bladder were performed in both the excretory and unenhanced phases.

RESULTS: In total, 139 patients were included in the analysis (mean age 52 ± 13 years; 60% women). Multivariate linear regression analysis combining the segmentation-derived variable with body surface area and age gave an adjusted R-square of 0.77 to mGFRiohexol (p < 0.001). GFRCT had the strongest relationship to mGFRiohexol with a mean absolute error of 12.8 mL/min, compared with 15.6 mL/min for eGFRCockcroft-Gault, 14.2 mL/min for eGFRcystatin C, and 13.0 mL/min for eGFRLMR18. Manual and automatic segmentations had similar performance. Patients evaluated for cisplatin treatment had greater variation in CT-estimated split renal function than donors.

CONCLUSION: Renal function can be estimated with high precision from clinical renal CT.

KEY POINTS: Question Accurate GFR assessment is critical, but current methods are either labor-intensive or imprecise. Can renal CT imaging provide a reliable alternative? Findings CT-derived eGFR showed the strongest correlation with iohexol clearance (R² = 0.77), with lower error compared to creatinine- and cystatin C-based estimates. Critical relevance statement Routine CT imaging can provide precise estimates of kidney function, supporting donor evaluations, chemotherapy dosing, and critical care decisions when accurate renal function is essential.

articles.title: Risk factors associated with hypertension in patients attending a pediatric sleep clinic: a prospective cohort study.
articles.abstract:
UNLABELLED: Pediatric patients with obstructive sleep apnea (OSA) are at risk of hypertension due to an interplay of factors. Twenty-four-hour ambulatory blood pressure monitoring (ABPM) is required to diagnose white coat hypertension (WCH) and masked hypertension (MH). However, ABPM is not routinely performed. We aim to detect hypertension using ABPM and to identify risk factors associated with hypertension. This was a prospective cohort study of pediatric patients (5-18 years of age) who had been referred to the sleep clinic. Polysomnography (PSG) or overnight pulse oximetry (OPO) were performed as per standard of care. ABPM was performed for all recruited patients. The primary outcome was hypertension, i.e., ambulatory hypertension or MH. Sixty-eight patients were recruited. Median age was 12.6 (interquartile range [IQR] 10.0-14.7) years. Fourteen (21%) did not return for the ABPM and ten (15%) had insufficient readings. Of the remaining 44 patients with complete ABPM data, hypertension was diagnosed in 18/44 (41%) with 10 (23%) having ambulatory hypertension and 8 (18%) having MH. Among the 18 patients with hypertension, one defaulted sleep study; 3/17 (18%) had primary snoring; 6/17 (35%), 4/17 (24%), and 4/17 (24%) had mild, moderate, and severe OSA, respectively. The prevalence of hypertension was 6/20 (30%), 4/10 (40%), 4/8 (50%), and 3/5 (60%) among patients with mild, moderate, and severe OSA and primary snoring, respectively. Age (relative risk [RR] 1.27, 95% confidence interval [CI] 1.07-1.52, p = 0.008) and primary snoring (RR 3.52, 95% CI 1.38-8.97, p = 0.004) were independently associated with hypertension.

CONCLUSION: Increasing age and primary snoring may be independently associated with hypertension among pediatric patients attending the sleep clinic. Larger studies will be required to validate these risk factors.

WHAT IS KNOWN: • Pediatric patients with obstructive sleep apnea (OSA) are at risk of hypertension which is often due to an interplay of multiple factors. • Twenty-four-hour ambulatory blood pressure monitoring (ABPM) is required to diagnose white coat hypertension (WCH) and masked hypertension (MH).

WHAT IS NEW: • In this prospective single-center study, ABPM was performed for all patients, classifying hypertension based on the 2022 update on ABPM in children from the American Heart Association. • Increasing age and primary snoring were independently associated with hypertension in pediatric patients attending the sleep clinic.

articles.title: Metabolic and oncological effects of metformin added to ADT in prostate cancer: systematic review and meta-analysis including STAMPEDE.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Androgen-deprivation therapy (ADT) is the cornerstone of advanced prostate cancer treatment but induces a metabolic syndrome phenotype that heightens cardiovascular risk. Metformin, an insulin-sensitising biguanide with emerging anticancer properties, is a rational ADT adjunct. Following STAMPEDE's 2025 publication, we aimed to quantify metformin's metabolic benefit and characterise its oncological signal by disease volume.

METHODS: This PRISMA 2020-guided review (PROSPERO CRD420261384520) searched five databases through 12 May 2026. Eligible RCTs compared metformin plus ADT versus ADT alone in prostate cancer. Primary metabolic outcomes were body weight, waist circumference, HbA1c, fasting glucose, and LDL cholesterol. Secondary (exploratory) oncological outcomes were overall survival (OS) and castration-resistant prostate cancer-free survival (CRPC-FS), derived predominantly from a single trial. Random-effects models with Hartung-Knapp correction were used; GRADE assessed certainty.

RESULTS: Six trials enroling 2415 participants (78% from STAMPEDE) were included: STAMPEDE (n = 1 874), PRIME (n = 166), PREMIUM (n = 83), MANSMED (n = 124), Mahalingam (n = 36), and Alagizy (n = 132). Disease status ranged from metastatic (STAMPEDE, Alagizy, majority MANSMED) to locally advanced or biochemically recurrent (PREMIUM, PRIME, Mahalingam); all excluded diabetes mellitus except MANSMED ( ~ 20%). At 12 months, metformin significantly reduced waist circumference (MD -1.12 cm; p = 0.014), HbA1c (MD -0.070%; p = 0.029), and fasting glucose (MD -0.100 mmol/L; p = 0.031). Body weight and LDL cholesterol reductions were non-significant (MD -1.60 kg; p = 0.090 and MD -0.130 mmol/L; p = 0.343, respectively). In STAMPEDE, metformin did not improve OS (HR 0.91; p = 0.15); the high-volume subgroup showed a survival benefit (HR 0.79; p = 0.007; volume interaction p = 0.12, non-significant). In MANSMED, CRPC-free survival was significantly prolonged (HR 0.50; p = 0.01), though this signal derives from a single small, open-label trial.

CONCLUSIONS: Metformin added to ADT produces moderate-certainty reductions in waist circumference and HbA1c. Oncological benefit in unselected patients was not demonstrated; the hypothesis-generating STAMPEDE high-volume subgroup signal, derived from a single trial, warrants evaluation in a prospective, volume-stratified RCT.

articles.title: Efficacy and safety of HRS-7535, a novel oral small-molecule glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonist, in participants with type 2 diabetes mellitus inadequately controlled by metformin and sodium-glucose co-transporter 2 inhibitors: a multicentre, randomised, double-blind, placebo-controlled, parallel-group Phase II trial.
articles.abstract:
AIMS/HYPOTHESIS: This study aimed to evaluate the efficacy and safety of HRS-7535, an oral small-molecule glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonist (GLP-1RA), in Chinese participants with type 2 diabetes mellitus inadequately managed by metformin and sodium-glucose co-transporter 2 inhibitors (SGLT2i).

METHODS: This multicentre, randomised, double-blind, placebo-controlled, Phase II study included participants aged 18-75 years with type 2 diabetes, HbA1c 58-97 mmol/mol (7.5-11.0%) and BMI 20.0-35.0 kg/m2 and on stable-dose metformin and sodium-glucose co-transporter 2 (SGLT2) inhibitor therapy for ≥8 weeks prior to screening. Participants were assigned in a 1:1:1 ratio to receive HRS-7535 30 mg, HRS-7535 60 mg or visually matching placebo tablets once daily using a stratified block randomisation method, with treatment assignments concealed until study completion. The primary endpoint was the change in HbA1c from baseline to week 16. Secondary efficacy outcomes included the proportions of participants achieving HbA1c targets of <53 mmol/mol (7.0%) and ≤48 mmol/mol (6.5%), and changes from baseline in fasting body weight to week 16.

RESULTS: A total of 155 participants with a mean baseline HbA1c of 69 mmol/mol (8.5%) were randomly assigned to HRS-7535 30 mg (n=51), HRS-7535 60 mg (n=53) or placebo (n=51). At week 16, the least‑squares mean differences in HbA1c from baseline for the HRS-7535 30 mg, HRS-7535 60 mg and placebo groups were -16 mmol/mol (95% CI -19, -14) (-1.5% [95% CI -1.7, -1.3]), -20 mmol/mol (95% CI -22, -17) (-1.8% [95% CI -2.0, -1.6]) and -4 mmol/mol (95% CI -7, -2) (-0.4% [95% CI -0.6, -0.2]), respectively (p<0.0001 for both HRS-7535 doses vs placebo). The proportions of participants achieving HbA1c <53 mmol/mol (7.0%) were 51.0% in the HRS‑7535 30 mg group, 66.0% in the HRS‑7535 60 mg group, and 9.8% in the placebo group; the corresponding proportions for HbA1c ≤48 mmol/mol (6.5%) were 35.3%, 37.7% and 3.9%, respectively. Body weight loss was -2.4% in the HRS-7535 60 mg group vs -0.7% in the placebo group. Most treatment-emergent adverse events (TEAEs) were mild to moderate, and gastrointestinal adverse events were the most common. No severe hypoglycaemia was reported. The only TEAE that led to treatment discontinuation occurred in the placebo group.

CONCLUSIONS/INTERPRETATION: Treatment with HRS-7535 resulted in significant improvements in glycaemic management in participants with type 2 diabetes, and the drug exhibited a favourable safety profile. To address a significant clinical data void, this research focused on the addition of HRS‑7535 to the background regimen of metformin and SGLT2i for glycaemic management in participants with type 2 diabetes. Trial registration ClinicalTrials.gov NCT06393348. Funding This study was funded by Jiangsu Hengrui Pharmaceuticals.

articles.title: Is time really spine? Early versus delayed surgical decompression in traumatic spinal cord injury: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
articles.journal: European spine journal : official publication of the European Spine Society, the European Spinal Deformity Society, and the European Section of the Cervical Spine Research Society
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: To evaluate whether earlier surgical decompression is associated with improved neurological and clinical outcomes compared with delayed decompression after traumatic spinal cord injury.

METHODS: MEDLINE, Scopus, Web of Science, CINAHL, the Cochrane Library and Google Scholar were searched from inception to February 2025. Comparative studies of early versus delayed decompression in adult or predominantly adult traumatic spinal cord injury cohorts were included. Three reviewers independently screened studies, extracted data and assessed risk of bias. Random-effects meta-analyses were performed where outcomes were sufficiently comparable. The primary outcomes were improvement of at least one grade and at least two grades on the American Spinal Injury Association (ASIA) Impairment Scale.

RESULTS: Seventy-eight studies comprising 31,190 reported participants were included. Surgery within 24 h was the most common definition of early decompression, although thresholds and timing origins varied substantially. Seventeen studies contributed to the analysis of AIS improvement of at least one grade. Early decompression was associated with a greater likelihood of improvement than delayed decompression (risk ratio [RR] 1.46, 95% confidence interval [CI] 1.27-1.68; I² = 48.3%). Eleven studies contributed to the analysis of AIS improvement of at least two grades, which also favoured early decompression (RR 2.18, 95% CI 1.69-2.81; I² = 0.0%). Four studies were pooled for overall complications, with no clear difference between early and delayed decompression (RR 0.97, 95% CI 0.60-1.56; I² = 74.9%). Functional recovery, mortality, length of stay, intensive care, ventilation and cost outcomes were reported inconsistently and were synthesised narratively.

CONCLUSION: Earlier surgical decompression was associated with greater AIS-grade neurological recovery after traumatic spinal cord injury, particularly for improvement of at least two grades. However, most evidence was observational and limited by heterogeneous timing definitions, inconsistent outcome reporting and residual confounding. These findings support timely decompression when medically feasible, but do not establish that surgical timing alone determines neurological recovery.

PROSPERO REGISTRATION: CRD420251000074.

articles.title: Stigma toward persons with mental illnesses in prison.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: The healthcare provision for mentally ill offenders in Germany remains inadequate, despite higher prevalence rates compared to the general population. We examined whether stigma-based discrimination is greater toward this group compared to individuals with somatic illnesses and/or non-incarcerated individuals.

METHODS: In February 2025, we conducted a quota-based online survey among adults living in Germany (aged 18 years or older; n = 1,609), in which respondents were randomly assigned to one of eight case vignettes varying by illness (schizophrenia vs. diabetes), incarceration status, and gender. Indicators for discrimination included desire for social distance and public rejection of healthcare provision.

RESULTS: The incarceration status and mental illness of the vignette person significantly predicted greater social distance, whereas the respondent's personal experience with mental illness predicted lower social distance. Public rejection of healthcare provision was lower among older and female respondents, respondents with high compared to low education, and those with experience of mental illness in their social environment. Rejection was also lower for vignette persons with mental rather than somatic illness, but significantly higher for incarcerated vignette persons and among respondents with personal experience of incarceration.

CONCLUSION: These findings highlight the role of stigma-related processes in shaping attitudes toward healthcare provision, particularly for socially marginalized groups. They underscore the importance of reducing perceived boundaries between social groups and suggest that targeted educational and contact-based interventions may improve healthcare provision, particularly for incarcerated individuals.

articles.title: MD2-IN-1 restores microglial lysosomal function and attenuates amyloid pathology through TREM2-associated signaling in 5×FAD mice.
articles.abstract: Triggering receptor expressed on myeloid cells 2 (TREM2) is a central regulator of microglial adaptation during Alzheimer's disease (AD), yet the development of small-molecule modulators associated with TREM2 signaling remains limited. Here, through a consensus pharmacophore-guided virtual screening strategy, MD2-IN-1 was identified as a candidate small molecule associated with TREM2 signaling. Biolayer interferometry and cellular thermal shift assays supported cellular target engagement related to TREM2 (KD = 13.85 μM). In Aβ-stimulated BV2 microglia, MD2-IN-1 increased SYK phosphorylation, promoted Aβ uptake, and shifted microglial responses toward a less proinflammatory phenotype. These effects were markedly attenuated following Trem2 knockdown, indicating the involvement of the TREM2-SYK signaling pathway. Mechanistically, MD2-IN-1 restored lysosomal acidification and increased the expression of the V-ATPase subunits ATP6v0c and ATP6v0a1, accompanied by increased intracellular Aβ degradation. In 5×FAD mice, chronic MD2-IN-1 administration improved cognitive performance without detectable behavioral abnormalities compared with WT animals. Multimodal PET imaging demonstrated reduced amyloid deposition and attenuated neuroinflammatory signals, which were further supported by histological analyses showing decreased plaque burden, reduced inflammatory microglial responses, and preserved neuronal integrity. In addition, MD2-IN-1 reduced P62 accumulation and restored ATP6v0c expression in vivo, whereas these effects were partially attenuated by pharmacological inhibition of TREM2. Collectively, these findings identify MD2-IN-1 as a small-molecule modulator associated with TREM2 signaling that restores microglial lysosomal degradative function and promotes Aβ clearance in AD models, providing pharmacological support for targeting adaptive microglial responses in AD.

articles.title: Cryogenic shock exfoliation for ultrahigh mobility rhombohedral graphite nanoelectronics.
articles.abstract: Rhombohedral multilayer graphene offers a tunable platform for correlated electron physics, featuring field-effect control of magnetic, superconducting and topological phases. The promise of these materials has been held back by the limited abundance of rhombohedral stacking in natural graphite, which constrains both sample yield and useful area. Here we introduce cryogenic shock exfoliation to produce large-area rhombohedral graphene flakes. This exfoliation, combined with a low-pressure van der Waals assembly technique that preserves stacking order, enables highly uniform devices exceeding 1,300 μm2 in area with fabrication yields of ∼90%. Using scanning nanoSQUID-on-tip imaging, we demonstrate uniform spin magnetism over the full central 10 × 10 μm2 area of our devices. Transverse magnetic focusing reveals a disorder mean free path exceeding 200 μm at low temperatures. Within the flat surface bands of rhombohedral multilayer graphene, we observe a size-driven crossover from Poiseuille to porous electron flow in the intermediate-temperature regime of strong electron-electron hydrodynamics, providing a further signature of ultrahigh device quality. Our approach overcomes a key materials bottleneck in the fabrication of mesoscopic rhombohedral graphene devices, paving the way for incorporating strongly correlated phases into two-dimensional nanoelectronics.

articles.title: Capillary-selective vasodilation through myosin inhibition halts ischaemic cascades.
articles.abstract: In acute myocardial infarction and acute kidney injury, capillary no-reflow denotes that capillary blood flow is still blocked despite successful arterial reperfusion. This is associated with substantially increased mortality and reinfarction risk; nevertheless, no targeted therapy exists so far1,2. Because capillary no-reflow is driven by smooth muscle myosin-mediated hypercontraction of capillary pericytes, we developed R(+)2501, a myosin-specific and capillary-selective vasodilator. In reperfused animal models of acute myocardial infarction and acute kidney injury, direct in vivo imaging showed that R(+)2501 rapidly restored capillary flow, an effect sustained even after rapid drug clearance. Ex vivo experiments confirmed reversal of pericyte constriction directly. Restoration of capillary blood flow, together with clearance of trapped neutrophils, linked resolution of capillary no-reflow to attenuation of an early driver of reperfusion injury. R(+)2501 enhanced capillary perfusion while preserving coronary autoregulation and systemic haemodynamics, and markedly improved survival during acute reperfusion. We further found that acute myocardial infarction induced renal capillary no-reflow, which was reversed by R(+)2501, suggesting that capillary no-reflow contributes to the pathophysiology of cardiorenal syndrome type I. These findings establish pericyte-targeted smooth muscle myosin inhibition as a therapeutic strategy to restore microvascular perfusion and halt the ischaemic cascade across organs, while defining a specific physiological role for capillaries and pericytes in circulatory regulation.

articles.title: Distinct birth size and postnatal growth patterns in preterm twins and singletons: an etiology-based analysis from the INTERPRACTICE-21st study.
articles.journal: Journal of perinatology : official journal of the California Perinatal Association
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Compare birth size and postnatal growth between preterm twins and singletons across gestational age categories and etiologic subgroups.

STUDY DESIGN: Preterm twins and singletons (n = 3245) were classified into nine subgroups based on predefined preterm birth etiologies. Postnatal growth (weight, length and head circumference) trajectories were evaluated using multilevel linear regression models accounting for repeated measurements, expressed as z-score changes from birth to hospital discharge based on INTERGROWTH-21st Standards.

RESULTS: Twins were significantly smaller at birth than singletons, particularly in late preterm category, but not in the very preterm category. Twin postnatal growth was slower (unadjusted models); most differences attenuated or reversed after adjusting for birth size and key covariates. Twins in the 'pre-eclampsia' subgroup showed greater adjusted postnatal weight, whereas weight gain was persistently lower in the 'perinatal sepsis' subgroup.

CONCLUSION: Preterm twins and singletons have distinct intrauterine and postnatal growth patterns, varying by preterm birth etiology and gestational age categories.

articles.title: Surgery to treat autonomic dysreflexia due to cubital tunnel syndrome in cervical spinal cord injury: a case report.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Autonomic dysreflexia (AD) is a potentially fatal syndrome in people with spinal cord injury (SCI) marked by episodic hypertension with flushing, diaphoresis, and bradycardia. Common etiologies include bladder distension and bowel impaction. Compressive neuropathies lack attention as a potential precipitant of AD. This report describes an individual with cervical SCI and with recurrent AD treated with ulnar nerve decompression surgery.

CASE PRESENTATION: A 74-year-old woman with a remote history of C6 SCI (American Spinal Injury Association Impairment Scale Grade B) presented to clinic with recurrent episodes of AD that had been refractory to standard treatment measures. History and clinical examination were suggestive of ulnar nerve compressive neuropathy at the elbow - cubital tunnel syndrome. The diagnosis was confirmed with electrodiagnostic studies and neuromuscular ultrasound. Treatment with surgery successfully resolved her episodes of AD.

DISCUSSION: This case identifies compressive neuropathy as a treatable cause of AD in individuals with cervical SCI. When more common etiologies of AD are excluded, clinicians should consider compressive peripheral neuropathies as potential causes of AD. Surgical decompression may alleviate symptoms of AD in select cases. Further research should investigate the prevalence and optimal management of compressive neuropathy in people with SCI.

articles.title: Study of the rapid vasodilating effect induced by 5β-dihydrotestosterone in the isolated pulmonary arteries of female and male rats.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: The vasoactive androgen 5β-dihydrotestosterone (5β-DHT), which lacks androgenic or estrogenic activity, induces potent vasorelaxation across vascular beds in several mammals, thereby eliciting hypotension. Therefore, a potential vasorelaxation may occur in the pulmonary arteries of rats, which could be relevant to pulmonary arterial hypertension.

METHODOLOGY: Pulmonary arteries from female and male rats were isometrically recorded and pre-constricted with KCl. 5β-DHT and its precursor, testosterone (T), were tested separately at different concentrations. Cumulative concentration-response curves were obtained, and potency (inhibitory concentration 50) and efficacy were calculated and compared.

RESULTS: The potency of T did not differ between females and males. 5β-DHT was 2.2 times more potent than T in females and 6.6 times more potent in males, with greater efficacy than T in males. The rank order of vasodilating potency was: 5β-DHT>>T in females and 5β-DHT >>>>>>>T in males. The acute vasorelaxation of 5β-DHT was operative in the pulmonary arteries of females and males; the effect had a very rapid time course and was reversible after washout. Protein synthesis or transcription inhibitors did not affect its vasodilating effect, indicating that it acts through a nongenomic mechanism in pulmonary arteries.

CONCLUSION: The data showed that 5β-DHT induced stronger nongenomic vasorelaxation than its precursor in females and males, which may be due to their different structural conformations. Pulmonary arteries are a target for this 5β-reduced androgen to induce relaxation.

articles.title: Deep Learning-Driven Multimodal Integration of Ultrasound and CT for Identifying Central Lymph Node Metastasis in Papillary Thyroid Carcinoma.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To evaluate the utility of multimodal imaging biomarkers in papillary thyroid carcinoma (PTC), this study developed a deep learning model using ultrasound (US) and computed tomography (CT) imaging to predict central lymph node metastasis (CLNM) in PTC by integrating radiomic features of perivascular adipose tissue (PVAT) at the cervical vertebra 6 (C6) level.

METHODS: We retrospectively analyzed 477 PTC patients from two centers. Using ResNet101 with Hierarchical Attention Integration (ResHAI-101), we extracted deep learning features of the tumor area from US images. Separately, we extracted radiomic features of PVAT from CT images. Univariate and multivariate analyses were conducted based on clinical data, followed by feature selection and integration.

RESULTS: Multimodal prediction model performance was quantified by the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC). Predictive performance was validated using an external test cohort (ETC). The Multimodal Prediction Model 3, integrating deep learning features, PVAT radiomic features and clinical features, showed superior diagnostic performance for predicting CLNM compared to the Unimodal Model, achieving AUCs of 0.915 in the internal test cohort and 0.890 in the ETC. Binary logistic regression identified gender, age, tumor size and extrathyroidal extension as independent risk factors for CLNM.

CONCLUSION: This study establishes and validates the significant impact of PVAT on CLNM in PTC, providing a non-invasive tool for pre-operative risk assessment to aid in surgical decision-making.

articles.title: Clinical experience with anti-interleukin-5 monoclonal antibodies in the treatment of eosinophilic granulomatosis with polyangiitis.
articles.journal: Farmacia hospitalaria : organo oficial de expresion cientifica de la Sociedad Espanola de Farmacia Hospitalaria
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Eosinophilic granulomatosis with polyangiitis is a rare disease whose standard treatment includes systemic glucocorticoids, bronchodilators, and immunosuppressive agents. Mepolizumab and benralizumab have recently emerged as therapeutic alternatives. The aim of this study was to evaluate the effectiveness and treatment outcomes in real-world practice.

METHODS: This retrospective observational study included 29 adult patients with eosinophilic granulomatosis with polyangiitis treated with mepolizumab and/or benralizumab at Hospital Universitario La Paz since 2017. Data were collected on oral glucocorticoid use, asthma therapies, immunosuppressive agents, eosinophil counts, and quality-of-life questionnaires to assess changes from baseline.

RESULTS: The mean initial dose of prednisone was 15.4 mg per day. At six months, 60.9% of evaluable patients had reduced their dose, and at one year, glucocorticoids had been completely discontinued in 11 of 23 evaluable patients. Five patients continued on immunosuppressive therapy, while the rest discontinued it. Eosinophil counts decreased significantly at one year. Quality-of-life measures showed numerical improvements after one year of treatment.

CONCLUSION: In this real-world cohort, treatment with mepolizumab or benralizumab was associated with reduced glucocorticoid use and eosinophil counts. Some patients continued to require concomitant immunosuppressive therapy, particularly those with more complex disease presentations.

articles.title: Transnasal endoscopy as a complementary tool for ambulatory detection of clinically significant portal hypertension.
articles.abstract: The efficacy, safety, and tolerability of transnasal endoscopy were evaluated as a complementary tool for detecting endoscopic signs consistent with portal hypertension in adults with compensated advanced chronic liver disease. Twenty-four patients underwent transnasal upper gastrointestinal endoscopy under local anesthesia and noninvasive assessment of liver fibrosis through elastography and platelet count. Procedure-related pain intensity and anxiety, adverse events, and impact on therapeutic decision-making were analyzed. The procedure was well tolerated, with no adverse events, and periprocedural discomfort and anxiety were minimal-to-mild. Transnasal endoscopy modified therapeutic decisions in 37.5% of cases, compared with the exclusive use of noninvasive methods. The findings suggest that transnasal endoscopy may provide additional value for the ambulatory detection of portal hypertension, as it is a rapid and practical procedure.

articles.title: Platelet Clearance: Mechanisms, Disorders, and Therapeutic Implications.
articles.abstract: Platelets are a critical, cellular component of thrombosis and hemostasis. Too few platelets can lead to increased bleeding events, seen in conditions like immune thrombocytopenia. Therefore, understanding the mechanisms by which platelets are cleared from the body leads to strategies to maintain platelets in circulation, supplement patients with platelets through transfusions, or induce platelet production in vivo. Here, we discuss 2 major platelet clearance mechanisms, glycan recognition by hepatocytes and apoptosis, and how they can be modulated to improve patient outcomes.

articles.title: Echocardiography-Detected Elevated Pulmonary Artery Systolic Pressure and Outcomes After Living Donor Liver Transplantation.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: The clinical significance of mild to moderate elevation in pulmonary artery systolic pressure (PASP) detected by transthoracic echocardiography during liver transplant evaluation remains uncertain, particularly in living donor liver transplantation (LDLT).

METHODS: A retrospective cohort study was conducted of adult living donor liver transplant recipients between 2018 and 2023. Preoperative PASP was estimated using transthoracic echocardiography, and patients were stratified into PASP ≤35 mm Hg and elevated PASP (>35 mm Hg) groups. The primary outcome was 5-year overall survival, and the secondary outcome was intensive care unit (ICU) stay.

RESULTS: Among 230 recipients, 141 had PASP ≤35 mm Hg and 89 had PASP >35 mm Hg. Five-year overall survival was similar between groups (70%vs 72%; log-rank p = 0.905). Elevated PASP was not associated with mortality on univariate Cox regression analysis. The proportion of patients with prolonged ICU stay (>5 days) did not differ significantly between groups. Higher body mass index was identified as a significant predictor of increased mortality risk.

CONCLUSION: Mild to moderate PASP elevation detected by echocardiography was not associated with inferior long-term survival or increased ICU utilization following LDLT. Modest PASP elevation on preoperative echocardiography alone should not preclude transplantation in carefully selected candidates.

articles.title: Profound Tacrolimus-Induced Catatonic Encephalopathy in a Kidney Transplant Recipient With Mitochondrial Myopathy: A Cautionary Case of Reversible Neurotoxicity.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Maternally inherited diabetes and deafness (MIDD) is a multisystem mitochondrial disorder most commonly caused by the m.3243A>G pathogenic variant in the MT-TL1 gene. Kidney transplantation in affected individuals presents unique perioperative and immunosuppressive management challenges due to underlying metabolic, neurologic, cardiac, and neuromuscular vulnerability.

CASE REPORT: We report a 64-year-old woman with end-stage renal disease secondary to insulin-dependent diabetes and MIDD (m.3243A>G) who underwent unrelated living donor kidney transplantation. The immediate postoperative period was complicated by diabetic ketoacidosis with lactic acidosis, transient slow graft function, and profound encephalopathy with catatonic features. Neuroimaging showed no acute abnormalities, and electroencephalography demonstrated severe diffuse encephalopathy without epileptiform activity. Tacrolimus levels were supratherapeutic in the early postoperative period. Given concern for calcineurin inhibitor neurotoxicity superimposed on mitochondrial dysfunction, tacrolimus was discontinued, and immunosuppression was switched to cyclosporine. Neurologic status gradually improved, and kidney allograft function fully normalized.

DISCUSSION: This case highlights the substantial perioperative metabolic and neurologic risks associated with kidney transplantation in patients with MIDD. Patients with compensated cardiac dysfunction and manageable neuromuscular impairment should not be excluded from transplantation solely on the basis of mitochondrial cytopathy.

articles.title: It Is Possible to Save the Kidney With Renal Artery Occlusion Without Autotransplantation: A Case Report.
articles.abstract: Renal artery stenosis is a rare but important cause of renovascular hypertension in children that may lead to malignant hypertension and renal failure. A 13-year-old girl presented with malignant hypertension and acute kidney injury, and imaging demonstrated occlusion of both renal arteries. Endovascular recanalization was unsuccessful because of complete, heavily fibrotic occlusions involving a long segment of the right renal artery extending to the hilum, leaving no suitable distal artery for reconstruction, and a 7.3-mm segment of the left renal artery at its aortic origin. To preserve renal function, surgical revascularization was performed by in situ reimplantation of the left renal artery into the aorta, without autotransplantation. Postoperatively, renal function recovered, the proteinuria present at admission regressed, and the patient became normotensive without antihypertensive medication.

articles.title: Incidentally Diagnosed Pulmonary Embolism Two Months After Living Liver Donation in a Donor With Homozygous MTHFR A1298C Mutation: A Case Report.
articles.abstract: Living donor liver transplantation (LDLT) is widely performed in countries with limited cadaveric organ donation. Although donor hepatectomy is generally safe, venous thromboembolic events such as pulmonary embolism (PE) remain rare but potentially life-threatening complications. Genetic thrombophilia, including methylenetetrahydrofolate reductase (MTHFR) mutations, may contribute to thrombotic risk. A 39-year-old female living liver donor underwent right donor hepatectomy for LDLT. The donor had no preoperative risk factors for venous thromboembolism, and a routine thrombophilia panel, including protein C, protein S, antithrombin III, factor V Leiden, and prothrombin gene mutations, was normal. Two months after surgery, an abdominal computed tomography (CT) scan performed due to fluid collection adjacent to the remnant liver in ultrasound (USG) during routine follow-up incidentally revealed partial PE. Pulmonary CT angiography confirmed the finding, while lower extremity Doppler USG showed no evidence of deep vein thrombosis. Laboratory tests revealed elevated D-dimer and homocysteine levels. Further genetic evaluation demonstrated a homozygous MTHFR A1298C mutation. The patient was treated with low molecular weight heparin followed by oral anticoagulant therapy for 6 months, resulting in complete radiological resolution of the embolism. PE after donor hepatectomy is rare but potentially fatal. This case suggests that MTHFR A1298C mutation may represent a previously underrecognized risk factor for venous thromboembolism in living liver donors. In populations with a high prevalence of MTHFR mutations, extended thrombophilia screening and appropriate thromboprophylaxis may help reduce the risk of postoperative thromboembolic complications.

articles.title: Randomized trial of counter-pressure and position maneuvers to prevent vasovagal syncope after intravenous cannulation for cardiac CT: The CoPPMan-IVC trial.
Design foresight and model humility for omics inference.
articles.abstract: Omics inference increasingly proceeds transcriptome-first: measure RNA, then ask how much biology can be extracted later. The ordering should be settled before the assay is chosen, not reconstructed from the data afterward. The first question is what the target requires to be directly observed; the second, what claims the data can honestly support. Design foresight means choosing assays, sampling, and orthogonal measurements based on the question and saying whether transcriptomics is primary, supporting, or insufficient for that claim. Model humility means refusing to promote computational output beyond what the data and assumptions can bear and writing measured, inferred, and predicted results in voices matched to their support. Using transcriptomics as the central case, we argue for question-first omics inference.

articles.title: Parallel culprit-thrombus transcriptomic and genome-wide association analyses in ST-segment elevation myocardial infarction: An exploratory pilot study.
articles.journal: Journal of the Formosan Medical Association = Taiwan yi zhi
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Direct molecular characterization of culprit coronary thrombi may provide insights into local mechanisms of ST-segment elevation myocardial infarction (STEMI) that are not captured by circulating blood. We investigated thrombus-associated transcriptomic patterns and their relationship with inherited genetic susceptibility.

METHODS: High-depth RNA sequencing was performed on paired aspirated culprit thrombi and peripheral blood from 10 patients with first-time STEMI. Differential expression was assessed using DESeq2, with exploratory signals defined by nominal P < 0.05 and absolute log2 fold change ≥ 1.5. Benjamini-Hochberg correction was applied across 44,525 transcripts. Transcript-clinical associations and sensitivity analyses were also performed. In parallel, a genome-wide association study included 1787 patients with STEMI and 17,837 age- and sex-matched controls.

RESULTS: Although 708 transcripts met the nominal exploratory criteria, none remained significant after transcriptome-wide correction. The nominal signals converged on biologically relevant processes, including extracellular matrix remodeling, inflammatory and chemokine signaling, lipid and apolipoprotein regulation, angiogenesis, and metalloprotease activity. These patterns likely reflected both local thrombus biology and differences in cellular composition between thrombi and peripheral blood. Clinical correlations and differences according to prior coronary artery disease were not robust after multiplicity correction or sensitivity analysis. Genome-wide association analysis identified rs74755602 at the MASTL locus (odds ratio, 2.08; 95% confidence interval, 1.65-2.63; P = 7.85 × 10-10), but MASTL showed no corresponding differential expression.

CONCLUSION: Paired thrombus-blood profiling revealed coherent but exploratory transcriptomic patterns related to thrombosis, inflammation, and vascular remodeling. The independent MASTL association lacked transcriptomic concordance, supporting cautious interpretation and further functional validation.

articles.title: FDG-PET in Infection Imaging of Immuno-compromised Patients.
articles.abstract: Infectious syndromes represent a monumental challenge in the management of immunocompromised patients, directly driving high rates of morbidity and critical mortality. This clinical cohort comprised oncological populations undergoing aggressive cytoreductive chemotherapy, end-stage renal disease patients dependent on specialized long-term dialysis access networks, and individuals undergoing treatment with advanced antiretroviral regimens. Because these individuals suffer from blunted or suppressed cellular immune mechanisms, standard structural imaging methodologies (such as standard digital radiography and cross-sectional computed tomography) exhibit prolonged diagnostic latency, frequently remaining negative or ambiguous during the crucial early windows of active pathogen replication.

articles.title: The DePICtion study: Implementing a diabetes classification tool in UK primary care-A qualitative study with primary care staff and patients.
articles.journal: Diabetic medicine : a journal of the British Diabetic Association
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The correct classification of diabetes (type 1, type 2 or rarer genetic forms) is essential for optimal treatment, but misclassification is common. The Diabetes in Primary Care Improving Classification (DePICtion) tool uses routinely collected clinical data to flag patients at risk of misclassification and prioritise them for further diagnostic testing.

AIM: To explore the acceptability and implementation of the DePICtion tool in primary care.

DESIGN AND SETTING: A qualitative study in 11 general practices across the Southwest and East Midlands, UK.

METHOD: Twelve practices were recruited to the study; 11 practices ran the tool and reviewed flagged patients. Semi-structured interviews were conducted with 10 staff and 11 patients to explore their experiences of the tool, reactions to the results and barriers and facilitators to use. Data were analysed thematically in NVivo.

RESULTS: Staff found the tool straightforward, compatible with existing workflows and clinically useful. Implementation required time and ownership of the process. Patients' responses were shaped by trust in staff and the personal meaning of their diabetes: Some viewed reclassification as a threat to their diagnostic identity, while others welcomed further diagnostic testing. Data privacy concerns were minimal but competing demands on staff time and resources were ubiquitously reported.

CONCLUSION: The DePICtion tool is acceptable and clinically useful for improving diabetes classification in primary care. Routine implementation is technically feasible but will require protected time, clear pathways for follow-up and support for patient communication and engagement.

articles.title: Nationwide Evolution of Durable Left Ventricular Assist Device Outcomes Following Introduction of the HeartMate 3 and Destination Therapy in Japan　- The Third Official Report From J-MACS.
articles.journal: Circulation journal : official journal of the Japanese Circulation Society
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The nationwide impact in Japan of contemporary improvement in the clinical management of durable left ventricular assist device (LVAD), together with the introduction of the HeartMate 3 (Abbott, Pleasanton, CA, USA), on clinical outcomes remains uncertain.

METHODS AND RESULTS: Using the Japanese Registry for Mechanically Assisted Circulatory Support (J-MACS), we analyzed all patients undergoing durable LVAD implantation in Japan between 2011 and 2025. Patients were divided into an early era (up to 2018) and the contemporary era (since 2019), reflecting introduction of the HeartMate 3 in Japan. The primary outcome was all-cause mortality during LVAD support. Among 1,859 patients, 1,587 underwent bridge-to-transplantation and 272 underwent destination therapy. Survival improved significantly in the contemporary era compared with the early era (5-year survival 84% vs. 76%, respectively; P=0.0002). Device dysfunction-free, pump thrombus-free, stroke-free, major bleeding-free, and pump exchange-free survival also improved significantly after 2019 (all P<0.0001). Right ventricular failure and ventricular arrhythmia that required appropriate defibrillation remained frequent complications. Among patients who received a durable LVAD since 2019, destination therapy recipients had lower survival than bridge-to-transplantation recipients (3-year survival 81% vs. 91%; P=0.0057).

CONCLUSIONS: Clinical outcomes after durable LVAD implantation improved substantially following the introduction of HeartMate 3 in Japan, particularly regarding pump-related and hemocompatibility-related complications. However, right ventricular failure and ventricular arrhythmia remain major unresolved challenges.

articles.title: Physiological within-day Variation in Lipoprotein(a): Is a Once-in-a-lifetime Measurement Sufficient for Cardiovascular Risk Evaluation?
articles.abstract:
AIMS: Lipoprotein(a) (Lp(a)) is a strong risk factor for cardiovascular events, independent of low-density lipoprotein cholesterol (LDL-C). Because the Lp(a) concentration is largely determined by genetic factors, some dyslipidemia guidelines recommend a once-in-a-lifetime measurement of Lp(a). Furthermore, a non-fasting lipid profile assessment is allowed for initial screening of dyslipidemia. Although the LDL-C concentration decreases slightly throughout the day, the within-day variation of Lp(a) remains unknown. We aimed to investigate whether the Lp(a) concentration remains stable throughout the day.

METHODS: Lp(a) concentrations were measured at seven time points throughout the day in 34 patients using a latex turbidimetric immunoassay. The Lp(a) values are expressed in molar units, which are equivalent to those determined by a mass spectrometry-based reference measurement procedure.

RESULTS: We found that the Lp(a) concentrations decreased by 2.9±5.2 nmol/L at 14:00 (p＜0.05), 3.6±4.8 nmol/L at 20:00 (p＜0.001), and 2.9±5.1 nmol/L at 24:00 (p＜0.05). The mean percent Lp(a) decreased significantly at 17:30 (-6.2±0.1%) and 24:00 (-7.0±0.1%) from the fasting level.

CONCLUSION: The Lp(a) concentration decreases slightly, but significantly, throughout the day. Considering physiological variations, it is preferable to re-evaluate the Lp(a) concentration in those with a borderline elevation.

articles.title: Associations of Albuminuria and eGFR with Stiffness Parameter β in Type 2 Diabetes.
articles.abstract:
AIMS: The stiffness parameter β is a clinical index of arterial stiffness that reflects systemic atherosclerosis. Chronic kidney disease (CKD) is a major cardiovascular risk factor in type 2 diabetes; however, it remains unclear whether a reduced kidney function or albuminuria is more strongly associated with arterial stiffness. This study examined the relative associations of estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR) and urinary albumin-to-creatinine ratio (UACR) with stiffness parameter β in patients with type 2 diabetes.

METHODS: This cross-sectional study enrolled 1,924 patients with type 2 diabetes. The stiffness parameter β was assessed at the common carotid artery using ultrasonography.

RESULTS: The participants were 58.8% male, with a median age of 63 years and a median HbA1c level of 8.3%. According to univariate analyses, stiffness parameter β was significantly correlated with both eGFR and UACR. However, after adjusting for conventional cardiovascular risk factors, stiffness parameter β remained independently associated with UACR, whereas no independent association was observed with eGFR. Similar findings were observed when eGFR and albuminuria were analyzed according to the CKD categories. No significant interactions were observed between UACR and either age or body mass index in relation to stiffness parameter β.

CONCLUSIONS: In patients with type 2 diabetes, albuminuria, but not eGFR, was independently associated with stiffness parameter β after multivariable adjustment. These findings suggest that albuminuria may serve as a marker of local carotid arterial stiffening and vascular injury.

articles.title: Capability, opportunity and motivation to support adults with type 1 diabetes experiencing fear of hypoglycaemia: A survey of Australian diabetes healthcare professionals.
articles.journal: Diabetic medicine : a journal of the British Diabetic Association
articles.abstract:
AIM: To explore the perceptions, experiences and unmet needs of diabetes healthcare professionals (DHPs) for supporting adults with type 1 diabetes (T1D) with fear of hypoglycaemia (FoH).

METHOD: An online survey explored Australian DHPs' perceived capability, opportunity, motivation and behaviours related to supporting adults with T1D with FoH. DHPs were recruited via online advertisements, e-newsletters and at conferences. Quantitative data were analysed using descriptive statistics, and qualitative data were analysed thematically.

RESULTS: A total of 106 eligible DHPs were included (83% credentialled diabetes educators, 92% women, mean (SD) age 49 (11) years), from all eight states/territories. DHPs indicated that FoH is experienced by almost two thirds of adults with T1D in their clinics. Most DHPs believe addressing FoH is within their scope of clinical practice (83%), and report motivation (89%) and capability (skills and confidence, 71% and 70% respectively) to do so. While more than half (50%-71%) perceive they have the social opportunity (e.g. social norms, workplace culture), few report physical opportunity (8%-24%), for example, access to validated screening tools; financial remuneration; affordable mental healthcare referral pathways. Free-text responses highlighted the need for affordable and timely access to mental health professionals with knowledge about diabetes. Approximately eight out of ten would be (very) likely to refer those experiencing FoH to online self-guided programs, if available.

CONCLUSION: These findings show that Australian DHPs report the motivation and capability, but lack the opportunity to support adults with T1D experiencing FoH. Innovative referral pathways, including online self-guided programmes, are perceived positively and may be useful in the Australian healthcare context.

articles.title: The impact of frailty on glycaemic control in older adults with type 1 diabetes mellitus: An observational study.
articles.journal: Diabetic medicine : a journal of the British Diabetic Association

articles.title: Estimating the long-term cost-effectiveness of a free online Diabetes Self-Management Education and Support service in England: Healthy living for people with type 2 diabetes, using a matched cohort study design.
articles.journal: Diabetic medicine : a journal of the British Diabetic Association
articles.abstract:
AIMS: The National Health Service (NHS) offers Healthy Living, an online Diabetes Self-Management Education and Support service, to help people Self Manage Type 2 Diabetes, with modest 1-year reductions in HbA1c levels, systolic blood pressure and body mass index. We aim to assess the cost-effectiveness of Healthy Living compared with usual care.

METHODS: A patient-level economic simulation model (UKPDS-OM2.1) was used to conduct an economic analysis from the NHS perspective over a lifetime horizon, discounted at 3.5%. The model translated risk factor reductions to long-term cost and quality-adjusted life year (QALY) estimates. Additional analyses estimated intervention and medication cost consequences.

RESULTS: The UKPDS-OM2.1 predicted a modest improvement in health (0.016 QALYs) and a small reduction in lifetime healthcare costs (-£4 per person). Offsetting with intervention costs (£7 per user) and increased medication costs (£212 per user) yielded a net cost of £216 per user. The cost-per-QALY of £13,192 was below the lower NICE threshold (£25,000/QALY), indicating that the programme is cost-effective. Sensitivity analyses largely demonstrated robustness, but the finding was sensitive to structural assumptions about disease progression post-intervention with the inclusion of medication costs.

CONCLUSION: Healthy Living appears to be a low-cost, online intervention for self managing type 2 diabetes, generating modest health benefits that are likely to be considered cost-effective use of NHS resources.
