BACKGROUND: Advanced 4D flow cardiovascular magnetic resonance (CMR) biomarkers such as kinetic energy (KE), vorticity (ω), and viscous energy loss (VEL) are increasingly used to characterize abnormal flow in repaired tetralogy of Fallot (rTOF), but their sensitivity to acquisition parameters including magnet vendor, sequence and signal quality has not been defined. We sought to evaluate the real-world variability in 4D flow sequences and technical correlates to 4D flow measurements of the aorta (Ao) and right ventricle, leveraging the multicenter Tetralogy of Fallot 4D flow Registry of Energetics and Kinetics (TREK).

METHODS: This was a multicenter observational analysis of clinically acquired 4D flow CMR processed at a core laboratory. The technical analysis focused on systolic Ao and diastolic RV hemodynamic measurements of KE, ω and VEL. Time-resolved hemodynamic curves were summarized and compared across sequence/reconstruction type, contrast agents and sequence parameters. Interobserver variability was assessed with Bland-Altman analysis and intraclass correlation coefficients. Apparent signal-to-noise ratio (aSNR), apparent velocity-to-noise ratio (aVNR) and presence of velocity aliasing were also measured. Multivariable linear/logistic regression was used to identify acquisition parameters associated with aSNR, aVNR and aliasing. Multivariable linear regression models were constructed to evaluate associations of aSNR, aVNR, and aliasing with KE, ω, and VEL after adjustment for clinical covariates.

RESULTS: The cohort included 345 datasets (295 rTOF studies and 50 controls). Sequence/reconstruction type, field strength, voxel volume, temporal resolution, and VENC were associated with aSNR and aVNR in multivariable models. Aliasing was associated with lower VENC. ω and VEL varied substantially across sequence/reconstruction type and contrast groups, whereas KE was comparatively more stable. In multivariable models, lower aSNR was associated with higher measured hemodynamic values after adjustment for clinical covariates, with stronger associations for ω and VEL rather than KE.

CONCLUSIONS: In a real-world multicenter 4D flow CMR registry, measured advanced hemodynamic biomarkers were associated with acquisition/reconstruction characteristics, apparent image quality, and residual aliasing. 4D Flow harmonization efforts should therefore extend beyond vendor types alone and explicitly account for aSNR, aVNR, and aliasing when interpreting derivative-based 4D flow measurements.

articles.title: Clinical Outcomes of Transperitoneal vs Retroperitoneal Approaches of Open Aortic Repair for Abdominal Aortic Aneurysm Stratified by the Iliac Bifurcation Involvement.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Aortic aneurysm involving the iliac bifurcation (AAAIB) is associated with higher rates of systemic comorbidities and increased complexity of open aortic repair (OAR), resulting in worse outcomes compared to OAR for isolated abdominal aortic aneurysm (IAAA). The Society for Vascular Surgery (SVS) practice guidelines recommend the retroperitoneal approach (RPA) for OAR in certain patients with abdominal aortic aneurysm (AAA). However, there is limited evidence to determine whether the relative advantages and disadvantages of RPA and the transperitoneal approach (TPA) change depending on whether the aneurysm distally involves the iliac bifurcation. This study aims to compare the outcomes of TPA and RPA for AAA, stratified by the iliac bifurcation involvement, in a multi-institutional, real-world setting.

METHODS: The SVS Vascular Quality Initiative (VQI) database was queried for patients who underwent OAR for AAA from January 2003 to September 2024. Patients were stratified as AAAIB or IAAA based on whether the aneurysm involved the iliac bifurcation and required a distal anastomosis beyond the common iliac artery (CIA) bifurcation, or not. Baseline characteristics, as well as outcomes such as overall 30-day mortality, Major Adverse Cardiovascular Events (MACE: death, myocardial infarction, stroke), and 1-year survival, were compared between the TPA and RPA groups in patients with IAAA and AAAIB. Univariable and multivariable analyses, as well as a confirmatory analysis with inverse probability-weighted regression (IPWR), were performed.

RESULTS: Of all reviewed patients, 17,009 were included in the final analysis, of whom 15,218 (89.5%) had IAAA, and 1,791 (10.5%) had AAAIB. Among patients with IAAA, compared to RPA, TPA was associated with higher odds of overall 30-day mortality (OR: 1.26, 95%CI: 1.05-1.49, p=0.011), MACE (OR: 1.26, 95%CI: 1.11-1.44, p=0.001), and a lower 1-year survival rate (HR: 1.23, 95%CI: 1.09-1.39, p=0.001). Among patients with AAAIB, TPA was associated with lower odds of lower extremity (LE) ischemia (OR: 0.47, 95%CI: 0.25-0.91, p=0.024) without significant differences in 30-day mortality (OR: 0.80, 95%CI: 0.42-1.51, p=0.485), MACE (OR: 0.86, 95%CI: 0.52-1.42, p=0.563), and 1-year survival (HR: 0.93, 95%CI: 0.59-1.47, p=0.768).

CONCLUSIONS: In this real-world study, involvement of the iliac bifurcation in AAA was an effect modifier for the outcomes of different OAR approaches. For patients with IAAA, compared with RPA, TPA was associated with worse 30-day mortality, MACE, and 1-year survival. Whereas for patients with AAAIB, TPA was associated with lower odds of LE ischemia, without significant differences in 30-day mortality, MACE, or 1-year survival. This study suggests that RPA may be the procedure of choice for IAAA if it is otherwise feasible. However, TPA may be the procedure of choice for patients with AAAIB who are otherwise anatomically suitable. Larger prospective studies are warranted to validate these findings.

articles.title: Effects of diagnostic thresholds for gestational diabetes on perinatal mental health: Data from the GEMS randomised clinical trial.
articles.abstract:
AIM: To assess the effect of diagnosis using the lower International Association of the Diabetes and Pregnancy Study Groups (IADPSG) criteria compared with the higher New Zealand criteria on perinatal mental health.

METHODS: Secondary analysis of the GEMS Trial, a randomised trial assessing optimum glycaemic diagnostic thresholds for gestational diabetes. Women completing any questionnaire assessing anxiety (6-item State-Trait Anxiety Inventory >15), depression (Edinburgh Postnatal Depression Scale >12) or health-related quality of life (SF-36) at enrolment, 36 weeks' gestation or 6 months postpartum were eligible. Generalised linear mixed-effects models adjusted for age, BMI, recruitment centre, and gestational age at randomisation generated adjusted relative risks (aRR) and adjusted mean differences (aMD).

RESULTS: Among 3452 women, 1737 (50.3%) were randomised to the lower criteria group and 1715 (49.7%) to the higher criteria group. No significant differences were observed between groups in anxiety, depression, or mental health-related quality of life at 36 weeks' gestation or 6 months postpartum after adjustment for baseline scores. However, women with mild GDM diagnosed and treated under the lower criteria reported better general health, vitality, social functioning, and postpartum mental component summary scores.

CONCLUSION: Use of the IADPSG criteria does not adversely affect maternal perinatal mental health.

articles.title: Effectiveness of technology-enabled teleophthalmology and emerging retinal imaging techniques for diabetic retinopathy screening: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Diabetic retinopathy (DR) is a major microvascular complication of diabetes and causes preventable visual loss. Technology-enabled screening can extend retinal assessment beyond specialist settings and strengthen screening, referral, and follow-up across diabetes care pathways.

METHODS: We systematically reviewed randomized and non-randomized implementation studies, diagnostic-accuracy and comparative retinal-imaging studies, and economic evaluations of technology-enabled DR screening. PubMed, EMBASE, Cochrane Library, Scopus, Web of Science, and Google Scholar were searched from inception to 23 May 2026 without language restriction. Two reviewers independently performed study selection, data extraction, and risk-of-bias assessment. Random-effects meta-analyses synthesized comparative and proportional outcomes, and GRADE assessed certainty.

RESULTS: Thirty-three studies were included. Teleophthalmology increased DR screening uptake/completion versus usual care or pre-implementation practice (RR 1.966, 95% CI 1.451-2.664; I2 = 75.2%) and improved adherence to recommended eye care (OR 2.464, 95% CI 1.477-4.112; I2 = 66.47%). The pooled ungradable-image rate was 7.4% (95% CI 3.0%-17.1%; I2 = 59.17%). Advanced retinal imaging showed pooled sensitivity of 97.59% (95% CI 94.50%-100.00%; I2 = 0%) and specificity of 91.22% (95% CI 78.46%-100.00%; I2 = 88.7%) for prespecified vascular lesion detection. OCTA demonstrated a pooled eye-level retinal neovascularization detection yield of 63.6% (95% CI 49.9%-75.4%; I2 = 46.29%). Economic evaluations supported cost-effective or cost-saving technology-enabled screening across assessed health systems.

CONCLUSION: Technology-enabled DR care improves screening participation, adherence, and health-system efficiency, supporting integration of teleophthalmology and advanced imaging into scalable diabetes complication-management pathways.

articles.title: Capturing human-machine interplay in automated insulin delivery systems through day-to-day variability of the automated correction index (ACI-V%).
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The Automated Correction Index (ACI) reflects the proportion of algorithm-driven correction boluses relative to total bolus insulin in advanced hybrid closed-loop (AHCL) systems. While mean ACI has been associated with glycemic outcomes in patients with type 1 diabetes mellitus (T1DM), the clinical significance of its day-to-day variability (ACI-V%) remains unknown.

METHODS: In this multicenter real-world study, 330 pediatric and adult patients with T1DM using the MiniMed™ 780G system were studied. ACI-V% was defined as the coefficient of variation of daily ACI values over a 30-day period. Associations between ACI-V% and continuous glucose monitoring (CGM) metrics were assessed.

RESULTS: Higher ACI-V% was associated with greater time in range (TIR70-180 mg/dL) and lower time above range, while no significant association with time below range was observed. ACI-V% showed an inverse correlation with mean ACI, suggesting greater day-to-day variability in settings of lower overall automated correction insulin delivery. Moreover, ACI-V% independently predicted achievement of TIR70-180 mg/dL > 70%, with a threshold of ≥ 32.6% identifying patients more likely to reach this target (sensitivity 52.4%, specificity 71.4%).

CONCLUSIONS: ACI-V% provides an exploratory descriptor of day-to-day variability in automated correction insulin delivery that may complement mean ACI for clinical interpretation of AHCL system behavior.

articles.title: Dapagliflozin and 54-week kidney function in kidney transplant recipients with post-transplant diabetes mellitus: a randomized controlled trial.
articles.abstract:
AIMS: To evaluate dapagliflozin effects on kidney function and safety in kidney transplant recipients with post-transplant diabetes mellitus (PTDM).

METHODS: In this single-center, prospective, open-label randomized trial, 68 participants were assigned 1:1 to dapagliflozin 10 mg daily plus standard care or standard care alone. Week-54 observed-data analyses included 27 participants per group; an intention-to-treat multiple-imputation sensitivity analysis included all randomized participants.

RESULTS: At week 54, the baseline-adjusted between-group eGFR difference was 6.81 mL/min/1.73 m2 (95 % CI, 1.68 to 11.94; P = 0.010) in the complete-case analysis and 6.05 mL/min/1.73 m2 (95 % CI, 0.99 to 11.11; P = 0.020) after multiple imputation. The estimate was attenuated after additional multivariable adjustment, with the 95 % CI including no difference. Serum magnesium declined less with dapagliflozin, whereas HbA1c and tacrolimus trough concentrations were similar. Observed adverse-event frequencies were similar between groups, although the trial was not powered to assess uncommon safety events.

CONCLUSIONS: Dapagliflozin showed an exploratory week-54 eGFR signal, but the estimate was sensitive to covariate adjustment and missing-data assumptions. This small trial does not establish a definitive clinically meaningful kidney benefit.

articles.title: Repeated metastasis-directed radiotherapy in patients with oligorecurrent prostate cancer: outcomes and risk stratification from a large multinational PSMA PET-guided cohort.
articles.journal: Radiotherapy and oncology : journal of the European Society for Therapeutic Radiology and Oncology
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND AND PURPOSE: Repeated metastasis-directed radiotherapy (MDRT) is increasingly used in patients with metachronous oligometastatic prostate cancer. However, the efficacy and optimal patient selection criteria remain insufficiently defined.

MATERIAL AND METHODS: Within the multinational PORTAL consortium, we evaluated outcomes of repeated MDRT in patients with PSMA-PET-detected oligorecurrent hormone-sensitive prostate cancer undergoing ≥ 2 MDRT cycles. The primary endpoint was androgen deprivation therapy-free survival (ADT-FS), secondary endpoints included polymetastatic-free survival, next-line systemic therapy-free survival, and overall survival, all calculated from start of repeated MDRT. A multivariable Cox regression model was developed to predict ADT-FS, and its performance was evaluated by bootstrapped internal validation using discrimination (C-index) and calibration.

RESULTS: A total of 177 patients were included. Median follow-up after second MDRT was 26.1 months. During follow-up, 86 patients initiated ADT, 59 developed polymetastatic disease, 38 received next-line systemic therapy, and 17 deaths occurred. Two-year ADT-FS was 50.2 % (95 % CI 41.4-58.3). Two-year polymetastatic-free, next-line systemic therapy-free, and overall survival were 64.4 % (95 % CI 55.4-72.0), 83.5 % (95 % CI 76.0-88.9), and 94.2 % (95 % CI 88.2-97.2), respectively. In the multivariable Cox regression model, a longer interval between first and second MDRT (HR 0.96 per month, 95 % CI 0.94-0.99; p = 0.003) and treatment of a single versus ≥ 2 new lesions (HR for ≥ 2 lesions 1.88, 95 % CI 1.22-2.90; p = 0.006) were independently associated with ADT-FS. Model discrimination was moderate (optimism-corrected C-index 0.68) with good calibration.

CONCLUSIONS: In this multicentre cohort of patients with PSMA PET-detected metachronous oligorecurrent prostate cancer undergoing repeated MDRT, favourable ADT-FS outcomes were observed, with approximately half of patients remaining ADT-free two years after second MDRT. Given the absence of a comparator group, these outcomes may reflect both the effects of treatment and favourable disease biology of patients who remained eligible for repeated MDRT. The interval between MDRT cycles, and the number of metastases, independently predicted ADT-FS and may support patient selection.

articles.title: Non-invasive Left Ventricular End Diastolic Wall Stress and the Risk of Incident Heart Failure in a Clinical Population.
articles.abstract: Greater left ventricular (LV) wall stress has been associated with adverse clinical outcomes among patients with heart failure (HF). We examined the relation between LV wall stress and the risk of incident HF. Using data from the Vanderbilt Synthetic Derivative, we studied 29,246 adult patients without prevalent HF or ≥ moderate valve disease who underwent transthoracic echocardiography between 2014-2020. LV end diastolic wall stress (LVEDWS) was calculated from chamber and wall thickness measures and E/e' as a surrogate for LV end diastolic pressure. Incident HF was ascertained from ICD-9/10 codes. Correlates of LVEDWS were examined with multivariable linear regression. The association between LVEDWS and risk of incident HF was tested in Cox regression adjusted for demographics, comorbidities, blood pressure, body mass index, laboratory data including B-type natriuretic peptide, LVEF, and LV mass index. The cohort had a median age of 59 years, 54% females, with 11% of individuals identifying as Black. Median LVEDWS was 14.5 (IQR: 11.8-18.0) kdynes/cm2. Cross sectional correlates of LVEDWS ranked according to Chi-squared value were LVEF, heart rate, female sex, and LV mass index. Over a maximum follow-up time of 8.2 years (median 3.7 years), 3,082 (11%) individuals developed incident HF. In multivariable Cox regression, each 1-unit increase in LVEDWS significantly associated with an increased risk of incident HF (aHR: 1.019; 95%CI 1.014-1.024), which was largely consistent across subgroups. In conclusion, among a broad range of patients clinically referred for echocardiography, greater non-invasively measured LVEDWS associates with higher risk for incident HF.

articles.title: Biomanufacturing Vascular Matrix-Mimetic Hydrogels from Quantified Arterial Micromechanics and Microstructure.
articles.abstract: The microstructural and micromechanical properties of the arterial extracellular matrix (ECM) are central to vascular cell behavior but are disrupted by disease and aging. Elastin and fibrillar collagens provide essential cues, yet the effects of disease-associated ECM remodeling on smooth muscle function remain poorly defined. Here, we imaged fibrillar ECM components across layers of healthy and hypertensive arteries in a large animal model and quantified their stiffness with submicron and piconewton resolution. These animal-derived data guided the fabrication of artery-mimetic hydrogels using image-derived 3D projection micro-stereolithography (µSTL) and thiol-ene clickable bioinks. The resulting hydrogels replicated fibril features down to 2 µm with emulated curvatures and tunable stiffness spanning physiological to pathological ranges (1-35 kPa). Systematic optimization of printing parameters, including light intensity, exposure time, monomer concentration, crosslinker type, optical configurations, and hydrogel swelling solutions, ensured high-fidelity structural replication. Vascular smooth muscle cells cultured on these hydrogels revealed that diseased ECM conditions promoted hypertrophy, impaired contractility, and reduced calcium responsiveness. Quantitative PCR showed reduced expression of contractile markers (MYH11, SMTN) and marked upregulation of PTK2 (focal adhesion kinase) on hypertensive-mimetic matrices, implicating focal adhesion-dependent mechanotransduction in this response. This image-guided biofabrication platform enables precise engineering of vascular microenvironments for mechanistic studies of remodeling, therapeutic testing, and modeling of complex vascular disease states. STATEMENT OF SIGNIFICANCE: Arterial extracellular matrix stiffens and reorganizes in hypertension, yet in vitro models rarely reproduce these micron-scale changes. We measured layer-specific stiffness and fibrillar architecture in arteries from normotensive and hypertensive steers, a large animal model with fattening-induced hypertension. These data were directly translated into projection micro-stereolithography of thiol-ene hydrogels. The resulting matrices, high-fidelity 3D hydrogel prints, reproduced fibrillar features down to 2 µm with emulated curvatures and tunable stiffness spanning 1-35 kPa. Vascular smooth muscle cells cultured on hypertensive-mimetic matrices exhibited hypertrophic morphology, reduced calcium responsiveness and agonist-induced contractility, altered contractile-marker expression, and increased PTK2 expression, linking disease-associated matrix remodeling to altered mechanotransduction. This measurement-to-fabrication workflow provides a physiologically informed platform for mechanistic studies of vascular remodeling and evaluation of therapeutic responses.

articles.title: When Is 4Gy Enough? Defining Dose Sufficiency and Durable Control in Indolent B-Cell Lymphoma.
articles.abstract: Ultra-low-dose radiotherapy, most commonly delivered as 4Gy in two fractions (2Gy × 2), is an established low-burden approach for radiosensitive indolent B-cell lymphoma. Its use as stand-alone definitive local therapy is constrained by a persistent gap between early tumor regression and durable local control. This review examines when 4Gy should be considered sufficient by integrating clinical intent, lesion biology, response assessment, immune context, and emerging biomarkers. We distinguish its use as stand-alone local treatment, palliation, response-adapted de-escalation, and immune-integrated strategies. Across these settings, early response indicates radiosensitivity but does not prove lesion sterilization or equivalence to standard-dose radiotherapy. Dose sufficiency depends on durable in-field control, tumor burden, anatomical definition, reassessment reliability, feasibility of salvage, and the consequences of local failure. Immune and cellular combinations may extend the value of 4Gy beyond local cytoreduction, but the contribution of irradiation should be tested separately from systemic or intratumoral partners. PET response, MRD, ctDNA, and immune correlates may help distinguish transient cytoreduction from durable clearance and local response from patient-level disease control. At present, these biomarkers are better suited to trial design and mechanistic validation than to routine dose selection. Future studies should move beyond response rates and define decision rules that link early response, immune modulation, biomarker dynamics, lesion-level durability, salvageability, and cumulative treatment burden.

articles.title: MicroRNA-145 hinders carotid plaque growth via suppression of tumor growth factor-β receptor type II and autophagy.
articles.journal: Biochimica et biophysica acta. General subjects
articles.abstract: Plaque erosion is increasingly recognized as a critical pathological mechanism in acute coronary syndrome. In this study, we found that microRNA-145 (miR-145) levels were significantly reduced in plaques with grade III-IV stenosis compared with controls. Using an apoE-/- mouse model fed a high-cholesterol diet, we demonstrated that inhibition of miR-145 with antagomiR-145 increased plaque volume and elevated LC3-II expression, a marker of autophagy. Transmission electron microscopy further confirmed a greater abundance of autophagosomes in carotid atherosclerotic plaques from antagomiR-145-treated mice. Mechanistically, miR-145 suppressed both transforming growth factor-β receptor type II (TGFβR-II) expression and autophagy in vascular smooth muscle cells (VSMCs). Silencing TGFβR-II with specific siRNA recapitulated the effects of antagomiR-145 in cultured VSMCs and in vivo. Collectively, these findings suggest that miR-145 may protect against carotid plaque progression by downregulating TGFβR-II and limiting autophagy.

articles.title: COMPREHENSIVE ORAL CARE IS ASSOCIATED WITH A SIGNIFICANT DECREASE IN VENTILATOR-ASSOCIATED PNEUMONIA: A SINGLE CENTER PROSPECTIVE COHORT STUDY.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Mechanically ventilated patients in the intensive care unit (ICU) are at risk for developing ventilator-associated pneumonia (VAP), with a 13% mortality rate and cost of $50,000 per patient. Toothbrushing is associated with positive outcomes, including lower VAP rates. Electric toothbrushes (eTBs) have greater effectiveness in the general population compared with manual toothbrushes (mTBs), and eTBs may provide benefits to ventilated patients.

OBJECTIVE: The aim of the study was to evaluate VAP rates for patients receiving a comprehensive oral care protocol (COCP) including an eTB versus a standard oral care protocol (SOCP) including an mTB.

METHODS: We conducted a prospective cohort study in a tertiary hospital's ICUs. SOCP or COCP consisting of an electric toothbrush was followed. VAP rates and hospital costs were compared between groups.

RESULTS: Our study included 72 ICU patients (63.9% male, mean age 53.5±16.6 years). Patients treated with COCP were less likely to develop VAP (2.6% vs 21.2%, P=0.020), had significantly fewer ventilation days (5.4±1.8 vs 6.2±1.3, P=0.031), and fewer ICU days (9.0±5.6 vs 13.8±9.1, P=0.012). The COCP group had significantly fewer VAPs per 1,000 patient ventilation days, 1 in 209 days, or 4.8 (0.1-26.7) events per 1,000 ventilation days versus standard oral care with 7 in 190 days or 36.8 (14.8-75.9), P=0.037. Cost savings if COCP would have been used in the SOCP group of 33 patients were estimated at $283,428.

CONCLUSION: We compared standard versus comprehensive oral care protocols. Significantly fewer patients treated with the comprehensive protocol developed VAP and hospital savings were significant.

articles.title: Association of Sleep Duration with MASLD Status and Hepatic Steatosis Index in Korean Adults: The Indirect Role of Sedentary Behavior.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: Metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD) affects nearly three in ten adults globally, while its prevalence in South Korea has risen by approximately 3-4% per year. Although MASLD is linked to lifestyle factors, few studies have examined the associations among sleep duration, MASLD status, and the hepatic steatosis index (HSI). Accordingly, we evaluated the relationship between sleep duration and MASLD status and separately assessed whether sedentary behavior formed an indirect pathway between sleep duration and HSI, an indicator of hepatic steatosis.

METHODS: The analysis included 26,909 adults aged 20 years or older who participated in the Korea National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey from 2014 through 2021. Logistic regression was used to estimate the relationship of sleep duration with MASLD status. Mediation analysis was conducted using HSI as the outcome variable to examine whether sedentary behavior indirectly linked sleep duration with HSI.

RESULTS: MASLD was identified in 23.2% of 26,909 participants. In the adjusted logistic model, MASLD odds were higher among participants sleeping ≤4 hours (OR = 1.44, 95% CI: 1.17-1.78) and those reporting ≥8 hours of sedentary time (OR = 1.17, 95% CI: 1.09-1.25). Correlations of HSI with sleep duration (r = -.06, p < .001) and sedentary behavior (r = .02, p < .001) were small. The mediation model yielded a direct association between sleep duration and HSI (β = -0.21, 95% CI: -0.26 to -0.16), whereas the indirect effect through sedentary behavior was statistically significant but minimal (β = -0.0073, 95% bootstrap CI: -0.0118 to -0.0032).

CONCLUSION: MASLD status was related to both shorter sleep and longer sedentary time. Nevertheless, the very small correlations among sleep duration, sedentary behavior, and HSI offered little empirical support for a meaningful mediation pathway. Longitudinal research is required to establish the direction and timing of these relationships.

articles.title: Construction, expression, and immunogenicity analysis of a fusion gene based on the PE/PPE family in combination with adjuvants.
articles.abstract: Tuberculosis (TB) remains the leading global cause of death from a single infectious agent and a major fatal infectious disease worldwide. However, the Bacillus Calmette-Guérin (BCG) vaccine-currently the only licensed TB vaccine in clinical practice-has critical limitations in preventing latent infection and disease reactivation, failing to deliver comprehensive protective immunity. Given these gaps, targeting Mycobacterium tuberculosis (M.tb) antigens with strong immunogenic potential is a key strategy for next-generation TB vaccine development. The pathogenic M.tb harbors the Pro-Glu (PE) and Pro-Pro-Glu (PPE) motif gene families, named for their N-terminal conserved proline (P) and glutamic acid (E) residues, which are increasingly recognized as promising vaccine targets due to their roles in host-pathogen interaction and immune modulation. To address BCG's limitations, this study selected the PE/PPE family members Rv0832 and Rv3653 for full-length gene synthesis to construct a fusion antigen designated ZMM6, which was expressed using the pET-28a vector. The immunogenicity of the ZMM6 subunit vaccine was then evaluated in M.tb-infected human cohorts and animal models. The results showed that the fusion protein ZMM6 induced peripheral blood mononuclear cells (PBMCs) from M. tb-infected individuals to secrete high levels of IFN-γ, IL-2, and IL-6 cytokines. Moreover, the levels of cytokine secretion induced by the fusion protein were higher than those induced by the individual subunit proteins, suggesting that the fusion protein possesses higher immunogenicity. In mice immunized with the protein vaccine (adjuvant formulation) ZMM6/MnJ, high titers of various IgG subclass antibodies were elicited, with the immune response skewed toward a Th1-type profile, accompanied by robust induction of multiple Th1-type cytokines. Flow cytometry (FCM) analysis further revealed a significant increase in CD4+IFN-γ+ single-positive T cells in ZMM6/MnJ-immunized mice. Collectively, these findings demonstrate that the protein vaccine (adjuvant formulation) ZMM6/MnJ exhibits strong immunogenicity.

articles.title: miRNAs: Current and future diagnostic biomarkers in liver fibrosis.
articles.journal: Clinica chimica acta; international journal of clinical chemistry
articles.abstract: Liver fibrosis is an abnormal response of the liver to various pathogenic factors. It represents a critical stage in the progression from chronic liver disease to cirrhosis and liver cancer. Without timely diagnosis and intervention, liver fibrosis can significantly reduce patients' survival rates and quality of life. In liver fibrosis, microRNA (miRNA) plays a dual role in disease progression by regulating gene expression and signaling pathways. Some miRNAs have antifibrotic effects by inhibiting the TGF-β/Smad signaling pathway or blocking the activation of hepatic stellate cells (HSCs). In contrast, other miRNAs accelerate fibrosis by activating the HIF-1α/VEGF pathway or promoting abnormal extracellular matrix deposition. This two-way relationship establishes a basis for investigating miRNAs as potential diagnostic markers. This narrative review synthesizes evidence on various miRNAs associated with liver fibrosis and their molecular mechanisms. It also evaluates their potential applications in serological testing. Research shows that miRNAs, because of their high stability and specificity, are likely to overcome the limitations of traditional methods for diagnosing liver fibrosis. Furthermore, this article evaluates the strengths and weaknesses of popular miRNA detection methods, such as real-time quantitative PCR, microarrays, and next-generation sequencing (NGS), emphasizing that optimizing standardized processes and high-throughput technologies is essential for facilitating the clinical use of miRNAs. In summary, miRNAs are promising non-invasive diagnostic tools for the early diagnosis and personalized treatment of liver fibrosis. Nonetheless, additional research is essential to improve the technology and clinical validation of miRNA detection for its widespread use in clinical settings.

articles.title: High-frequency rTMS attenuates cerebral ischemia/reperfusion injury and modulates mTOR-related signaling and brain-gut-immune phenotypes in MCAO/R rats.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: High-frequency repetitive transcranial magnetic stimulation (rTMS) may promote neurological recovery after ischemic stroke, but its protective effects after MCAO/R and associations with neurotrophic factors, mTOR-related autophagy markers, systemic inflammation, and gut microbiota phenotypes remain unclear.

METHODS: Cerebral ischemia/reperfusion injury was induced by right MCAO/R. Rats were assigned to Sham, MCAO/R, and MCAO/R + high-frequency rTMS groups. rTMS was initiated on postoperative day 3. Neurological and motor functions were assessed behaviorally. Western blotting, immunofluorescence, ELISA, and 16S rRNA sequencing were used to examine related proteins, inflammatory cytokines, and gut microbiota, followed by multivariate and correlation analyses.

RESULTS: High-frequency rTMS improved neurological and motor functions, reduced infarction and histopathological injury, decreased TUNEL positivity, and increased the number of Nissl-positive neurons. It upregulated FGF-2, BDNF, and the p-mTOR (Ser2448)/mTOR ratio, attenuated abnormal changes in Beclin-1, LC3-II/LC3-I, and p62, and reduced serum TNF-α, IL-1β, and IL-6 levels. 16S rRNA sequencing showed altered gut microbiota β-diversity and genus-level composition, with several genera associated with motor or inflammatory indices.

CONCLUSION: High-frequency rTMS alleviated cerebral ischemia/reperfusion injury and promoted neurological recovery after MCAO/R, accompanied by enhanced neurotrophic support, improvement in mTOR-related autophagy marker abnormalities, and lower serum pro-inflammatory cytokine levels. Gut microbiota alterations were also observed following rTMS treatment, although their functional significance remains exploratory.

articles.title: Genetic Modulation of ALT Leads to Underestimation of Liver Injury in Male ALDH2*2 Drinkers.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND & AIMS: Serum alanine aminotransferase (ALT) is commonly used to detect hepatocellular injury. However, genetic and metabolic factors may modulate ALT levels. We focused on the potential impact of an in-activating mutation in aldehyde dehydrogenase 2 (ALDH2*2, rs671) polymorphism, prevalent among East Asians, on ALT levels and its interaction with alcohol consumption.

METHODS: We analyzed Taiwan's Biobank data of 91,743 participants, 48.7% of whom were ALDH2*2 carriers, to assess the interaction between ALDH2 genotype, alcohol consumption and serum levels of liver enzymes. Mechanistic studies were conducted using ALDH2*2 knock-in (KI) mice exposed once to ethanol (1 g/kg), to evaluate ALT expression and serum levels, inflammation and liver injury. Integrative transcriptomic analyses, along with validation using publicly available datasets, were performed to identify transcriptional regulators of ALT.

RESULTS: Male ALDH2*1/*2 drinkers exhibited a significantly lower serum ALT levels compared to ALDH2*1/*1 drinkers, despite higher gamma-glutamyl transferase levels (p < 0.001). Following acute ethanol administration to ALDH2*1/*2 mice, serum ALT elevation remained minimal despite comparable or greater accumulation of lipid oxidation product, 4-hydroxynonenal, enhanced MAPK activation, increased chemokine expression, and markedly aggravated histological necrosis relative to ethanol-treated wildtype mice. Notably, hepatic Alt1 mRNA and ALT protein expression were significantly reduced in ethanol-treated ALDH2*1/*2 mice. Integrated ChIP-seq analysis suggested that the transcription factor Hnf4a/HNF4A may regulate Alt1/ALT1 transcription. Validation using publicly available datasets confirmed reduced hepatic ALT1 expression in early inflammatory states and in patients with alcoholic hepatitis.

CONCLUSIONS: ALDH2 deficiency blunts serum ALT elevation following alcohol exposure by limiting hepatic ALT expression. These findings underscore the importance of considering ALDH2 genotype when interpreting serum ALT levels in male drinkers and provide a rationale for further investigation of genotype-informed ALT interpretation in East Asian populations.

IMPACT AND IMPLICATIONS: We found that serum ALT levels may underestimate liver injury in alcohol-consuming individuals carrying the ALDH2*2 (inactive) allele; genetic background and environmental factors may be considered when interpreting liver injury based on serum ALT, a commonly used clinical biomarker. Since previous studies have shown that ALDH2*2 carriers are at increased risk of alcohol-related liver disease, incorporating genotype-informed clinical strategies may improve early detection and clinical outcomes. These findings are particularly important for East Asian populations, where ALDH2*2 is common.

CLINICAL TRIAL NUMBER: None.

articles.title: Spleen stiffness to rule out high-risk varices in advanced chronic liver disease: an individual patient data meta-analysis.
authors: of the Spleen Stiffness – IPD-MA Study Group; a study by the Baveno Cooperation, an EASL Consortium
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND & AIMS: Management of esophageal varices (EV) is of critical importance in compensated advanced chronic liver disease. We conducted an individual patient data (IPD) meta-analysis to (i) investigate the performance of spleen stiffness measurement (SSM)-based algorithms using vibration-controlled transient elastography (VCTE) to rule out high-risk varices (HRV); (ii) develop a new model for diagnosing any grade EV.

METHODS: We systematically searched databases for studies reporting endoscopy and SSM-VCTE data in adult patients, collecting their IPD. The main outcome was ruling out HRV. The tested algorithms were: i) Baveno-VI criteria, liver stiffness measurement (LSM) <20 kPa and platelet count (PLT) >150x109/L); ii) SSM ≤40 kPa; iii) combined Baveno-SSM criteria ≤40 kPa in patients outside Baveno VI criteria. We developed and internally validated logistic regression models to diagnose any grade EV.

RESULTS: Twenty studies comprising 2257 patients were included, with a summary HRV prevalence of 25%. The Baveno VI algorithm showed 100% (95%-CI:97-100%) sensitivity and 100% (95%-CI:95-100%) NPV; the rate of spared endoscopies was 17% (95%-CI:15-18%). The combined Baveno VI-SSM criteria performed best for ruling out HRV: 97% (95%-CI:94-99%) sensitivity, 98% (95%-CI:96-99%) NPV and rate of spared endoscopies of 35% (95%-CI: 34-38%). These results were robust in all sensitivity analyses, including patients with non-viral etiology (n=637) and studies using the 100 Hz module. We developed new logistic models with excellent accuracy for the diagnosis of EV, but the ability to identify patients at low risk (<10%) of EV was limited.

CONCLUSION: This large, multicenter, international study validated spleen stiffness measurement as an accurate tool to assess high-risk esophageal varices. The combined Baveno-SSM algorithm performed best in ruling out HRV.

IMPACT AND IMPLICATIONS: Spleen stiffness has been recommended to rule out high-risk varices, but the evidence supporting its use is of low-quality. Our individual patient data meta-analysis, which included more than 2200 patients with compensated cirrhosis, showed that spleen stiffness ≤40 kPa can rule out high-risk varices with a very low rate of false negatives. Its combination with Baveno VI criteria was the most efficient triage strategy, doubling the rate of endoscopies that could be safely avoided compared to using the Baveno VI criteria alone. The findings of our study strengthen the level of evidence supporting the use of spleen stiffness as an additional screening tool for high-risk varices.

articles.title: Acute Lymphocytic Myocarditis Complicated By Bidirectional Ventricular Tachycardia Treated With Early Steroid Use.
articles.abstract: Acute lymphocytic myocarditis can precipitate malignant ventricular arrhythmias, including the rare presentation of bidirectional ventricular tachycardia (BDVT), a rhythm associated with significant hemodynamic instability. Although BDVT is classically linked to catecholaminergic polymorphic ventricular tachycardia and digitalis toxicity, it is increasingly recognized in myocarditis, likely reflecting diffuse inflammatory involvement of the myocardium and Purkinje system. Emerging evidence suggests that early corticosteroid therapy may rapidly reduce arrhythmia burden and improve ventricular function in selected patients with active myocardial inflammation. We report the case of a 34-year-old woman who presented with palpitations and syncope and was found to have BDVT secondary to acute lymphocytic myocarditis. Despite typical medical management, she had refractory ventricular arrhythmias. Prompt initiation of corticosteroids led to marked suppression of arrhythmias and rapid recovery of left ventricular ejection fraction. While current data remain limited, this case supports the potential benefit of early immunosuppressive therapy when active lymphocytic inflammation is strongly suspected.

articles.title: Agriophyllum squarrosum oligosaccharides ameliorate inflammation and lipid accumulation in T2DM-induced MASLD via miR-155-regulated PPARγ signaling pathways.
articles.abstract:
ETHNOPHARMACOLOGICAL RELEVANCE: Agriophyllum squarrosum (L.) Moq., is a traditional medicinal herb first recorded in the "Four Medical Tantras" during the 8th century AD. It is commonly employed in Mongolian medicine for various therapeutic diseases, including the dispelling epidemics, heat clearance, detoxification, and diuresis. This herb is known to inhibit "He Yi," regulate "Ba Da Gan," and is utilized in the treatment of "Xi He Ri Xi Jing Bing" which corresponds to modern diabetes and xiaoke in traditional Chinese medicine. Agriophyllum squarrosum oligosaccharides (AOS) are recognized as major bioactive constituents, however, the molecular mechanisms underlying their therapeutic effects on type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM)-related metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD) remain unclear.

AIM OF THE STUDY: This study investigates the therapeutic effects of AOS in T2DM-MASLD and explores the underlying mechanisms involving miR-155-mediated signaling pathways.

MATERIALS AND METHODS: In vivo, db/db mice were treated with AOS, and hepatic lipid accumulation and insulin resistance were evaluated using biochemical and histological analyses. Hepatic expression of miR-155 and associated signaling proteins was observed by qRT-PCR, Western blotting, and immunohistochemistry. Exosomes derived from ATMs of db/db mice were co-cultured with AML-12 hepatocytes to investigate the role of exosomal miR-155 in MASLD progression. In vitro, inflammatory cytokine production and miR-155 expression were quantified using ELISA and qRT-PCR, while exosomal miR-155 secretion was evaluated in glucolipid-induced cellular injury models.

RESULTS: AOS treatment reduced hepatic steatosis and improved insulin resistance in db/db mice. AOS was associated with decreased hepatic miR-155 expression. Exosomal miR-155 derived from ATMs aggravated hepatocyte injury in the co-culture system, accompanied by increased expression of SREBP1c, NLRP3, and NF-κB p65. In vitro, AOS inhibited exosomal miR-155 secretion and downregulated the expression of SREBP1c, P2X7R, NF-κB p65, and inhibitor of IκBα, thus attenuating glucolipid metabolism-associated inflammatory responses and lipid dysregulation.

CONCLUSION: AOS ameliorates inflammation, hepatic lipid accumulation, and insulin resistance in T2DM-associated MASLD, possibly via suppression of miR-155 and modulation of downstream inflammatory and lipogenic signaling pathways. These results identify AOS as a promising therapeutic candidate for treating T2DM-associated MASLD.

articles.title: Di(2-ethylhexyl) phthalate (DEHP) exposure during cardiopulmonary bypass: A narrative review of human clinical evidence and future directions.
articles.abstract: BackgroundDi(2-ethylhexyl) phthalate (DEHP) is widely used as a plasticizer in polyvinyl chloride medical devices employed during cardiopulmonary bypass (CPB). Although migration from these devices and blood-storage systems has long been recognized, the human clinical evidence remains limited and methodologically heterogeneous.MethodsThis narrative review used a structured search of PubMed/MEDLINE, Scopus, and Google Scholar from database inception through 23 August 2026. Original peer-reviewed human clinical studies measuring parent DEHP or its metabolites in blood, plasma, or urine among patients undergoing CPB were eligible for the primary synthesis. Relevant mechanistic, biomaterial, transfusion-medicine, guideline, and regulatory sources were used for context.ResultsThe searches identified 237 database records; 33 duplicates were removed, and 204 unique records were screened. Thirteen full-text reports were assessed, and seven human clinical studies published between 1983 and 2025 were included. Across adult and pediatric settings, perioperative increases in parent DEHP and/or urinary or circulating metabolites were documented. The studies implicated multiple sources, including CPB components, blood-storage systems, and ancillary blood-contacting devices, but none provided complete patient-level source apportionment. DEHP-free tubing reduced, but did not eliminate, exposure. RBC washing reduced DEHP and MEHP in vitro, but a reduction in patient-level internal exposure has not been established.ConclusionHuman clinical evidence consistently demonstrates internal exposure to DEHP or its metabolites during cardiac surgery involving CPB. However, small heterogeneous cohorts, variable analytes and sampling schedules, and limited outcome follow-up preclude causal inference regarding clinical harm. Prospective multicenter studies using standardized biomonitoring and source-apportionment methods are required.

articles.title: Weight-stratified analysis of the heterogeneous effects of miniaturized cardiopulmonary bypass on perioperative outcomes in children with congenital heart disease: A retrospective cohort study.
articles.abstract: IntroductionMiniaturized cardiopulmonary bypass (CPB) circuits may reduce intraoperative transfusion in pediatric cardiac surgery, but their effects across body weight categories remain unclear. This study compared transfusion and outcomes between conventional and miniaturized CPB circuits, emphasizing weight-stratified analyses.MethodsThis retrospective study included 3,196 pediatric cardiac surgery patients (2015-2024) receiving conventional (n = 548) or miniaturized (n = 2,648) circuits. Primary outcomes were transfusion avoidance during CPB, in the ICU, and combined. Secondary outcomes included ICU length of stay, mechanical ventilation, ultrafast-track extubation, 24-h chest tube drainage (normalized to mL/kg), and hematocrit dynamics. Multivariable logistic regression and subgroup analyses were performed.ResultsMiniaturized circuits improved CPB transfusion avoidance overall (47.9% vs. 29.0%; P < 0.001), especially in children weighing 3-9 kg (all P < 0.01). ICU transfusion avoidance was lower with miniaturized circuits overall (82.1% vs. 94.5%; P < 0.001), except in the 1-2 kg subgroup. Combined avoidance was higher with miniaturized circuits across 3-9 and 12-13 kg (all P < 0.05). ICU length of stay was shorter with miniaturized circuits in most weight subgroups, whereas it was prolonged in the 2-3 kg subgroup (150 vs. 75 h; P < 0.001). Overall mean 24-h chest tube drainage was significantly lower in the miniaturized group (9.05 ± 9.10 vs. 10.82 ± 7.76 mL/kg; P < 0.001); however, stratified analysis showed a significant increase only in the 4-5 kg subgroup (14.52 ± 7.88 vs. 11.96 ± 6.69 mL/kg; P = 0.046), with no differences in other weight strata. Multivariable analysis indicated that miniaturized circuits were an independent predictor of increased ICU transfusion risk (OR 2.59; P < 0.001), whereas higher body weight was associated with reduced risk (OR 0.76 per kg; P < 0.001).ConclusionsMiniaturized CPB circuits reduce intraoperative transfusion, particularly in children weighing 3-9 kg, but are associated with higher postoperative ICU transfusion and variable effects on chest tube drainage that are weight-dependent. The net benefit appears weight-dependent. These findings underscore the need for weight-stratified circuit selection, although further prospective studies are warranted.

articles.title: The prevalence of MDR1/ABCB1 c.1930_1931delTC variant is rare in US domestic cats.
articles.journal: Journal of the American Veterinary Medical Association
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To determine the prevalence of the 2-bp deletion genetic variant (ABCB1 c.1930_1931delTC) in the feline multidrug resistance ABCB1 (previously MDR1) gene, which has been associated with sensitivity to P-glycoprotein (P-gp) substrate drugs in cats with homozygous mutations, utilizing a large population screen of genomic DNA samples from purebred and mixed-breed domestic cats in the US.

METHODS: This cross-sectional epidemiological study utilized conveniently available, unbiased, residual whole blood samples that were obtained from 12,000 US domestic cats and submitted to Idexx Laboratories between March and October 2025. Variant detection was performed with a validated dual-probe real-time PCR assay to detect 3 potential genotypes: wild type, homozygous mutant for variant allele, or heterozygous.

RESULTS: A majority of the cats tested were wild type (> 98%), while 1.5% (181 cats) had the heterozygous genotype. Only 0.025% (3 cats) were homozygous for the ABCB1 c.1930_1931delTC variant. The variant allele frequency was 0.8%.

CONCLUSIONS: This survey of domestic pet cats in the US demonstrated that the prevalence of the homozygous ABCB1 c.1930_1931delTC variant is rare.

CLINICAL RELEVANCE: The low prevalence of homozygous mutations in cats in this large-scale survey provides veterinarians confidence in prescribing products that are P-gp substrates, such as cyclosporine, loperamide, emodepside, and macrocyclic lactones (ivermectin, eprinomectin, selamectin, milbemycin oxime, and moxidectin). If concerns arise for individual cats, veterinarians can consider ABCB1 genotyping prior to administering P-gp substrates. While these results provide information on the prevalence of ABCB1 c.1930_1931delTC, future research on other known polymorphisms will help us fully understand ABCB1/MDR1 mutations in cats.

articles.title: Cross-scanner validation and time-stability analysis of STARE, a blood-free quantification tool for brain imaging with irreversible PET tracers.
articles.abstract: "Gold standard" blood-based quantification of dynamic 18F-fluorodeoxyglucose (18F-FDG) positron emission tomography (PET) data has limited practical clinical applications due to cost and complexity of data collection and analysis. We previously presented a blood-free quantification alternative, STARE (Source-to-Target Automatic Rotating Estimation), that was validated on 18F-FDG data acquired on an ECAT EXACT HR+ scanner. Here, we extend that initial work by applying STARE to within-subject data acquired with both a Siemens Biograph mCT scanner and a portable Brain Biosciences CerePET scanner. Approach: Performance was assessed by comparing regional net influx rates (Ki) estimated using STARE and the standard blood-based Patlak approach. Twenty participants underwent 60-minute brain 18F-FDG scans, on two different days, once in each scanner. The time-stability of both STARE- and Patlak-based Ki estimates was evaluated by applying each method to the first 20 (STARE only), 30, 40, and 50 minutes of data. Main results: STARE demonstrated high correlation with Patlak Ki estimates, particularly in the Biograph mCT (r = 0.82-0.93 (within-region)), with lower correlation in the CerePET (r = 0.27-0.62 (within-region)). In the Biograph dataset, STARE showed small deviations from the 60-min estimates across all evaluated durations (20 min and above), whereas deviations increased with shorter durations in CerePET data. The Patlak approach showed smaller changes across abbreviated scan durations in both datasets. Significance: STARE shows potential as a noninvasive alternative to traditional blood-based quantification of dynamic 18F-FDG PET brain data, facilitating shorter, blood-free acquisition. This advancement could make dynamic 18F-FDG PET brain imaging more accessible and comfortable for patients, potentially facilitating broader clinical adoption. &#xD.

articles.title: A harmonisation framework for multi-centre preclinical PET imaging across a national research infrastructure.
articles.abstract: Quantitative preclinical positron emission tomography (PET) imaging plays an important role in translational research, yet variability across scanners, sites, and analysis workflows remains a major barrier to robust multi-centre studies. In this work, we developed and evaluated a harmonisation framework across a national network of preclinical PET facilities. Approach. Six identical NEMA NU~4-2008 image quality phantoms were manufactured and distributed to six sites, where they were imaged using local acquisition and reconstruction protocols across multiple scanner platforms.Main Results. Substantial variability in contrast recovery, uniformity, and spill-over ratios was observed under site-specific conditions. Centralised automated re-analysis produced only minor reductions in variability, indicating that inter-user effects were relatively small, compared to site-specific protocol variations. In contrast, optimisation of reconstruction parameters led to a marked reduction in inter-scanner variability (an average of 60\% reduction across larger rods), particularly for voxel-wise maximum contrast recovery coefficients (CRC_max^vox), which are more sensitive to noise and reconstruction settings than the standard axial averaging NEMA CRC metric. Following harmonisation, the variability of CRC_max^vox approached and was lower that of conventional axial-averaged NEMA analysis (CRC_max^avg), with reductions ranging 7--33\% across the 1--5 mm rods, demonstrating improved quantitative consistency even at the voxel level.Significance. These findings show that scanner and site-specific protocol variations are the dominant factors for harmonisation in preclinical PET. By systematically evaluating acquisition, image reconstruction and analysis related sources of variability across a national network of heterogeneous preclinical PET systems, this work provides a practical framework for harmonisation. The proposed framework is conceptually aligned with clinical harmonisation initiatives such as EARL and provides a practical basis for the future development of harmonised performance ranges across preclinical scanners. This enables more reliable multi-centre studies and supports the use of quantitative, voxel-wise imaging biomarkers in translational research.

articles.title: Spatial sampling for triaxial OPM-MEG: understanding neurodevelopmental trajectory.
articles.abstract: Magnetoencephalography (MEG) measures magnetic fields generated by current flow in neural assemblies, providing a non-invasive means to track brain function. In recent years, the MEG field has been revolutionised by a new class of field sensor called an Optically Pumped Magnetometer (OPM). OPMs are small, lightweight, and allow construction of wearable and reconfigurable arrays of 'triaxial' field sensors (that measure magnetic fields along three axes simultaneously). These systems can be used to capture MEG data across the life span, from infancy to adulthood. With such multi-axis sensing arrays coming into routine use, here we aimed determine how dense a sensor array is required to adequately capture the spatial variation of neuromagnetic fields across the scalp.Approach: We simulated neuromagnetic fields based on realistic head geometries of individuals aged 15 months to 34 years. We then used two independent approaches to determine the sensor spacing required to capture the highest spatial variation of the field across the scalp surface: one method was based on spherical harmonic decomposition of neuromagnetic fields, and the other based on evaluating sensor redundancy in densely sampled arrays.Main results: Both methods agree in showing that the required sensor separation increases with age, from ~40 mm in a 1-year-old to ~55 mm in an adult.Significance: The sensor spacings obtained in our simulations represent upper bounds in the required values: separations above these bounds will not adequately capture spatial field variation; however, continuing to reduce sensor separation below these limits will continue to improve performance. These findings are important for the future development of OPM-MEG technology, particularly the construction of systems for neurodevelopmental applications.

articles.title: Spatial frequency domain imaging for assessment of skin fibrosis in systemic sclerosis: a prospective cohort study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Systemic sclerosis is an autoimmune disease with no approved skin-directed therapies. The modified Rodnan skin score (mRSS) is the standard measure of skin involvement in systemic sclerosis, but it has limitations. There is an unmet need for a non-invasive skin outcome measure that is objective, biologically anchored to dermal fibrosis, and scalable for multicentre trials. We evaluated spatial frequency domain imaging (SFDI), a wide field, non-contact optical method as a systemic sclerosis skin outcome measure.

METHODS: This single-centre, prospective, cohort study was done at the Division of Rheumatology at the Boston Medical Center (Boston, MA, USA). Eligible patients were aged 18 years or older with systemic sclerosis fulfilling the 2013 American College of Rheumatology-European League Against Rheumatism classification criteria. Control participants were people aged 18 years or older without autoimmune disease or known skin pathology. For all participants, exclusion criteria included skin malignancy, wounds or rashes at SFDI measurement sites (dorsal hands, forearms, and fingers). Participants in the pilot phase completed one study visit with SFDI, mRSS assessment, and optional forearm biopsy. In the expanded protocol phase, participants had a baseline visit, with follow-up visits once every 3 months during the first year and once every 6 months thereafter for 3 years. At each study visit, SFDI, high-frequency ultrasound, and durometry were done in all participants, and mRSS was assessed in patients with systemic sclerosis. Optional forearm biopsy and blood collection was done at baseline in consenting participants. Main analyses assessed baseline associations of SFDI parameters (diffuse reflectance [Rd] and reduced scattering coefficient [μs']) with mRSS and correlations with histological features of skin involvement in forearm biopsies (dermal fibrosis, collagen content, myofibroblast staining, epidermal and dermal thickness, and additional histological features). Linear mixed-effects models were used for associations and Spearman models for correlations. People with lived experience of systemic sclerosis were not involved in the study design.

FINDINGS: Between Oct 17, 2019, and June 18, 2025, 54 patients with systemic sclerosis and 30 healthy control participants were enrolled across the pilot and expanded protocol phases. The final analysis included 49 participants with systemic sclerosis and 25 control participants; biopsy samples were obtained from 34 participants with systemic sclerosis and 16 control participants. 38 (78%) of 49 participants with systemic sclerosis were female, 11 (22%) were male, 34 (69%) were White, and mean age was 50 years (SD 16). 20 (80%) of 25 control participants were female, five (20%) were male, 14 (56%) were White, and mean age was 49 years (SD 14). Rd and μs' were significantly lower in the systemic sclerosis cohort than in the control cohort across all mRSS strata, including sites where mRSS was 0. For each one-point increase in local mRSS there was a decrease in Rd (β=-0·0028, 95% CI -0·0050 to -0·0006; p=0·014) and μs' (β=-0·0158, 95% CI -0·0314 to -0·0003; p=0·047). SFDI correlations were weak to moderate with mRSS (r ranged from -0·38 to -0·48) and moderate with histological fibrosis (r ranged from -0·34 to -0·52).

INTERPRETATION: SFDI provides an objective, non-invasive measure of skin involvement in systemic sclerosis that aligns with established clinical, imaging, and histological assessments. These findings support its potential as a quantitative outcome measure for evaluating skin disease in systemic sclerosis, consistent with Outcome Measures in Rheumatology principles.

FUNDING: National Institutes of Health, National Scleroderma Foundation, Scleroderma Clinical Trials Consortium.

articles.title: Outcomes of hepatic artery thrombosis after paediatric liver transplantation (HEPATIC): an international, multicentre, retrospective registry study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Hepatic artery thrombosis after paediatric liver transplantation is a severe complication that can lead to acute graft failure, often requiring urgent re-transplantation. We aimed to assess the 1-year incidence of graft loss and mortality and to evaluate outcomes according to the timing of hepatic artery thrombosis and the treatment approaches in patients with hepatic artery thrombosis after paediatric liver transplantation.

METHODS: In this international, multicentre, retrospective study, the HEPATIC registry, which had 33 centres across 21 countries as of December, 2025, was used to identify patients who developed hepatic artery thrombosis at age younger than 18 years after paediatric liver transplantation between Jan 1, 2002, and Dec 31, 2021, and who either received a diagnosis of or received an intervention for hepatic artery thrombosis before Jan 1, 2023. Donor-related, recipient-related, and transplantation-related characteristics collected from local medical records were entered retrospectively into electronic case reports by participating centres, with centralised data quality control. Primary outcomes were 1-year graft loss and mortality after hepatic artery thrombosis diagnosis. The outcomes were examined based on when hepatic artery thrombosis occurred after paediatric liver transplantation (early [≤7 days] vs late [>7 days]), primary management strategy (conservative management, surgical revascularisation, endovascular therapy, or immediate listing for re-transplantation), and transplantation era (in 5-year intervals). The registry was registered with ClinicalTrials.gov, NCT05818644.

FINDINGS: Hepatic artery thrombosis occurred in 415 patients, of whom 216 (52%) were female and 199 (48%) were male, and median age was 1·7 years (IQR 0·8-6·5). Median follow-up was 50·9 months (IQR 17·0-112·6). Graft loss occurred in 180 patients by 1 month (cumulative incidence 43% [95% CI 38-48]) and 222 by 1 year (54% [49-58]); 51 patients died by 1 month (12% [9-15]) and 77 by 1 year (19% [15-22]). Surgical revascularisation was the first-line treatment approach in 195 (47%) patients. Other strategies included listing for re-transplantation in 99 (24%), conservative management in 79 (19%), and endovascular therapy in 42 (10%). Treatment approaches changed over time, with increased use of conservative management and endovascular therapy and reduced listing for re-transplantation (p<0·0001), with no accompanying change in 1-year mortality across eras (p=0·14). Early (≤7 days) hepatic artery thrombosis occurred in 282 (68%) patients and was associated with higher 1-year graft loss than late (>7 days) hepatic artery thrombosis (cumulative incidence 57% [95% CI 51-63] vs 47% [37-55], log-rank p=0·010). Surgical revascularisation was used in 167 (59%) patients and listing for re-transplantation in 66 (23%) patients with early hepatic artery thrombosis, whereas conservative management was used in 51 (38%) patients and endovascular therapy in 21 (16%) patients with late hepatic artery thrombosis; however, 1-year mortality did not differ between treatment strategies among patients with early versus late hepatic artery thrombosis.

INTERPRETATION: Hepatic artery thrombosis after paediatric liver transplantation is associated with notably high 1-year graft loss and mortality, particularly if hepatic artery thrombosis occurs within 7 days after the procedure. The management strategies for hepatic artery thrombosis differ according to the post-transplantation timing of hepatic artery thrombosis occurrence. Despite changes in management over the past 20 years, outcomes have remained poor, underscoring the need to improve therapeutic strategies for this complication.

FUNDING: None.

articles.title: Paediatric liver transplantation: the risk of hepatic artery thrombosis.
Endovascular treatment for ischemic stroke due to distal medium vessel occlusions: A nationwide multicenter registry.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The effectiveness and safety of endovascular treatment (EVT) for acute ischemic stroke attributable to distal medium vessel occlusion (DMVO) remain uncertain. This study aimed to compare the effectiveness and safety of EVT plus standard medical treatment (SMT) versus SMT alone in patients with DMVO.

METHODS: This nationwide multicenter registry included patients with DMVO presenting within 24 h of last known well at 116 sites in China between 2023 and 2025. The primary outcome was freedom from disability (modified Rankin Scale score of 0-1) at 90 days. Safety outcomes included symptomatic intracranial hemorrhage (sICH) within 48 h and 90-day mortality. The primary analysis was conducted using inverse probability of treatment weighting.

FINDINGS: Among 2,524 patients, 1,564 received EVT plus SMT, and 960 received SMT alone. EVT plus SMT was associated with a higher rate of freedom from disability at 90 days compared with SMT alone (adjusted risk ratio [aRR], 1.15; 95% confidence interval [CI], 1.02-1.29; adjusted risk difference, 4.36%; 95% CI, 1.73%-6.99%). However, EVT plus SMT was associated with an increased risk of sICH (aRR, 4.03; 95% CI, 2.46-6.59). Mortality at 90 days did not differ significantly between the groups (aRR, 0.97; 95% CI, 0.81-1.16).

CONCLUSIONS: In patients with DMVO, EVT plus SMT was associated with a modestly higher rate of freedom from disability at 90 days but an increased risk of sICH.

FUNDING: National Natural Science Foundation of China (82425021, 82571498, and 82271349), Natural Science Foundation of Chongqing (CSTB2024NSCQ-MSX0359 and CSTB2024NSCQ-KJFZMSX0063), and Chongqing Technology Innovation and Application Development Project (CSTB2022TIAD-KPX0160).

articles.title: The Effects of Age on the Presence of Atypical Corneal Nerve Formations.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: The aim of this study was to describe the presence of atypical nerve formations (ANFs, previously termed microneuromas) and their relation to standardized ocular surface parameters and changes in the sub-basal nerve plexus in a group of patients with suspected small fiber neuropathy or type 1 diabetes referred for in vivo confocal microscopy (IVCM).

METHODS: This retrospective single-center study enrolled 143 patients (286 eyes) referred for corneal nerve morphology evaluation between 2019 and 2024. Patients with severe dry eye disease, a history of ocular surgery, or recent eye drop use were excluded. All participants underwent comprehensive ocular surface assessment, including OSDI, Cochet-Bonnet esthesiometry, tear break-up time (TBUT), Oxford grading, tear osmolarity, and tear metalloproteinase-9 (MMP-9) concentration. IVCM was performed to obtain corneal nerve fiber metrics (corneal nerve fiber length, corneal nerve fiber density, corneal nerve branch density) and to manually identify ANFs. Generalized estimating equations were used to account for intereye correlation.

RESULTS: Corneal ANFs were identified in 25.5% of the 286 eyes. Age demonstrated a statistically significant association with ANF presence, with the odds increasing by approximately 5% for each additional year of age (odds ratio 1.05; P < 0.001). A statistically significant inverse association was observed with corneal sensitivity (P = 0.040). No statistically significant correlations were found between ANFs and TBUT, tear osmolarity, MMP-9 concentrations, OSDI scores, or standard IVCM metrics.

CONCLUSIONS: Corneal ANFs seem to be strongly associated with aging, suggesting that they may represent age-related degenerative remodeling rather than specific biomarkers for ocular neuropathic pain or inflammation in this population and, as such, should be interpreted with caution and within the broader clinical context.

articles.title: Neurodevelopmental risk in a referred sample of hospitalized children with congenital heart disease: interrelation between communication and feeding vulnerabilities.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To determine the prevalence of communication developmental risk in hospitalized children with Congenital Heart Disease (CHD) and to identify clinical, surgical, and hospitalization-related factors independently associated with increased risk.

METHODS: This cross-sectional observational study was conducted at a tertiary pediatric cardiac center between September 2024 and April 2025. Sixty-five children referred for speech-language pathology assessment underwent communication development screening using a structured developmental observation protocol. Functional feeding status was assessed using the Pediatric Functional Oral Intake Scale. Multivariable logistic regression was used to identify factors independently associated with communication developmental risk, with Firth's penalized logistic regression performed as a sensitivity analysis given the low events-per-variable ratio.

RESULTS: Twenty-five children (38%) were classified as being at risk for delayed communication development. Hospitalization in a ward setting, compared with intensive care, was independently associated with lower odds of risk classification (adjusted OR = 0.13, 95% CI 0.02‒0.77, p = 0.025), an association confirmed by the Firth sensitivity analysis (adjusted OR = 0.18, 95% CI 0.03‒0.80, p = 0.024). Length of hospital stay, cyanotic physiology, cardiopulmonary bypass duration, and aortic cross-clamp time were not independently associated with risk. Children classified as at risk also showed significantly greater feeding restrictions.

CONCLUSION: Communication developmental risk was common among hospitalized children with CHD. Hospitalization setting and feeding performance, rather than traditional markers of clinical severity, were associated with communication risk, suggesting a multifactorial model that integrates biological, functional, and environmental factors. These findings suggest that feeding function, alongside hospitalization setting, may help flag children at higher developmental risk before formal communication assessment is available. These exploratory findings support incorporating structured developmental surveillance into routine pediatric cardiac care.

articles.title: Earlier onset of type 2 diabetes mellitus as a risk factor for Irvine-Gass syndrome.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: To investigate the association between age at type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) onset and the risk of Irvine-Gass Syndrome (IGS) following uneventful phacoemulsification with intraocular lens implantation (PEI).

METHODS: This retrospective case-control study analyzed 190 participants (39 IGS, 151 non-IGS) who underwent uneventful PEI. Comprehensive demographic, systemic, and perioperative data were collected. Statistical analyses included between-group comparisons, logistic regression, and Receiver Operating Characteristic (ROC) curve analysis to identify independent IGS predictors and determine optimal risk-stratification thresholds.

RESULTS: While overall T2DM prevalence was comparable between groups (p = 0.168), IGS patients had significantly earlier diabetes onset (49.05±8.61 vs. 59.23±10.65 years, p < 0.001). Multivariable analysis confirmed younger T2DM onset age as an independent IGS predictor (OR = 1.094 per year decrease, 95% Confidence Interval [95% CI 1.015‒1.179], p = 0.019). ROC analysis identified T2DM onset age ≤ 55.5-years as the optimal predictive threshold (Area Under the ROC Curve [AUROC = 0.774], sensitivity = 73.7%, specificity = 78.9%). Participants stratified by this threshold showed significantly different IGS incidence (non-diabetic: 15.32%; younger-onset T2DM: 56.67%; older-onset T2DM: 10.20%; p < 0.001). Younger-onset T2DM patients had approximately 5.5-fold higher IGS odds versus non-diabetics (adjusted OR = 5.499, 95% CI 2.104‒14.373, p = 0.001).

CONCLUSIONS: Earlier T2DM onset (≤ 55.5-years) is a strong independent risk factor for IGS following uneventful PEI. This threshold provides a clinically useful tool for preoperative risk stratification, particularly valuable for identifying high-risk diabetic patients who may benefit from enhanced perioperative monitoring and management.

articles.title: Practical validation of synthetic pre-crash scenarios.
articles.abstract: The representativeness of synthetic pre-crash scenarios is crucial for assessing the safety impact of Driving Automation Systems through virtual simulations. However, a gap remains in the robust evaluation of synthetic pre-crash scenarios' practical equivalence to their real-world counterparts; that is, whether they are similar enough for the intended assessment purpose. Conventional significance testing is inadequate, as it focuses on detecting differences rather than establishing practical equivalence. This study addresses the research gap by extending our previous work on a Bayesian Region of Practical Equivalence (ROPE)-based equivalence testing framework by introducing a binning-based approach to define appropriate statistics and equivalence criteria. Two novel binning-based statistics are proposed to quantify localized and aggregate distributional discrepancies between synthetic and reference datasets. The statistics incorporate bin weights derived from system re-simulation outcomes, enabling discrepancies in regions with greater influence on safety-impact estimates to be emphasized. The proposed approach further provides diagnostic insight into the distributional regions driving non-equivalence, facilitating targeted dataset generation and improvements. The framework's applicability is demonstrated through a case study, which tests the practical equivalence of two synthetic rear-end pre-crash datasets with a previously developed reference dataset for the safety impact assessment of an Automatic Emergency Braking system. The results show that the framework provides informative assessments of practical equivalence and diagnostic insights into the divergence of datasets. Although the demonstration focuses on rear-end pre-crash scenarios, the framework is generic and extensible to broader validation contexts, providing an interpretable and principled basis for practical equivalence assessment across diverse synthetic data applications.

articles.title: Safety risks in Advanced driver Assistance Systems (ADAS): A systematic review of causation and analysis methodologies.
articles.abstract: Advanced Driver Assistance Systems (ADAS) have achieved rapid technological advancement, yet their widespread adoption has introduced new and multifaceted safety challenges. This review provides a systematic synthesis of ADAS-related accident scenarios and risk factors. Based on multinational accident databases and detailed crash reports, collision types are classified into three major categories: vehicle-to-vehicle, vehicle-to-pedestrian, and vehicle-to-non-motorized interactions. The underlying causes of these accidents are traced to sensor performance degradation under adverse weather, algorithmic limitations in dynamic traffic environments, and excessive driver dependence on automated functions. Furthermore, this review examines mainstream analytical approaches, including statistical modeling, system-theoretic frameworks, and AI-driven techniques, and evaluates their applicability in risk identification and mitigation. Finally, a forward-looking framework is proposed to advance multi-sensor data fusion and privacy-preserving governance, strengthen dynamic scene modeling and open scenario databases, and incorporate human factors into causal inference for proactive risk management. The findings are expected to enrich the methodological foundation of ADAS accident analysis and support future improvements in intelligent vehicle safety.

articles.title: Effect of upstream sequence modifications in pET vectors on the yield of recombinant proteins.
articles.abstract: Increasing the yield of recombinant proteins can save time and materials and, consequently, any strategy that seems promising for achieving this objective is worth investigating. Lately, it has been proposed that modifications of upstream sequences from pET vectors would enhance the transcription efficiency. To validate this approach, we expressed a pool of constructs in modified pET vectors and compared the yields with those obtained using unmodified pET-derived vectors. Constructs were selected according to their different structural properties and protein yields. In our experimental setting, the results were generally deceiving. However, improvements were observed when additional elements of the construct were optimized concurrently. In particular, repositioning the His-tag from the C-terminus to the N-terminus positively affected the final protein yield. Taken together, these findings indicate that the modified vectors developed in this study represent one of several factors to consider during the initial screening aimed at identifying optimal expression conditions for a new construct, rather than a broadly applicable solution for enhancing the yield of any protein construct.

articles.title: Airborne microplastics and associated heavy metal contamination in indoor and outdoor environments: Pollution levels and health risks in Metro Manila, Philippines.
articles.abstract: Airborne microplastics (MPs) have emerged as environmental pollutants that can co-occur with hazardous contaminants; however, evidence of heavy-metal associations with atmospheric MPs remains limited. This study investigated the abundance, characteristics, metal loadings, and health risks of airborne MPs in Metro Manila, Philippines. Air samples were collected from classroom, laboratory, dining room, office, living room, and store environments, followed by polymer identification via μFTIR and metal quantification using ICP-MS. MP concentrations ranged from 0.074 to 0.595 MP/m3 indoors (mean: 0.297 ± 0.20 MP/m3) and from 0.057 to 0.262 MP/m3 outdoors (mean: 0.173 ± 0.07 MP/m3), with no statistically significant difference. Fibers dominated the MP assemblage (52.38%), followed by fragments and films. PP, PET, and PE were the most prevalent polymers. Heavy metal concentrations ranged from 0.35 to 27521.66 mg/kg indoors and from 0.11 to 30556 mg/kg outdoors, with notable contributions from Zn, Cu, Ba, Pb, and Ag. These showed site-specific variations associated with room function and anthropogenic activity, with elevated Cu and Zn in high-activity indoor spaces. Pollution indices (PLI, MPI) indicated moderate pollution levels, while the ecological risk index indicated moderate ecological risk. Spearman analysis showed strong positive correlations between MPI-HM and As, Fe, and Zn (r = 0.70, p < 0.05), while PCA and HCA differentiated sampling sites by metal- and MP-related profiles. Inhalation risk assessment indicated low-to-moderate non-carcinogenic risk; however, the co-occurrence of toxic metals with respirable MPs highlights the occurrence of hazardous substances within the recovered airborne MP fraction. This study provides one of the first assessments of heavy metals associated with airborne MPs in indoor-outdoor urban environments.

articles.title: Machine learning-based prediction of hospital-acquired malnutrition at discharge using the GLIM criteria: A multicenter real-world study.
articles.abstract:
