OBJECTIVE: This study aimed to investigate the incidence and clinical impact of hospital-acquired malnutrition (HAM) and develop a machine learning model for early risk prediction.

METHODS: This secondary analysis included prospectively collected data from a multicenter observational study involving 34 tertiary hospitals in China. Adult patients hospitalized for 7 to 30 days were enrolled. Patients without malnutrition at admission were evaluated for HAM at discharge according to the Global Leadership Initiative on Malnutrition (GLIM) criteria. Machine learning models were developed using clinical and nutritional variables available at admission, and model performance was evaluated using discrimination, calibration, and clinical utility analyses.

RESULTS: Among 4746 hospitalized patients, 1364 (28.7%) had malnutrition at admission. Of the 3382 patients without baseline malnutrition, 731 (21.6%) developed HAM during hospitalization. Patients with HAM had significantly higher rates of hospital-acquired complications (9.0% versus 2.9%), longer hospital stays (14.93 versus 13.53 days), and higher healthcare costs (¥48 980 versus ¥20 640) compared with those without HAM (all P < 0.001). Male sex, older age, pre-admission weight loss, reduced calf circumference, decreased handgrip strength, reduced muscle mass phenotype according to GLIM, and malignant tumors were associated with HAM. The XGBoost model demonstrated the best predictive performance, achieving an area under the receiver operating characteristic curve of 0.882 (95% CI: 0.857-0.906) in the independent test set.

CONCLUSIONS: HAM is common among hospitalized patients without malnutrition at admission, and the developed machine learning model may enable early identification of high-risk patients for timely nutritional intervention.

articles.title: Estimating the eligible population for amyloid-targeting monoclonal antibody therapy in memory clinics: Application to lecanemab in France.
articles.journal: The journal of prevention of Alzheimer's disease
articles.abstract: Lecanemab was the first amyloid-targeting monoclonal antibody approved by the European Commission for treating patients with mild cognitive impairment (MCI) and mild dementia due to Alzheimer's disease (AD). While this marketing authorization led to heterogeneous situations across European countries, France declined reimbursement, citing limited clinical benefit and concerns about the healthcare system's capacity to implement this new care pathway. This capacity depends directly on the number of eligible patients, yet robust estimates remain limited and highly variable across studies. Our objective was therefore to estimate the population eligible for lecanemab in France. Using transportability methods based on inverse odds of selection weighting, we articulated the nationwide consultation data from the French National Alzheimer Database (BNA) with the deeply phenotyped MEMENTO clinical cohort. Eligibility for lecanemab followed the French appropriate use recommendations: 1) clinical eligibility (age 50-90 years, MCI with common AD phenotype or mild AD dementia, MMSE ≥22), 2) biological eligibility (amyloid confirmation determined sequentially using plasma p-tau217, cerebrospinal fluid biomarkers and amyloid-PET), 3) absence of contraindications (APOEε4 homozygosity, anticoagulant use, MRI risk markers for ARIA). Among patients consulting French memory clinics, 19.5% met clinical eligibility criteria. Of these, 73.0% (95%CI: 67.6-77.9) were amyloid-positive, and 49.7% (95%CI: 44.0-55.5) remained eligible after applying safety criteria. Overall, 9.7% (95%CI: 8.6-10.8) of patients consulting memory clinics were estimated to be eligible for lecanemab, representing approximately 18,200 individuals nationally (annual average, 2022-2024). These results inform healthcare planning for disease-modifying therapy implementation in France and comparable countries.

articles.title: Antimicrobial resistance and antibiotic therapy in patients with urinary tract infections and asymptomatic bacteriuria: A Peruvian perspective.
articles.abstract: Overdiagnosis and overtreatment of urinary tract infections (UTIs) and asymptomatic bacteriuria (AB) increase antimicrobial resistance. The aim of this study was to evaluate resistance patterns and antibiotic therapy in patients with UTIs and AB in Peru. Cross-sectional study based on 164 urine cultures and antimicrobial susceptibility testing. A total of 62 cases of AB and 102 of UTI were identified. Women (116, 70.7%) and older adults (60, 36.6%) predominated. A total of 4582 antibiotic prescriptions were recorded, with a therapeutic pattern in both UTI and AB centered on the use of meropenem (540, 21.3%) and (333, 16.3%), vancomycin (221, 8.7%) and (454, 22.2%), ceftriaxone (369, 14.5%) and (176, 8.6%) and ceftazidime (227, 8.9%) and (274, 3.4%), respectively. In general, antibiotic therapy was bactericidal in (87, 53.0%) cases, from the surveillance group in (98, 59.8%) cases, monotherapy in (112, 68.3%) cases, and in cycles of ≤7 days. UTI was associated with a higher burden of comorbidities, including chronic renal failure, hypertension, and diabetes. Fifteen bacterial species were isolated in both clinical entities, with a predominance of Gram-negative bacilli, mainly Escherichia coli and Klebsiella pneumoniae, both of which exhibited high resistance to cephalosporins, sulfonamides, and ampicillin/sulbactam. Among Gram-positive bacteria, Enterococcus faecalis and E. faecium showed resistance to erythromycin, tetracycline, and quinolones. The widespread use of antibiotics from the surveillance group and similar antibiotic therapy in AB and UTI, revealed a critical gap in the implementation of clinical guidelines and the urgent need to accurately differentiate between the two diagnoses to avoid overprescribing and help contain bacterial resistance.

articles.title: Surgical management of presternal recurrence in hyperparathyroidism related to chronic kidney disease.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To evaluate the surgical management and outcomes of recurrence localized in presternal autografts after total parathyroidectomy with autograft for hyperparathyroidism related to chronic kidney disease.

METHODS: A retrospective cohort study was conducted including patients submitted to total parathyroidectomy with presternal autograft between 2000 and 2024 who developed biochemical recurrence according to Brazilian Society of Nephrology criteria and required reoperation. Only cases occurring more than six months after an initially effective surgery were included. The primary outcome was sustained biochemical resolution.

RESULTS: Twenty-four patients required reoperation due to recurrence in the presternal autograft. All were on hemodialysis at initial surgery. Mean CKD duration was 96-months and mean preoperative PTH level was 1445.4 pg/mL. Thirty-one reoperations were performed; most patients (87.5%) required only one procedure. The mean interval between initial surgery and first graft reoperation was 62.6-months. No invasive growth beyond anatomical limits was observed. Mean intraoperative PTH reduction was 80.8%. Considerable variability was observed between intraoperative PTH reduction and subsequent clinical outcomes. Total graft removal was feasible when indicated.

CONCLUSION: Reoperation for recurrence in presternal autografts was feasible in this series and was associated with satisfactory biochemical control, even in patients requiring multiple procedures. The anatomical characteristics of the presternal region allowed controlled resections without evidence of invasive growth beyond the graft bed.

articles.title: What every intensivist should know about dynamic left ventricular outflow tract obstruction.
articles.abstract: Dynamic left ventricular outflow tract obstruction (LVOTO) is an underrecognized, load dependent cause of hemodynamic instability in critically ill patients. Although classically associated with hypertrophic cardiomyopathy, it frequently occurs in the ICU in settings such as septic shock, hypovolemia, postoperative states, and right ventricular failure. Standard shock therapies, including inotropes and afterload reduction, may paradoxically worsen obstruction and lead to escalating hemodynamic instability. Bedside echocardiography is central to diagnosis, typically revealing a small hyperdynamic left ventricle and a late-peaking Doppler profile. Management focuses on restoring preload, increasing afterload, and reducing excessive contractility. In some patients, LVOTO is secondary to right ventricular failure, requiring targeted right ventricular support. Dynamic LVOTO is a reversible and often iatrogenic cause of shock. Early recognition and physiology-guided management can rapidly improve hemodynamics and prevent harmful therapeutic escalation.

articles.title: Advancing early detection of Alzheimer's disease: from established biomarkers to future innovations.
articles.abstract: Alzheimer's disease (AD) is a major form of dementia, imposes an escalating global burden on public health and social care. Pathological changes in AD occur years before clinical symptoms, defining a prolonged preclinical phase. Currently, there is no effective treatment exist for late-stage AD, making early diagnosis and intervention indispensable, in which biomarkers play a pivotal role. While cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) and positron emission tomography (PET) biomarkers improved AD diagnostic accuracy, their clinical application is limited by invasiveness, high costs. Advances in ultrasensitive immunoassay technologies has rendered peripheral blood biomarkers easily accessible, cost-effective, minimally invasive, and suitable for continuous monitoring, offering noval opportunities for AD screening, diagnosis and progression tracking. Additionally, non-invasive body fluids including saliva, urine and tears are being explored as potential biomarkers. Artificial intelligence (AI)-driven multimodal fusion, integrated with large-scale multimodal computing frameworks, significantly improve the accuracy of early AD diagnosis. Recent studies have identified a series of promising synaptic and neuronal biomarkers, such as neurofilament light chain (NFL), neurogranin (Ng), β-secretase 1 (BACE1) and synaptosomal-associated protein 25 (SNAP-25). Inflammatory mediators and genetic factors also contribute to AD pathological evaluation. This review systematically characterizes biomarker profiles of emerging non-invasive carriers (saliva, urine and tears). It further synthesizes cohort-derived quantitative diagnostic metrics (AUC, sensitivity, specificity) of multimodal AD biomarkers and conducts head-to-head comparison to clarify their respective strengths and translational limitations, aiming to provide evidence-based insights for optimizing early AD screening and diagnostic strategies.

articles.title: Selective CB2 receptor activation attenuates neuroinflammation and preserves immune responsiveness after photothrombotic stroke.
articles.abstract: Ischemic stroke triggers neuroinflammation that can drive CNS injury-induced immunodepression syndrome (CIDS), a peripheral immunosuppressive state associated with increased infection risk. The endocannabinoid system, particularly cannabinoid receptor type 2 (CB2), represents a promising immunomodulatory target because of its anti-inflammatory actions and limited psychoactive liability. In this study, we investigated whether CB2 receptor activation confers neuroprotection and preserves systemic immune responsiveness in a murine photothrombotic stroke (PTS) model. Male C57BL/6 mice underwent PTS or sham surgery and were treated before stroke induction with the non-selective CB1/CB2 agonist WIN-55212, receptor antagonists, the selective CB2 agonist HU-308, or vehicle. Neurological deficits, infarct volume, cerebral inflammatory gene expression, and intestinal leukocyte-endothelial interactions following lipopolysaccharide (LPS) challenge were assessed using Neuroscore, TTC staining, RT-qPCR, and intravital microscopy. SIM-A9 microglia were used to evaluate the effects of HU-308 on viability and cytokine release under inflammatory conditions. PTS induced a CIDS-like phenotype characterized by reduced baseline leukocyte rolling and a markedly blunted leukocyte adhesion response following LPS challenge. Non-selective cannabinoid receptor activation improved neurological scores and reduced infarct size, while CB2 blockade abolished this protection. Selective CB2 activation with HU-308 reduced infarct volume, improved neurological outcome, and suppressed stroke-associated TNF and IL-6 expression in the ischemic hemisphere. In vitro, HU-308 reduced TNF release from LPS-stimulated microglia, while IL-4 enhanced microglial viability and IL-10 production. Importantly, HU-308 preserved leukocyte adhesion after LPS challenge following stroke, suggesting maintained peripheral immune responsiveness. These findings identify CB2 receptor activation as a promising neuroimmune strategy that limits acute stroke injury while attenuating the development of CIDS.

articles.title: Exploratory Analysis of the Innate Immune System in Aortic Stenosis Patients With and Without ASCVD.
articles.abstract: Calcific aortic valve disease (CAVD) leads to aortic stenosis (AS) through inflammation and fibro-calcific remodeling. Although CAVD and atherosclerosis share features, not all patients with AS develop atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease (ASCVD), suggesting mechanistic heterogeneity. This case-control study evaluated inflammatory profiles and valvular remodeling in 128 patients with AS (59.4% with ASCVD) and 105 controls. Immune cell composition and monocyte markers were analyzed by flow cytometry, whereas cytokine production was assessed after peripheral blood mononuclear cell (PBMC) stimulation. Both AS groups had higher interleukin (IL)-6, leukocyte, monocyte, and neutrophil counts than controls, with lower monocyte human leukocyte antigen-DR isotype and higher C-C chemokine receptor (CCR)2 expression. Cytokine responses were also elevated, particularly in AS patients with ASCVD. They also showed higher IL-6 concentrations, higher proportions of classical monocytes, and lower intermediate and non-classical monocytes compared with patients without ASCVD. Overall, AS was associated with a pro-inflammatory monocyte phenotype and function, most prominently in patients with ASCVD. ClinicalTrials.gov ID: NCT04717219.

articles.title: Nox4 Mediates Diastolic Function in a Genetic Model of Pitx2 Haploinsufficiency.
articles.journal: Canadian journal of physiology and pharmacology
articles.abstract: Heart failure with preserved ejection fraction (HFpEF) commonly coexists with atrial fibrillation (AF), but shared mechanisms remain unclear. In this study, we hypothesized that Pitx2, a transcription factor located near the strongest genetic locus associated with AF in humans, increases susceptibility to HFpEF-like remodeling. We also sought to understand pathways that might be central to this increased risk. Male and female Pitx2+/- mice and wild-type littermates received 3-week subcutaneous osmotic pump infusion of saline or angiotensin II (Ang II; 500 ng/kg/min). Cardiac structure and function were assessed by echocardiography and catheterization, and functional capacity by exercise treadmill. RNA transcriptomic profiling was performed to identify candidate pathways. In a separate cohort, Ang II-treated mice were randomized to oral GKT136901 (30 mg/kg/day) or vehicle during infusion. After Ang II infusion, Pitx2+/- mice developed exaggerated HFpEF-like changes, including greater left ventricular hypertrophy, left atrial enlargement, diastolic dysfunction, elevated left ventricular end-diastolic pressure, and reduced treadmill performance. RNA-seq showed enrichment of metabolic and stress-response pathways with selective upregulation of Nox4, confirmed by RT-qPCR. GKT136901 attenuated structural remodeling, diastolic dysfunction indices, elevated filling pressures, and cardiomyocyte hypertrophy, but did not improve endurance. These findings implicate redox signaling, including Nox4, in AF genetic susceptibility-HFpEF interactions.

articles.title: SGLT2-mediated glucose uptake defines early metabolic reprogramming in lung adenocarcinoma.
articles.abstract: The metabolic reprogramming taking place during early lung adenocarcinoma (LUAD) progression remain poorly understood. While early-stage LUAD frequently demonstrates low 18F-2-fluorodeoxyglucose (18FDG) uptake on positron emission tomography (PET), it is unclear whether this reflects metabolic quiescence or alternative glucose utilization pathways. We hypothesized that early lesions are metabolically active but preferentially utilize sodium-glucose cotransporter 2 (SGLT2), a non-canonical glucose transporter with low 18FDG affinity. This study investigates metabolic activity in early-stage LUAD and glucose transporter expression patterns across the adenocarcinoma spectrum. LDH, SGLT2 and GLUT1 expression were evaluated by immunohistochemistry in human lung cancers and compared with normal lung and benign inflammation. Expression levels were correlated with structural and radiologic features including tumor size, invasion, histology, radiographic features and PET avidity. Glycolysis was elevated in premalignant and early LUAD as indicated by LDH expression. SGLT2 was highly expressed in preinvasive and minimally invasive LUAD compared to normal lung and invasive tumors. Conversely, GLUT1 was upregulated in invasive, high-grade tumors. Radiographically, SGLT2 expression was associated with subsolid nodules and low PET avidity, while GLUT1 expression was higher in nodules with a solid component and high 18FDG avidity. Notably, SGLT2 was not elevated in inflammatory lesions compared to normal lung, unlike GLUT1, which was frequently upregulated in inflammation. Early lung adenocarcinoma lesions exhibit aerobic glycolysis despite low FDG avidity and preferentially utilize SGLT2-mediated glucose uptake. These findings highlight a distinct metabolic profile in early LUAD and underscore the need for alternative imaging modalities to enhance the detection of early lesions.

articles.title: Impact of HIV on Perioperative Organ Injury and Surgical Outcomes in 41 Million Surgical Patients: A Retrospective Cohort Study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: While antiretroviral therapy has improved surgical safety for people living with HIV, comprehensive data on perioperative organ injury and its impact on patient safety remain limited. This study aimed to compare the incidence of perioperative organ injury, in-hospital mortality, hospital length of stay, and hospitalization costs between people living with HIV and HIV-negative individuals undergoing surgery in the United States.

METHODS: This retrospective cohort study used data from the National Inpatient Sample (NIS) from 2016 to 2021. The population-based sample included adult patients (age >18 years) identified via International Classification of Diseases, Tenth Revision, Clinical Modification (ICD-10-CM) codes. Of 41,622,004 eligible surgical admissions, 2,088,307 (5.0%) were people living with HIV and 39,533,697 were HIV-negative. Primary outcomes were perioperative organ injury incidence and associated mortality; secondary outcomes included hospital length of stay and total hospital charges. Adjusted models accounted for baseline characteristics and surgical complexity.

RESULTS: Among the 41,622,004 surgical admissions, people living with HIV were found to be older and carried a significantly higher comorbidity burden, with a Charlson Comorbidity Index of 8 compared to 1 in the HIV-negative group. Perioperative organ injury occurred in 1,348,363 of 2,088,307 people living with HIV (64.6%) compared with 7,867,547 of 39,533,697 HIV-negative patients (19.9%). Acute myocardial infarction (33.5%) and acute kidney injury (22.0%) were the most common injuries among people living with HIV. In-hospital mortality occurred in 66,935 of 2,088,307 people living with HIV (3.2%) compared with 872,170 of 39,533,697 HIV-negative patients (2.2%). Hospital length of stay and hospital charges were also significantly higher. Adjusted analyses demonstrated that HIV status was independently associated with higher in-hospital mortality (odds ratio [OR], 1.66; 95% confidence interval [CI], 1.54-1.78), longer hospital length of stay (β = 2.73 days; 95% CI, 2.56-2.90), a decreased likelihood of home discharge (hazard ratio [HR], 0.73; 95% CI, 0.72-0.73), and increased hospitalization costs (β = $18,423; 95% CI, 16,712-20,134). Sensitivity analyses demonstrated that elevated perioperative risk persisted among patients with asymptomatic HIV infection, although the greatest risk was observed among patients with symptomatic HIV disease/AIDS.

CONCLUSIONS: People living with HIV incur a significantly higher risk of perioperative organ injury and worse surgical outcomes despite advances in antiretroviral therapy. HIV status was independently associated with adverse perioperative outcomes in adjusted models, supporting its inclusion as a risk stratification variable in surgical planning. Future research should incorporate immunologic markers, such as CD4 count and viral load, to further refine perioperative risk prediction and optimize outcomes for this population.

articles.title: Pulse pressure in heart failure - easy to assess, not so easy to understand.
Evaluating the Role of Lower Extremity Elastic Bandage in Patients with Acute Decompensated Heart Failure.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Lower extremity compression therapy has been proposed as an adjunct to mitigate diuretic resistance during acute decompensation of heart failure (ADHF). We evaluated the effect of lower leg compression with elastic bandages on diuretic efficiency in patients with diuretic-resistant ADHF.

METHODS: Historical cohort study enrolling adult cardiac ICU admissions with ADHF who used elastic bandages (EB) at Mayo Clinic in Minnesota from 2007 to 2017. The diuretic efficiency before and after applying EB was the primary outcome.

RESULTS: A total of 176 patients with heart failure who received elastic bandages were included. The in-hospital mortality rate, the median hospital length of stay, and 30-day hospital readmission were 9.7%, 11.4 days (IQR 7.1-19.0), and 11%, respectively. When EB was applied, the average daily loop diuretic dosage was decreased by a mean difference of 1.19 mg per 40 mg furosemide equivalent (95% CI: 0.22 to 2.2; p = 0.016). The average post-EB diuretic efficiency was 1,355 mL (IQR 1,119, 1,590) per 40-mg furosemide, which was significantly higher than before EB application, with a mean difference of 340 mL per 40-mg furosemide equivalent (95% CI: -554, -125; p = 0.002). A higher diuretic efficiency led to lower diuretic doses. Average daily urine output before and after EB application was not different (2,642 pre-EB vs. 2,792 post-EB mL/day; 95% CI: -455 to 154; p = 0.33).

CONCLUSION: EB use enhances diuretic efficacy during ADHF. Further studies are needed to determine the potential clinical benefits and risks of applying EB compression treatment in ADHF.

articles.title: Practical Application of the AO Spine Primary Infection Classification System: Clarifying Definitions, Borderline Cases and Common Misinterpretations.
articles.abstract: Study DesignNarrative review.ObjectiveTo clarify nuances when applying the AO Spine Primary Infection Classification.MethodsThe international validation of the AO Spine Primary Infection Classification System was successful but recurring themes caused confusion. This included the exact definition and reasons for infections to transition between categories, definition of canal involvement or neural compression and whether an epidural infection superimposed on degenerative disease escalates infection severity. There was uncertainty regarding handling of multi-level or junctional infection and clinicians encountered difficulty applying the modifiers.ResultsThe difference between a Type 0 and Type 1 infection is reasonably distinct given the former is purely extraspinal whilst the latter involves spondylodiscitis or osteomyelitis without canal involvement. Type 2 infections include those with any canal involvement, regardless of whether CSF effacement occurs, in the absence of neural compression. The spinal canal is defined as the compartment dorsal to the posterior longitudinal ligament and excludes infections that are ventral to this ligament but bow into the canal. Any neural compression of the thecal sac centrally or within the foramen escalates categorization to a Type 3 infection.ConclusionsPrimary spinal infections have the potential to rapidly progress and cause devastating neurological deficits. The introduction of the AO Spine Primary Infection Classification establishes a universal language to communicate disease severity. We clarify common nuances encountered during international validation of this system including definition of canal involvement and relevance of CSF effacement, whether foraminal involvement constitutes neural compression and the nomenclature concerning multi-level or junctional disease.

articles.title: In-patient evolution can heterogeneously impact biofilm formation and intraosteoblastic behavior of Staphylococcus aureus in relapsing bone and joint infections.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Bone and joint infections caused by Staphylococcus aureus are notoriously difficult to manage and are prone to relapse, often leading to serious clinical complications. Treatment failure is frequently attributed to bacterial persistence mechanisms, notably biofilm formation and intracellular survival within osteoblasts.

METHODS: To elucidate the underlying causes of relapse, we analyzed 25 relapse pairs, each consisting of an isolate collected during the initial infection and a corresponding isolate obtained at relapse from the same patient. We investigated mutation acquisition in relapse strain during host in-patient stay and assessed their phenotypic consequences, focusing on bacterial growth, biofilm formation, internalization into osteoblasts, intracellular persistence, and cytotoxicity.

RESULTS: Whole-genome comparisons revealed that most relapse strains accumulated mutations during the host in-patient stay, with mutation counts ranging from 0 to 391. These genetic changes variably affected key phenotypes across the relapse strains. Specifically, growth kinetics, biofilm-forming capacity, and intracellular behavior exhibited heterogeneity when compared to initial strains. Integrative analysis of genomic and phenotypic data indicates that mutations in genes involved in virulence regulation and metabolic pathways may contribute to the relapse of S. aureus BJIs. However, no association between specific mutations or phenotypes and the occurrence of relapse in bone and joint infections has been highlighted.

CONCLUSION: Despite its limitations, this study represents an essential first step toward large-scale investigations aimed at understanding how bacterial genome alterations and pathophysiological mechanisms contribute to relapse in bone and joint infections.

articles.title: The association between body mass index and perioperative outcomes by ethnicity and socioeconomic status: a systematic review of systematic reviews.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: Body mass index (BMI) is associated with adverse perioperative outcomes. This study investigated the completeness of ethnicity and socioeconomic status (SES) reporting in perioperative research and the association between BMI and perioperative outcomes by ethnicity and SES.

DESIGN: We extended a previous systematic review of reviews that compared perioperative outcomes by BMI categories. For this review, we extracted primary studies published from 2004 onwards from included systematic reviews that focused on seven frequently performed surgeries with some evidence of ethnic disparities: total hip arthroplasty, total knee arthroplasty, coronary artery bypass grafting, caesarean section, prostatectomy, breast reconstruction postmastectomy, and gynaecological surgery. We calculated the number (%) of primary studies reporting ethnicity and/or SES and extracted data for perioperative outcomes up to 90 days postoperatively by ethnicity and SES. Outcomes were based on the Standardised Endpoints in Perioperative Medicine initiative. Effect measures and incidence (%) were qualitatively summarised due to heterogeneity in reporting.

RESULTS: From 49 systematic reviews, 332 primary studies investigated the seven surgical procedures and only 39 (11.7%) reported ethnicity (10.8%) or SES (2.4%) at baseline. Among these, only 10 studies (3%) stratified perioperative outcomes by ethnicity and/or SES, with most adjusting for BMI in regression models. Only one study clearly stratified outcomes across BMI categories within each ethnicity. There was some evidence of increasing risk of postoperative atrial fibrillation by ethnicity and BMI. Two studies found that Black patients had higher odds of pulmonary embolism than White patients after adjusting for BMI. Findings for other outcomes and SES were inconsistent.

CONCLUSION: Poor reporting of ethnicity and SES data limits understanding of how these variables modify the association between BMI and perioperative outcomes. Deliberate inclusion of ethnicity and SES data in study design, analysis, and reporting is needed to address inequality in perioperative research.

articles.title: Prescribed insulin use in type II diabetes mellitus and skin cancer risk: A systematic review 3.
Perceived Family Functioning and Social Adaptation Levels in Patients with Depression.
articles.abstract: Depression is not only an individual disorder but also a condition associated with family systems. This cross-sectional study examined the relationship between perceived family functioning and social adaptation in adults diagnosed with depression. The sample consisted of 123 patients attending a state hospital psychiatric outpatient clinic. Data were collected using the Perceived Family Functioning Scale (PFFS) and Social Adaptation Self-Evaluation Scale (SASS). Descriptive statistics, Pearson's correlation, and hierarchical multiple linear regression analyses were performed. The mean PFFS and SASS scores were 104.59 ± 16.98 and 37.80 ± 8.49, respectively. A statistically significant but weak positive correlation was found between perceived family functioning and social adaptation (r = 0.366, p < 0.001). In regression analyses, the intra-familial communication and positive affect subscales were significantly associated with social adaptation, explaining 17.1% of the variance in the unadjusted model and 16.1% after controlling for age, gender, employment status, and illness duration in months. Other subscales were not statistically significant. These findings suggest that higher levels of intra-familial communication and positive affect are associated with better social adaptation in young adults with depression. Psychiatric nurses may consider the potential role of family functioning when assessing patients.

articles.title: A Prospective Randomized Trial to Assess Early versus Delayed Weight Bearing Following Operatively Treated Ankle Fractures in the United States.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: To determine the safety of early versus delayed weight bearing and effectiveness for improving return-to-work following ankle fracture repair.

METHODS: Design: Prospective randomized study.

SETTING: 19 United States Trauma Centers.

PATIENT SELECTION CRITERIA: Adult patients (≥18 years) with ankle fracture (OTA/AO 44 A, B or C) undergoing surgical fixation were included. Open Gustilo-Anderson (G-A) Type IIIB, IIIC, syndesmotic injuries with fixation, and injuries with arterial impaction that surgeons felt unsafe to weight were excluded.

OUTCOME MEASURES AND COMPARISONS: The co-primary outcomes were (1) non-inferiority of early versus delayed weight bearing for reoperation for complications of hardware failure, non-union, loss of reduction, infection, or fusion; and (2) gated superiority of early versus delayed weight bearing for time to return-to-work, both within 365 days of randomization. Reoperation and time to return-to-work was compared between patients assigned to early (2 weeks post-operatively) versus delayed (6 weeks post-operatively) weight bearing.

RESULTS: The modified intent to treat sample included 418 patients enrolled between January 2020 through October 2023; 214 early (mean age: 47; SD (15) range (18-84); 35% male); 204 delayed (mean age: 43; SD (15); 36% male). Reoperation for complication occurred in 5 early (2.3%, 95% Confidence Interval (CI): 0.3%, 4.4%), and 7 delayed patients (3.4%, 95% CI: 0.9%, 5.9%). Median time to return-to-work (95% CI) was 54 (42, 77) days and 69 (47, 89) days for the early and delayed groups, respectively. Early weight bearing was non-inferior to delayed weight bearing for reoperation (difference in complication free survival (early - delayed): 1.5 percentage points; 90% two sided CI: -1.7%, 4.8% which excluded the non-inferiority tolerance of -5.0%) and not superior for return-to-work (Hazard Ratio 1.1, 95% CI: 0.8, 1.6, p=0.475).

CONCLUSIONS: Trial findings add to the growing evidence demonstrating the safety of early weight bearing after fixation of bimalleolar and trimalleolar ankle fracture without syndesmotic disruption, a key concern for both clinicians and patients. However, no statistically significant benefit of earlier return-to-work was found.

LEVEL OF EVIDENCE: I.

articles.title: Development of Enhanced Reviews of Psychological Changes After Stroke (ENRICH): A complex Intervention to Monitor and Support Self-Management of Post-Stroke Psychological Changes Within a Matched Care Model.
articles.abstract: ObjectiveTo report the design and development of a complex intervention to monitor and support self-management of post-stroke psychological changes.DesignThe Medical Research Council framework for complex intervention research guided development work, which included a literature review, semi-structured interviews with stroke survivors (n = 26) and family members (n = 11), a Delphi survey with healthcare professionals and researchers (n = 42), and workshops with stroke survivors (n = 4), family members (n = 3), and healthcare professionals (n = 5).SettingStroke community care.ParticipantsStroke survivors, family members, healthcare professionals and researchers.InterventionThe Enhanced Reviews of Psychological Changes after stroke (ENRICH) programme is a brief intervention deliverable within the UK matched care model of post-stroke psychological support. It supports stroke survivors with mild to moderate cognitive changes, low mood, anxiety and fatigue by monitoring symptoms, providing personalised psychoeducation, and supporting self-management through three brief reviews at 1, 3, and 6 months. Those with more severe or persistent psychological changes are referred through local care pathways for specialist psychological input.Main measuresThe intervention is reported using the TIDieR checklist.ResultsThe logic model and programme theory suggest benefits for psychological wellbeing and quality of life, with stakeholder input likely to enhance acceptability and feasibility.ConclusionsENRICH has the potential to address gaps in UK post-stroke care for those with mild to moderate changes affecting cognition, mood, anxiety and fatigue when delivered within the matched care model. Feasibility testing is underway with future clinical effectiveness testing is planned.

articles.title: Necrotizing Myopathies: A Myopathology Experience from a Single Tertiary Care Center.
articles.journal: Annals of Indian Academy of Neurology
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND AND OBJECTIVES: Necrotizing myopathy (NM) is a rare inflammatory myopathy characterized by prominent necrosis and minimal to absent inflammation, arising from heterogeneous immune- and non-immune-mediated causes. Muscle biopsy aids diagnosis, especially in seronegative cases and those with overlapping presentations, helping to distinguish NM from other idiopathic inflammatory myopathies (IIMs). This tertiary center study examines the myopathologic spectrum in NM, correlating histopathologic findings with clinical features and autoantibody profiles.

METHODS: We studied the records and biopsies of 77 patients diagnosed with NM between June 2023 and December 2024. Clinical and myositis antibody data were obtained from the records. The biopsies underwent histologic evaluation, including enzyme histochemistry and immunohistochemistry. Descriptive statistics and Chi-square tests (GraphPad Prism 9.5.1) were used to assess features across etiologies.

RESULTS: This study included 77 patients (median age, 51 years; M:F, 2.4:1) with a mean creatine phosphokinase of 21,230 IU/L. All presented with acute/subacute proximal weakness ( n = 77, 100%), while myalgias ( n = 20, 25%) and fever ( n = 17, 22%) were less common. Identified etiologies included statin-associated myopathy ( n = 19, 24.6%), infections ( n = 22, 28.5%), anti-signal recognition particle myopathy ( n = 7, 9%), anti-hydroxy-3-methylglutaryl-coenzyme A reductase myopathy ( n = 4, 5.1%), others (overlap syndromes, alcohol-related myopathy, lipid storage myopathy, etc.), and idiopathic cases ( n = 15, 19.4%). Biopsy findings included scattered necrotic fibers ( n = 48, 62%), groups of necrotic fibers ( n = 29, 37.6%), fiber regeneration ( n = 52, 67.5%), perivascular inflammation ( n = 11, 14.2%), endomysial inflammation ( n = 4, 5.1%), and major histocompatibility complex class I (MHC-I) expression that was diffuse positive ( n = 22, 28.5%), focal positive ( n = 26, 33.7%), or negative ( n = 19, 24.6%). MHC-I expression significantly discriminated among etiologies ( P = 0.0013), unlike patterns of necrosis or inflammation ( P > 0.20).

CONCLUSIONS: NM encompasses diverse immune- and non-immune-mediated causes that share similar biopsy features, distinct from those of other inflammatory myopathies. Accurate diagnosis requires clinicoseropathologic correlation.

articles.title: Correction to "Application Value of Myocardial Segmental Thickness Variability Measured by Echocardiography in Distinguishing Ischemic and Nonischemic Dilated Cardiomyopathy".
Chronic total occlusion percutaneous coronary interventions in dialysis patients.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: To compare characteristics and in-hospital outcomes of dialysis vs non-dialysis patients undergoing chronic total occlusion percutaneous coronary intervention (CTO PCI).

METHODS: The authors analyzed 18 572 patients undergoing CTO PCI between 2012 and 2026. Outcomes were compared using multivariable logistic regression and propensity score-matching weights. Mortality was evaluated by cumulative center-enrollment category.

RESULTS: Overall, 447 patients (2.4%) were receiving dialysis. Compared with non-dialysis patients, they more often had diabetes mellitus (70.5% vs 43.1%), hypertension (93.5% vs 87.1%), heart failure (52.7% vs 27.0%), cerebrovascular disease (17.9% vs 9.1%), peripheral arterial disease (29.1% vs 12.7%), and moderately or severely calcified CTOs (68.2% vs 47.0%; all P < .001). Technical success (85.2% vs 87.4%; P = .190) and procedural success (83.9% vs 86.2%, P = .192) were similar. Retrograde approach (31.1% vs 31.3%; P = .90) and antegrade dissection re-entry (21.3% vs 19.8%; P = .40) were used similarly. In-hospital major adverse cardiac events (MACE) did not differ (2.9% vs 1.9%; P = .11), whereas in-hospital mortality was higher (1.8% vs 0.5%; P = .001) in dialysis patients. The mortality odds ratio (OR) was 2.36 (95% confidence interval [CI], 0.70-5.90; P = .106) in multivariable analysis and 2.42 (95% CI, 1.13-5.16; P = .022) after propensity score weighting. The dialysis-mortality association did not vary across center-enrollment categories (interaction P = .522).

CONCLUSIONS: Despite greater clinical and angiographic complexity, dialysis patients had no significant differences in procedural success or MACE but had higher in-hospital mortality. The mortality association remained imprecise, and residual confounding cannot be excluded.

articles.title: Spatiotemporal characteristics of traffic accidents on a high-volume expressway with closely spaced interchanges.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: The rapid saturation of expressway capacity in economically developed city clusters has intensified traffic conflicts and accident risks, yet accidents on high-volume expressways with closely spaced interchanges remain understudied. This study aims to clarify the spatiotemporal distribution patterns of such accidents and to identify the locations and characteristics of accident-prone segments.

METHODS: A total of 30,265 valid records from the Changhu Expressway in Dongguan, China, covering January 2019 to December 2023, were analyzed; these comprised 19,315 traffic accidents and 10,950 traffic incidents. Descriptive statistics were used to examine accident types and involved vehicle types by year and 15-min interval. Pearson correlation analysis assessed contemporaneous associations between accident counts and high-flow-event frequency, and a spatiotemporal overlap-rate indicator was used to identify accident-prone segments.

RESULTS: Rear-end collisions were the predominant accident type (85.3%), with trucks disproportionately involved during 02:00-04:00. Accidents showed four daily peaks, whereas high-flow events showed two. High-flow-event peaks preceded the morning accident peak, whereas accident peaks preceded high-flow-event peaks in the afternoon. The ends of acceleration lanes, areas preceding divergence points, downhill sections, and continuous-gradient segments contained notable accident concentrations. Using the spatiotemporal overlap rate, 14 accident-prone segments were identified.

CONCLUSIONS: On the studied high-volume expressway, traffic accidents showed pronounced spatiotemporal clustering. Accident counts were positively associated with high-flow-event frequency in most analyzed direction-period combinations, while interchange weaving areas and variable-gradient sections contained notable accident concentrations. The findings may inform time- and location-specific crash-prevention measures on similar facilities, but their transferability should be evaluated using exposure and severity data from additional corridors.
