articles.abstract: SUMMARYInvasive non-typhoidal Salmonella (iNTS) disease is a severe bloodstream and focal invasive infection caused by non-typhoidal serovars of Salmonella enterica, especially S. Typhimurium and S. Enteritidis. Its clinical importance is disproportionate to its routine visibility because disease often presents as undifferentiated fever, sepsis, meningitis, severe anaemia-associated deterioration, recurrent bacteraemia, or focal infection, while definitive recognition depends on blood or other sterile-site microbiology. Global estimates indicate substantial mortality, but the true incidence remains uncertain because blood-culture access, prior antimicrobial exposure, specimen volume, and surveillance intensity vary widely. The vaccine-development era has intensified the need for a unified clinical microbiology framework. Prevention of invasive disease requires host-risk recognition, laboratory-confirmed endpoints, antimicrobial susceptibility testing, lineage-aware genomic surveillance, reservoir assessment, and post-introduction systems able to detect residual disease, breakthrough infection, non-target serovars, lineage shifts, and resistant invasive clones. This narrative review synthesizes the clinical, immunological, genomic, diagnostic, antimicrobial resistance, and vaccine era evidence relevant to iNTS control. Emphasis is placed on immune evasion, macrophage survival, T-cell dysfunction, immunosuppressed hosts, diagnostic blind spots, treatment under uncertainty, and the integration of laboratory systems with surveillance and prevention policy.

articles.title: Cross-sectional Comparison of the PREVENT and Pooled Cohort Equations for 10-Year Atherosclerotic Cardiovascular Risk Estimates in a U.S. Cohort of Black and Latina Transgender Women with HIV.
articles.journal: Journal of acquired immune deficiency syndromes (1999)
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Transgender women with HIV face higher rates of atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease (ASCVD) than the general population. However, ASCVD risk estimators use binary sex variables that may misclassify their risk. We examined the effects of sex variable inputs in the Predicting Risk of Cardiovascular Disease Events (PREVENT) and Pooled Cohort Equation (PCE) risk calculations and tested for associations of ASCVD risk scores with HIV and hormone use.

SETTING: Participants were recruited from health centers in Boston, New York, and Washington, DC.

METHODS: We performed a cross-sectional comparison of PCE and PREVENT scores by sex variable inputs using data from 108 Black and Latina transgender women with HIV. Logistic regression models tested whether hormone duration and time since HIV diagnosis were associated with hyperlipidemia, diabetes, hypertension, or cardiac events.

RESULTS: Using an illustrative ≥ 5% risk score as the threshold for statin initiation, 40.6% with PCE versus 9.5% with PREVENT met or exceeded 5% risk when male was entered for all, compared with 17.7% with PCE versus 9.5% with PREVENT when female was entered for all, and 24.0% with PCE versus 8.4% with PREVENT when female was entered for participants taking hormones. Neither years since HIV diagnosis nor hormone duration were associated with ASCVD risk factors or events.

CONCLUSION: Use of the PREVENT calculator generates lower ASCVD risk estimates than PCE in transgender women with HIV. Research is needed to determine how best to incorporate gender diversity and intersecting factors into ASCVD risk calculations.

articles.title: Identifying disparities at the intersection of race and HIV in patients with sepsis and pneumonia.
articles.journal: Journal of acquired immune deficiency syndromes (1999)
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Pneumonia and sepsis remain leading causes of hospitalization and death among people with HIV (PWH) despite widespread antiretroviral therapy. Although disparities in critical illness have been described, it remains unclear whether the association between HIV status and mortality differs across racial groups.

SETTING: Retrospective cohort study of adults hospitalized with pneumonia and/or sepsis using the Healthcare Cost and Utilization Project State Inpatient Databases from seven U.S. states (2018-2021).

METHODS: We compared crude in-hospital mortality by HIV status and race. Multilevel logistic regression models adjusted for demographics, comorbidities, acute organ failures present on admission, do-not-resuscitate status, surgical status, and hospital-level clustering. We evaluated race as an effect modifier using an HIV × race interaction model to estimate race-specific adjusted odds ratios. Complementary analyses evaluated racial disparities separately among patients with and without HIV.

RESULTS: Among 3,949,906 hospitalizations, PWH had lower crude mortality than patients without HIV (8.4% vs. 10.2%; absolute risk difference, 1.8%, 95% CI, 1.6-2.0). A significant HIV × race interaction was observed (P=0.0033). HIV infection was associated with increased mortality among patients identified as White (aOR, 1.09; 95% CI, 1.03-1.16) and Asian (aOR, 1.53; 95% CI, 1.13-2.08), but not among patients identified as Black or Other race. Racial disparities also differed according to HIV status.

CONCLUSIONS: The association between HIV infection and pneumonia- and sepsis-related mortality differs across racial groups, indicating important heterogeneity masked by average population estimates. An intersectionality framework may provide insight into structural mechanisms underlying disparities in critical illness among PWH.

articles.title: Performance of a 15-Day Continuous Glucose Monitoring System in Children and Adolescents With Diabetes.
articles.journal: Journal of diabetes science and technology
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The CareSens Air (CSAir) continuous glucose monitoring system is approved for use in adults in South Korea and received adults-only CE marking in early 2024. The aim of this prospective, multicenter, pivotal study in children and adolescents with insulin-dependent diabetes mellitus was to determine if the performance and safety of CSAir in these populations are comparable to those observed in adults.

METHOD: Sensors were worn for 15 days on the upper arm in children and adolescents aged 7 to 17 years and on the upper arm and/or upper buttock in children aged 2 to 6 years. Frequent capillary comparator measurements were performed during in-clinic sessions at the beginning, middle, and end of the sensor-wearing period. Point accuracy was assessed via agreement rates (AR) and mean absolute relative difference (MARD). Additional assessments included clinical point accuracy, technical reliability, and safety.

RESULTS: For subjects aged 7 to 17 years, %20/20 AR was 90.8%, and MARD was 8.9%. A total of 99.9% of values fell within Zones A and B of the Diabetes Technology Society error grid. Sensor survival probability reached 75.2%. In children aged 2 to 6 years, %20/20 ARs were 86.6% and 98.4%, and MARDs were 10.3% and 7.8% for arm- and buttock-worn sensors, respectively. No serious adverse events were reported. Mild and moderate adverse device effects comprised skin issues such as itching or erythema at the sensor application or insertion site.

CONCLUSIONS: The observed performance and safety of CSAir in children and adolescents are similar to those in adults. These data may support an extension of regulatory approval of CSAir for children aged 2 years and older.

articles.title: IDEAL-GENOM: integrated downstream analytical toolkit for genomic analysis.
articles.abstract: There has been an exponential increase in the development of technologies that have offered unprecedented opportunities to unravel the genetic underpinnings of complex traits. However, despite the progress and availability of tools, there are still several challenges to overcome, such as the development of a unified framework that facilitates downstream analysis. To address this challenge, we present IDEAL-GENOM (Integrated Downstream Evaluation And anaLysis toolkit for GENOMic data), a Python-based wrapper designed to streamline the analytical workflow commonly implemented in binary (case-control) genome-wide association studies (GWAS). IDEAL-GENOM integrates widely used tools such as PLINK, GCTA, and bcftools along with custom-developed functionalities, enabling reproducible results through parameter sharing. IDEAL-GENOM provides a simplified framework for quality control (QC), GWAS, and downstream analysis that will enable beginners and advanced users to leverage the built-in functionalities to perform GWAS analysis for complex traits with binary outcomes. IDEAL-GENOM is a customizable tool that enables users to efficiently analyze genotyping data with reproducible QC, post-imputation, and GWAS pipelines.

articles.title: Effects of repetitive transcranial magnetic stimulation on global cognitive performance and activities of daily living in post-stroke patients: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Post-stroke cognitive impairment (PSCI) severely affects patients' daily living and independence, with limited treatment options. Repetitive transcranial magnetic stimulation (rTMS) shows promise but inconsistencies in reported effect sizes across cognitive domains.

METHODS: We systematically searched PubMed, Web of Science, Cochrane Library, and EMBASE up to March 2026 for randomized controlled trials evaluating rTMS combined with rehabilitation versus sham or rehabilitation alone in stroke patients. Outcomes included MMSE, MoCA, Digit Span Test (DST), and modified Barthel Index (MBI). Meta-analysis was performed using RevMan 5.4.

RESULTS: Ten RCTs involving 666 patients were included. rTMS significantly improved MMSE (MD = 1.76, 95%CI[1.10, 2.43], p < 0.00001, I2 = 5%) and MoCA scores (MD = 2.64, 95% CI[1.74,3.55], p < 0.00001, I2 = 0%). No significant effect was found on DST-forward (p = 0.13), but DST-backward showed mild improvement (MD = 0.77, 95% CI[0.35,1.18], p = 0.0003, I2 = 62%). MBI scores were significantly enhanced (MD = 10.68, 95% CI[7.91,13.46], p < 0.00001, I2 = 0%).

CONCLUSION: Based on low-to-moderate certainty evidence, rTMS combined with rehabilitation may improve global cognitive screening performance and daily living ability in stroke patients, with a mild benefit on working memory. Further studies are needed to optimize stimulation protocols.

articles.title: Epidemiology of Uncontrolled and Treatment‑Resistant Hypertension: A Registry‑Based Observational Study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: This study aimed to describe blood pressure control rates and prevalence of treatment resistant hypertension among diagnosed individuals.

METHODS: Randomly selected adults who had at least one primary or secondary healthcare visit and who were registered residents of Stockholm County, Sweden, on December 31st, 2019, were included. Blood pressure control in diagnosed individuals was assessed using two targets: <140/90 mmHg and <130/80 mmHg. The prevalence of treatment-resistant hypertension defined by three commonly used criteria was calculated and its association with clinical characteristics, drug treatment patterns, and comorbidities were assessed.

RESULTS: By the end of 2019, among those with a hypertension diagnosis, 57% (<140/90 mmHg) or 19% (<130/80 mmHg) had controlled blood pressure depending on the threshold used. The point prevalence of treatment-resistant hypertension ranged from <1% to 17% depending on definition and was associated with older age, higher body mass index, and multiple comorbidities including type 2 diabetes, cardiovascular disease, heart failure, and chronic kidney disease.

CONCLUSION: Blood pressure control remains a major clinical challenge, with fewer than one in five patients with a hypertension diagnosis achieving <130/80 mmHg. The prevalence of treatment-resistant hypertension varied widely depending on the definition used and was closely associated with a greater burden of comorbidities, indicating an unmet need for improved strategies for this clinically challenging subgroup.

articles.title: Serum CitH3 and PTX3 Levels for Early Prediction of Acute Respiratory Distress Syndrome Following Severe Traumatic Brain Injury.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To evaluate the predictive value of serum citrullinated histone H3 (CitH3) and pentraxin 3 (PTX3) for acute respiratory distress syndrome (ARDS) after severe traumatic brain injury (sTBI).

METHODS: This prospective observational study enrolled 395 consecutive sTBI patients admitted between April 2025 and February 2026. Patients were categorized into ARDS (n = 111) and non-ARDS (n = 284) groups. Serum CitH3 and PTX3 were measured by ELISA. Candidate predictors were selected by LASSO regression. Spearman correlation, multivariable logistic regression, and receiver operating characteristic (ROC) analyses were performed. The DeLong test, category-free net reclassification improvement (NRI), and integrated discrimination improvement (IDI) assessed incremental predictive value over the conventional model.

RESULTS: Serum CitH3 and PTX3 were significantly higher in the ARDS group (both P < 0.001) and were positively correlated with each other but negatively with oxygenation indices and albumin. Multivariable analysis identified pulmonary contusion, shock, fluid balance within 12 h of admission, APACHE II and SOFA scores, and elevated CitH3 and PTX3 as independent risk factors (all P < 0.05), whereas a higher GCS score and elevated albumin were protective. Their combination yielded an AUC of 0.841, superior to either alone. When added to the conventional model, biomarkers increased the AUC from 0.926 to 0.943 (P = 0.025), with category-free NRI of 0.554 (95% CI: 0.320-0.778, P < 0.001) and IDI of 0.072 (95% CI: 0.040-0.105, P < 0.001).

CONCLUSION: Combined serum CitH3 and PTX3 demonstrate early predictive potential for ARDS after sTBI but require external validation.

articles.title: Emerging therapeutic strategies and clinical trials in severe asthma management: current evidence and future directions.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Biologic therapies have transformed the management of severe asthma, particularly in type 2-high disease, but important unmet needs remain. Incomplete responses, uncertainty in treatment positioning, and the lack of effective options for non-type 2 or mixed inflammatory endotypes continue to limit the achievement of deeper and more durable disease control.

AREAS COVERED: This review examines the evolving therapeutic landscape of severe asthma, moving from currently approved biologics to emerging strategies directed at upstream mediators and novel pathways, including alarmins, tumor necrosis factor-like cytokine 1A (TL1A)-related signaling, multi-target biologics, and next-generation anti-immunoglobulin E (IgE) approaches. It also discusses how recent clinical trials have expanded traditional efficacy outcomes by incorporating inhaled corticosteroid reduction, biomarker modulation, small airway dysfunction, mucus plugging, treatment burden, remission, and possible disease modification.

EXPERT OPINION: The field is moving beyond exacerbation reduction toward deeper and more durable disease control. Future progress will depend on improved biological stratification, more informative biomarkers, comparative effectiveness data, and therapeutic strategies capable of extending benefit beyond conventional type 2-high disease. In parallel, greater emphasis on remission-oriented and potentially disease-modifying care is likely to reshape both trial design and clinical practice in severe asthma.

articles.title: Letter to the Editor on "Pediatric Patients Undergoing Enterocystoplasty and Risk of Metabolic Disease: A Single Center Retrospective Study".
Fluid Therapy in Mechanically Ventilated Critically Ill Adult Patients.
articles.abstract:
IMPORTANCE: Fluid therapy is ubiquitous in the intensive care unit (ICU) but carries risks, especially in mechanically ventilated patients. Contemporary global practice across dose, indication, and type is unknown.

OBJECTIVE: To characterize ICU fluid practices in mechanically ventilated adults.

DESIGN, SETTING, AND PARTICIPANTS: International prospective observational cohort study between April 2024 and July 2025, across 206 ICUs in 41 countries on 6 continents. Consecutive adult patients receiving invasive mechanical ventilation within 3 days of ICU admission and ventilated 24 hours or more. Exclusion criteria were age younger than 16 years and transfer under mechanical ventilation from another ICU.

EXPOSURES: Fluid volume, indication, and type after intubation.

MAIN OUTCOMES AND MEASURES: Key measures included (1) total infused volume and daily fluid balance over 7 days after intubation; (2) the indication for fluid therapy over the first 3 days after intubation; (3) the proportion of total administered fluid volume attributable to each fluid type over the first 3 days after intubation.

RESULTS: Among 2454 patients analyzed (median age, 63 years [IQR, 49-73 years]; 63.6% [1560] male), median daily fluid input peaked on day 1 at 3.0 L (IQR, 2.2-4.0 L) and declined to 2.6 L (IQR, 1.8-3.5 L) through day 6. Daily fluid balance (median, 0.9 L; IQR, 0.1-1.9 L on day 1) decreased to less than 0.3 L (IQR, -0.5 to 1.2 L) by day 3 and remained near-neutral through day 6. Maintenance and replacement fluids (to meet daily requirements and to correct ongoing losses; 31.9%) and creep fluids (to deliver medications and maintain catheter patency; 30.9%) were the primary indications, whereas resuscitation (to restore circulating blood volume; 16.0%) accounted for a smaller proportion. Isotonic balanced crystalloids (48.9%) and isotonic saline (0.9% sodium chloride) (27.0%) were common; colloids were rare (1.3%). Substantial between-site variation persisted after adjustment for case-mix.

CONCLUSIONS AND RELEVANCE: In this prospective international cohort study, fluid therapy varied widely among mechanically ventilated critically ill patients, with maintenance and creep fluids-rather than resuscitation fluids-accounting for most total volume.

articles.title: OneRF radiofrequency ablation system for the minimally invasive treatment of trigeminal neuralgia: initial clinical experience.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Percutaneous radiofrequency ablation is an established treatment for medically refractory trigeminal neuralgia (TN). Conventional systems use a single active tip and often require repeated repositioning. A multi-contact radiofrequency platform may permit contact-level interrogation and lesioning along a single fixed trajectory.

METHODS: We performed a retrospective review of patients with medically refractory TN treated with a multi-contact thin-film radiofrequency probe. Demographics, operative details, Barrow Neurological Institute (BNI) pain scores, medication use, and complications were reviewed. Contact-level localization was performed intraoperatively, including low-temperature thermal interrogation, followed by definitive lesioning.

RESULTS: Fifteen patients (mean age 66.5 years; 12 women) underwent treatment. Most had classical or idiopathic TN, purely paroxysmal involving the V2-V3 distribution. Contact-level mapping was successfully achieved in all cases with definitive lesioning along a fixed trajectory. At mean follow-up of 6.0 months, all patients had a good outcome (BNI I-IIIB), and most had reduced or discontinued pain medications. No off-target lesioning was observed.

CONCLUSIONS: This early clinical series suggests that a multi-contact radiofrequency platform can facilitate contact-level mapping and lesioning of trigeminal distributions along a single trajectory without repeated probe repositioning. Initial pain outcomes were favorable, although larger cohorts and longer follow-up are needed to define durability and comparative effectiveness.

articles.title: Accuracy of Machine Learning in Differential Diagnosis of Multiple System Atrophy: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Multiple system atrophy (MSA) is frequently misdiagnosed as Parkinson's disease (PD) or progressive supranuclear palsy (PSP), posing significant diagnostic challenges.

OBJECTIVE: The aim of the study was to systematically evaluate the efficacy of machine learning (ML) in differentiating MSA from other neurodegenerative disorders.

METHODS: We conducted a systematic search in PubMed, Embase, Cochrane Library, and Web of Science (up to July 5, 2025), including ML-based MSA diagnostic studies. QUADAS-2 assessed bias risk, and a bivariate mixed-effects model synthesized diagnostic metrics.

RESULTS: A total of 51 studies (comprising 3595 MSA patients and 18,189 total cases) were included in the systematic review. Of these, 38 studies contributed to the quantitative synthesis, whereas the remaining 13 studies were summarized qualitatively. In the primary analysis comparing MSA with PD, the pooled sensitivity was 0.86 (95% confidence interval [CI]: 0.81-0.90), specificity 0.87 (95% CI: 0.83-0.90), and the area under the summary receiver operating characteristic (SROC) curve (AUC) 0.93 (95% CI: 0.90-0.95). Overall, pooled sensitivity was 0.85 (95% CI: 0.82-0.88), specificity 0.92 (95% CI: 0.89-0.94), and AUC 0.94 (95% CI: 0.92-0.96). Positron emission tomography (PET)-based models achieved optimal performance (sensitivity: 0.90, specificity: 0.96, AUC: 0.97), whereas deep learning models outperformed others (sensitivity: 0.93, specificity: 0.98, AUC: 0.99).

CONCLUSION: ML models integrating PET/magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) data demonstrate high diagnostic accuracy for MSA. Future work should prioritize prospective multicenter validation and standardized external testing to facilitate clinical implementation.

articles.title: The relationship between gut microbiota-friendly diet and the prevalence and severity of asthma in children.
articles.journal: Journal of pediatric gastroenterology and nutrition
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: Dietary factors may impact asthma indirectly by modulating the composition and activity of the gut microbiota. This study aimed to explore the potential relationship between gut microbiota-friendly diet and both the prevalence and severity of asthma in children.

METHODS: We selected a total of 2256 children from the 2021-2023 National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey. The gut microbiota-friendly diet was assessed using the Diet-Gut Microbiome Index (DI-GM), which incorporates 14 specific food constituents. To calculate the DI-GM, two non-consecutive 24-h dietary recalls data were used, from which the relevant food constituents were derived. A higher DI-GM score indicates greater alignment with a gut microbiota-friendly diet.

RESULTS: Among the 2256 U.S. children, the weighted prevalence of asthma is 13.36%. In fully adjusted models, DI-GM was not significantly associated with asthma prevalence overall or within any subgroups. However, higher DI-GM (T2) was significantly associated with a lower risk of the mild asthma phenotype in the 5-16 age group. In contrast, no significant associations were observed between DI-GM and asthma severity in the other age groups. Subgroup analysis showed a higher DI-GM score was significantly correlated with a lower risk for asthma in subgroups stratified by obesity status.

CONCLUSIONS: Higher DI-GM scores were significantly inversely associated with asthma severity risk in children aged 5-16 years and in obese individuals. These cross-sectional findings support the need for longitudinal studies to determine whether dietary modulation may affect asthma severity via microbiota-dependent mechanisms.

articles.title: Development of an anthropometric-based algorithm to estimate feeding tube insertion depth in neonates.
articles.journal: Journal of pediatric gastroenterology and nutrition
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To develop an anthropometric-based algorithm for estimating feeding tube (FT) insertion depth in neonates using retrospectively collected radiographic data.

METHODS: This observational study reviewed records of infants admitted to a Danish level IV Neonatal Intensive Care Unit from January 2023 to December 2024. Infants with FT placement, using the conventional Nose-Ear-Xiphoid (NEX) method, and radiographic verification within 24 h were included. Radiographically verified FT position and anthropometric data were used to develop new linear and multivariate quadratic models to optimize placement.

RESULTS: Among 198 infants were included (median gestational age [GA] of 35 + 0 weeks [interquartile range, IQR:28 + 6-38 + 1]), 301 radiographic images showed, 144 FTs located at lumbar vertebra 1 (L1), 139 within one vertebra of L1, and 18 outside the stomach. Radiologists recommended adjustment in 107 images. Linear models (weight- or length-dependent) showed strong predictive power (R2 > 0.84), while the multivariate quadratic model reduced bias and achieved R2 = 0.88, confirmed by cross-validation. Prediction accuracy within the predefined target range (L1 ± 1.5 cm) was 77% n, compared with 64% of clinically acceptable NEX placed tubes (p < 0.001). The optimal algorithm was: FT depth = -3.46 + 0.00229 × weight (g) - 9.48 × 10-8 × weight (g)2 + 0.5992 × length (cm) -0.005918 × length(cm)2 + 0.07808 × correted GA(w).

CONCLUSION: The quadratic prediction model showed good internal performance and reduced bias at anthropometric extremes, offering a standardized approach to optimize FT placement and enhance safety in neonatal care. Prospective external validation is required before clinical implementation.

articles.title: Viral interference with SARS-CoV-2 during the COVID-19 pandemic: An individual participant data meta-analysis.
articles.abstract: Viral interference between SARS-CoV-2 and other respiratory virus infections has been implicated, but symptom-based testing in observational studies may bias estimations. We used individual participant data from ten cohort studies conducted during pandemic years 2020-2024 to study virus interference. Respiratory samples were PCR-tested for viruses including SARS-CoV-2. The primary analysis was based on samples collected from cohort participants regardless of respiratory symptoms. A secondary analysis included only symptom-based testing data. We estimated odds ratios for co-occurrence of SARS-CoV-2 with other respiratory viruses. The primary analysis included data from six cohorts (n = 1 023). In total 205 of 2 465 samples were SARS-CoV-2 positive (8.3%). Co-detections with SARS-CoV-2 occurred less frequently than expected under the assumption of zero interference (OR: 0.72; 95% CI: 0.40-1.25) for samples positive for another virus. The secondary analysis (five cohorts, n = 1 715) included 2 088 samples from symptomatic subjects, with 506 SARS-CoV-2 infections (24.2%). The OR of SARS-CoV-2 detection was 0.16 (95% CI: 0.10-0.25) for samples positive for another virus. Minimizing selection bias, our results still point towards negative viral interference with SARS-CoV-2, but effect-estimates are weaker and non-significant. Apart from selection bias, the stronger effects found in symptomatic individuals could also indicate that symptomatic infection enhances virus interference.

articles.title: Burden of RSV hospital disease and its comorbidities in adults in Spain (2016-2023).
articles.abstract: This observational descriptive study analyses the hospital burden of respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) among adults in Spain using the Minimum Basic Data Set (MBDS) from the Spanish National Hospital Data Surveillance System. Hospital admissions of adults diagnosed with non-bronchiolitis RSV infection between 2016 and 2023 were identified using ICD-10-CM codes. A total of 288,297 RSV-related hospitalizations were recorded, with a mean patient age of 76.18 years. The overall hospitalization rate was 92.43 per 100,000 inhabitants, and the mortality rate was 5.32 per 100,000. The most common severe comorbidities at admission were congestive heart failure, diabetes, and chronic obstructive pulmonary disease. Patients aged over 65 years had a significantly higher risk of in-hospital mortality (OR 1.78; 95% CI: 1.64-1.93) compared to those aged 40-64 years, increasing to 2.22 (95% CI: 2.05-2.40) in the presence of at least one severe comorbidity. Male sex was also associated with increased mortality risk (OR 1.24; 95% CI: 1.20-1.28). In conclusion, RSV represents a substantial cause of hospitalization and mortality among adults in Spain, particularly in patients over 60 years, males, and those with underlying comorbidities.

articles.title: The Importance of Molecular Imaging Response Criteria: Rationale and Overview.
articles.abstract: Assessment of therapeutic response in oncology is fundamental for evaluating treatment efficacy, guiding clinical decision-making, and determining prognosis. Historically, response evaluation relied primarily on anatomical imaging criteria derived from tumor size changes on computed tomography (CT), most notably the Response Evaluation Criteria in Solid Tumors (RECIST) and its adaptations. However, advances in molecular imaging, particularly positron emission tomography (PET) using [18F]-2-fluoro-2-deoxyglucose ([18F]FDG) and other radiopharmaceuticals, have introduced new biomarkers capable of detecting tumor response earlier than structural changes. Molecular imaging-based criteria, including EORTC, PERCIST, immune-adapted PET frameworks, and disease-specific systems such as Lugano, RANO, ENETS SSTR-PeRForm and RECIP, provide quantitative assessment of tumor burden and may better reflect biologic response to therapy. This review discusses the rationale behind molecular imaging response criteria, outlines the principles of CT-based and PET-based evaluation systems, and highlights the clinical relevance of integrating metabolic imaging into tumor response.

articles.title: Endoscopic secondary chordae transfer and edge-to-edge repair for the treatment of asymmetric anterior leaflet prolapse.
articles.journal: Multimedia manual of cardiothoracic surgery : MMCTS
articles.abstract: Anterior leaflet prolapse remains a challenging lesion in mitral valve repair, particularly in the presence of asymmetric degenerative disease. We present the case of a 59-year-old patient with severe mitral regurgitation due to asymmetric anterior leaflet prolapse in the setting of Barlow's disease, treated through a totally endoscopic right minithoracotomy. Intraoperative valve analysis demonstrated prolapse of the A2M2 and A3 segments with elongated secondary chordae. Mitral valve repair was performed using secondary chordae transfer, followed by asymmetric edge-to-edge repair at the A2-P2 scallops and ring annuloplasty. Intraoperative assessment showed satisfactory leaflet coaptation with trivial residual regurgitation. Postoperative echocardiography confirmed the absence of residual mitral regurgitation and no evidence of clinically significant mitral stenosis. This report describes the technical aspects of endoscopic secondary chordae transfer combined with asymmetric edge-to-edge repair and ring annuloplasty for the treatment of asymmetric anterior leaflet prolapse, demonstrating the feasibility of this repair strategy in a complex mitral valve anatomy.

articles.title: New and emerging pharmacological solutions for Behcet's syndrome.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Behçet's syndrome is a chronic multisystem inflammatory disease characterized by mucocutaneous lesions, ocular inflammation, and major-organ involvement. Treatment aims to prevent irreversible organ damage and maximize health-related quality of life.

AREAS COVERED: This review summarizes current therapeutic approaches based on the 2025 update of the European Alliance of Associations for Rheumatology recommendations for Behçet's syndrome. Core recommended therapies, including colchicine, glucocorticoids, apremilast, conventional immunosuppressants, and TNF inhibitors, are selected for individual organ involvement depending on severity. The updated recommendations refine treatment strategies and emphasize individualized management rather than substantially expanding therapeutic options. This review also examines emerging non-TNF biologics targeting IL-1, IL-6, IL-17, and IL-12/23, and Janus kinase inhibitors. PubMed was searched from database inception through August 2026.

EXPERT OPINION: The rarity of Behçet's syndrome and the lack of standardized assessment tools remain major obstacles to conducting high quality clinical trials. In addition, several anti cytokine therapies may be associated with organ-specific or paradoxical manifestations in Behçet's syndrome. Further evidence is required to clarify both the efficacy and safety profiles of new therapeutic agents, and prospective controlled studies will be essential to establish their roles in clinical practice.

articles.title: Genetic architecture of the personality meta-traits - stability and plasticity - and their transdiagnostic overlap with psychopathology.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The Five Factor Model (FFM) personality meta-traits, stability and plasticity, are thought to capture broad individual differences in the parameters of goal-directed, cybernetic mechanisms in the brain, which have implications for transdiagnostic psychopathology risk. It remains unknown whether these meta-traits represent genetically coherent dimensions. Here we conduct a genomic investigation into the FFM meta-traits and characterize their association with 11 psychiatric conditions.

METHODS: We combined recent genome-wide association study (GWAS) summary statistics with data from the 23andMe Research Institute (European ancestry; total N = 279,240-682,707) and applied Genomic Structural Equation Modelling to conduct a multivariate GWAS of the FFM meta-traits. We then conducted transcriptome-wide association studies (TWAS) and stratified linkage disequilibrium score regression (S-LDSC) to prioritize candidate effector genes and brain cell types for personality traits. Finally, we used LDSC regression and CAUSE Mendelian randomization to characterize the relationship between personality traits and 11 psychiatric conditions.

RESULTS: We identified 83 (14 novel) and 13 (4 novel) independent genome-wide significant loci for stability and plasticity respectively. TWAS prioritized hundreds of candidate effector genes for personality, and S-LDSC showed heritability enrichment across several neuronal cell types. Finally, genetic correlation and Mendelian randomization analyses provided genetic evidence suggesting bidirectional links between stability and psychopathology: higher genetic propensity for stability was protective against psychopathology, whereas greater genetic liability to psychopathology was associated with reduced stability.

CONCLUSIONS: The personality meta-traits capture modest shared architecture across personality, with genetic liability for lower stability potentially representing a broad transdiagnostic link between personality and psychiatric vulnerability.

articles.title: Cortisol and cognition in psychotic disorders: A systematic review and multi-level meta-analysis.
articles.abstract: Emerging evidence suggests that dysregulation of the hypothalamic-pituitary-adrenal (HPA) axis, particularly cortisol, may contribute to the cognitive deficits commonly observed in psychotic disorders. We conducted the first combined systematic review and quantitative synthesis of associations between cortisol and cognition in psychosis. Twelve studies met inclusion criteria (940 participants; 74.68% cases; 39.57% female; mean age = 31.83 years). Of these, nine studies (822 participants; 71.04% cases; 35.96% female; mean age = 32.72 years) contributed data to three-level meta-analyses examining associations between basal cortisol and composite cognition, attention, working memory and processing speed (AWP), executive functioning (EF), and verbal learning and memory (VM). Cortisol sampling time significantly moderated the relationship between cortisol and EF (F = 10.98, p = .004), with a significant negative association emerging between afternoon/evening cortisol and EF (r = -0.27, 95% CI [-0.42, -0.12], p = .01). No other robust cortisol-cognition associations were observed. However, sensitivity analyses revealed a negative association between morning cortisol and AWP following exclusion of an influential study. These findings do not support a general association between basal cortisol and cognitive functioning in psychosis. Instead, they suggest that cortisol-cognition relationships may be both domain- and sampling-time-specific, with the strongest evidence linking elevated afternoon/evening cortisol to poorer executive functioning. Further research using more precise assessments of cortisol dynamics is needed to clarify the role of HPA-axis dysregulation in cognitive impairment across psychotic disorders.

articles.title: Disparities in Social Determinants of Health and Health Outcomes Among Autistic Individuals Without Intellectual Disability in Middle-to-Late Adulthood.
articles.journal: Autism : the international journal of research and practice
articles.abstract: Autism is increasingly recognized across the lifespan, yet little is known about how structural social disadvantage contributes to long-term health risks among autistic adults in middle and later adulthood. Participants were identified from the UK Biobank study, comprising 576 autistic adults with no intellectual disability and an average of 15.2 years of education, and 5,760 controls matched on age, sex, residing area, race, and educational attainment. Social determinants of health (SDH) were assessed using a composite score calculated from 12 indicators that characterized economic, health care, neighborhood, and social domains. Mediation analysis was performed to estimate the extent to which SDH disparities mediated the elevated mortality and chronic disease risks among autistic adults. The study sample was 66.4% male and had a mean age of 51.6 years (SD, 8.03). Autistic adults had worse SDH levels across almost all dimensions. These disparities mediated 39% of the elevated mortality risk. In addition, autistic adults showed increased incidence of cardiovascular disease, dementia, hypertension, type 2 diabetes, depression, and anxiety, with SDH disparities mediating 17% to 38% of these elevated risks. These findings indicate that multifaceted disadvantage plays a substantial role in the health inequities experienced by autistic adults, underscoring the need for cross-sector interventions and policy reforms.Lay AbstractAutistic adults face persistent disadvantage in social conditions that shape health outcomes. These disadvantages may partially explain why autistic adults face higher rates of chronic illnesses and earlier death. From a large cohort in the United Kingdom, we compared 576 autistic adults with 5,760 adults without autism across 12 indicators of social determinants of health (SDH), covering economic, health care, neighborhood, and social domains. Autistic adults showed disadvantage across nearly all domains. These disparities mediated 39% of excess mortality and 17% to 38% of the increased risk for chronic conditions, including cardiovascular disease, dementia, type 2 diabetes, depression, and anxiety. Economic deprivation and social isolation showed relatively larger mediating effects. This study provides evidence that structural inequities in SDH substantially contribute to the long-term health trajectories of autistic adults. Addressing these inequities will require policies and interventions that move beyond individual-level supports to tackle systemic barriers in employment, health care access, housing, and community participation.

articles.title: Pulsed Field Ablation as First-Line Therapy for the Treatment of Atrial Fibrillation: a FARADISE Sub-Analysis.
articles.journal: Europace : European pacing, arrhythmias, and cardiac electrophysiology : journal of the working groups on cardiac pacing, arrhythmias, and cardiac cellular electrophysiology of the European Society of Cardiology

articles.title: Efficacy and Safety of the MiniMed™ Vivera™ Algorithm: Results from a First-in-Human Feasibility Trial.
articles.abstract: MiniMed™ Vivera™ is an automated insulin delivery algorithm designed to make meal announcements optional. This first-in-human feasibility trial evaluated the efficacy and safety of the algorithm under different meal-announcement strategies. Twenty-four adults with type 1 diabetes participated in this prospective study comprising three consecutive 3-week phases: full meal announcement (FA) phase, no meal announcement (NA) phase, and announcement-at-will phase where participants could decide whether to announce each meal (AW). Continuous glucose monitoring data and safety data were assessed for each phase. The international glycemic targets regarding time in, above, and below range were achieved on average across all three meal-announcement phases. Average time in range (70-180 mg/dL) was 82.3 ± 6.60%, 73.8 ± 7.67%, and 76.7 ± 8.98% during FA, NA, and AW phase, respectively. No device-related serious adverse events were reported. In conclusion, this feasibility trial demonstrated that the Vivera algorithm was safe and efficacious in adults with type 1 diabetes, supporting further evaluation in a pivotal trial.

articles.title: Relationships between supportive needs, perceived peer support, and well-being among unpaid cancer caregivers in regional, rural, and remote areas of Queensland, Australia.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: To identify associations between supportive care needs, perceived peer support, and well-being among unpaid cancer caregivers (UCCs) in regional, rural and remote (RRR) Queensland, Australia.

METHODS: A cross-sectional online survey was conducted among 202 adult UCCs for individuals with advanced cancer in RRR Queensland. Participants completed validated measures assessing unmet needs, perceived social support, psychological distress, caregiver burden, and spiritual need. Data were analyzed using descriptive statistics, Cronbach's alpha, Pearson correlations, multiple linear regression, and structural equation modeling (SEM).

RESULTS: CNAT-C, MSPSS, DASS-20, and CDS mean (SD) scores were 1.95 (0.48), 4.63 (1.30), 1.65 (0.59), and 2.66 (0.62), respectively. Practical support was the highest unmet need (M=2.04, SD=0.61), followed by hospital facilities/services (M=1.99, SD=0.59) and healthcare staff (M=1.98, SD=0.59). Internal consistency was high across measures (α=0.806-0.924). Higher unmet needs and perceived peer support were associated with greater distress and poorer well-being (all p<.001). CNAT-C and MSPSS predicted DASS-20 (R2=.236); CNAT-C predicted CDS (R2=.251), whereas MSPSS was not significant. The SEM demonstrated good model fit.

SIGNIFICANCE OF RESULTS: UCCs residing in RRR Queensland reported substantial unmet needs, especially for related to PS and healthcare services. Greater unmet needs were associated with poorer caregiver well-being. The positive association between perceived social support and distress suggests support may be mobilized in response to heightened caregiver strain and highlights the importance of considering the appropriateness and quality of support, alongside availability, for caregivers in RRR settings.

articles.title: Clinical Outcome Differences in Asia Versus Non-Asia Intracerebral Hemorrhage: IPD Analysis From BP-Lowering Clinical Trials.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Evidence of regional differences in clinical outcomes after intracerebral hemorrhage (ICH) is still scarce. We quantified differential outcomes and response to early intensive blood pressure lowering treatment by region in the Blood pressure in Acute Stroke Collaboration ICH data set.

METHODS: This was an observational analysis of pooled individual participant data from 16 completed randomized controlled trials of blood pressure-lowering treatment in acute ICH, based on the Blood pressure in Acute Stroke Collaboration data set. Generalized linear mixed models with inverse probability of treatment weighting (IPTW) were used to determine the association between regions (Asia [primarily East and South Asia] versus non-Asia) and clinical outcomes including neurological deterioration within 7 days, hematoma expansion at 24 hours (absolute ≥6 mL or relative ≥33%), and death or dependency (modified Rankin Scale scores, 3-6), major disability(modified Rankin Scale score, 3-5), death alone at 90 days.

RESULTS: Among 6221 patients (age, 63.3±13.0 years; female 36.4%), 3494 (56.2%) were from Asia. ICH participants from Asia had a significantly reduced risk of death or dependency (unadjusted odds ratio [OR], 0.44 [95% CI, 0.39-0.51]; IPTW-weighted OR, 0.67 [95% CI, 0.58-0.77]); and major disability (unadjusted OR, 0.49 [95% CI, 0.42-0.56]; IPTW-weighted OR, 0.67 [95% CI, 0.57-0.78]) at 90 days, neurological deterioration (unadjusted OR, 0.63 [95% CI, 0.52-0.77]; IPTW-weighted OR, 0.70 [95% CI, 0.56-0.89]) within 7 days, in comparison to those from non-Asia regions. However, there were no differences for hematoma expansion (P=0.97) at 24 hours or death (P=0.23) at 90 days using IPTW. Additionally, there were no significant interactions between blood pressure-lowering treatment and region (Asia versus non-Asia) for either outcome using IPTW.

CONCLUSIONS: Participants from East and South Asia had a favorable functional recovery and a lower risk of neurological deterioration compared with those from non-Asian regions after adjustment for confounders, with no differences in hematoma expansion at 24 hours after ICH. These findings suggest that future ICH studies on clinical outcomes should consider regional differences.

articles.title: Patterns of Delivery Following in Utero Transfer for Extremely Preterm Birth: A Retrospective Cohort Study From a London Tertiary Centre.
articles.abstract:
AIM: To evaluate delivery patterns following in utero transfer (IUT) to a London tertiary neonatal intensive care unit, examining gestational age, referral indication, transfer-to-delivery interval, and maternal length of stay.

METHODS: Retrospective cohort study of women accepted for IUT at St George's Hospital, London (2021-2025), between 22 + 0-27 + 6 weeks' gestation (or 28-29 weeks with multiples/expected birth weight < 800 g) for threatened extremely preterm birth. Data were extracted from BadgerNet, maternity records, and delivery suite databases; Fisher's exact test was used for categorical comparisons.

RESULTS: Of 126 IUT episodes, 53 (42%) delivered at the tertiary centre; median transfer-to-delivery interval was 1 day (mean 2.02). Delivery rates averaged ~10%/day over the first 5 days. Transfers from outside the local network delivered within 24 h more often (18%). Among 73 (58%) who did not deliver, median length of stay was 4 days. Delivery was less likely at 22-24 weeks (32% vs. 50% at ≥ 25 weeks) and significantly associated with sepsis (p = 0.01), chorioamnionitis (p < 0.001), pathological CTG (p = 0.006), and Doppler abnormalities (p = 0.02).

CONCLUSION: Over half of women undergoing IUT did not deliver during admission. Infection and fetal compromise indications were most strongly associated with delivery, supporting liberalised IUT acceptance and capacity planning.

articles.title: Cost-effectiveness of intravenous ferric derisomaltose for patients with heart failure and iron deficiency in the UK based on the IRONMAN trial results.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND AND AIMS: Iron deficiency is common in patients with chronic heart failure. The IRONMAN trial investigated the effect of intravenous (IV) ferric derisomaltose (FDI) compared to usual care on a composite endpoint of hospitalisations for heart failure and cardiovascular death in patients with either new or established heart failure, iron deficiency, and a left ventricular ejection fraction ≤45%. This analysis explores the health economic consequences of being assigned to FDI rather than usual care from the perspective of NHS England.

METHODS: A cost-utility model of FDI compared to usual care was developed based on individual patient-level data from the IRONMAN trial. The model included quality of life modelled on participant-completed EQ-5D-5L questionnaires, all non-elective hospitalisations and end-of-life care. The analysis was run over a one-year time horizon.

RESULTS: Quality-adjusted life years (QALYs) were numerically greater for FDI (0.563) compared to usual care (0.547), a nominal difference of 0.016 QALYs (95% credible interval [CrI]: 0.002-0.032 QALYs) in favour of FDI. The incremental costs of acquiring and administering FDI were £357, which was more than offset by savings of £936 due to avoided hospitalisations and end-of-life care, resulting in savings of £580 (95% CrI: £493-£678) per patient over one year, 15% less than the cost of usual care.

CONCLUSIONS: Over a one-year time horizon, a within-trial analysis showed that administering FDI to patients with heart failure and iron deficiency was cost saving compared to usual care, driven primarily by reduced rates of hospitalisation.

articles.title: Use of Myocardial Perfusion Imaging to Guide Prognosis and Management in Older Adults: Is There an Age Limit?
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Myocardial perfusion imaging is used to guide risk stratification and revascularization decisions. We aimed to determine whether the prognostic value of ischemia on myocardial perfusion imaging and the association with early revascularization (ER) and outcomes differ across age groups.

METHODS: We included 73 038 patients who underwent single photon emission computed tomography (n=45 252) or positron emission tomography (n=27 786) myocardial perfusion imaging across 20 sites from 2009 to 2024. ER was defined as revascularization within 90 days post-myocardial perfusion imaging. Propensity score-adjusted Cox models evaluated the interaction between age, ischemic burden (myocardial flow reserve for positron emission tomography), and ER for the primary outcome of all-cause death or nonfatal myocardial infarction.

RESULTS: Median age was 66 years; 45.3% were <65, 31.5% were 65 to 74, 19.1% were 75 to 84, and 4.2% were ≥85. ER was performed in 6.1%, rising to 7.0% in those aged 75 to 84 years and decreasing to 6.5% in those aged ≥85 years. During a median follow-up of 3.7 years, 10 757 deaths/myocardial infarctions occurred. Increasing ischemia was associated with lower event rates after ER versus medical therapy across most age groups, with no significant continuous age-ischemia-ER interaction (P=0.748). In an exploratory analysis of 3031 patients aged ≥85 years, this association appeared attenuated (hazard ratio for ischemia >10%: 0.90 [0.64-1.26]), although precision was limited, likely reflecting, in part, the small number of patients undergoing ER (n=198). Among positron emission tomography patients, the myocardial flow reserve×ER association did not vary with age (3-way interaction P=0.689). In analyses excluding patients with ER, ischemia remained prognostic in all age groups, though its associated risk declined with advancing age.

CONCLUSIONS: Ischemia remains prognostic across all ages and may help identify candidates who have improved outcomes with ER. In an exploratory analysis, this association appeared attenuated in patients aged ≥85 years, a hypothesis-generating observation. Positron emission tomography-derived myocardial flow reserve may provide complementary physiological information for treatment selection in older adults.

articles.title: Prevalence of urinary incontinence among women in Turkey: A systematic review and meta-analysis.
articles.abstract: Urinary incontinence (UI), defined as the involuntary leakage of urine, is a common condition that affects women's quality of life and overall health. UI becomes more frequent with age and is also observed during pregnancy and postpartum. This systematic review and meta-analysis aimed to determine the prevalence of UI among women. A literature search was conducted between December 2024 and February 2025 in Google Scholar, PubMed, Web of Science, Türkiye Citation Index, Ulakbim, and Turkish Medline. Risk of bias was assessed using the Joanna Briggs Institute checklist. Forty-five studies published between 2005 and 2025, including 41,038 participants, were analyzed. The pooled prevalence of UI among women aged 15 years and older was 36.7%. Prevalence estimates for stress, urgency, and mixed UI were 31.1%, 18.4%, and 27.5%. Definitions used influenced prevalence rates. Planning and delivering appropriate health services based on these findings can contribute to protecting and improving women's health. In Türkiye, it would be beneficial to develop a policy to raise awareness about urinary incontinence in women and to evaluate the condition. Interventions can be implemented nationwide in this way.

articles.title: Health literacy as a predictor of family planning attitudes in young men in Ankara, Türkiye.
articles.abstract: Family planning is a key component of reproductive health; however, young men's attitudes and knowledge remain understudied. This study aimed to examine the relationship between sexual health literacy and family planning attitudes among young men. This cross-sectional, descriptive, and correlational study was conducted with 370 young men aged 18-25 in Ankara using a snowball sampling method. Data were collected using the Family Planning Attitude Scale (FPAS) and Sexual Health Literacy Scale (SHLS). Descriptive statistics, independent samples t-test, one-way ANOVA, Pearson correlation, and multiple linear regression analyses were performed. The mean FPAS score was M=116.26, SD=26.20. A weak positive relationship was found between sexual health literacy and family planning attitudes (p<0.05). Regression analysis indicated that the variables explained 20% of the variance in family planning attitudes. The findings suggest that improving sexual health literacy may positively influence young men's attitudes toward family planning.

articles.title: Maternal risk factors for hypertension in pregnancy: A quantitative study on the role of demographics, obesity, and healthcare compliance.
articles.abstract: Hypertension in pregnancy is a major contributor to maternal and perinatal morbidity and mortality. This study examined the associations between maternal risk factors and hypertension in pregnancy. A prospective observational cohort study was conducted at Wonoayu Health Center, Sidoarjo, Indonesia, from November 2024 to January 2025. Fifty-seven pregnant women with a gestational age of at least 28 weeks and a positive mean arterial pressure screening result were recruited through consecutive sampling. Data were collected from medical records, interviews, adherence cards, physical examinations, blood pressure measurements, and proteinuria tests and analyzed using chi-square tests and multivariable logistic regression. Maternal age (p = 0.022; adjusted OR = 11.848; 95% CI: 1.422-98.739) and adherence to calcium lactate supplementation (p = 0.021; adjusted OR = 0.371; 95% CI: 0.160-0.858) were significantly associated with hypertension in pregnancy. Maternal age and adherence to calcium lactate supplementation may be important factors associated with hypertension in pregnancy.

articles.title: The effect of three- and six-session prenatal haptonomy on pregnancy-related anxiety, distress, and psychological well-being: A randomized controlled trial.
articles.abstract: This randomized controlled trial examined the effects of prenatal haptonomy on pregnancy-related anxiety, distress, and psychological well-being. A total of 102 pregnant women were randomly assigned to a three-session haptonomy group, a six-session haptonomy group, or a control group receiving routine antenatal care. Data were collected using the Pregnancy-Related Anxiety Questionnaire-Revised 2, Tilburg Pregnancy Distress Scale, and Psychological Well-Being Scale at baseline, post-intervention, and follow-up. Repeated measures analysis of variance was used to evaluate group, time, and group × time effects, and effect sizes were reported using partial eta squared (partial η²). In intragroup analyses, the six-session haptonomy group demonstrated a significant reduction in pregnancy-related anxiety, whereas the three-session haptonomy group showed significant reductions in distress and improvements in psychological well-being. Intergroup comparisons revealed statistically significant differences in anxiety, distress, and psychological well-being scores between the haptonomy groups and the control group at post-intervention and follow-up. Repeated measures analysis demonstrated significant group effects for pregnancy-related anxiety, distress, and psychological well-being. These findings suggest that prenatal haptonomy may contribute to improved maternal psychological health during pregnancy, with different intervention durations associated with benefits at different assessment points.

articles.title: Determinants of early antenatal care booking in Kisumu, Kenya: A hospital-based cross-sectional study applying the Andersen-Newman health service utilization model.
articles.abstract: Starting antenatal care early is important for healthy pregnancies. In 2016, the World Health Organization updated its antenatal care guidelines, recommending that pregnant women begin antenatal care by 12 weeks of gestation. Kenya adopted this model in 2022, yet only 29% of women initiate antenatal care early, compared with 37.5% in Sub-Saharan Africa. This study used a cross-sectional design to examine the proportion of women who booked antenatal care early and the factors associated with early booking. The study used Andersen-Newman's health services utilization model as its conceptual framework. A sample of 292 women was selected through systematic random sampling at Jaramogi Oginga Odinga Teaching and Referral Hospital in Kisumu, Kenya. Data was collected using questionnaires and the Kenya Mother and Child Health Handbooks. Analyses included descriptive statistics, the Mann-Whitney U test, the chi-square test, and multivariable logistic regression. The median time to booking antenatal care was 20.0 weeks (IQR: 16.0-24.0), and only 34.2% of women booked early. The most significant predictor of early antenatal care booking was receiving information from healthcare providers (AOR = 1.96; 95% CI: 1.06-3.71; P = 0.036). This study recommends improving healthcare providers' messaging to address social influences from family and friends and to encourage early ANC booking.

articles.title: Beyond conventional anthropometry: Muscle-related indicators and muscle strength in adults with congenital heart disease: A retrospective study with a comparison group.
articles.journal: Nutrition in clinical practice : official publication of the American Society for Parenteral and Enteral Nutrition
articles.abstract: Anthropometric characteristics and muscle strength remain insufficiently characterized in adults with congenital heart disease (CHD). The aim of the study was to characterize anthropometric indicators and muscle strength in hospitalized adults with CHD and examine differences according to cardiac lesion complexity. Exploratory comparisons with adults without CHD were performed as secondary analyses. This cross-sectional study included 109 hospitalized adults with CHD and an external convenience group of 115 adults without CHD. Body mass index (BMI), mid-upper arm circumference (MUAC), triceps skinfold thickness (TSF), mid-arm muscle circumference (MAMC), arm muscle area (AMA), corrected arm muscle area (cAMA), and handgrip strength (HGS) were assessed. Cardiac defects were classified as mild, moderate, or complex. Associations of lesion complexity and previous cardiac surgery with anthropometric indicators and HGS were examined using multivariable linear regression. Comparisons with adults without CHD were conducted as exploratory analyses using the same approach. Among adults with CHD, 57.8% had mild, 24.8% moderate, and 17.4% complex defects. Lesion complexity was associated with MAMC (P = 0.032); participants with complex defects had lower MAMC than those with mild defects (B = -2.44 cm; 95% CI: -4.26 to -0.63). Previous cardiac surgery was associated with higher BMI, MUAC, MAMC, and AMA. In adjusted exploratory comparisons, adults with CHD had lower weight, height, BMI, MUAC, MAMC, AMA, and HGS than adults without CHD, whereas TSF was similar. Values below reference ranges for BMI, MUAC, MAMC, cAMA, and HGS were more frequent in CHD. Greater lesion complexity was associated with lower MAMC, whereas previous cardiac surgery was associated with higher BMI, MUAC, MAMC, and AMA. Muscle-related anthropometric measures and HGS may provide complementary information beyond body size and adiposity in adults with CHD.

articles.title: Molecular Screening and Cell Cultured-Based Isolation of Carp Edema Virus in Koi Carp (Cyprinus carpio Koi) From Aquarium Shops in Tamil Nadu, India.
articles.abstract: This study aimed to explore the widespread occurrence of carp edema virus (CEV) in ornamental koi carp available at ornamental shops in Kolathur, Tamil Nadu. The affected koi carps showed various symptoms, such as ulcers, loss of scales, body and fin haemorrhage, fin necrosis, and gill hyperplasia. No known fish cell lines have been reported for the continuous culturing of CEV. To address this constraint, gill (ICG) and heart (SICH) cell lines derived from catla fish were used for the continuous in vitro cultivation of CEV. Virus-specific cytopathic effects (CPE) were similarly observed in all 12 consecutive passages in the infected cell lines. Furthermore, the in vitro replication efficacy of CEV in ICG and SICH cell lines was confirmed by PCR, and the viral copies were quantified using quantitative PCR (qPCR) at different passages. Initially, the levels of CEV copies were very low; however, they peaked by the 12th passage, indicating adaptation to the ICG and SICH cell lines. In addition, to study the virulence of the isolated CEV, filtrate from the pooled organ tissues of fish, as well as the supernatant of ICG culture of CEV infection, was injected into koi carp, and symptoms were observed and mortality was recorded. PCR and qPCR analyses were conducted to assess tissue tropism in various tissues experimentally CEV-infected koi carp. Based on the PCR and qPCR results, gill tissue was identified as the primary target organ for CEV infection. This study proves that CEV replication in fish cell lines supports future vaccine development.

articles.title: Effects of glucagon-like peptide-1 (GLP-1) mono-agonists on reward processing in animal models: a systematic review.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Glucagon-like peptide-1 (GLP-1), indicated in the treatment of type 2 diabetes mellitus, influences reward processing, integral to disparate mental disorders. Emerging evidence suggests that GLP-1 receptor mono-agonists (GLP-1RAs) are potential treatment strategies for select mental disorders. Herein, we systematically review preclinical research documenting how GLP-1 and GLP-1RAs may impact reward function.

METHODS: Relevant studies were identified through Web of Science, OVID (MedLINE, Embase, PsycInfo), and PubMed from database inception to June 28, 2026. Preclinical research investigating the association between GLP-1 and select GLP-1RAs and reward function was included. Reward functions assessed were food-, drug-, and sexual-related reward.

RESULTS: A total of 66 studies met inclusion and were synthesised herein. Taken together, results indicate that GLP-1 and GLP-1RAs affect measures of food-related, drug-associated, and sexual behaviours. GLP-1 administration was associated with a reduction in food intake and gross locomotor activity with respect to approaching and engaging in reward-seeking behaviours. When locally administered in selected brain regions of evaluated animal models, exenatide was associated with reduced substance use, food seeking, and sexual behaviours (p < 0.05). Similarly, liraglutide was observed to attenuate substance and food-related rewards (p < 0.05). In addition, semaglutide was demonstrated to reduce substance and sucrose intake, while dulaglutide is reported to reduce substance intake (p < 0.001).

DISCUSSION: Extant preclinical findings demonstrate a trend toward reductions in reward-associated behaviours following GLP-1RA administration. Our findings can also provide rationale and impetus for evaluating GLP-1RAs in the treatment of psychiatric disorders characterised by disturbance in hedonic function and behaviours.

articles.title: Pharmacotherapy for MASLD/MASH: approved therapies, drug repurposing, and emerging mechanism-based candidates.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease and metabolic dysfunction-associated steatohepatitis (MASLD/MASH) pharmacotherapy is changing rapidly after the approval of resmetirom and semaglutide for selected adults with noncirrhotic MASH and F2-F3 fibrosis; management must also address obesity, type 2 diabetes, dyslipidemia, cardiovascular risk, and kidney disease.

AREAS COVERED: This structured narrative review evaluates approved, comorbidity-directed, repurposed, and emerging therapies according to mechanism, regulatory status, endpoint strength, safety, interactions, and implementation. PubMed and ClinicalTrials.gov were searched without a lower date limit through September 2026 and supplemented by U.S. and European regulatory documents, society guidance, randomized trials, systematic reviews, meta-analyses, and selected mechanistic studies. Therapies include thyroid hormone receptor-beta agonism, incretin and glucagon-containing agonists, peroxisome proliferator-activated receptor pathways, sodium-glucose cotransporter 2 inhibition, de novo lipogenesis/fatty acid synthase inhibition, fibroblast growth factor 21 analogues, lipid/remnant pharmacology, farnesoid X receptor signaling, antioxidants, and lower-evidence repurposing candidates.

EXPERT OPINION: Resmetirom and semaglutide anchor approved MASH-directed treatment in eligible F2-F3 disease, while comorbidity-directed therapy should be individualized by liver stage and cardiometabolic priorities. Tirzepatide, FGF21 analogues, denifanstat, and rational combinations may broaden treatment, but cross-trial comparisons and surrogate endpoints require cautious interpretation.

articles.title: The Impact of Dual Antiplatelet Therapy on Bleeding and Thrombotic Risks in Diabetic Patients Following Coronary Stent Implantation: A Prospective Study.
articles.journal: Catheterization and cardiovascular interventions : official journal of the Society for Cardiac Angiography & Interventions
articles.abstract:
AIMS: To evaluate the 12-month clinical outcomes of short-term versus extended dual antiplatelet therapy (DAPT) in diabetic patients following drug-eluting stent (DES) implantation.

METHODS: In this single-center prospective cohort study, 536 diabetic patients undergoing DES implantation were categorized into short-term (< 6 months, n = 312) or extended (≥ 6 months, n = 224) DAPT groups based on actual treatment duration. Primary endpoints were major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE: cardiac death, myocardial infarction, and target vessel revascularization) and BARC type 2, 3, or 5 bleeding events at 12 months.

RESULTS: Extended DAPT significantly reduced the incidence of MACE compared to short-term therapy (7.8% vs. 10.5%; HR = 0.72, 95% CI: 0.53-0.98, p = 0.033), primarily driven by lower rates of target vessel revascularization (3.1% vs. 5.1%; p = 0.030). While overall bleeding rates did not differ significantly between groups (8.1% vs. 6.2%; p = 0.192), extended DAPT was associated with a significantly higher risk of recurrent bleeding in patients with a prior bleeding history (HR = 2.10, 95% CI: 1.20-3.60, p = 0.011).

CONCLUSION: Extended DAPT effectively mitigates ischemic risks in diabetic patients following stent implantation without significantly increasing overall clinically significant bleeding. However, clinicians should prioritize individualized DAPT durations, specifically avoiding extended regimens in patients with a history of bleeding to minimize the risk of hemorrhage recurrence.

articles.title: Gramine Suppresses Myofibroblast Activation and ECM Accumulation in Renal Fibrosis by Targeting the NF-κB/NLRP3 and TGF-β1/Smad Pathways.
articles.abstract: Chronic kidney disease (CKD) is driven by persistent inflammation and progressive fibrosis, leading to irreversible renal damage. Gramine (GMN), an indole alkaloid, has broad pharmacological benefits. However, its therapeutic potential against renal fibrosis remains unexplored. This study investigates the antifibrotic potential of GMN in an experimental model of CKD. Potential therapeutic targets of GMN associated with renal fibrosis were identified through network analysis, and functional enrichment analysis revealed the mechanisms regulated by these targets. In vitro validation was conducted in transforming growth factor-β1 (TGF-β1)-induced normal rat kidney fibroblast (NRK-49F) cells. Fibrosis in the left kidney was induced by ureter obstruction, and mice received GMN orally at doses of 10 and 30 mg/kg. GMN targets 110 genes related to renal fibrosis that regulate profibrotic pathways, including TGF-β1-mediated canonical Smad signaling. GMN effectively attenuated TGF-β1-induced fibroblast-to-myofibroblast transition by inhibiting Smad signaling, resulting in downregulation of collagen I and fibronectin. In vivo, oral administration of GMN ameliorated the histopathological damage induced by UUO and significantly improved renal function. Mechanistically, GMN suppressed NF-κB-mediated priming of the NOD-like receptor pyrin domain-containing 3 (NLRP3) inflammasome and inhibited IL-1β maturation, thereby mitigating renal inflammation. UUO-induced fibrotic responses, characterized by upregulation of TGF-β1, TGF-β receptor type II, p-Smad2/3, connective tissue growth factor (CTGF), alpha-smooth muscle actin, and extracellular matrix (ECM) components were significantly attenuated by GMN, suggesting its ability to inhibit pathological ECM remodeling. This study demonstrates that GMN attenuates renal inflammation, suppresses myofibroblast activation and ECM remodeling by concurrently inhibiting NF-κB/NLRP3 inflammasome axis and TGF-β1/Smad pathway.

articles.title: Inflammasome-Related Transcriptomic Profiles in Periodontitis and Peri-Implantitis Reveal a Shared Inflammatory Framework: A Cross-Sectional Study.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: To compare clinical, histological, immunohistochemical, and targeted gene-expression features related to inflammasome signaling across healthy tissues, periodontitis, and peri-implantitis.

MATERIALS AND METHODS: This exploratory cross-sectional study included supracrestal soft-tissue biopsies from 6 healthy controls, 17 periodontitis, and 18 peri-implantitis lesions. Evaluations included clinical data, histomorphometric collagen quantification, immunohistochemical staining (CD45, NLRP3, AIM2, CASP1, IL-1β), and targeted digital transcriptomic profiling of 20 preselected inflammasome-related genes using the NanoString nCounter platform. Data were analyzed using non-parametric statistics and FDR-corrected correlation matrices.

RESULTS: Periodontitis and peri-implantitis showed greater clinical inflammation, reduced collagen content, and increased inflammatory infiltrate compared with healthy tissues. Peri-implantitis displayed the more severe clinical phenotype and greater tissue disruption. At the molecular level, disease-associated changes were captured by AIM2, CASP1, IL1B, GBP5, TXNIP, CGAS, STING1, and PANX1 rather than NLRP3 alone. Except for a minor pairwise difference in CGAS (p = 0.031), individual gene expression did not differ between the diseased states. Stratified correlation analyses demonstrated coordinated within-group co-expression networks among priming, sensor, and effector transcripts, reflecting descriptive pathway patterns within each clinical cohort.

CONCLUSIONS: Periodontitis and peri-implantitis share a substantial inflammasome-related host-response framework. Rather than revealing a distinct inflammasome program, peri-implantitis exhibits a largely overlapping molecular profile that occurs within a clinically more severe and structurally more disrupted lesion environment. These findings suggest that the biological distinction between the two diseases may lie less in pathway identity than in the tissue context in which a shared inflammatory machinery is expressed.

articles.title: Higher risk of Long COVID among patients with autoimmune rheumatic diseases and immunomodulatory therapy: a retrospective cohort analysis of national US data.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Little is known about the prevalence of and factors associated with Long COVID in patients with autoimmune rheumatic diseases (AIRDs).

METHODS: We conducted a retrospective cohort study using data from the National Clinical Cohort Collaborative (N3C). We included adults with a first documented SARS-CoV-2 infection between September 2021 and December 2023, with follow-up through December 2024. Long COVID was defined as ICD-10-CM code U09.9 or a Long COVID clinic visit occurring 28 to 365 days after first infection. We compared patients with AIRD with matched non-AIRD controls using 1:1 nearest-neighbor propensity score matching on age with exact matching on sex, race/ethnicity, SARS-CoV-2 variant-dominant period, and data-contributing organization. We estimated hazard ratios using multivariable Cox regression models. Among people with AIRD, we assessed risk by AIRD type and medication exposure before acute COVID-19.

RESULTS: In the matched cohort of 187,106 patients, Long COVID occurred in 2.8% of AIRD patients and 1.5% among non-AIRD patients. In multivariable analyses, AIRD was associated with an increased risk of Long COVID compared with non-AIRD patients (aHR 1.56, 95% CI 1.45-1.67). Among patients with AIRD, higher acute COVID-19 severity, pulmonary disease, obesity, and exposure to rituximab or glucocorticoids were associated with an increased risk of Long COVID. Sjögren's syndrome was associated with a higher risk of Long COVID.

CONCLUSION: The higher risk of developing Long COVID among AIRD patients compared with those without AIRD underscores the need to identify potential risk factors for Long COVID in this population to minimize its long-term effects.

articles.title: Meet the Editorial Team. An Interview With Prof David Greening, Associate Editor, Proteomics, Baker Heart and Diabetes Institute, Melbourne, Australia.
Clinical Implications of Interleukin-17 as a Hepato-Dermal Link in Patients With Psoriasis and Concomitant Steatotic Liver Disease.
articles.journal: Journal of cutaneous medicine and surgery
articles.abstract: Psoriasis is increasingly recognized as a systemic inflammatory disease with impacts beyond the skin and joints. Metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD) and excessive alcohol consumption are common in the psoriasis population, affecting up to two-thirds of patients. Interleukin-17 (IL-17) has been identified as a potential key pro-inflammatory link between psoriasis and MASLD. IL-17 levels have been positively correlated with progression of MASLD to more advanced forms of liver disease, including steatohepatitis, cirrhosis and hepatocellular carcinoma. Given the high prevalence of concurrent psoriasis and liver disease, dermatologists should have an elevated index of suspicion of MASLD in patients with psoriasis, particularly those with concomitant metabolic risk factors and/or excessive alcohol consumption. Using 3 parameters, the Fibrosis-4 index is a validated, non-invasive screening tool that can be implemented in clinical practice. With the wide variety of therapeutics available to treat psoriasis, practitioners should be mindful of systemic agents carrying potential hepatotoxic adverse effects and could consider instead implementation of advanced therapies that have neutral or potentially beneficial effects on the liver. There is emerging data, pending larger prospective confirmatory studies, that support consideration of IL-17 inhibitors as a reasonable option in appropriate patients with or at risk of MASLD.

articles.title: Topical Tacrolimus in Ocular Disease: A Narrative Review of Mechanism of Action and Therapeutic Applications.
articles.journal: Journal of ocular pharmacology and therapeutics : the official journal of the Association for Ocular Pharmacology and Therapeutics
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: Immune-mediated inflammatory disorders of the ocular surface and anterior segment frequently require sustained immunosuppression, yet prolonged topical corticosteroid use carries the risk of glaucoma, cataract, and infection. Tacrolimus, a macrolide calcineurin inhibitor, has emerged as a steroid-sparing alternative for T-cell-mediated ocular disease. This review summarizes the mechanism of action, ocular pharmacology, clinical applications, and safety profile of topical tacrolimus.

METHODS: Narrative synthesis of the peer-reviewed literature.

RESULTS: Tacrolimus binds the immunophilin FK506-binding protein 12; the resulting complex inhibits the phosphatase calcineurin, preventing dephosphorylation and nuclear translocation of the nuclear factor of activated T-cells (NFAT) and thereby suppressing transcription of interleukin-2 and a broad program of pro-inflammatory cytokines. The downstream result is reduced activation across the Th1, Th2, and Th17 lineages, diminished T-follicular helper and B-cell responses, stabilization of mast cells and eosinophils, and anti-angiogenic effects. Compounded topical formulations (typically 0.01%-0.1%) penetrate the cornea and reach therapeutic aqueous concentrations. Topical tacrolimus has shown efficacy in vernal and atopic keratoconjunctivitis, anterior uveitis, scleritis, ocular graft-versus-host disease, cicatrizing conjunctivitis, Thygeson superficial punctate keratitis, autoimmune polyglandular syndrome-1-associated keratitis, and corneal graft rejection.

CONCLUSIONS: Topical tacrolimus is an effective steroid-sparing immunomodulator for a broad spectrum of T-cell-mediated ocular disease, with a favorable safety profile notable for the absence of steroid-related rises in intraocular pressure or cataractogenesis. Standardized formulations and prospective comparative trials remain priorities.

articles.title: Orbital Abscess Complicating Allergic Fungal Rhinosinusitis Due to Streptococcus halichoeri: A Rare Zoonotic Sinonasal Infection.
articles.journal: The Annals of otology, rhinology, and laryngology
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Secondary bacterial infections complicating allergic fungal rhinosinusitis (AFRS) are uncommon but can be serious given the expansile nature of the disease which can thin and erode the bone separating the sinuses from the brain and orbits. Zoonotic pathogens are rarely implicated as pathogens.

CASE REPORT: A 21-year-old African American male with several years of progressive nasal obstruction, facial pressure, and hyposmia, presented emergently with acute left eye pain and swelling, diplopia, afferent pupillary defect and inferior visual field deficit. Computed tomography and magnetic resonance imaging demonstrated acute on chronic sinusitis with a left orbital abscess.
