The patient underwent emergent endoscopic sinus surgery with left orbitotomy and drainage of the orbital abscess. Intraoperative findings, pathology, cultures, and allergy testing were reviewed demonstrating AFRS and a novel zoonotic bacterium, Streptococcus halichoeri.

CONCLUSIONS: This case represents the first otolaryngologic case of S. halichoeri infection, a severe and complicated sinus and orbital infection. It is unclear if the severity of this infection was a consequence of the unusual pathogen, of the long-term thinning of the bone around the orbit, or both. Although AFRS is not considered an infection, secondary bacterial infection may occur and cause severe complications. Early surgical intervention and culture-directed therapy are essential in managing complicated sinonasal diseases.

articles.title: Enlicitide: The First Oral PCSK9i for Lowering Low-Density Lipoprotein Cholesterol.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: This article describes pharmacology, pharmacokinetics, safety, and efficacy data of enlicitide, the first Food and Drug Administration (FDA)-approved oral proprotein convertase subtilisin/kexin type 9 inhibitor (PCSK9i).

DATA SOURCES: PubMed, Embase, Web of Science, and Cochrane were searched through July 17, 2026.

STUDY SELECTION AND DATA EXTRACTION: Clinical trials published in English were included. Relevant information from the methodology and results was extracted.

DATA SYNTHESIS: Enlicitide received FDA approval on July 16, 2026, based on results from phase 2 and 3 trials showing a 57.1% to 64.6% reduction in low-density lipoprotein-cholesterol (LDL-C) and reduced other atherogenic lipid particles at 24 weeks in patients with hypercholesterolemia, including those with heterozygous familial hypercholesterolemia, while maintaining a favorable adverse effect profile. Enlicitide represents the fifth FDA-approved agent targeting PCSK9, having similar efficacy to other agents in class while having a novel macrocyclic peptide formulation with permeation enhancers, allowing for oral administration.Relevance to Patient Care and Clinical Practice in Comparison With Existing Drugs:As PCSK9is continue to be at the forefront of dyslipidemia guidelines, the approval of an oral agent is paramount in ensuring patient access. Enlicitide mirrors LDL-C lowering compared with existing PCSK9is and surpasses LDL-C lowering compared with non-statin options such as bempedoic acid and ezetimibe. Confirmation of cardiovascular outcomes data with enlicitide will solidify its role in reducing atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease risk.

CONCLUSION: Enlicitide significantly lowered LDL-C similar to existing PCSK9is with few adverse effects. The oral formulation provides an essential option for LDL-C lowering, especially in patients adverse to injections.

articles.title: A large audit of Cobas CT/NG screening and Xpert CT/NG supplemental testing reveals low confirmatory rates in oropharyngeal samples with evidence of commensal cross-reactivity with an isolate of Neisseria lactamica.
articles.abstract: Sensitive and high-throughput testing for Neisseria gonorrhoeae (NG) is widely underpinned by automated commercial solutions using nucleic acid amplification tests. We outline our experience of using Roche Cobas 8800 CT/NG (Cobas NG) for primary testing of NG at scale. Over 360000 specimens were tested over a three-year period. A disproportionate number of 'indeterminate' oropharyngeal swabs (25%) tested positive by Cobas NG but failed to confirm by Xpert CT/NG, significantly higher than genital samples (4%) (chi-square p-value <0.05). Such samples are highly problematic, as they fail to provide a definitive result for the patient. To investigate this non-specificity, publicly available sequences for Cobas NG DR-9 targets were aligned with Neisseria genome databases. We found a strain of Neisseria lactamica (PubMLST 49718), isolated from a throat swab, which was predicted to cross-react with Cobas NG. We subsequently confirmed a Cobas NG false-positive result with this isolate. BLAST analysis showed the target gene NG DR-9 was rare among available non-NG Neisseria whole genome sequences. This may suggest the existence of an as-yet unknown and difficult to cultivate oral commensal that contains NG DR-9. Our findings further highlight the need for NG confirmatory testing of oropharyngeal samples screened with Cobas NG.

articles.title: Burden of healthcare-associated infections in tertiary care hospitals in six countries of the Gulf Cooperation Council: A point prevalence survey.
articles.abstract: A cross-sectional study using point prevalence survey (PPS) methodology was conducted on May 20, 2024, at 18 tertiary care hospitals located in the 6 Gulf Cooperation Council (GCC) countries to assess the prevalence of healthcare-associated infections (HAIs) and associated pathogens. The measured outcome was the presence of active HAIs in different hospital units. During the PPS day, 651 HAI events were detected among 580 patients after reviewing the information of 6826 patients. The prevalence of patients with HAIs was 8.5% (95% CI 7.8%-9.2%). The prevalence was higher in older patients (11.8%, 95% CI 10.2%-13.4%), in intensive care units (24.6%, 95% CI 21.5%-27.8%), and in specialty care areas (12.7%, 95% CI 9.8%-15.7%). The most frequent type of HAIs was pneumonia (27.8%), followed by bloodstream infection (25.0%), urinary tract infection (10.9%), and skin infection (9.7%). Device-associated HAIs represented 15.4% of all HAIs, with ventilator-associated pneumonia, central line-associated bloodstream infection, and catheter-associated urinary tract infection being the main types. Approximately 61.9% of HAIs were microbiologically confirmed. Out of them, 65.3% were caused by Gram-negative bacteria and 31.8% were caused by multidrug-resistant pathogens. The findings confirm that the high HAI burden in GCC hospitals is higher in high-resource countries but lower in lower/middle-resource countries.

articles.title: Presence of post-COVID-19 condition in six ethnic groups in Amsterdam, the Netherlands: a retrospectively reconstructed time interval approach.
articles.abstract: In this retrospective cohort study, we assessed the prevalence of post-COVID-19 condition (PCC) and its determinants among six ethnic groups in Amsterdam, the Netherlands. We analysed data from participants of the HELIUS cohort with SARS-CoV-2 infection who answered questions on the presence and duration of COVID-19-related symptoms between May and November 2022. We estimated the prevalence of PCC, defined as having ≥1 of 15 pre-determined COVID-19-related symptoms remaining for at least 3 months after infection, by ethnicity at several timepoints since infection adjusted for age and sex, and assessed determinants of PCC overall using logistic regression. Of 932 infected participants, 31% [95% confidence interval (95%CI): 27%-37%] developed PCC. At 3 months after infection the adjusted prevalence of PCC varied from 17% (95%CI: 13%-24%) in the Dutch-origin group to 41% (95%CI: 34%-48%) in the South-Asian Surinamese group, and was significantly higher among participants of South-Asian Surinamese, Turkish and Moroccan origin compared to those of Dutch origin (all P < 0.001). Participants who were of South-Asian Surinamese origin, older, female, without a vocational education or university degree, or obese were more likely to have PCC. Those of Ghanaian origin or infected during the period of Omicron predominance were less likely to have PCC. There were clear between-ethnic differences in the prevalence of PCC, which was more common in individuals of South-Asian Surinamese, Turkish, and Moroccan origin compared to those of Dutch origin. These differences mirror ethnic differences in SARS-CoV-2 infection and disease severity. Certain factors of PCC emerged, while consistent across ethnic groups.

articles.title: Modernizing Canada's Regulations for Clinical Trials in Medical Emergencies.
articles.journal: The Canadian journal of neurological sciences. Le journal canadien des sciences neurologiques

articles.title: Landscape of Canadian Stroke Motor and Cognitive Rehabilitation Trials: Trends, Strengths and Future Directions.
articles.journal: The Canadian journal of neurological sciences. Le journal canadien des sciences neurologiques
articles.abstract: This study aims to systematically identify and describe all randomized controlled trials (RCTs) evaluating post-stroke motor and cognitive rehabilitation conducted in Canada, within the broader context of global post-stroke rehabilitation research. The present secondary descriptive/bibliometric analysis used data derived from five integrated systematic reviews conducted by the same research group, from inception to 2024. A subset of data was examined in Canadian trials, including number of RCTs, sample size, participant sex, time post-stroke, methodological quality, intervention types and outcome measures. In total, 106 out of 3602 global RCTs were conducted in Canada. Canadian RCT relative contribution to global research has slowed down over time. Sample size was significantly smaller in the chronic post-stroke phase compared to acute and subacute phases in both Canadian (p = 0.013) and global trials (p < 0.001). Compared to global trials, Canadian RCTs had comparable sample size (p = 0.72) and methodological quality (p = 0.94) but were more likely to be conducted in the chronic phase (p = 0.001), evaluate exercise-based and rehabilitation-oriented interventions and assess activity and participation outcome measures. Chronic trials were more likely to be led by academic therapists (p = 0.031), while the acute and subacute trials were more likely to be led by academic physicians (p = 0.003). Canadian RCTs have made important contributions to stroke rehabilitation research. However, expanding research into earlier recovery phases, integrating technology-driven interventions and incorporating outcome measures across all three International Classification of Functioning, Disability and Health domains will be important to strengthening Canada's impact and advancing stroke rehabilitation evidence.

articles.title: Impact of Socioeconomic Status and Rurality on the Rate of Prenatal Detection of Major and Critical Congenital Heart Disease in Western Australia.
articles.journal: Journal of paediatrics and child health
articles.abstract:
AIM: Prenatal diagnosis of congenital heart disease (CHD) is associated with reduced infant morbidity and mortality. Location and subsequent socioeconomic status influence rates and timing of prenatal diagnoses of CHD. We investigated the impact of socioeconomic status and rurality on the rate of prenatal diagnosis of critical and major CHD in Western Australia (WA).

METHODS: This retrospective cross-sectional study reviewed all critical (surgical intervention ≤ 30 days of life) and major (surgical intervention ≤ 1 year of life) CHD in WA between 2017 and 2021. Patients were identified from the WA Fetal Cardiology and Perth Children's Hospital Cardiology Databases. Clinical records were used to identify diagnoses, outcomes, postcode, rurality (via the Modified Monash Model [MMM]) and socioeconomic status (Socio-Economic Indexes for Areas [SEIFA] Index of Relative Socio-economic Disadvantage). Postcode was used to estimate SEIFA index and MMM rurality.

RESULTS: There were 478 cases with major CHD; 282 (59%) were prenatally diagnosed, of which 268 cases were critical CHD, with a 77% detection rate. Seventy-four percent of patients were from metropolitan areas. The distribution of SEIFA decile (p = 0.15) and MMM (p = 0.09) were not significantly different between pre- and postnatal groups. The diagnosis rate of univentricular CHD was 94% (n = 102) and 49% (n = 180) for CHD undergoing biventricular repair.

CONCLUSION: Critical CHD increases the likelihood of prenatal diagnosis in WA; however, rurality and socioeconomic status were not found to influence diagnosis rates. Further studies are needed to review the availability of obstetric services in rural communities to ensure equitable healthcare.

articles.title: Use of Telestroke Prior to Endovascular Stroke Treatment in Canada: Results from the OPTIMISE Registry.
articles.journal: The Canadian journal of neurological sciences. Le journal canadien des sciences neurologiques
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Telestroke allows rapid assessment of acute stroke patients for intravenous thrombolysis and endovascular thrombectomy (EVT). While its safety and efficacy for thrombolysis are well established, evidence regarding EVT decision-making via telestroke is scarce.

METHODS: We analysed data from Optimising Patient Treatment In Major Ischaemic Stroke with EVT (OPTIMISE), an EVT registry of Canadian comprehensive stroke centres. We compared unadjusted time metrics and procedural outcomes between patients treated with EVT evaluated via telestroke and those evaluated without telestroke. A primary analysis included all EVT cases, and a sub-analysis focused on patients transferred from another centre. Mixed-effects logistic regression, adjusted for relevant clinical and radiological confounders, was used to assess symptomatic intracerebral haemorrhage (sICH), good functional outcome and all-cause mortality.

RESULTS: Between 2018 and 2021, a total of 6803 patients received EVT across 20 centres. Patients receiving telestroke consultation had longer onset-to-EVT centre door time and onset-to-groin puncture time. In unadjusted analyses, telestroke patients had higher sICH proportions (6.5% vs. 3.1%), lower proportions of good functional outcomes (35.6% vs. 40.6%) and higher all-cause mortality (39.9% vs. 27.5%) compared to those not receiving telestroke consultation. These differences did not persist in adjusted analyses. The sub-analysis with multivariate adjustment restricted to transferred patients also revealed no differences in outcomes between the two groups.

CONCLUSION: Patients evaluated with telestroke prior to EVT had longer treatment times than those not evaluated with telestroke. The higher risk for unfavourable outcomes did not persist after adjustment for confounders. There remains a strong need to optimise the delivery of EVT for patients evaluated at telestroke centres.

articles.title: High Yield of Pharmacogenetic Testing for Clopidogrel Resistance in a Canadian Outpatient Stroke Population.
articles.journal: The Canadian journal of neurological sciences. Le journal canadien des sciences neurologiques
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Clopidogrel is commonly prescribed for secondary stroke prevention, but routine pharmacogenetic testing is not typically performed. As the CYP2C19 enzyme activates clopidogrel into its effective form, clopidogrel-treated patients who carry CYP2C19 loss-of-function alleles may face an increased risk of recurrent stroke. We examined the prevalence of CYP2C19 loss-of-function variants and their potential influence on patient management within a Canadian stroke clinic population.

METHODS: We randomly selected and invited outpatients attending a regional stroke prevention clinic in Toronto, Canada, who had a non-cardioembolic ischemic stroke or transient ischemic attack and were prescribed clopidogrel for secondary stroke prevention. Participants completed a self-administered home DNA test (cheek swab) to determine their CYP2C19 status. The primary outcome was the prevalence of intermediate or poor metabolizers. The secondary outcome was the proportion of participants whose antiplatelet regimen was changed as a result of the testing.

RESULTS: Among 93 eligible participants who underwent the test (mean age 68.1; female 37.6%), 31 (33.3%) were intermediate metabolizers, 8 (8.6%) were poor metabolizers, 20 (21.5%) were rapid metabolizers, 9 (9.7%) were ultrarapid metabolizers and 25 (26.9%) were normal metabolizers. In 8 (100.0%) of the poor metabolizers and 20 (64.5%) of the intermediate metabolizers, treating physicians changed their antiplatelet prescriptions based on the test results.

CONCLUSION: In this cohort of post-stroke patients treated with clopidogrel, genetic testing showed a high prevalence (41.9%) of intermediate or poor clopidogrel metabolizers, resulting in a change in antiplatelet therapy prescriptions in over 70% of those cases. These findings have implications for secondary stroke prevention.

articles.title: Infection-Phase Biomolecular Coronas in Inhaled Nanomedicine.
articles.abstract: An inhaled nanomedicine encounters two successive forms of remodeling: device-related changes during aerosol generation and biological conditioning after deposition. Respiratory infection adds a moving interface, as epithelial secretion, surfactant composition, plasma leakage, and neutrophil-derived material vary across airway compartments and over time. Pulmonary and disease-corona studies already establish that host environments influence nanoparticle identity. The next question is how this knowledge should change formulation selection and dosing for infected lungs. We propose an infection-phase framework based on measured, overlapping airway environments. It connects the post-aerosol particle to its surface-associated biomolecules, distinguishes this interface from aggregation and bulk mucus effects, and links analytical measurements to functional delivery. A staged research program begins with one compartment and two contrasting environments, then adds controlled particle-transfer experiments, candidate-component perturbation, and donor-level validation. Lipid nanoparticles, polymeric carriers, and nanozymes require different functional endpoints within this shared framework. The immediate translational output is a biorelevant performance stress test that identifies robust or environment-selective formulations and guides the next experiment.

articles.title: Development and psychometric validation of a barrier assessment tool for adherence to prescribed medication regimens in post-PCI patients.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Coronary artery disease (CAD) is a leading cause of morbidity and mortality worldwide, affecting approximately 197 million people and causing over 9 million deaths annually. Although percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) improves survival, medication non-adherence affects more than one-quarter of patients after myocardial infarction. Validated instruments assessing multidimensional adherence barriers in post-PCI patients remain limited. This study developed and validated the Post-PCI Barrier Scale for Adherence to Prescribed Medication Regimens (PCI-BSAR).

METHODS: A methodological cross-sectional study was conducted in a tertiary care cardiology outpatient department. Questionnaire items were generated through literature review, patient interviews, and the WHO multidimensional adherence framework. Content validity, pilot testing (n = 50), exploratory factor analysis, reliability testing, and measurement model assessment were performed in 253 post-PCI patients.

RESULTS: The final 23-item PCI-BSAR demonstrated excellent content validity (S-CVI/Ave = 0.92). Exploratory factor analysis identified four domains: patient- and clinical-related, treatment and healthcare interaction-related, socioeconomic, and healthcare access and system-related barriers, explaining 69.6% of the variance. The questionnaire showed high internal consistency (Cronbach's α = 0.909), composite reliability (0.848-0.938), AVE >0.50, and HTMT <0.85.

CONCLUSION: PCI-BSAR is a reliable and valid instrument for identifying multidimensional medication adherence barriers in post-PCI patients and may support individualized adherence assessment during routine outpatient follow-up.

articles.title: Host Genetics and Gastric Cancer Risk beyond Helicobacter pylori Infection.
Rotating Frame Spin-Lock Cardiac MRI Method at 9.4 T Can Characterize Diffuse Fibrosis in Progressing Hypertensive Heart Disease in Mice.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: This study aimed to investigate the applicability of rotating frame spin-lock continuous wave (CW) T1ρ and relaxation along a fictitious field with Rank 2 (RAFF2) methods complementary to native T1 and late gadolinium enhancement (LGE) for cardiac magnetic resonance imaging (CMRI) of diffuse fibrosis in mice with advancing hypertensive heart disease (HHD) and diastolic dysfunction.

METHODS: HHD was induced in mice with angiotensin II infusion for 28 days; sham operated were used as controls. Phenotype progression was assessed with echocardiography. Characterization of diffuse fibrosis was performed with CMRI. CW-T1ρ and RAFF2 were compared with native T1 and LGE acquired on Days 14 and 28 of the experiment. Regions of interest in CMRI relaxation time maps and Picrosirius red-stained histological cardiac sections were compared.

RESULTS: Diffuse fibrosis in the left ventricle was visible on Day 14 with TRAFF2 relaxation time maps in the HHD group with early diastolic impairment, and CW-T1ρ showed a slight increase. Both CW-T1ρ and TRAFF2 showed elevated values on Day 28 in HHD mice, whereas native T1 showed an increase only on Day 28. LGE showed no accumulation. The presence of diffuse fibrosis was verified with cardiac histology.

CONCLUSIONS: Rotating frame spin-lock CW-T1ρ and RAFF2 are more sensitive to native T1 and LGE in the characterization of diffuse fibrosis in advancing HHD in mice, being an alternative for the imaging of fibrotic remodeling also in other cardiac pathologies.

articles.title: Transition-Specific Associations of Cardiometabolic Biomarker Burden With Cardio-Renal-Metabolic Multimorbidity Progression: A Multistate Cohort Study.
articles.abstract:
AIMS: To identify representative cardiometabolic biomarkers and examine how individual biomarkers and combined biomarker burden are associated with transition-specific progression of cardio-renal-metabolic multimorbidity (CRMM).

METHODS: This prospective cohort study included 262 464 UK Biobank participants free of cardiovascular disease (CVD), type 2 diabetes (T2D) and chronic kidney disease (CKD) at baseline. Forty-nine candidate biomarkers across five domains, including inflammation, insulin resistance, dyslipidemia, adiposity and blood pressure, were evaluated using time-dependent area under the curve and concordance index to select representative markers. Multistate models estimated associations of individual biomarkers, elevated-marker count and a weighted 5-Item Cardiometabolic Risk Score (5-CMRS) with sequential transitions from baseline to first cardio-renal-metabolic disease (FCRMD), FCRMD to Double CRMD and Double to Triple CRMD.

RESULTS: During a median follow-up of 15.62 years, 44 339 participants developed FCRMD, 7218 progressed to Double CRMD and 721 progressed to Triple CRMD. Five representative biomarkers were selected: C-reactive protein-to-albumin ratio, metabolic score for insulin resistance (METS-IR), triglyceride-to-HDL cholesterol ratio, waist-to-height ratio and systolic blood pressure. Higher elevated-marker count showed graded associations across all transitions. Compared with the lowest 5-CMRS category, the highest category was associated with hazard ratios of 2.80, 1.84 and 1.71 for the three sequential transitions. Disease-specific analyses showed the strongest associations with incident T2D. METS-IR showed the largest relative contributions across all transitions, whereas additive interactions were mainly observed during early CRMM progression.

CONCLUSION: Combined cardiometabolic biomarker burden was associated with graded, transition-specific risks across CRMM progression, supporting integrated cardiometabolic risk assessment across inflammatory, metabolic, adiposity, lipid and blood-pressure domains.

articles.title: Evaluation of different amplification targets for the detection of Necator americanus by PCR in stool samples.
articles.abstract: Hookworm infection, caused by Necator americanus and Ancylostoma duodenale, is prevalent in areas with poor sanitation. Coprology is the gold standard for diagnosis, but it has low sensitivity in low parasite loads. The objective of this study was to evaluate four Polymerase Chain Reaction (PCR) targets for molecular diagnosis. Stool samples were collected from 180 residents of the rural community Tierra Blanca, Bolívar State, Venezuela, in which coproparasitological tests were performed. Four DNA extraction methods were standardized, and four PCR techniques were studied: NaITS1F/NaITS1R (ITS1), Na58/Na158R (ITS2), NA/NC2 (ITS2-28S) and NC1/NC2 (ITS2-28S) for N. americanus. Only two of these techniques could be standardized and evaluated, as amplification was not achieved with the other two. The two standardized techniques were applied to all samples, and diagnostic indices were obtained. The results showed that extraction with the Wizard kit was the most suitable due to the quality of the DNA obtained. Primer analysis revealed high identity, but with sequences mainly from Asia and Africa, since there are very few available from America. PCR-NaITS1F/NaITS1R (ITS1) demonstrated the best diagnostic indices, significantly surpassing coprology. PCR-Na58/Na158R (ITS2) showed lower sensitivity than coprology. Therefore, PCR-NaITS1F/NaITS1R (ITS1) is recommended for molecular diagnosis. The prevalence of N. americanus in the Tierra Blanca community was 20.6 % by coprology, 88.3 % by PCR-NaITS1F/NaITS1R (ITS1) and 94.4% by the combination of these techniques. The high prevalence of infections underscores the need for molecular techniques but these must be previously evaluated with samples from the regions where they will be used.

articles.title: Development and validation of a multibiomarker model for 12-month adverse outcomes in acute heart failure.
articles.abstract:
AIMS: To develop a multibiomarker model for predicting 12-month major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE) in patients with acute heart failure (AHF) and assess incremental value.

MATERIALS AND METHODS: This study included 675 patients with AHF, comprising a development cohort (n = 303) and a validation cohort (n = 372). MACE comprised all-cause death or heart failure rehospitalization. Least absolute shrinkage and selection operator Cox regression and multivariable Cox regression were used for model development. Model performance was assessed using discrimination, calibration, decision curve analysis (DCA), and incremental value.

RESULTS: The final model included monocyte-to-lymphocyte ratio (MLR), N-terminal pro-B-type natriuretic peptide (NT-proBNP), heparin-binding protein (HBP), and soluble suppression of tumorigenicity 2 (sST2). Harrell's concordance index, the 12-month area under the time-dependent receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC), and Brier score were 0.710, 0.804, and 0.180 in the development cohort and 0.710, 0.760, and 0.203 in the validation cohort, respectively. Calibration demonstrated overall agreement between predicted and observed risks, and DCA suggested potential clinical net benefit. Adding HBP, sST2, and MLR to clinical variables and NT-proBNP increased the 12-month AUC from 0.753 to 0.824.

CONCLUSIONS: The multibiomarker model showed moderate predictive performance and may support post-discharge risk stratification in patients with AHF.

articles.title: Thirty years of scholarship in JDSDE: a systematic mapping review.
articles.journal: Journal of deaf studies and deaf education
articles.abstract: This study presents a journal-lifespan systematic mapping review of scholarship published in The Journal of Deaf Studies and Deaf Education (JDSDE) from 1996 to 2025. As a major interdisciplinary venue for research on Deaf individuals, language, literacy, development, and education, JDSDE provides a valuable archive for examining how the field has evolved across three decades. All issues from Volume 1 through Volume 30, Issue 1 were hand-searched, yielding 990 published items. Of these, 810 empirical articles were analyzed for participant characteristics, national and educational contexts, methodological orientations, research designs, and data sources. Publication-level variables, including article type, research focus, authorship, and collaboration patterns, were analyzed across the full corpus. Descriptive statistics and dictionary-assisted thematic mapping were used to identify overall and period-based trends. Findings show that JDSDE has sustained a strong intellectual core around sign language and linguistics, literacy and language arts, and early intervention and family, while also responding to field-level changes, including the rise of hearing technology and implants. Authorship shifted toward multi-authored and cross-institutional collaboration. Empirical articles remained centered on K-12 students, U.S.-based contexts, and quantitative designs, despite modest international, contextual, and methodological diversification.

articles.title: Pediatric Disaster Preparedness at Rural and Critical Access Hospitals: A Mixed-Methods Study.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: Over 80% of pediatric emergency department (ED) visits in the United States occur outside of children's hospitals. Although previous studies have described gaps in pediatric readiness, few studies have focused on pediatric disaster preparedness at rural and critical access hospitals (CAHs). During periods of pediatric surge, CAHs may be forced to manage pediatric patients with delayed transfer times. This mixed-methods study, conducted by the Region V for Kids (RV4K) Pediatric Disaster Center of Excellence, elicited strengths and barriers to pediatric disaster preparedness in rural and CAHs.

METHODS: We conducted a qualitative study of clinicians from CAHs in the Health Resources and Services Administration (HRSA) Region 5. After completing a demographic survey, respondents were invited to participate in focus groups about pediatric disaster preparedness, followed by an open-response questionnaire about how RV4K can support rural and CAHs. Descriptive statistics were calculated. Focus group transcripts and questionnaire responses were analyzed using a constant comparative approach to identify themes.

RESULTS: Of the 41 survey respondents, 19 participated in focus groups. Most study participants worked at EDs seeing <1800 children per year, and less than half had pediatric inpatient capabilities. Few hospital disaster plans considered children. Four focus group themes emerged: strengths of staff and community, staffing limitations, and desire for targeted pediatric education resources and pediatric disaster plan development.

CONCLUSIONS: Our study engaged directly with staff at rural and CAHs to gain insights about pediatric preparedness that will be used to develop resources specifically tailored to CAHs' unique clinical needs.

articles.title: Hybrid Molecular Imaging Using PET/CT and PET/MRI in Inflammatory Bowel Disease: Current Applications, Challenges, and Future Perspectives.
articles.journal: Medical science monitor : international medical journal of experimental and clinical research
articles.abstract: Hybrid molecular imaging is increasingly recognized as a valuable tool for the precision management of inflammatory bowel disease (IBD). Driven by the treat-to-target paradigm, the noninvasive quantification of transmural inflammation and the accurate differentiation of stricture phenotypes remain key clinical challenges. Current evidence indicates that although 2-deoxy-2-¹⁸F-fluoro-D-glucose (¹⁸F-FDG) positron emission tomography (PET) can effectively quantify the overall inflammatory burden, the integration of fibroblast activation protein inhibitor (FAPI)-targeted PET imaging provides important complementary value for characterizing fibro-inflammatory remodeling and distinguishing fibrotic strictures. By combining high metabolic sensitivity with high-resolution multiparametric soft-tissue characterization, PET/magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) has demonstrated potential advantages in assessing penetrating complications and facilitating longitudinal therapeutic monitoring. Pediatric and young adult patients requiring long-term follow-up may derive substantial benefit from the reduced radiation exposure offered by integrated PET/MRI systems. To overcome conventional method limitations, including physiologic intestinal uptake and attenuation-correction artifacts, the field is actively exploring novel molecularly targeted tracers, ultra-low-dose long-axial-field-of-view whole-body systems, and artificial intelligence-based image reconstruction techniques. Given that substantial current evidence is derived from small, single-center cohorts and experimental studies, these advanced modalities currently serve as adjunctive, problem-solving tools rather than routine replacements for standard endoscopy or conventional cross-sectional imaging. This review comprehensively evaluates the clinical performance, applicability, and translational barriers of hybrid molecular imaging in IBD, underscoring the urgent need to establish standardized, multicenter consensus protocols that can guide its future implementation in individualized therapeutic strategies.

articles.title: Temporary mechanical circulatory support in cardiogenic shock.
articles.abstract: Cardiogenic shock (CS) remains a heterogeneous syndrome associated with persistently high mortality despite advances in temporary mechanical circulatory support. One recent randomized controlled trial suggested a mortality benefit of a percutaneous microaxial flow pump in a cohort of patients with ST-elevation myocardial infarction complicated by CS, whereas routine veno-arterial extracorporeal membrane oxygenation in populations with acute myocardial infarction complicated by CS has not improved survival and is associated with higher complication rates. These findings underscore the importance of phenotype-driven patient selection, incorporating the Society for Cardiovascular Angiography and Interventions (SCAI) and Shock Academic Research Consortium (SHARC) classifications to guide device selection, timing, escalation, and de-escalation. This clinical consensus statement from the European Association of Percutaneous Cardiovascular Interventions (EAPCI) and the Association for Acute CardioVascular Care (ACVC) of the European Society of Cardiology (ESC) updates the 2020 expert consensus document and provides updated practical guidance based on the recent evidence on the use of temporary mechanical circulatory support in acute myocardial infarction complicated by CS. Emphasis is placed on patient/device selection according to recent evidence, multidisciplinary shock teams, regionalized hub-and-spoke systems, structured protocols for escalation and futility, and the integration of contemporary trial data and best practices to optimize outcomes in this high-risk population.

articles.title: Impact of the Extent, Pattern, and Location of Replacement Myocardial Fibrosis on Clinical Outcomes in Aortic Regurgitation.
articles.abstract:
AIMS: The prognostic significance of late gadolinium enhancement (LGE)-detected replacement myocardial fibrosis in aortic regurgitation (AR) remains incompletely understood. This study aims to explore the association between the extent, pattern, and location of LGE and clinical outcomes in patients with chronic AR.

METHODS AND RESULTS: Between 2010 and 2024, consecutive patients with moderate-to-severe AR and no significant coronary artery stenosis who underwent contrast-enhanced cardiac magnetic resonance (CMR) were included. The primary endpoint was major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE), defined as cardiovascular mortality, heart transplantation, or rehospitalization for heart failure. The association between LGE characteristics and MACE was evaluated. Overall, 363 patients (mean age 52.6 ± 14.2 years; 54 female) were included. Over a median follow-up of 56.6 months, 73 patients experienced MACE. LGE was present in 200 patients (55.1%). An LGE extent threshold of 2.6% provided robust risk stratification, yielding the highest C-index of 0.797, a likelihood ratio chi-square of 97.30, and the lowest Akaike information criterion of 681.06. Furthermore, predominant subendocardial-involved LGE was present in 13.5% of LGE-positive patients and was independently associated with MACE after adjusting for LGE extent (HR 3.028; 95% CI 1.216-7.539; P = 0.017). Kaplan-Meier analysis demonstrated that patients with both LGE extent >2.6% and predominant subendocardial-involved LGE pattern were at the highest risk of MACE.

CONCLUSIONS: In AR, an LGE extent > 2.6% predicts MACE better than LGE presence alone. Furthermore, non-ischemic predominant subendocardial-involved LGE is independently associated with MACE. The coexistence of both features further amplifies the risk of MACE.

articles.title: Iopanoic Acid in Severe Thyrotoxicosis: Rediscovering an Effective Therapy.
articles.journal: The Journal of clinical endocrinology and metabolism
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Severe thyrotoxicosis remains a high-risk endocrine emergency, particularly in thyroid storm and amiodarone-induced thyrotoxicosis (AIT), where morbidity and mortality remain substantial despite modern intensive care. Rapid reduction of circulating triiodothyronine (T3) is central to stabilization, yet conventional therapies are often slow, unpredictable, or ineffective, particularly in iodine-replete states such as AIT.

SUMMARY: We reviewed mechanistic, pharmacokinetic and clinical evidence for iopanoic acid, a potent inhibitor of type I and type II 5'-deiodinase that produces rapid, reversible suppression of peripheral thyroxine (T4) to T3 conversion, alongside comparative rescue strategies including Lugol's iodine, perchlorate, lithium, cholestyramine and therapeutic plasma exchange. Across early clinical studies and a contemporary tertiary-center case series, short-course iopanoic acid consistently produced large, rapid reductions in serum T3, typically within 24-48 hours, with parallel clinical improvement. In a recent series of 12 patients with treatment-resistant thyrotoxicosis, mean free T3 fell by approximately 55%, normalizing within a median of 2 days and enabling progression to definitive surgery in most cases. Reported use extends beyond thyroid storm to urgent pre-operative preparation of uncontrolled hyperthyroidism, amiodarone-induced thyrotoxicosis and destructive thyroiditis. Adverse effects are uncommon and generally mild, and withdrawal from routine clinical use reflects the obsolescence of oral cholecystography rather than safety concerns.

CONCLUSIONS: Iopanoic acid offers safe, rapid and predictable T3 reduction as short-course rescue or bridging therapy in thyroid storm and refractory, iodine-unresponsive AIT, where it can be lifesaving. It is not recommended for straightforward thyrotoxicosis. We synthesize the evidence into a pragmatic, protocol-based framework and argue that reliable, appropriately governed sourcing is now the principal barrier to its use.

articles.title: Health Outcomes and Medical Response in Military Maneuvers: A Study of Morbidity, Treatment, and Evacuation.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Military maneuvers represent a health care challenge: They are essential for preventing occupational accidents and providing rapid and appropriate care for injuries and conditions resulting from physical exertion and extreme environments.

OBJECTIVE: To describe and analyze medical support during military maneuvers and evaluate morbidity, treatments applied, and evacuation protocols in units from the Ceuta Command.

METHODS: A prospective, observational, and analytical study was conducted over 2 weeks of maneuvers in Zaragoza, Spain. Demographic and clinical variables were included (type of injury, treatment, need for evacuation, and follow-up). Statistical analysis employed descriptive statistics and comparative tests (χ2 test and Student t test), considering P < .05 as the level of significance.

RESULTS: A total of 219 medical consultations were recorded. Traumatic injuries accounted for 46.1% of the cases, followed by infections (20.1%). Only 6.8% required medical evacuation, and 14.2% required subsequent follow-up, demonstrating the effectiveness of in-field management (P < .05).

CONCLUSIONS: Medical support deployed during the maneuvers presented a high rate of in-field resolution (93%) and confirmed that traumatic injuries are the leading cause of consultation. These findings highlight the need to maintain robust health care protocols and strengthen preventive measures to reduce morbidity in future exercises, directly addressing the objectives set.

articles.title: Pediatric Infectious Encephalitis in Spain: Etiology, Outcomes and Acyclovir Use in Emergency Departments.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Pediatric infectious encephalitis remains a significant cause of neurologic morbidity. Prompt antiviral treatment is recommended in patients with suspected herpes simplex virus (HSV) encephalitis. This study aimed to describe the epidemiology and outcomes of infectious encephalitis and to evaluate acyclovir use in children with suspected encephalitis presenting to the pediatric emergency department (PED).

METHODS: We conducted a multicenter, retrospective, cross-sectional study involving 10 Spanish PEDs (2017-2023), including children ≤18 years who underwent cerebrospinal fluid polymerase chain reaction testing as part of the evaluation of a possible central nervous system infection. Patients meeting the International Encephalitis Consortium (IEC) criteria for infectious encephalitis were analyzed, and acyclovir prescription rates were assessed.

RESULTS: We registered 446 episodes; 118 patients (26.5%) met the IEC criteria, and 88 (74.6%) had microbiologic confirmation. The most common pathogens were enterovirus (43.2%), influenza virus (18.2%) and HSV (9.0%). Thirty-seven patients (31.4%) had an adverse outcome, including 75% of those with HSV infection. Acyclovir was administered to 56.9% and 53.1% of patients with and without an altered mental status, respectively. All patients meeting IEC criteria presented with altered mental status and ≥1 minor criterion at evaluation in the PED.

CONCLUSIONS: Enteroviruses were the leading cause of pediatric infectious encephalitis, whereas HSV infection was associated with the highest risk of adverse outcomes. Acyclovir use in the PED was suboptimal and poorly aligned with clinical criteria. Our findings suggest that empirical acyclovir should be considered in patients with altered mental status and at least one minor criterion, whereas it may be unnecessary in the absence of these features.

articles.title: Nonselective beta-blockers and hepatic encephalopathy in liver cirrhosis:A meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials.
articles.journal: Journal of the Chinese Medical Association : JCMA
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Liver cirrhosis leads to portal hypertension and related complications, including ascites, esophageal varices, and hepatic encephalopathy (HE). Non-selective beta blockers (NSBBs) decrease portal pressure, but it is not yet clear whether they contribute to HE development. Therefore, we examined the association between NSBB therapy and HE in randomized controlled trials (RCTs) involving patients with cirrhosis.

METHODS: We systematically searched PubMed, Web of Science, ScienceDirect, and the Cochrane Library (from inception to December 31, 2024) for RCTs comparing NSBBs with a placebo, endoscopic band ligation, or injection sclerotherapy for variceal bleeding prevention in relation to HE. The risk ratios (RRs) and 95% confidence intervals (CIs) were pooled using a random-effects model. Subgroups were defined according to the comparator, NSBB type, and hepatic function status (weighted mean Child-Pugh score ≤6 vs. >6). The risk of bias was assessed using the revised Cochrane risk-of-bias tool for randomized trials (RoB 2).

RESULTS: There were 12 relevant studies, which included 775 NSBB-treated and 771 comparator patients (54 and 57 HE events). NSBB therapy was not associated with a statistically significant change in HE risk (RR 1.04, 95% CI 0.73-1.47; p = 0.84; I² = 0%). Estimates were consistent across all subgroups of hepatic function statuses (compensation, RR 1.18, 0.44-3.14; decompensation, RR 1.02, 0.70-1.48; p = 0.79), comparators (placebo, RR 1.19, 0.79-1.80; endoscopic therapy, RR 0.72, 0.38-1.39; p = 0.20), and NSBB types (propranolol/timolol, RR 1.06, 0.72-1.55; carvedilol, RR 0.95, 0.42-2.15; p = 0.82).

CONCLUSION: Current evidence does not indicate a statistically significant association between NSBB therapy and HE development in patients with cirrhosis, regardless of disease severity.

articles.title: Post-COVID-19 Patterns of Respiratory Viruses in South African Children With Acute Respiratory Illness.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The COVID-19 pandemic disrupted respiratory virus epidemiology. We describe the postpandemic prevalence, seasonality and clinical presentation of viral respiratory tract infections (RTIs) among hospitalized South African children.

METHODS: Children 0-<13 years of age with acute RTIs were prospectively enrolled between October 2024 and October 2025. Nasopharyngeal aspirates were collected on admission and tested for 7 common respiratory viruses using a multiplex real-time polymerase chain reaction. Clinical, demographic and outcome data were recorded. Disease severity was classified as mild, moderate or severe based on the need for hospitalization, respiratory support, intensive care or major complications. Cluster analysis identified distinct clinical phenotypes.

RESULTS: We enrolled 315 children, median age 9.3 months [interquartile range 3.6-24.7, 132/315 (41.9%) female, 7/315 (2.2%) living with HIV and 53/315 (16.8%) HIV-exposed but uninfected. Disease severity was mild in 55 (17.5%), moderate in 184 (58.4%) and severe in 76 (24.1%) children. Respiratory viruses were detected in 276/315 (87.6%); most commonly human rhinovirus (167/276; 60.5%), respiratory syncytial virus (94/276; 34%) and adenovirus (59/315; 18.7%). Respiratory syncytial virus showed strong winter seasonality (P < 0.001), human rhinovirus circulated year-round (P < 0.001) and seasonal Severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus-2 activity was low at 10%. HIV exposure (adjusted odds ratio: 3.08)] and viral co-detection (43.5%; P = 0.015) were independently associated with disease severity. Cluster analysis revealed 3 distinct clinical phenotypes of RTIs, with unique symptom profiles, trajectories and virological patterns.

CONCLUSION: Respiratory viruses remained common in young South African children hospitalized with RTIs, with most returning to pre-COVID seasonal patterns and limited Severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus-2 activity. Distinct clinical phenotypes identify vulnerable subgroups and underscore the need for improved tools to distinguish severe disease from self-limiting illness.

articles.title: Computed Tomography-Derived Psoas Muscle Quantity, Attenuation, and 1 Year Mortality in Venovenous Extracorporeal Membrane Oxygenation.
articles.journal: ASAIO journal (American Society for Artificial Internal Organs : 1992)
articles.abstract: Computed tomography (CT)-derived skeletal muscle characteristics may provide prognostic information in patients receiving venovenous extracorporeal membrane oxygenation (VV ECMO), but the relative contributions of muscle quantity and attenuation remain uncertain. We retrospectively studied adults who received VV ECMO for severe respiratory failure between 2014 and 2023 and underwent abdominal CT within 48 h before ECMO initiation. Psoas muscle index (PMI) and attenuation were measured using an artificial intelligence-based pipeline, and combined PMI-attenuation phenotypes were evaluated for 1 year mortality. Among 92 patients, 53 (57.6%) died within 1 year. In Cox proportional hazards models adjusted for age, sex, and initial Sequential Organ Failure Assessment score and stratified by bridge-to-transplantation status, higher PMI (adjusted hazard ratio [aHR] per standard deviation increase, 0.58; 95% confidence interval [CI], 0.41-0.82) and higher attenuation (aHR per 5 Hounsfield unit increase, 0.87; 95% CI, 0.77-0.97) were associated with lower 1 year mortality. When modeled simultaneously, PMI remained significant, whereas attenuation did not. The low PMI/low attenuation phenotype had the highest mortality risk (aHR, 5.30; 95% CI, 2.10-13.34). PMI showed a more robust association with 1 year mortality, while combined PMI-attenuation phenotyping may identify a particularly high-risk subgroup.

articles.title: Chorioretinal Scars in Congenital Cytomegalovirus Infection Following Prenatal Valacyclovir Therapy.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Congenital cytomegalovirus infection is the most common congenital infection. Ocular abnormalities affect approximately 14% of symptomatic children, but fewer than 1% of asymptomatic children. Prenatal valacyclovir reduces vertical transmission, but ophthalmic outcomes in exposed infants are poorly described.

METHODS: We describe 2 neonates with congenital cytomegalovirus confirmed by amniotic fluid and urine polymerase chain reaction following first-trimester maternal primary infection. Both mothers received high-dose valacyclovir (8 g daily) from 13 weeks' gestation. Infants underwent neonatal evaluation, including dilated fundus examination and multimodal retinal imaging.

RESULTS: Maternal treatment continued to 36 weeks in 1 pregnancy and was discontinued at 22 weeks in the other, after amniocentesis. Both infants had macular chorioretinal scarring. Optical coherence tomography demonstrated focal ellipsoid zone disruption in a clinically normal fellow eye in 1 infant. Cranial ultrasonography demonstrated caudothalamic and temporal lobe cysts with lenticulostriate vasculopathy in 1 infant and isolated lenticulostriate vasculopathy in the other. Physical and neurologic examinations, head circumference, full blood count, liver function and auditory brainstem responses were normal in both. Both were classified as symptomatic with central nervous system involvement on the basis of ocular findings and therefore received valganciclovir for a planned 6 months. Retinal findings were stable at 3 months.

CONCLUSIONS: Macular chorioretinal scarring was present in both infants despite otherwise limited clinical findings, and the extent of cranial imaging abnormality did not correspond to ocular involvement. Ophthalmologic examination determined disease classification and management. These observations do not permit conclusions regarding the effect of prenatal valacyclovir on ocular outcome.

articles.title: Postoperative muscle mass depletion in older patients undergoing major elective surgery.
articles.journal: Journal of anesthesia, analgesia and critical care
articles.abstract: In older patients, the impact of surgery and postoperative recovery on skeletal muscle parameters remains poorly investigated. We aimed to assess changes in skeletal muscle parameters after major elective surgery and explore factors associated with total psoas index (TPI) reduction. This retrospective, post hoc analysis included 51 patients aged 70 years or older who underwent major elective general or urologic surgery and had preoperative and postoperative computed tomography (CT) scans available. The primary endpoint was the change in TPI between preoperative and postoperative CT. At postoperative CT follow-up, TPI decreased by 14% (mean [SD] paired difference -0.51 [0.77] cm2/m2) and muscle attenuation by 15% (both p < 0.001). The prevalence of low TPI increased from 13 patients preoperatively to 24 postoperatively. Preoperative low TPI was not significantly associated with postoperative outcomes, while greater TPI reduction was associated with longer hospital length of stay and intensive care unit admission in univariable analyses, but these associations were not confirmed after multivariable adjustment. These findings might suggest a postoperative decrease in skeletal muscle parameters in older adults, although their clinical relevance requires further investigation.

articles.title: Protocol for a cluster randomized controlled trial among young people and their peers to reduce substance use and inequitable gender beliefs in Southern Africa.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND AND AIMS: Substance use and the internalization of traditional gender norms, or inequitable gender beliefs, are co-occurring risk behaviors for poorer health and well-being in young people in Southern Africa. Addressing the social and structural factors that reinforce substance use and inequitable gender beliefs, including peer influence and socioeconomic adversity, such as lack of education or employment, is necessary to support sustainable change in these behaviors. However, most existing interventions focus only on changing individual behavior. This study will therefore aim to address this limitation by testing the efficacy of an intervention to reduce substance use and promote equitable gender beliefs, delivered to peer groups and embedded within existing vocational training (VT) programs.

DESIGN: Two-arm cluster randomized controlled superiority trial with assessments at baseline, 12-week, and 24-week follow-up.

SETTING: Selected VT programs in Zambia, Zimbabwe, and South Africa.

PARTICIPANTS: Sixty-six peer groups (N ~ 264 participants) will be recruited, comprised of an index case plus 2 to 5 peers aged 16-24 years old, who use substances together weekly, or binge drink at least monthly, and enrolled in eligible VT programs.

INTERVENTION AND COMPARATOR: Peer groups will be randomly allocated [1:1] to receive either: (i) the standard VT program plus Peer Education for Gender Inclusion and Substance Use in Southern Africa (PEGISUS), an 8-session interactive intervention delivered by VT program staff to peer groups or (ii) standard of care (SOC), namely the standard VT program and a referral for substance use services.

MEASUREMENTS: The primary outcome is the between-group (PEGISUS vs. SOC) mean difference in change in the total substance use involvement score on the ASSIST (Alcohol, Smoking, and Substance Involvement Screening Test) from baseline to the 12-week follow-up. Secondary outcomes compare the between-group mean difference in (1) other substance use scales on the ASSIST and at other timepoints (i.e. 24-week follow-up) (2); change in gender equitable beliefs using the GEMS (Gender Equitable Men's Scale) from baseline to the 12-week and 24-week follow-up; and (3) VT program attendance and completion rates, employment status, and income earned at the 24-week follow-up.

COMMENTS: This will be the first known study in Southern Africa to assess the efficacy of an intervention that addresses substance use and gender equity beliefs among young people and their peers delivered in VT programs. PEGISUS will address socioeconomic adversity and offer a potential pathway to sustainable delivery by embedding the intervention within existing VT programs. If unhealthy risk behaviors are reduced, and employment opportunities are improved, this can lead to improved well-being in the life trajectories of these young people.

TRIAL REGISTRATION: Clinicaltrials.gov Trials identifier: NCT06489899. Approved on July 8, 2024. url: https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT06489899?term=NCT06489899?rank=1 . Pan African Clinical Trials identifier: PACTR202502629432188. Approved February 14, 2025. url: https://pactr.samrc.ac.za/TrialDisplay.aspx?TrialID=33370 .

articles.title: Current strategies for controlling gastrointestinal nematodes of pigs in Europe.
articles.abstract: Gastrointestinal nematodes (GIN) remain an often-underestimated challenge in European pig production, affecting animal health, performance, and economic outcomes. The predominant species, Ascaris (A.) suum, Oesophagostomum (O.) spp., and Trichuris (T.) suis, impair growth, feed efficiency, and carcass quality, whilst also contributing to reproductive losses and liver condemnation. Moreover, GIN can modulate host immunity, interfere with vaccine responses, and influence coinfection outcomes, thereby compromising overall herd health. The zoonotic potential of A. suum and T. suis further highlights the need for effective control strategies. This review critically synthesises the available evidence on the occurrence, impact, and control of porcine GIN in Europe and identifies pig-specific knowledge gaps and priorities for integrated control. GIN occur across all European pig production systems. However, accurate surveillance remains challenging due to methodological heterogeneity, uneven geographical coverage, and limited recent large-scale epidemiological data. Reported farm-level prevalences therefore vary widely, ranging from 1 to 100% (A. suum), 2-27% (O. spp.), and 0.3-75% (T. suis). Higher infection levels are generally reported in outdoor, organic, and small-scale production systems. Current control strategies largely depend on anthelmintics. Reports of reduced efficacy and resistance, particularly in O. spp., highlight the need for improved surveillance and diagnostic-based treatment. Hygiene practices, housing design, flooring, bedding, pasture, and herd management can influence transmission, but their effectiveness under commercial conditions remains insufficiently evaluated. Alternative approaches, including dietary interventions, probiotics, genetic selection, and vaccine development, may complement conventional measures, although most are not yet established for routine use. Changes in climate, animal welfare requirements, production systems, and expectations concerning pharmaceutical use may further alter GIN exposure and control needs. Standardised surveillance, contemporary assessments of animal health and economic consequences, field-based intervention studies, and sustainable, integrated control programmes are therefore key priorities for European pig production.

articles.title: NAD+ Attenuates Neuroinflammation in Ischemic Stroke by Suppressing the cGAS- STING Pathway via Mitochondrial Homeostasis Restoration.
articles.abstract: Stroke remains one of the leading causes of death and disability worldwide, with neuroinflammation playing a critical role in its pathogenesis. The cyclic GMP-AMP synthase-stimulator of interferon genes (cGAS-STING) pathway is a major driver of innate immune responses activated by endogenous DNA, including mitochondrial DNA (mtDNA), and contributes significantly to post-ischemic neuroinflammation. Nicotinamide adenine dinucleotide (NAD+), a vital metabolic coenzyme, has demonstrated anti-inflammatory potential in various diseases, including stroke; however, its specific role in regulation of neuroinflammation following stroke remains unclear. In this study, we examined the protective effects of NAD+ against ischemic stroke and explored its role in modulating cGAS-STING-mediated neuroinflammatory responses. Utilizing a transient middle cerebral artery occlusion/reperfusion mouse model and an oxygen-glucose deprivation/reoxygenation BV2 microglia model, we observed that NAD+ treatment significantly reduced infarct volume and brain edema, and improved neurological outcomes. NAD+ reduced the levels of pro-inflammatory cytokines and facilitated the polarization of microglia from pro-inflammatory M1 to the anti-inflammatory M2 phenotype. This effect was associated with the inhibition of cGAS-STING-TBK1 signaling pathway activation. Pharmacological inhibition or genetic knockdown of STING largely abrogated the anti-inflammatory effects of NAD+ in BV2 microglia, indicating a STING-dependent mechanism. Furthermore, NAD+ restored mitochondrial respiratory function and reduced cytoplasmic mtDNA leakage, suggesting that the improvement of mitochondrial homeostasis may underlie the suppression of cGAS-STING-TBK1 signaling pathway by NAD+. Our findings indicate that NAD+ alleviates neuroinflammation following brain ischemia/reperfusion injury by regulating mitochondrial homeostasis and attenuates the cGAS-STING-TBK1 signaling pathway activation in microglia, thereby providing new therapeutic insights for ischemic stroke.

articles.title: Rethinking Plaque Stabilization with Evolocumab in Diabetes: Methodological Considerations from the YELLOW III Trial.
MSCs-derived Exosomal miRNA-335-5p Alleviates Apoptosis and Inflammation in Myocardial Infarction by Inhibiting BCL2L11.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Myocardial infarction (MI) leads to heart cell death and inflammation, resulting in permanent heart damage. Exosomes derived from mesenchymal stem cells (MSCs), which can deliver miRNAs to cells, have shown potential as therapeutic agents for MI, this study sought to elucidate the role of MSC-derived exosomal miRNA-335-5p in MI.

METHODS: Exosomes secreted from MSCs were observed using transmission electron microscope (TEM) and nanoparticle tracking analysis (NTA). Inflammatory cytokines, cell apoptosis were evaluated. The dual luciferase gene assay was used to validate the interaction between miRNA-335-5p and BCL2-like 11 (BCL2L11). Cardiac function indicators in MI rats were detected using echocardiography. The levels of lactate dehydrogenase (LDH), creatine kinase-MB (CK-MB) and cardiac troponin (cTnI) were detected by commercial kits. To confirm fibrosis detection, Masson staining was employed.

RESULTS: MSCs-derived exosomes (MSC-exos) are abundant in miR-335-5p. MSCs-derived exosomal miR-335-5p inhibited hypoxia induced H9c2 cells apoptosis and inflammation, while reducing miRNA-335-5p in MSC-exos does not produce this effect. Mechanically, miRNA-335-5p interacted with BCL2L11 and reduced its expression. Reducing miRNA-335-5p in MSC-exos or overexpressing BCL2L11 can counteract the improvement of MSC-exos on apoptosis and inflammation in H9c2 cells under hypoxic conditions and MI rats.

CONCLUSION: In MI, MSCs-derived exosomal miRNA-335-5p alleviated apoptosis and inflammation by targeting BCL2L11.

articles.title: Sex-related differences in clinical characteristics, management, and outcomes of Enterococcus faecalis bloodstream infection.
articles.journal: European journal of clinical microbiology & infectious diseases : official publication of the European Society of Clinical Microbiology
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: To evaluate whether clinical characteristics and outcomes of patients with Enterococcus faecalis bloodstream infection (EF-BSI) differ by biological sex.

METHODS: Quasi-experimental study conducted at two hospitals, comprising a retrospective phase (2017-2019) and a prospective intervention phase (2022-2024), including adults with a first episode of monomicrobial EF-BSI. Patients who died within 72 h or were receiving palliative care were excluded. A structured management bundle was implemented in the intervention phase. Clinical features, bundle adherence, and 90-day mortality were compared by sex. Cox regression was used to assess the association between sex and 90-day mortality.

RESULTS: Among 250 patients, 77 (31%) were females and 173 (69%) males. Females were younger than males (median 63 [50-76] vs. 73 [63-80] years; p < 0.001). Cardiovascular disease was more frequent in males (30 [39%] vs. 94 [54%]; p = 0.025), whereas immunosuppressive therapy (29 [38%] vs. 35 [20%]; p = 0.004) and connective tissue disease (9 [12%] vs. 2 [1%]; p < 0.001) were more frequent in females. Persistent bacteraemia (2/57 [4%] vs. 30/139 [22%]; p = 0.002) and infective endocarditis (14 [18%] vs. 59 [34%]; p = 0.011) were more frequent in males. Females received fewer bundle measures (5 [3-6] vs. 5 [4-6]; p = 0.028), largely because echocardiography and colonoscopy were less frequently indicated. Ninety-day mortality was 22% (17) in females and 14% (25) in males (p = 0.136). Female sex was associated with higher 90-day mortality after adjustment (aHR 2.00, 95%CI 1.04-3.83).

CONCLUSIONS: Further studies should explore the underlying causes of these differences and potential implications for individualized management.

articles.title: Genomic medicine knowledge, self-assessment, and training needs among Turkish pediatricians: a cross-sectional survey.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The integration of genomic medicine into clinical practice has become increasingly important for frontline clinicians. Pediatricians represent a particularly important group, as they routinely encounter patients with suspected genetic conditions. However, data on genomic knowledge among pediatricians in Turkey - a country with unique epidemiological and healthcare characteristics - remain scarce.

METHODS: A cross-sectional survey was conducted between February 10 and March 10, 2026 via Google Forms among 266 pediatricians at various career stages (residents, specialists, subspecialty trainees/specialists, and academics). The survey comprised a demographic section, four Likert-type self-assessment items, and 15 objective knowledge questions. Statistical analyses included the Shapiro-Wilk normality test, Kruskal-Wallis and Mann-Whitney U tests, chi-square test, one-way ANOVA with Tukey HSD post-hoc analysis, Dunn test with Bonferroni correction for non-parametric comparisons, and Spearman correlation analysis.

RESULTS: The mean knowledge score was 8.67 ± 2.99 out of 15 (57.8%). Mean subscores were 59.8% for basic clinical genetics and 53.8% for advanced genomic therapies, with low-scoring items in both domains. Professional title (H = 34.29, p < 0.001), years of experience (H = 23.70, p < 0.001), and structured genetics training (Mann-Whitney U, p < 0.001) were significantly associated with knowledge scores; in multivariable analysis, title and training, but not experience, remained associated. Overall, 51.5% of participants reported never having received structured genetics education. Knowledge scores did not differ by gender (p = 0.647). Genetics training was associated with genetic test-ordering frequency(χ²=15.46, p = 0.004).

CONCLUSIONS: Turkish pediatricians showed moderate knowledge of the genomic topics assessed, with gaps in both basic and advanced topics. Structured genetics education was associated with higher knowledge scores and more frequent genetic test ordering, although the cross-sectional design precludes causal inference. These findings support developing and evaluating targeted genomic education for pediatricians.

articles.title: Cross-scale genetic analysis prioritizes shared regulatory variation, cell-type contributions, co-expression programs, and exon-level patterns in atopic dermatitis and asthma.
articles.abstract: Atopic dermatitis (AD) and asthma frequently co-occur, yet the regulatory mechanisms connecting cutaneous and airway inflammation remain unclear. We integrated European genome-wide association statistics for AD (22,474 cases; 774,187 controls) and asthma (56,167 cases; 352,255 controls) with expression and splicing quantitative trait loci (QTLs), immune single-cell expression QTLs, single-cell transcriptomes, and spatial transcriptomics. The AD dataset compared lesional skin with healthy controls, whereas the asthma dataset paired allergen and diluent challenges in four participants. Each was analyzed within its own design, and cross-disease comparison used independently derived annotations and gene sets. Regulatory QTL enrichment implicated skin, lung, fibroblast, and immune-related tissues. Cell-stratified Mendelian randomization identified multi-instrument associations in memory B cells (odds ratio = 1.35, 95% confidence interval 1.18-1.56; false discovery rate = 1.1 × 10⁻⁴) and immature/naïve B cells (1.26, 1.10-1.45); single-instrument estimates were exploratory regardless of false discovery rate, and no association has been independently replicated. T-cell co-expression analysis identified three cross-disease module overlaps-translational, metabolic-cytoskeletal, and cytotoxic effector-each significant after multiple-testing correction across 42 module comparisons. Airway transcripts in the asthma T-cell compartment were attributed predominantly to ambient RNA. Bayesian colocalization identified signals at 19 AD and 72 asthma loci and 112 shared genes. Integrated evidence prioritized SLC22A4, CTSW, IL1R1, RMI2, and IRF1; four ranked in the top five under all eight scoring schemes and IRF1 under seven, and all five retained top-ten ranking in ≥ 98.9% of 10,000 moderately concentrated randomized weightings. These results prioritize shared regulatory candidates for validation.

articles.title: Clinical outcomes of low versus high intensity laser therapy in patients with subacute carpal tunnel syndrome: A randomized, single-blinded, controlled trial.
articles.abstract: A common entrapment of median nerve that causes pain, numbness, and functional impairment is called Carpal Tunnel Syndrome (CTS). Laser therapy is a noninvasive intervention for neural repair and pain modulation, but comparative evidence between Low-Level Laser Therapy (LLLT) and High-Intensity Laser Therapy (HILT) in subacute CTS is limited. The aims of this study were to compare the effects of LLLT and HILT on pain, functional status, electrophysiological, and ultrasonographic parameters in subacute CTS. A single-blinded randomized controlled trial (Reg. No. IRCT20241111063665N1) was conducted at the Department of Physiotherapy, The University of Lahore (UOL), Lahore, Pakistan, from August 2024 to March 2025. Sixty-nine participants with subacute CTS, confirmed by electromyography and nerve conduction studies, were randomly assigned to three groups (n = 23 each): Group A (HILT; 808 nm + physiotherapy), Group B (LLLT; 860 nm + physiotherapy), and Group C (physiotherapy + sham laser). Assessments were at baseline and week 6. Outcomes included pain (VAS), symptom severity and functional status (Boston Carpal Tunnel Questionnaire; BCTQ), grip strength, distal motor latency (DML), sensory nerve conduction velocity (SNCV), and median nerve cross-sectional area (CSA). ANCOVA with Bonferroni correction and effect size estimation was applied. At week 6, both HILT and LLLT showed significant improvements (p < 0.001). HILT achieved greater pain reduction (- 4.9) than LLLT (- 4.1) and control (- 2.2; p < 0.001), with greater improvement in BCTQ-SSS (- 2.2 points), BCTQ-FSS (- 1.9 points), grip strength (+ 9.9 kg), DML (- 1.2 ms), SNCV (+ 12.3 m/s), and CSA (- 3.7 mm²). Large effect sizes (Cohen's d > 0.8) were observed. Both LLLT and HILT are effective as adjuncts to physiotherapy in subacute CTS. HILT demonstrated greater improvements than LLLT within the parameters tested.Clinical Trial Number: IRCT20241111063665N1, Registration date: 17 March, 2025.

articles.title: Ambient artificial intelligence scribes in urology: a pilot evaluation of user experience and clinical efficiency gains.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: Ambient artificial intelligence (AI) scribes aim to reduce documentation burden, yet evidence in urology is limited. We evaluated the pilot rollout of an AI scribe system in our academic urology department, focusing on user experience and electronic health record-based efficiency metrics.

METHODS: AI scribes were introduced into outpatient urology clinics in June 2024. We developed a user experience questionnaire to assess navigation, functionality, workload reduction, and clinical impact at 1 and 11 months of implementation. Clinical efficiency was evaluated using changes in Epic Signal metrics from pre- to post-rollout. Descriptive statistics were stratified by AI scribe adoption status and documentation method.

RESULTS: Of 41 eligible clinicians, seven initially enrolled in the AI scribe pilot. Two clinicians discontinued use, and three additional clinicians adopted the technology, resulting in eight persistent AI scribe users (19.5%). Median utilization in office visit notes was 90%. User experience improved across all domains, most notably in workload reduction (3.1 to 4.7). Users reported reduced after-hours charting and improved patient interaction; limitations included lack of pre-charting capabilities and insufficient adaptation to urology-specific documentation needs. AI scribe users demonstrated consistent within-clinician reductions in time in notes per day (-28.7%; 14.0 min), time in notes per appointment (-21.9%; 0.9 min), and time outside scheduled hours (-28.6%; 13.4 min). Inconsistent background trends were observed among non-users.

CONCLUSION: AI scribe users reported positive experience with the technology and demonstrated reductions in documentation burden. Findings are exploratory and support larger, controlled evaluations of note quality and workflow impact.

articles.title: Anxiety in patients with cancer and emergency department use: a systematic review.
articles.journal: Supportive care in cancer : official journal of the Multinational Association of Supportive Care in Cancer
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Anxiety is common among patients with cancer, with up to 30% of patients experiencing clinically significant symptoms at some point following their cancer diagnosis. Although patients with cancer frequently use the emergency department (ED), the relationship between anxiety and ED use in this population remains unclear. The objective of this systematic review was to synthesize the existing literature examining the association between anxiety in adults with cancer and subsequent ED use.

METHODS: We conducted a systematic review comparing ED use among adult cancer patients with and without anxiety. Electronic searches of CINAHL, Cochrane, Medline, PsychInfo, PubMed, and Web of Science were conducted. Two reviewers independently screened titles and abstracts, followed by full text review, data extraction and quality assessment using the Newcastle-Ottawa scale for cohort studies. Due to substantial heterogeneity across studies, including differences in cancer populations, anxiety measurement, timing of assessment, ED outcome definitions, and analytic approaches, a meta-analysis was not performed. Findings were summarized and synthesized narratively.

RESULTS: Seven studies met inclusion criteria, including single-center, multicenter and population-based retrospective designs. Anxiety was identified using either diagnostic codes or patient-reported measures. Four studies found no statistically significant association between anxiety and ED use in multivariable analyses, although three reported small effect sizes with odds or hazard ratios near 1.0. In contrast, three studies reported a significant positive association between anxiety and increased ED use, with effect estimates ranging from 1.23 to 3.87. Variability in findings may be related to differences in anxiety measurement, timing of outcomes, and covariate adjustment.

CONCLUSION: Evidence of the association between anxiety and ED use among patients with cancer is mixed. However, when significant differences were observed, anxiety was consistently linked to increased ED use. Given the heterogeneity of existing studies, prospective longitudinal research using standardized anxiety measures across the cancer continuum is needed to better understand this relationship.

articles.title: Liraglutide ameliorates obese type 2 diabetes by regulating macrophage cholesterol metabolism and H3K27ac modification to promote M2 polarization and adipocyte thermogenic activation.
articles.abstract: Obesity-related type 2 diabetes mellitus (O&T2DM) has become a major global public health issue. Chronic low-grade inflammation in adipose tissue is one of its core pathological features, among which excessive infiltration of M1-type macrophages and impaired function of M2-type macrophages are key drivers of inflammation. Liraglutide, a glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonist, exhibits significant glucose-lowering, weight-reducing, and anti-inflammatory effects. However, the molecular mechanisms by which liraglutide regulates cholesterol metabolism and epigenetic modifications in adipose tissue macrophages remain to be fully elucidated. A high-fat diet combined with streptozotocin was used to establish an O&T2DM model in male C57BL/6 mice. After 8 weeks of intervention, metabolic phenotypes, adipose tissue macrophage polarization, and cholesterol metabolism-related indicators were assessed. Raw264.7 macrophages were cultured in vitro and stimulated with IFN-γ + LPS to induce M1 polarization. Following liraglutide pretreatment, cell polarization phenotypes, the expression of genes involved in cholesterol metabolic pathways, and histone modification levels were examined. Using shRNA gene silencing, p300 inhibitor intervention, and Acetyl-CoA supplementation experiments in combination with ChIP-qPCR, the central role of the cholesterol metabolism-epigenetic axis in macrophage polarization was elucidated. Finally, a Transwell co-culture system was employed to verify the regulatory effects of liraglutide-reprogrammed macrophages on adipocyte lipid accumulation and energy metabolism. Liraglutide significantly reduced body weight, fasting blood glucose, and HOMA-IR in O&T2DM mice, decreased visceral fat accumulation, and promoted adipose tissue browning. It also increased the proportion of M2 macrophages within adipose tissue and significantly activated the key cholesterol efflux pathway LXRα/ABCA1. In vitro experiments confirmed that liraglutide pretreatment suppressed IFN-γ + LPS-induced M1 polarization and promoted the expression of M2-type markers, upregulated the expression of ABCA1, ABCG1, PPARγ, and LXRα, and increased levels of histone H3K27ac. Mechanistic studies revealed that silencing ABCA1 or LXRα reversed the liraglutide-induced increase in H3K27ac and M2 polarization. Acetyl-CoA supplementation partially restored the macrophage polarization phenotype following ABCA1 silencing. ChIP-qPCR results showed that liraglutide significantly enhanced the enrichment of H3K27ac in the promoter regions of M2 polarization genes and cholesterol metabolism genes. Co-culture experiments demonstrated that liraglutide-reprogrammed macrophages significantly promoted adipocyte thermogenic gene expression, increased mitochondrial membrane potential-dependent staining intensity, and enhanced ATPase activity via paracrine signaling, an effect that was blocked by silencing ABCA1 or LXRα. This study demonstrates that liraglutide activates the ABCA1/LXRα-mediated cholesterol metabolism pathway, upregulates histone H3K27ac modification, and drives macrophage M2 polarization, which in turn induces adipocyte lipid accumulation and mitochondrial metabolic activation via paracrine signaling. These findings provide a new molecular mechanism for the anti-inflammatory and metabolic-improving effects of liraglutide, and also offers a potential epigenetic target for the treatment of O&T2DM.

articles.title: Fracture risk and fracture risk factor assessment among men at prostate cancer diagnosis.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Older men with prostate cancer, particularly those receiving androgen deprivation therapy, have an increased fracture risk. However, contemporary studies assessing baseline fracture risk in ethnically diverse populations of men at initial prostate cancer diagnosis remain limited.

METHODS: Men aged 50-89 years with newly diagnosed prostate cancer (2010-2022) in a US integrated healthcare system were identified. Demographic data, smoking, prior fracture, rheumatoid arthritis, recent glucocorticoid therapy, body mass index (FRAX variables), and other risk factors (diabetes, low 25OH-vitamin D level) were ascertained from electronic health records.
