Among 212 enrolled patients, 135 adults (18-60 yrs) and 77 elderly (>60 years) were analyzed. Elderly [p<0.001; adjusted odds ratio (AOR) 8.12], unemployed (p=0.016), more than 5 years of inhaler use (p=0.005; AOR 9.54) and metered dose inhaler (p<0.001; AOR 5.86) had more chances of committing at least 1 error in inhaler technique. Identifying and correcting the errors in inhalational technique is the easiest and cost effective method to decrease the exacerbations and improve disease control in patients suffering from OAD by further decreasing the healthcare burden.

articles.title: African recommendations for diagnosis and management of systemic juvenile idiopathic arthritis (sJIA) - a PAFLAR initiative.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: To develop evidence-based recommendations for diagnosis and treatment of children and adolescents with systemic juvenile idiopathic arthritis (sJIA), taking into consideration the socioeconomic status and availability of medications in African countries.

METHODS: A steering group composed of five PAFLAR members formulated questions in PICO format (Patient/Population, Intervention, Comparison, Outcome), conducted a systematic literature review, and identified experts in pediatric rheumatology throughout Africa. The Delphi method was used to reach consensus among the experts on the recommendations for diagnosis and treatment of sJIA patients.

RESULTS: The online Delphi questionnaire was sent to the 22 experts selected by the steering committee, who were asked to vote for each statement and to provide their suggestions for modifications or rewording. A 100% response rate was obtained. A minimum agreement of 70% among the voting panel was required. A total of 15 recommendations were formulated, 4 regarding diagnosis and 11 regarding treatment. The percentage of agreement with the recommendations ranged from 72.7% to 95%.

CONCLUSION: We present the first African recommendations for diagnosis and management of sJIA. The feedback about the application of these recommendations in pediatric rheumatology centers will serve as the basis for future revisions in the light of African-specific experiences and insights.

articles.title: Factors associated with 1-year health-related quality of life after neck-specific exercise in chronic whiplash-associated disorders: an exploratory secondary analysis of a randomized controlled trial.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Factors associated with changes in health-related quality of life (HRQoL) outcomes in neck disorders have not been investigated after internet-based support for exercise. The purpose of the study was to investigate baseline and short-term outcome factors associated with changes in HRQoL (EQ-5D-3L and EQ-VAS) at 3 and 15 months, respectively, after a neck-specific exercise programme (NSE) for individuals with chronic whiplash-associated disorders grades 2 and 3.

METHODS: This was a secondary analysis of a prospective randomized controlled multi-centre trial with concealed allocation. Participants (n = 140) were randomized to NSE at a physiotherapy clinic or internet-based NSE with four physiotherapy visits (NSEIT). Assessor-blinded investigators obtained measurements at baseline and at 3- and 15-month follow-up. Orthogonal partial least square (OPLS) and OPLS discriminant statistical analyses (OPLS-DA) were used.

RESULTS: There were no significant differences between the exercise programmes. Improvement in psychosocial measures, pain, disability and several objective measures were associated with improvements in HRQoL in OPLS models (R2 = 0.20 to 0.27, Q2 = 0.06 to 0.12, p < 0.05 to < 0.001). Higher baseline score on adverse psychosocial measures and disability, together with lower dizziness, self-efficacy, and neck-muscle endurance in extension, were associated with clinically relevant improvement in EQ-5D-3L at 15-month follow-up (R2 = 0.26, Q2 = 0.13, p < 0.01). The other models were non-significant.

CONCLUSIONS: Several factors, including adverse psychosocial measures, may be clinically relevant for HRQoL after neck-specific exercise interventions. Given the models' weak predictive ability, the findings should be regarded as exploratory and hypothesis-generating.

TRIAL REGISTRATION: The study was registered before data collection started, ClinicalTrials.gov Protocol ID: NCT03022812, initial release 12/20/2016. The study was approved by the regional ethical review board in Linköping, Sweden (Dnr 2016/135-31; 2016/526-32; 2017/45-32).

articles.title: Efonidipine inhibiting CYP4A attenuates palmitate-induced hepatocyte lipotoxicity.
articles.abstract: Efonidipine, a dual L-/T-type calcium channel blocker (CCB), is a clinically established antihypertensive agent with cardiovascular and renoprotective effects. However, whether efonidipine affects CYP4A, a previously established mediator of hepatic lipotoxicity, remains unknown. In the present study, palmitate (PA)-induced steatotic HepG2 and SNU-449 hepatocytes were used to evaluate the hepatoprotective effects of efonidipine and its underlying mechanism. Efonidipine inhibited CYP4A enzyme activity, revealing a previously unrecognized CYP4A inhibitor. It also reduced CYP4A protein expression in PA-treated hepatocytes. This was accompanied by reduced intracellular lipid accumulation and lipogenesis, suppressed oxidative and ER stress, and improved insulin signaling and glucose uptake. These effects were consistently observed in both hepatocyte cell lines. Taken together, these findings suggest that efonidipine may represent a potential repurposing strategy for hepatic lipotoxicity through CYP4A inhibition.

articles.title: Comparative transcriptomics identifies conserved gene signatures defining megakaryocyte development states across species.
articles.abstract: Megakaryocytes and platelets are essential for hemostasis, immune regulation and hematopoietic niche maintenance, while also promoting thrombosis. Comprehensive characterization of late-stage megakaryocyte maturation in mammals using single-cell RNA-sequencing (scRNA-Seq) remains challenging due to the large size of megakaryocytes and the low RNA content of platelets. Although zebrafish thrombocytes are functionally analogous and retain high transcriptional activity at maturity, their transcriptional similarities to mammals have not been systematically defined. To address this, we generated a single-cell transcriptomic atlas spanning the full developmental trajectory of zebrafish thrombocytes, demonstrating that lineage progression is continuous and functionally coordinated. Cross-species comparison with human and mouse datasets defined conserved differentiation stages and gene modules of the megakaryocyte-platelet lineage, indicating evolutionary conservation of lineage development at single-cell resolution. Moreover, we identified a gene set (M3pan-PLT) that marks a platelet-like transcriptional state in zebrafish thrombocytes, supporting their transcriptomic analogy to mammalian platelets. Finally, bulk transcriptomic analyses using these conserved gene signatures demonstrated their ability to capture physiological megakaryocyte states, as well as disease-associated transcriptional alterations in acute megakaryoblastic leukemia. Together, our study defines a conserved and continuous developmental framework of megakaryocytes at single-cell resolution and establishes zebrafish thrombocytes as a transcriptionally conserved model for dissecting late-stage megakaryocyte-platelet biology.

articles.title: Impact of symmetrical and asymmetrical foot pronation and arch deformities on three-dimensional pelvic kinematics during standing and walking: A systematic review and Meta-analysis.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Foot pronation and structural arch deformities may influence pelvic motion, but effects vary across conditions and tasks. This review examined whether three-dimensional pelvic responses differ by foot-condition symmetry and between standing and dynamic weight-bearing.

METHODS: Following PRISMA 2020, observational and non-randomized experimental studies of habitual foot arch dysfunction or experimentally induced calcaneal eversion/inversion were reviewed. Primary outcomes were sagittal pelvic tilt, frontal pelvic tilt or drop, and transverse pelvic rotation. Comparable standing pelvic angles were analyzed using exploratory random-effects mean differences (MDs, degrees); repeated-measures contrasts used reported paired-change statistics. Other outcomes were summarized narratively. Risk of bias was assessed with JBI tools and certainty with GRADE.

FINDINGS: Sixteen publications representing 15 independent study samples were included. Two bilateral 10° wedge studies showed increases in anterior pelvic tilt, but exploratory pooling was imprecise (MD 0.97°, 95% CI [-0.05, 1.99]; I2 = 81.8%). Habitual bilateral flatfoot was not pooled because compatible summary data were unavailable. Three studies reported positive lateral pelvic tilt differences for unilateral foot conditions; their exploratory pooled estimate was highly heterogeneous (MD 2.18°, 95% CI [-0.36, 4.71]; I2 = 96.5%). High-arched/inversion and dynamic transverse-plane outcomes were summarized narratively. Certainty was very low for pooled outcomes.

INTERPRETATION: Foot-condition type and assessment task appear relevant to pelvic alignment, but the small evidence base and substantial heterogeneity limit pooled conclusions. These results are preliminary biomechanical observations rather than evidence of causation or treatment effectiveness. PROSPERO registration number: CRD420261329855.

articles.title: Letter to the editor: endovascular therapy for mild-to-moderate stroke due to basilar artery occlusion: interpreting the certainty of excellent functional recovery.
Risk Factors, Ischemic Delay, and In-Hospital Outcomes by Sex in Adults Aged 18-50 Years with STEMI Undergoing Primary Percutaneous Coronary Intervention: An Exploratory Single-Center Cohort.
articles.journal: Turk Kardiyoloji Dernegi arsivi : Turk Kardiyoloji Derneginin yayin organidir
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To describe sex differences in cardiovascular risk factors and reperfusion delays and explore in-hospital outcomes in adults aged 18-50 years with ST-segment elevation myocardial infarction (STEMI) undergoing primary percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI).

METHOD: This retrospective single-center cohort included 497 consecutive patients (71 [14.3%] women) treated during 2023-2024. Hard major adverse cardiac and cerebrovascular events (MACCE) comprised all-cause death, recurrent myocardial infarction, or stroke. A nonstandard expanded clinical deterioration composite additionally included incident cardiogenic shock and, among patients admitted in Killip class I, incident heart failure. Sex comparisons and Firth penalized logistic models were exploratory.

RESULTS: Mean age was 40.7 +- 5.3 years. Current smoking was more frequent in men (69.0% vs 39.4%; P < 0.001), whereas obesity was more frequent in women (54.9% vs 26.8%; P < 0.001). Age-adjusted median symptom-to-first-medical-contact, first-medical-contact-to-device, and total ischemic times were 46, 10, and 48 minutes longer in women, respectively (all P < 0.001). Hard MACCE occurred in 21 patients (4.2%), incident heart failure occurred in 13 of 390 eligible patients (3.3%), and the expanded composite occurred in 46 patients (9.3%). The expanded composite occurred in 12 of 71 women and 34 of 426 men (16.9% vs 8.0%; unadjusted P = 0.025), and incident cardiogenic shock occurred in 7 women and 13 men (9.9% vs 3.1%; unadjusted P = 0.015). In the parsimonious baseline model, the adjusted odds ratio (OR) for female sex was 2.61 (95% confidence interval [CI], 1.21-5.42), attenuating to 1.90 (95% CI, 0.83-4.18) after adding admission Killip class ≥II.

CONCLUSION: Women had a different risk-factor distribution and longer documented ischemic delays. The association between sex and the expanded composite was sensitive to adjustment for baseline clinical severity. Sex-specific outcome estimates are hypothesis-generating given the small female subgroup and event counts. The retrospective single-center design, absence of post-discharge follow-up, and unavailable care- and referral-pathway variables limit causal interpretation.

articles.title: Bee Sting-Associated Kounis Syndrome Presenting as Myocardial Infarction: A Case Report and Systematic Review with Age-Based Analysis.
articles.journal: Turk Kardiyoloji Dernegi arsivi : Turk Kardiyoloji Derneginin yayin organidir
articles.abstract: Kounis syndrome (KS) is an uncommon acute coronary syndrome triggered by allergic or hypersensitivity reactions. Bee stings are a recognized precipitant, although the available evidence is largely limited to case reports and small case series. We present a 44-year-old man with probable bee sting-associated KS and systematically review published cases, including an exploratory age-based comparison using ≤45 years as the cutoff for myocardial infarction in younger individuals. PubMed/Medical Literature Analysis and Retrieval System Online (MEDLINE) and Scopus were searched in accordance with the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses (PRISMA) 2020 recommendations. A total of 47 patients were included, comprising 46 previously reported cases and our index case. The mean age was 55.7+-13.0 years, and 39/47 patients (83.0%) were male. Symptoms developed within 30 minutes in 29/47 patients (61.7%), and chest pain occurred in 41/47 (87.2%). Type II KS predominated (29/43, 67.4%), while ST-segment elevation myocardial infarction (STEMI) occurred in 37/47 patients (78.7%), and revascularization was performed in 27/47 (57.4%). Cardiogenic shock, cardiac arrest, and rhythm or conduction disturbances occurred in 11/46 (23.9%), 5/46 (10.9%), and 7/46 patients (15.2%), respectively. Recovery at the last reported assessment was documented in 45/46 patients (97.8%), with no reported deaths. No follow-up data were available after the index patient left the hospital against medical advice approximately five hours after presentation. Thirteen patients (27.7%) were aged ≤45 years; age-stratified descriptive analyses did not reveal clear differences in most clinical characteristics; however, interpretation was limited by the small number of younger patients. Bee sting-associated KS may cause severe acute coronary presentations, including in younger individuals. Given the case-based and heterogeneous nature of the evidence, these findings should be interpreted cautiously and confirmed in systematically collected cohorts.

articles.title: SGLT1/2 inhibitor sotagliflozin, but not SGLT2-selective inhibitor empagliflozin, attenuates platelet activation and thrombosis.
articles.abstract: As rates of type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) have risen, comorbidities of T2DM and cardiovascular disease (CVD) have similarly increased. The adoption of sodium-glucose cotransporter (SGLT) 2 inhibitors as a treatment for T2DM has provided an effective means of decreasing renal glucose reabsorption. In recent clinical trials, sotagliflozin, the first FDA-approved inhibitor of both isoforms of SGLT (SGLT1 and SGLT2), demonstrated a reduction in myocardial infarction and stroke in patients with T2DM at high cardiovascular risk. The cardiovascular protective effect of sotagliflozin compared to the SGLT2-selective inhibitor, empagliflozin, was investigated by evaluating effects on platelet activation and thrombus formation. Employing ex vivo models using blood from healthy donors or T2DM patients, and in vivo mouse models, we demonstrate an inhibitory effect on platelet activity and thrombus formation with sotagliflozin, while empagliflozin has minor to no effects. Further, no impact on hemostasis was observed with sotagliflozin. Finally, a platelet-specific deletion of SGLT1 via Slc5a1fl/fl Gp1ba-Cre⁺ mice resulted in reduced platelet integrin activation and thrombus formation. This study provides insight into a potential explanation for the cardiovascular protection conferred by sotagliflozin observed in patients with T2DM at risk of an ischemic event and reveals an added benefit to SGLT2-selective inhibitors.

articles.title: Phenotype-based risk stratification for deep vein thrombosis in Behçet's disease: a global 10-year longitudinal study.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: Vascular involvement, particularly deep vein thrombosis (DVT), is a major cause of morbidity and mortality in Behçet's disease (BD). This study aimed to identify independent risk factors for DVT and establish a robust framework for phenotype-based risk stratification.

METHODS: We conducted a retrospective cohort study using the TriNetX global health research network and identified 19,739 patients with BD. Three independent propensity score-matched cohorts were established to evaluate the impact of intestinal involvement, thrombophlebitis, and antiphospholipid syndrome (APS). A multivariable Cox proportional hazards model was used to identify independent predictors of DVT over a 10-year follow-up. To ensure the robustness of our findings and minimise peri-diagnostic detection bias, a 90-day landmark analysis was performed as a sensitivity analysis.

RESULTS: Multivariable analysis identified APS (adjusted hazard ratio [aHR] 6.28, 95% confidence interval [CI] 4.56-8.64) and a history of thrombophlebitis (aHR 5.92, 95% CI 4.72-7.41) as the strongest independent predictors of DVT. In the 90-day landmark analysis, these associations remained significant, with persistent risk observed for APS (aHR 5.10) and thrombophlebitis (aHR 2.50), confirming their long-term predictive value. Additional independent predictors included intestinal involvement (defined as non-infective inflammatory colitis; aHR 1.51), obesity (aHR 1.98), glucocorticoid use (aHR 1.78), and male sex (aHR 1.77).

CONCLUSIONS: APS and thrombophlebitis, markers of heightened inflammatory and thrombotic activity at diagnosis, also appear to be persistent indicators of elevated DVT risk in BD. These findings support phenotype-based risk stratification and highlight the need for intensive monitoring and individualised preventive strategies to improve long-term outcomes.

articles.title: Modeling patient variants of Cnot1 and Cdc42bpb results in distinct forms of congenital diaphragmatic hernia in mice.
articles.abstract: Congenital diaphragmatic hernia (CDH) is a severe congenital anomaly characterized by impairment of both diaphragm and lung development in utero. CDH presents as a spectrum of forms and severities, with diaphragm defects arising in the dorsal/posterior region typically correlating with more severe pulmonary disease and higher risk of mortality than those appearing in ventral/anterior regions. The genetic etiology underlying CDH is complex, with many implicated genes showing variable expressivity and incomplete penetrance in both human patients and mouse models. Here we present in vivo validation of two genes previously unassociated with CDH: the CDC42-interacting kinase CDC42BPB; and CNOT1, a scaffolding protein of the CCR4-NOT protein complex, critical for mRNA regulation through modifications such as deadenylation. Each gene was found to have a damaging, de novo missense variant in a recent large-scale CDH patient sequencing screen. Loss of Cdc42bpb leads to ventral diaphragmatic hernias, heart septal defects, and minor lung epithelial differentiation defects in mouse embryos. Installation of the orthologous patient-specific missense variant through CRISPR/Cas9 editing leads to less severe ventral diaphragm defects. Mouse embryos with either one or two copies of the orthologous Cnot1 variant, c.1867C > T (p.R623W), develop dorsal diaphragmatic hernias with low (<50%) penetrance, and mutants showed alterations in mRNA isoform expression consistent with the molecular role of Cnot1 in RNA splicing. These results underscore the power of in vivo functional modeling to validate genes and patient-specific variants uncovered by patient sequencing, reveal two previously unrecognized genetic causes of CDH, and highlight the heterogeneity of different patient anatomic presentations.

articles.title: Bayesian Predictive Inference for Future Order Statistics from the Two-Parameter Lomax Distribution under Type-II Censoring.
articles.abstract: This study develops Bayesian predictive procedures for future order statistics from the two-parameter Lomax distribution under Type-II censored sampling schemes. The proposed framework combines predictive likelihood inference with Bayesian prediction based on independent gamma priors and Markov Chain Monte Carlo (MCMC) simulation using the Metropolis-Hastings algorithm. Bayesian point predictors are derived under the squared error, LINEX, and general entropy loss functions, and predictive intervals are constructed from posterior predictive samples. A detailed Monte Carlo simulation study compares the proposed methods with the classical predictive maximum-likelihood approach across varying sample sizes and censoring levels. For the small-sample scenario (n = 20, r = 14), the Bayesian-LINEX predictor reduced the mean squared prediction error (MSPE) from 0.1542-0.1182, decreased the average predictive interval width (APIW) from 2.4512-2.1985, and increased the coverage probability (CP) from 0.938-0.952 compared with the predictive maximum likelihood method. Overall, the Bayesian methods consistently outperformed the classical approach across all simulation settings, with the Bayesian-LINEX predictor achieving the best predictive performance. These findings demonstrate that the proposed Bayesian framework provides a more accurate and consistent approach for predicting future order statistics from the Lomax distribution while accounting for parameter uncertainty.

articles.title: Impact of a Dynamic Visualized Pain Assessment Tool on Pediatric Pain Management: A Stepped-Wedge Cluster Randomized Trial.
articles.abstract: Effective pediatric pain management relies on accurate assessment; however, current behavioral scales are limited by observer subjectivity and fail to capture dynamic fluctuations. The primary goal of this protocol is to detail the implementation and evaluation of a dynamic visualized pain assessment tool, providing a standardized methodology to transition nursing practice from experience-based estimation to data-driven precision. Using a stepped-wedge cluster randomized trial design across five clinical wards, the study enrolled 15 infants and analyzed 45 video segments across three clinical contexts: baseline, acute procedural pain, and postoperative recovery. The system captured high-definition facial video synchronized with bedside physiological monitoring to generate real-time pain trajectory curves and trend-based alerts. Generalized linear mixed models showed that the tool reduced nursing response latency from 15.4 to 6.7 min (P < 0.001) and increased assessment consistency (intraclass correlation coefficient [ICC]: 0.71-0.93). Concurrently, pediatric satisfaction scores rose, and parental anxiety levels decreased. These findings suggest that dynamic visualization may improve clinical efficiency and patient outcomes through timely, objective decision support.

articles.title: Early Discharge Strategy Including Subcutaneous Furosemide in Hospitalized Heart Failure.
articles.journal: Journal of the American College of Cardiology
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Patients hospitalized for heart failure often require prolonged intravenous diuretic therapy, contributing to costs and risks associated with inpatient care.

OBJECTIVES: We evaluated whether an early discharge strategy using subcutaneous furosemide delivered via a wearable minipump could increase days alive and out of hospital (DAOH).

METHODS: In this multicenter, open-label, randomized, active-controlled trial in the United Kingdom, 172 patients hospitalized for heart failure requiring ongoing parenteral diuretics were randomly assigned to an early discharge strategy or usual care. Patients in the early discharge group received pH-neutral subcutaneous furosemide via a wearable, patient-operated minipump; postdischarge care included a review every 3 days while receiving subcutaneous furosemide. Both groups had a 2-week clinic review. The primary outcome was DAOH at 30 days after randomization.

RESULTS: A total of 92 patients were assigned to early discharge and 80 to usual care. The early discharge strategy resulted in 4.0 more DAOH at 30 days (95% CI: 2.1-5.8 days; P < 0.001). Index hospitalization was shorter by a mean of 5.5 days (95% CI: 7.4-3.6 days; P < 0.001). The benefit in DAOH was sustained at 60 days (difference 4.2 days; 95% CI: 0.9-7.6 days), despite more heart failure readmissions in the early discharge group (13 [14%] patients vs 5 [6%] patients; OR: 2.45; 95% CI: 0.81-7.43). Serious adverse events occurred in 25% and 23% of patients, respectively. Device-related problems occurred with 3% of minipump placements, but none were serious.

CONCLUSIONS: An early discharge strategy using a subcutaneous furosemide minipump increased DAOH compared with usual care. (Use of a Novel SUBCUTaneous Preparation of Furosemide to Facilitate Early Supported Discharge of Patients With Heart Failure [SUBCUT-HF II]; NCT05419115).

articles.title: Epidemiological Characteristics of Venous Thromboembolism and Associated Indicators for Catheter-Related Thrombosis Subtypes.
articles.abstract: Venous thromboembolism (VTE) is a severe and life-threatening complication in hospitalized patients, and central venous catheter (CVC) insertion significantly increases the risk of catheter-related thrombosis (CRT). Epidemiological profiles of hospitalized patients with confirmed VTE are characterized; indicators correlated with CRT subtype are identified; the discriminative performance of circulating biomarkers is evaluated; and VTE recurrence metrics are contrasted between cohorts with and without CVC placement. A single-center retrospective case-case comparative analysis is conducted on 862 patients with imaging-confirmed VTE. Analytical methodologies incorporate univariate and multivariate logistic regression, Kaplan-Meier survival analysis, and receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curve testing. The in-hospital VTE incidence was 2.1%, concentrated in elderly, malignancy, and postoperative patients. CRT incidence was 10.2%, highest with peripherally inserted central catheter (PICC). Five clinical indicators correlated with CRT subtype were identified: prolonged catheter indwelling, catheter malposition, elevated D-dimer levels, malignant tumor history, and prior VTE events. The combination of D-dimer and catheter indwelling time exhibited robust discriminative power (AUC = 0.82) for differentiating CRT from non-CRT VTE among patients with confirmed VTE. The 6-month VTE recurrence rate was 28.4% in the CVC group and 9.7% in the non-CVC group. These observational findings yield only tentative clinical hypotheses aimed at distinguishing thrombotic subtypes among VTE patients. Further multicenter prospective research is necessary to validate these indicators and develop mature, standardized prevention protocols for broad clinical application.

articles.title: Effects of 30- and 90-Minute Afternoon Nap Opportunities on Field-Test Performance in Female Collegiate Basketball Players.
articles.abstract: Afternoon napping is used as a recovery strategy in sport, but a scheduled nap opportunity is not equivalent to objectively verified sleep. This study compared no-nap seated wakefulness (N0), a 30-minute scheduled nap opportunity (N30), and a 90-minute scheduled nap opportunity (N90) in 18 female collegiate basketball players using a randomized, fully counterbalanced, three-period within-participant crossover design. Conditions were separated by at least 72 h and ended at 14:30, followed by a common 60 min wakefulness buffer, a standardized 15 min warm-up, and a fixed basketball field-test battery. Linear mixed-effects models included condition, period, and sequence as fixed effects, with participant as a random intercept; the nine omnibus condition tests were controlled for using the Benjamini-Hochberg false discovery rate procedure. Four of nine outcomes remained significant after false-discovery-rate correction: the modified-505 first 10 m split, combined modified-505 completion time, three-quarter-court sprint time, and 30-15 Intermittent Fitness Test final velocity. N90 differed from both N0 and N30 for these outcomes, whereas N30 did not differ from N0. The other five outcomes did not meet the false-discovery-rate threshold. Sensitivity analyses, including reanalysis of the pre-correction modified-505 data, preserved the same four-outcome pattern. Because sleep onset and duration were not objectively measured, the findings estimate the effects of assigned recovery-opportunity conditions rather than a physiological sleep-duration dose-response.

articles.title: Machine Learning, Radiomics, and Clinical Models Predicting Checkpoint Inhibitor Pneumonitis in Lung Cancer: A Systematic Review and Meta-analysis.
articles.abstract: Checkpoint inhibitor pneumonitis (CIP) is a potentially fatal immune-related adverse event of immune checkpoint inhibitor (ICI) therapy in lung cancer, and many machine-learning (ML), computed tomography (CT) radiomics, deep-learning, and clinical models have been proposed to predict it. This systematic review searched PubMed, Embase, Web of Science, CINAHL, and SinoMed, supplemented by citation searching and other sources, with independent dual-reviewer screening throughout and a reproducible PubMed verification search updated to August 16, 2026. Twelve peer-reviewed lung-cancer CIP-occurrence models (4,875 patients, 1,057 events) formed the main analysis; validation C-statistics were pooled on the logit scale with restricted maximum likelihood and Hartung-Knapp intervals, stratified by validation design. The pooled validation C-statistic was 0.82 (95% confidence interval 0.75-0.88) with high heterogeneity (I2 = 90.7%) and a wide 95% prediction interval of 0.51-0.95, which is the decision-relevant quantity. By validation design, internal cross-validation pooled to 0.83, internal split-sample to 0.76, and only two studies reported external validation (0.84 and 0.92, described narratively). Imaging-based models (k = 8) showed numerically higher discrimination than clinical models (k = 4; 0.85 versus 0.78, moderator p = 0.46) without a statistically significant difference, and this comparison is confounded by design covariates. Estimates were stable on leave-one-out, alternative-model, cohort-overlap, and standard-error-source sensitivity analyses (range 0.80-0.84). Under the standard Prediction model Risk Of Bias ASsessment Tool, applied independently by two reviewers with consensus resolution, two studies were at high, nine at unclear, and one at low overall risk of bias; certainty of evidence was low (very low under a stricter appraisal scenario, which left the pooled estimate essentially unchanged). Current models separate risk groups on average but remain unready for clinical use; adequately powered, externally validated, and calibration-reported models are needed.

articles.title: Premenstrual Syndrome and Premenstrual Dysphoric Disorder: A Systematic Review of Academic Performance and Well-Being in University Students.
articles.abstract: Premenstrual syndrome (PMS) and premenstrual dysphoric disorder (PMDD) are common among women of reproductive age and are associated with academic performance and general well-being at the university level. This review aimed to synthesize evidence on the prevalence of PMS and PMDD and their associations with academic, psychological, and well-being outcomes among female medical and health sciences students. Searches were conducted using PubMed, MEDLINE via Ovid, Web of Science, Wiley Online Library, and EBSCOhost, through which Academic Search Complete, MEDLINE, and PsycINFO were searched for studies published between January 2014 and December 2024. Of 317 identified records, 11 studies met the inclusion criteria; all were observational and cross-sectional. Prevalence estimates varied widely, with PMS ranging from 37.0% to 86.2% and probable PMDD from 13.8% to 66.9%. All PMDD estimates were based on questionnaire screening rather than prospective diagnostic confirmation and therefore represent screening-positive cases rather than confirmed diagnoses. Premenstrual symptoms were associated with impaired concentration, absenteeism, reduced class participation, lower perceived academic performance, and poorer psychological well-being. Associated factors included severe dysmenorrhea, family history, academic stress, irregular or shorter menstrual cycles, and low physical activity. The cross-sectional designs, heterogeneous diagnostic criteria, and varying outcome measures limit causal inference and generalizability. PMS and probable PMDD are associated with poorer academic performance and well-being among female medical and health sciences students. Universities should consider proportionate supportive responses, including menstrual health education, access to health services and counseling, and appropriate academic or social support. Future research should employ standardized diagnostic and outcome measures and prospective study designs.

articles.title: PTCD and Peroral Electronic Cholangioscopy with Holmium Laser Lithotripsy for CBD Stones in a Super-Elderly Patient Post-Billroth II Gastrojejunostomy.
articles.abstract: The management of impacted common bile duct stones in patients with prior Billroth II gastrectomy poses unique challenges. Altered gastrointestinal anatomy renders duodenoscope passage and biliary cannulation during conventional ERCP exceedingly difficult, resulting in a low success rate. Super‑elderly (over 90 years old) patients often have multiple comorbidities such as cardiovascular diseases and require rapid relief of biliary obstruction and infection control to create a subsequent therapeutic window. Meanwhile, traditional open biliary surgery and general anesthesia carry prohibitive risk, along with prolonged preoperative preparation and extensive trauma. Although percutaneous transhepatic choledochoscopic lithotripsy (PTCSL) is unaffected by gastrointestinal reconstruction, it often depends on a large mature biliary sinus tract, necessitating a multi‑stage procedure, entails a risk of hemorrhage, and has difficulty in managing stones, especially papillary impacted stones. To overcome these difficulties, an innovative stepwise strategy was devised comprising "urgent PTCD for rapid decompression followed by multimodal lithotripsy under direct visualization with a peroral electronic cholangioscope." A 92‑year‑old male had a history of multiple surgeries, including Billroth II gastrectomy, cholecystectomy, and colon resection, along with coronary heart disease and atrial fibrillation. Emergency PTCD was performed first, promptly controlling infection and relieving jaundice. After preoperative preparation, the tract was dilated to 10 Fr, and a peroral electronic cholangioscope was introduced through the sheath. Under direct visualization, the common bile duct stones were efficiently fragmented using a holmium laser, initially in a fragmentation mode and then in a dusting mode. Post‑procedural cholangiography confirmed complete stone clearance. The PTCD tube was subsequently removed uneventfully, and the patient recovered well without complications. This strategy successfully circumvents the anatomical alterations, integrates biliary drainage, direct intra‑ductal visualization, and lithotripsy, providing a minimally invasive treatment strategy for patients with bile duct stones after gastrointestinal reconstruction, especially for super‑elderly and other high‑risk individuals.

articles.title: Gliflozin-Derived SGLT2 Inhibitors: Recent Advances and Future Perspectives in the Management of Type 2 Diabetes.
articles.abstract: Gliflozin derivatives, a class of Sodium-Glucose Cotransporter (SGLT) inhibitors, have emerged as effective antidiabetic agents offering notable cardiovascular and renal protection. This class of compounds inhibits glucose reabsorption in the kidneys, thereby improving overall glycaemic control. This review provides a comprehensive overview of gliflozin derivatives, emphasizing their chemical characterization, safety, therapeutic efficacy, pharmacokinetic analysis, and potential future applications, focusing on clinical trials and new developments released between 2010 and 2026. Gliflozin derivatives slow the progression of chronic kidney disease and reduce the risk of heart failure. Some preliminary experimental evidence has reported the antibacterial activity of canagliflozin against MRSA. The Gliflozin derivatives dapagliflozin (IC50 =1.1nM), ertugliflozin (IC50 =0.9nM), sotagliflozin (IC50 =1.8nM), and bexagliflozin (IC50 =2.3nM), which has core motif, 1-chloro-2-(4-alkoxy benzyl) benzene as an aglycon unit and a glycon unit bind with SGLT2 receptor and lowered the HbA1c by 1.2%, 1.7%, 0.41% and 0.80%, respectively. Its selectivity, pharmacokinetics, and toxicity profiles are also optimal. Recent studies have demonstrated their involvement in conditions other than diabetes, including obesity, non-alcoholic fatty liver disease, Cardioprotective, Nephroprotective, Anti-inflammatory, and antihypertensive effects. Gliflozin derivatives represent a paradigm shift in the management of diabetes and have broad therapeutic potential. Future studies should emphasize creative structural changes to increase safety and efficacy.

articles.title: Synthesis of ultra-large Ti3C2T x MXene nanoflakes: enabling high-performance flexible transparent conductive coatings.
articles.abstract: Flexible transparent conductive electrodes (FTCEs) are critical components in next-generation wearable electronics and display technologies. However, achieving low sheet resistance without compromising optical transparency remains a significant challenge due to percolation limitations in thin conductive films. MXenes, a rapidly expanding class of two-dimensional (2D) transition metal carbides and nitrides, offer remarkable potential as transparent conducting electrodes (TCEs) owing to their exceptional electrical conductivity, mechanical flexibility, and intrinsically hydrophilic nature. In this work, a modified orbital shaker-assisted Minimally Intensive Layer Delamination (Orbital-MILD) etching method is introduced, yielding ultra-large Ti3C2T x MXene nanoflakes with an average lateral size of ∼30 µm (optical-microscopy statistics over 168 individual flakes) and individual flakes reaching up to 48 µm - among the largest reported to date for solution-processed MXenes. The gentle orbital mixing action prevents flake fragmentation during both the etching and delamination stages, preserving the large lateral dimensions of the parent MAX phase particles. These large-flake inks were formulated into aqueous colloids and deposited onto flexible polyethylene terephthalate (PET) substrates using slot-die coating - a scalable, alignment-promoting deposition technique. The resultant FTCEs demonstrated an electrical conductivity of 22 777 S cm-1 with a record figure of merit (FoMe) of 39, effectively eliminating the percolation bottleneck common in sparse nanomaterial networks. This work not only addresses a key limitation in MXene-based FTCE fabrication but also opens avenues for extending the method to other MXene systems, enabling scalable production of high-performance flexible electrodes.

articles.title: Resolution of proximal tubular dysfunction after liver transplantation in ATP8B1 deficiency: A case report.
articles.abstract: Progressive familial intrahepatic cholestasis type 1 (PFIC1), caused by ATP8B1 deficiency, is a multisystem disorder with extrahepatic manifestations; however, renal involvement has rarely been described. We report a child with genetically confirmed PFIC1 who underwent living donor liver transplantation (LT) for progressive liver disease. Before transplantation, serum creatinine was normal, but a Fanconi-like proximal tubular dysfunction was characterized by elevated urinary β2-microglobulin, proteinuria, phosphaturia, hypercalciuria, and metabolic acidosis requiring bicarbonate supplementation. Following transplantation, these abnormalities rapidly resolved, supporting the hypothesis of reversible cholestasis-associated tubular injury. This case identifies proximal tubular dysfunction as an underrecognized, potentially reversible manifestation of severe, prolonged cholestasis in PFIC1 and supports systematic evaluation of tubular markers before transplantation.

articles.title: Clinical management and multimodal imaging features of brucellar mastitis mimicking metastatic breast carcinoma: a rare case report and literature review.
articles.abstract: Brucella mastitis represents a rare infectious disease that is frequently misdiagnosed as metastatic breast carcinoma, particularly when older women present with systemic manifestations. Here, we report a 60-year-old woman presenting with a neck pain and left upper extremity numbness. Initial contrast-enhanced magnetic resonance imaging (CEMR) and 18F-FDG PET-CT highly suggested breast malignancy with osseous metastasis, while contrast-enhanced ultrasound (CEUS) provided critical microvascular perfusion insights favoring an inflammatory process. The diagnosis was ultimately confirmed via blood culture and pathological examination. The patient was successfully treated with targeted antimicrobial treatment. This case offers important insights into the multimodal imaging differentiation of atypical breast lesions and emphasizes the diagnostic challenges of Brucella mastitis accompanied by systemic osteoarticular involvement.

articles.title: Exploring Nurses' and Patients' Experiences of an Oral Care Intervention to Prevent Non-Ventilator Hospital Acquired Pneumonia.
articles.abstract:
AIM AND OBJECTIVES: To explore the enablers, barriers and experiences of implementing an oral care intervention in an acute hospital setting, from the perspective of nurses and patients.

BACKGROUND: Hospital-acquired pneumonia is a common healthcare-associated infection. Oral care can reduce the risk of hospital-acquired pneumonia but is often missed due to clinical priorities.

DESIGN: Exploratory qualitative study.

METHODS: Semi-structured interviews with 18 Registered Nurses and 8 Research Nurses facilitating an oral care intervention, and three patients who acquired pneumonia during admission to an intervention ward. Data were collected June to August 2025 and thematically analysed.

RESULTS: Four themes were identified: varied knowledge and capacity to empower practice; education as a catalyst for practice change; competing demands and resistance; and relational and functional support to achieve change. Participants highlighted that successful oral care delivery relied on understanding its connection to hospital-acquired pneumonia. Competing workload demands often resulted in oral care being deprioritised.

CONCLUSIONS: Strengthening nurses', patients' and families' understanding of oral care during hospitalisation can improve adherence to oral care practices and enhance patient engagement.

RELEVANCE TO CLINICAL PRACTICE: Acute care nurses are central to delivering oral care, yet competing priorities and limited awareness of its relationship to hospital-acquired pneumonia can affect implementation. These findings can inform nursing education and strategies to support patient, family and clinician engagement.

PATIENT OR PUBLIC CONTRIBUTIONS: Consumer and clinician feedback informed the development of interview questions. This study forms part of The HAPPEN study, which included consumer and partner input into intervention design, study materials and dissemination activities.

articles.title: Physical activity and quality of life in patients with hypertrophic cardiomyopathy in Japan: a quantitative study.
articles.abstract:
AIM: To describe the burden of hypertrophic cardiomyopathy (HCM) using patient-reported outcome tools and a study-specific questionnaire.

PATIENTS AND METHODS: This two-phase, cross-sectional, non-interventional, observational study (qualitative [previous] and quantitative [current]) included adults with HCM and New York Heart Association functional classification 2/3 recruited from healthcare facilities across Japan. The International Physical Activity Questionnaire (IPAQ), Kansas City Cardiomyopathy Questionnaire (KCCQ), Hypertrophic Cardiomyopathy Symptom Questionnaire (HCMSQ), and Hospital Anxiety and Depression Scale (HADS) were used alongside a questionnaire developed using the qualitative findings.

RESULTS: The analysis included 120 patients (mean age, 59.1 ± 16.3 years; 55.5% [66/120] male), 60 each with non-obstructive and obstructive HCM. Patients with (vs. without) lifestyle changes had lower median IPAQ score (495.0 [363.0-1803.5] vs. 990.0 [369.4-2295.0], p = 0.159) and KCCQ - Clinical Summary Score (81.3 [65.6-90.7] vs. 92.0 [81.4-97.9], p < 0.001), and higher HADS-Depression (5.0 [3.0-8.0] vs. 2.0 [1.0-6.0], p = 0.001) and HCMSQ-shortness of breath (5.0 [2.0-6.0] vs. 3.0 [0.0-4.5], p < 0.001) scores. Most patients (83.9%) noticed HCM symptoms, and some patients attributed symptoms to causes other than HCM. Most patients (89.0%) told others about their HCM. Primary care physicians were the main information source (99.2%).

CONCLUSIONS: In this quantitative analysis, HCM affected patients' lifestyles and physical activity.

CLINICAL TRIAL REGISTRATION: NCT06181617 (ClinicalTrials.gov).

articles.title: Arthroscopic Bankart Repair Is Associated With Lower 90-Day Emergency Department Use Than Open Repair, With Smoking, Medicaid Insurance, and Depression as Additional Independent Predictors.
articles.journal: Arthroscopy : the journal of arthroscopic & related surgery : official publication of the Arthroscopy Association of North America and the International Arthroscopy Association
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: To characterize the timing, frequency, and predictors of 90-day emergency department (ED) visits after Bankart repair using a national administrative database.

METHODS: Patients undergoing primary arthroscopic or open Bankart repair were identified from the 2010 to 2023 Q1 PearlDiver M170 database. Patients with infection or neoplasm within 90 days preoperatively or less than 90 days of database follow-up were excluded. Multivariable logistic regression identified independent predictors of ED visits within 90 days postoperatively. Among ED users, weekly visit timing was compared with a baseline rate (range of rates from postoperative weeks 53-57), and primary diagnoses at 1, 2, and 3 months were categorized.

RESULTS: Of 149,024 patients (age 33.4 years, 66.1% men, 95.5% arthroscopic), 11,760 (7.9%) visited the ED, with 25.8% of visits occurring during the first 2 postoperative weeks. Independent predictors of ED use included (in decreasing odds ratio order) recent smoking (odds ratio 2.99), Medicaid insurance (2.03), depression (1.70), prior opioid use (1.56), social determinants of health (1.55), diabetes (1.45), Medicare insurance (1.36), open surgical approach (1.34), female sex (1.33), body mass index  ≥ 30 (1.24), Midwest region (1.21), and age (1.01. per year decrease) (P < .001 for all). Shoulder-related visits accounted for 33.2% of ED encounters in month 1, declining to 17.6% and 13.0% by months 2 and 3, with shoulder pain as the leading subcategory at every postoperative month.

CONCLUSIONS: After Bankart repair, nearly 8% of patients presented to the ED within 90 days, with the highest incidence occurring during the first 2 postoperative weeks. The strongest independent predictors of ED visits included smoking (odds ratio 2.99), Medicaid insurance (2.03), depression (1.70), prior opioid use within 6 months (1.56), social determinants of health (1.55), diabetes (1.45), Medicare insurance (1.36), open surgical approach (1.34), and female sex (1.33). Shoulder pain was the most common shoulder-related reason for ED presentation across all 3 postoperative months.

LEVEL OF EVIDENCE: Level III, retrospective comparative study.

articles.title: Post-treatment risks of transcatheter aortic valve implantation: should we be increasing preventative measures?
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Transcatheter aortic valve implantation (TAVI) has become an established treatment for severe aortic stenosis across an expanding risk spectrum. As indications extend to younger and lower-risk patients, post-treatment complications with implications for survival, quality of life, and valve durability require attention.

AREAS COVERED: This narrative review discusses major post-TAVI complications with direct implications for procedural planning and lifetime management, including cerebrovascular events, conduction abnormalities, coronary obstruction and aortic root injury, bioprosthetic valve dysfunction, valve thrombosis, residual regurgitation, and TAVI-associated infective endocarditis. Evidence was reviewed from pivotal randomized trials, contemporary registries, consensus documents, systematic reviews, and mechanistic studies addressing incidence, pathophysiology, predictors, prognosis, prevention, diagnosis, and management of these complications.

EXPERT OPINION: Post-TAVI risk reduction should move beyond reactive complication management toward individualized prevention. Meticulous computed tomography-based planning, optimized valve selection and implantation technique, rational antithrombotic therapy, structured rhythm and valve surveillance, selective use of cerebral embolic protection, timely correction of clinically or hemodynamically significant residual regurgitation, and infection-prevention pathways are central components of contemporary care. Future progress will depend on better risk stratification, longer-term durability data, and targeted preventive strategies adapted to lower-risk patients with longer life expectancy.

articles.title: Association of Xeroderma Pigmentosum group F (XPF) with epigenetic regulation of T helper cell differentiation in coronary artery disease-associated prostate cancer.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Coronary artery disease (CAD) and prostate cancer share common genetic and epigenetic risk factors. Xeroderma Pigmentosum group F (XPF), a DNA repair endonuclease, has been implicated in genomic stability and epigenetic regulation. This study investigated the association between XPF expression and epigenetic changes during T helper (TH) cell differentiation in CAD-associated prostate cancer (CAD-PC).

RESEARCH DESIGN AND METHODS: CD4+ T cells isolated from healthy controls and CAD-PC patients were subjected to CRISPR/Cas9-mediated XPF knockout or overexpression. TH cell differentiation, chromatin enrichment, global m6A RNA methylation, DNA methylation, R-loop formation, and tumor cell cytotoxicity were evaluated using molecular and functional assays.

RESULTS: XPF overexpression was associated with increased TH1 differentiation and elevated expression of XPF and TP53, whereas TH2, TH17, and Treg-associated markers were reduced. Increased enrichment of XPF and H3K4me3, together with reduced HDAC1, γH2A.X, and H3K27me3 enrichment, was observed at the TBX21 and IFNG loci. XPF overexpression was also associated with increased global m6A RNA methylation, reduced DNA methylation at TH1-associated loci, decreased R-loop accumulation, and enhanced tumor cell cytotoxicity in vitro.

CONCLUSION: These findings suggest that XPF expression is associated with a TH1-skewed epigenetic and immune profile in CAD-PC. However, the absence of disease-specific comparison groups and in vivo validation limits mechanistic interpretation, and further studies are required to establish causality. The present findings demonstrate an association between XPF and the observed TH1-associated epigenetic changes.

articles.title: Estimands for combination therapy oncology trials with competing risks and their integration with Project SignifiCanT.
articles.abstract: The evaluation of combination therapies in oncology increasingly demands estimand frameworks that reflect component-specific treatment strategies, complex intercurrent events (ICEs), and competing or semi-competing risk structures. Traditional hazard-based analyses often lack causal interpretability in these settings, particularly when selective discontinuation, immune-mediated toxicity, or death modifies subsequent exposure and influences event pathways. To address these limitations, we propose a unified causal-estimand framework specifically tailored for combination oncology trials. Grounded in potential-outcomes theory and aligned with ICH E9 (R1), the framework (i) defines regimen-level, component-specific, and pathway-specific estimands; (ii) formally maps these estimands to ICE strategies - treatment policy, hypothetical, composite, principal stratum, and while-on-treatment; (iii) evaluates the compatibility of commonly used statistical approaches, including cause-specific hazards, subdistribution hazards, and multi-state models, with these estimands; and (iv) integrates these elements with the regulatory objectives of the FDA's Project SignifiCanT, with particular emphasis on mechanistic interpretability, benefit-risk assessment, and transparent justification of analytical choices. By expressing estimands as contrasts of counterfactual risk or state-occupation functions - rather than relying solely on model-based hazard ratios - the framework enhances clinical relevance, supports attribution of component-specific effects, and facilitates cross-trial comparability. This work provides a principled foundation for designing, analysing, and reporting combination oncology trials, thereby advancing both methodological rigour and regulatory clarity.

articles.title: Heat and childhood respiratory health: exploring the evidence and raising the red flags.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Climate change impacts on the health of vulnerable groups globally. Heat, as a specific component of climate change, affects the respiratory health of children, particularly those from marginalized communities and in low and middle-income countries. Understanding the exposure pathways for these outcomes is critical for interventions and policy development.

AREAS COVERED: A synthesis of the evidence for key heat-related childhood respiratory outcomes (asthma, infections, rhinitis and lung function) is presented. The knowledge gaps are highlighted. Interpreting the evidence requires understanding the approaches to heat exposure characterization in epidemiological studies. These exposure-response complexities are explored.

EXPERT OPINION: While the evidence for heat-related adverse events among children with asthma and respiratory infections is strong, it is less so for other respiratory outcomes. Inconsistencies exist across studies. These inconsistencies may be as a result of how exposure is characterized in studies. While acute outcomes have been investigated mostly from hospital records, sub-clinical effects among children in community-based studies are absent. Limited studies have been conducted in marginalized communities or in low- and middle-income countries. Understanding exposure-response relationships and addressing gaps in the evidence is necessary for the development of appropriate interventions to protect the respiratory health of children.

articles.title: [18F]fluorodeoxyglucose PET/CT refines staging and treatment selection in high-risk upper tract urothelial carcinoma.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: To evaluate the incremental clinical value of [18F]fluorodeoxyglucose positron emission tomography/computed tomography ([18F]FDG-PET/CT) beyond contrast-enhanced computed tomography (CECT) for primary staging of suspected high-risk upper tract urothelial carcinoma (UTUC).

PATIENTS AND METHODS: We conducted a consecutive paired-imaging cohort study of patients with suspected high-risk UTUC undergoing primary staging with both CECT and [18F]FDG-PET/CT at a tertiary cancer centre between 2013 and 2025. The primary outcome was clinically relevant stage migration, defined as a transition between non-metastatic and metastatic disease, and its impact on multidisciplinary treatment recommendation. Secondary outcomes included diagnostic performance in cases with histopathological verification.

RESULTS: Among 203 patients, [18F]FDG-PET/CT resulted in stage migration in 45 (22%), predominantly through upstaging (39 patients [19%]), comprising regional nodal upstaging in 19 patients (9.4%) and distant metastatic upstaging in 22 (11%), with both occurring in two patients. [18F]FDG-PET/CT led to treatment modification in 43 patients (21%). Stage migration was more frequent in the presence of CECT-suspicious lymph nodes (odds ratio 3.4, 95% confidence interval 1.6-7.3). Among the 62 patients with histopathological verification, [18F]FDG-PET/CT demonstrated significantly higher sensitivity for nodal metastases than CECT (74% vs 33%) with similar specificity (89% vs 86%). Limitations include the retrospective single-centre design and incomplete pathological confirmation, mostly due to neoadjuvant treatment and omission of surgery in metastatic disease.

CONCLUSION: [18F]FDG-PET/CT provides actionable staging information beyond CECT in high-risk UTUC, leading to treatment modification in one in five patients and in half of those with CECT-suspicious nodal disease. These findings support selective use of [18F]FDG-PET/CT in primary staging to refine treatment selection.

articles.title: Better data for better public health decision-making: perspectives on quantifying the intended and unintended impacts of public service modifications.
articles.abstract: Public services such as healthcare, schools, and transport constitute the infrastructure essential for a functioning and productive society. These services may undergo planned modifications because of interventions intended to manage societal challenges, or experience unplanned disruptions resulting from external shocks. For instance, schools might be closed to mitigate the spread of an infectious disease, or when an external shock, such as a heatwave, renders their continued operation infeasible. These modifications to public services, whether planned or unplanned, have both intended and unintended public health outcomes, as well as wider and longer-term societal consequences. To improve our response to various societal challenges, it is essential to assess the relation between the extent of modifications and the intended outcomes, and identify the full spectrum of unintended consequences, both beneficial and adverse. A central pillar of such an exercise would be timely and granular data on the modifications and outcomes - what was done, what happened, to whom, where, and when? However, these data are rarely, if ever, systematically collected. Instead, research into the evaluation of public service modifications relies on sporadic and bespoke data collection. In this perspective, we highlight a critical data gap in tracking public service availability, adaptations, and interventions, illustrating our arguments through two case studies. We examine the challenges in collecting and integrating such data and propose practical solutions to improve data infrastructure and cross-sectoral coordination.

articles.title: What is the significance of intra-operative oliguria with regard to post-operative acute kidney injury? A physiology-informed framework for intra-operative oliguria management.
articles.journal: Journal of anesthesia, analgesia and critical care
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Intra-operative oliguria is frequently interpreted as a surrogate for hypovolaemia or impaired renal perfusion, often prompting reflexive and potentially harmful fluid administration. However, urine output during anaesthesia is influenced by a complex interplay of neurohormonal activation, surgical stress, and positive pressure ventilation, which can decouple diuresis from actual renal blood flow. This perspective articles critically appraises the evidence linking intra-operative oliguria to acute kidney injury (AKI) and explores the physiological pitfalls of interpreting urine output as an isolated haemodynamic target.

RESULTS: Recent high-level evidence confirms a significant correlation between intra-operative oliguria and post-operative AKI, yet also highlights substantial heterogeneity in the thresholds and durations used across clinical practice. To address this, we propose a conceptual, physiology-informed framework that categorises reduced urine output into four distinct clinical phenotypes: adaptive (a physiologic neurohormonal response to stress), haemodynamic (potentially reversible hypoperfusion), high-risk/complex (occurring in major surgery or vulnerable patients), and injury-associated (established renal damage). In one highly selected high-risk population, a single randomised trial reported that targeting supranormal, urine-guided hydration was associated with a lower incidence of AKI. These findings are hypothesis-generating only and should not be generalised, but they raise the possibility that oliguria in narrowly defined contexts may represent a potentially modifiable signal warranting further prospective study rather than passive observation. Bedside adjuncts, such as ultrasound assessment of cardiac output or venous congestion, may assist in differentiating these phenotypes, although their intra-operative validation remains limited. This framework is intended as a hypothesis-generating conceptual aid to clinical reasoning, not as a validated clinical algorithm or practice recommendation.

CONCLUSION: Interpreting intra-operative oliguria requires a fundamental shift from binary thresholds to context-dependent phenotyping. Effective management must prioritise individualised assessment-integrating surgical risk, baseline patient vulnerability, and dynamic monitoring-rather than responding to isolated urine output triggers.

articles.title: Integrated physical, cognitive and psychological rehabilitation following multiple ACL reconstructions in a professional handball player: a case report.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Anterior cruciate ligament (ACL) injuries with repeated surgical interventions and postoperative complications pose a major challenge in sports rehabilitation. Beyond neuromuscular deficits, psychological and cognitive readiness often remain impaired, increasing reinjury risk and threatening athletic careers. This case highlights an integrated rehabilitation strategy addressing physical, psychological, and cognitive domains in a professional athlete with a complex surgical history.

CASE PRESENTATION: A 31-year-old white Serbian male professional handball player with a history of two ACL reconstructions, meniscal repairs, a postoperative knee infection, and multiple arthroscopic interventions presented with persistent knee instability, pain, and psychological distress. Following repeated failed return-to-play attempts, he underwent a ten-week intervention combining therapeutic exercises, sports psychology sessions, and neurocognitive dual-task training. Pre- and post-intervention assessments included gait analysis, postural control, strength testing, ACL-specific functional tests, and psychological evaluations. Post-intervention assessments showed improvements in gait mechanics, postural stability, neuromuscular strength, and reduced functional asymmetries, alongside lower cognitive anxiety and greater motivation.

CONCLUSIONS: This case suggests that an interdisciplinary, multimodal rehabilitation approach, integrating physical, psychological, and cognitive strategies, may help address both physical deficits and psychological barriers in athletes with multiple ACL surgeries and complex postoperative courses. Such integration may support function, confidence, and readiness in high-performance athletes facing career-threatening injuries.

articles.title: Proteomic identification of resistin as a NET-associated neutrophil activity marker in sepsis.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Neutrophil extracellular traps (NETs) contribute to organ dysfunction in sepsis, yet clinically accessible biomarkers reflecting NET-associated pathology remain limited. We sought to identify circulating proteins associated with NET formation and evaluate their clinical relevance in sepsis.

METHODS: Unbiased proteomic profiling of stimulated human neutrophil supernatants and serum from murine sepsis was performed to identify proteins released during NET formation and elevated in vivo. Candidate biomarkers were selected through integration of these datasets and filtering based on cell type-specific expression profiles, followed by validation in patients with sepsis and healthy controls.

RESULTS: Integrative analysis identified five candidate circulating markers associated with NET formation in sepsis: cathelicidin antimicrobial peptide, lactotransferrin, neutrophil gelatinase-associated lipocalin (NGAL), resistin, and histone H4. Among these, resistin, a recently recognized neutrophil-associated protein, and NGAL demonstrated the strongest associations with sepsis-associated complications. Both markers were elevated in patients with sepsis and correlated with circulating cell-free DNA levels. In receiver operating characteristic curve analyses, resistin discriminated multiple organ failure (AUC, 0.83) and disseminated intravascular coagulation (AUC, 0.81), whereas NGAL demonstrated similarly robust performance (AUC, 0.84 and 0.79, respectively). Both markers outperformed conventional clinical parameters for discriminating sepsis-associated complications.

CONCLUSIONS: These findings identify resistin as a circulating marker associated with NET formation that captures key features of sepsis-associated immunothrombosis and organ failure and may improve assessment of disease severity and risk stratification.

articles.title: Integration of Collaborative Cross and Hybrid Mouse Diversity Panel studies does not significantly improve genome wide association study results.
articles.abstract: Genome-wide association studies rely on maximizing cohort size and minimizing environmental noise to increase their efficacy. Model organism Genetic Reference Populations offer significantly reduced environmental noise and deep phenotyping, yet rarely are multiple populations merged together. We evaluated whether combining the Collaborative Cross (CC) and Hybrid Mouse Diversity Panel (HMDP), two well-studied murine Genetic Reference Populations would improve GWAS outcomes. Utilizing two prior studies by our group that had performed the same study for heart failure in each cohort, we examined each cohort individually and then together using the pyLMM GWAS algorithm. Surprisingly, the combined cohort of 175 strains produced only 123 loci, a modest gain over the 104-strain HMDP (114), and fewer than in the 71-strain CC (149) and did not systematically improve resolution. Locus overlap between the CC and HMDP cohorts was very sparse, with only a single locus (near Eprs1) found to be significant in each cohort, although nearly half of all combined loci were also found in the CC cohort. These results caution that merging divergent GRPs may act to dilute signal and complicate interpretation, despite larger sample sizes.

articles.title: Anticoagulation-associated hemorrhage in atrial fibrillation as a marker of occult malignancy: a narrative review.
articles.abstract: Atrial fibrillation (AF) is the most common arrhythmia in adults and significantly increases the risk of stroke. Due to common threats like systemic inflammation and treatment-related cardiotoxicity, individuals with cancer have a noticeably increased chance of developing AF. Managing AF in this population presents dual challenges: reducing thromboembolic risk while minimizing bleeding complications. Traditionally, warfarin, a vitamin K antagonist, has been the most widely used anticoagulant. However, the emergence of direct oral anticoagulants (DOACs), which offer equal or superior efficacy compared to warfarin with fewer dietary and drug interactions, has shifted clinical practice. This narrative review explores the complex clinical relationship between AF, anticoagulation, and bleeding as a potential early indicator of occult cancer. An expanding body of evidence from extensive cohort studies and meta-analyses supports this association, showing a significantly increased risk of gastrointestinal, genitourinary, respiratory, and, to a lesser extent, intracranial bleeding in anticoagulated patients that may precede cancer diagnosis. Although bleeding is a recognized difficulty of oral anticoagulation, it may expose occult malignancy, resulting in timely detection of cancer and more favorable outcomes. Perhaps it is time to regard occult gastrointestinal bleeding for what it may be: an early warning sign of malignancy. The increased risk of both thromboembolism and bleeding in cancer patients poses a challenge in clinical practice. Though bleeding has increasingly been recognized as a potential harbinger of occult cancer, uniform guidelines for malignant lesion screening after a hemorrhagic episode remain to be established. It is essential to establish a solid, evidence-based therapeutic protocol to achieve the best possible treatment and results for patients.

articles.title: Metabolic convergence on TOR signaling in the chestnut blight fungus and its regulation by host plant signals.
articles.abstract: Transcriptomic analysis of the chestnut blight fungus Cryphonectria parasitica identified 22 core genes regulated by Cryphonectria hypovirus 1 (CHV1) infection and sectorization. Twelve genes with common phenocopies were analyzed: all mutants displayed restricted colonial growth, intense pigmentation, hyperbranched terminal hyphae with swollen globose cells, and reduced conidiation. Although gene-specific mutant phenotypes existed, responses to most stressors were similar to those of the wild-type. Mutant growth was highly sensitive to nutrient conditions, and growth restriction was notably alleviated by supplementation with 1.0 M sorbitol, nutrient-deficient media, or skim milk. All mutants showed hallmarks consistent with reduced target of rapamycin (TOR) signaling. Trehalose accumulation, a canonical fungal response to TOR inhibition, was observed in mutants via transcriptional upregulation of core trehalose biosynthetic genes, resulting in altered hyphal osmolarity and common mutant cell phenotypes. Plant signals overrode the mutants' phenotypes, strongly promoting their growth and differentiation. Although a severely retarded growth defect was observed in mutants, mutants' virulence remained intact, which can be ascribed to the host-plant signals. Cryphonectria hypovirus 1 (CHV1)-infected mutants exhibited greater growth restriction, accompanied by genotype-specific CHV1 titers. Despite gene-specific variation, common phenocopies indicate that diverse metabolic pathways converge on the TOR pathway in the fungal response to host-plant and CHV1 infection.

articles.title: Temporal changes in clinical practices for patients considered clinically brain dead: a single-center cohort study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Patients considered clinically brain dead undergo neurological assessment and critical care management, along with discussions with their families regarding goals of care and, when appropriate, organ donation. However, how these clinical and organ donation-related practices have evolved over time remains poorly characterized in Japan. We aimed to evaluate temporal changes in neurological assessment, critical care management, and organ donation-related processes among patients considered clinically brain dead.

METHODS: We conducted a retrospective single-center cohort study including consecutive patients considered clinically brain dead in the Emergency ICU of Okayama University Hospital between January 2017 and December 2025. Patients were identified through routine auditory brainstem response testing during evaluation for a brain-death-compatible state. Temporal changes in the determination of a brain-death-compatible state, organ donation discussion, and critical care management were evaluated by calendar year, with three study phases (2017-2019, 2020-2022, and 2023-2025) used for descriptive presentation. Annual trends were assessed using logistic regression and nonparametric trend analyses.

RESULTS: Among 128 eligible patients, organ donation was discussed with the families of 110 (85.9%), and 41 (37.3%) subsequently underwent organ donation after brain death. Calendar-year analyses showed increasing corticosteroid use (odds ratio [OR] per year, 1.64; 95% confidence interval [CI] 1.34-2.01; p < 0.001) and earlier initiation of corticosteroids and vasopressin, whereas no significant trends were observed in vasopressin use or in the timing of determination of a brain-death-compatible state or the initial organ donation discussion. The likelihood of organ donation discussion increased significantly over time (OR per year, 1.44; 95% CI 1.17-1.79; p = 0.001) and remained significant in a sensitivity analysis restricted to patients in whom discussion was considered feasible (OR per year, 2.11; 95% CI 1.42-3.15; p < 0.001).

CONCLUSIONS: The opportunity for organ donation discussion increased over time among patients considered clinically brain dead, while the proportion of families consenting to donation remained relatively stable. This increase occurred alongside the progressive development of structured multidisciplinary processes, although their contribution to the observed temporal trend cannot be determined from this descriptive study.

articles.title: Early versus deferred intravenous calcium in patients with sepsis and ionized hypocalcemia: a target-trial emulation.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Intravenous calcium is frequently administered during sepsis, yet whether early treatment improves 24-h hemodynamic recovery remains uncertain. We compared 24-h hemodynamic recovery between calcium initiation within 2 h of a non-emergency low-ionized calcium (iCa) result and no calcium initiation during the first 6 h after the result.

METHODS: We conducted a retrospective target-trial emulation of 2016-2025 high-resolution electronic health records from Zigong Fourth People's Hospital. Adults with sepsis, final or corrected iCa of 0.90-1.10 mmol/L, and no emergency indication were eligible at result availability. Strategies were executed calcium within 2 h versus no calcium through 6 h; care after 6 h was unrestricted. Clone-censor weighting and overlap tilting addressed grace periods, measured time-varying confounding, and clinical equipoise. The primary outcome was being alive and vasopressor-free at 24 h. Estimates and two-sided 95% percentile intervals came from 2,000 patient-level bootstrap samples with model refitting.

RESULTS: Of 5,993 patients, 1,538 initiated calcium within 2 h, 147 initiated at 2-6 h, and 4,308 received none through 6 h; none of the latter initiated calcium during 6-24 h. The standardized probability of 24-h hemodynamic recovery was 69.9% with early calcium and 61.1% with deferral, corresponding to a risk difference of + 8.69 percentage points (95% percentile interval, + 4.66 to + 12.84) and a risk ratio of 1.142 (1.074-1.214). The estimated association varied with baseline norepinephrine-equivalent dose (Holm-adjusted P = 2.00 × 10⁻⁶), whereas the iCa interaction did not remain statistically supported after adjustment (P = 0.097). Early calcium was associated with a 1.29-percentage-point higher observed risk of hypercalcemia (95% percentile interval, + 0.64 to + 2.05). Intervals for severe arrhythmia, new renal replacement therapy, and hospital mortality included the null.

CONCLUSIONS: Early intravenous calcium was associated with a higher probability of 24-h hemodynamic recovery than the deferred strategy, whose observed pathway involved no calcium through 24 h. Estimated effects were larger at higher vasopressor doses. Early calcium was associated with a modestly higher observed risk of hypercalcemia. These findings support randomized evaluation in vasopressor-treated patients. Baseline iCa modification remains exploratory.

articles.title: Biventricular Assist Devices Versus Total Artificial Heart as Bridge-to-Transplantation Strategies: A Systematic Review and Meta-analysis.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: Biventricular assist devices (BiVADs) and total artificial heart (TAH) are the principal bridge-to-transplantation strategies for patients with advanced biventricular heart failure awaiting heart transplantation, but their comparative effectiveness and safety remain uncertain. This systematic review and meta-analysis compared pretransplant outcomes between the two approaches.

METHODS: A systematic review and meta-analysis was conducted in accordance with the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses guidelines. PubMed, Scopus, Web of Science, and Cochrane Library were searched from inception through January 2026 for studies comparing BiVADs and TAH as bridge-to-transplantation strategies. Study quality was assessed using the Newcastle-Ottawa Scale, and certainty of evidence was evaluated using the GRADE framework. Random-effects models were used to compare survival to transplantation, mortality during support, support-related complications, and duration of support.

RESULTS: Ten retrospective studies involving 2,242 patients met the inclusion criteria. The overall analysis showed no significant difference in survival to transplantation between patients supported with BiVADs and TAH (RR = 0.97, 95% CI (0.84, 1.13), P = 0.74). However, after excluding potentially overlapping cohorts, sensitivity analysis showed a higher rate of survival to transplantation in those supported with TAH (RR = 0.88, 95% CI (0.80, 0.97), P = 0.01). No significant difference was observed in mortality during support in the overall analysis (RR = 1.19, 95% CI (0.88, 1.61), P = 0.26) or after excluding potentially overlapping cohorts (RR = 0.98, 95% CI (0.79, 1.21), P = 0.84). BiVADs were associated with higher rates of bleeding and stroke (RR = 2.79, 95% CI (1.70, 4.59), P < 0.0001 and RR = 2.31, 95% CI (1.53, 3.50), P < 0.0001, respectively), whereas infection did not differ significantly between the two groups (RR = 1.18, 95% CI (0.50, 2.78), P = 0.70). Sensitivity analysis for stroke after excluding potentially overlapping cohorts showed a similarly higher rate in patients supported with BiVADs (RR = 2.39, 95% CI (1.46, 3.93), P = 0.0006). Duration of support did not differ significantly between both groups in the overall analysis (MD = 2.25 days, 95% CI (- 16.46, 20.96), P = 0.81) or after excluding potentially overlapping cohorts (MD = - 0.90 days, 95% CI (- 24.26, 22.46), P = 0.94).

CONCLUSION: TAH may be associated with higher rates of survival to transplantation after excluding potentially overlapping cohorts, while BiVAD support may be associated with higher rates of bleeding and stroke. However, all included studies were retrospective, and the certainty of evidence was low for most outcomes. These findings should therefore be interpreted with caution and require confirmation in prospective multicenter studies.
