articles.title: LC-MS profiling and antiulcer mechanisms of Rumex pictus extract and its isolated emodin-8-O-β-glucoside against ethanol-induced gastric damage.
articles.abstract: Peptic ulcer disease is considered a global health concern, commonly caused by Helicobacter pylori infection, chronic NSAID use, and ethanol-induced gastric mucosal injury. Although proton pump inhibitors and anti-secretory drugs are effective, their prolonged use increases risks of fractures, infections, and nutrient deficiencies, highlighting the urgent need for safer alternatives. The Rumex genus, particularly R. pictus Forssk. aerial parts, has long been employed in Middle Eastern traditional medicine to alleviate gastric inflammation and ulcers. The antiulcer bioassays of the 70% aqueous methanolic R. pictus extract (RPE) (150-300 mg/kg) and its isolated emodin-8-O-β-glucoside (EGL) (15-30 mg/kg) were assessed using an in vivo ethanol-induced gastric injury model. Additionally, LC-ESI-MS/MS was used to identify the phenolic constituents from RPE. 42 Metabolites were identified from LC-ESI-MS/MS profiling of RPE including phenolic acids (e.g. caffeic, ferulic, chlorogenic), flavonoid C- and O-glycosides (e.g. orientin, isoorientin, vitexin, isovitexin, hyperoside), and anthraquinones (e.g. emodin, chrysophanol, physcion, and their glycosides). Both RPE and EGL restored gastric antioxidant defenses by elevating glutathione and glutathione-S-transferase while lowering MDA levels, downregulated pro-inflammatory cytokines: TNF-α and IL-1β, and enhanced cytoprotective PGE2 production. Notably, the higher dose of EGL (30 mg/kg) produced superior gastroprotection as it demonstrated greater suppression of oxidative stress and cytokine release alongside enhanced mucosal regeneration. Histopathological analysis further confirmed reduced hemorrhage, edema, and epithelial necrosis, particularly at higher doses. These findings establish RPE and EGL as promising gastroprotective candidates, reinforcing their ethnomedicinal value and supporting further development as safer alternatives for peptic ulcer management.

articles.title: Diagnostic Value of Skin Biopsy in Fatal Histoplasmosis-Associated Hemophagocytic Lymphohistiocytosis: A Case Report.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Hemophagocytic lymphohistiocytosis (HLH) is a rare, life-threatening hyperinflammatory syndrome most commonly triggered in adults by infection, malignancy, or autoimmune disease. Disseminated histoplasmosis is an uncommon but recognized infectious trigger, particularly in immunosuppressed patients. Its cutaneous manifestations may be subtle and nonspecific but can provide accessible tissue for diagnostic evaluation.

CASE REPORT: A 41-year-old man with psoriasis treated with adalimumab presented with 5 months of progressive constitutional and abdominal symptoms followed by fever, shock, pancytopenia, hepatosplenomegaly, coagulopathy, hypertriglyceridemia, and extreme hyperferritinemia (>  89,000 ng/mL). Bone marrow biopsy demonstrated hemophagocytosis but was negative for fungal organisms on Grocott methenamine silver staining. Punch biopsy of scattered pink-to-violaceous acneiform papules on the forehead and scalp demonstrated numerous tissue-invasive microorganisms, and subsequent molecular testing identified Histoplasma capsulatum. He received dexamethasone, ruxolitinib, and liposomal amphotericin B; etoposide was withheld because of ongoing hemorrhage. Despite treatment, he succumbed to hemorrhagic shock and multiorgan failure and died. Autopsy demonstrated widespread histoplasmosis.

CONCLUSIONS: In patients with HLH, subtle skin lesions may provide accessible tissue for demonstrating invasive infection and obtaining organism-specific confirmation, even when fungal staining of another tissue is negative. Careful skin examination and targeted biopsy of new, atypical, or evolving lesions should be considered in immunocompromised adults with unexplained systemic inflammation, particularly those receiving tumor necrosis factor-alpha inhibitors.

articles.title: Eczema-Psoriasis Overlap: An eDelphi Consensus on Clinical Presentation and Therapeutic Management Among Italian Experts.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Atopic dermatitis and psoriasis (PsO) are common chronic inflammatory skin diseases traditionally considered distinct, driven by Th2 and Th1/Th17 pathways, respectively. However, evidence reveals that some patients may present with both eczematous and psoriatic lesions, either simultaneously or sequentially. This study's objective was to establish an Italian consensus on the clinical definition and management of eczema-psoriasis overlap.

METHODS: A steering committee of eight dermatologists identified three key areas: problem definition, clinical presentation and therapeutic management. Forty-three statements were drafted and distributed to 131 dermatologists for evaluation via an eDelphi process, using a 1-9 numeric rating scale. Consensus was defined as a mean score ≥ 7.

RESULTS: Of the 131 invited participants, 104 responded (79.4%). Consensus was reached for 42/43 statements. The only statement that failed to achieve consensus concerned the influence of respiratory atopic comorbidities on biologic choice in PsO; as a result of its dichotomous nature, it was not revised or re-voted on.

CONCLUSIONS: Eczema and PsO exist on a continuum of immune dysregulation, which may manifest sequentially or concomitantly, with phenotypic switches that can be spontaneous or drug induced. Assessment of risk factors for drug-induced forms should guide therapeutic choices. Mild cases can often be managed with topical therapies, while moderate-to-severe forms may require broader T cell-targeting treatments.

articles.title: Health State Valuation in Nigeria: An Insight into Discrete Choice Experiment-Based Preferences for Children and Adolescents from the Lenses of Adult Respondents.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Developing local value sets for child and adolescent health is critical for economic evaluation in Nigeria. Discrete choice experiments (DCEs) can elicit these preferences, yet data on choice behaviour from Nigerian populations are lacking.

OBJECTIVES: The aim of this study was to analyse DCE-based preferences for EQ-5D-Y-3L health states among Nigerian adult proxies, examining dimension-level drivers of choice, prevalence and correlates of preference reversals, and overall data quality.

METHODS: A DCE was administered to 2699 adults across six Nigerian states, generating 40,485 choice task observations. Paired health states were constructed using an efficient design. The EuroQol Portable Valuation Technology (EQ-PVT) recorded choices and identified logical reversals. Analyses included descriptive statistics, mixed-effects logistic regression, and comparative tests examining differences between reversed and normal tasks.

RESULTS: Reversals, which reflect respondent-level software orientation rather than task-level choice behaviour, occurred in 50.32% of tasks; severity, extreme-problem status, and demographics did not differ between EQ-PVT-reversed and normal tasks, confirming this measure as a data-entry artifact rather than evidence of decision strategy. A level-sum-score-based measure of substantive preference inconsistency, distinct from the EQ-PVT reversal, identified inconsistency in 10.7% of non-tied pairs. Pain/discomfort (β = - 1.544) and anxiety/depression (β = - 1.328) were the strongest predictors of choosing the better health state (p < 0.001).

CONCLUSIONS: This large-scale DCE provides foundational evidence for a Nigerian EQ-5D-Y-3L value set, confirming pain/discomfort and anxiety/depression as primary drivers of proxy preferences for child health. The EQ-PVT reversal rate reflects a balanced software-orientation assignment rather than flawed decision making; the true behavioural inconsistency rate (10.7% of non-tied pairs) was low and supports the feasibility of generating locally relevant preference data for health technology assessment in Nigeria.

articles.title: Representation of the LGBTQIA+ Patient Community in Cardiovascular Disease Clinical Guidelines.
articles.abstract: Cardiovascular disease (CVD) is the leading cause of death worldwide1, yet gaps remain for underrepresented populations in CVD research and clinical guidelines. The LGBTQIA+ community comprises 7% of the U.S. population2, and evidence suggests a higher predisposition to CVD from increased psychosocial stressors, obesity, smoking, and use of gender-affirming therapy5,6. Our study assesses existing CVD clinical guidelines' approach to the LGBTQIA+ community. In total, 313 cardiology clinical guidelines published by American, European, and international societies were reviewed. A systematic search for LGBTQIA+ related terms was conducted; guidelines containing these terms were analyzed. Only six guidelines (1.9%) contain LGBTQIA+-related terms. The 2023 ACC/AHA/ACCP/HRS Atrial Fibrillation Guideline mentions stroke risk reduction therapies should be offered equitably regardless of sex and gender diversity. The 2023 AHA/ACC/ACCP/ASPC/NLA/PCNA Chronic Coronary Disease (CCD) Guideline identifies sexual orientation as a social determinant of health (SDOH), which warrants future research on cardiovascular risk in hormone-treated transgender women with established CCD. The 2020 VA/DoD Obesity Guideline recommends research on individual differences, including transgender identity, in predicting bariatric procedure outcomes. The minimal acknowledgment of LGBTQIA+ patients in existing CVD guidelines highlights the need for tailored recommendations to improve outcomes in this community.

articles.title: Virtual Wards for Acute Care Patients: A Scoping Review.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Increasing capacity pressures and overcrowding in hospitals and emergency departments (EDs) have led to a global surge in the adoption of technology-enabled hospital-at-home programs, also known as virtual wards (VWs). These models provide hospital-level care in patients' homes supported by remote monitoring, aiming to shorten or avoid hospital admission. While substantial evidence supports the feasibility of VWs for chronic care, evidence for use in patients with acute conditions remains limited. This scoping review aimed to map existing evidence on VWs for acute medical patients within acute care settings.

METHODS: In February 2025, multiple databases were searched to identify studies evaluating VWs for adult acute care populations. Outcomes included clinical and safety variables, length of stay, functional outcomes, cost and resource use, barriers and facilitators to implementation, user experiences, and qualitative analyses.

RESULTS: Twenty-two studies were included (RCTs n = 3, case-controls n = 9, cohort n = 7, qualitative n = 3), with substantial heterogeneity in VW models and telemonitoring approaches. The most common indication was infection (e.g. pneumonia, urinary tract). Results of this narrative synthesis suggest care delivered in VWs may be similar to hospital care for rates of ED visits, readmission, short-term mortality, and adverse events. Length of stay in the hospital tended to be shorter. Functional outcomes may be better in VWs. Cost analyses were limited and showed mixed results. Surveys and qualitative analyses indicated high acceptability and generally positive experiences among patients, carers, and healthcare staff.

DISCUSSION: Evidence from the predominantly non-randomized studies included in this review suggests that VWs may be a feasible alternative for selected acute care patients, with outcomes broadly similar to standard hospital care. Substantial heterogeneity in study designs, alongside the descriptive nature of this synthesis, limits the evaluation of evidence strength and comparability. Robust randomized trials and comprehensive cost-effectiveness analyses are needed.

articles.title: Assessing the Impact of Routine Intervention for Perioperative Hyponatremia on Postoperative Outcomes.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Preoperative hyponatremia is associated with poorer outcomes, including increased mortality, ICU admissions, prolonged hospital stays, and readmissions. Whether routine intervention improves outcomes remains unclear.

OBJECTIVE: To assess an institutional protocol requiring internist referral and treatment for serum sodium < 130 mmol/L before surgery.

DESIGN: Retrospective registry-based study using a quasi-experimental regression discontinuity design. Sharp, kink, and triangular kernel models estimated effects at the intervention threshold. Subgroup analyses included patients with cardiac disease, chronic kidney disease, moderate operative risk, and emergency surgery.

PARTICIPANTS: Of 180,926 adult patients between 2013 and 2020, 24,846 had preoperative serum sodium 125-135 mmol/L. After excluding 43 with incomplete data, 24,803 remained.

INTERVENTIONS: Protocolized internist referral and treatment for preoperative serum sodium < 130 mmol/L.

MAIN MEASURES: The primary outcome was 30-day mortality. Secondary outcomes included 1-year mortality, ICU admissions, length of stay, and rapid postoperative sodium correction.

KEY RESULTS: Compared with serum sodium 130-135 mmol/L, sodium < 130 mmol/L was associated with higher unadjusted 30-day mortality (3.32% vs 1.33%), 1-year mortality (21.25% vs 11.03%), ICU admission (18.65% vs 11.50%), and mean length of stay (20.64 ± 25.51 vs 13.42 ± 21.01 days; all p < 0.001). No significant threshold effects were seen for 30-day mortality (treatment effect = 1.22, p = 0.138), ICU admissions (0.014, p = 0.564), or length of stay (0.184, p = 0.943). Significant discontinuity was observed for 1-year mortality (0.081, p = 0.010), particularly among patients with cardiac disease (0.162, p < 0.001), with chronic kidney disease (0.071, p = 0.012), with moderate operative risk (0.779, p = 0.013), or undergoing emergent surgery (0.100, p = 0.001). Lower preoperative sodium predicted rapid postoperative correction (OR = 1.190, p < 0.001).

CONCLUSIONS: Protocolized internist referral and treatment for preoperative serum sodium < 130 mmol/L did not affect short-term perioperative outcomes but may have reduced 1-year mortality, particularly in subgroups with cardiac and renal disease. Further studies are required to determine if this reflects treatment of underlying comorbidities rather than the effect of sodium normalization alone.

articles.title: Use of Machine Learning and Imaging to Predict Outcomes After Lumbar Spine Surgery: A Systematic Review.
articles.journal: Journal of imaging informatics in medicine
articles.abstract: Postoperative outcomes following lumbar spine surgery remain variable, and existing clinical risk stratification methods offer limited predictive accuracy. Advances in machine learning enable quantitative analysis of routinely acquired spinal imaging, creating opportunities to improve preoperative outcome prediction. However, the methodological quality and clinical readiness of imaging-based machine learning models in lumbar spine surgery have not been systematically evaluated. This systematic review followed PRISMA 2020 guidelines. PubMed, Embase, and Scopus were searched through October 2025 for studies using machine learning models trained on imaging data (MRI, CT, or radiographs) to predict postoperative outcomes after lumbar spine surgery. Two reviewers independently screened studies, extracted data, and assessed risk of bias using the Prediction model Risk Of Bias ASsessment Tool (PROBAST). Twenty-six studies published between 2019 and 2025 met inclusion criteria. Most models predicted patient-reported or clinical outcomes, with fewer addressing complications, structural outcomes, or imaging-derived biomarkers. MRI was the predominant modality. Model discrimination was frequently moderate to high (median AUC, 0.83), though external validation and calibration reporting were uncommon. All studies demonstrated high risk of bias, primarily related to analysis and validation practices. Imaging-based machine learning models show promise for improving preoperative outcome prediction after lumbar spine surgery, but methodological limitations limit current clinical applicability. Greater emphasis on external validation, standardized outcomes, and prospective evaluation is needed to support safe translation into routine spine care.

articles.title: Efficacy of Ibuprofen Versus Acetaminophen for Acute Fever Management in Febrile Children: A Systematic Review and Meta-analysis of Randomized Controlled Trials.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Ibuprofen and acetaminophen are the most widely used antipyretic agents in pediatric practice. Despite their common use, comparative evidence on their relative efficacy in febrile children remains heterogeneous, and clinical recommendations vary across guidelines and countries.

OBJECTIVE: We aimed to evaluate the comparative antipyretic efficacy of ibuprofen versus acetaminophen in febrile children through a systematic review and meta-analysis restricted to randomized controlled trials.

METHODS: A systematic search was conducted in Scopus, PubMed, and Web of Science using a predefined strategy combining terms for ibuprofen, paracetamol/acetaminophen, fever/febrile/pyrexia, and pediatric populations. The primary outcome was the proportion of children afebrile at 4 h. Continuous outcomes included temperature reduction at 4 h, time without fever during the first 4 h, and time-weighted summary temperature differences over 0-8 h. The study protocol was registered in PROSPERO (CRD420261353471).

RESULTS: A total of 479 records were identified; after duplicate removal and screening, seven studies were included in the quantitative synthesis. For the primary outcome of afebrile status at 4 h, the pooled risk ratio was 1.26 (95% confidence interval [CI] 0.88-1.80; p = 0.106). Temperature reduction at 4 h was significantly greater with ibuprofen (mean difference 0.31 °C, p = 0.024). The time-weighted summary temperature outcome over 0-8 h numerically favored ibuprofen but did not reach statistical significance (mean difference - 3.52, 95% CI - 21.24 to 14.21; p = 0.240; I2 = 57.6%). An exploratory standardized mean difference analysis across heterogeneous continuous outcomes (seven comparisons) yielded a near-null pooled effect (Hedges' g - 0.08, 95% CI - 0.40 to 0.25; p = 0.645; I2 = 84.0%).

CONCLUSIONS: The primary outcome-the proportion of children achieving afebrile status at 4 h-did not differ significantly between ibuprofen and acetaminophen (risk ratio 1.26, 95% CI 0.88-1.80; p = 0.106). Ibuprofen produced a statistically greater reduction in temperature at 4 h compared with acetaminophen (mean difference 0.31 °C), although this difference is unlikely to be clinically meaningful. These findings suggest a marginal quantitative advantage of ibuprofen to decrease body temperature, without a clinically significant difference between the two agents.

articles.title: RAPID perfusion CT in acute ischemic stroke: an educational pictorial review of common patterns, pearls, and pitfalls.
articles.abstract: Rapid processing of Perfusion and Diffusion (RAPID) software for CT perfusion (CTP) is a valuable tool for the evaluation of acute ischemic stroke and therapeutic decision-making in extended therapeutic windows. However, automated maps should not be interpreted in isolation. A structured, pattern-based approach, integrating qualitative visual assessment with automated quantitative output and clinical information to refine therapeutic selection, remains essential to mitigate pitfalls and optimize patient care. The aim of this article is to provide an educational pictorial review based on selected illustrative cases of the most common imaging patterns, interpretive pitfalls, and technical features of CTP processed with RAPID software in acute ischemic stroke, that may serve as a practical guide for radiologists and neuroradiologists. KEY POINTS: Question How can radiologists effectively interpret automated RAPID CT perfusion maps in acute ischemic stroke while avoiding common technical traps, diagnostic pitfalls, and anatomical limitations? Findings Integrating qualitative visual assessment, quantitative RAPID outputs, and clinical-vascular data within a structured workflow minimizes diagnostic errors and optimizes patient selection for reperfusion. Critical relevance statement This educational pictorial review provides a practical, pattern-based approach to RAPID CT perfusion interpretation, highlighting clinical applications, technical limitations, software variability, and diagnostic pitfalls to advance everyday neuroradiological practice and personalized stroke management.

articles.title: Successful management of long-term venovenous ECMO for severe PARDS in a child with acute lymphoblastic leukemia.
articles.journal: Journal of artificial organs : the official journal of the Japanese Society for Artificial Organs
articles.abstract: Pediatric acute respiratory distress syndrome (PARDS) is an important cause of morbidity and mortality in pediatric intensive care units. We report successful prolonged venovenous extracorporeal membrane oxygenation (VV-ECMO) support in a child with severe PARDS and acute lymphoblastic leukemia (ALL). A 5-year-old boy with low-risk B-cell ALL developed severe refractory PARDS during induction therapy. VV-ECMO was initiated for profound hypoxemia and continued for 34 days, after which he was successfully decannulated. He was discharged after 235 days of hospitalization. This case suggests that prolonged VV-ECMO may be a feasible rescue strategy in carefully selected children with ALL when respiratory failure is potentially reversible and the oncological prognosis is favorable.

articles.title: Hemi-see-saw nystagmus with superimposed pendular oculopalatal tremor: case report and systematic review.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Hemi-see-saw nystagmus (HSSN) is an uncommon subtype, characterized by elevation and intorsion of one eye with contralateral depression and extorsion, typically in a jerk pattern. It is associated with unilateral lesions of the interstitial nucleus of Cajal and the medial longitudinal fasciculus, both of which are involved in the ocular tilt reaction (OTR). Although its association with oculopalatal tremor (OPT) has been described, it is rare.

METHODS: We performed a systematic review of seven databases on HSSN, extracting data on demographics, etiology, lesion location, oculomotor findings, nystagmus pattern, outcomes, and in addition we presented a representative case.

RESULTS: A systematic review of seven databases identified 18 reports comprising 57 cases of HSSN or closely related dissociated vertical-torsional nystagmus, including the present index case. The mean age was 56.2 ± 16.3 years, and 63.2% of patients were male. Ischemic stroke was the most frequent etiology (75.4%), followed by hemorrhagic stroke (14.0%). Less frequent causes included Chiari I malformation, demyelinating/inflammatory disease, cavernous malformation, ataxia with oculomotor apraxia type 2, Joubert syndrome, and brainstem encephalitis (1.8% each). Jerk nystagmus predominated (82.5%), whereas pendular nystagmus was identified in 17.5%, exclusively in the setting of OPT or inferior olivary hypertrophy. Among jerk HSSN cases, the pontine tegmentum was the most frequent lesion site (63.8%), with INO present in all pontine cases and OTR in 90.0%. Complete resolution was reported predominantly in cases associated with INO, whereas lack of improvement was confined to OPT-related cases, with one exception of spontaneous resolution after 20 years. We describe a 30-year-old man with a pontomedullary arteriovenous malformation presenting with pendular HSSN, right one-and-a-half syndrome, gaze-evoked nystagmus, OTR, incomplete Horner syndrome, and OPT.

CONCLUSIONS: HSSN is an uncommon nystagmus, most often vascular in origin and frequently involving the pontine tegmentum. While it usually presents with a jerk waveform, association with OPT may produce a pendular phenotype, suggesting a distinct brainstem-cerebellar mechanism. Larger anatomically and oculographically characterized series are needed to clarify structure-function correlations and prognosis.

articles.title: Evaluating automated pollen monitoring for thunderstorm asthma and public health forecasting: a comparative study in Melbourne, Australia.
articles.abstract: High-quality pollen measurements are essential for effective environmental monitoring and reliable public health forecasting. Automated pollen counters offer continuous, high-resolution observations that have the potential to reduce reliance on labour-intensive manual microscopy, but their performance must be evaluated against established methods. This study evaluates the performance of the SwisensPoleno Mars by comparing its daily and sub-daily pollen measurements of total pollen, and the two dominant airborne pollen types in Melbourne, grass and cypress, with those from a co-located Burkard Hirst-type spore trap at the University of Melbourne over the 92-day spring monitoring period in 2022. Data from the automated system showed a strong linear relationship with the co-located manual trap, with coefficients of determination (R2) of 0.92 for total daily pollen counts, 0.92 for grass pollen, and 0.86 for cypress pollen. Grass pollen measurements, which are central to epidemic thunderstorm asthma (ETSA) risk forecasting in Victoria, showed particularly high correspondence, including consistent classification into low, moderate, and high operational thresholds. The SwisensPoleno Mars also reproduced expected diurnal variation in pollen concentrations, demonstrating its ability to capture short-term changes in airborne pollen levels. These results indicate that automated pollen counters can deliver reliable observations at both daily and sub-daily scales while substantially reducing labour demands. The strong performance of the automated system supports its use for routine pollen monitoring, its suitability for supplementing or replacing manual counting in Victoria and its value and suitability for applications that benefit from high temporal resolution, including ETSA risk forecasting.

articles.title: Efsubaglutide Alfa: A Comprehensive Pharmacological Review.
articles.abstract: Efsubaglutide alfa (also known as supaglutide) is a long-acting glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonist (GLP-1RA) engineered as a GLP-1 analogue fused to a human immunoglobulin G2 (IgG2) fragment crystallisable (Fc) domain. This narrative review summarises published and publicly available evidence on efsubaglutide alfa pharmacology, pharmacokinetics/pharmacodynamics, dose-exposure-response relationships, drug-drug interaction potential, and clinical efficacy and safety in type 2 diabetes (T2D) and overweight/obesity. Efsubaglutide alfa has prolonged exposure (terminal half-life approximately 182-215 h) and low steady-state fluctuation, but dosing-interval selection should not be inferred from half-life alone. Available population pharmacokinetic and exposure-response analyses indicate that steady-state trough concentration is most informative for glycaemic response, whereas average and peak concentrations contribute to interpretation of weight response and gastrointestinal tolerability. Across available studies, predominantly conducted in Chinese populations, efsubaglutide alfa shows class-consistent improvements in glycaemic control and body weight, with gastrointestinal adverse events as the main tolerability limitation. Exploratory every 2-week dosing and post-discontinuation glycaemic durability findings remain hypothesis-generating. No head-to-head comparative trials dedicated cardiovascular or renal outcome trials, or large globally diverse datasets are yet available; therefore, the current evidence should be interpreted as a clinical pharmacology synthesis rather than a comparative positioning claim.

articles.title: "So much other stuff going on": Factors influencing syphilis and STBBI testing among street-involved communities in Kingston, Ontario.
articles.journal: Canadian journal of public health = Revue canadienne de sante publique
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Syphilis is a re-emerging public health threat in Canada, disproportionately affecting street-involved communities. This qualitative study aimed to identify the multilevel factors influencing access to timely syphilis testing among people who are street-involved in Kingston, Ontario.

METHODS: Using an interpretive description approach, we conducted in-depth, semi-structured interviews with clients of local harm reduction and housing services and focus groups with community-based organization service providers to explore their perspectives surrounding factors influencing syphilis and sexually transmitted and blood-borne infection (STBBI) testing decisions. Interviews were audio-recorded, transcribed, coded using NVivo, and analysed using reflexive thematic analysis within the socio-ecological framework.

RESULTS: A total of 23 individuals were included: 16 clients and 7 providers. A majority of clients identified as being un(der)housed (n = 13) and/or people who use drugs (n = 10), with a median age of 26 years. At the structural and systems level, institutional broken trust, availability of testing services and information, and transportation emerged as salient factors influencing access to testing. Social- and community-level factors included the influence of trusted providers, close social networks, and privacy and confidentiality. Knowledge level, perceived risk, competing priorities, and testing preferences also influenced testing decision-making.

CONCLUSIONS: Our findings highlight the complexity of the multilevel factors that influence syphilis testing decisions among street-involved communities. Clients' and providers' concordance in their emphasis on socio-structural factors underscores the necessity of shifting the onus of syphilis testing uptake beyond the individual level, and implementing models of care that address barriers and structural interventions that address root causes.

articles.title: Imaging modalities for detecting jaw bone invasion in oral squamous cell carcinoma: a systematic review and diagnostic test accuracy meta-analysis.
articles.abstract: To evaluate the diagnostic accuracy of preoperative imaging modalities for detecting jaw-bone invasion in oral squamous cell carcinoma (OSCC), with particular emphasis on studies using histopathology as the reference standard. PubMed, Scopus, and Web of Science were searched. Diagnostic accuracy was assessed using bivariate random-effects models and hierarchical summary receiver operating characteristic curves. Imaging modalities were compared using meta-regression. Additional analyses were restricted to OSCC-only cohorts and studies with histopathological verification. Thirty-eight studies contributed 78 modality-specific diagnostic datasets. Computed tomography (CT; 30 datasets) yielded pooled sensitivity and specificity of 78.7% and 84.2%, respectively, compared with 84.3% and 81.6% for magnetic resonance imaging (MRI; 21 datasets). Single-photon emission computed tomography (SPECT; nine datasets) showed high sensitivity (96.7%) but lower specificity (57.5%). Corresponding estimates were 88.6% and 77.1% for cone-beam CT (five datasets), 80.2% and 81.5% for PET/CT (six datasets), and 65.7% and 90.0% for panoramic radiography (seven datasets). In analyses restricted to OSCC-only cohorts with histopathological verification, sensitivity and specificity were 78.9% and 81.7% for CT (17 datasets) and 87.2% and 75.4% for MRI (15 datasets). The formal CT comparison did not establish a significant difference between OSCC-only and mixed-site cohorts. CT and MRI showed consistent diagnostic performance for jaw-bone invasion. SPECT was highly sensitive but produced more false-positive findings. Evidence for CBCT and PET/CT remains limited. Imaging selection should consider the clinical question and the consequences of false-positive and false-negative results.

articles.title: Multimodal artificial intelligence in dental diagnosis: influence of reasoning depth and domain-specific medical model on diagnostic performance.
articles.abstract: Large language models are increasingly explored as clinical decision-support tools, but the relationship between configurable reasoning effort and multimodal diagnostic performance remains unclear. This study evaluated the association between API-configured reasoning effort and multimodal oral and dental diagnostic performance in GPT-5 and compared its outputs with those of the compact open-weight medical-domain model MedGemma-1.5-4b-it. Eight anonymized multimodal case reports representing dental trauma, odontogenic cysts, odontogenic tumors, implant-associated infection, oral mucosal disorders, hereditary mucosal disease, and restorative management were reformatted into structured evaluation scenarios. Final diagnostic labels, definitive treatment plans, author interpretations, answer-revealing captions, and postoperative outcomes were excluded to reduce answer leakage. Five configurations were evaluated: GPT-5 under four API-configured reasoning-effort settings (high, medium, low, and minimal) and MedGemma-1.5-4b-it as a compact medical-domain comparator. Outputs were assessed using a six-domain 0-5 rubric covering diagnostic accuracy, diagnostic completeness, reasoning quality, treatment planning, safety and risk awareness, and scope adherence. Diagnostic scores were checked against the exact archived outputs and source reference diagnoses before final analysis, and a domain-level Safety Override was applied to clinically dangerous recommendations. Repeated-measures differences were analyzed at the case level, with complementary exploratory analyses of primary-diagnosis agreement, reference-diagnosis inclusion, clinical-pathway appropriateness, and safety. Inter-rater reliability of the original independent blinded ratings was excellent (intraclass correlation coefficient = 0.92; 95% confidence interval, 0.87-0.95). Total scores differed across configurations (Friedman χ²(4) = 27.24, p = 0.000018; Kendall's W = 0.85). Mean scores were 28.0 ± 2.5 for GPT-5 high, 27.8 ± 1.6 for medium, 22.8 ± 4.0 for low, 18.9 ± 2.8 for minimal, and 17.1 ± 3.3 for MedGemma-1.5-4b-it. Primary-diagnosis agreement with the published reference diagnosis occurred in 6/8 cases for GPT-5 high, 6/8 for medium, 5/8 for low, 4/8 for minimal, and 1/8 for MedGemma; reference-diagnosis inclusion either as the primary diagnosis or within the differential occurred in 8/8, 8/8, 8/8, 7/8, and 3/8 cases, respectively. One safety-critical error occurred in GPT-5 low; none occurred in the other configurations. GPT-5 high and medium had the highest observed mean scores, but no pairwise Wilcoxon comparison remained significant after Holm correction. Primary-diagnosis agreement, reference-diagnosis inclusion, clinical-pathway appropriateness, and safety provided complementary views of open-ended clinical performance. MedGemma showed lower primary-diagnosis agreement and reference-diagnosis inclusion, while no MedGemma response met the final source-verified safety-critical criterion. The between-family comparison remains a pragmatic comparison of distinct deployment paradigms rather than a controlled test of training-domain specialization. In this dataset, higher GPT-5 reasoning-effort settings were associated with higher observed multimodal performance, particularly in diagnostically complex cases. Reasoning-effort configuration may therefore be an important design consideration for future dental decision-support systems, but the association is descriptive and requires confirmation in larger prospective studies.

articles.title: Clinical impact of admission estimated glomerular filtration rate categories in patients with acute myocardial infarction.
articles.abstract: Chronic kidney disease (CKD) is a well-established risk factor in acute myocardial infarction (AMI); however, the clinical relevance of admission estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR)-based categories remains unclear. We analyzed 10,870 patients from a prospective multicenter AMI registry in Japan. Patients were stratified into stages 1 (≥ 90), 2 (60-89), 3a (45-59), 3b (30-44), 4 (15-29), and 5 (< 15 mL/min/1.73 m2) based on the admission eGFR. The primary endpoint was 30-day major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE), defined as cardiovascular death, non-fatal myocardial infarction, or non-fatal stroke. Bleeding was defined as BARC type 3 or 5. More advanced admission eGFR stages were associated with a higher risk of adverse events. After multivariable adjustment, stages 4 and 5 were associated with a significantly higher risk of MACE compared with the reference group of stages 1 and 2 (stage 4: HR 2.12, 95% CI 1.03-4.33; stage 5: HR 4.14, 95% CI 1.54-11.09), whereas stages 3a and 3b were not significantly associated with MACE. In patients with AMI, clinical outcomes varied across admission eGFR categories, with more advanced renal dysfunction, particularly stages 4 and 5, associated with a higher risk of short-term MACE. Detailed categorization of admission eGFR may provide additional prognostic information for early risk assessment.

articles.title: Are Asymmetry-Focused Training Interventions More Effective than General Programs in Reducing Interlimb Asymmetries and Improving Athletic Performance? A Systematic Review.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Interlimb asymmetries (ILA) have been associated with an increased risk of injury and decreased athletic performance. However, despite the growing number of training interventions targeting ILA, their comparative effectiveness relative to general strength and conditioning approaches has not yet been systematically reviewed.

OBJECTIVE: This systematic review aimed to compare the effectiveness of asymmetry-focused training interventions versus general training programs in reducing ILA and improving physical performance in athletic populations. Specifically, it sought to compare individualized training programs that first identify the weaker limb during pre-testing and subsequently prescribe a greater training stimulus to that limb with general training protocols that apply the same training stimulus to both limbs, as well as unilateral approaches with bilateral training strategies.

METHODS: Following PRISMA 2020 guidelines, a systematic search was conducted in Web of Science, PubMed, and SPORTDiscus up to April 2025. Eligible studies involved healthy athletes (aged 12-30 years) who completed ≥4-week lower-limb training interventions that either applied a greater stimulus to the weaker limb (e.g., starting sets with the weaker side or adding volume) or used unilateral training approaches that applied the same training stimulus to both limbs regardless of baseline ILA values. To be included, studies were required to assess both pre-to-post changes in ILA and at least one physical performance outcome. The risk of bias was assessed using a modified Cochrane tool.

RESULTS: Eleven studies comprising 297 athletes met the inclusion criteria. Reductions in ILA were more consistent in asymmetry-focused and unilateral training groups compared to general and bilateral training groups, respectively. Most interventions also led to improvements in physical performance, with asymmetry-focused and unilateral protocols typically producing greater gains in single-limb tasks, although bilateral training showed more favourable effects in bilateral tasks. However, variability in training protocols and outcome measures across studies limits the generalizability of these findings.

CONCLUSION: Asymmetry-focused strategies, such as starting unilateral exercises with the weaker limb or increasing its training volume, appear to be more effective for reducing ILA than non-individualized unilateral training. These approaches are practical, safe, and potentially beneficial in athletic settings. However, further high-quality research is needed to confirm their superiority over non asymmetry-focused unilateral or bilateral training and to establish clear guidelines for their implementation. Registration PROSPERO-CRD420251023232.

articles.title: An introduction to the methodological corpus of systematic observation and its quality assessment.
articles.abstract: Observational methodology (OM) has evolved into a rigorous and flexible mixed-methods framework for studying spontaneous behavior in natural settings. By systematically recording behavioral streams and converting qualitative data into quantitative parameters, OM provides ecologically valid evidence often unattainable in experimental designs. This article presents a comprehensive methodological framework that synthesizes the conceptual, methodological, and analytical foundations of OM, along with recent advances in quality assessment. It traces OM's evolution from qualitative traditions to a mature scientific methodology grounded in technological innovations and robust analytical procedures. A central element is the taxonomy of observational designs, which guides decisions on instrument development, sampling, and data analysis. This paper examines the structure of observational instruments, highlighting the complementary roles of structured category systems and flexible field formats, as well as the growing use of hybrid instruments that combine theoretical rigor with practical flexibility. Key components of the QUAL-QUANT-QUAL sequence are described, including behavioral segmentation, qualitative data typologies, and their transformation into quantitative parameters such as frequency, order, and duration. Analytical techniques used in OM include classical statistics and three field-specific procedures: lag sequential analysis, polar coordinate analysis, and T-pattern detection, which together enable precise identification of recurrent behavioral patterns. The article also addresses quality assessment, reviewing key frameworks that promote transparency, standardization, and evidence synthesis across behavioral science domains. Overall, this work offers an updated reference for designing, implementing, evaluating, and synthesizing studies based on OM.

articles.title: Interspecies regulation of virulence through gingipain inhibition by a Tannerella forsythia serpin.
articles.abstract: Periodontitis is driven by dysbiotic microbial communities in which Porphyromonas gingivalis (Pg) acts as a keystone pathogen through its caspase-like fold (Clan CD) proteases, gingipains. Tannerella forsythia (Tf), another member of the periodontal pathogenic community, uniquely produces the broad-spectrum serpin termed miropin, yet its biological significance as an inhibitor in periodontal inflammation remains unclear. Here, we demonstrate that miropin directly inhibits the lysine-specific gingipain Kgp and the calpain-like protease Tpr produced by Pg, forming irreversible covalent inhibitory complexes. While recombinant native miropin impairs Pg growth, an engineered variant targeting both lysine- and arginine-specific gingipains entirely abolishes bacterial growth in a defined medium. In vivo, recombinant miropin reduces Pg virulence and, when co-infected with wild-type Tf, prevents lethal infection and significantly reduces alveolar bone loss, but not when co-infected with a miropin-deficient mutant. Protection is associated with inhibition of gingipain activity and normalization of the RANKL/OPG ratio in periodontal tissues. These findings identify miropin as a potent interspecies virulence modulator and challenge the prevailing view of Tf as an exclusively pathogenic member of the oral microbiome.

articles.title: Exercise management in pediatric type 1 diabetes: a multicenter study of healthcare professionals' perspectives.
articles.abstract:
UNLABELLED: Regular exercise is an important component of care for children with type 1 diabetes (T1D), supporting both physical and psychological health. However, many do not meet recommended activity levels, and exercise does not consistently improve glycemic control. Exercise management in T1D is complex and influenced by multiple factors, including child, activity, and treatment characteristics. These challenges highlight the importance of comprehensive exercise-directed guidance (EDG). This study aimed to characterize EDG practices in pediatric T1D and identify key challenges faced by healthcare professionals (HCPs). Physicians, nurses, and dietitians from 11 pediatric diabetes centers participated. Participants completed anonymized electronic questionnaires assessing current practices, content, and perceived challenges related to EDG. Response rate was 87.2%; 130 HCPs participated; all reported providing EDG to patients. Considerable variability was observed in the timing, content, and educational resources used. While the majority (85.9%) reported offering guidance to all patients, others indicated guiding only when specific needs arose. The most frequently addressed topics included the immediate effects on blood glucose, adjusting carbohydrate intake, and general preparations for exercise. Less frequently discussed topics were planning exercise regimens and encouraging involvement of family or peers. Challenges by order of prevalence were insufficient teaching aids (42.3%), EDG complexity (40.0%), visit duration (36.2%), and knowledge gaps (33.1%).

CONCLUSION: Although HCPs acknowledge the importance of exercise in pediatric T1D and incorporate EDG into clinical care, substantial variability exists in its delivery. Improving the availability and usability of educational tools and strengthening social support components may enhance exercise education for children with T1D.

WHAT IS KNOWN: • Exercise-directed guidance (EDG) is essential for children with type-1-diabetes, yet challenging to implement. • Knowledge of barriers to EDG is growing, but evidence remains limited across healthcare settings and professional groups.

WHAT IS NEW: • In this national multicenter study of healthcare professionals, all participants reported providing EDG, yet its timing,content, and availability of educational tools varied. • Limited teaching aids, the complexity of EDG, and time constraints were the main barriers; addressing family and peer involvement and exercise-specific planning were identified as areas for improvement.

articles.title: Comments on "Nationwide trends in cardiac anesthesia requiring cardiopulmonary bypass and intraoperative transesophageal echocardiography use in Japan: a claims-based analysis, 2019-2023".
Repurposing adult AI radiograph models for neonatal care through continual learning: an international multicentre study.
articles.abstract: Despite growing clinical adoption of artificial intelligence in radiology, fewer than one in five commercially available models are cleared for paediatric use. Existing systems are trained predominantly on adult data and generalize poorly to neonates, yet efficient strategies for repurposing them without data sharing or large-scale local data curation are lacking. Here we present an international retrospective study of neonatal chest radiographs from 30 neonatal intensive care units across 20 countries and territories, evaluating continual learning as a privacy-preserving approach to adapt a deep learning model for adult endotracheal tube assessment to neonatal care. Each hospital contributed 50 radiographs for sequential model retraining without centralized data pooling. Continual learning achieved lower anatomical landmark localization error (0.67 cm versus 1.29 cm for hospital-specific fine-tuning and 4.30 cm for adult-only models) at 29 of 30 sites, with improved detection of deep intubations at 27 of 30 sites. These findings demonstrate that privacy-preserving collaborative learning can address critical gaps in paediatric AI deployment.

articles.title: A multiview video-text model detects obstructive coronary stenosis and predicts 1-year cardiovascular events from angiography.
articles.abstract: Invasive coronary angiography is the reference standard for diagnosing coronary artery disease, yet assessment is subjective, and existing artificial-intelligence tools typically assess stenosis in individual frames or videos and do not integrate the full multiview angiographic study. Here we show that DeepCORO-CLIP, trained on 203,808 angiographic videos and reports from 28,117 patients, interprets whole multiple-video angiograms at once. It detects obstructive stenoses (≥70%), with an area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUROC) of 0.89 internally and externally, and identifies chronic total occlusion (AUROC = 0.90 to 0.95), intra-coronary thrombus and calcification (AUROC = 0.90 to 0.91). It also predicts 1-year cardiovascular events (AUROC = 0.79, 95% CI of 0.74 to 0.84, versus 0.65 for a model derived using clinical variables) and left ventricular ejection fraction (mean absolute error 7.3% versus 8.8% for a previous model), both achieved using coronary angiography alone. In a blinded review of 365 evaluations across 288 angiograms, its reports were clinically usable in 76% of evaluations versus 88% for cardiologists, with comparable false positives (17% versus 14%, P = 0.38); residual missed stenoses reflected an adjustable threshold rather than an absent signal.

articles.title: Integrated Perioperative Infection Management Measures (PSMS-11) for ePTFE Rhinoplasty in East Asian Patients: A Large-Sample, Long-Term Retrospective Study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Expanded polytetrafluoroethylene (ePTFE) has been widely utilized in east Asian rhinoplasty due to its favorable stability and biocompatibility. However, postoperative infection which is one of the major complications affecting surgical outcomes and patient satisfaction presents receive much concern. Evidence based on large cohorts with long-term follow-up in this population remains limited.

METHODS: A retrospective review of 1153 consecutive patients who underwent ePTFE rhinoplasty at our institution from January 2018 to December 2024 was performed. We compared Demographics, surgical techniques, and postoperative outcomes between infected and non-infected cases to identify risk factors for infection. Based on literature review and accumulated clinical experience, a perioperative systematic management strategy-11 Decision Nodes (PSMS-11) was applied consistently in routine practice. Infection characteristics, management approaches, and long-term outcomes were evaluated.

RESULTS: Postoperative infection occurred in a small proportion of patients, with an overall incidence of approximately 1.6% during long-term follow-up. Notably, more than half of infection events presented beyond six months after surgery, including late-onset cases occurring more than one year postoperatively. Revision surgery, active skin inflammation, smoking history, and unfavorable postoperative behaviors were associated with increased infection risk. Early localized infections could be considered for conservative management under close surveillance, whereas persistent or progressive infections required implant removal.

CONCLUSIONS: In this large-sample, long-term retrospective study of East Asian patients, a consistently low infection rate was observed following ePTFE rhinoplasty. These findings suggest that structured integration of perioperative management measures, as summarized by PSMS-11, may contribute to maintaining low infection rates in high-volume clinical practice. Long-term follow-up and individualized treatment decisions remain essential.

LEVEL OF EVIDENCE IV: This journal requires that authors assign a level of evidence to each article. For a full description of these Evidence-Based Medicine ratings, please refer to the Table of Contents or the online Instructions to Authors www.springer.com/00266 .

articles.title: Strategies to increase participant diversity in pediatric research: a systematic review.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Multiple strategies have been introduced to improve research recruitment and retention of underserved children and young people (CYP) with long-term conditions. For the first time, this systematic review presents a structured description of CYP and caregiver preferences for these strategies and collates evidence of their impact on participation.

METHODS: The Embase, MEDLINE, CINAHL, PsycINFO, Scopus, and Cochrane CENTRAL databases were searched. Studies were included from the inception of the database to September 2025 if they were undertaken in a high-income country, with CYP under 19 years with a long-term condition.

RESULTS: We assessed 16,727 records and included 21 studies published between 1998 and 2024, all based in the USA, predominantly drawn from African American and Latino populations. We determined preferences for the positive impact of the use of familiar venues and culturally attuned community events for study activities; communication that was bilingual, used educational games or social media; reliable and equitable relationships with study facilitators; and the co-production of recruitment strategies and study interventions.

CONCLUSIONS: There was a lack of comparative evidence across individual approaches. The time and resources needed to build awareness, trust, and facilitate research participation in underserved CYP need broader acknowledgement from funders and policymakers.

IMPACT: The review highlights how building trust, maintaining contact, and using familiar language and venues for study activities can improve research recruitment and retention in under-researched children and young people. The additional time and resources required to increase the diversity of children and young people participating in research need to be understood by funding bodies. The review's structured description of recruitment and retention strategies and their comparative effectiveness provides valuable and practical insight for those wishing to diversify research participation.

articles.title: Building a resilient system to improve blood pressure control in the UK: lessons from our Canadian cousins.
articles.abstract: The Stanley Peart Essay Competition is an annual event run by the British and Irish Hypertension Society toencourage Early Career Researchers to continue the ethos of Sir Stanley Peart. Sir Stanley Peart was a clinician andclinical researcher who made a major contribution to our understanding of blood pressure regulation. He was the fi rstto demonstrate the release of noradrenaline in response to sympathetic nerve stimulation. He was also the fi rst topurify, and determine the structure of, angiotensin and he later isolated the enzyme, renin, and carried out manyimportant investigations of the factors controlling its release in the body. This year, the essay topic was "Why doesCanada outperform all other countries in blood pressure control, and how would you implement a Canadian approachinto the UK system?". In his prize-winning essay, Steven Mitchell argues that Canada's rise and subsequent fall inblood pressure control was driven not by new drugs but by the infrastructure built to implement guidelines, and itslater dismantling. He proposes that the UK already has the necessary components to translate the lessons fromCanada into a resilient, UK-specifi c model for blood pressure control.

articles.title: Joint association of growth hormone and cerebral small vessel disease with antihypertensive treatment burden after stroke: an exploratory prospective study.
articles.abstract: Growth hormone (GH) and cerebral small vessel disease (SVD) may influence blood pressure regulation. This study investigated the individual and joint associations of GH and SVD severity with antihypertensive management following stroke. We prospectively enrolled patients admitted for acute stroke between October 2020 and December 2022. Patients with pre-existing or newly diagnosed hypertension during the initial hospitalization were included. We examined whether baseline GH levels and severe SVD burden (total SVD score ≥2) during the index hospitalization were associated with high antihypertensive medication burden defined as the use of ≥2 antihypertensive agents, as well as with high antihypertensive treatment intensity using an antihypertensive treatment intensity score (TIS) ≥ 1 at 12 months post-stroke. Among 171 registered patients, 129 were included (107 ischemic stroke/transient ischemic attack and 22 intracerebral hemorrhage; median age, 60 years; 95 male). High antihypertensive medication burden at 12 months was observed in 19 patients (15%). Elevated GH levels (≥0.49 ng/mL) and severe SVD burden were independently associated with high antihypertensive medication burden and TIS ≥ 1. Moreover, the coexistence of elevated GH and severe SVD burden was significantly associated with high antihypertensive medication burden and TIS ≥ 1 compared with the absence of both factors. Elevated GH levels and severe SVD burden were independently associated with antihypertensive medication burden and treatment intensity 12 months after stroke. The combined presence was associated with both outcomes, suggesting a potential joint contribution of neuroendocrine and structural vascular factors to post-stroke blood pressure management.

articles.title: Top ten surgical tricks: infrapubic inflatable penile prothesis implantation.
articles.abstract: The infrapubic penile prosthesis implantation approach represents a surgical variant to the traditional penoscrotal approach, characterized by a distinctive incision site used to maintain excellent surgical exposure for a penile prosthesis implantation. Its peculiar features include short operative time, minimally invasive nature, low-reported infection rate, and a direct line of sight for reservoir placement; its specific technical challenges include preservation of the dorsal neurovascular bundle, a restricted working space, and a non-negligible learning curve. In the present manuscript, we describe ten surgical tips covering patient selection and positioning, incision placement, fascial dissection, corporotomy and corporal dilation, reservoir dissection and placement, scrotal pump positioning, hemostasis and drain management, intra-operative device testing, tubing routing, and postoperative care. Each tip is supported, where available, by published evidence and is otherwise drawn from surgical experience.

articles.title: AEGIS: an operational infrastructure for post-market governance of adaptive medical AI under US and EU regulatory frameworks.
articles.abstract: Medical AI requires governance preserving safety during continuous improvement. FDA Predetermined Change Control Plans (PCCP) and EU post-market surveillance address iterative updates but lack operational tooling. We present AEGIS, an internal governance and post-market-monitoring infrastructure designed to support the documentation of predetermined governance pathways for PCCP and Medical Devices Regulation alignment. AEGIS comprises dataset assimilation and retraining, model monitoring, and conditional decision-making modules. It utilizes a four-category taxonomy (APPROVE, CONDITIONAL APPROVAL, CLINICAL REVIEW, REJECT) and an independent ALARM signal. Instantiating AEGIS for sepsis prediction (PhysioNet) and brain-tumor segmentation (BraTS) exercised all decision categories, successfully routing failures to the critical REJECT + ALARM state (no deployable model; released model at risk). On real cross-site data, drift detection ROC-AUC rose from 0.82 to 1.00, reliably triggering near 500-patient batches with zero false alarms. This proof-of-concept utilizes illustrative clinical models; drift scoring quantifies covariate shift only, leaving concept drift for future work.

articles.title: Resting skin sympathetic nerve activity spectral characteristics are associated with orthostatic sympathetic responses and exaggerated orthostatic pressor response in hypertension.
articles.journal: Hypertension research : official journal of the Japanese Society of Hypertension
articles.abstract: Substantial interindividual variability exists in orthostatic sympathetic and blood pressure (BP) responses among patients with hypertension. We investigated whether resting skin sympathetic nerve activity (SKNA) spectral characteristics are associated with this variability and with exaggerated orthostatic pressor responses (EPR). In 108 patients with hypertension, BP and SKNA were recorded in the supine and active standing positions. SKNA amplitude (average SKNA [aSKNA]) and frequency-domain parameters (low-frequency [LF] and high-frequency [HF] components, LF/HF ratio) were analyzed. Patients were stratified into low-LF/HF and high-LF/HF groups based on the median supine SKNA-derived LF/HF ratio. EPR was defined as a systolic BP increase of ≥ 20 mmHg at 3 min of active standing. Active standing significantly increased aSKNA (P < 0.001), whereas the overall SKNA-derived LF/HF ratio showed no significant change (P = 0.081). Upon standing, the low-LF/HF group exhibited a significant increase in LF/HF (P = 0.004), whereas the high-LF/HF group exhibited a decrease (P < 0.001), with an attenuation of the between-group difference during standing (P = 0.162). EPR occurred exclusively in the low-LF/HF group (13.0% vs. 0%, P = 0.013). In a receiver operating characteristic analysis, the supine LF/HF ratio discriminated EPR with an area under the curve of 0.863 (95% confidence interval, 0.775-0.950). Resting SKNA spectral characteristics may characterize interindividual variability in orthostatic sympathetic responses and be associated with EPR, offering a non-invasive approach for sympathetic phenotyping in hypertension In patients with hypertension, the supine SKNA-derived LF/HF ratio was inversely associated with its orthostatic change. LF/HF ratio increased during standing in the low-LF/HF group but decreased in the high-LF/HF group, with smaller group difference during standing. The supine LF/HF ratio showed potential for discriminating exaggerated orthostatic pressor responses.

articles.title: Association between caregiving duration and hypertension among family caregivers: the TMM CommCohort study.
articles.journal: Hypertension research : official journal of the Japanese Society of Hypertension
articles.abstract: With the global increase in elderly individuals requiring long-term care, family caregivers face significant physical and psychosocial burdens. This study examined the association between caregiving duration and hypertension using three indices: morning and evening home blood pressure (HBP) and research blood pressure (BP). This cross-sectional study included 13,518 participants from the Tohoku Medical Megabank Community-Based Cohort Study. Caregiving time was categorized via questionnaire. Hypertension was defined according to the Japanese Society of Hypertension Guidelines for the Management of Elevated Blood Pressure and Hypertension 2025 (HBP ≥ 135/85 mmHg, research BP ≥ 140/90 mmHg, or medication use). Multivariable robust Poisson regression estimated prevalence ratios (PRs), adjusted for demographics, lifestyle and social psychological factors. Participants providing care "almost all day" had significantly higher PRs for morning (PR: 1.26; 95% CI: 1.07-1.48) and evening hypertension (PR: 1.27; 95% CI: 1.03-1.56) than non-caregivers. Notably, no significant association was observed with research BP-defined hypertension. Stratified analyses revealed that these associations were particularly prominent among caregivers aged <65 years (P-interaction for morning hypertension = 0.003). The interaction between sex and caregiving time was not significant. Prolonged caregiving burden is associated with a higher prevalence of hypertension in the morning and evening, particularly among working-age caregivers. Because these risks were not captured by research BP, HBP monitoring is essential for cardiovascular risk management in caregivers. Social policies and clinical interventions should target younger caregivers to mitigate the physiological strain of 24-h caregiving responsibilities.

articles.title: Comparing two case definitions for including severe acute respiratory infection patients in influenza and COVID-19 vaccine effectiveness studies among older adults using the test-negative design: VEBIS hospital network, seven European countries, 2023/24.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Two severe acute respiratory infection (SARI) case definitions (CDs) are often used in test-negative design (TND) hospital-based vaccine effectiveness (VE) studies. SARI-CD1 requires ≥1 symptom (cough, fever, shortness of breath, anosmia, ageusia, or dysgeusia); SARI-CD2 requires both fever and cough. Using VEBIS hospital network end-of-season 2023/24 data, we compared the effect of these CDs on influenza and COVID-19 VE estimates in Europe.

METHODS: Using the TND, we restricted analysis to seven countries recruiting patients using SARI-CD1; we created a subset of SARI patients also meeting SARI-CD2. Cases were RT-PCR-positive for influenza A(H1N1)pdm09, A(H3N2), or SARS-CoV-2; controls were influenza or SARS-CoV-2 RT-PCR-negative. We estimated VE among patients ≥65 years using logistic regression adjusted for country, onset date, age, sex, and chronic conditions. We estimated VE overall, by age group (65-79, ≥80 years) and time since vaccination (14-59, 60-119, ≥120 days). Absolute VE differences ≥10% were considered relevant.

RESULTS: Patient characteristics and outcomes were similar across CDs. SARI-CD1 had slightly more vaccinated cases, with little difference in controls between the two CDs. For influenza, the absolute VE difference between SARI-CD1 and SARI-CD2 was 10% for influenza A(H1N1)pdm09 (34% vs 44%), 19% among those aged ≥80 years (21% vs 40%) and 18% at 60-119 days post-vaccination (4% vs 22%). For SARS-CoV-2, absolute VE differences were 11% overall (29% vs 40%), 11% among ≥80 years (33% vs 44%), and 12% at 60-119 days (34% vs 46%). All other absolute VE differences were < 10%.

CONCLUSIONS: VE was similar for influenza A(H3N2), adults 65-79 years and 14-60 days post-vaccination. We observed signals of higher VE with SARI-CD2 for influenza A(H1N1)pdm09 and SARS-CoV-2, particularly among adults ≥80 years and ≥ 60 days post-vaccination, although 95% CIs overlapped. These signals suggest CDs may contribute to VE variability and VE studies should clearly indicate CDs used.

articles.title: Altered frontal and dorsal hemodynamic engagement during mandarin aspiration processing in post-stroke aphasia: an fNIRS study.
articles.abstract: Auditory and speech-perception difficulties are common in post-stroke aphasia (PSA), but cortical responses during passive listening to Mandarin speech remain underexplored. Seventeen Mandarin-speaking individuals with PSA and 18 matched healthy controls listened to auditory oddball blocks containing /ba/ standards and /pa/ deviants during functional near-infrared spectroscopy (fNIRS). Although these syllables instantiate an aspiration contrast strongly cued by voice onset time (VOT), standard and deviant trials were combined within a single block-level condition. The resulting measures therefore indexed activation during speech-containing blocks relative to silent inter-block intervals rather than phonemic discrimination, categorization, or VOT-specific processing. Seven theory-driven channels covering bilateral auditory, sensorimotor, inferior frontal, and dorsolateral prefrontal regions were analyzed using three HbO indices: β coefficient, peak amplitude, and temporal centroid. The PSA group showed an overall reduction in task-related HbO activation, reflected by a significant Group effect for the β coefficient. Peak amplitude also showed significant Group and Group × Channel effects, although no individual channel remained significant after correction for multiple comparisons. Temporal centroid showed no significant group or interaction effects. These findings provide preliminary evidence for reduced block-evoked cortical recruitment during passive auditory exposure to Mandarin speech sounds in PSA. Because the analysis did not include a direct standard-deviant or active auditory control comparison, the findings do not establish a selective impairment of phonemic discrimination, categorization, or VOT processing. Because patients were assessed 6-7 months after stroke onset, the activation differences may reflect both persistent impairment and recovery-related reorganization during the early chronic stage.

articles.title: Women's perceptions of maternity care quality in China: Findings from the Chinese version of the Quality Maternal and Newborn Care Framework index.
articles.journal: Women and birth : journal of the Australian College of Midwives
articles.abstract:
PROBLEM: Improving maternity care quality is key to reducing adverse outcomes and ensuring maternal and newborn safety in China.

BACKGROUND: Evaluating service quality is an important step in promoting quality improvement. The Chinese version of the Quality Maternal and Newborn Care Framework index (C-QMNCFi) is a comprehensive and reliable tool to assess maternity care quality based on women's perceptions.

AIM: To conduct a large-scale assessment of maternity care quality in China using the C-QMNCFi and to examine factors associated with women's perceived care quality.

METHODS: An online survey using the C-QMNCFi was conducted between March and November 2025 among women between 42 days to 12 months postpartum recruited from nine hospitals across eastern, central, and western China. Descriptive statistics summarized scores, and quantile regression was used to identify factors associated with the global index score.

FINDINGS: A total of 1453 women participated. The mean C-QMNCFi global index score was 91.4% (IQR 84.3%-95.2%). Lower scores were observed in the Care providers (continuity of carer) and Information-giving and advice. Quantile regression showed that higher scores were associated with residence in central or eastern China, higher household income, receiving midwife-led care, and receiving pregnancy care or giving birth in public tertiary or private hospitals (all p < 0.05). Lower scores were associated with urban residence, longer travel time to hospitals, and maternal complications (p < 0.05).

CONCLUSION: Women generally reported positive maternity care experiences. It is recommended to optimize maternity care provision according to the characteristics of women.

articles.title: The role of cytokines as immunological biomarkers of disease severity during respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) infection in children.
articles.abstract: Respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) remains a leading viral cause of lower respiratory tract infections in infants and young children. The RSV infection of the respiratory epithelium elicits a complex immune response characterized by the production of a broad spectrum of pro- and anti-inflammatory cytokines. Emerging evidence indicates that the magnitude and temporal dynamics of these cytokine responses are closely associated with disease severity and clinical outcomes. Recent advances in immunopathological profiling have highlighted the potential of cytokine signatures as biomarkers of severe RSV disease, offering opportunities for early risk stratification and targeted clinical intervention. Although therapeutic options remain largely supportive, substantial progress in preventive strategies, including the introduction of monoclonal antibodies and newly licensed vaccines, represents an important step toward reducing the global burden of RSV disease. Despite these advances, reliable immunological biomarkers for clinical decision-making remain an unmet need. In this review, we synthesize current evidence on cytokine responses associated with severe RSV infection in children, with particular emphasis on their clinical utility as biomarkers of disease severity.

articles.title: The science-to-practice gap in allergology: a critical appraisal of determinants and knowledge-translation strategies across health systems.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Evidence-based medicine assumes that high-quality research, once produced, will reach the bedside. In allergology this assumption is repeatedly violated. Solid evidence accumulates while its uptake in daily practice remains incomplete and variable across health systems.

AREAS COVERED: This critical appraisal characterizes the science-to-practice gap in allergology using current data, drawn from a search of PubMed, MEDLINE, Embase, and the Cochrane Library covering January 2015 to March 2026. It examines the gap's determinants across institutional and economic contexts and evaluates knowledge-translation (KT) strategies with the strongest evidence base. ARIA, GINA, and EAACI adherence is quantified for allergic rhinitis, asthma, and AIT, with AIT uptake estimates treated as setting-specific rather than universal. Four determinant domains, education, conflicts of interest, reimbursement, and local adaptation, are compared across high-income EU countries, the UK, and low- and middle-income countries, and five KT strategies are appraised.

EXPERT OPINION: The gap is measurable, clinically consequential, and modifiable. Its persistence reflects structural and policy factors more than clinician knowledge. Combinations of audit-and-feedback and academic detailing, tailored to local environments and supported by clinical decision tools, offer the most durable improvement documented to date. Allergological societies should integrate implementation science and independent conflict-of-interest management into their strategic priorities.

articles.title: Ginsenoside Ra1 alleviates endothelial barrier dysfunction and multi-organ injury in experimental sepsis via NMMHC IIA inhibition.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND AND PURPOSE: Non-muscle myosin heavy chain IIA (NMMHC IIA) has emerged as a significant therapeutic target in vascular diseases and sepsis. However, effective interventions targeting NMMHC IIA in sepsis-induced endothelial dysfunction remain unelucidated. Here, we have assessed ginsenoside Ra1 (Ra1) as a potent NMMHC IIA inhibitor and evaluate its efficacy and underlying mechanisms in sepsis.

EXPERIMENTAL APPROACH: We used the caecal ligation and puncture model of polymicrobial sepsis in mice. Survival rate, body temperature, pathological changes, vascular permeability and plasma biochemical indicators were measured to evaluate the effects of Ra1 treatment. Molecular docking technique, cellular thermal shift assay, microscale thermophoresis assay and surface plasmon resonance were performed to confirm the binding of Ra1 with NMMHC IIA. Downstream genes affected by Ra1 were screened via RNA-sequencing and validated using western blotting and immunofluorescence. In vitro, a lipopolysaccharide-induced endothelial barrier injury model in human umbilical vein endothelial cells was established, and endothelial permeability was evaluated.

KEY RESULTS: Ra1 bound strongly to NMMHC IIA, whose knockdown ameliorated sepsis-induced endothelial barrier disruption and multi-organ injury (lung, intestine, liver and kidney). Ra1 attenuated mortality, hypothermia, multi-organ injury, vascular hyperpermeability and endothelial junction disruption in septic mice. Mechanistically, Ra1 inhibited TLR4/NF-κB/NLRP3 signalling to exert its protective effects, which were absent after NMMHC IIA was silenced, demonstrating an NMMHC IIA-dependent mechanism.

CONCLUSION AND IMPLICATIONS: Our findings identify Ra1 as a potential inhibitor of NMMHC IIA and provide mechanistic insight into therapeutic strategies targeting endothelial dysfunction in sepsis, which warrants further investigation in clinical studies.

articles.title: Yield and disparities in newly diagnosed HIV identified through a universal emergency department-based screening program in South Florida.
articles.abstract: HIV disproportionately affects populations by age, sex/gender, race/ethnicity, and transmission mode. This study evaluated the yield of new HIV diagnoses through a universal emergency department (ED) -based screening program in South Broward County, Florida, and examined disparities across demographic and behavioral subgroups. A retrospective cohort study was conducted using electronic health records from six EDs within a single public, non-profit healthcare system. Between July 2018 and February 2024, all patients aged ≥18 years were offered free opt-out HIV combination assay testing. Patients with known HIV infection or who declined testing were excluded. Annual case detection rates were calculated, and year-adjusted Poisson regression with annual testing volume as an offset estimated incidence rate ratios (IRRs) and 95% confidence intervals (CIs). Among 111,758 tests, 671 were positive, yielding a positivity rate of 0.60% and an annual case detection rate of 600 per 100,000 patients screened. Case detection was significantly higher among males than females (IRR 1.83, 95% CI 1.56-2.15) and among Black patients than White (IRR 4.28, 95% CI 3.45-5.31) or Hispanic patients (IRR 3.56, 95% CI 2.91-4.34). These findings support continued universal opt-out ED-based HIV screening in high-burden communities while emphasizing persistent demographic disparities in newly diagnosed HIV.

articles.title: [When pulmonary sequestration is hidden behind arteriovenous pulmonary malformation].
articles.abstract: A 33-year-old patient was stabbed, causing a perforating thoracic wound complicated by cardiorespiratory arrest due to hemorrhagic shock. Emergency surgery was performed with hemostatic and resuscitative bithoracotomy, revealing an incidental lesion suspected of being a pulmonary arteriovenous malformation (PAVM). This lesion being organized, and following embolization of the abnormal arteries arising from the descending thoracic aorta which were causing a systemic-pulmonary shunt, left lower lobectomy was performed. After anatomopathological study, a diagnosis of intralobar pulmonary sequestration was established. Pulmonary sequestration is not included in the international classification of vascular abnormalities. It is defined as a condition in which parts of pulmonary tissue are irrigated by an abnormal systemic artery. There exist two forms of pulmonary sequestration: intralobar and extralobar. Contrarily to most arteriovenous malformations, surgical excision is generally recommended, even though transcatheter embolization could be considered as an option in specific situations. Differential diagnosis of PAVM is difficult and raises questions on risks of progression, which differ between the two pathologies. While transcatheter embolization is a key component of PAVM treatment, radical surgery is usually required for pulmonary sequestration.

articles.title: Role of Fluorodeoxyglucose PET/Computed Tomography in Post-radiation Treatment Inflammatory Changes.
articles.abstract: Radiation therapy induces inflammatory changes in normal tissues that can persist for months and confound fluorodeoxyglucose positron emission tomography/computed tomography interpretation, particularly when assessing for tumor recurrence. This review examines the pathophysiology, time course, and imaging characteristics of post-radiation inflammatory changes across major organ systems including pulmonary, head and neck, gastrointestinal, genitourinary, musculoskeletal, and cardiovascular sites.
