Key topics include the conformational pattern of inflammatory uptake matching the radiation field, limitations of standardized uptake value-based quantitative criteria, optimal timing considerations, common pitfalls in interpretation, and emerging strategies, including novel radiotracers and multimodality imaging for differentiating post-treatment inflammation from residual or recurrent malignancy.

articles.title: 18F-Fluorodeoxyglucose PET/CT in Sepsis.
articles.abstract: 18F-Fluorodeoxyglucose positron emission tompgraphy/computed tomography (18F-FDG PET/CT) has emerged as a valuable whole-body metabolic imaging modality in sepsis and related systemic infectious disorders. Exploiting increased glucose metabolism in activated inflammatory cells, it facilitates localization of occult infective foci, detection of septic embolization, and guidance of source control when conventional investigations are inconclusive. Evidence demonstrates high diagnostic yield and meaningful impact on clinical management, particularly in sepsis of unknown origin and high-risk bacteraemia. However, diagnostic accuracy depends on appropriate patient preparation and timing. This review summarizes current evidence, practical challenges, emerging applications, and future research priorities for integrating 18F-FDG PET/CT into sepsis care.

articles.title: The Relationship among Obesity, Intracranial Hypertension, and Cerebrospinal Fluid Leak.
articles.abstract: Idiopathic intracranial hypertension (IIH) is a disorder characterized by elevated intracranial pressure without identifiable lesion or secondary cause. Patients can often present with otolaryngologic manifestations of IIH, such as pulsatile tinnitus, aural fullness, and cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) leak. Obesity plays an important role as a risk factor for both IIH and CSF leak as similar pathophysiological processes underly both presentations. Understanding the nuanced presentation of this condition is important for the otolaryngologist who routinely evaluates patients with these symptoms and has implications for management decisions. In this article, we discuss the relationship among obesity, IIH, and CSF leak.

articles.title: Interpreting the neutrophil-to-lymphocyte ratio in stable chronic obstructive pulmonary disease: severity, case mix, and clinical utility. Author's reply.
Comparison of the efficacy of three-dimensional printing-assisted strategy and traditional total ankle arthroplasty in the treatment of end-stage ankle arthritis.
articles.journal: Journal of orthopaedic science : official journal of the Japanese Orthopaedic Association
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To compare perioperative parameters, early functional outcomes, and complication profiles between 3D printing-assisted total ankle arthroplasty strategy incorporating preoperative virtual planning, patient-specific osteotomy guides, and a customized talar component and conventional total ankle arthroplasty (TAA) in the treatment of end-stage ankle arthritis.

METHODS: A retrospective analysis was conducted on data from 44 patients diagnosed with end-stage ankle arthritis who were admitted to our hospital between January 2021 and December 2023. Among them, 20 patients (observation group) underwent total ankle arthroplasty (TAA) using a 3D-printed patient-specific TAA strategy, while 24 patients (control group) received conventional TAA using the same tibial component and polyethylene liner but a standard off-the-shelf talar component, together with standard instrumentation. The following parameters were recorded and evaluated: operative duration, intraoperative blood loss, length of postoperative hospital stay, intraoperative fluoroscopy time, preoperative and postoperative American Orthopaedic Foot and Ankle Society (AOFAS) scores, visual analogue scale (VAS) scores, and ankle range of motion (ROM). Additionally, the occurrence of soft tissue-related complications was monitored.

RESULTS: The AOFAS score, VAS score, and ankle range of motion (ROM) in both groups showed significant improvement postoperatively compared to preoperative values (P < 0.05). However, no statistically significant differences were observed between the two groups (P > 0.05). With regard to surgical outcomes, including operative time, intraoperative blood loss, postoperative hospitalization duration, and the intraoperative fluoroscopy time, the observation group demonstrated significantly better results than the control group (P < 0.001). Concerning postoperative complications, the observation group experienced only one case of superficial infection, whereas the control group had two cases of superficial infection and one case of wound edge necrosis. Although the total complication rate was slightly lower in the observation group, the difference between the two groups was not statistically significant (P = 0.389). Postoperative radiographic analysis confirmed significantly improved alignment accuracy of the tibial component in the observation group compared to the control group (P < 0.05).

CONCLUSION: The 3D printing-assisted TAA strategy appears to improve perioperative efficiency and short-term radiographic alignment accuracy compared with conventional TAA, whereas short-term functional outcomes and wound-related complication rates remain comparable between groups. Given the additional preoperative preparation time and cost, its theoretical promise for patients with complex deformities and its potential effect on long-term implant survival require further confirmation through prospective, randomized studies with long-term follow-up.

articles.title: Multidisciplinary perspectives on managing functional/dissociative seizures in the emergency department: A survey of medical, nursing, and allied health clinicians.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Patients with functional/dissociative seizures (FDS) commonly present to emergency departments (ED), but the practices of the multidisciplinary emergency care workforce have not been described.

METHODS: A cross-sectional survey was administered to medical, nursing, and allied health clinicians at two EDs of an Australian metropolitan tertiary health service, between August-December 2025. Closed items were analysed descriptively; open-ended responses were analysed using conventional qualitative content analysis.

RESULTS: Of 930 clinicians invited, 101 participated (55 medical, 36 nursing, 10 allied health); 93 (92%) had witnessed a FDS in their ED work, yet 88 (87%) reported little to no training and 73 (72%) had little to no understanding of FDS. Management approaches employed included reassurance (49%), a safe low-stimulus environment (28%) and watchful waiting (29%), with deliberately conservative pharmacology amongst more experienced medical staff. Challenges included treatment disagreement (30%), patient or family expectations (30%) and stigma (21%). Three priorities emerged: a departmental pathway (32%), patient-specific management plans (18%), and multidisciplinary training (18%).

CONCLUSIONS: Multidisciplinary emergency care clinicians manage FDS based on clinical experience rather than formal training. The three priorities identified by ED clinicians for practice development require prospective evaluation.

articles.title: One-year outcomes of hepatic artery stenosis after pediatric liver transplantation: Results from the international, multicenter HEPATIC registry.
articles.journal: Digestive and liver disease : official journal of the Italian Society of Gastroenterology and the Italian Association for the Study of the Liver
articles.abstract:
AIM: This study aimed to describe one-year graft and patient survival after hepatic artery stenosis (HAS) following pediatric liver transplantation (pLT), and to explore outcomes by timing of HAS diagnosis and treatment strategy within the HAS cohort.

METHODS: Patients who developed HAS after pLT were included as per definition from the HEPATIC registry. The registry contains data from 32 centers across 21 countries over a 20-year period, during which 10,564 primary pLTs were performed. Donor-, recipient-, and transplant-related characteristics were analyzed. The primary outcome was one-year graft and patient survival.

RESULTS: HAS was diagnosed in 1.2% of patients (n = 130; 51% female; median age 4.4 years [IQR 1.4-11.6]), of whom 5% (n = 7) progressed to thrombosis (HAT). One-year graft and patient survival were 93% and 96%, respectively. Management consisted mainly of antithrombotic therapy alone (41.5%) or endovascular therapy (EVT; 41.5%), with no significant difference in one-year graft or patient survival between these approaches. Early HAS (≤21 days post-pLT) was associated with significantly higher one-year graft loss than late HAS (16%vs. 1%; p < 0.001). All deaths occurred in the early HAS group.

CONCLUSIONS: One-year graft and patient survival after HAS were high. Antithrombotic therapy alone and EVT were the most common management strategies. Early HAS was associated with lower one-year survival. Prospective studies with standardized diagnostic and treatment criteria are needed for validation.

articles.title: Effectiveness and safety of three years of bulevirtide monotherapy in patients with HDV-related compensated cirrhosis: the Italian compassionate use program.
articles.journal: Digestive and liver disease : official journal of the Italian Society of Gastroenterology and the Italian Association for the Study of the Liver
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Bulevirtide (BLV) monotherapy for up to 144 weeks was safe and effective in patients with chronic hepatitis D (CHD) in a phase III trial, but long-term real-world data are limited. We evaluated its effectiveness and safety in patients with HDV-related cirrhosis in clinical practice.

METHODS: Consecutive patients with HDV-related cirrhosis treated with BLV 2 mg/day monotherapy through the Italian compassionate use program were included. Virological (VR), biochemical (BR), and combined responses (CR), undetectable HDV RNA, virological and biochemical breakthroughs (VBK and BBK), non-invasive tests (NITs), safety, and liver-related events were assessed.

RESULTS: Ninety-seven patients were enrolled: median age, 52 years (interquartile range, 40-61); 53% were male; 96% were European; and 92% had Child-Pugh class A cirrhosis. VR, BR, CR, and HDV RNA target-not-detected/below-the-limit-of-detection rates increased over time, with 144-week cumulative incidences of 77%, 84%, 64%, and 53%, respectively. Overall, 11% and 5% of patients experienced a VBK and BBK, respectively. LSM, APRI, FIB-4, and LSPS, but not SSM, declined significantly during therapy. The 3-year cumulative probabilities of decompensation and HCC were 1.3% (95% CI, 1-3%) and 10% (95% CI, 4-19%), respectively. Treatment was well tolerated.

CONCLUSION: Long-term BLV 2 mg/day monotherapy was safe and effective in patients with cirrhosis. Response rates increased over time, while decompensating events remained uncommon.

articles.title: Corrigendum to "Mechanisms and precision intervention strategies of time-dependent dynamic regulation of matrix metalloproteinase-mediated cerebrovascular barrier disruption and neurovascular unit remodeling in stroke" [Exp. Neurol. 407 (2026) 116039].
Characterization of nucleus accumbens dopamine dynamics during positive and negative operant reinforcement in rats.
articles.abstract: We previously reported, using in-vivo fiber photometry, that operant responding reinforced by access to a peer (social self-administration) is associated with phasic dopamine increases in nucleus accumbens (NAc) core following lever insertion (reward-availability cue) and gradual increases preceding lever-pressing. Here, we sought to replicate these findings and determine whether dopamine signals (1) generalize to responding for high-carbohydrate palatable food, (2) show opposite patterns during negative reinforcement (shock avoidance/escape), and (3) depend on whether reinforcers are experienced alone or together. We trained male and female rats to lever-press for access to a same-sex peer (15 s/trial) and palatable food (45-mg pellet/trial), followed by shock avoidance/escape (0.18-0.28 mA). After training, we expressed the dopamine sensor GRAB-DA2m and implanted optic fibers into NAc core. We measured dopamine activity during sessions with either one- or three-reinforcers. During social self-administration, dopamine activity showed phasic increases following lever insertion and gradual increases preceding lever-pressing; responses were moderately greater during sessions with all three reinforcers. Palatable food self-administration showed a similar pattern, but responses were approximately twofold greater during single-reinforcer sessions. During shock avoidance/escape, dopamine activity showed phasic decreases at warning onset, lever insertion, and shock onset; responses were also greater during single-reinforcer sessions. Results suggest that NAc core dopamine signaling distinguishes positive from negative reinforcement and is modulated by reinforcer availability. Compared with single-reinforcer sessions, dopamine responses during food self-administration and shock avoidance/escape were reduced during sessions with all three reinforcers, whereas responses during social self-administration modestly increased.Significance statement Nucleus accumbens (NAc) dopamine is critical for processing the valence of positive reinforcers, whereas its role in negative reinforcement is less well understood. Here, we extended our prior work on operant social self-administration to determine whether these findings generalize to food reinforcement, show the opposite pattern during operant negative reinforcement (shock avoidance/escape), and depend on whether reinforcers are experienced alone or together. Results suggest that NAc core dopamine activity differentiates positive and negative reinforcement and is modulated by the presence of other available reinforcers. Specifically, dopamine responses during food self-administration and shock avoidance/escape were reduced when all three reinforcers were available together compared with when each reinforcer was experienced alone, whereas responses during social self-administration showed the opposite pattern.

articles.title: Leadership in the intensive care unit: an international perspective.
Association of caregiver burden with the healthcare use and outcomes of older patients attending the ED.
Cardiogenic shock networks: breaking the link between geography and survival?
Implementation and outcomes of a regional cardiogenic shock network in the UK.
Association Between Cataract Diagnosis and Depressive Symptoms in Peruvian Adults Aged 50 Years and Older: Analysis of a Nationally Representative Survey.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: Cataract has been linked to depressive symptoms, yet the contribution of functional distance-vision impairment remains understudied in Latin America. We examined the association between cataract diagnosis(with and without distance-vision difficulty) and depressive symptoms among Peruvian adults aged ≥ 50 years who had undergone a prior ophthalmological evaluation.

METHODS: This cross-sectional study analyzed data from the 2018-2019 Survey of Peru. The analytic sample comprised adults aged ≥ 50 years who reported a lifetime ophthalmological evaluation and completed the PHQ-9 (n = 20,320). Depressive symptoms were defined as a PHQ-9 score ≥ 10. Analyses used complex-survey weights with the subpopulation option. Weighted chi-square and t tests, and Poisson regression estimating prevalence ratios (PR) with 95% confidence intervals (CI), were performed.

RESULTS: Depressive symptoms were present in 8.7% (95% CI, 7.6-9.8) of adults aged ≥ 50 years, and 14.5% (95% CI, 13.1-16.0) had a cataract diagnosis. Participants with cataract and distance-vision difficulty had a higher prevalence of depressive symptoms than those without cataract (adjusted PR, 1.68; 95% CI, 1.08-2.61); no association was found for cataract without distance-vision difficulty (adjusted PR, 1.03; 95% CI, 0.65-1.62). Higher wealth was protective: rich (adjusted PR, 0.65; 95% CI, 0.42-1.00) and very rich (adjusted PR, 0.51; 95% CI, 0.32-0.95) quintiles showed lower prevalence of depressive symptoms. Older age, female sex, diabetes, and lower education were independently associated with depressive symptoms.

CONCLUSIONS: Among Peruvian adults aged ≥ 50 years with prior ophthalmological evaluation, cataract accompanied by distance-vision difficulty, but not cataract alone, is independently associated with depressive symptoms.

articles.title: Functional outcome after ischaemic stroke and intracerebral haemorrhage from two national cohorts.
articles.journal: Journal of neurology, neurosurgery, and psychiatry

articles.title: Performance of large language models in complex coronary artery disease decision-making and potential improvement strategy in a real-world cohort.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Previous studies have demonstrated that large language models (LLMs) can achieve performance comparable to multidisciplinary heart teams (HTs) in coronary revascularisation decision-making but limited by population bias. We aimed to assess LLMs’ performance in complex coronary artery disease (CAD) decision-making using a real-world cohort and to explore the potential improvement strategy.

METHODS: Patients with stable CAD and angiographically confirmed three-vessel or left main disease randomly selected from a consecutive angiography registry study were included in this cross-sectional study. ChatGPT-4.1 was used to provide five-category treatment decisions based on inputted patient information and a prompt most commonly used by real-world patients. The primary outcome was the agreement rate between HT and LLM recommendations. Three predefined prompting strategies were further evaluated for their potential to enhance agreement rates.

RESULTS: A total of 564 patients were included. The agreement rate between HT and LLM recommendations was 47.0% based on initial prompt. LLM performed poorly in further testing (sensitivity=0.0%) decision. LLM performed well in patients with Synergy between Percutaneous Coronary Intervention with Taxus and Cardiac Surgery score ≥33 (94.1%) but poorly in 23–32 (61.7%) and 0–22 (20.9%). After using prompting strategies, the agreement rate increased significantly (79.3%, p<0.001).

DISCUSSION: Simple patient-style queries cannot independently generate reliable decisions for real-world complex revascularisation scenarios. While prompt engineering and subgroup analysis can partially improve LLM’s performance, the potential safety risk remains emphasised.

CONCLUSION: Among a real-world cohort of patients with complex CAD, the agreement rate of decision-making between LLM and HTs was only half, but could be improved with appropriate prompts.

articles.title: Clinical heterogeneity in performance of a commercial prediction model for clinical deterioration.
Validation of ICD-10-CM algorithms for repeated eGFR-defined chronic kidney disease in the TriNetX network.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: Chronic kidney disease (CKD) is increasingly identified using electronic health records for real-world research, yet the validity of International Classification of Diseases, Tenth Revision, Clinical Modification (ICD-10-CM) CKD algorithms remains uncertain. We evaluated the diagnostic accuracy of ICD-10-CM algorithms against repeated estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR)-defined CKD in the TriNetX network.

METHODS: Adults with ≥2 eGFR measurements between 2021 and 2025 in the TriNetX US Collaborative Network were included. Repeated eGFR-defined CKD served as the reference standard. Diagnostic performance of algorithms requiring ≥1 or ≥2 ICD-10-CM codes was assessed, with additional temporal analyses restricting code ascertainment to ±3, ±6 and ±12 months around the index eGFR measurement.

RESULTS: Among 8 239 691 adults with ≥2 eGFR measurements, 1 328 952 met laboratory-defined criteria for CKD stage ≥3. For stage ≥3, an ICD-10-CM code yielded sensitivity of 64.1%, specificity of 95.6%, positive predictive value (PPV) of 73.8% and negative predictive value (NPV) of 93.3%. For stage ≥4, sensitivity was 79.2%, specificity was 98.0%, PPV was 57.3% and NPV was 99.3%. Requiring ≥2 codes reduced sensitivity but increased PPV. Temporal restriction increased PPV to approximately 96% for stage ≥3 and 93% for stage ≥4, but reduced sensitivity.

DISCUSSION: Increasing the number of required ICD-10-CM codes and temporal restriction reduced sensitivity but increased PPV, highlighting trade-offs between diagnostic certainty and case ascertainment.

CONCLUSIONS: ICD-10-CM algorithms provide a valid but incomplete approach for identifying repeated eGFR-defined CKD in the TriNetX network. No single ICD-based phenotype or temporal ascertainment strategy is optimal; algorithm selection should therefore be guided by the research application. Future phenotyping strategies combining diagnosis codes with longitudinal laboratory data may further improve identification.

articles.title: Low Allergic Sensitisation in Wheezing Children With Down Syndrome: A Case-Control Study.
articles.journal: Journal of intellectual disability research : JIDR
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Respiratory disorders are frequent in children with Down syndrome (DS), causing prolonged hospitalisations and increased healthcare system costs. Among these, recurrent wheezing is common in these children despite indications of lower rates of allergic sensitisation and asthma. This discrepancy is concerning because wheezing is often misinterpreted as asthma, leading to inappropriate treatment. Therefore, this study compared the profiles of allergic sensitisation among children with wheezing with and without DS.

METHODS: This case-control study retrospectively reviewed medical records of children (2-12 years) with recurrent wheezing, comparing 98 with DS (cases) and 96 without DS (controls). Clinical variables (pneumonia episodes, respiratory hospitalisations), biological markers (serum total IgE, eosinophil counts) and aeroallergen sensitisation (skin prick tests and/or specific IgE) were analysed. Multivariate logistic regression was used to calculate adjusted odds ratios (OR). We analysed 194 children aged 2-12 years with recurrent wheezing, including 98 with DS (cases) and 96 without (controls).

RESULTS: Allergic sensitisation was less prevalent in children with DS (7.1%) than in the control group (59.3%). Analysis revealed that DS was a protective factor, indicating that children with DS were 95% less likely to be sensitised than those without DS. Additionally, children with DS had significantly lower eosinophil counts and total IgE levels. Among sensitised children, allergic profiles were similar between groups, with Dermatophagoides farinae as the most common allergen.

CONCLUSION: The findings support the hypothesis of a non-allergic wheezing phenotype in children with DS, highlighting the need for individualised, precision-based management to optimise respiratory care in this population.

articles.title: Efficacy of low-dose pioglitazone in combination with exenatide on glucose control in patients with T2DM.
Association between weight/body mass index and insulin dose requirements in gestational diabetes: a retrospective cohort study.
Effectiveness and safety of coenzyme Q10 in people with heart failure with preserved ejection fraction (HFpEF): a systematic review and meta-analysis.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: Coenzyme Q10 (CoQ10) supplementation has previously shown efficacy in improving symptoms and outcomes for people with heart failure with reduced ejection fraction. This review aims to assess whether CoQ10 may also be effective and safe for those with heart failure with preserved ejection fraction (HFpEF).

DESIGN: Systematic review and meta-analysis of randomised controlled trials.

DATA SOURCES: We searched databases including Embase, MEDLINE, CENTRAL, Web of Science, CINAHL, AMED, ClinicalTrials.gov and the ISRCTN registry on 25 June 2025.

ELIGIBILITY CRITERIA: We included randomised controlled trials (RCTs) enrolling adults (≥18 years) with HFpEF, defined as an ejection fraction of ≥50%. Eligible studies compared any CoQ10 regimen with placebo or standard care.

DATA EXTRACTION AND SYNTHESIS: Two reviewers independently screened studies and extracted data. Risk of bias was assessed using RoB2 and the certainty of evidence using Grading of Recommendations Assessment, Development and Evaluation (GRADE). We conducted random-effects pairwise meta-analysis where possible, using the RevMan V.5.4 software. Synthesis without meta-analysis was conducted for other outcomes.

RESULTS: Three RCTs (264 participants) with a treatment duration of 8–24 weeks were included. The effect of CoQ10 on mortality in individuals with HFpEF was very uncertain (2/101 participants receiving CoQ10 vs 0/105 participants receiving placebo). No cardiovascular deaths occurred in either group (206 participants, very low certainty evidence). The effect of CoQ10 on hospitalisation due to heart failure was very uncertain (1/19 participants receiving CoQ10 vs 0/20 participants receiving placebo). Evidence on quality of life was mixed and also considered very uncertain, with one study indicating benefit from CoQ10 (mean difference (MD) 22.41 points on the Kansas City Cardiomyopathy Questionnaire, 95% CI 12.18 to 32.64, 73 participants) and another indicating no benefit (MD −8.52 points, 95% CI −19.20 to 2.16, 66 participants).

CONCLUSION: Current evidence is insufficient to determine whether CoQ10 improves outcomes in HFpEF. Larger, high-quality and adequately powered RCTs using consistent diagnostic criteria are needed before CoQ10 can be recommended in clinical practice.

PROSPERO REGISTRATION NUMBER: CRD420251027238.

articles.title: Cross-sectional study on norovirus genotyping and epidemiology among hospitalised children with acute gastroenteritis in Tianjin, North China, 2020-2023.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: To understand the molecular epidemiological and clinical characteristics of norovirus in children with acute gastroenteritis in Tianjin from 2020 to 2023.

METHODS: A total of 6714 faecal samples were collected from children aged 0–17 years with acute gastroenteritis who visited Tianjin Children’s Hospital from August 2020 to July 2023. All samples were initially screened for norovirus using reverse transcription PCR. The polymerase region and capsid protein region of the initially screened positive samples were amplified using reverse transcription PCR, the sequences were aligned and a phylogenetic tree was constructed.

RESULTS: Of the 6714 children with acute gastroenteritis, 1395 (20.78%) tested positive for norovirus in stool samples. Among them, 810 were male (20.62%, 810/3929) and 585 were female (21.01%, 585/2785). Norovirus detection rate showed seasonal differences, with the detection rates of norovirus-RNA in spring, summer, autumn and winter being 27.97% (605/2163), 11.04% (195/1767), 12.04% (141/1171) and 28.15% (454/1613), respectively. 155 norovirus-positive specimens were subjected to dual-region typing and clinical symptom-related information was collected. They were divided into nine genotypes, all of which were GII type. The three most prevalent genotypes were GII.4(P16), GII.3(P12) and GII.2(P16). The GII.4(P16) genotype accounted for 38.06% (59/155), the GII.3(P12) genotype for 27.74% (43/155) and the GII.2(P16) genotype for 19.35% (30/155).

CONCLUSION: From 2020 to 2023, the main age of onset of diarrhoea in children in Tianjin was 13–36 months, with a higher incidence in spring and winter. The most susceptible genotypes were GII.4(P16), GII.3(P12) and GII.2(P16). Abdominalgia, aminotransferase, C-reactive protein, procalcitonin and neutrophil count are statistically associated with norovirus genotypes in paediatric patients. Close monitoring of the norovirus’s spread in the population is crucial to prevent outbreaks in childcare facilities, schools and other places where children congregate, which could increase the risk of severe cases, burden family care and strain public health control efforts.

articles.title: Barriers and challenges to peer support in chronic kidney disease: a landscape review using thematic synthesis.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: Peer support is increasingly considered a useful approach to complement chronic kidney disease (CKD) care. However, establishing and sustaining peer support programmes remains challenging because of barriers affecting their delivery and uptake. This qualitative evidence landscape review aimed to explore and synthesise qualitative evidence on barriers and challenges to peer support among people living with CKD.

DESIGN: A qualitative evidence landscape review was conducted using thematic synthesis following the approach described by Thomas and Harden. The review was reported in accordance with the Enhancing Transparency in Reporting the Synthesis of Qualitative Research (ENTREQ) statement.

DATA SOURCES: Web of Science, PubMed and Scopus were searched from January 2000 to August 2026. Additional searches were conducted using Google Scholar, manual searching and the reference lists of included studies.

ELIGIBILITY CRITERIA FOR SELECTING STUDIES: Qualitative studies and mixed-methods studies with a distinct qualitative component were included if they examined barriers, challenges or experiences related to peer support among people with CKD, peer supporters, carers or healthcare professionals. Methodological quality was assessed using the Critical Appraisal Skills Programme (CASP) qualitative checklist, and confidence in the synthesised findings was assessed using the Grading of Recommendations Assessment, Development and Evaluation-Confidence in the Evidence from Reviews of Qualitative Research (GRADE-CERQual) approach.

RESULTS: A total of 3321 records were identified, including 3271 database records and 50 additional records; 15 studies were included in the synthesis. Five themes were identified: ineffective communication, organisational challenges, challenges of access to peer support programmes, personal fears and concerns and information challenges. These reflected interpersonal, organisational, access-related, individual and informational barriers.

CONCLUSION: Barriers to peer support in CKD span interpersonal, organisational, access-related, individual and informational dimensions. Attention to communication, accessibility, organisational support and the quality of information shared may support the implementation and sustainability of peer support programmes in kidney care.

articles.title: Causal discovery and treatment effect heterogeneity of futile recanalisation (CADISTH) for large vessel occlusion stroke: protocol and rationale for a multicentre prospective cohort study.
Antithrombotic therapy regimens after transcatheter valve-in-valve and valve-in-ring procedures: a scoping review.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: To describe the existing literature on antithrombotic strategies employed after transcatheter valve-in-valve (ViV) and valve-in-ring (ViR) procedures across all valve groups and to provide recommendations for areas of further research.

DESIGN: We conducted a scoping review reported in accordance with the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses Extension for Scoping Reviews guidelines.

DATA SOURCES: We systematically searched CENTRAL, EMBASE and MEDLINE from database inception until 19 January 2026. Reference lists of included studies were also manually screened.

ELIGIBILITY CRITERIA: Randomised-controlled trials, cohort or case-control studies reporting efficacy and/or safety outcomes of antithrombotic therapy in patients undergoing transcatheter ViV or ViR procedures involving aortic, mitral, tricuspid and/or pulmonary valves were included.

DATA EXTRACTION AND SYNTHESIS: Records were screened for eligibility and data were extracted using a structured charting form. Results were synthesised descriptively and grouped according to valve type.

RESULTS: Of 444 studies screened, 41 were included (10 aortic ViV, 27 mitral ViV/ViR, 1 pulmonary ViV, 1 tricuspid ViV and 2 aortic and mitral ViV). Median sample size was 32 (IQR 14–91; range 5–4243). Ten studies reported a uniform antithrombotic strategy; 30 reported variable strategies, and 1 reported only a protocol-recommended strategy without observed use or adherence. Anticoagulation, with or without antiplatelet therapy, was commonly reported following mitral ViV/ViR, while regimens reported following aortic ViV were highly variable but antiplatelet therapy predominated slightly over anticoagulant therapy. Thrombotic and bleeding outcomes were reported in a highly heterogenous manner.

CONCLUSIONS: Evidence guiding antithrombotic therapy after ViV is heterogeneous and largely observational, underscoring the need for high-quality studies to inform optimal management.

TRIAL REGISTRATION NUMBER: This scoping review is registered on the Open Science Framework and can be accessed at: https://osf.io/exvc2/overview?view_only=aeb99d7b79734510826a8ce408e70b03.

articles.title: Developing the supportive care bundle for mothers of infants hospitalised in the neonatal intensive care unit: protocol for a multimethod study.
Development and description of a logic model for a guided, low-intensity cognitive behavioural therapy intervention for parents of persons treated for cancer during childhood: the EJDeR intervention.
Adaptive pulsatile aspiration leads to improved thrombectomy outcomes during in vivo large vessel occlusion for acute ischemic stroke.
Adult-onset food protein-induced enterocolitis syndrome after cord blood transplantation mimicking gastrointestinal graft-versus-host disease.
Multiple cranial neuropathies in a patient with eosinophilic granulomatosis with polyangiitis.
articles.abstract: Eosinophilic granulomatosis with polyangiitis (EGPA) is a rare vasculitis characterised by asthma, eosinophilia and sinonasal disease. Although peripheral neuropathy is common, central nervous system involvement occurs in only 3%–5% of patients and may cause significant morbidity. We present an older adult male with antineutrophil cytoplasmic antibody-negative EGPA, that relapsed after discontinuing mepolizumab and developed sequential cranial neuropathies involving cranial nerves V, VII, II and X, causing trigeminal neuropathy, bilateral facial palsy, optic neuropathy and vocal cord dysfunction. MRI demonstrated hypertrophic pachymeningitis (HP) with multifocal pachymeningeal enhancement. The patient received pulse intravenous methylprednisolone followed by cyclophosphamide infusion, resulting in headache resolution, stabilisation of visual symptoms, improvement in hoarseness and decreased pachymeningeal enhancement on follow-up MRI. He was transitioned to methotrexate and monthly mepolizumab maintenance therapy. This case highlights a rare presentation of EGPA with sequential multiple cranial neuropathies secondary to HP, emphasising the importance of early recognition and aggressive immunosuppressive therapy.

articles.title: Caustic agent ingestion leading to a difficult airway and oesophageal stricture: an anaesthesia-guided, bougie-assisted technique for oesophageal access.
Acute gastric and distal oesophageal necrosis associated with acute portosplenic-mesenteric venous thrombosis: a rare surgical emergency.
UN adopts political declaration on pandemic preparedness-but without crucial consensus.
Reporting completeness of clinical trials evaluating large language model interventions in medicine: systematic review.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To characterise the reporting completeness of clinical trials involving large language model (LLM) interventions using established reporting guidelines.

DESIGN: Systematic review and meta-research analysis.

DATA SOURCES: Bibliographic databases (Embase, Medline, and CENTRAL) were searched for trial reports and protocols, and trial registries (ClinicalTrials.gov and World Health Organization International Clinical Trials Registry Platform) were searched for trial registrations published from 1 January 2017 to 6 December 2025.

ELIGIBILITY CRITERIA: Trial reports, trial protocols, and trial registrations describing clinical trials of LLM interventions in medicine. LLM interventions used for a healthcare function in a clinical trial setting included patient education, clinical documentation, communication support, triage, care navigation, management recommendations, or clinical decision support. Eligible studies prospectively assigned human participants to the intervention and evaluated a health related biomedical or behavioural outcome.

MAIN OUTCOME MEASURES: Overall study level and item level reporting completeness assessed using reporting guidelines matched to study design and purpose, including TRIPOD-LLM (Transparent Reporting of a multivariable prediction model for Individual Prognosis Or Diagnosis-LLM), CONSORT (Consolidated Standards of Reporting Trials) 2025 and CONSORT-AI, SPIRIT (Standard Protocol Items: Recommendations for Interventional Trials) 2025 and SPIRIT-AI, CHART (Chatbot Assessment Reporting Tool), and the WHO Trial Registration Dataset (version 1.3.1). Two reviewers independently screened and extracted trial and intervention characteristics, and three calibrated raters assessed item level reporting completeness.

RESULTS: The systematic search yielded 461 records, including 68 trial reports, 15 protocols, and 378 registrations. Trial reports were predominantly small sample, single site randomised studies published between 2024 and 2025, spanning diverse clinical specialties and primarily targeting patient facing education and management recommendations. Mean reporting completeness was modest across eligible trial reports (TRIPOD-LLM 40%, CONSORT 2025 44%, CONSORT-AI 59%, CHART 52%), trial protocols (SPIRIT 2025 51%, SPIRIT-AI 57%), and trial registrations (WHO Trial Registration Dataset 61%). Clinical trial reports of LLM interventions prioritise narrative framing and commentary over the methodological detail needed for replication, risk-of-bias assessment, and governance of model performance over time. Critical methodological elements for reproducibility, including data and intervention provenance, input preprocessing, model versioning and access modality, inference parameters, output postprocessing, as well as protocol, data, and code access, were inconsistently reported. Harms planning, monitoring, and reporting were often incompletely reported, limiting the critical appraisal of the safety of LLM interventions in healthcare.

CONCLUSION: Clinical trials of LLM interventions show modest adherence to established reporting guidelines, with persistent underreporting of LLM specific methodological details, reproducibility artefacts (protocols, data, code), and harms reporting required to support reproducibility and confident appraisal of safety risks before their clinical translation.

articles.title: Empowerment in advanced liver disease: UK experiences of care from the perspectives of people with lived experience, carers and healthcare professionals.
articles.abstract: ObjectivesLiver disease is a leading cause of morbidity and mortality, with alcohol-related liver disease, metabolic-associated steatotic liver disease, and viral hepatitis comprising most cases in the UK. Advanced liver disease presents challenges due to unpredictable disease trajectories, high symptom burden, psychosocial impacts, and stigma. This study aimed to develop an explanatory theory of care experiences in decompensated advanced liver disease from the perspectives of individuals living with the condition, carers, and healthcare professionals, with public involvement embedded throughout.MethodsUsing Charmaz's Constructivist Grounded Theory methodology, semi-structured interviews were conducted across the UK with individuals with advanced liver disease, carers, and healthcare professionals. Data collection and analysis occurred concurrently using constant comparison, focused coding, memoing, and theoretical sampling.ResultsTwenty-four people participated in interviews. Analysis generated the Empowerment Continuum, an explanatory theory conceptualising empowerment as a dynamic, relational process shaped by personal, relational, and systemic factors. Five conceptual categories informed the theory: self-care, navigating healthcare services, healthcare professionals' contributions, carers' involvement and support, and information and communication.DiscussionThe Empowerment Continuum provides a framework for understanding care experiences in advanced liver disease. Supporting empowerment requires collaborative, accessible, and person-centred approaches involving people with liver disease, carers, and healthcare professionals.

articles.title: Feasibility of Online and On-Site Physical Activity Delivery Among Older Adults: Mixed Methods Pilot Randomized Controlled Trial.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Physical activity (PA) is central to healthy aging, yet interventions targeting older adults often report substantial attrition and variable adherence. Although digital and internet-based exercise programs broaden accessibility and flexibility, their ability to sustain engagement compared with traditional on-site formats remains unclear. Understanding how delivery mode influences attrition and adherence-and why participants persist or withdraw-is essential for designing inclusive and sustainable PA interventions.

OBJECTIVE: This pilot study evaluates the feasibility of delivering a 26-week PA intervention to older adults through 2 modes: online or on-site. Feasibility was assessed primarily by attrition, adherence, and participants' experiences of factors influencing continued participation or withdrawal. Additionally, the study explores preliminary patterns in PA levels and physical and mental health outcomes to inform the design of a future definitive trial.

METHODS: This 26-week pragmatic pilot trial used an embedded convergent mixed methods design. Community-dwelling adults aged 60 years or older (N=35) from 3 residential areas in Sweden were cluster-randomized, without blinding, by site to an online (prerecorded video-based Otago exercises; n=12) or on-site (group-based, in-person Otago exercises; n=23) delivery mode. Feasibility outcomes included attrition and adherence. Exploratory outcomes included PA level (Godin-Shephard Leisure-Time Exercise Questionnaire), lower-body strength (Chair Stand Test), depressive symptoms (Geriatric Depression Scale), and health-related quality of life (EQ-5D-3L), assessed at baseline, midintervention (14 weeks), and postintervention (26 weeks). Exploratory quantitative analyses included t tests, chi-square tests, analysis of covariance, and mixed-design ANOVAs. We analyzed semistructured interviews with completers (n=17) and dropouts (n=7) using qualitative content analysis. Findings were integrated using the COM-B (Capability, Opportunity, Motivation-Behavior) framework.

RESULTS: The overall attrition rate was 37% (13/35), with no significant difference between delivery modes (P=.29). Most dropouts occurred within the first 2 weeks. Mean adherence appeared higher in the online delivery mode (mean 17.0, SD 6.7) than in the on-site delivery mode (mean 12.1, SD 10.1) but did not differ significantly (P=.15). Qualitative findings indicated that attrition was primarily driven by physical health issues and a perceived lack of fit, whereas adherence was supported by appeal and reward, routine and commitment, flexibility, feedback and PA overview, and (often) social presence. Mixed methods findings suggest that capability, opportunity, and motivation supported participation across both delivery modes. No intervention-related adverse events were reported.

CONCLUSIONS: Both online and on-site delivery modes for PA interventions appeared feasible for many older adults. Although no statistically significant between-group differences were observed, the study was not powered to evaluate effectiveness. Feasibility may depend more on supporting capability, opportunity, and motivation than on delivery mode. Larger, adequately powered trials are needed to test effectiveness, identify optimal formats for different populations, and evaluate strategies to reduce early attrition.

TRIAL REGISTRATION: ClinicalTrials.gov NCT05885308; https://clinicaltrials.gov/ct2/show/NCT05885308.

articles.title: Ankle-Foot Orthosis and Footwear Interactions in Adult Healthy and Patient Populations: Systematic Review of Biomechanical Outcomes.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Both ankle-foot orthoses (AFOs) and footwear adaptations are used to improve gait across a broad range of neuromuscular disorders. AFOs and footwear can each independently influence gait through the manipulation of certain design parameters, such as AFO footplate stiffness or the use of a forefoot rocker. While the effects of design parameters from AFOs and footwear on gait have been investigated independently, how these parameters interact to influence walking biomechanics remains poorly understood.

OBJECTIVE: This systematic literature review aims to provide an overview of the interacting effects between AFOs and footwear on gait biomechanics from both a theoretical standpoint and through the synthesis of existing literature.

METHODS: A search of existing literature was conducted across 4 major databases. Studies were eligible if they included adult participants from healthy or patient populations. Studies included should have investigated biomechanical gait outcomes recorded during walking with an AFO and at least two different footwear conditions. Quality assessment was performed using the Downs and Black checklist and AFO reporting guidelines.

RESULTS: A total of 14 studies were included in this review. Across these 14 studies, a total of 204 participants (108 healthy, 84 patients after stroke, and 12 unilateral ankle weakness or pain) were included. The majority of these studies were within-subjects designs. Footwear adaptations were primarily changes to the heel-sole differential (HSD; 7/14), followed by forefoot rockers (5/14), with some studies on changes to heel shape and hardness (3/14), and a study on mediolateral wedging. These adaptations were used in combination with primarily rigid AFOs (10/14), with studies also using dorsiflexion-free and frontal plane restrictive AFOs.

CONCLUSIONS: Increasing the HSD can be used to increase knee flexion across the stance phase in rigid AFO users, including in the third rocker when HSD is manipulated between the shoe and AFO. Beyond changing the HSD, there is a lack of well-designed experimental studies exploring footwear adaptations. Detailed reporting of both AFO and footwear design choices is necessary for future work in order to make informed statements on biomechanics.

articles.title: Unsuccessful Healing of Tympanic Membrane Perforations Following Myringoplasty-A Nationwide Retrospective Study.
articles.journal: Clinical otolaryngology : official journal of ENT-UK ; official journal of Netherlands Society for Oto-Rhino-Laryngology & Cervico-Facial Surgery
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Risk factors for unsuccessful healing of a tympanic membrane perforation following myringoplasty lack consensus. Large cohort studies are missing.

METHODS: Data were collected for myringoplasties (with/without concomitant ossiculoplasty) performed the years 2014-2019 with a follow-up visit using the Swedish Quality Register for Ear Surgery (SwedEar). Risk factors for unsuccessful surgical outcome, defined as non-healed tympanic membrane at follow-up, were calculated using logistic regression.

RESULTS: The study population included 3622 cases and 12.8% had a non-healed tympanic membrane at follow-up. The most commonly used graft material was fascia, used in 94.6% of the cases. Of the analysed variables, prior ear surgery (adjusted (a)OR 1.43, p = 0.005), age younger than 8 years (aOR 1.73, p = 0.015), a postoperative infection within 6 weeks after surgery (aOR 1.92, p < 0.001) and the surgical aim of achieving a dry/infection free ear (aOR 1.53, p = 0.045) were predictors for unsuccessful healing. For simultaneous ossiculoplasty at surgery, there was a significantly higher chance of having a healed tympanic membrane (aOR 1.49, p = 0.016). For other variables such as gender, operated side, season, graft material, perioperative antibiotics and infection free status at surgery, there was no significant effect on tympanic membrane healing.

CONCLUSION: The present evaluation of the surgical results in SwedEar constitutes one of the largest studies on myringoplasty outcome. The results showed that the age of the patient, surgical aim, prior ear surgery and postoperative infection constituted risk factors for unsuccessful healing after myringoplasty. Surprisingly, ears requiring a concomitant ossiculoplasty had a higher healing rate.

articles.title: Oral Fluid Inflammatory Biomarker Profile in Long COVID: Evaluation of Oral Active and Total MMP-8, MMP-9, and TIMP-1 in Relation to BMI and Disease Status.
articles.journal: International journal of infectious diseases : IJID : official publication of the International Society for Infectious Diseases
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Long COVID (LC) is characterized by persistent systemic symptoms, but its oral inflammatory profile remains unclear. This study evaluated oral inflammatory biomarkers, particularly matrix metalloproteinase (MMP) -8, -9 and their regulators in oral rinse samples from LC patients.

METHODS: This cross-sectional study analyzed oral rinse samples from 115 LC patients and 103 comparable controls. Periodontal inflammation was screened using a chair-side active MMP-8 (aMMP-8) point-of-care test (POCT). Biomarkers (aMMP-8, total MMP-8, MMP-9, TIMP-1, and MPO) were quantified and validated by Western blotting and gelatin zymography. Associations with LC and clinical variables were assessed using bivariate analysis and multivariable regression.

RESULTS: LC patients had significantly higher total MMP-8, MMP-9, TIMP-1, and MMP-9/TIMP-1 ratio (all p<0.05 in both analyses). IFMA-measured active MMP-8 became independently associated with LC after multivariable adjustment. Chair-side aMMP-8 POCT showed a non-significant trend toward higher positivity in LC (16.5% vs. 8.7%). BMI was positively associated with aMMP-8, tMMP-8 and tMMP-8/TIMP-1 molar ratio. Antidepressant use was associated with tMMP-8/TIMP-1 molar ratio. Western blotting confirmed active MMP-8 species and gingipain.

CONCLUSION: These findings suggest an altered oral inflammatory biomarker profile in LC. The potential role of chair-side aMMP-8 POCT for screening oral inflammation in this population merits further investigation.

articles.title: Prevalence and Factors Associated with Cognitive Impairment Among Sepsis Survivors: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
articles.journal: International journal of infectious diseases : IJID : official publication of the International Society for Infectious Diseases
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Sepsis survivors frequently experience cognitive impairment, which negatively affects long-term quality of life and functional recovery. However, the prevalence and associated factors remain insufficiently characterized.

OBJECTIVE: This study aimed to evaluate the prevalence of cognitive impairment among sepsis survivors across different follow-up periods and identify associated factors using systematic review and meta-analysis.

METHODS: PubMed, Embase, Web of Science, Cochrane Library, CNKI, SinoMed, Wanfang Data, and VIP Database were searched from inception to March 19, 2026. Cohort and cross-sectional studies were included. Random-effects models were used to estimate pooled prevalence and odds ratios, and the certainty of evidence was evaluated using the GRADE approach.

RESULTS: Eighteen studies involving 218,152 sepsis survivors were included. Cognitive impairment remains common among sepsis survivors, with prevalence estimates varying across follow-up time points. Older age, prolonged delirium duration, hyperglycemia, and hypoxemia were positively associated with cognitive impairment (ORs ranging from 1.12 to 2.84). The certainty of evidence ranged from very low to low.

CONCLUSIONS: The pooled prevalence of cognitive impairment among sepsis survivors differed across follow-up time points. However, because estimates at different time points were largely based on different studies and populations, these findings should be interpreted as study-level time-stratified differences rather than evidence of within-individual cognitive recovery or decline. Older age, prolonged delirium duration, hyperglycemia, and hypoxemia were associated with cognitive impairment among sepsis survivors. Given the low to very low certainty of the available evidence, the observed associations should be interpreted cautiously. Further well-designed prospective studies are needed to confirm these findings.

articles.title: treatable trait in COPD: is LVDD the potential next?
Diffusion MRI Assessment of White Matter Microstructure and Free-Water Fraction in Drug-Naïve Children with SeLECTS.
articles.abstract: Self-limited epilepsy with centrotemporal spikes (SeLECTS) is a common childhood-onset focal epilepsy syndrome. Although seizures are typically self-limited, some children may show neurodevelopmental or cognitive vulnerability. Diffusion MRI may provide insight into white matter alterations in SeLECTS. Objective To evaluate white matter diffusion differences in newly diagnosed, drug-naïve children with SeLECTS using tract-based spatial statistics (TBSS) and white matter free-water fraction (FW-WM), and to explore within-patient associations with selected seizure-related and cognitive variables. Methods Fifty-three newly diagnosed, drug-naïve children with SeLECTS and 53 healthy controls with a similar age and sex distribution were prospectively enrolled in this cross-sectional case-control study. Diffusion MRI was acquired at 3.0T, and white matter diffusion differences were assessed using TBSS and FW-WM analyses. Voxelwise between-group differences in fractional anisotropy (FA) were tested with age and sex as covariates and corrected using threshold-free cluster enhancement-based family-wise error correction. FW-WM was compared between groups using age- and sex-adjusted general linear models, with additional adjustment for years of education in a sensitivity analysis. Exploratory within-patient associations between imaging measures and selected clinical or cognitive variables were assessed using partial Spearman correlations with false-discovery-rate correction. Results Children with SeLECTS showed lower FA than healthy controls in multiple TBSS-defined white matter regions after correction for multiple comparisons, mainly involving commissural, projection, and association pathways. No between-group differences in mean, axial, or radial diffusivity survived correction for multiple comparisons. FW-WM was higher in the SeLECTS group after adjustment for age and sex (adjusted mean difference = 0.0085; 95% CI, 0.0023 to 0.0147; P = 0.008), with similar results after additional adjustment for education. In exploratory cluster-level analyses, mean FA in a left-sided cluster involving the posterior internal capsule, posterior thalamic radiation, and sagittal stratum was inversely associated with disease duration after FDR correction (r = -0.413; P = 0.003; q = 0.010). No imaging-cognition or within-patient FW-WM-FA association survived FDR correction. Conclusions Newly diagnosed, drug-naïve children with SeLECTS showed white matter diffusion differences, including lower FA in distributed TBSS-defined regions and higher FW-WM. These findings support diffusion MRI-based characterization of white matter alterations at diagnosis, before antiseizure treatment. Longitudinal studies are needed to clarify their clinical and developmental relevance.

articles.title: Dupuytren's disease: From the first signs to the most advanced stages.
articles.abstract: Dupuytren's disease is a benign fibroproliferative condition of the palmar fascia, characterized by onset of nodules that develop into cords causing irreducible digital contracture. Prevalence increases with age. It mainly affects males of Northern European origin. Etiopathogenesis is multifactorial, combining genetic predisposition and environmental factors such as alcohol consumption, smoking, microtrauma and diabetes. Management is based on precise clinical assessment, with Tubiana classification and diathesis screening, to adapt therapeutic strategy. In the early stages, monitoring may be combined with medical treatment (radiotherapy, collagenase, corticosteroids, anti-TNF) aimed at slowing progression. In case of functional impairment or significant retraction, several surgical options are available: percutaneous fasciotomy, limited or segmental fasciectomy, dermofasciectomy with skin grafting, or even phalangectomy in severe recurrent cases. This narrative review provides an up-to-date summary of epidemiological, pathophysiological and therapeutic data, emphasizing the importance of a decision-tree that takes account of the progression, diathesis and severity of the contracture.

articles.title: Divergent bacterial signatures in dental clinic bioaerosols: a real-field investigation.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Dental procedures generate bioaerosols containing oral microorganisms, posing a potential cross-infection risk. Effective infection control requires real-world data on aerosol behaviour in clinical settings.

OBJECTIVE: To characterize particulate matter and bacterial profiles during active ultrasonic periodontal scaling under routine clinical conditions.

METHODS: Sampling occurred under background and ultrasonic scaling conditions. Airborne particles were monitored in real-time using an optical particle sizer. Bioaerosols were collected using an Andersen six-stage sampler (culturable) and a filter-based high-flow pump (non-culturable). Surface samples were obtained from personal protective equipment (PPE) and environmental surfaces. Bacterial communities were analyzed via 16S rRNA sequencing.

FINDINGS: A notable decoupling was observed between physical and biological aerosol profiles: although ultrasonic instrumentation produced a substantial surge in sub-micron particles, culturable microbial recovery was predominantly concentrated within the respirable 1.1-3.3 μm fractions. High-throughput sequencing revealed clear spatial differentiation in bacterial communities. Microbial contamination was heavily confined to the clinician's PPE within the immediate splash zone. Airborne bacteria differed significantly from those on PPE (ANOSIM R = 0.633, p = 0.001), whereas clinical air and peripheral non-touch surfaces shared an indistinguishable ambient microbiome (R = 0.095, p = 0.249), with oral pathogens rarely detected in either compartment.

CONCLUSION: Under the specific conditions evaluated, total particle counts do not reflect culturable bacterial load, which is concentrated in the 1.1-3.3 μm respirable fraction. Bacterial contamination remains predominantly localized to the operative field and PPE, with minimal dispersion to ambient air. Accordingly, physical particle metrics should not be used as direct indicators of bacterial hazard, and clinician protection relies primarily on strict PPE compliance.

articles.title: Impact of Earthquake-Related Mass Casualty Burden on Hospital Microbial Ecology and Surgical Site Infections After Elective Orthopaedic Surgery: A Retrospective Cohort Study.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: The aim of this study was to compare surgical site infections (SSIs) developing after primary elective orthopaedic procedures before and after the February 6, 2023 earthquakes and to investigate the incidence, causative pathogen distribution, and antimicrobial resistance patterns.

MATERIALS AND METHODS: This single-center retrospective cohort study included patients undergoing primary total or partial hip arthroplasty, total knee arthroplasty, or open reduction and internal fixation. The Patients were divided into pre-earthquake (June 1, 2018-February 5, 2023) and post-earthquake (June 1, 2023-November 1, 2025) periods. The SSI cases were defined according to periprosthetic joint infection (ICM 2025) and fracture-related infection (FRI 2018) criteria. Microbiological profiles, resistance patterns, and clinical outcomes were compared between groups.

RESULTS: A total of 99 and 118 SSI cases were identified in the pre- and post-earthquake cohorts, respectively. Overall SSI rates were similar between groups (0.98% vs. 1.19%; p=0.143). However, post-earthquake infections were associated with significantly longer hospital stays (28 vs. 22 days; p=0.025) and increased debridement procedures (2.0 vs. 1.0; p=0.006). Polymicrobial infections increased significantly (12.1% vs. 23.7%; p=0.028). A marked microbiological shift was observed, with Gram-negative organisms becoming predominant (67.7% vs. 47.6%; p=0.004), while Gram-positive organisms decreased. Staphylococcus aureus isolation significantly declined (35.4% vs. 17.2%; p=0.008). Meticillin resistance among Gram-positive isolates increased (34.9% vs. 60.0%; p=0.022), whereas no significant change in Gram-negative carbapenem resistance was observed.

CONCLUSION: Our study results showed that the rates of polymicrobial infections and meticillin resistance among Gram-positive isolates increased significantly. This microbiological shift was also associated with clinically relevant outcomes, including prolonged hospital stay and an increased number of debridement procedures. Taken together, in centers exposed to a high burden of mass casualty patients, the infection dynamics of routine elective surgical cases may continue to evolve even months after the disaster. Reassessment of existing empirical treatment protocols is warranted in such settings.

articles.title: Am I receiving good care? A qualitative study exploring the moral experiences of MDRO carriers in Dutch hospitals and nursing homes.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Carriership of multi-drug resistant organisms (MDROs) and associated infection prevention and control (IPC) measures can negatively affect hospital patients and nursing home residents. Little is known about how carriers appraise these experiences in light of what matters to them - i.e. the moral dimension. This study explores the moral experiences of carriers receiving care in hospitals and nursing homes.

METHODS: We conducted a qualitative analysis of moral experiences present in semi-structured interviews with 20 MDRO carriers.

RESULTS: Carriers reported that some values were upheld, whereas others were undermined during care. We identified four themes. First, carriers felt responsible for protecting loved ones or the public by preventing transmission, yet perceived inconsistencies in IPC protocols generated doubt, frustration and feelings of injustice. Second, carriers described being visited less frequently or treated differently by healthcare providers (HCPs). Some felt guilty towards HCPs and other patients that their care required additional staff time. Third, carriers experienced burdens in receiving care like not seeing HCPs' faces, loss of freedom or feeling dirty, but also moments of compassion from empathic HCPs. Fourth, concerns about carriership extended beyond hospital care, with uncertainties about implications in daily life.

DISCUSSION: Identifying which values carriers perceive as upheld or undermined can guide more proportionate and equitable IPC policies and improve quality of care. HCPs should support carriers in navigating the many questions and uncertainties they face during care and in their daily lives. Future research should normatively evaluate IPC policies and explore how to address undermined values in care.

articles.title: Ferroptosis in endodontic pathobiology: Emerging evidence, mechanistic rationale, and translational uncertainties.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Ferroptosis is an iron-dependent form of regulated cell death characterized by lipid peroxidation and impaired antioxidant defense. Its defining biochemical features, including iron-redox imbalance and lipid peroxide accumulation, overlap with biological conditions present in infected, hypoxic, and cytokine-rich endodontic tissues. This narrative review examined the potential role of ferroptosis in endodontic pathobiology, with emphasis on separating direct endodontic evidence from indirect or extrapolated oral evidence.

METHODS: Electronic searches were performed in PubMed, Scopus, and Web of Science using terms related to ferroptosis, endodontics, pulpitis, apical periodontitis, dental pulp, root canal infection, Enterococcus faecalis, periodontal ligament, ferritinophagy, iron metabolism, lipid peroxidation, and major ferroptosis-related regulators. Ferroptosis-associated papers were classified according to proximity to endodontic disease and strength of evidence.

RESULTS: Current evidence suggests that ferroptosis-associated pathways may participate in pulpitis and apical periodontitis. Direct evidence is strongest for active pulpitis and apical periodontitis, where ferroptosis-related changes have been reported in human tissues, animal models, and endodontic-relevant cell systems, including dental pulp fibroblasts, dental pulp cells, dental pulp stem cells, endothelial cells, and macrophages. Extrapolated evidence from periodontitis, periodontal ligament cells, oral bone models, and dental stem-cell studies provides biological context but does not establish causation in endodontic disease. Evidence for complete pulp necrosis, inflammatory root resorption, post-treatment healing, and regenerative endodontics is indirect, limited, or absent.

CONCLUSIONS: Ferroptosis-associated pathways represent a credible but still emerging area of endodontic pathobiology. Current evidence suggests a possible contributory role in pulpal and periapical inflammation, but causal relevance, disease-stage specificity, and clinical significance remain unresolved. Future studies should use polymicrobial or infected-dentin models, human tissue validation, standardized ferroptosis criteria, and longitudinal intervention designs before ferroptosis-related mechanisms can be translated into endodontic diagnosis, treatment, or regenerative strategies.

articles.title: Cellular toxicity and apoptosis-related responses to individual and combined exposure to microplastics and perfluorooctane sulfonic acid (PFOS) in Hediste diversicolor coelomocytes.
articles.abstract: Microplastics (MPs) are emerging contaminants of increasing concern in marine ecosystems due to their widespread occurrence and ability to adsorb and transport hazardous chemicals such as perfluorooctane sulfonic acid (PFOS). PFOS is a persistent per- and polyfluoroalkyl substance (PFAS) with high environmental stability, bioaccumulative potential, and well-documented toxicity to aquatic organisms. However, the combined effects of MPs and PFOS on marine invertebrates remain poorly understood. This study evaluated the individual and combined effects of environmentally relevant concentrations of MPs (50 mg kg-1 sediment) and PFOS (0.1, 0.5, and 1 μg kg-1 sediment) on the coelomic fluid of the benthic polychaete Hediste diversicolor after 7 days of sediment exposure. The MPs consisted of particles <30 μm composed of PVC, PET, PS, HDPE, LDPE, and PE with heterogeneous morphologies. PFOS accumulated in the coelomic fluid in a dose-dependent manner, with higher concentrations observed under co-exposure, suggesting that the presence of MPs may influence PFOS bioavailability and uptake. This increased accumulation was accompanied by pronounced cytotoxic and genotoxic effects, including lysosomal membrane destabilization, increased micronucleus frequency, and DNA fragmentation. Co-exposure also upregulated the pro-apoptotic genes p53, Bax, and Casp-3, while downregulating the anti-apoptotic gene Bcl-2, indicating activation of apoptotic pathways. Overall, the effects of combined exposure varied according to the endpoint and PFOS concentration, with co-exposure producing greater responses for some endpoints but not consistently across all treatments. These findings highlight the increased hazard posed by the co-occurrence of MPs and PFOS and emphasize the need to consider contaminant mixtures in marine environmental risk assessment.

articles.title: Transgenerational Effects of Paternal in Utero Arsenic Exposure on MASLD-like Phenotypes.
articles.abstract: Previous study indicated that early-life arsenic (As) exposure caused adulthood metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD)-like phenotypes. This study aimed to investigate the impacts of paternal in utero As exposure on MASLD-like phenotypes in offspring. Pregnant dams received NaAsO2 (15 mg/L) through drinking water. In utero As-exposed male pups were designated as F0 mice and mated with untreated females to produce F1 offspring. F1 males were subsequently mated with untreated females to generate F2 offspring, both without further As exposure. MASLD-like phenotypes were evaluated in F1 and F2 offspring. On PNW28, As-exposed F1 offspring exhibited hepatic steatosis, glucose intolerance, insulin resistance, and obesity, accompanied by altered metabolic hormones, such as GLP-1, GIP, insulin, and ADPN. The core MASLD-like phenotypes, including hepatic steatosis, glucose intolerance and insulin resistance, exhibited transgenerational transmission from F1 to F2 generations. In F2 offspring, these metabolic abnormalities were detected at PNW45 but not at PNW28, predominantly in male offspring. In contrast, As-induced obesity and metabolic hormone alterations exhibited transgenerational attenuation. F2 offspring retained only adipocyte hypertrophy, with no significant changes in white or brown adipose tissue weight. Furthermore, hormonal alterations in F2 mice were limited to reduced GLP-1 and elevated ADPN levels, while other altered hormones normalized. This study is the first to confirm that paternal in utero As exposure causes MASLD-like phenotypes in F1 offspring and transgenerational transmission to F2 generation.

articles.title: Early-life animal exposure was not associated with risk of inflammatory bowel disease: a nationwide birth cohort study.
articles.journal: Clinical gastroenterology and hepatology : the official clinical practice journal of the American Gastroenterological Association
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND AND AIMS: The incidence of inflammatory bowel disease (IBD) continues to rise globally. Early-life environmental exposures may influence immune development, but evidence regarding animal exposure remains inconsistent. We examined whether early-life exposure to pets or farm animals was associated with offspring risk of IBD in a prospective birth cohort.

METHODS: In this nationwide cohort study based on the Danish National Birth Cohort, prenatal offspring exposure to pets or farm animals, based on maternal reports, was used as the primary indicator of early-life animal exposure. Early-childhood exposure from birth to 18 months was examined in exposure-window analyses. Incident IBD, Crohn's disease (CD), and ulcerative colitis (UC) were identified through national registries. Associations were estimated using Cox proportional hazards models.

RESULTS: Among 90,306 offspring, 46% were prenatally exposed to pets and 7% to farm animals. During median follow-up of 24 years, 615 offspring developed IBD. Pet exposure was not associated with IBD risk (aHR 1.05, 95% CI 0.89-1.24), nor was farm animal exposure (aHR 1.00, 95% CI 0.73-1.37). Findings were consistent across specific animal categories and in analyses of CD and UC separately. In exposure-window analyses restricted to 63,958 offspring with maternal reports of both pre- and postnatal exposure, no associations were observed among offspring exposed only during pregnancy (aHR 1.10, 95% CI 0.75-1.63) or only during early childhood (aHR 0.73, 95% CI 0.46-1.15).

CONCLUSIONS: Early-life exposure to pets or farm animals was not associated with offspring risk of IBD. These findings suggest that early-life animal exposure may not be a major determinant of disease development.

articles.title: Fibromyalgia Subgroups Identified Using Model-Based Clustering: Results from UK Biobank.
articles.abstract: Fibromyalgia (FM) is a heterogeneous chronic condition with wide variability in symptom burden, psychosocial distress, and functional impact. This study aimed to identify latent FM subgroups reflecting multidimensional patient profiles using comprehensive biopsychosocial variables and model-based clustering methods within UK Biobank. Individuals meeting the 2016 American College of Rheumatology FM criteria (n = 4,172) were analysed using Gaussian mixture clustering. Twenty-eight variables across sociodemographic, clinical symptoms, and psychological/behavioural domains were included. Cluster stability was evaluated using bootstrap resampling and adjusted Rand indices (ARI). Variable importance was assessed using Random Forest analysis. Three distinct subgroups were identified: the Resilient Majority (62.3%) with low symptoms and psychological resilience; the Severe Phenotype (20.1%) with pronounced pain, fatigue, and psychological distress; and the Socially Vulnerable Minority (17.6%) characterized by ethnic diversity, rural residence, and social isolation. Sociodemographic and psychological/behavioural variables (e.g. frequency of feeling down, home area population density, ethnicity, frequency of home visits, and smoking status) demonstrated greater discriminative contribution than clinical symptom variables. All clusters demonstrated high stability (ARI > 0.93). These findings identify subgroups within FM defined not only by symptom severity but also by structural vulnerabilities and psychosocial factors. Recognizing such heterogeneity has implications for developing stratified, equitable management approaches that integrate psychosocial dimensions alongside clinical symptoms. PERSPECTIVE: Three fibromyalgia subgroups were identified: a resilient majority, a severe phenotype with socioeconomic disadvantage, and a socially vulnerable minority characterized by ethnic diversity and rural isolation patterns. Psychosocial factors outperformed clinical symptoms in discriminating subgroups, underscoring the need for stratified and patient-centred management addressing the biopsychosocial complexity of fibromyalgia.

articles.title: WSSV355 enhances IDH1 enzymatic activity and promotes efficient WSSV replication.
articles.abstract: White spot syndrome virus (WSSV) drives extensive metabolic reprogramming to support viral replication, including activation of reductive carboxylation, a pathway in which host isocitrate dehydrogenase 1 (IDH1) has a central role. However, the mechanisms by which viral factors regulate IDH1 and associated metabolic networks remain unclear. Here, we identified WSSV355 as a key viral regulator that contributed to IDH1 binding and activation during infection. Using yeast two-hybrid screening, WSSV355 was identified as an LvIDH1-interacting protein and further validated by co-immunoprecipitation and co-localization analyses. Functional assays demonstrated that WSSV355 enhanced IDH1 enzymatic activity, whereas truncation mapping revealed that distinct regions of WSSV355 contributed to IDH1 binding and activation. In vivo silencing of WSSV355 suppressed viral gene expression, and decreased viral genome copy number, establishing its role in promoting efficient WSSV replication. Affinity purification-mass spectrometry (AP-MS) further revealed that WSSV355 identified a set/network of WSSV355-associated proteins enriched in cytoskeletal, RNA-processing, and metabolic pathways. Integration with infection-responsive proteomic datasets identified candidate modules linking the WSSV355-associated protein network to host infection responses, suggesting broader potential involvement of WSSV355 in host cellular processes during infection. Collectively, these findings identify WSSV355 as an LvIDH1-interacting viral protein that enhances IDH1 enzymatic activity and is required for efficient WSSV replication. To our knowledge, WSSV355 is the first reported virus-encoded protein shown to enhance IDH1 enzymatic activity, providing new insights into how aquatic viruses exploit host metabolic machinery to promote infection.

articles.title: Schisandra chinensis in sepsis intervention through multi-target mechanisms and organ protection.
articles.abstract: Sepsis is a life-threatening syndrome characterized by overwhelming inflammation, oxidative stress, immune imbalance, endothelial dysfunction, and progressive multiple organ injury. Schisandra chinensis (S. chinensis) and its bioactive constituents possess anti-inflammatory, antioxidant, immunomodulatory, and organ-protective properties, but their sepsis-related evidence has not been comprehensively summarized. This narrative review critically summarizes the current evidence on S. chinensis and its bioactive constituents in sepsis, with emphasis on inflammatory regulation, immune homeostasis, oxidative stress, endothelial dysfunction, regulated cell death, and sepsis-associated organ injury. PubMed/MEDLINE, Web of Science, Scopus, Google Scholar, China National Knowledge Infrastructure, and Wanfang Data were searched without restriction on publication year, and the reference lists of relevant publications were also screened. Eligible studies were narratively synthesized according to intervention type, experimental model, biological effects, signaling pathways, and organ outcomes, with evidence from isolated or chemically characterized constituents distinguished from that derived from multicomponent preparations. Current evidence, derived predominantly from in vitro and LPS- or CLP-induced animal studies, indicates that S. chinensis constituents may attenuate inflammatory responses, oxidative stress, ferroptosis, endothelial barrier disruption, and sepsis-associated lung and myocardial injury through the TLR4/MyD88/NF-κB, JAK2/STAT3, NLRP3, Nrf2/GPX4, RhoA/ROCK1/MLC and MAPK pathways. However, clinical evidence remains limited and is mainly based on multicomponent traditional Chinese medicine preparations, preventing determination of the independent contribution of S. chinensis. Overall, S. chinensis is a promising but investigational adjunctive candidate for sepsis. Future studies should prioritize chemically standardized preparations, pharmacokinetic and safety characterization, causal validation of reproducible mechanisms, and biomarker-based identification of responsive sepsis phenotypes before early-phase and randomized clinical trials.

articles.title: Dietary Patterns and Chronic Disease Risk: A Proteomic Framework to Strengthen Causal Inference.
articles.abstract: The strength of evidence in nutrition research is hampered by the difficulty of maintaining long-term dietary compliance in randomized trials. Despite providing valuable evidence, short-term feeding trials typically rely on a limited set of surrogate outcomes, and observational studies are susceptible to measurement error and residual confounding.
