This aberrant Ca2+ signal bidirectionally upregulated TGF-β and suppressed Cx43 effects reversible by SOCE inhibition or Orai3 overexpression. Orai3 has been proposed to function as a molecular rheostat that down tunes STIM1 mediated gating when in complex with Orai1, its loss removes this brake, unleashing pathological SOCE. Consequently, Orai3 deficient rats exhibited increased AF susceptibility, with disrupted Cx43 distribution, shortened gap junctions, and impaired STAT3 mediated Cx43 transcription.

CONCLUSIONS: Orai3 acts as an endogenous protective brake against atrial cardiomyopathy. The Orai3-SOCE-TGF-β/Cx43 axis links calcium dyshomeostasis to both fibrotic and electrical remodeling, positioning Orai3 as a potential prognostic biomarker and therapeutic target for AF.

articles.title: Prevalence and diagnostic evaluation of Strongyloides stercoralis infection among the Temiar Orang Asli in Kelantan, Malaysia: A Bayesian latent class analysis using molecular and serological methods.
articles.abstract: Strongyloides stercoralis remains one of the most neglected soil-transmitted helminths because diagnosis is hindered by the lack of a reliable reference standard and the poor sensitivity of conventional parasitological methods. The true burden of infection among Malaysia's Orang Asli communities remains poorly defined. This population-based cross-sectional study determined the prevalence of S. stercoralis infection among 134 Temiar Orang Asli from two villages in Kelantan, Malaysia, and evaluated the diagnostic accuracy of molecular and serological assays using Bayesian latent class analysis (BLCA). Stool specimens were examined by direct microscopy, agar plate culture, Harada-Mori filter paper culture, and real-time PCR targeting the 18S rRNA gene, while plasma was tested using a recombinant NIE-based IgG4 rapid diagnostic test (IgG4-RDT) and the Bordier Strongyloides IgG ELISA. Because no single method was considered a gold standard, BLCA estimated the 'true' prevalence and diagnostic accuracy. Overall, 67.9% of participants had at least one intestinal parasitic infection, with polyparasitism in 38.8%, but no S. stercoralis larvae were detected by conventional methods. Crude positivity rates were 31.1% for IgG4-RDT, 34.8% for ELISA, and 46.2% for PCR. BLCA-estimated prevalence was 22.5% (95% CrI: 12.4-34.0%). The IgG4-RDT demonstrated the highest sensitivity (90.8%) and specificity (86.7%), outperforming ELISA (81.0%, 72.5%) and PCR (77.9%, 77.0%). Posterior predictive checks identified excess PCR-positive/serology-negative results, suggesting biologically meaningful diagnostic discordance. BLCA revealed a hidden burden and showed that the IgG4-RDT had the best diagnostic performance for community screening. Further investigation of PCR-serology discordance using species-specific molecular methods is warranted.

articles.title: Alcohol Exposure Alters Proximodistal Nephron Segmentation During Zebrafish Embryogenesis.
articles.abstract: Fetal alcohol spectrum disorders (FASD) encompass a broad range of effects caused by prenatal alcohol exposure. In the United States, conservative estimates place the incidence of FASD at a rate of 5 in 100 births. Children with FASD can have morphological afflictions including congenital defects of the brain, spinal cord, heart, eyes, and skeleton, as well as poor formation of facial structures such as the nose and mouth. Cognitive and behavioral abnormalities such as learning disabilities, socio-developmental delays and emotional disorders are also highly prevalent. There is no known cure for FASD and in utero detection methods are not available. In terms of urinary tract defects, kidney and renal related maladies may represent underreported aspects of FASD. To better understand the renal phenotypes associated with prenatal alcohol exposure, we employed the zebrafish, Danio rerio, a vertebrate species well suited for developmental nephrology and teratological work that has been used extensively to model FASD. We treated zebrafish embryos with ethanol then examined pattern formation and physiological activity of nephrons, which are the basic structural and functional unit of the kidney. Using whole mount in situ hybridization, we found that the formation of several cell types in the nephron blood filter and tubule, as well as renal progenitor populations, were perturbed by alcohol exposure. Interestingly, supplementation with all-trans retinoic acid, a vitamin A derivative associated with mitigating the effects of ethanol exposure in zebrafish and other animals, was sufficient to completely or partially rescue multiple ethanol induced kidney cell defects and restore nephron physiological activity. These studies have revealed several consequences of ethanol exposure that lead to the deregulation of renal ontogeny, and implicate a key role for reduced RA levels, thereby contributing useful insights relevant to the broader field of FASD research.

articles.title: Porcine Circoviruses in Mainland China: A Nationwide Systematic Review and Meta-analysis of Reported Positivity and Epidemiological Patterns.
articles.abstract: Porcine circoviruses (PCVs) are important viral pathogens affecting swine health and production in China, but national epidemiological evidence remains fragmented. This systematic review and meta-analysis estimated the reported PCV positivity and epidemiological characteristics of PCVs in pigs in mainland China. Six English and Chinese databases were searched from inception to 3 February 2026. Eligible studies reported both the total number of tested pigs or samples and the number positive for PCVs. Random-effects meta-analysis, subgroup analysis, and univariable meta-regression were performed to estimate pooled positivity and explore potential sources of heterogeneity. A total of 389 studies covering 32 provincial-level regions were included. Considerable between-study heterogeneity was observed. Reported positivity varied according to PCV type, diagnostic method, specimen type, pig category, sampling period, and co-detection pattern. Among the established PCV types, pooled positivity was 45.33% for PCV2, 22.37% for PCV3, 16.32% for PCV1, and 9.41% for PCV4. ELISA-based estimates were higher than PCR-based estimates, and fattening pigs showed the highest estimate among the major production stages. PCV2-PRRSV was the most frequently reported co-infection pattern. PCVs remain widely detected in Chinese swine populations, particularly PCV2. Standardized type-specific surveillance, separate reporting of serological and molecular outcomes, and comprehensive studies integrating viral-load, pathological, and sequence data are needed to better define the epidemiological and clinical significance of PCVs and inform evidence-based surveillance and control strategies in China's swine industry.

articles.title: Immunogenicity of recombinant porcine parainfluenza virus 5 expressing the spike protein of porcine epidemic diarrhea virus.
articles.abstract: The porcine epidemic diarrhea virus (PEDV) induces severe diarrhea in neonatal piglets, often resulting in high mortality rates. Consequently, the development of effective and safe vaccines is a critical priority for controlling PEDV infection. Vaccines vectored by the parainfluenza virus 5 (PIV5) exhibit distinct advantages in terms of safety, genomic stability, and immunogenicity. In this study, two novel porcine-origin PIV5 strains (PIV5-HuB and PIV5-DP1-1) were isolated from pigs in China, and their whole-genome sequences and phylogenetic relationships were analyzed. Subsequently, the PIV5-HuB strain, which exhibited superior growth characteristics, was selected for the construction of infectious clones and a reporter virus. Furthermore, the recombinant PIV5 expressing the full-length spike (S) protein of G2a subtype PEDV was developed, and its immunogenicity was evaluated in murine models. Immunization with the recombinant rPIV5-PEDV-S in mice elicited robust PEDV-specific IgG in serum, secretory IgA (sIgA) in bronchoalveolar lavage fluid (BALF), and neutralizing antibody responses against PEDV G2a, G1b, and G2c subtypes. Additionally, the recombinant rPIV5-PEDV-S enhanced PEDV-specific lymphocyte proliferation and increased the proportions of CD3+CD8+ T cells and CD3+CD4+ T cells. This study provides evidence supporting the potential of PIV5 as a vaccine delivery vector for enteric viral diseases in swine.

articles.title: The mechanism of dietary intervention in delaying brain aging and neurodegenerative diseases.
articles.abstract: With the global aging population, age-related neurodegenerative diseases and cerebrovascular diseases have become major public health challenges. As a modifiable lifestyle strategy, dietary intervention shows significant potential in delaying brain aging and reducing the risk of neurodegenerative and cerebrovascular diseases. Caloric restriction (CR) and dietary restriction (DR), two important nutritional intervention approaches, exhibit substantial neuroprotective potential through multiple mechanisms. This review systematically summarizes the mechanisms of CR and DR in brain aging and related diseases, focusing on: (1) modulating gene expression and epigenetic modifications; (2) regulating proteostasis and autophagy; (3) inhibiting neuroinflammation to delay inflammaging; (4) improving mitochondrial function and oxidative homeostasis; and (5) optimizing nutrient-sensing pathways and metabolism. Additionally, this review discusses the mechanistic evidence of CR and DR in disease models such as Alzheimer's Disease (AD), Parkinson's Disease (PD), stroke, and Vascular Dementia (VaD). Despite promising preclinical findings, their clinical translation faces challenges including individual variability, safety concerns, and uncertainty regarding mechanism prioritization. Future research should focus on conducting more high-quality clinical trials, integrating multi-omics technologies with precision nutrition strategies to promote the practical application of CR and DR in advancing healthy brain aging.

articles.title: Chrononutrition in the aging era: Circadian regulation of metabolism, resilience, and healthy longevity.
articles.abstract: The increasing prevalence of obesity, type 2 diabetes, cardiovascular disease, and age-related disorders has been linked to a growing mismatch between modern lifestyles and the biological rhythms that regulate human physiology. Chrononutrition, which explores the interaction between meal timing, circadian rhythms, and metabolism, has emerged as a promising strategy to improve metabolic health and support healthy aging. This review examines the molecular and physiological foundations of chrononutrition, focusing on the interplay between central and peripheral circadian clocks, metabolic regulation, and aging processes. We discuss the role of environmental and behavioural zeitgebers, including light exposure, feeding schedules, sleep, and physical activity, in maintaining circadian alignment and metabolic homeostasis. Attention is given to Time-Restricted Eating (TRE) and related meal-timing interventions. Current evidence indicates that aligning food intake with endogenous circadian rhythms improves insulin sensitivity, metabolic flexibility, lipid metabolism, blood pressure regulation, and inflammatory balance, often independently of weight loss. Mechanistically, chrononutrition may also modulate key biological processes associated with aging, including mitochondrial function, autophagy, nutrient sensing, oxidative stress, and inflammaging. By restoring temporal organization across physiological systems, chrononutrition may enhance metabolic resilience and contribute to healthspan extension. Future studies should clarify its long-term effects on biological aging, resilience, and healthy longevity, while defining personalized interventions based on circadian phenotypes.

articles.title: A centrifuge-free, plate-based protocol to prepare chemically competent Escherichia coli.
articles.abstract: Classical calcium-chloride protocols for Escherichia coli transformation achieve high efficiency but rely on equipment (refrigerated centrifuges, shakers, turbidity control) that is often unavailable in teaching or resource-limited laboratories. We developed a centrifuge-free, plate-based workflow for preparing chemically competent E. coli and systematically optimized its key parameters. On solid LB medium, DH5α reached exponential growth by 2 h post re-streak and remained log-phase until 6 h; harvesting at 2 h yielded the highest competence. Buffer titrations identified 0.25 M CaCl₂ with 15% (v/v) glycerol as optimal. For post-shock outgrowth, SOC consistently outperformed LB and 0.5 × LB. Transformation displayed a DNA-dose dependence: 1-0.1 ng supercoiled plasmid per 100 μL reaction maximized efficiency. The simplified CaCl₂/glycerol buffer produced 105-106 transformants per μg DNA, sufficient for routine cloning. Temperature-dependency experiments revealed that on-ice DNA-cell co-incubation is the only essential low-temperature step; competent cells can be prepared at room temperature and the heat-shock step may be omitted without loss of efficiency. This streamlined protocol reduces equipment and time requirements while delivering reproducible performance, making it well suited for teaching laboratories and other low-resource settings.

articles.title: Cinnamic Acid Attenuates Ethanol-Exacerbated Hepatocyte Pyroptosis in Type 2 Diabetes via AMPK-Mediated NLRP3/GSDMD Inhibition.
articles.abstract: Type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) is frequently accompanied by chronic ethanol (ET) consumption, which worsens metabolic dysregulation and organ damage. Cinnamic acid (CA), a natural compound with anti-diabetic and hepatoprotective effects, shows therapeutic potential, but its role in mitigating ET-exacerbated hepatocyte injury in diabetes remains unclear. This study thus investigated whether CA protects against ET-induced hepatocyte pyroptosis under diabetic conditions and explored the underlying mechanisms. In vitro, HepG2 cells cultured under high-glucose (HG) conditions were exposed to ET to simulate a diabetic state with concomitant alcohol intake. Pyroptosis was evaluated by morphological examination and annexin V/PI staining. The involvement of the NACHT, LRR and PYD domains-containing protein 3 (NLRP3)/gasdermin D (GSDMD) pathway and AMP-activated protein kinase (AMPK) activation was assessed via immunoblotting, reactive oxygen species (ROS) detection, and molecular docking. In vivo, a T2DM mouse model was established using a high-fat diet combined with streptozotocin injection, followed by ET exposure and CA treatment. Metabolic parameters, histopathological changes, and hepatic signaling pathways were analyzed. Our results showed that ET exposure significantly increased pyroptotic body formation, ROS production, and NLRP3/GSDMD pathway activation in HG-treated HepG2 cells-all of which were reversed by CA in a concentration-dependent manner. Mechanistically, CA directly bound to and activated AMPK, and the protective effects were abolished by the AMPK inhibitor Compound C. In T2DM mice, ET exposure aggravated insulin resistance, dyslipidemia, hepatic steatosis, and histopathological abnormalities, whereas CA intervention ameliorated these adverse effects and modulated the AMPK-NLRP3/GSDMD signaling axis in liver tissue. Collectively, these findings demonstrate that CA alleviates ET-exacerbated hepatocyte pyroptosis under diabetic conditions by activating AMPK and subsequently inhibiting the NLRP3/GSDMD signaling cascade. This study provides novel insights into the therapeutic potential of CA in T2DM complicated by alcoholic hepatocellular injury.

articles.title: Author Correction to "Opening Up the Future of Valvular Heart Disease." Canadian Journal of Cardiology. Volume 42, Issue 5, Supplement, May 2026, Pages S59-S67. https://doi.org/10.1016/j.cjca.2025.12.015.
Preoperative Risk-assessment Score for Elective Total Aortic Arch Repair: AAORTA Risk Tool.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Total transverse aortic arch replacement is a complex operation performed to address aortic aneurysm with and without chronic aortic dissection. To predict 90-day survival after this procedure, we created a holistic tool for predicting postoperative mortality in patients who undergo total arch repair (TAR): the Aortic Arch Operation Risk Tool for Assessment (AAORTA) score.

METHODS: Univariate and multivariate analyses were performed on data from patients (N=470; 243 with nondissecting aneurysm, 227 with chronic Type A dissection) who underwent TAR at a high-volume practice between April 2006 and November 2024. Regression analysis identified variables to be used in the AAORTA score. The predictive performance of the score was assessed with the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUROCC), Brier score, and linear fitting.

RESULTS: Of 470 patients who underwent TAR, 65 (13.8%) died within 90 days of repair. The AAORTA score relied on five preoperative variables: heritable thoracic aortic disease, prior coronary artery bypass grafting (CABG), kidney disease, pulmonary disease (restrictive or obstructive), and no history of smoking. Previous CABG was the strongest predictor of 90-day mortality. The AAORTA score had an AUROCC of 0.784, a Brier score of 0.105, and a goodness-of-fit R 2 of 0.954.

CONCLUSION: The AAORTA score can accurately stratify 90-day mortality risk in patients who undergo elective TAR, using only five variables easily acquired during standard preoperative evaluation. This score could be used to aid preoperative counseling with patients and families. Prospective multicenter validation will help establish its generalizability.

articles.title: Consensus on the use of intrathecal gene therapy for spinal muscular atrophy.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Intrathecal (IT) delivery of gene therapy is an emerging strategy for Spinal Muscular Atrophy (SMA), aiming to enhance central nervous system targeting while potentially reducing systemic exposure. The new administration route of Onasemnogene abeparvovec is associated with a distinct safety profile, including dorsal root ganglia toxicity, and requires structured monitoring beyond existing intravenous guidelines, including planning for long-term multidisciplinary follow-up in pediatric and adult care as well as structured transition protocols.

METHODS: We expanded the existing intravenous monitoring guideline by incorporating surveillance for potential dorsal root ganglia-related adverse effects. The protocol integrates clinical, laboratory, electrophysiological, imaging, and long-term follow-up recommendations.

RESULTS: The protocol defines pre-treatment assessment, peri-procedural management, and longitudinal follow-up in both pediatric and adult care settings, with emphasis on proactive evaluation of dorsal root ganglia function and structured transition of adolescents treated before adulthood to specialized multidisciplinary adult neurology services.

CONCLUSIONS: A structured, multimodal monitoring approach-including dorsal root ganglia surveillance, multidisciplinary long-term follow-up, and coordinated transition from pediatric to adult care-is essential for the safe implementation of intrathecal Onasemnogene abeparvovec in SMA.

articles.title: Antithrombotic Therapy in Coronary Embolism: A Multicenter Study.
articles.abstract: Background Coronary embolism (CE) is an uncommon cause of acute myocardial infarction, and the optimal post-discharge antithrombotic strategy remains uncertain. Methods Retrospective multicenter study including patients with definite or probable CE. Three groups of patients were identified: i) requiring with specific management, ii) with atrial fibrillation (AF), and iii) with no indication for oral anticoagulation (OAC). The latter two groups were further classified according to the antithrombotic treatment received, and long-term outcomes (composite of recurrent CE, stroke, systemic embolism, cardiovascular or all cause death and major bleeding at 5 years) were subsequently evaluated Results A total of 489 patients were considered. Among 189 patients with AF, 85 received direct oral anticoagulants (DOAC) and 104 vitamin K antagonists (VKAs). VKA users showed a higher rate of the composite endpoint compared with DOACs (40% vs. 18%, p < 0.001) with the difference primarily driven by all-cause mortality. In multivariable analysis, VKA therapy remained independently associated with worse outcomes (HR 1.9, 95% CI 1.02-3.5; p=0.04). In the 182 patients without an indication for anticoagulation, 115 received antiplatelet therapy and 67 OAC. Those treated with OAC had a higher incidence of the composite outcome (16% vs. 7%, p=0.049) with the difference primarily driven by all-cause mortality. Multivariable analysis confirmed OAC as an independent predictor of adverse prognosis (HR 3.4 (95%CI 1.2-9.7;p=0.02). Conclusions In patients with CE, stratification based on underlying etiology and embolic risk before hospital discharge might serve as a decision-making approach for determining optimal antithrombotic strategies and improved clinical outcomes.

articles.title: Low complication rates are reported in cats presenting for neurological complaints and undergoing cerebrospinal fluid collection.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To assess complications, outcomes, and associated risk factors of cats undergoing CSF collection.

METHODS: This was a single-center retrospective cohort study of client-owned cats presenting to 3 referral hospitals for CSF collection from January 2012 through December 2022. Cats were excluded for nonspecific and/or extraneural presenting complaints. If cats had multiple CSF collection presentations, only the first was included. Records were retrospectively assessed for signalment, physical examination findings, modified Glasgow coma scale, general anesthesia (GA) records, diagnostic imaging, clinical pathology results, and suspected or confirmed final diagnosis. Outcomes included complications and nonsurvival > 24 hours following CSF collection. Univariable logistic regression included breed, sex, body weight, age, modified Glasgow coma scale, evidence of herniation, evidence of intracranial hypertension (ICH) without herniation, GA protocol, GA duration, CSF analysis, collection site, inflammatory/infectious, and neoplasia diagnosis. P values were adjusted for multiple comparisons using the Benjamini-Hochberg procedure.

RESULTS: 120 cats were identified, with 2 excluded for nonspecific and/or extraneural presenting complaint, leaving 118 cats. Seven (5.9%) did not survive > 24 hours following CSF procedure, and 9 (7.6%) reported complications, including apnea, suspected iatrogenic spinal cord trauma, and Cushing reflex. After multiple-comparison correction, no variable was significantly associated with outcome. Evidence of ICH without herniation and nonsurvival reported the largest effect estimate (OR, 36.99). Estimates are imprecise and reported as hypothesis generating.

CONCLUSIONS: Feline CSF collection in this cohort reported low complication rates, and the majority survived > 24 hours after CSF collection.

CLINICAL RELEVANCE: Imaging review for abnormalities associated with ICH is recommended prior to CSF collection.

articles.title: Per-Class Conformal Risk Control for Multi-Label ECG Classification: Achieving Clinically-Justified False Negative Rate Guarantees.
articles.abstract: Automated electrocardiogram (ECG) classifiers require uncertainty procedures that address class-specific clinical risk in intrinsically multi-label data.Approach: We propose per-class risk-controlling prediction sets for multi-label ECG classification. For each diagnostic class, binary false-negative-rate (FNR) loss is calibrated with a one-sided exact-binomial upper confidence bound. The nine disease-specific targets are controlled simultaneously at 95% family-wise confidence using Bonferroni allocation. The final operating threshold is the more inclusive of the exact-binomial threshold and a conservative reference threshold derived from a concentration bound; this safeguard uses calibration data only and cannot weaken the exact guarantee.Main results: We evaluated the method on PTB-XL (21,388 retained recordings) and Chapman-Shaoxing (10,199 retained recordings), using a patient-disjoint PTB-XL split and fitting-partition-only normalisation. The proposed method met all 9/9 prespecified disease-specific FNR targets on held-out test sets and produced non-vacuous simultaneous exact-binomial guarantees for all nine targets; uniform standard conformal prediction met 5/9. Test FNR was 0.0% for myocardial infarction (exact 95% upper bound 0.35%, at 80.3% FPR), 1.0% for ST/T changes, and 0.3% for atrial fibrillation; the high-sensitivity operating point is purchased with substantially reduced specificity. Under PTB-XL-to-Chapman shift, macro class coverage fell from 94.3% to 45.5%, demonstrating that the guarantees do not transport without local recalibration.Significance: Exact-binomial per-class risk control provides a transparent high-sensitivity operating point for ECG triage while making its specificity, prediction-set-size, calibration-support, and exchangeability limitations explicit.&#xD.

articles.title: Second-season observations after prophylaxis in the evaluation of the impact of nirsevimab in Galicia (NIRSE-GAL) study: mechanistic interpretation and implications for respiratory syncytial virus prevention strategy.
articles.abstract: The evaluation of the impact of nirsevimab in Galicia (NIRSE-GAL) study reported that universal infant nirsevimab prophylaxis was associated with a substantial reduction in respiratory syncytial virus-related lower respiratory tract infection hospitalisations in the first season (85·9%; 95% CI 80·2-90·0) and a substantial reduction persisting into the second season (55·3%; 95% CI 22·5-74·3). These effects were accompanied by reductions in recurrent severe outcomes, without evidence of enhanced disease or an age-related severity shift. Although this second-season observation has not yet been replicated in other cohorts and should be interpreted with caution, it raises important mechanistic questions because nirsevimab does not provide sterilising immunity. A key unproven assumption is that children spared severe disease in season one would otherwise have mainly contributed to second-season hospitalisations. If valid, several biological mechanisms would explain the sustained benefit: preservation of lung structure during important developmental windows (ie, lung-sparing), selective protection of high-risk susceptibility endotypes, prevention of severity-driven immune and epigenetic reprogramming, controlled antigen exposure, and a modest pharmacokinetic tail. The absence of enhanced disease after prophylaxis with nirsevimab is reassuring and informs sequencing of current passive and future active strategies. Together, these frameworks outline testable hypotheses for future programme-embedded research and mechanistic studies.

articles.title: [Molecular-Based Diagnostics and Therapy of Metastatic Hormone-Sensitive Prostate Cancer (mHSPC)].
articles.abstract: Metastatic hormone-sensitive prostate cancer (mHSPC) represents a biologically and clinically heterogeneous disease entity. While traditional clinical parameters such as metastatic burden and timing of metastasis remain prognostically relevant, molecular biomarkers are increasingly gaining importance for individualized treatment planning. Genetic alterations in tumor suppressor genes and DNA repair pathways, particularly BRCA, PTEN, and TP53 aberrations, are associated with more aggressive disease courses and poorer prognosis. At the same time, these molecular alterations provide novel therapeutic opportunities, including the use of PARP inhibitors and AKT inhibitors.In addition to genetic alterations, transcriptomic characteristics also play an important role. In particular, androgen receptor (AR) pathway activity influences prognosis and treatment response. Low AR activity and reduced PSMA expression have been associated with reduced sensitivity to hormonal therapies and increased biological heterogeneity. Conversely, high PSMA expression appears to correlate with improved responses to androgen deprivation therapy as well as PSMA-targeted radioligand therapies.Advanced imaging modalities such as PSMA PET imaging further contribute to a refined understanding of metastatic disease biology and increasingly challenge traditional disease classifications. Moreover, biomarkers including PSA nadir or circulating tumor DNA (ctDNA) may help identify progression patterns and guide future treatment intensification or de-escalation strategies.Overall, current evidence suggests that integrating genetic, transcriptomic, and imaging biomarkers may substantially improve the biological characterization of mHSPC. In the future, these approaches could enable a more accurate prognostic stratification and support the development of personalized therapeutic concepts.

articles.title: Endoscopic duodenal injection of autologous stromal vascular fraction in type 2 diabetes: a pilot clinical study of safety, feasibility, and preliminary metabolic effects.
A high-dimensional population code in the bat motor cortex during natural dexterous flight.
articles.abstract: Elucidating the neural computations underlying natural, complex movement remains a fundamental challenge in neuroscience. Bat flight presents a formidable motor control challenge, requiring hand-like wings whose many degrees of freedom must be precisely coordinated to enable rapid three-dimensional (3D) maneuvers. Here, we performed large-scale wireless recordings from the wing motor cortex of freely flying bats, combined with 3D tracking of wing kinematics. Despite the complexity of flight control, bats repeatedly executed accurate flights through precise adjustments of individual wingbeats. Surprisingly, motor cortical activity was not dominated by the wingbeat cycle. Instead, neurons were sparsely active, exhibiting mixed selectivity for flight kinematics and variable entrainment to the wingbeat phase reaching millisecond-scale precision. This yielded a high-dimensional population code driven by successive wingbeats occupying distinct neural states. These findings reveal a mode of motor cortical population dynamics expressed during natural dexterous movement that is not well captured by prevailing views derived from constrained paradigms.

articles.title: The chytrid fungus threatens the last epidemiologically naive Neotropical montane amphibian biodiversity hotspot.
articles.abstract: The amphibian chytrid fungus Batrachochytrium dendrobatidis (B. dendrobatidis) has caused catastrophic biodiversity loss worldwide.1,2,3 Although B. dendrobatidis is now widespread across environmentally suitable regions,4 the absence of amphibian declines in some high-suitability areas suggests the existence of refuges supporting epidemiologically naive communities. Epidemiologically naive refuges have not experienced past B. dendrobatidis epizootics despite suitable environmental conditions and may be B. dendrobatidis-free, harbor less virulent B. dendrobatidis lineages, or contain resistant host communities. As eradication of virulent B. dendrobatidis lineages is rarely successful after establishment, identifying epidemiologically naive refuges is imperative.5,6 Here, following extensive multi-year disease surveillance, we report a major epidemiologically naive refuge in the Neotropical highlands, the Sierra Nevada de Santa Marta (SNSM) in northern Colombia. We found no evidence for contemporary B. dendrobatidis presence, despite detecting the hypervirulent Global Panzootic Lineage in a neighboring Andean mountain range. Population genomic analyses in SNSM-endemic harlequin toads found no demographic signatures indicative of cryptic epizootic decline. Niche modeling predicted high suitability for B. dendrobatidis occurrence and B. dendrobatidis-induced declines throughout the SNSM, with climatic conditions in lowland regions surrounding the SNSM likely acting as a dispersal barrier and preventing B. dendrobatidis invasion, creating a "sky island." Infection trials using three SNSM-endemic amphibian species revealed tolerant and susceptible species. Together, our results indicate that the SNSM is an epidemiologically naive refuge at risk of invasion by hypervirulent B. dendrobatidis, which could result in the loss of 25 endemic amphibian species. We highlight the urgent need for proactive conservation action and the strict implementation of biosecurity to safeguard the unique and vast amphibian diversity of the SNSM.

articles.title: Reverse transcribed ssDNA derepresses translation of a retron antiviral protein.
articles.abstract: Retrons are bacterial immune systems that prevent phage propagation by initiating a toxic response within infected hosts. Previously characterized retrons produce abundant multicopy single-stranded DNA (msDNA) by reverse transcription, which acts as an antitoxin in the absence of phage. However, we describe here a non-canonical mechanism for type VI retrons, which do not produce detectable msDNA in the absence of phage yet still provide defense. Focusing on Retron-Vpa2 from V. parahaemolyticus, we show broad defense against phages and identify triggers of the system when expressed in E. coli. Within the retron operon, we find a highly enriched, structured transcript that we term a hybrid RNA (hyRNA). The hyRNA contains the reverse transcription template and a toxin coding sequence that is repressed by a riboregulator. In our model of triggering, phage infection induces accumulation of msDNA, which hybridizes to the riboregulator and enables RNase H cleavage, derepressing translation of the toxin.

articles.title: Case of Bundibugyo Virus Disease in Goma, Democratic Republic of the Congo with Lack of Transmission to Breastfeeding Infant.
articles.journal: The American journal of tropical medicine and hygiene
articles.abstract: Disease due to Bundibugyo virus (BDBV), an Orthoebolavirus species, reemerged in April 2026, in Ituri Province, Democratic Republic of the Congo. A 35-year-old woman transported the body of a possible BDBV-infected patient from Bunia in Ituri Province to Goma for burial; she was accompanied by an 8-month-old breastfeeding child. Six days after arrival in Goma, she noted onset of fever and malaise and was empirically started on therapy for malaria; 4 days later she developed bloody diarrhea and a bloody vaginal discharge and was started on metronidazole for possible amebic dysentery. When her condition worsened she was admitted to hospital in Goma, where a blood sample was positive by real-time polymerase chain reaction (RT-PCR) test for BDBV, with a second positive test on hospital day 7. By day 14 of hospitalization fever and major symptoms had resolved and repeat RT-PCR tests × 2 were negative. Her child did not show evidence of infection, and no family members or health care workers at HEAL Africa Hospital developed illness.

articles.title: Disseminated Histoplasmosis Presenting as Mucocutaneous Lesions in an Immunocompetent Patient.
articles.journal: The American journal of tropical medicine and hygiene
articles.abstract: A case of an immunocompetent male patient in his 50s, an oil field worker from the northeastern part of India who presented with fever, weight loss over 4 months, and multiple umbilicated papulonodular lesions on his face and nodular lesions over the hard palate, is reported. The initial suspicion was talaromycosis, which is endemic in that part of the country. Periodic acid-Schiff and Grocott-Gomori's methenamine silver staining of the skin biopsy specimen from the forehead revealed numerous yeast-like bodies morphologically resembling Histoplasma within the histiocytes. A culture of the skin biopsy grew Histoplasma capsulatum. The patient received liposomal amphotericin B (3 mg/kg/day) but later was shifted to oral itraconazole because of acute kidney injury. The patient exhibited improvement, with flattening of skin lesions and no development of new lesions during treatment. This case highlights histoplasmosis mimicking talaromycosis and the importance of tissue diagnosis for accurate identification.

articles.title: Outcomes in Patients with Tuberculous Meningitis: A Prospective Cohort Study in North India.
articles.journal: The American journal of tropical medicine and hygiene
articles.abstract: Tuberculous meningitis (TBM) is the most severe form of extrapulmonary tuberculosis, carrying the highest mortality among all forms. This multicentric prospective cohort study conducted in North India aimed to determine the incidence of complications, functional outcome (modified Rankin scale [mRS]), and mortality in TBM. Patients 12 years old and older with TBM were followed up until completion of 9 months of antitubercular treatment. Patients with concomitant HIV infection, other infections causing meningitis, or multidrug-resistant tuberculosis were excluded. The primary outcome was mRS at 9 months. Secondary outcomes included mRS at 6 months, poor mRS (>2), Barthel Index, and mortality at 6 and 9 months. Between October 1, 2019 and March 31, 2024, 585 eligible patients were enrolled, of whom 495 (84.6%) completed follow-up. The median age was 24.0 years old, and the majority were female (n = 304/495; 61.4%). Complications were present in 377 patients (76.2%): focal neurological deficits (41.6%), seizures (38.6%), immune reconstitution inflammatory syndrome (32.7%), hydrocephalus (24.8%), and drug-induced liver injury (14.1%). Complications were associated with worse mRS on unadjusted analysis (odds ratio [OR]: 2.5 [1.7-3.7]; P <0.001); however, this association was no longer statistically significant after adjustment for age, sex, baseline mRS, study center, and disease stage and category (OR: 1.3 [0.8-2.0]; P = 0.30). The median mRS improved from 4.0 at presentation to 2.0 at 6 months and 1.0 at 9 months. Death occurred at a median of 91.0 days after presentation. Mortality at 6 months was 9.3% and at 9 months was 10.7%.

articles.title: Increased Insulin Resistance after Praziquantel Treatment in Human Opisthorchiasis.
articles.journal: The American journal of tropical medicine and hygiene
articles.abstract: Opisthorchiasis caused by Opisthorchis viverrini is a significant public health problem in northeast Thailand, a region where the prevalence of type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) substantially exceeds the national average. Although recent evidence suggests that hyperglycemia may occur after praziquantel (PZQ) treatment, the underlying mechanisms remain poorly understood. We conducted a prospective 12-month follow-up study of 110 O. viverrini-infected patients receiving PZQ treatment, assessing fasting plasma glucose (FPG), oral glucose tolerance test (OGTT), and fasting serum insulin (FSI) at baseline and 12 months posttreatment. Praziquantel treatment was associated with significant increases in FPG (87.4 ± 1.0 versus 92.4 ± 1.7 mg/dL; P = 0.010), FSI (9.6 ± 0.7 versus 13.4 ± 1.1 µU/mL; P = 0.003), and homeostatic model assessment of insulin resistance (HOMA-IR; 2.2 ± 0.2 versus 3.0 ± 0.3; P = 0.001) at 12 months, whereas OGTT values did not differ significantly (P = 0.790). General linear model analysis identified age 50 years old and older and baseline obesity as significant factors associated with elevated FPG, whereas female sex, alcohol consumption, and baseline obesity correlated with higher OGTT values. Interestingly, HOMA-IR was significantly associated with underweight status at both baseline and follow-up. These findings suggest that O. viverrini eradication by PZQ increases insulin resistance in opisthorchiasis patients, potentially elevating T2DM risk. This effect likely reflects the loss of helminth-induced immunomodulation after parasite clearance, which is potentially compounded by improved appetite and increased food consumption after treatment, suggesting that metabolic surveillance should be integrated into liver fluke control programs.

articles.title: Viral deISGylation holds the key to the metabolic kingdom.
articles.abstract: The interferon-induced modification of cellular and viral proteins by ISG15 inhibits viral infection and is reversed by virus-encoded deISGylases, but the broad physiological impacts of this host-pathogen clash remain unclear. In this issue of Immunity, Zhu et al. reveal that ISG15 modification broadly restricts key metabolic pathways that deISGylation relieves to promote viral replication.

articles.title: Central line-associated bloodstream infections outside the intensive care unit: Burden, pathogens, and antimicrobial susceptibility identified through a Victorian surveillance program.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Prevention of central line-associated bloodstream infection (CLABSI) is a priority in Australian intensive care units (ICUs). However, the epidemiology of CLABSI in non-ICU settings remains inadequately characterised, despite extensive use of central lines beyond the ICU. We aimed to determine CLABSI rates and microbiological aetiology in non-ICU wards and to compare these with corresponding ICU data from Victorian hospitals.

METHODS: CLABSI surveillance was undertaken voluntarily in non-ICU wards by Victorian health services between 2014 and 2025, utilising the Victorian Healthcare Associated Infection Surveillance System (VICNISS) CLABSI surveillance module, capturing CLABSI rates per 1000 central line days (CLD) as well as bloodstream infections related to mucosal barrier injury (MBI-BSI), in accordance with CDC/NHSN criteria. Retrospective analysis was performed to determine rates, pathogens, and antimicrobial susceptibility.

RESULTS: Sixteen facilities participated in surveillance during the study period. 67 CLABSI events and 66,096 central line days were reported in non-ICU wards (predominantly haematology-oncology), corresponding to a CLABSI rate of 1.01 per 1000 CLD, which was significantly higher than the contemporaneous ICU CLABSI rate of 0.50 per 1000 CLD (IRR 3.13, 95% CI 1.88-5.22, p = 0.000). The most frequent pathogens responsible for non-ICU CLABSI were coagulase-negative Staphylococcus spp., Staphylococcus aureus, and Pseudomonas spp. A large burden of MBI-BSI events (n = 90) were also reported.

CONCLUSIONS: CLABSI rates outside ICU are significantly higher than those reported in ICU settings. A substantial burden of CLABSI and MBI-BSI events were identified in haematology-oncology populations, supporting focused surveillance and infection prevention efforts in these high-risk cohorts.

articles.title: An Epi(c) Path to LMNA Cardiomyopathy.
Algorithmic Guardrails for Echocardiography AI: Deep Feature Representations for Error Slicing and Selective LVEF Estimation.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Automated echocardiography analysis using artificial intelligence (AI) currently lacks effective guardrails or oversight mechanisms to ensure its safe and reliable deployment.

OBJECTIVES: This study investigated whether deep feature representations can identify echocardiograms at risk of misinterpretation by echocardiography AI-based left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF) estimation models.

METHODS: We retrospectively validated 2 state-of-the-art models for LVEF estimation, EchoNet (single-task model) and PanEcho (multitask foundation model), on 4,010 apical-4-chamber videos from 1,353 studies (n = 1,208) with biplane LVEF measurements in the MIMIC-IV-ECHO database (2017-2019). We extracted 4 deep feature representations from a view classifier, a left ventricle segmentation model, and the 2 validated LVEF estimation models. These features were evaluated for their ability to identify systematic misinterpretations (error slicing) and automatically exclude AI estimates for high-risk inputs (selective estimation).

RESULTS: While PanEcho performed better relative to EchoNet (EchoNet minus PanEcho [Δ], Δmean absolute error: 0.31 [0.07, 0.55]; ΔR2: -0.07 [-0.11, -0.03]), both models systematically overestimated LVEF at lower values (proportional bias slope, EchoNet: -0.33 [-0.39, -0.28], P < 0.001, PanEcho: -0.31 [-0.36, -0.26], P < 0.001). All investigated deep feature representations identified error slices for both models. Shared error slices between the models revealed 2 common failure modes: contrast-enhanced echocardiograms and poor-quality apical-4-chamber views. Selective estimation using intermediate features from EchoNet achieved the best performance across both estimation models (area under risk-coverage curve, EchoNet: 5.04 [4.45, 5.66]; PanEcho: 5.21 [4.54, 5.92]).

CONCLUSIONS: Deep feature representations can be leveraged to identify and automatically flag misinterpretation-prone echocardiograms, enabling promising guardrail mechanisms for the reliable deployment of echocardiography AI.

articles.title: Enhanced Early Risk Stratification in Cardiogenic Shock Using Machine Learning: A Hierarchical Clustering Analysis.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Cardiogenic shock (CS) exhibits marked clinical heterogeneity, limiting the performance of conventional risk stratification tools like the Society for Cardiovascular Angiography and Interventions (SCAI) staging system. Machine learning (ML) has identified reproducible CS phenotypes that improve risk prediction, but their temporal consistency across the progression of shock remains incompletely described.

OBJECTIVES: The purpose of this study was to evaluate the temporal evolution of ML-derived CS phenotypes across the first 3 intensive care unit (ICU) days and determine whether phenotype trajectories enhance mortality stratification beyond SCAI staging.

METHODS: In a multicenter retrospective registry of 2,906 adults with CS admitted to ICUs between 2016 and 2022, hierarchical agglomerative clustering was applied independently to clinical variables on ICU days 1, 2, and 3.

RESULTS: On day 1, 3 phenotypes emerged: Cardiac (younger, acute myocardial infarction-predominant, preserved renal function; 15% mortality), Cardio-Renal (older, non-acute myocardial infarction-predominant, isolated renal extracardiac impairment, predominantly SCAI A and B on admission; 27% mortality), and Cardio-Metabolic (severe renal and tissue malperfusion, predominantly SCAI D and E on admission; 55% mortality). Similar phenotypes persisted on day 2 and day 3. These ML-derived phenotypes enhanced mortality stratification within each SCAI stage across days 1 to 3.

CONCLUSIONS: Hierarchical clustering reproduced previously identified CS phenotypes that were consistent across the first 3 days of ICU stay, providing an enhanced framework for early risk stratification. Prospective validation is required for clinical implementation.

articles.title: Associations of Physical Activity and Diet Quality With Mortality and Cardiovascular Disease in Cardiovascular-Kidney-Metabolic Syndrome.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Physical activity (PA) and diet are cornerstones for cardiovascular disease (CVD) prevention, yet their associations with CVD within the cardiovascular-kidney-metabolic (CKM) framework remain unexplored.

OBJECTIVES: This study aims to evaluate the independent and joint associations of PA and/or diet quality with mortality and incident CVD across CKM stages.

METHODS: Our study included 339,074 UK Biobank participants (51.3% women, mean age 56.4 years) with CKM syndrome stage 0 to 4. PA was categorized as high (≥150 min/wk of walking or moderate-to-vigorous activity) or low using self-reported and accelerometer-measured data. Diet quality was classified as low/median/high. Cox proportional hazards models assessed associations with incident CVD, cause-specific CVD mortality, and all-cause mortality across CKM stages.

RESULTS: High PA was associated with lower risks of all-cause mortality (HR: 0.76 [95% CI: 0.74-0.79]), composite CVD mortality (0.74 [0.70-0.77]), and incident composite CVD (0.90 [0.88-0.92]); for high diet quality, corresponding HRs (95% CIs) were 0.81 (0.77-0.85), 0.81 (0.75-0.88), and 0.87 (0.84-0.90). PA showed nonlinear associations with these outcomes, plateauing at approximately 2,500 metabolic equivalent min/wk. High PA combined with high diet quality showed stronger inverse associations with all-cause mortality (0.64 [0.60-0.68]), composite CVD mortality (0.61 [0.54-0.68]), and incident composite CVD (0.83 [0.79-0.88]). Significant multiplicative interactions between PA and diet quality were observed for stroke mortality, composite CVD, and heart failure. The joint associations with these outcomes were stronger at more advanced CKM syndrome stages.

CONCLUSIONS: Beyond individual benefits, joint PA-diet modification was associated with lower risk of mortality and CVD across CKM stages, highlighting the value of integrated behavioral strategies.

articles.title: Electrophysiologic Phenotype Outperforms Left Ventricular Ejection Fraction for Mortality Prediction in Immune Checkpoint Inhibitor Myocarditis.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Immune checkpoint inhibitor (ICI)-associated myocarditis carries mortality rates approaching 50%. Risk stratification relies heavily on left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF), yet many fatal cases occur despite preserved systolic function.

OBJECTIVES: The study aims to compare the prognostic value of electrophysiologic involvement vs LVEF in ICI-associated myocarditis.

METHODS: We systematically searched PubMed for ICI-associated myocarditis cases with extractable patient-level data. Electrophysiologic phenotype (EP) was defined by clinically significant conduction disease or ventricular arrhythmia, including high-grade atrioventricular block, ventricular tachycardia, ventricular fibrillation, or cardiac arrest. LVEF was dichotomized at ≤35%. Cluster-robust logistic regression was used to assess associations with mortality.

RESULTS: From 242 publications, 319 cases were extracted; 180 with complete data comprised the analytical cohort (77 deaths; 42.8% mortality). EP involvement (66.7% of cases) was associated with significantly higher mortality vs EP-negative cases (55.0% vs 18.3%; risk ratio: 3.00; 95% CI: 1.72-5.24; P < 0.001). LVEF ≤35% was not significantly associated with mortality (50.7% vs 38.1%; P = 0.125). Among patients with an LVEF >35%, EP involvement was associated with markedly higher mortality (55.1% vs 11.4%; P < 0.001). In adjusted models, EP remained associated with mortality on both the odds-ratio scale (OR: 5.27; 95% CI: 2.29-12.13; P < 0.001) and risk-ratio scale (RR: 2.94; 95% CI: 1.54-5.59; P < 0.001), whereas LVEF ≤35% was not independently associated with mortality.

CONCLUSIONS: Electrophysiologic involvement is a dominant prognostic marker in ICI-associated myocarditis, particularly for risk stratification among patients with an LVEF >35%. Risk stratification should prioritize cardiac rhythm monitoring and identification of conduction abnormalities over reliance on LVEF alone.

articles.title: Machine Learning of Echocardiographic Left Ventricular Myocardial Radiomics for Identification of Transthyretin Amyloid Cardiomyopathy.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Transthyretin amyloid cardiomyopathy (ATTR-CM) is an important cause of heart failure (HF) with increased left ventricular (LV) wall thickness that can be challenging to distinguish from other LV hypertrophic processes. Echocardiographic myocardial radiomic texture analysis may identify imperceptible amyloid-induced structural changes.

OBJECTIVES: The study aims to develop and validate an echocardiography-based machine learning model using myocardial radiomics to identify ATTR-CM.

METHODS: In this retrospective and prospective multicenter study, 854 echocardiographic scans were analyzed. Conventional and novel radiomic features were extracted from parasternal short-axis views at basal, mid, and apical LV levels, with incorporated age and sex from echocardiogram metadata. A machine learning pipeline was developed using a balanced training set (150 ATTR-CM, 150 nonamyloid HF). Performance was evaluated on an independent internal validation set (50 ATTR-CM, 399 nonamyloid HF) and an external validation set (10 ATTR-CM, 10 immunoglobulin light-chain-amyloid, 10 hypertrophic cardiomyopathy, 75 nonamyloid HF).

RESULTS: In internal validation, the model achieved 86% sensitivity (95% CI: 73.8%-93%), 92% specificity (95% CI: 88.9%-94.3%), 57.3% positive predictive value (95% CI: 46.1%-67.9%), 98.1% negative predictive value (NPV) (95% CI: 96.2%-99.1%), and receiver operating characteristic-area under the curve 0.938 (95% CI: 0.891-0.985). Performance was consistent in the external validation (100% sensitivity, 78.9% specificity, 33.3% positive predictive value, 100% NPV, and receiver operating characteristic-area under the curve of 0.917). The model correctly classified 77.3% of nonamyloid HF, 70% of AL-amyloid cases, and 100% of hypertrophic cardiomyopathy cases as non-ATTR in subgroup analysis.

CONCLUSIONS: We developed an echocardiographic radiomics-based tool to identify ATTR-CM with excellent discrimination and very high NPV in a cohort that approximates clinical experience. These preliminary findings require validation in larger, more diverse cohorts.

articles.title: Risk factors and preventive strategies for pressure injury and medical device-related pressure injury in ICU patients receiving invasive mechanical ventilation: A scoping review.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: Adult ICU patients receiving invasive mechanical ventilation (IMV) are at risk of pressure injury (PI) and medical device-related pressure injury (MDRPI) due to immobility, impaired perfusion, and device contact. This scoping review synthesized evidence on PI and MDRPI risk factors and preventive strategies.

METHODS: This scoping review followed the Arksey and O'Malley framework and PRISMA-ScR guidelines. Five databases (PubMed, CINAHL, Scopus, MEDLINE, ScienceDirect) were searched from inception to April 2026. Studies of adult ICU patients receiving IMV reporting PI, MDRPI, risk factors, or preventive strategies were eligible.

RESULTS: Forty-two studies from 14 countries (2009-2026) were included. PI incidence ranged from 10.3 to 36.3% (up to 88.7% when prone-positioned); MDRPI (oral mucosal injury) ranged from 25.9 to 43.1% (80.1% with a broader erythema criterion). Cutaneous PI mainly affected the sacrum, heels, occiput, face, and thorax (generally Stage 1-2); oral mucosal MDRPI, assessed using heterogeneous severity criteria, was typically mild-to-moderate. Onset was commonly reported on days 3-9. PI risk factors included immobility, impaired perfusion, vasopressor therapy, and poor nutrition; MDRPI risk factors involved prolonged intubation and device exposure. Preventive strategies included device repositioning, securement adjustment, device-contact protection, and oral care.

CONCLUSIONS: Prolonged mechanical loading and reduced tissue tolerance are intensified by immobility, sedation, hemodynamic instability, impaired perfusion, vasopressor use, and device exposure. Early-stage cutaneous PI and mild-to-moderate mucosal MDRPI were more commonly reported than severe cutaneous and mucosal injuries; given the descriptive, non-comparative evidence, this cannot be attributed to preventive effectiveness. Early monitoring may be important for detecting early-stage injury and identifying progression toward more severe injury.

IMPLICATIONS FOR CLINICAL PRACTICE: Prevention should combine pressure redistribution with tolerance-based repositioning, skin monitoring, device securement, device-contact protection, and oral mucosal care. An exploratory, hypothesis-generating observation is that the first 10 days of ICU stay may be a high-risk period, requiring prospective validation.

articles.title: Predicting acute kidney injury in type B aortic dissection: development and validation of a clinical nomogram.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: Acute Kidney Injury (AKI) is a frequent and serious complication in patients with Type B Aortic Dissection (TBAD). Existing prediction models are mainly derived from type A or mixed cohorts and do not account for the distinct pathophysiology of TBAD. This study aimed to develop and validate a nomogram for individualized AKI risk prediction in TBAD patients.

METHODS: Data were obtained from the eICU Collaborative Research Database (eICU-CRD) and the Medical Information Mart for Intensive Care IV (MIMIC-IV). The eICU-CRD cohort was used for model development and internal validation, while MIMIC-IV served for external validation. A three-step variable selection strategy combining Least Absolute Shrinkage and Selection Operator (LASSO), univariate, and multivariate logistic regression analyses was applied. Model performance was evaluated using the Area Under the receiver operating characteristic Curve (AUC), calibration curves, and Decision Curve Analysis (DCA).

RESULTS: Six independent predictors were identified: ICU length of stay, minimum glucose, minimum sodium, maximum bicarbonate, minimum creatinine, and minimum diastolic blood pressure. The nomogram showed excellent discrimination, with AUCs of 0.926 (95% CI: 0.893-0.956), 0.922 (95% CI: 0.869-0.967), and 0.921 (95% CI: 0.895-0.944) in the training, internal validation, and external validation cohorts, respectively. Calibration analysis demonstrated good agreement, and DCA indicated clinical utility within a threshold probability range of 0-70%.

CONCLUSIONS: This study developed a practical nomogram based on six readily available variables for dynamic in-hospital prediction of AKI in TBAD patients. The model may assist early risk stratification, although further prospective validation is warranted.

articles.title: Navigating Infection Control and Dialysis Delivery in Nursing Homes: Organizational Perspectives From 2020 to 2025.
articles.journal: Journal of the American Medical Directors Association
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: Nursing home (NH) residents with end-stage kidney disease requiring thrice-weekly hemodialysis faced challenges during the COVID-19 pandemic, as infection control imperatives conflicted with access to life-sustaining care. This study examines how NHs and dialysis organizations navigated dialysis care for NH residents from 2020 to 2025, exploring how pandemic-era adaptations continue to shape care delivery.

DESIGN: Descriptive qualitative study that synthesized interview data from the qualitative arms of three mixed-methods studies conducted between 2020 and 2025.

SETTING AND PARTICIPANTS: Participants included NH administrators, clinical staff, and residents, as well as Medicare Advantage plan executives, kidney care management company leadership, and dialysis organization administrative leadership and staff across diverse US health care markets.

METHODS: Semistructured interviews were conducted. Interview transcript coding used a modified grounded theory approach. Theme and subtheme development used thematic and content analysis.

RESULTS: Three hundred nine interviews were conducted with representatives from 66 NHs, 8 Medicare Advantage plans, 5 kidney care management companies, and 6 dialysis organizations. Three themes were identified, reflecting varied perspectives on the impact of the COVID-19 pandemic on dialysis care for NH residents. First, during the pandemic, NHs and dialysis centers prioritized infection mitigation through spatial distancing, cohorting, extended quarantine protocols, and reduced admissions of residents requiring dialysis. Second, NH residents experienced significant barriers to dialysis access, including transportation and schedule disruptions. Third, the pandemic continues to affect dialysis care for this population: although infection control practices have become routine, transportation challenges remain unresolved, and many NHs have reduced admissions of dialysis-dependent residents, threatening access for this vulnerable population.

CONCLUSIONS AND IMPLICATIONS: Although the COVID-19 pandemic prompted more rigorous infection control practices at NHs and dialysis centers, it also intensified longstanding vulnerabilities in cross-sector health care coordination for NH residents requiring dialysis. Insights from this study's findings could inform efforts to design more resilient, better coordinated models of care.

articles.title: Chaperoning post-thaw cryo-competence: HSP90 abundance as a molecular signature of sperm quality, oxidative status, cellular integrity, and fertility potential in Indonesian dairy bulls.
articles.abstract: Improving reproductive efficiency in dairy cattle is critical for sustainable artificial insemination (AI)-based breeding systems in Indonesia. Variability in semen freezability and the limited predictive value of conventional sperm assessments remain challenges for fertility evaluation. This study investigated Heat Shock Protein 90 (HSP90) as a molecular marker associated with sperm cryotolerance and fertility in Indonesian Holstein-Friesian bulls. Cryopreserved semen from 20 bulls was classified into good freezability (GF) and poor freezability (PF) groups based on post-thaw sperm plasma membrane integrity, determined using SYBR-14/propidium iodide (PI) double staining and flow cytometry. Sperm quality, oxidative stress markers (malondialdehyde, MDA; aspartate aminotransferase, AST), HSP90 mRNA and protein abundance, and field fertility (first-service conception rate) were evaluated. GF bulls exhibited higher HSP90 mRNA (0.068 ± 0.003 vs. 0.018 ± 0.003) and protein abundance (0.72 ± 0.02 vs. 0.41 ± 0.02 ng/mL), together with improved motility, kinematic parameters, acrosome integrity, and mitochondrial membrane potential and fewer sperm abnormalities than PF bulls (P < 0.05). PF bulls showed higher MDA and AST levels (P < 0.05). HSP90 expression was strongly correlated with fertility rate (r = 0.964 for mRNA; r = 0.945 for protein) and sperm functional parameters (r ≈ 0.95-0.99), while negative correlations were observed with MDA, AST, and sperm defects (r ≈ -0.92 to -0.98). Multivariable regression models were highly significant (P < 0.001), with post-thaw sperm quality and fertility-related parameters collectively explaining 98.4% and 99.2% of the variation in HSP90 mRNA and protein expression, respectively. Overall, HSP90 abundance was strongly associated with post-thaw sperm quality, biochemical indicators of cellular damage, and field fertility, supporting its potential as a candidate molecular biomarker for evaluating post-thaw sperm quality and reproductive performance in Indonesian dairy bulls. Further validation using paired pre-freezing and post-thaw assessments is needed to determine whether HSP90 abundance is associated with the preservation of sperm quality during cryopreservation.

articles.title: 12-week yoga intervention effect on metabolome in Polyendocrine Metabolic Ovarian Syndrome (PMOS): An LC-MS-based study.
articles.journal: Journal of Ayurveda and integrative medicine
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Polyendocrine metabolic ovarian syndrome (PMOS) is a complex, heterogeneous disorder affecting endocrine, reproductive, and metabolic health. It is fundamentally a systemic metabolic defect that, if not addressed in time, can compromise the function of multiple systems, resulting in conditions such as impaired glucose tolerance, insulin resistance, cardiovascular disease, dyslipidemia, fatty liver disease, and type 2 diabetes mellitus. It is a lifestyle disorder with long-term health implications, requiring a holistic approach for management.

METHODS: This prospective quasi-experimental study involved 60 women (30 diagnosed with PMOS, 30 age and BMI-matched controls). Women with PMOS underwent a 12-week Yoga practice that included physical postures (Asanas), regulated breathing practice (Pranayama), and meditation (Dhyana) under the guidance of a trained therapist. Clinical characteristics and laboratory biochemical data were recorded, followed by an untargeted metabolomics analysis using high-resolution Orbitrap Fusion Tribrid Mass Spectrometer technology to study plasma metabolome changes.

RESULTS: Following Yoga intervention, women with PMOS showed significant improvements in hormonal, anthropometric parameters, and lipid profile. The metabolomics analysis showed that post-Yoga intervention, several key metabolites were significantly downregulated, including glucose, fructose, d-ribose, 3-hydroxybutanoate, taurine, and methylmalonate. However, metabolites like succinate and ascorbate were upregulated. Besides, AUC suggests significant metabolic shifts following Yoga intervention.

CONCLUSION: Yoga offers a holistic, integrated mind-body approach to managing the endocrine, metabolic, and reproductive dysfunction in PMOS and lowers the risk of developing long-term comorbidities.

articles.title: LAP inhibits the clearance of Staphylococcus aureus by neutrophils and suppressed excessive inflammatory responses in mice.
articles.abstract: Staphylococcus aureus (S. aureus) is a major cause of acute pneumonia, which leads to various complications, including lung abscess, respiratory distress syndrome, and myocarditis. With the rapid development of drug resistance, it is urgent to find new strategies for the treatment of S. aureus infectious diseases. The LC3-associated phagocytosis (LAP) has been reported to play a defensive role in various bacterial infections. However, certain pathogens have evolved strategies to resist LAP and even utilize the LAP effect exerted by the host for bacterial reproduction. In this article, we demonstrated that during the acute pulmonary infection caused by S. aureus, the LAP function is detrimental to the host's ability to eliminate the bacteria. LAP hinders the bactericidal effect of neutrophils by inhibiting the production of ROS, the secretion of NO, and the degranulation of cells. However, LAP helps to control the excessive inflammation in the host. The LAP effects of neutrophils and macrophages inhibit the inflammatory response through the MAPK and NF-κB pathways. These data suggest that targeting LAP may become a promising new treatment for S. aureus infections.

articles.title: Medication adherence and health-related quality of life among patients with heart failure: a cross-sectional study.
articles.journal: Heart & lung : the journal of critical care
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Heart failure (HF) continues to be a significant public health concern. Adherence to guideline-directed medical therapy (GDMT) is essential for improving clinical outcomes and quality of life (QoL) in these patients.

OBJECTIVES: This study aimed to evaluate how well patients with chronic HF adhere to GDMT and to assess their health-related QoL.

METHODS: This cross-sectional study was conducted using data collected between March and May 2025. Eligible participants were adult outpatients with a confirmed diagnosis of HF who were able to complete the study questionnaires. Medication adherence was assessed using the 8-item Morisky Medication Adherence Scale (MMAS-8), while health-related QoL was evaluated with the Minnesota Living with Heart Failure Questionnaire. Data were analyzed using SPSS version 25, with statistical significance set at p < 0.05.

RESULTS: Among 300 HF patients (64.7% male; median age of 63), sixty-nine percent had reduced ejection fraction (median EF 30%), with 62.4% classified as NYHA III or IV. Medication adherence was low in 25%, moderate in 44.6%, and high in 30.3%. Patients with more severe HF symptoms (higher NYHA class) reported significantly lower QoL, while higher adherence correlated significantly with better QoL. Older patients had a lower risk of low adherence, while intracardiac devices were linked to a higher risk.

CONCLUSION: Despite GDMT's critical role in HF management, a notable proportion of patients demonstrated low adherence, which was associated with diminished QoL. Special attention and targeted interventions for high-risk groups, particularly patients with intracardiac devices, are imperative for enhancing outcomes.

articles.title: Curcumin-loaded silk fibroin nanoparticle-stabilized pickering emulsions for co-delivery of resveratrol: Synergistic efficacy in strawberry preservation.
articles.abstract: Strawberries are nutrient-dense and economically vital fruits with extremely high perishability. They frequently suffer from postharvest losses and safety hazards due to their thin epidermis, active metabolism, and susceptibility to microbial infection. Conventional preservation strategies including refrigeration, chemical fungicides and polymer coatings suffer from chilling injury, health risks and high costs. Herein, we developed a novel Pickering emulsion stabilized by curcumin-loaded silk fibroin nanoparticles (Cur-SF NPs) for the co-delivery of resveratrol (Res) to synergistically enhance strawberry preservation. Formulated via a facile eco-friendly route, Cur-SF NPs serve as bifunctional stabilizers to enhance emulsion stability as well as solubility and stability of Res. Physicochemical characterization, antioxidant assays, and microbial tests verified the emulsion's favorable properties, revealing enhanced antioxidant activity and broad-spectrum antibacterial efficacy against Aspergillus niger and Escherichia coli. Integrated into chitosan edible coating, the emulsion effectively reduced strawberry weight loss, maintained firmness and inhibited spoilage. This green, sustainable strategy presents a highly viable approach for the postharvest preservation of soft fruits.

articles.title: UBA6 confers neuroprotection against sepsis-associated encephalopathy through facilitating LCN2 ubiquitin-dependent degradation.
articles.abstract: Sepsis-associated encephalopathy (SAE) is a common secondary complication of sepsis, accompanied by neuroinflammation and neuronal apoptosis. As an E1 ubiquitin-activating enzyme, ubiquitin-like modifier-activating enzyme 6 (UBA6) deficiency aggravates inflammation. Herein, we first confirmed that UBA6 is decreased in brain tissues of cecal ligation and puncture (CLP)-induced SAE mice. Lentivirus was bilaterally injected into the hippocampus to establish in vivo UBA6 overexpression. Lentivirus-mediated overexpression of UBA6 effectively inhibited microglial activation, downregulated the levels of pro-inflammatory mediators, and reduced inflammatory cytokine release. Furthermore, UBA6 upregulation mitigated neuronal apoptosis and improved spatial learning and memory functions in SAE model mice. For in vitro validation, BV-2 microglial cells were stimulated with 100 ng/mL LPS for 24 h. Consistent with in vivo observations, exogenous UBA6 decreased the proportion of CD86-positive pro-inflammatory microglia. After culturing HT-22 neuronal cells with BV-2 cell conditioned medium, UBA6 overexpression elevated neuronal viability and restrained caspase-3-mediated neuronal apoptosis. Quantitative proteomics was applied to screen and identify lipocalin 2 (LCN2) as a downstream interacting partner of UBA6. Mechanistically, UBA6 binds LCN2 at residue 147 to accelerate K48 ubiquitination and degradation of LCN2, which attenuates neuronal apoptosis induced by LCN2 paracrine. Rescue assays revealed that ectopic LCN2 expression reversed the protective effects of UBA6 against neuroinflammation and neuronal apoptosis. In summary, UBA6 ameliorates SAE-induced cerebral damage, neuroinflammation and cognitive dysfunction via accelerating LCN2 ubiquitination and degradation. These findings advance the mechanistic understanding of SAE progression and establish UBA6/LCN2 as a prospective therapeutic target for SAE intervention.

articles.title: The PGC-1α-ferroptosis axis mediates empagliflozin-induced epithelial barrier protection in sepsis-associated acute lung injury.
articles.abstract: Sepsis-associated acute lung injury is characterized by epithelial barrier failure, excessive oxidative stress, and inflammatory tissue damage. Ferroptosis has emerged as an important mechanism linking lipid peroxidation to epithelial dysfunction, but the regulatory mechanisms governing ferroptosis resistance in sepsis-associated lung injury remain unclear. Using an LPS-induced acute lung injury model and LPS-challenged A549 cells, we investigated whether empagliflozin protects epithelial barrier integrity by modulating PGC-1α-associated ferroptosis resistance. Endotoxin challenge suppressed PGC-1α expression, disrupted PI3K/AKT signaling, weakened the SLC7A11-GPX4 anti-ferroptotic defense axis, and promoted ROS accumulation, lipid peroxidation, tight junction loss, impaired epithelial repair, and lung pathological injury. Empagliflozin reversed these pathological alterations, preserving ZO-1, Occludin, and Claudin-1 expression while reducing ferroptosis-associated oxidative damage. Mechanistically, PGC-1α emerged as a central node linking metabolic stress adaptation, PI3K/AKT signaling, ferroptosis resistance, and epithelial barrier maintenance. Pharmacological inhibition or siRNA-mediated knockdown of PGC-1α weakened the protective effects of empagliflozin, indicating that PGC-1α is functionally required for empagliflozin-mediated epithelial protection. These findings identify a PGC-1α-associated ferroptosis-epithelial barrier mechanism through which empagliflozin protects against LPS-induced lung injury and provide mechanistic insight relevant to sepsis-associated acute lung injury.

articles.title: Variation in procedure selection for end stage ankle arthritis management in England.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: End-stage ankle arthritis is a debilitating condition presenting with pain and functional limitations. Surgical management typically involves ankle arthrodesis (AA) or total ankle replacement (TAR). This study aimed to investigate demographic, socioeconomic, and clinical factors associated with receiving TAR versus AA in England.

METHODS: A retrospective cohort analysis was conducted using Hospital Episode Statistics (HES) data for all elective AAs and TARs performed in England between April 2013 and March 2025. Patients aged 17 years and over were included. Multivariable logistic regression was used to assess associations between procedure type and patient-level factors.

RESULTS: A total of 26,331 procedures were identified, comprising 8836 (33.6%) TARs and 17,495 (66.4%) AAs. Older age and female sex were independently associated with increased odds of TAR (age ≥80 years relative to 17-29 years: odds ratio (OR) 12.89, 95% confidence interval (CI) 9.86-17.29; female sex: OR = 1.46, 95% CI 1.36-1.56). Relative to no frailty, mild and moderate frailty increased the likelihood of TAR, whereas severe frailty reduced it (OR 0.51, 95% CI 0.37-0.71). Patients from less deprived areas were more likely to receive TAR (IMD 5th quintile relative to 1st quintile OR 1.40, 95% CI 1.25-1.58). Compared with White patients, those of Asian ethnicity were less likely to undergo TAR.

CONCLUSION: Older age, female sex, lower deprivation, and mild-to-moderate frailty are associated with higher odds of TAR, while Asian ethnicity, higher deprivation and severe frailty are associated with reduced likelihood. These findings likely highlight patterns in clinical decision making, but may also suggest possible variation in access to ankle arthroplasty.

articles.title: Incision and Drainage of Acute Paronychia in the Emergency Department.
articles.abstract: Paronychia is a common emergency department presentation, representing up to 35% of hand infections. Standard of care involves incision and drainage, with systemic antibiotic therapy dependent upon the severity of the presentation. The treating emergency nurse practitioner (ENP) should consider factors that may impact wound healing, medications, comorbidities, and perform a thorough history and physical examination to properly address this common infection. This article describes a case of a 43-year-old female with about four weeks of gradually developing paronychia that presented to a community emergency department (ED) for treatment. This article will review the patient's case, including history and management to increase the skills of Emergency Advanced Practice Registered Nurses.

articles.title: Variability and Misalignment in Pre-Clinical Veterinary Microbiology Education: Implications for Competency-Based Training.
articles.abstract: Microbiology is fundamental to veterinary medicine, providing the scientific basis for infectious disease diagnosis, antimicrobial stewardship, vaccination, bio-security, zoonotic disease management, and public health. Despite its importance, little information exists regarding how pre-clinical veterinary microbiology is taught or how curricular content aligns with competency-based veterinary education (CBVE). A survey conducted in collaboration with the American Association of Veterinary Medical Colleges (AAVMC) examined curricular structure, faculty composition, instructional methods, and conceptual priorities among accredited veterinary colleges in North America and Europe. Responses from 24 institutions and reviews of 24 course syllabi revealed substantial variability in disciplinary organization, instructional approaches, faculty expertise, and assessment practices. Most programs delivered microbiology through discipline-specific courses and relied primarily on lecture-based instruction. Learning objectives were common, but explicit competency statements and mapping to CBVE competencies were rare. These findings suggest a disconnect between traditional microbiology curricula and emerging competency-based educational frameworks. Development of discipline-specific competencies, systematic curriculum mapping, and greater integration of foundational sciences with clinical training may improve alignment between microbiology education and professional outcomes.

articles.title: Diabetes and work participation at older ages: evidence from the HEAF cohort.
articles.journal: Journal of occupational and environmental medicine
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To examine associations between diabetes and work participation in adults aged 50-64 years, by treatment regimen.

METHODS: Diabetes of all types was ascertained through Clinical Practice Research Datalink linkage in the Health and Employment After Fifty cohort and categorised by treatment (no glucose-lowering medication, oral medication, insulin). Health-related job loss (HRJL) and prolonged sickness absence over nine years were examined among 4,813 employed adults using mixed-effects logistic regression.

RESULTS: Compared with no diabetes, diabetes treated with oral glucose-lowering medication (OR 1.89, 95%CI 1.26-2.82) and insulin (OR 3.07, 95%CI 1.83-5.15) was associated with HRJL. No treatment category was associated with prolonged sickness absence.

CONCLUSIONS: Diabetes at older ages is associated with HRJL, most strongly among those on insulin. Treatment regimen likely marks disease severity and self-management burden rather than itself increasing risk.

articles.title: Treatment variability among people assigned male at birth with repeat positive Mycoplasma genitalium tests: a case series.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Mycoplasma genitalium (MG) can cause nongonococcal urethritis (NGU) and symptomatic proctitis. Rising antimicrobial resistance and lack of clinically available molecular resistance assays make MG treatment challenging. This study adds systematic data on the effectiveness of alternative MG regimens.
