These PU were previously classified through multivariate statistics; PCA (12 variables related to the structure, management and feeding of livestock; KMO = 0.608 with a Bartlett chi-square test of 1367.419 (P < 0.05), four components that explained 74.23% of the total variance of the model) and cluster analysis(using the coordinates of the first four factors obtained from PCA through Ward's method and squared Euclidean distance and the distance cutoff was 200) into four groups according to their feeding management: (i) cow supplementation (G1CS), (ii) semi-intensive (G2SI), (iii) fattening supplementation (G3FS), and (iv) traditional (G4T). Subsequently, social, structural, and economic variables were analyzed using analysis of variance (ANOVA) based on the general linear model (GLM), and Tukey's test was applied for multiple comparisons among groups. No significant differences were observed in most social variables (P > 0.05); however, differences were detected in certain structural variables, as well as in income, costs, and economic indicators (P < 0.05). Feeding represented the main component of production costs across all groups, accounting for up to 70% of total costs (P < 0.05). Group G1CS showed the highest income and economic indicators (P < 0.05), whereas G3FS ranked second in incomes, mainly associated with cattle fattening. In contrast, G2SI registered the lowest economic indicators (P < 0.05), reflecting a limited capacity to generate incomes. Finally, G4T exhibited the lowest costs (P < 0.05) and greater efficiency in the management of its own resources. It is concluded that the economic performance of dual-purpose systems is primarily determined by the efficiency of resource use rather than by the level of intensification or land size.

articles.title: Bioactive adrenomedullin dynamics and microcirculatory changes in a porcine model of hemorrhagic shock.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Hemorrhagic shock is a leading cause of preventable trauma death, marked by impaired oxygen delivery and endothelial dysfunction. Bioactive adrenomedullin (bio-ADM) regulates endothelial barrier integrity, but its dynamics during hemorrhagic shock and resuscitation remain unclear. This secondary analysis of a porcine hemorrhagic shock model investigated bio-ADM and its association with macro- and microcirculatory parameters during resuscitation. All animals received crystalloid infusion (10 mL/kg/h) from anesthesia induction onward. Shock was induced by blood withdrawal to maintain MAP at 40 ± 5 mmHg for 60 min (T5), before randomization to control (n = 7), fluid (n = 6), or noradrenaline (n = 7) groups, with intervention groups titrated to MAP targets of 65 then 90 mmHg (60 min each). Macrocirculation was assessed via vital signs and pulse contour analysis; microcirculation via hyperspectral imaging (tissue oxygenation, hemoglobin, water index).

RESULTS: Fluid resuscitation improved macrohemodynamics and microcirculatory oxygenation versus control and noradrenaline, which failed to sustain perfusion and impaired microcirculatory oxygenation. Bio-ADM increased after shock induction (p < 0.001), peaking at T9 (120 min of therapy). At T5, levels were comparable among control (16.8 [13.6-18.9] pg/ml), fluid (15.65 [15.43-16.55] pg/ml), and noradrenaline (14.3 [7.85-18.95] pg/ml). Thereafter, bio-ADM continued to rise in control (19.7 [17.4-32.6] pg/ml) and noradrenaline (21.2 [14.4-33.45] pg/ml), while stabilizing in the fluid group (12.05 [10.65-15.18] pg/ml); accordingly, the T5-T9 increase was smaller in the fluid group than in control (p = 0.022) or noradrenaline (p = 0.003). The fluid group received ~3-fold more fluid by T9. Higher bio-ADM correlated with lower MAP, higher lactate, and lower ScvO₂, but not oxygen delivery (DO₂); a higher tissue water index correlated with a smaller rise.

CONCLUSIONS: Bio-ADM increased during hemorrhagic shock, extending previous observations from cardiogenic and septic shock, and represents a comparatively non-specific marker of endothelial and microcirculatory stress rather than specific to any single shock etiology. Effective resuscitation was associated with stabilization, rather than a clear decrease, of bio-ADM levels, though this coincided with higher fluid administration, and dilution cannot be excluded. Whether bio-ADM offers therapeutic utility to guide resuscitation remains unclear, warranting further prospective evaluation in animal and human studies.

articles.title: Mother-to-child transmission of HIV and risk of prematurity according to the time of art initiation.
authors: Madrid Cohort of HIV-Infected Mother-Infant Pairs
articles.abstract:
UNLABELLED: Antiretroviral therapy (ART) is recommended once the HIV infection is diagnosed during pregnancy. However, some antiretroviral regimens have been associated with an increased risk of preterm birth. This retrospective study aimed to assess the rates of prematurity in newborns according to the timing of ART initiation in a cohort of 1,062 mother-infant pairs. Early ART initiation was not associated with an increased risk of prematurity (ART initiation before conception: 16.8%; before 14 weeks of gestation: 15.6%; ART initiation between 14 and 27 weeks: 16.3%; ART initiation after 27 weeks: 21%; and no ART: 30.7%). Furthermore, exposure to INSTIs for more than 12 weeks during pregnancy was not associated with an increased risk of preterm birth (adjusted OR 1.65, 95% CI 0.46-5.95; p = 0.444). These results support current recommendations for early ART initiation during pregnancy.

CONCLUSION: In conclusion, these results support current recommendations for early ART initiation during pregnancy.

WHAT IS KNOWN: • Mother-to-child HIV transmission rates approach zero in women receiving ART before pregnancy and maintaining viral suppression. • Infants born to women living with HIV have been reported to have higher rates of prematurity, although the contribution of ART exposure and timing remains uncertain.

WHAT IS NEW: • Early ART initiation was not associated with an increased risk of prematurity and rates were lowest among women who started ART before conception. • Prolonged exposure to INSTI-based ART was not associated with an increased risk of preterm birth, supporting their current recommendations for treatment during pregnancy.

articles.title: Allograft versus xenograft for alveolar ridge preservation in non-molar extraction sockets: a systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: To compare the clinical, radiographic, and histological outcomes of allograft and xenograft materials used for alveolar ridge preservation following non-molar tooth extraction through a systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials.

MATERIALS AND METHODS: This systematic review and meta-analysis was conducted in accordance with the PRISMA 2020 guidelines and registered in PROSPERO (CRD420261333947). Electronic searches of PubMed/MEDLINE, the Cochrane Central Register of Controlled Trials (CENTRAL), and ClinicalTrials.gov were performed through May 2026. Randomized controlled trials directly comparing allograft and xenograft materials for alveolar ridge preservation in non-molar extraction sockets were included. Risk of bias was assessed using the revised Cochrane Risk of Bias (RoB 2) tool. A qualitative synthesis and random-effects meta-analysis were performed where appropriate.

RESULTS: Seven randomized controlled trials met the inclusion criteria, of which three were included in the meta-analysis. Both allograft and xenograft materials were associated with preservation of alveolar ridge dimensions following tooth extraction, although clinical and radiographic findings did not demonstrate a consistent advantage of either material. Histological findings suggested greater new bone formation, fewer residual graft particles, and faster graft remodeling with allografts, whereas xenografts were associated with slower resorption and greater persistence of residual graft particles. Meta-analysis demonstrated no statistically significant difference between allografts and xenografts in buccal height loss (SMD = - 0.177; 95% CI: -1.822 to 1.468; p = 0.833), with substantial heterogeneity (I² = 82%).

CONCLUSIONS: Current evidence does not demonstrate a consistent clinical or radiographic superiority of either allograft or xenograft for alveolar ridge preservation following non-molar tooth extraction. Although biological differences in graft remodeling were observed, the limited number of studies, small sample size, and substantial heterogeneity reduce the certainty and precision of these findings. The absence of a statistically significant difference should not be interpreted as evidence of equivalence between the two materials. Further well-designed randomized controlled trials with standardized outcome measures and longer follow-up are needed to strengthen the available evidence.

CLINICAL RELEVANCE: Available evidence does not demonstrate a consistent clinical or radiographic advantage of either allograft or xenograft for preservation of alveolar ridge dimensions following non-molar tooth extraction. The findings may assist clinicians in considering graft material selection for alveolar ridge preservation based on clinical requirements, while recognizing the limited and heterogeneous evidence and the absence of established superiority of either material.

articles.title: Establishing the reliability of non-contrast 4D flow in congenital heart disease at 1.5T.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: 4D flow has been shown to correlate well with 2D phase-contrast (2D PC) flow measurements, although most of the current literature is based on post-contrast imaging.

OBJECTIVE: Given recent interest in non-contrast techniques, we hypothesized that non-contrast 4D flow (NC 4D Flow) would correlate well with 2D PC and ventricular stroke volumes.

METHODS AND MATERIALS: A prospective cohort of pediatric and young adult patients with suspected/confirmed congenital heart disease (CHD) underwent cardiac MRI at 1.5T with acquisition of NC 4D Flow and 2D PC. Pearson correlation, linear mixed-effect correlations, and Bland-Altman comparisons were performed to compare these methods with secondary analyses of internal consistency and image quality/noise.

RESULTS: In our cohort of 30 patients (age, 8-20 years), NC 4D Flow correlated strongly with 2D PC for net flow (r=0.76), peak velocity (r=0.9, P<0.001), and regurgitant fraction (r=0.75, P<0.001). By Bland-Altman comparison, NC 4D Flow was 10.1% lower for net flows and 18.9% higher for peak velocity compared to 2D PC. NC 4D Flow also slightly underestimated ventricular stroke volumes (18.1% lower for ascending aorta vs. left ventricular stroke volume and 13.9% lower for main pulmonary artery vs. right ventricular stroke volume). Both datasets were internally consistent; 2D PC had a higher relative signal intensity, but no difference in signal-to-noise or contrast-to-noise ratios (SNR/CNR).

CONCLUSION: Non-contrast 4D flow correlates well with 2D PC in CHD with a slight underestimation in flows and overestimation in peak velocities, but good internal consistency and comparable SNR/CNR.

articles.title: Dynamic course and outcomes of acute-on-chronic liver failure in the intensive care unit : Insights from a real-world cohort.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Acute-on-chronic liver failure (ACLF) frequently requires intensive care unit (ICU) management, yet real-world data on dynamic disease course, organ support and mortality predictors in critically ill ACLF patients remain scarce.

METHODS: All ACLF patients admitted to a tertiary care hepatology ICU between 2013 and 2023 were analyzed in this retrospective single-center study for ACLF grade trajectories, organ support, and independent predictors of 90-day mortality.

RESULTS: Among 209 patients (228 admissions), 54.4% had ACLF grade 3 at ICU admission (median CLIF‑C ACLF 56). Most patients required vasopressors (86.8%), invasive mechanical ventilation (59.6%), and renal replacement therapy (53.5%). The ICU and 90-day survival were 56.1% and 34.2%, respectively. One third of the patients (33.3%) showed improvement in ACLF grade during the ICU stay, including grade 3 patients, indicating meaningful reversibility under comprehensive organ support. The CLIF‑C ACLF score (OR: 1.07, 95% CI: 1.03-1.11, p < 0.001) and the peak noradrenaline dose (OR: 13.5, 95% CI: 3.18-69.7, p < 0.001) were identified as independent predictors of 90-day mortality.

CONCLUSION: Critically ill ACLF patients retain potential for partial recovery under full organ support, justifying ICU escalation even in grade 3 disease. Peak noradrenaline dose, alongside the established prognostic scores, provides a readily available parameter to guide individualized decision-making regarding full organ support or timely de-escalation.

articles.title: Prehospital recognition of sepsis is associated with earlier antibiotic administration in the emergency department : A retrospective cohort study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Early antibiotic administration is crucial in the treatment of sepsis. The impact of prehospital sepsis recognition remains unclear. We investigated whether an emergency medical services (EMS) suspicion of sepsis was associated with earlier antibiotic administration after patients arrived at the emergency department (ED).

METHODS: We conducted a retrospective, single-center observational cohort study involving adult patients (≥ 18 years) admitted via EMS between January 2022 and June 2025 with a sepsis diagnosis made in the ED. Prehospital sepsis recognition was defined as documentation of the term "sepsis" in the EMS protocol. The primary outcome was the percentage of patients who received antibiotic treatment within 1 h of ED admission. Logistic regression was used to adjust for age, sex, and illness severity (quick sequential organ failure assessment [qSOFA]).

RESULTS: We included 134 patients (43% female; mean age 71 ± 15 years). The EMS suspected sepsis in 30 patients (22%). Among these, 63.3% received antibiotics within 1 h of ED admission, compared with 19.2% of patients without an EMS suspicion (p < 0.001). The median time to antibiotic administration was shorter in the EMS suspected group (32.0 min, interquartile range, IQR 16.5-76.8 min versus 124.5 min, IQR 72.5-211.5 min; p < 0.001). Prehospital sepsis suspicion was independently associated with antibiotic administration within 1h (adjusted odds ratio, OR 5.77, 95% confidence interval, CI 2.14-16.4; p < 0.001).

CONCLUSION: Prehospital recognition of sepsis by EMS was strongly associated with earlier antibiotic treatment after ED admission. This highlights the potential of systematic sepsis detection in prehospital settings.

articles.title: [Chances and challenges in the prevention and treatment of early childhood hearing loss: the AWMF guideline on congenital CMV infection].
articles.abstract: After genetic causes, congenital cytomegalovirus (cCMV) infection is the leading infectious cause of congenital and early childhood hearing loss. The 2025 German S2k guideline on prevention, diagnosis, and treatment of CMV infection in pregnant women and congenital CMV infection in neonates and children published by the Association of the Scientific Medical Societies in Germany (Arbeitsgemeinschaft der Wissenschaftlichen Medizinischen Fachgesellschaften, AWMF; 093-003 [24]) provides corresponding recommendations and summarizes the current evidence. Hygiene counseling of pregnant women, targeted diagnostic testing during pregnancy and in neonates, and antiviral therapeutic options are important measures for prevention and treatment of congenital CMV infection. Universal newborn hearing screening (UNHS) is decisive for the diagnosis of congenital hearing loss. If abnormal results are revealed in the initial and follow-up testing, polymerase chain reaction (PCR) analysis of CMV DNA in urine (gold standard) or saliva should be performed immediately-as it should be in the case of other symptoms-preferably in the maternity or pediatric hospital and certainly not later than in the second to third week of life. In the case of symptomatic congenital CMV infection, causal treatment of congenital hearing loss can be offered as early as during the first 30 days of life-both for clinically symptomatic infants and for those with isolated hearing loss. Treatment may reduce the severity of hearing loss, stabilize hearing, or prevent progression. Long-term aftercare is essential to recognize progression or a late onset of hearing loss and to ensure adequate management. In addition to dissemination of these guideline recommendations, interdisciplinary cooperation-particularly between the maternity and neonatal departments performing UNHS and otorhinolaryngology and pediatric audiology departments-is essential.

articles.title: [Osteoporosis in rheumatology-Diagnostics, risk assessment and modern treatment strategies].
articles.abstract: Inflammatory rheumatic diseases such as rheumatoid arthritis (RA) lead to local periarticular demineralization through localized arthritis in one or more joints; however, the autoimmune-mediated systemic inflammatory process is also a driver of systemic bone loss, osteoporosis, which leads to an increased risk of fractures. The Umbrella Organization Osteology (DVO) guidelines 2023 recommend a risk-adapted approach involving systematic fracture risk assessment, early baseline diagnostics and consistent specific osteoporosis treatment, including antiresorptive and osteoanabolic strategies. For rheumatology practice this means firmly integrating osteological assessment, including fracture risk management as well as pharmacological and nonpharmacological osteological treatment into the structured care of patients with inflammatory rheumatic diseases.

articles.title: Risk Factors for Recurrence Following Surgery for Apical Prolapse: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION AND HYPOTHESIS: Most of the existing literature focuses on patient-level risk factors for recurrence after prolapse surgery in general, rather than specifically for uterovaginal prolapse (U-POP). As uterine-preserving procedures are increasingly performed, understanding patient-level risk factors for recurrence after U-POP is essential.

METHODS: Following Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses guidelines, we searched for studies including women undergoing U-POP surgery to evaluate risk factors for recurrence. Risk of bias was assessed using the Grading of Recommendations Assessment, Development and Evaluation framework. Odds ratios were pooled using random-effects meta-analysis. Findings informed a Delphi process at the Global Consensus Conference on Controversies in Surgical Management of Primary U-POP (April 2026) resulting in consensus statements (≥80% agreement threshold).

RESULTS: Of the 4,149 abstracts screened, 25 studies (14,860 women; median follow-up 24 months) met the eligibility criteria. Meta-analyses were performed for 9 of the 16 risk factors identified. Advanced preoperative prolapse stage (OR 2.75; 95% CI 1.39-5.46), prior prolapse surgery (OR 2.09; 95% CI 1.16-3.75), and higher body mass index (BMI; OR 1.10 per unit increase; 95% CI 1.06-1.15) were each significantly associated with an increased risk of recurrence. No significant associations were identified for age, diabetes, smoking, parity, menopause, or preoperative estrogen use. Where there were insufficient data, expert consensus identified levator ani avulsion, enlarged genital hiatus, and connective-tissue disorders as additional risk factors.

CONCLUSIONS: Advanced preoperative prolapse stage, prior prolapse surgery, and higher BMI were each significantly associated with U-POP recurrence. Together with expert consensus, these findings should inform preoperative counseling and individualized surgical planning to improve long-term outcomes.

articles.title: Restaging the primary tumor in localized pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma after systemic therapy: a scoping review of the role of CT, FDG-PET, and CA19-9.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: The introduction of improved multi-agent systemic therapies has made restaging and treatment response assessment in patients with localized pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC) increasingly complex. This scoping review aims to assess and compare methods for local disease restaging and treatment response assessment in localized PDAC, with a focus on their association with resectability, overall survival (OS), and R0-resection rates.

MATERIALS AND METHODS: This scoping review included studies on restaging in patients with PDAC following systemic therapy using CT and PET/CT from MEDLINE, Embase, and CENTRAL.

RESULTS: Among 4680 identified studies, 20 fulfilled the eligibility criteria. Most (n = 15) studies analyzed CT, and 5 analyzed PET/CT. Groups of restaging methods included new response categories, size-based metrics, volume, vascular contact, tumor attenuation, fluorine-18 fluorodeoxyglucose (18F-FDG) PET/CT derived metabolic parameters, and resectability criteria. Dual-energy CT-derived extracellular volume (DECT-ECV) was evaluated as a baseline predictive biomarker. Associations between restaging methods and outcomes were reported inconsistently: some studies found significant associations for specific methods, whereas others did not. No restaging method showed a consistent association with both R0-resection and survival across all studies.

CONCLUSION: Restaging of localized PDAC after systemic treatment remains challenging due to the limited accuracy of RECIST 1.1, particularly for the classifications partial response and stable disease. The current evidence suggests that integrating additional imaging features, alternative imaging modalities, and the biomarker carbohydrate antigen (CA)19-9 may improve the assessment of resectability and prognosis. These findings support a future version of RECIST 1.1 to alert clinicians to this issue.

KEY POINTS: Question How effective are current (PET/)CT-based restaging methods in assessing local disease resectability and prognosis in localized PDAC after modern multi-agent systemic therapy? Findings Current restaging methods show inconsistent association with R0-resection and survival; RECIST 1.1 is particularly limited for the assessment of partial response and stable disease. Clinical relevance Current evidence confirms a need to integrate additional imaging features and the biomarker CA19-9, during restaging in patients with localized pancreatic cancer after modern systemic therapy to improve accuracy and reduce the risk of missed treatment options.

articles.title: Cangrelor Dosing, Administration, and Clinical Outcomes for Patients Undergoing Complex and High-Risk Percutaneous Coronary Interventions.
articles.journal: Catheterization and cardiovascular interventions : official journal of the Society for Cardiac Angiography & Interventions
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Cangrelor reduces thrombotic events in patients undergoing percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI), with the advantage of rapid onset and offset. However, premature discontinuation may increase the risk of acute thrombosis for patients undergoing complex/high-risk PCI (CHIP).

AIMS: We evaluated the real-world administration of cangrelor and related health outcomes for CHIP patients.

METHODS: A US retrospective physician panel medical chart review (1/1/2020 to 6/26/2025) included patients 18+ years old who received cangrelor (1st dose = index date) during CHIP. We summarized patients' characteristics in the 6 months pre-index (baseline), cangrelor dosing and administration (IV bolus and/or infusion), and clinical outcomes within 48 h. We described MACE occurrence by dosing adherence.

RESULTS: Patients (n = 200) were mostly male (85.5%), had a mean age of 63 years, and had a BMI of 30.2 kg/m2. Most (87.5%) received a cangrelor bolus (30.0 µg/kg) and maintenance infusion (4.0 µg/kg/mins), aligned with intended use recommendations. Of patients analyzed for infusion duration (n = 134), 64.9% deviated from the recommendation of at least 2 h or PCI length. Forty (29.9%) received cangrelor for less than the recommended duration. Overall, 30 (15%) patients experienced MACE, with a higher proportion of MACE seen in those who deviated from the recommended duration (16.1% [95% CI: 3.5%-23.1%] vs. 10.6% [95% CI: 9.1%-25.5%]).

CONCLUSIONS: Our study provides real-world insight into cangrelor use and clinical outcomes in CHIP patients, highlighting notable variability in infusion duration and differences in MACE occurrence by dosing adherence. Further comparative effectiveness studies are warranted to examine the potential impact of deviation from intended dose/duration on clinical outcomes in CHIP.

articles.title: Effects of tirzepatide (GIP/GLP-1 dual receptor agonist) on cardiorenal biomarkers and functional capacity in heart failure: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
articles.journal: The Journal of clinical endocrinology and metabolism
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Tirzepatide, a dual glucose-dependent insulinotropic polypeptide (GIP) and glucagon-like peptide-1 (GLP-1) receptor agonist, has demonstrated clinical benefits in heart failure with preserved ejection fraction (HFpEF) and obesity. However, its effects on cardiorenal biomarkers and functional capacity have not been comprehensively synthesized. We hypothesized that tirzepatide produces significant reductions in cardiorenal biomarkers and improvements in functional capacity compared to placebo or standard of care.

METHODS: This systematic review and meta-analysis (PROSPERO: CRD42026137255) searched PubMed, Embase, CENTRAL, Web of Science, and Scopus from inception to April 17, 2026, without restrictions. Randomized controlled trials and prospective observational studies reporting NT-proBNP, high-sensitivity C-reactive protein (hsCRP), Kansas City Cardiomyopathy Questionnaire Clinical Summary Score (KCCQ-CSS), 6-minute walk test (6 MWT), or renal outcomes with tirzepatide vs placebo or standard of care were included. Data were pooled using random-effects models with Hartung-Knapp-Sidik-Jonkman adjustment.

RESULTS: Seven studies (5 RCTs, 2 observational; 5406 participants) were included. Tirzepatide significantly reduced hsCRP by 34.3% (95% CI: -38.4% to -30.1%; P < .0001; I2 = 0.0%; 6 studies) and NT-proBNP by 17.6% (95% CI: -26.7% to -8.5%; P = .0001; I2 = 58.1%; 3 studies). In the SUMMIT trial, KCCQ-CSS improved by 5.1 points (P < .001) and 6 MWT by 15.8 m (P = .004). Single-trial data demonstrated estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR) preservation (+2.90 mL/min/1.73 m2/year; 95% CI: 0.94 to 4.86) and urine albumin-to-creatinine ratio reduction (-25.0%; 95% CI: -36.0% to -13.0%).

CONCLUSION: Tirzepatide produces consistent anti-inflammatory effects and significant natriuretic peptide reductions, supported by moderate Grading of Recommendations Assessment, Development and Evaluation certainty. Evidence for functional and renal outcomes remains limited to single-trial analyses and should be considered hypothesis-generating pending larger dedicated heart failure trials.

PROSPERO REGISTRATION: CRD42026137255.

articles.title: Development and external validation of a nomogram for predicting in-hospital mortality in status epilepticus patients in the intensive care unit: A MIMIC-IV and eICU-CRD study.
articles.journal: Epileptic disorders : international epilepsy journal with videotape
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To develop and externally validate a nomogram for predicting in-hospital mortality in ICU patients with SE, using readily available clinical data collected within the first 24 h of ICU admission.

METHODS: We identified adult SE patients from MIMIC-IV (training cohort, 2008-2019) using ICD-9/ICD-10 codes. Twenty-seven candidate predictors were screened by LASSO logistic regression with 10-fold cross-validation. The final model was constructed with multivariable logistic regression and presented as a nomogram. Internal validation used 1000 bootstrap resamples with optimism correction. External validation was performed in an independent SE cohort from the eICU-CRD database (2014-2015).

RESULTS: The training cohort comprised 299 patients (69 deaths, 23.1% mortality). LASSO selected nine predictors: age, first ICU care unit, Glasgow Coma Scale, temperature, SpO2, white blood cell count, glucose, bicarbonate, and the Elixhauser comorbidity index. The optimism-corrected AUC was .807 (95% CI, .754-.860) with a Brier score of .124. External validation in 597 eICU patients yielded an AUC of .750 (95% CI, .685-.815). In sensitivity analyses, a reduced model without the comorbidity score achieved an optimism-corrected AUC of .786 and an external AUC of .730, and a model without the ICU care-unit type achieved .817 and .764, respectively.

SIGNIFICANCE: This nine-variable nomogram provides a validated, bedside-applicable tool for mortality risk stratification in ICU SE patients, enabling manual risk calculation without electronic computation.

articles.title: Generalizability, discrimination, and interpretability of a machine learning-based Fontan failure risk calculator.
articles.journal: The Journal of thoracic and cardiovascular surgery

articles.title: The Fast Care Model and Clinical Leadership in the Emergency Department: A Randomized Clinical Trial.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: The increasing use of emergency departments for the management of minor emergencies represents a major global challenge, with negative implications for organizational efficiency and patient flow. Despite the adoption of different throughput models, prolonged waiting times and incomplete care pathways remain common. This study aimed to evaluate the effectiveness of a nurse-led Fast Care model, based on early assessment and continuity of care, in improving the management of minor emergencies and patient flow within the emergency department.

METHODS: A randomized clinical trial was conducted in a university emergency department. Adult patients presenting with minor emergencies were randomized in a 1:1 ratio to Fast Care or usual care. The primary outcomes were waiting time and overall length of stay. Secondary outcomes included the number of patients who left without being seen and 72-hour emergency department readmission rates. Data were analyzed using descriptive and inferential statistics.

RESULTS: A total of 801 patients were enrolled. Compared with usual care, participants in the Fast Care group experienced reductions of 77.6 minutes in waiting time, 156.9 minutes in treatment time, and 178.1 minutes in overall length of stay. In the Fast Care group, the care pathway was completed in nearly all cases, with early departures (patients leaving before clinical evaluation) occurring in 2.5% of participants, compared with 32.2% in the usual care group.

DISCUSSION: The nurse-led Fast Care model improved patient flow and reduced delays in the management of minor emergencies, supporting a more efficient and appropriate emergency department care pathway.

articles.title: Cardiac Manifestations of EGPA: An Overlap Phenotype of Inflammatory Myocardial Injury and Takotsubo-Like Syndrome.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Eosinophilic granulomatosis with polyangiitis (EGPA) often presents with eosinophilic myocarditis, but the spectrum of cardiac findings is scarcely reported. We describe a case of EGPA with an unusual presentation of acute left ventricular (LV) dysfunction associated with lymphocyte-predominant myocardial inflammation and Takotsubo-like syndrome with LV thrombus.

CASE SUMMARY: A 42-year-old woman with history of asthma presented with chronic cough, dyspnea, and rash. Findings of peripheral eosinophilia, cutaneous vasculitis, mononeuritis multiplex, and myocardial inflammation confirmed antineutrophil cytoplasmic antibodies-negative EGPA. Her course was complicated by transient severe LV systolic dysfunction with Takotsubo-like regional wall-motion abnormalities, lymphocyte-predominant myocardial inflammation on biopsy, and LV thrombus. Management included pulse-dosed steroids, rituximab, and mepolizumab.

DISCUSSION: Although EGPA frequently causes cardiac manifestations, typically eosinophilic myocarditis, an overlap phenotype of inflammatory myocardial injury, Takotsubo-like cardiomyopathy, and LV thrombus is exceedingly rare.

TAKE-HOME MESSAGES: Cardiac involvement remains the leading cause of mortality in EGPA. This case highlights the heterogeneity of its cardiac phenotypes, illustrating the importance of early cardiology evaluation and diagnostics.

articles.title: Transcatheter Edge-to-Edge Repair of Mitral Valve Leaflet Perforation Guided by 3D Multiplanar Reconstruction Imaging.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Mitral valve leaflet perforation is generally considered unsuitable anatomy for transcatheter edge-to-edge repair (TEER), with published experience largely limited to bailout treatment of iatrogenic perforations.

CASE SUMMARY: A 75-year-old man with severe symptomatic mitral regurgitation (MR) was referred for TEER. Intraprocedural transesophageal echocardiogram (TEE) unexpectedly revealed a large posterior mitral leaflet perforation. Guided by 3D multiplanar reconstruction imaging, 2 XTW MitraClip devices were deployed on both sides of the perforation, effectively "sandwiching" the defect between the clips and reducing MR from severe to mild.

DISCUSSION: This case supports the feasibility of MitraClip as a primary treatment for mitral leaflet perforation in carefully selected patients. TEE with 3D multiplanar reconstruction imaging enabled accurate anatomic characterization and facilitated precise device positioning, resulting in an excellent procedural outcome.

TAKE-HOME MESSAGES: Mitral valve leaflet perforation may be amenable to TEER in select cases. 3D TEE imaging is critical for procedural planning and helps to facilitate precise device positioning.

articles.title: Anatomy Before Occlusion: When an Aorto-Right Ventricular Tunnel Replaces the RCA.
Refractory Ventricular Tachycardia-Induced Severe Cardiomyopathy in a Child: Successful Radiofrequency Ablation With ECMO Support.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Ventricular tachycardia (VT)-induced cardiac dysfunction is a recognized but uncommon cause of cardiomyopathy in children.

CASE SUMMARY: A 7-year-old girl presented with severely depressed left ventricular function and incessant VT that was refractory to multiple antiarrhythmics and attempted cardioversions. Because of hemodynamic instability, the patient required extracorporeal membrane oxygenation (ECMO) support and ultimately radiofrequency ablation of a focal VT that was localized to the right midventricular septum near the moderator band. The patient had a subsequent return of normal biventricular function.

DISCUSSION: Focal VT causing severe dysfunction, unresponsive to both medical therapy and cardioversion, originating from the moderator band of the right ventricle, requiring ECMO support and radiofrequency ablation is extremely rare in the pediatric population, with few reports in the literature.

TAKE-HOME MESSAGE: High-risk radiofrequency ablation of unusual focal VT originating from the right ventricular midventricular septum during ECMO may be accomplished with excellent clinical outcomes.

articles.title: STEMI at Term Managed With IVUS-Guided Percutaneous Coronary Intervention and Cesarean Delivery.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Acute myocardial infarction complicating pregnancy is rare, with a maternal case-fatality rate of 4.5%. ST-elevation myocardial infarction in a near-term gravida requires revascularization, fetal radiation protection, and multidisciplinary coordination.

CASE SUMMARY: A 32-year-old woman at 38 weeks of gestation with no cardiovascular risk factors presented with anterior STEMI from total left anterior descending artery occlusion. Emergent radial-access percutaneous coronary intervention was performed without sedation; intravascular ultrasound confirmed wire position through a thrombus-laden occlusion. Overlapping drug-eluting stents restored TIMI flow grade-3, with air kerma below fetal thresholds. Uninterrupted dual antiplatelet therapy continued through cesarean delivery, with blood loss controlled by hemostatic agents. Mother and neonate were discharged in good health.

DISCUSSION: This case highlights the ambiguity between thrombotic occlusion and spontaneous dissection in pregnancy, the role of intravascular ultrasound when angiography is unreliable, and antiplatelet decision-making when surgery follows percutaneous coronary intervention.

TAKE-HOME MESSAGES: Emergent intravascular ultrasound-guided percutaneous coronary intervention is feasible at 38 weeks of gestation. Multidisciplinary planning, radiation mitigation, and individualized antiplatelet strategy determine outcomes.

articles.title: Adverse event reporting of golimumab: A disproportionality analysis of the FDA Adverse Event Reporting System (FAERS) database.
articles.abstract: This study conducted a retrospective disproportionality analysis of 50,031 adverse drug event (ADE) reports from the FDA Adverse Event Reporting System (FAERS) database spanning Q2 2009 to Q3 2025, in which golimumab was identified as the primary suspect drug. Four disproportionality algorithms were simultaneously applied: the reporting odds ratio (ROR), proportional reporting ratio (PRR), Bayesian confidence propagation neural network (BCPNN), and multi-item gamma Poisson shrinker (MGPS). A total of 397 positive signals were identified across 25 system organ classes (SOCs). The SOCs with concordant positive signals across all four algorithms were identified for infections and infestations and surgical and medical procedures. High-frequency signals included pneumonia, lower respiratory tract infection, influenza, nasopharyngitis, sinusitis and cellulitis. Comparison with the current prescribing information revealed several previously undocumented ADEs, including urinary tract infection, ear infection, flavivirus infection, Zika virus infection and Dengue fever. Twenty-nine positive malignancy signals absent from the prescribing information were identified, including basal cell carcinoma, colorectal cancer, cervical cancer and breast cancer. Time-to-onset analysis revealed that the risk of ADEs was the highest within the first few months of treatment initiation. Clinicians should rigorously monitor for infectious complications and malignancies when prescribing golimumab to ensure patient safety.

articles.title: "Baseline Characteristics and Utilization of Medical Therapies in Acute Hospitalized and Chronic Heart Failure Patients Enrolled in GRASP-HF: Differences Between ICARe-HF and Non-ICARe-HF Centres".
authors: GRASP-HF Study National Leaders and Investigators
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The Global Registries and Surveys Programme-Heart Failure (GRASP-HF) is a prospective, multicentre, international observational study assessing implementation of the 2021/2023 ESC-HF-Guidelines. GRASP-HF is aligned with the Improving Care through Accreditation and Recognition in Heart Failure (ICARe-HF) programme, which links centre-characteristics with guideline-implementation performance.

AIMS: To compare baseline characteristics, guideline-directed-medical-therapy (GDMT) implementation, and in-hospital outcomes between GRASP-HF patients managed in centres participating or not participating in the ICARe-HF programme.

METHODS: GRASP-HF patients were stratified by ICARe-HF participation, clinical settings, acute (AHF) vs chronic HF (CHF) and ejection fraction (EF) subtypes. Hierarchical multivariable logistic regression models evaluated associations with quadruple therapy implementation and in-hospital mortality.

RESULTS: Among 10,936 patients (63.3% CHF, 36.7% AHF), patients from ICARe-HF participating centres (51.3%) were older, more comorbid but with less severe congestion. In both CHF and AHF, ICARe-HF centres demonstrated greater GDMT utilization, particularly angiotensin receptor-neprilysin inhibitors and sodium-glucose-cotransporter-2 inhibitors. In HFrEF, quadruple therapy was more frequently implemented (47% vs 40% in CHF; 27% vs 24% at AHF discharge) and remained associated with ICARe-HF participation after adjustment, Odd Ratio (OR) =1.73, 95% Confidence Interval (CI) :1.17-2.55. Target doses remained suboptimal, particularly after AHF. Although crude in-hospital mortality was lower in ICARe-HF centres (2.3% vs 5.5%), this association was attenuated after multivariable adjustment (OR=0.87, 95% CI:0.48-1.56).

CONCLUSIONS: Participation in the ICARe-HF programme was associated with more comprehensive implementation of contemporary GDMT, particularly in HFrEF. The association with in-hospital mortality was attenuated after adjustment and should be considered exploratory.

articles.title: TRIM25 promotes neuronal ferroptosis in ischemic stroke by suppressing YBX1/H3K4me1/FTH1 axis.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Ferroptosis impairs neurological function in ischemic stroke (IS). This study elucidated the mechanism by which Tripartite motif 25 (TRIM25) promotes neuronal ferroptosis during IS.

METHODS: CCK-8 detected cell viability. Flow cytometry and corresponding kits quantified ferroptosis-related parameters. TTC staining determined cerebral infarct volume. Neurological impairment was assessed using neurological deficit scoring and Nissl staining. RT-qPCR, Western blot, and immunohistochemistry assessed the mRNA and protein expression. Co-IP analyzed the ubiquitinated level of Y-box binding protein 1 (YBX1) and the interaction between TRIM25 and YBX1. ChIP assessed the binding of YBX1 and H3K4me1 at the Ferritin heavy chain 1 (FTH1) promoter. Peptide pull-down assessed the interaction between YBX1 and H3K4me1.

RESULTS: TRIM25 promoted neuronal ferroptosis in IS. TRIM25 promoted YBX1 ubiquitination and degradation. YBX1 knockdown counteracted the suppressive outcome of TRIM25 depletion on OGD/R-induced ferroptosis. YBX1 upregulated FTH1 by recognizing H3K4me1 enrichment at the FTH1 promoter, thus inhibiting OGD/R-induced neuronal ferroptosis. In vivo, TRIM25 knockdown attenuated MCAO/R-induced brain injury via YBX1 upregulation.

CONCLUSION: TRIM25 induces YBX1 ubiquitination and degradation, impairing YBX1-dependent H3K4me1 enrichment at the FTH1 promoter to downregulate FTH1, thereby promoting neuronal ferroptosis in IS.

articles.title: Machine learning in comparative effective research of pharmacological interventions: a scoping review.
articles.journal: Expert review of pharmacoeconomics & outcomes research
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Machine learning (ML) is rapidly transforming the evaluation of the comparative effectiveness research (CER) of pharmacological interventions. It offers an attractive data-driven alternative to traditional statistical causal inference methods for estimation of heterogeneous and individualized treatment effects and is particularly well-suited for high-dimensional real-world data. While variety of ML algorithms have been applied to CER, methodological challenges and limitations remain, and recommendations for conducting, reporting, and evaluating such studies have only recently been proposed.

AREAS COVERED: This paper conducts a scoping review of ML approaches used in CER for pharmacological interventions. We searched multiple databases from January 2020 to January 2026, supplemented by reference mining, and included 28 primary studies. We focused on research topics, ML methodologies, reporting, validity, and robustness of the findings, and appraised risk of bias.

EXPERT OPINION: Although the use of ML methods in CER of pharmacologic intervention is relatively recent, it is expanding and consolidating around few specific methods, notably doubly robust estimators paired with ensemble learners. However, methodological rigor and reporting consistency remain uneven, yielding a moderate risk of bias. Standardized methods, transparent reporting, and dedicated appraisal tools are needed before these approaches can reliably inform research, clinical practice, and policy.

articles.title: Temporal trends of heart failure epidemic in the Rotterdam Study over three decades.
articles.abstract:
AIM: There is limited information on the heart failure (HF) epidemic and its temporal changes. Current research aimed to report the HF epidemic over the past three decades in the Rotterdam Study, covering the prevalence and incidence of HF, comorbidities and risk determinants.

METHODS: Using data from the population-based Rotterdam cohort, three Epoch groups [Epoch 1990s (1989-1993, N=7,983), Epoch 2000s (1997-2001, N=7,738), and Epoch 2010s (2009-2014, N=6,170)] were identified, with a mean age of nearly 70 years. For each Epoch group, point prevalence at baseline and 5-year HF incidence rate, comorbidities at baseline, and HF risk determinants (using Cox proportional hazards models) were calculated.

RESULTS: Point prevalence of HF was 3.3% in Epoch 1990s, 6.0% in Epoch 2000s, and 4.8% in Epoch 2010s, with an increase from the 1990s to 2000s followed by a decline in the 2010s, yielding an overall statistically significant upward trend (p<0.001). 5-year incidence of HF per 1,000 person-years was 16.3 (95%CI: 15.0 to 17.8), 10.3 (95%CI: 9.2 to 11.4) and 7.9 (95%CI: 6.9 to 9.0) in respective epochs, with a downward trend. Hypertension was the most common comorbidity in HF patients, followed by dyslipidemia and kidney dysfunction. The association of hypertension and diabetes with risk of incident HF decreased over time. Coronary heart disease (CHD), atrial fibrillation (AF) and stroke all showed increasing hazard ratios across groups.

CONCLUSIONS: The prevalence of HF increased during the past decades in a population-based setting, while HF incidence declined. Hypertension and diabetes tended to become less critical risk factors for new-onset HF nowadays, while CHD, AF, and stroke showed trends toward stronger associations with HF risk over time.

articles.title: The evolution of Brucella as a model intracellular pathogen.
articles.abstract: Brucella species are intracellular bacterial pathogens that cause brucellosis, one of the most common zoonoses worldwide. This review traces how Brucella, first discovered in the 19th century through investigations of human and bovine disease, became a modern experimental model system. Work on Brucella has illuminated how intracellular bacteria evade and adapt to host defenses and how they remodel host cell biology to establish a replicative niche. It has also yielded insights that extend beyond pathogenesis into bacterial cell envelope architecture and development. Though long regarded as a small, homogeneous group of mammalian pathogens, the genus has expanded in recent years as "non-classical" Brucella have been isolated from unexpected animal hosts, opening new opportunities to understand the fascinating host preferences and evolutionary history of these closely related Alphaproteobacteria. More than a century after their discovery, Brucella species remain versatile models for the study of intracellular infection, bacterial cell biology, and physiology, and the evolution of host association.

articles.title: Anti-mycobacterial activity of phage-encoded lysterases.
articles.abstract: Mycobacterium abscessus is a non-tuberculous Mycobacterium (NTM) that is often associated with respiratory infections in persons with cystic fibrosis. High levels of antibiotic resistance make M. abscessus infections difficult to treat, highlighting the urgent need for alternative therapeutic strategies. Mycobacteriophage therapy-treatment of infections with viruses that infect Mycobacterium hosts-shows considerable promise, but the narrow host specificity of the current mycobacteriophage repertoire limits this approach to personalized therapies. Here, we characterize the anti-M. abscessus activity of mycobacteriophage-encoded Lysin B enzymes (lysterases). Lysterases are serine-esterases that cleave the ester bonds linking mycolic acids to either arabinogalactan or trehalose in the mycobacterial cell envelope to complete the lysis process. In this study, we explored their ability to kill a spectrum of clinically isolated M. abscessus strains when administered exogenously. Six phylogenetically distinct lysterases were purified, characterized on the surrogate M. smegmatis, and their activity against a diverse panel of 24 M. abscessus clinical strains was assessed. The enzymes exhibit a range of activities against these strains, but most have broad-spectrum activity with only minor variations among the M. abscessus isolates. However, the activities can be quite potent, resulting in up to six orders of magnitude of reduction in viability within 4 h with one activity unit of the enzymes, and act synergistically with amikacin. Overall, mycobacteriophage-encoded lysterases show considerable potential for antimycobacterial control, especially for topical applications.IMPORTANCEMycobacterium infections are clinically challenging, and there is a high failure of resolving Mycobacterium abscessus infections using antibiotics. Mycobacteriophages show promise in treating M. abscessus infections, but there is substantial variation among clinical isolates in their phage infection profiles. Mycobacteriophages are unusual in coding for lysis enzymes-lysterases-that target cell wall exposed constituents, and these can have potential antibacterial activity. Exploring the vast sequence diversity of thousands of phage-encoded lysterases identifies a subset that was expressed, purified, and tested for their ability to kill a broad range of M. abscessus clinical strains. Lysterases with the broadest and greatest activity offer substantial potential for treatment of M. abscessus infection, especially where they display synergism with current antibiotics.

articles.title: Pre-exposure prophylaxis for HIV: a review for dermatovenereologists.
articles.journal: Italian journal of dermatology and venereology
articles.abstract: Human immunodeficiency virus (HIV) infection remains a significant public health issue, with 112,883 new diagnoses reported in Europe in 2023. The rise is particularly notable in Eastern Europe, where new cases increased by 20% between 2010 and 2023. Late diagnosis is a major barrier to HIV control, with nearly 50% of new infections in Europe - and up to 60% in Italy - detected at an advanced stage. Dermatovenereologists are key in early detection, as over 90% of people living with HIV show at least one HIV-related dermatologic condition before diagnosis. Thus, dermatovenereology services are well-positioned to promote routine HIV testing and prevention. Pre-exposure prophylaxis (PrEP) is a highly effective HIV prevention method but is unevenly implemented across Europe. In Italy, PrEP is mostly prescribed by infectious disease specialists, except at a pioneering sexually transmitted infections (STI) center in Florence where dermatovenereologists can also prescribe it. Expanding this prescribing authority nationwide could improve access and prevention efforts among underserved populations. Integrating PrEP into dermatovenereology would enhance the continuum of care by linking STI screening, treatment, counseling, and HIV prevention, supporting UNAIDS' goal of ending AIDS by 2030. This narrative review summarizes key studies leading to PrEP approval, outlines approved administration methods for at-risk groups, discusses potential side effects, and highlights emerging therapeutic options under regulatory review (such as long-acting PrEP). It aims to equip dermatovenereologists with all the necessary tools to prescribe and manage PrEP effectively during follow-up.

articles.title: Ionizing radiation-induced remodelling of the heart: Cellular pathways and crosstalk relevant to stereotactic arrhythmia radioablation (STAR).
articles.abstract: Stereotactic arrhythmia radioablation (STAR) has emerged as a promising non-invasive therapy for refractory ventricular tachycardia, yet its biological mechanisms remain poorly defined. While conventional catheter ablation achieves arrhythmia control through structural remodelling, radiotherapy was initially assumed to act similarly. However, STAR reduces ventricular arrhythmia burden within weeks, preceding the development of radiation-induced structural remodelling. This temporal mismatch indicates that early anti-arrhythmic effects are probably driven by functional adaptations. Human tissue findings and preclinical large- and small-animal models have provided the first insights into how the myocardium responds to focal high-dose radiation, yet experimental data on STAR's underlying cellular mechanisms remain limited. Across these studies, a consistent observation is the temporal dissociation between early functional effects and delayed structural remodelling, which provides a key framework for interpretating STAR's anti-arrhythmic action. In this review, we synthesize current evidence on cell-type-specific responses to ionizing radiation by integrating insights from the emerging STAR literature, oncology and radiation heart disease models. By linking time-resolved cellular responses to clinical observations, we aim to distinguish mechanisms most relevant to early therapeutic effects from those contributing to delayed remodelling, and to define key knowledge gaps for guiding safe and effective clinical implementation.

articles.title: BeatVecNet classifies drug-induced contractile phenotypes from beat-gated motion vectors in micropatterned human induced pluripotent stem cell-derived cardiomyocytes.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND AND PURPOSE: Assessment of electrophysiological cardiotoxicity in vitro has advanced, yet scalable assays for contractile dysfunction remain limited. BeatVecNet, an interpretable deep-learning framework, classifies drug-induced contractile phenotypes from beat-gated motion vectors in human induced pluripotent stem cell-derived cardiomyocytes (hiPSC-CMs).

EXPERIMENTAL APPROACH: BeatVecNet was developed and evaluated using beat-gated motion-vector tensors derived from hiPSC-CMs recorded by label-free phase-contrast imaging at 150 fps. hiPSC-CMs were cultured on micropatterned substrates to provide a consistent contraction axis for directional motion analysis. Dense optical flow was used to derive motion vectors, which were retained as beat-gated spatiotemporal tensors rather than reduced to scalar traces. The model uses two convolutional branches to process horizontal and vertical velocity components separately and was evaluated on independent assays containing control, doxorubicin, trastuzumab and sunitinib.

KEY RESULTS: BeatVecNet distinguished drug-induced contractile phenotypes with a macro-F1 of 0.916, outperforming conventional kinematic classifiers (best baseline 0.706), with the largest advantage at low doses. Branch-replacement ablation indicated non-redundant contributions of horizontal and vertical motion components, with trastuzumab classification showing greater sensitivity to horizontal-component replacement and sunitinib classification to vertical-component replacement. Phase-resolved attribution further identified temporal patterns within the beat cycle not explained by peak velocity alone. Micropatterning improved signal consistency and contractile coherence, enabling robust directional motion analysis.

CONCLUSION AND IMPLICATIONS: BeatVecNet extracts drug-associated contractile signatures not captured by conventional scalar analysis while providing direction- and phase-resolved interpretability at the motion-representation level. This platform complements electrophysiology-centred safety assessment and provides proof of concept for classification of subtle drug-induced contractile phenotypes.

articles.title: Reimagining Dental Education Summit Working Group 4: Consensus Recommendations for Structural Interprofessional Education in Dental Training.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Despite decades of attention to interprofessional education (IPE) in dental education, many programs still operationalize IPE as episodic exposure rather than as a durable, assessable competence embedded in clinical workflows. This gap limits the translation of IPE into interprofessional collaborative practice (IPCP), particularly for medically complex patients and populations most affected by fragmented care.

OBJECTIVE: To move IPE from ceremonial participation to structural integration across predoctoral dental education and clinical training environments, by developing consensus recommendations from Working Group 4 of the Reimagining Dental Education Summit (Harvard School of Dental Medicine, June 11-13, 2026).

CONSENSUS PROCESS: Working Group 4 consisted of nine dental education leaders and experts (two co-chairs, one summit scholar, and six members). Recommendations were developed using a structured "future-back" methodology in working sessions, iterative drafting, and plenary report-out. Evidence inputs included competency frameworks (IPEC), accreditation standards (CODA), staged integration frameworks, implementation tools, and exemplars of integrated care delivery (e.g., federally qualified health centers [FQHCs] and integrated health systems). Consensus was achieved through iterative discussion and a nominal group technique to reach unanimous agreement on final recommendations and proposed evaluation metrics.

RECOMMENDATIONS: The group recommends: (1) defining IPE competence as measurable, dentistry and oral health-specific outcomes; (2) prioritizing strategic partnerships beyond medicine (e.g., pharmacy, nursing, social work, nutrition, occupational/physical therapy); (3) anchoring IPE in IPCP settings such as FQHCs and integrated systems; (4) building an alumni/outcomes follow-up system to assess whether IPE training changes practice behaviors; and (5) strengthening communication and referral processes, including closed-loop referrals, even when electronic health records are not shared.

CONCLUSIONS: Structural IPE requires outcome-based performance expectations, practice-linked implementation models, and accountability mechanisms that measure behavior change and care-process improvement for both the learner and the patient, during training and after graduation. These consensus recommendations offer a practical roadmap for dental education programs, accreditors, and partners seeking to operationalize integrated oral health care.

articles.title: Kiwifruit Xylem Sap Promotes Pseudomonas syringae pv. actinidiae Proliferation and Vascular Colonization.
articles.abstract: The xylem has traditionally been considered a nutrient-poor environment, yet it is associated with systemic colonization by Pseudomonas syringae pv. actinidiae (Psa), the causal agent of kiwifruit bacterial canker. To clarify how Psa proliferates within this niche, we combined histopathology, metabolomics, bacterial growth kinetics, and gene-expression analyses. Psa exhibited a proliferation-during-migration pattern, reaching approximately 109 CFU·g-1 while traversing the vasculature at 0.24 cm·h-1 under condition of 16°C and 70% relative humidity, causing irreversible vascular necrosis. Crucially, xylem sap from Actinidia chinensis cv. 'Hongyang', in which systemic infection is readily established, and A. deliciosa cv. 'Hayward', in which systemic spread is uncommon, supported comparable ex vivo bacterial growth. Metabolomics revealed conserved pathogen-induced metabolic reprogramming, marked by targeted depletion of key carbon/nitrogen sources coupled with coordinated shifts in glycolysis-TCA flux and amino acid metabolism. A synthetic xylem medium containing 7 amino acids, 3 sugars, and 4 organic acids recapitulated high-density proliferation. Xylem sap exposure also increased the expression of selected motility- and type III secretion system-associated genes. These findings indicate that kiwifruit xylem sap provides a permissive nutritional environment and supports virulence-related traits, but does not by itself determine whether Psa becomes systemic. Cultivar differences in systemic infection are more likely associated with host defenses and pathogen containment before xylem entry.

articles.title: Functional characterization of a 3-O-sulfate tolerant heparin lyase from Bacteroides eggerthii.
articles.abstract: Heparin is a sulfated glycosaminoglycan, and the most used pharmaceutical anticoagulant worldwide. Heparin is isolated primarily from porcine sources, and possesses a complex variable structure, wherein anticoagulant activity is principally derived from the pentasaccharide GlcNS6S-GlcA-GlcNS3S6S-IdoA2S-GlcNS6S (AGA*IA) motif, containing an infrequent 3-O-sulfated glucosamine that enhances antithrombin stabilization. Pedobacter heparinus heparin lyases are currently widely employed for characterization of heparin and its derivatives, but have limited activity near regions of 3-O-sulfation, hindering analyses of anticoagulation relevant sequences. Here, using a panel of biophysical and structural techniques, we show that Bacteroides eggerthii lyase I liberates ΔUA-GlcNS3S6S disaccharides from the defined pentasaccharide, fondaparinux. This activity provides improved access to 3-O-sulfated heparin standards, with potential to aid heparin quality control.

articles.title: Progression of Tricuspid Regurgitation After Cardiac Implantable Electronic Device Implantation and Its Impact on Mortality and Hospitalization: A Single-Center Cohort Study.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Tricuspid regurgitation (TR) progression is a recognized complication of cardiac implantable electronic device (CIED) implantation, yet its prognostic impact on long-term clinical outcomes remains incompletely defined.

METHODS AND RESULTS: In this single-center retrospective cohort, 303 patients undergoing CIED implantation between 2005 and 2023 were followed for a median of 4.8 years. TR severity was assessed echocardiographically at baseline and 12 months. The primary endpoint was TR progression (≥ 1-grade worsening); secondary endpoints were all-cause mortality, cardiovascular hospitalization, their composite, and progression to severe TR, analyzed by Kaplan-Meier and Cox regression. TR progressed in 103 patients (34.0%), regressed in 33 (10.9%), and remained stable in 167 (55.1%), a net rightward shift (p < 0.001). Progression differed by device type (p = 0.031): among the larger subgroups, VVI-ICD showed the greatest net progression (31.8% worsened vs. 6.9% improved; p < 0.001) and CRT-D the highest regression (18.8%). During follow-up, 67 patients (22.1%) died and 164 (54.1%) were hospitalized. Overall TR progression was not independently associated with mortality (HR 1.118, p = 0.693) but independently predicted cardiovascular hospitalization (HR 1.640, p = 0.003) and the composite endpoint (HR 1.480, p = 0.014). On unadjusted analysis, progression specifically to severe TR (n = 15) was associated with increased mortality (HR 1.99, p = 0.024) and cardiovascular hospitalization (HR 2.45, p < 0.001).

CONCLUSION: TR progression occurs in approximately one-third of CIED recipients within the first year and independently predicts cardiovascular hospitalization. Progression to severe TR identifies a higher-risk subset, supporting routine post-implant echocardiographic surveillance.

articles.title: Different Factors Drive Initiation of Gametocytogenesis Versus Gametocyte Carriage in Plasmodium falciparum Infections.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Gametocyte carriage varies across Plasmodium falciparum infections. The extent to which this variation reflects differences in the initiation of gametocytogenesis and/or gametocyte maturation remains unclear. We investigated determinants of initiation of gametocytogenesis and gametocyte carriage in P. falciparum infections from Malawi.

METHODS: A total of 1108 P. falciparum infections from a cohort study conducted in Malawi between 2019 and 2020 underwent ccp4 and pfmget qRT-PCR to measure gametocyte carriage, ap2-g and sbp1 RT-PCR to quantify gametocytogenesis initiation in ring-stage parasites, and pfs230 DNA amplicon sequencing to estimate infection complexity. Mixed-effects logistic regression was used to evaluate predictors of gametocytogenesis initiation and gametocyte carriage, and mixed-effects linear regression was used to evaluate predictors of ap2-g gene transcript abundance and gametocyte density.

RESULTS: Gametocyte marker transcripts were detected in 54% (594/1108) of infections and ap2-g transcripts were detected in 41% (429/1047) of infections with detectable ring-stage parasites. Parasite density was positively associated with ap2-g expression, and ap2-g expression was more likely in polyclonal compared to monoclonal infections. Children <6 years old had lower ap2-g transcript abundance than adults but were more likely to carry gametocytes and have higher gametocyte density. Asymptomatic infections showed higher ap2-g transcript abundance and greater gametocyte prevalence and density than symptomatic infections.

CONCLUSIONS: Our findings suggest that infection complexity and parasite density may play a role in the initiation of gametocytogenesis, whereas host immunity and duration of infection may play a larger role in gametocyte carriage in P. falciparum infections.

articles.title: Substance use, related harms and public health responses in Colombia: A national profile.
articles.abstract:
AIMS: To provide a comprehensive national profile of substance use patterns, drug-related harms, treatment and harm reduction responses, and policy developments in Colombia, and to analyze how public health reforms coexist with historically prohibitionist frameworks.

METHODS: We synthesized data from national household, school, and university surveys, epidemiological surveillance systems, official statistics, policy documents, and peer-reviewed research. Evidence was analyzed to describe trends in substance use, overdose and related harms, treatment access, harm reduction initiatives, and the broader legal and institutional context.

RESULTS: Alcohol, tobacco, and cannabis remain the most widely used substances in Colombia, while emerging synthetic drugs and opioid use have increased pressure on health and social services. Drug-related harms, including overdose and mental health problems, show significant regional and socioeconomic disparities. Although treatment coverage and harm reduction interventions, including community-based programs and supervised consumption services, have expanded in recent years, access remains uneven, particularly in rural and peripheral areas. Colombia's contemporary drug policy reflects a hybrid governance model in which constitutional protections of personal autonomy and recent harm reduction reforms coexist with enforcement-oriented practices shaped by illicit drug markets, armed conflict, and territorial inequality.

SUMMARY: Colombia illustrates both the opportunities and the structural constraints of public health-oriented drug policy in middle-income countries deeply embedded in transnational drug economies. Strengthening surveillance systems, expanding territorially adapted services, and integrating health policy with broader social and development strategies will be essential to consolidate more coherent and equitable responses.

articles.title: A comparative analysis of cell death signalling in RNA and DNA virus infections and potential inhibitory strategies.
articles.abstract: The recent COVID-19 pandemic and the epidemic outbreak of Mpox have demonstrated that viruses, despite their apparently simple structure, are sophisticated microorganisms that have evolved complicated pro-survival mechanisms. Their potential to manipulate cell death pathways can affect and determine the outcome of the infection cycle and the host's immune response. RNA viruses typically display a more acute and aggressive nature, as they often promote cell death. In this way, they proliferate and release their virions to infect adjacent cells and perpetuate their life cycle. Common consequences of RNA virus infection include hyperinflammatory responses in hosts, typically leading in damage to the epithelial barrier. Conversely, DNA viruses modulate these pathways to sustain a balance between the lytic cycle, during which they replicate, and latency, wherein they remain inactive until an appropriate stimulus triggers reactivation. Achieving this balance and transitioning between stages of infection requires the inhibition of cellular death processes. In both instances, the viruses seem to respond to the cellular context, enhancing their adaptability through mutations, so to deceive host defenses and therefore secure their survival. This highlights the necessity to comprehend the processes via which these biological threats induce cell death, thereby facilitating the development of broad-spectrum or targeted antiviral treatments.

articles.title: Impact of inoculum effect on in vitro activity of intermittent and continuous piperacillin-tazobactam infusion against ESBL-producing Escherichia coli in a hollow-fiber infection model.
articles.abstract:
UNLABELLED: Use of piperacillin-tazobactam (TZP) in the treatment of severe extended-spectrum β-lactamase (ESBL)-producing Escherichia coli (ESBL-EC) infections is controversial. Two features may explain treatment failures: the inoculum effect and suboptimal pharmacokinetic/pharmacodynamic (PK/PD) target attainment, particularly in critically ill patients. To study the combined impact of the inoculum effect and a PK/PD optimization on the in vitro efficacy of TZP against ESBL-EC infections. Five-day hollow-fiber infection model simulating TZP pharmacokinetics in critically ill patients was performed: two TZP infusion regimens (4/0.5 g q6h over 30 min, and 16/2 g q24h continuous infusion), three ESBL-EC clinical strains: 1146 (blaCTX-M-15, MIC = 2 mg/L), 3383 (blaCTX-M-15 + blaTEM-1, MIC = 4 mg/L), and 2262 (blaCTX-M-15 + blaOXA-1, MIC = 8 mg/L), and two initial inocula (5 and 7 log10 CFU/mL). Intermittent infusion was associated with systematic bacterial regrowth within 24 h, consistent with failure to reach the 100%fT >4× MIC threshold. Continuous infusion resulted in undetectable bacterial count for the strains 3383 (MIC = 4 mg/L, low inoculum) and 1146 (MIC = 2 mg/L, low and high inocula). For strain 3383, the inoculum effect was demonstrated by total bacterial killing in continuous infusion with low inoculum, whereas early regrowth (>10 log10 CFU/mL) with resistance emergence (MIC > 256 mg/L) was observed with high inoculum. Strain 2262 (MIC = 8 mg/L) exhibited systematic treatment failure regardless of infusion mode or inoculum size. Continuous infusion of TZP may be considered as a carbapenem-sparing agent in ESBL-EC infection with a TZP MIC ≤ 2 mg/L regardless of inoculum, or a TZP MIC of 4 mg/L at low inoculum. TZP should not be used for strains with an MIC of 8 mg/L or suspected OXA-1 co-production, irrespective of the infusion mode.

IMPORTANCE: Infections caused by extended-spectrum β-lactamase (ESBL)-producing Escherichia coli represent a growing therapeutic challenge, particularly in critically ill patients. Carbapenems remain the reference treatment, but their overuse drives resistance emergence. Piperacillin-tazobactam is a potential carbapenem-sparing agent, but its clinical efficacy remains debated, partly due to the inoculum effect (a reduction in antibiotic activity at high bacterial densities) and suboptimal dosing regimens. Using a hollow-fiber infection model simulating the pharmacokinetics of critically ill patients, this study demonstrates that continuous infusion of piperacillin-tazobactam can overcome the inoculum effect under specific conditions, defined by the MIC of the infecting strain and the estimated bacterial density. These findings support a stratified approach to piperacillin-tazobactam use in severe ESBL-producing E. coli infections, based on MIC, inoculum size, and β-lactamase profile, and may help clinicians identify patients who could safely receive piperacillin-tazobactam instead of a carbapenem.

articles.title: Cohort methods: the CANadian RADiation workers (CANRAD) cohort.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: The long-term follow-up of workers with protracted exposure to low dose occupational ionizing radiation is important to understand the health effects and risks of radiation. This paper describes the creation and record linkage of the CANadian RADiation workers (CANRAD) cohort, including the work to resolve data issues and linkage challenges to outcome databases.

MATERIALS AND METHODS: The CANRAD cohort includes all workers with occupational exposure to ionizing radiation (1951-2018) in Canada's National Dose Registry (NDR) and three facility-based sub-cohorts: Eldorado uranium workers (1932-1980), Ontario uranium miners (1954-1996), and Atomic Energy of Canada Limited nuclear workers (1956-1985). The sub-cohorts were added to the NDR to update workers' employment histories and radiation exposures to 2018. Deterministic and probabilistic record linkage methods linked the CANRAD cohort to national population-based mortality (1950-2020), cancer incidence (1969-2019), and tax (1981-2020) data.

RESULTS: Of 957,580 CANRAD workers, 883,150 (92.2%) successfully linked to Statistics Canada vital statistics databases. The analytical cohort includes 860,650 (89.9%) workers, including 427,920 (49.7%) females. At the end of follow-up, 751,520 (87.3%) of the cohort were alive and 94,410 (11.0%) were dead. Neoplasms and circulatory disease represented 63.8% (57,030) of all known causes of death (89,330). Prostate, breast, lung & bronchus, and colorectal cancer represented 49.9% (40,780) of first primary cancers (81,670). The mean cumulative effective dose was 17.1 mSv; but most cumulative doses were <10 mSv (∼85.0% of males and 98.1% of females). Females (350,510, 82.4%) dominated the medical sector.

CONCLUSIONS: The CANRAD cohort is a large and valuable cohort of Canadian occupationally exposed radiation workers with employment histories, radiation exposures and long-term follow-up of tax, mortality, and cancer incidence. Analysis of this cohort will support the radiation protection framework.

articles.title: Metaproteomic analysis of human sonicate fluid highlights neutrophil extracellular trap formation associated with periprosthetic joint infection.
articles.abstract:
UNLABELLED: Periprosthetic joint infection (PJI) is a devastating complication of total joint arthroplasty that can be challenging to diagnose and treat. Neutrophils are a prominent feature in PJI, with neutrophil extracellular traps (NETs) known to be present; little is known, however, about the physiology of PJI-associated NETs. Here, the proteomes of PJI and non-infectious arthroplasty failure (NIAF), analyzed using liquid chromatography tandem mass-spectrometry (LC-MS/MS) and proximity extension assay (PEA)-based profiling of fluids derived from sonication of arthroplasty components removed from patients who had undergone revision arthroplasty, were compared, with a focus on NET formation. In addition, in vitro effects of synovial fluid components on Staphylococcus aureus-induced NET formation were characterized. LC-MS/MS (PJI n = 85, NIAF n = 26) and PEA (PJI n = 95, NIAF n = 39) showed NET formation and neutrophil degranulation to be associated with PJI, with the complement cascade and platelet activation pathways identified as potential contributors. In vitro studies showed delayed NET formation in artificial synovial fluid compared to standard cell culture media conventionally used to evaluate NETs. Together, these results demonstrate the presence of NETs in PJI, identify potential pathways involved in PJI-associated NETosis, and point to an influence of synovial components on NET formation during PJI.

IMPORTANCE: Periprosthetic joint infection (PJI) is a major complication of joint replacement, placing a significant burden on patients and the healthcare system. Our research reveals that neutrophils and their antimicrobial "traps" are dominant features of the immune response at the infection joint site. Importantly, we found that the unique environment of the joint delays the formation of these traps, potentially contributing to the pathogenesis of PJI. By establishing a new experimental platform tailored for the infected joint, this work provides a foundational platform for probing these mechanisms and supports the development of improved diagnostic and therapeutic strategies.

articles.title: Avian influenza A virus polymerase gene leads to temperature-resistant genome replication.
articles.abstract: Influenza A viruses (IAV) pose a persistent pandemic threat. Successful cross-species transmission from waterfowl to mammals requires host adaptation for efficient replication and spread. Avian IAVs are adapted to the temperature of the avian gut, approximately 41°C, while human IAVs replicate at 33°C in the upper respiratory tract. PB1, the catalytic core of the viral heterotrimeric RNA-dependent RNA polymerase (RdRp), is essential for viral RNA synthesis. Three pandemic IAV strains (1918, 1957, and 1968) carried an avian-origin PB1 gene, suggesting a selective advantage. Fever, a critical antiviral response, elevates body temperature to 38°C or higher and can restrict viral replication. We hypothesized that avian PB1 may allow IAV replication at febrile temperatures. Using a mini-replicon system, we demonstrate that a polymerase of a seasonal human H1N1 IAV fails to replicate viral RNA efficiently at 40°C, whereas substitution of the PB1 with that from the 1918, 1957, and 1968 pandemic viruses, or a low-pathogenic avian H2N1 virus, restores RNA synthesis. Chimeric seasonal human H1N1 viruses expressing avian or 1918 PB1 replicate at 40°C in MDCK cells, unlike wild-type H1N1. Activity assays with purified chimeric IAV polymerases further suggest that avian-origin PB1 may intrinsically enhance polymerase activity at elevated temperatures. Together, these data show that avian-origin PB1 enables IAV replication at febrile temperatures, highlighting its role in zoonotic emergence and host adaptation. Surveillance of avian-origin PB1 genes in IAVs circulating in mammals may help identify strains with pandemic potential and inform the development of countermeasures.IMPORTANCEInfluenza A viruses of avian origin remain a persistent threat to human health. The 1918, 1957, and 1968 pandemic influenza viruses each acquired an avian-origin PB1 gene, but the adaptive advantage conferred by these genes remains incompletely understood. Here, we show that avian-origin PB1 genes enhance viral RNA replication by a seasonal human influenza virus polymerase at elevated temperature and enable replication of a human influenza virus at 40°C, a temperature relevant to both avian hosts and human febrile illness. PB1-dependent effects were observed in cell-based polymerase assays, with purified polymerase, and during authentic virus infection. These findings identify temperature-resistant genome replication as a potential adaptive property of avian-origin PB1 and suggest that acquisition of an avian PB1 may help influenza viruses overcome temperature barriers encountered during adaptation to mammalian hosts.
