These may be applied as continuous or discrete palettes, depending on the software vendor or even on individual user settings. The lack of standardisation of colour schemes across the medical community, especially in medical imaging, risks misinterpretation of quantitative data and potential unintended negative clinical consequences. The purpose of this article is to review the colour schemes used for quantitative imaging across US, computed tomography (CT), magnetic resonance imaging (MRI), and positron emission tomography (PET), the way in which they are applied, the clinical applications where their use is desirable for enhanced interpretation, and the pitfalls where standardisation is lacking in a variety of clinical applications. Finally, we discuss some solutions that could be employed to enable standardisation and augment the use of colour in image interpretation. KEY POINTS: Question Colour schemes in medical imaging can highlight pathology, but standardisation is lacking for most imaging modalities, thus risking misinterpretation of quantitative data. Findings For T1, T2, and T2* maps and their inverses, colour map recommendations have recently been proposed, but are mostly lacking for other quantitative data. Critical relevance statement Standardised colour maps can enhance data analyses across scanners and institutions, which is important for multicentre studies and handling big data. Furthermore, standardised and harmonised colour maps could improve lesion conspicuity, cross-platform comparability, and longitudinal reliability.

articles.title: Opportunities for age-friendly emergency care: a mixed-methods study of older adult experiences in a Canadian Emergency Department.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: The aim of this study was to gain insight into the perceptions of care quality and ED experiences of older adults in a Canadian emergency department to develop targeted interventions to improve care experience and outcomes.

METHODS: This study utilized a mixed-methods approach. Semi-structured phone interviews were conducted within 30 days of the index ED visit for 19 consenting participants. Survey data were analyzed using descriptive statistics, while qualitative data from interviews were coded using Nvivo software until thematic saturation was achieved.

RESULTS: Surveys were administered to 120 older adults (65 years and older). The majority of older adults surveyed use the ED 2-5 times per year and primarily resided in an urban setting. Survey results identified that older adults were hungry and thirsty during their stay (56.7%), relied on care partners for help during their ED visit (29.2%), and the majority felt heard at triage (93.3%). Interview results identified four major themes and 12 subthemes, highlighting many challenges and opportunities in the care of older adults in the ED. Major themes were communication, care, facilities, and attitudes. While older adults expressed appreciation and general acceptance of current ED conditions, they highlighted several areas needing improvement, including enhanced communication from physicians, better privacy measures, parking accessibility, and improved accommodations for caregivers.

CONCLUSIONS: This study highlights the unique challenges older adults face in the ED. While many expressed satisfaction and appreciation for their care, key areas for improvement emerged, especially in communication, privacy, and support services. Targeted interventions, such as geriatric friendly infrastructure and multidisciplinary teams, could improve care quality, patient satisfaction, and outcomes for older adults in the ED.

articles.title: The use of hook acetabular cage after intralesional surgery in secondary bone tumors of the acetabulum: indications and results at medium term.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: The acetabulum is a common site for metastatic lesions. When lytic lesions involve this region, the surgical approach often consists of intralesional treatment and reconstruction to restore stability and ambulation. Reconstruction using a hook acetabular cage represents a viable reconstructive option. The aim of this study was to evaluate the reliability of the hook acetabular cage for reconstruction after curettage of secondary tumors of the acetabulum.

MATERIALS AND METHODS: Patients undergoing intralesional surgery for acetabular roof metastases between 2006 and 2022 at two referral centers were included; surviving patients were required to have at least 1 year of follow-up. Staging involved whole-body CT or FDG-PET; local extension was assessed with radiographs, CT, and MRI. All cases were evaluated by a multidisciplinary tumor board. Statistical analysis included descriptive data, implant survival, and overall survival (OS) using the Kaplan-Meier method.

RESULTS: Twenty patients (10 men and 10 women), with a mean age of 61.6 ± 15.5 years, were included. Seventeen patients had acetabular metastases from solid tumors, whereas three had acetabular involvement from multiple myeloma. During a mean follow-up of 34.2 ± 29.1 months, six patients (30%) experienced complications, including three infections and three dislocations. Eleven patients (55%) died during follow-up, including five from causes unrelated to the underlying malignancy. At 36 months, implant survival was 74.4% (95% CI, 48.9-88.5%) and overall survival was 65.1% (95% CI, 37.7-82.8%). Median overall survival was 61 months.

CONCLUSIONS: Hook acetabular cage reconstruction may provide reliable of the acetabulum after tumor surgery, restoring joint stability and function. The reconstruction system used demonstrated sufficient durability to cover the average survival of the patients. Implant mid-term survival supports their use in selected metastatic cases. Further comparative studies are needed to establish their efficacy relative to alternative devices.

articles.title: A New Method for Creating Lower-Lid Pretarsal Fullness by Fixation of Orbicularis Oculi Muscle-Wrapped Fascia-Fat Flap to the Tarsal Plate.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The study aimed to evaluate the clinical efficacy of orbicularis oculi muscle-wrapped fascia-fat flap fixed to the tarsal plate in creating the pretarsal fullness of the lower eyelids.

PATIENTS AND METHODS: This retrospective study included 213 patients who underwent lower pretarsal augmentation surgery between November 2022 and December 2024. The surgical procedure involved wrapping of fascia-fat flap by orbicularis oculi muscle, followed by fixation to the tarsal plate. After surgery, patients were followed up at 1, 3, 6, and 12 months postoperatively. Clinical outcomes, including the contour of the pretarsal fullness of the lower eyelids and patient satisfaction, were evaluated. The occurrence of complications such as hematomas, scarring, infection, trichiasis, lower eyelid retraction, and ectropion were recorded.

RESULTS: The study comprised 5 males and 208 females, with an age range of 20-50 years. Sutures were removed at 7 days after surgery in all patients. The contour of the pretarsal fullness was good, with complete eyelid closure. At 3- and 6-month follow-up, the pretarsal fullness appeared natural, without the occurrence of lower eyelid retraction or incomplete eyelid closure. Depressed scars were not found at the incision site. Among the 213 patients included, 195 were satisfied with the results, 18 were basically satisfied, and none were dissatisfied, yielding a satisfaction rate of 91.5%.

CONCLUSION: Fixation of orbicularis oculi muscle-wrapped fascia-fat flap to the tarsal plate is effective in creating both static and dynamic pretarsal fullness, yielding excellent clinical outcomes.

LEVEL OF EVIDENCE IV: Eyelid Surgery. This journal requires that authors assign a level of evidence to each submission to which Evidence-Based Medicine rankings are applicable. This excludes Review Articles, Book Reviews, and manuscripts that concern Basic Science, Animal Studies, Cadaver Studies, and Experimental Studies. For a full description of these Evidence-Based Medicine ratings, please refer to the Table of Contents or the online Instructions to Authors www.springer.com/00266 www.springer.com/00266 .

articles.title: Advanced Age is Not Associated With An Increased Risk of Postoperative Complications in Breast Reduction Surgery: A Comparative Study on 1716 Patients.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Age is frequently cited as a surgical risk factor; yet, its influence on outcomes following breast reduction remains unclear. With increasing numbers of elderly patients presenting with macromastia, determining whether advanced age independently affects complication rates is clinically important.

AIMS AND OBJECTIVES: To evaluate whether age ≥ 65 years is an independent risk factor for postoperative complications following bilateral reduction mammaplasty and to identify associated patient- and procedure-related variables.

MATERIALS AND METHODS: This retrospective cohort study included 1716 female patients who underwent bilateral breast reduction at a single tertiary center (2005-2024), stratified into older (≥ 65 years, n = 174), and non-older (< 65 years, n = 1542) groups. Primary outcome was Clavien-Dindo grade II or higher complications requiring surgical intervention. Multivariable logistic regression identified independent risk factors.

RESULTS: Older patients had significantly higher comorbidity prevalence (69.0% vs. 46.1%; p < 0.001), including diabetes and hypertension, and greater bilateral resection weights. Despite this, overall complication rates were significantly lower in the older group (8.6% vs. 16.1%; OR 0.49, 95% CI 0.28-0.85; p = 0.009). Hematoma and deep wound infection rates were also lower, while fat necrosis occurred more frequently and was managed conservatively in most cases. On multivariable analysis, higher BMI (OR 1.10; p = 0.004) and active smoking (OR 1.80; p = 0.004) were independent predictors of complications; age ≥ 65 was not significantly associated with complications (OR 0.55; p = 0.062).

CONCLUSIONS: Advanced age alone was not independently associated with increased complications. BMI and smoking were the main modifiable factors associated with postoperative risk. Age-based exclusion criteria are not supported by these findings in this cohort of selected surgical patients; individualized risk assessment should be applied to all candidates.

LEVEL OF EVIDENCE III: This journal requires that authors assign a level of evidence to each article. For a full description of these Evidence-Based Medicine ratings, please refer to the Table of Contents or the online Instructions to Authors www.springer.com/00266 .

articles.title: Tetrodotoxin (TTX): What do we currently know? The state of the art.
articles.abstract: Tetrodotoxin (TTX) is one of the most potent naturally occurring neurotoxins and continues to attract considerable scientific, clinical, forensic, and regulatory attention. Historically associated with pufferfish poisoning in East and Southeast Asia, TTX has recently emerged as a global food safety concern due to its detection in an increasing number of marine and terrestrial organisms and its expanding geographical distribution, including European coastal waters. Despite decades of research, important questions regarding its biosynthesis, ecological origin, toxicokinetics, and environmental dissemination remain unresolved. This review provides a comprehensive overview of current knowledge on TTX. The chemical structure, physicochemical properties, proposed biosynthetic origin, and diversity of naturally occurring TTX analogues are discussed. Attention is devoted to the toxin's mechanism of action, which involves high-affinity binding to voltage-gated sodium channels and subsequent inhibition of sodium ion conductance, leading to neuromuscular paralysis and potentially fatal respiratory failure. Current evidence regarding toxicokinetics, tissue distribution, elimination pathways, and the suitability of different biological matrices for laboratory confirmation of exposure is also summarized. The review further examines the analytical challenges associated with TTX determination, including its high polarity, occurrence at trace concentrations, rapid elimination from blood, and frequent co-occurrence with structurally related analogues. The evolution of analytical methodologies is presented, from early bioassays and chromatographic techniques with fluorescence or UV detection to advanced liquid chromatography-mass spectrometry platforms, high-resolution mass spectrometry, capillary electrophoresis, immunochemical assays, and emerging biosensor-based approaches. Finally, current regulatory perspectives and risk assessment strategies are discussed in the context of the increasing occurrence of TTX in seafood and the growing need for harmonized monitoring programs. Collectively, this review summarizes the current state of the art, identifies key knowledge gaps, and highlights future directions in TTX research.

articles.title: The boundary between microbial detection and implant-related infection: a structured narrative review of analytical credibility, biological persistence, host response, and clinical causality.
articles.journal: Archives of orthopaedic and trauma surgery
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Unexpected microbial signals are frequently encountered in patients with orthopaedic implants who do not satisfy validated criteria for confirmed infection. The central interpretive problem is not limited to periprosthetic joint infection (PJI); it also arises in fracture-fixation and spinal instrumentation, and it involves conventional culture, sonication, histopathology, broad-range polymerase chain reaction (PCR), 16 S rRNA sequencing, and metagenomic next-generation sequencing (mNGS).

METHODS: We performed a structured narrative review of literature identified in PubMed, Embase, and Web of Science, updated through 27 June 2026. Eligible publications addressed microbial or biofilm-associated signals in orthopaedic implants without unequivocal infection at the time of sampling, or reported outcomes after unexpected positive cultures. Evidence was organized by implant type, indication for implant removal, detection method, host-response evidence, and longitudinal outcome. Particular attention was paid to the distinction between routinely removed fracture-fixation devices and failure-related arthroplasty or spinal revisions.

RESULTS: Routine removal of fracture-fixation devices provides the least confounded clinical window and demonstrates that microbial signals may be recovered from implants in the absence of recognized failure or overt infection. By contrast, arthroplasty and spinal cohorts labelled "presumed aseptic" are intrinsically confounded because pain, loosening, osteolysis, or pseudarthrosis may represent occult infection. Molecular positivity is further limited by low-biomass contamination and inability to distinguish viable organisms from relic DNA. Favorable outcomes after revision do not prove that infection was never present, because revision surgery itself may eradicate or substantially reduce an occult microbial burden.

CONCLUSIONS: Microbial detection should be interpreted through three sequential domains: analytical credibility, biological activity or persistence, and clinical causality supported by host response or implant-related pathology. "Stable coexistence" is best treated as a longitudinal clinical phenotype or testable mechanistic hypothesis, not as an established diagnostic category. This framework complements, but does not replace, validated PJI, fracture-related infection (FRI), or other implant-specific definitions.

articles.title: Heart-specific T cell responses: from antigens to disease mechanisms.
articles.abstract: The field of immunology has transformed our understanding of myocardial cell biology and paved the way for new pathophysiological concepts in cardiology. Researchers have sought to elucidate the contributions of nonspecific inflammatory mechanisms to cardiac diseases, and an increasing number of clinical trials have explored anti-inflammatory approaches in cardiovascular disease. Moreover, adaptive immune mechanisms directed to cardiac proteins released by dying cardiomyocytes have been reported across a broad spectrum of conditions, including acute myocarditis, myocardial infarction and heart failure, and have gained increasing attention. This concept of antigen-specific cardio-immune crosstalk could pave the way for a deeper understanding of tissue-specific disease mechanisms and facilitate the development of targeted interventions. However, only a small number of cardiac antigens have been identified so far, and an immunological definition of heart specificity remains elusive. This Review revisits the molecular composition of the heart from the perspective of T cells to describe the most relevant cardiac antigens identified to date, thus defining a framework for identifying novel T cell reactivities in the injured heart. Going forward, these insights might pave the way for the development of new tools to track specific T cells across various cardiac diseases, in contexts ranging from model organisms to patients.

articles.title: Built-in waste: a narrative analysis of the hidden environmental impact of battery-containing surgical devices.
authors: SAGES, EAES Sustainability in Surgery Committee
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Efforts to align surgical practice with environmental sustainability has highlighted the need to address overlooked sources of waste in surgical practice. Single-use surgical devices containing embedded batteries are widely used across specialties and are frequently discarded in clinical waste streams without separation or recycling. The environmental and regulatory implications of this practice remain poorly characterized.

METHODS: We conducted a structured exploratory mapping of battery-containing single-use surgical devices currently in clinical use across multiple surgical specialties. Devices were identified through a combination of clinical expertise, targeted web-based searches, and review of publicly available manufacturer documentation, including instructions for use (IFU), product catalogues, and technical data sheets. For each device, battery chemistry, integration type, removability, and availability of manufacturer-provided disposal instructions were recorded based solely on publicly accessible documentation.

RESULTS: A total of 23 battery-containing single-use surgical devices were identified across 9 technological categories. Battery chemistry was specified in publicly accessible documentation for 13 devices (alkaline, n = 7; lithium-based primary cells, n = 3; silver oxide, n = 3). Explicit manufacturer-provided disposal instructions were available for 9 devices (39%), partial guidance for 9 (39%), and no guidance was identified for 5 (22%). A marked disparity was observed between integration types: devices with user-removable batteries provided explicit disposal guidance in 88% of cases (7/8), whereas no sealed single-use device provided explicit guidance (0/11). In 3 of 23 devices, no publicly accessible regulatory documentation was retrievable. Regulatory analysis revealed a structural tension between mandatory separate battery collection under EU regulation 2023/1542 and the infectious waste exemption that permits routine incineration of contaminated surgical devices, resulting in systematic loss of recoverable battery materials.

CONCLUSIONS: Battery-containing surgical disposables represent a regulatory and environmental blind spot at the intersection of infection control and circular economy policy. Clearer reporting standards, improved device design, and stronger manufacturer accountability are required to reconcile patient safety with sustainable resource management. Professional societies, regulators, and procurement bodies should prioritize transparent battery disclosure and explicit end-of-life guidance as part of sustainability frameworks for surgical care.

articles.title: Comparison of mesh infection management following ventral hernia repair with poly-4-hydroxybutyrate, synthetic, and biologic mesh: a retrospective review.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Mesh infections are a feared complication of ventral hernia repair. This retrospective review compares infection characteristics and management among patients with poly-4-hydroxybutyrate (Phasix) and synthetic mesh while presenting biologic cases descriptively.

METHODS: A retrospective review was conducted of patients undergoing ventral hernia repair from 2014 to 2025. Outcomes were evaluated among patients receiving Phasix, synthetic, or biologic mesh. Primary outcomes included infection rates, microbiology, antibiotic therapy, readmission, length of stay, and need for intervention. Risk factors such as wound class, immunosuppression, and prior mesh infection were assessed.

RESULTS: A total of 407 patients underwent ventral hernia repair with Phasix (n = 47), synthetic (n = 337), and biologic (n = 23) mesh. Mesh infections developed in six patients with Phasix, seven with synthetic, and two with biologic. Of the people with mesh infections, the Phasix group demonstrated higher rates of risk factors compared to the synthetic and biologic groups: pre-existing mesh infections (33% vs. 0% vs. 0%), CDC wound class ≥  3 (83% vs. 29% vs. 0%), and immunosuppression (33% vs. 0% vs. 0%). The bacterial profile of these mesh infections includes E. coli, Proteus mirabilis, Stenotrophomonas maltophilia, and Klebsiella pneumoniae in the Phasix group, Staphylococcus, Enterococcus faecium, and Streptococcus in the synthetic group, and Staph aureus in the biologic group. Phasix infections required a mean of 36 days of antibiotic therapy versus 15 days for synthetic and 23 days for biologic mesh (p = 0.25). Readmission rates were 67, 86, and 100%, respectively (p = 0.56). Mean hospital stays were 11, 9, and 4 days (p = 0.4). No Phasix patients required mesh excision, whereas 71.4% of synthetic mesh patients and 50% of biologic mesh patients underwent mesh explantation (p = 0.04).

CONCLUSION: Infections involving poly-4-hydroxybutyrate mesh were successfully managed without mesh explantation in this series despite occurring in higher-risk patients. Because of the retrospective design, small sample size, and potential selection bias, these findings should be considered hypothesis-generating rather than evidence of superiority.

articles.title: Preoperative prediction model for critical view of safety achievement in laparoscopic cholecystectomy: a retrospective cohort study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: We developed and validated a preoperative model to predict the difficulty in achieving the critical view of safety (CVS) during laparoscopic cholecystectomy (LC).

METHODS: Patients who underwent LC with preoperative computed tomography (CT) and magnetic resonance cholangiopancreatography between January 2015 and December 2023 were retrospectively analyzed and randomly assigned to derivation and validation cohorts (8:2). Surgical difficulty was defined as failure to achieve CVS. Logistic regression analysis was used to identify independent predictors. Model performance was evaluated using the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve and Brier score.

RESULTS: Independent preoperative risk factors included age ≥ 65 years, American Society of Anesthesiologists physical status ≥ 3, preoperative endoscopic gallbladder drainage or stenting, CT attenuation of the CVS window ≥ - 26 HU, and common bile duct disruption on magnetic resonance cholangiopancreatography (all p < 0.05). The prediction score (0-13) demonstrated an area under the receiver operating characteristic curve of 0.732 (95% confidence interval 0.528-0.936) in the validation cohort. Risk stratification identified low-, moderate-, and high-risk groups with increasing rates of failure to achieve CVS.

CONCLUSIONS: This preoperative imaging-based scoring system may help predict CVS failure in LC and guide surgical decision-making.

articles.title: Oral eplerenone in first-episode acute central serous chorioretinopathy: results of a double-masked randomized trial.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Central serous chorioretinopathy (CSCR) is a pachychoroid disorder characterized by serous retinal detachment driven by choroidal vascular dysfunction and mineralocorticoid receptor (MR) overactivation. Eplerenone, a selective MR antagonist, has been proposed as a therapeutic option, although clinical evidence remains inconsistent.

METHODS: In a randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial, 44 patients with first-episode acute CSCR received either oral eplerenone (25 mg twice daily) or placebo for three months. Outcomes included best-corrected visual acuity (BCVA), central macular thickness (CMT), subretinal fluid (SRF) height, subfoveal choroidal thickness (CT), and OCT-angiography parameters of retinal and choroidal microvasculature.

RESULTS: Both groups demonstrated significant reductions in CMT and SRF over time, but SRF absorption was significantly greater in the eplerenone group at 3 months (P < 0.05). Choriocapillaris vessel density and flow index improved significantly with eplerenone (P < 0.001), while superficial, deep, and radial peripapillary plexus densities did not differ between groups. BCVA improved similarly in both groups.

CONCLUSION: Eplerenone accelerates SRF resolution and enhances choriocapillaris perfusion in acute CSCR, although visual outcomes remain comparable to placebo. Early MR antagonism may offer anatomical and microvascular benefits in CSCR management.

articles.title: FDXR upregulation by p63/p73 is a prognostic and therapeutic marker of adult T-cell leukemia/lymphoma.
articles.abstract: Infection with HTLV-1 can lead to severe diseases, including adult T-cell leukemia/lymphoma (ATL), for which current therapies are inadequate. Selective elimination of chronically infected cells requires identifying cellular markers dysregulated by HTLV-1 that can be exploited therapeutically. Combining metabolomics and proteomics analyses, we identified increased expression of the mitochondrial enzyme ferredoxin reductase (FDXR) as a hallmark of HTLV-1-infected cells. In patient cells, FDXR upregulation mirrored disease severity, was enriched in proliferating tumour cells and predicted worse ATL prognosis. Mechanistically, FDXR upregulation in ATL cells is driven by the transactivating isoforms of two p53 family members, TAp63 and TAp73, and TAp63 expression is, in turn, induced by the IRF4/BATF3 transcriptional axis. In silico drug susceptibility predictions, followed by targeted cytotoxicity, proliferation and Drug-Seq assays demonstrated that FDXR upregulation is associated with increased sensitivity of ATL cells to repurposed chemotherapeutic agents, particularly fluorouracil. Overall, our findings establish FDXR as a novel biomarker of HTLV-1-associated disease progression and ATL prognosis, elucidate its upstream molecular regulation, and highlight its predictive potential for chemotherapeutic sensitivity of ATL cells.

articles.title: Spatiotemporal heterologous vaccination relies on type I interferons at priming to enhance mucosal immunity.
articles.abstract: Parenteral vaccines against respiratory viruses poorly block infection and transmission due to suboptimal induction of mucosal immunity. In contrast, hybrid immunity and heterologous-route immunization regimens generate protective mucosal and systemic immunity. Herein, we examine how chronological order in heterologous prime/boost immunization regimens impacts immune responses using combinations of intramuscular mRNA and intranasal adjuvanted subunit vaccines against SARS-CoV-2. Enhanced long-lived mucosal and systemic immunity depended strongly on vaccine delivery sequence, with heterologous regimens administered in alternate order of routes yielding markedly distinct immune profiles with different Th-biases and divergent localizations. Immunity imparted through heterologous immunization was more durable and responsive to delayed boosting than parenteral-only regimens. Furthermore, intramuscular mRNA immunization uniquely shaped gene expression locally and systemically through IFN-I induction, allowing for enhanced responses to subsequent mucosal immunizations. These findings demonstrate that the context of initial antigen exposure-including the route of exposure and associated inflammatory signals-profoundly shapes responses to subsequent encounters. Thus, vaccine responses in antigen-experienced hosts differ fundamentally from those induced on a naive baseline, reflecting the influence of pre-existing innate and adaptive immune memory.

articles.title: Impact on mortality of inhaled nitric oxide in newborns ≤34 weeks with early hypoxemic respiratory failure: systematic review and meta-analysis.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Inhaled nitric oxide (iNO) is approved for hypoxemic respiratory failure (HRF) associated with pulmonary hypertension (PH) in term and near-term neonates; however, its use in preterm infants ≤34 weeks' gestation remains controversial, with limited and inconsistent evidence of survival benefit.

OBJECTIVE: To evaluate the association between iNO use and mortality in preterm neonates ≤34 weeks' gestation.

METHODS: A systematic review and meta-analysis were conducted following PRISMA 2020 guidelines. Major databases were searched up to October 11, 2025. Observational studies and clinical trials reporting mortality in preterm infants with early HRF treated with iNO were included. A random-effects meta-analysis was performed.

RESULTS: Nineteen studies were included in the qualitative synthesis, and six (n = 556 infants) in the meta-analysis. Study quality ranged from poor to good, with limitations related to confounding and heterogeneity. No significant reduction in mortality was observed with iNO compared with standard care (RR 0.65; 95% CI 0.29-1.48; I² = 55.7%). Infants receiving iNO were more severely ill at baseline. A positive oxygenation response was associated with improved outcomes and varied by gestational age (GA), timing of PH onset, echocardiographic confirmation, and hypoxemia severity.

CONCLUSIONS: Current evidence regarding the survival benefit of iNO in preterm infants ≤34 weeks remains inconclusive.

IMPACT: This systematic review and meta-analysis show that inhaled nitric oxide (iNO) is not associated with a consistent reduction in mortality in preterm infants ≤34 weeks at the population level. It adds evidence that outcomes are strongly influenced by clinical context, particularly, illness severity, gestational age, timing of pulmonary hypertension onset, echocardiographic confirmation, and response to therapy. These findings support a selective, phenotype-driven approach rather than routine iNO use in all preterm infants with hypoxemic respiratory failure. The results may inform clinical decision-making and highlight the need for well-designed randomized trials in this high-risk population.

articles.title: Ensemble model-based prediction of school-age asthma risk in children with food allergy.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Early-life food allergy (FA) is a major childhood asthma risk, but prospective screening tools for high-risk infants aged 0-2 are lacking, delaying early intervention.

OBJECTIVE: To develop an ensemble-learning model with cost-sensitive optimization for early asthma risk screening in FA infants (0-2 years) and provide quantitative clinical decision support.

METHODS: This prospective cohort enrolled 447 FA-confirmed infants (0-2 years), collecting 135 baseline predictors across 7 categories. After median 4.5-year follow-up to school age (≥6 years), we generated 3 clinically interpretable features and built a two-stage weighted ensemble (Random Forest, XGBoost, LightGBM, Deep Residual Networks) with cost-sensitive learning (missed-to-false-alarm ratio = 5:1) to optimize thresholds.

RESULTS: On the independent test set, AUC = 0.886, recall = 1.00 (zero missed). Decision-curve analysis showed superior net benefit across broad thresholds, including optimal cutoff 0.09. Top predictors: RSV infection, wheeze frequency, nocturnal sleep, antibiotic exposure, and rhinitis duration. Sensitivity analysis confirmed stable zero missed at cost ratios ≥5:1, indicating 5:1 was not the key driver.

CONCLUSION: The model preliminarily predicts school-age asthma risk in FA infants. Its high-recall design avoids missed diagnoses and offers quantitative references for early intervention and individualized follow-up before age 2.

IMPACT: Core finding: A performance-weighted ensemble model predicts school-age asthma in food-allergic infants (0-2 years) with an AUC of 0.886 and recall 1.00 using only clinical data. Contribution: A cost-sensitive, feature-engineered model tailored to this high-risk population; identifies RSV, wheeze grading, and antibiotic load as top predictors.

SIGNIFICANCE: Enables early, non-invasive screening before age 2, avoids missed high-risk children, and supports targeted preventive interventions in primary care.

articles.title: Angiotensin peptide and aldosterone concentrations in response to four classes of blood-pressure-lowering drugs in hypertensive patients: A randomized trial.
articles.abstract: The renin angiotensin aldosterone system (RAS) regulates blood pressure and fluid balance by a cascade of angiotensin (Ang) peptides. Antihypertensive drug classes differentially modulate this cascade. This study examined how four mechanistically distinct antihypertensive drugs affect plasma concentrations of 10 Ang peptides and aldosterone in untreated hypertensive patients. In this randomized, open-label, parallel-group study, 88 patients received 4 weeks of monotherapy with angiotensin-converting enzyme inhibitor (ACEi), angiotensin receptor blocker (ARB), calcium channel blocker (CCB), or hydrochlorothiazide (HCT). Equilibrium concentrations of 10 Ang peptides and aldosterone were quantified by LC-MS at baseline and after 4 weeks, both pre- and 4 h post-dose; drug exposure was confirmed by measured drug concentrations. Seventy-two participants completed the 4-week treatment (ACEi n = 18, ARB n = 17, CCB n = 20, HCT n = 17). The most prominent effects were seen for Ang I, Ang II, and aldosterone and were reflected in biomarkers for plasma renin activity (PRA-Q; Ang I+Ang II), ACE activity (ACE-Q; Ang II/Ang I), and the aldosterone/Ang II ratio (AA2-R). Downstream peptides showed minimal or no changes. Relative to baseline, ACEi increased Ang I and reduced ACE-Q. ARB increased Ang I and Ang II and lowered AA2-R without altering ACE-Q. CCB and HCT produced only minor changes. ACE-Q < 1.05 pM/pM identified ACEi use, and AA2-R < 0.85 pM/pM as well as Ang II > 175 pM identified ARB use. RAS-targeted monotherapy produces distinct peptide-level signatures that can be captured by Ang-derived biomarkers, supporting their potential utility for monitoring drug intake in personalized hypertension management.

articles.title: Potential under-recognition of primary aldosteronism in young adults with hypertension.
articles.abstract: The aldosterone-to-renin ratio (ARR) is the primary screening test for primary aldosteronism (PA), but it is strongly influenced by renin activity, which varies with age. Fixed ARR thresholds may therefore under-recognize PA in younger adults. We retrospectively analyzed 14,750 hypertensive patients who underwent saline infusion testing for suspected PA. An ARR of 20 was consistently used as the local reference threshold, but confirmatory testing could proceed despite ARR < 20 when clinical suspicion was high. Baseline plasma renin activity (PRA), aldosterone concentration (ALD), and ARR were measured before saline infusion. Of 13,428 patients with calculable ARR, 8703 (64.8%) underwent saline infusion testing despite ARR < 20, and 1578 had confirmed PA. Among 3966 confirmed PA patients with classifiable age-ARR data, ARR < 20 occurred in 57.5, 50.6, 35.4, and 33.2% of patients aged <35, 35-44, 45-54, and ≥55 years, respectively. Increasing age remained associated with lower odds of ARR < 20 after adjustment for sex, body mass index, blood pressure, potassium, creatinine, and a documented adrenal nodule (adjusted OR per year, 0.975; 95% CI, 0.967-0.984). The gradient persisted after restricting analyses to patients without a documented adrenal nodule, with potassium ≥3.5 mmol/L and eGFR ≥60 mL/min/1.73 m². Younger adults with confirmed PA frequently had baseline ARR values below 20, largely with relatively preserved PRA. Although residual referral bias cannot be excluded, these findings support cautious, age-informed interpretation of ALD, PRA, and ARR.

articles.title: Effect of vitamin D supplementation on serum vitamin D levels and health outcomes in pediatric population with obesity/overweight: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Because 25-hydroxy cholecalciferol is lipophilic, children with obesity/overweight are at increased risk of its deficiency, potentially leading to health issues such as compromising bone mineralization and cardiometabolic health.

OBJECTIVES: Our goal was to assess the impact of 25-hydroxy cholecalciferol supplementation on serum Vitamin D levels and various health parameters such as BMI and cardiovascular risk markers.

METHODOLOGY: Data were extracted from PubMed, Embase, and Google Scholar. Following search string was used in each database: (Vitamin D OR 25(OH)D OR cholecalciferol) AND (Obese OR Overweight) AND (randomized trial OR RCT OR intervention) AND (children OR adolescent OR pediatric). Clinical trials assessing the impact of 25-hydroxy cholecalciferol D supplementation in pediatric populations with overweight or obesity, regardless of formulation, dosage, or duration, were included. A total of 24 studies were included in the systematic review, of which 11 randomized controlled trials were eligible for meta-analysis. The included studies' quality was evaluated using the Cochrane Risk of Bias (ROB-2) tool. Primary outcome was serum Vitamin D levels while secondary outcomes include cardiovascular risk markers, lipid profile, insulin sensitivity, and change in BMI. Follow-up done at 8 weeks, 12 weeks, 24 weeks, 26 weeks, 3 months, 6 months, and 12 months.

RESULTS: Supplementing with 25-hydroxy cholecalciferol significantly raised the levels of serum vitamin D in children with obesity/overweight. No adverse events occurred following supplementation. Decrease in BMI, serum triglycerides and inflammatory markers were observed but its effects on metabolism and cardiovascular health remained insignificant. According to meta-analysis, vitamin D supplementation (interventional) arm group differed from the placebo by a standardized mean difference of 3.12 ng/ml (95% CI:1.72-4.52).

CONCLUSION: Vitamin D supplementation in children with overweight /obesity correct the deficiency and significantly raise Vitamin D levels with no adverse events. To assess effective therapies to enhance metabolic and cardiovascular outcomes in the pediatric population with overweight/obesity, new trials should be conducted.

articles.title: Long-term outcomes of preterm infants admitted to single-family rooms versus an open-bay neonatal intensive care unit: A randomized controlled trial.
articles.journal: Journal of perinatology : official journal of the California Perinatal Association
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To compare long-term outcomes of preterm infants in single-family room (SFR) vs. open-bay (OB) neonatal intensive care unit (NICU).

STUDY DESIGN: This randomized controlled trial took place in a tertiary NICU from April 2018 to June 2019. Infants <31 weeks gestation or ≤1500 grams birthweight were randomly assigned upon admission to SFR or OB. The primary outcome was death or neurodevelopmental impairment (NDI; cerebral palsy, language delay, cognitive delay, blindness, or deafness) at 36 months corrected age. Secondary outcomes were mortality, NDI components, and safety measures.

RESULTS: Of 85 infants (43 SFR, 42 OB), there was no difference in primary outcome (40.5% SFR vs. 47.4% OB, p = 0.644). Secondary outcomes did not differ except mortality, which was lower in SFR (1/41, 2.4%) than OB (8/42, 19.0%), p = 0.029.

CONCLUSIONS: Composite outcome of death/NDI at 36 months corrected age was similar; however, reduction in mortality was noted in SFR. This trial was registered 6 Mar 2019 with ClinicalTrials.gov, NCT03867669 ( https://clinicaltrials.gov/search?cond=NCT03867669 ).

articles.title: Lenacapavir scale-up: a window to strengthen sexually transmitted infection services.
Evidence of Integrated Care for Critically Ill Children Through a Linguistic Examination of Progress Notes.
articles.abstract: A child's critical care hospitalization is stressful for families, immersing them in a highly technical and unfamiliar environment in which they encounter multiple healthcare providers. Medical decisions regarding the child's care must frequently be made, sometimes on relatively short notice. Providers in the pediatric critical care unit (PICU) have primary responsibility to care for the child and communicate with the family. Palliative care (PC) providers may be consulted for their expertise in the holistic care of the child and family and to elicit the family's goals of care for the child. This study's purpose was to characterize the linguistic properties of PICU and PC providers' progress notes and improve goal-concordant care by conducting a secondary analysis of their daily notes during a child's terminal critical care admission in a 467-bed quaternary pediatric hospital system in the midwestern United States. Notes were partitioned into PICU and PC notes, and their linguistic characteristics were quantified using Linguistic Inquiry and Word Count software, which returns the percentage of words in a text for over 90 parameters. Differences were analyzed using the Wilcoxon signed‑rank test. We present key differences between documented wording by PICU and PC providers, including linguistic convergence in most domains over the course of a child's terminal critical care admission. We also note that such convergence must be reestablished with each admission. We attribute linguistic differences to distinctive roles and expertise.

articles.title: Enhanced electrochemically-directed oligonucleotide synthesis via porous silica thin-film for DNA data storage.
articles.abstract: DNA-based data storage has emerged as a promising alternative for long-term information archiving and its implementation accelerates the development for on-chip large scale oligonucleotide synthesis. Among various technological routes, electrochemically directed synthesis offers exceptional synthesis-site density thanks to its compatibility with semiconductor microfabrication processes. Yet increasing density typically comes at the expense of reduced per-site oligonucleotide yield, compromising the practical utility of these synthesis platforms for reliable data recovery. Here we report a porous silica thin-film strategy in order to address this fundamental trade-off by substantially increasing the effective on-chip synthesis surface area while preserving spatial confinement during electrochemically generated acid-mediated deblocking. The porous thin-film, fabricated via a sacrificial templating approach, forms an interconnected high-surface-area porous network that enables efficient reagent transport and stable electrochemical control. The presented method enables an areal oligonucleotide yield of more than 1821 pmol/cm², which represents more than 11-fold enhancement compared to a planar silica substrate. Moreover, this platform achieves comparable error statistics of deletion, insertion and substitution compared to other laboratory-built DNA data writing systems. Using this platform, we demonstrated parallel synthesis of 121-nt oligonucleotides and successful encoding, writing and error-corrected recovery of digital information. These results establish a scalable strategy for high-yield on-chip DNA synthesis and provide a practical pathway towards integrated molecular data storage systems.

articles.title: Akabane virus reprograms the PKR-eIf2α-SGs/PBs axis to fine-tune cap-snatching efficiency.
articles.abstract: Akabane virus (AKAV) initiates transcription in the cytoplasm via the cap-snatching mechanism. Cytoplasmic host mRNAs act as the primary cap donors, whereas the impact of their subcellular localization on the cap-snatching process remains unclear. Herein, we demonstrate that the AKAV-induced disassembly of polysomes, stress granules (SGs), and processing bodies (PBs) collectively facilitates viral cap-snatching. Mechanistically, AKAV infection activates the PKR-eIF2α signaling axis, leading to the disassembly of polysomes and subsequent translational shutoff. Intriguingly, the viral N protein disassembles SGs and PBs by competing for sequestered RNAs within these granules, whereas mutations of its RNA-binding residues abolish this activity. Moreover, PKR-eIF2α inhibition impairs AKAV replication and cap-snatching efficacy. Whereas, inhibition of SGs via G3BP1 knockdown or chemical agents significantly enhances viral replication and cap-snatching efficiency, indicating that polysomes and SGs disassembly favor caps acquisition. Additionally, N protein-mediated PBs disassembly protects mRNA from degradation, and PBs inhibition enhances cap-snatching. Taken together, AKAV has evolved a sophisticated strategy to reprogram mRNA distribution to create an optimal cellular environment for viral cap-snatching.

articles.title: [Acupuncture regulates the Th17/Treg axis for chronic spontaneous urticaria: a randomized controlled trial].
articles.journal: Zhongguo zhen jiu = Chinese acupuncture & moxibustion
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To observe the clinical efficacy of acupuncture for chronic spontaneous urticaria (CSU) and its effect on the helper T cell 17(Th17)/regulatory T cell (Treg) axis.

METHODS: Eighty CSU patients were randomly divided into an observation group (40 cases, 2 cases dropped out) and a control group (40 cases, 2 cases dropped out). The observation group received acupuncture at bilateral Jianyu (LI15), Shousanli (LI10), Quchi (LI11), Pianli (LI6), Xuehai (SP10), Zusanli (ST36) and Sanyinjiao (SP6), each session lasting for 30 min, 3 times per week. The control group received oral ebastine tablets, 10 mg each time, once daily. Both groups were treated for 8 weeks. The 7-day urticaria activity score (UAS7), dermatology life quality index (DLQI) score and Hamilton anxiety scale (HAMA) score were observed, peripheral blood Th17 and Treg cell proportions, and serum levels of interleukin (IL)-17, IL-23, IL-10, and IL-35 were detected, and the ratio of Th17/Treg was calculated before and after treatment in the two groups.

RESULTS: After treatment, the UAS7, DLQI and HAMA scores in the two groups were decreased compared with those before treatment (P<0.05), and the scores in the observation group were lower than those in the control group (P<0.05). After treatment, the peripheral blood Th17 cell proportions, the ratios of Th17/Treg and serum levels of IL-17, IL-23 in the two groups were decreased compared with those before treatment (P<0.05), those indexes in the observation group were lower than those in the control group (P<0.05). After treatment, the peripheral blood Treg cell proportions, and serum levels of IL-10, IL-35 in the two groups were increased compared with those before treatment (P<0.05), those indexes in the observation group were higher than those in the control group (P<0.05).

CONCLUSION: Acupuncture can effectively alleviate the symptoms of CSU, and its mechanism of action may be related to the regulation of the Th17/Treg axis.

articles.title: [Herbal cake-separated moxibustion combined with Bufei Tongluo decoction in treatment of diabetes-induced pulmonary fibrosis of qi-yin deficiency with blood stagnation: a randomized controlled trial].
articles.journal: Zhongguo zhen jiu = Chinese acupuncture & moxibustion
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To observe the clinical efficacy of herbal cake-separated moxibustion combined with Bufei Tongluo decoction on diabetes-induced pulmonary fibrosis (DiPF) of qi-yin deficiency with blood stagnation.

METHODS: A total of 102 DiPF patients were randomly divided into an observation group (51 cases, 1 case dropped out) and a control group (51 cases, 1 case was eliminated and 1 case dropped out). In the control group, Bufei Tongluo decoction was administered, one dose per day; and in the observation group, herbal cake-separated moxibustion was operated at Danzhong (CV17) and bilateral Feishu (BL13), Gaohuang (BL43), Zusanli (ST36), etc. on the basis of the treatment in the control group, once every two days, three times a week. The interventions in the two groups were operated continuously for 8 weeks. The TCM symptom score, high-resolution CT (HRCT) score, the 6-minute walk test (6MWT), the indexes of pulmonary function test (the percentage of measured values of the total lung capacity [TLC], forced vital capacity [FVC], and lung carbon monoxide diffusion capacity [DLCO] relative to predicted values), and the levels of serological markers (hydroxyproline [Hyp], interleukin-10 [IL-10] and transforming growth factor-β [TGF-β]) were compared before and after treatment in the twogroups. The clinical efficacy and safety of both groups were evaluated.

RESULTS: After treatment, the scores of each symptom (dry cough with little phlegm, shortness of breath and fatigue, dry mouth and throat, feverish sensations in the palms and soles, and stabbing pain in the chest and hypochondriac region) and the total scores of TCM syndrome, HRCT scores, and the levels of serum Hyp, IL-10, and TGF-β in both groups decreased in comparison with those before treatment (P<0.05); and the scores of dry cough with little phlegm, shortness of breath and fatigue, stabbing pain in the chest and hypochondriac region, the total score of TCM syndrome, HRCT score, the levels of serum IL-10 and TGF-β in the observation group were lower than those in the control group (P<0.05). After treatment, the 6MWT and the percentages of measured values of TLC, FVC and DLCO relative to predicted values in both groups increased in comparison with those before treatment (P<0.05); and the percentages of measured values of TLC, FVC and DLCO relative to predicted values in the observation group were higher than those in the control group (P<0.05). The clinical efficacy of the observation group was superior to the control group (P<0.05). The total effective rate in the observation group was 98.0% (49/50), without statistically significant difference compared with the control group (87.8% [43/49], P>0.05). There was no statistically significant difference in the incidence of adverse reactions between the two groups (P>0.05).

CONCLUSION: Herbal cake-separated moxibustion combined with Bufei Tongluo decoction can effectively alleviate clinical symptoms, improve pulmonary function, and reduce inflammatory response and fibrosis in DiPF patients of qi-yin deficiency with blood stagnation.

articles.title: [Tiaoshen acupuncture for shift work circadian rhythm sleep-wake disorder: a randomized controlled trial].
articles.journal: Zhongguo zhen jiu = Chinese acupuncture & moxibustion
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To observe the clinical efficacy of Tiaoshen (regulating the mind) acupuncture for shift work circadian rhythm sleep-wake disorder (SWD).

METHODS: A total of 84 patients with shift work circadian rhythm SWD were randomly divided into a Tiaoshen acupuncture group (42 cases, 1 case dropped out) and a non-meridian non-acupoint group (42 cases, 2 cases dropped out). Both groups received sleep health education as basic treatment. The Tiaoshen acupuncture group was treated with Tiaoshen acupuncture, Baihui (GV20), bilateral Fengchi (GB20), Touwei (ST8), Shenmen (HT7), Zusanli (ST36), as well as auricular points Shenmen (TF4), Xin (CO15) were selected. The non-meridian non-acupoint group received shallow needling at non-meridian non-acupoint points, as well as non-related auricular points. Both groups were treated 3 times per week for 4 weeks. Before treatment, after treatment, and after 3 months of treatment completion, the morningness-eveningness questionnaire (MEQ), Pittsburgh sleep quality index (PSQI), self-rating anxiety scale (SAS), and self-rating depression scale (SDS) were used to assess the sleep and emotional status in the two groups.

RESULTS: Compared before treatment, the MEQ scores were increased after treatment and after 3 months of treatment completion in the two groups (P<0.001, P<0.01); the scores of PSQI, SAS and SDS were decreased after treatment and after 3 months of treatment completion in the Tiaoshen acupuncture group (P<0.001), and the scores of SAS and SDS were decreased after treatment in the non-meridian non-acupoint group (P<0.01). After treatment and after 3 months of treatment completion, the MEQ scores in the Tiaoshen acupuncture group were higher than those in the non-meridian non-acupoint group (P<0.001), and the PSQI scores in the Tiaoshen acupuncture group were lower than those in the non-meridian non-acupoint group (P<0.001); after treatment, the SAS and SDS scores in the Tiaoshen acupuncture group were lower than those in the non-meridian non-acupoint group (P<0.05, P<0.01).

CONCLUSION: Tiaoshen acupuncture can effectively improve the sleep-wake rhythm and sleep quality of patients with shift work circadian rhythm SWD, alleviate the accompanying anxiety and depression.

articles.title: [Target trial emulation in acupuncture-moxibustion clinical research: from real-world data to causal inference].
articles.journal: Zhongguo zhen jiu = Chinese acupuncture & moxibustion
articles.abstract: In order to elucidate the application value and implementation pathway of target trial emulation (TTE) in clinical research of acupuncture and moxibustion, this article reviews the key methodological components of TTE, including data readiness assessment, target trial protocol specification, treatment strategy allocation, alignment of time zero (T0), definition of outcomes and follow-up, estimation-based target choice, control of confounding and censoring, diagnostic and sensitivity analyses, and reporting standards. Key operational points are also summarized based on real-world study (RWS) cases of acupuncture and moxibustion. Using a hypothetical randomized controlled trial (RCT) as the reference, TTE translates a research question into an executable observational study protocol, thereby helping to address pre-control design bias, enhance research transparency and strengthen causal interpretation. The application of TTE in acupuncture- moxibustion research should rely on standardized case registration system and emphasize the structured collection of real-world data. Findings from TTE studies may serve as an important complement to RCT evidence, but they remain the limitations such as data quality, unmeasured confounding factors, and the difficulty in simulating sham-acupuncture controls. Hence, these findings should be interpreted and applied with caution.

articles.title: Novel Compound Heterozygous ATAD3A Variants in Harel-Yoon Syndrome With Congenital Cataracts and Dilated Cardiomyopathy.
articles.journal: American journal of medical genetics. Part A
articles.abstract: Harel-Yoon syndrome is a rare mitochondrial disorder caused by pathogenic variants in ATAD3A, typically characterized by neonatal respiratory insufficiency, cataracts, developmental delay, hypotonia, and cerebellar atrophy. We report a pediatric patient with compound heterozygous missense variants in ATAD3A (c.655C>T, p.R219C and c.980G>C, p.R327P) who presented with an atypical phenotype manifested as early-onset congenital cataracts and progressive dilated cardiomyopathy. Notably the patient did not show typical neurological manifestations nor the cardiac presentations of hypertrophic cardiomyopathy. The maternally inherited c.655C>T variant was absent from population databases, while paternally inherited c.980G>C was previously associated with Harel-Yoon syndrome. In silico protein structure modeling demonstrated that the mutant ATAD3A hexamer showed a looser and more disorganized conformation compared to that of the wild-type, suggesting functional impairment. This case expands the phenotypic spectrum of ATAD3A-related disorders and highlights the importance of long-term surveillance in patients with ATAD3A variants, even in the absence of classical neurological features. In addition, our findings support the inclusion of ATAD3A in the genetic differential diagnosis for patients with congenital cataracts and cardiomyopathy.

articles.title: Clinical characteristics and outcomes of congenital diaphragmatic hernia (CDH) in neonates in an Australian neonatal intensive care unit network: a population-based cohort study.
Diabetes and Family Out-of-Pocket Medical Spending Relative to Income Across Adult Age Groups in the United States.
GLP-1 Receptor Agonists and Thromboembolic Risk in Patients With Atrial Fibrillation or Flutter and Type 2 Diabetes: A Propensity Score-Matched Cohort Study.
Comparative Cardiorenal Efficacy and Safety of SGLT2 Inhibitors and Finerenone in Chronic Kidney Disease With Type 2 Diabetes: A Systematic Review and Network Meta-Analysis.
articles.abstract:
AIMS: No randomized trial has compared SGLT2 inhibitors with finerenone in chronic kidney disease (CKD) with Type 2 diabetes. We estimated their comparative cardiorenal efficacy and safety.

MATERIALS AND METHODS: MEDLINE, Embase, CENTRAL and trial registries were searched from inception to August 2026 for placebo-controlled outcome trials. Hazard ratios (HRs) were pooled in a frequentist random-effects network meta-analysis, and the between-class contrast was derived indirectly through placebo. Risk of bias followed RoB 2 and certainty followed CINeMA.

RESULTS: Ten trial datasets formed a star network without closed loops. Versus placebo, both classes reduced kidney function progression (SGLT2 inhibitors HR: 0.64, 95% CI: 0.56-0.73; finerenone 0.84, 0.77-0.92) and heart-failure hospitalization (0.61, 0.53-0.69; 0.78, 0.66-0.92). Indirectly, SGLT2 inhibitors were favoured for kidney function progression (0.76, 0.64-0.90) and heart-failure hospitalization (0.77, 0.63-0.95), with no significant difference for atherothrombotic events or mortality. The kidney contrast remained significant after excluding high-risk-of-bias datasets, restricting to dedicated CKD trials and applying a uniform endpoint; the heart-failure contrast did not persist in dedicated CKD trials. Finerenone increased hyperkalemia without increasing acute kidney injury. Certainty was low or very low for every between-class comparison.

CONCLUSIONS: SGLT2 inhibitors and finerenone both provide cardiorenal protection and appear complementary rather than interchangeable. Indirect differences favouring SGLT2 inhibitors derive from a loop-free network with unverifiable transitivity and low certainty; they are hypothesis-generating and should not be used to rank the agents. Safety domains are not reported comparably across classes.

TRIAL REGISTRATION: CRD420261439899.

articles.title: Electrophysiologic Demyelinating Features Are Common in Vasculitic Neuropathy: A Cohort of Biopsy-Confirmed Cases.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION/AIMS: Electrophysiologic features suggestive of demyelination have been reported in vasculitic neuropathy, complicating the diagnostic process, but their frequency is unknown. We aimed to determine the prevalence of demyelinating features, including fulfillment of European Academy of Neurology/Peripheral Nerve Society (EAN/PNS) electrophysiological criteria for demyelination in suspected CIDP, in a cohort of patients with biopsy-confirmed vasculitic neuropathy.

METHODS: Clinical data and nerve conduction studies from patients with biopsy-confirmed vasculitic neuropathy (definite or probable) were retrospectively analyzed in two centers in France between 2014 and 2020.

RESULTS: Sixty-three patients were included (mean age 58 ± 16 years; 30% were male), including 28 with non-systemic vasculitic neuropathy (NSVN) and 35 with systemic vasculitic neuropathy (SVN). Pain and sensory disturbances were present in all patients, whereas motor deficits occurred in 73% of patients. The predominant electrophysiological pattern was a symmetrical distal polyneuropathy (n = 26). Twenty-seven (42.9%) patients showed demyelinating NCS abnormalities, and 11 (17.5%) patients fulfilled the EAN/PNS criteria for demyelination. Motor conduction block was the most frequent demyelinating abnormality, followed by prolonged F-wave latency. Demyelinating abnormalities were present in 7.1% of NSVN patients and 25.7% of SVN patients, with no statistically significant difference between groups.

DISCUSSION: Electrophysiological patterns suggestive of demyelination are common in vasculitic neuropathy. Nevertheless, most patients presented with pain and a symmetrical distal polyneuropathy, a phenotype not typically associated with demyelinating neuropathy. Future studies integrating detailed clinical data may help identify key diagnostic features and improve recognition despite potentially misleading electrodiagnostic findings.

articles.title: Glycaemic Management and Pregnancy Outcomes in HNF1A-MODY.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Birthweight of HNF1A-affected offspring is largely similar to the background population with rarely reported cases of large for gestational age (LGA) and neonatal hypoglycaemia (NH). Conventional clinical management of pre-gestational diabetes appears to be sufficient in managing HNF1A-affected women in pregnancy. This study aims to evaluate pregnancy outcomes and review glucose management in a cohort with HNF1A-MODY.

METHODOLOGY: This is a retrospective review of 183 offspring (142 maternal and 41 paternal) of 73 parents with confirmed HNF1A-MODY. Data were obtained from maternal/paternal recall and/or review of maternity charts. Variables included glycaemic treatment, HbA1c, fructosamine, gestational weight gain, neonatal birthweight, gestation, incidence of NH, and offspring genotype status.

RESULTS: Maternal offspring had a higher incidence of LGA (39.4% vs. 15%, p = 0.012). LGA was associated with maternal dysglycaemia independent of neonatal mutation status. Rate of LGA was lower with insulin treatment compared to diet (35.1% vs. 64.3%, p = 0.004). Subgroup analysis of insulin treated pregnancies showed LGA was associated with higher mean capillary glucose (p = 0.005) (n = 34), third trimester insulin doses (p = 0.04) (n = 33), HbA1c (p = 0.04) (n = 34) and maternal gestational weight gain (p = 0.011) (n = 31). Weight adjusted total daily dose of insulin was 0.61 unit/kg/day (0.49-0.62) in Trimester 3 (n = 26). Persistent NH was more prevalent in maternally inherited cases with dysglycaemia (8 vs. 0 offspring, p = 0.067).

CONCLUSION: Large birthweight and NH occur in offspring of parents with HNF1A mutations. These sequelae are more frequent and clinically significant in maternally inherited cases. It is prudent to counsel relevant obstetric and neonatal teams around specific perinatal concerns to reduce potential morbidity.

articles.title: Prognostic Value of Pulmonary Elastance Methods in HFrEF: A Comparative Study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Pulmonary vascular resistance (PVR) is commonly used to quantify right ventricular (RV) afterload in heart failure with reduced ejection fraction (HFrEF), yet it reflects primarily the steady component of pulmonary vascular load. Simplified pulmonary arterial elastance indices may better characterise the integrated arterial load experienced by the RV. The comparative prognostic value of different elastance formulations in HFrEF remains incompletely defined.

METHOD: This retrospective study included 352 patients with HFrEF who underwent right heart catheterisation between 2018 and 2022. Pulmonary elastance was calculated using three simplified formulations: systolic pressure-based elastance (EasPAP=sPAP/SV), transpulmonary gradient-based elastance (EaTPG=[mPAP PCWP]/SV), and pulse pressure-based elastance (EaPP=PP/SV), together with their indexed forms. Discriminatory performance was evaluated using receiver operating characteristic curve analysis. Associations with all-cause mortality were assessed using univariate and multivariable Cox regression analyses adjusted for age, New York Heart Association functional class, and renal function. Subgroup analyses by PVR (<3 vs ≥3 Wood units [WU]) and combined PVR-EaPP phenotype analyses were performed.

RESULTS: During a median follow-up of 23 months, 139 patients (39.5%) died. In multivariable models, EasPAP (adjusted hazard ratio [HR] 1.31; p=0.002), EaPP (adjusted HR 1.63; p=0.005), and their indexed forms remained independently associated with mortality, whereas EaTPG-based formulations did not. In patients with PVR <3 WU, EasPAP and EaPP demonstrated stronger associations with mortality than in the high-PVR subgroup. In the combined phenotype analysis, elevated EaPP identified increased mortality risk irrespective of PVR category.

CONCLUSIONS: In patients with HFrEF undergoing right heart catheterisation, simplified pulsatile elastance indices, particularly EasPAP and EaPP, were independently associated with all-cause mortality. Notably, elevated EaPP identified higher-risk patients even in the absence of elevated PVR, suggesting that resistance-based metrics alone may not fully capture RV afterload. Prospective validation is warranted.

articles.title: The Quo Vadis for COVADIS Diagnostic Criteria.
authors: Coronary Vasomotor Disorders International Study Group (COVADIS)
articles.abstract: The Coronary Vasomotor Disorders International Study group (COVADIS) developed the diagnostic criteria for vasospastic angina and microvascular angina more than 8 years ago. This article critically reappraises these criteria (Latin: quid fecisti - what has been done) and proposes the strategies for their advancement (Latin: Quo Vadis - where are you are going?). Although the criteria have some limitations, they remain relevant considering their multifaceted clinical perspective including the presence of symptoms, myocardial ischaemia and objective evidence of coronary vasomotor dysfunction. To improve the criteria, the following strategic directions (Quo Vadis) are proposed, (1) optimising invasive functional coronary angiography assessment - the benchmark diagnostic investigation for coronary vasomotor disorders, (2) diagnosing mixed macrovascular and microvascular coronary vasomotor disorders, (3) advancing non-invasive coronary vasomotor assessment methods, (4) linking coronary vasomotor disorder criteria to clinical outcomes, (5) evaluating coronary vasomotor disorders in the presence of obstructive coronary artery disease, and (6) global partnering of coronary vasomotor disorder initiatives in national networks and patient forums. These strategies will improve the diagnostic approaches to coronary vasomotor disorders thereby facilitating the evolution of the COVADIS Diagnostic Criteria and thus management of these elusive disorders.

articles.title: Coronary Revascularisation Strategies for Patients with Obstructive Coronary Artery Disease Requiring Lung Transplantation: A Narrative Review and Single-Centre Experience.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Lung transplant (LTx) candidates often have multiple risk factors for coronary artery disease (CAD), which was previously considered a contraindication to transplantation. Improvements in revascularisation techniques have broadened transplant eligibility; however, because available evidence is based on small and heterogeneous cohorts, the optimal revascularisation strategy remains unclear.

METHOD: We conducted a literature review and describe our centre's experience with current approaches to revascularisation in LTx candidates with obstructive CAD.

RESULTS: The literature review identified 174 studies in the initial search, of which 29 studies were considered relevant. However, only six retrospective studies directly compared percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) and coronary artery bypass graft surgery (CABG), comprising 376 revascularised patients. In some cohorts, CABG was associated with longer ventilation time and longer intensive care unit (ICU) stay and overall hospital stay, although this finding was not consistent across all studies. At our centre, 20 patients underwent concomitant CABG, and 11 underwent PCI within 12 months before transplant listing, after obstructive CAD was diagnosed during transplant assessment. Procedure time in patients undergoing concomitant CABG was significantly longer (1.2 hours; p<0.05); however, all patients in this group underwent bilateral transplantation. Three patients in the PCI group experienced postoperative coronary events, and overall mortality was higher in this group. There were no differences in other outcomes, including ICU and overall length of stay.

CONCLUSIONS: These findings highlight the heterogeneity and complexity of this patient cohort. Although no patients who underwent CABG experienced postoperative coronary events, the limited published evidence does not support a single preferred revascularisation strategy for patients being considered for lung transplantation. Case-by-case management guided by a multidisciplinary team is therefore warranted.

articles.title: [Translated article] Depression, stress and medication adherence in patients with type 2 diabetes: A crosssectional study in Mexico.
articles.journal: Farmacia hospitalaria : organo oficial de expresion cientifica de la Sociedad Espanola de Farmacia Hospitalaria
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To describe the level of adherence to pharmacological treatment and explore, using a bivariate analysis, its unadjusted association with mental health variables (depression and stress) in patients with type 2.

METHOD: A cross-sectional study was conducted with 326 patients with T2D and beneficiaries of a multidisciplinary center of a social security institution in Morelos, Mexico. Sociodemographic, clinical, and mental health variables such as stress and depression were evaluated, in addition to adherence to pharmacological treatment in patients with T2D, using instruments with evidence of validity and reliability. Bivariate statistical analysis was used to evaluate the association between the variables of interest and pharmacological adherence.

RESULTS: A statistically significant association was found between pharmacological adherence with depression (χ2 = 7.3, p = 0.01; OR = 0.28, p = 0.01), and with depression and stress as concomitance (OR = 0.18, p = 0.02). No statistically significant associations were found with sociodemographic factors.

CONCLUSIONS: In this cross-sectional study, a bivariate association was observed between depression-and its co-occurrence with stress-and pharmacological adherence. These findings should be interpreted with caution and require confirmation through studies with adjusted analyses.

articles.title: Soft drink ketosis as the initial presentation of ketosis-prone type 2 diabetes mellites in an adult with intellectual disability.

177Lu-Prostate-specific Membrane Antigen Prior to Stereotactic Ablative Radiotherapy in Oligorecurrent Prostate Cancer: Secondary and Exploratory End Point Results from the Randomized Phase 2 LUNAR Trial.
articles.abstract: The phase 2 randomized LUNAR trial previously demonstrated that neoadjuvant 177Lu-PNT2002 before stereotactic body radiotherapy (SBRT) significantly improved progression-free survival (PFS) in patients with oligorecurrent hormone-sensitive prostate cancer (orHSPC). We report updated efficacy and safety outcomes with extended follow-up. Patients with prostate-specific membrane antigen (PSMA) positron emission tomography/computed tomography (PET/CT)-detected orHSPC and one to five metastatic lesions amenable to SBRT were randomized 1:1 to SBRT alone or two cycles of neoadjuvant 177Lu-PNT2002 followed by SBRT. The primary end point was PFS, defined as new lesions on PSMA PET/CT, initiation of salvage hormonal therapy, or death. Secondary end points included hormonal therapy-free survival (HT-FS) and 24-mo progression-free status. Exploratory end points included polymetastatic PFS (poly-PFS), castration-resistant disease-free survival (CRFS), and conventional imaging progression-free survival (CT-PFS). Between September 2022 and November 2023, 92 patients were randomized to SBRT alone (n = 47) or 177Lu-PNT2002 plus SBRT (n = 45). At a median follow-up of 31.9 mo, 177Lu-PNT2002 significantly improved PFS (median 17.6 vs 7.4 mo; hazard ratio [HR] 0.38, 95% confidence interval [CI] = 0.23-0.61; p < 0.001) and HT-FS (HR 0.57, 95% CI = 0.34-0.95; p = 0.03). Exploratory analyses demonstrated improved poly-PFS (HR 0.28, 95% CI = 0.08-1.03; p = 0.04), CRFS (HR 0.13, 95% CI = 0.02-1.10; p = 0.03), and CT-PFS (HR 0.46, 95% CI = 0.19-1.09; p = 0.07). No new safety signals were observed. With extended follow-up, neoadjuvant 177Lu-PNT2002 before SBRT produced durable improvements in PFS and HT-FS. While poly-PFS, CRFS, and CT-PFS were exploratory end points, their improvement provides hypothesis-generating evidence that the addition of radioligand therapy to SBRT may alter disease trajectory beyond delaying PSMA PET/CT-detected recurrence.

articles.title: [Infectious disease prevention: PAPPS update 2026].
authors: Grupo de Prevención de Enfermedades Infecciosas del PAPPS
articles.abstract: Vaccination is one of the most effective preventive measures against infectious diseases and should be considered an essential intervention throughout life. Prevention through vaccination in adults is part of a healthy lifestyle. Vaccination needs vary according to age, health conditions, the presence of chronic diseases, or immunosuppression, making it crucial to keep vaccination schedules up-to-date at every stage of life. Despite the proven benefits of vaccines, adult vaccination coverage remains below recommended levels. In this context, the role of healthcare professionals is key in providing information, answering questions, and promoting vaccination, thus contributing to disease prevention and improving the population's quality of life. The 2026 update incorporates the main changes related to indications, modifications to vaccination schedules, and new vaccines included in the adult vaccination schedule. It also reinforces the importance of vaccination in at-risk groups, pregnant women, and healthcare professionals, and expands the approach to traveler vaccination. Finally, the «One Health» perspective is highlighted, which recognizes vaccination as a fundamental tool for improving population health, reducing antibiotic use, and preventing the emergence of bacterial resistance. For more detailed information on individual vaccines, especially those that have not required updating, please refer to the documents «Prevention of Infectious Diseases: Vaccine Update, 2022» and «Vaccine Update 2024».

articles.title: Navigating machine learning and classical statistics in sarcopenia screening for community-dwelling older women.
articles.journal: Journal of the Formosan Medical Association = Taiwan yi zhi
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Machine learning (ML) is increasingly used for sarcopenia screening, but its added value over conventional models remains uncertain when datasets are moderately sized and predictors are few. We compared logistic regression (LR) with five ML algorithms in older women.

METHODS: We analyzed 433 community-dwelling women aged ≥65 years. Sarcopenia was defined as handgrip strength <18 kg and bioelectrical impedance-derived appendicular skeletal muscle mass index <5.7 kg/m2. LR, XGBoost, random forest, a CART decision tree, support vector machine (SVM), and multilayer perceptron (MLP) were evaluated using stratified five-fold cross-validation and pooled out-of-fold predictions. Analyses included a full nine-predictor set and a previously identified set comprising age, height, and calf circumference. A sensitivity analysis used nested cross-validation for hyperparameter selection.

RESULTS: Mean age was 76.2 ± 7.0 years, and 105 women (24.2%) had sarcopenia. In the primary nine-predictor analysis, LR and XGBoost achieved areas under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUROCs) of 0.845 and 0.838, respectively, followed by random forest at 0.832. SVM, CART, and MLP showed lower discrimination. The three-predictor LR model achieved an AUROC of 0.852. With nested tuning, full-model AUROCs were numerically similar for LR (0.835), SVM (0.843), and MLP (0.840); corresponding three-predictor AUROCs were 0.865, 0.850, and 0.852.

CONCLUSION: LR remained competitive with the evaluated ML models, and the previously identified three-predictor model showed good discrimination. Relative performance depended on model configuration and training procedures. Independent external validation is required before clinical implementation.

articles.title: Inadvertent Coronary Sinus Cannulation During Central Venous Catheter Placement in a Liver Transplant Recipient with Persistent Left Superior Vena Cava: A Case Report.
articles.abstract: Persistent left superior vena cava (PLSVC) is the most common thoracic venous anomaly and is usually asymptomatic. Central venous catheterization through a PLSVC can be challenging, and inadvertent advancement of catheters into the coronary sinus may result in arrhythmias, perforation, thrombosis, or inaccurate hemodynamic measurements. We report a case of coronary sinus cannulation by a left internal jugular dialysis catheter in a liver transplant recipient with previously unrecognized PLSVC. Initial chest radiography suggested catheter termination within a duplicated left superior vena cava; however, intraoperative transesophageal echocardiography (TEE) demonstrated the catheter tip within the coronary sinus. The catheter was withdrawn under direct echocardiographic guidance, avoiding potential complications. This case highlights the utility of intraoperative TEE for definitive localization of central venous catheters in patients with anomalous thoracic venous anatomy.

articles.title: Risk Factors and Clinical Predictors of Urinary Tract Infections in Kidney Transplant Recipients: A Retrospective Single-Center Study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Urinary tract infections (UTIs) remain a significant complication following kidney transplantation (KT), contributing to morbidity and potential graft-related complications. This study investigates the incidence, risk factors, recurrence patterns, and multidrug-resistant (MDR) characteristics of UTIs in KT recipients.

METHODS: A retrospective cohort study was performed, including 236 KT recipients transplanted between 2016 and 2023 at the University of Debrecen. Patients were classified according to UTI occurrence: 131 patients remained UTI-free, while 105 patients developed at least one microbiologically confirmed UTI. A total of 234 UTI episodes were analyzed, including 177 non-MDR and 57 MDR episodes. Clinical, donor-related, operative, viral, and immunosuppressive variables were evaluated. Univariate and multivariate logistic regression analyses were performed to identify independent predictors.
