RESULTS: UTIs occurred in 44.5% of recipients. Among 234 UTI episodes, 149 (63.7%) were recurrent and 57 (24.4%) were MDR. Patient-level risk factors associated with UTI occurrence included older age (P = .036), female sex (P < .001), higher Charlson Comorbidity Index (P = .040), and increased Kidney Donor Profile Index (P = .030). Prolonged hospitalization was independently associated with UTI occurrence and recurrence (P = .004 and P = .001, respectively). After multivariate adjustment, Extended-release calcineurin inhibitor formulations were independantly associated with reduced UTI occurrence and recurrence. Mycophenolic acid exposure was associated with increased UTI occurrence and MDR episodes in univariate analyses (P = .001 and P < .001, respectively), but no independent predictors of MDR infection were identified on multivariate analysis (P = .082).

CONCLUSIONS: UTIs remain a frequent complication following KT, with recurrent and MDR episodes representing a substantial proportion of infections. Recipient characteristics, donor factors, prolonged hospitalization, and immunosuppressive regimen characteristics contribute to infection risk. Optimization of perioperative management and immunosuppressive strategies may help reduce infectious morbidity, although prospective studies are required for validation.

articles.title: Circular comparison of finish lines obtained from digital scans and conventional impressions: A clinical study.
articles.abstract:
STATEMENT OF PROBLEM: Clinical studies that have investigated whether intraoral scanners (IOSs) are equivalent or even superior to conventional impressions in capturing subgingival finish lines are sparse.

PURPOSE: The purpose of this clinical study was to compare circumferentially the course of subgingival chamfer preparations captured by both digital scans (DIGI) and conventional impressions (CONI) using CONI as reference.

MATERIAL AND METHODS: Sixteen patients with a total of 50 teeth requiring crown preparations were included. For each die, a conventional polyether double-mix impression was made for the CONI workflow, and an intraoral scan was obtained for the DIGI setup. The CONI definitive casts were digitized, and the finish lines of the dies were defined for both workflows. The corresponding CONI and DIGI dies were registered. The deviations of the finish lines were analyzed circumferentially using an inspection software program with CONI as the reference. Positive (apical) and negative (coronal) deviations were calculated. Descriptive statistics were computed, normality was assessed using the Shapiro-Wilk test, and differences among tooth regions were analyzed using a linear mixed-effects model (α=.05).

RESULTS: On average, 9% of the DIGI finish lines were apical relative to the CONI margins, with a mean ±standard deviation of 68 ±54 µm. In contrast, 91% of the DIGI finish lines were located coronally, with a mean ±standard deviation of 245 ±108 µm. There were no statistically differences among tooth regions (P>.05).

CONCLUSIONS: The results of this study suggest that digital scans may not capture subgingival preparation margins with the same accuracy as conventional methods.

articles.title: Diagnostic performance of sexually transmitted infection screening in men with sterile leukocyturia detected by flow cytometry.
authors: Díaz de Tuesta Del Arco JL
articles.journal: Enfermedades infecciosas y microbiologia clinica (English ed.)
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Sexually transmitted infections (STIs) have increased in recent years, especially amongst young men. However, genitourinary symptoms continue to be initially managed as a urinary tract infection. The aim of this study was to evaluate the diagnostic yield of STI screening in urine samples submitted for culture from men with sterile leukocyturia and to assess the discriminative ability of leukocyturia for detecting STIs.

METHODS: A prospective study (June 2019-May 2024) was conducted using midstream urine samples from men aged 15-59 years with leukocyturia ≥20 leukocytes/μL detected by flow cytometry (UF-1000i and UF-5000i, Sysmex®) and negative urine culture. STI detection was performed using multiplex PCR (Allplex™ STI Essential Assay, Seegene). Demographic variables and leukocyturia were analyzed.

RESULTS: A total of 495 samples were included, with STIs diagnosed in 201 (40.6%). Chlamydia trachomatis was the most frequently detected pathogen (59.7%). Diagnostic yield was similar in Primary Care and the Emergency Department (41.6% vs 37.6%). Patients with STIs were younger (29 vs. 35 years; p< 0.001) and more frequently of foreign origin (51.6% vs. 35.3%; p< 0.001). Leukocyturia was higher in STI-positive than STI-negative samples [median (IQR): 358 (110-959) vs. 85 (35-315) WBC/μL; p < 0.001], mainly due to Neisseria gonorrhoeae [median (IQR): 1264 (690-3526) WBC/μL].

CONCLUSIONS: Opportunistic STI screening in men with sterile leukocyturia showed a high diagnostic yield and supports the systematic inclusion of molecular STI testing in this population. However, the discriminative ability of leukocyturia was limited.

articles.title: Experiences and challenges of pediatric intensive care unit nurses in Iran: a qualitative content analysis study.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: Pediatric intensive care units (PICUs) are demanding places to work. Nurses there provide complex, continuous care to critically ill children and support distressed families, often with too few staff and limited resources. In Iran, little is known about how PICU nurses experience these pressures. This study explored their experiences and considered how these challenges may affect nurses' well-being and the quality and safety of care.

PROCEDURES: We used conventional content analysis, following Graneheim and Lundman. Fifteen nurses were recruited by purposive maximum variation sampling from four PICUs in three tertiary pediatric referral hospitals in Iran. Between February and December 2025, we conducted 17 in-depth, semi-structured interviews and non-participant observations. Recordings were transcribed verbatim and analyzed inductively. Trustworthiness was supported by member checking, peer debriefing, reflexive field notes, and the Consolidated Criteria for Reporting Qualitative Research (COREQ) checklist.

FINDINGS: We identified 213 initial codes, grouped into 15 subcategories and five interrelated categories: working under structural constraints; professional role complexity; interactional challenges in critical situations; limited professional empowerment and organizational support; and emotional challenges. Nurses spoke about staffing shortages, limited equipment, heavy workload, difficult communication with parents and conscious children, insufficient structured education, and repeated exposure to child suffering, death, and moral distress. These stressors interacted and threatened their well-being and sense of professional effectiveness.

CONCLUSIONS: PICU nurses in Iran face interrelated structural, professional, interactional, and emotional challenges. Responding to them requires coordinated organizational, educational, ethical, and psychological strategies, including better staffing and resources, PICU-specific professional development, support for family-centered communication, and structured emotional and ethical support.

articles.title: Delivery fidelity was high with variable uptake of optional components in a remote multicomponent rehabilitation intervention in intensive care unit survivors (iRehab): a mixed-methods fidelity assessment.
articles.abstract:
QUESTION: What was the fidelity of a remote multicomponent rehabilitation intervention in intensive care unit survivors (iRehab) across the National Institutes of Health Behavior Change Consortium Treatment Fidelity framework domains (design, training, delivery, receipt and enactment)?

PARTICIPANTS: iRehab participants (n = 429; 231 intervention, 198 standard care); interviews involved 20 intervention participants, 15 standard care participants and six intervention staff.

METHODS: A mixed-methods fidelity assessment was embedded within the process evaluation of a multicentre randomised controlled trial. Quantitative fidelity was assessed using structured checklists, participant-level tracking data and longitudinal monitoring of potential drift. Qualitative interviews explored fidelity processes across domains.

RESULTS: Study design fidelity was maintained, with clear differentiation between the experimental intervention and standard care. Provider training included structured training, competency assessment and ongoing multidisciplinary support. Delivery fidelity was high for one-to-one sessions, with no systematic drift in sampled sessions. Of 231 participants allocated to iRehab, 169 (73%) attended at least five one-to-one appointments. The uptake of optional group-based components was more variable. Qualitative findings indicated participant understanding and engagement, whereas tracking data and participant accounts provided evidence of strategies being applied in daily life.

CONCLUSION: The iRehab intervention was delivered with high delivery fidelity while allowing individualisation to patient needs. For physiotherapists, monitoring of fidelity should extend beyond attendance and exercise prescription to whether patients can independently apply rehabilitation strategies when symptoms, fatigue and everyday demands fluctuate. Defined core components, staff training, staff competency assessment, ongoing support and fidelity monitoring may help support consistent remote delivery.

articles.title: Continuous glucose monitoring for diabetes mellitus in the perioperative and intensive care setting: a prospective observational validation study✰.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: In-hospital diabetes mellitus management currently relies on intermittent glucose monitoring with point-of-care (POC) testing, rather than continuous glucose monitoring (CGM). Most studies on CGM have focused on its benefits and accuracy in the outpatient setting, in contrast to the hospital setting, where the accuracy may be different.

METHODS: In this prospective observational study (NCT06297850), we assessed the accuracy of CGM (Dexcom G7, Dexcom Inc.) compared with POC monitors in people with diabetes mellitus requiring glucose-lowering medication undergoing surgery or admission to the ICU. The primary outcome was agreement between CGM and POC measurements, defined as median absolute relative difference (MARD). Clarke error grid (CEG) and Bland-Altman analyses were used to quantify the accuracy. Secondary analyses assessed agreement during periods of hypoperfusion, defined as a mean arterial pressure of <65 mm Hg, infusions with vasopressors, or reduced peripheral perfusion index.

RESULTS: In 58 participants (mean [standard deviation] age 71 [11]yr; 34% female), the median MARD was 10.9% (5.1-19.4%); 1186 of 1212 paired POC and CGM measurements (98%) were within clinically acceptable ranges (CEG zones A and B). MARD was 4.5% higher (95% confidence interval 2.3-6.7%) during periods of hypoperfusion. Given that hypoglycaemia (<4 mM) did not occur, no paired readings were obtained. Bland-Altman analysis showed similar CGM and POC measurements, with a mean difference of -1 mM (95% limits of agreement -5.6 to 3.4 mM).

CONCLUSIONS: For the vast majority of interstitial glucose measurements, CGM was accurate in people with diabetes mellitus. Although overall performance was good, caution may be warranted when interpreting CGM data during periods of impaired peripheral perfusion.

CLINICAL TRIAL REGISTRATION: NCT06297850.

articles.title: Myo-inositol to prevent gestational diabetes: "What do conflicting trials tell clinicians?".
articles.journal: American journal of obstetrics and gynecology
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: A recent meta-analysis reported that myo-inositol supplementation was associated with a reduced risk of gestational diabetes mellitus. However, the primary outcome showed substantial between-study heterogeneity, complicating the interpretation and clinical applicability of the evidence.

OBJECTIVE: To discuss why randomized trials may have produced different results and identify the information needed to guide future research and clinical interpretation.

STUDY DESIGN: We critically appraised the clinical and methodological characteristics of the randomized controlled trials included in the published meta-analysis to explore factors that may have contributed to their variability in results.

RESULTS: Substantial differences were found in population characteristics, including the prevalence of a family history of diabetes, previous gestational diabetes mellitus, and overweight or obesity. Trials also differed in the timing of treatment initiation (before or after the 14th week) and in their supplementation protocols. The available evidence does not allow conclusions regarding treatment effect modification, because study-level analyses cannot distinguish true differences in treatment effects from differences in statistical power or other study characteristics. Short-term tolerability has been consistently reported; however, long-term neonatal outcomes have rarely been reported, and safety data remain limited.

CONCLUSION: The recent meta-analysis provided a signal of benefit of myo-inositol for prevention of gestational diabetes mellitus. This clinical perspective identifies and discusses clinical and methodological differences that may have contributed to the variability in results across trials. However, the available evidence does not establish the optimal target population, supplementation protocol, or timing of treatment initiation. Adequately powered randomized trials focusing on short- and long-term neonatal outcomes are needed to better define the efficacy and safety of myo-inositol for the prevention of gestational diabetes mellitus.

This forum highlights some proposed mechanisms of SGLT2i efficacy, limitations of these studies, and potential future directions.

OCT-guided versus angiography-guided stent optimisation for post-interventional FFR in patients with complex coronary artery lesions: protocol for a multicentre, open-label, randomised controlled trial (PRECISION-COMPLEX).
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Whether intravascular imaging-guided percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) reduces adverse events in complex coronary lesions remains debated. Although optical coherence tomography (OCT) improves stent optimisation, its effect on the physiological result of PCI has not been tested in a dedicated randomised trial. The PREcise percutaneous coronary intervention for stent OptimizatION in treatment of COMPLEX lesion (PRECISION-COMPLEX) trial aims to determine whether algorithm-driven OCT-guided stent optimisation improves the physiological result of PCI, assessed by post-optimisation fractional flow reserve (FFR), compared with angiography-guided PCI.

METHODS AND ANALYSIS: PRECISION-COMPLEX is an investigator-initiated, multicentre, open-label, superiority randomised controlled trial at four Korean academic hospitals. Patients with stable or unstable angina and at least one prespecified complex lesion are randomised 1:1 to OCT-guided or angiography-guided PCI with current-generation drug-eluting stents. In the OCT arm, stent sizing follows a prespecified algorithm, and post-PCI OCT must confirm adequate expansion, apposition and absence of major edge dissection. Post-PCI FFR is mandated in both arms. The primary endpoint is the proportion of patients with a suboptimal post-optimisation FFR (<0.85); secondary endpoints at 2 years include target-vessel failure and its components, any revascularisation and stent thrombosis. A total of 320 patients gives 90% power to detect a reduction in the primary endpoint from 30% to 15%. Enrolment ran from 15 November 2022 to 4 December 2024; follow-up is ongoing, with main results expected in early 2027.

ETHICS AND DISSEMINATION: The trial protocol was approved by the Institutional Review Board of Chonnam National University Hospital (CNUH-2022-283), the Institutional Review Board of Samsung Medical Center (SMC2022-11-012), the Institutional Review Board of Seoul National University Hospital (H2303-104-1414) and the Institutional Review Board of Chung-Ang University Gwangmyeong Hospital (2212–048-077). It conforms to the Declaration of Helsinki and Good Clinical Practice. All participants provide written informed consent. Findings will be disseminated through peer-reviewed publication and presentation at scientific meetings. PRECISION-COMPLEX will define the incremental impact of OCT-based optimisation on the physiological result of PCI and indicate whether anatomy-integrated and physiology-integrated guidance improves outcomes in complex coronary lesions.

TRIAL REGISTRATION NUMBER: NCT05493904.

articles.title: Evaluation of percutaneous cryoneurotomy compared with surgical open neurotomy for the management of post-stroke spastic equinovarus foot in France: protocol for a multicentre, randomised controlled, open-label, non-inferiority trial.
Prognostic implications of sex-related disparities in severity assessment of primary mitral regurgitation following intervention.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Current guidelines advocate for intervention in primary mitral regurgitation (PMR) based on detection of severe MR using standardised thresholds. We sought to quantify sex-related differences in transthoracic echocardiography (TTE)-derived MR severity and long-term mortality after PMR intervention.

METHODS: Consecutive patients undergoing PMR intervention with validated vena contracta (VC) measurements were included. Proximal isovelocity surface area radius (PISAr), effective regurgitant orifice area (EROA) and regurgitant volume (RVol) were also measured in a subset of patients. Using Cox models adjusted for PMR mortality risk factors, VC was modelled as a restricted cubic spline with an interaction term for sex. Sex-stratified receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curves were used to identify potential differences in risk calibration.

RESULTS: Within 420 patients, females (n=168, 40%) displayed significantly lower absolute values of VC (median (interquartile range): 0.60 (0.55–0.80) vs 0.70 (0.60–0.80) cm, p=0.003), PISAr (0.85 (0.70–1.00) vs 1.10 (0.90–1.30) cm, n=96, p<0.001), EROA (0.35 (0.22–0.50) vs 0.60 (0.40–0.80) cm2, n=58, p=0.018) and RVol (51 (43–83) vs 88 (67–108) mL, n=53, p=0.013) compared with males. In multivariable regression, sex-related differences in long-term all-cause mortality were moderated by VC (Pinteraction=0.013). In ROC curve analysis, VC had similar discriminatory ability in both sexes (p=0.768), although the optimum cut-off was lower in females (females: 0.67 cm vs males: 0.74 cm).

CONCLUSIONS: The present study demonstrates significant sex differences in TTE-measured MR severity and subsequent prognosis following intervention for PMR, which may merit sex-specific individualised thresholds.

articles.title: Aspects of hand use development in infants aged 4 to 18 months with or at risk of cerebral palsy: a longitudinal study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND AND OBJECTIVE: Promoting hand use is a key goal in the rehabilitation of infants with or at risk of cerebral palsy (CP). To inform treatment planning, this study aimed to describe aspects of hand use development in these infants aged four to 18 months.

METHOD: Longitudinal design with repeated measurements using the Hand Assessment for Infants (HAI) from four to 12 months of age. At 18 months of age, the Assisting Hand Assessment (AHA), Both Hand Assessment (BoHA), Peabody Developmental Motor Scale (PDMS-2), and mini-MACS (Manual Ability Classification System) were applied. Descriptive statistics identified developmental trajectories for hand use. Linear mixed models estimated growth curves among infants diagnosed with CP. Associations between HAI scores at six and 8 months and outcomes at 18 months were examined using Spearman rank correlation and regression analyses.

RESULTS: In total, 41 infants with or at risk of CP participated. Developmental hand use trajectories for each infant showed a clear pattern, with trajectories clustering according to manual ability at 18 months, classified by mini-MACS level for infants with CP (bilateral [n = 17], unilateral [n = 12]) and as "typical manual ability" for infants without CP (n = 12). Growth curve, defined by CP subtype and mini-MACS level at 18 months, showed modest differences between groups in the early months, relatively weak linear improvement in HAI scores over time in infants with higher mini-MACS, steeper gains over time in infants with lower mini-MACS, and a similar pattern with overlapping confidence intervals for the two CP subtype within the same mini-MACS level. A strong negative correlation was found between HAI scores and mini-MACS level. Regression analyses demonstrated a statistically significant and positive association between HAI scores and BoHA, AHA, or PDMS-2 subtest (Visual-Motor Integration) scores.

DISCUSSION: HAI scores at 6 months of age may indicate the subsequent development of hand use up to 18 months of age. This contributes important knowledge to early treatment planning. The results must be interpreted with caution due to the small sample size. Larger studies are needed before firm conclusions are made.

articles.title: Short-Duration [18F]florbetapir PET Reconstructions: Centiloid Agreement and Temporal-Window Analysis.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND AND PURPOSE: Shorter [18F]florbetapir PET acquisitions could improve workflow, but the effects of reconstruction duration and temporal-window position on Centiloid values are not well characterized. We evaluated quantitative agreement across short-duration reconstructions, temporal-window effects, and visual agreement.

MATERIALS AND METHODS: This retrospective study included a primary cohort of 32 patients with early 1-, 2-, and 5-min reconstructions and a 10-min reference. A temporal-window cohort of 22 patients underwent early and late 5-min analysis. A validation cohort of 37 examinations underwent early, centered, and late 1- and 5-min reconstructions and a 10-min reference. Two readers independently classified early 1-min, early 5-min, and 10-min images across three separate reading sessions. Centiloid agreement was assessed using paired differences, Bland-Altman limits of agreement, and categorical agreement.

RESULTS: In the primary cohort, mean differences from the 10-min reference were -3.70, -2.97, and -1.65 CL for early 1-, 2-, and 5-min reconstructions, respectively. In the temporal-window cohort, late 5-min values averaged 2.86 CL higher than early values. The validation cohort reproduced both findings: early-to-late shifts were +5.53 CL at 1 min and +3.07 CL at 5 min. In the reader study, agreement with 10 min was 70.3%-86.5% at 1 min and 94.6%-100% at 5 min; interreader κ was 0.49, 0.77, and 0.89 at 1, 5, and 10 min, respectively.

CONCLUSIONS: Early short-duration reconstructions yielded systematically lower Centiloid values, while later temporal windows yielded higher values at fixed duration. Visual agreement with 10 min was high at 5 min but lower at 1 min. Reconstruction duration and frame timing should be standardized before abbreviated protocols are considered substitutes for standard 10-min imaging.

articles.title: Advanced Practice Providers in Spinal CSF Leak Programs: A Multi-Institutional Study of Current Roles and Perceived Impact on Patient Care.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND AND PURPOSE: Advanced practice providers (APPs), including nurse practitioners and physician assistants, are increasingly integrated into radiology practices. However, their utilization and clinical responsibilities in dedicated spinal CSF leak programs have not been characterized. Using a multicenter survey, we investigated APP training, clinical responsibilities, perceived impact, and challenges of APP integration at US spinal CSF leak programs.

MATERIALS AND METHODS: A survey was distributed to physicians at US institutions with dedicated spinal CSF leak programs and APP involvement. Candidate institutions were identified through the International Society for Spinal CSF Leak and American Society of Spine Radiology. Survey questions addressed program characteristics, APP training and structure, clinical responsibilities, perceived impact, and challenges. Responses were summarized descriptively.

RESULTS: Twelve institutions completed the survey. Eight (67%) reported caring for more than 250 spinal CSF leak patients annually. APPs included nurse practitioners at 4 centers (33%), physician assistants at 3 (25%), and both at 5 (42%); 7 centers (58%) had APPs dedicated exclusively to spinal CSF leak care. APP training was primarily informal and on-the-job at all institutions. Common primary APP responsibilities included obtaining outside imaging, patient intake and symptom review, procedure and sedation orders, informed consent, post-procedural follow-up, pain management, and treatment of rebound intracranial hypertension. Shared APP and physician responsibilities commonly included outside record review, determining evaluation urgency, preliminary imaging review, sedation assessment, and multidisciplinary coordination. Procedural responsibilities such as lumbar puncture, intrathecal contrast administration, myelography planning, and CSF leak treatment were primarily performed by physicians in most programs. At least 75% of respondents strongly agreed that APP participation improved continuity of care, patient communication/accessibility, clinic efficiency, patient satisfaction, physician administrative burden, and multidisciplinary coordination. Common barriers included funding/support, billing/reimbursement, and limited procedural privileges.

CONCLUSIONS: APPs are widely integrated into dedicated spinal CSF leak programs, with substantial involvement in pre-procedural evaluation, care coordination, and post-procedural management, while advanced myelography and CSF leak treatment remain predominantly physician-directed. APP participation was perceived to improve patient care and clinical workflow. These findings provide a framework for APP integration into specialized spinal CSF leak programs.

articles.title: Building multinational interoperability in Defence Engagement (Health) training: outcomes from a two-cycle action research methodology.
Peripheral blood innate lymphoid cell profiles of patients with COPD reflect their clinical phenotype as identified by cluster analysis.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) has a heterogeneous clinical and immunological presentation. Although proportions of group 1 innate lymphoid cells (ILC1) in peripheral blood were shown to correlate with COPD severity, no analysis of ILC subsets in relation to clinical outcomes has been performed yet. Our aim was to explore the relationship between clinical phenotype clusters and ILC subsets in COPD.

METHODS: 24 patients with COPD were included in this explorative cross-sectional study. Forced expiratory volume in 1 s (FEV1), diffusion capacity for carbon monoxide, COPD Assessment Test (CAT) and body mass index (BMI) values were collected. Clinical clusters were defined, ILC populations in peripheral blood were quantified and characterised by flow cytometry. Data were analysed using a combination of multiple factor and principal component analysis.

RESULTS: First, we identified three clinical clusters. C1 (n=12) had low FEV1 and BMI values and the highest disease burden, as determined by CAT. C2 (n=11) comprised older patients with increased BMI and the most pack-years. C3 (n=11) had the highest FEV1 values and fewer exacerbations. Based on leucocyte differentiation and phenotypic characterisation of ILC subsets, two immunological clusters of patients with COPD were identified. C1, the most severe COPD group, was associated with reduced frequencies of circulating ILCs with a potentially inflammatory phenotype.

CONCLUSIONS: The finding that clinical clusters of patients with COPD were strongly associated with peripheral blood immunophenotype and ILC profile suggests a role for ILCs in disease course and may have relevance for the development of personalised therapies.

articles.title: An Unexpected Cause of Left Main Coronary Artery Occlusion: Embolization From a Mitral Papillary Fibroelastoma.
Novel Iatrogenic Atrial Septal Defect Closure Method for Peri-Cannular Left-Atrial Thrombosis During LAVA-ECMO Explant.
First Report of Wire-Anchored BA-BASILICA Enabling TAVR in Type-0 Bicuspid Aortic Stenosis Complicated by Cardiogenic Shock.
PCI Through the Axillary VA-ECMO Return Cannula Using a Cannula-in-Cannula Technique.
1-Year Outcomes of Early Intra-Aortic Balloon Pump in Heart Failure-Related Cardiogenic Shock.
Conduction System Versus Right Ventricular Pacing in Patients Undergoing TAVR: A Multicenter Propensity-Matched Study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Pacemaker implantation after transcatheter aortic valve replacement (TAVR) is common and has been associated with adverse clinical outcomes. Cardiac physiological pacing (CPP) may preserve ventricular synchrony and reduce heart failure (HF) events compared with right ventricular pacing (RVP).

OBJECTIVES: This study sought to compare long-term clinical outcomes of CPP vs RVP in patients requiring permanent pacing after TAVR.

METHODS: Registro de Estimulación Fisiológica-TAVR is a retrospective, multicenter nationwide registry including patients undergoing TAVR and pacemaker implantation within 30 days. Propensity score matching (1:1) was performed using baseline clinical and echocardiographic variables, yielding 466 matched pairs. The primary endpoint was the composite of cardiovascular death or HF hospitalization. Cox proportional hazards models were used for time-to-event analyses. Median follow-up was 24 months.

RESULTS: In the propensity score-matched cohort, CPP was associated with a lower incidence of the primary endpoint than RVP (9.7% vs 17.6%; HR: 0.57; 95% CI: 0.39-0.83; P = 0.003). This difference was driven by fewer HF hospitalizations (7.9% vs 13.9%; HR: 0.57; 95% CI: 0.37-0.86; P = 0.008). No significant differences were observed in cardiovascular death or all-cause mortality between groups.

CONCLUSIONS: In this multicenter propensity score-matched study, CPP after TAVR was associated with a lower risk of the primary endpoint, driven by fewer HF hospitalizations. These findings support the need for further randomized clinical trials to evaluate the role of CPP in post-TAVR patients requiring ventricular pacing.

articles.title: CAD Complexity in TAVR Patients: Who Benefits From PCI?
Impact of Extent of Coronary Artery Disease in Transcatheter Aortic Valve Replacement: A PRO-TAVI Substudy.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Coronary artery disease is present in one-half of patients undergoing transcatheter aortic valve replacement (TAVR). The recent randomized controlled PRO-TAVI (Percutaneous Coronary Intervention Before Transcatheter Aortic Valve Implantation) trial indicated that deferral of percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) is safe in patients with concomitant coronary artery disease at 1-year follow-up. The SYNTAX (Synergy between Percutaneous Coronary Intervention with TAXUS and Cardiac Surgery) score quantifies the extent of coronary artery disease, which may guide individualized revascularization strategies.

OBJECTIVES: The aim of this study was to evaluate the association between SYNTAX score (SS) and clinical outcomes in patients undergoing TAVR.

METHODS: This study was a substudy of the PRO-TAVI trial, including 466 patients with significant coronary artery disease undergoing TAVR randomized to deferral of PCI or PCI before TAVR. SS was calculated from preprocedural coronary angiograms, and patients were stratified by SS quartiles. The primary outcome was a composite of all-cause mortality, myocardial infarction, stroke, and major bleeding at 1 year. An ischemic composite outcome of all-cause mortality, myocardial infarction, and stroke was also assessed.

RESULTS: The primary composite outcome did not differ across SS categories between the deferral and PCI groups at 1-year follow-up, which was completed by all but 1 patient. In patients with SS >17, the ischemic composite outcome occurred more often in the deferral group (30.9% vs 14.8%; adjusted HR: 2.43; 95% CI: 1.04-5.64; P = 0.04), driven primarily by all-cause mortality and stroke. Bleeding events were less frequent in the deferral group across all SS subgroups.

CONCLUSIONS: In patients with concomitant coronary artery disease undergoing TAVR, deferral of PCI reduced bleeding risk and appeared safe across all SS categories. Deferral of PCI in patients with more complex coronary artery disease (SS >17) was associated with higher risk for the ischemic composite outcome. These post hoc findings require confirmation in randomized trials. (Percutaneous Coronary Intervention Before Transcatheter Aortic Valve Implantation [PRO-TAVI]; NCT05078619).

articles.title: Intraprocedural Cardiac Arrest in Patients Undergoing Percutaneous Coronary Interventions in the United States: An Analysis of the NCDR CathPCI Registry.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Cardiac arrest (CA) during percutaneous coronary interventions (PCI) is a catastrophic procedural complication. Contemporary rates of CA during PCI are unknown.

OBJECTIVES: This study sought to understand contemporary rates of CA, associated mortality, and identify predictors of CA during PCI.

METHODS: Patients with CA during PCI from 2018 to 2023 were identified from the National Cardiovascular Data Registry CathPCI Registry. Trends in intraprocedural CA (IPCA) incidence and in-hospital death were evaluated. Predictors of IPCA and risk-adjusted mortality were identified.

RESULTS: A total of 36,755 IPCA occurred during 3,956,840 PCIs (0.93%), including in 0.24% of elective PCIs, 0.32% of PCIs for stable coronary artery disease, and 1.28% of acute coronary syndrome interventions. The incidence of IPCA increased over time (0.62% in 2018 to 1.07% in 2023; P < 0.0001). In-hospital death occurred in 40.5% of patients with IPCA, 45.4% of whom died in the cardiac catheterization laboratory. Notably, although risk-adjusted IPCA increased (0.79% to 0.95%; P = 0.042), slight declines in risk-adjusted mortality (45.1% to 43.6%; P = 0.027) were observed over time. PCI for ST-segment elevation myocardial infarction, non-ST-segment acute coronary syndromes, increasing age, ventricular arrhythmias, severe aortic stenosis, vasopressors or inotrope use, mechanical circulatory support, coronary perforation, coronary dissection, cardiac tamponade, intraprocedural heart failure or myocardial infarction, and temporary cardiac pacemaker implantation were associated with increased adjusted odds of IPCA.

CONCLUSIONS: IPCA complicates 0.93% of contemporary PCI. Despite an increasing incidence of risk-adjusted IPCA, there were slight declines in risk-adjusted in-hospital mortality in the study period. Several patient and procedural characteristics were independently associated with intraprocedural CA.

articles.title: Immediate Versus Staged Complete Revascularization in Multivessel Disease and STEMI: A Meta-Analysis of Randomized Trials.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: For patients with ST-segment elevation myocardial infarction (STEMI) and multivessel disease, complete revascularization is recommended. The timing of nonculprit lesion intervention, either immediately during the index procedure or staged at a later time, has been investigated in randomized controlled trials (RCTs).

OBJECTIVES: This study sought to perform a meta-analysis of RCTs comparing immediate vs staged complete revascularization in patients with multivessel disease presenting with STEMI.

METHODS: We conducted a frequentist, pairwise meta-analysis. Studies were selected based on the following inclusion criteria: multicenter RCTs comparing immediate vs staged nonculprit revascularization in patients presenting with STEMI; exclusive use of second-generation (or newer) drug-eluting stents; a follow-up duration of ≥1 year; and publication in a peer-reviewed journal. The primary outcome of interest was all-cause mortality, whereas secondary outcomes included myocardial infarction (MI), cardiac death, and unplanned revascularization. Summary estimates were computed using random-effects models with inverse-variance weighting based on trial-level HRs and 95% CIs. The study protocol was registered on PROSPERO (CRD420251124207).

RESULTS: After a systematic search, 4 randomized trials comprising 2,651 patients were included in the meta-analysis. The risk of all-cause death at 1-year was higher with immediate complete revascularization (HR: 1.50; 95% CI: 1.02-2.21; P = 0.04; prediction interval [PI]: 0.80-2.81; I2 = 0%; t2 = 0). Immediate complete revascularization reduced the risk of recurrent MI when using the protocol specified definitions which included procedural MI (HR: 0.58; 95% CI: 0.36-0.94; P = 0.02; PI: 0.22-1.54; I2 = 0%; t2 = 0.034) but did not reduce risk of spontaneous MI (HR: 0.91; 95% CI: 0.55-1.48; P = 0.90; PI: 0.41-2.00; I2 = 0%; τ2 = 0.00). The risk of cardiac death and unplanned revascularization was comparable between the treatment groups.

CONCLUSIONS: In STEMI and multivessel disease, immediate complete revascularization may be associated with an increased risk of all-cause death at 1-year when compared with staged complete revascularization. The treatment effect on mortality should be interpreted cautiously because of the relatively low number of deaths across the 4 trials and the statistical fragility of the findings. The findings from this analysis do not support an immediate complete revascularization strategy in these patients.

articles.title: Occlusion Myocardial Infarction: Beyond STEMI and NSTEMI.
Frequency and Prognosis of Alternative Definitions of Occlusion Myocardial Infarction Across the Whole Spectrum of Acute Coronary Syndromes.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Occlusion myocardial infarction (OMI) refers to a myocardial infarction caused by a persistent or transient, complete or near-complete coronary artery occlusion. Multiple definitions have been proposed, yet their frequency and comparative prognostic relevance remain unclear.

OBJECTIVES: This study sought to evaluate the frequency and prognosis of previously proposed OMI definitions across the whole spectrum of acute coronary syndromes (ACS) from the MATRIX trial.

METHODS: Five alternative OMI definitions were assessed: 1) culprit artery (CA) TIMI flow grade 0; 2) CA-TIMI flow grade 0-1; 3) CA-TIMI flow grade 0-2; 4) CA-TIMI flow grade 0-2 or TIMI flow grade 3 with cardiac troponin >30× upper reference limit; and 5) CA-TIMI flow grade 0-2 or CA-TIMI flow grade 3 with cardiac troponin >100× upper reference limit. The endpoint of interest was 1-year all-cause mortality.

RESULTS: Among 6,558 patients with ACS, OMI frequency ranged from 37.8% for definition 1 to 76.1% for definition 4. OMI was independently associated with higher 1-year mortality according to definitions 1-4 (adjusted HR: 2.08 [95% CI: 1.56-2.78], 1.97[1.47-2.63], 1.70 [1.25-2.32], 1.47 [1.01-2.12], respectively) but not according to definition 5 (adjusted HR: 1.26 [0.90-1.75]). OMI definitions exclusively based on impaired CA flow (ie, definitions 1-3) improved discrimination, reclassification, and model fit when added to the conventional STE/NSTE-ACS classification. One-year mortality did not differ among patients with NSTE-ACS with OMI definition 1 or 2 compared with ST-segment elevation MI (STEMI) patients.

CONCLUSIONS: OMI defined by impaired CA flow confers prognostic implications beyond the presence or absence of ST-segment elevation in a broad ACS population and identifies patients without ST-segment elevation with 1-year mortality similar to that of STEMI.

articles.title: Occlusion-Focused Triage vs Very-High-Risk NSTEMI Criteria: A DIFOCCULT-3 Substudy.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The current ST-segment elevation myocardial infarction (STEMI)/NSTEMI framework may not fully identify patients with ACO who present without diagnostic STE. Although immediate invasive management is recommended for patients with very-high-risk NSTEMI features, these criteria are inconsistently applied in clinical practice. The OMI/NOMI framework has been proposed as an alternative strategy.

OBJECTIVES: This study sought to compare the occlusive and nonocclusive myocardial infarction (OMI/NOMI) classification with guideline-defined very-high-risk non-ST-segment elevation myocardial infarction (NSTEMI) criteria for the identification of acute coronary occlusion (ACO) in patients without diagnostic STE.

METHODS: This was a substudy of the multicenter, cluster-randomized DIFOCCULT-3 (Time for a Diagnostic Paradigm Shift From ST-Elevation/Non-ST-Elevation to Occlusion/Non-Occlusion Myocardial Infarction-3) trial. Consecutive adult patients without diagnostic STE on the admission electrocardiogram were included and managed according to either the conventional STEMI/NSTEMI or the OMI/NOMI approach. Very-high-risk NSTEMI was defined according to current guidelines. Outcomes included immediate invasive management (within 2 hours) and adjudicated ACO.

RESULTS: Among 4,398 patients, very-high-risk NSTEMI criteria identified a small proportion of patients and were inconsistently translated into early intervention. The OMI/NOMI approach selected more patients for early invasive management compared with the STEMI/NSTEMI framework (45.4% vs 13.6%; P < 0.001). Adjudicated ACO was identified within 2 hours more frequently under the OMI/NOMI approach (35.1% vs 16.7%; P < 0.001), without reduction in angiographic yield.

CONCLUSIONS: An occlusion-focused diagnostic approach was associated with substantially higher rates of immediate invasive management and earlier identification of patients with adjudicated ACO.

articles.title: Acute Coronary Occlusions in NSTEMI Undergoing Percutaneous Coronary Intervention: Insights From the CathPCI Registry.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Patients may present with acute coronary occlusions (ACOs) without manifesting electrocardiographic criteria for ST-segment elevation myocardial infarction (STEMI).

OBJECTIVES: The aim of this study was to examine the incidence, clinical characteristics, and in-hospital outcomes of non-ST-segment elevation myocardial infarction (NSTEMI) with ACO.

METHODS: The study included patients with STEMI and NSTEMI in the CathPCI Registry who underwent percutaneous coronary intervention between April 1, 2018, and June 30, 2023. ACO was defined as 100% stenosis deemed acute. The cohort was stratified into STEMI (including STEMI equivalents), NSTEMI-ACO, and NSTEMI-no-ACO. The primary outcome was a composite of in-hospital stroke, myocardial infarction, or cardiovascular mortality. A sensitivity analysis with ACO defined as 100% acute occlusion or TIMI flow grade 0 or 1 in the culprit artery was performed.

RESULTS: Of 1,198,544 patients, 26.1% had STEMI, 11.0% had NSTEMI-ACO (15% of whom had NSTEMI), and 62.9% had NSTEMI-no-ACO. Compared with those with NSTEMI-no-ACO, NSTEMI-ACO patients had more cardiogenic shock (9.0% STEMI vs 3.8% NSTEMI-ACO vs 1.9% NSTEMI-no-ACO; P < 0.001), ventricular arrhythmias (4.9% vs 2.0% vs 1.3%; P < 0.001), and in-hospital cardiac arrest (6.1% vs 2.7% vs 1.6%; P < 0.001). Patients with NSTEMI-ACO had a higher risk for the primary composite compared with those with NSTEMI-no-ACO (adjusted OR: 2.26; 95% CI: 2.18-2.34; P < 0.001) but a lower risk compared with those with STEMI (adjusted OR: 0.54; 95% CI: 0.52-0.56; P < 0.001). Using a definition of ACO including TIMI flow grade 0 or 1, NSTEMI-ACO accounted for 216,054 presentations (24.4% of NSTEMI). In-hospital outcomes were similarly worse compared with NSTEMI-no-ACO and better compared with STEMI.

CONCLUSIONS: ACO occurs in a substantial proportion of patients with NSTEMI and is associated with worse in-hospital outcomes relative to those with NSTEMI-no-ACO. Further studies of early identification and reperfusion practices for NSTEMI-ACO are warranted.

articles.title: Trends in Inflation-Adjusted Pharmacotherapy Costs and Cardiovascular Risk Factor Management in Type 2 Diabetes: A 26-Year Study from Tertiary Diabetes Centres in Greece Drug Costs and Risk Factors in Type 2 Diabetes.
articles.journal: Experimental and clinical endocrinology & diabetes : official journal, German Society of Endocrinology [and] German Diabetes Association
articles.abstract:
AIMS: We evaluated long-term trends in pharmacotherapy costs and cardiovascular target achievement among people with type 2 diabetes attending tertiary diabetes centres in Greece.

METHODS: This periodic, multicenter, cross-sectional study analysed data from 4,963 people with type 2 diabetes followed in each of the three diabetes centres at specific time points: 1998, 2006, 2012, 2018, and 2024. We compared HbA1c, systolic blood pressure, LDL-C, and BMI and the achievement of individual cardiovascular targets (HbA1c <7%, systolic blood pressure <140 mmHg, LDL-C <100 mg/dL) and all three simultaneously. Annual pharmacotherapy cost comparisons used inflation-adjusted values.

RESULTS: Simultaneous achievement of all three cardiovascular targets increased from 0.6% in 1998 to 29.1% in 2024. Individual target achievements improved: HbA1c from 29.4% to 58.6%, systolic blood pressure from 45.3% to 62.5%, and LDL-C from 6.3% to 73.4%. Mean LDL-C showed the greatest reduction, from 128.4 mg/dL to 79.0 mg/dL. Median BMI increased until 2018, then declined in 2024. Total pharmacotherapy costs per patient rose from €341 in 1998 to €1,609 in 2024, primarily due to glucose-lowering therapies (€167 to €1,257).

CONCLUSION: Over 26 years, people with type 2 diabetes attending tertiary diabetes centres in Greece demonstrated improvements in cardiovascular target achievement, alongside rising pharmacotherapy costs, primarily driven by glucose-lowering therapies.

articles.title: Dabrafenib Alleviates the Effects of Lipopolysaccharides in Endothelial Cells.
articles.abstract: The vascular endothelium forms a monolayer which regulates the passage of solutes and gases-including oxygen-between blood and tissues. Endothelial barrier dysfunction has been associated with sepsis, acute lung injury and acute respiratory distress syndrome. Dabrafenib is a food and drug administration-approved v-raf murine sarcoma viral oncogene homolog B1 inhibitor associated with anti-inflammatory responses, which targets the never in mitosis A-related kinase 9 and cyclin-dependent kinase 16. The present study suggests that dabrafenib ameliorates lipopolysaccharide-induced vascular injury by suppressing MLC2, MAPK, and STAT activation; paracellular leak and ROS generation, suggesting its potential use in diseases related to barrier dysfunction.

articles.title: Feasibility and Outcomes of External Cephalic Version among Small for Gestational Age (SGA) births.
articles.abstract: OBJECTIVE- The American College of Obstetricians and Gynecologists recommends that external cephalic version (ECV) be offered to patients with malpresentation. The objective of our study was to evaluate the efficacy and perinatal outcomes among births with small for gestational age (SGA) infants after an ECV. STUDY DESIGN- This was a population based, cross sectional study using National Vitality Statistics data of singleton, non-anomalous, neonates born after 36 weeks of gestation, with birthweight of < 2500g between 2021 and 2023. Births with a maternal history of previous cesarean delivery (CD) were excluded. Births were divided into those who had an ECV attempt and those with a breech fetus at CD without a trial of labor. Adverse maternal outcomes (blood transfusion, intensive care unit (ICU) admission, unplanned hysterectomy) and neonatal outcomes (assisted ventilation use, neonatal ICU (NICU) admission, seizures, surfactant use, death) were compared between groups using logistic regression. RESULTS- A total of 8,021 births were included. Of the 8,021 births, 812 (10.1%) had an ECV attempt and 7,209 (89.9%) had a primary breech CD. There were significant differences in baseline characteristics between groups. Among the 812 births who had an ECV attempt, 338 (41.6%) had a successful ECV, of which 233 (68.9%) subsequently delivered vaginally. After adjusting for differences, births that had an ECV attempt had lower odds of neonatal assisted ventilation use (aOR 0.65, 95% CI [0.46-0.92]) and NICU admission (aOR 0.48, 95% CI [0.40-0.58]) than those who had a primary breech CD. There were higher odds of maternal transfusion in breech CD cohort as compared to those who had an ECV attempt (OR 2.81, 95% CI [1.42- 5.56]). CONCLUSION- Although ECV was successful in 41.6% births with SGA infants, there were lower rates of assisted ventilation use and NICU admission among those who underwent an ECV attempt.

articles.title: Saving the Limb-Tissue Collectors, Growth Factors, and Antibiotics in a War Injury.
articles.abstract:
ABSTRACT: As a life-saving procedure, limb amputation is frequently indicated in severe war injuries, especially in suboptimal medical supply. We report of a 56-year-old Ukrainian male who was wounded on the battlefield by an air attack during Russian early invasion in Zaporizhzhia. The blast injury caused a critical soft-tissue defect of the lower leg combined with comminuted fractures of the tibia and fibula. Although indicated, the patient refused the amputation of the lower leg. Initially closed reduction and stabilization by an external fixator, local debridement as well as soft-tissue coverage by a porcine skin were performed at a local field hospital. Due to destroyed infrastructure and missing escape corridors, further evacuation was difficult. Thus, it took 15 days to transfer the patient by ground transportation to our institution. Based on the massive tissue loss, superinfection necrosis and questionable blood supply, the indication for amputation was confirmed, but the patient insisted on limb preservation. To save the lower leg, a brought spectrum of regenerative strategies was applied, accompanied by standard trauma treatment regimens (debridement, vacuum sealing, antibiotics, intramedullary nailing, suralis flap).

ABSTRACT: These included the local application of growth factors, the use of innovative tissue collectors, the implementation of biomaterial/tissue combinations and the application of a vasodilator. Six months after treatment, the patient was free of pain and infection. However, further follow-up was complicated by delayed bone healing and required revision surgery. Although the limb was saved, it ultimately took 1 year until full rehabilitation was achieved. This case illustrates the special demands in war lower leg injuries but also demonstrates that a combination of standardized and innovative treatment protocols can save a limb, even when amputation might be indicated as a first-line therapy.

articles.title: Antiviral immunity via telomerase-like reverse transcription in bacteria.
articles.abstract: Defense-associated reverse transcriptases (DRTs) employ diverse and distinctive mechanisms of cDNA synthesis to protect bacteria against viral infection1. However, the functions and mechanisms of many DRTs remain unknown2. Here we identify a new antiviral defense system, DRT10, that associates with a noncoding RNA (ncRNA) to catalyze processive, protein-primed synthesis of tandem-repeat DNA. Reverse transcription is templated by a defined ncRNA region with a characteristic sequence pattern and template boundary elements, both of which are conserved and essential for DNA repeat addition. Cryo-EM reconstructions reveal an unanticipated 2:1 architecture, wherein two RT monomers bind opposite sides of a pseudo-symmetric ncRNA. Biochemical experiments further demonstrate that each RT monomer reverse transcribes the template encoded on its respective side of the ncRNA, but only one generates the long repetitive product, whose template is defined by the distance between two flanking stem-loop anchors. This mode of iterative, boundary-delimited cDNA synthesis exhibits direct parallels to the mechanism of telomeric repeat addition by eukaryotic telomerase, and phylogenetic analyses of RTs across domains of life place telomerase in a monophyletic clade with the DRT family, suggesting a common origin for their DNA polymerization activities. Together with earlier studies of DRT2, DRT3, and DRT93-5, our findings identify a conserved mechanistic logic underlying RNA-templated DNA repeat addition across diverse DRTs, despite vastly different architectural solutions, and expand the repertoire of reverse transcription-based strategies for antiviral immunity in bacteria.

articles.title: First-Trimester Metabolic Dysfunction-Associated Steatotic Liver Disease and Risk of Hypertensive Disorders of Pregnancy: A Prospective Cohort Study.
articles.journal: Clinics and research in hepatology and gastroenterology
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Metabolic-dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease is the most common chronic liver condition globally, increasingly relevant in pregnancy due to rising maternal metabolic risks. The study explores MASLD in early pregnancy as a potential independent risk factor for hypertensive disorders of pregnancy (HDPs).

METHODOLOGY: In this prospective study, we assessed MASLD in 198 pregnant women at 10-14 weeks' gestation using demographic, clinical, metabolic, and hepatic parameters measured by transient elastography. We followed participants prospectively for the development of HDPs. We used standardised protocols, blinded operators, and validated cutoff values. We used multivariable logistic regression to assess the association between MASLD and HDPs, adjusting for prespecified clinical and metabolic covariates.

RESULTS: MASLD was present in 48 (24.2%) women. HDPs developed in 11/48 (22.9%) women with MASLD compared with 9/150 (6.0%) without MASLD (p=0.002). In the fully adjusted model, MASLD was associated with higher odds of HDPs, although the association did not reach statistical significance (adjusted OR 2.89, 95% CI 0.90-9.54; p=0.075). In the exploratory bidirectional stepwise model, MASLD remained associated with HDPs (aOR 2.99, 95% CI 1.08-8.29; p=0.035).

CONCLUSION: MASLD was detected in 24% of women in early pregnancy. Early-pregnancy MASLD was associated with higher odds of subsequent HDPs in this cohort. Although the fully adjusted model did not demonstrate a statistically significant association, the effect estimate was approximately threefold and was similar in the exploratory stepwise model. Given the small number of HDPs events and the limitations of stepwise variable selection, these findings should be considered hypothesis-generating and require confirmation in larger prospective studies.

articles.title: Immunomodulatory, Antioxidant, and Growth-Promoting Effects of Hylocereus undatus Peel Powder in Pacific White Shrimp (Litopenaeus vannamei).
articles.abstract: Shrimp aquaculture is a primary supplier of high-quality aquatic protein worldwide. Incorporating natural feed additives can strengthen health and disease resilience in cultured species. This study evaluated the dietary effects of Hylocereus undatus (dragon fruit, HU) peel powder on growth performance, metabolic profiles, digestive capacity, immune response, antioxidant capacity, tissue integrity, and disease resistance against Vibrio parahaemolyticus in Pacific white shrimp (Litopenaeus vannamei). Shrimp with an initial weight of 4.23±0.03 (n = 60 per treatment) were randomly distributed into four dietary groups and fed diets containing varying levels of HU peel powder (0, 2, 4, and 6 g/kg diet; designated as HU0, HU2, HU4, and HU6) for 10 weeks. Dietary supplementation with HU peel powder significantly enhanced growth performance, food conversion ratio (FCR), and survival rate, with the HU6 diet demonstrating peak efficacy (P < 0.05). Fortification with HU improved metabolic profiles by significantly elevating serum total protein, albumin, and globulin concentrations, while markedly diminishing aspartate aminotransferase (AST) and alanine aminotransferase (ALT) activities (P < 0.05). Shrimp fed HU-supplemented diets exhibited notable improvements in whole-body proximate composition alongside elevated digestive enzyme activities (amylase, lipase, and protease; P < 0.05) compared with HU0 group. Furthermore, HU supplementation displayed strong immunomodulatory and antioxidant capacity, evidenced by significant increases in total hemocyte count (THC), lysozyme, and nitroblue tetrazolium (NBT) activities, accompanied by upregulation of antioxidant enzyme activities (SOD, CAT, and GPx) and a marked reduction in malondialdehyde levels (P < 0.05). Hepatopancreas structural integrity was improved in all HU-supplemented shrimp compared to the HU0 treatment. At the transcriptomic level, HU-fortified diets significantly upregulated the mRNA expression of prophenoloxidase, lysozyme, CAT, and SOD genes (P < 0.05). Following the V. parahaemolyticus challenge, post-infection survival rates were increased to 55%, 65%, and 80% in the HU2, HU4, and HU6 groups, respectively, compared to 35% in the control group. Overall, these findings demonstrate that H. undatus peel powder serves as an effective functional dietary additive to enhance growth, immunocompetence, and pathogen resistance in L. vannamei, presenting a sustainable feed additives strategy for shrimp aquaculture.

articles.title: Association between obesity and asthma among Arab Israeli adolescents compared with Jewish Israeli peers.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Ethnic differences in the health implications of adolescent obesity, including asthma, are understudied in Israel. We compared associations between adolescent weight categories and asthma among Arab Israeli and Jewish Israeli adolescents.

METHODS: This retrospective cross-sectional study used the computerized database of Clalit Health Services (CHS). It included Arab Israeli adolescents aged 14-19 years with at least one recorded height and weight measurement between 2007 and 2022. A Jewish Israeli comparison group meeting the same eligibility criteria was selected, with a socioeconomic status distribution corresponding to that of Arab Israeli adolescents. The final sample included 313,936 Arab Israeli and 289,616 Jewish Israeli adolescents. Logistic regression assessed associations between weight categories and asthma overall and asthma with inhaled corticosteroid (ICS), inhaled bronchodilator (IBD), or systemic corticosteroid (SCS) use, separately by group.

RESULTS: Higher weight categories were associated with higher odds of asthma, with similar patterns in both groups. Among adolescents with class 3 obesity, adjusted odds ratios (95% CI) were 1.52 (1.35-1.70) for asthma overall, 2.02 (1.23-3.10) for asthma with ICS use, 2.81 (1.49-4.78) for asthma with IBD use, and 3.81 (2.16-6.19) for asthma with SCS use. Jewish Israeli adolescents had higher ICS use, whereas Arab Israeli adolescents had higher SCS use.

CONCLUSIONS: Asthma management should address obesity through healthy diet and physical activity while considering lifestyle differences between Arab Israeli and Jewish Israeli adolescents. Greater ICS use and reduced SCS use among Arab Israeli adolescents may warrant attention.

articles.title: A Decade of Asthma Emergency Department Presentations in New South Wales: Temporal, Seasonal and Age-Specific Trends.
articles.abstract: Asthma remains a major contributor to emergency department (ED) utilisation. Although international studies have described temporal, seasonal and age-specific patterns of asthma-related ED utilisation, contemporary Australian evidence remains limited. We conducted a retrospective population-based ecological time-series study of monthly asthma-related ED presentations in New South Wales, Australia, between 2015 and 2024. A total of 231,670 presentations were recorded, averaging 1,931 per month (24.1/100,000 population). Children aged 0-15 years experienced the highest presentation rates. Rates showed marked seasonal variation, peaking in May and June (30.2 and 29.3/100,000 population respectively). These findings support targeted prevention and healthcare resource planning during peak season.

articles.title: Post-stroke depression, but not anxiety, is independently associated with executive and visuospatial function: A five-year longitudinal cohort study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Post-stroke anxiety and depression frequently co-occur, and whether each is independently associated with cognitive impairment remains unclear because most studies model one without adjusting for the other. In a five-year cohort, we tested whether anxiety and depression have distinct cognitive correlates and whether 6-month affective status predicted subsequent cognitive recovery.

METHODS: Patients from the STROKDEM cohort (n = 191) were assessed at 6, 12, 36, and 60 months post-stroke for anxiety, depression, and five cognitive domains (memory, executive functioning, attention, visuospatial functioning, and language). Two symmetric random-intercept linear mixed models regressed each affective score on the cognitive domains while adjusting for the other. Repeated-measures correlations, multiple imputation for attrition, and exploratory trajectory and prognostic models were also used.

RESULTS: After mutual adjustment and correction, depression was independently associated with executive and visuospatial function, whereas anxiety showed no independent cognitive correlate. Repeated-measures correlations confirmed this dissociation. The executive association and the absence of an anxiety correlate were robust to all sensitivity analyses, including multiple imputation for attrition, whereas the visuospatial association was attrition-sensitive. Exploratory associations between 6-month affect and cognitive recovery did not survive multiple imputation and were inconclusive.

LIMITATIONS: Attrition was substantial and selective on baseline cognition; the persistent-anxiety subgroup was small; and psychiatric history, psychotropic medication, and cognitive reserve beyond education were unavailable.

CONCLUSIONS: The cognitive burden of post-stroke affective disorders is carried by depression rather than anxiety. Screening for depression, rather than anxiety alone, may better identify stroke survivors at cognitive risk.

articles.title: High burden of Carbapenem-resistant Enterobacterales: A prospective cross-sectional study at a tertiary hospital in Morocco.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: The present study aimed to determine and update the prevalence of Carbapenem-resistant Enterobacterales, to characterize carbapenemase production, and to assess antimicrobial susceptibility in a Moroccan tertiary hospital.

PATIENTS AND METHODS: A prospective cross-sectional study was conducted from January 2021 to December 2022, during which time 6672 Enterobacteriaceae isolates were recovered from clinical specimens from patients with suspected bacterial infections. Species were identified using MALDI-TOF-MS and the BD Phoenix® M50 for antimicrobial susceptibility according to EUCAST screening criteria. NG-Test® CARBA 5 assay was used for carbapenemase detection and characterization.

RESULTS: Among the 6672 Enterobacteriaceae isolates, 1289 showed decreased susceptibility to ertapenem (19.3%). Klebsiella pneumoniae was the predominant species (47.4%), followed by Enterobacter cloacae complex (20.8%). The neonatal intensive care unit was the main reservoir of cases (22.0%). Blood and purulent specimens were the most frequent sources of isolation (62.8% combined). Among the 322 non-duplicate isolates tested, 252 (78.3%) were carbapenemase producers. Antibiotic susceptibility profile displayed high rates of resistance to ciprofloxacin (91.0%), gentamicin (85.1%), and cotrimoxazole (86.6%). NDM (34.8%) and OXA-48-like (30.1%) were the predominant enzymes. NDM and OXA-48-like co-production was observed in 12.1% of isolates. A novel VIM + OXA-48-like combination was detected in an Enterobacter cloacae complex isolate.

CONCLUSIONS: This study demonstrates an alarming increase in the proportion of Enterobacterales exhibiting decreased susceptibility to carbapenems, highlighting a need for robust infection prevention measures, rapid diagnostics, and continuous epidemiological surveillance in high-dependency units.

articles.title: Network toxicology, machine learning, single-cell analysis, and molecular docking reveal 6PPD/6PPD-Q-associated atrial fibrillation signatures.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Atrial fibrillation (AF) is the most prevalent sustained arrhythmia worldwide, and environmental factors are increasingly recognized as contributors to its complex pathogenesis. The tire antioxidant N-(1,3-dimethylbutyl)-N'-phenyl-p-phenylenediamine (6PPD) and its oxidation product 6PPD-quinone (6PPD-Q) are emerging environmental contaminants with reported cardiotoxicity; however, their molecular relationship with AF remains unclear.

OBJECTIVES: This study aimed to identify potential molecular targets and pathways that link 6PPD/6PPD-Q exposure to AF using an integrated network toxicology and machine learning strategy.

METHODS: Multicohort atrial microarray datasets from patients with AF were integrated to identify AF-related genes using differential expression analysis, weighted gene coexpression network analysis, and GeneCards database screening. Putative targets of 6PPD/6PPD-Q were predicted using multiple in silico databases and intersected with AF-related genes. Network toxicology, enrichment analysis, machine learning with SHAP interpretation, single-cell RNA sequencing, and molecular docking were utilized to identify and characterize hub genes. Key targets were validated using qRT-PCR and western blotting in human cardiac fibroblasts. A mouse exposure model was further used to assess AF inducibility, duration, and cardiac gene expression in vivo.

RESULTS: Sixteen putative AF-associated target genes of 6PPD/6PPD-Q were identified. Machine learning analysis highlighted four hub genes as key candidate hubs. Single-cell RNA analysis revealed cell type-specific expression, with enrichment in cardiomyocytes and vascular structural cells. Molecular docking predicted favorable binding interactions between 6PPD/6PPD-Q and the key target proteins. In vitro exposure to 6PPD or 6PPD-Q at the tested concentrations upregulated the mRNA and protein levels of all four candidate genes. In vivo exposure significantly increased pacing-induced AF inducibility, prolonged AF duration, and upregulated the expression of all these genes in cardiac tissues.

CONCLUSION: These findings suggest that 6PPD and 6PPD-Q may contribute to AF by targeting specific genes and signaling pathways, with DDR1, BCHE, HTR2B, and KCNJ3 identified as core exposure-related hubs.

articles.title: UDP-glucose ceramide glucosyltransferase (UGCG) is a novel positive regulator of MyD88-driven inflammation in sepsis.
articles.abstract: Excessive activation of MyD88 in sepsis drives uncontrolled cytokine production, leading to multi-organ injury and high mortality. However, the mechanisms that regulate MyD88 activation and link it to glycosphingolipid metabolism remain incompletely understood. Here, we identify UDP-glucose ceramide glucosyltransferase (UGCG) as a novel positive regulator of MyD88-mediated signaling and a potential biomarker for sepsis. UGCG expression was elevated in septic patients and LPS-stimulated cells. Transcriptomic analysis showed that UGCG knockdown broadly suppresses inflammatory pathways. Functionally, UGCG deficiency selectively impaired MyD88- but not TRIF-dependent signaling and reduced cytokine production. Pharmacological inhibition of UGCG using the FDA-approved drug N-butyl-deoxynojirimycin (NB-DNJ) suppressed inflammatory gene expression, immune cell infiltration, and lung injury in an LPS-induced murine sepsis model. Mechanistically, UGCG interacts with the MyD88 TIR domain to promote MyD88 protein stability, while UGCG deficiency is associated with impaired ligand-triggered MyD88 oligomerization. Together, these findings uncover a previously unrecognized UGCG-MyD88 axis that directly links UGCG to innate immune signaling independently of its enzymatic activity, and highlight UGCG as a promising therapeutic target for sepsis.

articles.title: Alcohol-associated liver disease.
articles.journal: Clinical gastroenterology and hepatology : the official clinical practice journal of the American Gastroenterological Association
articles.abstract: Alcohol-associated liver disease (ALD) is the leading cause of liver-related mortality in Western countries. The assessment of histological severity in ALD now relies predominantly on non-invasive methods, particularly elastography and blood-based tests, commercially available or laboratory-developed. These non-invasive approaches have largely replaced the need for liver biopsy. Management of ALD is based primarily on the treatment of alcohol use disorder, and access to pharmacological therapies and addiction specialists should be improved. At present, there is no specific treatment for ALD, with the exception of corticosteroid therapy for severe alcohol-associated hepatitis (AH), a distinct clinical entity associated with a poor prognosis that requires specialized management. In patients with advanced ALD who fail to improve despite sustained alcohol abstinence, liver transplantation remains the only effective therapeutic option. In this setting, a dedicated and multidisciplinary care pathway should be established to optimize patient selection, management, and long-term outcomes.

articles.title: Cutaneous Effects and Aesthetic Management of Glucagon-like Peptide-1 Receptor Agonists: A Narrative Review.
articles.abstract: Glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists (GLP-1RAs) are among the most widely prescribed medications in the United States, with expanding indications beyond type-2 diabetes mellitus to include obesity, cardiovascular risk reduction, and metabolic dysfunction-associated steatohepatitis. As their utilization increases, the dermatologic effects of these agents become increasingly relevant to clinical practice. This narrative review examines the cutaneous effects of GLP-1RAs across six domains: facial volume loss and accelerated skin aging, changes in hair density, wound healing, striae distensae and body skin laxity, cutaneous adverse events, and emerging therapeutic benefits in inflammatory skin disease. Herein, we review proposed mechanisms and evidence-based management strategies for each domain, including biostimulatory fillers, energy-based devices, nutritional optimization, and pharmacologic interventions. Prospective, large-scale clinical studies are needed to clarify mechanisms of GLP-1RA modulation in skin and to guide management of these AEs as next-generation agents enter clinical practice.

articles.title: The Prognostic Value of Entropy from T1 Mapping in Pulmonary Arterial Hypertension.
articles.journal: Journal of cardiovascular magnetic resonance : official journal of the Society for Cardiovascular Magnetic Resonance
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The prognostic value of left ventricular (LV) entropy from T1 mapping in pulmonary arterial hypertension (PAH) remains unexplored.

STUDY DESIGN AND METHODS: This prospective study enrolled patients with PAH who underwent cardiovascular magnetic resonance (CMR) within 72h of right heart catheterization (RHC). Myocardial native T1, extracellular volume fraction (ECV) and entropy were calculated in mid-ventricular short-axis slice. The primary endpoint was defined as all-cause mortality or lung transplantation. Outcomes were further analyzed across groups stratified by survival status using Cox proportional hazards regression and Kaplan-Meier survival analysis.

RESULTS: A total of 312 patients were analyzed over a median follow-up of 36.10 months, with 59 deaths. Elevated LV entropy was positively correlated with log-transformed NT-proBNP, right ventricular (RV) end-systolic, end-diastolic volume indices, LV native T1 and ECV, and inversely correlated with RV ejection fraction (all P < 0.01). LV entropy did not differ significantly across etiological subgroups, whereas LV entropy without IPs was higher in congenital heart disease-associated PAH. Both LV entropy ≥8.60 and LV entropy without IPs ≥8.30 independently predicted all-cause mortality (HR, 2.207; 95% CI, 1.324-3.678; P = 0.002; and HR, 2.357; 95% CI, 1.405-3.955; P = 0.001, respectively) and were associated with reduced survival (both log-rank P < 0.005). Adding LV entropy improved ESC models (χ²: 55.79 to 60.61, C-statistic: 0.782 to 0.801) and ESC-CMR models (χ²: 35.31 to 41.77, C-statistic: 0.805 to 0.813).

CONCLUSIONS: Elevated LV entropy was related to disease severity, RV dysfunction, and adverse clinical outcomes, and served as an independent predictor of all-cause mortality in patients with PAH.

articles.title: Hepatitis Delta in Spain: A Nationwide Prospective Characterization of Active Infection and Liver Disease Severity.
articles.journal: Clinical microbiology and infection : the official publication of the European Society of Clinical Microbiology and Infectious Diseases
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: Hepatitis delta virus (HDV) infection is associated with rapid progression to cirrhosis and liver-related complications. We aimed to characterize the clinical and virological profile of anti-HDV-positive individuals in Spain and identify factors associated with active infection and advanced fibrosis.

METHODS: This nationwide, multicentre, prospective observational study included adults with positive anti-HDV serology enrolled between April 2024 and March 2026 across 72 hospitals in 15 Spanish Autonomous Communities. Demographic, virological, laboratory and clinical data were collected in a centralized database. Multivariable logistic regression was used to identify factors independently associated with active HDV infection and advanced liver fibrosis.

RESULTS: Among 1,112 anti-HDV-positive individuals, 670/1,112 (60%) were male, median age was 54 years (IQR 43-61), and 457/926 (49%) were born in Spain. HIV co-infection and anti-HCV positivity were present in 189/944 (20%) and 217/1,112 (21%), respectively. HDV-RNA was detectable in 436/1,047 patients (42%), with a median viral load of 4.1 log IU/mL (IQR 2.9-5.1). Genotype 1 accounted for 108/121 (89%) genotyped infections. Advanced fibrosis was present in 222/536 (41%) evaluable patients and was more frequent in those with active infection than in non-viremic individuals (155/261, 59% versus 59/256, 23%; p<0.001). Active HDV infection was independently associated with younger age, hepatitis B virus (HBV) antiviral therapy, lower platelet count and lower albumin levels, whereas African origin was associated with lower odds of detectable HDV-RNA. Advanced fibrosis was independently associated with active HDV infection, HBV antiviral therapy and higher gamma-glutamyltransferase levels, while higher platelet count and haemoglobin levels were associated with lower odds of advanced fibrosis.

CONCLUSIONS: Active HDV infection and advanced liver disease remain common in Spain. These findings support systematic HDV-RNA testing, standardized fibrosis assessment and close clinical follow-up of anti-HDV-positive individuals.

articles.title: Corrigendum to "Noninvasive diagnosis of pulmonary tuberculosis using face mask sampling: a prospective study in adults" Clinical Microbiology and Infection, Volume 32, Issue 4, 2026, Pages 644-649.

articles.title: Circulating SARS-CoV-2 RNA detection in acute COVID-19 disease and Post-COVID Condition.
articles.journal: Clinical microbiology and infection : the official publication of the European Society of Clinical Microbiology and Infectious Diseases
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: To determine the clinical significance of circulating plasma SARS-CoV-2 RNA across acute COVID-19 and post-COVID condition (PCC) by investigating prevalence, determinants, and kinetics in a large longitudinal cohort, accounting for hospitalization and vaccination.

METHODS: We consecutively enrolled individuals with confirmed SARS-CoV-2 infection. Acute COVID-19 was classified as mild, severe, or critical per WHO criteria. PCC was assessed three months post-symptom onset, plasma SARS-CoV-2 RNA (RNAemia) was quantified during acute infection (T0) and at follow-up (T1) by RT-qPCR. Associations between RNAemia and acute disease severity or PCC were evaluated using multivariable logistic regression. RNAemia was analyzed as tertiles, binary detectability, and continuous levels.

RESULTS: 442 COVID-19 individuals were included, of whom 195 (44.1%) had mild disease, 161 (36.4%) severe, and 86 (19.5%) critical. At a median of 3.2 (IQR 2.7-3.9) months from symptoms onset, 184/442 subjects were followed up, and 144/184 (78.3%) reported at least one persistent symptom compatible with PCC, most commonly asthenia (22.9%), myalgic pain (26.4%), brain fog (19.4%), dyspnea (31.3%), and cough (42.4%). RNAemia was detected in 67.4% of participants at baseline and in 53.6% at follow-up. RNAemia in the II-III tertiles or any detectable RNAemia were associated with critical COVID-19. Neither baseline nor follow-up RNAemia, were associated with PCC, and results were unchanged in a sensitivity analysis excluding vaccinated individuals. RNAemia trajectories were not associated with PCC, PCC clusters, or upper respiratory tract viral clearance..

CONCLUSIONS: SARS-CoV-2 RNAemia was closely linked to acute COVID-19 severity but showed no association with PCC or PCC phenotype which were assessed at 3 months from symptoms onset in a cohort predominantly experiencing severe COVID-19 and hospitalization during acute infection. This dissociation may suggest that viral RNA in the peripheral blood is primarily involved in acute pathogenesis, whereas PCC likely arises from distinct biological mechanisms.

articles.title: Dominant lung involvement and heterozygous IFIH1 variants.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Heterozygous gain-of-function (GoF) variants in IFIH1 are associated with rare autoinflammatory diseases characterized by heightened interferons-stimulated gene (ISG) signatures. These include Aicardi-Goutières syndrome, presenting with slowly progressive spastic paraparesis of the lower limbs, intracerebral calcifications, and neuroinflammation, and Singleton-Merten syndrome, defined by tooth loss, bone demineralization, and vascular calcification.

RESEARCH QUESTION: Do rare IFIH1 GoF variants contribute to an interstitial lung disease phenotype, thereby expanding the spectrum of IFIH1-related disorders?

STUDY DESIGN AND METHODS: Among 559 children with interstitial lung disease (chILD) and exome sequencing as part of their diagnostic work-up, 12 rare heterozygous IFIH1 variants were identified. Of these, 10 were missense variants of unknown significance, which were functionally assessed in vitro using luciferase assay and ISG-expression profiling. Genome-wide RNA analysis was performed on available patient samples to explore broader transcriptional effects.

RESULTS: Four variants with increased basal IFNβ transcription in vitro and elevated ISG expression in vivo indicating GoF behaviour were identified. Disease severity correlated with GoF potential of the respective variant.
