Two patients harbouring IFIH1 variants with strong GoF activity displayed multisystem involvement and died from respiratory failure at 3 and 4 months of age, respectively. Two additional patients showed milder phenotypes with chronic lung disease stabilizing by the age of 8 and 10 years, respectively. Lung biopsies showed alveolar hypoplasia and alveolar macrophage pneumonia (=desquamative interstitial pneumonia) of varying severity.

INTERPRETATION: We report a dominant interstitial lung disease phenotype in individuals harbouring novel IFIH1 variants, expanding IFIH1-related disease to the group of type I interferonopathies with pulmonary manifestations like STING-associated vasculopathy with onset in infancy (SAVI) and COPA syndrome.

articles.title: Standardized Preparation and Characterization of Leukocyte-Rich and Leukocyte-Poor PRP Using PrecurCell® Kits.
articles.journal: Transfusion clinique et biologique : journal de la Societe francaise de transfusion sanguine
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: To compare the cellular composition of leukocyte-rich platelet-rich plasma (LR-PRP) and leukocyte-poor platelet-rich plasma (LP-PRP) prepared using PrecurCell® PRP and PrecurCell®-LP PRP kits, with particular emphasis on platelet enrichment, leukocyte content, and residual red blood cells.

MATERIAL AND METHODS: Whole blood samples from healthy donors were processed using the two PRP preparation systems. Platelet concentration and red blood cell content were quantified using a hematology analyzer, and leukocyte content was assessed to characterize the resulting LR-PRP and LP-PRP preparations. Platelet enrichment was determined relative to baseline whole blood values.

RESULTS: The preparations achieved platelet concentrations up to six times the baseline whole blood values. Differences in leukocyte content distinguished the LR-PRP and LP-PRP preparations. No residual red blood cells were detected in the analyzed PRP samples.

CONCLUSION: The evaluated systems produced platelet-enriched preparations with distinct leukocyte profiles and no detectable residual red blood cells. These findings characterize the cellular differences between LR-PRP and LP-PRP and may inform further investigation of their application-specific biological effects. Functional and clinical studies are required to establish their therapeutic relevance.

articles.title: Haemovigilance and Epidemiological Surveillance of Transfusion-Transmitted Infections in Greece, 1996-2023: National Donor Screening Data and Recipient Investigations.
articles.journal: Transfusion clinique et biologique : journal de la Societe francaise de transfusion sanguine
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Surveillance of transfusion-transmitted infections (TTIs) supports blood safety, particularly for multi-transfused patients such as those with haemoglobinopathies.

MATERIALS AND METHODS: Retrospective descriptive analysis of aggregated national surveillance data from Greece. We report aggregate infectious-marker positivity values from national surveillance summaries for 1996-2009. We also report NAT yields in 2007-2023, the transmission categories of HIV-positive donors in 2010-2019 and recipient investigations reported to the national haemovigilance system in 2005-2023.

RESULTS: More than 14 million donations were tested in 1996-2023. For 1996-2009, the surveillance summaries reported aggregate positivity of 0.39% for HBsAg, 0.09% for anti-HCV, 0.017% for syphilis and 0.008% for anti-HIV1/2. In 2007-2023, NAT detected 1,393 serology-negative infectious donations among 8,389,862 donations reported as tested (estimated 16.6 per 100,000; 95% CI 15.7-17.5), of which 1,321 were HBV. In 2010-2019, 56.9% of HIV-positive donors were men who have sex with men and 25.3% were heterosexual. Fifteen recipient investigations were reported among 13.6 million issued components; transmission was excluded in one.

CONCLUSION: In 2007-2023, NAT detected infectious donations that serology missed, mostly HBV. Reported recipient infections were rare but included emerging pathogens. Annual data are needed to assess trends.

articles.title: Perspectives on changes in abortion policy by sex among Latine young adults in an agricultural setting in California.
articles.journal: Journal of pediatric and adolescent gynecology
articles.abstract:
STUDY OBJECTIVE: To examine perspectives on abortion policy changes and self-managed abortion awareness by sex among Latine young adults from an agricultural community in California.

STUDY DESIGN: We utilized data from a prospective longitudinal cohort study of eighth graders followed into young adulthood (N=389) from Salinas, California. Participants completed in-person or remote visits; sensitive questions were asked via computer-assisted self-interviewing. Primary outcomes included measures related to abortion perspectives and awareness of self-managed abortion by sex at birth at two study visits (2023-2025). We assessed differences using chi-squared statistics or fisher's exact tests (categorical) and t-tests (continuous). Secondary outcomes included qualitative data from open-ended questions about self-managed abortion. We analyzed open-ended responses qualitatively using an inductive approach.

RESULTS: Abortion policy changes that mattered most to participants varied significantly by sex (p<0.001). Few (16.5-17.8%) participants had heard of self-managed abortion; awareness varied significantly by sex (p<.05). In open-ended responses, participants discussed self-managed abortion methods, sources of information, perception safety, and likely motivations.

CONCLUSION: Our study explores how Latine young adults from an agricultural community in California view the shifting U.S. reproductive health legal landscape, finding differences between sexes regarding the changing abortion legal landscape and awareness of self-managed abortion. Our findings point to the need for public health interventions that improve young adults' awareness of abortion policies and self-managed among populations underrepresented in abortion research.

articles.title: 1-Year Outcomes of Endovascular Repair of Zone 0/1 Aortic Arch Lesions with a Thoracic Branched Endoprosthesis.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The GORE® TAG® Thoracic Branch Endoprosthesis (TBE) pivotal non-randomized, multicenter, prospective trial evaluated 1-year outcomes in patients at high risk for open surgical repair undergoing aortic arch and descending thoracic aorta endovascular repair (Zone 0/1).

METHODS: Endpoints evaluated from endovascular procedure through 12 months included aortic-related death, disabling stroke, permanent paraplegia or paraparesis, new onset renal failure, and unanticipated reintervention. Core-lab identified endpoints included aortic rupture or enlargement (≥5 mm), Type I/III endoleak, device integrity, device migration, fistula, patency, and new dissection.

RESULTS: The 77 enrolled patients had aneurysm (n=50), dissection (n=24), or other isolated lesion types (n=3); 90.9% had a Zone 0 proximal stent landing zone. Patients were a mean age of 70.8±10.8 years, 66.2% male, and 57.1% white and all had the aortic and side branch component implanted. Technical success was 94.8%. Early outcomes to 12 months included 8 (10.4%) aortic-related deaths, 6 (7.8%) disabling strokes (all aneurysm cohort), 4 (5.2%) unanticipated reintervention, 2 (2.6%) aortic ruptures, and 1 (1.3%) renal failure. Type IA/IB or Type III endoleaks occurred in 6 (7.8%) patients. Loss of side branch patency occurred in 1 (1.3%) patient. There was no permanent paraplegia or paraparesis or loss of device integrity or migration. A total of five patients had aortic enlargement; none required reintervention.

CONCLUSIONS: Early data from this prospective investigation of the TBE device in Zone 0/1 applications signals that the device is a reasonable therapeutic alternative in patients with appropriate anatomy deemed high risk for open arch surgery.

articles.title: Individual susceptibility to disgust modulates neural and systemic immune responses to virtual infections.
articles.abstract: Disgust is a key psychological mechanism for avoiding pathogen exposure and constitutes a central component of the behavioral immune system. While disgust is thought to reduce infection risk through avoidance, it remains unclear how individual differences in disgust sensitivity shape downstream neuroimmune responses to perceived pathogen threats. Here, we show that lower disgust sensitivity is associated with stronger activation of type 1 innate lymphoid cells during exposure to infectious, compared with neutral, avatars in virtual reality. Disgust sensitivity further correlated with circulating signaling factors involved in immune regulation, including hormones related to the hypothalamic-pituitary-adrenal (HPA) axis, and eicosanoids. Linear models incorporating disgust sensitivity and threat exposure predicted these signaling factors, which in turn enabled accurate prediction of type 1 innate lymphoid cells responses using a pretrained neural network. Recreating this putative pathway, we were able to predict immune responses solely by disgust scores. Additionally, resting-state functional magnetic resonance imaging revealed that exposure to infectious avatars altered hypothalamic connectivity with brain regions involved in visual processing, peripersonal space representation, and social cognition, and these effects were modulated by individual disgust sensitivity. Together, these findings suggest that disgust sensitivity modulates multiple levels of the neuroimmune response to perceived pathogen threats. Across two complementary experiments, our results are consistent with a model linking sensory threat detection, hypothalamic signaling, and systemic immune activation. Rather than uniformly amplifying immune responses, higher disgust sensitivity appears to bias pathogen defense toward neural processing, whereas lower disgust sensitivity is associated with stronger physiological immune activation.

articles.title: Blood-brain barrier disruption and microglia-associated synaptic pruning contribute to cognitive decline after electroconvulsive therapy.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Modified electroconvulsive therapy (MECT) is a highly effective intervention for major depressive disorder (MDD), yet its broader clinical application is constrained by poorly understood cognitive side effects. We hypothesized that MECT disrupts hippocampal blood-brain barrier (BBB) integrity, permitting extravasation of peripheral factors that activate microglia, drive synaptic phagocytosis, and precipitate cognitive decline.

METHODS: We employed a multi-modal translational approach integrating: (1) clinical neuroimaging (rs-fMRI and DCE-MRI) and cognitive assessments in 41 MDD patients undergoing MECT (including 9 with DCE-MRI); (2) a chronic restraint stress (CRS) mouse model subjected to electroconvulsive shock (ECS), with behavioral, molecular, and transcriptomic analyses; and (3) causal validation via microglial depletion (PLX5622) and targeted BBB repair (Axitinib). In vitro, HT22 hippocampal neurons were stimulated with soluble inflammatory mediators released by primed microglia to assess direct synaptic injury.

RESULTS: MECT significantly impaired immediate and delayed associative memory and reduced left hippocampal ALFF in MDD patients; memory decline correlated with ALFF reduction. In a paired subgroup of patients, DCE-MRI revealed increased hippocampal Ktrans after MECT, providing preliminary clinical imaging support for treatment-associated BBB hyperpermeability. In CRS mice, ECS downregulated tight junction proteins (Claudin-5, ZO-1, Occludin), induced Evans blue extravasation, and promoted hippocampal deposition of fibrinogen and complement C3. ECS also triggered microglial activation, enhanced PSD95 synaptic phagocytosis, elevated IL-6/IL-1β, and reduced synaptic proteins. Critically, both PLX5622-mediated microglial depletion and Axitinib-mediated BBB repair reversed these pathological changes and rescued cognitive function, establishing a dual causal validation system. Axitinib failed to suppress LPS-induced microglial activation, suggesting its protective effects were mediated via BBB restoration rather than direct immunomodulation.

CONCLUSIONS: In conclusion, this study identifies a hippocampus-centered neurovascular-immune mechanism underlying MECT/ECS-related cognitive impairment. Our findings demonstrate that BBB disruption is an early upstream event that permits peripheral factors to enter the brain, activate microglia, and drive synaptic injury and cognitive decline. These results establish a novel mechanistic framework for the cognitive side effects of MECT and highlight BBB protection and microglial modulation as potential strategies for cognitive protection.

articles.title: Exercise-driven glucocorticoid signaling acts as a systemic circuit breaker to reprogram microglia and resolve post-stroke inflammation.
articles.abstract: Following ischemic stroke, neuroinflammation drives severe secondary immunopathology, yet how systemic interventions coordinate peripheral and central immunity for neuroprotection remains elusive. Here, we demonstrate that acute-phase exercise accelerates motor rehabilitation and neural repair by activating the hypothalamic-pituitary-adrenal (HPA) axis to function as a potent systemic circuit breaker. Systemically, exercise-driven glucocorticoids, validated via targeted receptor blockade, induce profound spleen atrophy to restrict the peripheral immune pool, effectively depriving the ischemic brain of infiltrating leukocytes. By leveraging high-resolution single-cell transcriptomics, we identify microglia as the primary, highly sensitive central sensors of this glucocorticoid-mediated immunosuppression. These endocrine-reprogrammed microglia transition from a highly pro-inflammatory state toward a regulated, homeostatic quiescence. Mechanistically, they decisively blunt interferon (IFN) signaling to abrogate CXCL9/10-CXCR3 chemotaxis, attenuate antigen presentation and co-stimulation, thereby arresting the recruitment and in situ activation of effector T and B cells. Furthermore, this early suppression of neuroinflammation limits neural tissue damage, preserving the broader neuroglial niche in a quiescent, physiological state. Accordingly, the reactive repair signals typically provided by microglia to astrocytes and oligodendrocytes are substantially attenuated, underscoring that early protection from neuroinflammation effectively obviates the need for intense compensatory repair. Collectively, our findings delineate a novel systemic-to-central neuroimmune axis. By demonstrating how exercise harnesses systemic endocrine signals to interrupt the pathological inflammatory cascade, we highlight microglial glucocorticoid signaling as a precise therapeutic target for post-stroke neuroimmune modulation.

articles.title: Exogenous anti-MoPMK1 microRNA and precursor formats reduce Magnaporthe oryzae infection in rice.
articles.journal: Plant science : an international journal of experimental plant biology
articles.abstract: Exogenous RNA application is emerging as a useful strategy to investigate plant-pathogen interactions. Most studies against fungal pathogens have focused on long double-stranded RNAs, whereas the potential of artificial miRNA and miRNA-precursor formats remains less explored. Here, we targeted the Magnaporthe oryzae MAP kinase gene MoPMK1, a central regulator of appressorium-mediated penetration, invasive growth and host tissue colonization, using three exogenous RNA formats: chemically synthesized mature miRNA duplexes, in planta-produced anti-MoPMK1-containing small RNA fractions and in vitro-synthesized miRNA precursors. All three anti-MoPMK1 formats reduced blast symptoms in rice leaves and were accompanied by lower accumulation of fungal MoPMK1 transcripts. Under the mass-based doses and assay conditions tested, the in vitro-synthesized precursor was associated with a marked reduction in lesion development despite being applied at a lower molar concentration than the mature duplex. Leaf sheath infection assays further showed altered fungal development after anti-MoPMK1 precursor treatment, whereas appressorium formation was reduced most clearly at the highest precursor concentration tested. In addition, application of the precursor through the leaf base reduced disease symptoms at a distal infection site in detached leaves. Direct incubation of fungal spores with the precursor in liquid culture did not reveal a clear inhibitory effect, suggesting that the infection context in plant tissue contributes to precursor activity. Together, these results identify mature and precursor anti-MoPMK1 microRNA formats as sequence-defined RNA tools with biological activity in the rice-M. oryzae interaction, while highlighting RNA format and plant tissue context as important determinants of exogenous RNA activity.

articles.title: Genetic susceptibility in Takotsubo syndrome: a candidate gene association analysis in the French TAKOGENE cohort.
articles.abstract: Takotsubo syndrome (TTS) is a stress-induced left ventricular (LV) cardiomyopathy with an unclear genetic predisposition. We investigated whether single nucleotide polymorphisms (SNPs) previously associated with other cardiomyopathies or LV physiological traits contribute to TTS susceptibility. We conducted a case-control study based on the French multicentre TAKOGENE study (NCT01520610), including 261 unrelated TTS patients and 259 sex- and age-matched controls presenting with acute coronary syndrome. All participants were of European ancestry. A total of 325 SNPs were selected from large-scale genome-wide association studies of cardiomyopathies (n=202) and LV structural/functional traits (n=123), derived from polygenic risk scores. Genotyping was performed using the Infinium OmniExpressExome-8 array. Associations were assessed by logistic regression under an additive model, adjusted for age and sex, with group-specific Bonferroni correction. A sensitivity analysis compared the 261 TTS cases with 973 French population controls from the EPP3 cohort. After quality control and statistical analysis, seventeen SNPs (nine related to cardiomyopathies and eight to LV traits) showed nominal associations (P < 0.05), but none remained significant after group-specific Bonferroni correction. The strongest signal was observed for rs6885658 in the CPEB4 gene (OR 1.62, 95% CI 1.23-2.15; P = 5.8 × 10-4) related to cardiomyopathy traits. The EPP3 population-control sensitivity analysis was consistent with the primary analysis, with no association remaining significant after correction. In conclusion, common genetic variants previously associated with cardiomyopathies or LV traits do not appear to have a major effect on TTS risk. These findings support a disease-specific polygenic architecture of TTS, distinct from that underlying chronic cardiomyopathies and baseline LV traits. Future studies should explore alternative approaches, such as pathway-based analyses focusing on stress-response mechanisms.

articles.title: The role and mechanism of heat shock proteins in the development of pulmonary arterial hypertension.
articles.abstract: Pulmonary arterial hypertension (PAH) is a progressive pulmonary vascular disease characterized by increased pulmonary vascular resistance, right ventricular overload and premature death. Current therapies improve symptoms and hemodynamics but do not adequately reverse pulmonary vascular remodeling. Heat shock proteins (HSPs), key regulators of proteostasis and stress adaptation, are increasingly implicated in PAH pathogenesis. Among them, Hsp70, Hsp90 and Hsp110 have attracted particular interest because of their distinct roles in chaperone networks and vascular remodeling. This review summarizes the structural and functional features of these HSPs, their roles in PAH-associated remodeling and the therapeutic potential and challenges of HSP-targeted strategies.

articles.title: Characterizing Recent HIV Infection by High-Fidelity Multiplexed Primer ID-Based Next-Generation Sequencing among Newly Diagnosed Individuals in Zhuhai, China: A Cross-Sectional Study.
articles.journal: International journal of infectious diseases : IJID : official publication of the International Society for Infectious Diseases
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Differentiating recent from chronic HIV infections is critical for interrupting transmission chains. However, conventional Next-Generation Sequencing (NGS) is confounded by technical errors that inflate genetic diversity, blurring this distinction and compromising downstream molecular epidemiological analyses.

METHODS: We applied Multiplexed Primer ID-Based Next-Generation Sequencing (MPID-NGS) to plasma from 153 antiretroviral therapy (ART)‑naïve newly diagnosed with HIV individuals in Zhuhai, China (2022‑2024) to generate error‑corrected template consensus sequences, from which infection recency was classified using genetic diversity thresholds. We then benchmarked this approach against standard NGS and serological Limiting Antigen Avidity Enzyme Immunoassay (LAg-EIA), and further assessed selection pressures and reconstructed molecular transmission networks.

RESULTS: MPID‑NGS removed >93% of Reverse Transcriptase (RT) and 69% of Variable Regions 1 to 3 (V1V3) low‑frequency artifacts. Primer ID (PID)‑corrected V1V3 diversity showed the strongest correlation with LAg‑EIA Normalized Optical Density (ODn) (ρ = 0.52), while other PID-corrected measures also showed significant but weaker associations, supporting the utility of error-corrected genetic diversity as a staging metric. We classified 15.7% as recent and 76.5% as chronic, with serological concordance of 87.5% and 86.4%, respectively. Despite overall purifying selection in RT, recent infections had significantly higher ω than chronic ones (p < 0.001), reflecting stage‑specific adaptive evolution. Men who have sex with men (MSM) showed higher RT ω than non‑MSM (p < 0.001) and independently predicted transmission clustering (aOR = 3.247, p = 0.003). An acute case exhibited transmitted/founder virus (T/F virus) hallmarks: ultra‑low diversity, star‑like phylogeny, reduced Potential N-Linked Glycosylation Sites (PNGS), and estimated infection time of only 19.5 days.

CONCLUSIONS: MPID-NGS integrates high-fidelity staging, evolutionary profiling, and network analysis, revealing that recent MSM infections are strongly associated with local molecular clusters, elevated clustering risk, and distinct adaptive evolution, thus offering a robust tool for HIV-1 surveillance and intervention.

articles.title: Residential setting as an effect modifier of intellectual and physical disability associations with COVID-19 infection, hospitalisation and mortality in Scotland.
articles.journal: International journal of infectious diseases : IJID : official publication of the International Society for Infectious Diseases
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: People with intellectual and physical disabilities experienced disproportionately adverse COVID-19 outcomes, and communal residential settings were major sites of transmission. However, whether residential setting modifies the associations of these specific disability groups with recorded infection, hospitalisation and mortality has not been examined at population scale. We assessed interaction on both multiplicative and additive scales.

METHODS: We conducted a population-wide retrospective cohort study of 3,719,651 adults aged 16 years or older who were alive and resident in Scotland on 1 March 2020. Disability status was derived from the 2011 Scottish Census and classified as intellectual disability, physical and/or sensory disability without intellectual disability, or no recorded intellectual or physical disability. The latter category was the prespecified comparison group and could include people with other long-term conditions. Residential setting was classified as private dwellings, small communal establishments (<50 residents) or large communal establishments (50 or more residents). Outcomes were first laboratory-confirmed SARS-CoV-2 infection, first COVID-19 hospitalisation and COVID-19-related mortality from 1 March 2020 to 30 April 2022. Cox proportional hazards models estimated joint category hazard ratios and departures from multiplicative and additive no-interaction models.

RESULTS: For recorded infection, interaction was positive on both scales. Multiplicative interaction was significant (χ²(4) = 541.42, p < 0.001), with joint hazard ratios for intellectual disability increasing from 2.54 (95% CI 2.46-2.62) in private dwellings to 9.42 (95% CI 8.08-11.00) in large communal establishments; corresponding estimates for physical disability increased from 1.55 (95% CI 1.53-1.57) to 5.67 (95% CI 5.37-5.98). RERI was 6.09 (95% CI 4.63-7.54) for intellectual disability and 3.31 (95% CI 3.00-3.62) for physical disability in large communal establishments. For hospitalisation, there was no clear evidence of interaction (χ²(4) = 9.32, p = 0.050; all RERI confidence intervals included zero). For mortality, interaction was negative on both scales (χ²(4) = 106.58, p < 0.001), with predominantly negative RERI estimates in communal establishments, most notably for intellectual disability in small communal establishments (RERI -2.07, 95% CI -3.21 to -0.93).

CONCLUSIONS: Residential setting modified associations between intellectual and physical disability and COVID-19 outcomes, with positive interaction for infection, no clear interaction for hospitalisation, and negative interaction for mortality. These findings support pandemic preparedness that considers disability and residential setting together, including tailored infection prevention in communal settings.

articles.title: Constraint-induced movement therapy after ischemic stroke: From cortical reorganization to molecular plasticity.
articles.abstract: Stroke recovery is a dynamic, multilevel process involving structural, functional, and molecular reorganization of surviving neural circuits. Constraint-induced movement therapy (CIMT) has emerged as one of the most effective rehabilitation strategies for improving upper-limb motor function after stroke by overcoming learned nonuse and promoting activity-dependent plasticity. This review integrates clinical and experimental evidence to provide a comprehensive mechanistic framework of CIMT-induced recovery. At the systems level, motor recovery is governed by peri-infarct plasticity, diaschisis reversal, and behavioral adaptation within a temporally defined plasticity window. Experimental studies using middle cerebral artery occlusion (MCAO) models demonstrate that CIMT enhances synaptic remodeling, neurogenesis, angiogenesis, and neurovascular adaptation in peri-infarct regions. At the molecular level, CIMT engages coordinated signaling pathways, including brain-derived neurotrophic factor (BDNF)-TrkB signaling, synaptic structural proteins (GAP-43, synaptophysin, PSD-95), modulation of axonal growth inhibition via the Nogo-A/ROCK pathway, and regenerative processes that support neural circuit reorganization. Comparative analysis indicates that CIMT primarily drives task-specific cortical plasticity, whereas treadmill exercise promotes global neuroplasticity through neurotrophic and neurovascular mechanisms. Combined rehabilitation strategies integrate these complementary effects, leading to synergistic recovery across multiple functional domains. From a translational perspective, optimal rehabilitation likely requires a multimodal framework integrating task-specific, aerobic, and neuromodulatory interventions. Future research should focus on identifying biomarkers of responsiveness and defining optimal timing, intensity, and sequencing of therapies to enable personalized rehabilitation strategies.

articles.title: Technical and clinical feasibility of a pulmonary telerehabilitation model for people with COPD.
articles.journal: Archives of physical medicine and rehabilitation
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: To evaluate (1) the technical feasibility of transmitting data from devices connected to an application used for pulmonary rehabilitation (PR) in people with chronic obstructive pulmonary disease, (2) the clinical feasibility of a home-based PR (HBPR) program using an application integrating essential components of PR, and (3) exploratory clinical outcomes. (NCT05314686).

DESIGN: Prospective two-phase feasibility study.

SETTING: Single-center HBPR program.

PARTICIPANTS: Twenty participants were included in Phase 1 and 20 in Phase 2.

INTERVENTIONS: Phase 1 assessed technical feasibility during endurance sessions using a pulse oximeter and a physical activity tracker connected to the application. Phase 2 assessed clinical feasibility of an 8-week HBPR program.

MAIN OUTCOME MEASURES: Technical feasibility was assessed using the percentage of clinical agreement between locally stored and transmitted data. Clinical feasibility included retention, satisfaction, and usability. Exploratory clinical outcomes were assessed before and after the program.

RESULTS: Locally stored data and those transmitted throughout the application were similar for heart rate, transcutaneous oxygen saturation, and daily step count with a percentage of clinical agreement of at least 99%. Nineteen participants (95%) completed HBPR with high level of satisfaction (Client Satisfaction Questionnaire-8 (median 30, IQR 25 to 32)), and usability (System usability scale (median 80.0, IQR 62.5 to 100.0)). Endurance time during the constant work-rate exercise test increased following HBPR (median of paired differences 171.00 seconds, 95% CI 17.00 to 725.00).

CONCLUSIONS: Devices connected to the application can monitor patients accurately while delivering PR. The HBPR program was feasible and highly accepted by patients and their family members. Future randomized controlled studies are needed to further assess its clinical efficacy.

articles.title: Abnormal left ventricular mass as a prognostic marker for outcomes in infants and children with cirrhosis.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND/AIMS: Cirrhotic cardiomyopathy (CCM), a clinically consequential comorbidity of cirrhosis, remains undefined and underappreciated in children. This study aimed to characterize myocardial structural, functional, morphometric, and histopathologic features in pediatric cirrhosis and objectively derive a reliable echocardiographic (2DE) metric to predict perioperative adverse events, including mortality.

METHODS: 2DE, morphometry, histopathology, and vasoactive-inotropic score (VIS) were compared between children with (n=226) and without (n=160) cirrhosis listed for liver transplantation (LT) over 2011-2021. Discriminatory performance of left ventricular mass index (height)2.7(LVMI g/m2.7) for predicting waitlist decompensation, composite serious adverse events post liver transplant and mortality was assessed using ROC analysis, with AUCs and optimal thresholds compared against PELD-Cr/MELD scores.

RESULTS: LV mass was significantly higher in children with cirrhosis on 2DE and necropsy specimens compared to non-cirrhotic controls, with ∼25% demonstrating LV hypertrophy, with OR of 6.9 [CI 3,16], p< 0.0001. In the cirrhotic cohort, LVMI correlated with vasoactive needs under stress of LT (p <0.001) and was significantly higher in patients with WLD, CSAE, and non-survivors. In cirrhosis, LVMI values ≥ 88 g/m2.7, ≥ 91 g/m2.7, and ≥ 95 g/m2.7 were independently associated with WLD, CSAE, and mortality, when adjusting for PELD-Cr/MELD, bilirubin, and INR (p <0.01). Combining LVMI + PELD-Cr/MELD significantly outperformed PELD-Cr/MELD in discriminating both WLD and CSAE, whereas LVMI alone significantly outperformed PELD-Cr/MELD for CSAE and was comparable for WLD. All three models performed comparably in discriminating death.

CONCLUSION: LVMI is a strong predictor of morbidity and mortality, serving as a prognostic marker in children with cirrhosis. Incorporating LVMI into PELD-Cr/MELD may enhance risk stratification and organ allocation.

articles.title: Mixed Strain Infections and Microevolution of Mycobacterium tuberculosis: Genetic Diversity in a High-Burden Setting of Northeastern Brazil.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Tuberculosis (TB) control in high-burden settings is complicated by the genetic diversity of Mycobacterium tuberculosis (Mtb), which influences transmission. This study assessed the prevalence of mixed strain infections (MSIs) and microevolutionary events, analyzing their association with biosocial and clinical variables in Fortaleza, northeastern Brazil.

METHODS: This prospective study included 168 patients with pulmonary TB from two referral hospitals serving socioeconomically vulnerable populations. Mtb isolates were subjected to drug resistance testing using Xpert MTB/RIF, MGIT 960, SIRE kit, and 24-locus mycobacterial interspersed repetitive unit-variable number tandem repeat typing. Genetic diversity was classified as MSI when multiple alleles were detected at two or more loci, or as a microevolutionary event when multiple alleles were detected at a single locus. Clinical and socioeconomic data were correlated with the genotypic profiles of the patients.

RESULTS: Genetic diversity was observed in 10 isolates (6%), comprising three (1.75%) MSIs and seven microevolutionary events. Among the 10 patients with genetic diversity, the median age was 46 years, and illicit drug use was reported in this subgroup. All MSIs were rifampicin-sensitive; four of the seven cases with microevolution showed rifampicin resistance. Half of the patients with genetic diversity showed poor treatment outcomes in the form of death, failure, and loss of follow-up; comorbid conditions such as diabetes, syphilis, and previous TB were common in this subgroup.

CONCLUSIONS: The patterns of Mtb genetic diversity in this high-burden setting coexist with conditions of social vulnerability and complex disease presentations. These findings highlight the coexistence of Mtb genetic diversity with social and clinical vulnerability in this setting and support further investigation using larger cohorts and higher-resolution genomic approaches.

articles.title: Characterizing the Adverse Event Profile of Semaglutide: A Comprehensive U.S. Food and Drug Administration Adverse Event Reporting System-Based Pharmacovigilance Study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Semaglutide, a glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonist, is increasingly used for the management of type 2 diabetes mellitus and obesity. Given its expanding clinical use, a comprehensive evaluation of its safety profile using real-world data is warranted. This study aimed to characterize adverse event signals associated with semaglutide using the U.S. Food and Drug Administration Adverse Event Reporting System (FAERS).

METHODS: Adverse event reports associated with semaglutide were extracted from the FAERS database from 2004 Q1 to 2025 Q3. After data extraction and screening, cases in which semaglutide was recorded as the primary suspected drug were included. Adverse events were classified according to the Medical Dictionary for Regulatory Activities (MedDRA) at the preferred term (PT) and system organ class (SOC) levels. Signal detection was performed using disproportionality methods, including reporting odds ratio (ROR), proportional reporting ratio (PRR), relative reporting ratio (RRR), and empirical Bayes geometric mean (EBGM).

RESULTS: A total of 43,754 reports were identified. Gastrointestinal disorders were the most frequently reported system organ class, with nausea (n = 5,637; 12.88%), vomiting (n = 4,097; 9.36%), diarrhoea (n = 3,276; 7.49%) and constipation (n = 2,257; 5.16%) being the most frequently reported adverse events. Impaired gastric emptying (n = 2,200; 5.03%) showed a markedly elevated reporting signal. Significant signals were also observed for metabolic and nutritional events, including decreased appetite (n = 2,221; 5.08%), dehydration (n = 1,231; 2.81%) and diabetic ketoacidosis. Notably, high disproportionality signals were detected for weight loss poor and optic ischaemic neuropathy. Additional signals involved psychiatric, renal and hepatobiliary systems. The consistency of findings across multiple statistical methods, including empirical Bayes geometric mean, supports the robustness of the detected signals.

CONCLUSION: Semaglutide is primarily associated with gastrointestinal and metabolic adverse events consistent with its pharmacological effects; however, several less common but potentially important safety signals were identified. These findings highlight the need for continued pharmacovigilance and careful clinical monitoring in real-world use.

articles.title: Anabolic responsiveness in critically ill children: a narrative review and conceptual perspective on nutrient utilization and muscle response.
articles.abstract: Critical illness alters energy metabolism, substrate use, and protein turnover in children, while skeletal muscle loss may continue despite apparently adequate energy and protein delivery. Nutritional adequacy may depend not only on nutrient delivery but also on how effectively nutrients are utilized to preserve muscle and support anabolic responsiveness. This hypothesis-generating narrative review synthesizes evidence on metabolic alterations and anabolic responsiveness in critically ill children, focusing on indirect calorimetry, respiratory quotient (RQ), non-protein RQ (npRQ), nitrogen balance, and quadriceps and diaphragm ultrasound. PubMed/MEDLINE was searched from inception to July 2026, prioritizing pediatric evidence and incorporating adult studies when pediatric data were insufficient. Indirect calorimetry remains the reference bedside method for measuring resting energy expenditure but cannot determine whether nutrients are incorporated into skeletal muscle protein. RQ and npRQ provide information on whole-body substrate oxidation but lack validated pediatric thresholds. Nitrogen balance estimates whole-body protein retention or loss but does not directly reflect skeletal muscle protein balance. Serial ultrasound can track regional muscle changes, although quadriceps and diaphragm measurements reflect different physiological influences. Pediatric studies demonstrate early peripheral muscle loss, while direct measurements of muscle protein synthesis and breakdown remain limited. No routinely available bedside method can directly assess anabolic responsiveness or confirm anabolic resistance. Integrating metabolic measurements with serial muscle assessment may identify mismatches between nutrient delivery and tissue response but remains hypothesis-generating. Prospective studies incorporating direct protein kinetics are needed to determine when anabolic responsiveness is restored and whether this can guide nutritional and rehabilitation strategies.

articles.title: Balloon-occluded pulmonary arteriography and n-butyl cyanoacrylate embolization of angiographically occult pulmonary artery pseudoaneurysms.
articles.journal: Journal of vascular and interventional radiology : JVIR
articles.abstract: Angiographically occult pulmonary artery pseudoaneurysms - suspected on computed tomography but not shown at selective pulmonary angiography - have been presumed to have an occluded parent artery, and systemic-feeder embolization alone is often not curative. Three consecutive men with infection-related pseudoaneurysms presenting with massive hemoptysis were treated. In each, selective pulmonary angiography without occlusion showed proximal washout of injected contrast, consistent with reversed flow in the parent branch. The branch was occluded immediately proximal to the sac with a 4.0-mm microballoon - or, initially in one patient, a fortuitously wedged 5-F catheter - and hand injection under occlusion opacified the previously occult sac, which was then embolized with 25% n-butyl cyanoacrylate through a microballoon, without same-session systemic-artery embolization. All three achieved technical and clinical success, without recurrent hemoptysis over 17-22 months. Occultness does not equate to an occluded parent artery.

articles.title: In Vitro Development and Evaluation of an Endovascular Islet Cell Stent for Type 1 Diabetes Mellitus.
articles.journal: Journal of vascular and interventional radiology : JVIR
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: To describe the in vitro development and benchtop evaluation of the IsletStent, an endovascular biologic stent-graft incorporating expanded polytetrafluoroethylene (ePTFE) semipermeable membranes, designed for portal venous delivery of pancreatic islets as a treatment for type 1 diabetes mellitus.

MATERIALS AND METHODS: Prototypes with a 0.22 μm pore ePTFE membrane were seeded with murine (approximately 5,000-6,000 islet equivalents [IEQ]) or human (approximately 10,000 IEQ) islets. A benchtop normothermic perfusion circuit simulated intravascular deployment. Glucose-stimulated insulin secretion (GSIS) was assessed in a repeated-measures design (n = 4 devices per experiment); murine islet-seeded devices were perfused under zero (0 mM), low (2.8 mM), and high (28 mM) glucose, and human islet-seeded devices under low and high glucose only, with insulin quantified by ELISA. Computational fluid dynamics (CFD) modeling under idealized, non-physiologic single-fluid conditions evaluated candidate device geometries.

RESULTS: Murine islet-seeded devices demonstrated glucose-responsive insulin secretion: 3-hour insulin concentrations were 83 ± 8 vs. 145 ± 20 μIU/mL under low vs. high glucose (p = 0.02), and secretion rates were 5,344 ± 144 vs. 6,795 ± 503 μIU/hr (p = 0.008). Human islet-seeded devices responded concordantly, with 3-hour insulin concentrations of 229 ± 13 vs. 300 ± 17 μIU/mL (p = 0.014).

CONCLUSION: In this benchtop perfusion model, islets housed within an ePTFE-based endovascular stent-graft retained glucose-responsive insulin secretion. In vivo evaluation of islet viability, direct immunoisolation, hemodynamic impact, and long-term function is required before clinical translation.

articles.title: Impact of Simple Vascular Quality Initiative Frailty Score on Outcomes of Venous Leg Ulcer Healing and Recurrence.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Up to 1% of patients with chronic venous disease will present with a primary venous Leg Ulcer (VLU). This study aimed to analyze the impact of frailty as measured by the Simple Vascular Quality Initiative-Frailty Score (sVQI-FS) on the outcomes of patients undergoing treatment for a VLU.

METHODS: Between 2012 and 2024, all patients presenting with a VLU were analyzed. Inclusion criteria were an active VLU, in the presence of superficial truncal venous incompetence, and without total deep venous incompetence (classified as involving all 18 named venous segments) on duplex imaging. Frailty was assessed by the sVQI-FS (congestive heart failure, renal impairment, chronic obstructive pulmonary disease, not living at home, not ambulatory, anemia, and underweight status with a BMI of less than 18.5). An sVQI-FS score of 0.3 or greater was considered frail. Demographics and interventions to effect healing were recorded. The primary outcomes were ulcer healing at 24 weeks and VLU recurrence within one year.

RESULTS: 534 patients (61% female, age 67 ± 9 years, mean ± SD) presented with an active VLU. 43% of patients were classified as frail by the sVQI-FS. 31% had their ulcer for >12 months. Frail patients were more likely to have longer ulcer duration (7.1 ± 0.9 vs. 4.7 ± 1.1 months; Frail vs. Non-Frail; Mean ± SD; p=0.001) and have a longer interval before referral compared to non-frail patients (5.6 ± 1.2 vs. 3.9 ± 1.1 months, mean ± SD; p=0.001). Frailty was associated with more severe ulcers as measured by wound bed scores (11 ± 3 vs. 15 ± 5; Non-Frail vs. Frail; Mean ± SD; Frail vs. Non-Frail; p=0.001). The intensity of therapy, as measured by the sum of scheduled and unscheduled clinic visits and all interventions, was 1.8 times higher in the frail group than in the Non-Frail group (p = 0.001). Initial VLU healing was 26 ± 2% and 16 ± 2% at 12 weeks for Non-Frail and Frail, respectively (mean ± SEM; p=0.001). By 24 weeks, initial VLU healing was 67 ± 4% and 38 ± 4%, for Non-Frail and Frail, respectively (p=0.003). Freedom from VLU recurrence was 59 ± 4% and 36 ± 5% at 1 year (mean ± SEM; p=0.002). and 30 ± 6%, and 18 ± 7% at 3 years for Non Frail and Frail, respectively (p=0.002).

CONCLUSIONS: Frailty significantly affects early referral for VLU care, is associated with more severe ulcers, and impacts both VLU healing rates and recurrence rates. Intervening to identify and ameliorate frailty is necessary to enhance VLU care.

articles.title: Assessing the incidence of retinal hemorrhage in pediatric patients following COVID-19 vaccination.
articles.journal: Journal of AAPOS : the official publication of the American Association for Pediatric Ophthalmology and Strabismus
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Retinal hemorrhages (RHs) are a cardinal finding in abusive head trauma (AHT) for which a broad differential diagnosis is appropriate to consider. The frequency of COVID-19 vaccination and reports of subsequent ocular manifestations have led to the consideration of whether COVID-19 vaccination should be included in the RH differential. This study aimed to investigate the frequency of RH following COVID-19 vaccination in children.

METHODS: In this single-center, retrospective, observational cohort study, we reviewed the medical records of children ≤8 years of age who received a COVID-19 vaccine from July 1, 2020, to July 1, 2024, and underwent a fundus examination within 21 days of vaccination. The main outcome measure was incidence and characteristics of RH on fundus examination.

RESULTS: Of 17,926 children vaccinated during this period, 203 subjects met inclusion criteria and underwent 212 unique examinations, with mean age of 4.56 years (0-8) at the time of first examination. Twenty examinations were also in the setting of prior COVID-19 infection. No examinations revealed RH. Based on Hanley's rule of zero incidence, the 95th percentile upper limit of incidence of RH after COVID-19 vaccination is 4.11% at 7 days, 2.04% at 14 days, and 1.42% at 21 days following vaccination.

CONCLUSIONS: RHs were not seen in any children within 21 days of COVID-19 vaccination. This suggests that RH is rare following COVID-19 vaccination and perhaps of little relevance to the differential diagnosis of RH in the evaluation for AHT.

articles.title: Investigation of CardioFreeze Motion Correction for Cardiac PET/CT.
articles.journal: Journal of nuclear cardiology : official publication of the American Society of Nuclear Cardiology
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Cardiac imaging with positron emission tomography and computed tomography (PET/CT) is a principal technique in the diagnosis and prognostication of coronary artery disease. PET/CT image quality can be negatively impacted by patient, cardiac, and respiratory motion.

METHODS: We evaluated images from 102 patients clinically referred for cardiac rest/stress Rb-82 PET/CT myocardial perfusion imaging. Patient images were processed with a prototype data-driven motion detection algorithm and stratified by motion severity. Images were subjected to cardiac (CS) or cardiac and respiratory (CD) motion correction via a novel reconstruction tool. Validated image quality markers including target-to-background ratio (TBR) were assessed between corrected and non-corrected images and analyzed via student's t-tests.

RESULTS: The motion detection algorithm identified 36 (35.3%) patients with significant motion. Image processing via CS yielded a statistically significant increase in mean image contrast (TBR 3.65±0.07, p<0.01) and intensified when respiratory motion correction was applied (3.78±0.07, p<0.005). Motion correction is more effective when applied to images containing greater motion, improving mean TBR by 3% (p<0.05) in non-motion scans but >10% (p<0.01) in significant motion cases. Three months post-imaging, 18 patients underwent clinically indicated coronary angiography: seven patients demonstrated significant motion, and CD motion correction improved their image quality to that of patients with no motion.

CONCLUSIONS: Over 1/3 of patients undergoing cardiac PET/CT have detectible motion leading to potential artifacts with clinical significance. Cardiac and respiratory motion correction improves image quality and may improve diagnostic accuracy, particularly when respiratory motion is severe. Further studies are critical to investigate the clinical impacts of improved image quality.

articles.title: Early Pregnancy Exposure to Per- and Polyfluoroalkyl Substances and Hypertensive Disorders of Pregnancy: A Cohort Study in China.
articles.abstract: Maternal exposure to per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFAS) has shown inconsistent associations with hypertensive disorders of pregnancy (HDP). This prospective cohort study examined the associations between early pregnancy serum PFAS concentrations and HDP risk, evaluating potential effect modification by fetal sex among 2,984 pregnant women in Henan Province, China (2018-2021). Sixteen PFAS were measured in early pregnancy serum samples, with nine retained for analysis based on detection rates ≥70%. Multivariable logistic regression models estimated odds ratios (ORs) and 95% confidence intervals (CIs) adjusting for confounders. Of the participants, 112 (3.8%) developed gestational hypertension and 137 (4.6%) developed preeclampsia. Doubling of serum PFDoA concentration was nominally associated with increased odds of both gestational hypertension (OR = 1.31; 95% CI: 1.08, 1.60) and preeclampsia (OR = 1.21; 95% CI: 1.01, 1.45). Conversely, doubling of 6:2Cl-PFESA was nominally associated with lower odds of preeclampsia (OR = 0.86; 95% CI: 0.77, 0.97). Quantile g-computation indicated that although the overall PFAS mixture was not significantly associated with HDP risk, PFDoA consistently contributed substantial positive weights to the mixture effects for both outcomes. In exploratory analyses, fetal sex appeared to modify the association between PFDoA and gestational hypertension (P-interaction = 0.035), with elevated odds observed among female fetuses (OR = 1.71; 95% CI: 1.27, 2.35) compared to male fetuses (OR = 1.07; 95% CI: 0.82, 1.39). These findings suggest congener-specific effects and sex-modulated susceptibility, indicating that early pregnancy PFDoA exposure may be associated with elevated HDP risk, warranting further investigation to validate these associations.

articles.title: The 2026-27 El Niño event: what should UK infection services expect?
articles.abstract: A strong 2026-27 El Niño is developing, with potentially important consequences for infectious-disease epidemiology worldwide. For UK infection services, the principal effect is likely to arise indirectly through changes in the incidence and geographical distribution of infections among returning travellers, particularly vector-borne and enteric infections, rather than through substantial increases in infections acquired within the UK. Changes in rainfall, temperature, flooding and drought may alter transmission patterns internationally, while invasive mosquito detections, changing vector ecology and extreme weather provide smaller and less predictable potential routes to domestic effects. However, associations between El Niño and infectiousdisease outbreaks are complex, and should not be interpreted deterministically. For UK infection specialists, the appropriate response is proportionate vigilance; this includes obtaining detailed travel and exposure histories, using contemporary outbreak surveillance to inform differential diagnoses, and recognising and acting on unusual epidemiological signals promptly. El Niño should be viewed as a temporary modifier of infectious-disease risk rather than a predictor of individual outbreaks.

articles.title: Management of suspected infectious and autoimmune encephalitis in adults - National Guidelines from the United Kingdom Joint Societies.
articles.abstract: Encephalitis, characterised by inflammation of the brain parenchyma, is a neurological emergency with diverse infectious, autoimmune and inflammatory causes. Delays in recognition and treatment carry significant risks of morbidity and mortality. Since the first UK guideline for management of suspected viral encephalitis in adults was published in 2012, there have been substantial developments in this field. Advances in molecular diagnostics, antibody testing, alongside improved access to neuroimaging and electrophysiology have broadened the capacity to identify underlying aetiologies. The recognised spectrum of infectious and immune-mediated causes has expanded, and clinical experience with immunomodulatory therapies has grown considerably. A multidisciplinary national working group, representing neurology, infectious diseases, microbiology, virology, neuroimmunology and acute medicine, alongside national professional and third-sector organisations, was convened in Liverpool in 2023 to develop updated UK Joint Societies guidelines for the management of suspected infectious and autoimmune encephalitis in adults. This guideline provides pragmatic, evidence-informed recommendations on clinical recognition, investigation, diagnosis, acute management and rehabilitation. It emphasises early identification and parallel consideration of infectious and immune-mediated causes, with particular attention to decision-making during the critical first 24-72hours of presentation. Standardised diagnostic and therapeutic pathways are presented to support consistent care across healthcare settings. Where the evidence base remains limited, the need for multidisciplinary input is highlighted. These recommendations aim to reduce mortality, limit long-term neurological morbidity and improve outcomes for adults with encephalitis across the UK.

articles.title: Impaired muscle quality and physical performance in diabetic neuropathy: associations with skeletal characteristics from the Deep Phenotyping Study.
articles.abstract:
AIMS: We examined whether diabetic neuropathy is associated with altered muscle morphology, strength, and physical performance, and whether muscle characteristics relate to skeletal health.

METHODS: In this cross-sectional study, 123 individuals with type 2 diabetes were classified into +/- neuropathy based on peripheral and autonomic assessments. Tibial muscle morphology and bone microarchitecture were assessed using high-resolution peripheral quantitative computed tomography, while dual-energy X-ray absorptiometry assessed appendicular lean mass (ALM/height2) and femoral neck bone mineral density (FN aBMD). Muscle strength was evaluated by handgrip and knee extension, and physical performance by chair stand test (CST), timed up-and-go (TUG), and usual gait speed (UGS). Associations were examined using multivariate linear regression adjusted for age, sex, and BMI.

RESULTS: Neuropathy was associated with lower muscle volume and density, but not ALM/height2 or muscle strength. Individuals with neuropathy performed fewer CST repetitions, had longer TUG times, and slower UGS. Higher muscle density was associated with higher FN aBMD, favorable cortical bone parameters, and greater estimated bone strength.

CONCLUSIONS: Diabetic neuropathy is associated with lower distal muscle density and volume, poorer physical performance but preserved strength and ALM. Associations between muscle density and bone characteristics suggest an interrelationship between neuropathy, muscle quality and skeletal fragility in type 2 diabetes.

articles.title: Metagenomic and systematic analyses reveal the association between hemoglobin levels and metabolic disorders: an open cohort study of Tibetan adults in Qinghai Plateau.
articles.abstract:
AIM: Hemoglobin (Hb) varies with altitude, but evidence linking Hb levels to metabolic diseases in high-altitude populations remains limited. We examined associations between Hb and seven metabolic diseases in high-altitude adults and potential mediation by gut microbiota.

METHODS: We analyzed an observational cohort of 1,646 Tibetan adults from the Qinghai Plateau, stratified by Hb tertiles. Mixed-effects logistic regression and generalized additive mixed models assessed Hb-metabolic disease associations using pooled person-time data. Gut metagenomic sequencing and mediation analysis were performed on 534 fecal samples, with KEGG annotation characterizing microbial functional potential.

RESULTS: Hb correlated positively with six metabolic diseases (P < 0.05). Compared with the lowest tertile (122-151 g/L), the highest Hb tertile (169-252 g/L) showed significantly increased adjusted ORs for diabetes (10.02; 95% CI 3.00-33.43), hypertension (2.08; 1.14-3.80), hypercholesterolemia (3.04; 1.24-7.45), hypertriglyceridemia (4.66; 1.60-13.56), overweight/obesity (5.15; 1.83-14.48) and metabolic syndrome (4.58; 2.50-8.38). High Hb were associated with differences in gut microbiota β-diversity (P = 0.001) and composition. Prevotella and Collinsella were enriched in high-Hb, Bifidobacterium and Anaerostipes dominated low-Hb. Twenty-three microbial species mediated Hb-metabolic relationships. Fructose-mannose metabolism and oxidative phosphorylation were enriched in high-Hb, while ABC transporters and fatty acid biosynthesis/metabolism were upregulated in low-Hb.

CONCLUSION: Hb may serve as a useful biomarker for metabolic risk assessment in high-altitude populations, with gut microbiota potentially mediating this association.

articles.title: Co-designed workplace resistance exercise training to improve metabolic and musculoskeletal health in office workers with Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus, A mixed-methods formative evaluation study.
articles.abstract:
AIMS: This mixed method study aimed to co-design a feasible, evidence-informed, and stakeholder-endorsed workplace-based resistance exercise (RE) intervention.

METHODS: Following a systematic review based informed pool of RE and their dose, a 12-member multidisciplinary expert panel and end-user office workers with T2DM participated in a two-round consensus process. A two-round survey was conducted to inform quantitative suitability of RE exercise and concurrently qualitative focus group discussions were administered to capture operational barriers, facilitators, and behavioral modification parameters.

RESULTS: Seventeen RE's were systematically identified from the contemporary literature. Twelve exercises met the predefined numeric consensus threshold, while five were excluded (I-CVI < 0.80). Finally, 7 RE's achieved a high final content validity score (I-CVI = 0.869). The final co-designed intervention prescribes following dose, 3  days per week across 3 brief workday micro-sessions (10-15-minute morning, 10-15-minute postprandial lunchtime, and 10-15-minute late afternoon. Qualitative analysis synthesized data across seven distinct operational themes, prescription, challenges, behavioral factors, social support, personal factors, general and occupational health considerations.

CONCLUSIONS: A feasible, accessible, context specific and stakeholder-validated workplace RE program was developed for desk-bound workers with T2DM. Long-term tracking of specific glycemic fluctuations and musculoskeletal adaptive capabilities will be formally evaluated in upcoming clinical trials.

TRIAL REGISTRATION: Clinical Trial Registry-India (CTRI/2025/08/092670).

articles.title: Automated detection of inflammation in foot thermographic images of patients with diabetes acquired in an uncontrolled clinical environment.
articles.abstract:
AIMS: Quantitative methods for detecting diabetic foot inflammation remain limited, though localized skin-temperature elevation is a promising early indicator. Because background variability can hinder AI-based foot identification, we evaluated AI-driven thermal imaging for diabetic foot inflammation under uncontrolled clinical backgrounds and assessed whether curtain-based background control and grayscale conversion improved detection.

METHODS: Cross-sectional study design was conducted in Makassar, Indonesia, 100 plantar thermal images from 50 diabetic patients were acquired with and without a curtain, preprocessed (sensitivity, 1.5; emissivity, 0.98), and converted to grayscale. Expert-identified inflammatory hotspots were annotated and used to train a YOLO11n model with 5-fold cross-validation, evaluated using accuracy, precision, sensitivity, specificity, ROC-AUC, IoU, and case-error analysis.

RESULTS: With a curtain, color-map images achieved sensitivity of 0.773, versus 0.455 without one. Grayscale images performed consistently across conditions, with best results in the mixed dataset (accuracy, 0.980; precision, 0.976; sensitivity, 0.932; specificity, 0.994; AUC 0.966 vs. 0.886 for color-map). Correctly detected cases showed IoU > 0.9. Low thermal contrast and small region of interest were the most frequent failure categories.

CONCLUSIONS: AI-driven thermal imaging detects diabetic foot inflammation under uncontrolled conditions. A curtain improved color-map detection, but grayscale imaging provided robust, curtain-independent performance, supporting its use for clinical screening.

articles.title: Allergen-induced trained immunity in alveolar macrophages predisposes to long-lasting airway hypersensitivity.
articles.abstract: Allergic asthma is characterized by airway hypersensitivity to various allergens and chronic airway inflammation. The mechanisms underlying such a prolonged and broad-responsive airway hypersensitivity remain not fully understood. In this study, we systematically investigated the role of allergen-induced trained immunity in tissue resident alveolar macrophages (AMs) and its impact on long-lasting airway hypersensitivity. Here, we utilized flow cytometry and single-cell transcriptomics to analyze immune cell dynamics in murine asthma model, and we compare the differences between allergen-experienced AMs and naïve AMs. Specifically, we introduce and delve into the concept of allergen-induced trained immunity within these particular cells (Trained alveolar macrophages, Tr-AMs). Our findings demonstrated that Tr-AMs preferentially produce pro-eosinophilic chemokines upon subsequent allergen exposure and, therefore, induce exacerbated eosinophilic inflammation in the lung. The induction of Tr-AMs was potentially associated with their interactions with other immune cells, such as natural killer cells, dendritic cells, and Th2 cells. Both IFN-γ and IL-4 are critical for AM activation, we found that their simultaneous action on AMs induced the development of an MHCII+ CD206+ Tr-AM phenotype, which was specialized in producing pro-eosinophilic chemokines, including CCL24 (eotaxin-2) and CCL5 (RANTES). This study highlights the establishment and roles of Tr-AMs in pro-asthmatic airway hypersensitivity, providing a new understanding of the pathogenesis and recurrence of allergic asthma.

articles.title: Assessing the ability of cross-trained pharmacy technician-community health workers to identify non-medical drivers of health resources.
articles.journal: Journal of the American Pharmacists Association : JAPhA
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Community pharmacies are increasingly attempting to address non-medical drivers of health (NMDoH) by screening patients for health-related social needs (HRSNs). Cross-training pharmacy technicians as community health workers (PhT-CHWs) may expand pharmacies' capacity to provide these services, but little is known about the community resources identified by PhT-CHWs during training or their associated Z-codes. Characterizing these resources may inform implementation of pharmacy-based community resource referral services.

OBJECTIVE: To describe the NMDoH resources identified by PhTs who completed CHW training and the Z-codes assigned to those resources to characterize the community resource infrastructure available to support pharmacy-based CHW services.

METHODS: This cross-sectional study analyzed resource development assignments completed by PhTs enrolled in a nationally recognized CHW training program between 2021 and 2022. Data included community resource information and learner-assigned ICD-10-CM Z-codes. Descriptive statistics were used to summarize resource characteristics and Z-code assignments.

RESULTS: A total of 297 PhT-CHWs from 182 community pharmacies completed the training and identified 4,480 community resources. Most resources had a physical location (n = 4,405; 98.3%), while 65 (1.5%) were online only and 10 (0.2%) were telephone-only. Community resources were assigned 12,538 Z-codes, with an average of 3.13 Z-codes (range: 1-11; median: 2; IQR: 1-4) per resource. The most frequently assigned Z-code categories related to housing and economic circumstances, food insecurity, insurance and welfare support, and education and literacy.

CONCLUSION: PhTs who completed CHW training identified a broad range of community resources that address diverse HRSNs. These findings provide foundational information on the community resource infrastructure that may support implementation of pharmacy-based CHW services and community resource referral workflows. Future research should evaluate how these resource inventories are integrated into pharmacy practice and their impact on patient care.

articles.title: Cost-effectiveness of insulin regimens and insulin types for adults with type 1 diabetes: a systematic review.
articles.journal: Value in health : the journal of the International Society for Pharmacoeconomics and Outcomes Research
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To assess the global cost-effectiveness of insulin regimens, comparing long- and short-acting insulin analogues to human insulins, in adults with T1D.

METHODS: Systematic review (CRD420250654279). We searched MEDLINE, Embase, Web of Science, WHO Global Index Medicus, and the HTA database on 17 March 2025. We included full economic evaluations comparing insulin regimens for adults with T1D. Incremental Cost Effectiveness Ratios (ICERs) and Incremental Cost Utility Ratios (ICURs) were converted and adjusted into a common currency (2024 US dollar) using purchasing power parity. The SBU and the CHEERS checklists were used for quality assessment.

RESULTS: We included 35 studies, covering 50 insulin comparisons across 19 countries, predominantly in Europe. Most studies were model-based (97%) and industry-funded (86%). Several studies indicated that analogue-based regimens may be cost-effective under study-specific assumptions (ICURs ranging from USD 4,550 to 10,720.28 per QALY). Among 35 comparisons of long-acting insulins, findings were mixed: ICERs ranged from USD 17 to 10,940 per 1% HbA1c reduction, and ICURs ranged from USD 102 to 124 million per QALY. Short-acting insulins were also cost-effective (ICERs ranging from USD 88 to 7,844 per 1% HbA1c annual reduction per patient; ICURs from USD 7,382 to 34,769 per QALY).

CONCLUSIONS: Long- and short-acting insulin analogues are often reported to be cost-effective compared with human insulins in adults with T1D, but this conclusion rests on an evidence base with recurrent methodological limitations, wide statistical uncertainty and a high risk of sponsor-related bias and limited evidence from low- and lower-middle-income countries.

articles.title: A nonexercise equation to predict VO2 peak in chronic heart failure: Integrating clinical variables for prognostic assessment.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Peak oxygen consumption (pVO2) has been widely recognized to identify potential pathophysiological mechanisms of exercise intolerance and to stratify risk in patients with heart failure (HF).

AIMS: To develop a non-exercise equation to estimate pVO2 (esVO2) and to determine its association with all-cause mortality.

METHODS: A total of 5176 HF patients (age 48 ± 17 years) who underwent a CPET for clinical reasons, and were followed between May 2011, and December 1, 2023. Clinical and historical variables and forced expiratory volume in 1-s (FEV1) were used in a stepwise multivariate regression analysis to predict pVO2 measured from CPET. Kaplan-Meier curves and Cox proportional hazards analyses were used to determine the association between esVO2 and all-cause mortality.

RESULTS: The first esVO2 model was significantly associated with pVO2 (multiple R = 0.73, P < 0.001). Two other models considered gender separately (male: multiple R = 0.72, P < 0.001 and female (multiple R = 0.70, P < 0.001). A fourth model was proposed when spirometry is not available (age, BMI, resting SBP, HR and gender (multiple R = 0.69, P < 0.001)). The fifth proposed model included history of atrial fibrillation and previous stroke (multiple R = 0.70, P < 0.001). Kaplan-Meier survival curves differentiated patients according to esVO2 and pVO2 ≤ and > 14 mL/kg-1 per min-1. Univariate Cox proportional hazard analyses indicated significant prognostic value when esVO2 and pVO2 were ≤ 14 mL/kg-1 per min-1 (P = 0.001).

CONCLUSIONS: Multivariable nonexercise models combining spirometry and/or clinical variables commonly obtained during a clinical assessment predict pVO2 reasonably accurately in HF.

articles.title: Hypertension and clinical outcomes following thoracic radiotherapy.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Radiation therapy (RT) is highly efficacious in treating thoracic malignancies. However, RT has been linked to potential cardiotoxicity. Yet, the long-term incidence, severity, and implications of HTN-development post-RT are unknown.

METHODS: Leveraging a large US-based Comprehensive-Cancer-Center-cohort of patients treated with thoracic-RT from 2007 to 2019, we included patients ≥18 years old with histologically confirmed esophageal or lung cancers. The primary outcome was incidence of incident/new or worsened HTN [systolic-blood-pressure-(SBP) ≥130 mmHg] after RT-initiation. The secondary outcomes were major-adverse-cardiac-events (MACE- heart-failure, myocardial-infarction, arrhythmia, stroke, and sudden-death), disease-progression, and overall-survival, by HTN-status. Differences in outcomes by HTN-status were also evaluated via landmark-analysis, excluding those with undiagnosed HTN. Observed new HTN rates were compared to Framingham-predicted-rates, and absolute-excess-risks were estimated. Multivariate regression was used to define the relation between clinical and RT measures and both new or worsened HTN-development and survival-outcomes.

RESULTS: Overall, 439 RT-treated patients (238 esophageal; 201 lung; 66.7% male; mean age 63.6 years; 65% baseline HTN) were identified. Over a median follow-up of 23 months, 255 (58.1%) developed new or worsened HTN; median SBP increase of 7 mmHg. In landmark-analysis, the cumulative incidence of new or worsened HTN by 1-year was 48.0% and 63.4%, respectively. Using the JNC-8 cutoff of ≥140/90 mmHg, the new HTN rate was 21.6% at 1-year, translating to a 3.4-fold higher rate than the Framingham-predicted-rate (RR 3.37, P < 0.001). In multivariate regression, RT-dose was consistently associated with new or worsened HTN-development (P < 0.05); those with RT-induced-HTN saw improved progression-free-survival and overall-survival (HR 0.67 and 0.54, P < 0.01, respectively). Beyond traditional factors, only RT-dose is consistently associated with MACE (P < 0.05). No specific antihypertensive class prevented RT-related HTN.

CONCLUSIONS: These data suggest that thoracic-RT increases early HTN risk.

articles.title: Nanotechnology-Enabled Delivery of trans-Resveratrol, Quercetin, and Curcumin for Obesity and Type 2 Diabetes.
articles.abstract: Obesity and type 2 diabetes mellitus, as chronic metabolic diseases, contribute to increased global morbidity and mortality. The long-term effectiveness of current approaches, such as lifestyle changes, medications, and surgery, is often limited by poor adherence, side effects, cost, etc. Dietary polyphenols, including trans-resveratrol, quercetin, and curcumin, have shown potential because of their health benefits. However, their clinical use is restricted by low solubility, poor stability, low bioavailability, and limited target specificity. Biocompatible and biodegradable delivery systems, such as liposomes, emulsions, solid lipid nanoparticles, nanostructured lipid carriers, micelles, and polymeric nanoparticles, have emerged as useful tools to overcome these limitations. This review summarizes advances over the past decade in the use of polyphenol-loaded nanoparticles for the treatment of obesity and experimental diabetes, and discusses their potential relevance to type 2 diabetes. It also reviews the reported metabolic outcomes and underlying mechanisms, including inflammation, oxidative stress, adipose tissue remodeling, glucose homeostasis, etc. Finally, this review discusses current challenges and future directions for translating these nanotechnologies from research to practical use.

articles.title: When Does Polyendocrine Metabolic Ovarian Syndrome (PMOS) Change Definition? A Lifespan Perspective on Menopause and Metabolic Health.
articles.journal: Endocrine practice : official journal of the American College of Endocrinology and the American Association of Clinical Endocrinologists
articles.abstract: The evolving concept of Polyendocrine Metabolic Ovarian Syndrome (PMOS) reflects a growing recognition that this condition extends beyond reproductive dysfunction and ovarian morphology to encompass complex interactions among metabolic, endocrine, inflammatory, and cardiometabolic pathways. While PMOS is most commonly diagnosed during the reproductive years, increasing numbers of affected women are now entering perimenopause and menopause, highlighting important limitations of current diagnostic paradigms. Traditional reproductive markers-including ovulatory dysfunction and ovarian morphology-become progressively less informative with advancing age, raising questions about whether the diagnosis remains relevant after menopause. Despite the attenuation of ovarian manifestations, many women with a history of PMOS continue to exhibit persistent metabolic and endocrine abnormalities, including insulin resistance, visceral adiposity, dyslipidemia, metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease, chronic low-grade inflammation, and elevated cardiovascular risk. Emerging evidence suggests that these metabolic consequences may persist across the lifespan and contribute to trajectories of accelerated cardiometabolic aging. This review examines the challenges of applying reproductive-age diagnostic frameworks to midlife and older women and proposes a lifespan model in which PMOS evolves from a predominantly ovarian and reproductive syndrome into a broader metabolic-endocrine phenotype. We explore the clinical implications of this transition for risk assessment, long-term surveillance, and therapeutic decision-making during perimenopause and beyond. As understanding of PMOS continues to evolve, menopause may represent not the end of the syndrome, but rather a shift in its clinical expression. Reframing PMOS as a dynamic lifespan condition may provide a more comprehensive approach to the care of women across aging and support the development of age-appropriate diagnostic and management strategies.

articles.title: Pathological Injury and Gastrointestinal Microbiota Changes in Lambs Infected with Eimeria ovinoidalis Isolate from Gansu, China.
articles.abstract: Coccidiosis poses a serious threat to the sheep industry, with Eimeria ovinoidalis recognized as the primary causative agent. However, quantitative analyses of the pathological damage induced by Eimeria ovinoidalis infection across the entire intestinal tract of sheep, together with investigations into the structural characteristics of the gastrointestinal microbiota, remain scarce. In this study, Eimeria ovinoidalis was isolated and purified from the feces of naturally infected sheep in Gansu Province, China. Purified sporulated oocysts were orally administered to lambs to establish an experimental infection model. Clinical signs were monitored throughout the experimental period, and following successful model establishment, oocyst burdens were quantified in each intestinal segment. Histopathological changes and alterations in the gastrointestinal microbiota were systematically evaluated using hematoxylin-eosin (H&E) staining, Sirius Red staining, and 16S rRNA gene high-throughput sequencing. The infected lambs developed typical clinical manifestations, including diarrhea and emaciation, and exhibited a significant reduction in body weight at 14 days post-infection (dpi) (P < 0.05). The highest oocyst burdens were detected in the ileum, cecum, colon, and rectum. Histopathological examination revealed that infection with the Gansu isolate primarily affected intestinal segments extending from the ileum to the colon and was characterized by mucosal epithelial sloughing, lamina propria edema and hemorrhage, crypt destruction, and massive inflammatory cell infiltration. Following infection, eosinophil density increased markedly throughout the intestinal tract (P < 0.01), with the greatest relative increase observed in the colon (1113.13%) and the highest absolute density detected in the ileum (12.01 ± 4.46 cells/10⁴ μm²). Analysis of the 16S rRNA gene sequencing data demonstrated that microbial richness and diversity were significantly reduced in the cecum, colon, and several other intestinal segments of infected lambs (P < 0.05). At the phylum level, the relative abundance of Firmicutes decreased, whereas that of Campylobacterota increased in the hindgut; in contrast, the abundance of Bacteroidota increased in the stomach. At the genus level, pathogenic bacteria, including Campylobacter, were enriched, whereas beneficial bacterial genera were depleted in the hindgut. These findings indicate that infection with the Gansu isolate of Eimeria ovinoidalis induces severe intestinal tissue damage and gut microbial dysbiosis in sheep. These findings provide an important theoretical foundation for elucidating the pathogenic mechanisms of ovine coccidiosis and for developing more effective prevention and control strategies.

articles.title: Obesity and Change in NT-proBNP with Angiotensin-Neprilysin Inhibition in Patients with Mildly Reduced or Preserved Ejection Fraction and a Worsening Heart Failure Event: PARAGLIDE-HF.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To determine the relationship between obesity status and the effect of sacubitril/valsartan (sac/val) vs valsartan (val) on change in NT-proBNP and a hierarchical outcome of clinical benefit among patients with heart failure with mildly reduced or preserved ejection fraction (HFpEF).

BACKGROUND: In the PARAGLIDE-HF trial, patients with HFpEF and a recent worsening HF event randomized to sac/val vs. val had a greater decrease in NT-proBNP over 8 weeks and showed a trend towards clinical benefit. Patients with HFpEF and obesity represent a unique population with high symptom burden and elevated risk for HF hospitalization. The efficacy and safety of sac/val in this high-risk population following a recent worsening HF event is not well characterized.
