Oxidized mitochondrial DNA (Ox-mtDNA), which combines mitochondrial stress with innate immune activation and dysregulated Ca2+ signaling to sustain hyperproliferation and apoptosis resistance in pulmonary arterial endothelial and smooth muscle cells, is a persistent danger signal rather than just a result of mitochondrial injury. Vasodilator therapy targeting the prostacyclin, nitric oxide, and endothelin pathways has made great strides, yet many patients still make progress. These treatments primarily enhance hemodynamics and vasomotor tone, but they do not directly reverse the cellular and molecular mechanisms that sustain pulmonary vascular remodeling. In this model, inflammatory signaling and mitochondrial redox imbalance are mutually reinforcing rather than strictly sequential: oxidative stress produces Ox-mtDNA, which mediates inflammatory activation, and cytokine and interferon signaling from the inflammatory process further weakens antioxidant defenses and mitochondrial respiration, increasing reactive oxygen species (ROS) output. Because Ox-mtDNA's synthesis, escape, sensing, and clearance all influence inflammatory tone and Ca2+ homeostasis, convergent experimental and clinical observations support Ox-mtDNA as an upstream, therapeutically actionable node. This review describes how mtDNA oxidation, reactive oxygen species amplification, and mitochondrial Ca2+ overload are all facilitated by the convergence of chronic hypoxia, inflammatory cytokines, altered shear stress, and genetic vulnerability. According to the literature, oxidative lesions increase mtDNA bioactivity and persistence when nuclease and autophagy-lysosome clearance systems are overloaded. Pathways of cytosolic and extracellular mtDNA escape, such as vesicular export, mitochondrial permeability transition pore (mPTP) or voltage-dependent anion channel (VDAC)-dependent leakage, and sublethal membrane permeabilization, are summarized in this review. It is also explained how Ox-mtDNA rewires the autophagy-mitophagy axis through reduced flux and skewed signaling, allowing injured mitochondria to continue acting as signal emitters. ER Ca2+ handling and stress-induced remodeling of ER-mitochondria contact sites (MAMs) as upstream amplifiers of mitochondrial damage are also covered. Instead of using prospective, longitudinal cohorts, the majority of these mechanistic data and the correlation between circulating Ox-mtDNA and PAH severity are now based on cross-sectional human sampling and non-PAH disease models. Therefore, until such validation is completed, the biomarker potential of Ox-mtDNA should be considered hypothesis-generating.

articles.title: From Computational Models to Clinical Decision-Making in Epilepsy: Bridging the Gap Between Theory and Practice.
articles.abstract: Epilepsy is one of the most heterogeneous and unpredictable neurological disorders, characterized by complex brain dynamics, significant interindividual variability, and a therapeutic response that is often difficult to predict. Despite major advances in neuroimaging, electrophysiology, and antiepileptic treatments, clinical decision-making still faces major challenges, including precisely localizing the epileptogenic zone, predicting seizures, identifying drug-resistant patients, and optimizing personalized therapeutic strategies. Over the past two decades, computational models have gradually emerged as promising tools for addressing these challenges. Early approaches relied primarily on mechanistic biophysical models aimed at reproducing the neural dynamics and mechanisms of hyperexcitability involved in epileptogenesis. More recently, the rise of artificial intelligence and deep learning has facilitated the development of predictive models capable of leveraging large-scale multimodal data. Finally, the emergence of digital brain twins and adaptive closed-loop systems now paves the way for personalized computational medicine integrating simulation, prediction, and real-time therapeutic intervention. This review provides a critical analysis of the major international initiatives developed between 2004 and 2026, including the EPICLUSTER/EBRAINS, EPINOSTICS, ENIGMA-Epilepsy, NeuroPace RNS, SeizeIT, EpiBioS4Rx, and NeuroVista projects, as well as several translational platforms based on artificial intelligence and biophysical modeling. We evaluate the actual contribution of these models to clinical decision-making in epilepsy, their translational contributions, their methodological limitations, and the challenges associated with their integration into hospital settings. We argue that the future of computational epileptology does not rest on the opposition between artificial intelligence and mechanistic models, but on their convergence within explainable, personalized, and clinically interpretable hybrid architectures.

articles.title: Next-generation pharmacological strategies for Parkinson's disease: a systematic literature review of symptom management and disease modification.
articles.journal: Neurological sciences : official journal of the Italian Neurological Society and of the Italian Society of Clinical Neurophysiology
articles.abstract: Parkinson disease is an ongoing neurodegenerative disorder, and both motor and non-motor symptoms are involved with the existing therapies having minimal effects on the disease but only symptom alleviation. The goal of this systematic literature review was to generalize up-to-date evidence on the next-generation pharmacological strategies to manage the symptoms and the disease in a patient with Parkinson disease. The review was based on PRISMA 2020 and included the analysis of peer-reviewed studies of human research published in 2015-2026 and retrieved in the key databases, such as PubMed, Scopus, Web of Science, and Cochrane Library. This included 30 eligible studies consisting of randomized studies, observational studies, and early clinical trials. The results show that, although dopaminergic treatment continues to play a central role in managing motor symptoms, new methods such as gene therapy, gene editing, stem cell-based regeneration, nanomedicine delivery systems, repurposed drugs, artificial intelligence-based precision medicine approaches have a good neuroprotective and disease-modifying potential. Nonetheless, the majority of new interventions are still in preclinical or first line clinical phase, with a defined subset of emerging gene-, cell-, and nanotechnology-based approaches evaluated only in animal or in-vitro models rather than in PD patients and associated with small sample size, invasive delivery, limited follow-up and lack of long-term safety information. In general, the review concludes by stating that there has been significant advancement in diversification of therapeutic targets and mechanisms, but rigorous large-scale biomarker-directed clinical trials are needed to translate these advances to effective and sustainable treatment of the Parkinson disease.

articles.title: Impact of a dietary and exercise intervention on health-related quality of life of prostate cancer patients on active surveillance with overweight/obesity: a secondary analysis of a randomized controlled trial.
articles.journal: Supportive care in cancer : official journal of the Multinational Association of Supportive Care in Cancer
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: Quality of life (QOL) is important for men on active surveillance (AS) for prostate cancer (PCa). To improve QOL, interventions such as those focused on diet and exercise have been proposed. However, their effectiveness remains unclear, especially in individuals with overweight/obesity.

METHODS: We previously conducted and published a randomized controlled trial of a lifestyle intervention for PCa patients on AS with overweight/obesity. Men were randomized to as follows: (1) 6-month diet and exercise intervention with a 7% weight loss goal vs (2) provided US Dietary and Physical Activity Guidelines. Herein, we report the secondary QOL findings from the trial. QOL was assessed at baseline and conclusion of the intervention via four validated questionnaires. Linear regression and two-sided t-tests evaluated mean differences. Subset analyses of the questionnaires were performed using cut-points correlating with clinical assessments.

RESULTS: Between 2016 and 2020, 100 men completed the trial. The intervention group had a mean weight loss of 7.1% vs 1.8% in controls. Despite this, no significant difference was observed between groups in general QOL (EQ-5D-5L), urinary QOL (IPSS), PCa-related QOL (EPIC-26), or PCa specific anxiety (MAX-PC). However, exploratory subgroup analyses demonstrated that participants with poor "bowel function," low "sexual bother," and good "sexual function" had clinically significant improvements of 12 (95% CI 0.1-24.0), 22 (95% CI 4.2-39.0), and 19 points (95% CI 4.4-34.0) on the EPIC-26.

CONCLUSION: In this secondary analysis of a previously published randomized trial, a 6-month diet and exercise intervention did not improve overall QOL among men with overweight/obesity on AS for PCa. While diet and exercise interventions may not universally improve QOL in this population, they remain important for broader health benefits and may offer targeted value for certain patients.

articles.title: Antibiotic-loaded synthetic calcium sulfate (Stimulan) in the surgical management of fracture-related complications in a low-middle income country.
articles.journal: European journal of orthopaedic surgery & traumatology : orthopedie traumatologie
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: The use of calcium sulfate antibiotic delivery systems are underreported in low- and middle-income countries (LMICs), despite the high burden of fracture-related infections and complications. This study evaluates the use of Stimulan in fracture-related complications in a resource-limited setting.

METHODS: A prospective analysis was conducted of all patients treated with Stimulan (Biocomposites Ltd., Keele, UK) for fracture-related complications, between July-September 2023 at Children's Surgical Centre, Cambodia. Patients were followed up regularly at six, nine, and 12 months post-operatively and assessed on the following outcomes: radiological union, radiological/clinical infection remission and functional outcome.

RESULTS: Five out of six patients (83.3%) treated for FRI were clinically and radiologically infection-free, and six out of eight patients (75%) achieved fracture union, at 12 months follow-up. Surgical wounds had healed with no evidence of infection in seven (87.5%) patients. Five non-unions (71.4%) had radiologically healed by 12 months. All patients were fully weightbearing at one year, with two (25%) still requiring walking aids.

CONCLUSION: The use of Stimulan in LMICs appears to provide an effective adjunct for managing fracture-related complications, however more research is required to investigate its efficacy in the treatment of infected non-unions in a LMIC setting.

articles.title: Prospective results of locally delivered low-cost mesh inguinal hernia repair in a low resource setting.
articles.journal: Hernia : the journal of hernias and abdominal wall surgery
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: To assess patient outcomes after locally processed ultra-low-cost hernia mesh placement became routine practice in a government hospital in one of the world's poorest countries.

METHODS: Observational study with comprehensive prospective data collection via electronic registry from June 2023 to January 2026. Interrogation of database after 2.5 years assessed demographics, hernia types and complexity, short term complications and outcomes at 2 years.

RESULTS: Between 01.06.2023 and 01.06.2025, 121 inguinal hernia repairs were repaired with mesh. 76% of inguinal hernias were primary and 24% were recurrent or re-recurrent. No Surgical Site Infection was seen after primary inguinal hernia repair. A 10% superficial wound infection rate was seen after repair of recurrent and re-recurrent inguinal hernias. No mesh infections occurred. Heavy use of prophylactic antibiotics was observed but reduced during the study period. This is a report of the first two years of an on-going service and patients are at varying time points post-surgery. 108 repairs (89%) were > one year post-surgery and one-year FU is documented for 108 repairs (100%). No hernia recurrences identified to date 0% 95% CI [0, 3.35]. 66 repairs were > 2 years post-surgery and 2-year FU is documented for 58 repairs (88%). No hernia recurrences identified to date 0% (95% CL: 0%, 6.16%).

CONCLUSION: Robust, prospective outcome monitoring is feasible in low-income-countries, even outside of the clinical trial situation. Structured training and local implementation have produced good early hernia outcomes.

articles.title: Resilience interventions for stress-related health outcomes in patients with cancer: Findings from a systematic review of randomized controlled trials.
articles.journal: Supportive care in cancer : official journal of the Multinational Association of Supportive Care in Cancer
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: This systematic review aimed to synthesize evidence from randomized controlled trials evaluating the effectiveness of resilience interventions in improving stress-related health outcomes among patients with cancer and to provide a theoretical and practical foundation for advancing non-pharmacological interventions in nursing practice.

METHODS: This study adhered to the 2020 Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses (PRISMA) guidelines. A literature search was conducted using five major databases: PubMed, EBSCO, Embase, Web of Science, and CINAHL. In addition, a manual search was performed using Google Scholar. Two independent researchers assessed the methodological quality of the included studies using the Revised Cochrane risk-of-bias tool for randomized trials (RoB 2). This study has been registered in PROSPERO (registration number: CRD420261283027).

RESULTS: The 33 included randomized controlled trials reported 70 outcome measures across 3,614 patients with cancer. The methodological quality of the included studies ranged from low risk to high risk, with most studies classified as having some concerns or a high risk of bias. Among the 19 outcomes assessing depression, 12 showed significant post-intervention reductions. Of the 21 outcomes evaluating anxiety, 16 showed significant post-intervention reductions. Of the 26 outcomes related to quality of life, 23 showed significant post-intervention improvements. Finally, among the 4 outcomes assessing perceived stress, 3 showed significant post-intervention reductions.

CONCLUSION: Overall, resilience interventions are associated with improvements in stress-related health outcomes in patients with cancer. However, substantial heterogeneity in intervention content, delivery, and outcome reporting across studies precluded quantitative synthesis. Future research should prioritize developing standardized resilience intervention programs and conducting methodologically rigorous randomized controlled trials to validate the practical benefits of resilience interventions in nursing practice.

articles.title: Anatomical variation in the cervical branch of the facial nerve: a systematic review.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: There is a paucity of literature on the anatomical variations of the cervical branch of the facial nerve (CBFN). Poor awareness of its anatomy and variations risks intraoperative damage, misdiagnosis of facial nerve injury and undesirable functional and aesthetic outcomes for patients.

PURPOSE: To review anatomical studies on the CBFN and synthesise data on its course, innervations and common variations.

METHODS: A PRISMA-compliant systematic review of anatomical studies of the cervical branch of the facial nerve was conducted. PubMed, Embase, Scopus, Cochrane Library, Web of Science, and Google Scholar were searched up to July 2025. Papers were quality appraised, and data relevant to the anatomy of the CBFN were extracted.

RESULTS: Thirty-five papers with a collated sample size of 867 hemi-necks were identified: 25 with anatomical dissections and 10 case reports. The mean number of CBFN branches was 1.34 (sensitivity range 1.31-1.36). Communication with the marginal mandibular nerve, transverse cervical nerve and great auricular nerve was variable, with prevalences ranging from 22-97%. Distances between the nerve and anatomical landmarks were heterogeneous. Many individual cases of cervical branch variation in course and relationship to nearby vasculature were identified.

CONCLUSION: The cervical branch of the facial nerve displays wide variability in its course. Pre-operative mapping, careful dissection and intra-operative nerve stimulation to aid accurate identification are recommended to prevent iatrogenic damage.

articles.title: Family resilience and quality of life in breast cancer care: a correlational study of matched patient-caregiver pairs.
articles.journal: Supportive care in cancer : official journal of the Multinational Association of Supportive Care in Cancer
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: Breast cancer is a "family disease" that significantly affects the well-being of both patients and their caregivers. This study aimed to determine the level of family resilience among primary caregivers of breast cancer patients, identify influencing factors, and analyze the relationship between family resilience and patient quality of life (QoL).

METHODS: This descriptive, cross-sectional, and correlational study was conducted with 208 matched patient-caregiver pairs at a university hospital in Türkiye. Data were collected using the Patient and Caregiver Information Forms, the World Health Organization Quality of Life Scale-Brief Form (WHOQOL-BREF-TR), and the Family Resilience Assessment Scale (FRAS-TR). Data were analyzed using descriptive statistics, Spearman's correlation, and comparative tests (t-test, ANOVA).

RESULTS: The mean family resilience score was 3.14 ± 0.32, with the highest scores in "Making Meaning of Adversity" and the lowest in "Utilization of Social and Economic Resources." Caregivers with higher education levels reported greater family connectedness, while lower education was associated with higher spirituality scores (p < 0.05). Patients' QoL was moderate across all domains. A statistically significant positive correlation was found between caregivers' total family resilience and patients' environmental QoL domain (r = 0.264, p < 0.001). No significant correlations were found with other QoL domains.

CONCLUSION: Higher family resilience in caregivers is positively associated with better environmental QoL for breast cancer patients. Supportive care interventions should focus on strengthening the family unit's ability to mobilize social and economic resources, especially for caregivers with multi-generational responsibilities, to enhance the overall recovery environment.

articles.title: Adherence to the Nordic Nutrition Recommendations 2023 and incidence of type 2 diabetes: a Danish cohort study.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: Type 2 diabetes (T2D) is one of the most burdensome chronic diseases. Unhealthy dietary patterns are associated with greater risk of T2D, whereas plant-predominant and climate-friendly diets may be associated with lower risk of T2D. This study aimed to examine the association between adherence to the Nordic Nutrition Recommendations 2023 (NNR23) and risk of T2D in Danish middle-aged adults.

METHODS: This cohort study used data from the Danish Diet, Cancer and Health cohort. The study population was defined among participants with complete baseline data and no cancer at baseline, excluding those with T2D at baseline (n = 54,313). Diet was assessed using a validated semi-quantitative 192-items food frequency questionnaire. Adherence to NNR23 was measured using the Nordic Nutrition Recommendations 2023 Food-Based Diet Score (range 0-15 points). Incident cases of T2D were identified through linkage to the National Diabetes Register. The associations were analysed using Cox proportional hazards regression.

RESULTS: During a median follow-up time of 15.3 years, 7,143 participants developed T2D. Participants with moderate-high adherence (> 10-15 points) to NNR23 had a lower risk of T2D compared to those with low adherence (0-8 points) to NNR23 (HR: 0.63, 95% CI 0.57;0.70). Restricted cubic spline analysis showed a significant non-linear inverse association between adherence to NNR23 and T2D (p-value < 0.001 for non-linearity).

CONCLUSION: Greater adherence to NNR23 was associated with lower risk of T2D, supporting the potential relevance of the NNR23 for T2D prevention.

articles.title: Innate and adaptive immunity pathways linking Mycoplasma pneumoniae to pediatric asthma phenotypes.
articles.abstract:
UNLABELLED: Mycoplasma pneumoniae (Mp) is repeatedly detected during pediatric wheeze and asthma exacerbations, but its clinical significance depends on the host-response context. This review evaluates the clinical and mechanistic evidence linking Mp to pediatric asthma phenotypes and examines approaches for distinguishing biologically meaningful infection from incidental detection. We narratively synthesized clinical, experimental, immunological, toxin, and proteomic literature addressing Mp-associated wheeze, asthma exacerbation, epithelial injury, allergic amplification, and inflammatory endotyping. Evidence was distinguished by population and experimental system. Experimental studies show that Mp adheres to airway epithelium; disrupts mucociliary function; activates TLR2/TLR4, NF-κB, autophagy, and inflammasome pathways; and promotes cytokine networks that overlap with allergic asthma. In experimental allergic-airway models, epithelial alarmins, IgE responses, mast cells, and type 2 inflammation may amplify Mp-driven signals, whereas IL-23/IL-17 pathways recruit neutrophils and suggest mixed endotypes; altered corticosteroid responsiveness has not been established in pediatric Mp-associated asthma. CARDS toxin induces eosinophilic inflammation, mucus metaplasia, airway hyperresponsiveness, functional IgE responses, and worsening allergen-driven disease in experimental models. Upper-airway PCR positivity, however, may reflect carriage or prolonged detection rather than active lower-airway infection.

CONCLUSION: Quantitative pathogen testing, paired serology, viral co-detection, age, atopy, microbiome context, and host-response biomarkers merit integrated evaluation in research. Proteomic and multi-omics signatures may support precision endotyping, improve causal attribution, and strengthen pediatric asthma trial design. Their diagnostic and treatment-predictive value remains unvalidated.

WHAT IS KNOWN: • M. pneumoniae is linked to pediatric wheeze and asthma exacerbations, but upper-airway PCR may reflect carriage rather than active lower-airway infection. • Epithelial injury, type 2/Th17 responses, and CARDS toxin can promote asthma-like inflammation in experimental systems.

WHAT IS NEW: • This review integrates diagnostic attribution, toxin biology, immune crosstalk, and proteomic endotyping in one pediatric framework. • It proposes an unvalidated combined pathogen-load and host-response assessment to investigate clinically meaningful M. pneumoniae-driven endotypes and guide trials.

articles.title: Laparoscopic and robotic management of symptomatic calyceal diverticula: a systematic review on behalf of YAU and EAU endourology.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Calyceal diverticula (CD) are outpouchings of the pelvicalyceal system into the renal parenchyma. The purpose of this systematic review is to summarize the outcomes associated with laparoscopic and robotic-assisted approaches for the management of symptomatic CD.

MATERIALS AND METHODS: Our findings were structured according to the PRISMA statement. We queried three electronic databases, PubMed, Cochrane Library, and Web of Science, to systematically review the literature. Relying on the March 2009 guidelines from the Oxford Centre for Evidence-Based Medicine, two authors independently judged the quality and evidence level of the final articles.

RESULTS: Nine studies were included in final qualitative synthesis. The operative time ranged from 80 to 172 (107-197) minutes, while Estimated Blood Loss ranged from 40 (5-100) to 150 (50-300) ml. The Grade I-II complications according to Clavien-Dindo Classification System ranged from 0% to 66.7%, while no Grade III-IV complications were reported in either of the nine studies. The rate of patients reporting flank pain recurrence during the follow-up period ranged from 0% to 28.5%, while recurrence of the diverticulum ranged from 0% to 33.3%. None of the patients with flank pain or diverticulum recurrence needed a reoperation.

CONCLUSIONS: The findings of this systematic review suggest that laparoscopic and robotic approaches are feasible and have shown favorable outcomes in selected patients with symptomatic CD, particularly in cases with complex anatomy or after failed endourological treatment. However, the available evidence remains limited.

articles.title: Diagnostic and therapeutic yield of postoperative imaging after complicated appendicitis: a western pediatric surgery research consortium prospective study.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: While laparoscopic appendectomy is the standard of care for acute appendicitis, postoperative imaging practices for complicated cases remains variable, and abscesses are a frequent source of morbidity. Postoperative imaging variation may influence the timing of abscess diagnosis and intervention. This study examines the association between postoperative imaging timing and both diagnostic yield (abscess detection) and therapeutic yield (intervention rate), recognizing that detection of an abscess on imaging does not always result in intervention.

METHODS: We conducted a prospective study of children with complicated appendicitis across nine children's hospitals (2022-2024). Patients were stratified by postoperative day (POD) of first imaging (US/CT/MRI). Primary outcomes were diagnostic yield of imaging for abscess formation and therapeutic yield for drainage or reoperation. We performed multivariable logistic regression to examine the association of POD windows and yield. Pairwise comparisons of marginal predicted probabilities were obtained with post-estimation margins and delta-method standard errors.

RESULTS: Among 2,560 patients with complicated appendicitis, 578 (22.5%) underwent postoperative abdominal imaging. Of these, 327 (56.6%) occurred prior to discharge and 251 (43.4%) after discharge. Therapeutic yield varied as a continuous function of postoperative day; LOWESS analysis demonstrated increasing probability of drainage through approximately POD7-10 followed by decline, with sliding window analysis identifying peak therapeutic yield between POD6-8 (42.3% of scans resulted in drainage). Diagnostic yield was highest when imaging occurred before POD10, while imaging after POD10 identified significantly fewer abscesses (37.2% vs. 69.2%, p < 0.001) and resulted in fewer interventions (20.0% vs. 37.2%, p < 0.001). When stratified by discharge status, pre-discharge therapeutic yield peaked between POD6-10, while post-discharge yield plateaued around POD6-8. Therapeutic yield was higher among patients imaged before discharge, who represent a clinically distinct population with persistent failure to meet discharge criteria.

CONCLUSION: Postoperative imaging performed before POD10 demonstrated the highest diagnostic and therapeutic yield for detecting intra-abdominal abscess following appendectomy for complicated appendicitis. Therapeutic yield for postoperative imaging peaked between POD 6-8. Imaging performed after POD10 was significantly less likely to identify drainable collections. Among patients who re-present after discharge, imaging yield declines after POD10, which may inform the timing and modality of imaging in this population, balancing diagnostic utility against radiation exposure. Diagnosing an abscess does not always lead to intervention; clinicians should prioritize the POD6-8 window to maximize actionable yield.

articles.title: Correction to: Sacubitril/valsartan compared to equivalent/sub-equivalent dose angiotensin receptor blocker or angiotensin-converting enzyme inhibitor in heart failure with reduced ejection fraction: a meta-analysis of randomized trials.
Alternative splicing acts as a strategic switch for heat shock network diversification under escalating heat stress.
articles.abstract: Alternative splicing (AS) is a pivotal post-transcriptional mechanism for plant thermal adaptation, yet its dynamics in heat-tolerant woody species remain poorly understood. Here, we map the temperature-resolved AS landscape of the highly thermotolerant woody plant Rhododendron hainanense by combining Iso-Seq with RNA-seq. Transcriptomic profiling revealed a graded regulatory architecture: moderate heat (37 °C) elicited a targeted proteostatic response, whereas severe heat (42 °C) provoked a massive transcriptome expansion. Notably, this global AS surge coincided with a widespread downregulation of core splicing factors, a correlation suggesting that a more permissive splicing environment may contribute to the rapid generation of diverse stress-responsive isoforms. The heat shock protein (HSP) family emerged as the principal hub of this AS-associated diversification; the core chaperone genes ClpB1, HSP83, and HSP70 generated the greatest transcript complexity, with HSP83 alone producing 29 distinct AS transcripts that resolved into three temperature-dependent expression groups. Within the heat shock factor network, HSFA2 showed the strongest and most sustained induction, and DAP-seq identified in vitro HSFA2 binding at the promoters of ClpB1, HSP83, and HSP70, supporting these core chaperones as putative direct DNA-binding targets. Functional complementation in Arabidopsis further showed that three structurally distinct HSFA2 splice variants each restored thermotolerance to the hsfa2 mutant and consistently induced expression of the core ATP-dependent chaperone arm, suggesting that this central chaperone-induction capacity is retained across the tested splice variants in this heterologous system. Together, these findings provide a comprehensive atlas of temperature-modulated AS in a thermotolerant woody plant and support a model in which splicing-mediated diversification of the HSP chaperone network contributes to heat adaptation, offering post-transcriptional insights for breeding climate-resilient crops.

articles.title: eIF3i inhibits nelson bay orthoreovirus replication via interaction with the σNS protein.
articles.abstract: L929 cells exhibit relatively strong resistance to infection by Nelson Bay orthoreovirus (NBV), primarily due to the unique virus-host interaction that suppresses NBV infection at multiple stages, including viral entry, genome replication, and virion assembly. This study investigates the role of host factor eIF3i in NBV replication. Co-immunoprecipitation and immunofluorescence co-localization assays were performed to verify whether eIF3i interacts with the σNS protein in vitro. The results demonstrated that eIF3i significantly inhibits NBV replication through specific binding to σNS. This finding not only provides mechanistic insights into host protein-mediated regulation of viral replication, but also offers a theoretical basis for developing novel anti-NBV therapeutic strategies.

articles.title: Inflammatory bowel disease and breast cancer: epidemiological evidence, shared biology, and clinical management.
articles.journal: Inflammation research : official journal of the European Histamine Research Society ... [et al.]
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE AND DESIGN: This narrative review examines epidemiological, genetic, mechanistic, microbial, and therapeutic evidence concerning inflammatory bowel disease (IBD) and breast cancer.

METHODS: Relevant literature was identified through targeted PubMed searches completed through May 2026 and reference-list screening. Evidence was selected for its relevance to epidemiology, candidate mechanisms, microbiome-related pathways, and treatment interactions.

RESULTS: Pooled cohort evidence does not show a significant overall increase in breast cancer risk among patients with IBD. Several inflammatory, stromal, microbial, and endocrine pathways are relevant to both diseases, although most evidence comes from separate study populations and experimental models. Studies of patients with prior malignancy have not shown a clear increase in new or recurrent cancer during commonly used IBD therapies, but few analyses have focused specifically on breast cancer. Microbiome-directed treatments have been studied in IBD and, more recently, in oncology; their value for patients with both diseases is unknown.

CONCLUSIONS: Current evidence does not support classifying IBD as a breast cancer risk state. The main clinical concern is the interaction between treatments for the two diseases, which requires individualized assessment and coordinated gastroenterology and oncology care.

articles.title: Ultrastructural insights of infection and biological control of Alternaria alternata Kl3 mediated leaf spot disease in kohlrabi.
articles.abstract: Rapid shifts in agro-climatic conditions have accelerated the emergence and severity of fungal plant diseases necessitating continuous pathogen monitoring and development of sustainable control strategies. Consequently, plant-beneficial bacteria-based biological control is one such prime and widely used strategy. Leaf spot diseases caused by Alternaria spp. pose a serious threat to Brassica cultivation, yet etiological and mechanistic insights into kohlrabi (Brassica oleracea var. gongylodes) leaf spot disease remian limited. In this comprehensive study a dominant fungal isolate Kl3, was recovered from diseased leaves of kohlrabi in Santiniketan, India. Based on combined micromorphological features and multilocus phylogeny (ITS-5.8S, gapdh, tef1, alt a1); Kl3 was identified as Alternaria alternata Kl3; which successfully produced disease symptoms in detached kohlrabi leaves ensuring its phytopathogenic potential. Considering the increasing risks of fungicide resistance, the biocontrol potential of plant growth promoting rhizobacteria (PGPR); including Paenibacillus sp. DRP1 and Enterobacter sp. DRP2 was evaluated. Both strains significantly inhibited conidial germination and induced severe mycelial damage to Kl3; which was observed using calcofluor white-based fluorescence microscopy and FE-SEM analysis. Chitinase and protease were the predominant antifungal compounds. Furthermore, FE-SEM analysis provided unique ultrastructural insights and established a timeline for Kl3 infection, starting from conidial germination, direct and indirect invasion by Kl3 mycelia, colonization in mesophyll tissue and conidiogenesis on kohlrabi leaves. Concurrently, PGPR inoculation resulted in significant disease reduction, elicitation of plant defense response and improved kohlrabi yield even in the presence of Kl3 in vivo.

articles.title: Comparative genomics of hypervirulent Klebsiella pneumoniae isolates from Brazil.
articles.abstract: Klebsiella pneumoniae represents a major public health threat at the convergence of antimicrobial resistance and hypervirulence. While classical K. pneumoniae (cKp) is a leading cause of healthcare-associated infections, hypervirulent K. pneumoniae (hvKp) causes severe invasive disease in otherwise healthy individuals. We performed a comparative genomic analysis of hvKp (n = 8) and cKp (n = 17) isolates recovered in Salvador, Brazil. The eight Brazilian hvKp isolates displayed the canonical hypervirulence genotype, encoding the five major biomarkers (iroB, iucA, peg-344, rmpA, and rmpA2) while carrying only a limited repertoire of intrinsic antimicrobial resistance genes. These isolates belonged to sequence types ST23, ST65, ST86, ST3690, and ST5750 and were associated with K1 or K2 capsular types and the O1 antigen. In three isolates, iroB was detected in both chromosomal and plasmid-associated regions, a dual localization reported at low frequency among hvKp. The predominant plasmid replicons were IncHI1B (pNDM-MAR) and repB_KLEB, with IncFIB (K) in two isolates. Screening for mobile genetic elements recovered an F-type conjugative transfer locus in these two isolates only. Chromosomes and plasmids showed high similarity with well-characterized reference hvKp strains, including SGH10 and NTUH-K2044, as well as the pLVPK virulence plasmid. Comparative proteomics analysis identified 53 protein clusters conserved across hvKp strains examined. Among these were four hypothetical proteins previously associated with invasive liver infection, containing DUF1471, DUF417, and carboxymuconolactone decarboxylase-related domains, suggesting potential roles in pathogenicity. Collectively, these findings expand current knowledge of hvKp genetic diversity in Salvador, Brazil and highlight genomic features that may contribute to the emergence and maintenance of the hypervirulent phenotype.

articles.title: Dietary modulation of the gut microbiota in type 2 diabetes and obesity: mechanisms, interventions, and clinical perspectives.
articles.abstract: Obesity and type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) are associated with heterogeneous changes in gut microbial composition and function, while mechanistic studies support plausible links among diet, microbial metabolism, intestinal barrier function, immune signaling, and host metabolism. This narrative review integrates diet-microbiome mechanisms, dietary-assessment and multi-omics methodology, major dietary patterns, quantitative clinical intervention evidence, treatment-related microbiome modulation, and implications for precision nutrition. High-fiber, Mediterranean, plant-based, and Western-style dietary patterns can modify microbial functions and metabolites, but responses vary across populations, substrates, baseline microbiota, medications, and study methods. Randomized trials and meta-analyses show selected metabolic effects of dietary and microbiome-targeted interventions; effects are generally modest and heterogeneous, and prebiotics, probiotics, synbiotics, and postbiotics are not interchangeable across products or populations. Medication and procedural exposures can also alter microbiome and metabolome readouts and confound interpretation. Current evidence does not provide a validated basis for routine microbiome-guided pharmacological or surgical treatment selection. Integration of dietary, microbiome, metabolome, and clinical data may identify metabotypes and candidate response patterns, but individualized microbiome-based nutrition remains an emerging, validation-dependent research domain rather than routine clinical practice.

articles.title: Prognostic value of diabetes-related clinical indices in patients with non-small cell lung cancer and comorbid type 2 diabetes receiving immune checkpoint inhibitor therapy.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICIs) targeting programmed cell death protein 1 (PD-1) or programmed death-ligand 1 (PD-L1) have transformed the treatment of non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC). However, diabetes-induced immune dysfunction may attenuate ICI efficacy. Clinical evidence further suggests poorer outcomes in patients with NSCLC and comorbid type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM). Reliable prognostic tools for this subgroup remain lacking.

METHODS: We conducted a three-part study. First, a two-sample Mendelian randomization (MR) analysis was performed to assess the causal relationship between T2DM and PD-L1. Second, Cox regression was applied to evaluate associations between diabetes-related clinical indices and progression-free survival (PFS) and overall survival (OS). Third, machine learning models were developed to predict prognosis using diabetes-related features.

RESULTS: MR analysis supported a causal association between T2DM and PD-L1. Cox regression identified HbA1c as significantly associated with PFS. Among the machine learning models, the support vector machine (SVM) achieved the best performance for predicting PFS (AUC = 0.935, 95% CI: 0.872-0.997; C-index: 0.763). For OS prediction, the best-performing model was a random forest model based on HbA1c (AUC = 0.863, 95% CI: 0.736-0.990; C-index: 0.618).

CONCLUSION: Diabetes-related indices-particularly HbA1c-are meaningful prognostic markers in patients with NSCLC and comorbid T2DM receiving ICI therapy. The proposed machine learning models may support individualized outcome prediction and clinical decision-making.

articles.title: The cGAS-STING signaling axis in Type 2 diabetes-associated cognitive decline: from mitochondrial DNA sensing to neurodegeneration.
articles.abstract: Type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) is increasingly recognized as a major contributor to cognitive decline, substantially elevating the risk of dementia through mechanisms that extend beyond chronic hyperglycemia. Among the interconnected pathological processes underlying diabetic neurodegeneration, mitochondrial dysfunction has emerged as a pivotal upstream event that promotes oxidative stress, impairs mitophagy, and leads to the cytosolic release of mitochondrial DNA (mtDNA). Recent evidence identifies the cyclic GMP-AMP synthase-stimulator of interferon genes (cGAS-STING) pathway as a critical innate immune sensor that detects aberrant cytosolic mtDNA and orchestrates sustained neuroinflammatory responses. Activation of the cGAS-STING axis initiates TBK1/IRF3- and NF-κB-dependent signaling, driving the production of type I interferons and pro-inflammatory cytokines that amplify glial activation, compromise blood-brain barrier (BBB) integrity, disrupt synaptic homeostasis, and suppress adult hippocampal neurogenesis, ultimately contributing to progressive cognitive impairment. Although the cGAS-STING pathway has been extensively investigated in infection, cancer, and autoimmune disorders, its mechanistic contribution to diabetes-associated cognitive decline remains insufficiently synthesized. This review proposes cGAS-STING as a central molecular hub that integrates mitochondrial damage with innate immune activation, thereby linking metabolic dysfunction to neurodegeneration. We critically evaluate current experimental and emerging clinical evidence and examine the interplay among cGAS-STING, mitochondrial quality control, neurovascular dysfunction, and key signaling networks, including AMPK/SIRT1/PGC-1α, the NLRP3 inflammasome, PI3K/Akt-mTOR, and autophagy. Finally, we discuss the therapeutic potential of targeting the cGAS-STING axis and identify major knowledge gaps that must be addressed to facilitate biomarker development and the development of disease-modifying interventions for T2DM-associated cognitive decline.

articles.title: Risk factors for cardiovascular disease, chronic kidney disease, and type 2 diabetes in populations with overweight and obesity: an umbrella review and cohort analysis.
articles.abstract:
AIMS: Individuals with overweight and obesity are at high risk of cardiovascular disease (CVD), chronic kidney disease (CKD), and type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM). We aimed to identify the risk factors for CVD, CKD, and T2DM among individuals with overweight and obesity, and to validate the associations of these risk factors with the three outcomes.

METHODS: We conducted an umbrella review and a cohort analysis. Seven databases were searched from inception to December 31, 2025. Systematic reviews reporting the risk factors in populations with overweight and obesity, and CVD, CKD, or T2DM were included. The ROBIS and GRADE tools were used to assess the methodological quality and certainty of evidence. A cohort study dataset from the China Health and Retirement Longitudinal Study (CHARLS) was used for validation. Associations with the composite outcome and its individual components (CVD, CKD, and T2DM) were examined.

RESULTS: Nine systematic reviews were included in the umbrella review, and three key factors were identified. Anthropometric measures were associated with CVD (HRs 1.10-1.29) and T2DM (RRs 1.31-1.88). Compared with metabolically healthy individuals, those with metabolically unhealthy phenotypes had HRs ranging from 1.46 to 2.68. Metabolically unhealthy individuals had higher risks (RRs 2.42-5.90). Unhealthy dietary patterns increased CVD, CKD and T2DM risk (HRs 1.11-2.05), whereas healthy dietary patterns reduced risk. In this cohort study, 1,305 participants were included, and 538 developed CVD, CKD or T2DM. Transitioning from a metabolically healthy to a metabolically unhealthy phenotype (OR 1.66 [1.19, 2.30]), transitioning from a metabolically unhealthy to a metabolically healthy phenotype (OR 1.56 [1.08, 2.24]), and maintaining a stable metabolically unhealthy status (OR 1.88 [1.39, 2.54]) were significantly associated with an increased risk of incident CVD, CKD and T2DM composite; disease-specific analyses indicated that this association was driven primarily by T2DM.

CONCLUSIONS: Our analyses revealed that anthropometric measures, metabolic phenotypes, and dietary patterns are associated with CVD, CKD, and T2DM among individuals with overweight and obesity, especially T2DM. Integrated prevention strategies targeting these modifiable risk factors should be prioritized to optimize clinical management.

SYSTEMATIC REVIEW REGISTRATION: PROSPERO CRD420261350841.

articles.title: Targeting ceramides in metabolic syndrome: recent advances and therapeutic opportunities.
articles.abstract: Ceramides are bifunctional molecules that act as both structural constituents of cellular membranes and bioactive effectors in sphingolipid signaling. Their metabolic perturbation is a hallmark of metabolic syndrome, such as obesity, insulin resistance, type 2 diabetes mellitus, metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease, and atherosclerosis. Among the numerous ceramide species, the long-chain species C16:0 and C18:0 have garnered particular attention due to their robust pathogenic roles and strong associations with human disease. This review critically examines the potential of ceramides as predictive biomarkers and provides novel translational perspectives for the clinical management of metabolic syndrome.

articles.title: Diagnostic approach and treatment options for myoclonus.
articles.abstract: Myoclonus is a hyperkinetic movement disorder characterized by sudden, brief involuntary movements that are shock-like and/or jerky. Positive myoclonus is generated by abrupt muscular contractions, which occur synchronously in the affected body part, while negative myoclonus, also referred to as asterixis, results from a brief interruption or silencing of muscle activity leading to a sudden movement due to loss of muscle tone. Myoclonus manifests across a highly heterogeneous group of neurologic and systemic disorders. Due to its varied clinical presentations and multiple etiologies, diagnosing and managing myoclonus in clinical practice remains challenging. The authors retrieved publications that focus on myoclonus as a movement disorder from various electronic databases. The included articles contained discussion on clinical or electrophysiologic findings of myoclonus and its classification. This review outlines a practical diagnostic guide for clinicians that includes consideration of the newly developed 2025 International Association of Parkinsonism and Related Disorders (IAPRD) Axis classification system. This consensus-based framework organizes the diagnostic process into clinical features (Axis 1 A), clinical neurophysiology (Axis 1B), and etiology (Axis II). By systematically evaluating historical data, physical examination findings, and ancillary tests, clinicians can successfully arrive at a clinical syndrome which helps guide investigations to determine the underlying etiology. Neurophysiological assessments are important in determining the specific neuroanatomic generator (cortical, cortical-subcortical, subcortical, brainstem, spinal, propriospinal, peripheral). Categorizing myoclonus by its physiological subtype ultimately dictates the most effective symptomatic treatments. While resource-limited settings may necessitate a primarily clinical approach, employing this step-by-step localization aids in avoiding unnecessary testing and ensures optimal patient care.

articles.title: Retraction Note: Cardioprotective role of GTS-21 by attenuating the TLR4/NF-κB pathway in streptozotocin-induced diabetic cardiomyopathy in rats.
Association of 24-hours net positive fluid balance with log-transformed vancomycin trough concentrations in the early phase of therapy among critically ill patients.
articles.abstract: Early vancomycin troughs are frequently low in critical illness and fluid accumulation may contribute through distribution effects. This study estimated the association between net positive fluid balance and early vancomycin troughs as a hypothesis-generating analysis and explored variation across early-therapy windows and by hypoalbuminemia. A retrospective cohort study used ICU electronic health record data from MIMIC-IV. ICU stays with a timing-validated trough were included. The primary cohort N = 255 required at least 80% EMAR dose capture in the prior 24 h and delta serum creatinine at or below 0.2 mg/dL across the 48 h before trough and trough within 72 h of first IV dose. Net fluid balance in the prior 24 h was modeled per + 5 L. Outcome was log trough. Models adjusted for serum creatinine and administered dose and administration count in the prior 24 h. Sensitivity windows were within 48 h (N = 162) and within 96 h (N = 289). Hypoalbuminemia below 3 g/dL was explored in the measured subset. Median trough was 14.00 mg/L (IQR 10.15 to 18.15) and 62 of 255 were below 10 mg/L (24.3%). The point estimate suggested an 11.7% lower trough concentration per + 5 L net positive balance (β =  - 0.1247; SE = 0.079; p = 0.115), but the 95% CI (- 24.4% to + 3.1%) included no association. Serum creatinine had a positive coefficient (β = 0.2995; p = 0.061). Point estimates were similar across early-therapy windows with all confidence intervals including no association. The exploratory albumin interaction was imprecise and limited by substantial missingness and small subgroup sizes. The point estimate suggested lower early vancomycin troughs with higher net positive fluid balance, but the confidence interval included no association. These hypothesis-generating findings require prospective validation to clarify whether fluid balance is associated with early trough concentrations and area under the curve exposure.

articles.title: Primary leiomyosarcoma arising adjacent to a femoral stem following total hip arthroplasty: a case report with radiologic and histopathological correlation.
articles.abstract: Periprosthetic sarcomas associated with total hip arthroplasty (THA) are exceedingly rare, and most reported cases represent undifferentiated pleomorphic sarcoma or osteosarcoma. Primary leiomyosarcoma of bone is also an uncommon malignancy, accounting for less than 1% of primary malignant bone tumors. The occurrence of primary leiomyosarcoma adjacent to an orthopedic implant is therefore exceptionally rare. A 69-year-old woman presented with progressive left thigh pain 13 years after THA. Radiographs demonstrated osteolysis and cortical thinning at the distal femoral stem. Computed tomography (CT) and magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) revealed an intramedullary lesion with cortical thinning and contrast enhancement. 18F-fluorodeoxyglucose positron emission tomography-CT showed increased uptake at the lesion (SUV max, 11.9), without evidence of other primary tumors. The differential diagnoses included implant-related osteolysis, infection, metastatic tumor, and primary bone tumor. An open biopsy was performed, and a diagnosis of pleomorphic sarcoma was made. Wide resection with proximal femoral replacement was performed. Histopathological examination established the diagnosis of primary leiomyosarcoma of bone. Prominent lymphocytic infiltration and immunohistochemical findings, including p53 overexpression and partial loss of Rb expression, within the tumor, raise the possibility of chronic inflammation and associated molecular alterations as theoretical contributing factors to tumorigenesis. Periprosthetic sarcomas can mimic more common postoperative complications, making diagnosis challenging. Delayed diagnosis may adversely affect prognosis. This case highlights the importance of considering malignancy in atypical periprosthetic lesions and underscores the role of multimodality imaging and biopsy in achieving an accurate diagnosis.

articles.title: Baseline history of primary fragility fracture is associated with medical complications and revision through 1 year in adult spinal deformity patients undergoing thoracolumbar spinal fusion.
articles.journal: European spine journal : official publication of the European Spine Society, the European Spinal Deformity Society, and the European Section of the Cervical Spine Research Society
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: Fragility fractures (FFx) can indicate osteoporosis following posterior spinal fusion (PSF) in adult spinal deformity (ASD) patients. We sought to evaluate the impact of a history of FFx on adverse postoperative outcomes following ≥ 3-level PSFs.

METHODS: This retrospective cohort study queried the Mariner10 PearlDiver database to identify patients aged ≥ 50 years undergoing ≥ 3-level PSF for ASD from 2010 to 2022. All trauma, infection, and tumor indications were excluded. Patients with and without a history of FFx (hip, proximal humerus, distal radius, vertebral body, or pelvis fracture) were stratified. Multivariable logistic regression identified factors associated with adverse outcomes (covariates: age, sex, CCI, obesity, FFx history).

RESULTS: 439 ASD patients were identified, of which 33 (7.5%) had FFx. These patients had higher overall medical complications (38.3% vs. 5.2%), respiratory failure (8.3% vs. 2%), DVT (8.3% vs. 0.6%), and infection (6.7% v 0.9%) at 90-day postoperatively, all p < 0.05. FFx patients had higher surgical complications (20% vs. 2.5%), revision/extension (15% vs. 0.4%), and decompression/laminectomy (6.7% vs. 0.8%) at 1-year, all p < 0.005. FFx history was associated with higher risk of wound disruption (OR = 3.9), respiratory failure (OR = 3.1), pneumonia (OR = 2.4), and PE (OR = 1.1). FFx history was associated with higher odds of revision/extension (OR = 3.5), all p < 0.05.

CONCLUSIONS: FFx history was associated with both medical and surgical complications through 1-year postoperatively, demonstrating how important risk stratification/optimization data can be identified from simple preoperative assessment of FFx history.

LEVEL OF EVIDENCE: III.

articles.title: Composite inflammatory, immune, and nutritional indices for predicting surgical site infection following spine surgery: a systematic review with narrative synthesis.
articles.journal: European spine journal : official publication of the European Spine Society, the European Spinal Deformity Society, and the European Section of the Cervical Spine Research Society
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Surgical site infection (SSI) is an important complication after spine surgery, with a reported incidence of approximately 1%-4% and a substantial associated healthcare burden. Early identification of high-risk patients remains difficult. Composite indices derived from routine laboratory tests that integrate inflammatory, immune, and nutritional parameters may assist perioperative SSI risk stratification.

METHODS: This systematic review with narrative synthesis was conducted in accordance with the PRISMA 2020 statement and was registered in PROSPERO (registration number blinded for peer review). PubMed, Web of Science, and Embase were searched from database inception to May 28, 2026. Non-randomized clinical studies evaluating composite inflammatory, immune, or nutritional indices for predicting SSI after spine surgery were eligible. Two reviewers independently performed study selection, data extraction, and quality assessment. Observational studies were appraised using the Newcastle-Ottawa Scale (NOS), prediction-model studies using PROBAST, and studies reporting diagnostic or discriminative performance using QUADAS-2 as a supplementary tool. Because the included studies differed in surgical procedures, index definitions, sampling time points, thresholds, and statistical methods, the evidence was synthesized narratively.

RESULTS: Twenty-one retrospective studies comprising 13,853 patients and 763 SSI or SSI-related infectious outcome cases were included. The evaluated indices comprised NLR, PLR, PNI, NRI, AGR, CAR, CLR, SIRI, SII, AISI, CALLY, CONUT, mGPS, and MNA-SF, among others. NLR was the most frequently studied inflammatory index. Postoperative NLR, particularly when measured between postoperative days 3 and 7, showed potential for early SSI detection. Associations with SSI were relatively consistent for CAR and mGPS, whereas findings for PNI and other nutritional indices were more variable. Five studies developed or evaluated prediction models or composite scoring systems. These models often reported higher discrimination than individual markers, but most were derived from retrospective cohorts, with limited external validation and heterogeneous calibration or clinical-utility assessment.

CONCLUSIONS: Composite inflammatory, immune, and nutritional indices may assist SSI risk stratification after spine surgery. Postoperative NLR, CAR, mGPS, PNI, and SIRI appear to be clinically relevant adjunctive markers, but current evidence remains limited by retrospective designs, heterogeneous SSI definitions, variable sampling times, and insufficient external validation. Multivariable and machine-learning models have reported high discrimination in some cohorts, but their clinical use remains uncertain without robust calibration, independent validation, and clinical-utility assessment. At present, these measures should support, rather than replace, comprehensive clinical assessment.

articles.title: [The eye as a mirror of the heart-retinal findings in heart failure and cardiovascular diseases].
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Due to its unique anatomical and functional characteristics, the retina represents a promising organ for the evaluation of systemic vascular diseases. Modern imaging techniques, particularly optical coherence tomography angiography (OCT-A), enable noninvasive and quantitative assessment of retinal microcirculation. The aim of this review is to present current findings on the significance of retinal biomarkers in cardiovascular diseases, with a focus on heart failure.

RESULTS: Numerous studies show associations between retinal vascular changes and arterial hypertension, coronary heart disease, left ventricular hypertrophy, and heart failure. Changes in retinal vascular parameters such as vascular density and perfusion density correlate with structural and functional cardiac changes. Patients with retinal vascular occlusions have an increased risk of stroke, myocardial infarction, and higher cardiovascular mortality. Initial studies in patients with acute decompensated heart failure have demonstrated changes in retinal vascular and perfusion density that can be reversed by recompensation. These observations led to the introduction of the term "cardio-ocular syndrome," which describes the interactions between cardiac function, systemic congestion, and retinal microcirculation.

CONCLUSION: Retinal imaging opens up new possibilities for the noninvasive assessment of systemic microcirculatory disorders in cardiovascular diseases. OCT‑A could contribute in the future to risk stratification, assessment of disease progression, and monitoring of therapy in heart failure.

articles.title: [Perimenopause and postmenopause: acute diagnostic and therapeutic aspects for the DACH region : Consensus paper of the Austrian Society for Gynecology and Obstetrics (OEGGG), the German Society for Gynecology and Obstetrics (DGGG), the German Menopause Society (DMG) and the Swiss Society for Gynecology and Obstetrics (SGGG)].
articles.abstract: There are currently approximately 13 million women in the DACH region who are in the perimenopause or postmenopause. This phase of life leads to relevant physical, psychological, and metabolic changes. Unfortunately, even now, many symptoms remain untreated, which has a major impact on women's quality of life and ability to work. Modern approaches to menopausal hormone therapy as well as nonhormonal treatment options, are designed to specifically improve the health and quality of life of affected women; however, these approaches are still underutilized. This DACH consensus paper reviews the currently available evidence, addresses risk factors, and provides specific recommendations for daily clinical practice.

articles.title: Diagnostic Testing Is Not Associated with Patient Experience in Common Pediatric Cardiology Referrals.
articles.abstract: To describe patient and family experience (PFE) scores for common new pediatric cardiology referrals and to evaluate whether the intensity of cardiac testing is associated with patient experience. We performed a retrospective study of PFE surveys completed following new outpatient pediatric cardiology visits at a single tertiary center from 2022 to 2023. Patients ≤ 18 years old referred for chest pain, palpitations, murmur, or dizziness/syncope were included. Survey domains included overall experience, provider respect, communication, and time spent with the provider. Responses were dichotomized, with top-box approach scores designated as 9-10 on a 0-10 Likert scale or a response of "yes, definitely." Additional variables included patient demographics, clinic location, referral-to-visit interval, cardiac testing performed and follow-up recommendations. Univariable and multivariable statistical analysis were used to identify factors associated with top-box scores. A total of 1293 surveys were analyzed. The performance of cardiac testing-including echocardiography, exercise stress testing, or ambulatory monitoring-was not associated with higher PFE scores. PFE scores also did not differ significantly by referral reason, clinic location, referral-to-visit interval, or follow-up recommendation. Overall PFE scores were high (91% in top-box category). Among common pediatric cardiology referrals, greater testing intensity was not associated with improved patient and family experience. These findings suggest that reducing non-essential testing may represent an opportunity to optimize resource utilization without negatively affecting perceived quality of care.

articles.title: Early-Onset Gastric Varices After Fontan Completion Associated with a Pre-Existing Gastro-Renal Shunt.
articles.abstract: Gastroesophageal varices are recognized complications of Fontan-associated liver disease, but clinically significant varices have generally been reported more than 10 years after Fontan completion. The mechanisms of early variceal formation remain unclear. We report a child with tricuspid atresia who developed isolated gastric varices approximately 7 years after extracardiac Fontan completion in the presence of a pre-existing gastro-renal shunt (GRS). The patient underwent bidirectional Glenn palliation at 9 months of age. Contrast-enhanced computed tomography (CT) performed before Fontan completion incidentally demonstrated a GRS, which progressively dilated after Fontan completion. At 8 years of age, contrast-enhanced CT obtained during evaluation for hypoxemia incidentally revealed isolated gastric varices. The patient had no ascites, marked splenomegaly, thrombocytopenia, or evidence of advanced hepatic dysfunction. Cardiac catheterization showed an inferior vena cava (IVC) pressure of 14 mmHg. Given the potential risk of massive hemorrhage, the gastric varices were successfully treated with transvenous coil embolization and balloon-occluded retrograde transvenous obliteration through the GRS. No recurrence was observed during follow-up. This case suggests that a pre-existing GRS may contribute to the relatively early development of gastric varices after Fontan completion, even in the absence of markedly elevated systemic venous pressure or other clinical features of advanced portal hypertension. Because a pre-existing GRS could predispose patients to gastric variceal formation after Fontan completion, preoperative assessment of the abdominal venous anatomy using contrast-enhanced CT could be important.

articles.title: Dynamics and functional heterogeneity of FOXP3+ regulatory T cells in Trypanosoma cruzi infection: a systematic review.
articles.journal: Inflammation research : official journal of the European Histamine Research Society ... [et al.]
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The role of regulatory T cells (Tregs) in Trypanosoma cruzi infection remains unresolved, with conflicting evidence suggesting either protection from immunopathology or impairment of parasite control.

METHODS: We performed the first systematic review integrating data on Treg phenotype and function in human and experimental Chagas disease. A comprehensive search of PubMed, Embase, Scopus, and LILACS (2003-2025) identified studies assessing Tregs during T. cruzi infection. Study selection, data extraction, and risk-of-bias assessment followed PRISMA 2020 and Cochrane guidelines.

RESULTS: Twenty-seven studies met eligibility criteria (9 human, 18 murine). Human studies consistently showed that individuals with indeterminate Chagas disease harbor functionally stable Tregs enriched for CD39, CD25high, and CTLA-4 expression. In contrast, Chagas cardiomyopathy was associated with Treg instability, PD-1 upregulation, and partial acquisition of Th1-like features. Murine models revealed a phase-dependent role: transient Treg restriction during acute infection enhanced CD8⁺ T cell-mediated parasite control, whereas failure to re-establish regulatory balance promoted chronic cardiac inflammation. Key modulatory pathways included IL-10, IL-2, IL-33/ST2, G-CSF, and CD39.

CONCLUSION: These findings support a dual-role model in which Tregs dynamically coordinate disease tolerance. Treg-associated signatures, particularly CD39 expression and activated/resting Treg ratios, emerge as promising biomarkers and therapeutic targets for Chagas disease.

articles.title: A cohort electron blood self-dose fraction and its propagated uncertainty for ¹²⁴I PET pre-therapy dosimetry in radioiodine therapy of differentiated thyroid cancer.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Pre-therapy blood-marrow dosimetry for ¹³¹I treatment of differentiated thyroid cancer (DTC) requires serial imaging and blood sampling, limiting clinical adoption. When blood data are unavailable, operators fall back to fixed or imaging-only prescribing, usually without an explicit uncertainty bound. We characterise the cohort electron blood self-dose fraction (βfrac) in a single-centre ¹²⁴I PET cohort and quantify the uncertainty incurred by substituting that reference for patient-specific blood data.

METHODS: Retrospective single-centre analysis of 18 pre-therapy ¹²⁴I PET courses in 15 DTC patients with paired serial venous blood-counting, all prepared by thyroid-hormone withdrawal. Time-activity curves were fitted in the ¹³¹I therapy frame following the EANM Standard Operational Procedure, separating Dblood into its electron (β, blood self-dose) and photon (γ, body cross-fire) components. The substitution uncertainty was propagated analytically, then validated against patient-level errors by leave-one-patient-out cross-validation.

RESULTS: The cohort β fraction was 84.3 ± 4.8% across 18 courses (mean ± SD; median 85.4%; 95% CI 82.0-86.7%), and 84.4 ± 4.6% over the 15 patients. The β fraction decreased with body weight (- 0.113 pp/kg, p = 0.019), although not significantly when reduced to one value per patient (p = 0.118); the association is therefore exploratory. Substitution gave a per-patient 1-σ uncertainty on the imaging-only Dblood estimate of ≈ 30%. Under leave-one-patient-out cross-validation the mean absolute percentage error was 26.3% and the RMSE 32.7%, with 12 of 18 courses within ± 30% of their reference.

CONCLUSIONS: A cohort β fraction of 84.3 ± 4.8% is proposed as a fall-back reference for blood-free prescribing in DTC radioiodine therapy. Because the estimator's error is multiplicative on the estimate, a prescribing cap must come from the lower tail of that error, giving approximately 1.0-1.2 Gy in this cohort. No 95% coverage is demonstrated at this sample size, and the cap is offered as an exploratory observation requiring local confirmation rather than a validated threshold. The decomposition is imaging-modality agnostic for ¹³¹I clearance studies and therefore potentially applicable to low-dose ¹³¹I SPECT, although no SPECT data were analysed here.

articles.title: Predictive value of left ventricular 18F-FDG PET/CT derived parameters and uptake patterns for chemotherapy-induced cardiotoxicity in patients with lymphoma.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Anthracycline-induced cardiotoxicity significantly impacts the survival and quality of life of lymphoma patients. Since traditional echocardiographic markers often detect injury only after irreversible damage, there is an urgent need for early biomarkers. We aimed to evaluate the predictive value of myocardial FDG uptake patterns and quantitative parameters from routine oncologic PET/CT for cancer therapy-related cardiac dysfunction (CTRCD).

METHODS: This retrospective cohort study included lymphoma patients treated with anthracycline-based regimens at a single hospital between 2015 and 2024. Patients underwent FDG PET/CT at baseline and after chemotherapy. CTRCD was operationally defined using the LVEF-based component of the 2022 ESC cardio-oncology guidelines on follow-up echocardiography. Metabolic parameters including maximal standard uptake value (SUVmax), cardiac metabolic volume (CMV), cardiac metabolic activity (CMA), and visual uptake patterns were analyzed on pre and post-treatment PET scans.

RESULTS: Post-treatment SUVmax, CMV, and CMA were significantly higher in patients who developed cardiotoxicity (p = 0.04, 0.017, and 0.03, respectively). In univariable logistic regression, focal/diffuse myocardial uptake was significantly associated with CTRCD, whereas SUVmax ≥8.49 and CMV ≥66.9 showed borderline associations. In multivariable analysis including SUVmax, CMV, and focal/diffuse uptake pattern, only the focal/diffuse uptake pattern remained independently associated with CTRCD (OR = 10.71, 95% CI: 2.10-54.69, p = 0.004). Notably, absent myocardial FDG uptake after treatment was observed only in patients without CTRCD in this cohort. Baseline PET parameters showed no significant predictive value (p = n.s.).

CONCLUSION: Routine post-treatment oncologic FDG PET/CT may provide exploratory information on myocardial metabolic changes associated with CTRCD in lymphoma patients receiving anthracycline-based chemotherapy. Although quantitative PET parameters differed between patients with and without CTRCD, the focal/diffuse myocardial uptake pattern was the only imaging variable that remained independently associated with CTRCD after multivariable adjustment. These findings should be considered hypothesis-generating and require prospective validation using standardized myocardial metabolic preparation and predefined imaging timepoints.

articles.title: Head-to-head comparison of ⁶⁸Ga-FAPI and ¹⁸F-FDG PET/CT in intracranial space-occupying lesions.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: Intracranial space-occupying lesions (SOL), including primary brain tumors, metastases, and inflammatory lesions, require accurate characterization for diagnosis and management. Although ¹⁸F-FDG PET/CT reflects tumor glucose metabolism, its performance in the brain is limited by high physiological uptake. ⁶⁸Ga-FAPI PET/CT targets fibroblast activation protein in the tumor microenvironment and may provide complementary biological information with improved lesion conspicuity. This study aimed to compare ⁶⁸Ga-FAPI and ¹⁸F-FDG PET/CT for the evaluation of intracranial SOL.

METHODS: Thirty-five patients with 55 intracranial lesions underwent paired ⁶⁸Ga-FAPI and ¹⁸F-FDG PET/CT within a 7-day interval. Imaging findings were compared with histopathology (n = 9) and/or MRI (n = 46) as reference standards. Lesion detection rate, diagnostic performance, tumor-to-background ratio (TBR), and semi-quantitative uptake parameters normalized to lean body mass (SUL) were evaluated. Receiver operating characteristic (ROC) analyses were performed to assess the ability of each tracer to differentiate neoplastic from non-neoplastic lesions.

RESULTS: ⁶⁸Ga-FAPI PET/CT detected more lesions than ¹⁸F-FDG PET/CT (48/55, 87.3% vs. 36/55, 65.5%) and approached the detection rate of MRI (54/55, 98.2%). FAPI demonstrated higher sensitivity and accuracy, whereas FDG showed higher specificity. FAPI demonstrated a significantly higher tumor-to-background ratio (TBR) than FDG (median, 342.00 [IQR, 164.25-502.00] vs. 4.71 [IQR, 3.48-7.42]; Z = 5.07, p < 0.001) in paired analysis of 34 lesions with measurable uptake on both tracers. In primary tumors, FAPI detected all lesions (13/13), whereas FDG detected 9/13 lesions. ROC analysis showed comparable diagnostic performance for differentiating neoplastic from non-neoplastic lesions (AUC 0.794 for FAPI vs. 0.796 for FDG). Exploratory analysis in high-grade tumors (n = 5) suggested a potential association between higher FDG uptake and shorter overall survival.

CONCLUSION: In this cohort, intracranial lesions were predominantly metastatic, with MRI showing the highest detection rate. Compared with ¹⁸F-FDG PET/CT, ⁶⁸Ga-FAPI PET/CT demonstrated higher lesion detection and tumor-to-background contrast, approaching MRI performance. These findings support a complementary role for ⁶⁸Ga-FAPI PET/CT alongside MRI and ¹⁸F-FDG PET/CT in selected intracranial lesions, particularly when lesion conspicuity is limited by the high physiological brain uptake of FDG.

articles.title: Association of SUVmax and never-smoker/never- or minimally-drinker history with PD-L1 expression in resected oral squamous cell carcinoma: a nodal-status-stratified analysis.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Programmed death-ligand 1 (PD-L1) is a critical biomarker for immunotherapy selection in oral squamous cell carcinoma (OSCC). However, the relationships between PD-L1 expression and non-invasive indicators, such as metabolic parameters derived from 18F-FDG PET/CT and never-smoker/never- or minimally-drinker (NSND) history, remain poorly defined. Moreover, whether these associations differ across nodal subgroups has not been investigated.

METHODS: This retrospective study included 147 patients with resected OSCC who underwent preoperative PET/CT. Factors associated with high PD-L1 expression (combined positive score [CPS] ≥ 20) were assessed using logistic regression in the overall cohort and with subgroup analyses stratified by nodal status and formal interaction testing.

RESULTS: In the overall cohort, maximum standardized uptake value (SUVmax) (odds ratio [OR] per unit increase = 1.067; 95% confidence interval [CI]: 1.013-1.123; P = 0.014) and gender (OR = 2.254; 95% CI: 1.029-4.936; P = 0.042) were independently associated with high PD-L1 expression. After stratification by nodal status, no clinicopathological or metabolic variable was significantly associated with PD-L1 expression in pN0 patients. In contrast, among pN+ patients, SUVmax (OR per unit increase = 1.113; 95% CI: 1.015-1.222; P = 0.024) and NSND (OR = 4.127; 95% CI: 1.362-12.501; P = 0.012) emerged as independent predictors. The NSND × pN interaction was significant (P = 0.004), whereas the SUVmax × pN interaction was not (P = 0.225).

CONCLUSIONS: SUVmax may serve as a candidate non-invasive indicator, whereas the association between NSND and high PD-L1 expression was modified by nodal status, with a significant effect in node-positive patients. These findings are hypothesis-generating and require external validation.

articles.title: A case of renal hypouricemia type 1 associated with compound heterozygous URAT1/SLC22A12 variants A209V and F379L: clinical evidence for their pathogenic significance.
articles.abstract: Renal hypouricemia (RHUC) is an inherited renal tubular disorder characterized by low serum uric acid levels and excessive urinary uric acid excretion due to impaired urate reabsorption in proximal tubules. Type 1 RHUC (RHUC1) is caused by pathogenic variants in URAT1/SLC22A12. In Japanese patients, recurrent variants such as W258X and R90H account for a substantial proportion of RHUC1 cases; however, the clinical significance of rare URAT1 variant combinations remains incompletely understood. A 69-year-old woman was referred to our hospital for evaluation of renal dysfunction and hypouricemia. Laboratory examination revealed severe hypouricemia (serum uric acid, 0.7 mg/dL) and markedly increased urinary uric acid excretion (Cua/Ccr, 60.5%). She had chronic kidney disease (CKD) stage G3b and a renal stone. Genetic analysis identified two heterozygous variants, A209V and F379L, in URAT1/SLC22A12 gene. The variants were considered likely to represent compound heterozygosity based on the clinical phenotype and their previously reported functional impairment. Although A209V and F379L have individually been reported to impair urate transport, the clinical phenotype associated with this variant combination has not been well characterized. The severe hypouricemia and excessive urinary uric acid excretion observed in this patient provide clinical evidence supporting the pathogenic significance of the A209V and F379L combination. The coexistence of nephrolithiasis and CKD further raises the possibility that excessive urinary urate excretion and stone formation may contribute to renal dysfunction. In addition, the improvement in stone-related urinary abnormalities during potassium citrate treatment suggests that urinary alkalization may be beneficial in the management of nephrolithiasis associated with RHUC.

articles.title: Allergic profile and pre-diagnostic exposure to allergen-specific immunotherapy in eosinophilic granulomatosis with polyangiitis (EGPA): a single-centre retrospective observational study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Eosinophilic Granulomatosis with Polyangiitis (EGPA) combines asthma, eosinophilic inflammation and small- to medium-vessel vasculitis. The relationship between conventional allergic phenotypes, allergen-specific immunotherapy (AIT) and subsequent EGPA remains uncertain.

OBJECTIVE: To describe specialist-adjudicated allergic manifestations in a selected EGPA cohort and explore whether pre-diagnostic AIT exposure was associated with age at EGPA onset or clinical phenotype.

METHODS: We retrospectively analysed 53 patients with expert-diagnosed EGPA, complete historical records and an allergy evaluation adequate to classify aeroallergen sensitisation, respiratory allergy, food allergy and drug hypersensitivity. Continuous variables were assessed for normality and compared using Mann-Whitney U tests; categorical variables were compared using Fisher exact tests. Analyses were exploratory.
