This case highlights the coumadin ridge as an exceptionally rare site of PFE attachment and a potential source of recurrent cardioembolism. TEE and CMR are crucial for diagnosis, while surgical resection provides definitive treatment.

articles.title: Interventricular septal thickness for cardiomyopathic phenotype enrichment in patients with established left ventricular hypertrophy.
articles.journal: The international journal of cardiovascular imaging
articles.abstract: We evaluated whether interventricular septal thickness in diastole (IVSd) ≥ 15 mm enriches cardiomyopathic phenotypes among adults with established left ventricular hypertrophy (LVH) and whether broader clinical-echocardiographic features improve triage. We studied 1,127 adults undergoing echocardiography from 2017 to 2019 who met established LVH criteria (sex-specific left ventricular mass index elevation and both IVSd and posterior wall thickness ≥ 13 mm). The primary phenotype was hypertrophic cardiomyopathy, Fabry disease, or amyloidosis. The composite phenotype occurred in 108 patients (9.6%) and was more frequent with IVSd ≥ 15 mm than 13.0-14.9 mm (16.2% vs. 3.6%, p < 0.001). After adjustment, IVSd ≥ 15 mm remained associated with the composite phenotype (odds ratio 2.38, 95% CI 1.35-4.20), with a graded association per 1-mm increase (odds ratio 1.50, 95% CI 1.33-1.70). At 15 mm, sensitivity, specificity, positive predictive value, and negative predictive value were 80.6%, 55.7%, 16.2%, and 96.4%; at 18 mm, case-finding yield increased to 41.7% but 58 of 108 cases were missed. A five-variable model improved discrimination over IVSd alone (area under the curve [AUC] 0.839 vs. 0.787; ΔAUC 0.052; p = 0.007; derivation AUC 0.857, temporal validation AUC 0.788), whereas adding binary IVSd ≥ 15 mm to conventional clinical-echocardiographic variables yielded minimal incremental discrimination (ΔAUC 0.003) and minimal additional net benefit. In established LVH, IVSd ≥ 15 mm identifies cardiomyopathic enrichment, with the composite association driven predominantly by hypertrophic cardiomyopathy, but is best used as a prompt for etiologic review rather than a diagnostic rule. A compact five-variable model may support triage.

articles.title: Coronary artery imaging in Kawasaki disease: recent updates in imaging techniques and clinical indications.
articles.journal: The international journal of cardiovascular imaging
articles.abstract: Coronary artery involvement in Kawasaki disease should be evaluated throughout all disease stages. Generally, multimodality imaging is necessary for both the acute and chronic phases of coronary artery abnormalities. This review summarizes current clinical indications and recent technical advances in coronary artery imaging in Kawasaki disease with an emphasis on the roles of computed tomography and magnetic resonance imaging. Echocardiography remains the first-line modality in all disease stages for evaluating coronary artery lesions and ventricular function. Recent technical developments in coronary computed tomography angiography can provide the accurate diagnosis of coronary artery lesions including stenosis and thrombus at substantially reduced radiation dose, supporting its selective use in serial follow-up. Cardiac magnetic resonance imaging offers the comprehensive evaluation of inducible myocardial ischemia, ventricular function, inflammation, and fibrosis. Invasive catheter angiography is reserved for complex or interventional cases. This review also addresses technical considerations and potential pitfalls for each imaging modality. Continued technical developments and their optimization with standardized imaging protocols and reports are expected to enhance diagnostic precision and eventually improve clinical outcomes in children with Kawasaki disease.

articles.title: Accuracy of visual estimation of coronary artery calcifications on low-dose CT from oncologic FDG PET/CT.
articles.journal: The international journal of cardiovascular imaging
articles.abstract: To evaluate the feasibility and accuracy of visual ordinal coronary artery calcium (CAC) scoring on low-dose, non-gated CT scans acquired as part of oncologic PET/CT, using CAC scoring from ECG-gated non-contrast cardiac CT as the reference standard. 210 oncological patients who underwent both PET/CT and single-photon emission computed tomography (SPECT) myocardial perfusion imaging (MPI) with ECG-gated non-contrast cardiac CT within 6 months were retrospectively included. Four independent readers graded image quality and assessed CAC burden using a visual ordinal scoring system (scores ranging from 0 to 12) on non-gated CT images from PET/CT. CAC scores as well as information on presence of myocardial ischemia and/or scars were recorded from the dedicated cardiac diagnostic workup and were used for comparison. Image quality was considered diagnostic in 99.6% of scans. Interreader agreement of ordinal scores was excellent among all four readers (Krippendorff's alpha = 0.95). Non-gated CT demonstrated favorable diagnostic performance for detecting CAC per-patient, with a sensitivity/specificity/positive predictive value/negative predictive value of 92.2%/95%/99.3%/62.1%. Ordinal scores showed a strong correlation with quantitative reference standard CAC scores (Spearman's rho = 0.9, p < 0.001). Receiver operating characteristic (ROC) analysis indicated that ordinal scores effectively differentiated patients based on reference standard CAC score cutoffs of 100, 400, and 1000, with AUC values of 0.96, 0.92, and 0.95, respectively. Additionally, using ordinal scores, ROC analysis yielded an AUC of 0.7 for differentiating patients with and without ischemia/scars. Visual ordinal scoring of CAC burden on low-dose non-gated CT of oncologic PET/CT scans is accurate, effective and strongly correlates with reference standard measurements. The lower negative predictive value indicates that (mild) coronary calcifications are occasionally underestimated.

articles.title: Surgical architecture and component identifiability in robot-assisted radical prostatectomy: a systematic review and network meta-analysis.
articles.abstract: Robot-assisted radical prostatectomy (RARP) combines preservation, reconstruction, and support maneuvers within named surgical packages, making component attribution difficult. To determine whether comparative evidence can identify independent surgical-component effects on strict early perfect continence while preserving oncological context. Comparative RARP studies were synthesized within a prespecified surgical-architecture framework. The primary outcome was perfect continence (0 pads/day) at 10-14 weeks. All prespecified bibliographic databases and registries were rerun through 26 September 2026. Randomized evidence underwent pairwise and network meta-analysis; component estimates were interpreted only after a prespecified structural-identifiability gate. Forty-eight reports representing 48 nonoverlapping study families, 98 arms, and 6,665 arm-level participants were included. Six randomized families provided exact strict 3-month events and formed three disconnected subnetworks; four families formed the largest connected network. In that four-family network, risk ratios versus standard RARP were 1.07 (95% confidence interval [CI] 0.65-1.78) for posterior reconstruction (PR), 2.94 (0.92-9.33) for PR plus anterior reconstruction/suspension, and 1.49 (0.63-3.52) for PR plus sling. PR was the only component meeting the prespecified structural gate; this denotes evidence structure, not a precise or validated independent causal effect. Descriptive positive surgical margin estimates were sparse (PR 0.96 [0.50-1.86]; PR plus anterior reconstruction/suspension 1.74 [0.57-5.25]). Confidence in all primary network comparisons was very low. The literature is broad at the level of named RARP techniques but insufficiently connected and replicated to isolate most component-specific effects. Package-level signals should not be reassigned to individual maneuvers unless those components vary independently across replicated comparisons. Future trials should report exact time-specific continence outcomes, explicit arm-level technical details, and replicated component contrasts.

articles.title: Clinical characteristics and associated factors of difficult-to-treat rheumatoid arthritis: a cross-sectional study.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: This study aimed to describe the clinical characteristics and explore factors cross-sectionally associated with difficult-to-treat rheumatoid arthritis (D2T RA) in a Chinese population, providing evidence for characterizing the clinical phenotype and identifying current associated factors in a Chinese population.

METHODS: A cross-sectional study was conducted, enrolling RA patients treated at the Rheumatology Department of Dongfang Hospital, Beijing University of Chinese Medicine, from September 2022 to September 2024. Based on the 2020 EULAR criteria, adapted in accordance with the 2021 Chinese consensus on refractory rheumatoid arthritis, patients were categorized into a D2T RA group (n = 61) and a conventional RA group (n = 182). An exploratory subsample (n = 6 per group) underwent plasma cytokine analysis via Luminex assay. Data on demographics, disease activity measures, laboratory inflammatory parameters, comorbidities, and medication use were collected. Plasma cytokine levels were measured using Luminex technology. Statistical analysis was performed using R software, and associated factors were analyzed via univariate and multivariate logistic regression.

RESULTS: Patients in the D2T RA group were significantly younger than those in the RA group (P = 0.009) and exhibited significantly higher values in swollen joint count, VAS pain score, DAS28-ESR, CDAI, and SDAI (all P < 0.05). The prevalence of osteoporosis was significantly higher in the D2T RA group (85.25% vs. 61.54%, P = 0.001), and the usage of JAK inhibitors was also notably elevated (85.25% vs. 1.10%, P = 0.027). Regarding inflammatory markers, except for elevated plateletcrit, no significant differences were observed in CRP, ESR, IL-6, or composite inflammation indices between groups. Exploratory cytokine analysis (n = 6 per group) showed that IL-6 and IL-17A levels were significantly elevated in the D2T RA group compared to healthy volunteers, whereas no significant differences were observed between the RA and D2T RA groups. Multivariate logistic regression identified that older age was associated with lower odds of D2T RA (OR = 0.94, 95% CI: 0.91-0.98, P =  0.011), while OP remained independently associated with higher odds (OR = 4.95, 95% CI: 1.96-12.15, P < 0.001).

CONCLUSION: In this single-center Chinese cohort, D2T RA was characterized by younger age, higher disease activity, and a higher comorbidity rate of osteoporosis. Younger age and comorbid osteoporosis were cross-sectionally associated with D2T RA. These findings may assist clinicians in recognizing high-risk clinical phenotypes and inform the development of targeted intervention strategies, but require confirmation in prospective, multicenter studies.

articles.title: Post-market safety signals of energy-based surgical devices: a cross-specialty disproportionality analysis of the FDA MAUDE database with robotic-platform validation and regulatory triangulation, 2015-2025.
articles.abstract: Post-market safety evidence for energy-based surgical devices is fragmented. We characterized adverse-event signals in the FDA MAUDE database, validated them on a third (robotic) platform, and triangulated across regulatory and international sources. Medical Device Reports (2015-2025) under electrosurgical and ultrasonic product codes were analyzed with reporting odds ratios (RORs), stratified by specialty and procedure, with robustness checks. All reports under the robotic-system code were retrieved as a third-platform validation cohort. Signals were triangulated with FDA recalls, 510(k) clearances, the Health Canada and Australian TGA databases, exposure descriptors, and a retrospectively applied Poisson CUSUM feasibility analysis. Among 110,183 deduplicated reports (65.8% electrosurgical, 34.2% ultrasonic), electrosurgical devices showed an electrical-thermal fingerprint (burns ROR 3.84; electric shock ROR 15.34) and ultrasonic devices a mechanical-integrity fingerprint (foreign-body removal ROR 92.74), replicated directionally in Canada and Australia. The fingerprint localized to generator/monopolar components and varied by specialty and procedure. Within the robotic validation cohort, component-stratified analysis partly reproduced these signatures-robot-mounted monopolar instruments retained a burn signal, and robot-mounted ultrasonic instruments carried the highest injury-report share-while cross-platform, same-modality contrasts are reported strictly as report-composition (share-level) comparisons. Reporting artifacts (19.5% placeholder narratives; a 2025 robotic mass-reporting episode comprising 55.8% of the robotic cohort) left fingerprint RORs materially unchanged. A retrospectively applied CUSUM flagged the burn theme more than five years before the 2023-2024 Class I recalls, illustrating-without establishing prospective lead time-the potential of automated monitoring. Energy-modality failure-injury fingerprints were consistent across specialties, delivery platforms, three national databases, and regulatory actions. Automated, artifact-aware surveillance of vigilance databases is a promising complement to pre-market review and warrants prospective evaluation.

articles.title: Robot-assisted ileal ureter replacement for complex ureteral strictures: a systematic review and single-arm meta-analysis of surgical and functional outcomes.
articles.abstract: Complex, long-segment ureteral strictures present significant reconstructive challenges. While open ileal ureter replacement is the historical gold standard, it carries substantial perioperative morbidity. This systematic review and single-arm meta-analysis evaluate the surgical and functional outcomes of robot-assisted ileal ureter replacement (RIUR). Following Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses (PRISMA) guidelines, a comprehensive search of four databases was conducted through September 2026 to identify studies reporting adult RIUR outcomes for complex strictures. Outcomes were pooled using random-effects models. Five retrospective cohort studies comprising 110 patients met the inclusion criteria, with radiation-induced injury representing the predominant etiology (44.5%). The pooled surgical success rate was 93.9% (95% confidence interval [CI]: 87.0-97.2%). The pooled major complication rate (Clavien-Dindo grades III-V) was 10.0% (95% CI: 4.0-24.0%), driven primarily by urinary anastomotic leaks, typically managed with prolonged stenting. Pooled rates for metabolic acidosis requiring supplementation and stricture recurrence were 7.4% and 2.6%, respectively, while renal function remained stable or improved across all evaluated cohorts. Pooled mean operative time and estimated blood loss were 339.1 min (95% CI: 310.5-367.7) and 103.7 mL (95% CI: 54.9-152.6), respectively, while length of hospital stay varied widely by regional institutional pathway (median 3.0 days in early-discharge cohorts to 14.2 days in inpatient testing protocols). Current evidence suggests that RIUR represents a feasible and promising minimally invasive option for complex ureteral defects, with observed success rates meeting historical clinical benchmarks and an acceptable perioperative safety profile.

articles.title: Stereotactic body radiotherapy versus conventional external beam radiotherapy for bone metastases: a meta-analysis.
articles.abstract: Stereotactic body radiotherapy (SBRT) and conventional external beam radiotherapy (cEBRT) are widely used treatment options for the management of painful bone metastases. Randomized phase III trials have provided direct comparative evidence for SBRT and cEBRT; however, their results vary according to treatment regimen and clinical endpoint, supporting a broader quantitative synthesis of pain response, local control, retreatment, and safety outcomes. A systematic search was conducted in PubMed, Scopus, the Cochrane Library, and Google Scholar from database inception through January 2026. Comparative clinical studies evaluating SBRT versus cEBRT for bone metastases were included. Outcomes assessed encompassed pain-related measures (change in Visual Analog Scale scores at 3 and 6 months; complete, partial, stable, and progressive pain response), opioid consumption at 3 and 6 months, radiologic local progression or treatment failure at 8 months, re-irradiation at 12 months, skeletal-related events (vertebral and non-vertebral compression fractures), spinal cord compression, treatment-related toxicity, and overall survival at 1 year. Pooled analyses were performed using random-effects models. Early pain reduction at 3 months, partial and stable pain response, and opioid consumption at 3 and 6 months were comparable between SBRT and cEBRT (all p > 0.05). However, SBRT demonstrated superior mid-term outcomes, with a significantly higher complete pain response at 6 months (RR = 1.43; p = 0.001) and a significantly lower rate of progressive pain response at 6 months (RR = 0.61; p = 0.03). SBRT was also associated with markedly improved local disease control, reflected by lower rates of radiologic local progression or treatment failure at 8 months (RR = 0.36; p < 0.001) and a substantially reduced need for re-irradiation at 12 months (RR = 0.13; p < 0.001). Rates of vertebral and non-vertebral compression fractures, spinal cord compression, treatment-related toxicity, and overall survival at 1 year did not differ significantly between treatment modalities. This meta-analysis demonstrates that both SBRT and cEBRT are safe and effective treatment options for patients with painful bone metastases. While early pain palliation and safety outcomes are comparable, SBRT provides superior durability of pain control, reduced pain progression, improved local tumor control, and a markedly lower need for re-irradiation. SBRT may be particularly advantageous for patients with longer expected survival, oligometastatic disease, or lesions at higher risk of progression, whereas cEBRT remains an effective and accessible option for rapid symptom palliation in patients with limited prognosis.

articles.title: Anesthesiological considerations and complications in robotic surgery: a retrospective analysis.
articles.abstract: Robotic-assisted surgery has become increasingly prevalent across various surgical disciplines. Understanding anesthesiological factors influencing perioperative outcome is essential for optimizing patient care. This retrospective analysis evaluated 200 patients who underwent robotic surgery across three surgical categories: gastrointestinal (GI, n=60), hepatopancreticobiliary (HPB, n=28), and colorectal (n=112) procedures. We conducted an exploratory analysis of associations between anesthesiological parameters-including fluid management, surgical duration, and blood loss-and clinical outcomes such as intensive care unit (ICU) length of stay, total hospital length of stay, complication severity (Clavien-Dindo classification) using univariable and multivariable regression models. The exploratory analyses suggested potential associations between surgical duration and outcomes across surgical specialties in multivariable analysis. For GI procedures, longer surgical duration was associated with higher odds of severe complications (Clavien-Dindo grade ≥III; OR = 1.80 (1.21, 2.66)). In colorectal surgery, surgical duration was independently associated with both development of severe complications (OR = 1.28 (1.01, 1.62)) and total hospital length of stay (log-scale, β = 0.08 (0.03, 0.12)). Fluid intake was associated with an increased hospital length of stay in colorectal surgery (log-scale, β = 0.10 (0.03, 0.17)). Anesthesiological management, particularly surgical duration and fluid management, showed associations with perioperative outcomes in robotic surgery. The estimated effects provide preliminary insights into the magnitude of these associations and may serve as a basis for hypothesis generation and the design of future prospective studies. Further studies are needed to confirm these findings and to investigate the potential clinical relevance of anesthesiological and perioperative management strategies.

articles.title: COVID-19 triggers pulmonary tumor outgrowth through hypoxia- and inflammation-induced VEGF-dependent angiogenesis.
articles.abstract: Pulmonary nodules are highly prevalent in adult human populations, with a substantial proportion representing dormant cancerous lesions. We hypothesized that these pulmonary dormant cancers debilitate in growth owing to the lack of an angiogenic switch in tumors. In this study, we comprehensively investigated the hypothesis that specific pathological triggers can activate this angiogenic switch utilizing severe acute respiratory coronavirus 2 (SARS-CoV-2) infection-induced hypoxia as a primary physiological stimulus. Our findings provide compelling experimental evidence demonstrating that SARS-CoV-2 infection induces profound pulmonary hypoxia and severe tissue inflammation in animal models. This microenvironmental disruption markedly upregulates the expression of vascular endothelial growth factor (VEGF) and vascular endothelial growth factor receptor 2 (VEGFR2) within lung tissues. The resulting hyperactivation of the downstream VEGF-VEGFR2 signaling pathway effectively drives robust pulmonary neovascularization, a phenomenon frequently documented in clinical observations of COVID-19 patients. Furthermore, employing an established experimental tumor model, we demonstrated that SARS-CoV-2 infection directly accelerates tumor outgrowth via this specific VEGF angiogenesis-dependent cascade. Crucially, the targeted administration of a neutralizing antibody to block VEGF significantly suppressed tumor progression and outgrowth in SARS-CoV-2-infected, tumor-bearing animals. Our data show that the COVID-19-induced hypoxia-VEGF-angiogenesis axis serves as one of the mechanisms for initiating tumor outgrowth in pulmonary tissues.

articles.title: How coronary artery disease is portrayed in images from educational websites and resources in Aotearoa New Zealand: a content analysis.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Coronary artery disease (CAD) is a leading cause of global morbidity and disproportionately affects Māori and Pacific peoples in Aotearoa New Zealand (NZ). Poor understanding of symptoms and management contributes to delayed care. Yet visual health information can enhance patient comprehension, engagement, and long-term health outcomes.

AIM: This content analysis aims to explore how CAD is portrayed in images within NZ-based online educational webpages and resources.

METHODS: A content analysis was conducted on publicly available CAD images from NZ-based health educational websites. Data were collected in January 2026 using a systematic Google search strategy. Images were coded using a pre-defined framework categorising content into themes, and descriptive frequencies and proportions were calculated.

RESULTS: Of the 279 webpages identified in the search, 105 met the inclusion criteria, yielding 257 images. Photographs (44.8%) and digital graphics (24.9%) were most common. Only 30% of images depicted people, with slightly more males with neutral expressions. Content primarily focused on prevention and healthy lifestyle choices (24.9%) and anatomical images (21.8%). Clinical aspects were significantly underrepresented, including depictions of screening and diagnoses (13.2%), consequences (9.0%), and medications (7.0%).

DISCUSSION: CAD images in NZ webpages and educational resources emphasise healthy lifestyles and diet, but are less focused on treatment and long-term management. The scarcity of images depicting CAD symptoms, screening, medications, disease pathophysiology, and long-term management represents a missed opportunity to support health literacy. Culturally appropriate and clinically balanced visual resources are needed to improve patient understanding and reduce health inequities in NZ.

articles.title: Congenital Cytomegalovirus Testing Following Pennsylvania Hearing-Targeted Screening Legislation.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Congenital cytomegalovirus infection (cCMV) occurs in approximately 1/200 to 1/250 US newborns each year and can cause progressive sensorineural hearing loss. Since 2022, Pennsylvania law mandates cCMV testing for infants who fail newborn hearing screening.

OBJECTIVES: To assess changes in cCMV testing rates and diagnosis before and after Pennsylvania hearing-targeted legislation.

METHODS: Retrospective cohort study of all live births at 3 university-affiliated birth centers. We identified all infants tested for CMV at 21 days of age or younger and analyzed cCMV testing rates in pre- (January 2018-June 2022) and post- (July 2022-December 2024) legislation eras using interrupted time-series analysis. We assessed other clinical signs associated with cCMV testing using standard statistics.

RESULTS: The study cohort included 85 324 infants. Among 54 909 born prelegislation, 3168 (5.8%) had cCMV testing; among 30 415 born postlegislation, 3197 (10.5%) were tested. cCMV testing rates increased significantly among term (by 3.2%) and preterm infants (by 15.5%) at the beginning of the postlegislation era (P = .003 and .001, respectively). Among 5224 infants with hearing-based criteria for screening, CMV testing increased from 36.7% prelegislation to 74.0% postlegislation (P < .001). In the postlegislation period, testing associated with isolated microcephaly increased, but isolated small for gestational age-associated testing decreased. Among 61 infants diagnosed with cCMV, 16 (26.2%) were identified based on hearing criteria alone (2.3/1000 infants prelegislation, 6.0/1000 infants postlegislation, P = .04).

CONCLUSIONS: CMV testing and diagnosis based on hearing criteria alone increased significantly post passage of Pennsylvania hearing-targeted cCMV testing legislation, but infants tested for hearing criteria alone accounted for less than half of identified cCMV cases.

articles.title: Improving Professional Billing Practices in a Pediatric Hospital Medicine Section.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Professional billing translates clinical complexity and physician work into Current Procedural Terminology (CPT) codes and work relative value units (wRVUs), which inform reimbursement and resource planning. Pediatric hospital medicine (PHM) involves complex, cognitive, and time-intensive care, making accurate documentation and code selection essential. Baseline data in our PHM section suggested underuse of appropriate codes, contributing to undercapture of physician work. We aimed to increase wRVUs per patient-day by 25% over 12 months.

METHODS: We conducted a quality improvement initiative at an academic children's hospital from March 2024 to February 2025. Key drivers were billing knowledge, standardized documentation, workflows, and shared culture around billing. The primary outcome was wRVUs per patient-day; the secondary outcome was professional revenue. Process measures included targeted CPT code use. Balancing measures included coding, denial, or compliance concerns identified by the Revenue and Compliance team. Four Plan-Do-Study-Act cycles tested education, a billing guide, documentation tools, and billing data feedback. Statistical process control charts identified special cause variation.

RESULTS: We analyzed 23 772 CPT codes. Mean wRVUs per patient-day increased from 1.9 to 2.5, a 32% increase sustained through December 2025. Professional revenue increased 31% during intervention and 40% during sustainability. Use of level 3 initial inpatient care codes increased from 11% to 58%, level 3 subsequent inpatient care codes from 12% to 54%, and prolonged discharge codes from 13% to 42%. Neonatal intensive care and critical care code use increased. No denial or compliance concerns were identified.

CONCLUSIONS: A section-wide quality improvement approach improved capture of physician work and professional revenue without billing or compliance concerns.

articles.title: Perspectives on Gender Equity: A National Survey of Pediatric Hospital Medicine Division Leaders.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To assess pediatric hospital medicine (PHM) division leaders' perspectives on gender equity in their divisions and organizations.

METHODS: In 2025, we conducted a cross-sectional Research Electronic Data Capture survey distributed via email to 236 PHM division leaders. The survey consisted of 53 items on division and leader demographics, promotion, leadership, benefits, and gender-related experiences. Descriptive statistics summarized numeric responses, and qualitative content analysis identified emerging themes in free-text responses.

RESULTS: Responses from 125 PHM division leaders (53% response rate) were received. Leaders were predominately women (69%) and held PHM subboard certification (84%), with a median of 15 years of practice as a hospitalist. According to leaders, 76% of their faculty were women. No gender differences were reported in faculty rank or leadership roles. Compensation analysis by gender was reported by only 26% of responding institutions. Similarly, although wellness support was common, gender-stratified analyses of outcomes were rarely performed (19%). Mean paid parental leave offered to birth parents was 8 weeks. Qualitative analysis of leaders' suggestions to drive change toward gender equity revealed 6 major themes: (1) compensation transparency, (2) caregiver support, (3) career development, (4) countering gender bias through education and allyship, (5) fostering psychological safety, and (6) advancing institutional accountability.

CONCLUSIONS: Division leaders reported gaps in gender equity practices alongside systemic challenges in PHM. Identified priorities include transparent compensation practices, caregiver-inclusive benefits, career pathways, and leadership accountability. As the first national assessment of PHM leaders' perceptions, these findings highlight opportunities to strengthen structural support for gender-equitable advancement for all clinicians.

articles.title: Clinical and genetic risk factors for apolipoprotein L1-mediated chronic kidney disease in people of African ancestry with HIV.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE OF REVIEW: To summarize current understanding of the epidemiology, pathogenesis and management of HIV-Associated Nephropathy (HIVAN) and other forms of Apolipoprotein L1 (APOL1)-mediated chronic kidney disease (CKD) in people of African ancestry with HIV.

RECENT FINDINGS: The G1 and G2 variants of the APOL1 gene, which have emerged in trypanosomiasis-endemic areas of Africa, predispose to HIV-associated nephropathy (HIVAN) and other forms of CKD. The risk of APOL1-mediated CKD is attenuated with HIV control and carriage of the p.N264K genetic variant. Several treatments targeting the APOL1 gene and the transmembrane ion channel encoded by the APOL1 gene are being evaluated in clinical trials; early findings indicate they achieve rapid and marked reductions in proteinuria in those with established APOL1-mediated CKD.

SUMMARY: Genetic variants of APOL1 are causally implicated in HIVAN and other forms of severe CKD in populations of African ancestry with HIV. Genetic, epigenetic and environmental factors influence the risk of developing APOL1-mediated CKD, and emerging APOL1-directed therapies offer the prospect of clinical remission to those with established APOL1-mediated CKD.

articles.title: Screening for multidrug-resistant organism: clinical benefit or unquestioned routine.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE OF REVIEW: Current strategies for multidrug-resistant organism (MDRO) screening are primarily intended to support infection prevention programs. However, accumulating evidence indicates that intestinal colonization also provides clinically relevant information for antimicrobial stewardship. This review examines the biological basis and clinical utility of mucosal screening for optimizing empirical antibiotic therapy and proposes a new conceptual framework linking intestinal pathobiont burden with endogenous bloodstream infection.

RECENT FINDINGS: Recent studies consistently show that the absence of MDRO carriage is associated with a very low risk of subsequent infection, supporting well tolerated antimicrobial de-escalation in patients with negative clinical cultures. Emerging evidence further indicates that prolonged exposure to antianaerobic antibiotics promotes expansion of intestinal pathobionts, whereas preservation or restoration of the gut microbiota limits this process. Experimental and clinical observations suggest that the abundance of pathobionts, rather than simple carriage status, determines the probability of bacterial translocation and invasive infection.

SUMMARY: We propose that physiological bacterial translocation from the intestinal microbiota is a common phenomenon and may represent one of the mechanisms of bloodstream infection in critically ill and immunocompromised patients. In this model, progression to invasive infection depends on intestinal pathobiont burden exceeding the capacity of host immune clearance. If validated, this concept would support a transition from qualitative MDRO screening to quantitative assessment of intestinal pathobiont burden to guide antimicrobial stewardship and targeted preventive strategies.

articles.title: Complications associated with thoracic endovascular aortic repair: highlighting the role of peri- and post-operative cardiac monitoring.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Thoracic endovascular aortic repair (TEVAR) is first-line therapy for most descending thoracic aortic pathologies, yet it is performed in patients with a heavy burden of coronary disease, hypertension and limited cardiac reserve, and its cardiac complications remain underemphasized relative to neurological and device-related events.

AREAS COVERED: We summarize the complication profile of TEVAR briefly and then concentrate on its cardiac dimension: myocardial injury after non-cardiac surgery, arrhythmia, acute heart failure, and the chronic ventricular consequences of stent-graft-induced aortic stiffening. We review the mechanisms linking endograft deployment to ventricular-arterial uncoupling, the echocardiographic markers of interest, blood pressure management, and a phase-based framework for peri- and post-operative cardiac monitoring, distinguishing guideline-supported recommendations from expert opinion and from evidence extrapolated from general vascular surgery. PubMed/MEDLINE were searched from database inception to August 2026.

EXPERT OPINION: Cardiac surveillance around TEVAR is inconsistent and largely informal. We argue for baseline echocardiography in all elective patients, protocolized high-sensitivity troponin and natriuretic peptide measurement, defined-duration rhythm monitoring, structured blood pressure control, and longitudinal assessment of ventricular-arterial coupling within a heart-team pathway. TEVAR-specific outcome data and Windkessel-preserving graft design are the priorities for the next phase of endovascular aortic care.

articles.title: Rapid decline in smart insulin pen decision-support use in youth with type 1 diabetes: a randomized crossover pilot trial.
articles.journal: Journal of pediatric endocrinology & metabolism : JPEM

articles.title: Interface-Programmed Growth of High-Aspect-Ratio 1D Ni-MOF Nanofibers on MXene for Wearable Enzyme-Free Glucose Sensing.
articles.abstract: Noninvasive wearable glucose sensors capable of real-time sweat analysis offer a less discomforting alternative for long-term monitoring in patients with diabetes. However, practical implementation remains challenging. Major barriers include insufficient catalytic sensitivity to quantify the low glucose levels in sweat, limited compatibility between nanomaterial synthesis and scalable manufacturing processes, and the lack of a biofluid microenvironment suitable for enzyme-free electrochemical sensing. Here, we address these challenges by combining strong interfacial anchoring on a conductive template with surfactant-assisted growth control to engineer high-aspect-ratio (∼100) 1D Ni-TCPP MOF nanofibers as an active shell on MXene-NH2. In contrast to conventional electrospinning-assisted approaches, the resulting 1D MOF shell is polymer-template-free and thus avoids insulating scaffold components. The resulting fluffy, self-supporting Ni-MOF@MXene architecture is inherently compatible with printed electronics, enabling large-area fabrication of wearable enzyme-free glucose-sensing patches. To overcome the constraints of enzyme-free sensing in physiological biofluids, we further develop an integrated system that combines microfluidics with a NaOH/Nafion/PVA alkaline sustained-release membrane, establishing a localized alkaline microenvironment within sweat to enable continuous analysis.

articles.title: Indicators for Computed Tomography Angiography Following Nonfatal Strangulation: A Scoping Review.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Nonfatal strangulation (NFS) is common in intimate partner violence and sexual assault and may result in blunt cervical vascular injury detectable with computed tomography angiography (CTA). Clinical indicators that reliably predict vascular injury and guide imaging decisions remain unclear.

METHODS: A scoping review following PRISMA-ScR guidelines examined studies evaluating associations between clinical presentation and CTA-confirmed vascular injury after manual NFS. Searches of PubMed, CINAHL, Web of Science, Embase, and the Cochrane Library were conducted in November 2025. Studies were eligible if they included adolescents or adults with manual NFS and reported clinical assessment findings and CTA outcomes.

RESULTS: Seven retrospective studies met the inclusion criteria. Substantial variation in assessment methods, documentation, and imaging referral practices limited comparisons across studies. Vascular injuries were rare, and inconsistent reporting prevented identification of reliable clinical predictors.

DISCUSSION: Valid predictors of vascular injury following NFS have not been established. Standardized forensic nursing assessment and documentation are essential to developing reliable CTA prediction tools.

articles.title: From Bruising to Blindness: A Practical Guide to Identifying and Managing Hyaluronic Acid Filler Complications.
articles.journal: Dermatologic surgery : official publication for American Society for Dermatologic Surgery [et al.]
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: To provide a comprehensive, evidence-based review of the complications associated with hyaluronic acid (HA) dermal fillers and to offer practical guidance for their identification, prevention, and management.

DESIGN: Narrative review of the peer-reviewed literature, consensus guidelines, and postmarket surveillance data addressing the classification, pathophysiology, prevention, and treatment of HA filler complications.

FINDINGS: Hyaluronic acid fillers carry a favorable safety profile, with severe complications reported in fewer than 0.01% of injection sites. Complications are classified by onset. Early-onset events include ecchymosis, injection-site and hypersensitivity reactions, product displacement, and vascular occlusion. Late-onset events include biofilm-associated infection, delayed inflammatory nodules, granulomas, and hyperpigmentation. Vascular occlusion is the most feared complication and may progress to skin necrosis, vision loss, or stroke; prompt recognition and high-dose hyaluronidase, increasingly aided by ultrasound guidance, are central to management. Prevention rests on sound anatomic knowledge, appropriate product selection, and careful injection technique, while treatment is tailored to the specific complication.

SUMMARY: As filler use continues to expand, clinicians must be prepared to recognize, prevent, and manage the full spectrum of complications. This review consolidates current evidence into a practical framework intended to support safe practice and optimal patient outcomes.

articles.journal: The Medical letter on drugs and therapeutics

articles.title: Integrating radiomic features and spatial semantic features from multiparametric MRI for IDH genotyping in glioma.
articles.abstract: Gliomas, one of the most prevalent primary tumors of the central nervous system, have IDH molecular subtypes that are strongly linked to patient survival, prognosis, and treatment plans. However, there are currently few noninvasive preoperative prediction techniques, and postoperative pathology and genetic testing are the main approaches used to assess IDH status. Radiomics features can quantitatively characterize intratumoral heterogeneity, whereas spatial semantic features may provide additional information related to tumor location and macroscopic growth patterns. When it comes to characteristics like glioma invasiveness, growth patterns, and angiogenesis, spatial semantic features can enhance radiomics features. In order to predict IDH molecular subtypes in gliomas, this study suggests a combined analytical approach that incorporates clinical data, spatial semantic features, and multiparametric magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) radiomic features. This technique uses the IBSI standard to extract radiomic data from raw multiparametric MRI images and combines morphological analysis, gradient statistics, and 3D geometric modeling to create spatial semantic information. To eliminate redundant features and account for multicollinearity, Pearson correlation analysis and the variance inflation factor were utilized. The best feature subset was then obtained through a multi-stage feature selection procedure that combined random forests (RFs), LASSO regression, and recursive feature elimination. Lastly, imaging characteristics and clinical data were combined using a RF model to identify IDH molecular subtypes in gliomas. According to experimental findings, the suggested model's area under the ROC curve (AUC) in a five-fold cross-validation was 96.08%. The model had the AUC of 95.62%, ACC of 91.67%, sensitivity of 88.89%, and specificity of 93.94% in the final test set. The limitations of radiomics in conveying tumor macroscopic development patterns and spatial invasion relationships can be somewhat compensated for by spatial semantic aspects, according to additional investigation. The source code at:.

articles.title: Observation of a hole-sidev= 7/2 fractional quantum hall state in trilayer graphene.
articles.abstract: The intertwined many-body correlation, nontrivial topology, and symmetry can lead to exotic low-energy quasiparticle excitation, such as fractional quantum Hall (FQH) states, Fermi liquids, etc. Some FQH states with even denominators appearing at the half-filling of Landau levels can be interpreted by Moore-Read theory, and the corresponding composite fermions satisfy non-Abelian statistics and have the potential to realize topological quantum computation. Possessing extraordinary tunability that stems from the intricate interplay of spin, valley, and orbital degrees of freedom, few-layer graphene stands out as an ideal platform for studying the FQH effect. Here we report the observation of theFQH state on the hole side of Bernal-stacked trilayer graphene unilaterally encapsulated with hexagonal boron nitride-the first realization of this state on the hole side of pristine trilayer graphene. In contrast to recently reported electron-side even-denominator states hosted in the monolayer-likeorbital, thestate emerges in the bilayer-likeorbital near its crossing with thelevel, and exhibits a transport activation gap ofK, nearly two orders of magnitude larger than its electron-side counterparts. This value, obtained from Arrhenius analysis of the temperature-dependent residual resistance, is a conservative lower bound, as the analysis is limited by the residual-resistance floor. Our results suggest that few-layer graphene is an ideal platform for studying low-dimensional correlation states.

articles.title: [Mycobacterium persicum pulmonary disease misdiagnosed as tuberculosis: a case report].
articles.journal: Zhonghua jie he he hu xi za zhi = Zhonghua jiehe he huxi zazhi = Chinese journal of tuberculosis and respiratory diseases
articles.abstract: Mycobacterium persicum (M. persicum) is a nontuberculous mycobacterium that predominantly affects the lungs, causing pulmonary lesions, and is readily misdiagnosed as tuberculosis. Here we report a 48-year-old man with AIDS and M. persicum pulmonary disease who was initially misdiagnosed with pulmonary tuberculosis and received standard anti-TB therapy, yet showed no radiological or clinical improvement. Sputum specimens were subsequently subjected to targeted next-generation sequencing (tNGS), which identified M. persicum and established the definitive diagnosis. After switching to an anti-M. persicum regimen, the pulmonary lesions gradually resolved, and the patient was cured. This case highlights that in immunocompromised individuals, M. persicum pulmonary disease closely mimics tuberculosis in both imaging and clinical presentation, and reliance solely on CT and sputum acid-fast staining readily leads to misdiagnosis. Molecular diagnostics are central to precise diagnosis and treatment, and this case offers a valuable clinical reference.

articles.title: [Clinical risk factors and molecular epidemiological characteristics of carbapenem-resistant Klebsiella pneumoniae infection].
articles.journal: Zhonghua jie he he hu xi za zhi = Zhonghua jiehe he huxi zazhi = Chinese journal of tuberculosis and respiratory diseases
articles.abstract: Objective: To investigate the molecular epidemiological characteristics, antimicrobial resistance mechanisms, and clinical risk factors for infection with carbapenem-resistant Klebsiella pneumoniae (CRKP), and to examine the relationship between antimicrobial resistance and virulence. Methods: A total of 528 Klebsiella pneumoniae (KP) isolates and corresponding clinical data were collected from hospitalized patients at Qingdao Municipal Hospital between November 2016 and October 2023. Based on antimicrobial susceptibility testing results, 80 patients with CRKP infection were assigned to the CRKP group. Patients with carbapenem-susceptible K. pneumoniae (CSKP) isolates recovered within 7 days before or after the CRKP isolation date were selected as matched controls for each patient in the CRKP group. If insufficient eligible controls were available, the matching window was expanded to 30 days before or after the isolation date. Ultimately, 160 matched patients were included in the CSKP group. Whole-genome sequencing was performed on all included isolates to systematically characterize their molecular epidemiological features and resistance and virulence gene profiles. A multivariable logistic regression model was used to identify independent risk factors for CRKP infection. Spearman rank correlation analysis was performed to assess the correlation between resistance and virulence gene scores. Results: Multivariable logistic regression analysis showed that a history of antimicrobial agent use in the 30 days before infection (OR=4.411, 95%CI: 1.749-11.128; Wald χ²=9.882; P<0.01) and invasive abdominal procedures in 30 days before infection (OR=6.846, 95%CI: 3.141-14.922; Wald χ²=23.411; P<0.01) were independent risk factors for CRKP infection. ST11 was the predominant sequence type among CRKP isolates (80.0%), and the blaKPC-2 gene was the predominant resistance determinant (88.8%). The predominant CRKP clone, ST11, underwent a serotype transition from ST11-K25/O5 to ST11-K64/O2a. At the overall population level, the antimicrobial resistance gene score was negatively correlated with the virulence gene score (Spearman ρ=-0.321, P<0.001). However, subgroup analysis showed no significant correlation between the two scores within the same ST11 clone (Spearman ρ=0.020, P=0.872). These findings suggest that the overall negative correlation was a population-level artifact caused by inherent phenotypic differences among distinct clonal groups, rather than an evolutionary trade-off in which the acquisition of antimicrobial resistance within the same clone resulted in reduced virulence. The intensive care unit (ICU) was the central hub for nosocomial clonal transmission of CRKP. The predominant clone may have disseminated from the ICU to general wards through patient transfers, healthcare workers, or medical equipment, thereby forming interdepartmental transmission chains. Conclusions: A history of antimicrobial agent use and invasive abdominal procedures in the 30 days before CRKP infection were independent risk factors for CRKP infection. CRKP isolates frequently carried plasmids coharboring multiple antimicrobial resistance determinants and exhibited extensive antimicrobial resistance.

articles.title: [Standardized establishment scheme for asthma outpatient clinics (pilot)].
authors: Chinese Thoracic Society, Chinese Medical Association
Respiratory Medicine Professional Committee, Chinese Research Hospital Association
Expert Group of the Pulmonary and Critical Care Medicine Asthma Specialty Capacity Enhancement Program
articles.journal: Zhonghua jie he he hu xi za zhi = Zhonghua jiehe he huxi zazhi = Chinese journal of tuberculosis and respiratory diseases
articles.abstract: Bronchial asthma (asthma) is a common chronic respiratory disease in China, yet the quality of diagnosis and treatment varies across regions and levels of health care institutions. Asthma, particularly severe asthma, is often poorly controlled and associated with frequent acute exacerbations, substantially impairing patients' quality of life and imposing a considerable socioeconomic burden. Considering the current state of asthma diagnosis and treatment in China, the writing group drew on domestic and international asthma guidelines and literature to develop standards for asthma outpatient clinics within the framework of the standardized development criteria for Pulmonary and Critical Care Medicine (PCCM) and formulated this implementation plan. The plan is intended to provide a reference for the establishment of disease-specific asthma clinics in China and to enhance the capacity for the management of asthma, particularly severe asthma.

articles.title: [Expert consensus on the operational protocol for radionuclide pulmonary ventilation/perfusion scintigraphy of pulmonary thromboembolism].
authors: Chinese Thoracic Society, Chinese Medical Association
National Collaborative Group for Prevention and Treatment of Pulmonary Embolism and Pulmonary Vascular Diseases
Expert Committee, National Project of Standardized Diagnosis and Treatment of Pulmonary Hypertension
Expert Committee of Pulmonary Embolism and Pulmonary Vascular Diseases, National Center for Respiratory Medicine
Cardiopulmonary Vascular Group, Nuclear Medicine Branch, Beijing Medical Association
Nuclear Medicine Physicians Branch, Chinese Medical Doctor Association
articles.journal: Zhonghua jie he he hu xi za zhi = Zhonghua jiehe he huxi zazhi = Chinese journal of tuberculosis and respiratory diseases
articles.abstract: Radionuclide pulmonary ventilation/perfusion (V/Q) imaging is an important non-invasive tool for diagnosing pulmonary thromboembolism (PTE) and is used for screening, follow-up, and assessment of treatment response of PTE and chronic thromboembolic pulmonary hypertension (CTEPH). Currently, hospitals in China differ in their use of planar and tomographic acquisition methods for V/Q imaging, and interpretation requires a high level of expertise among nuclear medicine physicians. After surveying the nuclear medicine departments of multiple hospitals and holding expert discussions, the working group developed the Expert consensus on the operational protocol for radionuclide pulmonary ventilation/perfusion scintigraphy of pulmonary thromboembolism. This consensus covers examination procedures, diagnostic approaches, and precautions, with the aim of standardizing the clinical application of V/Q imaging procedures and their clinical application in PTE diagnosis. The following recommendations were formulated.Summary of RecommendationsRecommendation 1: For ventilation imaging, 99mTc-Technegas is recommended as the preferred radiopharmaceutical. During the preparation of Technegas, the working group recommends wetting the crucible with anhydrous ethanol before the addition of the sodium pertechnetate solution to improve the efficiency and quality of Technegas generation. If Technegas is unavailable, 99mTc-Diethylenetriaminepentaacetic acid (99mTc-DTPA) aerosol may be used as an alternative (Consensus level: 100%).Recommendation 2: Routine supplemental oxygen is suggested before pulmonary perfusion imaging to prevent false-positive images caused by pulmonary vasospasm. The recommended oxygen flow rate is 2-4 L/min, with an inhalation duration of 5-10 minutes (Consensus level: 83.3%).Recommendation 3: For pulmonary perfusion imaging, 200 000-700 000 radiopharmaceutical particles (mean, approximately 400 000) should be administered, with the recommended activity of 120-240 MBq (3-6 mCi). For patients with severe pulmonary hypertension, conditions with right-to-left heart shunting, or a history of single-lung transplantation, the particle number should be reduced to 100 000-200 000 (Consensus level: 83.3%).Recommendation 4: Gently agitate and homogenize the suspension of 99mTc-macroaggregated human serum albumin (99mTc-MAA) prior to injection. With the patient supine and breathing at normal tidal volume, slowly inject the tracer over several respiratory cycles through a patent intravenous line, continuously monitoring for adverse reactions; discontinue immediately if discomfort occurs. Strictly avoid backflow of blood into the syringe, which may cause particulate aggregation and bolus formation, leading to artifactual hot spots (Consensus level: 100%).Recommendation 5: For patients with protein allergies, a routine skin test is recommended before pulmonary perfusion imaging. Inject 0.1 ml of 99mTc-MAA suspension into the appropriate part of the forearm and observe for 15-20 minutes. If there is no positive reaction, perfusion imaging can be proceeded, with close observation and emergency medications on standby. If the skin test is positive, pulmonary perfusion imaging is not recommended. Routine skin testing is not indicated in patients without a history of allergy (Consensus level: 83.3%).Recommendation 6: For the 2-day acquisition protocol, perform pulmonary perfusion imaging on the first day. If the result is abnormal, perform pulmonary ventilation imaging the following day to aid diagnosis; if the perfusion imaging result is normal, pulmonary ventilation imaging may be omitted (Consensus level: 83.3%).Recommendation 7: For pregnant women with suspected PTE, if V/Q imaging is considered necessary after clinical assessment, a 2-day protocol is recommended. Dose reduction is recommended for lung perfusion imaging, the recommended dose of 99mTc-MAA is 50 MBq (1.35 mCi) (Consensus level: 100%).Recommendation 8: When the 1-day acquisition protocol is used, perfusion imaging may be performed immediately after completion of ventilation imaging. To ensure the clarity and accuracy of pulmonary perfusion imaging, the perfusion count rate should be 3-4 times the ventilation count rate (Consensus level: 100%).Recommendation 9: Avoid ambiguous phrasing such as "possible pulmonary embolism" in image reports. Interpretations should provide a definitive conclusion, such as "pulmonary embolism present", "pulmonary embolism absent", or another specific conclusion, after excluding other causes of impaired pulmonary perfusion (e.g., Takayasu arteritis, mediastinitis or pulmonary arterial sarcoma). When the diagnosis remains uncertain, the report should state, "pulmonary embolism cannot be excluded; correlation with clinical findings and other imaging examinations is recommended" to support subsequent clinical assessment and therapeutic decision-making (Consensus level: 100%).Recommendation 10: For patients with CTEPH, visual semi-quantitative analysis (Begic/Meyer score) may serve as an adjunctive tool for efficacy assessment after percutaneous pulmonary balloon angioplasty (BPA) or pulmonary endarterectomy (PEA). Where institutional resources permit, structured reporting is encouraged to improve the clarity and reproducibility of segmental impairment documentation (Consensus level: 100%).

articles.title: [Chinese expert consensus on the clinical application of lung biopsy in interstitial lung disease].
authors: Chinese Thoracic Society, Chinese Medical Association
articles.journal: Zhonghua jie he he hu xi za zhi = Zhonghua jiehe he huxi zazhi = Chinese journal of tuberculosis and respiratory diseases
articles.abstract: Interstitial lung disease (ILD) comprises a highly heterogeneous group of pulmonary disorders, whose diagnosis often requires the integration of clinical, radiologic, and pathologic evidence. Lung biopsy is a key method for obtaining a histopathologic diagnosis, but unified standards are lacking for determining indications, selecting biopsy techniques, managing patients perioperatively, and integrating pathologic and clinical information. To address these gaps, the Respiratory Physicians Branch of the Chinese Medical Doctor Association and the ILD Group of the Chinese Thoracic Society spearheaded this initiative, collaborating with national experts in respiratory medicine, radiology, pathology, thoracic surgery, and rheumatology to formulate this consensus. Developed in strict adherence to evidence-based medicine principles, this consensus is founded on systematic literature reviews and evidence grading, utilizing the Delphi method for anonymous voting. It culminates in 15 recommendations, each explicitly annotated with the level of evidence and strength of recommendation. This consensus systematically delineates the multidisciplinary discussion (MDD)-centered full-process management of lung biopsy. The main contents encompass: assessment of the necessity and feasibility of lung biopsy; indication stratification strategies based on HRCT patterns; applicability scenarios and selection pathways for the four major lung biopsy techniques; shared decision-making; perioperative comprehensive management; management strategies for acute exacerbation of ILD (AE-ILD); standardization of tissue processing and pathological reporting; the post-biopsy MDD process for integrated diagnosis; and biopsy decision-making in special clinical contexts, such as ILD complicated by lung cancer or connective tissue disease-associated ILD (CTD-ILD). This consensus aims to provide clinicians with clear, safe, and practical guidance on lung biopsy, promote standardized and precise decision-making, and improve patient outcomes.Summary of RecommendationsRecommendation 1: For patients with suspected ILD, a comprehensive multidisciplinary discussion (MDD) is mandatory prior to lung biopsy. This evaluation should establish the diagnostic certainty of the preliminary clinical assessment, evaluate the clinical utility of the biopsy, and facilitate shared decision-making (SDM) that incorporates patient preferences (Level of evidence: 3, Recommendation: strong).Recommendation 2: For ILD patients in whom the diagnosis remains uncertain following a comprehensive non-invasive evaluation, or when precise histopathologic subtyping is required, a lung biopsy is recommended to establish a definitive diagnosis and guide the therapeutic management (Level of evidence: 4, Recommendation: strong).Recommendation 3: For patients with an interstitial pattern, a lung biopsy is strongly discouraged if HRCT demonstrates a definite UIP pattern and secondary etiologies have been excluded. A conditional recommendation for a lung biopsy applies to patients with a probable UIP patterns in whom NSIP or fibrotic HP cannot be ruled out. A lung biopsy is strongly recommended to achieve a definitive diagnosis in patients with an indeterminate or non-UIP patterns and insufficient clinical evidence (Level of evidence: 4, Recommendation: conditional).Recommendation 4: For patients with an alveolar filling pattern, a lung biopsy is recommended to clarify the etiology once infection, alveolar hemorrhage, and pulmonary edema have been systematically excluded, and there is either a lack of response to empirical therapy or a clinical necessity to differentiate the lesion from malignancy (Level of evidence: 2, Recommendation: strong).Recommendation 5: For suspected rare ILDs, including PAP, iEP, LAM, and LIP, non-invasive or minimally invasive diagnostic modalities should be prioritized; a lung biopsy is conditionally recommended if these approaches are non-diagnositic. Conversely, a lung biopsy is strongly recommended for patients with clinically suspected AFOP or PLCH (Level of evidence: 2, Recommendation: conditional).Recommendation 6: Lung biopsy is not recommended for patients with acute respiratory failure, severe pulmonary functional impairment, recent cardiovascular events, hemodynamic instability, significant pulmonary hypertension, severe coagulopathy, or end-stage systemic debilitation (Level of evidence: 1, Recommendation: strong).Recommendation 7: Site selection for lung biopsy should target active lesions identified on HRCT (e.g., ground-glass opacities or fine reticulation). Specimens must include the interface between diseased and normal parenchyma to facilitate pattern assessment. High-risk areas, such as major vessels and severe bullae, must be strictly avoided. Multi-lobar sampling from at least two sites of varying severity is recommended to adequately capture disease heterogeneity (Level of evidence: 4, Recommendation: strong).Recommendation 8: A TBLB is recommended as the first-line diagnostic approach for suspected granulomatous diseases (e.g., sarcoidosis) and specific alveolar filling patterns. If a TBLB is non-diagnostic, escalation to TBLC or SLB is advised. A TBLB is not recommended for the evaluation of predominantly fibrotic ILDs (e.g., UIP or NSIP) (Level of evidence: 4, Recommendation: strong).Recommendation 9: TBLC is recommended as the preferred modality in expert centers, particularly for patients who are poor candidates for or are averse to SLB. The procedure should be standardized under general anesthesia with prophylactic balloon placement for hemorrhage control and integrated with imaging or navigational guidance to optimize diagnostic yield while minimizing procedural complications (Level of evidence: 2, Recommendation: strong).Recommendation 10: SLB is recommended for patients in whom TBLC yields a non-diagnostic result, provided their cardiopulmonary physiological reserve permits surgical intervention. Video-assisted thoracoscopic surgery (VATS) is the preferred approach, requiring sampling from at least two distinct lobes. Biopsies should prioritize the dependent segments of the upper lobes or the superior segments of the lower lobes; sampling from the lingula or the right middle lobe should only be considered if these sites harbor the most representative lesions and no superior alternatives exist (Level of evidence: 2, Recommendation: strong).Recommendation 11: PTNB is recommended for the diagnosis and differential diagnosis in ILD patients presenting with solitary nodules, masses, or focal consolidations, particularly to rule out malignancy. However, it is not recommended for the histopathological evaluation of diffuse fibrosing ILDs (Level of evidence: 2, Recommendation: strong).Recommendation 12: A shared decision-making model is recommended throughout the biopsy selection process. Clinicians should thoroughly counsel patients regarding the benefits, risks, and alternatives of the procedure, ultimately formulating a clinical plan that aligns medical evidence with patient values (Level of evidence: 4, Recommendation: strong).Recommendation 13: Histological or imaging patterns of usual interstitial pneumonia (UIP), active disease phase, and reduced diffusing capacity for carbon monoxide (DLCO) are the main risk factors for acute exacerbation of interstitial lung disease (AE-ILD). Routine prophylactic use of glucocorticoids or antifibrotic therapy is not recommended for all patients; instead, meticulous perioperative management is recommended to prevent acute exacerbations. Once AE occurs, the underlying cause should be promptly investigated, and high-dose glucocorticoids along with supportive therapy may be considered (Level of evidence: 2, Recommendation: strong).Recommendation 14: Histopathological reports must adhere to current international standardized nomenclature, prioritizing the description of the predominant histological patterns and their salient features, while specifically noting any findings indicative of a specific etiology. Diagnostic limitations secondary to suboptimal specimen quality must be explicitly stated. Pathologists are required to provide a systematic and standardized microscopic description of the tissue pathology, formulate a histopathological classification, and offer etiological insights whenever feasible (Level of evidence: 4, Recommendation: strong).Recommendation 15: Post-biopsy MDD is central to formulating an integrated diagnosis and should be conducted by the same cohort of clinicians, radiologists, and pathologists involved in the initial evaluation. A systematic correlation between the histopathology and the clinical andradiologic data is required; any discordances must be thoroughly analyzed to achieve a consensus integrated diagnosis and guide therapeutic planning. If an integrated diagnosis cannot be established, a subsequent MDD or referral to an expert center for a repeat biopsy is warranted (Level of evidence: 2, Recommendation: strong).

articles.title: [Advances in early bedside etiological diagnosis of severe pneumonia].
articles.journal: Zhonghua jie he he hu xi za zhi = Zhonghua jiehe he huxi zazhi = Chinese journal of tuberculosis and respiratory diseases
articles.abstract: The case fatality rate of severe pneumonia remains high, early and accurate etiological diagnosis is a prerequisite for precision antimicrobial therapy. Conventional culture techniques are limited by long turnaround times and low positivity rates. In recent years, novel detection systems such as microbiological rapid on-site evaluation(M-ROSE), point-of-care immunoloassays, multiplex PCR, and metagenomic sequencing have advanced rapidly, markedly shortening the time to pathogen identification. The integration of rapid detection assays for antimicrobial resistance genes has further facilitated precision antimicrobial therapy. Multi-omics analysis integrating the pathogen spectrum with host immune response status helps distinguish colonization from infection, thereby helping prevent antibiotic overuse. This article reviews techniques for pathogen and antimicrobial resistance gene detection together with strategies to distinguish colonization from infection to inform rapid bedside etiological diagnosis in severe pneumonia.

articles.title: [Early identification and protective strategies for pulmonary and extrapulmonary organ injury secondary to severe pneumonia].
articles.journal: Zhonghua jie he he hu xi za zhi = Zhonghua jiehe he huxi zazhi = Chinese journal of tuberculosis and respiratory diseases
articles.abstract: Severe pneumonia is one of the critical illness with the highest incidences and mortality rates in the intensive care unit. Its core threat lies not in the pulmonary infection itself, but in the subsequent multiple organ dysfunction syndrome (MODS). This review systematically delineates how severe pneumonia collectively accelerates organ injury through systemic inflammatory responses, type 2 immunity mediated by airway epithelial alarmins, endothelial thrombo-inflammatory pathways, as well as inappropriate oxygen therapy and mechanical ventilation. It further reviews the key points for early identification at the subclinical state, specific early-warning biomarkers, and bedside monitoring techniques applicable to extrapulmonary organs, including the heart, kidney, liver, and gastrointestinal tract, and proposes an integrated organ-protective strategy. This review emphasizes the concept of shifting the diagnostic and therapeutic window earlier, and aims to provide a reference for improving the comprehensive management of severe pneumonia by synthesizing current evidence and clinical practice.

articles.title: [Precision fluid management and artificial intelligence-assisted decision-making in severe pneumonia induced septic shock].
articles.journal: Zhonghua jie he he hu xi za zhi = Zhonghua jiehe he huxi zazhi = Chinese journal of tuberculosis and respiratory diseases
articles.abstract: Severe pneumonia-induced septic shock is one of the most representative complex syndromes in pulmonary critical care medicine. Its pathophysiology results from the combined effects of alveolar-capillary barrier injury, infection-associated vasodilation, microcirculatory perfusion abnormalities, cardiopulmonary interactions related to mechanical ventilation, and multiple organ dysfunction. Therefore, fluid management should emphasize a dynamic balance between lung injury, circulatory benefit, and etiological control. In recent years, international guidelines and clinical studies have indicated that the focus of treatment for severe pneumonia-induced septic shock has shifted from conventional fluid resuscitation to precision resuscitation based on dynamic fluid responsiveness, fluid tolerance, and phase-specific goals. In the setting of acute respiratory distress syndrome (ARDS) or at high risk of ARDS, the importance of early vasopressor administration and negative fluid balance management has further increased. Meanwhile, advances in artificial intelligence-including the identification of ARDS subphenotypes, early prediction of sepsis-associated ARDS, sepsis early warning systems have provided a foundation for identifying "fluid-intolerant" subpopulations, optimizing the timing of negative fluid balance, and constructing multimodal closed-loop decision-support systems. This article reviews the hemodynamic characteristics of severe pneumonia-induced septic shock, phenotype identification, etiological control, and an integrated closed-loop pathway combining ventilator waveforms, hemodynamics, ultrasonography, and artificial intelligence. It aims to provide a reference for clinical practice and future research.

articles.title: Problematic social media use and adverse childhood experiences: A systematic review.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND AND AIMS: Problematic social media use (PSMU) is highly prevalent among young people today and is associated with numerous negative outcomes. Adverse childhood experiences (ACEs) have increasingly been identified as a risk factor for the development of PSMU. The aim of this systematic review was to examine the relationship between ACEs and PSMU, as well as the mediators and moderators that have been investigated in this association.

METHODS: The systematic review was conducted in accordance with the PRISMA protocol. The literature search was performed in the following databases: Web of Science, ScienceDirect, PubMed, PsycINFO, MEDLINE and Google Scholar. The quality of the studies was assessed using the JBI Critical Appraisal Checklist for Analytical Cross-sectional Studies.

RESULTS: A total of 20 studies met the inclusion criteria. The vast majority of them showed a positive association between ACEs and PSMU. The results highlighted some cognitive and emotional processes that mediate the relationship between ACEs and PSMU, which were examined in 12 studies, while three studies examined the presence of moderators.

DISCUSSION AND CONCLUSIONS: ACEs represent an important risk factor for the development of PSMU. While existing studies have already highlighted the presence of mediators that help explain this relationship, more studies should be directed toward examining moderators, particularly demographic variables and protective factors. In addition to ACEs, the role of positive childhood experiences could also be examined as a protective factor.

articles.title: Mindfulness-based and mindfulness-informed interventions for internet use disorders in adolescents and young adults: A three-level random-effects meta-analysis.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The pervasive integration of the internet into daily life has rendered Internet Use Disorders (IUDs) a particular threat to adolescents and young adults, whose vulnerability is amplified by a developmental stage characterized by ongoing neurodevelopment and self-exploration. This systematic review and meta-analysis aimed to evaluate the efficacy of mindfulness-based and mindfulness-informed interventions (MBIIs) for this population.

METHODS: Seven databases were searched from inception to April 2026 for randomized controlled trials (RCTs). Risk of bias was assessed using the Revised Cochrane Risk of Bias tool (RoB 2), data were synthesized via three-level random-effects models, and the certainty of evidence was evaluated using the Grading of Recommendations, Assessment, Development, and Evaluation (GRADE) framework.

RESULTS: From 28 included RCTs (26 for final analysis; 88 effect sizes), MBIIs yielded a significant overall reduction in IUDs (d = -1.32, 95% CI [-1.73, -0.91], p < .001). Moderator analyses identified three significant factors influencing treatment efficacy: geographical region, measurement tool, and comparator condition.

DISCUSSION AND CONCLUSIONS: Our findings indicate that MBIIs represent an effective intervention for IUDs in youth, offering both therapeutic benefits and preventive potential. These results provide empirical evidence to inform clinicians and policymakers in developing targeted intervention strategies for IUDs.

articles.title: Chemotherapy-free phase 1/2 trial of HRS-4642 plus adebrelimab in previously treated metastatic KRAS G12D-mutant pancreatic cancer.
articles.abstract: KRAS G12D mutations drive approximately 40% of pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC) cases and foster an immunosuppressive tumor microenvironment. This phase 1/2 trial (NCT06427239) evaluated HRS-4642, a selective KRAS G12D inhibitor, combined with the PD-L1 blockade adebrelimab in 48 pretreated patients with metastatic KRAS G12D-mutant PDAC. Dose escalation revealed no dose-limiting toxicities, establishing the recommended phase 2 dose (RP2D), and no treatment-related deaths occurred; hypercholesterolemia and anemia (each 50%) were the most common treatment-related adverse events. In the RP2D cohort (n = 37), the confirmed objective response rate was 43.2% (95% confidence interval [CI], 27.1-60.5), disease control rate was 81.1% (95% CI, 64.8-92.0), median duration of response was 6.9 months (95% CI, 4.8-8.6), median progression-free survival was 5.7 months (95% CI, 4.0-7.5), and median overall survival was 11.5 months (95% CI, 9.2-16.9). This chemotherapy-free regimen is tolerable and shows encouraging antitumor activity in refractory KRAS G12D-mutant PDAC, warranting further investigation.

articles.title: Psychological interventions for harmful gambling: Systematic review and network meta-analysis.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND AND AIMS: Gambling causes harms for the individual, their families and wider society. Psychological interventions have been shown to improve gambling severity, but their relative effectiveness is not well understood.

METHODS: Systematic review and network meta-analysis (NMA) of psychological interventions for harmful gambling. Outcomes were gambling symptom severity and gambling frequency (expressed as standardized mean differences [SMDs]).

RESULTS: We included 52 randomized controlled trials (RCTs), 9013 participants and 14 intervention classes. For gambling symptom severity, group CBT was the most effective intervention (SMD -1.09, 95% credible intervals [95%CrIs] -1.75 to -0.44) followed by individual CBT (SMD -0.56, 95%CrIs -1.07 to -0.07). Waitlist showed increased symptom severity compared with no treatment (SMD 0.96, 95%CrIs 0.47 to 1.46). All other intervention effects were characterized by uncertainty. For gambling frequency, all active interventions showed similar effects to treatment as usual.

DISCUSSION: Included studies were of low or very low quality and there was moderate-to-high heterogeneity for the gambling symptom severity NMA. However, threshold analysis suggested that conclusions based on the NMA were robust to potential biases and sampling variation in the included evidence. Bias adjustment analyses did not show evidence of bias associated with small studies or industry funding.

CONCLUSIONS: Group CBT shows clinically important benefits and should be regarded as the best intervention for harmful gambling. For individuals who decline group CBT, or where this is not possible or suitable, individual CBT shows the next best evidence of benefit.

articles.title: The ZmMIR319A-ZmTCP5/44 module bifurcates into two pathways to coordinately regulate leaf angle and thermotolerance in maize.
articles.abstract: Global warming increasingly threatens agricultural productivity, necessitating the development of new crop varieties that combine high yield potential with climate resilience. Optimizing plant architecture, particularly by reducing leaf angle (LA), enables dense planting and enhances light capture, yet the mechanisms that coordinate architectural improvement with heat tolerance remain largely unknown. Here, we identify the microRNA ZmMIR319A as a key regulator of both LA and thermotolerance in maize. ZmMIR319A increases LA by post-transcriptionally repressing the Teosinte branched1/Cycloidea/PCF (TCP) transcription factors ZmTCP5 and ZmTCP44, thereby relieving their suppression of the auxin transporter genes ZmPIN1 and ZmPIN8 and stimulating parenchyma cell proliferation in the ligular region. Under heat stress, rapid downregulation of ZmMIR319A leads to the accumulation of ZmTCP5 and ZmTCP44 proteins, which repress the heat shock chaperone genes ZmHSP70-4 and ZmHSP90-5 in leaves to modulate thermotolerance while continuing to restrain ZmPIN1/8-mediated growth. Thus, the maize ZmMIR319A-ZmTCP5/44 module bifurcates into two regulatory pathways that coordinately govern LA through auxin transport and thermotolerance through heat shock protein signaling. Notably, ZmMIR319A-knockout mutants exhibit increased grain yield under high-density planting conditions despite reduced thermotolerance, highlighting a trade-off between architectural optimization and stress adaptation. Collectively, our findings reveal that a single regulatory module simultaneously controls plant architecture and stress adaptation, thereby providing a dual-target strategy for the molecular breeding of maize varieties with ideal plant architecture and climate resilience.
