articles.title: One-End-Truncated Au52 and Au70 Quantum Rods: High-Quantum-Yield NIR-II Emitters With Aspect-Ratio-Dominated Photophysics.
articles.abstract: Precise control over absorption/emission in NIR-II (1000-1700 nm) is essential for advancing photonic technologies. Atomically precise gold quantum rods (QRs) provide a structurally well-defined platform for fine-tuning NIR-II anisotropic excitonic behavior at the atomic level. In this study, we report Au52(PET)38 and Au70(PET)50 (PET = 2-phenylethanethiolate) as members of a distinct branch of Au QRs with one-end-truncated kernel topology. The Au52 and Au70 exhibit NIR-II absorption at 1032 and 1275 nm and nanosecond fluorescence at 1100 and 1360 nm, respectively. Their high quantum yields (20.9% for Au52 and 14.8% for Au70) together with high brightness (5.6 × 104 M-1 cm-1 for Au52 and a similar order of magnitude for Au70) substantially exceed those of most molecular NIR-II dyes, highlighting their promise as efficient inorganic NIR-II fluorophores. Comparative analysis across two structurally distinct Au QR families, including one-end-truncated and double-pointed rods, reveals that the longitudinal absorption and emission peak wavelengths, as well as the fluorescence linewidths, follow a common aspect-ratio-dependent scaling relation, suggesting length-dependent modulation of the ground- and excited-state electronic structure. These findings uncover a hierarchical interplay between rod elongation and kernel topology in defining NIR-II excitonic behavior and expand the structural design space of atomically precise QRs.

articles.title: Pre-Implant Angiography and Vascular Complications During Microaxial Flow Pump Support.
Impact of endoscopic ultrasound in cholangiocarcinoma staging: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Accurate staging is crucial for managing cholangiocarcinoma (CCA). Endoscopic ultrasound with tissue acquisition (EUS-TA) may enhance cross-sectional imaging-based staging; however, the impact of EUS on CCA management decision-making is unclear.

METHODS: 6 electronic databases were searched through to 10 July 2025 for studies on EUS-TA in staging CCA cases eligible for surgical resection or liver transplantation. The primary outcome was the pooled proportion of patients excluded from curative-intent surgery based on the EUS findings, which included newly detected findings and confirmation by EUS-TA of cross-sectional imaging findings. Secondary outcomes included the pooled incremental benefit of EUS (IBEUS) over cross-sectional imaging and EUS-specific adverse events. The IBEUS was defined as the proportion of patients with malignant lymph nodes identified by EUS-TA but not by cross-sectional imaging, relative to all patients who underwent cross-sectional imaging.

RESULTS: 9 studies with 831 patients were included. The rate of exclusion from curative-intent surgery based on EUS findings was 10% overall (95%CI 6%-18%; 9 studies), 7% for perihilar CCA (pCCA; 95%CI 2%-19%; 5 studies), 10% for those planned for resection (95%CI 4%-22%; 5 studies), and 8% for those planned for transplantation (95%CI 3%-22%; 3 studies). The pooled IBEUS was 3% (95%CI 1%-10%; 5 studies) overall, 4% (95%CI 1%-17%; 3 studies) for pCCA, 1% (95%CI 0%-3%; 2 studies) in patients intended for operative resection, and 7% (95%CI 1%-26%; 2 studies) in those intended for transplantation.

CONCLUSION: EUS may impact CCA staging and support treatment decisions.

articles.title: Farnesyltransferase Enables Modular Assembly of Dual-Functional Nanobody Conjugates for in Vivo Imaging of Inflammation.
articles.abstract: Non-invasive imaging of inflammation is critical for disease diagnosis, monitoring, and therapeutic evaluation. Nanobodies, due to their many unique properties, are emerging as powerful imaging agents; however, conventional non-specific conjugation strategies often yield heterogeneous products that limit in vivo performance. Here, we report a chemoenzymatic strategy that enables precise and modular assembly of nanobody conjugates using farnesyltransferase (FTase)-mediated site-specific modification. We developed a trifunctional FTase substrate that introduces two orthogonal bioorthogonal handles, an aldehyde and an azide, onto nanobodies in a single enzymatic step. These handles enable independent and controlled conjugation of imaging payloads (fluorophores or radioisotopes) and pharmacokinetic modifiers (i.e. PEG), which enhance in vivo signal-to-noise ratios. Applying this strategy to nanobodies targeting CD45 and CD11b, markers broadly expressed on all immune cells and myeloid subsets, respectively, we generated well-defined, dually modified constructs that enabled high-contrast in vivo visualization of immune organs, including the spleen and lymph nodes. In a mouse model of localized inflammation, these probes robustly delineated inflamed tissue with high sensitivity and specificity. Together, this FTase-enabled dual-labeling approach provides a versatile and generalizable platform for the rapid generation of precisely defined nanobody-based imaging agents, advancing non-invasive detection and monitoring of inflammation across diverse disease contexts.

articles.title: Molecular Basis for Activation to Inhibition Switching in Kv7.2 Channel Modulators.
articles.abstract: Kv7 voltage-gated potassium channels play a critical role in controlling electrical properties of excitable tissues. Neuronally-expressed Kv7 channels are involved in both common and rare neuropsychiatric disorders, ranging from epilepsy to depression and neurodegenerative diseases; thus, they represent attractive therapeutic targets. However, no Kv7 modulator is currently available for clinical use. Improved knowledge of the functional and structural determinants responsible for ligand-induced Kv7 channel modulation is likely to fill this gap. In the present work, we describe the cryo-electron microscopy structures of human Kv7.2 channels in complex with two retigabine analogues: compound 60 (c60), which we previously described as a Kv7 activator with improved pharmacokinetic and pharmacodynamic properties, and the newly designed compound 106 (c106), which acts as a potent Kv7 blocker. Although both compounds occupy the same pocket at the S5-S6 interface in the pore domain, docking and molecular dynamics simulations and electrophysiological experiments revealed that the opposite functional behavior is due to their differential interaction, involving the L307 residue. Thus, we herein provide novel mechanistic insights into the molecular mechanisms governing Kv7 channel modulation by exogenous ligands which may prove useful to target Kv7 channels with more potent and selective modulators.

articles.title: Surgical strategy and outcomes in renal cell carcinoma with inferior vena cava tumor extension: A tertiary center experience.
articles.journal: Turk gogus kalp damar cerrahisi dergisi
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Renal cell carcinoma (RCC) may extend into the inferior vena cava (IVC) and, in advanced cases, into the right atrium. Radical nephrectomy with IVC thrombectomy remains the mainstay of treatment; however, the role of cardiopulmonary bypass (CPB) in advanced tumor thrombus remains controversial. This study aimed to evaluate the surgical and early oncologic outcomes of patients with RCC and IVC tumor thrombus and to assess the impact of CPB on perioperative outcomes while cautiously interpreting the findings because of the limited sample size.

METHODS: We retrospectively analyzed 22 consecutive patients who underwent synchronous radical nephrectomy and IVC thrombectomy between 2009 and 2025 at a tertiary referral center. Patients were divided into two groups: Group I (n=8), who underwent surgery with CPB (± total circulatory arrest), and Group II (n=14), who underwent surgery without CPB. Tumor thrombus level was classified according to the Mayo clinic classification system. Operative variables, perioperative complications, recurrence rates, and survival outcomes were compared.

RESULTS: Level II thrombus was the most common presentation, whereas all Level IV cases required CPB. Operative time was significantly longer in the CPB group (267.5±121.4 vs. 190.4±38.7 minutes, p=0.038). Postoperative bleeding was significantly greater in Group I (p=0.001), whereas transfusion requirements, intensive care unit stay, and total hospital stay did not differ significantly between the groups. Perioperative mortality occurred in two patients (25%) in the CPB group and in none in Group II (p=0.16). The overall recurrence rate was 45% and was significantly higher in Group I (p=0.002). The overall 1-year survival rate was 77.2%, with no significant difference between the groups (p=0.12).

CONCLUSION: Radical nephrectomy with IVC thrombectomy may provide acceptable perioperative and early survival outcomes in patients with RCC and venous tumor extension. In this limited series, the use of CPB in patients with advanced tumor thrombus did not appear to significantly increase overall morbidity and may improve operative safety in technically demanding cases. Nevertheless, the interpretation of these findings is limited by the unequal distribution of disease stage between the two groups.

articles.title: Endovascular treatment of thoracoabdominal aortic pathologies using 3D printer-assisted physician-modified stent-grafts.
articles.journal: Turk gogus kalp damar cerrahisi dergisi
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Thoracoabdominal aortic aneurysms (TAAAs) and dissections are among the most challenging vascular diseases. Endovascular interventions have gained prominence in the treatment of these diseases in recent years. However, the frequent involvement of the visceral or supra-aortic artery ostia in the proximal or distal landing zone increases the complexity of the procedure. Therefore, several techniques have been developed to address this challenge. In this study, we present our experience with thoracic endovascular aortic repair using three-dimensional (3D) printer-assisted physician-modified stent-grafts (PMSGs) for thoracoabdominal aortic pathologies involving the left subclavian artery, celiac trunk, superior mesenteric artery, or renal arteries.

METHODS: Between January 2020 and January 2023, a total of 18 patients presenting with complex aortic pathologies were screened for eligibility. Four patients were excluded because of active systemic infection/mycotic etiology (n=2) or unsuitable iliofemoral access (n=2). Consequently, 14 patients (12 with TAAAs and 2 with aortic arch dissections) were treated using 3D printer-assisted PMSGs. All aortic arch dissections extended to the left subclavian artery.

RESULTS: Fourteen patients underwent surgery with 3D printing guidance. The technical success rate was 92.8%. There were no perioperative deaths. The mean age was 68.07±10.6 years. The mean procedure time was 4.27±1.23 hours, including a mean custom graft preparation time of 1.3±0.6 hours. The mean intensive care unit stay was 5.64±11.54 days, and the mean hospital stay was 13.07±10.6 days. All 14 patients were followed for 2-12 months, with a mean follow-up of 6 months. Mortality occurred in 1 patient (7.1%).

CONCLUSION: The 3D printer-assisted PMSG technique offers significant technical advantages by improving procedural precision and simplifying the creation of fenestrations for complex aortic pathologies. Our findings suggest that this technique provides a high technical success rate and represents a safe and feasible alternative for preserving vital side branches, particularly in settings where patient-specific custom-made grafts are not readily available.

articles.title: Frequency and determinants of reintubation following pediatric cardiac surgery.
articles.journal: Turk gogus kalp damar cerrahisi dergisi
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Reintubation is a significant complication after pediatric cardiac surgery and is associated with increased morbidity and prolonged intensive care unit (ICU) stay. This study aimed to evaluate the incidence of reintubation and to identify the independent risk factors in this patient population.

METHODS: A retrospective analysis was performed across three tertiary centers between January 1, 2023, and January 1, 2025. Pediatric patients undergoing congenital heart surgery and monitored in the cardiac ICU were included. Demographic characteristics, operative details, and intensive care parameters were extracted from medical records. Reintubation was defined as the need for reintubation within 72 hours following initial extubation. Statistical analyses were conducted to determine predictors of reintubation.

RESULTS: Among 4.000 pediatric cardiac surgery patients, the reintubation rate was 4%, with most events occurring within 24 hours. In a matched cohort of 320 patients, reintubated patients more frequently had airway anomalies, genetic syndromes, newborn status, higher surgical complexity, and technical performance score (TPS)-3 scores. They also experienced longer mechanical ventilation, prolonged ICU and hospital stays. Multivariable analysis showed independent associations between reintubation and airway anomalies, genetic syndromes, newborn status, risk adjustment for congenital heart surgery-1 ≥4, TPS-3, pre-extubation extracorporeal membrane oxygenation support, diaphragm paralysis or vocal cord dysfunction, and sternal closure ≥2 days. Mortality did not differ between groups.

CONCLUSION: The incidence of reintubation after pediatric cardiac surgery remains relatively high, with multifactorial underlying causes. The identification of these potential risk factors may facilitate the detection of high-risk patients following cardiac surgery and contribute to improved clinical outcomes by ensuring a more cautious approach to extubation in these groups.

articles.title: Serum creatinine as both yardstick and predictor: reading chronic kidney disease in the global CLEARED cohort.
Relationship between serum potassium concentration, NT-pro-BNP, and risk of MACE in elderly patients with chronic heart failure.
articles.journal: Turk gogus kalp damar cerrahisi dergisi
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: This study aimed to investigate the association between serum potassium concentration, N-terminal pro-B-type natriuretic peptide (NT-pro-BNP) levels, and short-term major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE) in elderly patients with chronic heart failure (CHF) after percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI), and to evaluate their predictive value.

METHODS: General clinical characteristics, echocardiographic parameters, and laboratory indices were collected from 124 enrolled patients. All patients were followed for 3 months beginning immediately after PCI, encompassing both the in-hospital and post-discharge periods. According to the occurrence of MACE (defined as cardiovascular death, non-fatal myocardial infarction, stroke, or rehospitalization due to worsening heart failure) during follow-up, patients were categorized into a MACE group (n=44) and a non-MACE group (n=80). Multivariate logistic regression analysis was performed to identify independent factors associated with MACE. Restricted cubic spline (RCS) analysis was used to evaluate the dose-response relationships between serum potassium concentration, NT-pro-BNP levels, and MACE risk. Receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curve analysis was conducted to assess the predictive performance of each indicator individually and in combination.

RESULTS: Multivariate logistic regression analysis demonstrated that each natural log-unit increase in NT-pro-BNP (corresponding to an approximately 2.72-fold increase in NT-pro-BNP concentration) was an independent risk factor for MACE (odds ratio [OR] =1.27), whereas each 0.1 mmol/L increase in serum potassium concentration was independently associated with a lower risk of MACE (OR =0.82). RCS analysis revealed a non-linear inverse association between serum potassium concentration and MACE risk, whereas NT-pro-BNP levels showed a significant positive association with MACE risk. The area under the ROC curve for the combined assessment of serum potassium and NT-pro-BNP was 0.73, which was significantly greater than that of either biomarker alone.

CONCLUSION: Hypokalemia and elevated NT-pro-BNP levels are closely associated with an increased short-term risk of MACE in elderly patients with CHF. The combined assessment of these two indicators may provide clinical value for the early identification of high-risk patients.

articles.title: Interhospital transfer dynamics in foreign body aspiration: Age-stratified nationwide retrospective cohort study.
articles.journal: Turk gogus kalp damar cerrahisi dergisi
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Foreign body aspiration (FBA) is an acute clinical emergency that is particularly common in the pediatric population and, if not managed promptly, can lead to serious morbidity and mortality across all age groups. The need for bronchoscopy, intensive care capabilities, and experienced teams often makes interhospital transfer unavoidable. This study aimed to evaluate the transfer dynamics of patients transferred due to FBA and to identify potential differences among age groups.

METHODS: In this retrospective cohort nationwide study, patients who underwent interhospital transfer due to FBA across Türkiye between 2022 and 2024 were included. Patients were stratified into three age groups: Pediatric (0-17 years), adult (≥18 years), and geriatric (≥65 years). The primary variables analyzed included transfer distance, transfer timing (working hours vs. off-hours), transfer type (intra-provincial vs. inter-provincial), and transfer mode (ground vs. air ambulance).

RESULTS: A total of 2.816 patients were analyzed, including 1.135 (40.3%) females and 1.681 (59.7%) males. The median age was three years (12, 0-97). Pediatric patients were more frequently transferred to out-of-province centers compared to adults (odds ratio [OR] 1.90; 95% confidence interval [Cl]: 1.44-2.52; p<0.001) and had significantly longer transfer distances (p<0.001). In comparisons with other age groups, geriatric patients had higher rates of intra-provincial transfers (OR =1.65; 95% Cl: 1.08-2.51; p=0.013) and shorter transfer distances (p=0.010). However, when directly compared with pediatric patients, geriatric patients were more frequently transferred out of province (OR 1.74; 95% CI 1.18-2.57; p=0.006) and over longer di stances (p=0.004).

CONCLUSION: Age groups have a significant impact on the type and distance of interhospital transfers in FBA cases. In contrast, the timing of transfer and mode of transportation do not differ significantly by age.

articles.title: The effects of revascularization of lower extremity arterial disease on cardiac diastolic functions.
articles.journal: Turk gogus kalp damar cerrahisi dergisi
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Lower extremity arterial disease (LEAD) is a systemic atherosclerotic condition associated with increased arterial stiffness, impaired ventricular-arterial coupling, and a higher prevalence of left ventricular diastolic dysfunction (LVDD). Although endovascular revascularization improves limb perfusion, its early effects on echocardiographic indices of LVDD function and their clinical significance remain unclear. This study aimed to evaluate early changes in selected echocardiographic indices of LVDD function following successful revascularization in patients with LEAD.

METHODS: This prospective single-center study included 74 patients who underwent endovascular revascularization for aortoiliac or femoropopliteal disease. Transthoracic echocardiography was performed 24-48 hours before and 48-120 hours after the intervention. Diastolic indices, including e' velocity, E/e' ratio, isovolumetric relaxation time (IVRT), and IVRT/TE-e' ratio, were measured according to American Society of Echocardiography/EACVI guidelines. Longitudinal changes were analyzed using linear mixed-effects models incorporating lesion location and lesion laterality as covariates.

RESULTS: Statistically significant early changes were observed in selected diastolic parameters following revascularization. Mitral annular e' velocity increased from 7.91±2.43 to 8.69±2.35 cm/s (p=0.036), while the E/e' ratio decreased from 8.97±2.44 to 7.53±2.27 (p<0.001). IVRT (p=0.029) and the IVRT/TE-e' ratio (p=0.018) also decreased significantly. No changes were observed in blood pressure, heart rate, or left ventricular systolic function. Lesion location did not influence changes in e' velocity or E/e' ratio; however, aortoiliac disease was associated with a greater reduction in the IVRT/TE-e' ratio (p=0.021). Lesion laterality did not affect diastolic outcomes.

CONCLUSION: Successful endovascular revascularization in patients with LEAD was associated with early changes in selected echocardiographic indices of LVDD. The clinical significance of these changes and whether they translate into long-term outcomes warrant further investigation.

articles.title: Applying Lifestyle Medicine to Improve Health Outcomes in People With Intellectual and Developmental Disabilities.
articles.abstract: Individuals with intellectual and developmental disabilities (I/DD) and autism spectrum disorder experience disproportionately high rates of chronic disease, often exacerbated by systemic care barriers. Despite these concerns, interventions for this population rarely target overall health and wellness and often rely on practices that can contribute to poor health outcomes. This retrospective review includes data collected at The Center for Discovery, a residential care program for people with severe and complex disabilities. This analysis evaluates health outcomes among 295 adults with I/DD, including autism, who received a comprehensive lifestyle medicine intervention. Prevalence rates of chronic conditions among those receiving the intervention were compared to national and New York State disability benchmarks. Results suggest an association with substantially lower prevalence of key conditions, including obesity, diabetes, and hypertension, with a median risk ratio of 0.325 (range: 0.23-0.76) compared to U.S. population benchmarks. These findings suggest that participation in an integrated lifestyle medicine model, SynergE6® Healthspan Model, could be associated with lower chronic disease prevalence among adults with I/DD. Because this was a retrospective observational study using external benchmark comparisons, prospective controlled studies are needed to determine whether these associations are causal.

articles.title: Where Eastern Medicine Meets Western Medicine: A World Review of the Management of Chronic Cough.
articles.journal: World journal of otorhinolaryngology - head and neck surgery
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: To summarize current Western and Eastern approaches to the evaluation and management of chronic cough, with particular emphasis on etiology-directed therapy, cough hypersensitivity, behavioral interventions, neuromodulators, procedural treatments, and traditional remedies.

METHODS: A literature search of PubMed, Web of Science, CNKI, and Ovid Medline was conducted on February 1, 2024. Adults with chronic cough lasting at least 8 weeks were eligible. Pediatric studies, studies involving immunocompromised patients, smokers or patients with lung cancer, animal studies, and non-English or non-Mandarin publications were excluded. Because of substantial heterogeneity in etiologies, interventions, study designs, and outcome measures, findings were synthesized narratively rather than quantitatively. Twenty-three primary studies were included in the final narrative synthesis.

RESULTS: Chronic cough commonly reflects cough hypersensitivity involving vagal sensory pathways and receptors including TRPV1, TRPA1, and P2X3. Common clinical contributors included upper airway cough syndrome, gastro-esophageal reflux disease, and cough-variant asthma. Management was most appropriately organized as a stepwise approach involving identification and treatment of the underlying cause, behavioral cough suppression therapy, and selected pharmacological treatment. Gabapentin and P2X3 antagonists may benefit refractory cough, although adverse effects and limited long-term data remain important limitations. Superior laryngeal nerve block and antireflux surgery may be considered in carefully selected patients. Acupuncture and selected traditional preparations may provide adjunctive benefit, but the evidence remains heterogeneous and should not replace standard evaluation or treatment.

CONCLUSION: Chronic cough should be managed using a personalized, stepwise strategy that combines etiology-directed treatment with interventions targeting cough hypersensitivity. Traditional therapies may have a complementary role, but further well-designed comparative studies are required.

articles.title: Systemic inflammation in optic neuropathies: comparative insights from hematological and composite indices.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: To compare complete blood count (CBC)-derived inflammatory indices among patients with multiple sclerosis-associated optic neuritis (MS-ON), non-arteritic anterior ischemic optic neuropathy (NAION), idiopathic intracranial hypertension-related optic neuropathy (IIH-ON), and healthy controls, while accounting for demographic confounding.

METHODS: This retrospective study included 135 participants: 36 patients with MS-ON, 29 with NAION, 34 with IIH-ON, and 36 healthy controls. Six composite inflammatory indices, neutrophil-to-lymphocyte ratio (NLR), platelet-to-lymphocyte ratio (PLR), systemic immune-inflammation index (SII), systemic inflammation response index (SIRI), pan-immune-inflammation value (PIV), and hemoglobin-albumin-lymphocyte-platelet (HALP) score, were calculated from routine laboratory measurements obtained at diagnosis before treatment. Log-transformed indices were compared using analysis of covariance adjusted for age and sex. False discovery rate correction was applied across the six indices. Receiver operating characteristic (ROC) analysis was performed for indices showing significant adjusted group effects.

RESULTS: Significant differences in age and sex distribution were observed among the groups. After adjustment for age and sex, overall group effects remained for NLR (p = 0.008) and SIRI (p = 0.033), although only NLR remained significant after false discovery rate correction (q = 0.047). Bonferroni-adjusted pairwise comparisons demonstrated higher NLR in MS-ON than in healthy controls (adjusted geometric means 2.83 vs. 1.80, p = 0.005). NLR discriminated MS-ON from controls with an area under the ROC curve (AUC) of 0.681 (95% CI, 0.554-0.807), while SIRI showed a comparable AUC of 0.661 (95% CI, 0.535-0.787). Among conventional hematological parameters, red cell distribution width remained elevated in IIH-ON, whereas serum albumin remained lower in MS-ON and IIH-ON after adjustment.

CONCLUSIONS: In the primary analysis, NLR was the only index that retained significance after adjustment for age, sex, and multiple testing, with higher values in MS-ON than in healthy controls. The sensitivity of several other indices to robust inference and the modest ROC performance warrant cautious interpretation and prospective validation.

articles.title: Implications of Serum Transthyretin to NT-proBNP Ratio in Transthyretin Amyloid Cardiomyopathy: Insights From ATTRibute-CM.
Heterogeneous effects of donor-related risk factors in 954 pediatric liver transplantations.
articles.journal: Journal of pediatric gastroenterology and nutrition
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: Accepting a suitable donor for a child awaiting pediatric liver transplantation (pLT) is increasingly challenging. Donor-specific risk factors influence post-transplant outcomes, but evidence in pediatric patients remains inconsistent. We aimed to identify their influence on mortality and graft loss and investigate their dependence on recipient- and transplant-associated variables.

METHODS: We analyzed 954 consecutive pLT cases (1983-2024). Patient and graft survival was analyzed and correlated to donor- and graft-specific variables by univariate and multivariate regression analyses, with a subgroup analysis for time era and indication for pLT.

RESULTS: Multivariate analysis showed that patient/graft survival was significantly impaired by elevated donor creatinine (hazard ratio [HR]: 1.951/1.728, p = 0.011/0.007) and cerebrovascular cause of death (HR: 1.691/3.797, p = 0.020/<0.001). ABO-incompatible pLT negatively correlated with patient survival (HR, 2.628; p = 0.002). Prolonged cold ischemic time (HR: 2.912, p = 0.005) and donor age >50 years (HR: 1.623, p = 0.042) impaired graft survival. Living donor liver transplantation (LDLT) showed improved patient survival (HR: 0.267, p < 0.001). The impact varied clearly by era and indication, as creatinine and AB0-incompatible pLT showed a significant impact only up to 2006, while higher donor age impaired graft survival in the current era. Cold ischemic time affected graft survival only in recipients with chronic cirrhotic liver disease.

CONCLUSIONS: Our results strengthen the position of LDLT in pLT in current times of organ shortages. Newly identified donor-specific risk factors as renal impairment alongside confirmed factors, like advanced donor age, prolonged CIT and cerebrovascular disease, help to identify marginal donors. Their impact is clearly dependent on recipient and transplant conditions, which underlines the importance of individually tailored donor profiles.

articles.title: Hiding Behind the Decoy: Michaelis-Gutmann Bodies Overlooked Among BK Decoy Cells in Voided Urine From a Patient With Vaginal Malakoplakia.
The influence of loneliness & social isolation on cardiovascular risk factors: a narrative review.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Despite substantial advances in treatment and preventive medicine, heart disease remains the leading cause of morbidity and mortality worldwide. While traditional risk factors have been identified, emerging research continues to underscore the importance of social interactions.

AREAS COVERED: This review examines research on how loneliness and social isolation influence the major risk factors for heart disease. Studies from 2000 up to April 2026 were searched using PubMed, Science Direct, and Web of Science. The included research focused on loneliness and social isolation, alongside seven primary risk factors such as smoking, stress, dyslipidemia, hypertension, diabetes, obesity, and lack of physical activity, and showed that people who are lonely and socially isolated have approximately a 29% higher chance of developing heart disease. Loneliness and isolation are linked with both physiological and behavioral changes, and many of these relationships are bidirectional, creating feedback loops in which social disconnection and cardiometabolic risk reinforce one another.

EXPERT OPINION: Treating loneliness as a modifiable and deeply integrated risk factor helps patient well-being and long-term health outcomes, and supports more effective clinical care, community health, and policy planning.

articles.title: Retrospective Evaluation of the Association of Hypoalbuminemia With Acute Treatment Outcomes in Methicillin-Susceptible Staphylococcus Aureus Bacteremia.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Cefazolin and antistaphylococcal penicillins (ASP) are first-line agents for methicillin-susceptible Staphylococcus aureus (MSSA) bacteremia. These agents are substantially protein-bound; however, scant data exist evaluating the impact of hypoalbuminemia on microbiologic and patient outcomes for this indication.

OBJECTIVE: The purpose of this study was to assess whether hypoalbuminemia is associated with delayed blood culture clearance in patients with MSSA bacteremia being treated with cefazolin or ASPs as definitive therapy.

METHODS: This retrospective cohort study included patients admitted for MSSA bacteremia between January 1, 2006 and December 31, 2019, with a serum albumin obtained between the date of an initial positive blood culture result and 72 hours following initiation of definitive therapy with cefazolin or an ASP. The primary outcome was the rate of persistently positive blood cultures, defined as failure to clear blood cultures within 72 hours of definitive therapy initiation. Patients with a serum albumin ≤2.5 g/dL were compared with those with an albumin >2.5 g/dL. Propensity score weighting was used to account for differences in cohort characteristics.

RESULTS: A total of 123 patients were included. After propensity score weighting, patients with hypoalbuminemia had a higher rate of persistently positive blood cultures, both in the overall cohort (45.0% vs 13.2%, P < .001) and in the subgroups of cefazolin (33.0% vs 9.1%, P = .015) and ASP (60.1% vs 18.3%, P = .001) when analyzed separately. After propensity weighting in the combined cohort, the length of stay was longer in the hypoalbuminemic cohort, but no differences in mortality were observed.

CONCLUSIONS AND RELEVANCE: Hypoalbuminemia was associated with a delayed 72-hour blood culture clearance in patients with MSSA bacteremia treated with either cefazolin or ASPs.

articles.title: When Gratitude Outlasts Cure: A Reflection from a Chinese Neonatal Intensive Care Unit.
Albumin Orchestrates Type-I ROS Conversion for Efficient Intracellular Bacterial Clearance.
articles.abstract: Type-I photosensitization addresses the dilemma of intracellular bacterial hypoxia-induced photodynamic therapeutic (PDT) inefficacy, yet precise targeting and eradicating sequestered pathogens remains a formidable challenge. Herein, we engineer an albumin-based photodynamic conversion nanoparticles integrating target-specific recognition with controlled antibacterial functions to precisely eliminate intracellular pathogens and restore infected cell activity. Mechanistic studies reveal a vertically-crossed conformation that promotes intramolecular electron transfer and charge separation, redirecting photosensitizer (PS) reactivity toward type-I reactive oxygen species (ROS) generation. Electron-rich albumin further enhances cationic PS+• recycling, photostability, and O2 -• production, while its selective cytoplasmic delivery via receptor/charge interactions enables preferential accumulation in intracellular bacteria, with reduced off-target organelle engagement. We demonstrate application in S. aureus-infected sepsis showing high type-I ROS levels for antibacterial function from the nanoparticles to restore redox and immune homeostasis without noticeable toxicity. This work pioneers a conformationally-gated ROS conversion approach for eliminating intracellular bacterial infections, merging mechanistic precision with therapeutic potential for clinical sepsis management.

articles.title: Minimally Invasive Inguinal Hernia Repair in Elderly Patients Over 70 Years: Postoperative Outcomes and Complications.
articles.journal: Journal of laparoendoscopic & advanced surgical techniques. Part A
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Minimally invasive surgery (MIS) for inguinal hernia repair offers postoperative advantages over conventional techniques and is considered the gold standard. As the population ages, concerns regarding comorbidities and anesthetic risks may limit the use of MIS in patients over 70 years.

OBJECTIVE: To compare postoperative outcomes after elective MIS inguinal hernia repair between patients aged ≥70 and <70 years.

METHODS: Retrospective analysis of a prospectively maintained database including 200 patients, of whom 57 were elderly (≥70 years). Three of the initial 203 patients were excluded because they underwent open repair: two (<1%) due to anesthetic contraindications associated with age and comorbidities, and one because of a previous radical prostatectomy and pelvic radiotherapy. Outcomes included surgical technique, operative time, hospital stay, postoperative pain assessed using the Numeric Pain Rating Scale (NPRS), and complications (seroma, ecchymosis, and surgical site infection). Assessments were performed immediately after surgery, at 7, 30, and 90 days, and at 6 and 12 months.

RESULTS: Elderly patients had a longer mean operative time (83.4 ± 56.0 versus 65.7 ± 36.1 minutes; P = .049). However, after excluding associated procedures (n = 183), the difference was no longer significant (71.8 ± 43.6 versus 66.3 ± 35.7 minutes; P = .39). Postoperative complication rates were similar between groups. Elderly patients reported lower NPRS scores both immediately after surgery (0.99 versus 1.4; P = .008) and at 30 days (0.17 versus 0.38; P = .007). Hospital stay was comparable between groups.

CONCLUSION: MIS inguinal hernia repair, including laparoscopic and robotic approaches, appears safe and effective in elderly patients, even in the presence of significant comorbidities. Complication rates and hospital stay were comparable between age groups, while elderly patients reported lower postoperative pain scores. Age alone should not be considered a contraindication to minimally invasive inguinal hernia repair.

articles.title: Assessing the quality of end-of-life care in systemic sclerosis.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Systemic sclerosis (SSc) is a rare autoimmune disease with the highest mortality among rheumatic diseases, yet little is known about the quality of end-of-life care in SSc.

AIMS: To evaluate end-of-life care in SSc against the Australian National Consensus Statement's Essential Elements for high-quality end-of-life care and compare care between palliative care unit (PCU) and non-PCU deaths.

METHODS: This retrospective single-centre study included adults with SSc who died between 2013 and 2023 at a tertiary SSc referral centre. Terminal admission records for expected deaths were mapped to the National Consensus domains. Fisher exact and Mann-Whitney U tests compared PCU and non-PCU deaths.

RESULTS: Thirty-three patients died. Six unexpected deaths were excluded, leaving 15 PCU and 12 non-PCU deaths. Multidisciplinary involvement was extensive, particularly from rheumatology and allied health. Palliative care engagement was common, goals of care were frequently reviewed and communication about dying with next-of-kin occurred in most cases. Patients dying outside the PCU had lower rates of documented recognition of dying, significantly greater intensive care involvement and more frequent medical emergency team calls. They also received more potentially non-beneficial investigations and treatments during the final 48 h of life and incurred substantially higher terminal admission costs.

CONCLUSION: End-of-life care in SSc was broadly consistent with the National Consensus standards, identifying strong rheumatology involvement, multidisciplinary care and frequent palliative care referral. However, differences in care according to site of death highlight opportunities to increase proactive palliative care involvement and regular review of goals of care to ensure high-quality end-of-life care across all settings.

articles.title: Clinical Prediction Models in Elderly Acute Coronary Syndrome: A Bibliometric Analysis of Research Hotspots.
articles.abstract: Rapid global aging has intensified the cardiovascular disease burden, making clinical prediction models (CPMs) crucial for risk stratification and management of elderly patients with acute coronary syndrome (ACS), yet the knowledge structure of this field remains insufficiently characterized. Literature published up to November 14, 2025, was retrieved from the Web of Science Core Collection, and Bibliometrix, VOSviewer, and CiteSpace were used to analyze annual publication trends, core contributors, collaboration networks, cocited references, and keyword clusters. A total of 3,899 articles were included. From 2007 to 2025, annual publications increased from 98 to 281, with an average annual growth rate of 6.03%, peaking at 303 articles in 2022. The United States was the most productive country (1,419 articles), Harvard Medical School the leading institution (130 articles), and Krumholz HM the most prolific author (52 articles). Research hotspots concentrated on mortality and prognostic risk prediction, models associated with clinical interventions (particularly those related to percutaneous coronary intervention), and machine learning applications; since 2018, the research frontier has evolved toward intelligent technologies. Research on CPMs in elderly ACS thus shows stable and continuous growth, with a shift from traditional statistical methods toward intelligent and individualized approaches. Future priorities include externally validated models incorporating geriatric-specific variables, multicenter validation in real-world settings, and standardized comparisons of modeling approaches. The mapped evidence also informs regenerative cardiology, in which validated prediction models are needed to select elderly patients for emerging tissue engineering and regenerative interventions. Bibliometric mapping characterizes publication patterns and knowledge structures but cannot by itself establish model quality or clinical benefit.

articles.title: A Machine Learning-Based Fall Risk Prediction Model for Middle-Aged and Older Adults with Comorbid Cardiovascular Disease and Arthritis: Development and Geographic Split-Sample Validation.
articles.abstract: Falls impose a major public health burden on middle-aged and older adults. Coexisting cardiovascular disease (CVD) and arthritis further increases fall risk, yet targeted prediction models remain scarce, especially in Chinese populations. We analyzed 633 China Health and Retirement Longitudinal Study participants aged ≥45 years with comorbid CVD and arthritis at the 2015 baseline. Seven predictors were selected through univariate analysis, LASSO logistic regression (LR), and clinical review. Eight machine-learning algorithms were compared. Among models with an area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) ≥0.72, the model with the highest specificity was preferred to reduce false-positive referrals. A geographically defined holdout group (n = 110) from different provincial-code regions, but within the same CHARLS source population, was treated as a geographic split-sample rather than independent external validation. Performance was assessed using AUC, sensitivity, specificity, positive predictive value (PPV), negative predictive value (NPV), F1-score, calibration, decision-curve analysis, precision-recall curves, and SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP). During cumulative follow-up, 296 participants (46.8%) reported at least one fall. Random forest (RF) and LR achieved similar internal-validation AUCs (0.730 vs. 0.729); RF was selected because of higher specificity. Internally, RF showed 87.5% specificity, 37.7% sensitivity, 70.3% PPV, 64.2% NPV, and an F1-score of 0.491. Its AUC in the geographic holdout sample was 0.735. Despite similar AUCs, sensitivity and specificity differed substantially between samples, suggesting limited regional stability of the fixed threshold. SHAP identified fall history, ankle pain, activities of daily living impairment, and sleep duration as the most influential predictors. The RF model showed moderate discrimination and a conservative, high-specificity profile. However, its low internal sensitivity means it should not be used alone to rule out falls or as a diagnostic tool. Pending independent validation and regional threshold calibration, it may serve only as adjunctive stratification within a stepped assessment pathway and should not replace routine clinical fall-risk screening.

articles.title: Baby-Friendly Hospital Initiative and Breastfeeding Outcomes Across Social Determinants of Health in Oklahoma, USA: A Secondary Data Analysis.
articles.journal: Breastfeeding medicine : the official journal of the Academy of Breastfeeding Medicine
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Breastfeeding improves maternal and infant health, reducing risks of cancer, diabetes, cardiovascular disease, and infant mortality. Despite national gains in breastfeeding initiation, disparities persist in exclusivity and duration across social determinants of health (SDOH). The Baby-Friendly Hospital Initiative (BFHI) promotes evidence-based maternity care practices to support breastfeeding, yet its effectiveness across diverse populations remains unclear.

PURPOSE: This study examined whether BFHI designation is associated with breastfeeding outcomes including initiation, exclusive breastfeeding at 8 weeks, and any breastfeeding at 8 weeks among Oklahoma mothers who delivered between 2016 and 2018, and whether these associations differ across SDOH including race, ethnicity, household income, educational attainment, marital status, maternal age, parity, and geographic location.

METHODS: A retrospective secondary analysis of linked Oklahoma Pregnancy Risk Assessment Monitoring System and birth certificate data (2016-2018; N = 4,234) was conducted. Weighted logistic regression estimated associations between BFHI designation and breastfeeding outcomes, stratified by SDOH, and adjusted for demographic and socioeconomic factors.

RESULTS: BFHI designation at birth facility was associated with higher odds of initiation among primiparous mothers (adjusted odds ratio [aOR] = 1.89, 95% confidence interval [CI]: [0.98-3.64]), Native American mothers (aOR = 1.43, 95% CI: [0.95-2.15]), and unmarried mothers (aOR = 1.34, 95% CI: [0.89-2.03]). Among mothers with moderate household income ($24,001-$48,000), BFHI designation was associated with significantly greater odds of exclusive breastfeeding at 8 weeks (aOR = 1.85, 95% CI: [1.19-2.89]); a similar, nonsignificant pattern was observed for any breastfeeding at 8 weeks (aOR = 1.63, 95% CI: [0.99-2.70]).

CONCLUSIONS: BFHI demonstrates differential effects across SDOH, benefiting first-time and moderate-income mothers but not Black mothers. Culturally responsive nursing care and tailored interventions are needed to achieve breastfeeding equity.

articles.title: A cross-sectional analysis of cardiometabolic and lifestyle-related profiles in men living with HIV in Japan using linked nationwide claims and health checkup data.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: To compare objectively measured cardiometabolic health between people living with HIV (PLWH) and individuals without HIV using nationwide health checkup data linked to administrative claims, thereby partially mitigating surveillance bias associated with routine HIV care.

METHODS: We conducted a cross-sectional matched analysis using the JMDC database, which links administrative claims with annual health checkup data. Men with HIV receiving antiretroviral therapy (ART) and men without HIV who underwent health checkups between 2017 and 2023 were included. PLWH were exact-matched 1:5 to individuals without HIV by age and calendar year. Cardiometabolic outcomes included hypertension, diabetes mellitus, dyslipidaemia and BMI, defined using treatment information and objectively measured clinical parameters. Conditional logistic regression and matched-set fixed-effects linear regression were used.

RESULTS: We included 2596 PLWH and 12 980 matched individuals without HIV (median age 45.0 years [IQR 37.0-51.0]). PLWH were more likely to receive treatment for hypertension, diabetes mellitus and dyslipidaemia, whereas measured systolic blood pressure, HbA1c and LDL-C were comparable to or lower than those in individuals without HIV. HIV infection was not independently associated with hypertension (aOR 0.95, 95% CI 0.82-1.09) or diabetes mellitus (aOR 1.00, 0.82-1.22) but was associated with dyslipidaemia (aOR 1.22, 1.08-1.39) and slightly higher BMI (adjusted mean difference 0.28 kg/m2, 0.02-0.55).

CONCLUSIONS: Among men receiving contemporary HIV care in Japan, HIV infection was associated with modest differences in BMI and dyslipidaemia but not with hypertension or diabetes mellitus.

articles.title: Adaptation of suspension Vero cells to commercially available cell culture media and enhanced production of vaccine-strain mumps virus.
articles.abstract: Vero cells (referred to as "Vero" henceforth) are a commonly used host for the production of a wide variety of vaccines, but due in part to the typically anchorage-dependent nature of the cells, Vero cells also pose multiple challenges during process development, scale-up, and commercialization. The adaptation of Vero to proliferate in a serum-free suspension culture while remaining non-tumorigenic can be a challenging endeavor, and where successful, has often utilized undisclosed and/or complex custom-designed medium formulations. Additional and expanded options for commercially available serum-free media that can support the robust expansion of suspension-adapted Vero cells for viral vaccine manufacturing would be a significant advantage for increasing the industrial adoption of suspension Vero, as virus production can also be highly medium-dependent and sensitive. In this work, we have successfully transitioned suspension-adapted Vero cells from a proprietary medium to a commercially-available base medium (ExCell VPRO) with supplementation of additional commercially-available components, and subsequently infected the resulting ExCell VPRO cell bank lineage with an attenuated vaccine strain Mumps virus. Like many suspension cell line media formulations, off-the-shelf commercially available ExCell VPRO medium contains dextran sulfate, which serves to minimize cell clumping, but is also well-known to directly impact the infectivity of some viruses. Unexpectedly, we have observed that the presence of dextran sulfate in the infection medium increased both culture longevity and infectious virus titers for attenuated Mumps, potentially eliminating the need for a medium exchange between cell growth and infection for a more streamlined and easily scalable attenuated Mumps virus production process.

articles.title: Nutrient Sensing and Growth Control in Plasmodium: Beyond mTOR Signaling.
articles.abstract: The mechanistic target of rapamycin (mTOR) signaling pathway is a central regulator of nutrient sensing, metabolism, growth, and stress adaptation in most eukaryotes. Malaria parasites of the genus Plasmodium, however, lack identifiable orthologues of mTOR kinase and its associated signaling complexes, raising the question of how these organisms coordinate environmental sensing with developmental progression and proliferation. Here, we discuss emerging evidence suggesting that Plasmodium has evolutionarily replaced the canonical mTOR signaling axis with a distributed regulatory architecture composed of parasite-specific nutrient sensors, kinase-based signaling pathways, translational repression mechanisms, and unconventional autophagy processes. Components such as KIN, PI3K, eIF2α kinases, eIF4E-interacting protein DOZI, and Maf1 collectively preserve many hallmark outputs of mTOR signaling, including metabolic adaptation, stress tolerance, developmental plasticity, and reversible quiescence. In addition, malaria parasites interact with host mTOR pathways during infection, potentially exploiting host-derived anabolic signaling environments to support intracellular development. These findings suggest that Plasmodium exemplifies an extreme case of signaling plasticity in eukaryotic evolution, demonstrating how essential mTOR-associated functions can be maintained despite the apparent loss of the pathway itself.

articles.title: Clinical outcomes after intravenous thrombolysis for acute ischemic stroke in low- and middle-income countries: a pooled analysis of 67,917 patients and systematic review.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Stroke is a leading cause of disability and mortality worldwide. Patients in low- and middle-income countries (LMICs) are disproportionately affected, yet thrombolysis outcomes in these settings are underexplored.

METHODS: We searched PubMed, Embase, Scopus, Web of Science, and Global Index Medicus through April 2024. Outcomes were 90-day functional independence (mRS 0-2), symptomatic intracerebral hemorrhage (sICH), and 90-day mortality. Risk of bias used Cochrane RoB 2 and ROBINS-I; random-effects meta-analyses estimated pooled proportions with I2.

RESULTS: Of 1,865 records screened, 79 studies (67,917 patients; 24 countries) were included. Most used alteplase; others examined tenecteplase, recombinant prourokinase, or reteplase; eight compared low- vs standard-dose alteplase. Pooled estimates were functional independence 63% (95% CI, 58-67), sICH 4% (95% CI, 3-5), and mortality 8% (95% CI, 6-10). Functional independence was similar across continents; sICH was lowest in Asia, mortality lowest in Africa. Heterogeneity was high, partly explained by baseline stroke severity and study size. Overall risk of bias was low to moderate.

CONCLUSIONS: Standard-dose thrombolysis within 4.5 hours in LMICs shows efficacy and safety comparable to reports from high-income countries, with regional variation in safety and mortality. These results support broader implementation of thrombolysis in resource-limited settings to reduce global stroke disparities.

articles.title: Blanking Period after Atrial Fibrillation Catheter Ablation: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Atrial arrhythmias that recur within the first 3 months after atrial fibrillation (AF) catheter ablation are conventionally attributed to a "blanking period" and not classified as procedural failure. Accumulating evidence suggests that such early recurrences of atrial tachyarrhythmias (ERAT) may instead predict late recurrence, raising concern that the conventional 3-month window overestimates the duration during which recurrences are benign.

OBJECTIVE: To assess the association between ERAT during each of the first 3 months after AF catheter ablation and late recurrence of atrial tachyarrhythmias (LRAT), and whether this association differs by ablation energy source.

METHODS: We searched Ovid MEDLINE, Embase, and Web of Science without restriction on date or publication status for studies of AF catheter ablation reporting ERAT during defined intervals of the blanking period, stratified by subsequent LRAT status. Ablation energy sources included radiofrequency, cryoballoon, and pulsed field. The exposure was ERAT during the first, second, and third months after ablation, and the outcome was LRAT. Odds ratios (ORs) with 95% confidence intervals (CIs) were pooled using random-effects models.

RESULTS: Twelve studies comprising 7,751 patients (2,505 with LRAT, 5,246 without) were included. Mean follow-up was 22.0 months, mean age 60.7 years, 25.8% were women, 52.5% had paroxysmal AF, mean CHA2DS2-VASc score was 2.1, mean left atrial diameter 42.6 mm, and mean left ventricular ejection fraction 58.1%. ERAT was associated with subsequent LRAT, and the strength of this association increased across the blanking period: month 1 (12 studies; OR 1.76, 95% CI 1.01-3.08; p = 0.05), month 2 (10 studies; OR 3.46, 95% CI 2.15-5.57; p < 0.001), and month 3 (10 studies; OR 21.4, 95% CI 10.9-42.2; p < 0.001). The graded association was reproduced within the radiofrequency and cryoballoon subgroups.

CONCLUSION: ERAT was associated with subsequent LRAT throughout the blanking period, with a graded relationship that strengthened month by month and was strongest in the third month. These findings support a blanking period shorter than the conventional 3 months.

articles.title: Increased Risk of Thyrotoxicosis After COVID-19 in Adolescents and Young Adults During the Omicron-Predominant Period: A Nationwide Matched Study.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Thyroid dysfunction has been increasingly reported after the coronavirus disease 2019 (COVID-19) pandemic. To date, no population-based study has examined this association using more than 10 million matched pairs. We compared the risk of documented thyroid outcomes after COVID-19 with that after influenza during the Omicron-predominant period.

METHODS: We conducted a nationwide retrospective cohort study using the Japanese National Database of Health Insurance Claims, including patients with COVID-19 between January 2022 and March 2023, and those with influenza between September 2017 and March 2023. Individuals with pre-existing thyroid disease were excluded. After 1:1 propensity score matching, 24,173,646 pairs were analysed. Database-recorded outcomes assessed within 90 days of documented COVID-19 infection included diagnoses of thyrotoxicosis, hypothyroidism and subacute thyroiditis, as well as initiation of antithyroid drugs (ATDs) and thyroid hormone replacement therapy (THRT).

RESULTS: Among database-recorded outcomes, COVID-19 was associated with higher risks of thyrotoxicosis diagnosis (risk ratio [RR], 1.08), hypothyroidism diagnosis (RR, 1.12), ATD initiation (RR, 1.06) and THRT initiation (RR, 1.22) than influenza, but not subacute thyroiditis diagnosis. Age-stratified analyses showed markedly higher risks in individuals aged 0-19 years for thyrotoxicosis diagnosis (RR, 1.38) and ATD initiation (RR, 1.77).

CONCLUSIONS: In this nationwide cohort, COVID-19 was associated with higher risks of database-recorded diagnoses of thyrotoxicosis and hypothyroidism than influenza during the Omicron-predominant period. The strongest association was observed for thyrotoxicosis diagnosis and ATD initiation in younger individuals, underscoring the importance of post-COVID-19 thyroid monitoring in adolescents and young adults.

articles.title: How does pre-stroke physical activity influence physical activity one year after minor stroke, and what role does cognitive impairment play?
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To examine the association between pre-stroke physical activity and physical activity levels 12 months after stroke, and to explore whether cognitive impairment modifies this association.

METHODS: This study was a secondary analysis of data from a prospective cohort study of 100 patients with stroke at Aarhus University Hospital. Physical activity was assessed using the Physical Activity Scale for the Elderly, and cognitive function was measured using the Repeatable Battery for the Assessment of Neuropsychological Status. Logistic regression analyses were performed to examine associations between pre- and post-stroke physical activity, adjusting for relevant covariates.

RESULTS: Low pre-stroke physical activity had significantly higher odds of low physical activity 12-months post-stroke (OR = 5.81, 95% CI: 1.61-24.0, p = 0.010). The estimated odds ratio for effect modification by cognitive impairment was 7.44 (95% CI: 0.81-89.9, p = 0.092), although the wide confidence interval indicates substantial uncertainty.

CONCLUSIONS: Pre-stroke PA was associated with PA levels 12 months post-stroke in individuals with mild stroke. Assessing pre-stroke PA may help identify patients at risk of persistent inactivity and guide personalized rehabilitation. The modifying role of cognitive impairment remains inconclusive and warrants further investigation.

articles.title: Association Between Interhospital Transfer, Readmission, and Inpatient Mortality Among Older Adults.
articles.journal: Journal of the American Geriatrics Society
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Interhospital transfer (IHT) is a key strategy for providing access to specialty care; however, it is associated with multiple adverse outcomes, including prolonged length of stay, increased risk of inpatient mortality, and reduced rates of discharge home, particularly among older adults. We hypothesized that older patients who experience IHT would have a higher rate of acute-care hospital readmissions compared to older adults who do not experience IHT.

METHODS: We used the Healthcare Cost and Utilization Project's 2019 National Readmissions Database to identify adults 65+ who had and had not undergone IHT. We used unadjusted and adjusted logistic regression stratified by region, clustered by hospital and weighted by individual to measure the association between IHT and the odds of readmission and in-hospital mortality.

RESULTS: Of the 11,836,556 older adults included in the weighted analysis, 0.9% experienced IHT. After adjusting for confounders including mortality risk, risk of readmission, admitting service, insurer, procedure characteristics, and others, IHT was associated with increased readmission rates (AOR 1.09, 95% CI: 1.01-1.18) and with increased risk of in-hospital mortality (AOR 1.91, 95% CI: 1.81-2.02). In a sensitivity analysis, odds of readmission within 30 days were 29% higher for older adults who had undergone IHT compared to those who had not (AOR 1.29, 95% CI: 1.19-1.40). All comparisons are p < 0.001.

CONCLUSION: IHT is associated with increased readmission and mortality risk among older adults. These findings add to a burgeoning evidence base suggesting that IHT is associated with many long-term risks to older adults. Further research is needed to characterize the underlying drivers of these findings and to develop evidence-based practices to improve IHT processes for older adults.

articles.title: Newly Recorded Cardiometabolic Diagnoses in Adolescents With Hidradenitis Suppurativa.
Chronic alanine aminotransferase elevation in people with HIV: Time trends over 22 years and genetic predisposition.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Chronic elevation of alanine aminotransferase (cALT) is common in people with HIV. Published reports on cALT prevalence time trends have not been uniform. It is unknown whether genetic background is associated with cALT in people with HIV.

METHODS: cALT was defined as ALT levels (male, >50 U/L, female, >35 U/L) at ≥2 consecutive, 6-monthly per protocol Swiss HIV Cohort Study (SHCS) visits. We calculated cALT prevalence plus trends in time-updated clinical and HIV-related cALT risk factors per calendar year in SHCS participants without viral hepatitis co-infection. In cALT cases and matched controls, we obtained uni- and multivariable odds ratios (ORs) for cALT, adjusting additionally for a polygenic risk score (PGS) associated with transaminase levels in the general population.

RESULTS: Between 2002 and 2023, 8'909 SHCS participants contributed 203'832 ALT values obtained per protocol, and 8'414 cALT events occurred. The yearly cALT prevalence increased significantly (p < 0.001) from 7.5% (95% confidence interval, 6.3%-8.9%) in 2002 to the highest level of 10.1% (9.1%-11.1%) in 2005, followed by a significant (p < 0.001) decline to 5.3% (4.8%-5.9%) in 2018, with stable rates thereafter (p = 0.280). An increased multivariable cALT-OR was noted for obesity (OR = 2.84; 1.99-4.07), for 6-12-month exposure to non-nucleoside reverse transcriptase inhibitors (OR = 2.09; 1.09-4.03) and tenofovir disoproxil fumarate (OR = 1.99; 1.15-3.46). Participants with unfavourable genetic background (top vs. bottom quintile of PGS) had a multivariable-adjusted cALT-OR of 4.44 (3.09-6.39).

CONCLUSION: cALT prevalence has decreased by almost half in people with HIV in Switzerland since 2005. Unfavourable genetic background is a strong independent risk factor for cALT.

articles.title: Hepatic Lipid Stress Drives Metabolic Dysfunction-Associated Steatohepatitis Progression through FTO O-GlcNAcylation-Induced m6A Demethylation of HRAS.
articles.abstract: Metabolic dysfunction-associated steatohepatitis (MASH) is driven by nutrient stress through incompletely defined epigenetic mechanisms. This study demonstrates that lipid stress activates the hexosamine biosynthesis pathway (HBP), elevating O-linked β-N-acetylglucosamine (O-GlcNAc) modification of the N6-methyladenosine (m6A) demethylase fat mass and obesity-associated protein (FTO) at Ser195. This post-translational modification recruits the deubiquitinase ubiquitin-specific peptidase 20 (USP20), displaces the E3 ligase F-box and WD repeat domain containing 7 (FBXW7), and enhances FTO protein stability and m6A demethylase activity. O-GlcNAc-dependent FTO activation removes m6A from Harvey rat sarcoma viral oncogene homolog (HRAS) mRNA, evades YTH N6‑methyladenosine RNA binding protein 2 (YTHDF2)‑mediated degradation, and prolongs transcript half-life. Subsequent HRAS upregulation activates the PI3K/AKT signaling pathway, driving hepatic steatosis and inflammation. Administration of a novel cell-penetrating peptide (CPP) designed to block FTO O-GlcNAcylation at Ser195 effectively ameliorates MASH progression in vitro and in vivo. These findings establish FTO O-GlcNAcylation as a druggable metabolic-epigenetic checkpoint in MASH pathogenesis, revealing a promising therapeutic strategy for this increasingly prevalent liver disease.

articles.title: Diabetes-Associated Cognitive Impairment: Pathophysiology and Emerging Therapies.
articles.journal: Annals of clinical and translational neurology
articles.abstract: Diabetes-associated cognitive impairment (DACI) is a common yet underrecognized condition, manifesting along a spectrum from mild cognitive impairment to dementia. DACI encompasses patients who develop vascular dementia (VaD) or Alzheimer's disease (AD) with diabetes as a risk factor; however, in certain patients, particularly those lacking clear VaD or AD features, diabetes may act as a primary driver of neurodegeneration. Mechanistically, DACI can be conceptualized as a neurovascular-metabolic disorder characterized by disruption of the neurovascular unit, impaired cerebral glucose metabolism, brain insulin resistance, and chronic neuroinflammation, contributing to small vessel disease, regional brain atrophy, and accelerated brain aging. In this narrative review, we synthesize current evidence on the clinical and imaging features of DACI, outline key mechanistic pathways linking diabetes to neurodegeneration, and discuss emerging therapeutic strategies, including GLP-1 receptor agonists and SGLT2 inhibitors, with potential neuroprotective effects. Greater recognition of DACI as a neurovascular-metabolic entity may facilitate earlier identification, inform biomarker development, and guide future trials aimed at preserving cognitive function in individuals with diabetes.

articles.title: Zonation Hallmarks in Human PSC-Derived Hepatic Organoids Integrated into an Immune-Compatible Organ-on-Chip for Liver Injury Modeling.
articles.abstract: Liver metabolic zonation enables hepatocytes to carry out diverse, spatially organized functions essential for liver homeostasis and metabolism. However, in vitro recapitulation of zone-specific diversity, particularly in human pluripotent stem cell (PSC)-derived hepatocyte-like cells (HLCs), remains challenging, as these cells typically exhibit an immature phenotype. Here, we report a scalable differentiation protocol for generating 3D organoids from PSCs with defined zone 1 (z1-HLCs) or zone 3 (z3-HLCs) identities. When benchmarked against primary human hepatocytes (PHHs), these HLCs exhibit zone-specific enhanced postnatal metabolic functions. z1-HLCs reveal high albumin and urea production, whereas z3-HLCs show elevated glutamine secretion and cytochrome P450 (CYP) enzyme activity, including CYP3A4, CYP1A2, and CYP2C9. Hallmarks of functional zonation were further confirmed via proteomics, transcriptomics, metabolic assays, and oxygen consumption. z3-HLCs show increased sensitivity to acetaminophen-induced cytotoxicity and distinct immune interactions with primary monocytes. Collectively, the zonated liver organoids provide a promising platform for studying zone-specific liver metabolism, drug metabolism, toxicology, and liver disease, including liver injury.

articles.title: Prostate Cancer Patient-Derived Organoids (PDOs) as Functional Avatars for Antisense Oligonucleotide (ASO)-Based Personalized Therapy.
articles.abstract: Patient-derived tumor organoids (PDOs) closely preserve the cellular heterogeneity, histopathology, and molecular features of the original tumors, making them powerful preclinical models. Antisense oligonucleotides (ASOs) are an emerging class of precision medicines that modulate gene expression at the RNA level with high target specificity, yet their application in organoid systems remains underexplored. Here, we adapted previously described protocols to establish a biobank of prostate cancer (PC) PDOs, achieving a high initial growth success rate (>90%). Histological and molecular analyses confirmed the preservation of key tumor features. Using these models, we assessed several ASOs, with particular emphasis on OGX-427 (Apatorsen), an ASO targeting heat shock protein 27 (HSP27) that has been evaluated in phase I/II clinical trials. While OGX-427 effectively suppressed HSP27 expression and inhibited cell growth in 2D cultures, its efficacy was markedly limited in 3D organoids, likely due to extracellular matrix and structural barriers. Removing Matrigel and applying single-cell transfection overcame these barriers, achieving efficient ASO uptake, significant target protein downregulation, and robust, dose-dependent inhibition of organoid growth. These findings underscore the utility of PDOs for evaluating ASO-based therapies and their potential to accelerate precision oncology strategies for PC and other malignancies.

articles.title: Re: The Impact of Systematic Latent Tuberculosis Infection Screening in Kidney Transplant Candidates: Experience From a Single UK Transplant Center.
articles.journal: Transplant infectious disease : an official journal of the Transplantation Society

articles.title: ADHD symptoms and learning difficulties: co-occurrence and directionality from Grades 1 to 9.
articles.journal: Journal of child psychology and psychiatry, and allied disciplines
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Children with attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder (ADHD) are at increased risk of learning difficulties. This association may reflect shared risk factors, ADHD symptoms hindering learning, or learning difficulties increasing ADHD symptoms. We aimed to map rates of co-occurrence among ADHD, dyslexia, dyscalculia, and reading comprehension difficulties and to investigate directional influences between ADHD symptoms and reading fluency, arithmetic, and reading comprehension.

METHODS: Reading fluency, arithmetic, and reading comprehension were assessed longitudinally in approximately 2,000 Finnish children across Grades 1-9 (ages 7-16). Attention/hyperactivity symptoms were measured with teacher ratings (Grades 1-4) and self-reports (Grades 6-9). ADHD, dyslexia, dyscalculia, and reading comprehension difficulties were based on a 10th percentile cut-off. Directionality between ADHD symptoms and academic skills was examined using random intercept cross-lagged panel models (RI-CLPMs) to separate stable traits from time-specific states.

RESULTS: Children with a learning difficulty were 1.14-1.76 times more likely to have ADHD, whereas children with one learning difficulty were 4.32-4.62 times more likely to have another. The RI-CLPMs showed consistent autoregressive effects across all domains, indicating stable within-person variation over time. At the between-person level (i.e. trait), academic skills were negatively related to ADHD symptoms, especially those reported by teachers. At the within-person level (i.e. state), ADHD symptoms were unrelated to reading fluency and arithmetic. However, at multiple time points, cross-lagged effects emerged from ADHD symptoms to subsequent reading comprehension, indicating that elevated ADHD symptoms predicted subsequent declines in reading comprehension.

CONCLUSIONS: Learning difficulties co-occurred more frequently with each other (homotypic) than with ADHD (heterotypic co-occurrence). Both ADHD symptoms and learning difficulties showed trait-like stability. After accounting for these, ADHD symptoms were no longer linked to reading fluency or arithmetic. However, more ADHD symptoms predicted later declines in reading comprehension, likely because comprehension requires sustained attention - often impaired in children with hyperactivity and inattention.

articles.title: Long-term outcomes following modified Blalock-Taussig-Thomas shunt placement in 13 dogs with cyanotic congenital heart disease.
articles.journal: The Journal of small animal practice
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: To describe long-term outcome and owner-perceived quality of life in dogs with cyanotic congenital cardiac disease undergoing modified Blalock-Taussig-Thomas shunt procedure.

MATERIALS AND METHODS: Medical records of dogs that underwent Blalock-Taussig-Thomas shunt between 2009 and 2025 at a small animal referral hospital were retrospectively reviewed. Complications, long-term outcomes and quality of life were assessed via clinical examination and/or contact with owners or referring veterinarians.

RESULTS: Thirteen dogs were included. The predominant clinical signs were exercise intolerance, cyanosis and a heart murmur. Diagnosis included tetralogy of Fallot (n = 8), double outlet right ventricle (n = 3); tetralogy of Fallot-double outlet right ventricle spectrum (n = 1) and tetralogy of Fallot with pulmonary atresia spectrum (n = 1). All dogs survived surgery. Follow-up was available for 12 dogs, ranging from 58 to 2094 days. Eight dogs died or were euthanased for cardiac-related reasons, three were alive at follow-up and one dog was alive 278 days after surgery at last point of contact. All dogs showed a marked postoperative clinical improvement. Shunt obstruction or partial obstruction was documented in three of 12 dogs at 265, 587 and 693 days. Postoperative balloon valvuloplasty was performed in three of the 12 dogs, one died during the procedure and two dogs showed clinical improvement and extended good quality survival. Owners' perception of the procedure outcome and quality of life was described as good, with only mild adjustments needed for exercise.

CLINICAL SIGNIFICANCE: Blalock-Taussig-Thomas shunt is an effective palliative option for dogs with cyanotic congenital cardiac diseases associated with reduced pulmonary blood flow, providing sustained clinical improvement and quality of life. Recurrence of clinical signs could indicate shunt obstruction and warrants prompt assessment.

articles.title: Gaps in diabetes care among people living with HIV and hypertension in Botswana: A cross-sectional analysis of the InterCARE study.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: Data on diabetes screening and monitoring, within HIV care programmes in sub-Saharan Africa, remain limited. This study describes the quality of diabetes screening and management among people living with HIV with comorbid hypertension receiving care at facilities participating in the InterCARE trial in Botswana.

METHODS: We conducted a cross-sectional analysis of adults aged 20-75 years with a documented diabetes diagnosis at enrolment in InterCARE (January-September 2023). All participants were people living with HIV with hypertension receiving routine HIV clinic care. Descriptive statistics were used to summarize baseline characteristics and key diabetes care indicators, including glycated haemoglobin (HbA1c), low-density lipoprotein (LDL) cholesterol and blood pressure (BP), and their level of control.

RESULTS: Of 4655 InterCARE participants, 138 (3.0%) had a prior diabetes diagnosis. In this diabetes subgroup, 69.6% were female (n = 99), and the median age was 58 years (IQR 52-64). Among the 87 participants receiving diabetes treatment, 80.0% (n = 70) were on oral agents and 20.0% (n = 17) on insulin-based therapy. Glycaemic and LDL monitoring had been performed in only 5.1% and 2.2% of participants, respectively. Blood pressure control (BP <130/80 mmHg) was achieved in 60.9%. Among those with HbA1c results (n = 75.1%), only 28.6% (n = 2) had glycaemic control (HbA1c <7%); however, interpretation is limited by the small number of HbA1c measurements. Lipid control could not be assessed due to insufficient data. Among participants without diabetes, documented screening was rare (17/4517; 0.3%).

CONCLUSION: Diabetes care among people living with HIV ith hypertension in Botswana is suboptimal with major gaps in screening and metabolic monitoring. These findings highlight broader challenges in the delivery of integrated chronic disease care within HIV services. Strengthening the integration of non-communicable disease care into HIV programmes, including routine diabetes screening and cardiometabolic risk management, is urgently needed to improve health outcomes and reduce the burden of cardiovascular and other chronic complications among people living with HIV.

articles.title: Innate immune response to Streptococcus suis infection: advances and future challenges.
articles.abstract: Streptococcus suis is a pathogenic bacterium primarily found in pigs, where it causes sudden death and meningitis, but it is also capable of causing septic shock and meningitis in humans, being the most important cause of adult bacterial meningitis in Southeast Asia. As the host's innate immune system serves as the first line of defense against microbial invaders, it is crucial to understand the intricate relationship between the bacterium and this system. Despite an increasing number of studies performed in the last 20 years, the pathogenesis of S. suis infection is not fully understood, and there is still an absence of effective vaccines on the market. Recent population-genomic studies have further highlighted that pathogenic S. suis is not a single uniform entity but comprises multiple lineages with distinct genome content and disease associations, raising the possibility that innate immune evasion mechanisms may not be equivalent across lineage. In the current article, we conducted a comprehensive review of the literature, focusing on the innate response developed mainly by phagocytes against this Gram-positive bacterium. Our aim was to summarize the last findings and to identify the main gaps in knowledge to guide future research efforts toward areas that require further investigation.

articles.title: PRRSV infection induces mitochondrial damage and releases mitochondrial dsRNA to activate the NLRP3-dependent inflammatory response.
articles.abstract: Porcine reproductive and respiratory syndrome (PRRS), caused by the PRRS virus (PRRSV), remains one of the most economically significant infectious diseases affecting the global swine industry, resulting in annual losses exceeding US $1.2 billion in the USA alone. PRRSV infects porcine alveolar macrophages (PAMs) and induces profound mitochondrial dysfunction, leading to the release of mitochondrial DNA (mtDNA). However, the mechanisms by which PRRSV-induced mitochondrial damage acts as a damage-associated molecular pattern (DAMP) to trigger inflammatory responses have not been fully elucidated. Here, we report that highly pathogenic PRRSV (HP-PRRSV) infection upregulates interleukin-1β (IL-1β) messenger RNA (mRNA) expression and protein secretion in a dose- and time-dependent manner. Transmission electron microscopy revealed progressive mitochondrial swelling, cristae disorganization, and matrix loss during HP-PRRSV infection. Using RNAscope combined with MitoGreen staining, we discovered that mitochondrial double-stranded RNA (mtdsRNA), generated from bidirectional transcription of mitochondrial DNA, is released into the cytosol during PRRSV infection. In vitro, transcription-driven mtdsRNA or mtdsRNA isolated from PAMs directly activated the NLRP3 inflammasome, inducing caspase-1 cleavage and IL-1β secretion.
