Mechanistically, the PRRSV-encoded nonstructural protein 11 (nsp11) inhibited NLRP3-dependent inflammatory responses by suppressing the oligomerization of the apoptosis-associated speck-like protein containing a caspase recruitment domain (CARD) (ASC), thereby constraining excessive inflammation and establishing a delicate balance between pro-inflammatory signaling and viral immune evasion. Collectively, our findings identify mtdsRNA as a previously unrecognized mitochondrial DAMP that links PRRSV-induced mitochondrial injury to NLRP3 inflammasome activation, while also revealing a counter-regulatory role for nsp11 in modulating inflammation.

articles.title: Heel movement and foot biomechanics in aluminium nail-on and indirect glue-on fabric cuff shoes in horses.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Heel movement is critical to shock absorption and vascular perfusion of the equine digit. Conventional horseshoeing techniques are suspected to restrict natural hoof deformation, affecting hoof biomechanics. Several studies have explored the effects of shoeing on hoof function, though many have been limited to artificial conditions, cadavers, or homogenous populations.

OBJECTIVE: We aimed to compare the effects of two aluminium shoeing techniques, nail-on versus indirect glue-on fabric cuff shoes, on heel movement in horses. Our objective was to determine which technique allowed greater heel movement on hard and soft footing.

STUDY DESIGN: A controlled in vivo experimental study using a repeated-measures design.

METHODS: Fifteen healthy horses underwent three trials: (1) indirect glue-on fabric cuff shoes, (2) barefoot, and (3) aluminium nail-on shoes. A displacement sensor was affixed to the heels of one forelimb. Measurements were taken on hard and soft footing. Data were analysed using mixed-model ANOVA to determine differences in heel movement.

RESULTS: Heel movement was significantly greater when barefoot (p < 0.0001). Mean heel displacement for the walk on hard ground was highest in barefoot horses (3.03 ± 0.67 mm), followed by glue-on shoes (2.23 ± 0.58 mm), and aluminium nail-on shoes (1.96 ± 0.48 mm). At the trot, mean heel movement was greatest in barefoot horses (3.29 ± 0.62 mm), followed by glue-on shoes (2.56 ± 0.55 mm), and aluminium nail-on shoes (2.12 ± 0.47 mm).

MAIN LIMITATIONS: The two main limitations were: (1) The lack of an absolute zero baseline measurement, preventing differentiating between heel expansion and contraction. (2) Low heel conformation in some horses prevented recordings on soft footing, reducing the statistical power.

CONCLUSIONS: This study reinforces previous findings that shoeing restricts heel movement. Indirect glue-on shoes allow for more heel movement than nail-on shoes at the trot; both techniques limit heel movement compared to barefoot.

articles.title: Racial and Socioeconomic Inequities in COVID-19 In-Hospital Mortality in Brazil in the Post-Emergency Era: A National Cohort Study of 19,718 Hospitalized Adults in 2024.
articles.journal: Journal of racial and ethnic health disparities
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: In 2024, COVID-19 entered a post-emergency phase, but in-hospital mortality remains a relevant public health concern in Brazil. As population immunity, vaccination, and clinical management evolved, the hierarchy of mortality predictors may have shifted from traditional metabolic risk factors toward clinical severity and social vulnerability. This study aimed to identify sociodemographic, clinical, management, and vaccination-related variables associated with in-hospital COVID-19 mortality among adults in Brazil in 2024, with emphasis on racial and socioeconomic inequities.

METHODS: A retrospective national cohort study was conducted using the SIVEP-Gripe surveillance database. Adults aged ≥ 18 years hospitalized with laboratory-confirmed COVID-19 between January and December 2024 were included. The primary analysis was restricted to patients with observed hospital outcomes, resulting in an analytical sample of 19,718 individuals. Crude and adjusted associations were estimated using binary logistic regression. Race/color was modeled using White patients as the reference category. Robustness to unmeasured confounding was assessed using E-values, and model performance was evaluated using AUC-ROC.

RESULTS: The in-hospital fatality rate was 23.5% (n = 4,633). Invasive ventilatory support was the strongest predictor of death (aOR: 7.574; 95% CI: 6.801-8.435; E-value: 4.95). Black patients had higher odds of death compared with White patients (aOR: 1.506; 95% CI: 1.233-1.838; E-value: 1.76), as did Pardo/mixed-race patients, although with lower magnitude (aOR: 1.103; 95% CI: 1.006-1.209). A strong educational gradient was observed, with illiterate patients having more than twice the odds of death compared with those with higher education (aOR: 2.148; 95% CI: 1.628-2.833). Incomplete COVID-19 vaccination was also associated with increased mortality, while influenza vaccination was associated with lower odds of death. Diabetes, obesity, and chronic cardiovascular disease were not independently associated with mortality after adjustment.

CONCLUSIONS: In-hospital COVID-19 mortality in Brazil in 2024 was shaped by respiratory severity, incomplete vaccination, and persistent racial and socioeconomic inequities. Although structural racism was not directly measured, the persistence of racialized mortality differences after adjustment is compatible with structural barriers in the healthcare pathway. Equity-oriented strategies should complement vaccination and clinical management to reduce preventable mortality among socially vulnerable populations.

articles.title: Social Network Theory in Behavior Change Interventions with Black Women to Reduce Inequities in Cardiovascular Health: A Scoping Review of Application and Measurement.
articles.journal: Journal of racial and ethnic health disparities
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Black women in the United States face disproportionate rates of hypertension and cardiovascular disease, driven by the compounding effects of structural inequity and socially embedded stress. Social networks are a critical and underutilized lever for health promotion in Black communities. Behavioral change interventions to improve cardiovascular health are frequently delivered in group formats. Yet, it is unclear to what extent these interventions deliberately apply social network theory or measure network-level mechanisms.

METHODS: We conducted a scoping review using a systematic search of 37 databases, supported by a health sciences librarian, plus a snowball search of related review articles. Studies were eligible if they targeted at least one cardiovascular health behavior, blood pressure, or a stress-reduction outcome, included a social network or social relationship measure, and enrolled samples in which at least 51% of participants identified as Black or African American.

RESULTS: Of 524 records, eight articles representing six unique interventions met the inclusion criteria. Participants were predominantly middle-aged women from the Southern and Midwestern U.S. Social cognitive theory was the predominant theoretical framework. Network processes, including network size, cohesion, and relationship strength, were measured in half the studies and were positively associated with physical activity and weight loss outcomes.

CONCLUSIONS: The existing literature consistently underutilizes social network theory and rarely measures how network dynamics contribute to, or constrain, intervention outcomes. Future research should integrate network measurement as both a process and outcome variable and attend to the dual nature of social ties as sources of both support and strain.

articles.title: Predictors of false-positive and invalid results in postmortem blood testing of tissue donors: a case-control study.
articles.abstract: Postmortem blood screening for infectious diseases is crucial for safe tissue transplantation. However, false-positive and invalid results occur more often than in living donors, potentially leading to unnecessary graft rejection, based on the acceptance criteria of the Dutch Transplant Foundation. This study aimed to identify factors associated with unreliable postmortem test outcomes. A matched case-control study was conducted using data from Dutch tissue donors screened between 2018 and 2023. Cases included 174 donors with false-positive or invalid results, and controls included 460 donors with reliable results. Logistic regression assessed associations between test unreliability and donor factors, including age, body mass index (BMI), sepsis, and malignancy, and procedural factors, including postmortem interval (PMI) and method of blood collection. Prolonged PMI and pathologist-collected samples with delayed processing were significantly associated with unreliable test results. Each additional hour of PMI increased the odds by 10 percent (adjusted OR 1.10, 95% CI: 1.06-1.13, p < 0.001). Blood collection prior autopsy showed over fourfold higher odds of an unreliable result (adjusted OR 4.54, 95% CI: 1.61-13.9, p = 0.005). Donor-related characteristics showed no significant associations. Unreliable postmortem test results are primarily associated with procedural factors. Reducing the PMI and standardizing sampling methods may improve test accuracy.

articles.title: Ultrasound findings across liver fibrosis stages defined by transient elastography in patients with chronic hepatitis B in Georgia.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: Chronic hepatitis B (CHB) remains a major cause of chronic liver disease and may progress to liver fibrosis, cirrhosis, and hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC). This study aimed to evaluate conventional abdominal ultrasound (US) findings across liver fibrosis stages defined by transient elastography (TE) in patients with CHB.

METHODS: In this cross-sectional study, 232 adults with CHB were included. Conventional abdominal US and TE data were available for 231 patients. US findings were evaluated in relation to liver fibrosis stages defined by TE-derived liver stiffness measurements. Differences in liver stiffness according to US findings were assessed using the independent-samples t-test.

RESULTS: Patients with heterogeneous liver echotexture had significantly higher liver stiffness than those with normal liver echotexture (8.71 ± 6.89 vs. 5.65 ± 1.30 kPa; mean difference, 3.06 kPa; 95% CI 1.78-4.34 kPa; p < 0.001). Patients with splenomegaly had significantly higher liver stiffness than those without splenomegaly (17.31 ± 15.18 vs. 6.55 ± 2.82 kPa; mean difference, 10.77 kPa; 95% CI 2.00-19.54 kPa; p = 0.020). Among the 231 patients, 71.9% were classified as F0-F1, 21.6% as F2-F3, and 6.5% as F4. Four patients were diagnosed with HCC, including three with cirrhosis (F4) and one with F0-F1 fibrosis.

CONCLUSIONS: Conventional abdominal US findings, particularly heterogeneous liver echotexture and splenomegaly, were associated with higher liver stiffness in patients with CHB. These findings support the complementary role of conventional abdominal US in the comprehensive non-invasive evaluation of patients with CHB.

articles.title: Expression patterns of CD24 and CD27 resolve the origins and gradual differentiation of CD11c+ atypical memory B-cells after malaria infection.
articles.abstract: Atypical B-cells (ABCs) are observed across infections, yet their ontogeny and differentiation remain unclear. Using high-dimensional flow cytometry, single-cell transcriptomics, V(D)J sequencing, and functional assays in samples from individuals with malaria and healthy donors, we identify markers of cellular origin while tracking ABC differentiation. Early ABCs express CD11c and arise predominantly from memory B-cells. Two intermediate states originate from germinal center-derived and marginal zone-like B-cells. Pseudotime and lineage analyses reveal trajectories marked by progressive loss of CD24 and CD27, which is recapitulated in vitro, defining bona fide differentiation programs. Differentiation culminates in late ABCs lacking CD24, CD27, and CD21, while expressing CD11c, T-bet, and NKG7 at high levels, exhibiting partial overlap with double-negative-2 B-cells. Early and intermediate stages show greater plasma-cell differentiation potential and cytokine production capacity, whereas later stages acquire transcriptomic signatures of antigen presentation and association with microbial particles, defining stage-dependent functions that reconcile conflicting ABC roles. Comparable ABC populations occur in healthy blood and tonsils, with tissue-associated class switching and CD86 expression consistent with recent T-cell interaction. This framework consolidates ABC definitions along a single differentiation axis and clarifies their cellular origins.

articles.title: Evaluation of PET-detected nodal upstaging and planning target volume expansion in esophageal cancer radiotherapy planning.
articles.journal: Strahlentherapie und Onkologie : Organ der Deutschen Rontgengesellschaft ... [et al]
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: While 18F-fluorodeoxyglucose positron emission tomography (FDG-PET/CT) is known to influence staging, its quantitative impact on clinically meaningful target volume expansion remains incompletely characterized. We evaluated whether PET-detected nodal upstaging is associated with significant planning target volume (PTV) expansion.

METHODS: Fifty consecutive eligible patients with esophageal cancer undergoing computed tomography (CT)- and PET-based radiotherapy planning between January 2018 and January 2022 were retrospectively analyzed, with no predefined target sample size. Clinically significant PTV expansion was predefined as a > 10% increase from CT-based to PET-based planning. Associations between PET-detected nodal upstaging and PTV expansion were evaluated using Fisher's exact test, logistic regression, receiver operating characteristic (ROC) analysis, and nonparametric testing. Given the limited number of events, a parsimonious multivariable model and threshold sensitivity analyses were additionally performed.

RESULTS: Patients with nodal upstaging had a significantly higher risk of > 10% PTV expansion (48.0% vs. 16.7%; absolute risk difference 31.3%, 95% CI 6.7-55.9%; p = 0.032). The median percent PTV change was significantly higher in patients with nodal upstaging (9.49% vs. 0.31%; Wilcoxon p < 0.001). In a parsimonious multivariable model adjusting for tumor length, nodal upstaging remained independently associated with clinically significant PTV expansion (odds ratio (OR) 4.38, 95% confidence interval (CI) 1.12-17.10; p = 0.033). Model discrimination was acceptable (area under the curve (AUC) 0.7254), with stable performance on bootstrap internal validation (bootstrap mean AUC 0.733). Sensitivity analyses using alternative expansion thresholds (> 5%, > 10%, and > 15%) demonstrated directionally consistent associations. Patients meeting the PTV expansion threshold also demonstrated significantly greater increases in lung dose-volume burden (mean lung dose, and lung volumes receiving 5 Gy and 20 Gy; all p < 0.001) in paired dosimetric comparison, supporting the clinical relevance of this threshold.

CONCLUSION: During esophageal cancer radiotherapy planning, PET-detected nodal upstaging was independently associated with clinically meaningful target volume expansion. The association was consistent across alternative expansion thresholds and in bootstrap internal validation, and a paired lung dose-volume comparison indicated that the expansion threshold corresponds to a measurable increase in lung dose burden.

articles.title: Physical activity during pregnancy and the risks of excessive gestational weight gain and large-for-gestational-age: a dose-response meta-analysis of observational studies.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Existing studies have established associations between physical activity and excessive gestational weight gain (EGWG) and large-for-gestational-age (LGA) infants. However, the dose-response relationships have been overlooked.

METHODS: Studies on the associations between physical activity and EGWG/LGA were searched from eight databases, and 34 independent studies were finally included for eligibility. Quality assessment was performed using the Newcastle-Ottawa Scale (NOS), and publication bias was examined with Begg's and Egger's tests. Physical activity volume was harmonized to the common unit of MET-h/week. Restricted cubic splines were employed to model the dose-response relationship. All analyses were performed using Stata 16.0.

RESULTS: Compared to the lowest level of physical activity, pregnant women with the highest level of physical activity had a 30% lower risk of EGWG and a 16% lower risk of delivering an LGA infant. A linear relationship was observed both throughout pregnancy and within specific trimesters. Overall, pregnant women who accumulated 10, 20, and 50 MET-h/week of physical activity had 4%, 9%, and 20% lower risks of EGWG, respectively. No significant dose-response association was observed during the second trimester. In contrast, during the third trimester, the corresponding reductions in EGWG risk were 8%, 16%, and 35%, respectively.

CONCLUSION: Higher levels of physical activity were associated with a reduced risk of EGWG and LGA. A linear dose-response relationship between physical activity and EGWG was observed overall, particularly during the third trimester, highlighting the importance of maintaining adequate physical activity throughout pregnancy.

articles.title: Genetic background modulates MafAS64F-mediated islet ageing in male mice.
articles.abstract:
AIMS/HYPOTHESIS: In monogenic diabetes, there is increasing recognition that common polygenic factors can modulate diabetes penetrance beyond the causative mutation(s). A naturally occurring mutation in the gene encoding the essential islet-enriched transcription factor MafA (MafAS64F) produces an unusually long-lived variant protein that predisposes male carriers to MODY. Here we investigated how genetic background modulates disease penetrance in MafaS64F/+ male mice.

METHODS: MafaS64F/+ male mice, either on a mixed genetic background (C57BL/6J and SJL/J) or backcrossed to a C57BL/6J background, were assessed for glucose levels, beta cell function and gene signatures associated with cellular ageing. RNA-seq analysis was performed to identify unique differentially expressed genes (DEGS) and pathways in mixed-background or C57BL/6J MafaS64F/+ male mouse islets. These were overlaid on MafA CUT&RUN peaks to identify direct targets that could differentially impact beta cell function in each background.

RESULTS: MafaS64F/+ male mice on a mixed background manifested overt diabetes, impaired insulin secretion, accelerated beta cell senescence and dysregulated circadian gene expression, while backcross to C57BL/6J prevented dysglycaemia and maintained insulin secretion in MafaS64F/+ male mice, comparable with control littermates. RNA-seq of C57BL/6J MafaS64F/+ male mouse islets revealed relative normalisation of DEGs associated with cellular ageing and circadian regulation. In addition, islets from C57BL/6J MafaS64F/+ male mice showed unique downregulation of retinoic acid signalling and cell cycle inhibitor p21, the latter of which modulates cellular ageing and diabetes seen in the mixed-background mouse islets. CUT&RUN mapping revealed that MafA directly impacted expression of (at least) retinoic acid receptor-α (encoded by Rara) in islets from C57BL/6J MafaS64F/+ male mice and circadian regulation in islets from mixed-background mice.

CONCLUSIONS/INTERPRETATION: In sum, these data show that genetic modifiers can impact beta cell regulation of retinoic acid signalling and circadian entrainment to modulate beta cell ageing and disease penetrance in mice modelling MAFA-MODY.

DATA AVAILABILITY: Sequencing data were deposited in the National Center for Biotechnology Information (NCBI) Gene Expression Omnibus (GEO) database (accession no. GSE299343 for bulk RNA-seq and GSE298664 for CUT&RUN analyses).

articles.title: The Relationship Between Kinesiophobia, Anxiety and Depression in Patients With Heart Failure: The Role of Patients' Perception of Nursing Care.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Heart failure is associated with psychological and behavioural challenges. Kinesiophobia and perceived nursing care may influence psychological outcomes, but their relationships remain unclear. This study examined the links between kinesiophobia, perceived nursing care, anxiety and depression in heart failure patients.

METHODS: A cross-sectional descriptive-correlational study using structural equation modelling was conducted with 300 hospitalized patients. Data were collected using the Tampa Scale for Kinesiophobia, Hospital Anxiety and Depression Scale and Patient-Centred Care Scale and analysed via correlation multiple regression and structural equation modelling.

RESULTS: Prevalence of high kinesiophobia was 39.3%, severe depression 43.7% and severe anxiety 17.0%. Kinesiophobia correlated positively with anxiety (r = 0.119) and depression (r = 0.290). Better perceived care correlated negatively with anxiety (r = -0.142) and depression (r = -0.241). Regression showed care negatively predicted anxiety (β = -0.13) and kinesiophobia positively predicted depression (β = 0.27). The final structural model revealed that care was negatively associated with anxiety (β = -0.202) and depression (β = -0.302), while kinesiophobia was positively associated only with depression (β = 0.225), not anxiety (p = 0.129). Model fit was suboptimal (RMSEA = 0.095).

CONCLUSION: Although associations were modest, kinesiophobia and perceived nursing care were linked to psychological distress. Addressing movement-related fears and patient-centred care is important in multidimensional heart failure management.

RELEVANCE TO CLINICAL PRACTICE: Nurses should screen for kinesiophobia and psychological distress alongside routine assessments. Identifying fear-related barriers to physical activity and addressing concerns through person-centred communication, tailored education and appropriate referral can support more responsive and holistic nursing care.

REPORTING METHOD: The STROBE statement checklist was used as a guide to reporting this cross-sectional study.

PATIENT/PUBLIC CONTRIBUTION: No patient or public contribution was involved in the design, conduct, analysis or interpretation of this study.

articles.title: Unmasking Iododerma: A Distinctive Histopathologic Pattern of Neutrophil-Rich Dermatosis With Haloed Cryptococcoid Bodies in the Setting of Hydralazine Exposure and Autoimmune Serologic Abnormalities.
articles.abstract: Cutaneous iododerma is a rare adverse reaction to iodine-containing compounds that may clinically and histopathologically mimic infection, vasculitis, malignancy, and other neutrophilic dermatoses. Although most commonly associated with iodinated contrast exposure, a variety of predisposing factors and potential associations have been reported, including impaired renal function, repeated iodine exposure, and more recently, hydralazine therapy in isolated cases. We report two women with chronic kidney disease and recent iodinated contrast exposure who developed rapidly progressive, painful, bullous, erosive, and retiform eruptions after contrast administration. Both patients had concurrent hydralazine exposure. Initial clinical considerations included deep fungal infection, ecthyma, Sweet syndrome, drug eruption, and vasculitis. Histopathologic examination demonstrated a neutrophil-rich dermal infiltrate with numerous basophilic haloed cryptococcoid bodies and vasculitis with fibrinoid necrosis. Fungal, bacterial, and acid-fast stains were negative, and extensive infectious evaluations were unrevealing. Markedly elevated serum and urine iodine levels supported the diagnosis of iododerma. Both patients exhibited multiple immunologic abnormalities, including positivity or elevated levels of p-ANCA and antinuclear, anti-histone, anti-myeloperoxidase, and anti-proteinase 3 antibodies. These findings were interpreted cautiously given concurrent hydralazine exposure, the absence of definitive systemic autoimmune vasculitis, and the potential for reactive serologic abnormalities in the setting of intense neutrophilic inflammation. Both patients improved following corticosteroid therapy, iodine clearance, and discontinuation of hydralazine. These cases emphasize the diagnostic importance of recognizing haloed cryptococcoid bodies within a neutrophil-rich infiltrate associated with vasculitic injury as part of the histopathologic spectrum of iododerma. The significance of hydralazine exposure in the pathogenesis of iododerma remains uncertain and warrants further investigation.

articles.title: Transcriptomic analysis reveals the immune response mechanisms of Acrossocheilus fasciatus against Citrobacter freundii infection.
articles.abstract: Acrossocheilus fasciatus is an economically important freshwater fish species in China. In recent years, Citrobacter freundii infection has caused significant harm to the aquaculture industry. In this study, we performed histological observation and RNA-seq analysis of the intestines and spleens of control (CK) and C. freundii infected A. fasciatus (EG). The results showed that infected fish exhibited abdominal haemorrhage, intestinal villous shedding, hydropic degeneration of hepatocytes and splenic sinus dilation with congestion. RNA-seq analysis identified 3054 DEGs in the intestine and 7706 DEGs in the spleen, with 1247 overlapping DEGs identified by combined analysis. A substantial portion of these genes clustered within biological activities linked to immunity and metabolic regulation, particularly engaging immune-related routes such as endoplasmic reticulum-based protein maturation, alongside the complement system and coagulation signalling cascades. This study systematically reveals the synergy and division of labor between the intestine and spleen during C. freundii infection, providing fundamental data for understanding the immune response mechanisms of A. fasciatus and a theoretical basis for optimising disease prevention and control strategies.

articles.title: The Power of Two: Harnessing Dual Glucagon and Incretin Signaling for Treatment of Obesity and Metabolic Dysfunction-Associated Steatohepatitis-A Narrative Review with a Translational Focus.
articles.journal: Obesity reviews : an official journal of the International Association for the Study of Obesity
articles.abstract: A resurgence in glucagon research has repositioned this pancreatic hormone as a promising target in the treatment of obesity and related metabolic disorders. Glucagon is classically known for contributing to glucose homeostasis, but emerging evidence points to a much wider role in metabolism, including energy balance and liver health. These findings are fueling attempts to understand how to leverage glucagon signaling to treat obesity and metabolic dysfunction-associated steatohepatitis (MASH). Due to potential hyperglycemic effects of glucagon signaling, most investigational compounds are dual agonists of both the glucagon and glucagon-like peptide-1 (GLP-1) receptors to harness the antihyperglycemic and anorectic effects of the latter hormone, analogs of which such as semaglutide are already proven to be potent obesity medications. Glucagon receptor/GLP-1 receptor dual agonists reduce food intake, decrease hepatic fat, and increase energy expenditure in animal models of obesity and MASH. In early clinical trials, some dual agonists substantially reduced body weight, hepatic steatosis, and hepatic fibrosis. Whether they are more effective than GLP-1 receptor mono-agonists remains to be established in definitive head-to-head studies. The precise balance between glucagon and GLP-1 signaling within individual compounds appears important for overall therapeutic effects-including glycemic control, which worsened with some dual agonists. However, the two most clinically advanced compounds-mazdutide (approved for chronic weight management and type 2 diabetes in China) and survodutide (ongoing global phase 3 trials)-had potent weight-loss and antihyperglycemic effects in people with obesity, with survodutide also improving liver health in people with MASH. Therefore, the research into glucagon physiology that led to glucagon receptor/GLP-1 receptor dual agonists is translating to advantageous new therapies for the highly prevalent diseases of obesity and MASH.

articles.title: GLP-1-based therapies in lung diseases.
articles.abstract: Glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists (GLP-1 RAs), initially developed for the treatment of type 2 diabetes and obesity, are increasingly recognised as multi-system agents with cardiovascular, renal and anti-inflammatory benefits. Emerging evidence suggests that their pleiotropic metabolic and immunomodulatory effects may have therapeutic relevance in chronic lung diseases. The lung is a metabolically active organ in which obesity, insulin resistance and systemic inflammation contribute to disease susceptibility, progression and treatment response. Chronic lung diseases such as asthma, COPD, pulmonary hypertension and interstitial lung disease share overlapping inflammatory, vascular and fibrotic pathways that may be modifiable through GLP-1 RA-based therapies. Preclinical studies demonstrate that GLP-1R signalling influences airway inflammation, oxidative stress, endothelial function and fibroblast activation. Observational and early clinical data suggest potential benefits in asthma control, exacerbation reduction in COPD, vascular remodelling in pulmonary hypertension and a reduction in all-cause mortality in interstitial lung disease. In addition to weight loss and glycaemic improvement, GLP-1 RAs exert direct anti-inflammatory and immune-regulatory effects that may act independently of metabolic change. Despite promising mechanistic and translational signals, high-quality randomised controlled trials with GLP-1 RAs in pulmonary populations remain limited. Key questions include patient selection, interaction with established anti-inflammatory and antifibrotic therapies, and the relative contribution of metabolic versus direct pulmonary effects. This review aims to synthesise current mechanistic, experimental and clinical evidence supporting GLP-1 RA use in chronic lung disease and outlines future research priorities within a precision-medicine framework.

articles.title: Dysregulated NK cell phenotype in exacerbation-prone severe asthma.
authors: National Heart Lung and Blood Institute's Severe Asthma Research Program 3
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Natural killer (NK) cell dysfunction and defective inflammation resolution pathways are associated with chronic airway inflammation in asthma. NK cells are targets for regulation by essential polyunsaturated fatty acid-derived specialized pro-resolving mediators (SPMs), including resolvin D2 (RvD2), to stimulate inflammation resolution.

METHODS: Multiparameter flow cytometry was utilized to examine expression patterns of select activating and inhibitory receptors, including the RvD2 receptor DRV2, on circulating NK cells in SARP3 severe and non-severe asthma subjects and healthy controls. Plasma RvD2 and serum amyloid A (SAA) was measured, and RvD2 and SAA regulation of NK cell cytotoxicity was examined in vitro.

RESULTS: Expansion of circulating NK cells with downregulated activating receptors NKp30 and NKp46 and inhibitory receptor CD161 were linked with exacerbation susceptibility and longitudinal lung function trajectory in asthma. Circulating SAA levels were higher in severe asthma patients (median 8.8 μg·mL-1) than healthy individuals (2.2 μg·mL-1; p=0.003). In contrast, plasma RvD2 levels were lower in severe asthma (153 pg·mL-1 versus 208 pg·mL-1 in health; p=0.041), concomitant with a two-fold higher NK cell DRV2 receptor expression than in non-severe asthma subjects (3973 MFI versus 1798; p=0.003). High-dose SAA exposure downregulated NK cell triggering receptors and resulted in a 22% suppression of cytotoxicity (48.9±9.7% versus 62.5±9.2% in vehicle; p=0.001). In contrast, RvD2 enhanced NK cell cytotoxicity (38.1±8.8% versus 33.1±8.3%; p=0.007) and partially reversed SAA-mediated suppression (5.4±2.7% change; p=0.031).

CONCLUSIONS: These findings identify a perturbed counterregulatory network for inflammation resolution in severe asthma comprised of excess pro-inflammatory SAA, deficient pro-resolving RvD2, and altered NK cell immune signatures that were associated with increased asthma morbidity. The beneficial impact of RvD2 in counteracting SAA-mediated suppression of NK cell effector function supports a pivotal mechanistic role for SPMs to enhance cell-type specific resolution pathways to combat persistent airway inflammation in asthma.

articles.title: Eurotransplant experience with Model for End-Stage Liver Disease standard exceptions for hepatopulmonary syndrome and portopulmonary hypertension.
ERS/ESRS clinical practice guideline for continuous positive airway pressure for the treatment of adult obstructive sleep apnoea.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Continuous positive airway pressure (CPAP) is the primary treatment for obstructive sleep apnoea (OSA), although its effectiveness may vary across OSA subtypes. This joint European Respiratory Society (ERS)/European Sleep Research Society (ESRS) clinical practice guideline evaluates CPAP's impact on patient-centred and prognostically relevant outcomes, comparing it to no or sham treatment in different OSA subgroups.

METHODS: The joint ERS/ESRS Task Force consisted of experts in pulmonology, cardiology and respiratory sleep medicine, patient representatives and methodologists. Questions were formulated using the PICO (Population, Intervention, Comparator, Outcomes) framework. A systematic review assessing the effects of CPAP on critical outcomes was performed. The certainty of evidence for all outcomes was assessed using the GRADE (Grading of Recommendations Assessment, Development and Evaluation) approach. Consensus on the direction and strength of the recommendation was informed by Evidence-to-Decision frameworks and achieved through discussions and voting.

RECOMMENDATIONS: The Task Force generally suggests CPAP treatment for OSA because of its beneficial effects on sleepiness, other patient-reported outcomes and blood pressure (conditional recommendations). CPAP is recommended in patients with excessive daytime sleepiness (EDS) (strong recommendation). Additional specific conditional recommendations are given for patients with moderate-to severe OSA, the elderly, and patients with arterial and treatment-resistant hypertension. The Task Force suggests either CPAP or no treatment in patients without EDS (but taking into account other OSA-related symptoms), in patients with atrial fibrillation with the aim of reducing its recurrence and in patients with impaired glucose metabolism to improve glycaemic control.

CONCLUSION: CPAP is an effective treatment for adults with OSA. However, recommendations for its use vary across different patient subgroups.

articles.title: Paediatric escalation area and corridor care in the emergency department: a secondary analysis of the UNCORKED study.
authors: Trainee Emergency Research Network UNCORKED study group

articles.title: Dual Host-Pathogen Screening of the Lung During Severe Influenza Using Spatial Transcriptomics.
articles.abstract: Here, we assessed whether spatially resolved capture of polyadenylated mRNA permitted simultaneous screening of host and viral responses in situ. Fresh-frozen lung samples from mice infected with H1N1 influenza A strain, PR8, were processed via genome-wide, spatial transcriptomics (ST) at 10-μm resolution. To determine if specific cell-types were detectable within the ST data, we first performed cellular deconvolution using publicly available, single-cell RNA-seq data of immune and non-immune cells from PR8-infected lungs. This revealed expected structures such as rings of epithelial cells lining airways, and at Day 10 post-infection (p.i.) unexpected structures dominated by B cells. We next screened ST data alone for groups of genes displaying similar spatial expression patterns. This again identified at Day 10 p.i. cellular aggregates enriched for genes associated with B cell biology. Mapping these gene signatures to a B cell transcriptomic atlas suggested plasmablasts had emerged early in the lung, which was confirmed by flow cytometry. Finally, by mapping ST data to the influenza A genome, we observed widespread expression of all 10 viral transcripts across samples at Day 4 but not Day 10 p.i., consistent with viral clearance. Cellular deconvolution analysis at Day 4 p.i. revealed proportions of every detected cell-type harbored viral transcripts, suggesting indiscriminate infection across the specific area of tissue examined. Subsequent whole-section immunohistochemical assessment further supported the phenomenon of localized indiscriminate infection, with these areas found adjacent to minimally infected zones. Thus, spatial screening of mRNA in tissues can simultaneously inform upon viral pathogenesis and host responses to infection.

articles.title: Sociodemographic, Criminological and Clinical Determinants in Suicide After Release From Prison: A 23-Year National Cohort Study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Suicide risk is elevated after prison release, but population-level evidence on temporal risk patterns and associated factors remains limited. We aimed to describe characteristics of individuals who die by suicide after release from Norwegian prisons, compare their suicide mortality with the general population, and examine risk factors over time.

MATERIAL AND METHODS: Data from the Norwegian Prison Release Study (nPRIS), including all people in prison in Norway (2000-2022), were linked to the Norwegian Cause of Death Registry, the Norwegian Prison Registry, the Norwegian Patient Registry, and Statistics Norway. We calculated crude mortality rates (CMR) per 100,000 person-years, standardized mortality ratios (SMR), annual age-standardized years of life lost rate (ASYR), and Cox proportional hazards models.

RESULTS: From 2000 to 2022, 1183 suicides (9.1% of all deaths; CMR 81; 95% CI 76-85) occurred after release (90% male). The SMR was higher in women (SMR 8.64; 95% CI 7.17-10.34) than men (SMR 3.98; 95% CI 3.76-4.22). In multivariable models (2009-2022; n = 57,034; 516 suicides), strong independent associations with suicide 6 months post-release included self-harm (adjusted HR [aHR] 4.76; 95% CI 2.60-8.72), severe mental illness (aHR 1.95; 95% CI 1.16-3.27), release from high-security prisons (aHR 1.93; 95% CI 1.12-3.33), and pretrial detention (aHR 1.82; 95% CI 1.06-3.13).

CONCLUSIONS: Suicide risk is substantially and persistently elevated relative to the general population, peaks immediately after release, and is concentrated among people with prior self-harm, severe mental illness, and those released from high-security settings.

articles.title: Hypoxic Burden Is an Important Determinant of Height in Nonobese Children With Sleep-Disordered Breathing.
articles.abstract: The relationship between linear growth and obstructive sleep-disordered breathing (SDB) has not been extensively studied. Hypoxic burden (HB) is a new metric that may better capture end-organ damage in paediatric SDB compared to the traditional apnea-hypopnea index (AHI). This observational cross-sectional study examined the association between HB and linear growth in nonobese children aged 3-9 years with SDB. HB was assessed as the area under the peripheral oxygen desaturation curve, alongside standard polysomnography indices. A cohort of 164 children without comorbidities except for asthma was evaluated for suspected SDB, with demographic and anthropometric data collected. The mean ± standard deviation height z score was -0.05 ± 1.09, and the median [25th; 75th percentile] HB was 1.4 [0.4; 3.5] %min/h. Forty children (24%) had an obstructive AHI greater than 5/h. HB and frequent snoring (≥ 3 nights/week) were significantly and negatively associated with height z score (standardized β = -0.21, p = 0.036 and -0.37, p = 0.043, respectively), whereas AHI did not predict linear growth outcomes. In multivariate analyses, HB remained independently associated with lower height z score and accounted for 7.5% of its variance, compared with 12.7% for ethnicity and 6.4% for body mass index z score. The oxygen desaturation index was also a significant predictor, but it explained less variance in height z score than HB. These findings suggest that intermittent hypoxia may contribute to impaired linear growth in children with SDB, although its contribution is modest and other determinants of growth remain important.

articles.title: Impaired lung function as an important risk factor for blood stream infections.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The association of impaired lung function with blood stream infections has only been studied for a limited number of pathogens. We tested the hypothesis that impaired lung function is independently associated with higher risk of any blood stream infections and by specific pathogens in the general population.

METHODS: Copenhagen General Population Study participants had spirometry performed at baseline and were followed for up to 10 years with linkage to the Danish Microbiology Database. The 10-year absolute risk, multivariable adjusted hazard ratio (HR), and population attributable fraction for blood stream infections were determined according to impaired lung function. Outcomes were any and pathogen-specific blood stream infections.

RESULTS: In 118,565 participants, we identified 4160 blood stream infections among 3438 individuals during 950,718 person-years of follow-up. The HR was 1.5 (95% confidence interval (CI), 1.4-1.7) for individuals with obstructive spirometric pattern and 1.4 (95% confidence interval (CI), 1.2-1.5) for individuals with PRISm. The HR for blood stream infections were 1.4 (95% CI: 1.3-1.6) for forced expiratory volume 1-second (FEV1) 50-79% predicted and HR 2.5 (95% CI: 2.0-3.2) for FEV1 below 50% of predicted. A similar pattern was seen for all pathogen specific blood stream infections. The 10-year risk of blood stream infections was 5.4.3% (95% CI: 5.1-5.9) and 4.3% (95% CI: 3.9-4.7) for individuals with PRISm and obstructive spirometric pattern, respectively. The population-attributable fraction of blood stream infections attributable to abnormal spirometric pattern was 9.5% (95% CI: 6.4%-12.7%).

CONCLUSION: Impaired lung function is an important risk factor for blood stream infections and not limited to respiratory tract pathogens.

articles.title: Hepatic retromer is essential for systemic cholesterol homeostasis by regulating lysosomal cholesterol handling.
articles.abstract: Disturbed hepatic cholesterol homeostasis is associated with atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease (ASCVD) and metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD). The endo-lysosomal system plays a central role in cholesterol uptake and intracellular trafficking, yet the molecular mechanisms governing these processes remain poorly understood. Here, we identify hepatic vacuolar protein sorting 35 (VPS35), a core component of the retromer complex, as a critical regulator of hepatocellular and systemic cholesterol homeostasis. Liver-specific VPS35 ablation in mice elevated plasma and hepatic cholesterol levels due to impaired hepatic uptake of atherogenic lipoproteins, defective cholesterol trafficking through the endo-lysosomal system, and increased de novo cholesterol biosynthesis. The decreased hepatic uptake of atherogenic lipoproteins was associated with altered subcellular distribution of the low-density lipoprotein receptor (LDLR) and reduced levels of LDLR-related protein 1 (LRP1). The increased hepatic cholesterol content was associated with altered lysosomal ultrastructure and pH and decreased levels of a wide range of lysosomal proteins, including key proteins for lysosomal cholesterol egress, such as lysosomal acid lipase (LAL), scavenger receptor class B member 2 (SCARB2), Niemann-Pick type C1 (NPC1), and NPC2. Collectively, these findings reveal a previously unrecognized function of the hepatic retromer complex in systemic cholesterol homeostasis. Beyond its established role in endosomal cargo transport, VPS35 is essential for lysosomal cholesterol handling by preserving key proteins involved in lysosomal cholesterol metabolism.

articles.title: The gene expression signature of multinucleated giant cells in the spleens of Leishmania donovani-infected mice.
articles.abstract: Multinucleated giant cells (MGCs) are associated with chronic inflammation and infectious diseases, but their biological characteristics in vivo remain poorly understood because intact cells are difficult to isolate from tissues. In visceral leishmaniasis, heavily parasitized, hemophagocytic MGCs are observed in the spleens of Leishmania donovani-infected mice, suggesting that these cells may contribute to parasite persistence and disease pathology. In this study, we established a method for isolating intact MGCs from the spleens of chronically infected BALB/c mice and performed transcriptomic analysis of manually collected single cells. Gentle enzymatic digestion of infected spleens enabled the recovery of large, multinucleated, F4/80-positive cells, indicating that size-based manual selection efficiently enriched for MGCs. Principal component analysis of single-cell RNA-seq data from 10 isolated MGCs showed that most MGCs formed a cluster distinct from those of naïve and infected bulk-spleen samples and RAW264.7 macrophage cells. Differential expression analysis identified genes that were upregulated during infection and further enriched in MGCs, including Ccl8, Cd63, Cebpb, and Fabp5, which are associated with macrophage activation and immune regulation. These findings provide a practical approach for isolating splenic MGCs and offer preliminary insight into the transcriptional features of L. donovani-induced MGCs in vivo.

articles.title: Large esophageal varices predict hepatocellular carcinoma in newly diagnosed cirrhosis: insights from machine learning and propensity score analysis.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION AND OBJECTIVES: Hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) is a major complication of chronic liver disease (CLD) requiring improved risk stratification. Esophageal varices (EVs), as manifestations of severe portal hypertension, may promote HCC development through vascular remodeling and hypoxia-related pathways. We aimed to evaluate whether variceal size independently predicts HCC risk and whether specific biomarker profiles can be identified.

PATIENTS AND METHODS: In this 12-year prospective cohort study, 545 patients with newly diagnosed compensated advanced chronic liver disease (cACLD) were enrolled at a tertiary hepatology center and followed for a median of 81 months. Baseline evaluations included endoscopy, elastography, hepatic venous pressure gradient measurement, imaging, and laboratory tests. EVs were classified as absent, small, or large according to Baveno VI nomenclature; large EVs were the primary exposure. Propensity score methods and Cox models assessed their impact on HCC risk, and random survival forests evaluated predictive value.

RESULTS: During follow-up, 92 patients (16.9%) developed HCC. Large EVs at baseline emerged as the strongest independent predictor of HCC onset, surpassing alpha-fetoprotein, hepatic venous pressure gradient, and liver stiffness. Hazard ratios ranged from 7.2 to 14.7 (all p < 0.001). After correction for multiple testing, HA, CA9, I-FABP, and TGF-β1 remained associated with large varices, suggesting extracellular matrix remodeling, hypoxia, intestinal barrier injury, and profibrogenic signaling.

CONCLUSIONS: Large esophageal varices independently predict HCC in cACLD, reflecting severe portal hypertension and a pro-tumorigenic milieu, and should inform improved surveillance and preventive strategies targeting vascular and fibrotic pathways.

articles.title: Anticoagulation in cirrhosis: Indications, drug selection, and disease-modifying potential.
articles.abstract: Anticoagulation in cirrhosis has evolved from a perceived contraindication to an integral component of modern liver disease management. Recognition of the fragile rebalanced hemostatic state has challenged the traditional concept of cirrhosis as an exclusively hemorrhagic disorder and provided the biological rationale for anticoagulation in selected patients. Beyond preventing thrombus extension and promoting portal vein recanalization, accumulating experimental and clinical evidence suggests that anticoagulants may exert disease-modifying effects by attenuating intrahepatic coagulation, hepatic fibrogenesis, sinusoidal dysfunction, and portal hypertension. The therapeutic landscape has also changed substantially. Direct oral anticoagulants have emerged as effective and generally safe alternatives to vitamin K antagonists and low-molecular-weight heparin in carefully selected patients, although important differences in pharmacokinetics, hepatic metabolism, renal elimination, and drug interactions require individualized anticoagulant selection. At the same time, management of portal vein thrombosis has shifted from a uniform treatment approach to a patient-centered strategy that considers thrombus characteristics, transplant candidacy, bleeding risk, and the increasing role of endovascular portal vein recanalization. This review summarizes current evidence regarding the indications for anticoagulation in cirrhosis, anticoagulant selection, management of portal vein thrombosis, and available clinical outcomes. It also examines the emerging concept of anticoagulation as a disease-modifying therapy and highlights key knowledge gaps that should guide future research. Together, these advances position anticoagulation as an increasingly important component of comprehensive cirrhosis care rather than a treatment reserved solely for thrombotic complications.

articles.title: Venous thromboembolism after laparotomic and laparoscopic myomectomy with large myoma burden.
articles.abstract:
STUDY OBJECTIVE: To investigate the incidence of venous thromboembolism (VTE) in patients undergoing myomectomy. To evaluate the impact of route of surgery, myoma burden, and operative time in the development of VTE in this population.

DESIGN: Retrospective cohort study (Canadian Task Force Classification II2) of targeted myomectomy data from the American College of Surgeons National Surgical Quality Improvement Program (NSQIP) SETTING: NSQIP Database PATIENTS OR PARTICIPANTS: Women aged ≥18 years undergoing laparotomic and laparoscopic myomectomy between 2011 and 2022. Patients were classified by Current Procedural Terminology (CPT) codes as having low or high myoma burden (>250 g or >4 fibroids). Patients undergoing hysterectomy, vaginal or hysteroscopic myomectomy, with malignant pathology, or missing operative time were excluded.

INTERVENTIONS: Cases were identified by CPT codes. Variables including age, ethnicity, body mass index (BMI), smoking status, diabetes, hypertension, blood transfusion, inpatient status, and American Society of Anesthesiologists classification system scores were collected. Clinical predictors of VTE were evaluated by stratifying cases according to surgical route, operative time, year of procedure, and myoma burden.

MEASUREMENTS AND MAIN RESULTS: A total of 38,167 myomectomies occurring between 2011-2022 were included. Of these, 20,943 (54.9%) patients underwent laparotomy, and 17,224 (45.1%) patients underwent laparoscopy. The incidence of VTE after myomectomy was 0.28%. Patients undergoing laparotomy had twice the VTE rate (0.36%) compared with those undergoing laparoscopy (0.18%). Patients undergoing laparotomy were more likely to be younger, of non-Hispanic African American ethnicity, inpatient, with higher BMI, require blood transfusion, have higher myoma burden, and have shorter operative times. After multivariable adjustment, neither myoma burden nor surgical route was independently associated with VTE. However, longer operative time (>186 min, 75 percentile) was independently associated with increased odds of VTE (aOR 2.73; CI:1.52-4.90).

CONCLUSION: The occurrence of VTE after laparoscopic and laparotomic myomectomy is uncommon. The rate of VTE is higher with longer operative times, but this outcome is not significantly associated with surgical route or myoma burden.

articles.title: Magneto-controllable cell robots for targeted myocardial infarction repair.
articles.abstract: Myocardial infarction (MI) triggers irreversible cardiomyocyte loss, maladaptive remodeling, and heart failure processes exacerbated by insufficient endogenous angiogenesis and unresolved inflammation. While pro-angiogenic therapies hold promise, their clinical translation is hindered by poor lesion targeting, subtherapeutic drug accumulation, and transient bioactivity. To overcome these barriers, we engineered "magnetically guided cellular robots", M2a-polarized macrophages intracellularly loaded with superparamagnetic Fe3O4 nanoparticles and genetically programmed for sustained VEGF secretion (Mag-M2). Mag-M2 exhibits dual responsiveness: chemotactic homing to ischemic myocardiumandprecise magnetic navigation under a 0.5-T field, enabling enhanced transendothelial migration and deep infarct-zone penetration. In MI models, intravenous Mag-M2 administration followed by magnetic guidance significantly preserved left ventricular ejection fraction (67.8 % vs. 40.7 %), reduced infarct size (25.96 % vs. 37.67 %), attenuated fibrosis, and improved survival without systemic toxicity. Mechanistically, Mag-M2 activates a novel VEGF/METRNL/KIT axis: VEGF upregulates the adipokine METRNL, which acted as a high-affinity KIT ligand, driving peri-infarct neovascularization and suppressing pro-inflammatory cytokines (IL-1β, IL-6, TNF α). This integrative platform synergizes immunomodulation, magnetic targeting, and pathway-specific regenerative signaling, offering a rationally designed, translatable strategy for precision myocardial repair.

articles.title: An integrated prediction model using machine learning and dynamics simulation for the selection of transdermal penetration enhancers.
articles.journal: Journal of controlled release : official journal of the Controlled Release Society
articles.abstract: Penetration enhancers (PEs) are widely used in transdermal drug delivery systems (TDDS) due to their cost-effectiveness and excellent biocompatibility. However, the rapid selection of PEs for TDDS is hindered by two critical challenges: first, in vitro permeation tests (IVPT) are costly and time consumption; second, the datasets for drug-PE matching are relatively limited. To address these issues, this study established a rapid screening platform for PEs in transdermal formulations using machine learning (ML) approaches based on a self-constructed database and further explored the permeation process of "drug-PE" systems via molecular dynamics simulation (MD). Systematic evaluation of five ML algorithms showed that the Light Gradient Boosting Machine (LightGBM) model achieved the optimal predictive performance using 5-fold cross-validation based on random selection and unseen drug-excipient combination splitting, with R2 values of 0.78 ± 0.03 (random split), 0.73 ± 0.01 (unseen PE split), and 0.72 ± 0.06 (unseen drug-PE combination split) on the test sets, respectively. In contrast, performance decreased substantially for the unseen-drug split (R2 = -0.40), indicating that the model performs well primarily for interpolation within the chemical space represented in the dataset but does not reliably extrapolate to entirely unseen drugs. Feature importance analysis revealed a dose-dependent relationship between PE concentration and transdermal efficiency, while the log S of drugs exerted a non-singular effect on transdermal flux. Moreover, transdermal database analysis indicated that drugs with log P values of 2-3, when paired with PEs possessing log P values of 4-6, tended to achieve higher transdermal permeation efficiency. The accuracy of the prediction model was verified by IVPT using two model drugs, berberine and ferulic acid. Furthermore, MD simulations were employed to elucidate the penetration mechanism of the model drugs in "drug-PE" combinations at the atomic level. Finally, a rapid screening platform (https://permapp-online.streamlit.app) was developed, which enabled transdermal flux prediction through the input of molecular descriptors. This platform can provide valuable support for the future design of transdermal formulations.

articles.title: Factors affecting serum neurofilament light chain in transthyretin amyloid cardiomyopathy.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: While serum neurofilament light chain (sNfL) has shown promise as a biomarker for the development of peripheral neuropathy (PN) in hereditary transthyretin (TTR) amyloidosis (vATTR), its role in all-comers with ATTR cardiomyopathy (ATTR-CM) is less well defined, and it is unknown how CM severity and TTR stabilizer therapy affect sNfL.

METHODS: Study participants included those with ATTR-CM not on gene-silencer therapy referred to Oregon Health & Science University. The association between sNfL and baseline patient characteristics, including age, sex, body mass index (BMI), presence of PN, ATTR subtype, N-terminal pro b-type natriuretic peptide (NT-proBNP), estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR) and tafamidis treatment, were evaluated utilizing linear regression.

RESULTS: 66 patients (age: 78.5 ± 6.9 years, 6.1% female, 16.7% with diabetes mellitus, 10.6% vATTR-CM, 43.9% with PN symptoms, 30.3% receiving tafamidis at baseline) were included. There was no difference in sNfL levels when stratified by ATTR subtype (p = 0.168), PN symptoms (p = 0.881), or tafamidis treatment measured categorically (p = 0.418). In 17 patients (17.6% vATTR-CM) with available paired pre-tafamidis and on-tafamidis samples, there was no difference in sNfL level. In our univariable and multivariable analysis, NT-proBNP and eGFR were associated with sNfL.

CONCLUSIONS: In ATTR-CM, cardiomyopathy severity and renal dysfunction impact sNfL more than presence of PN or other clinical factors.

articles.title: Isoform differentiation studies of arginase: From structural function to design strategies for specific ligands and their application prospects.
articles.abstract: Arginase (ARG), a binuclear manganese metalloenzyme, hydrolyzes L-arginine to L-ornithine and urea, competitively regulating NO bioavailability with NOS. Mammals express two isoforms, ARG1 (cytosolic) and ARG2 (mitochondrial), that share a conserved catalytic core yet exert distinct physiological and pathological effects. ARG1 is essential for hepatic urea detoxification, as systemic Arg1 knockout mice develop hyperammonemia within 10-12 days after birth; in contrast, Arg2 knockout mice show only slightly elevated plasma arginine levels with no overt phenotypic abnormalities, this significant difference highlights the importance of a thorough analysis of the functional divergence between ARG1 and ARG2. Pathologically, ARG1 drives immunosuppression in the tumor microenvironment, promotes vascular dysfunction in hypertension and atherosclerosis, and contributes to fibrotic remodeling; ARG2 fuels M1 macrophage inflammatory responses, modulates mitochondrial metabolism, and participates in neurodegeneration. This review systematically examines isoform differences across four dimensions: structural-functional divergence, localization-driven functional segregation, differential pathological contributions, and the current landscape of isoform-selective inhibitors. We further discuss rational design strategies for specific ligands and highlight the translational prospects of isoform-targeted therapies. Exploiting ARG1/ARG2 differentiation represents a promising avenue for precision intervention in cancer, cardiovascular disease, inflammation, and neurodegenerative disorders.

articles.title: The dual immunomodulatory roles and signaling mechanisms of toll-like receptor 2 in different diseases.
articles.abstract: Toll-like receptors are important components of the pattern recognition receptor (PRR) family, and Toll-like receptor 2 (TLR2) is one of the most important Toll-like receptors involved in defending against infection and injury. TLR2 senses a wide array of pathogen- and damage-associated molecular patterns and has very broad functions in infectious diseases and other diseases. On one hand, TLR2 drives pro-inflammatory responses through the classical MyD88/NF-κB pathway, which is crucial for pathogen clearance; on the other hand, TLR2 can also limit excessive inflammation by activating the PI3K/Akt pathway, inducing IL-10, and promoting the expansion of regulatory T cells (Tregs), thereby maintaining immune tolerance. Such functional plasticity is regulated by ligand milieu, cell types and disease stages, which underpin the dual roles of TLR2 under diverse pathological conditions including infection, inflammation, autoimmunity and organ transplantation. This review systematically summarizes advances in TLR2 signaling transduction and its immunological functions across various diseases and enables a more cautious evaluation of its pleiotropic effects in distinct disease contexts.

articles.title: A dual-bioeffect nanoengineered piezoelectric-photothermal hydrogel induces endochondral ossification and promotes critical-sized bone regeneration.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Critical-sized bone defects remain a major clinical challenge in orthopedics. Current strategies including inert implants and autologous bone grafts suffer from complications like loosening, infection, and donor site morbidity. Piezoelectric and photothermal stimuli synergistically regulate bone regeneration, and black phosphorus nanosheets (BPNSs) possess both effects and biodegradability, but are prone to oxidation and aggregation.

OBJECTIVES: This study aims to develop an injectable biomimetic hydrogel with dual piezoelectric-photothermal bioeffects for minimally invasive and efficient repair of irregular critical-sized bone defects.

METHODS: BPNS@rhCOL1MA composite system was constructed by embedding BPNSs into recombinant human methacrylated type I collagen hydrogel. Physicochemical characterization, in vitro cell assays, transcriptomic analysis, and in vivo validation in a rabbit rib defect model were performed.

RESULTS: The material exhibited stable network, injectability, and controllable dual-responsive properties. It significantly enhanced osteogenic differentiation of BMSCs in vitro. Transcriptomics revealed activation of electrical/thermal signal transduction and angiogenesis pathways. In vivo, it markedly improved new bone formation, bone mineral density, and mechanical properties.

CONCLUSION: This work first integrates the dual bioeffects of BPNSs with injectable human-derived collagen hydrogel, providing a novel strategy for minimally invasive repair of irregular bone defects.

articles.title: Association of protein signature of fine particulate matter with MASLD: the underlying pathways and Mendelian randomization analysis.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: MASLD is a common chronic liver disease worldwide; identifying modifiable risk factors is crucial. Although fine particulate matter (PM2.5) has been epidemiologically linked to MASLD, its mechanism remains unclear.

OBJECTIVES: To explore the mediating role of protein signature on the association between PM2.5 and metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD), and the underlying biological pathways.

METHODS: We included 52,190 participants free of MASLD at baseline of a large cohort. Annual average PM2.5 exposure was estimated by bilinear interpolation, and time-weighted method. PM2.5-related protein signature was constructed by elastic net regression, and KEGG/GO enrichment analysis was performed to identify potential pathways. Cox models were used to evaluate the associations of PM2.5 and the protein signature with incident MASLD. Mendelian randomization (MR) analysis was applied to examine potential causality between proteins and MASLD. Structural equation modeling (SEM) was employed to the evaluate statistical mediation involving the protein and metabolic signatures.

RESULTS: During a median follow-up of 11.8 years, 624 incident MASLD cases were identified. The PM2.5-related protein signature comprised 700 proteins, which were mainly enriched in pathways including NF-κB signaling pathway, and cytokine-cytokine receptor interaction. Both PM2.5 exposure, and protein signature were significantly associated with incident MASLD, with hazard ratios (95 % confidence intervals) of 1.19 (1.10, 1.30), and 1.19 (1.08, 1.31). MR analysis provided genetic evidence supporting that CD28, CSF3 and HAVCR2 were associated with MASLD. Mediation analysis indicated that PM2.5-related protein signature mediated 15 % (95 % CI: 2.7 %, 37.7 %) of the PM2.5-MASLD association. SEM further suggested that PM2.5-related protein signature might mediate the PM2.5-MASLD association by regulating metabolic signatures.

CONCLUSIONS: The PM2.5-related protein signature was associated with MASLD, and showed statistical mediation of PM2.5-MASLD association potentially involving inflammatory and metabolic pathways.

articles.title: Patient-Reported Benefits of Acoramidis Across Genotypes in Transthyretin Amyloid Cardiomyopathy: KCCQ and EQ-5D-5L Outcomes From ATTRibute-CM.
Left Ventricular Functional Improvement is Associated With Lower Morbidity and Mortality During Long-Term Mechanical Circulatory Support: An STS Intermacs Analysis.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: A subset of patients with advanced heart failure (HF) supported with durable left ventricular assist devices (LVADs) demonstrate significant improvement in left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF), but the impact of such functional improvement on clinical outcomes is unclear.

METHODS: We analyzed adults in the STS-Intermacs registry who underwent continuous-flow LVAD implantation (2006-2017) and had echocardiographic data ≥6 months post-implant. Post-LVAD myocardial function was defined by the maximum LVEF after ≥6 months of support and categorized as <40% vs ≥40% and into finer strata. Outcomes included all-cause mortality, clinically significant sustained cardiac arrhythmia, hepatic and renal dysfunction, CVA/TIA, right HF during follow-up, and HF hospitalization. Incidence rates and incidence rate ratios were calculated during 6-month landmarked follow-up through 5 years, and associations were assessed using landmarked multivariable Cox models.

RESULTS: Among 9,518 eligible patients (age 56.6±13.2 years, 21.4% female), 1,131 (12%) achieved LVEF ≥40% over a median 27.0 months of follow-up. Compared with LVEF <40%, LVEF ≥40% was associated with lower adjusted incidence rates of death (adjusted IRR 0.85, 95% CI 0.73-0.98), arrhythmia (0.59, 0.48-0.72), hepatic dysfunction (0.58, 0.35-0.97), and HF hospitalization (0.65, 0.51-0.82), whereas adjusted differences in right HF and renal dysfunction were not significant. In adjusted time-to-event analyses, LVEF ≥40% was independently associated with lower hazards of all-cause mortality (aHR 0.82, 95% CI 0.71-0.96), HF hospitalization (0.63, 0.50-0.80), cardiac arrhythmia (0.69, 0.58-0.83), and hepatic dysfunction (0.57, 0.37-0.88). Across ordered LVEF strata, higher LVEF was associated with progressively lower risks of death and HF-related events.

CONCLUSIONS: In a large multicenter LVAD cohort, LV functional response to durable support spanned a spectrum, with ∼1 in 8 (12%) durable LVAD recipients achieving a maximum post-implant LVEF ≥40% after ≥6 months of support. Higher post-implant LVEF was independently associated with improved survival and fewer HF-related events. These findings support viewing myocardial improvement during LVAD support as a clinically meaningful target that affects positively the outcomes of patients while being on mechanical support.

articles.title: Cardiac resynchronization therapy outcomes by sex and QRS duration: insights from AdaptResponse and a Real-world registry.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Sex-related differences in cardiac resynchronization therapy (CRT) outcomes in heart failure (HF) patients, particularly at shorter QRS durations, remain incompletely defined. We evaluated outcomes by sex and QRS duration in AdaptResponse trial and, pooled with Medtronic product surveillance registry (PSR) data, evaluated mortality comparing CRT and no CRT.

METHODS AND RESULTS: AdaptResponse patients (symptomatic HF, LVEF≤35%, Strauss-LBBB, and normal atrioventricular conduction; 43% women) were analyzed by sex and baseline QRS (150ms cut-off), and pooled with PSR CRT and No CRT groups meeting CRT indications. Average treatment effect on treated (ATT) propensity weighting was used to standardize the PSR groups to AdaptResponse baseline characteristics. All-cause mortality was compared between the pooled CRT patients and No CRT controls with weighted Cox models. In AdaptResponse, adjusted mortality rates did not differ significantly between women and men (HR 0.91, 95% CI: 0.72-1.15; p=0.45), and no interaction was observed between sex and QRS (p=0.31). Adjusted mortality in women with QRS<150ms was not statistically different from men with QRS≥150ms (HR 1.02, CI: 0.75-1.38). After ATT-weighting and adjustment, CRT was observed to be associated with lower mortality versus No CRT across sex and QRS subgroups (QRS 120-149ms: HR 0.50, CI: 0.31-0.82 for women and HR 0.51, CI: 0.31-0.86 for men; QRS≥150ms: HR 0.46, CI: 0.28-0.74 for women and HR 0.46, CI: 0.29-0.72 for men; all p<0.05).

CONCLUSION: In this exploratory analysis, among patients with QRS 120-149ms, CRT was associated with a 49% and 50% relative mortality reduction in men and women, respectively, through five years of follow-up compared to No CRT controls. In AdaptResponse, mortality in women with these shorter QRS durations was similar to men with QRS≥150ms. These observational findings are hypothesis-generating and suggest a potential benefit of CRT in this patient population, particularly for women, but have not been confirmed in a randomized trial.

articles.title: Continuous Vutrisiran Reduces Cardiovascular Events and Hospitalizations in Patients With Transthyretin Amyloidosis With Cardiomyopathy in the HELIOS-B One-Year Open Label Extension.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Vutrisiran significantly reduced the risk of all-cause mortality and recurrent cardiovascular (CV) events vs placebo in patients with transthyretin amyloidosis with cardiomyopathy (ATTR-CM) in the phase 3 HELIOS-B study (NCT04153149). Here, we report the long-term impact of vutrisiran on hospitalizations and urgent heart failure (HF) visits from the ongoing HELIOS-B open-label extension (OLE).

METHODS: In HELIOS-B, patients received vutrisiran 25 mg or placebo every 3 months over a 33-36-month double-blind period, followed by a 24-month OLE continuing with vutrisiran (continuous treatment), or if previously receiving placebo, initiating vutrisiran (delayed treatment). Hospitalizations and urgent HF visits were analyzed through 48 months (12 months of the OLE) in the overall and monotherapy (not receiving tafamidis at baseline) populations, and the baseline tafamidis subgroup.

RESULTS: Of 654 participants, 466 entered the OLE. Continuous vutrisiran reduced the risk of all-cause hospitalizations vs delayed treatment in the overall population (relative rate ratio [RRR] 0.71, 95% confidence interval [CI] 0.62-0.82, P<0.001) and the monotherapy population (RRR 0.60, 95% CI 0.50-0.72, P<0.001). Continuous vutrisiran also significantly reduced the risk of CV hospitalizations, HF hospitalizations, and non-CV hospitalizations vs delayed vutrisiran in the overall and monotherapy populations, and urgent HF visits in the overall population and baseline tafamidis subgroup.

CONCLUSIONS: Continuous vutrisiran reduced the risk of CV events and hospitalizations relative to patients originally randomized to placebo in HELIOS-B. Many treatment effects were of greater magnitude at 48 months vs 36 months with continuous vutrisiran, highlighting the benefits of earlier diagnosis and treatment.

articles.title: Ultra-processed food consumption in people with chronic kidney disease.
articles.journal: Journal of renal nutrition : the official journal of the Council on Renal Nutrition of the National Kidney Foundation

articles.title: High Infection Rate in Open Anterior Talofibular Ligament Repair with Internal Brace Augmentation and Immediate Permissive Weight Bearing.
articles.journal: The Journal of foot and ankle surgery : official publication of the American College of Foot and Ankle Surgeons
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Modified Broström repair is the gold standard for chronic lateral ankle instability. Internal brace augmentation was introduced to increase ligament strength and allow earlier rehabilitation, but concerns exist regarding surgical site infection (SSI).

PURPOSE: To compare the incidence of SSI following anterior talofibular ligament (ATFL) repair with internal brace augmentation and immediate permissive weight bearing versus ATFL repair without augmentation and restricted rehabilitation.

STUDY DESIGN: Retrospective cohort study.

METHODS: Patients undergoing open ATFL repair with internal brace augmentation and immediate permissive weight bearing (ATFL-IB group) between January 2022 and February 2024 (n = 34) were compared with patients undergoing open ATFL repair without augmentation and restricted rehabilitation (ATFL group) between January 2016 and March 2019 (n = 31). The primary outcome was SSI, defined as infection within 90 days requiring antibiotic therapy or surgical intervention. Secondary outcomes included other complications. Baseline characteristics and SSI-related risk factors were assessed.

RESULTS: SSI occurred in 5 patients (15%) in the ATFL-IB group and none in the ATFL group (0%) (p = .034). Other complications included persistent ankle instability (3%) and malposition (3%) in the ATFL-IB group and knot pain (3%) in the ATFL group. Baseline characteristics and operative time were comparable, only smoking prevalence was higher in the ATFL group.

CONCLUSIONS: ATFL repair with internal brace augmentation and immediate permissive weight bearing was associated with a higher SSI rate compared with ATFL repair without augmentation and restricted rehabilitation. Because augmentation and rehabilitation differed concurrently, their relative contributions could not be determined.

articles.title: A temporal framework of redox dysregulation in autoimmunity: interplay between oxidative deficiency and oxidative stress.
articles.abstract: Reactive oxygen species (ROS) occupy a paradoxical position in autoimmune disease: excessive or dysregulated ROS contribute to oxidative injury and inflammatory amplification, whereas physiological ROS function as spatially and temporally regulated signals required for immune homeostasis. This duality suggests that redox dysregulation may involve not only excessive ROS but also failure of physiologically required ROS signaling. We define this latter state as oxidative deficiency: a functionally defined state in which an inadequate physiological ROS signal impairs a specific redox-dependent biological process, rather than simply reflecting low total ROS or increased antioxidant capacity. Genetic and experimental studies of NADPH oxidase (NOX) pathways demonstrate that impaired NOX-dependent ROS generation can modify immune regulation and autoimmune susceptibility in selected contexts, with particularly strong support in systemic lupus erythematosus and experimental arthritis. However, divergent findings in experimental autoimmune encephalomyelitis and protection from autoimmune diabetes following reduced NOX2 activity demonstrate substantial disease- and function-specific effects. We therefore propose that oxidative deficiency and pathological oxidative stress represent distinct, independently testable dimensions of autoimmune-associated redox dysregulation whose relationship may be sequential, concurrent, or absent depending on disease context. In selected settings, oxidative deficiency may precede and later coexist with pathological oxidative stress, although direct temporal evidence for this trajectory in human autoimmune disease remains limited. The framework is experimentally falsifiable: evidence for oxidative deficiency requires demonstration of an inadequate physiological ROS signal, impairment of the corresponding biological function, and, where feasible, functional rescue following selective restoration of the deficient signal. This framework extends established redox concepts by distinguishing failure of physiological ROS signaling from pathological oxidant excess and provides testable criteria for defining their roles in autoimmune disease.

articles.title: Usp3 negatively regulates Mda5-mediated antiviral response by attenuating its K63-linked ubiquitination in black carp.
articles.abstract: Melanoma differentiation-associated gene 5 (MDA5) is a critical cytosolic RNA sensor that initiates type I interferon (IFN) signaling upon viral infection, and its activity must be tightly regulated to maintain immune homeostasis. Ubiquitin-specific protease 3 (USP3) has been identified as a negative regulator of RLR-mediated IFN signaling in mammals, yet its role in teleost antiviral immunity remains unknown. In this study, we cloned and characterized usp3 (bcusp3) from black carp (Mylopharyngodon piceus). The full-length coding sequence of bcusp3 encodes a protein of 524 amino acids containing conserved ZnF-UBP and UCH domains. Overexpression of bcUsp3 significantly suppressed bcMda5-induced ifn promoter activation in a dose-dependent manner, whereas knockdown of bcUsp3 in MPF cells markedly enhanced ifn and interferon-stimulated gene (isg) expression and inhibited SVCV replication. Mechanistically, co-immunoprecipitation (Co-IP) assays revealed that bcUsp3 directly interacts with bcMda5. Furthermore, bcUsp3 over-expression reduced both total and K63-linked ubiquitination of bcMda5, indicating that bcUsp3 attenuates the K63-linked ubiquitination of bcMda5. Collectively, our findings demonstrate that bcUsp3 functions as a negative regulator of bcMda5-mediated Ifn signaling by attenuating its K63-linked ubiquitination, providing the first evidence for the regulatory role of Usp3 in teleost antiviral innate immunity.

articles.title: Veratric acid ameliorates metabolic-dysfunction-associated fatty liver disease via targeting PPARG.
articles.abstract: Metabolic dysfunction-associated fatty liver disease (MAFLD) is one of the most common metabolic syndromes worldwide. Its pathogenesis is multifactorial, involving disruptions in lipid metabolism, insulin resistance, chronic inflammation, and mitochondrial dysfunction. Veratric acid (VA), a naturally occurring phenolic compound, is known for its antioxidant and anti-inflammatory properties; however, its therapeutic potential and underlying mechanisms in the context of MAFLD remain largely uncharacterized.
