This study aimed to investigate the protective effects and underlying mechanisms of VA in a high-fat diet induced mouse model of MAFLD. In this study, C57BL/6J mice were fed an HFD with or without VA supplementation. Metabolic phenotypes, hepatic steatosis, and serum biochemical parameters were evaluated. In vitro experiments were conducted in HepG2 cells to assess lipid accumulation, mitochondrial function, oxidative stress, and gene expression. Network pharmacology, molecular docking, CETSA, and DARTS assays were employed to identify potential targets. The results demonstrated that VA significantly alleviated HFD-induced weight gain, adipose tissue accumulation, and hepatic steatosis. VA also improved glucose homeostasis, reduced serum lipid levels, and ameliorated liver injury. Mechanistically, VA modulated lipid metabolism by enhancing fatty acid β-oxidation and lipolysis. Network pharmacology, molecular docking, and biochemical validation further identified peroxisome proliferator-activated receptor gamma (PPARG) as a key target of VA. VA stabilized the PPARG protein, thereby promoting lipid metabolic reprogramming. These findings provide new insights into the bioactivity of VA and suggest its potential as a natural therapeutic agent for MAFLD.

articles.title: Precision medicine in MASLD: Integrating genetics, multi-omics, and artificial intelligence for risk stratification and targeted therapy.
articles.journal: Clinica chimica acta; international journal of clinical chemistry
articles.abstract: Metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD), formerly termed nonalcoholic fatty liver disease (NAFLD), encompasses a heterogeneous clinical spectrum ranging from isolated hepatic steatosis to metabolic dysfunction-associated steatohepatitis (MASH), fibrosis, cirrhosis, and hepatocellular carcinoma. Differences in susceptibility to disease, progression and extrahepatic complications between individuals are due to many different variables, such as genetic, metabolic and environmental factors, sex, reproductive status and gut microbiota. Precision medicine offers a framework to navigate this complexity by combining clinical phenotyping with inherited genetic variation and large-scale multi-omics data including transcriptomics, epigenomics, proteomics, metabolomics, lipidomics, glycomics and microbiome analysis. Here we review the current evidence on important susceptibility genes, novel multi-omics biomarkers and polygenic risk scores, and discuss how these tools can improve risk prediction and sub-phenotyping. We also discuss artificial intelligence and machine learning algorithms that integrate clinical, imaging and molecular information to allow for non-invasive diagnosis and staging. Finally, we highlight precision-based therapeutic approaches such as oligonucleotide-based agents, genotype-stratified lifestyle and pharmacological interventions, and digitally supported personalized lifestyle programs. We outline the remaining challenges and research priorities needed to integrate precision hepatology into routine care, highlighting the identification of clinically actionable MASLD subtypes and the equitable translation of findings into improved long-term outcomes.

articles.title: Pulsed field ablation with Renal denervation for persistent Atrial fibrIllation: Rationale and design of the PRAISE-AF randomized trial.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Atrial fibrillation (AF) is the most common sustained cardiac arrhythmia worldwide and is associated with increased risks of stroke, heart failure, hospitalization, disability, and mortality. Catheter ablation has become an established rhythm-control strategy for symptomatic AF; however, the recurrence rate after ablation remains substantial, especially in patients with persistent AF. Pulsed field ablation (PFA) is an emerging nonthermal ablation technology with myocardial tissue selectivity and a potentially improved safety profile compared with conventional thermal ablation. Renal denervation (RDN) reduces sympathetic nervous system activity and has shown promising effects in reducing AF recurrence when combined with catheter ablation, mainly in patients with paroxysmal AF and hypertension. Whether RDN combined with PFA improves rhythm outcomes in patients with persistent AF remains unknown.

TRIAL DESIGN: This is a single center, prospective, randomized, patient-blinded, sham-controlled pilot exploratory trial. A total of 86 patients with symptomatic persistent AF undergoing first-time catheter ablation will be enrolled and randomly assigned in a 1:1 ratio to receive either PFA combined with RDN or PFA combined with a sham RDN procedure. Antiarrhythmic drugs (AADs) will be discontinued after the index procedure in both groups. The primary endpoint is freedom from documented atrial tachyarrhythmia recurrence, including AF, atrial flutter, or atrial tachycardia lasting more than 30 seconds, within 12 months after a single ablation procedure without AADs. Secondary endpoints include freedom from atrial tachycardia recurrence within 3 months, AF burden, blood pressure changes, and major adverse cardiovascular events. Safety endpoints include cardiac, vascular, renal, and other procedure-related adverse events.

CONCLUSIONS: This trial will assess the safety and efficacy of PFA with RDN in a postablation contemporary persistent AF patient population.

TRIAL REGISTRATION: ClinicalTrials.gov:NCT07320768.

articles.title: Chitosan nanoparticles enhance the anti-inflammatory and anti-adipogenic effects of tart cherry anthocyanin in 3T3-L1 adipocytes.
articles.abstract: Obesity-associated adipose inflammation and gut dysfunction represent critical targets for dietary intervention. Tart cherry juice (TCJ)-derived anthocyanins (ACNs) exhibit potent anti-inflammatory and gut-protective bioactivity, but their poor stability and low oral bioavailability limit efficacy. Although nanotechnology can improve ACN delivery, conventional nanocarriers contain surfactants or emulsifiers that may impair gut health with chronic use. To overcome these challenges, we developed a surfactant-free nanoparticle platform using polysaccharides. Void nanoparticles (Vnano) were fabricated by ionic gelation of chitosan and carboxymethyl chitosan, followed by ACN adsorption through hydrogen bonding and electrostatic interactions to generate ACN-loaded nanoparticles (Tnano). Optimized Tnano achieved 80% ACN adsorption efficiency with spherical morphology (about 200 nm), narrow size distribution, and positive zeta potential (23 mV). Compared to free TCJ, Tnano demonstrated sustained ACN release, and fluorescence imaging showed dose- and temperature-dependent binding of the chitosan nanoparticles to 3T3-L1 preadipocytes. Tnano more effectively suppressed lipopolysaccharide (LPS)-induced inflammation, reducing interleukin-6 and monocyte chemoattractant protein-1 secretion by 39% (p < 0.0001) and 35% (p = 0.0316) in preadipocytes, and by 56.8% (p = 0.05) and 20% (p < 0.0001) in mature adipocytes, respectively, compared to LPS groups. Compared to control, Tnano reduced adipogenic lipid accumulation by 35%, versus only 14.2% for TCJ (p = 0.0003). As a proof of concept for future oral delivery applications, Tnano was encapsulated within an alginate hydrogel shell by electrospray to form a nano-in-micro format. This fully natural polysaccharide-based nanoplatform offers a strategy to enhance anthocyanin bioavailability and combat obesity-associated inflammation and metabolic disease.

articles.title: Subclinical Leaflet Thrombosis, Transcatheter Heart Valve Characteristics and Structural Valve Deterioration: Rationale and Design of the POPular PET TAVI Study.
articles.journal: Journal of nuclear cardiology : official publication of the American Society of Nuclear Cardiology
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Subclinical leaflet thrombosis is common after transcatheter aortic valve implantation (TAVI) and may contribute to structural valve deterioration over time, this may be influenced by transcatheter heart valve (THV) design and other valve-related factors.

METHODS: The 'Effect of Subclinical Leaflet Thrombosis and Prosthesis Type on Transcatheter Aortic Valve Degeneration (POPular PET TAVI)' study is an international, multicenter, cross-sectional cohort study. Patients (n=180) are enrolled at five years after TAVI for a detailed assessment of THV structure and function using a multi-modality imaging approach. High-resolution four-dimensional cardiac computed tomography (4D-CT) is used to assess subclinical leaflet thrombosis and THV characteristics (e.g. neosinus volume, prosthesis deformation index, valve expansion and commissural alignment). 18F-sodium fluoride (18F-NaF) positron emission tomography (PET) is used to measure micro-calcification activity in the THV leaflets as a marker of structural valve deterioration. Transthoracic echocardiography is performed to evaluate THV and cardiac function. Obtained images are analyzed by dedicated Core Laboratories for PET and 4D-CT. To facilitate comparisons between balloon-expandable, intra-annular and self-expanding, supra-annular prostheses, enrollment is stratified for valve size and type. As of September 2026, 159 patients have been enrolled successfully, completion is anticipated in December 2026.

CONCLUSION: The POPular PET TAVI study evaluates the interplay between subclinical leaflet thrombosis, THV characteristics and structural valve deterioration at five years after TAVI. Improved understanding of these mechanisms may inform individualized antithrombotic strategies and optimized valve design aiming to enhance long-term valve durability.

articles.title: Emerging novel therapies for the treatment of hereditary haemorrhagic telangiectasia.
articles.abstract: Hereditary haemorrhagic telangiectasia is the second most common heritable bleeding disorder worldwide, with a prevalence more than twice that of haemophilia, and is the most morbid inherited bleeding disorder of women. As an autosomal dominant vasculopathy due to dysregulated angiogenic signalling, patients with hereditary haemorrhagic telangiectasia develop telangiectasias and arteriovenous malformations which cause numerous complications. These complications include moderate-to-severe chronic epistaxis, gastrointestinal bleeding, iron deficiency anemia, and requirement for intravenous iron or red cell transfusion. Additionally, incidence of intracranial haemorrhage is high and morbid non-bleeding complications, such as venous thromboembolism, stroke, and liver disease, are common. Despite this serious disease burden, hereditary haemorrhagic telangiectasia remains without licensed therapies worldwide. However, many novel, investigational agents targeting vascular and haemostatic systems are now rapidly undergoing formal development specifically in hereditary haemorrhagic telangiectasia. These agents include the selective AKT1/AKT2 inhibitor engasertib, AKT1-selective inhibitors ATV-1601 and TER-4480, plasminogen siRNA agent ALN-6400, activin receptor-like kinase 1-bone morphogenetic protein receptor type II (ALK1-BMPRII) bispecific clustering antibody DIAG723, and apelin receptor antagonist antibody TX2100. This comprehensive Review provides essential background information and illustrations summarising relevant hereditary haemorrhagic telangiectasia pathophysiology, followed by focused, detailed discussions of each of the novel agents in development, including the mechanisms, therapeutic rationale, clinical trial programmes, and potential therapeutic effects.

articles.title: Statement of Retraction: Predictors of futile recanalization following mechanical thrombectomy in acute ischemic stroke: a single-center retrospective cohort study.
Postoperative infections after cardiac surgery with cardiopulmonary bypass - incidence, performance of diagnostic procedures, and predictive factors.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: Cardiac surgery using cardiopulmonary bypass (CPB) induces a systemic inflammatory response that affects common inflammatory markers, including C-reactive protein (CRP), white blood cell count (WBC), and body temperature, complicating postoperative diagnosis of infections. The objective of this study was to assess the incidence of postoperative infections and evaluate the performance of clinically used biomarkers.

DESIGN: This was a bidirectional cohort study including patients undergoing cardiac surgery with CPB between 1st of February 2020 and 22nd of September 2021. Patients with postoperative infection were compared to patients without. Multivariable logistic regression was used to identify independent predictors of postoperative infections. Receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curves evaluated the diagnostic ability of current biomarkers to detect infection.

RESULTS: A total of 1,222 patients were included. The incidence of postoperative infections (during hospitalisation and/or late infection) was 17.3%. Patients with postoperative infection had more comorbidities, underwent more complex procedures, and had higher mortality (90-day mortality 3.8% vs 1.5%, p = 0.045; 1-year mortality 5.7% vs 2.7%, p = 0.032). CRP, WBC, and temperature performed poorly in detecting postoperative infection, although peak CRP (OR 1.069, p < 0.001) and peak temperature (OR 2.408, p = 0.005) were independent predictors of postoperative infection. Peak temperature occurred on postoperative day 5 in infected patients versus day 2 in those without infection.

CONCLUSION: Postoperative infections following cardiac surgery with CPB remain common and are associated with increased postoperative complications and mortality. Common inflammatory biomarkers perform poorly in detecting infection. Improved diagnostic tools are needed to facilitate early detection and treatment.

articles.title: Prominent V Waves Augment Right Ventricular Afterload Independent of the Lung Vessels in Heart Failure: Implications for Clinical Assessment of Pulmonary Vascular Disease.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Left atrial (LA) stiffening augments the LA V wave, pressurizing the pulmonary artery (PA) out of proportion to left ventricular end-diastolic pressure. We characterized the pathophysiologic, diagnostic, and clinical implications of LA stiffening, as defined by prominent V waves, in heart failure with preserved ejection fraction.

METHODS: In this retrospective cohort study, patients with heart failure with preserved ejection fraction and less than moderate mitral regurgitation at rest underwent invasive hemodynamic exercise testing. Patients with heightened operant LA stiffening were defined by the PA wedge pressure (PAWP) V wave exceeding mean PAWP by ≥10 mm Hg. A previously used formula for V wave-corrected PAWP was validated against the PAWP waveform pressure-time-area to explore impact of the V wave on transpulmonary pressure gradients. Clinical, echocardiographic, hemodynamic, and outcome data were compared for patients with and without prominent V waves.

RESULTS: Compared with patients without prominent V waves (n=844, 79%), those with prominent V waves (n=225, 21%) were older and more likely to be women, with more severe LA myopathy, evidenced by greater LA volume index (42.2±15.0 versus 32.5±13.0 mL/m2, P<0.001), lower LA reservoir strain (16.4±7.5% versus 23.2±8.3%, P<0.001), more atrial fibrillation (61.3% versus 22.9%, P<0.001), and increased operant LA reservoir stiffness (0.59±0.25 versus 0.23±0.24 mm Hg/mL, P<0.001). Patients with prominent V waves had markedly higher PA systolic pressure than those without (54±16 versus 38±12 mm Hg, P<0.001) despite no difference in end-diastolic PAWP-PA pressure gradient (3±5 versus 3±4 mm Hg, P=0.950). Incorporating the V wave into PAWP improved correlation between directly measured PAWP pressure-time integral compared with mid-A wave PAWP (R2=0.96 versus R2=0.86, P<0.001 for comparison). In patients with prominent V waves, the prevalence of combined pre- and postcapillary pulmonary hypertension decreased from 60.2% to 29.3% after V wave correction for the transpulmonary pressure gradients. Despite similar corrected pulmonary vascular resistances in patients with and without prominent V waves, apparent PA compliance was much lower in patients with prominent V waves (3.03±1.56 versus 4.90±2.27 mL/mm Hg, P<0.001), augmenting right ventricular afterload, and these changes were coupled with more severe right ventricular dysfunction, tricuspid regurgitation, blunted cardiopulmonary exercise reserve, and increased risk of hospitalization for heart failure or death in patients with versus without prominent V waves (adjusted hazard ratio, 2.09 [95% CI, 1.53-2.86]; P<0.001).

CONCLUSIONS: More than 1 in 5 patients with heart failure with preserved ejection fraction display prominent V waves in excess of end-diastolic PAWP. This augments right ventricular afterload due to backward transmission of the V wave, contributing to right heart failure that is independent of the pulmonary vasculature. Failure to account for the V wave during hemodynamic assessment overestimates the severity of pulmonary vascular disease present.

articles.title: Clarifying the Clinical Relevance of V Waves.
Cardiometabolic disease burden and first health-related cessation of work among middle-aged Chinese adults: a longitudinal competing-exit study.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: To examine whether a time-updated count of physician-diagnosed cardiometabolic conditions is associated with first survey-reported health-related cessation of work among adults in China.

METHODS: We analyzed 4,404 participants aged 45-60 years working and neither formally retired nor reporting baseline health-related work disruption in the China Health and Retirement Longitudinal Study. Across three intervals from 2011 to 2018, the exposure was the lagged, time-updated count of physician-diagnosed hypertension, diabetes, heart disease, stroke, and kidney disease. The outcome was first health-related work exit, with retirement, other exit, and death as competing states. The primary association was estimated with discrete-time cause-specific pooled logistic regression, participant-clustered standard errors, and 50 longitudinal imputations.

RESULTS: The cohort contributed 10,852 observed person-periods and 346 health-related work exits. Each additional diagnosed cardiometabolic condition was associated with higher odds of health-related work exit after adjustment for interval, age, sex, education, work type, smoking, alcohol, and body mass index (odds ratio 1.73, 95% confidence interval 1.51-1.97). Estimates were similar across clustering, weighting, and other sensitivity analyses. By Wave 4, standardized cumulative incidence was 6.4%, 10.5%, and 16.6% for condition counts 0, 1, and 2.

CONCLUSIONS: A higher count of physician-diagnosed cardiometabolic conditions was prospectively associated with first survey-reported health-related cessation of work, although residual confounding by unmeasured socioeconomic and job-demand factors cannot be excluded. Replication with adjudicated employment outcomes and cross-cohort validation is needed before policy or causal interpretation.

articles.title: Perfusion quality does not necessarily predict ultrastructural preservation after hyperosmotic brain perfusion.
articles.abstract: Perfusion fixation is widely used in neuroscience to prepare mammalian brain tissue for histological and ultrastructural analysis. Perfusion protocols are commonly assessed using macroscopic indicators such as gross appearance and neuroimaging, which assess the extent to which perfusate has been distributed throughout the brain. There is a critical need to determine to what extent these metrics can accurately predict high-quality ultrastructural preservation, particularly as new perfusion protocols are developed for connectomics. In this technical report, we describe evidence that these two measures can be decoupled by the addition of dehydrating agents to the perfusate solution. In three human brain donors and one canine brain donor perfused with a fixative solution containing 10% mannitol and 10% polyethylene glycol 35 kDa, macroscopic and radiological indicators of perfusion quality appeared adequate or favorable. However, electron microscopy revealed expanded extracellular space, shrunken cellular processes, and distorted cell membranes, consistent with an osmotic shock artifact resulting from severe hyperosmotic dehydration. Similar ultrastructural artifacts were observed in a canine brain donor perfused with 20% mannitol in 20% neutral buffered formalin without PEG. We compare these ultrastructural findings with findings from previously reported cases perfused with standard neutral buffered formalin without osmotic additives. These findings illustrate a risk of optimizing brain perfusion protocols designed to preserve neural circuitry based on macroscopic or radiological perfusion quality metrics alone, since these metrics can be satisfied while the ultrastructure is severely compromised.

articles.title: Development and Validation of a Novel Contact Force-Integrated Pulsed Field Quantization Index for Pulmonary Vein Isolation in a Porcine Model.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: There is no bipolar-specific quantitative ablation index currently available to guide pulsed field ablation (PFA). We aimed to develop and validate a novel contact force (CF)-integrated pulsed field quantization index (PFQI) for real-time lesion depth prediction during bipolar PFA.

METHODS AND RESULTS: In total, 27 healthy Yorkshire swine were included in a two-phase preclinical study. In Phase I, a nonlinear multivariable model was developed to derive a novel PFQI incorporating real-time CF, pulse train number, delivery voltage, and impedance variation. In Phase II, the PFQI was prospectively validated by comparing predicted with actual lesion depth, followed by PFQI-guided circumferential pulmonary vein isolation (PVI). Acute procedural success, 30-day PVI durability, and extracardiac safety were evaluated using serial electroanatomic mapping and blinded histopathological examination. Lesion depth was strongly associated with CF, pulse train number, voltage, and impedance change. The PFQI predicted actual depth with high accuracy (R = 0.94, R2 = 0.88; validation R2 = 0.82, slope = 1.014). In the validation cohort, 92% of predicted depths fell within ±0.75 mm of measured values. PFQI-guided PVI achieved 100% (6/6) acute isolation and 100% 30-day durable electrical isolation, with contiguous transmural fibrosis on histology. No collateral phrenic nerve, esophageal, or pulmonary vein injury occurred, and phrenic capture thresholds remained unchanged.

CONCLUSION: The PFQI is the first bipolar-specific, CF-integrated quantitative metric for PFA, enabling accurate, real-time lesion depth prediction. PFQI-guided PVI achieved consistent, durable, and safe PVI in a porcine model, providing a promising operator-independent quantitative strategy to optimize clinical bipolar PFA for atrial fibrillation.

articles.title: Left Atrial Appendage Closure Versus Oral Anticoagulation for Prevention of Stroke or Systemic Embolism in Patients With Atrial Fibrillation: An Updated Meta-Analysis of 7004 Patients Across Six Randomized Trials.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Left atrial appendage closure (LAAC) is an emerging alternative for stroke prevention in patients with atrial fibrillation (AF) who are unsuitable for long-term oral anticoagulants (OACs). However, its efficacy and safety relative to OACs remain uncertain.

METHODS: Three databases were searched up to April 7, 2026, for randomized controlled trials comparing LAAC with OAC in patients with AF. Risk ratios with 95% confidence intervals were pooled using a random-effects model.

RESULTS: Six RCTs (n = 7004 patients) were analyzed. The risk of stroke or systemic embolism (SSE) did not differ significantly between the LAAC and OAC groups (RR: 1.10 [0.87-1.39]; p = 0.42). The risk of ischemic SSE was significantly increased with LAAC (RR: 1.41 [1.07-1.85]; p = 0.02) compared with OAC. No significant differences were observed in all-cause mortality (RR: 0.94 [0.81-1.09]), cardiovascular mortality (RR: 0.91 [0.69-1.21]), non-cardiovascular mortality (RR: 0.91 [0.75-1.12]), or hemorrhagic stroke (RR: 0.58 [0.29-1.17]). LAAC was associated with a similar risk of overall major bleeding (RR: 0.92 [0.77-1.09]) and low risk of non-procedural bleeding (RR: 0.61 [0.52-0.73]; p < 0.001) compared with OAC. Upon sensitivity analysis comparing LAAC with DOACs, the findings remained consistent across most clinical outcomes.

CONCLUSION: LAAC demonstrates comparable risks of SSE and major bleeding to OACs, but is associated with a higher risk of ischemic SSE and reduced non-procedural bleeding, supporting its use in selected patients at high risk for long-term bleeding while emphasizing individualized shared decision-making.

articles.title: Social Engagement Programs of Area Agencies on Aging: Understanding Efforts to Reduce Social Isolation and Loneliness Among Older Adults.
articles.journal: Journal of applied gerontology : the official journal of the Southern Gerontological Society
articles.abstract: BackgroundSocial isolation and loneliness in later life are major public health concerns associated with increased morbidity and premature mortality. Area Agencies on Aging (AAAs) constitute the primary local infrastructure for aging services in the US.ObjectiveTo describe social engagement program types and partnership structures among AAAs and to examine rural-non-rural differences.MethodsWe analyzed data from the 2025 National Survey of AAAs (n = 449). Descriptive statistics summarized program and partnership prevalence; item-level Pearson chi-square tests with Bonferroni adjustments compared rural and non-rural agencies.ResultsMost AAAs offered multiple social engagement programs; volunteer engagement (66.0%), arts and creative activities (62.2%), visiting/calling programs (57.7%), and technology engagement (55.5%) were common. Non-rural AAAs were more likely to offer visiting/calling, technology-based activities, and memory cafes, while rural AAAs were more likely to partner with public health units. Rural-non-rural differences suggest context-specific influences of resources and infrastructure on program availability.

articles.title: Electrical Alternans With Alternating Left Ventricular Apical Ballooning Mimicking Takotsubo Cardiomyopathy in a Patient With Extreme QT Prolongation.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: We report unique and rare findings of coupled electrical and mechanical alternans in a patient with extreme QT prolongation.

METHODS: A 5-year-old girl with congenital long QT syndrome type 3 developed alternate left ventricular apical ballooning precipitated by mycoplasma pneumonia and azithromycin exposure.

RESULTS: During atrial pacing, electrocardiography showed beat-to-beat alternation not only in T-wave morphology but also in QRS configuration, ST segment, and QT interval. These electrical changes were tightly associated with mechanical alternans: beats with markedly prolonged QT intervals showed normal left ventricular (LV) contraction, whereas beats with shorter QT intervals and ST elevation exhibited LV apical ballooning. Treatment with mexiletine shortened the QT interval, abolished both electrical and mechanical alternans, and restored normal LV function.

CONCLUSIONS: Alternate LV apical ballooning mimicking Takosubo cardiomyopathy can be seen in a patient with extreme QT prolongation. These findings probably reflected a functional intraventricular conduction block due to marked spatial heterogeneity of repolarization between the LV base and apex.

articles.title: Changes in Lead Parameters of Cardiac Implantable Electronic Devices After VT/VF Ablation Using a Dual-Energy Lattice-Tip Catheter.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Interactions between cardiac implantable electronic devices (CIEDs) and pulsed field ablation (PFA) have been studied mainly in the context of atrial ablation, whereas the effects of ventricular ablation using a dual-energy lattice-tip catheter on ventricular leads remain unclear.

METHODS: This retrospective study involved 79 patients (mean age 60.9 ± 13.6 years) with an implantable cardioverter-defibrillator or cardiac resynchronization therapy defibrillator who underwent ventricular ablation using a lattice-tip catheter between February 2024 and November 2025. Pacing thresholds were assessed before, immediately after, and 3 months after ablation and standardized to a pulse width of 0.4 ms using the Lapicque-Weiss model. Marked acute threshold elevation was defined as an increase in pacing threshold of ≥ 1.0 V immediately after ablation. The anatomical relationship between ablation sites and ventricular lead locations was assessed based on the American Heart Association 17-segment model of the left ventricle and classified as corresponding when ablation involved the same or opposing ventricular region as the lead location, adjacent when ablation involved a directly adjacent region, and remote otherwise.

RESULTS: Marked acute pacing-threshold elevation occurred in 5 of 79 right ventricular (RV) leads (6.3%) and 2 of 22 evaluable left ventricular (LV) leads (9.1%). For RV leads, marked threshold elevation occurred in 4 of 14 patients (28.6%) in the corresponding group, 1 of 19 (5.3%) in the adjacent group, and none of 46 (0%) in the remote group. When threshold change was analyzed as a continuous variable, the acute increase was significantly greater in the corresponding group (+ 0.74 V; 95%CI 0.465-1.018) than in the adjacent (+ 0.31 V; 95%CI 0.076-0.550) and remote (+ 0.007 V; 95%CI - 0.145-0.160) groups. For LV leads, the pacing threshold increased significantly after ablation involving the corresponding segment (+ 0.71 V; 95%CI 0.167-1.245), although the overall association between anatomical relationship and threshold change was not significant. At 3 months, pacing thresholds in the corresponding groups were not significantly different from baseline for either RV or LV leads.

CONCLUSION: Marked acute pacing-threshold elevation was observed in both RV and LV leads after ventricular arrhythmia ablation using a dual-energy lattice-tip catheter. However, both RV and LV thresholds were no longer significantly different from baseline at 3 months. These findings suggest the importance of considering the anatomical relationship between ablation sites and CIED leads and of careful peri-procedural assessment of lead function during ventricular ablation.

articles.title: Borrowing-dependent estimands in external-control trials: Identification, efficiency, and sensitivity in survival analysis.
articles.abstract: Augmenting randomised trials with external controls is increasingly common in oncology and rare diseases. This paper reviews the methodology of externally controlled trials - estimands, identification assumptions, estimation, efficiency and sensitivity analysis - for right-censored survival outcomes, and organises it around a single question: what quantity does a borrowing analysis actually deliver? We distinguish the intended estimand, fixed in advance by the clinical question and the target population, from the borrowing-dependent estimand, the quantity to which a given borrowing rule is consistent. The two coincide under source-conditional exchangeability and separate otherwise, so that the borrowing-dependent estimand names, and makes estimable, a discrepancy that is otherwise reported only as unquantified bias. Within a nonparametric potential-outcomes framework we (i) define borrowing-weighted causal contrasts indexed by a weighting kernel and set out when such a contrast is, and is not, a scientifically meaningful target in its own right; (ii) establish nonparametric identification and derive the efficient influence function; (iii) construct a doubly robust, locally efficient estimator with n-consistency; (iv) introduce a sensitivity-analysis framework yielding closed-form bias bounds, E-values, and tipping points; and (v) characterise the sensitivity of the delivered estimand to the pre-specified borrowing rule via Fréchet differentiability. Simulations across 12 factorial scenarios confirm up to 49% RMSE reduction under compatibility, show that the estimators remain unbiased for the borrowing-dependent estimand when compatibility fails, and validate the sensitivity bounds. A worked example in metastatic colorectal cancer illustrates the complete analytical workflow.

articles.title: [Principles of treating patients with chronic obstructive pulmonary disease].
articles.abstract: Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) is a heterogeneous condition characterized by inflammation of the airways and lung parenchyma, manifested by persistent respiratory symptoms such as dyspnoe and cough. As a global pandemic, it affects approximately 10.3% of the population over the age of 40 and remains among the leading causes of death with an increasing mortality trend. In Hungary, the estimated actual prevalence is approximately three times higher than the number of officially registered cases. COPD imposes a significant economic burden, primarily driven by the hospital care required for acute exacerbations. The systemic consequences of chronic inflammation contribute to the development of frequent comorbidities, such as atherosclerosis and heart failure. The primary objectives in managing stable COPD are symptom reduction, improvement of quality of life, and the prevention of disease progression. The cornerstones of therapy include smoking cessation, maintenance inhalation pharmacotherapy, and various non-pharmacological interventions. The latter encompasses appropriately indicated pulmonary rehabilitation, long-term oxygen therapy, and non-invasive ventilation, as well as lung volume reduction interventions and lung transplantation in selected cases. The selection of optimal, individualized therapy combined with high patient adherence significantly improves survival rates. Orv Hetil. 2026; 167(41): 1639-1645.

articles.title: [Successful treatment of hypokalemic cardiac arrest with massive potassium replacement in a patient with Bricker urinary diversion].
articles.abstract: Severe hypokalemia is a rare but potentially reversible cause of malignant arrhythmias and cardiac arrest. Early recognition of significant fluid, electrolyte, and acid-base disturbances in patients with intestinal urinary diversion may be life-saving. We present the clinical course of a 55-year-old woman who developed severe hyperchloremic metabolic acidosis and extreme hypokalemia following prolonged vomiting and high-output fluid loss through a Bricker ureteroileocutaneostomy. The patient was admitted to the intensive care unit in a peri-arrest condition, where cardiac arrest occurred shortly thereafter. The monitored rhythm was ventricular fibrillation alternating with "torsade de pointes" ventricular fibrillation. During advanced life support, targeted high-dose intravenous potassium replacement, magnesium sulfate administration, and bicarbonate substitution were performed. A total of 120 mL of 7.4% potassium chloride was administered during resuscitation, resulting in return of spontaneous circulation after approximately 18 minutes. During the first 24 hours, a total of 460 mmol potassium chloride replacement was required. Following the return of spontaneous circulation, intermittent hemodialysis was performed to correct severe metabolic acidosis. During subsequent intensive care treatment, sepsis and bilateral pneumonia developed; however, with targeted antimicrobial therapy, organ support, and continuous electrolyte correction, the patient's condition gradually improved. Successful extubation was performed on day 7, and the patient was transferred back to the nephrology ward with favourable neurological outcome. This case highlights that rapidly developing severe hypokalaemia and metabolic acidosis in patients with Bricker urinary diversion may lead to malignant arrhythmias and cardiac arrest; however, prompt recognition of reversible metabolic abnormalities and aggressive targeted potassium replacement can be life-saving. Orv Hetil. 2026; 167(41): 1664-1668.

articles.title: [Atypical cutaneous manifestations of B19 parvovirus infection in children].
articles.abstract: The most well-known skin manifestation of human parvovirus B19 infection is erythema infectiosum, also known as fifth disease. In atypical cases, particularly among young adults, purpuric-petechial glove-and-sock syndrome (PPGSS) is observed, which is a condition characterized by a symmetrical distribution in the acral areas. Its onset is attributed to the active viremia phase; therefore, patients exhibiting symptoms are contagious, which is of particular importance in the case of immunocompromised individuals and pregnant women. In our report, we present three cases: in two patients, the skin manifestations appeared as an atypical petechial-purpuric exanthem, while in the third child, they manifested as pityriasis rosea; to our knowledge, the parvovirus-associated form of this condition has not been described in the literature to date. During laboratory testing, in addition to typical abnormalities, we observed monocytosis in the blood counts of all three patients. Detecting the virus or the virus-specific antibody response is a highly challenging, comprehensive microbiological task in which molecular tests play a key role alongside serological tests. With our cases, we wish to draw attention to the rising prevalence of diseases caused by parvovirus B19, the periodic clusters and small outbreaks, the appearance of unusual skin symptoms, and the difficulties in detecting the virus. Orv Hetil. 2026; 167(41): 1669-1675.

articles.title: Pulmonary Artery Approach for Radiofrequency Catheter Ablation of Atrial Tachycardia Originating From Left Atrial Post Wall: A Case Report.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Due to limitations in ablation energy delivery and myocardial wall thickness, endocardial ablation of atrial tachycardia can sometimes be challenging.

METHODS AND RESULTS: In this case, ablation of the left atrial posterior wall shifted the earliest endocardial breakthrough site from the posterior wall to the roof, suggesting a potential epicardial origin near left atrial roof. The atrial arrhythmia was successfully eliminated via a right pulmonary artery approach.

CONCLUSION: The right pulmonary artery approach may be an effective strategy for ablating epicardial atrial arrhythmias, particularly those originating from the left atrial posterior roof.

articles.title: The Curse of Black Sigatoka: A Backward Bifurcation Perspective.
articles.abstract: Black Sigatoka disease (BSD), also known as black leaf streak disease, is an airborne fungal infection caused by Pseudocercospora fijiensis that severely impacts global banana and plantain production. Its persistence and resistance to eradication make it one of the most challenging plant diseases to manage. In this paper, we propose a deterministic pathogen-host model to describe BSD dynamics. Due to dual transmission pathways (ascospores and conidia) and mate limitation in sexual reproduction, the model exhibits a backward bifurcation: a stable endemic equilibrium coexists with the disease-free equilibrium for certain parameter values in which the basic reproduction number, R 0  , is less than 1. This phenomenon explains why control strategies that solely reduce R 0  below one may fail. For the backward bifurcation regime, we perform sensitivity analysis of the endemic equilibrium using normalized forward sensitivity indices, Latin Hypercube Sampling, and Partial Rank Correlation Coefficients. Results indicate that effective control must extend beyond R 0  reduction and prioritize (1) limiting production of new susceptible leaves during high-risk periods and (2) developing and deploying disease-resistant plant varieties. To incorporate transmission variability, we also formulate a stochastic version of the model using the Stochastic Simulation Algorithm (SSA). Extensive numerical simulations compare stochastic realizations with deterministic predictions and quantify variability in disease dynamics. To identify the principal drivers of persistence and variability, we analyze the endemic equilibrium using Sobol's variance-based sensitivity method, which highlights the role of nonlinear parameter interactions in shaping variability.

articles.title: Sustainable iodine contrast media for a healthy future (SUSTAINED): a global survey of practice.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: To investigate healthcare professionals' knowledge, attitudes, and practices (KAPs) of the environmental impact and sustainability of iodinated contrast media (ICM).

MATERIALS AND METHODS: A cross-sectional web-based survey was distributed to members of professional societies and advertised via social media between June and December 2024. The questionnaire covered themes including sustainability attitudes, reduction strategies, waste management, patient awareness, and institutional policies. Data were analysed using descriptive statistics, chi-square tests, and analysis of variance (ANOVA).

RESULTS: 231 respondents from 44 countries completed the survey, primarily diagnostic radiographers (59%) and radiologists (38%). Most respondents (60%) reported that their institutions had sustainable ICM policies, and there was a significant association between institutional size and alignment with sustainability goals    X 2  = 14.2 , p = 0.003   . Adoption of reduction strategies such as protocol optimisation, saline chasers, and multi-patient systems varied significantly across institutions    X 2  = 18.5 , p = 0.001   , with younger professionals (25-44 years) more engaged  A N O V A , F = 5.62 , p = 0.001   . Respondents reported waste management practices being inconsistently applied, with 26% of respondents reporting "never engaging"    X 2  = 19.6 , p  <  0.001   . Patient awareness was perceived as low, 47% "strongly disagreeing" that patients understood the environmental impact of ICM use    X 2  = 16.9 , p = 0.002   . Variability in KAPs across European countries was minimal    s 2  = 0.0068   .

CONCLUSIONS: This survey highlights widespread professional awareness of ICM sustainability issues but reveals variability in institutional practices, limited patient awareness, and inconsistent waste management. Findings emphasise the importance of stronger institutional policies, targeted education, and international collaboration to promote sustainable ICM use.

KEY POINTS: Question How do healthcare professionals perceive and implement sustainable practices in the use of iodinated contrast media (ICM) within clinical practice? Findings While many institutions endorse sustainability, notable gaps exist in waste management, patient and practitioner education, and consistency of reduction strategies. Critical relevance statement Strengthening institutional frameworks and professional and patient engagement can enhance sustainable ICM use, safeguard resources, and mitigate environmental impact.

articles.title: Time-Dependent Prognostic Value of the sCD25-to-Ferritin Ratio in Chronic Active Epstein-Barr Virus-Associated Hemophagocytic Lymphohistiocytosis.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Chronic active Epstein-Barr virus infection (CAEBV) is an EBV-positive T/NK-cell lymphoproliferative disease characterized by persistent EBV infection in T or NK cells. CAEBV-HLH refers to hemophagocytic lymphohistiocytosis secondary to CAEBV. As important markers of HLH activity, soluble CD25 (sCD25) and serum ferritin reflect lymphocyte activation and macrophage-mediated inflammation, respectively. The sCD25-to-ferritin ratio may therefore integrate information between the underlying EBV-driven T/NK-cell lymphoproliferative process and HLH-related hyperinflammation. Considering the heterogeneous clinical course varying over time, we evaluated the time-dependent prognostic value of baseline sCD25/ferritin in CAEBV-HLH.

METHODS: This multicenter retrospective study included 108 patients with CAEBV-HLH diagnosed between January 2015 and February 2026. Baseline sCD25/ferritin was calculated at diagnosis. All-cause mortality within the first year was assessed across cumulative monthly follow-up. Time-restricted Cox regression and time-dependent receiver operating characteristic (ROC) analysis were performed to evaluate prognostic association and discriminative performance over time. The optimal cutoff was determined using the Youden Index, and the AUC was validated by bootstrap resampling (1000 iterations) to correct for optimism bias. Survival was compared by Kaplan-Meier analysis. The discriminative performance of the sCD25/Fer ratio was further compared against the existing HScore using DeLong's test for paired ROC curves. Analyses were repeated in patients who did not undergo hematopoietic stem cell transplantation (HSCT).

RESULTS: During follow-up censored at 12 months, 43 (39.81%) deaths occurred. Baseline sCD25/ferritin was significantly higher in non-survivors than in survivors (P = 0.002). In the overall cohort, the sCD25/ferritin was significantly associated with mortality from month 3 onward (HR, 1.23; 95% CI, 1.02-1.47), with stable estimates through 12 months. The 4-month window was selected as an early clinically informative time point, with an AUC of 0.705 in conventional ROC analysis. A cutoff of 27.98 stratified the overall cohort into distinct survival groups (P < 0.001). In the non-HSCT subgroup, predictive performance became significant from month 4 onward, and the 4-month AUC increased to 0.766, with a cutoff of 22.80. Notably, sCD25/Ferritin ratio significantly outperformed the conventional HScore for 4-month mortality prediction (AUC 0.730 vs. 0.584; P = 0.022 by DeLong's test), with consistent superiority in the non-HSCT subgroup (AUC 0.768 vs. 0.597; P = 0.029).

CONCLUSIONS: The baseline sCD25/ferritin ratio is a disease-relevant biomarker in CAEBV-HLH. Its prognostic value became statistically significant from month 3 onward and was more pronounced in patients without HSCT, indicating that this ratio may better reflect the natural disease course when outcomes are less influenced by transplantation.

articles.title: Necroptosis as a key player in cervical cancer progression and management: a systematic review and transcriptomic cross-study consensus analysis.
articles.journal: Apoptosis : an international journal on programmed cell death
articles.abstract: Immunotherapy has improved outcomes for a subset of patients with locally advanced cervical cancer. However, many tumors remain immunologically "cold" and fail to respond. Strategies that enhance tumor immunogenicity are therefore of increasing interest. Necroptosis, a regulated form of inflammatory cell death, has emerged as a potential mechanism capable of promoting the anti-tumor immune responses through the release of damage-associated molecular patterns and enhanced antigen presentation. In this study, we performed a systematic review and transcriptomic cross-study consensus analysis of all studies carried out describing the role and mechanisms of necroptosis occurrence in cervical cancers. We analyzed all published necroptosis-related prognostic gene signatures and integrated these findings into an exploratory transcriptomic analyses to identify mechanistic insights into interlinked biological pathways, and potential therapeutic targets. Following PRISMA guidelines, we analyzed seven published prognostic models, from studies using RNA sequencing and least absolute shrinkage and selection operator (LASSO)-based feature selection to generate a prognostic risk score for patients. We then conducted a comparative analyses of eight overlapping genes and their reported risk score coefficients. Across studies, seven necroptosis-related genes were identified, many of which are functionally linked to mitochondrial transport and permeability regulation, reactive oxygen species (ROS) generation, and inflammatory signaling. Overall, our findings support a key role for necroptosis in cervical cancer, where activation thereof is generally associated with enhanced immune infiltration and activation; thereby improved prognosis. These findings position necroptosis as a promising target for combination therapy strategies aimed at converting immunologically "cold" tumors into more responsive phenotypes. By integrating published signatures with exploratory analyses, we identify potential avenues to modulate necroptotic signaling in ways that may enhance synergy with immunotherapies, and have synthesized a hypothetical cell signaling and interaction diagram. Collectively, this work provides a foundation for future experimental validation and therapeutic development.

articles.title: An update on neuro-otology and neuro-ophthalmology - focusing on new developments in the last three years.
articles.abstract: Vertigo, dizziness, and imbalance are among the most frequent presenting symptoms in primary care and in the emergency department (ED). The clinical diagnosis is based on a structured patient history and bedside examination of the vestibular system and the ocular motor system, looking especially for central ocular motor signs. Recent guidelines, such as the GRACE-3 guideline on acute vertigo and dizziness, the increasing availability of bedside diagnostic algorithms, and the use of quantitative vestibular and ocular motor testing in both the ED-setting and in the outpatient center have facilitated and standardized the approach to the dizzy patient. Here we review recent developments in neuro-otology and neuro-ophthalmology, covering the period after the latest neuro-otology update was published in this journal in 2023. Both new-onset acute, episodic and chronic vestibular conditions are discussed separately, highlighting advancements in disease characterization, diagnostic criteria, and treatment strategies. While major progress has been made in terms of the pathophysiology, etiology, genetics, and diagnostic criteria of peripheral, central, and functional vestibular diseases as well as ocular motor disorders, this knowledge has to be transferred into clinical practice. Systematic teaching of doctors to increase knowledge and to improve skills in applying the different tests in clinical practice on a high level are identified challenges. In terms of treatment, there is still a very great need for state-of-the art clinical trials applying approved therapies.

articles.title: Methotrexate in Still's Disease: An Updated Perspective on Efficacy and Safety.
articles.abstract: The EULAR/PreS and American College of Rheumatology (ACR) guidelines for Still's disease (SD) were recently published with new therapeutic management strategies to achieve therapeutic targets within a specified timeframe. The early use of interleukin (IL)-1 or IL-6 inhibitors associated with short-term corticosteroids is recommended. Methotrexate (MTX) is not recommended as initial monotherapy for the acute systemic phase and should not be considered an alternative to early cytokine-targeted therapy when biologic treatment is available. Nevertheless, observational and real-world studies retain clinical utility of MTX as a corticosteroid-sparing agent with a favorable safety profile particularly in adult patients with residual arthritis and preserved organ function. Beyond its well-known immunomodulatory effects, MTX has been hypothesized to influence IL-1-related inflammatory pathways; however, this hypothesis is extrapolated from other inflammatory diseases, and no SD-specific mechanistic study has directly demonstrated an IL-1-mediated therapeutic effect of MTX. Reported remission rates varied according to the therapeutic regimen and study definition and should therefore be interpreted cautiously. In settings where access to biologic agents is limited, MTX may also represent a pragmatic therapeutic option, although this use reflects healthcare constraints rather than evidence of equivalence to IL-1 or IL-6 inhibition. In children with SD, MTX is mainly used for residual arthritis or as a steroid-sparing agent after control of systemic inflammation. Moreover, combining MTX with biologic agents may provide additional benefit in selected patients with residual arthritis or corticosteroid dependence. This review provides an updated perspective on the efficacy and safety of MTX in SD, with particular emphasis on its complementary role within the current biologic-first therapeutic landscape.

articles.title: Perinatal Outcomes of Pleuro-Amniotic Shunting in Isolated Pleural Effusions: Systematic Review and Meta-analysis.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Pleuro-amniotic shunting has been proposed for fetal pleural effusion, although its safety and efficacy remain uncertain. Therefore, we aimed to evaluate the perinatal outcomes of the fetal therapy for isolated pleural effusion through a systematic review and single-arm meta-analysis.

METHODS: PubMed/MEDLINE, Embase, Scopus, and Cochrane Central were searched for studies reporting outcomes of fetuses undergoing pleuro-amniotic shunting for isolated pleural effusion. The primary outcomes were overall survival and resolution of fetal hydrops. Single-arm random-effects meta-analyses were performed to estimate pooled event rates with 95% confidence intervals (CI).

RESULTS: Ten retrospective cohort studies comprising 416 fetuses treated with pleuro-amniotic shunting were included. The pooled overall survival rate was 65.36% (95% CI 59.46-70.83; I2 = 30.7%). Resolution of fetal hydrops occurred in 62.25% of cases (95% CI 54.27-69.62; I2 = 0%). A total of 62 catheter displacements were recorded, corresponding to a combined prevalence of 17.13% (95% CI 13.59-21.36). Overall, there were 155 preterm births, resulting in a pooled prevalence of 69.67% (95% CI 61.24-76.95; I2 = 26.9%). Preterm premature rupture of membranes (PPROM) prevalence was 17.65% (95% CI 7.78-35.28; I2 = 84.5%; p < 0.001).

CONCLUSION: Pleuro-amniotic shunting achieves overall survival in approximately two-thirds of treated fetuses and resolving fetal hydrops in most cases. However, the procedure may be associated with preterm birth and PROM, underscoring the need for multidisciplinary perinatal management. Although the evidence is limited, these findings support pleuro-amniotic shunting as a promising treatment for progressive isolated fetal pleural effusion and highlight the need for prospective studies to optimize patient selection and perinatal care.

articles.title: Pharmacogenomics of cancer therapy-related cardiomyopathy in childhood cancer survivors.
articles.abstract: Cancer therapy-related cardiomyopathy (CTR-cardiomyopathy) is the leading noncancer late effect contributing to morbidity and mortality among adult survivors of childhood cancer. Anthracycline chemotherapy and thoracic radiotherapy are the primary treatment-related risk factors. However, substantial variability among similarly treated individuals highlights the role of germline genetic susceptibility. This review summarizes pharmacogenomic evidence for CTR-cardiomyopathy and the integration of genetic and clinical risk factors for individualized risk prediction. We searched PubMed through July 2026 for studies examining the molecular underpinnings and risk prediction in these survivors. Candidate gene studies identified associations across pathways involved in drug transport (ABCC1, ABCC2, SLC28A3), metabolism (CBR3), oxidative stress (SOD2, CYBA, NCF4), DNA damage response (RARG, XRCC5, MGMT), and inflammation (P2RX7). Genome-wide studies have identified additional loci, including HAS3, ancestry-specific signals (PHTF1/MAGI3, AGBL1), and a doxorubicin-specific locus (KCNK17). Despite progress, barriers to clinical implementation remain, including heterogeneous phenotype definitions, limited replication, especially in non-European populations, and lack of prospectively validated risk models. Integration of multi-omics approaches may improve detection of subclinical cardiac injury. Ultimately, combining polygenic and other omic risk scores with clinical factors and validating these models prospectively across diverse populations will be essential for advancing precision survivorship care.

articles.title: A grounded theory of compassionate care among clinical nurses.
articles.abstract: BackgroundCompassionate care is a core ethical obligation in nursing, yet the processes through which nurses enact and sustain it remain insufficiently theorized. Existing grounded theory models have not examined an East Asian care context in which nursing staff may assume both clinical and daily living care.Research question/aim/objectivesHow do clinical nurses experience, construct, and sustain compassionate care, and what ethical challenges shape this process?Research designA grounded theory design following Strauss and Corbin was employed. Semi-structured interviews were analysed using open, axial, and selective coding with constant comparison. Ethics of care and moral distress served as sensitizing concepts, while categories were generated inductively. Trustworthiness followed Lincoln and Guba's criteria.Participants and research contextParticipants were thirteen female nurses from tertiary and secondary hospitals in South Korea, working across intensive care, hospice and palliative care, general and haematology wards, and emergency settings (mean clinical experience 14.9 years). Interviews were conducted from July 2020 to February 2021 during the COVID-19 pandemic.Ethical considerationsInstitutional Review Board approval was obtained, and all participants provided written informed consent.Findings/resultsThe core category-comprehensive care grounded in an understanding of the illness trajectory-described compassionate nursing as a practice in which anticipating where a patient stands in the illness course shaped responses to present and emerging needs. Workload and time pressure constrained compassionate engagement, while collegial support helped nurses sustain it. Professional fulfilment and emotional depletion appeared as consequences that could influence subsequent care.ConclusionsCompassionate care was shaped by the integration of clinical understanding, relational engagement, and organizational conditions. Sustaining this practice may require workload governance and structured collegial support rather than reliance on individual resilience alone.

articles.title: A cross-sectional study of transplant clinicians' moral distress and grit.
articles.abstract: BackgroundWhen transplant clinicians encounter ethical challenges and are constrained by their institution from acting in a manner within their professional ethical obligations, they may experience moral distress. Moral distress has been associated with negative effects such as burnout and turnover. Conversely, high grit has been positively correlated with job satisfaction, job performance, and organizational commitment.Research questionsWhat is the level of grit and moral distress among transplant clinicians? What correlations between demographics, grit, moral distress, and intent to leave exist among transplant clinicians?Research designThis cross-sectional study was conducted from October 2024 through March 2025. Three instruments, an investigator-developed demographic survey, the 12-Item Grit Scale, and the Measure of Moral Distress for Healthcare Professionals, were used to capture transplant clinician's grit and level of moral distress. Data were analyzed using descriptive statistics, Pearson correlation, and generalized structural equation modeling.Participants and research contextThe target population for this study consisted of organ transplant clinicians (e.g., surgeons, physicians, coordinators, advanced practice providers, nurses, and allied health team members) in the United States.Ethical considerationsEthics review and approval was obtained prior to subject recruitment.ResultsAmong 101 transplant clinicians, higher moral distress was observed in those with advanced education, frequent ethical challenges, and specific transplant roles (e.g., advanced practice providers, physicians, multi-organ), while grit remained consistent across demographic and clinical factors. Generalized structural equation modeling suggests a potential mediating role between clinician characteristics (education), workforce factors (frequent ethical issues and specific transplant roles), and turnover intentions.ConclusionTransplant clinicians who experience moral distress frequently and at high intensity may express an intent to leave their role regardless of their level of grit. Healthcare organizations must create targeted interventions and resources to mitigate moral distress and support transplant clinicians who experience moral distressing events.

articles.title: RETRACTION: Prospective Study of the Effect of Maternal Body Mass Index on Labor Progress in Nulliparous Women in Egypt.
articles.journal: International journal of gynaecology and obstetrics: the official organ of the International Federation of Gynaecology and Obstetrics
articles.abstract: A.M. Maged, D.S. Belal, H.M. Marie, H. Rashwan, S. Abdelaziz, A. A. Gabr, and A.R. Elzayat, "Prospective Study of the Effect of Maternal Body Mass Iwndex on Labor Progress in Nulliparous Women in Egypt," International Journal of Gynecology & Obstetrics 139, no. 3 (2017): 329-335, 10.1002/ijgo.12322. The above article, published online on 08 September 2017 in Wiley Online Library (wileyonlinelibrary.com) has been retracted by agreement between the journal Editor-in-Chief, Michael Geary; and John Wiley & Sons Ltd. Concerns were raised on PubPeer [1] that the reported p-values in Table 1 are not consistent with the reported summary statistics, including maternal age, maternal height, and pregnancy duration at admission. When the editorial team re-calculated the p-values, they showed a very high statistical significance, as opposed to the non-significance presented in the article. The publisher asked the authors to clarify these inconsistencies and provide the raw data for the study. The authors did not provide the requested data as the study was conducted more than 10 years ago, but responded to the concerns by acknowledging that there may have been errors in reporting, including the cervical dilation measurements, the p-values, and the sub-group data. Without the study data to clarify and correct further, the Editor-in-Chief has lost confidence in the reported data and conclusions. Therefore, a retraction is warranted. [1] J. Thornton, and N. Brown "Prospective Study of the Effect of Maternal Body Mass Index on Labor Progress in Nulliparous Women in Egypt," PubPeer, May 2024-May 2026, https://pubpeer.com/publications/850968C31F9E584350E0445D5A5BEC.

articles.title: The chicken or the egg? Unravelling the role of vascular remodelling in HFpEF.
Metabolic stress exacerbates Ca2+ dysregulation and arrhythmias in catecholaminergic polymorphic ventricular tachycardia.
articles.abstract: Catecholaminergic polymorphic ventricular tachycardia (CPVT) is a genetic arrhythmic syndrome caused by mutations in the sarcoplasmic reticulum (SR) calcium (Ca2+) release channel RyR2 or its accessory proteins, including calsequestrin-2 (CASQ2). RyR2 dysfunction or leak is the hallmark feature of CPVT and directly triggers arrhythmias. Despite this electrical instability, CPVT hearts are typically anatomically normal and lack pathological remodelling. Therefore, we hypothesized that introducing additional stressors, such as metabolic stress, would worsen cardiac arrhythmias and potentially trigger pathological remodelling. To test this hypothesis, metabolic stress was introduced by crossbreeding a CPVT model of CASQ2-/- mice with the Akita mouse, a genetic model of diabetes that also lacks cardiac remodelling. We found that dysregulation of myocyte Ca2+ handling was exacerbated in Akita-CASQ2-/- cells, which exhibited slower Ca2+ transient decay kinetics and increased arrhythmogenic Ca2+ waves. Akita-CASQ2-/- mice also displayed more severe arrhythmias, diastolic dysfunction, and cardiac hypertrophy, but without evidence of fibrosis, cell death, or worsened metabolic dysfunction. Finally, mitochondrial reactive oxygen species production was increased in Akita-CASQ2-/- cardiomyocytes, which may contribute to the more severe pathological phenotype. Overall, our results suggest that metabolic stress can aggravate dysregulated myocyte Ca2+ handling and promote cardiac dysfunction in CPVT hearts.

articles.title: Clinical burden and outcomes of pediatric carbapenem-resistant Klebsiella pneumoniae bloodstream infections in a tertiary care center.
articles.journal: European journal of clinical microbiology & infectious diseases : official publication of the European Society of Clinical Microbiology
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Carbapenem-resistant Klebsiella pneumoniae (CRKP) is an emerging threat in pediatric healthcare settings because of limited treatment options and high morbidity and mortality. However, data regarding pediatric CRKP bloodstream infection (BSI) remain limited. This study aimed to evaluate the clinical characteristics and outcomes of CRKP BSI in children.

METHODS: A retrospective cohort study was conducted among children hospitalized with Klebsiella pneumoniae BSI between 2020 and 2025. Demographic characteristics, healthcare exposures, laboratory findings, antimicrobial therapy, and clinical outcomes were analyzed.

RESULTS: A total of 86 children were included; the median age was 12 months, and 50% were male. Overall, 91.9% had at least one underlying comorbidity, 89.5% had a history of previous hospitalization, 83.3% had prior antibiotic usage, and 25.9% had undergone surgical intervention. During the index hospitalization, 57.0% required intensive care unit admission and 77.6% had at least one invasive device. Fifteen children (17.4%) had CRKP BSI. Prior carbapenem exposure and longer antibiotic use were more frequent in the CRKP group, although the differences were not statistically significant. White blood cell, neutrophil, lymphocyte, and platelet counts were significantly lower in patients with CRKP BSI. Three-month mortality was 40.0% in the CRKP group and 15.9% in the CSKP group, with no statistically significant difference (p = 0.069). Length of hospital stay was also similar between the groups.

CONCLUSION: CRKP accounted for 17.4% of K. pneumoniae BSIs in this pediatric cohort. No independent factor associated with carbapenem resistance was identified. The small number of CRKP cases limited the statistical power of the study. Larger multicenter studies are needed to better define factors associated with CRKP and its clinical outcomes in children.

articles.title: Food-Associated Kounis Syndrome: Clinical Spectrum and Diagnostic Considerations from a Case Report and Systematic Qualitative Synthesis of Published Cases.
articles.abstract: Kounis syndrome (KS) is a hypersensitivity-associated acute coronary syndrome. Food-associated KS remains poorly characterized, and its clinical presentation may be mimicked by non-immune food-related toxic reactions. To characterize the food exposures, clinical and cardiovascular presentations, allergological assessment, potential cofactors, KS phenotypes, management, and outcomes reported in food-associated KS. PubMed, Scopus, and Web of Science Core Collection were searched from inception to August 22, 2026. Original case reports, case series, and sufficiently informative conference reports describing objective coronary involvement temporally associated with a food or food-derived exposure were included. Patient-level data were synthesized qualitatively. KS diagnostic certainty, coronary phenotype, food causality, and presumed mechanism were assessed separately. Planned sensitivity analyses restricted the synthesis to confirmed or suspected food allergy, definite or probable KS, and cases without epinephrine administration before coronary onset or its first objective documentation. The synthesis included 50 publications or reports describing 53 unique patients. Food-related mechanisms comprised confirmed food allergy in 20 patients, clinically suspected food allergy in 26, scombroid poisoning in six, and a Coprinopsis atramentaria-alcohol interaction in one. The reported coronary spectrum ranged from transient vasospasm and nonobstructive presentations to plaque-related myocardial infarction, native-coronary thrombosis, and stent or graft thrombosis. Type I was the most frequently assigned phenotype. Allergological assessment, paired acute and baseline tryptase measurements, treatment chronology, and long-term follow-up were inconsistently reported. The main cardiovascular patterns remained broadly consistent across the planned sensitivity analyses. Food-associated KS encompasses a heterogeneous spectrum of allergic coronary presentations. Clinically similar non-immune food-related toxic reactions, including scombroid poisoning, should be recognized as differential diagnoses and analyzed separately from true allergic KS. Diagnosis requires integration of exposure chronology, objective cardiovascular findings, coronary substrate, allergological evidence, potential cofactors, and competing exposures. Intramuscular epinephrine remains the first-line treatment for anaphylaxis, and temporal precedence should not be interpreted as evidence that epinephrine caused the coronary event.

articles.title: From young aces to injury cases: a qualitative study of stakeholder perspectives on injury risk in junior to elite badminton.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Competitive badminton is associated with a considerable burden of injuries, particularly during the transition from junior to elite level (ages 16-20). While the sport's dynamic stroke and movement patterns may contribute to injury risk, the factors stakeholders use to assess injury vulnerability remain poorly understood. However, identifying specific causes and indicators that point to an increased risk of injury is essential for prevention. Given the limited case numbers, combining data driven approaches with stakeholders' experiential knowledge may enhance risk assessment. This study explores expert judgement and heuristics regarding injury risk assessment as well as options for risk mitigation during the transitional phase.

METHODS: Twenty semi-structured in-person interviews were conducted with national-level stakeholders (9 coaches, 5 athletes, 2 association doctors, 2 physiotherapists, 2 strength and conditioning coaches) between October 2023 and July 2024. The interviews had an average duration of 54.4 min. Thematic analysis helped identify common patterns across assessments.

RESULTS: Four higher-order themes were identified: Excessive pressure, recovery deficits, unprofessional attitude, and disruptions in training continuity. Six cue families were perceived by stakeholders as informing injury risk assessment: signs of over-motivation, unprofessional attitude, the coaches' subjective perception ('coaches' eye'), upheavals in private life, exposure and signs of wear. While overlaps with the literature were found, stakeholders often downplayed commonly cited objective factors like injury history. Many cues were based on intuitive, experience-driven judgments and were therefore difficult to standardize or quantify.

CONCLUSIONS: Experts relied on relative risk judgments shaped by experience and situational impressions rather than absolute probabilities. Integrating these practitioner-derived qualitative cues with objective data may enhance context-sensitive injury risk assessment during the junior-to-elite transition. By making experiential heuristics more transparent, the findings offer a foundation for developing more targeted injury mitigation strategies in this critical developmental phase. Further empirical validation is required.

articles.title: Consensus-based perspectives on integrating IPX203 into Parkinson's disease management.
articles.abstract: Motor fluctuations are a common and burdensome complication of Parkinson's disease (PD) when the disease progresses, largely driven by the short half-life and variable absorption of immediate-release (IR) levodopa. IPX203 is a next-generation modified-release levodopa/carbidopa formulation that delivers rapid onset and sustained plasma levodopa concentrations through IR granules and extended-release pellets. Clinical studies have shown that IPX203 increases Good ON time (ON time without dyskinesia plus ON time with non-troublesome dyskinesia, equivalent to ON time without troublesome dyskinesia), reduces OFF time and improves motor symptom control compared with IR levodopa/carbidopa. In anticipation of the introduction of IPX203 in Europe, nine PD specialists convened to develop consensus recommendations for its use in clinical practice. Through a structured process incorporating predefined statements, voting and moderated discussion, the group reached high levels of agreement (88.9% to 100%) across seven topics. These included defining motor symptoms control, identifying patients most likely to benefit from IPX203, positioning of IPX203 within the treatment pathway, practical considerations for switching to IPX203 from current regimens and recommendations for monitoring and follow-up. The experts emphasised that IPX203 should be considered for patients with motor fluctuations insufficiently controlled on optimised oral levodopa therapy, before introduction of device-aided therapies. They highlighted the need for flexible dose adjustments, comprehensive patient and neurologist education and practical tools to support conversion to IPX203. This consensus insight provides practical guidance for integrating IPX203 into routine care of PD patients with motor fluctuations, aiming to increase mobility and reduce treatment burden for patients with PD.

articles.title: Adverse Outcomes of Transthyretin p.V142I Carriers With Non-Amyloid Heart Failure:The SCAN-MP Study.
One-Year Systolic Blood Pressure and Subsequent Cardiovascular Outcomes After Acute Coronary Syndrome: Insights from a Swiss Prospective Cohort.
articles.abstract:
AIMS: Current guidelines recommend targeting systolic blood pressure (SBP) below 130 mmHg in patients at high cardiovascular risk, including after acute coronary syndrome (ACS), although evidence specific to the post-ACS setting remains limited. We evaluated the prognostic value of SBP measured 1 year after ACS on subsequent cardiovascular outcomes.

METHODS: The ELIPS cohort prospectively enrolled ACS patients across four Swiss tertiary-care centers (2009-2017). Patients alive at 1 year with available SBP measurements were included. The association between SBP at 1 year and 3-point major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE; cardiovascular death, non-fatal stroke/transient ischemic attack, or non-fatal myocardial infarction) was modeled using restricted cubic splines, adjusted for age, sex, renal function, cardiovascular risk factors, index-event type, coronary revascularization, cardiac rehabilitation, heart-failure history, and antihypertensive medication classes.

RESULTS: Among 2,074 patients (age 63±12 years; 82% male; 53% STEMI), 229 MACE events occurred over a median follow-up of 4.0 years (2.7 per 100 patient-years). The SBP-MACE relationship was nonlinear and J-shaped (P-non-linearity=0.007), with lowest risk between ∼130 and 140 mmHg (formally estimated nadir 138 mmHg [95%CI 116-152]). Above 140 mmHg, each 5-mmHg increase was associated with a borderline increase in MACE risk (adjusted HR 1.08; 95%CI 1.00-1.17). The pattern was broadly consistent across sex, age and hypertension status, with a possible interaction with diabetes that could not be excluded (P-interaction=0.08).

CONCLUSIONS: In this large, predominantly male, well-characterized post-ACS cohort, SBP measured 1 year after ACS showed a J-shaped association with cardiovascular risk, with lowest risk at 130-140 mmHg.

articles.title: Hypertension in women- is inflammation the key?
Cardiovascular health in transgender and gender diverse individuals: an expert opinion on gender-affirming hormone therapy, risk assessment and clinical management.
articles.abstract: Transgender and gender diverse (TGD) individuals represent a growing population with specific cardiovascular health needs. Current cardiovascular prevention strategies are largely derived from cisgender populations and may not adequately account for the combined effects of gender-affirming hormone therapy (GAHT) and other determinants. This expert opinion summarizes current evidence regarding cardiovascular health in TGD individuals, focusing on the cardiovascular effects of GAHT, population-specific cardiovascular risk factors, practical approaches to cardiovascular risk assessment, and future research priorities. Available evidence indicates that GAHT is associated with changes in cardiometabolic risk factors, haemostasis, vascular function, and cardiac physiology. Feminizing GAHT is associated with an increased risk of venous thromboembolism, whereas masculinizing GAHT is associated with adverse lipid changes, erythrocytosis, and a potentially increased risk of major cardiovascular events. However, causal inference is limited by the predominance of observational studies, relatively young study populations, heterogeneous GAHT regimens, short follow-up, and the absence of randomized study evidence. Population-level cardiovascular disparities in TGD should not be attributed to GAHT alone and smoking, obesity, physical inactivity, minority stress, socioeconomic disadvantage, and unequal access to healthcare may independently or interactively influence cardiovascular risk. Current cardiovascular risk prediction tools have not been validated or calibrated in TGD populations and do not account for GAHT exposure or TGD-specific psychosocial and structural determinants. Cardiovascular risk assessment in TGD individuals should integrate conventional risk factors, transgender-related cardiovascular risk factors, and patient involvement regarding individual goals. A coordinated multidisciplinary approach may facilitate personalized cardiovascular prevention while supporting access to gender-affirming care. Future research should prioritize long-term prospective studies and development of risk prediction models tailored to TGD populations.

articles.title: Defective Inflammation Resolution in Cystic Fibrosis: Cellular Mechanisms and Emerging Pro-resolving Therapies in the CFTR Modulator Era.
articles.journal: Current topics in microbiology and immunology
articles.abstract: Cystic fibrosis (CF) is a fatal monogenic hereditary disease that affects approximately 100,000 people worldwide. It is caused by mutations in the cystic fibrosis transmembrane conductance regulator (CFTR) gene, impairing biosynthesis and/or function of a protein that regulates chloride and bicarbonate fluxes. CFTR loss of function is associated with aberrant, non-resolving inflammation that in combination with recurrent infection leads to respiratory insufficiency. Cellular and molecular studies have uncovered failures in key mechanisms of inflammation resolution, consequent to loss of function of CFTR expressed by leukocytes, platelets, and epithelial and endothelial cells. This chapter illustrates these processes and discusses pro-resolving therapeutic approaches to combat CF inflammation.

articles.title: [Pythium keratitis: a case report].
