articles.journal: [Zhonghua yan ke za zhi] Chinese journal of ophthalmology
articles.abstract: A 31-year-old female presented with a 3-week history of right eye redness, ocular pain, photophobia and decreased vision after tap water exposure. Slit-lamp examination revealed corneal lesions with pseudopodia and hill-shaped hypopyon. In vivo confocal microscopy (IVCM) detected filament-like structures in the corneal stroma. The patient was initially suspected of having fungal keratitis, but the condition deteriorated despite standardized antifungal treatment. Repeated corneal scraping culture and targeted DNA sequencing confirmed the infection of Pythium insidiosum. After switching to linezolid-based antibacterial therapy, corneal perforation still occurred, and total keratoplasty with a scleral ring was performed. The infection relapsed at 2 weeks postoperatively and was finally controlled by multiple intracameral and intrastromal injections of linezolid. A secondary penetrating keratoplasty was subsequently performed. No recurrence was observed during the 11-month follow-up; the corneal graft remained transparent, and the best corrected visual acuity improved to 0.6. Pythium species are oomycetes instead of true fungi, which are intrinsically resistant to conventional antifungal agents but susceptible to specific antibacterial drugs such as linezolid. For clinically suspected Pythium keratitis unresponsive to antifungal treatment, early targeted DNA sequencing is essential for rapid pathogen identification. Timely administration of sensitive antibacterial agents and individualized surgical intervention are critical to control infection and optimize visual prognosis.

articles.title: [Effects of simulated combined visual acuity and visual field impairments on obstacle avoidance walking and searching abilities].
articles.journal: [Zhonghua yan ke za zhi] Chinese journal of ophthalmology
articles.abstract: Objective: To investigate the interactive effects of combined visual acuity and visual field impairments on obstacle avoidance walking and searching abilities. Methods: A randomized controlled trial was conducted. Healthy volunteers with normal visual acuity and visual fields were recruited from the Eye Hospital of Wenzhou Medical University between March and September 2024. Binocular presented visual acuity (PVA) was measured using a standard logarithmic visual acuity chart, and binocular visual field was examined using a Humphrey perimeter. Visual function impairments were simulated. Four levels of visual acuity impairment (PVA<0.05, 0.05≤PVA<0.3, 0.3≤PVA<0.5, and PVA≥0.5) were induced by applying occlusion foils of different densities onto the spectacle lenses. Two levels of concentric visual field constriction (visual field radius≤10° and≤20°) were simulated using modified goggle-based tunnel vision simulation glasses. Participants were randomly assigned to four visual acuity simulation groups using computer-generated random numbers, and further randomly assigned in a 1∶2 ratio to the 10° and 20° visual field subgroups within each group. Each participant completed an obstacle avoidance walking task and a target search task under both simulated visual field impairment and normal visual field conditions. The primary outcome measures were task completion time, number of collisions, and target detection rate. The Kruskal-Wallis test and linear mixed-effects model were used for statistical analysis. Results: A total of 143 participants were included [aged(23.94±2.23) years; 55 males and 88 females], with 95 under the simulated 20° visual field condition and 48 under the simulated 10° visual field condition. Under the normal visual field condition, participants in the PVA<0.05 group showed longer obstacle avoidance walking completion time (23.00 s vs. 17.50 s), an increased mean number of collisions (0.75 vs. 0.00), and a decreased target detection rate (80% vs. 100%) compared with those in the PVA≥0.5 group (all P<0.05). At any given level of visual acuity, participants with 20° or 10° visual field constriction demonstrated prolonged task completion time, a reduced target detection rate, and an increased mean number of collisions compared with those with normal visual field (all P<0.05). For example, in the PVA≥0.5 group, the obstacle avoidance walking completion time increased from 17.50 s under normal visual field to 25.50 s and 39.88 s under 20° and 10° visual field constriction, respectively, with the target detection rate decreasing from 100% to 90% and 80%. Both tasks were affected by the interaction between visual acuity and visual field impairments under specific deficit combinations. The combination of 20° visual field constriction and PVA<0.05 showed the most extensive impact, with the obstacle avoidance walking completion time reaching 55.50 s, mean number of collisions reaching 5.50, and target detection rate decreasing to 50%, and significant interaction effects were observed on the task completion time, target detection rate, and collision counts (all P<0.05). Conclusions: Visual field impairment exerts a more pronounced effect on obstacle avoidance walking and target search tasks than visual acuity impairment. Combined visual acuity and visual field impairments produce a compounded interference effect on the performance of both tasks.

articles.title: [Chinese expert consensus on high-dose anti-vascular endothelial growth factor therapy for neovascular age-related macular degeneration (2026)].
authors: Ophthalmology Group of China Alliance for Rare Diseases/Beijing Society of Rare Disease Clinical Care and Accessibility
articles.journal: [Zhonghua yan ke za zhi] Chinese journal of ophthalmology
articles.abstract: Neovascular age-related macular degeneration (nAMD) is primarily characterized by the formation of abnormal choroidal neovascularization and can lead to substantial visual impairment. Intravitreal administration of anti-vascular endothelial growth factor (anti-VEGF) agents has become the standard first-line treatment for nAMD. However, challenges remain, including the need for frequent injections, considerable treatment burden, and suboptimal responses in a subset of patients. In recent years, the emergence of high-dose anti-VEGF therapies has provided a novel strategy for extending treatment intervals and optimizing long-term disease management. To address these clinical needs, the Ophthalmology Group of China Alliance for Rare Diseases/Beijing Society of Rare Disease Clinical Care and Accessibility organized a multidisciplinary panel of experts to develop this consensus. Based on the latest evidence-based medical findings, together with international guidelines and the realities of clinical practice in China, a standardized consensus-development methodology was employed. Consensus recommendations were formulated for eight key clinical questions regarding the use of high-dose anti-VEGF therapies in the treatment of nAMD. The aim of this document is to provide evidence-based guidance and clinical reference for the standardized application of high-dose anti-VEGF therapies in nAMD, thereby further improving the quality of standardized diagnosis, treatment, and long-term management of nAMD in China.

articles.title: [Chinese expert consensus on the management of corneal and ocular surface adverse events related to antibody-drug conjugates (2026)].
authors: Dry Eye Research Group of Ophthalmology Branch of Chinese National Health Association
Dry Eye Rehabilitation Specialty of Vision Rehabilitation Committee of Chinese Rehabilitation Medicine Association
articles.journal: [Zhonghua yan ke za zhi] Chinese journal of ophthalmology
articles.abstract: Antibody-drug conjugates (ADCs), as a novel class of targeted anticancer therapies, have demonstrated significantly enhanced efficacy. However, the associated ocular adverse events have emerged as a critical issue impacting patients' quality of life and treatment compliance. ADC-induced ocular adverse events primarily affect corneal and ocular surface tissues. With the recent approval of multiple ADC agents in China and the extensive ongoing clinical trials, standardized guidance for managing corneal and ocular surface adverse events is urgently needed. The Dry Eye Research Group of Ophthalmology Branch of Chinese National Health Association and the Dry Eye Rehabilitation Specialty of Vision Rehabilitation Committee of Chinese Rehabilitation Medicine Association, together with experts from relevant fields, have developed consensus recommendations based on integrated international research and Chinese clinical practice, using the standardized consensus development methods. These recommendations address eight clinical questions concerning corneal and ocular surface adverse events associated with ADCs, aiming to provide evidence-based guidance for the prevention, diagnosis, and management of ADC-related corneal and ocular surface adverse events. Through multidisciplinary collaboration, this consensus seeks to enhance therapeutic benefits of ADC treatment and maximize patients' visual health and quality of life.

articles.title: Cost-effectiveness of microaxial flow pump versus standard of care in the management of Cardiogenic shock in Spain.
articles.journal: Expert review of pharmacoeconomics & outcomes research
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Cardiogenic shock (CS) remains the leading cause of death in patients with ST-elevation myocardial infarction (STEMI) despite timely revascularization and advances in pharmacological therapy. This study assessed the cost-effectiveness of a microaxial flow pump (mAFP) plus standard of care (SoC) versus SoC alone in patients with STEMI complicated by CS from the perspective of the Spanish National Health System (NHS).

RESEARCH DESIGN AND METHODS: A cost-effectiveness analysis was conducted using a partitioned survival model over a lifetime horizon. Clinical efficacy inputs were derived from DanGer Shock trial, while adverse and long-term clinical events were obtained from DanGer Shock and literature. Direct healthcare costs (expressed in 2025 euros), including device acquisition, hospitalization, adverse and clinical events management, and cardiac rehabilitation.

RESULTS: In the base-case analysis, mAFP+SoC yielded 3.430 life-years gained (LYG) and 2.645 quality-adjusted life-years (QALY) per patient, compared with 1.657 LYG and 1.272 QALYs with SoC alone. Total costs were €51,980 and €17,008, respectively, resulting in an incremental cost-utility ratio of 25,468/QALY. Deterministic and probabilistic sensitivity analyses supported model robustness.

CONCLUSIONS: From the Spanish NHS perspective, mAFP+SoC could be a cost-effective strategy for STEMI-CS, providing substantial gains in survival and health-related quality of life at a reasonable incremental cost.

articles.title: Targeting CDK2 ameliorates allergic asthma through suppression of epithelial chemokine production and T cell inflammatory responses.
articles.abstract: Allergic asthma is a chronic inflammatory airway disease driven by dysregulated type 2 immunity and aberrant epithelial-immune crosstalk. Despite advances in biologic therapies, many patients remain refractory to current treatments, underscoring the need for novel strategies that simultaneously target multiple pathogenic axes. Here, we show that cyclin-dependent kinase 2 (CDK2) is upregulated in bronchoalveolar lavage cells from asthmatic patients and its expression correlates with enhanced cell cycle activity, inflammatory signatures, and T cell activation in bronchial epithelium across six independent cohorts. In an ovalbumin (OVA)-induced murine model, pharmacological inhibition with a highly selective small-molecule CDK2 inhibitor (CDK2i) markedly alleviated airway hyperresponsiveness (AHR), eosinophilic inflammation, mucus hypersecretion, and peribronchial fibrosis, with effects comparable to those of dexamethasone. Mechanistically, CDK2i suppressed chemokine production in airway epithelial cells, thereby reducing T cell recruitment, while concurrently inducing G1/S cell-cycle arrest in T lymphocytes and blunting their production of Th2 cytokines. Integrated transcriptomic and functional analyses suggested that CDK2 may be involved in two pathways: epithelial-driven immune cell trafficking and T cell clonal expansion. Together, these findings suggest that selective CDK2 inhibition represents a promising experimental strategy for attenuating allergic airway inflammation and warrants further investigation in preclinical models of asthma.

articles.title: From equilibrium to dynamic metabolic imaging: the evolving role of magnetic resonance spectroscopic imaging in neurodegenerative disorders.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Dysregulated brain metabolism is increasingly recognized to play a significant role in the development and progression of neurodegenerative diseases (NDDs). Conventional imaging methods, such as positron emission tomography (PET), are limited to assessing tracer uptake and offer no insight into its downstream metabolic fate. Additionally, PET provides no insight into dynamic metabolic fluxes and turnover, which reflect biochemical processes. In contrast, magnetic resonance spectroscopy and spectroscopic imaging MRS(I) allow non-invasive, spatially resolved in vivo investigation of specific metabolites, without the use of radioactive tracers.

MAIN BODY: 1H-MRS(I) is one of the most widely utilized techniques due to its accessibility, while heteronuclear approaches, including 2H-, 13C-, 15N-, and 17O-MRS(I), broaden MRS(I)'s utility by expanding the scope of accessible metabolites. Technical and methodological advances in nuclear spin hyperpolarization-enhanced MRI further improve signal-to-noise ratio, enabling in vivo detection of low-abundance metabolites. Furthermore, revival of 2H-MRS(I) has opened new avenues for dynamic metabolic investigation without hyperpolarization. In this review, we provide a conceptual framework for transitioning from a static to a dynamic MRS(I) approach and discuss key considerations for tracer selection, nuclear spin hyperpolarization methods, acquisition hardware, reconstruction, preprocessing, and metabolic modeling. We outline major methodological and translational challenges, including low signal-to-noise ratio, field strength, and vendor hardware variability, as well as a lack of standardization across acquisition, reconstruction, preprocessing, and modeling strategies.

CONCLUSION: Dynamic MRS(I) provides a promising foundation for in vivo brain metabolism investigation in NDDs, offering mechanistic insights into metabolic fluxes, reprogramming, and bottlenecks. Although dynamic MRS(I) is limited to a few research institutions, ongoing technical and methodological advances are improving its feasibility, biochemical specificity, and broader implementation. Standardized and harmonized acquisition, reconstruction, and preprocessing protocols are necessary to enable broad clinical implementation of these approaches. Nevertheless, the shift from static to dynamic MRS(I) has great potential to advance biomarker and diagnostic tool development, patient stratification, and longitudinal disease monitoring in NDDs, provided that current challenges and limitations are sufficiently addressed.

articles.title: Phenotyping Heart Failure With Preserved Ejection Fraction in Japan　- Position Paper on Current Evidence and Future Directions.
articles.journal: Circulation journal : official journal of the Japanese Circulation Society
articles.abstract: Heart failure with preserved ejection fraction (HFpEF) is rapidly increasing in Japan in parallel with population aging, rising from just over half of all heart failure cases in 2015 to approximately 54% in 2025 and projected to reach nearly 57% by 2040-2050. HFpEF is a multifactorial syndrome shaped by diverse clinical and pathophysiological drivers. In East Asia, where obesity is less prevalent than in Western countries, the relative contribution of these different drivers may differ, underscoring the need for region-specific phenotypic characterization. In recent years, multiple Japanese registries have reported machine learning-based phenotyping analyses in HFpEF, identifying broadly similar but not identical patient clusters. In this position paper, we provide an integrative overview of major Japanese HFpEF cohorts and synthesize these findings to propose a pragmatic consensus framework for interpreting HFpEF heterogeneity in Japan. Despite methodological differences across cohorts, several clinical domains consistently emerged, including atrial remodeling/atrial fibrillation, vascular-cardiorenal dysfunction, metabolic burden, and systemic vulnerability. Based on these shared features, we propose 4 consensus phenogroups: (1) low structural and comorbidity burden; (2) vascular and cardiorenal remodeling; (3) atrial remodeling with right heart dysfunction; and (4) systemic vulnerability. This framework may support interpretation of HFpEF heterogeneity and guide future phenotype-informed research.

articles.title: Unilateral eosinophilic fasciitis: a case report and review of the literature.
articles.abstract: A 59-year-old Japanese man developed pruritus and swelling of the right dorsal foot after weeding his garden in a crouching position for approximately one hour. Over a period of five months, the swelling, as well as skin induration, progressed unilaterally from the right thigh to the lower leg and dorsal foot. Laboratory tests, including eosinophil fraction and inflammatory markers, were within normal limits, and computed tomography showed no evidence of deep vein thrombosis or malignancy. A full-thickness biopsy including the fascia revealed marked fascial thickening with fibrosis of the subcutaneous connective tissue, and perivascular lymphocytic inflammatory infiltrates without conspicuous eosinophils, leading to a diagnosis of eosinophilic fasciitis. Oral prednisolone (30 mg/day) resulted in gradual improvement. To the best of our knowledge, 11 cases of unilateral eosinophilic fasciitis have been reported (three in Japan and eight outside Japan). Including the present case (total 12), six cases lacked peripheral blood eosinophilia, and seven lacked significant eosinophilic infiltration in tissue; five showed neither. Eosinophilic fasciitis should be considered even in the absence of eosinophilia; therefore, early full-thickness biopsy including the fascia is essential for accurate diagnosis.

articles.title: Non-communicable diseases among subcontract and primary workers involved in decontamination after the fukushima daiichi nuclear power plant accident: an observational study.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Evidence on the population-level burden of major non-communicable diseases (NCDs) among Fukushima decontamination workers is limited, and it remains unclear whether subcontracted employment, a potential marker of employment-related vulnerability, is associated with NCD prevalence and health risk awareness. We therefore compared the prevalence of NCDs by employment status.

METHODS: We conducted a cross-sectional study using health checkup data from 2,790 workers (2011-2017). Data concerning hypertension, diabetes mellitus, and dyslipidemia were evaluated, along with the workers' self-reported awareness of diagnosis or treatment. Employment status was categorized as subcontracted worker or prime contractor worker. Group differences were assessed using Welch's t-tests and chi-squared tests, and quantile regression adjusted for age and sex.

RESULTS: The study included a total of 2,790 decontamination workers, of whom 1,716 were subcontracted workers (median age, 51 years; range, 18-82). The subcontracted workers had higher mean systolic blood pressure, a lower prevalence of self-reported hypertension, and higher blood glucose levels in extreme cases.

CONCLUSIONS: The subcontracted workers had higher systolic blood pressure despite lower self-reported hypertension. Future studies should investigate factors contributing to differences in NCD prevalence between subcontracted and prime contractor workers, such as lower self-awareness and barriers to healthcare access among subcontracted workers.

articles.title: FFAs secreted by A1 astrocytes contribute to RGCs apoptosis via PERK/eIF2α/ATF4/CHOP pathway in retinal ischemia/reperfusion injury.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: To explore the specific mechanisms of retinal neuronal apoptosis induced by A1 polarization of astrocytes under retinal ischemia/reperfusion (RI/R) injury.

METHODS: 1) In vivo, SD rats were selected for acute intraocular hypertension (AIH) model. In vitro, A1 astrocytes model was induced by the tumor necrosis factor α (TNF-α), interleukin-1α (IL-1α) and complement 1q (C1q) and oxygen and glucose deprivation/recovery (OGD/R) model of R28 cells. 2) Immunofluorescence was used to assess the expression of GFAP, C3, S100A10 and ELOVL1 genes morphologically. Apoptotic cell death was assessed by TUNEL and PI staining. 3) Quantitative real-time polymerase chain reaction (qRT-PCR) was performed to detect the mRNA expression levels of inflammatory factors. 4) The expression levels of GFAP、C3、S100A10、ELOVL1、p-PERK、p-eIF2α、ATF4、CHOP、Bax and Bcl-2 were measured by western blot (WB) assay. 5) The relative content of long-chain saturated free fatty acids (FFAs) in astrocyte medium was measured by lipidomic sequencing.

RESULTS: 1) Retinal astrocytes polarized to neurotoxic A1 phenotype after RI/R injury. 2) Compared to normal astrocytes, the release of long-chain saturated FFAs from A1 astrocytes increased. The inhibition of the production of saturated FFAs could significantly inhibit neuronal apoptosis. 3) A1 Astrocytes conditioned medium induced neuronal apoptosis by activating the PERK/eIF2α/ATF4/CHOP signaling pathway.

CONCLUSION: Under conditions of RI/R injury, retinal astrocytes polarized to A1 phenotype and secreted long-chain saturated FFAs, which mediated ER stress via the PERK/eIF2α/ATF4/CHOP pathway and finally caused retinal neuronal apoptosis.

articles.title: Integrated [68Ga]Ga-FAPI-7ND PET/CT and stromal profiling of immunocompetent syngeneic tumor models for FAP-targeted radionuclide therapy.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Most preclinical studies of fibroblast activation protein (FAP)-targeted radionuclide therapy (FAP-RNT) use immunodeficient xenografts, limiting evaluation within an intact immune microenvironment. This study aimed to characterized FAP-associated stromal and FAP inhibitor (FAPI) imaging phenotypes across immunocompetent syngeneic tumors and explored FAP-RNT effects in a representative model.

METHODS: Four syngeneic models (MC38, PAN02, LLC1, and 4 T1) were assessed using [68Ga]Ga-FAPI-7ND PET/CT, Western blotting, immunohistochemistry, and multiplex immunofluorescence for tracer uptake, FAP and α-SMA expression, and co-expression. Based on these findings, 4 T1-bearing mice underwent an exploratory therapeutic evaluation with saline or a single intravenous injection of [177Lu]Lu-FAPI-7ND. Tumor volume and body weight were measured every 2 days, and tumors were harvested on day 7 for histological and molecular analyses.

RESULTS: All models showed higher tumor uptake than contralateral muscle (all P < 0.05), with significant inter-model differences (P = 0.005) but comparable tumor-to-background ratios (P = 0.369). PAN02 had the highest uptake and enriched FAP+α-SMA+ stroma, whereas 4 T1 combined relatively high uptake with pronounced α-SMA-associated stromal activation. Because FAP-RNT response may reflect both tracer accumulation and stromal state, 4 T1 was selected for exploratory treatment. [177Lu]Lu-FAPI-7ND inhibited tumor growth (P < 0.0001) without significant body-weight loss. Treatment reduced CD8+ T-cell (P < 0.0001) and FOXP3+ regulatory T-cell densities (P = 0.012), did not alter their ratio (P = 0.537), and increased CD206-associated macrophage features (P < 0.05).

CONCLUSION: Syngeneic models exhibit distinct FAP-associated stromal and imaging phenotypes. In 4 T1 tumors, [177Lu]Lu-FAPI-7ND showed antitumor activity accompanied by immune microenvironmental alterations, supporting integrated model selection for immunocompetent FAP-RNT studies.

articles.title: Wearable Health-Tracking Devices and Adherence to Physical Activity Guidelines Among US Adults, Including Those with Elevated Anxiety Symptoms: A Nationally Representative Cross-Sectional Analysis of HINTS 7 (2024).
articles.abstract: Physical activity is a pillar of lifestyle medicine, yet most US adults do not meet aerobic guidelines, and inactivity is especially common among people with anxiety. Wearables enable self-monitoring, but population-level evidence linking them to guideline adherence among distressed adults is limited. We analyzed 6686 adults from the nationally representative Health Information National Trends Survey 7 (2024). The outcome was meeting the aerobic guideline (≥150 weekly minutes of at least moderate-intensity activity); the exposure was wearable device use for health tracking. Elevated anxiety was defined as a 2-item Generalized Anxiety Disorder scale score ≥3. Weighted logistic regression yielded odds ratios (ORs) adjusted for sociodemographic and health covariates. Wearable users were more likely than non-users to meet the guideline (48.1% vs 36.4%; adjusted OR, 1.59; 95% CI, 1.33-1.91; P < .001). The association was consistent across anxiety strata (interaction P = .33); among distressed adults, 48.2% of users vs 28.1% of non-users met the guideline. In secondary analyses, wearable use was not associated with meeting ≥300 min/wk (adjusted OR, 1.09; 95% CI, 0.84-1.40). Wearable use was independently associated with meeting activity guidelines, including among adults with elevated anxiety, supporting its potential as a scalable lifestyle-medicine adjunct. Cross-sectional data preclude causal inference.

articles.title: Catheter-related bloodstream infection reduction using systematic training in a Portuguese tertiary care hospital.
articles.abstract: Catheter-related bloodstream infections (CRBSI) are a major cause of morbidity, mortality, and increased healthcare costs among hospital-acquired infections. To reduce CRBSI, the Infection Prevention and Control and Antimicrobial Resistance Program (UL-PPCIRA) reviewed current guidelines and implemented an intensive training project for healthcare professionals. Following the publication of care bundles, cascade training was conducted for staff involved in central line insertion and maintenance. This study aimed to evaluate the impact of this continuous quality improvement project on CRBSI incidence in a tertiary hospital. Three consecutive periods of 2 years were analyzed: two before and one after implementation. CRBSI rates were 1.84, 1.68, and 0.65 per 1000 catheter-days in periods 1, 2, and 3, respectively. No significant difference was observed between periods 1 and 2 (IRR 0.92, 95% CI 0.52-1.63). In contrast, period 3 showed a significant reduction compared to period 2 (IRR 0.35, 95% CI 0.14-0.78; p = .02). The implementation of standardized care bundles, supported by structured training, was associated with a significant reduction in CRBSI. Ongoing monitoring and reinforcement strategies are essential to ensure long-term sustainability.

articles.title: Age-group-specific associations of admission nutritional status and sarcopenia-related indicators with functional outcomes after stroke.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Globallly, patients aged ≥80 years represent a growing proportion of stroke patients and frequently experience unfavorable prognoses. Although nutritional status and sarcopenia-related indicators have been proposed as prognostic factors, whether these factors differ between patients aged <80 years and those aged ≥80 years remains unclear. This study aims to examine the associations of admission nutritional status and sarcopenia-related indicators with functional outcomes separately in two age groups.

METHODS: This retrospective cohort study includes patients with acute stroke in a single stroke center. Nutritional status (body mass index [BMI], Mini Nutritional Assessment Short Form) and sarcopenia-related indicators (i.e., calf circumference, grip strength) were assessed at admission. Functional outcomes at 3 months were evaluated using the modified Rankin scale (mRS), with poor outcomes defined as mRS ≥ 3 and failure to recover to prestroke mRS. Multivariable analyses were conducted for each age group.

RESULTS: A total of 633 patients were included (median age, 80 years). The patients in the ≥80 years group showed significantly higher rates of poor outcomes compared with those in the <80 years group. In adjusted analyses, low BMI, malnutrition risk, and low muscle strength were associated with poor outcomes in the <80 years group, whereas only low muscle strength remained significant in the ≥80 years group (adjusted odds ratio = 6.51, 95% confidence interval 1.41-43.21, P = 0.029).

CONCLUSIONS: Nutritional status was associated with poor outcomes in <80 years patients with stroke. However, low muscle strength at admission was consistently associated with poor functional outcomes in both <80 years and ≥80 years stroke groups.

articles.title: Interpreting Respiratory Viral Risk with Benralizumab: From Treatment Assignment to Eosinophil Depletion.
articles.journal: QJM : monthly journal of the Association of Physicians

articles.title: Bimekizumab efficacy across GRAPPA domains to 3 years in patients with psoriatic arthritis: a post hoc analysis of two phase 3 studies.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: To evaluate the long-term efficacy of bimekizumab in patients with psoriatic arthritis (PsA) across the Group for Research and Assessment of Psoriasis and Psoriatic Arthritis (GRAPPA) domains, PsA-related conditions, and comorbidities.

METHODS: Post hoc analysis of pooled data from BE OPTIMAL (NCT03895203; biologic-naïve patients) and BE COMPLETE (NCT03896581; patients with prior inadequate response/intolerance to tumour necrosis factor inhibitors) phase 3 studies, and their open-label extension BE VITAL (NCT04009499), which assessed subcutaneous bimekizumab 160 mg every 4 weeks in patients with active PsA. Efficacy was assessed to 3 years (Week 148) across GRAPPA core domains, PsA-related conditions (inflammatory bowel disease [IBD] and uveitis), and inflammatory markers of cardiovascular risk.

RESULTS: Among 1,112 bimekizumab-treated patients with PsA, improvements were sustained across the GRAPPA core domains to 3 years. Resolution of swollen and tender joint count at 3 years was achieved by 59.2% and 34.6% of patients, respectively, while 54.8% achieved ≥50% improvement from baseline in American College of Rheumatology response criteria (modified non-responder imputation [mNRI]). Enthesitis (LEI=0) and dactylitis (LDI=0) resolution was also achieved by 56.6% (mNRI) and 68.6% (NRI) of patients, respectively. A high proportion of patients achieved skin and nail psoriasis clearance (PASI100: 64.6%; mNAPSI=0: 68.0%; mNRI). IBD and uveitis events were rare, and inflammatory cardiovascular risk marker improvements were sustained.

CONCLUSION: Bimekizumab provided long-term, sustained disease control across GRAPPA domains and systemic inflammation markers in patients with PsA, with low rates of IBD and uveitis, supporting its use as a long-term treatment for the heterogeneous manifestations of PsA.

CLINICAL TRIAL REGISTRATION: BE OPTIMAL: NCT03895203; BE COMPLETE: NCT03896581; BE VITAL: NCT04009499.

articles.title: Plasma metabolomic profiles associated with breastfeeding history and subsequent ovarian cancer risk.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Breastfeeding reduces ovarian cancer risk, but the underlying biological mechanisms remain unclear.

METHODS: We examined the association between a previously reported metabolite-based breastfeeding score with incident epithelial ovarian cancer risk in case-control studies nested within the Nurses' Health Studies (NHS/NHSII, n = 436) and Prostate, Lung, Colorectal, and Ovarian Cancer Screening Trial (PLCO, n = 300) using conditional logistic regression to calculate odds ratios (ORs) and 95% confidence intervals (CIs) for each study and conducted a meta-analysis. We investigated 606 individual breastfeeding-metabolite associations among 9,904 mid-life parous women in NHS/NHSII and 663 one-year postpartum women in the Vitamin D Antenatal Asthma Reduction Trial (VDAART). Metabolites associated with breastfeeding at p ≤ 0.05 after multiple testing correction for number of effective tests (NEF) were then assessed for their associations with ovarian cancer. Metabolite set enrichment analysis using Normalized Enrichment Score (NES) identified metabolite classes associated with breastfeeding using false discovery rate (FDR) were used for multiple testing correction.

RESULTS: The highest quartile of metabolite-based breastfeeding score was inversely associated with ovarian cancer risk (meta-analyzed odds ratio [OR]=0.62, 95%CI=0.39-0.99). Of the 14 individual metabolites associated with breastfeeding in NHS/NHSII and also measured in VDAART, similar direction of associations was observed for 11 metabolites. Phosphatidylcholines (PCs; NES=1.94; FDR=0.004) and phosphatidylethanolamines (PEs; NES=1.82; FDR=0.01) were positively enriched with increased breastfeeding duration. Ten metabolites including PCs and PEs were positively associated with breastfeeding and inversely associated with ovarian cancer.

CONCLUSION(S): Our results suggest alterations of systemic metabolism, particularly among PC and PE pathways, provide insight into biological pathways underlying the inverse breastfeeding-ovarian cancer association.

articles.title: Surgical Ligation for Partial Anomalous Pulmonary Venous Connection With Dual Drainage in an Elderly Patient.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Partial anomalous pulmonary venous connection with dual drainage into both the superior vena cava (SVC) and left atrium (LA) is a rare congenital anomaly, with few reported cases.

CASE SUMMARY: A 78-year-old woman presented with exertional dyspnea. Cardiac computed tomography revealed that the right pulmonary vein drained into both the SVC and LA, resulting in a significant left-to-right shunt. We ligated the anomalous connection with a median sternotomy. This approach allowed avoidance of complex reconstructions and cardioplegic arrest.

DISCUSSION: Simple ligation may represent a less invasive surgical option that avoids cardiac arrest and shortens operative time. Moreover, it may prevent pulmonary venous obstruction and future heart failure caused by right heart volume overload.

TAKE-HOME MESSAGE: In elderly patients with heart failure caused by partial anomalous pulmonary venous connection with dual drainage into both the SVC and LA, ligation of the left-to-right shunt may be less invasive and prevent late complications.

articles.title: Prospective evaluation of ultrasound shear-wave elastography for predicting outcomes of extracorporeal shock-wave lithotripsy in proximal ureteral stones.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: Predicting extracorporeal shock-wave lithotripsy (ESWL) success is central to ureteral stone management. This prospective study evaluated shear-wave elastography (SWE) in 10-20 mm proximal ureteral calculi.

METHODS: Ninety patients with a 10-20 mm proximal ureteral stone were enrolled. Before ESWL, each underwent non-contrast computed tomography for Hounsfield unit (HU) quantification and ultrasound SWE. A stone-free result (residual fragments ≤4 mm) at 4 weeks defined success.

RESULTS: A stone-free result occurred in 62.2% (56/90). Stone-free patients had lower stiffness (14.6±6.1 vs. 27.6±9.1 kPa) and HU values (786±194 vs. 1,137±195 HU, both p < 0.0001). ROC-derived cut-offs were 21.2 kPa (AUC 0.871) and 935 HU (AUC 0.890). Against a zero-fragment endpoint, SWE discrimination fell (AUC 0.64). On Firth-corrected modelling, lower body mass index (p = 0.043), SWE below 21.2 kPa (p = 0.033) and HU below 935 (p = 0.004) independently predicted success. For SWE, this held only at the dichotomised cut-off; the continuous association did not reach significance (OR = 0.904 per kPa, p = 0.055). Within-session repeatability was moderate-to-good (ICC = 0.74). Adding SWE to an HU-only model did not improve discrimination (AUC 0.890 to 0.898; DeLong p = 0.585), although the likelihood-ratio test (p = 0.025) and integrated discrimination improvement (+ 0.055, p = 0.019) were significant. SWE correlated strongly with HU (ρ = 0.76, p < 0.0001).

CONCLUSION: Lower stone stiffness, dichotomised at a cohort-derived threshold, was independently associated with a stone-free outcome. SWE largely overlapped with HU and did not improve discrimination; it may therefore provide similar information by a radiation-free route where repeat CT is undesirable, rather than adding to CT. The 21.2 kPa threshold should be regarded as exploratory pending multicentre validation.

articles.title: Stress hyperglycemia ratio as a predictor of in-hospital mortality in patients with acute kidney injury: a retrospective cohort study.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To investigate the relationship between the stress hyperglycemia ratio (SHR) and the risk of in-hospital mortality in patients with acute kidney injury (AKI), and to evaluate its predictive performance.

METHODS: A retrospective cohort study used the Medical Information Mart for Intensive Care (MIMIC-IV) and MIMIC-III databases. SHR was defined as the ratio of admission blood glucose to estimated average glucose. Restricted cubic spline regression analyzed the nonlinear relationship between SHR and in-hospital mortality. Multivariate logistic regression and subgroup analyses were applied to validate the robustness of the association. Receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curve analysis was employed to evaluate the predictive performance of SHR.

RESULTS: Among 2180 patients, in-hospital mortality was 18.8% (263/1,398) in MIMIC-IV and 19.8% (155/782) in MIMIC-III. SHR showed a U-shaped relationship with in-hospital mortality, where SHR > 1.19 or < 0.50 significantly increased death risk (P < 0.05). The overall pattern was consistent across subgroup and sensitivity analyses. ROC curve analysis demonstrated that SHR had better predictive performance than conventional severity and comorbidity scores for hospital mortality in AKI patients. The highly consistent results from both databases indicate reliability.

CONCLUSION: SHR is an independent predictor of in-hospital mortality in AKI patients. By distinguishing the extreme low-SHR range from the intermediate lowest-risk range, this study further characterized the bidirectional nonlinear risk pattern, facilitating early identification of high-risk patients for risk stratification.

articles.title: First-in-human experience and one-year outcomes using a novel conformal pulsed-field ablation balloon catheter for pulmonary vein isolation in paroxysmal atrial fibrillation.
articles.journal: Journal of interventional cardiac electrophysiology : an international journal of arrhythmias and pacing
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Thermal balloon catheters have improved the efficiency of pulmonary vein isolation (PVI) in atrial fibrillation (AF). Reports assessing additional safety and effectiveness of pulsed field ablation (PFA) balloon catheters for PVI are limited. This study aims to assess the safety and effectiveness of a conformal PFA balloon catheter for PVI in paroxysmal AF.

METHODS: 35 patients with paroxysmal AF (PAF) were treated with a PFBalloon catheter (Biphasic, Bipolar, 750 V). The balloon was inflated with 10:1 saline/contrast, with volume adjusted for spherical wide-antral or pear-shaped ostial-junction PV ablation to ensure optimal tissue contact. The primary safety endpoint was absence of periprocedural primary adverse events. The primary effectiveness endpoint was acute PVI. The secondary effectiveness endpoint included durable PVI assessed by remapping at three months post-ablation and 1-year clinical outcomes.

RESULTS: All targeted PVs (142/142) in 35 patients were acutely isolated, with 32.3 ± 4.5 applications per patient and 7.9 ± 1.0 per vein. Procedure and left atrial dwell times were 133 ± 46 and 56 ± 25 min, respectively. No hemolysis-related acute kidney injury or severe device-related complications occurred. PVI durability was 76.0% (19/25) per patient and 93.1% (95/102) per vein. After a median follow-up of 367 (interquartile range 357-380) days, 1-year Kaplan-Meier estimate for freedom from atrial arrhythmia (AF/atrial flutter/atrial tachycardia) ≥30 s was 90.7% (95% CI, 81.2%-100%).

CONCLUSIONS: The conformal PFBalloon catheter demonstrated favorable safety, efficiency, and effectiveness for PVI in PAF patients, achieving durable lesions and a high rate of freedom from atrial arrhythmias recurrence.

TRIAL REGISTRATION: clinicaltrials.gov NCT07320976.

articles.title: The Economic and Humanistic Burden of Phenylketonuria Among Patients and Their Caregivers: A Systematic Literature Review.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND/OBJECTIVES: Phenylketonuria (PKU) is a rare autosomal recessive metabolic disorder resulting from a deficiency in phenylalanine hydroxylase (PAH) enzyme activity. This systematic literature review (SLR) aims to synthesize the available evidence on the economic and humanistic burden of PKU on patients and their caregivers.

METHODS: A comprehensive SLR was conducted using PubMed, Embase, Cochrane Library, International Prospective Register of Systematic Reviews (PROSPERO), EconLit, and the Cost-Effectiveness Analysis (CEA) Registry, from database inception to June 2026. Eligible studies were published in English, included individuals diagnosed with PAH deficiency (including PKU) and/or their caregivers, and reported original data on either the economic or humanistic burden of the condition.

RESULTS: Of 2131 records identified, 1330 were screened after deduplication, and 313 underwent full-text review. A total of 130 studies were included, with 44 reporting on economic burden and 87 covering humanistic burden-related outcomes. The economic burden of dietary management was substantial, with mean per patient per year (PPPY) costs ranging from US$1634 to US$35,946, and an estimated 233-359 h PPPY dedicated to diet-related activities. Humanistic burden was also significant; the long-term metabolic control significantly influenced multiple domains of health-related quality of life (HRQoL). In a study involving adults with PKU (n = 88), dietary protein restriction was found to be negatively associated with HRQoL (Rp = 0.265, p < 0.05), and similarly, anxiety was also negatively correlated with blood phenylalanine (Phe) levels (Rs = 0.186-0.209, p < 0.05).

CONCLUSIONS: Findings underscore the substantial financial, time, and psychological burden of PKU, particularly in relation to dietary management.

articles.title: Recent advances in antituberculosis drugs and therapeutics: from mechanistic breakthroughs to clinical translation.
articles.abstract: Tuberculosis (TB), caused by Mycobacterium tuberculosis, reclaimed its status as the deadliest single-pathogen infectious disease globally in 2023, accounting for 10.8 million new cases and 1.25 million deaths in 2023. The escalating crisis of drug-resistant TB, suboptimal BCG vaccine efficacy in adults, and persistent treatment gaps for vulnerable populations collectively drive an urgent shift toward mechanism-driven, precision-oriented therapeutic strategies.This review presents a critically integrated appraisal of anti-TB research advances spanning 2020 to 2025, drawing on structural biology, multi-omics, and real-world clinical evidence. It distinguishes itself from conventional descriptive literature compilations through systematic cross-population efficacy comparisons, in-depth dissection of translational bottlenecks, and explicit maturity stratification of emerging biotherapies. We synthesize progress across six interconnected domains: mechanistic insights into drug targets and spatiotemporal resistance evolution, novel short-course therapeutic regimens, precision medicine strategies, host-directed therapies, targeted delivery systems for extrapulmonary TB, and next-generation vaccine development. Three transformative breakthroughs are particularly highlighted: structural biology-guided rational drug design, spatial immune profiling of tuberculous granulomas, and AI-assisted diagnostic pipelines.We conclude by delineating priority research directions aligned with the WHO End TB Strategy, providing a translational roadmap to advance global TB elimination efforts. This rigorous, multi-dimensional synthesis offers an authoritative reference for advancing basic and translational anti-TB research and informing global public health strategy.

articles.title: Floating knee injuries: a retrospective analysis of treatment outcomes and prognostic factors.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND/ AIMS: Floating knee injury is a rare high-energy trauma pattern frequently associated with concomitant organ injuries. Optimal treatment timing and the role of external fixation remain subjects of ongoing debate.

METHODS: Twenty-one patients who underwent surgery for ipsilateral femoral and tibial fractures were retrospectively reviewed. Fractures were classified using the Fraser and Gustilo-Anderson systems. Functional outcomes were assessed using the Karlström-Olerud criteria.

RESULTS: The mean age was 31 ± 12.1 years; 85% of patients were male. The mean follow-up was 66.6 months. The most common injury mechanism was motorcycle accident (71.4%). According to Karlström criteria, 76.1% of patients achieved excellent or good functional outcomes. External fixation was associated with significantly longer total hospital stay (p = 0.003) and higher superficial infection rates (60.0% vs. 6.3%, p = 0.028) however, this likely reflects greater initial injury severity in patients selected for this approach rather than a direct effect of the device. Patients requiring postoperative ICU admission had significantly higher complication rates (75% vs. 23.1%, p = 0.032). The Injury Severity Score (ISS) correlated significantly with operative time (rs = 0.549, p = 0.010). Delayed definitive surgery was associated with longer total hospital stay (rs = 0.492, p = 0.024) but had no effect on functional outcomes or complication rates. Fraser classification and Gustilo-Anderson grade did not significantly influence functional outcomes.

CONCLUSION: Floating knee injuries carry significant morbidity despite favourable functional outcomes in the majority of patients. External fixation prolongs hospitalisation and increases infection risk, highlighting the importance of early conversion to definitive fixation in eligible patients. Postoperative ICU admission may serve as a useful indicator for heightened complication risk.

articles.title: Multimorbidity patterns and outcomes among adults (non-maternity) with community-onset sepsis in Ireland: a retrospective national analysis of acute hospital data, 2020-2025.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Community-onset sepsis accounts for most sepsis cases and frequently occurs in individuals with underlying comorbidity. While national analyses in Ireland have described its epidemiology, impact of multimorbidity and how comorbidities co-exist to form patterns remain poorly characterised.

OBJECTIVES: To identify multimorbidity patterns among adult (non-maternity) episodes with community-onset sepsis and examine their association with critical care admission and in-hospital mortality.

METHODS: We conducted a secondary analysis of Hospital In-Patient Enquiry data from all acute public hospitals in Ireland from January 2020 to December 2025. Community-onset sepsis was defined using the present-on-admission flag. The sample comprised adult episodes aged ≥ 16 years excluding maternal admissions from conception to 6 weeks postpartum. K-means clustering identified patterns of co-occurring diseases. Multivariable logistic and negative binomial regression examined associations between patterns and outcomes.

RESULTS: Of 80,628 sepsis admissions, 58,101 (72.0%) were community-onset. Of these, 53,812 (93.0%) were adult (non-maternity); of these, 35,316 (65.6%) had at least one Charlson comorbidity. Five data-derived multimorbidity patterns were identified: metabolic-multimorbid (31%), oncological-dominant (29%), renal-metabolic (15%), progressive metabolic (13%) and cardiopulmonary (12%). Outcomes varied across patterns, with differences in critical care admission and in-hospital mortality. Cardiopulmonary pattern had the highest odds of in-hospital mortality (adjusted-OR 2.01, 95% CI 1.86-2.17).

CONCLUSIONS: Charlson comorbidity was recorded in approximately two-thirds of adult community-onset sepsis episodes and formed data-derived patterns associated with differences in critical care admission and in-hospital mortality. Multimorbidity clustering may support future risk stratification research and targeted clinical vigilance for episodes at highest risk of adverse outcomes.

articles.title: Cerebral cavernous malformations: epidemiology, molecular pathogenesis, diagnosis and therapy.
articles.abstract: Cerebral cavernous malformations (CCMs) are cerebrovascular diseases characterized by vascular lesions of the central nervous system (CNS) that can result in epileptic seizures, headaches, focal neurologic deficits (FNDs), and hemorrhagic stroke. Germline and somatic loss-of-function (LOF) mutations in one of the three established CCM-associated genes, namely CCM1 (or krev interaction trapped protein 1, KRIT1), CCM2, and CCM3 (or programmed cell death 10, PDCD10), which have been validated as core drivers of CCM pathogenesis and progression. Over the past few decades, a substantially improved understanding of the hallmarks and molecular basis of CCMs has been achieved. Key pathological hallmarks include but are not limited to excessive angiogenesis, vascular leakage, endothelial-mesenchymal transition (EndMT), defective autophagy, inflammation and immune response, oxidative stress, influenced gut microbiome and altered brain vascular microenvironment. These hallmarks are orchestrated by dysregulated signaling cascades, notably MEKK3-KLF2/4, PI3K-mTOR, and RhoA-ROCK, which integrate genetic, inflammatory, and hemodynamic cues. Concurrently, sophisticated neuroimaging (MRI with SWI/QSM) and genetic testing now enable precise diagnosis and risk stratification. Although surgical resection remains the mainstay for accessible symptomatic lesions, a wave of mechanism‑based pharmacological candidates has shown promising efficacy in preclinical models, and several have advanced to early‑phase clinical trials. This review summarizes the current understanding of CCM epidemiology, molecular pathogenesis, diagnosis and therapy, highlighting how the evolving multi‑hit concept and the dissection of downstream signaling are paving the way towards personalized management of this complicated vascular disease.

articles.title: Bone marrow adipose tissue in cardiometabolic disease: marrow niche remodeling, inflammatory hematopoiesis, and vascular pathology.
articles.abstract: Bone marrow adipose tissue (BMAT) is increasingly recognized as a metabolically active, endocrine, and immunomodulatory component of the marrow niche rather than a passive fat depot. This narrative review synthesizes biological, imaging, epidemiological, and therapeutic evidence linking BMAT and marrow metabolic activation with cardiometabolic disease. BMAT arises from marrow stromal progenitors and exhibits depot-specific heterogeneity, endocrine activity, insulin responsiveness, and context-dependent expansion during aging, diabetes, obesity, menopause, osteoporosis, and chronic kidney disease. Mechanistically, experimental studies indicate that marrow adipocytes and adipocyte-lineage niche cells can influence hematopoiesis through metabolic and local signaling, whereas trained immunity is established primarily in HSPCs, myeloid progenitors, and monocyte/macrophage populations. Human MRI/MRS studies characterize BMAT quantity and composition, whereas 18F-FDG PET reflects non-BMAT-specific marrow activation associated with vascular inflammation and early atherosclerosis; direct BMAT-cardiovascular evidence remains limited. Emerging population imaging and genetic analyses support BMAT as a disease-associated phenotype, particularly for osteoporosis and fractures. Interventions affecting metabolic, inflammatory, skeletal, or marrow pathways have differing degrees of BMAT-related evidence, and none has established that modifying BMAT improves cardiovascular outcomes. This review identifies BMAT as an emerging research phenotype while emphasizing that its causal, prognostic, and therapeutic relevance to cardiovascular disease remains unresolved.

articles.title: Chronic kidney disease as a potential risk factor for pituitary hormone dysregulation: a review of the underlying mechanisms.
articles.abstract: Chronic Kidney Disease (CKD) is a condition of abnormal kidney structure or function, pathologically characterized by chronic inflammation, tubular atrophy, vascular rarefaction, glomerulosclerosis, and interstitial fibrosis. CKD potentially represents a risk factor for several disease conditions, such as cardiovascular disease, mineral bone disorder, and electrolyte imbalance. Hormone dysregulation within the pituitary axis is yet another condition that CKD influences. Notably, CKD dysregulates several anterior pituitary hormones, either by directly influencing hypothalamic-pituitary secretion or by altering downstream hormones, which then dysregulate pituitary secretion via negative feedback. In the context of CKD-influenced hormone dysregulation, several contributors, including high uremic toxins, inflammatory cytokines, mineral imbalance, and dysregulated molecular mediators related to fibroblast growth factor 23-Klotho signaling, circulating microRNAs, the kidney-gut-brain axis, and glial and endothelial modulation, play integral roles. In conclusion, this review highlights the potential participation of CKD in pituitary dysregulation and provides insights into its potential contributors.

articles.title: Post-dexamethasone cortisol levels in non-functioning adrenal incidentalomas: a pooled individual participant data analysis.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Non-functioning adrenal incidentalomas (NFAI) are defined by 1 mg-dexamethasone suppression test (F-1mgDST) cortisol levels < 1.8 µg/dL. However, many individuals with NFAI may exhibit subtle hypercortisolism associated with increased cardiometabolic and skeletal risk. The aims of the present study are to compare F-1mgDST distributions between individuals with NFAI and population-based controls and to explore whether alternative F-1mgDST thresholds would meaningfully modify patient classification.

METHODS: This is a pooled individual participant data analysis of 7 studies evaluating cortisol secretion in patients with type 2 diabetes, osteoporosis and/or fragility fractures, hypertension, or adrenal incidentalomas. The study included 1681 participants (915 NFAI, 766 controls) with F-1mgDST < 1.8 µg/dL. Data included age, sex, body mass index (BMI), F-1mgDST, and adrenocorticotroph hormone (ACTH). We assessed the between-group differences in F-1mgDST and ACTH and the accuracy of different F-1mgDST thresholds for identifying NFAI.

RESULTS: Compared to controls, patients with NFAI had lower age and ACTH levels (62.1 ± 9.8 and 59.8 ± 12.0 years, 25.1 ± 14.1 pg/mL and 16.3 ± 10.4, respectively, p < 0.001 for all comparisons), but higher BMI and F-1mgDST values (28.1 ± 4.9 and 29.0 ± 5.0 kg/m2, 1.04 ± 0.37 µg/dL and 1.13 ± 0.39 µg/dL, respectively, p < 0.001 for all comparisons) and were more less frequently females (48.0% and 38.6%, respectively, p < 0.001). A propensity score analysis performed on 730 patients and 730 age-, BMI- and gender-matched controls confirmed these findings. We did not identify any F-1mgDST threshold with an accuracy exceeding 60% for distinguishing controls from patients with NFAI. The F-1mgDST threshold the best balance between sensitivity (54.8%) and specificity (57.2%) was set at 1.1 µg/dL (30 nmol/L), although with a low accuracy of 55.8%.

CONCLUSIONS: Individuals with NFAI have higher F-1mgDST levels than controls. More than 40% overlap exists in F-1mgDST values between NFAI and controls.

articles.title: The Role of Point-of-Care Lung Ultrasound in Diagnosing Ventilator-Associated Pneumonia in Pediatric Patients.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: This study aimed to assess the diagnostic accuracy of LUS for diagnosing VAP and to develop a new score based on Clinical Pulmonary Infection Score (CPIS) incorporating LUS to assess its accuracy for pediatric VAP diagnosis.

METHODS: A prospective observational study was conducted over one year (Nov 2022-Nov 2023) in the PICU of a tertiary care hospital in North India. A total of 112 mechanically ventilated children, aged 1-12 y with new respiratory deterioration and CPIS > 6 were enrolled. LUS, CXR, and endotracheal aspirate cultures were performed. LUS characteristics were analysed, and a composite score, the Lung Ultrasound Pulmonary Assessment Score (LUPAS), was developed.

RESULTS: Among 94 culture-confirmed VAP cases, LUS demonstrated high diagnostic performance. Coalescent B-lines (55.3%) and subpleural consolidations with air bronchograms (17%) had sensitivities and specificities of 75%/90% and 70%/95%, respectively. Integration of LUS into CPIS improved diagnostic accuracy, with the combined score yielding 90% sensitivity and 95% specificity, PPV of 85% and NPV of 95%, AUC 0.925.

CONCLUSIONS: LUS appears to be a promising adjunctive imaging modality for evaluating VAP in mechanically ventilated paediatric patients.

articles.title: Effect of Hepatitis B virus X T118N mutant protein in HepG2 cell cycle and apoptosis regulation.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Hepatitis B virus (HBV) belongs to Hepadnaviridae family and caused liver infection. HBV infection can develop into hepatocellular carcinoma, one of which is due to presence of HBV X protein (HBx). Some mutations are known to be associated with development of liver carcinoma, for instance HBx K130M/V131I (HBx_KV). In Indonesia, HBx T118N (HBx_T) has been found at similar frequency as the HBx_KV. This study aims to examine the effect of HBx T118N mutant on cell cycle and apoptosis regulation.

METHODS AND RESULTS: In this study, analysis of CyclinE, p21, Bax, and Bcl-2 gene expression was performed using RT-qPCR. Cell cycle and apoptosis analysis was done using flowcytometry with PI and Annexin V-PI staining, respectively. Caspase 3 activity assay was performed using CaspACE™ Colorimetric Assay Kit. The presence of HBx_T mutant increased CyclinE expression at 72 h post transfection, similarly to HBx_KV. Both Bax and Bcl-2 mRNA level were also increased HepG2 cells expressing HBx_T in comparison to HBx_KV expression at 72 h post transfection. HBx_T expression in HepG2 cells at 48 h post transfection caused increase of AnnexinV+/PI- and AnnexinV+/PI+ cell populations, as compared to HBx_wt expression.

CONCLUSIONS: Our data suggests that HBx_T influences cell cycle and apoptosis regulation in slightly different mechanism to HBx_KV. Further investigations are still required to understand HBx_T mutant involvement in development of chronic liver disease and liver cirrhosis.

articles.title: Cardiovascular events in aging Japanese people with hemophilia: a 3-year interim analysis of the ADVANCE Japan cohort.
articles.abstract: As life expectancy increases in people with hemophilia (PWH), cardiovascular disease (CVD) has emerged as an important comorbidity. However, prospective data on CVD occurrence and its clinical management remain limited. We performed a prespecified 3-year interim analysis of ADVANCE Japan, an ongoing 10-year multicenter prospective cohort study of PWH aged ≥ 40 years, to describe CVD occurrence, clinical management, bleeding outcomes, and associated changes in hemostatic treatment. We also explored factors associated with CVD occurrence using Cox proportional hazards models. Among 588 participants, 24 developed CVD, yielding 26 events over 3 years (cumulative incidence, 4.1%). Ischemic heart disease was the most frequent event. Exploratory analyses suggested that older age, dyslipidemia, and current smoking were associated with CVD occurrence, although estimates were imprecise because of the limited number of events. Antiplatelet or anticoagulant therapy was administered to selected patients, and hemostatic management was frequently modified following CVD events. One major bleeding event was observed among patients receiving antithrombotic therapy. This prespecified interim analysis provides prospective real-world data on the occurrence and clinical management of CVD in aging Japanese PWH. Risk factor analyses should be considered exploratory, and continued follow-up is required to define long-term cardiovascular risk and outcomes in this population.

articles.title: Metabolic basis of post-infectious sequelae after Ebola virus disease.
articles.journal: Metabolomics : Official journal of the Metabolomic Society
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Ebola virus disease (EVD) survivors often present with clinical sequelae after acute disease resolution, called post-Ebola syndrome (PES). Why some survivors develop these sequelae and others do not is poorly defined. Altered metabolism has been noted in acute EVD but has not been studied in PES. Here, we identified distinct metabolic pathways in EVD survivors with PES compared to asymptomatic survivors and potential biomarkers of PES.

OBJECTIVES: The purpose of this study was to determine if EVD survivors with PES demonstrated differential metabolism compared to asymptomatic EVD survivors.

METHODS: Plasma was collected from EVD survivors in Sierra Leone as part of an ongoing cohort study. Untargeted metabolomics (LC-MS/MS) was performed on survivors with and without sequelae as well as household contacts. Univariate, multivariate, biomarker and pathway analyses were performed in MetaboAnalyst. Spearman's R correlation was performed using JMP.

RESULTS: We identified differential expression of metabolites involved in multiple metabolic pathways in EVD survivors with PES compared to asymptomatic survivors. These pathways include the tricarboxylic acid cycle as well as amino acid, nucleotide, and short chain fatty acid metabolism. Several of these pathways are associated with immune dysfunction. The identified metabolites have potential use as biomarkers of PES.

CONCLUSION: EVD survivors with PES exhibit differing metabolism compared to asymptomatic EVD survivors in several pathways. Other studies have linked these pathways to immune dysfunction and chronic viral infection, however further immunometabolic studies of EVD survivors with PES are needed.

articles.title: Hemostatic dysfunction and thrombotic risk in metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease.
articles.abstract: Metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD) is increasingly recognized as a systemic disorder with clinically relevant vascular and thrombotic consequences. Beyond hepatic steatosis, inflammation, and fibrosis, MASLD is associated with disturbances in hemostatic regulation that may shift the overall balance toward thrombosis. The prothrombotic phenotype of MASLD arises from the interaction of metabolic dysfunction, chronic inflammation, endothelial injury, platelet hyperreactivity, increased procoagulant activity, reduced natural anticoagulant capacity, and impaired fibrinolysis. These abnormalities may be detectable at early disease stages and appear to evolve with progression to steatohepatitis, advanced fibrosis, and cirrhosis. Epidemiological and clinical studies associate MASLD with venous thromboembolism, portal vein thrombosis, myocardial infarction, and ischemic stroke, with population-based data indicating approximately 1.8-fold higher venous thromboembolism risk and 3.4-fold higher PVT risk. However, conventional coagulation tests do not adequately reflect the net hemostatic balance, while candidate biomarkers and global hemostatic assays remain insufficiently validated for routine risk stratification. Hemostatic dysfunction in MASLD, particularly hypercoagulability, impaired fibrinolysis, endothelial dysfunction, and platelet activation, represents a clinically relevant but still underrecognized component of the disease. Clinical management should integrate liver disease stage, cardiometabolic burden, conventional thrombotic risk factors, and bleeding or procedural risk. Routine antiplatelet or anticoagulant therapy cannot currently be recommended solely on the basis of MASLD-related laboratory abnormalities.

articles.title: Admission serum mitochondrial DNA relative abundance is associated with angiographic no-reflow or slow-flow after primary percutaneous coronary intervention in STEMI.
articles.abstract: This study aimed to evaluate the independent association of admission serum mitochondrial DNA (mtDNA) relative abundance with no‑reflow or slow‑flow (NR/SF) after primary percutaneous coronary intervention (PPCI) in patients with acute ST‑segment elevation myocardial infarction (STEMI), and to quantify its incremental predictive value along the clinical timeline. We prospectively enrolled 892 consecutive STEMI patients undergoing PPCI and measured pre‑procedural serum mtDNA relative abundance using quantitative real‑time polymerase chain reaction (qPCR). After overlap weighting adjustment for 17 baseline covariates, high mtDNA abundance was independently associated with an increased risk of NR/SF (OR = 2.461, 95% CI 1.535-3.948, P < 0.001), with an absolute risk difference of 11.73%, and the exposure-response relationship exhibited a significant non‑linear threshold pattern (non‑linear P = 0.006). This association remained significant for both the NR component (OR = 2.689, 95% CI 1.377-5.250, P = 0.004) and the SF component (OR = 1.940, 95% CI 1.044-3.604, P = 0.036), and high mtDNA levels were also associated with higher in‑hospital risks of cardiogenic shock, acute heart failure, and severe arrhythmias. In predictive modeling, adding mtDNA to the early admission baseline model significantly improved the area under the curve (AUC) from 0.616 to 0.680 (ΔAUC = 0.064, DeLong P = 0.001), with a net reclassification improvement index of 0.453 and an integrated discrimination improvement index of 0.035. However, once angiographic or periprocedural characteristics were introduced, the incremental predictive value no longer reached statistical significance (ΔAUC = 0.023, P = 0.056-0.068). In conclusion, elevated admission serum mtDNA relative abundance is independently associated with post‑PPCI angiographic NR/SF in STEMI patients, showing a threshold‑like exposure-response relationship; its incremental predictive value is confined to the pre‑angiographic phase, suggesting that it may serve as an auxiliary biomarker for pre‑procedural risk stratification rather than an independent predictive tool.

articles.title: Severity-associated endothelial dysfunction in post-COVID-19 patients: flow-mediated dilation and vasoactive biomarkers.
articles.abstract: COVID-19 is frequently associated with endothelial dysfunction, characterized by an imbalance between vasodilatory and vasoconstrictive mediators. This study evaluated endothelial function in the early post-COVID-19 period across groups of acute disease severity using flow-mediated dilation (FMD), circulating vasoactive biomarkers, and echocardiography. Serum endothelin-1 (ET-1), arginase-1 (Arg1), thromboxane A₂ (TxA₂)-related immunoreactivity, and prostacyclin (PGI₂)-related immunoreactivity were measured by enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay. An impaired FMD response was defined as < 10% brachial artery dilation from baseline. Overall, 502 post-COVID-19 patients were classified by acute COVID-19 severity as mild (n = 262), moderate (n = 183), severe (n = 41), or critical (n = 16); 27 healthy individuals served as a reference group. Impaired FMD responses were more frequent after severe (90.24%) and critical (100.00%) disease than in the reference group (18.52%). Greater acute disease severity was associated with progressively lower FMD values, smaller absolute brachial artery diameter changes, higher ET-1, Arg1, and TxA₂-related immunoreactivity, and lower PGI₂-related immunoreactivity. After adjustment for age, sex, body mass index, systolic blood pressure, smoking, diabetes mellitus, pre-existing cardiovascular disease, and post-COVID-19 interval, acute disease severity remained associated with impaired FMD (adjusted odds ratio 3.32, 95% confidence interval 2.29-4.82; p < 0.001 per one-category increase). Biomarker-FMD correlations were generally weak. Among patients assessed during the early post-COVID-19 period, greater acute COVID-19 severity was associated with greater impairment of endothelium-dependent vasodilation and an altered profile of circulating vasoactive biomarkers. These findings indicate associated functional and biochemical vascular abnormalities without establishing causality or a mechanistic relationship. Prospective longitudinal studies are needed to clarify their temporal evolution and clinical significance.

articles.title: Discussion of mechanism behind "bamboo blind" sign observed in fatty liver parenchyma.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: To elucidate the mechanism behind the so-called "bamboo blind" sign frequently observed on B-mode images as multiple low-echoic lines in nonalcoholic steatohepatitis and highly fatty liver cases.

METHODS: Six types of acoustic shadowing artifacts that might be the cause of the bamboo blind sign were defined. B-mode images were acquired for 21 fatty liver cases (inc. 9 highly fatty liver cases). The cases were then pathologically diagnosed. A phantom experiment was also performed to investigate whether refraction occurs due to the gap of sound velocity between two different media.

RESULTS AND DISCUSSION: The mechanism of the bamboo blind sign corresponded well to the acoustic shadowing from small vessels in the liver. The phantom experiment validated the same phenomenon at a larger gap in sound velocity, which can be regarded as the same level as that in highly fatty liver cases.

CONCLUSION: The refraction between blood vessels and highly fatty liver parenchyma with decreased sound velocity is the dominant reason for the bamboo blind sign.

articles.title: Effect of web-based education on NIV-related side effects and insomnia severity in COPD patients using home NIV: a randomized controlled trial.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: This study aimed to evaluate the effect of web-based education on NIV-related side effects and insomnia severity in COPD patients using home noninvasive ventilation (NIV).

METHODS: This randomized controlled trial was conducted with 75 patients between October 2023 and May 2024. Data were collected using the S³-NIV Questionnaire and the Insomnia Severity Index (ISI). The intervention group received web-based education regarding NIV-related side effects and insomnia management. Independent samples t-tests were used to compare numerical descriptive characteristics between groups, while Pearson chi-square and Fisher's exact tests were used for categorical variables. Repeated-measures ANOVA was performed to evaluate changes over time and between groups.

RESULTS: Compared with the control group, the intervention group demonstrated significantly higher total S³-NIV Questionnaire scores and higher respiration, sleep, and side-effect subscale scores at weeks 4 and 8. Significant group × time interaction effects were observed for total S³-NIV scores (p < 0.001, η²p = 0.753) and ISI scores (p < 0.001, η²p = 0.352). For insomnia severity, no significant between-group difference in ISI scores was observed at Week 4, whereas ISI scores were significantly lower in the intervention group at Week 8.

CONCLUSION: Web-based education may help improve patient-reported NIV-related symptoms and reduce insomnia severity in patients with COPD using home NIV. These findings suggest that web-based educational interventions may support symptom management and patient adaptation in clinical practice.

articles.title: Body Mass Index Variability and Cardiovascular Risk: Contemporary Evidence and Clinical Implications for Diabetes Care.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE OF REVIEW: To synthesize contemporary evidence on body mass index (BMI) variability as a determinant of cardiovascular risk, integrate mechanistic insights, and clarify its clinical relevance in individuals with and without diabetes.

RECENT FINDINGS: Large cohort studies demonstrate that greater BMI or weight variability is associated with increased risks of all-cause mortality, atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease, heart failure and atrial fibrillation, independent of mean BMI. Mechanistic evidence to explain the observed association implicates adipose tissue dysfunction, ectopic fat deposition, metabolic instability, systemic inflammation, and autonomic imbalance. Diabetes may amplify these pathways through impaired metabolic flexibility and treatment-related weight fluctuations. Evidence from diabetes-specific cohorts suggests that structured, intentional weight loss may attenuate the adverse associations seen with unstructured weight cycling. BMI variability is an emerging marker of cardiometabolic instability with implications for cardiovascular risk, particularly in diabetes. Defining actionable thresholds and determining whether stabilizing weight improves outcomes are key future research priorities.

articles.title: EORTC QLQ-C30 symptom components and their functional correlates during adjuvant chemotherapy for early breast cancer: a multivariate analysis. Data from GEICAM/2003-02 study.
articles.journal: Quality of life research : an international journal of quality of life aspects of treatment, care and rehabilitation
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: Understanding how multiple symptoms jointly impact functioning is essential for interpreting patient-reported outcomes (PROs) in oncology. We aimed to characterize the main dimensions underlying change-from-baseline (CFB) in symptom scores during adjuvant chemotherapy for early breast cancer, and to examine their associations with functional outcomes.

PATIENTS AND METHODS: We analyzed EORTC QLQ-C30 CFB scores from 820 patients enrolled in the GEICAM/2003-02 trial. Principal component analysis (PCA) was used to summarize correlated symptom changes into a smaller number of components, and graphical LASSO network modelling was applied to explore relationships among Health-Related Quality of Life (HRQoL) domains. Associations between components and functional scales and global health status were assessed using Spearman correlations.

RESULTS: Three components were identified in the pooled sample, explaining 53.6% of the variance: a dominant general symptom burden component, a gastrointestinal component, and a diarrhea-specific component. The general component, primarily defined by fatigue, pain, appetite loss, insomnia, nausea/vomiting and dyspnea, showed consistent negative correlations with all functional scales and global health status. Similar patterns were observed across treatment arms, although gastrointestinal-related components differed. Graphical LASSO identified fatigue as the symptom most strongly connected to functional impairment.

CONCLUSION: Symptom changes during chemotherapy are not independent, but follow a multivariate structured pattern in which a general symptom burden, anchored by fatigue, plays a central role in functional decline. These findings suggest that multivariate approaches may provide a complementary exploratory framework for summarizing correlated patterns of treatment-related burden and generating hypotheses regarding PROs. Trial registration number ClinTrials.gov: GEICAM/2003-02: NCT00129389.

articles.title: Dynamic transitions from prediabetes to diabetes and incident cardiovascular events in middle-aged and older chinese adults: a nationwide longitudinal study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Prediabetes is a heterogeneous metabolic state that may revert to normoglycemia, persist, or progress to type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM). However, the cardiovascular implications of different prediabetes transition patterns and the ability to predict diabetes progression among middle-aged and older Chinese adults remain unclear. We aimed to characterize glycemic transitions, examine their associations with incident cardiovascular events, and develop prediction models for progression from prediabetes to T2DM.

METHODS: This longitudinal cohort study used data from the China Health and Retirement Longitudinal Study. Glycemic status was defined according to American Diabetes Association criteria using fasting plasma glucose, HbA1c, self-reported diabetes, and medication use. Four-year glycemic transitions from Wave 1 to Wave 3 were assessed among 7,927 participants. Among participants with baseline prediabetes, multinomial logistic regression was used to identify factors associated with reversion to normal glucose tolerance or progression to T2DM. A Wave 3 landmark design was applied to examine subsequent incident heart disease and stroke in separate outcome-specific cohorts. Prediction models for 4-year T2DM progression were developed and internally validated using a stratified 70:30 training-test split; no external validation was performed.

RESULTS: Among 3,313 participants with baseline prediabetes, 696 (21.01%) reverted to normal glucose tolerance, 2,007 (60.58%) remained in prediabetes, and 610 (18.41%) progressed to T2DM over 4 years. Higher BMI, fasting glucose, HbA1c, dyslipidemia, smoking, and C-reactive protein, together with lower grip strength, were associated with higher odds of progression. Older age, male sex, higher fasting glucose, and higher HbA1c were associated with lower odds of reversion. Compared with stable normal glucose tolerance, prediabetes progression was associated with higher odds of incident heart disease (adjusted odds ratio [aOR], 1.53; 95% CI, 1.13-2.09), whereas the association with incident stroke was not statistically significant (aOR, 1.29; 95% CI, 0.90-1.87). Stable T2DM was associated with higher odds of both incident heart disease (aOR, 1.36; 95% CI, 1.04-1.79) and stroke (aOR, 1.44; 95% CI, 1.05-1.97). The full-variable logistic regression model achieved the highest discrimination for T2DM progression (AUC, 0.715; 95% CI, 0.674-0.754), modestly outperforming the clinical baseline model (AUC, 0.699; 95% CI, 0.656-0.739) and the evaluated tree-based models.

CONCLUSIONS: Prediabetes showed dynamic 4-year transitions within the analytic cohort. Progression from prediabetes to T2DM was associated with higher subsequent odds of incident heart disease, whereas its adjusted association with incident stroke was not statistically significant. The full-variable logistic regression model showed moderate discrimination and only limited incremental improvement over the clinical baseline model; it should therefore be considered an exploratory risk-stratification tool requiring external validation rather than a clinically deployable prediction model.

articles.title: The impact of ventilation mode on systemic inflammation and organ dysfunction in a porcine model of abdominal sepsis-associated acute respiratory distress syndrome.
articles.abstract:
