CONCLUSION: The simplified STP approach provides reliable MBF and MFR estimates from standard static scans, showing strong agreement with dynamic 13N-Ammonia PET. By eliminating the requirement for full dynamic protocols, this method facilitates absolute flow quantification using existing conventional SPECT infrastructure.

articles.title: Including other body size measures with BMI does not meaningfully change estimates of excess adiposity for surveillance purposes.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The Lancet Diabetes & Endocrinology Commission on the Definition and Diagnosis of Clinical Obesity proposed definitions and diagnostic criteria for pre-clinical (excess adiposity, ExAdip) and clinical obesity (ClinOb).

OBJECTIVE: To investigate the impact definitions of ExAdip and ClinOb on obesity surveillance among US adults ≥20 years.

METHODS: National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey August 2021-August 2023 data for US adults (n=5554) were used to compare obesity defined by body mass index (BMI) alone to prevalences based on 4 ExAdip definitions: defined as high BMI and high 1) waist circumference, 2) waist to hip ratio, 3) waist to height ratio, or 4) ≥2 high body size measures regardless of BMI (2BS). ClinOb prevalence, based on 5 of 18 proposed measures of dysfunction, (≥Stage 1 hypertension, metabolic cluster, metabolic liver dysfunction with fibrosis, kidney dysfunction, and limitations of activities of daily living) was also calculated. Differences between demographic subgroups within one definition were tested using t-tests. Definition estimates were compared to BMI-alone 95% confidence intervals to assess differences from the current obesity definition.

RESULTS: Obesity prevalence using BMI alone (40.8%, 95% CI 37.2-44.4%) was similar to ExAdip prevalence based on definitions that included BMI and other body size measures (∼40%), but differed compared to high 2BS (77.5%, 95% CI 74.0-80.8%). Almost 39% (38.7%, 95% CI 34.4-43.1%) of adults with BMI<25 had high 2BS. Similarly, ClinOb prevalence was comparable across ExAdip definitions that included BMI (∼25%) but higher based on high 2BS (43.4%, 95% CI 40.2-46.7%). Patterns by demographic subgroups were similar based on definitions that included BMI but differed based on ExAdip defined as high 2BS.

CONCLUSIONS: Including other body measures beyond BMI to define ExAdip did not change ExAdip or ClinOb prevalence in the US. However, using two body size measurements regardless of BMI resulted in higher ExAdip.

articles.title: 161Tb Radiopharmaceutical Therapy as a Treatment for RANKL-Positive Multiple Myeloma.
articles.journal: European journal of pharmaceutical sciences : official journal of the European Federation for Pharmaceutical Sciences
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Denosumab, an anti-RANKL monoclonal antibody, is clinically approved for bone protection in multiple myeloma (MM) but lacks direct cytotoxic effects on tumor cells. Herein, we repurpose this well-tolerated antibody as a targeted delivery vehicle by conjugating it with the emerging radionuclide 161Tb, which emits low-energy conversion and Auger electrons with ultra-short tissue range, offering high relative biological effectiveness against single tumor cells and micrometastases. However, 161Tb-based radiopharmaceutical therapy has not been explored in MM. Our purpose is to evaluate the therapeutic potential of [161Tb]Tb-DOTA-Denosumab compared to [177Lu]Lu-DOTA-Denosumab for RANKL-positive MM.

METHODS: DOTA-conjugated Denosumab was labeled with 161Tb and 177Lu. Radiochemical purity, in vitro stability and biodistribution were assessed. Therapeutic efficacy was evaluated in U266 and H929 subcutaneous xenograft models. Tumor volume, survival, body weight, hematologic, and biochemical parameters were monitored. Administered-activity-escalation toxicity studies were performed in tumor-free mice.

RESULTS: Both radiolabeled conjugates showed high radiochemical purity (>95%), excellent in vitro stability and comparable tumor uptake. [161Tb]Tb-DOTA-Denosumab demonstrated significantly enhanced antitumor efficacy compared to [177Lu]Lu-DOTA-Denosumab at equivalent (1.85 MBq) or lower activities. In the U266 model, median survival was prolonged from 33 days (saline) to 45 days with 161Tb (1.85 MBq) versus 39 days with 177Lu (1.85 MBq). In the H929 model, median survival extended to 47 days with 161Tb (1.85 MBq) versus 31 days (saline) and 41 days with 177Lu (1.85 MBq). Toxicity studies confirmed reversible hematologic changes only at administered activities ≥3.70 MBq, with no severe organ damage.

CONCLUSIONS: This is the first demonstration of 161Tb-based radiopharmaceutical therapy targeting RANKL in MM. [161Tb]Tb-DOTA-Denosumab exhibits superior antitumor efficacy and prolonged survival compared to its 177Lu-labeled counterpart. The unique Auger/conversion electron emission of 161Tb enables potent cytotoxicity against MM cells with favorable organ tolerability. These findings support 161Tb as a next-generation theranostic radionuclide for RANKL-positive malignancies and provide a strong rationale for clinical translation, highlighting the value of repurposing a clinically established antibody for radiopharmaceutical therapy.

articles.title: Benzothiazoloquinolines as protease-activated receptor 4 (PAR4) antagonists with excellent rat pharmacokinetic properties.
articles.abstract: A novel series of quinoline-based PAR4 antagonists with single digit nanomolar potency has been discovered through iterative structure-activity relationship optimization. This series of quinoline antagonists demonstrates excellent rat pharmacokinetic properties with favorable oral exposure and Cmax.

articles.title: Wound Infections Following Snake-Related Injuries in Malaysia: A Retrospective Analysis of Remote Envenomation Consultancy Services Data.
articles.journal: Toxicon : official journal of the International Society on Toxinology
articles.abstract: Snake-related injuries (SRI) in Malaysia are a medical emergency. SRI may be accompanied by wound infection requiring medical and surgical intervention. Despite its clinical relevance, local epidemiological and microbiological data remain limited in Malaysia. This was an observational analysis conducted on 72 hospitalised patients with wound infections following snake-related injuries who received consultation from the Remote Envenomation Consultancy Services (RECS). Data were collected using a standardised collection form. Among 559 hospitalised SRI cases, 72 patients (12.9%) developed wound infections. Males accounted for 70.8%, and most patients with wound infections were young adults aged 18 to 44. The most frequent symptoms were swelling (91.7%) and erythema (69.4%). SRI from Naja species were the most frequently identified cause of wound infections. Bacterial cultures were positive in 15.3% of cases, with Enterococcus species being the most frequently identified. Amoxicillin/clavulanate was the most used antibiotic. Wound debridement was performed in 27.8% of cases. Most patients were hospitalised for more than 5 days, and the most common outcome was healed with a scar (34.7%). No mortality was reported. This study emphasises the need for accurate clinical assessments to distinguish between venom-induced inflammation and subsequent bacterial infection. Although the culture-positive rate was low, the presence of pathogens such as Enterococcus species, which are often resistant to standard antibiotics, emphasises the need for cultures and sensitivity testing in snakebite-related infections. Early antivenom therapy, adequate antibiotic usage, and prompt surgical intervention, such as debridement, will improve patient outcomes. These findings provide useful local insights for clinical guidelines and for better management of wound infections following snake-related injuries in Malaysia.

articles.title: Functional characterization of grass carp OXR1 in response to GCRV infection.
articles.abstract: Oxidation resistance protein 1 (OXR1) protects cells from oxidative injury in several vertebrate systems, but its role during viral infection in teleosts is unknown. We cloned and characterized grass carp OXR1 (Ctenopharyngodon idella; CiOXR1) and examined its response to grass carp reovirus (GCRV). The 959-bp CiOXR1 cDNA contains a 774-bp open reading frame encoding a 257-amino-acid TLDc-domain protein. CiOXR1 transcripts were detected in all tissues examined in healthy grass carp, with the highest basal abundance in brain, followed by heart. Following genotype II GCRV-HZ08 challenge in grass carp, CiOXR1 transcript abundance increased in brain and heart. In vitro, treatment with LPS, poly(I:C), or H2O2 increased CiOXR1 transcript abundance in grass carp ovary (GCO) cells. GFP-CiOXR1 localized mainly to the cytoplasm of GCRV-infected GCO cells. Cell-based localization and functional assays used genotype I GCRV-873, which increased DCFH-probe fluorescence. Infected cells transfected with 3HA-CiOXR1 showed lower DCFH fluorescence, lower SOD1 and SOD2 transcript abundance, and reduced accumulation of viral RNA and total-protein markers. TCID50 assays further supported inhibition of infectious-virus production by CiOXR1. Total caspase-3 and caspase-9 protein abundance, their transcript levels, and selected innate immune-response markers were also reduced, whereas no significant difference in STING transcript abundance was detected. Cas13d-mediated knockdown of CiOXR1 yielded reciprocal transcript-level changes. Together, the complementary expression and knockdown results show that CiOXR1 expression is inversely related to GCRV molecular-marker accumulation and accompanies coordinated changes in intracellular oxidation, total caspase abundance, and selected innate immune-response markers. These findings further support an antiviral role for CiOXR1 and provide a foundation for research on the prevention and control of grass carp hemorrhagic disease.

articles.title: The lncRNA-mediated ceRNA network of Largemouth Bass contribute to immune regulation during LMBV Infection.
articles.abstract: Largemouth bass ranavirus (LMBV) inflicts substantial economic losses on largemouth bass aquaculture; however, the contributions of long non-coding RNAs (lncRNAs) and competing endogenous RNA (ceRNA) networks to the host antiviral immune response remain poorly understood. In this study, we performed a comprehensive analysis of lncRNA-mediated ceRNA regulatory networks during LMBV infection, aiming to elucidate their functional roles in modulating immune defenses in largemouth bass.We performed whole transcriptome sequencing (RNA-seq and miRNA-seq) on head kidney tissues from LMBV-infected fish at 24, 48, 72 hours post-infection (hpi) and NC (PBS-injected control). Differential expression analysis identified numerous significantly dysregulated lncRNAs, miRNAs, and mRNAs. Functional enrichment revealed their involvement in key immune pathways like PI3K-Akt, Toll-like receptor, and NF-kappa B signaling. A comprehensive ceRNA network was constructed, highlighting key interactions such as MSTRG.4391.5-miR-146-x-TIRAP and MSTRG.11433.4-miR-155-x-ANGPT4. RT-qPCR validation confirmed the expression trends of selected ceRNAs. The results demonstrate that LMBV infection induces dynamic changes in lncRNA expression, which likely function as ceRNAs to sponge miRNAs and regulate immune-related genes, potentially leading to immunosuppression. Our findings provide novel insights into the lncRNA-mediated post-transcriptional regulatory networks in antiviral immunity and identify potential targets for future disease control strategies in largemouth bass aquaculture.

articles.title: Using data-driven, lesion-symptom mapping to study the relationship between neural and theoretical components of numeracy.
articles.abstract: Numeracy, the ability to understand and manipulate numbers, is a crucial foundational ability for many daily life skills. Numeracy tasks have been categorized using different taxonomic approaches, and understanding of the relationship between tasks categories and neural models of numeracy remains poor. In this study, we use the lesion method to address this key gap. The study employs a data-driven approach with support vector regression lesion-symptom mapping (SVR-LSM) of extracted factors from two left hemisphere chronic stroke survivor datasets: one with data from a battery of math and language tests (N = 100) and the other with data from the EC301 math battery (N = 64). We find that our data best support a separation of number tasks requiring verbal vs. magnitude number knowledge, aligning with a broad theme that emerges across theories in different variations. This is supported by distinct neuroanatomical correlates that link verbal coding of number to the language-centered regions including left perisylvian area and insula, and that link magnitude coding to the parietal lobe, as described in prior models. Our findings indicate that these two different sources of representation variously contribute to a range of math tasks, including different types of arithmetic calculation tasks, in ways which cannot be cleanly defined by one singular theoretical model of math cognition.

articles.title: Otoneurology myths. A review endorsed by the SEORL-CCC Otoneurology Committee.
articles.abstract: Throughout the history of medicine, successive scientific advances have led to the abandonment of certain previously established statements or clinical practices. Otoneurology has been no exception, and this has resulted in substantial changes in the traditional approach to these topics. These facts are reflected in the following paper, where, based on concepts previously published in the literature and selected in accordance with the PRISMA guidelines, we examine the objective data that would make it necessary to discard them in favour of a better clinical practice.

articles.title: Endoplasmic reticulum stress, redox signaling, and neutrophil effector functions in chronic lung diseases: Evidence and research priorities.
articles.abstract: Endoplasmic reticulum (ER) stress and unfolded protein response (UPR) signaling intersect with inflammatory and redox pathways. Experiments in primary neutrophils link selected UPR pathways to mitochondrial reactive oxygen species, neutrophil extracellular trap (NET) formation, antimicrobial activity, and immune regulation under defined conditions. This review organizes these findings by cell type, experimental model, and the relationship tested, distinguishing them from cell-line experiments, other-cell mechanisms, clinical associations, and database connections. We examine calcium signaling, compartmentalized oxidant production, antioxidant defenses, and redox-dependent UPR sensor modifications. Several molecular mechanisms of sensor modification derive from non-neutrophil systems and require separate validation in neutrophils. Their relevance is assessed across chronic obstructive pulmonary disease, asthma, and pulmonary fibrosis, with cystic fibrosis (CF) blood-neutrophil transcript measurements distinguished from functional pathway evidence. To our knowledge, no study has established direct causality between neutrophil-intrinsic UPR signaling and NET formation in primary neutrophils obtained from human chronic lung disease tissue or pulmonary neutrophilic patient cohorts. We identify dose-, time-, and branch-resolved experiments needed to evaluate individual neutrophil functions without assigning their direction to acute or prolonged stress. Pharmacological UPR modulation is considered separately from delivery platforms evaluated with non-UPR cargoes. This evidence-based assessment defines the cellular boundaries of current knowledge and prioritizes experiments needed to establish disease relevance and preserve antimicrobial defense.

articles.title: GLS2 Promotes Early Ferroptosis Followed by Apoptosis and p53 Signaling in Renal Ischemia-Reperfusion Injury.
articles.abstract: Renal ischemia-reperfusion injury (IRI) is a major cause of acute kidney injury (AKI), particularly in the settings of kidney transplantation and perioperative care. In IRI-induced AKI, ferroptosis, an iron-dependent, lipid peroxidation-driven form of regulated cell death, occurs early in proximal tubular epithelial cells; however, the precise molecular mechanisms underlying ferroptosis, its crosstalk with other forms of regulated cell death, and its clinical relevance remain incompletely understood. We previously identified glutaminase 2 (GLS2) as a key regulator of ferroptosis via α-ketoglutarate (αKG). Because GLS2 is expressed in renal tubular cells, we investigated the role of the GLS2-αKG-ferroptosis axis using Gls2 knockout (KO) mice and an in vitro hypoxia-reoxygenation model mimicking renal IRI. Compared with wild-type (WT) mice, KO mice showed markedly attenuated tubular injury, accompanied by reduced mitochondrial shrinkage and decreased chromatin condensation in tubular cell nuclei. At 12 h post-IRI, ferroptosis-associated gene expression and GLS2-αKG-driven lipid peroxidation were significantly reduced in KO mice. At 24 h post-IRI, p53 and apoptosis-related gene expression, as well as caspase-3 cleavage, were also reduced. Moreover, intraperitoneal administration of a ferroptosis inhibitor, as well as local glutaminase inhibition via glutaminase inhibitor-impregnated surgical gauze applied to the kidney during ischemia, attenuated ferroptosis, subsequent apoptosis, and tubular injury in vivo in WT mice. To assess the clinical relevance of these findings, we analyzed publicly available Gene Expression Omnibus (GEO) datasets and found increased PTGS2 and GLS2 expression in human kidneys following IRI. These findings suggest that targeting the GLS2-ferroptosis axis represents a promising therapeutic strategy for ischemic AKI.

articles.title: Driver or Passenger? A Bradford Hill Framework for Aging-Associated lncRNAs.
articles.abstract: Transcriptomic surveys of aging tissues routinely report hundreds to thousands of differentially expressed long non-coding RNAs (lncRNAs), and the field has no agreed way of separating causal drivers from passengers that merely track the aging phenotype. I translate Sir Austin Bradford Hill's nine criteria for causal inference, formulated in 1965, into operational tests for aging-associated lncRNAs. Each criterion is recorded as 0, 1 or 2, and the per-criterion profile is the result: no sum or band decides a category. Hill offered viewpoints, not independent quantities to be added; here half of the cited studies support two or more criteria, so a total counts some evidence twice. Two axes are reported separately - molecular causal evidence, and organism-level validation (criterion 8), recorded as supportive, not evaluated, or in vivo at a non-aging endpoint - so that an animal experiment on development, reproduction, cancer or injury is not read as a negative test of aging. Applied to ten worked examples chosen to illustrate rather than to sample the field - NEAT1, MEG3, lincRNA-p21, MALAT1, MIR31HG, SALNR, TERRA, PANDAR, HOTAIR, TUG1 - the profiles separate candidates awaiting an animal experiment from those whose animal experiments addressed something else. MALAT1 is instructive: of six in-vivo perturbation studies, one assays a senescence endpoint. No candidate has an aging experiment that returned a negative result, and none reaches the top of criterion 8, which requires conditional deletion or a titrated antisense regimen with rescue. Organism-level evidence, not literature volume, is the structural bottleneck.

articles.title: Waterless versus soap-and-water perineal hygiene in fully dependent hospitalized patients: a multicenter randomized trial.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: This study evaluated the microbiological effectiveness and organizational impact of waterless perineal hygiene compared with traditional soap-and-water cleansing in fully dependent hospitalized patients, addressing a gap in evidence within acute care settings.

METHODS: This multicenter, randomized, open-label superiority trial was conducted in 10 medical and geriatric wards across four hospitals in Northern Italy. Fully dependent adult inpatients were randomized 1:1 to waterless hygiene or standard soap-and-water care. The primary outcome was the proportion of participants achieving a ≥90% reduction in microbial load between pre- and post-procedure perineal swabs. Secondary outcomes included procedure duration, patient and healthcare professional satisfaction, and agreement between evaluations.

RESULTS: A total of 468 participants were analyzed (239 control; 229 experimental). The experimental procedure achieved a higher proportion of ≥90% microbial reduction compared with standard care (47.2% vs 37.2%; p=0.030), corresponding to an absolute risk difference of 9.9% (95% CI 1.0-18.8) and a risk ratio of 1.27 (95% CI 1.02-1.57). Procedure duration was similar between groups (median 10 vs 11 minutes; p=0.311). Satisfaction was high in both groups, with more favorable perceptions of fragrance and overall hygiene in the experimental group.

CONCLUSIONS: Waterless perineal hygiene demonstrated greater immediate microbiological cleansing effectiveness than standard soap-and-water hygiene without increasing procedure time. Further studies are needed to determine whether these microbiological findings translate into improved clinical outcomes, including healthcare-associated infections.

articles.title: Neighborhood Walkability, Green Space, and Incident Hip Fracture among Older U.S. Adults: The Cardiovascular Health Study.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: Neighborhood walkability and green space are associated with walking behavior and physical activity, but evidence linking them to fracture is limited and inconsistent, and potential sex differences remain understudied. We evaluated associations of neighborhood walkability and green space with incident hip fracture in older, community-dwelling U.S. adults.

METHODS: We conducted a prospective cohort study of adults aged ≥65 years from the Cardiovascular Health Study (CHS). Neighborhood exposures were defined using 1-km radial buffers around geocoded residential addresses from 1992-1993 (baseline). Walkability was the sum of standardized population and walkable destination densities. Green space was the proportion of satellite-derived green land cover. Hip fractures were prospectively ascertained over 12 years using International Classification of Diseases, Ninth Revision (ICD-9) codes from hospital discharge abstracts. Cox hazard models adjusted for individual-level (age, sex, race, weight, height, smoking status, current heavy alcohol use, medication use, diabetes, renal function, marital status, education level, annual household income) and neighborhood-level (median household income, median value of owner-occupied housing, proportion of persons in managerial/professional occupations) covariates evaluated associations, overall and by sex.

RESULTS: Among 3,676 participants (58% women), 359 experienced hip fracture over a median 10-years observation. Greater neighborhood walkability was significantly associated with lower hip fracture incidence among women (hazard ratio per 1 standard deviation increase of 0.72 [95% confidence interval, 0.53-0.98]), but not overall or among men. Neighborhood green space was not significantly associated with hip fracture.

CONCLUSION: Greater neighborhood walkability, but not green space, was associated with lower hip fracture risk among older women.

articles.title: The Impact of a Low Glycemic Load Breakfast on Diurnal Glucose Profiles in Women with Gestational Diabetes Mellitus: The GLIDING Randomized Crossover Trial.
articles.journal: The American journal of clinical nutrition
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Medical nutrition therapy is first-line treatment in gestational diabetes (GDM) management, yet evidence-based approaches remain lacking. In women with GDM, increased morning insulin resistance often results in postprandial (breakfast) hyperglycemia, potentially leading to increased 24-h glycemic variability (GV).

OBJECTIVE: In a short-term randomized crossover control trial, we compared the effects of a low glycemic load (GL) breakfast (LGL-B) to a high GL breakfast (HGL-B) on 1-h postprandial breakfast glucose (PPG) and 24-h GV (coefficient of variation [%CV]) in women with GDM.

METHODS: Women were provided an LGL-B (245 kcal; 10.9g carbohydrate) and HGL-B (247 kcal; 43.4g carbohydrate) in random order for 7 days, separated by a 7-day washout. Fasting blood was drawn on Days 1, 8, 15 and 22 (pre/post 7-day interventions) and blinded continuous glucose monitoring was undertaken. Breakfast 1-h PPG and %CV were analyzed using mixed effect models to compare between intervention effects with Bonferroni adjustments.

RESULTS: Of 32 women with GDM randomized (median 34.2 years, BMI 28.1 kg/m2, 27 weeks' gestation), 20 women completed both 7-day interventions and had ≥48-h CGM data for each breakfast intervention. Compared to an HGL-B, an LGL-B had lower 1-h PPG (HGL-B: mean 7.5 mmol/L [95% CI 7.2, 7.8]; 134 mg/dL [129, 140]; LGL-B: 5.0 mmol/L [4.7, 5.2]; 89 mg/dL [84, 94], p<0.001) and 24-h %CV (HGL-B: 20% [18, 21]; LGL-B: 17% [15, 18], p<0.001). There were no detectable differences between interventions for fasting lipids, ketones, satiety scores and physical activity.

CONCLUSIONS: In women with GDM, an LGL-B was associated with lower breakfast PPG and 24-h %CV. Targeting breakfast may be a simple dietary strategy to improve glycemia and reduce morning bolus insulin requirements.

articles.title: Altered stimulus-intensity encoding occurs in the primary somatosensory cortex of a central post-stroke pain rat model.
articles.abstract: Central post-stroke pain (CPSP) is a chronic form of pain that develops after ventral posterolateral thalamus (VPL) lesions and may involve maladaptive plasticity within central somatosensory pathways. Although abnormalities in the primary somatosensory cortex (S1) are observed in patients and animal models, the mechanism by which thalamic lesions alter cortical processing of sensory stimuli remains unclear. Here, we investigated stimulus intensity encoding and dendritic remodeling in S1 using a VPL-lesion CPSP rat model. Behavioral assessments were conducted, and mechanical allodynia was observed 3 weeks after lesion induction. Accordingly, the animals were examined during the early (1 week) and late (4-5 weeks) phases after VPL lesions. A distorted stimulus-response relationship was observed in S1 during the late phase, as indicated from voltage-sensitive dye imaging. The responses to low-intensity stimuli were enhanced, and response scaling at higher stimulus intensities was reduced. Increased cortical sensitivity to weak stimuli was associated with the severity of mechanical allodynia. Additionally, morphological analyses were conducted on layer II/III pyramidal neurons. Distinct patterns of dendritic remodeling were observed. Apical dendritic length and branching diminished during the early phase, while basal dendritic arborization increased during the late phase. These findings suggest that time-dependent structural and functional reorganization occurs in S1 following thalamic injury. This reorganization may contribute to abnormal sensory processing in patients with CPSP and offer new insights into the underlying pathophysiological mechanisms.

articles.title: Real-World Effectiveness of Dupilumab in Patients with Severe Asthma in Europe: Findings from the EU-ADVANTAGE Study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Dupilumab is approved in Europe for severe asthma (SA) characterized by type 2 inflammation. However, real-world effectiveness data from European countries are limited. EU-ADVANTAGE study aimed to evaluate the real-world effectiveness of dupilumab across five European Union (EU) countries: France, Germany, Italy, the Netherlands, and Spain.

METHODS: This retrospective chart review study leveraged patient medical records captured by physicians within their clinical practice across 5 EU countries. Patients (≥12 years) with physician-confirmed SA who initiated dupilumab (index) between May 2019 and February 2022 and had 12 months of pre- and post-index data were included. SA exacerbations, oral corticosteroid (OCS) prescriptions, and healthcare resource utilization were compared between the 12-month pre- and post-dupilumab initiation. Poisson regression models with robust variance were used to estimate incidence rate ratios (IRRs) for SA exacerbations and OCS prescriptions, after adjusting for COVID-19 and seasonality.

RESULTS: Overall, 1,281 patient records (mean±standard deviation age, 46.0±15.6 years; males, 61.4%) were extracted by 547 physicians. Most patients (91.3%) were biologic naïve before dupilumab initiation. A significant 50% reduction in SA exacerbations (IRR, 0.50; 95%CI, 0.41-0.61) was observed post-dupilumab initiation despite a concurrent 68% reduction in OCS prescriptions (IRR, 0.32; 95%CI, 0.25-0.41) (both P<0.001). Consistent reductions were observed in patients with type 2 inflammatory subgroup. Overall, 9.2% and 3.1% of patients had ≥1 hospitalization during the pre- and post-dupilumab initiation, respectively.

CONCLUSIONS: In this retrospective study, dupilumab was associated with a significant reduction in SA exacerbations and OCS prescriptions, confirming its utility in routine clinical settings.

articles.title: Advances in genetically engineered and humanized mouse models for dissecting sepsis mechanisms and therapeutic response.
articles.abstract: Sepsis remains a major cause of global mortality, yet translation from preclinical studies to effective targeted therapies has been limited. A key barrier is that conventional animal models incompletely capture human immune circuitry and patient heterogeneity. Recent progress in mouse genetics, CRISPR/Cas-based genome editing, conditional alleles (Cre-loxP), and next-generation humanized platforms has expanded the toolkit for functional interrogation of host pathways that shape sepsis outcomes. Germline and cell-type-restricted perturbations have helped map roles for pattern-recognition signaling, inflammasome modules, cell-death effectors, and immune checkpoints, while also showing that the same pathway can produce different phenotypes depending on cellular context. Cross-species differences in innate immune gene networks and caspase biology motivate validation in humanized systems and integration with human genetic evidence. Emerging "wildling" and genetically diverse panels provide complementary approaches to model environmental exposure and host variation. Coupling these platforms with single-cell multi-omics and endotype stratification can link genotype-to-phenotype mechanisms with biomarker-informed therapeutic testing.

articles.title: Assessment of Thoracic Ultrasound as a Diagnostic Tool for Lower Respiratory Tract Disorders in Sheep.
articles.abstract: Lower respiratory tract diseases (LRTDs) are a major cause of morbidity and mortality in sheep. Diagnosis is challenging not only because clinical signs are often mild or absent under field conditions, but also because adult sheep may develop a wide range of diseases affecting the lower airways with overlapping clinical presentations. This study evaluated the diagnostic performance of distance observation, comprehensive clinical examination, and thoracic ultrasonography (TUS) in sheep with suspected LRTDs, using post-mortem findings as the reference standard. A total of 103 sheep from different ages and production systems were examined following a standardised protocol including distance assessment, detailed respiratory examination, TUS, and complete necropsy with histopathology and pathogen detection. Distance observation identified very few clinically suspected animals and showed poor agreement with post-mortem diagnosis. Clinical examination detected 73 pulmonary lesions, mainly associated with the ovine respiratory complex (ORC), small ruminant lentiviral infection (SRLV), and gangrenous pneumonia (GP). TUS identified 72 lesions and showed high sensitivity for pulmonary consolidation, interstitial patterns, abscesses, cavitations, and subpleural abnormalities. Ultrasonographic patterns correlated closely with necropsy findings. Compared with distance assessment and clinical examination, TUS provided superior detection and characterisation of LRTDs. This study demonstrates the value of a standardized TUS-based approach for the ante-mortem differential diagnosis of the main ovine LRTDs and supports its incorporation as a rapid, reliable, and practical complementary diagnostic tool to improve clinical decision-making at flock level.

articles.title: A Holistic Approach to Potato Suberin Analysis: A Time Travel from Breakdown Products to Suberin Deposition to Metabolite Profiling of Wound Periderm.
articles.abstract: The outer skins of potato tubers undergo healing after the wounding that occurs during cultivation and processing of this major food crop, but the macromolecular structure of the suberized cell wall barriers that mitigate drought and infection has remained elusive. Because many prior models have drawn upon top-down analyses of depolymerization treatments that are known to be incomplete, we devised a comprehensive strategy of bottom-up monitoring of wound-healing metabolites at several time points, solid-state NMR (ssNMR) compositional analysis of the suberized cell wall, and top-down chemical analysis of soluble chemical depolymerization products. Liquid and gas chromatography - mass spectrometry (LC-MS and GC-MS) metabolite profiling were conducted for extracts from wound tissues in four potato cultivars with differing skin morphologies at 0, 1, 2, 3, and 7 days post wounding. In parallel, 13C ssNMR was used to characterize the suberin-enriched polymeric material. Finally, the biopolymer composite was subjected to mild chemical breakdown followed by LC-MS and GC-MS analyses. By coordinating these phytochemical analyses, we found new glycoalkaloid, sterol, and phenolic amine compounds that are incorporated within the biopolymer composite. These findings enrich our picture of the suberin macromolecular structure that develops after wounding or in native skins to protect potato tubers from environmental threats.

articles.title: Association of ophthalmic disease and physical activity in All of Us Research Program.
articles.journal: Journal of sport and health science
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The association between physical activity (PA) and ophthalmic disease remains uncertain, as most studies relied on self-report. This study aimed to evaluate the associations between long-term, objectively measured PA by wearable devices (Fitbit) and the incidence and prevalence of common ophthalmic diseases in the All of Us Research Program.

METHODS: We conducted cross-sectional and longitudinal analyses of 14,757 adults with electronic health record (EHR) and Fitbit data. Participants had at least 6 months of valid Fitbit wear (≥10 h/day and ≥100 steps/day). The cohort had a mean age of 55.0 ± 15.7 years (mean ± SD); 70.4% were female, and 79.1% were White. Mean daily step counts and minutes of moderate-to-vigorous physical activity (MVPA) were evaluated in relation to age-related macular degeneration (AMD), diabetic retinopathy (DR), primary open-angle glaucoma (POAG), and senile cataract identified using International Classification of Diseases codes. Logistic regression estimated odds ratios (ORs) for prevalent disease, and Cox proportional hazards models estimated hazard ratios (HRs) for incident disease. Models were adjusted for age, sex, race, and body mass index. DR analyses were also restricted to participants with diabetes mellitus.

RESULTS: In cross-sectional analyses, higher PA was significantly associated with lower odds of DR among participants with DM (steps per 1000: OR = 0.91, 95% confident interval (95%CI): 0.86-0.95; p < 0.001; MVPA per 10 min: OR = 0.87, 95%CI: 0.82-0.93; p < 0.001). No significant cross-sectional associations were observed between PA and AMD, POAG, or senile cataract. In longitudinal analyses, higher PA predicted a lower risk of incident DR among participants with DM (steps: HR = 0.93, 95%CI: 0.87-0.99; p = 0.022; MVPA: HR = 0.86, 95%CI: 0.79-0.93; p < 0.001). No significant longitudinal associations were found between PA and AMD, POAG, or senile cataract.

CONCLUSION: Our findings suggest a strong inverse association between sustained PA and incident DR and underscore the value of long-term wearable data for ophthalmic research.

articles.title: A GLP-1/apelin dual receptor agonist shows neuroprotective effects in the MPTP mouse model of Parkinson's disease.
articles.abstract: Parkinson's disease (PD) is a chronic disorder with no disease-modifying treatment available. The glucagon-like peptide-1 (GLP-1) class of drugs is on the market to treat diabetes and obesity. GLP-1 drugs have also shown neuroprotective effects in animal models and clinical trials in PD patients. Apelin (APJ) is an adipokine peptide hormone with neuroprotective actions in preclinical studies. Here, we test the effects of a rationally designed bifunctional peptide, namely ELA (exendin-4-linker-apelin), in the MPTP mouse model of PD. The single GLP-1 receptor agonist liraglutide was used as a comparator. Motor activity was improved by both drugs (open field, pole test, Rotarod), and the inflammation response was reduced (activation of microglia and astrocytes, pro-inflammatory cytokine levels). In addition, synapse numbers were improved in the striatum (Golgi strain, TEM), expression of synapse-associated proteins was enhanced, alongside reduced expression of genes that increase mitochondrial fission. Mitochondrial fusion gene expressions (Opa1, Mfn2, Drp1) and mitochondrial morphology were also normalized (TEM). ELA was superior to liraglutide in some, but not all, parameters measured. The results suggest that the rational design of bifunctional peptides targeting both GLP-1 and APJ pathways-with optimized pharmacokinetics and enhanced blood-brain barrier (BBB) permeability-merits further investigation as a strategy for developing more effective treatments for PD.

articles.title: Vitamin D Deficiency Associated Dyslipidemia in Type 2 Diabetes and Changes Following Vitamin D2 Supplementation.
articles.journal: The Journal of steroid biochemistry and molecular biology
articles.abstract: Vitamin D deficiency (VDD) is common in type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) and has been linked to dyslipidemia, but the specific lipids associated with low vitamin D status are not well defined. To address this, we sought to characterize lipidomic alterations associated with VDD in T2DM and describe the changes following vitamin D₂ (VD2) supplementation. Specifically, untargeted serum lipidomics with anthropometric and clinical measurements were performed in 219 adults with T2DM, classified as VDD (25(OH)D < 20ng/mL; n = 138) or non-VDD (25(OH)D ≥ 20ng/mL; n = 81). A subset of VDD participants (n = 20) completed a 3-month VD2 supplementation trial. Lipids were profiled by UHPLC-HRMS and analyzed in relation to metabolic and anthropometric measures. Our analysis identified 112 lipid species differentially expressed in VDD, characterized by reduced ether-linked phosphatidylcholines (EtherPCs) and elevated ceramide 16:0. EtherPCs showed negative correlation with HbA1c, BMI, as well as body fat, and positive associations with muscle mass and bone mineral content, whereas ceramides inversely associated with these metabolic indices. Following 3-month VD2 supplementation, increases in circulating 25(OH)D and reductions in HbA1c were observed, accompanied by changes on the targeted lipidome, including elevated EtherPCs and reduced ceramide profiles (Cer 20:0, Cer 22:0, Cer 16:0/24:0). In conclusion, VDD in T2DM is associated with a distinct lipidomic profile marked by EtherPCs depletion and ceramide accumulation. The observed lipidomic changes following VD2 supplementation suggest the presence of a VD2-responsive lipid signature, which may have potential implications for metabolic risk management in T2DM.

articles.title: Raising diagnoses or doubts? RAISE score for transthyretin cardiac amyloidosis identification in aortic stenosis.
Effectiveness of Continuous Automatic Endotracheal Cuff Pressure Monitoring in Preventing Ventilator-Associated Pneumonia in the Pediatric Intensive Care Unit: A Randomized Controlled Trial.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Ventilator-associated pneumonia (VAP) is a major healthcare-associated infection in critically ill children, primarily driven by microaspiration around the endotracheal tube cuff.

RESEARCH QUESTION: Does continuous automatic cuff pressure monitoring (CACPM) reduce the incidence of VAP compared to intermittent manual cuff pressure monitoring (IMCPM) in critically ill pediatric patients requiring mechanical ventilation?

STUDY DESIGN AND METHODS: In this open-label, randomized controlled superiority trial, pediatric patients requiring mechanical ventilation for ≥48 hours were randomly assigned (1:1) to either CACPM or IMCPM. The target cuff pressure was strictly maintained at 20-25 cmH2O. The primary outcome was the proportion of patients developing VAP within 28 days following intubation, evaluated in the intention to treat population. Secondary outcomes included time to VAP diagnosis and target pressure compliance. Statistical approaches included Kaplan-Meier survival analysis and multivariable Cox proportional hazard regression.

RESULTS: Among 241 randomized patients, ITT analysis showed lower VAP with CACPM than IMCPM (13.3% vs 24.0%; risk difference, -10.6 percentage points; 95% CI, -20.3 to -0.8; P=0.034), with similar PP findings (15.0% vs 26.6%; P=0.044). ITT incidence density was 15.7 vs 27.1 per 1,000 ventilator-days (IRR, 1.73; 95% CI, 0.94-3.18; P=0.080). Unadjusted time-to-VAP was nonsignificant (HR, 1.80; 95% CI, 0.976-3.321; P=0.060), whereas adjusted Cox analysis narrowly indicated a higher VAP hazard with IMCPM (HR, 1.90; 95% CI, 1.024-3.510; P=0.042). Target-pressure compliance was higher with CACPM (P<0.001).

INTERPRETATION: CACPM significantly reduces the proportion of critically ill pediatric patients developing VAP compared with IMCPM. This preventive effect appears directly linked to improved target pressure compliance, suggesting that automated regulation could be a valuable addition to pediatric VAP prevention strategies.

CLINICAL TRIAL REGISTRATION: ClinicalTrials.gov, NCT05918172.

articles.title: Inflammatory rheumatic diseases under mogamulizumab: a multicenter series of 11 cases.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Mogamulizumab (MOGA), an anti-CCR4 monoclonal antibody for mycosis fungoides (MF) and Sézary syndrome (SS), can trigger immune-mediated complications, such as rashes or endocrine disorders. Rheumatological manifestations are rare.

OBJECTIVES: To describe cases of inflammatory rheumatism (IR) induced or worsened by MOGA in MF/SS patients.

METHODS: A retrospective study collected cases of IR (polymyalgia rheumatica [PMR], rheumatoid arthritis [RA], spondylarthritis, or unclassified IR) in MF/SS patients treated with MOGA across centers of the French Cutaneous Lymphomas Group. Clinical, biological, and imaging data were analyzed.

RESULTS: Eleven patients (7 men, 4 women; median age: 72 years) developed IR during (10/11) or soon after (1/11) MOGA treatment. Symptoms included joint pain, stiffness, and functional impairment. All had biological inflammatory syndrome, synovitis on ultrasound, and no autoantibodies. PET-CT confirmed hypermetabolism consistent with intense joint inflammation (SUV=8.0). Management with systemic corticosteroids ± methotrexate led to remission in most cases. MOGA had to be discontinued in 8 patients, with lymphoma control maintained in 6.

CONCLUSIONS: MOGA may induce disabling IR, potentially via CCR4+ regulatory T-cell depletion. Early recognition and treatment with corticosteroids ± methotrexate are essential, though MOGA discontinuation may be required.

articles.title: Transcranial magneto-acoustic stimulation modulates M1-PPN spike-LFP coupling and improves motor dysfunction in parkinsonian rats.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: This study aimed to investigate whether transcranial magneto-acoustic stimulation (TMAS) improves motor dysfunction in Parkinson's disease (PD) model rats and whether its effects are associated with modulation of bidirectional spike-local field potential (LFP) coupling between the primary motor cortex (M1) and the pedunculopontine nucleus (PPN).

METHODS: Two primary cohorts (n = 24 each) comprised WT + Sham, PD + Sham, and PD + TMAS groups (n = 8/group). An independent supplementary healthy-control experiment included newly allocated WT + Sham and WT + TMAS groups (n = 8/group; 16 rats total), both of which followed the Experiment 1 workflow. Pre-treatment APO rotation counts were compared between the two PD groups as a functional index of lesion severity. Motor performance, TH and c-Fos immunofluorescence, and in vivo M1-PPN electrophysiology were evaluated. Spike-LFP coherence and phase-locking value (PLV) were compared among the three primary groups separately within each putative neuronal class, behavioral state, and frequency band.

RESULTS: APO rotation counts did not differ between PD + Sham and PD + TMAS rats before treatment in either experiment. TMAS-treated PD rats showed improved behavioral performance, and the pattern of differences in M1-PPN spike-LFP coherence and PLV relative to PD + Sham rats varied across frequency bands, behavioral states, and putative neuronal classes. At the terminal histological assessment, PD + TMAS rats showed a higher proportion of TH-positive cells in the SNc than PD + Sham rats. In the independent healthy-control experiment, WT + TMAS did not significantly differ from WT + Sham in most behavioral indices or TH-positive cell proportion, but it showed a shorter pole-test turning time and a higher c-Fos-positive cell proportion.

CONCLUSION: TMAS ameliorated motor deficits in PD model rats and was associated with frequency band, behavioral-state, and putative-class-dependent changes in M1-PPN spike-LFP coupling. These findings provide preliminary evidence supporting TMAS as a potential noninvasive neuromodulation strategy for PD-related motor dysfunction, while the disease specificity of the electrophysiological effects remains to be established.

articles.title: A Visual LGE Extent Cutoff for Mortality Risk Stratification in Ischemic Cardiomyopathy.
articles.journal: Journal of cardiovascular magnetic resonance : official journal of the Society for Cardiovascular Magnetic Resonance
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Late gadolinium enhancement (LGE) extent has been linked to adverse outcomes in ischemic cardiomyopathy (ICM). While quantitative methods of LGE assessment are widely accepted, semi-quantitative methods remain debated but still hold value. This study aimed to determine an optimal LGE segments cutoff for ICM patients with left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF) <50% in a large bicentric cohort.

METHODS: This bicentric retrospective French study included 3,591 patients with ICM (defined by prior myocardial infarction and/or coronary revascularization), LVEF <50%, and ischemic-LGE on cardiovascular magnetic resonance performed between 2008 and 2022. Ischemic LGE extent was assessed semi-quantitatively using the 17-segment model. An optimal cutoff for LGE extent was derived in the derivation cohort (Center 1, N=2,900) using a conditional inference tree and externally validated in an independent cohort (Center 2, N=691). The primary outcome was all-cause mortality. Prognostic performance was compared between a conventional model based on LVEF ≤35% alone and a combined model integrating LVEF ≤35% with the newly identified ischemic-LGE cutoff. Model discrimination and reclassification were assessed using Harrell's C-index, continuous net reclassification improvement (NRI), and integrated discrimination improvement (IDI).

RESULTS: During a median follow-up of 9 years, 549 patients (15.3%) died. The optimal cutoff of visual LGE extent to predict mortality was 5 segments. Patients with high ischemic LGE extent (>5 segments) had a markedly increased risk of all-cause mortality compared with those with ≤5 segments (adjusted hazard ratio, 3.8; 95% CI: 3.0-4.8; p<0.001). Survival discrimination according to this cutoff was consistent across derivation and validation cohorts. Compared with the conventional LVEF ≤35% model alone, the combined model integrating the >5 ischemic-LGE segment cutoff significantly improved risk discrimination and patient reclassification (ΔC-index: +16%; continuous NRI: +36%; IDI: +4%; all p<0.001).

CONCLUSION: In patients with ICM, reduced LVEF (<50%), and detectable ischemic LGE, a visually assessed segment-based cutoff of >5 ischemic-LGE segments was independently associated with all-cause mortality and validated in an independent second-center cohort. This pragmatic, software-independent assessment may complement conventional risk stratification, although prospective studies are required before integration into clinical decision-making.

articles.title: Global Sociodemographic Disparities in the Severity of Alcohol-Associated Hepatitis.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION AND OBJECTIVES: Alcohol-associated hepatitis (AH) carries high short-term mortality, yet the contribution of sociodemographic factors to disease severity and outcomes is poorly defined.

PATIENTS AND METHODS: We conducted a prospective cohort study across 30 centers in 14 countries (January 2015-September 2024). We included adults who met National Institute on Alcohol Abuse and Alcoholism (NIAAA) criteria for AH. Outcomes included infections, access to liver transplantation (LT), and survival. Mortality was analyzed with Fine-Gray competing-risk models.

RESULTS: Among 726 participants (median age, 49 years; 90.1% male), 24.8% had less than secondary education, and 37.6% reported good social support. Severe AH was more frequent in those without secondary education than in those with at least secondary education (97.2% vs. 81.7%; P<0.0001). The 30- and 90-day survival rates were lower among participants without secondary education (66.4% and 50.4%, respectively) than among those with at least secondary education (88.4% and 81.2%, respectively). In adjusted analyses, moderate and good social support were associated with lower mortality (each sHR 0.58, 95% CI, 0.38-0.89 and 0.38-0.94, respectively), as were secondary (sHR 0.48, 95% CI, 0.24-0.97) and tertiary education (sHR 0.44, 95% CI, 0.20-0.97) and corticosteroid use (sHR 0.63, 95% CI, 0.42-0.95).

CONCLUSIONS: Lower educational attainment and poorer perceived social support were associated with greater AH severity at presentation and higher mortality, independent of clinical risk factors. These findings highlight the need to address social determinants and favor equitable access to evidence-based therapies, including early LT.

articles.title: Recurrence of autoimmune liver diseases after liver transplantation: exploratory analysis of a pooled Latin American cohort.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION AND OBJECTIVES: Autoimmune liver diseases (AILDs) are an increasingly frequent indication for liver transplantation in Latin America. Recurrence after transplantation may affect graft function and long-term outcomes; however, recurrence patterns and associated factors remain incompletely characterized. We aimed to describe recurrence after liver transplantation in a pooled cohort of AILDs and to explore factors associated with recurrence, overall survival, and retransplantation.

PATIENTS AND METHODS: We conducted a retrospective cohort study of adult patients with AILDs who underwent liver transplantation between 2005 and 2023. Recurrence was defined using biochemical, serological, and histological criteria. Associations were evaluated using logistic regression and Kaplan-Meier survival analyses.

RESULTS: A total of 154 patients were included, of whom 64 (41.5%) developed recurrence after a median of 49 months (IQR 21.2-91). In the primary analysis, recurrence was associated with elevated pre-transplant ALT and AST levels and a history of acute rejection. In sensitivity analyses, elevated AST levels showed the most consistent association with recurrence. Associations involving ALT were attenuated after subgroup restriction, whereas the association with acute rejection varied across analyses. No significant differences were observed in overall survival or retransplantation rates between patients with and without recurrence.

CONCLUSIONS: Recurrence after liver transplantation was frequent and varied across autoimmune liver disease subtypes. Elevated pre-transplant AST levels were consistently associated with recurrence across exploratory analyses. Despite the high frequency of recurrence, no significant association was observed with impaired overall survival or increased retransplantation. These findings require confirmation in larger multicenter studies with disease-specific analyses.

articles.title: MIND Diet Adherence and Parkinson's Disease Risk, Progression, and Age at Onset: A Systematic Review.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The Mediterranean-DASH Intervention for Neurodegenerative Delay (MIND) diet has been associated with cognitive benefits, but its relationship with Parkinson's disease (PD) remains unclear. We systematically reviewed evidence on associations between MIND diet adherence and PD-related outcomes.

METHODS: PubMed, Embase, and Google Scholar were searched through June 2026. Eligible observational and interventional studies evaluated MIND diet adherence in relation to PD risk, incident parkinsonism, disease progression, severity, or age at onset. Study quality was assessed using the Newcastle-Ottawa Scale. In case of substantial heterogeneity, findings were synthesized qualitatively.

PROSPERO: CRD420251123365.

RESULTS: Five observational studies (73,790 participants) were included. Higher MIND diet adherence was associated with lower incident parkinsonism (HR 0.89, 95% CI 0.83-0.96), slower progression of parkinsonian signs, lower PD incidence (HR 0.75, 95% CI 0.58-0.97), and later PD onset. One study found no association with PD risk or progression, whereas another reported lower patient-reported symptom burden with greater MIND diet adherence. Three studies were rated poor quality and one good quality. Certainty of evidence was low for PD incidence and very low for all other outcomes. Quantitative synthesis was not performed because of heterogeneity in outcomes, designs, and effect measures.

CONCLUSIONS: Evidence linking MIND diet adherence to PD is limited and observational. Higher adherence may be associated with lower incident parkinsonism, slower progression, reduced PD incidence in selected women, and later PD onset. However, certainty of evidence was low to very low, precluding causal inference. Prospective cohorts and randomized dietary trials are needed.

articles.title: Factors Associated With Mineralocorticoid Receptor Antagonist Initiation in Newly Diagnosed Heart Failure.
Values-Centered Discussions Among Family Caregivers of Patients with Left Ventricular Assist Devices: A Mixed Methods Study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Family caregivers of left ventricular assist device (LVAD) recipients play a central role in managing complex care and navigating ongoing healthcare decisions. Although personal values may influence caregiving experiences and decision-making, little is known about how caregivers engage in values-centered discussions with the healthcare team.

OBJECTIVE: To examine LVAD caregivers' engagement in values-centered discussions and identify factors influencing these interactions.

METHODS: A sequential explanatory mixed methods study among LVAD caregivers at an outpatient mechanical circulatory support clinic in the Southeastern United States. Survey data were analyzed using descriptive statistics to summarize patterns of values-centered discussions. Interviews with a subset of participants were analyzed using thematic analysis to identify factors influencing these interactions. Quantitative and qualitative findings were integrated using joint displays.

RESULTS: Caregivers (N=32) reported high levels of feeling heard and understood in healthcare interactions (median [IQR], 3.50 [3.00-4.00] and moderate assertiveness in communicating care-related concerns (median [IQR], 7.00 [4.00-8.00]). Values discussions most often occurred with spouses/partners (75%), family members (69%), and LVAD coordinators (56%). Discussions were more common after implantation (89%) and during hospitalizations (93%) and clinic visits (86%) than via telehealth (31%). Three themes (n=11) explained these patterns: emotional readiness, relational trust, and situational context. Emotional overwhelm in the early post-implant period limited discussions, whereas trust, accessibility, and longitudinal relationships facilitated engagement.

CONCLUSIONS: Values-centered discussions depend not only on opportunity but also emotional readiness, healthcare team relationships, and care context. Prioritizing relationship-building and ongoing opportunities for discussion may enhance engagement and support more value-concordant advanced heart failure care.

articles.title: Tricuspid Edge-to-Edge Repair in Patients With Prior Cardiac Transplantation: Results From the TRILUMINATE Pivotal Trial.
Sacubitril/Valsartan Versus ACEi/ARB Across the Ejection Fraction Spectrum: A Multistate Real-World Cohort.
Vasorelaxant and Antihypertensive Effects of Salicylaldehyde: Involvement of Renin-Angiotensin System and Calcium/Potassium Channel Modulation.
articles.abstract:
ETHNOPHARMACOLOGICAL RELEVANCE: Natural products are widely used in traditional medicine for managing cardiovascular disorders, including hypertension. Salicylaldehyde, a naturally occurring aromatic aldehyde found in plant-derived preparations, remains poorly characterized regarding its vascular effects.

AIM OF THE STUDY: This study aimed to evaluate the vasorelaxant and antihypertensive properties of salicylaldehyde and to elucidate its underlying mechanisms of action.

MATERIALS AND METHODS: Molecular docking was performed to assess interactions with key vascular targets. In vitro vasorelaxant activity was investigated using isolated rat thoracic aortic rings precontracted with epinephrine (EP, 10 μM) or potassium chloride (KCl, 80 mM). The involvement of endothelium-dependent and independent pathways was examined using pharmacological inhibitors and angiotensin II-induced contraction assays. In vivo effects were evaluated following oral administration of salicylaldehyde (20 and 40 mg/kg) in normotensive and N-nitro-L-arginine methyl ester (L-NAME)-induced hypertensive rats. Blood pressure was measured using a tail-cuff system during acute (6 h) and sub-chronic (7 days) treatments.

RESULTS: Salicylaldehyde showed strong binding affinities toward angiotensin-converting enzyme (ACE) and angiotensin II Type 1 Receptor. It induced concentration-dependent vasorelaxation, significantly reduced after endothelial removal and under KCl-induced contraction. Its effects were attenuated by inhibitors of ACE, ACE2, ATP-sensitive K+ channels, and L-type calcium channels, and it inhibited angiotensin II-induced contraction. In vivo, it significantly reduced systolic and diastolic blood pressure in hypertensive rats.

CONCLUSION: Salicylaldehyde exerts antihypertensive effects via multiple mechanisms and may contribute to the cardiovascular activity of plant-derived remedies.

articles.title: Successful bilateral lung transplantation in a patient with severe pulmonary blastomycosis.
articles.journal: American journal of transplantation : official journal of the American Society of Transplantation and the American Society of Transplant Surgeons
articles.abstract: Severe pulmonary blastomycosis may progress to acute respiratory distress syndrome (ARDS) necessitating prolonged extracorporeal support, and ultimately lead to irreversible pulmonary injury. Whether these patients should proceed to lung transplantation remains controversial. We report a 38-year-old man with type 2 diabetes mellitus who developed fulminant pulmonary blastomycosis following environmental exposure in Ontario, Canada. Despite prolonged treatment with liposomal amphotericin B and azole therapy, his course was complicated by respiratory failure requiring mechanical ventilation, and prolonged venovenous extracorporeal membrane oxygenation (VV-ECMO), with concomitant recurrent ventilator-associated bacterial pneumonias and treatment-related nephrotoxicity. Although microbiologic markers gradually improved, including declining urinary Blastomyces antigen levels and negative respiratory fungal cultures, lung function recovery failed to occur. Ongoing uncertainty persisted regarding uncontrolled infection versus irreversible pulmonary injury. The patient ultimately underwent successful bilateral lung transplantation while receiving antifungal therapy. Post-transplant recovery progressed slowly but smoothly, with liberation from ECMO and no evidence of recurrent fungal disease. This case suggests that concern for invasive fungal infection persistence should not automatically preclude lung transplantation as a means of survival for irreversible lung injury when assessment supports favorable microbiologic control.

articles.title: "Interstitial lung disease with associated severe pulmonary hypertension is rarely idiopathic by clinical or pathologic measures".
articles.journal: The Journal of heart and lung transplantation : the official publication of the International Society for Heart Transplantation
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Interstitial lung disease (ILD) patients who develop severe pulmonary hypertension (PH) have rapidly progressive disease and increased mortality, but their clinical and pathologic phenotypes are poorly defined. Improved understanding and identification of these patients will expedite beneficial PH-targeted therapeutics and referral for lung transplantation.

METHODS: We conducted a comprehensive retrospective study of a large cohort of ILD patients who underwent lung transplant at UCLA. Multidisciplinary Discussion (MDD) was used to establish ILD etiologies incorporating all available clinical, radiographic, and pathologic data. Severe pre-capillary PH was defined as pulmonary vascular resistance >5 Wood units on cardiac catheterization. Quantitative histopathologic analysis of explanted idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis (IPF) lungs was performed using blinded whole-slide annotation by two pulmonary pathologists, comparing the pathologic features of IPF with severe PH to IPF without PH.

RESULTS: Among 347 ILD patients, 13% had severe PH. In the large majority of cases (86%), the correct ILD diagnosis/etiology was established clinically with MDD alone. Only 20% of severe PH cases were classified as IPF, with the most common subtype identified as autoimmune-associated ILD. On histopathology, IPF patients with severe PH demonstrated a similar extent of usual interstitial pneumonia but markedly less normal lung and a greater burden of atypical pathology, particularly nonspecific interstitial pneumonia, compared to IPF patients without PH.

CONCLUSIONS: Our study illustrates the low prevalence of IPF in severe PH-ILD, describes a novel finding of distinct histopathologic features of IPF patients with severe PH versus no PH, and demonstrates the diagnostic utility of MDD without explant pathology.

articles.title: Inadequate empirical therapy and unnecessary broad-spectrum antibiotic use in community-onset bloodstream infection: A retrospective cohort study.
articles.journal: International journal of infectious diseases : IJID : official publication of the International Society for Infectious Diseases
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: To evaluate empirical antimicrobial therapy (EAT) adequacy, risk factors for inadequate EAT (IEAT) and multidrug-resistant (MDR) infection, and unnecessary broad-spectrum use in emergency department (ED) patients with bloodstream infection (BSI).

METHODS: Retrospective cohort study of adults with community-onset BSI at a tertiary-care ED (2022-2024). Adequate EAT (AEAT) was ≥1 administered agent with in vitro activity. Logistic regression identified factors associated with IEAT, unnecessary broad-spectrum therapy, and MDR infection. Cox regression assessed 7- and 30-day mortality.

RESULTS: Among 1,716 BSI episodes, 464 (27%) received IEAT or no EAT. MDR organisms accounted for 370 cases (21.6%) and were associated with IEAT (aOR 7.40, 95% CI 5.55-9.93). Of 606 patients receiving broad-spectrum EAT, 490 (80.9%) regimens were unnecessary. Community-acquired infection was associated with unnecessary broad-spectrum therapy (aOR 3.96, 95% CI 1.65-11.79), and healthcare-associated infection with MDR infection (aOR 2.02, 95% CI 1.31-3.14). Seven-day mortality was associated with polymicrobial infection (aHR 2.14, 95% CI 1.39-3.30), long-term care facility residence (aHR 1.72, 95% CI 1.20-2.46), and vasopressor requirement (aHR 3.20, 95% CI 2.21-4.62).

CONCLUSIONS: IEAT was associated with MDR pathogens, and unnecessary broad-spectrum use was common. Improved MDR risk stratification may optimise EAT by reducing inadequate coverage and avoidable broad-spectrum exposure in the ED.

articles.title: A Propensity-Matched Analysis of Pre Versus Concomitant Percutaneous Coronary Intervention in Patients Undergoing Transcatheter Aortic Valve Replacement With Frailty-Related High-Risk Features.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) is frequently performed in patients undergoing transcatheter aortic valve replacement (TAVR); however, the optimal timing of PCI remains uncertain, particularly in patients with frailty-related high-risk features. Evidence comparing pre-TAVR versus concomitant PCI strategies in this vulnerable population is limited.

METHODS: We conducted a retrospective cohort study using the TriNetX Research Network to identify patients with frailty-related high-risk features undergoing TAVR with either pre-TAVR PCI (3 months to 2 weeks before TAVR) or concomitant PCI (same day as TAVR). Propensity score matching (1:1) was performed using demographics, comorbidities, frailty-related features, and antiplatelet and anticoagulant therapy. The primary outcome was a 90-day composite including all-cause mortality, acute kidney injury, bleeding requiring transfusion, gastrointestinal bleeding, intracranial hemorrhage, acute coronary syndrome, and ischemic stroke. Secondary outcomes included the composite outcome at 30 days and 1 year, as well as individual components.

RESULTS: After propensity score matching, 361 patients were included in each group with adequate baseline balance. The primary 90-day composite outcome occurred in 27.4% of patients undergoing pre-TAVR PCI and 29.4% undergoing concomitant PCI (RR 1.07, 95% CI 0.85-1.35; p=0.56). At 30 days, the composite outcome occurred in 21.9% and 24.4% of patients, respectively (RR 1.11, 95% CI 0.85-1.45; p=0.43). At 1 year, the composite outcome occurred in 37.1% of the pre-TAVR PCI group and 38.5% of the concomitant PCI group (RR 1.04, 95% CI 0.86-1.25; p=0.70). No significant differences were observed in all-cause mortality at any time point.

CONCLUSIONS: Among patients with frailty-related high-risk features undergoing TAVR, pre-TAVR PCI and concomitant PCI were associated with similar short- and longer-term clinical outcomes. No significant differences were observed in the 90-day composite outcome or all-cause mortality. These findings support an individualized approach to PCI timing in frail, high-risk patients.

articles.title: Prognostic implications of asymptomatic COVID-19 infection in non-small-cell lung cancer patients receiving active anticancer treatment: an observational study with prospective survival follow-up.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: We previously reported that non-small-cell lung cancer (NSCLC) was a significant predictor of delayed viral clearance from their COVID-19 infection during the Omicron variant attack between January and April 2022. We now evaluated the survival outcomes of these NSCLC patients with or without COVID-19 infection during this period.

METHODS: This prospective cohort study included 276 NSCLC patients recruited. Of them, 39 patients were SARS-CoV-2 positive through PCR testing, with viral load indicated by cycle threshold (ct) values. Propensity score matching was used to ensure the COVID-positive and COVID-negative groups were comparable in demographics, disease staging, and treatment modalities. Kaplan-Meier survival analysis and Cox regression were performed to evaluate overall survival and identify OS prognostic factors.

RESULTS: After a median follow up of 39.9 months from diagnosis (interquartile range 31.3-55.5), 20 died of COVID-19 and NSCLC. OS differences counting from either their NSCLC diagnosis, or the start of anticancer treatment were insignificant among various stages of NSCLC patients infected with COVID-19, but they were significant for COVID-negative patients (P = 0.050 and P = 0.009, respectively). Exploratory analysis revealed that ct value cutoff of > 34.14 correlated with a better OS (P = 0.039). Multivariable analysis identified chemotherapy (P = 0.002), immune checkpoint inhibitor (P = 0.019), and receipt of ≥ 2 doses of COVID-19 vaccines (P = 0.011) as significant prognosticators of OS, counting from the date of anticancer treatment.

CONCLUSION: Asymptomatic COVID-19 infection might compromise survival outcomes of NSCLC patients in this study. Closer attention may be needed.

articles.title: Borrelia miyamotoi exceeds Borrelia burgdorferi sensu lato in human exposure despite the opposite in ticks: an integrated serological, entomological and molecular study in southeastern Kazakhstan.
articles.abstract: Lyme borreliosis (LB) and hard tick-borne relapsing fever caused by Borrelia miyamotoi are emerging tick-borne infections, yet in Kazakhstan routine LB diagnosis relies on single-tier enzyme immunoassay (EIA) without confirmatory testing, and B. miyamotoi is absent from national diagnostic protocols. In 2024-2026, 1300 participants were enrolled in the Ixodes persulcatus-endemic Almaty and Jetisu regions and the non-endemic Zhambyl and Turkistan regions, across diverse clinical and tick-exposure groups. All sera were screened for IgM and IgG to both pathogens by multi-antigen protein arrays, with subsets tested by the LymeBest ELISA and the Anti-Borrelia EUROLINE-WB immunoblot. In addition, 503 ticks removed from participants were tested for borrelial DNA by PCR. Seroreactivity to B. burgdorferi sensu lato (s.l.) was rare (4/1300, 0.3%), whereas B. miyamotoi seroreactivity was more frequent (31/1300, 2.4%) and concentrated in tick-exposed groups. In ticks the pattern was the opposite: B. burgdorferi s.l. DNA was detected in 37/503 ticks (7.4%; 45.3% in I. persulcatus) and B. miyamotoi DNA in 7/64 I. persulcatus (10.9%), with four ticks co-infected, the single B. miyamotoi strain typed by eight-locus MLST matched a sequence type reported from Japan, Mongolia and China. Of the 28 participants bitten by Borrelia DNA-positive ticks who provided follow-up sera, three (10.7%) seroconverted, one to B. burgdorferi s.l. and two to B. miyamotoi. One of the latter, PCR-positive for B. miyamotoi DNA in baseline blood, is, to our knowledge, the first molecularly confirmed case of B. miyamotoi infection in Kazakhstan. The LymeBest ELISA agreed poorly with the other two assays: none of its 27 positive baseline results was confirmed by immunoblot or protein array. In contrast, immunoblot confirmed two of the four baseline samples seroreactive to B. burgdorferi s.l. by protein array, as well as the B. burgdorferi s.l. seroconversion. These findings support two-tier serological testing for LB and dedicated B. miyamotoi diagnostics in Kazakhstan.

articles.title: Strength training attenuates hepatic inflammation and potentiates mitochondrial adaptations in IL-10-deficient mice.
articles.abstract: The liver plays a central role in metabolic and immunological homeostasis through integrated signaling networks coordinating inflammation, mitochondrial markers, oxidative stress, nitric oxide bioavailability, and autophagy. Interleukin-10 (IL-10) is a key anti-inflammatory cytokine involved in tissue homeostasis, whereas physical exercise is a non-pharmacological strategy capable of improving mitochondrial markers and attenuating inflammation. However, whether IL-10 is required for hepatic autophagy-mitochondrial-inflammatory adaptations induced by strength training remains unclear. Here, we investigated the effects of IL-10 deficiency on hepatic mitochondrial markers, autophagic flux, inflammatory signaling, nitric oxide metabolism, and liver morphology, as well as the effects of strength training. Wild-type (WT) and IL-10 knockout (IL-10 KO) mice were allocated to sedentary or strength-trained groups for 8 weeks. Liver samples were analyzed by RT-qPCR, western blotting, electron paramagnetic resonance, chemiluminescence-based detection of nitric oxide metabolites, and histological assessment. Global IL-10 deficiency was associated with reduced liver autophagic flux and total STAT3 protein levels, together with increased hepatic inflammation and hepatic lipid volume fraction. Strength training improved physical performance in both genotypes and potentiated mitochondrial adaptations in IL-10 KO mice, including upregulation of respiratory chain complexes and bioenergetic gene expression. In IL-10 KO mice, strength training attenuated hepatic inflammation and modulated nitric oxide metabolism but did not restore autophagic flux or reduce hepatic lipid volume fraction. Exploratory bioinformatic analyses identified associations between IL-10 expression, selected autophagy-related genes, and chronic liver disease stage. Together, these findings suggest that strength training induces beneficial, but incomplete, hepatic adaptations in IL-10-deficient mice and highlight an association between IL-10 deficiency and alterations in hepatic autophagy, mitochondrial markers, and inflammatory status.

articles.title: Evaluation of the immunobiological properties of the attenuated strain CP-65 K for the development of a cowpox vaccine.
articles.abstract: This study evaluated the suitability and immunobiological characteristics of the attenuated strain CP-65 K for the development of a cowpox vaccine. The attenuated strain CP-65 K was non-reactogenic in both laboratory and target animals and demonstrated higher immunogenicity than vaccinia virus (VACV) strains RIBSP-B and RIBSP-V, as well as the camelpox virus (CMLV) strain KM-40, supporting its potential as a live vaccine candidate. After 15 serial passages in lamb kidney cell culture, CP-65 K retained its infectious titer (6.50 ± 0.14 to 6.67 ± 0.08 log₁₀ TCID₅₀/mL) and induced specific antibodies in vaccinated rabbits by day 21 post-immunization, confirming phenotypic stability. Administration of vaccine doses ranging from 3162 to 316,200 TCID₅₀ to laboratory animals caused no clinically significant adverse effects or mortality. Subcutaneous immunization with 10,000 TCID₅₀ induced a strong humoral immune response, with neutralizing antibody titers ranging from 1:16 to 1:64 in the virus neutralization test (VNT) and enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay (ELISA) optical density values of 1.031-1.328. In vaccinated cattle, antigen-specific antibodies against cowpox virus (CPXV) were detected from day 14 after primary vaccination and increased following booster immunization. However, no statistically significant activation of T-cell responses, including changes in CD4+/CD8+ lymphocyte populations or expression of TNF-α, IFN-γ, and IL-4 after in vitro CPXV stimulation, was observed. Challenge infection with the epizootic strain Cowpox-CAM on day 30 post-vaccination did not induce clinical signs of cowpox in vaccinated animals, whereas control animals developed hyperthermia, characteristic skin lesions, local necrosis, and evidence of systemic infection. Histological analysis confirmed pronounced local dermal lesions in non-vaccinated cattle. Antigen-specific lymphocyte proliferation observed in vitro was not accompanied by statistically significant changes in proliferating CD4+ or CD8+ T-cell subsets, and the cellular origin of the proliferating population requires further phenotypic characterization.

articles.title: Nursing management of postoperative hemorrhagic shock: A case study in intensive care.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Postoperative hemorrhagic shock is a time-critical complication associated with high morbidity and mortality, particularly in older surgical patients, requiring rapid, coordinated management in the intensive care unit (ICU). This case report describes specialized nursing management guided by the International Classification for Nursing Practice (ICNP®/CIPE®) and Benner's Clinical Wisdom Theory.

CASE PRESENTATION: An 89-year-old woman underwent emergency gastrojejunostomy for intestinal obstruction and subsequently developed hemorrhagic shock with profound anemia (hemoglobin nadir 5.8 g/dL), severe hyperlactatemia (12 mmol/L), hypothermia (33.6 °C), peripheral hypoperfusion, and hypotension (mean arterial pressure <65 mmHg). She required orotracheal intubation, invasive mechanical ventilation, and deep sedation. Diagnostic reassessment included serial hemoglobin and arterial blood gas analyses, lactate trending, invasive hemodynamic monitoring, and surgical re-exploration with intraoperative upper endoscopy, which suggested an upper gastrointestinal source (suspected Mallory-Weiss type lesion) treated endoscopically. Nursing priorities, structured using ICNP®, focused on perfusion restoration and correction of the lethal triad (hypothermia, acidosis, coagulopathy), multimodal analgesia, continuous monitoring, prevention bundles (infection and pressure injury prevention), and structured family communication.

DISCUSSION: The patient progressively stabilized, with hemoglobin increasing to 9.6 g/dL, lactate decreasing to <1 mmol/L, normothermia recovery, discontinuation of vasopressors, and no documented ICU-acquired complications during the ICU stay. This case highlights how standardized nursing language (ICNP®/CIPE®), combined with advanced clinical reasoning and evidence-based ICU bundles, can improve the structure, traceability, and continuity of nursing care in postoperative hemorrhagic shock.

articles.title: Guidelines for Decisions to Withhold or Withdraw Life-Sustaining Treatments (LST) in Adult ICU.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: The French Society of Anaesthesia and Intensive Care Medicine (Société française d'anesthésie et de réanimation, SFAR) and the French Society of Physical Medicine and Rehabilitation (Société Française de Médecine Physique et de Réadaptation (SOFMER)) aimed at providing guidelines for decisions to withhold or withdraw life-sustaining treatments (LST) in adult ICU.

DESIGN: A consensus committee of 20 experts from the SFAR and the SOFMER was convened. A formal conﬂict-of-interest (COI) policy was developed at the beginning of the process and enforced throughout. The entire guideline construction process was conducted independently of any industrial funding (i.e., pharmaceutical, medical devices).
