The authors were required to follow the rules of the Grading of Recommendations Assessment, Development and Evaluation (GRADE) system to guide the assessment of the quality of evidence. The potential drawbacks of making strong recommendations in the presence of low-quality evidence were emphasized.

METHODS: 3 fields were defined: (1) modalities of the LST decision-making process; (2) modalities for implementing an LST decision; (3) Relationships with family members, communication, disagreements, and conflicts. For each field, the objective of the recommendations was to answer a number of questions formulated according to the PICO model (population, intervention, comparison, and outcomes). Based on these questions, an extensive bibliographic search was carried out using predefined keywords according to PRISMA guidelines and analyzed using the GRADE® methodology. The recommendations were formulated according to the GRADE® methodology and then voted on by all the experts according to the GRADE® grid method.

RESULTS: The experts' work on synthesis and application of the GRADE® method resulted in 9 recommendations. Among the formalized recommendations, 1 was found to have a high level of evidence (GRADE 1), and 2 had low levels of evidence (GRADE 2). For 6 recommendations, the GRADE® methodology could not be fully applied, resulting in an expert's opinion. 2 questions could not be answered due to a lack of literature. After 1 round of rating, strong agreement was reached for all the recommendations.

CONCLUSIONS: There was strong agreement among experts to provide recommendations to improve practices for decisions to withhold or withdraw LST in the adult ICU.

articles.title: MRI-specific anxiety, patient experience, beta-blocker therapy, and image quality during cardiac magnetic resonance imaging.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Cardiac magnetic resonance (CMR) is performed in a confined scanner environment and requires patient cooperation during repeated breath-holds, factors that may contribute to distress. This mixed-methods study examined how patient experiences, emotional states, and perceived distress influence breath-hold performance and image quality during CMR, and whether these relationships differ by previous magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) experience, sex or beta-blocker therapy.

METHODS: Fifty-three patients undergoing early post-infarction CMR were included. State anxiety was assessed before and after CMR, and MRI-specific anxiety post-scan. Breath-hold effort, duration and heart rate were recorded across predefined sequences. Image quality was rated using a predefined scale. Sixteen semi-structured interviews were analysed using reflexive thematic analysis.

RESULTS: State anxiety decreased modestly after CMR (p = 0.01), with no differences related to previous MRI experience or beta-blocker therapy. MRI-specific anxiety was significantly higher among patients not receiving beta-blocker therapy, consistent with qualitative reports of bodily stress and claustrophobic sensations. Patients receiving beta-blockers described calmer emotional states. Perceived breath-hold effort was light to moderate and comparable across subgroups. Overall image quality was high, with respiratory ghosting in Grid-tagging short axis (SAX) and blurring and mis-triggering in Cine and late gadolinium enhancement SAX sequences.

CONCLUSION: Beta-blocker therapy was associated with lower MRI-specific anxiety but not general state anxiety, suggesting modulation of scanner-related physiological arousal. Procedural and emotional factors shaped cooperation during CMR.

IMPLICATIONS FOR PRACTICE: Patients not receiving beta-blockers may benefit from enhanced preparatory information and reassurance. Clear communication, breath-hold guidance and protocol flexibility may support comfort, cooperation and diagnostic image quality.

articles.title: Incentivizing Faculty and Promoting Engagement in General Surgery Residency Entrustable Professional Activities Assessments.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: The American Board of Surgery (ABS) implemented Entrustable Professional Activities (EPAs) to facilitate transition to competency-based resident assessments in July 2023. To improve faculty engagement, our institution established an intervention with a required target of less than 25% expired faculty EPA assessments for the 2024 to 2025 academic year (AY) to qualify for a shortened end-of-rotation resident evaluation form.

DESIGN: A retrospective review of de-identified institutional EPA data for the AYs 2023 to 2024, preintervention, and 2024 to 2025, postintervention, obtained from the ABS website was conducted. Faculty rater, division, activity name, phase of care, entrustability score, and narrative feedback were analyzed. Descriptive statistics were employed to assess EPA assessment volume, number of faculty raters and evaluations by division, expired assessments, and details by postgraduate training year (PGY). Chi-Square, 2-proportion z-tests, and paired t-tests were employed to compare pre and postintervention EPA assessment completion and qualities.

SETTING: Affiliate hospitals of the Medical College of Wisconsin including Froedtert Hospital, a tertiary referral center in Milwaukee; Clement J. Zablocki Veteran's Affairs Hospital; and 3 community hospitals in the Milwaukee area.

PARTICIPANTS: De-identified data from general surgery residents and faculty who completed any EPA assessment in AYs 2023 to 2024 and 2024 to 2025 were included.

RESULTS: A total of 1111 and 1464 EPA assessments were completed for the 2023 to 2024 and 2024 to 2025 AYs, respectively, yielding a 1.32-fold increase post-intervention. There was a 1.27-fold increase in participating faculty raters (63 vs 80). Meaningful narrative feedback increased from 53.3% to 57.8% (p = 0.02). Of 11 service rotations with participating faculty raters, 5 met the <25% EPA assessment expiration metric in 2023 to 2024, compared to 8 in 2024 to 2025. The overall EPA assessment expiration rate decreased from 40.0% pre-intervention to 13.9% postintervention (p < 0.001).

CONCLUSIONS: Incentivizing faculty to improve upon expired EPA assessments using a shortened end-of-rotation resident evaluation form increased EPA assessment completion, improved narrative feedback quality, and decreased expired EPA assessments. Initiatives to motivate faculty and residents to engage in timely and high-quality feedback will aid the ongoing transition to competency-based surgical education.

articles.title: Cardiometabolic health-frailty phenotypes and bidirectional transitions between atrial fibrillation and heart failure: multistate trajectories and proteomic signatures.
articles.journal: The journal of nutrition, health & aging
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To examine whether a joint cardiometabolic health-frailty phenotype is associated with incident atrial fibrillation (AF), incident heart failure (HF) and progression to AF-HF comorbidity, and to identify candidate circulating protein signals related to this phenotype.

METHODS: Among 319,048 UK Biobank participants without AF or HF, cardiometabolic status (healthy [CMH] or unhealthy [CMU]) and Frailty status (non-frail [NF] or pre-frail/frail [F]) defined four phenotypes. Cox and clock-forward multistate models estimated disease-specific and transition-specific hazards. Proteomic feature selection and exploratory mediation analyses included 28,206 participants with Olink plasma proteomic data.

RESULTS: During follow-up, 17,844 participants developed AF, 5,410 developed HF, and 2,403 and 791 progressed from AF and HF, respectively, to comorbidity. Compared with CMH-NF, CMU-F was associated with the greatest risks of incident HF (hazard ratio (HR), 2.76; 95% confidence interval (CI), 2.59-2.95) and AF (HR, 1.49; 95% CI, 1.43-1.55). Corresponding multistate HRs were 2.98 (95% CI, 2.76-3.22) for baseline-to-HF, 1.45 (1.39-1.51) for baseline-to-AF, 1.76 (1.57-1.98) for AF-to-comorbidity, and 1.27 (1.02-1.57) for HF-to-comorbidity. Positive additive interactions indicated excess risk from coexisting cardiometabolic unhealthiness and frailty. Thirteen proteins showed statistical mediation signals for both outcomes; FABP4 yielded the largest positive mediated proportions (AF, 49.8%; HF, 32.9%) and transition-specific signals for baseline-to-AF and AF-to-comorbidity.

CONCLUSIONS: Coexisting cardiometabolic unhealthiness and frailty identified individuals at greatest risk of AF, HF, and subsequent comorbidity. Exploratory proteomic analyses identified FABP4 as the most consistent preliminary signal, which warrants further validation in independent cohorts.

articles.title: Validating crash surrogates: a causal graphical framework and a SHRP2 case study of hard braking.
articles.abstract: Although there has been a variety of crash surrogates have been applied in traffic safety areas, formal discussions on how to validate crash surrogates for practical use remain limited. To fill this gap, this study seeks to propose a validation procedure suitable for traffic safety applications. To first establish key assumptions required for valid crash surrogates, this study reviews discussions on surrogate outcome from causal mediation, medical research, epidemiology clinical trials, and economics perspectives. A causally valid surrogate, whether full or partial, is a special type of mediator that lies on the causal pathway from the primary explanatory variable for a given research question (i.e., the "treatment") to the final crash outcome. Moreover, it captures an identifiable portion of the treatment's effect on the outcome, thereby enabling causal inference on the final crash outcome through the surrogate. To determine whether a candidate surrogate satisfies the above properties, the proposed validation procedure consists of three main components: (1) verifying the assumptions required for identifying the causal relationship between the candidate crash surrogate and the crash outcome; (2) quantifying the extent of surrogacy; and (3) evaluating the absence of a surrogate paradox and the comparability of the surrogate. A case study using SHRP2 Naturalistic Driving Study data is then presented to demonstrate the proposed procedure. Specifically, the case study examines whether hard braking is a causally valid surrogate for rear-end crash occurrence.

articles.title: Redox-mitochondrial-epigenetic network disruption and its intergenerational impact in zebrafish: Protective effects of metformin.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Oxidative stress is a central mechanism of chronic toxicity, disrupting metabolic, inflammatory, apoptotic, mitochondrial, and epigenetic processes. Potassium bromate (KBrO₃) induces oxidative stress, but its systemic effects following chronic exposure and modulation by metformin remain insufficiently characterized. This study evaluated chronic KBrO₃ toxicity in zebrafish, the effects of concurrent metformin exposure, and molecular responses in F1 offspring following parental exposure.

METHODS: Adult zebrafish were exposed to KBrO₃ for 28 days with or without metformin co-treatment. Histopathological analyses of liver, ovary, intestine, and testis were performed. IL-1β, insulin, and vitellogenin were analyzed by ELISA, wheras oxidative stress, metabolic, inflammatory, apoptotic, and epigenetic markers by qPCR. Global DNA methylation, mitochondrial DNA copy number, and relative telomere length were evaluated in F0 and F1 cohorts. Data were analyzed using conventional statistics, principal component analysis, and Spearman correlation.

RESULTS: KBrO₃ exposure was associated with alterations in antioxidant defence, metabolism, inflammation, apoptosis, mitochondrial and epigenetic endpoints, and tissue pathology. Metformin co-treatment attenuated multiple KBrO₃-associated molecular and histopathological alterations. In F1 offspring, selected gene-expression and DNA methylation alterations were observed, whereas mtDNA copy number and relative telomere length did not differ significantly among groups, indicating endpoint-specific intergenerational responses. Multivariate analyses identified coordinated biomarker patterns associated with treatment.

CONCLUSION: Chronic KBrO₃ exposure produced coordinated molecular and tissue alterations, while metformin co-treatment attenuated several associated responses. Selected F1 molecular and epigenetic alterations indicate intergenerational responses following parental exposure, although F2/F3 generations were not assessed. These findings support further investigation of metformin as a pharmacological modulator of oxidative stress-associated toxicity.

articles.title: Biological Specificities of Fetal Anemia Induced by Parvovirus B19 Infection.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To describe the biological fetal parameters in cases of severe anemia induced by parvovirus B19 (B19V) infection.

METHOD: A retrospective single center study was conducted including cases of fetal anemia due to B19V receiving in utero transfusion (IUT) from January 2011 to May 2024. Biological data from fetal blood at first IUT were collected.

RESULTS: 65 cases were included. Median Hemoglobin was 3 g/dL [IQR 2.1-3.8] and median reticulocyte count was low (39.9 G/L [IQR 17.0-71.1]). Lymphopenia and elevated erythroblasts were noted in 37.5% and 59.1% of cases, respectively. High Aspartate aminotransferase (AST) levels and hypoproteinemia were observed in 97.6% and 71.4% of cases, respectively. The median lactate dehydrogenase (LDH) level was high (1556.0 U/L [IQR 611.0-2405.0]). Hydropic fetuses significantly exhibited lower hemoglobin levels (median 2.5 g/dL vs. 3.8 g/dL; p = 0.0315), lower platelet counts (median 30.5 G/L vs. 71.5 G/L; p = 0.0014), higher AST (median 97.0 vs. 20.0 U/L; p = 0.0002) and LDH levels (median 2068 vs. 329.5 U/L; p = 0.0002) compared to non-hydropic cases.

CONCLUSION: Severe fetal anemia due to B19V infection is associated with specific hematological and biochemical anomalies, some of which are more pronounced in case of hydrops.

articles.title: Perinatal Outcomes and Determinants of Elective Embryo Reduction in Trichorionic Triplet Pregnancies.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To evaluate whether elective embryo reduction (ER) reduces maternal obstetric complications in trichorionic triamniotic triplet pregnancies, to identify the maternal characteristics associated with the decision to undergo ER and its extent, and to describe associated perinatal outcomes.

METHODS: This retrospective study included 120 trichorionic triamniotic triplet pregnancies managed at two tertiary hospitals in Spain (2002-2024). ER to twins or a singleton was offered before 14 weeks of gestation. Maternal characteristics, obstetric complications, and perinatal outcomes were compared between the groups.

RESULTS: ER was performed in 27 pregnancies (22.5%): 21 were reduced to twins and six to a singleton. ER was not associated with lower rates of preeclampsia, gestational diabetes, or intrahepatic cholestasis during pregnancy. Women undergoing ER were older, more likely to be multiparous, and less likely to have conceived using assisted reproductive technologies, although on post hoc testing only the difference in mode of conception between the two reduction subgroups remained significant after correction for multiple comparisons. Median gestational age at delivery was significantly higher after ER (36.2 and 36.6 weeks) than with expectant management (33.1 weeks; p < 0.001). Admissions for threatened preterm labor were less frequent after ER (15.0% and 16.7% vs. 42.7%; overall p = 0.033), though this difference did not remain significant after Holm correction for multiple comparisons (adjusted p = 0.068 and p = 0.791, respectively).

CONCLUSIONS: Elective embryo reduction did not reduce maternal obstetric complications in trichorionic triplet pregnancies, despite prolonging gestation, as previously reported. Maternal age, parity, and mode of conception were associated with the decision to undergo ER, particularly to a singleton, supporting individualized, non-directive counseling.

articles.title: Beyond the Room: Bed-Level Isolation as Surge-Capable Infrastructure for Pandemics and Disasters-A Conceptual Framework.
articles.journal: Disaster medicine and public health preparedness
articles.abstract: The COVID-19 pandemic exposed a structural limit of hospital isolation infrastructure: airborne infection isolation and protective-environment rooms are fixed assets that cannot be multiplied at the speed of a respiratory surge, and the constraint is more severe in field hospitals after disasters. Pandemic workarounds (ward conversion, portable negative-air machines, and modular container construction) each addressed part of the problem at the cost of bed capacity, sustained containment, or deployment speed. This concept paper aims to synthesize the failure modes of room-scale isolation into a device-agnostic set of clinical and engineering criteria for deployable bed-level single-patient isolation with switchable pressure polarity, in-enclosure air-quality monitoring, and on-board between-patient decontamination. These criteria are summarized in a requirements matrix, and one illustrative implementation is outlined. The intended contribution is a framework to guide future design, testing, and evaluation, not a validated solution; no validation data are presented, and none should be inferred.

articles.title: Relationship-centred care in CHD: promoting belonging, psychosocial adaptation, and family well-being.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: CHD is the most common congenital anomaly worldwide. Advances in paediatric cardiology and cardiac surgery have transformed survival, shifting attention towards long-term psychosocial adaptation, neurodevelopment, quality of life, and relational well-being for children and their families.

METHODS: This narrative review examines the psychosocial, developmental, familial, and relational dimensions of childhood CHD. Literature was identified through PubMed, Scopus, and Google Scholar, with thematic synthesis of evidence relating to psychosocial adaptation, parental mental health, neurodevelopment, resilience, belonging, peer relationships, and models of family- and relationship-centred care.

RESULTS: Childhood CHD is associated with repeated hospitalisation, developmental disruption, emotional distress, and lifelong uncertainty, with psychosocial effects extending beyond the child to parents, siblings, grandparents, peers, schools, and healthcare professionals. Families frequently experience anxiety, depression, chronic vigilance, and posttraumatic stress symptoms, while children and adolescents face challenges related to identity, belonging, and social participation. Supportive relationships, multidisciplinary psychosocial care, educational integration, peer support, and developmentally informed interventions may strengthen resilience and improve long-term adaptation. Patients with advanced heart failure requiring ventricular assist devices or heart transplantation, and their families experience additional uncertainty and psychological burden that warrant dedicated psychosocial support.

CONCLUSION: Psychosocial outcomes in CHD are shaped not only by medical care but also by the quality of the relationships surrounding the child. Relationship-centred care builds upon established family-centred care by recognising the broader relational ecosystem that influences development, resilience, participation, and quality of life. Future paediatric cardiology care should integrate longitudinal psychosocial, developmental, educational, and relational support alongside advances in medical treatment.

articles.title: Towards data-driven refinement of an automated cluster alert system: assessing the concordance of epidemiological expert assessment and genotyping.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: An automated CLuster AleRt system (CLAR) is employed at our hospital to detect clusters of relevant microorganisms. Alerts are subsequently assessed by infection prevention and control (IPC) experts to determine their epidemiological relevance. This study compares expert assessment of CLAR alerts with genotyping results.

DESIGN: Retrospective observational study.

METHODS: We analyzed all CLAR alerts and genotyping reports generated during routine IPC activities between 08/2019 and 12/2024. CLAR alerts were classified relevant/not relevant based on epidemiological assessment by IPC physicians. Selected isolates were genotyped when transmission was suspected. Where multiple alerts and genotyping reports were available for an epidemiological cluster, only the first alert with genotyped isolates and the first corresponding genotyping report were considered, in order to emulate conditions at the onset of potential outbreaks. Genotyping was performed either by whole-genome sequencing (cgMLST) or repetitive-sequence-based polymerase chain reaction (rep-PCR). We calculated the proportion of CLAR alerts with ≥1 genotypically clustering isolate and performed a multivariable regression analysis to identify parameters associated with a higher likelihood of concordance.

RESULTS: We identified 116 relevant CLAR alerts corresponding to first genotyping reports (n = 77 cgMLST, n = 39 rep-PCR) of epidemiological clusters. Overall, these alerts contained 253 genotyped isolates. Genotypic clustering of ≥1 CLAR alert isolate was confirmed for 87 CLAR alerts (75.0%). A higher proportion of concordance with genotyping was seen for relevant alerts in neonatology (93.8%) and with carbapenem-resistant Enterobacterales (94.4%), also confirmed by multivariable analysis.

CONCLUSIONS: Expert-assessed epidemiological relevance of CLAR alerts showed promising concordance with genomic findings and may inform future machine learning-based predictions.

articles.title: Investigating the effect of leucine and dipalmitoylphosphatidylcholine on aerosolization properties of high-dose dry powder inhaler formulations of itraconazole nanoparticles.
articles.abstract: This study aims to develop a high-dose dry powder inhaler (DPI) formulation of itraconazole (ITZ) nanoparticles with leucine and/or dipalmitoylphosphatidylcholine (DPPC) as excipients to increase drug solubility and aerosolization performance. To do this, we co-spray-dried leucine and DPPC with an optimized ITZ nanosuspension and measured the physical properties, dissolution and aerosolization characteristics of the formulations. Among the formulations, those containing 50% (w/wITZ) leucine (N3) or 30% (w/wITZ) leucine with 20% (w/wITZ) DPPC (N5), which had the highest FPF (68.88 ± 1.90% for N3 and 78.81 ± 1.17% for N5) and dissolved percentage of the drug (cumulative release percentage in 180 min, 69.10 ± 1.46% for N3 and 94.34 ± 1.30% for N5), were selected for in vivo pharmacokinetic studies and insufflated intratracheally to rats. An ITZ suspension was administered as a control by gavage. Among the selected formulations, N3 produced the highest AUC in lung tissue, approximately two-fold higher than N5. Furthermore, the AUCLung-to-AUCPlasma ratio for N3 was approximately 24-fold and 800-fold higher than those of N5 and the oral formulations, respectively, indicating enhanced pulmonary retention and potentially reduced systemic exposure. Overall, N3 represents a promising high-dose DPI formulation for further preclinical development of inhaled ITZ.

articles.title: Focusing on VaIN2+: Development and validation of a prediction nomogram based on a large colposcopy population.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Vaginal intraepithelial neoplasia 2 or worse (VaIN2+) has long remained in a largely passive diagnostic pattern due to the lack of specific clinical manifestations and routine screening strategies. This study aimed to explore its clinical characteristics and develop a prediction model for individualized risk assessment.

MATERIAL AND METHODS: We retrospectively analyzed the clinical characteristics and human papillomavirus (HPV) genotype distribution in 3259 women undergoing colposcopy at a single center between September 2012 and December 2024. A nomogram was developed based on predictors initially screened by least absolute shrinkage and selection operator regression and finalized through multivariable logistic regression. The model's discriminative ability, calibration, and clinical utility were assessed in both training and validation sets.

RESULTS: Among 1192 women with VaIN2+, older age, HPV infection, cytology worse than atypical squamous cells of undetermined significance (ASCUS), and concurrent cervical/vulvar lesions were more prevalent than in 2067 women without vaginal lesions. HPV16, HPV58, HPV52, HPV33, and HPV18 were the most common genotypes. A nomogram was developed based on 10 independent predictors identified by multivariable analysis, including age, hysterectomy history, specific HPV genotypes (16, 58, 56, 35, 39), cytological results (ASCUS and worse), concurrent cervical lesions (cervical intraepithelial neoplasia 1, cervical intraepithelial neoplasia 2 or 3, cervical squamous cell carcinoma), and concurrent vulvar lesions. The nomogram demonstrated good discrimination, with an area under the receiver operating characteristic curve of 0.771 in the training set and 0.791 in the validation set. Calibration was satisfactory, and decision curve analysis confirmed superior clinical net benefit across a wide threshold probability range.

CONCLUSIONS: By profiling VaIN2+ characteristics, this study developed the first prediction model integrating specific HPV genotypes with multiple clinical factors. This model enables clinicians to proactively identify high-risk individuals, thereby facilitating earlier diagnosis and intervention for VaIN2+.

articles.title: Analysis of pharmacist authorship in leading critical care journals.
articles.journal: American journal of health-system pharmacy : AJHP : official journal of the American Society of Health-System Pharmacists
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: To evaluate first and last (senior) pharmacist authorship in high-impact critical care journals with a focus on the representation and evolution of pharmacist contributions over time.

METHODS: This literature-focused review analyzed pharmacist authorship across 6 high-impact critical care journals: Intensive Care Medicine, American Journal of Respiratory and Critical Care Medicine, Critical Care, Critical Care Medicine, CHEST, and Annals of Intensive Care. First and last authors were assessed for pharmacy-related degrees using article data and supplemental searches, with articles with unconfirmed pharmacist authorship excluded. Included study designs encompassed a variety of research and review article types, including, but not limited to, retrospective cohort studies, case-control studies, systematic reviews, case reports, surveys, narrative reviews, literature reviews, animal studies, clinical studies, evaluation studies, methods studies, and observational studies; nonresearch publications were excluded.

RESULTS: A total of 83,608 articles published between 1973 and 2024 were identified, of which 24,257 met the inclusion criteria. Pharmacist authorship was identified in 272 articles (1.12%), with an overall upward trend observed over time. The highest annual representation occurred in 1988 (12 articles; 3.67%). CHEST, evaluated from 2020 to 2024, had the highest proportion of articles with pharmacist authorship (11 articles; 4.47%). Pharmacist-authored studies were commonly classified as "other study designs," including narrative reviews, literature reviews, experimental studies, and survey studies.

CONCLUSION: Pharmacist authorship generally increased over the study period, although interpretation of temporal trends is limited by differences in journal inclusion across years; however, pharmacists remain underrepresented as first and last authors.

articles.title: Efficacy of Topical Emollients on Skin Biophysical Properties and Inflammatory Markers in Stasis Eczema.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Stasis eczema is a chronic inflammatory skin condition commonly associated with chronic venous insufficiency and represents a significant clinical burden. Emollients are widely used to improve skin hydration and barrier function; however, their effects on inflammation and skin remodeling in stasis eczema remain unclear. This study aimed to evaluate the impact of a topical emollient on skin barrier integrity and systemic inflammatory markers in affected patients.

METHODS: Fifty patients with stasis eczema were randomized to receive either a topical emollient or placebo for six weeks. Skin parameters, including melanin content, hydration, and transepidermal water loss (TEWL), were assessed using Tewameter. Plasma levels of pro-inflammatory cytokines (IL-6, IL-1β, TNF-α), anti-inflammatory cytokine IL-10, and matrix metalloproteinases (MMP-1, MMP-2, MMP-3, and MMP-9) were measured using enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay (ELISA) at baseline and after treatment.

RESULTS: Baseline clinical assessment demonstrated a high prevalence of comorbidities, particularly hypertension, chronic venous insufficiency, diabetes mellitus, and dyslipidemia. No statistically significant changes were observed in skin barrier parameters or circulating cytokine levels following six weeks of treatment. MMP-1 and MMP-2 concentrations remained stable in both groups. However, post-treatment MMP-3 levels were significantly higher in the emollient group than in the placebo group, while MMP-9 demonstrated a significant within-group change in the placebo group only.

CONCLUSION: Short-term use of a topical emollient may help maintain skin barrier function and systemic inflammatory status but does not appear to produce clinically meaningful improvements in most skin barriers or inflammatory parameters, despite isolated significant changes observed in specific MMP biomarkers in patients with chronic stasis eczema. These findings highlight the complexity of disease management in this population and suggest that longer treatment durations, larger sample sizes, consideration and statistical adjustment for baseline comorbidities are warranted in future studies.

articles.title: Exploring Maximality Criteria of Cardiopulmonary Exercise Testing in Healthy Subjects and Patients with Chronic Respiratory Disease: A Practical Clinical Framework.
articles.journal: Respiration; international review of thoracic diseases
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Incremental cardiopulmonary exercise testing (CPET) is used to assess exercise capacity and identify mechanisms of exercise limitation. Identification of test maximality is essential for correct interpretation, yet no consensus exists on the defining criteria. This study evaluated the performance of different <mml:math id="m1" xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mml:mrow><mml:mover accent="true"><mml:mi mathvariant="normal">V</mml:mi><mml:mo>˙</mml:mo></mml:mover><mml:msub><mml:mi mathvariant="normal">O</mml:mi><mml:mn>2</mml:mn></mml:msub></mml:mrow></mml:math> plateau definitions and the contribution of secondary maximality criteria in patients with chronic respiratory disease and healthy controls.

METHODS: We retrospectively analyzed 395 CPETs (84 healthy, 135 chronic obstructive pulmonary disease, 99 interstitial lung disease, 77 pulmonary hypertension), comparing consensus-based visual identification of a <mml:math id="m2" xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mml:mrow><mml:mover accent="true"><mml:mi mathvariant="normal">V</mml:mi><mml:mo>˙</mml:mo></mml:mover><mml:msub><mml:mi mathvariant="normal">O</mml:mi><mml:mn>2</mml:mn></mml:msub></mml:mrow></mml:math> plateau by three pulmonologists with three commonly used plateau definitions. Additionally, five secondary maximality criteria were evaluated, using strict and liberal thresholds.

RESULTS: The relative <mml:math id="m3" xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mml:mrow><mml:mover accent="true"><mml:mi mathvariant="normal">V</mml:mi><mml:mo>˙</mml:mo></mml:mover><mml:msub><mml:mi mathvariant="normal">O</mml:mi><mml:mn>2</mml:mn></mml:msub></mml:mrow></mml:math> plateau definition showed strong agreement with visual assessment (κ = 0.75-0.93), while absolute thresholds were discordant (κ = 0.02-0.31). Overlap between maximality criteria was high in healthy individuals but low in disease groups, suggesting that evaluating multiple criteria in parallel is necessary. However, combining more than 2 secondary criteria in healthy subjects and more than 3 in patients on top of <mml:math id="m4" xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mml:mrow><mml:mover accent="true"><mml:mi mathvariant="normal">V</mml:mi><mml:mo>˙</mml:mo></mml:mover><mml:msub><mml:mi mathvariant="normal">O</mml:mi><mml:mn>2</mml:mn></mml:msub></mml:mrow></mml:math> plateau provided minimal additive value.

CONCLUSION: CPET maximality assessment depends strongly on the criteria applied, potentially altering CPET interpretation and clinical decision-making.

articles.title: Effects of extreme environmental conditions on the skin barrier: a pilot study from the "Under The Pole" project with spectral and biometric measurements.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Under The Pole is an ambitious underwater exploration program in extreme environments, particularly in deep and polar regions. Diving in the cold and saline waters of the Arctic exposes the skin to intense thermal and osmotic stress, potentially altering its barrier function. This study aimed to evaluate both the acute and long-term effects of repeated cold-water diving on skin hydration and barrier integrity during a two-month Arctic expedition.

METHODS: Seven healthy Caucasian male participants without facial skin lesions were monitored throughout the expedition. Skin appearance, hydration and transepidermal water loss (TEWL) were measured. Stratum corneum (SC) samples were collected by tape stripping and analyzed using Raman spectroscopy and Attenuated Total Reflection-Fourier Transform Infrared (ATR-FTIR) spectroscopy to assess molecular changes in lipids and proteins.

RESULTS: The findings reveal a dynamic, multiphasic adaptation process of the skin barrier under extreme polar conditions: (i) Immediate phase (hours): Acute hydration increase and transient barrier disruption due to immersion and temperature shock. (ii) Short-term phase (days): Adaptive homeostatic response, characterized by decreased water loss and lipid disorganization and protein structural rearrangement within the SC. (iii) Long-term phase (weeks): Gradual barrier fatigue with partial recovery of lipid order and protein structure, but persistent microstructural alterations evidenced by reduced hydration and elevated TEWL.

CONCLUSION: This study provides in situ evidence of dynamic skin adaptation to extreme Arctic conditions. Initial barrier disruption was followed by molecular reorganization and partial recovery, yet prolonged exposure led to cumulative dehydration and barrier fatigue. These insights improve understanding of cutaneous resilience and support the design of protective skincare strategies for extreme environments.

articles.title: Effect of mucopolysaccharide polysulfate on sweating function and skin dryness in a mouse model of streptozotocin-induced diabetes.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Asteatosis is characterized by reduced water content in the stratum corneum. Patients with diabetes have been reported to experience reduced sweating, potentially leading to asteatosis. A common treatment approach for asteatosis is the use of moisturizers, such as mucopolysaccharide polysulfate (MPS) cream. However, the therapeutic mechanism of MPS in diabetes-induced asteatosis remains unknown. In this study, we investigated the role of sweating in the pathophysiology of asteatosis in diabetes and to confirm the therapeutic effect of MPS cream using a streptozotocin-induced diabetic mouse model (STZ-DM mice).

METHODS: STZ-DM mice generated by administering streptozotocin (STZ) to C57BL/6JJcl mice. Approximately 2 weeks after STZ administration, sweating function and skin surface hydration in the footpads, where sweat glands are located, were evaluated, with or without topical occlusive application of moisturizers including MPS cream for more than 10 days.

RESULTS: After STZ treatment, sweating function in STZ-DM mice gradually decreased from Week 3 to 9. Furthermore, skin surface hydration and sweating function decreased over time. Topical application of MPS cream alleviated diminished sweating and skin surface hydration in STZ-DM mice. Moreover, pilocarpine-induced sweating response was attenuated in STZ-DM mice, indicating that impairment of sweating function in these mice involves neuropathic dysfunction. Topical application of MPS cream improved the pilocarpine-induced sweating response.

CONCLUSION: The effects of MPS on the increasing water content of SC in STZ-DM mice may be partly mediated by sweating. This is the first study to demonstrate that the ameliorative effect of MPS on diabetic dry skin is mediated by enhanced sweating via neuropathy inhibition.

articles.title: Sociodemographic and clinical factors associated with seven domains of digital health literacy: A cross-sectional study (NORFAST).
articles.abstract: Introduction Due to limited digital health literacy (DHL), stroke survivors frequently face barriers in using digital health tools essential for post-stroke rehabilitation and self-management. DHL is a multidimensional construct, encompassing several distinct skill domains. Although sociodemographic and clinical characteristics may influence overall DHL, their associations with specific DHL domains remain poorly understood. This study therefore explores how individual DHL domains relate to patient characteristics in stroke survivors. Methods In this cross-sectional NORFAST study, stroke survivors aged 18-80 years with a first-ever stroke in 2021 or 2022 were recruited through the Norwegian Stroke Registry. Registry data included diagnosis, stroke type, aphasia, and scores on the National Institutes of Health Stroke Scale (NIHSS), modified Rankin Scale (mRS), and Barthel Index for Activities of Daily Living. Cognitive function was assessed before inclusion using the Mini/5min MoCA, a brief telephone-administered cognitive screening tool. Participants also completed self-report questionnaires (telephone or electronic), assessing sociodemographics, self-rated health status (EQ-VAS) and fatigue interference (Fatigue Severity Scale, FSS-7). The primary outcomes were DHL dimensions, assessed with the 7-domain eHealth Literacy Questionnaire (eHLQ). Linear regression models examined unadjusted and adjusted associations between patient characteristics and each DHL domain. Results Among 177 stroke survivors (mean age 69), most had experienced minor strokes and cerebral infarction. Patients scored highest on the domain "feel safe and in control", and lowest on "digital services that suit individual needs". In multivariable regression models, older age was associated with lower scores on Using technology, Engage, Motivation, and Needs; female sex with lower scores on Motivation and Needs; college/university education with higher scores on Understanding, Engage, Motivation and Needs; and better health status with higher scores on domains Using technology, Understanding, Motivation, Access and Needs. Living alone, aphasia, cognitive function, and fatigue interference were not significantly associated with any DHL domain after multivariable adjustment. Conclusion This study demonstrates considerable variation in DHL across domains among stroke survivors. After adjustment, age, education level, and self-rated health status were the factors most consistently associated with DHL dimensions. These findings suggest that older stroke survivors, those without college or university education, and those with lower self-rated health may warrant particular attention when designing, implementing, and evaluating digital health interventions. Co-creation with stroke survivors, healthcare professionals, and technology designers may support the development of accessible and clinically meaningful digital solutions.

articles.title: Age-Related Differences in Asthma Recognition, Follow-up, and Home-Based Exacerbation Management Among Children Hospitalized for Acute Asthma Exacerbations.
articles.journal: International archives of allergy and immunology
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: To evaluate age-related differences in asthma diagnosis and management among children hospitalized for moderate-to-severe asthma exacerbations and to examine the relationship of regular follow-up and home-based exacerbation management with clinical outcomes.

METHODS: This retrospective observational study included children aged 25 months to <18 years who were hospitalized for moderate-to-severe asthma exacerbations. Patients were categorized as preschool-aged (25-60 months) or school-aged (61 months to <18 years). Asthma diagnosis before hospitalization, regular follow-up, controller therapy use, caregiver education, initiation of home-based treatment, exacerbation history, and healthcare utilization were compared.

RESULTS: A total of 104 children were included. Preschool children were less likely than school-aged children to have received an asthma diagnosis before hospitalization (56.5% vs. 83.3%, p=0.008) and were more frequently managed with diagnoses such as bronchiolitis or bronchitis. Antibiotic use before asthma diagnosis was reported in 87.5% of the cohort. Patients attending regular follow-up had higher rates of controller therapy use, home-based exacerbation management education, and initiation of treatment at home (all p<0.001). They also had fewer moderate-to-severe exacerbations (p<0.001) and fewer emergency department visits (p=0.036). Although children initiating home treatment had a greater previous exacerbation burden, they had fewer moderate-to-severe exacerbations during the preceding year than those who did not initiate treatment at home (p=0.004). In multivariable analysis, regular follow-up remained independently associated with lower odds of recurrent moderate-to-severe exacerbations (aOR 0.03, 95% CI 0.004-0.20; p<0.001).

CONCLUSION: Asthma was less often recognized before hospitalization in preschool children, and antibiotic use before diagnosis was common. Children attending regular follow-up more often received controller therapy and home-management education and had fewer moderate-to-severe exacerbations and emergency department visits. These findings highlight the importance of timely asthma recognition, regular follow-up, and practical caregiver education in children with recurrent wheezing or asthma, while the observational design precludes causal inference.

articles.title: Monitoring of Remote Ischemic Conditioning with a Tissue Reflectance Sensor: A Randomized Control Trial.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Remote ischemic conditioning (RIC) is delivered by a transient (5 min) pressure increase in the arm BP cuff by a variable 30-50 mmHg above systolic BP to a maximum of 200 mmHg. This inconsistency in pressure application may affect the fidelity of intervention delivery. We tested the hypothesis that monitoring remote ischemic conditioning (RIC) with an adjunct forearm skin tissue reflectance sensor (STRS) device may be feasible in patients with acute ischemic stroke (AIS) and cerebral small vessel disease (cSVD).

METHODS: We screened patients with AIS within 7 days of symptom onset for moderate-to-severe cSVD. Eligible patients were randomized 2:1 to receive intervention RIC or sham RIC. The primary outcome measure was a composite feasibility of the forearm STRS (patient-level comfort and technical aspects measured by IOx1 and IOx2). The secondary outcome was changes in forearm STRS-derived tissue reflectance responses during the pressure-on phase (5 min) and the early pressure-off phase (1 min) of RIC. Multivariable linear regression analysis assessed the relationship between IOx1 and intervention allocation. We also used receiver operating characteristic curve analysis to propose candidate thresholds for classifying the magnitude of the tissue oxygenation response to RIC.

RESULTS: Fifty-one [34 intervention (68 RIC sessions), 17 sham (29 RIC sessions)] patients with mean ± SD age of 69±12.8 years, 24(47.1%) were females, were enrolled at a median (IQR) 42(26-78) hours after symptom onset, and median baseline National Institute of Health stroke Scale of 5(3-7). STRS-derived median relative IOx1(β = 0.33, p = 0.002) and median relative IOx2 (β = 0.23, p = 0.04) slopes during the pressure-on phase were different in the intervention arm compared to the sham arm. A percent IOx1 change of 4- 13.7% can be considered a threshold to differentiate between intervention and sham treatment. The median Likert scale score was similar: 3.5 (3-4) in the intervention group and 4 (4-5) in the sham group.

CONCLUSION: RIC monitoring with forearm STRS is feasible in patients with AIS. Clinical trials evaluating the efficacy of RIC interventions can use STRS to assess fidelity.

CLINICAL TRIAL REGISTRATION NUMBER: ClinicalTrials.gov ID: NCT05408130 (https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT05408130).

articles.title: Papaverine administration during labor induction in nulliparous patients: a retrospective cohort study.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: To evaluate the association between papaverine administration during labor induction and maternal and neonatal outcomes among nulliparous patients, with particular emphasis on cesarean delivery, labor duration, and timing of administration relative to rupture of membranes.

DESIGN: Retrospective cohort study. Participants/Materials: The study included 1,889 nulliparous patients with singleton pregnancies who underwent medically indicated labor induction with intravenous oxytocin between January 2020 and December 2024. Patients were categorized according to papaverine exposure: no papaverine (n=1,185), one 80-mg intramuscular dose (n=618), or two 80-mg intramuscular doses (n=86).

SETTING: A tertiary university-affiliated medical center in northern Israel.

METHODS: Maternal, intrapartum, postpartum, and neonatal data were extracted from electronic medical records. The primary outcome was mode of delivery. Secondary outcomes included cesarean delivery due to non-progressive labor, delivery within 24 hours, postpartum hemorrhage, puerperal endometritis, 5-minute Apgar score <7, umbilical cord pH <7.2 and <7.1, and neonatal intensive care unit admission. Pairwise comparisons were performed between each papaverine group and the no-papaverine group using the independent-samples t test, Mann-Whitney U test, Pearson's chi-square test, or Fisher's exact test, as appropriate. A multivariable logistic regression model was used to evaluate factors associated with cesarean delivery. Mode of delivery was also evaluated according to the timing of papaverine administration relative to rupture of membranes.

RESULTS: Compared with no papaverine, one-dose papaverine administration was associated with a lower cesarean delivery rate (24.4% vs. 33.9%; RR 0.72, 95% CI 0.61-0.85; P<0.001), whereas the cesarean delivery rate did not differ significantly between the two-dose and no-papaverine groups (30.2% vs. 33.9%; P=0.484). Cesarean delivery due to non-progressive labor was less frequent with one dose compared with no papaverine (11.5% vs. 17.1%; RR 0.67, 95% CI 0.52-0.86; P=0.002), whereas no significant difference was observed between the two-dose and no-papaverine groups (20.9% vs. 17.1%; P=0.369). Delivery within 24 hours was more frequent with one dose than with no papaverine (65.0% vs. 53.9%; RR 1.21, 95% CI 1.12-1.30; P<0.001) and less frequent with two doses than with no papaverine (37.2% vs. 53.9%; RR 0.69, 95% CI 0.52-0.91; P=0.003). Vaginal delivery rates were highest when papaverine was administered before rupture of membranes (77.0%), followed by administration after rupture of membranes (73.0%) and no papaverine exposure (66.1%; P<0.001). In multivariable analysis, papaverine administration was independently associated with lower odds of cesarean delivery (adjusted OR 0.64, 95% CI 0.50-0.81; P<0.001). Maternal postpartum complications and neonatal outcomes were generally similar between groups.

LIMITATIONS: The retrospective, single-center design may introduce selection bias and residual confounding. Papaverine administration was based on clinician discretion, and the relatively small two-dose group limited evaluation of dose-dependent effects. Long-term maternal and neonatal outcomes were not assessed.

CONCLUSIONS: Papaverine administration during labor induction, particularly as a single dose, was associated with a lower cesarean delivery rate and a greater likelihood of delivery within 24 hours, without an observed increase in adverse maternal or neonatal outcomes. Vaginal delivery was most frequent among patients who received papaverine before rupture of membranes; however, this exploratory finding requires prospective confirmation.

articles.title: The Solitary Functioning Kidney: From Pathophysiology to Long-Term Management.
articles.abstract: Solitary functioning kidney (SFK) is a clinical condition characterized by the presence of a single functioning kidney, arising from either congenital anomalies or acquired causes. It is recognized as an important risk factor for chronic kidney disease (CKD) and, in some patients, for progression to end-stage kidney disease (ESKD). Congenital solitary functioning kidney is commonly associated with renal hypoplasia or dysplasia, genetic abnormalities, and congenital anomalies of the kidney and urinary tract, whereas acquired solitary functioning kidney is often secondary to unilateral nephrectomy for renal tumors, trauma, tuberculosis, severe infection, or living kidney donation. The principal pathophysiological mechanisms underlying the progression from SFK to CKD are compensatory renal hypertrophy and glomerular hyperfiltration in the remnant kidney. Although these adaptive responses may initially maintain renal function, sustained compensation can lead to glomerular injury, proteinuria, tubulointerstitial damage, and renal fibrosis. Early diagnosis relies primarily on imaging modalities, such as ultrasonography and magnetic resonance imaging, together with assessment of renal function and emerging biomarkers, including neutrophil gelatinase-associated lipocalin and cystatin C. Prognostic evaluation of patients with SFK should comprehensively consider etiology, age, compensatory renal growth, associated urinary tract anomalies, comorbidities, and markers of kidney injury. Effective long-term management is essential to prevent or delay progression to CKD and ESKD, with particular emphasis on individualized follow-up, lifestyle modification, blood pressure control, reduction of proteinuria, and avoidance of additional nephrotoxic insults. Previous publications have often addressed pediatric congenital solitary functioning kidney (CSFK), living kidney donors, and disease-related nephrectomy cohorts separately, limiting the translation of heterogeneous evidence into a common clinical approach. This review integrates congenital and acquired SFK across the life course, distinguishes shared markers of established kidney injury from etiology-specific determinants of renal reserve, and proposes an evidence-informed framework for dynamic risk stratification and risk-adapted follow-up and management. This framework is conceptual and requires prospective validation.

articles.title: Application of antibiotic-loaded bone cement in unicompartmental knee arthroplasty: inhibiting IL-6 levels and reducing postoperative infection rate.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: We aim to clarify the inhibitory effect of antibiotic-loaded bone cement (ALBC) on inflammatory factors, and its preventive effect on postoperative infections in unicompartmental knee arthroplasty (UKA).

METHODS: This prospective randomized controlled trial enrolled 104 osteoarthritis patients undergoing UKA, randomly assigned to the non-ALBC group (n = 52, bone cement without antibiotics) and ALBC group (ALBC with 1.0 g vancomycin hydrochloride, n = 52). Primary outcomes were postoperative inflammatory markers (CRP, ESR, TNF-α, IL-6); secondary outcomes included infection rate and HSS score. Independent-samples t-tests were used for continuous variables, χ2 test for categorical variables (infection rate, efficacy), and repeated measures analysis of variance for intra-group longitudinal comparisons.

RESULTS: The ALBC group demonstrated lower inflammatory markers at postoperative day 7 and at 3 months [CRP (3.52 ± 0.81 vs 6.92 ± 1.17, Cohen's d = 3.379), ESR (16.29 ± 2.31 vs 20.19 ± 4.05, Cohen's d = 1.183), TNF-α (29.71 ± 4.03 vs 36.25 ± 5.17, Cohen's d = 1.411), and IL-6 (17.05 ± 3.72 vs 22.05 ± 4.38, Cohen's d = 1.230)] (all p < 0.001), and also showed superior clinical outcomes, with lower postoperative infection rate (p = 0.016), higher HSS score (p < 0.001), and better overall clinical efficacy (p = 0.010) than the non-ALBC group.

CONCLUSION: The application of ALBC in UKA was associated with reduced postoperative inflammatory markers such as IL-6 and a lower incidence of postoperative infection. These findings suggest that ALBC may play a beneficial role in postoperative recovery and joint function rehabilitation.

articles.title: Effect of a single high-concentration sodium bicarbonate bolus on contrast-induced nephropathy in STEMI patients undergoing Primary PCI: a prospective randomized study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Contrast-induced nephropathy (CIN) remains an important complication following primary percutaneous coronary intervention (PPCI) in patients with ST-segment elevation myocardial infarction (STEMI). In emergency settings, preventive strategies must be rapid and compatible with timely reperfusion. This study evaluated whether a single preprocedural bolus of high-concentration sodium bicarbonate was associated with a lower incidence of CIN.

METHODS: In this prospective randomised study, 110 STEMI patients undergoing PPCI at two tertiary centres were enrolled. All patients received standard care, including isotonic saline hydration. Participants were assigned to saline hydration alone or saline plus a single intravenous bolus of 20 mEq of 8.4% sodium bicarbonate administered 5-10 min before contrast exposure. The primary endpoint was CIN within 48 ± 12 h, defined as an increase in serum creatinine ≥0.5 mg/dL or ≥25% from baseline.

RESULTS: Baseline characteristics were generally comparable, although baseline blood urea nitrogen was higher and estimated glomerular filtration rate lower in the control group. CIN occurred more frequently in controls than in the sodium bicarbonate group (16.4% vs. 1.8%; p = 0.008). Renal function trajectories also favoured sodium bicarbonate. However, sodium bicarbonate did not remain an independent predictor of CIN after multivariable adjustment (OR 0.061, 95% CI 0.003-1.205; p = 0.066).

CONCLUSIONS: Sodium bicarbonate administration was associated with a lower unadjusted incidence of CIN. These findings should be considered hypothesis-generating and require confirmation in larger multicentre studies.

articles.title: Surgery and/or biologics in chronic rhinosinusitis with nasal polyps: EUFOREA/EPOS consensus paper.
articles.abstract: The therapeutic landscape of chronic rhinosinusitis with nasal polyps (CRSwNP) has rapidly evolved over the past 6 years with the arrival of biologics, prompting a re-evaluation of the traditional stepwise management centred on corticosteroids and endoscopic sinus surgery (ESS). Although both ESS and biologics have proven efficacy, the optimal sequence, extent and timing of ESS relative to biologics remains a matter of debate. The international multidisciplinary panel of experts of EUFOREA/EPOS reached consensus on the aims, indications, timing, and therapeutic positioning of ESS, and biologics in CRSwNP. Evidence from pivotal RCTs, real-life studies and recent guidelines was critically reviewed. Consensus statements were drafted and refined through multiple rounds of discussion and voting. This EUFOREA/EPOS report provides key definitions and clinical criteria for ESS and biologics particiin CRSwNP, offering a unified framework for personalized, evidence-based care with the aim to achieve the best outcomes for patients. The expert group agreed that patients with diffuse disease should have at least a primary complete ESS, that concurrent initiation of sinus surgery and biologic therapy is not recommended with current evidence, and the indication for biologic therapy as established by earlier guidelines were enforced. It was emphasized that with the current knowledge on side effects of systemic corticosteroids, their long-term use is no longer accepted especially where biologics are available. By emphasizing complementary and disease-modifying effects of novel care strategies, this initiative aims at optimizing outcomes across the entire airway continuum in line with EPOS/EUFOREA's mission.

articles.title: Sestrin2 mitigates obesity-associated HFpEF via adaptive IRE1α-XBP1 signaling and redox regulation.
articles.abstract: Obesity-associated heart failure with preserved ejection fraction (HFpEF) is a metabolic cardiac disorder characterized by diastolic dysfunction. Sestrin2 is a stress-inducible regulator of metabolic and redox homeostasis, but its role in HFpEF remains incompletely defined. This study demonstrates that Sestrin2 has cardioprotective effects on obesity-associated HFpEF. In an obesity-associated HFpEF mouse model, cardiac Sestrin2 overexpression attenuates diastolic dysfunction, myocardial lipid accumulation, fibrosis, hypertrophy, and mitochondrial dysfunction without significantly affecting adiposity, circulating lipid levels, or whole-body substrate utilization. Mechanistically, Sestrin2 overexpression increases IRE1α phosphorylation and XBP1 splicing, indicating enhanced adaptive unfolded protein response signaling. Sestrin2 overexpression is also associated with increased Sigma-1 receptor (Sigmar1) expression, whereas Sigmar1 knockdown attenuates Sestrin2-associated IRE1α-XBP1 activation in vitro, suggesting the involvement of Sigmar1 in endoplasmic reticulum-mitochondrial stress adaptation. In addition, Sestrin2 overexpression enhances AMPK activation, increases acetyl-CoA carboxylase (AAC) and eNOS phosphorylation, suppresses mTOR signaling, enhances Nrf2-HO-1 antioxidant responses, and reduces inflammatory marker expression and mitochondrial ROS production. Metabolomic analysis further reveals partial alterations in metabolites associated with endoplasmic reticulum stress and redox homeostasis. Collectively, these findings suggest that Sestrin2 alleviates obesity-associated HFpEF and is associated with the activation of adaptive IRE1α-XBP1 signaling involving Sigmar1, together with improved metabolic and redox homeostasis.

articles.title: PKP2 orchestrates OXPHOS expression in cardiomyocytes via a PGC1α-dependent mechanism.
articles.abstract:
AIMS: Arrhythmogenic cardiomyopathy (ACM) is an inherited cardiac disease in which most patients carry (likely) pathogenic variants in desmosomal genes, most commonly in plakophilin-2 (PKP2). While the genetic causes are well described, the molecular mechanisms driving disease progression-particularly in response to exercise-remain poorly understood.

METHODS AND RESULTS: To investigate disease-driving pathways in ACM, we used PKP2 mutant human-induced pluripotent stem cell-derived cardiomyocytes (hiPSC-CMs) and myocardial tissue from ACM patients. Transcriptomic profiling revealed consistent downregulation of oxidative phosphorylation (OXPHOS) genes in PKP2 mutant hiPSC-CMs, which was confirmed in explanted ACM hearts carrying PKP2 variants. Reduced expression of OXPHOS-related genes was associated with lower PPARGC1A expression and decreased mitochondrial spare capacity in PKP2 mutant hiPSC-CMs. The reduction in PPARGC1A expression appeared to result, at least in part, from decreased AMPKα protein levels, a known activator of PPARGC1A previously shown to localize at the intercalated disc, as PKP2 mutant cells failed to increase PPARGC1A expression following treatment with AICAR, an AMPK activator. To directly assess whether increasing PPARGC1A expression could compensate for this defect, we overexpressed PPARGC1A, which partially restored OXPHOS gene expression and improved contractility in PKP2 mutant cells.

CONCLUSION: Our study identifies a novel transcriptional mechanism linking PKP2 loss to reduced mitochondrial function via decreased PGC1α signaling, partially through reduced AMPKα levels. Disruption of this axis reduces OXPHOS gene expression and mitochondrial function in PKP2 mutant hiPSC-CMs, potentially impairing the heart's ability to meet increased energy demands during stress, and offering a mechanistic explanation for the detrimental effects of exercise in ACM. Furthermore, these findings highlight PGC1α induction as a potential therapeutic strategy to restore OXPHOS gene expression and mitochondrial adaptability in ACM.

articles.title: Iron oxide nanoparticles for hepatocellular carcinoma theranostics: From nanoplatform design to clinical translation.
articles.abstract: The challenges in early diagnosis and effective treatment of hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) are largely attributable to the underlying cirrhosis, impaired hepatic reserve, and the added complexity of heterogeneous tumor vascularity in many patients. Iron oxide nanoparticles (IONPs) are promising platforms for HCC diagnosis and treatment because of their magnetic properties, tunable magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) contrast, magnetothermal conversion capability, and modifiable surface chemistry. These features enable IONPs to be used for image-guided diagnosis, liver-directed locoregional therapy, systemic drug delivery, and treatment monitoring. In this review, we summarize the composition, crystal structure, size-dependent magnetic properties, surface modification, and in vivo fate of IONPs, along with how these characteristics influence their performance in HCC imaging and therapy. For diagnostic applications, we focus on passive accumulation, particularly mononuclear phagocyte system (MPS)-mediated hepatic contrast, ligand-mediated active targeting, and multimodal imaging. We then review therapeutic strategies, including magnetic hyperthermia (MHT), stimuli-responsive drug delivery, and combination therapy. Major barriers to clinical translation are also addressed, encompassing the heterogeneous enhanced permeability and retention (EPR) effect, high background uptake by non-tumoral liver tissue, liver function-related safety concerns, limitations of alternating magnetic fields, and manufacturing reproducibility.

articles.title: Correction to: The Role of Echocardiography in the Assessment of Epicardial Adipose Tissue: A Systematic Review and Meta-analysis.
Robotic systems in cranial surgery: a systematic review of accuracy, clinical outcomes, and adverse events.
articles.abstract: Robotic-assisted surgery is becoming more prevalent in neurosurgery. Many studies have classified the advantages and disadvantages, particularly in spinal robotic surgeries. However, the use of robotics in cranial procedures has been limited to individual studies without large-scale review of the different modalities. This study is a comprehensive systematic review of the major robotics utilized in cranial neurosurgical procedures and their respective outcomes. Following Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses (PRISMA) guidelines, a systematic review was conducted over PubMed, Cochrane, and Embase for articles published between January 2000 to February 2025. EndNote and Rayyan were utilized to organize the 1,409 identified studies and conduct a blinded multiphase process for including and excluding studies. Originally, studies were intended to be run as a meta-analysis to compare robotic modalities, but the existing data was too heterogeneous to statistically contrast outcomes. Overall, 51 studies were included, with six robots being discussed in more than one study. The use of robotics in cranial neurosurgery stretches mostly across functional neurosurgery, with different applications in brain tumor biopsies and resection, hemorrhage drainage, and endoscopic surgeries. Cranial neurosurgical procedures primarily apply robotics in the world of functional neurosurgery. Outside of this subspecialty, robotic-assisted cranial surgery remains sparse in the literature. As technology evolves, more use cases may be realized.

articles.title: Online vs. In Person Gambling: Does Exposure to Brick-and-Mortar Gambling Shops Lead to Increased Online Gambling?
articles.abstract: The rise of online gambling in Great Britain in the past two decades has caused increased public health concerns. This study adds to existing evidence on physical gambling environment as a driver of gambling participation, using a 2022 national survey. With respect to gambling-related risks, existing evidence suggests a relationship, albeit complex, between gambling opportunities and increased levels of related problems. The study cuts into this complexity by factorising the risk of online gambling, and leveraging a double negative control design to estimate the causal effect of exposure to physical gambling shops on individuals' online gambling participation. Our findings show that, for the survey sample, an increase in shop exposure predicts an increased average risk of online gambling. Measuring shop exposure by distance to nearest shops, we find that for all-type gambling (i.e gaming and betting), being in the highest versus lowest exposure decile raises the risk of online gambling by around 1.49 fold for the general population, and around 1.69 fold for the rural-suburban residents. These observations are in line with existing research reporting gambling risk differentials across exposure levels. Besides contributing causal estimates of these risk differences on average and for urban, rural residents, the study provides novel insights on the interpretations of the main findings in terms of partial substitution between online vs. land-based gambling. The results and methods from this study are relevant for theoretical as well as policy debates on possible interventions to prevent and mitigate online gambling harms.

articles.title: Treadmill exercise impedes cognitive decline in type 2 diabetic rats by improving mitochondrial function and modulating the TGF-β/Smad-3 pathway.
articles.journal: Pflugers Archiv : European journal of physiology
articles.abstract: Chronic hyperglycemia and cerebral insulin resistance are the major contributors to cognitive impairment in the ageing population. Due to the increased number of the worldwide type - 2 diabetic mellitus (T2DM) population, the prevalence of cognitive decline and dementia has also increased. It is well documented that moderate aerobic exercise dramatically improves cognitive function in individuals with diabetes. However, the impact of exercise on T2DM-associated cognitive decline modulating TGF-β/Smad-3 signalling is yet to be explored. In this study, we assessed the impact of treadmill exercise on cognitive health in a preclinical model of T2DM, focusing on neuroinflammation, mitochondrial function, and the TGF-β/Smad-3 signalling pathway. To develop an experimental type - 2 diabetic model, rats were fed a high-fat diet (HFD), followed by an intraperitoneal injection of a single low dose of streptozotocin (STZ, 35 mg/kg). After confirmation of diabetes, rats underwent moderate-intensity treadmill exercise for 14 weeks. We observed a significant alternation in behavioural patterns in diabetic rats compared to controls, which reversed on exercise treatment. Moreover, chronic Type - 2 diabetes compromises mitochondrial function and increases inflammation in the hippocampal region of the brain. An increase in pro-inflammatory cytokines, such as IL-1β and TNF-α, was observed in the hippocampus of T2DM animals and was reduced by exercise. Oxidative stress is markedly increased in the type - 2 diabetic brain, resulting in compromised mitochondrial function with elevated hippocampal MDA and decreased GSH and ATP levels, which are reversed in the exercise group. Furthermore, we evaluated the role of exercise on TGF-β/Smad-3 signalling in the type - 2 diabetic brain. Exercise suppresses the overexpression of this signalling cascade in the diabetic brain. In summary, moderate-intensity treadmill exercise ameliorated type - 2 diabetes-associated cognitive impairment by decreasing oxidative stress, neuroinflammation, mitochondrial dysfunction and downregulating the TGF-β/Smad-3 signalling pathway.

articles.title: Outcomes of total temporomandibular joint replacement: a systematic review.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Temporomandibular joint replacement (TMJR) is a reconstructive surgical modality that is available to patients with end-stage temporomandibular disorders (TMDs) that fail conservative treatment. Alloplastic prostheses are either custom-made or stock devices used to restore mandibular function and reduce pain; however, comparative data and long-term outcomes are limited. This systematic review aimed to assess post-surgical functional, pain, and quality-of-life outcomes following alloplastic total TMJR.

METHODS: We searched PubMed, Google Scholar, Scopus, and institutional databases through March 2025, following PRISMA guidelines, to identify outcomes of alloplastic TMJR. Three reviewers independently screened and extracted the data, and a fourth reviewer resolved discrepancies. Results were summarised narratively because of variability in clinical and methodological approaches. We used ROBINS-I to evaluate study quality and the GRADE system to rate evidence certainty.

RESULTS: Eleven studies (569 patients, follow-up 12-62 months) fulfilled the inclusion criteria. Alloplastic TMJR was consistently associated with improved MMO, reduced pain, and better patient-reported QoL, although lateral excursion and protrusion were often lower than in healthy controls. Custom-made prostheses were more prevalent than stock devices, and no evidence supported one type over the other. Transient facial nerve paresis was a rare complication, and the 5-year survival rate of prostheses was > 90%. Nine out of eleven studies were at serious or critical risk of bias; however, across all outcomes, GRADE certainty was rated very low.

CONCLUSIONS: Although alloplastic TMJR holds promise of functional, pain, and quality-of-life improvements in carefully selected patients with end-stage TMD, current evidence is of very low certainty. Future multicentre trials with agreed-upon outcome measures and direct comparisons between custom and stock systems are required to reach definitive conclusions.

articles.title: Association between gestational diabetes mellitus and periodontal inflammation in a South African cohort.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: To investigate the association between gestational diabetes mellitus (GDM), periodontal status, and systemic inflammatory gene expression among pregnant women in South Africa.

MATERIALS AND METHODS: This case-control study included 105 pregnant women, comprising 52 women with GDM and 53 normoglycaemic controls. Participants were classified into four groups according to GDM and periodontal status. Periodontal assessment included probing depth (PD), clinical attachment level (CAL), and bleeding on probing (BOP). Peripheral blood expression of CRP, IL-6, TNF-α, MMP-8, and MMP-9 was assessed using quantitative real-time PCR and expressed as relative gene expression. Multivariable logistic regression was adjusted for maternal age, BMI, gestational age, parity, smoking status, ethnicity, and toothbrushing frequency.

RESULTS: PD, CAL, and BOP differed significantly across the four groups (all p < 0.001), with the highest BOP observed in women with both GDM and periodontitis. By GDM status, BOP was significantly higher in women with GDM [median 32.5% (range 8-70) vs. 13.0% (range 1-38); p < 0.001], whereas PD and CAL did not differ significantly in unadjusted analyses. After adjustment, BOP, PD, and CAL were significantly associated with GDM. MMP-9 relative expression differed overall across the four groups (p = 0.047), although adjusted post-hoc pairwise comparisons were not significant. IL-6 differed by GDM status in unadjusted analysis (p = 0.039) but not after adjustment.

CONCLUSION: GDM was associated with greater periodontal inflammatory burden, particularly BOP. Systemic inflammatory gene-expression differences were less consistent and showed no independent associations with GDM after adjustment.

articles.title: Sex-specific skeletal muscle fiber atrophy and reduced macrophage inflammation in a rodent transverse aortic constriction model.
articles.journal: Pflugers Archiv : European journal of physiology
articles.abstract: Heart failure is associated with systemic skeletal muscle remodeling, where sex-specific differences suggest differential peripheral involvement in disease progression. Skeletal muscle macrophages regulate angiogenesis and tissue remodeling and may contribute to early alterations in muscle structure and function during cardiac pressure overload. We tested whether chronic pressure-overload induces sex-specific skeletal muscle remodeling and alters macrophage abundance and paracrine signaling in male and female Sprague Dawley rats that underwent transverse aortic constriction (TAC) or sham surgery at 4 weeks of age and were studied after 40 wk. TAC induced 12% greater heart mass (p = 0.049) and 17% greater heart-to-body mass ratio (p = 0.018) in males, while females showed minimal cardiac remodeling. In extensor digitorum longus (EDL) muscle, TAC males exhibited ~ 10% smaller fiber perimeter corresponding with higher capillary-to-fiber perimeter exchange (p < 0.05 for both), while female TAC rats had no difference in fiber size and 17% lower capillary-to-fiber ratio than female sham (p = 0.033). In soleus muscle, TAC rats had higher capillarization indices (p < 0.05) regardless of sex. Muscle macrophage abundance was 19% lower in TAC males than sham males (p = 0.005). TAC macrophages secreted less MCP-1 (- 35%, p = 0.0058), IL-1β (- 16%, p = 0.0167), TNF-α (- 16%, p = 0.0337), and VEGF-A (- 16%, p = 0.0120) and produced less complex endothelial networks (18% larger mesh size, p = 0.001). These findings indicate that TAC is associated with skeletal muscle remodeling and macrophage immunosuppression, with some changes occurring in a sex-specific manner. This suggests the potential for immune-microvascular coupling in peripheral adaptations to cardiac pressure overload.

articles.title: Longitudinal Functional Magnetic Resonance Imaging to Assess Lung Disease in Cystic Fibrosis.
articles.journal: Annals of the American Thoracic Society
articles.abstract:
RATIONALE: Matrix pencil decomposition magnetic resonance imaging (MP-MRI) enables quantitative assessment of lung ventilation and perfusion and was shown to correlate with contrast-enhanced (CE) perfusion MRI.

OBJECTIVES: To determine the longitudinal course of MP-MRI parameters in people with cystic fibrosis (pwCF).

METHODS: Morpho-functional MRI including CE perfusion MRI and MP-MRI were performed twice in 136 pwCF with a median (range) baseline age of 14.5 (0.1-56.0) years to obtain the morpho-functional MRI score. Perfusion defect percentage (QDP) and ventilation defect percentage (VDP) were calculated by automated software. Additionally, lung clearance index (LCI) and forced expiratory volume in one second (FEV1) z-score were assessed. The participants were divided in subgroups depending on the clinical course according to cystic fibrosis transmembrane conductance regulator modulator therapy, pulmonary exacerbation status and Pseudomonas aeruginosa infection status.

RESULTS: In the total cohort, VDP improved at follow up. Change in VDP correlated with change in MRI global score, MRI CE perfusion score and FEV1 z-score. Additionally, change in QDP correlated with change in MRI global score, MRI morphology score, MRI CE perfusion score and FEV1 z-score. QDP and VDP remained stable in clinically stable pwCF (n = 55) and improved in clinically improved pwCF (n = 67). In the stable and improved group, change in QDP correlated moderately with change in MRI CE perfusion score.

CONCLUSIONS: MP-MRI assesses stability and improvement of lung perfusion and ventilation in pwCF. Changes correlate with those of established MRI scores. Therefore, QDP and VDP are sensitive longitudinal outcome parameters for future clinical studies.

articles.title: Rare Coding Variants in FOXF1 are Associated with Pulmonary Arterial Hypertension.
articles.journal: American journal of respiratory and critical care medicine
articles.abstract:
RATIONALE: Most patients with nonheritable forms of pulmonary arterial hypertension (PAH) lack identifiable pathogenic variants. Increasing evidence suggests that, in addition to high-impact predicted loss-of-function variants, rare missense coding variants may also contribute to disease pathogenesis.

OBJECTIVES: We identified ultra-rare missense variants in FOXF1 in two index cases with PAH. FOXF1 encodes a highly conserved transcription factor essential for lung vascular development. We sought to define the frequency of FOXF1 variants, characterize FOXF1 expression, and assess the functional relevance of FOXF1 alterations in PAH.

METHODS: Three independent international PAH cohorts were analyzed for predicted deleterious FOXF1 variants. FOXF1 expression was evaluated using bulk and single-cell RNA sequencing and immunofluorescence. Bioinformatic and chromatin-profiling approaches were used to identify potential downstream transcriptional targets, followed by promoter-reporter assays in vitro.

MEASUREMENTS AND MAIN RESULTS: Nine novel and one rare missense variants, one start-site variant, and one in-frame deletion in FOXF1 were identified across the three cohorts. FOXF1 expression was reduced in PAH lungs and localized predominantly to the endothelial cell compartment. Histopathological analysis revealed heterogeneous FOXF1 expression, with the lowest levels in phenotypically abnormal endothelial cells within complex vascular lesions. Single-cell analyses confirmed reduced endothelial FOXF1 expression in PAH, whereas broad FOXF1 downregulation across endothelial populations was not observed in other chronic lung diseases. Integration of CUT&Tag and ATAC-seq identified a canonical FOXF1-binding motif within the BMPR2 promoter. Promoter-reporter assays further supported FOXF1-dependent transcriptional regulation of BMPR2 and demonstrated reduced transcriptional activity of PAH-associated FOXF1 variants.

CONCLUSIONS: Large-scale genomic and transcriptomic analyses support an association between FOXF1 dysregulation and PAH and identify BMPR2 as a potential downstream transcriptional target.

articles.title: A Birth, a Death: The Grief Experiences of Mothers Who Lose One of Their Twins after Birth.
articles.abstract: This study explores the unique grief experiences of mothers who have lost one of their babies after a twin pregnancy. It aims to provide an in-depth understanding of their emotions, the challenges they faced, and their coping strategies. The data were analyzed using six-phase thematic analysis.
