CONCLUSIONS: Both training approaches improved MIP, whereas multidimensional functional training resulted in higher weaning success and greater improvements in peripheral muscle strength, functional independence, pain, weaning duration, and ICU length of stay than high-intensity IMT+CPT in patients following emergency abdominal surgery.

articles.title: Amine-PEG functionalized graphene oxide enhances the mechanical performance and biocompatibility of bovine pericardium for cardiovascular applications.
articles.abstract: Valvular heart disease remains a global health challenge, with increasing demand for aortic valve replacement procedures worldwide. Tissue engineering has emerged as a promising strategy to overcome limitations of conventional bioprosthetic valves, particularly long-term degeneration and limited durability. In this study, graphene oxide (GO) functionalized with amine-polyethylene glycol (GO-PEG-NH2) was incorporated into bovine pericardium by adsorption and chemical reaction to improve mechanical performance for cardiovascular applications. Structural, chemical, and morphological characterizations supported successful GO synthesis and functionalization with PEG-NH2. Atomic force microscopy demonstrated surface modifications and reduced roughness, particularly through chemical reaction. Mechanical assays revealed improvements in stiffness, 0.2% offset yield strength, tensile strength, and maximum load, with chemically incorporated membranes showing superior performance. GO reduced cell viability at concentrations ≥50 μg/mL, whereas GO-PEG-NH2 did not significantly reduce CHO cell viability at 10-200 μg/mL. Isolated atrial reactivity showed a more favorable biological response to GO-PEG-NH2 than to unmodified GO under the evaluated conditions.

articles.title: Clinical Characteristics and Transplacental Treatment of Fetal Ventricular Tachycardia: A Nationwide Survey in Japan.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Fetal ventricular tachycardia (VT) is an ultra-rare form of tachyarrhythmia, and no established management strategy currently exists.

OBJECTIVES: This study aimed to clarify the current diagnostic and management approaches for fetal VT.

METHODS: A nationwide survey of suspected fetal VT was conducted across 77 tertiary referral facilities in Japan between 2014 and 2023.

RESULTS: In total, 24 fetal VT cases from 18 facilities were analyzed. Twenty cases were diagnosed based on atrioventricular dissociation. Four were initially diagnosed as supraventricular tachycardia. VT occurred by 32 6/7 weeks of gestation in all nine long QT syndrome (LQTS) cases (LQT 2 in six, LQT 3 in two, and other in one), whereas 8/15 non-LQTS cases occurred at term. Eight of 20 cases managed as fetal VT, and three of four cases managed as fetal supraventricular tachycardia received fetal treatment. Fetal treatments were effective in 9/11 cases overall and in 8/9 LQTS cases. Side effects were observed in 6/11 cases; however, no serious adverse events occurred, except one case of lidocaine toxicity. After birth, LQTS cases were more likely to be refractory to treatment than non-LQT cases (8/9 vs. 6/14), requiring multidisciplinary management. Neurodevelopmental delay was more frequent in LQTS cases than in non-LQTS cases (6/9 vs. 2/14).

CONCLUSIONS: Transplacental treatment is highly recommended for preterm fetal VT. In particular, in cases of fetal VT diagnosed before 33 weeks of gestation, aggressive fetal treatment including magnesium sulfate and β-blockers should be considered with the possibility of LQT 2 or 3.

articles.title: Substrate Comprising Fibrosis and Epicardial Adipose Tissue-Associated Electrophysiological Remodeling Can Sustain Atrial Fibrillation Drivers: Insights from Image-Personalized Computational Simulations.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Computational models of atrial fibrillation (AF) help clarify arrhythmia mechanisms, but the contribution of left atrial (LA) epicardial adipose tissue (EAT) is rarely included.

OBJECTIVE: To assess whether incorporating EAT-associated effects into fibrosis-based atrial models alters reentrant arrhythmia inducibility, and to characterize the pro-arrhythmic properties of EAT-affected tissue.

METHODS: LA fibrosis and EAT were quantified by LGE and Dixon MRI in 19 patients with persistent AF. For each patient, three anatomically identical image-personalized models were built (fibrosis only; fibrosis plus half-epicardial EAT effects, 0.5 mm; fibrosis plus full-epicardial EAT effects, 1.0 mm), yielding 855 simulations. In EAT regions, inward rectifier K+ current was reduced by 35%, intracellular K+ by 50%, and conduction velocity by 25%.

RESULTS: Sustained reentry occurred in 370 simulations (43.3%), of which 306 had a functional (rotor-driven) component. Functional reentry inducibility rose from 22.8% (fibrosis only) to 41.4% (half-EAT) and 43.2% (full-EAT). At least one functional reentry was inducible in 12/19 fibrosis-only models, 18/19 half-EAT models, and 19/19 full-EAT models. Median inducible simulations per patient increased from 4 to 6 (p=0.004) and 7 (p=0.003), without significant difference between half- and full-EAT (p=0.895). Fibrosis/EAT overlap regions comprised only 2.1% of the LA wall but were the most arrhythmogenic, with a median 65.5% of their volume harboring reentry versus 8.8% (non-substrate), 37.3% (fibrosis), and 42.8% (EAT) (all p<0.001). In an exploratory analysis of PVI-only ablation patients (n=13), fibrosis-EAT overlap outside the PVI region was associated with 1-year recurrence (log-rank p=0.007).

CONCLUSION: Adding EAT effects to fibrosis-based models increased sustained functional reentry, with transmural depth contributing only modestly. Reentry anchored preferentially where fibrosis and EAT effects coexisted.

articles.title: Differences in Tricuspid Valve Insufficiency, Mechanical Synchrony, and Cardiac Remodeling Between Left Bundle Branch Area Pacing and Right Ventricular Pacing.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Cardiac implantable electronic device-induced tricuspid regurgitation (CIED-induced TR) involves primary (lead-induced) and functional etiologies. The impact of left bundle branch area pacing (LBBAP) versus right ventricular pacing (RVP) on these mechanisms remains unclear.

OBJECTIVE: To compare the incidence and mechanisms of TR among pacing modalities, and evaluate the prognostic significance of these mechanisms.

METHODS: We analyzed 225 patients with first-time RV apical pacing (RVAP, n=97) or RV septal pacing (RVSP, n=78) using stylet-driven leads, and LBBAP (n=50) using lumenless leads. Echocardiography and electrocardiography were performed at baseline and 2 years post-implantation. Three-dimensional echocardiography assessed lead interference. Kaplan-Meier analysis compared event-free survival between lead-induced (LITR) and functional TR (FTR) groups. Cox regression identified predictors for adverse outcomes.

RESULTS: Despite a higher baseline heart failure burden than RVP (P< .001), LBBAP showed the lowest TR progression rate (20.0% vs RVAP 43.3% vs RVSP 35.9%, P=.020) over 25.8 months. Mechanistically, LBBAP shortened QRS duration (vs RVP widening, P< .001) and demonstrated less lead interference than RVAP (28.0% vs 50.5%, P= .009). Furthermore, LBBAP showed greater left-heart reverse remodeling and improvement in mitral regurgitation, while preserving right-heart structure and function better than RVP. Over 37.4 months, LITR showed worse outcomes than FTR (P= .03). LITR, pulmonary hypertension, reduced left ventricular ejection fraction, and elevated creatinine were independent predictors for adverse outcomes.

CONCLUSION: LBBAP was associated with less CIED-induced TR than RVP, likely through reduced mechanical interference, superior electrical synchrony, and favorable cardiac remodeling. Furthermore, LITR was associated with a worse prognosis than FTR.

articles.title: A Rounding Error Dressed as Reform: The Implications of a Large Private Health Insurance Company's Prior Authorization Concession for the Electrophysiology Patient.
Nuclear magnetic resonance-derived lipoprotein profile and risk of atrial tachyarrhythmia recurrence after catheter ablation: a case-cohort design within the PREDIMAR trial.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Lipoproteins could be potential biomarkers of atrial tachyarrhythmia recurrence (TAR) after catheter ablation; however, their association remains inconclusive and based exclusively on routine lipid measurements. Nuclear magnetic resonance (NMR) enables detailed lipoprotein characterization beyond conventional assays.

OBJECTIVE: To identify a baseline NMR-derived lipoprotein profile associated with the risk of TAR after catheter ablation.

METHODS: We conducted a case-cohort study (212 cases and 238 participants in a random sub-cohort, with 93 overlapping cases) nested in the PREDIMAR (PRevención con DIeta Mediterránea de Arritmias Recurrentes) trial. Conventional lipoprotein profiles were measured using the Pentra C-200 and advanced lipoprotein profiles were assessed by NMR. Lipoprotein values were normalized and scaled to one standard deviation using Blom's inverse normal transformation. Cox models were used to assess the associations between baseline lipoproteins and TAR. Additionally, a cholesteryl ester transfer (CETP)-mediated lipoprotein exchange score was constructed and evaluated.

RESULTS: After 18-month follow-up, higher baseline remnant cholesterol (hazard ratio = 1.26, 95% confidence interval= 1.06-1.51, per SD), higher cholesterol and triglyceride content in very-low-density lipoproteins (VLDL) (hazard ratioperSD = 1.22, 95% confidence interval= 1.03-1.46) or in intermediate-density lipoproteins (IDL) (hazard ratioperSD = 1.29, 95% confidence interval= 1.09-1.52), showed increased risks of TAR. Higher triglyceride-to-HDL cholesterol ratio was directly associated, and higher triglyceride-to-VLDL cholesterol and triglyceride-to-IDL cholesterol ratios were inversely associated with recurrence. A CETP-mediated lipoprotein exchange score was directly associated with recurrence.

CONCLUSION: An atherogenic lipoprotein profile characterized by elevated remnant cholesterol is associated with a higher risk of TAR after catheter ablation.

articles.title: Altered cardiac progenitor transcriptional program accompanies NOS-associated DNA damage in a human Duchenne muscular dystrophy organoid model.
articles.abstract: Duchenne muscular dystrophy (DMD), a rare X-linked disorder caused by dystrophin mutations, leads to progressive muscle degeneration and cardiomyopathy. We previously showed elevated DNA damage and mutagenesis in DMD pluripotent stem cells, due to nitric oxide synthase (NOS) dysregulation and reactive species. Here we examined how these disruptions influence cardiac tissue development. In developing cardiac organoids, the DMD cardiovascular progenitor (CP) population shows a premature, elevated activation of CP markers, followed by early maturation gene expression and reduced proliferation. DMD organoids exhibit elevated DNA damage in CPs, persistent pro-inflammatory signaling, and increased expression of inducible NOS. These early molecular disruptions lead to an impaired cardiac differentiation with a lower fraction of spontaneously contracting organoids. DMD organoids show higher cardiac troponin release and accelerated collagen accumulation, mirroring heart failure pathology in mdx mice and DMD patients. Inducing DNA damage in early-stage wild-type organoids reproduced part of the altered gene expression seen in DMD. NOS inhibition in DMD organoids reduced DNA damage and improved organoid contraction, though it did not prevent CM death or collagen accumulation or restore normal gene expression. Together, these findings position NO/NOS modulation as relevant to early cardiac differentiation defects, with isoform balance likely shifting across developmental stages.

articles.title: A stewardship framework for incretin-based therapies in weight management.
articles.journal: Journal of the American Pharmacists Association : JAPhA
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Use of incretin-based therapies, including GLP-1 and GIP receptor agonists, for weight management and related cardio-kidney-liver-metabolic comorbidities has expanded rapidly, yet real-world practice is challenged by inconsistent prescribing, access barriers, limited long-term safety data, low treatment persistence, and concerns regarding equity and financial sustainability. These gaps highlight the need for a structured, coordinated stewardship model to guide safe and evidence-based use of incretin-based therapies.

OBJECTIVES: To develop a scalable, multidisciplinary stewardship framework for incretin-based therapies that supports consistent and efficient prescribing practices, optimizes patient outcomes, strengthens medication access and safety monitoring, and defines the role of pharmacists in chronic weight management.

METHODS: Two sequential expert workgroups were convened, composed of clinicians and pharmacy leaders from 21 health systems. Workgroup 1 identified foundational stewardship elements drawing from established antimicrobial and opioid stewardship models. Workgroup 2 applied these core principles to incretin-based therapies, informed by real-world challenges, emerging evidence, and clinical experience in weight and diabetes management. Consensus was established using a Delphi process, with ≥60% agreement required for inclusion.

RESULTS: Workgroups reached consensus on a stewardship framework comprising multidisciplinary leadership, stakeholder engagement, pharmacy expertise, defined priorities, evidence-based interventions, education, data and reporting strategies, communication pathways, and mechanisms for feedback and continuous assessment. In addition, consensus-based pharmacist-led initiatives and metric categories were developed to support implementation and program evaluation across varied ambulatory environments, with pharmacists identified as central to therapy initiation and titration, adverse effect management, access navigation, patient education, and care coordination.

CONCLUSION: A structured stewardship model offers a feasible and scalable approach to optimize incretin-based therapies in weight management. By integrating multidisciplinary collaboration with pharmacy expertise and clinical and operational strategies, health systems can promote safe, equitable, and sustainable use of these therapies, improve population-level outcomes, and safeguard long-term value amid rapidly expanding utilization.

articles.title: Allergic bronchopulmonary mycosis associated with Talaromyces boninensis: A case report.
articles.journal: Journal of infection and chemotherapy : official journal of the Japan Society of Chemotherapy
articles.abstract: Allergic bronchopulmonary aspergillosis is a chronic inflammatory pulmonary disorder characterized by type I and III hypersensitivity reactions to Aspergillus fumigatus in the airways of patients with asthma or cystic fibrosis. However, other filamentous fungi can cause similar pathophysiological changes, a condition referred to as allergic bronchopulmonary mycosis (ABPM). Data on ABPM involving non-Aspergillus fungi remain limited. To the best of our knowledge, we present the first case of ABPM associated with Talaromyces boninensis. The patient met the diagnostic criteria proposed by the Japan ABPM Research Program, and T. boninensis was isolated from bronchial lavage fluid and identified by molecular analysis.

articles.title: Affective prosody and facial expression cues differentially augment spoken sentence and discourse comprehension for acute left and right hemisphere stroke survivors.
articles.abstract: Comprehension for spoken sentences and discourse is differentially impacted by left- (LH) and right-hemisphere (RH) brain damage, such as that caused by stroke. Comprehension deficits can have disabling effects on one's ability to process information, participate in everyday life, and create and maintain relationships. This cross-sectional, observational study evaluated differences in sentence- and discourse-level comprehension between LH and RH stroke survivors across different prosodic conditions and examined relationships between comprehension and damage to key LH and RH regions. Participants included 43 LH and 46 RH acute stroke survivors and 39 controls. All participants completed an in-house clinical assessment that included short passages presented in three conditions: neutral prosody, affective prosody, and affective prosody plus facial expression cues. Stroke survivors also completed magnetic resonance imaging. Consistent with expectations, stroke participants achieved lower comprehension accuracy than controls across conditions. LH participants' accuracy in the 'affective prosody plus facial expressions' condition was greater than in the neutral prosody condition, and total LH lesion volume was associated with performance. RH participants' accuracy in the 'affective prosody' and 'affective prosody plus facial expressions' conditions was greater than in the neutral prosody condition. Overall, both groups' scores increased linearly from Condition 1 to 3. None of the prespecified LH or RH brain regions were significantly associated with performance. Findings suggest that some acute LH and RH stroke survivors with comprehension deficits can benefit from affective prosody and facial expression cues, but different or additional cues may be needed for greatest benefit.

articles.title: Prevalence of Diabetic Retinopathy and Cardiovascular Risk Factors Among Diverse Hispanic/Latino Adults: HCHS/SOL and SOL Ojos Results.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To estimate diabetic retinopathy (DR) prevalence among Hispanic/Latino adults with diabetes, assess heterogeneity by background group, and evaluate cardiovascular disease (CVD) risk factors.

DESIGN: Cross-sectional analysis of SOL Ojos, a multicenter ancillary study embedded within the population-based Hispanic Community Health Study/Study of Latinos (HCHS/SOL).

PARTICIPANTS: Adults aged ≥40 years completing HCHS/SOL Visit 3 (V3; 2020-2024) from Chicago and Miami were examined (3,294/3,864; 85.2%). The analytic sample included 1,224 participants with diabetes and gradable retinal imaging (mean age, 62.7 years [95% CI, 61.4-64.0]; 48.6% female).

METHODS: Participants underwent standardized ophthalmic examinations with centrally graded ultra-widefield fundus imaging. Major CVD risk factors (diabetes, hypertension, hypercholesterolemia, obesity, smoking) were assessed at V3 and analyzed individually and cumulatively. DR, macular edema (ME), and vision-threatening DR (VTDR) were graded using Early Treatment Diabetic Retinopathy Study (ETDRS) protocols. Survey-weighted analyses estimated age-standardized prevalence, and sequentially adjusted logistic regression evaluated associations.

MAIN OUTCOME MEASURES: Age-standardized prevalence of DR outcomes and associations with CVD risk factors.

RESULTS: Age-standardized any DR prevalence was 34.7% (95% CI, 29.2-40.2). Among men, any DR and VTDR prevalence was 41.8% (95% CI, 33.5-50.0) and 13.4% (95% CI, 7.4-19.5), versus 27.2% (95% CI, 19.5-34.9) and 9.4% (95% CI, 1.4-17.4) among women. Any DR ranged across Hispanic/Latino backgrounds from 13.9% (95% CI, 1.8-26.0) to 55.4% (95% CI, 49.2-61.6) in men and 15.3% (95% CI, 4.4-26.2) to 39.2% (95% CI, 22.3-56.1) in women, with the highest estimates among Cuban individuals. CVD risk factors were common and clustered (≥4: men 42.7% [95% CI, 34.5-50.9]; women 35.6% [95% CI, 29.3-41.9]). In adjusted models, hypertension was associated with any DR (OR, 3.16 [95% CI, 1.76-5.65]) and VTDR (OR, 2.86 [95% CI, 1.05-7.79]). Overall cumulative CVD risk burden was not significantly associated with VTDR (Type III F test, P=0.1193), despite adjustment for diabetes duration; the 3-risk-factor category had higher estimated odds than the 1-risk-factor category (OR, 5.10 [95% CI, 1.22-21.39]).

CONCLUSION: In this cross-sectional study of Hispanic/Latino adults with diabetes, more than one-third had DR, with substantial heterogeneity across background groups. Hypertension was associated with DR outcomes, particularly VTDR. Findings provide contemporary prevalence estimates and support longitudinal evaluation of cardiometabolic risk and DR outcomes.

articles.title: Assessment of the Necessity for High-Level Disinfection (HLD) of Reusable Ophthalmic Devices: A Multisociety Position Paper.
articles.abstract: Regulatory agencies in the United States and abroad are increasingly citing clinics and surgical facilities for what they deem to be inadequate disinfection of Goldmann applanation tonometry (GAT) tips, gonioscopy lenses, laser lenses, and other reusable clinic devices that contact the ocular surface. These regulators require routine high-level disinfection (HLD) of these reusable devices to prevent infection transmission. A multisociety task force formed to assess the necessity of HLD found no published evidence that these devices transmit sight-threatening infections or that HLD reduces infection transmission compared with lower-level disinfection methods. Meanwhile, routine use of chemical HLD reduces clinic efficiency, increases healthcare costs and waste, and may damage device surfaces potentially affecting patient care. Underlying these mandates for HLD is the nearly century-old Spaulding classification system, which inappropriately groups the ocular surface with heavily contaminated mucous membranes. A task force survey with more than 1000 ophthalmologist respondents found that the most common reprocessing methods were alcohol wiping for GAT tips and either alcohol wiping or soap and water for diagnostic or laser lenses. Many respondents using chemical HLD reported adverse effects, including ocular surface chemical toxicity and device damage. Despite infrequent use of HLD, reported infection transmission was exceedingly rare and generally limited to self-limited adenoviral conjunctivitis. The task force agreed with the majority (88%) of ophthalmologists surveyed that HLD should not be required for these reusable devices in routine clinical care. Instead, HLD should be a discretionary consideration in higher-risk circumstances, such as following use of these devices in patients with suspected infection. This paper presents the summary recommendations of a policy statement approved by the American Academy of Ophthalmology Board of Trustees and endorsed by four subspecialty societies.

articles.title: Pre-participation cardiovascular evaluation in Italian elite athletes (2023-2026): diagnostic yield, accuracy, and cost analysis.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Elite athletes represent a unique population within competitive sports. Despite repeated cardiovascular screening during their careers, they may harbour clinically silent but potentially serious cardiovascular diseases. Therefore, cardiovascular evaluation in elite athletes may require a sensitive and comprehensive diagnostic approach.

METHODS: We analyzed 1505 elite athletes, undergoing comprehensive PPS including resting ECG, transthoracic echocardiography (TTE), and cardiopulmonary exercise testing (CPET). Major cardiovascular abnormalities (MCA) and cardiomyopathies were established according to the final clinical diagnosis, served as the reference standard. Sensitivity, specificity, positive and negative predictive values (NPV), and ROC analyses were assessed for ECG alone and for ECG combined with CPET or TTE.

RESULTS: MCA were identified in 17 athletes (1.13%), including 7 cardiomyopathies (0.46%) and 6 channelopathies (0.40%). CPET identified additional cardiomyopathies through exercise-induced arrhythmias, including cases not detected by resting ECG, whereas TTE identified structural and coronary abnormalities not evident on ECG. Resting ECG showed a sensitivity of 58.8% and specificity of 94.0% for MCA, with a NPV 99.5%. The addition of CPET increased sensitivity to 82.4%, although specificity decreased to 82.2%. ECG + TTE achieved a sensitivity of 76.5% and specificity of 91.5%. ROC analysis showed AUCs of 0.76 for ECG, 0.82 for ECG + CPET, and 0.84 for ECG + TTE for MCA.

CONCLUSION: In this highly selected cohort of elite athletes, integrating ECG, CPET, and TTE provided complementary diagnostic information and increased the detection of MCA compared with resting ECG alone. These findings support the feasibility of a comprehensive cardiovascular evaluation model in highly selected athletes evaluated within specialized sports cardiology settings.

articles.title: Evaluation of Active Surveillance Testing for Candidozyma (Candida) auris and Impact on Infection Control Behaviors in an Acute Healthcare System.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To evaluate the impact of active surveillance testing (AST) for Candidozyma auris on healthcare system epidemiologic trends and infection prevention and control (IPC) behaviors.

DESIGN: Explanatory sequential mixed methods study using retrospective electronic medical record review, hand hygiene observations, and healthcare personnel focus groups.

SETTING AND PATIENTS: Five acute care hospitals within a suburban healthcare system. Chart reviews included 3,688 patients who underwent AST for C. auris or had positive clinical cultures for C. auris from 2020-2023.

METHODS: Incidence and prevalence were calculated by year and location. Logistic regression examined associations with C. auris events. Observations and focus groups explored barriers and facilitators to IPC behaviors.

RESULTS: AST volume increased from 66 tests in 2020 to 1,619 in 2023, while positivity decreased from 7.58% to 2.47%. Concurrent increases in community-onset and hospital-onset prevalence were observed over time. Focus groups identified barriers including fatigue and accountability, and facilitators including role modeling and supply accessibility.

CONCLUSIONS: AST facilitated early identification of colonized or infected patients and supported systemic surveillance of C. auris, while behavioral assessment identified opportunities to strengthen adherence to core IPC practices. These findings demonstrate the value of integrating epidemiologic and behavioral evaluation when assessing IPC programs.

articles.title: Benefits and Harms of Dose Escalation of Inhaled Corticosteroids in Uncontrolled Asthma.
articles.journal: The journal of allergy and clinical immunology. In practice

articles.title: Inhaled, nasal and topical corticosteroid burden and association with corticosteroid-associated adverse events.
articles.journal: The journal of allergy and clinical immunology. In practice
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Patients with type 2 inflammation-associated diseases are often treated with multiple formulations of corticosteroids. Long-term risks of using combinations of local corticosteroids are poorly characterised.

OBJECTIVE: Using Danish nationwide databases, investigate associations between local corticosteroid exposure and 11 corticosteroid exposure-associated conditions compared to non-users, and eventual dose-response relationship for exposed individuals.

METHODS: Systemic corticosteroid-naïve adults who redeemed inhaled, nasal and/or topical corticosteroids 2000-2012 were matched with non-initiators and followed for up to 23 years. Overall (inhaled, nasal and topical) exposure was calculated for 6-month periods as low (<1.25 daily prednisolone-equivalent mg), moderate (1.25-2.5 mg) or high (>2.5 mg). Competing risk Cox models with time-varying effects were used, presented as HR per additional 6-month period of exposure.

RESULTS: Overall, 292,393 local corticosteroid users were included (mean age 45, 47.7% female). Corticosteroid exposure-associated condition incidences were generally low, but all conditions had higher subdistribution-HRs in users, ranging from 1.4 to 3.8 for cataracts and obesity (p<0.001).For local corticosteroid users, increased risk per 6-month exposure was observed for osteoporosis (low-high dose: HRs 1.01-1.10), obesity (1.03-1.03) and pneumonia (1.03-1.15). Risk of cardiovascular disease, heart failure, cataract and gastroesophageal reflux disease increased with high-dose exposure only at HRs 1.03, 1.02, 1.04 and 1.04 per additional 6-month period of exposure, respectively.Stratified by formulation, high-dose inhaled and topical corticosteroids demonstrated the strongest associations.

CONCLUSION: In individuals using local corticosteroids, the overall corticosteroid burden, including shorter periods of high-dose exposure, associates with corticosteroid exposure-associated adverse events albeit with generally low incidence and hazard.

articles.title: "Bridging the Gap: Increasing Participation of Underrepresented Populations in Allergy and Immunology Research".
articles.journal: The journal of allergy and clinical immunology. In practice
articles.abstract: Despite decades of national initiatives, racial, ethnic, socioeconomic, and historically underrepresented populations remain inadequately represented in allergy and immunology research. This limits the generalizability of findings, impedes identification of differences in treatment response and safety, and contributes to persistent disparities among populations disproportionately affected by allergic and immunologic diseases. Underrepresentation reflects patient-, provider-, investigator-, institutional-, and regulatory-level barriers: mistrust of research, financial and logistical burdens, restrictive eligibility criteria, language and health literacy challenges, limited community engagement, and inequitable recruitment practices. We summarize current evidence of barriers to participation in allergy and immunology clinical research and highlight practical, evidence-based strategies to improve equitable recruitment and retention. Key approaches include culturally and linguistically appropriate recruitment materials, community advisory boards and trusted community partners, collaboration with clinicians serving underserved populations, decentralized and hybrid designs that reduce participant burden, broader eligibility criteria when scientifically appropriate, improved investigator and staff training, and participant-centered retention strategies. Sustained partnerships and dissemination of findings to participating communities foster long-term trust. Increasing diversity requires a coordinated, systems-level approach that embeds equity throughout study design, recruitment, implementation, retention, and dissemination. Doing so strengthens the validity and generalizability of the evidence base and ensures that future advances benefit all populations equitably.

articles.title: An update on miRNAs as non-invasive diagnostic markers for endometriosis: Why have we not reached consensus?
articles.abstract: The objective of this narrative review is to provide an update on microRNAs (miRNAs) as non-invasive biomarkers for endometriosis diagnosis focusing on publications from 2016 to 2026. In addition to updating miRNAs reported during this time frame, we also discuss why consensus has not been reached on identification of miRNAs with suitable sensitivity and specificity as diagnostic markers. A literature search was performed on PubMed from January 1, 2016 to September 1, 2026 using the keywords endometriosis, miRNA, and biomarker. A total of 238 articles were retrieved of which 101 were reviews, meta-analysis, or database searches, 46 articles focused on tissue or cell assessment of miRNA expression limiting the non-invasive approach, 24 were not focused on endometriosis but diseases comorbid with endometriosis, 17 focused on exosomes, 15 focused on other body fluid assessment of miRNAs, 4 focused on AI/machine learning, and 2 focused on animal model assessment of miRNA expression leaving 29 publications for further evaluation. The search for non-invasive biomarkers for endometriosis remains ongoing. From the studies presented in this review, while several miRNAs have emerged as candidate biomarkers, there is still considerable variability with respect to differentially expressed miRNAs between women with and without endometriosis. Focused assessment on methodologies employed for isolating serum/plasma, extraction of RNA/miRNAs, amplification and data normalization from these samples and if and how sample hemolysis was assessed and revealed differences among the studies all which impact miRNA profiles. As such, it is imperative to develop a standardized protocol when assessing miRNAs from blood if we hope to identify miRNAs which may prove useful in non-invasive diagnosis of endometriosis.

articles.title: Mid-Term Clinical Outcomes of Tendyne Transcatheter Mitral Valve Replacement: A Prospective Cohort of 100 Patients with Follow-up to 4 Years.
articles.journal: The Journal of thoracic and cardiovascular surgery
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: Transcatheter mitral valve replacement (TMVR) is an emerging therapy option currently mainly used in patients at high surgical risk and a mitral valve anatomy not eligible for transcatheter edge to edge repair (TEER). Clinical TMVR data are sparse as currently only two devices were granted CE or FDA certification. This study evaluates mid-term clinical outcomes of 100 consecutive single-center Tendyne-TMVR patients.

METHODS: From the institutional TMVR database, the first 100 consecutive patients undergoing implantation of the Abbott Tendyne mitral valve were identified. Baseline and procedural characteristics, clinical and echocardiography follow-up were prospectively recorded and retrospectively analyzed and reported following MVARC recommendations. according To evaluate a procedure-specific learning curve, the cohort was analyzed for 30-day mortality across four consecutive chronological groups (n=25 each).

RESULTS: The study enrolled 100 high surgical risk patients (mean age 76.3 ± 7.0 years; mean STS predicted risk of mortality 7.7 ± 6.4%). Mitral valve pathologies included primary MR (62.0%), functional MR (29.0%), severe MAC (30%) and previous mitral valve intervention (19%). Technical success was 96.0% and 30-day device success was 74.0%. Kaplan-Meier estimated survival at 30-days was 90.0% (95% CI: 82.2-94.5%), 71.2% (95% CI:61.1-79.2%) at 1 year, 64.3% (95% CI: 53.4-73.4%) at 2 years and 54.8% (95% CI: 41.7-66.1%) at 3 years. Chronological analysis revealed no significant inter-group differences in 30-day survival across the four groups composed of consecutive 25 patients (p=0.522).At 2 years, echocardiography revealed durable MR reduction with 100% MR Grade ≤1+ (none/trace MR 84.4%) and significant relief of heart failure symptoms with 84.9% NYHA class I/II.

CONCLUSIONS: TMVR with the Tendyne mitral valve system provided effective MR elimination in a cohort presenting with heterogenous mitral valve disease without evidence for a significant learning curve. Durable mitral valve function was confirmed up to 3 years. Mid-term mortality is associated with cardiovascular and non-cardiovascular mortality.

articles.title: Comparative Durability of Porcine and Bovine Mitral Valve Bioprostheses.
articles.journal: The Journal of thoracic and cardiovascular surgery
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: The objective of this study was to compare the durability of bovine pericardial and porcine bioprostheses in patients who underwent surgical mitral valve replacement.

METHODS: From 1/1/2000-1/1/2024, 6,515 adults underwent 6,789 mitral valve replacements with either porcine(n=4,597) or bovine(n=2,192) stented bioprostheses. Propensity score matching yielded 1,853 well-matched pairs. Durability was assessed by explant for structural valve deterioration(SVD) and longitudinal analysis of echocardiographic data(≥moderate mitral regurgitation and mean mitral gradient). Mortality and competing risks of explant for SVD and infective endocarditis were modeled using multiphase hazards.

RESULTS: Bovine bioprostheses were more commonly used before 2010, and porcine more recently. Within the matched groups, 352 reinterventions were identified, primarily for SVD(70%; n=253) and endocarditis(19%; n=69). At 15 years, conditional probability of reintervention for SVD was 34% in the porcine versus 45% in the bovine group(early P=.61; late P=.003). The porcine group had an increased risk of reintervention for endocarditis in the first year(P=.046), but similar risk thereafter(P=.54). Risk of ≥moderate mitral regurgitation at 10 years was 3% among porcine and 12% among bovine bioprostheses(P<.0001), with higher mean gradients in the bovine group(6.6 mmHg vs. 8.2 mmHg; late P<.0001). Survival 15-years after porcine mitral valve replacement was 18%, compared to 22% after bovine(P=.21).

CONCLUSIONS: The stent-mounted porcine bioprosthesis had better durability than the bovine bioprosthesis in the mitral position and is preferred over a bovine bioprosthesis with excellent late outcomes, particularly in patients under 60 years of age.

articles.title: A transmural t-tubule gradient in the human left ventricle is lost in heart failure: implications for myocardial biopsy assessment.
articles.journal: Journal of molecular and cellular cardiology
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The transverse tubular system (t-system) of ventricular cardiomyocytes is essential for excitation-contraction coupling and disrupted in chronic heart failure (HF). Whether physiological transmural gradients of t-tubule density exist in the non-failing human left ventricle (LV), and how representative small myocardial samples and biopsies are of the whole LV in HF, is unknown, limiting the translational use of t-tubules.

METHODS: We performed quantitative microscopic imaging of transmural LV slices created from 8 non-failing donor hearts and 13 end-stage failing HFrEF hearts (HTx/LVAD), generating a total of >400 confocal volumes and > 100 confocal area scans. Established image processing pipelines extracted t-tubule skeleton volume density, intracellular t-tubule and sarcolemma distance (ΔTT, ΔSL), extracellular matrix (ECM) fraction, and a cell-width proxy. LV endomyocardial-forceps biopsies were obtained ex vivo from a subset of samples to model clinical biopsy procedures.

RESULTS: In non-failing hearts, t-tubule skeleton density was 45% higher at the subepicardium than the subendocardium (0.16 ± 0.01% vs 0.11 ± 0.01%, p < 0.01), with correspondingly lower ΔTT (0.89 vs 1.05 μm, p < 0.001) and ΔSL. Failing hearts showed ~40% lower t-tubule density, increased ECM (~28% vs ~20%), and ~ 50% wider myocytes. The transmural gradient was lost. Apical regions showed the most pronounced TT remodeling but predicted the remaining LV t-tubule parameters with mean relative errors of ~10%. Mean ΔSL in endomyocardial biopsies correlated best with the corresponding wall section (R2 = 0.62, p = 0.0003), allowing a threshold for the separation of samples with from samples without t-system remodeling.

CONCLUSIONS: A subendo-to-subepicardial t-tubule gradient exists in the non-failing human LV and is abolished in HFrEF. These findings define the sampling constraints under which myocardial specimens may be used to stratify advanced t-system remodeling in human heart failure.

articles.title: Intracranial hypertension in a child with vitamin D deficiency.
articles.journal: Journal of AAPOS : the official publication of the American Association for Pediatric Ophthalmology and Strabismus

articles.title: Escalation of Care: Association of Weekend and Nighttime Postoperative ICU Admission with Poor Outcomes After Gastrointestinal Cancer Surgery.
articles.journal: Journal of gastrointestinal surgery : official journal of the Society for Surgery of the Alimentary Tract
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Postoperative intensive care unit (ICU) admission represents an important escalation of care after surgery. We evaluated the association between ICU admission timing and outcomes after gastrointestinal (GI) cancer surgery.

METHODS: Adults undergoing GI cancer surgery with postoperative ICU care were identified in Epic Cosmos from 2016 to 2025 and classified as weekday, weekend-day, weeknight, or weekend-night admission. Outcomes included complications during the index hospitalization and within 30 days, 30-day mortality, readmission, discharge home, and prolonged length of stay (LOS ≥75th percentile of the cohort). Multivariable logistic regression evaluated associations between ICU timing and outcomes.

RESULTS: Among 77,054 patients, 36.4% were classified as weekday, 15.4% weekend-day, 25.0% weeknight, and 23.2% weekend-night. Weekend-night classification was associated with the highest adjusted odds of 30-day mortality (aOR 1.52, 95% CI 1.42-1.63), any 30-day complication (aOR 1.76, 95% CI 1.69-1.84), and prolonged LOS (aOR 2.32, 95% CI 2.21-2.44), as well as lower odds of discharge home (aOR 0.70, 95% CI 0.67-0.73). Weeknight classification was also associated with higher odds of mortality (aOR 1.28, 95% CI 1.20-1.37), complications (aOR 1.42, 95% CI 1.36-1.48), and prolonged LOS (aOR 1.55, 95% CI 1.47-1.64).

CONCLUSIONS: Nighttime ICU classification, particularly weekend-night classification, identified patients at elevated postoperative risk after GI cancer surgery and may help inform surveillance and escalation strategies during off-hours.

articles.title: Polydatin alleviates vascular calcification via the TP53/PI3K/AKT axis.
articles.abstract: Vascular calcification (VC) is a major complication of chronic kidney disease (CKD), diabetes, atherosclerosis, and aging that significantly increases cardiovascular mortality, yet effective therapeutic interventions are currently limited. In this study, we demonstrated that Polydatin (PD), a natural polyphenolic compound, effectively alleviated VC across in vitro, ex vivo and in vivo models. PD treatment markedly reduced calcium deposition, decreased alkaline phosphatase (ALP) activity, and downregulated the expression of osteogenic markers (RUNX2 and BMP2). Network pharmacology analysis identified TP53 as a central candidate target. Molecular docking and cellular thermal shift assays (CETSA) confirmed a direct interaction between PD and P53 protein. Mechanistically, PD facilitated the degradation of P53 via the ubiquitin-proteasome pathway, thereby activating the PI3K/AKT signaling pathway. Notably, the anti-calcific effect of PD was abolished upon TP53 overexpression, confirming the indispensability of this regulatory pathway. Collectively, our findings establish PD as a potent inhibitor of VC and unveil the targeted modulation of the TP53-PI3K/AKT axis as a promising therapeutic strategy.

articles.title: Rosmarinic acid alleviates renal tubular injury in obesity-related hypertension by inhibiting the IL-18R1/MYD88/IRAK4 pathway.
articles.abstract: Renal tubular injury induced by pro-inflammatory cytokines is the key pathological basis for the progression of obesity-related hypertensive (OBH) nephropathy. Rosmarinic acid (RA) is an important active ingredient in many traditional Chinese medicines and exhibits a variety of pharmacological properties in the treatment of kidney diseases. Further work is needed to understand the underlying molecular mechanisms. In this study, the results showed that in OBH rats, RA significantly decreased blood pressure and Lee index, and improved pathological injury of the renal tubulointerstitial region. Luminex liquid chip assay revealed high levels of IL-18 in the circulation of OBH rats, and that RA had an inhibitory effect on this pro-inflammatory marker. Treatment with RA attenuated the levels of IL-18R1, MYD88, IRARK4, p-IKKα and p-NF-κB proteins and improved the injury and inflammatory response of renal tubules both in vivo and in vitro. The same effect was also observed in NRK-52E cells stimulated with RA-treated rat serum. In vitro, further results revealed that the inhibitory effects of RA on the MYD88/IRAK4/NF-κB pathway and inflammatory injury in MRK-52E cells were blocked in the presence of IL-18R1 overexpression, but were enhanced in the presence of IL-18 neutralizing antibodies. In conclusion, RA alleviates renal tubular injury in OBH rats by inhibiting IL-18-mediated activation of IL-18R1/MYD88/IRAK4 pathway, thereby delaying the progression of OBH-induced kidney disease.

articles.title: Association between Socioeconomic Deprivation and Clinical Outcomes of Glucagon-Like Peptide-1 Receptor Agonists in Heart Failure.
articles.abstract: The impact of socioeconomic deprivation on the effectiveness and safety of glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists (GLP-1RAs) in heart failure (HF) remains unclear. We evaluated GLP-1RA-associated outcomes across socioeconomic strata and quantified residual disparities among GLP-1RA users. Using the TriNetX Global Network (2020-2024), adults with HF initiating GLP-1RA therapy were categorized as socioeconomically deprived or non-deprived. Cohorts were 1:1 propensity-score matched within each stratum, enabling three comparisons: GLP-1RA users vs non-users in deprived patients, GLP-1RA users vs non-users in non-deprived patients, and deprived vs non-deprived among GLP-1RA users. Cox models estimated adjusted hazard ratios (aHRs) for 12-month mortality and hospitalization outcomes. Among deprived patients, GLP-1RA users (n=22,585) were compared with non-users (n=194,967); among non-deprived patients, users (n=116,439) were compared with non-users (n=2,254,050). In a direct comparison restricted to GLP-1RA users, deprived (n=21,171) and non-deprived (n=104,887) patients were analyzed. GLP-1RA therapy was associated with similar relative reductions in all-cause mortality or hospitalization in deprived (aHR 0.68, 95% CI 0.66-0.70) and non-deprived patients (aHR 0.68, 95% CI 0.67-0.69). However, deprived users had worse outcomes than non-deprived users (35.5% vs 27.1%; aHR 1.50, 95% CI 1.44-1.55), driven by higher hospitalization (aHR 1.53, 95% CI 1.48-1.58) and mortality (aHR 1.13, 95% CI 1.02-1.24). HF exacerbation (aHR 1.11) and ischemic stroke (aHR 1.16) were also increased. GLP-1RA use was associated with similar relative reductions in adverse outcomes across socioeconomic groups; however, socioeconomically deprived patients continued to experience higher absolute event rates, likely reflecting persistent baseline disparities and residual risk.

articles.title: Long-lasting survival, migration and functional maturation of transplanted human reprogrammed neurons in vivo.
articles.abstract: Direct reprogramming of glial progenitor cells (GPCs) into induced neurons (iNs) represents a promising strategy for future brain regenerative therapies. This approach uses forced expression of neuronal fate-determining genes to convert non-neuronal cells into neurons, bypassing a pluripotent intermediate stage and enabling potential in vivo applications. However, evidence for long-term survival and maturation of human reprogrammed neurons in vivo remains limited. Here, we present a longitudinal in vivo analysis of human iNs following transplantation into the immunodeficient mouse cortex. Using 3D cultures of reprogrammed human iNs to enhance graft survival, we demonstrate survival of human iNs for up to 5 months post-transplantation with a proportion of cells remaining up to 10 months. The transplanted cells exhibit widespread migration from the grafted core into anatomically connected brain regions and protracted neuronal maturation, reflected by increased cellular complexity and expression of neuronal markers. Functional analyses reveal gradual electrophysiological maturation and the establishment of afferent synaptic connectivity with host circuits. Importantly, non-reprogrammed GPC grafts retain their glial identity. Together, these findings provide in vivo evidence for long-term survival, neuronal maturation and long-range migration in the intact mouse brain, supporting their potential for future cell repair strategies.

articles.title: Modeling internalizing symptoms and substance use comorbidity using causal network methodology.
articles.abstract: The cooccurrence of internalizing and substance use disorders can be explained from several perspectives, yet most are modeled in isolation and limited to correlational evidence. Advancements on two common etiological perspectives - i) internalizing symptoms predisposing toward substance use disorder symptoms, ii) transdiagnostic factors predisposing toward both symptom domains - are therefore hampered by scarce multivariate and causal evidence. The present study addressed this gap by modeling direct (causal) links from internalizing symptoms to substance use behaviors and (causal) links to the transdiagnostic factors cognitive control, locus of control (LOC), and meaning in life. We analyzed data from wave 7 (2019-2023; N = 1725), the 15-year follow-up of the ongoing longitudinal cohort study the Netherlands Study of Depression and Anxiety, using a correlational network and a causal network based on the fast causal inference algorithm. The correlational network showed that depression and social anxiety symptoms were positively related to alcohol-related problems and negatively related to alcohol consumption. Cognitive control and external LOC correlated positively with alcohol consumption. Meaning in life was negatively associated with depression and social anxiety symptoms, alcohol consumption, alcohol problems, and drug use. The causal network showed causal relations of external LOC to depression and social anxiety symptoms. Although our correlational findings gave some support to both perspectives on internalizing and substance use comorbidity, the present findings do not support a causal, etiological interpretation of these perspectives.

articles.title: Consensus on components of psychological treatment for depression to reduce symptoms and target relapse risk factors in young adults: A modified Delphi study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Depression is increasingly prevalent in young adults and relapse is common. This study aimed to obtain consensus on Cognitive Behavioural Therapy (CBT)-based treatment components considered important by experts for reducing symptoms and targeting relapse risk factors in young adults (18-25 years).

METHODS: We conducted a modified-Delphi study of three survey rounds, two panels and a consensus meeting. Academics/clinicians (n = 46) and young adult experts-by-experience (n = 24) rated treatment components, therapist competencies, relapse risk factors and interventions, content of relapse-prevention sessions, and post-treatment relapse-prevention strategies. Items were rated on 1-9 Likert scales. "Consensus-important" was defined as ≥70% of either panel rating the item 7-9 and ≤15% rating 1-3.

RESULTS: Behavioural experiments were the highest-rated CBT component in both panels, though the target differed. The Academic/Clinician panel rated experiments targeting negative automatic thoughts highest (97%, n = 30) while the Young Adult panel rated those targeting rumination highest (71%, n = 24). Social isolation/loneliness, stress in relationships and cognitive biases were the top-rated relapse risk factors pooled across both panels. Identifying and challenging negative automatic thoughts, problem solving and behavioural activation often reached consensus as important to target relapse risk factors. Consensus was reached on the content of relapse prevention session(s) with identifying triggers rated most highly by both panels.

CONCLUSIONS: The findings identify stakeholder-endorsed candidate treatment components for co-design and prospective evaluation of feasibility, effectiveness and relapse risk reduction. A modular approach may be beneficial, including core CBT components and modules targeting relapse risk factors such as social isolation/loneliness, interpersonal stress, cognitive biases, sleep and rumination.

REGISTRATION: Open Science Framework (https://osf.io/gu7tm; DOI 10.17605/OSF.IO/GU7TM).

articles.title: Impact of metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease on the development of hepatocellular carcinoma after HCV cure.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION AND OBJECTIVES: The impact of metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD) on hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) development after hepatitis C virus (HCV) elimination remains incompletely understood. This study aimed to clarify this association in a cohort of patients stratified by fibrosis severity.

PATIENTS AND METHODS: We analyzed the data of 2596 eligible patients obtained from a multicenter database between 2014 and 2025. The FIB-4 index was used to assess fibrosis status, with patients categorized into three groups: <1.45, 1.45-3.25, and >3.25. Cox proportional hazards and Fine-Gray subdistribution hazards models were used to evaluate factors independently associated with HCC development.

RESULTS: The median follow-up duration was 6.7 years. MASLD was present in 975 patients (36.3%) and was more frequent among men and patients with diabetes. During follow-up, 156 patients (6.0%) developed de novo HCC. Patients with MASLD had a higher cumulative incidence of HCC than those without MASLD (log-rank test, P<0.001); however, no HCC occurred in patients with FIB-4<1.45. MASLD was associated with HCC development in multivariable analysis of the overall cohort and in patients with FIB-4 1.45-3.25 and >3.25. Older age, male sex, lower albumin level, and higher AFP level at post-treatment week 12 were also independently associated with HCC development, whereas individual cardiometabolic risk factors were not significant after adjustment.

CONCLUSIONS: MASLD was significantly associated with an increased risk of HCC after HCV cure, even among patients with intermediate FIB-4 values of 1.45-3.25. These findings support the need for tailored surveillance and management strategies.

articles.title: Weight changes differentially impact MASLD incidence, progression and outcomes based on genetic and metabolic risk profiles.
articles.journal: Clinical gastroenterology and hepatology : the official clinical practice journal of the American Gastroenterological Association
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND & AIMS: Metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD) comprises heterogeneous subgroups with liver- vs. cardiovascular-related adverse outcomes. Weight management is crucial in MASLD prevention and treatment, but its effect on MASLD subgroups is unclear.

METHODS: We assessed the impact of body weight dynamics on incident MASLD, steatosis resolution, fibrosis risk regression and related cardiovascular diseases (CVD) from the UK biobank. Genetic subgroups (i.e., hepatic and systemic) were defined by polygenic risk scores, a metabolic risk group by lipid accumulation product. A Cox proportional model evaluated impacts across the general population and sex-stratified subgroups.

RESULTS: Among 11,882 participants without MASLD, 1,350 developed MASLD during a median follow-up of 4 years. Each 1% reduction in body weight was associated with a 10% lower risk of MASLD (HR = 0.90 [0.89-0.91]). Among 6,013 participants with MASLD, 753 achieved MASLD resolution; each 1% weight reduction was associated with a 9% higher rate of resolution (HR = 1.09 [1.08-1.10]). Weight loss was also associated with a lower risk of MASLD-related CVD (HR = 0.98 [0.97-0.99]). Recommended weight loss for MASLD prevention (male/female) differed across hepatic (8.7%/13.1%), systemic (8.0%/11.8%), and metabolic-risk (10.9%/14.4%) groups. Estimated lower weight-loss thresholds associated with MASLD resolution were 5.3%/13.3% in hepatic-risk, 10.2%/10.7% in systemic-risk, and 5.7%/5.8% in metabolic-risk participants (male/female). For fibrosis-risk regression, no robust threshold was identified in hepatic-risk participants, but 7.7%/5.6% in metabolic-risk participants (male/female).

CONCLUSION: Individualized weight management should be recommended according to the genetic and metabolic risk profiles of individuals.

articles.title: Immunoactive alginate-eugenol microbeads driving synchronized drug delivery and host immune reprogramming in Aeromonas hydrophila-challenged Nile tilapia.
articles.abstract: Nanotechnology-driven feed additives provide an effective approach to enhance aquaculture sustainability through the improved delivery and bioavailability of bioactive compounds. This study aimed to formulate eugenol-loaded sodium alginate beads (E-SABs) as a biopolymer-mediated sustained-delivery system and to evaluate their effects on growth performance, antioxidant and immune status, and resistance to Aeromonas hydrophila infection in Nile tilapia (Oreochromis niloticus). The formulated E-SABs had a mean particle (Z-average) diameter of 79.66 nm, a polydispersity index of 0.413 and a zeta potential of -9.18 mV, and released eugenol in a sustained manner in vitro (20-25% burst release within 2 h, reaching 96% cumulative release at 24 h; Korsmeyer-Peppas model, R2 = 0.999, release exponent n = 0.69, indicating non-Fickian diffusion). Juvenile Nile tilapia (initial weight approximately 20-100 g; n = 100) were randomly allotted to four dietary groups (a basal-diet control and E-SABs at 0.25, 0.50 and 1.0 mg kg-1 feed) and fed for 30 days. Final body weight, specific growth rate and survival were significantly higher, and feed conversion ratio significantly lower, in all E-SAB groups than in the control (P < 0.05), with the greatest improvement at 1.0 mg kg-1 (e.g., final weight 69.90 ± 0.45 g vs. 59.20 ± 0.52 g; survival 98.8 ± 0.85% vs. 90.0 ± 1.5% in the control). E-SAB-fed fish also showed higher serum total protein, albumin and globulin, and lower AST, ALT, ALP, cholesterol and glucose, than the control (P < 0.05). Innate immunity was enhanced, with dose-dependent increases in phagocytic activity and phagocytic index, lysozyme activity and serum IgM (P < 0.05), together with higher activities of the antioxidant enzymes SOD, CAT and GPx and lower malondialdehyde levels (P < 0.05). These physiological changes were paralleled by up-regulation of genes governing somatic growth (GH, IGF-1 and IGF1-R), immune signalling (IL-1β and IL-8) and antioxidant defence (SOD, CAT and GPx). Following experimental A. hydrophila challenge, cumulative survival at day 15 was significantly higher in E-SAB-fed fish (60-85%, dose-dependent) than in the control (30%) (P < 0.05). Collectively, these findings establish alginate-eugenol microbeads as an effective biomacromolecular delivery platform that couples sustained release with immunomodulation, and support the dietary inclusion of E-SABs, particularly at 1.0 mg kg-1 feed, as a practical, antibiotic-free strategy for improving growth, immune competence and disease resilience in Nile tilapia aquaculture; further evaluation under commercial farm conditions is recommended.

articles.title: 3-Indoleacetonitrile inhibits Singapore grouper iridovirus via dual mechanisms: direct interference with viral life cycle and activation of IRF3-mediated type I interferon response.
articles.abstract: Singapore grouper iridovirus (SGIV) causes severe systemic infections and high mortality in farmed groupers, leading to substantial economic losses. Natural products with immunomodulatory properties have emerged as promising eco-friendly alternatives for antiviral prevention and control in aquaculture. In this study, the antiviral activity and underlying mechanisms of 3-indoleacetonitrile against SGIV were investigated in grouper spleen (GS) cells and in hybrid grouper. The results showed that 3-indoleacetonitrile exhibited no cytotoxicity at concentrations up to 62.5 μg/mL in GS cells, and significantly inhibited SGIV replication in a dose-dependent manner. Further mechanistic studies revealed that 3-indoleacetonitrile targeted multiple steps of SGIV infection by reducing viral particle infectivity, disrupting viral attachment and entry, and inhibiting intracellular viral replication. Furthermore, 3-indoleacetonitrile alone strongly induced the expression of type I interferon (IFN) and interferon-stimulated genes (ISG15 and MXI), and promoted the nuclear translocation of interferon regulatory factor 3 (IRF3). Notably, 3-indoleacetonitrile also enhanced the IFN response triggered by SGIV infection. In vivo, 3-indoleacetonitrile pretreatment significantly reduced SGIV load in grouper liver and spleen. Overall, these findings demonstrate that 3-indoleacetonitrile inhibits SGIV infection through both direct antiviral action and activation of the IRF3-mediated type I IFN pathway, suggesting its potential as a natural candidate for the prevention and control of grouper iridovirus disease. To our knowledge, this is the first report describing the antiviral efficacy of 3-indoleacetonitrile against the aquatic ranavirus SGIV.

articles.title: Hematology-centered characterization of systemic host responses and atypical circulating cells during Aeromonas salmonicida subsp. salmonicida infection in mandarin fish (Siniperca scherzeri).
articles.abstract: Aeromonas salmonicida subsp. salmonicida is an important bacterial pathogen causing systemic disease in cultured fish, but the associated hematological responses remain poorly understood. This study characterized temporal host responses following experimental infection in mandarin fish (Siniperca scherzeri) using a hematology-centered approach integrating complete blood count, blood biochemistry, leukocyte morphology, and comparative immune gene expression in peripheral blood and kidney. Experimental infection caused approximately 60% cumulative mortality. Conventional leukocyte parameters remained largely unchanged, whereas platelet counts increased approximately sixfold at 2 days post-infection (dpi). Circulating triglyceride levels progressively declined by approximately 68% and represented the highest-ranked variable in multivariate analyses. Peripheral blood smears revealed marked leukocyte remodeling characterized by vacuolization, nuclear abnormalities, and cytoplasmic disruption. Most notably, atypical circulating leukocyte-like cells transiently emerged at 4-6 dpi and were classified into three distinct morphological phenotypes. Immune gene expression analyses revealed compartment-specific responses, with most immune-related genes peaking at 3 dpi in peripheral blood, whereas delayed but sustained activation occurred in the kidney, where IL6 expression increased up to 67-fold at 8 dpi. These findings demonstrate coordinated yet compartment-specific hematological, metabolic, molecular, and cytological responses despite relatively limited alterations in conventional hematological parameters. This study establishes a hematology-centered disease trajectory for A. salmonicida subsp. salmonicida infection and highlights the value of integrated blood-based profiling for characterizing distinct host responses during bacterial disease progression.

articles.title: Domain-aligned self-supervision: CT-specialized DINOv3 enhances PET/CT tumor segmentation.
articles.abstract: This study investigates how domain-aligned self-supervised pretraining influences downstream PET/CT tumor segmentation, with a focus on disentangling the roles of domain proximity and pretraining dataset scale.Approach: We compared nnU-Net segmentation models initialized from random weights or from DINOv3 encoders pretrained on natural images, X-ray mammography, CT, or PET, using datasets of different sizes. To disentangle the effects of pretraining domain and dataset size, CT-DINOv3 encoders were pretrained using different numbers of 2D CT slices, including subsets matched in size to the pretraining datasets from other domains. Models were evaluated on two PET/CT benchmarks, autoPET (whole-body, FDG/PSMA) and HECKTOR (head-and-neck primary tumors and metastatic lymph nodes), using five-fold cross-validation with frozen encoders.Main results: CT-pretrained models achieved the highest Dice scores for lymph nodes, FDG lesions, and PSMA lesions. For primary tumors, PET pretraining produced the highest observed Dice score, followed by CT pretraining, suggesting the potential benefit of in-domain representations when PET data are sufficient. Notably, PET pretraining exceeded CT pretraining using equally sized datasets for PSMA but remained below models pretrained on larger CT datasets for both PSMA and FDG targets. In contrast, natural-image pretraining did not outperform from-scratch training despite its much larger pretraining scale, indicating that scale alone is insufficient when domain proximity is low. Across comparisons, strong transfer reflected the combination of domain proximity and sufficient pretraining scale, especially for CT-based models with broad data availability.Significance: These results demonstrate that both domain proximity and dataset scale jointly determine the effectiveness of self-supervised pretraining. While higher domain alignment improves performance at comparable scale, sufficient data is required to realize this benefit. CT-based pretraining provides a favorable balance between domain relevance and data availability, leading to robust performance across tasks. This study provides practical guidance for selecting pretraining strategies in PET/CT segmentation.

articles.title: Predictors of carbapenem-resistant Enterobacterales enteric colonization among patients admitted to a companion animal intensive care unit.
articles.journal: Journal of the American Veterinary Medical Association
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To estimate prevalence and identify factors associated with carbapenem-resistant Enterobacterales (CRE) enteric colonization in companion animals admitted to an ICU.

METHODS: The study population included canine and feline patients admitted to The Ohio State University Veterinary Medical Center ICU between January 2024 and June 2025. In total, 5,552 rectal swabs were collected from 3,834 patients during routine screening. A retrospective case-control study included all CRE-positive patients (n = 61) and randomly selected CRE-negative controls (137). Cases were defined as ICU patients with at least 1 positive CRE fecal culture during hospitalization, whereas controls had no positive CRE fecal cultures during their hospitalization.

RESULTS: Prevalence of CRE colonization was 1.59% (61 of 3,834 patients; 95% CI, 1.24% to 2.04%). Escherichia coli carrying blaNDM was the most frequently identified isolate, accounting for 78.7% (48 of 61 patients; 95% CI, 66.9% to 87.1%). Predictors of CRE colonization included increased comorbidity burden (unit OR, 1.96; 95% CI, 1.43 to 2.75), intact reproductive status (OR, 4.39; CI, 1.47 to 11.03), longer hospitalization (unit OR, 1.31; CI, 1.14 to 1.53), recent surgery (OR, 2.72; CI, 1.29 to 5.87), and antimicrobial use within the previous 3 months (OR, 2.71; CI, 1.23 to 6.07).

CONCLUSIONS: These predictors suggest targets for infection prevention and control measures to protect patients and staff. The association between recent antimicrobial exposure and CRE colonization reinforces the importance of antimicrobial stewardship in veterinary medicine.

CLINICAL RELEVANCE: Although uncommon, CRE-colonized patients can serve as reservoirs for transmission and are at risk of subsequent infection.

articles.title: Role of the urobiome in urinary tract infections: current knowledge and research prospects.
articles.abstract: Urinary tract infections (UTIs), particularly cystitis, are among the most common bacterial infections worldwide, with a disproportionate burden on adult female individuals, who often have recurrence. The discovery of the urobiome, a low microbial biomass community in the urinary tract, has transformed our understanding of UTI pathogenesis and infection susceptibility. Experimental and omics approaches provide insights into the taxonomic and functional complexity of the urobiome, highlighting the importance of microbial metabolites, ecological interactions, and host-microbe dynamics. Polymicrobial interactions within the urobiome further modulate pathogenicity, with some microbes inhibiting or promoting uropathobionts. Advancing UTI management will require combining omics and experimental research with ecological and evolutionary insights. This approach can enable the development of personalised, non-antibiotic interventions, such as live biotherapeutics and prebiotics, to improve diagnostics, reduce antibiotic resistance, and enhance treatment efficacy.

articles.title: The future of cholera genomics through the lens of clinical, public health, and research practitioners in Africa.
articles.abstract: Cholera remains a persistent public health threat, complicating efforts to track transmission across borders and undermining control measures. Surveillance systems often remain fragmented and reactive, and many aspects of Vibrio cholerae evolution continue to be challenging, restricting the development of effective, data-driven interventions. Although genomics is increasingly transforming our understanding of cholera by revealing new insights into pathogen biology, transmission dynamics, and evolution, its routine integration into public health practice remains low. In this Personal View, we present the perspectives of those working at the frontline of cholera control in Africa (clinicians, public health practitioners, and researchers) who are rarely heard from, yet who actively shape strategies, navigate technological hurdles, and address system-level challenges to incorporate genomics into routine practice. These insights emerged through the Vibriowatch and Cholera Genomics Course, funded by the Gates Foundation and hosted by the Centre for Infectious Disease Research in Zambia in Lusaka, Zambia, on Feb 9-14, 2025. The course convened 36 participants from 18 African countries to exchange practical experience on how genomic data can be translated into public health decision making. A key outcome of this convening was the establishment of the Community of Practice for Cholera Genomics, which has since evolved into a sustained and structured platform for collaboration, peer learning, and collective problem solving, bringing together practitioners working across cholera surveillance, genomics, and response systems, ensuring that genomic approaches are grounded in local realities and appropriately embedded within cholera-control approaches. The thematic workstreams of the Community of Practice for Cholera Genomics meet regularly to deliver defined technical priorities, with seminar sessions bringing the whole community together to review progress, align priorities, and engage external experts. Accountability is embedded through shared ownership of workplans within each thematic team, with members jointly responsible for tracking progress. Grounded in real-world experience, in this Personal View, we offer timely, policy-relevant recommendations to strengthen genomic approaches, centring African leadership, equity, and long-term sustainability.

articles.title: Lymphatic constraint of germinal centers optimizes protective antibody responses.
articles.abstract: Immunization strategies are central to pathogen control, where efficacy relies on antigen distribution and inflammatory context. Lymphatic vessels are necessary conduits for antigen transport that actively remodel in peripheral tissues and draining lymph nodes (LNs) in response to their inflammatory context. In this study, we found that inhibiting viral-induced lymphatic remodeling in skin and LNs prompted germinal center (GC) expansion but, paradoxically, decreased the protective antibody response. While GCs scaled proportionately, larger GCs failed to support proliferative bursts consistent with clonal selection due to impaired T-B cell interactions. Accordingly, follicle and GC size are evolutionarily conserved across diverse mammals despite increased LN size. Lymphatic vessels controlled GC size through two coordinated processes: lymphatic remodeling in infected skin limited viral transport to the LN, while the resulting permissive environment in the LN supported perifollicular lymphangiogenesis that constrained GC expansion.

articles.title: Mapping transcriptional responses to cellular perturbations with RNA fingerprinting.
articles.abstract: Single-cell perturbation dictionaries measure how cells respond to genetic and chemical perturbations, creating the opportunity to assign causal interpretations to observational data. We introduce RNA fingerprinting, a statistical framework that maps transcriptional responses from new experiments onto reference perturbation dictionaries. RNA fingerprinting learns perturbation representations, or "fingerprints," from single-cell data, then probabilistically assigns query cells to one or more candidate perturbations. We benchmark on ground-truth datasets, demonstrating accurate assignments at single-cell resolution, scalability to genome-wide screens, and the ability to resolve combinatorial perturbations. We demonstrate broad utility across diverse biological settings: identifying context-specific regulators of p53 under ribosomal stress, characterizing dose-dependent drug mechanisms of action, and uncovering cytokine-driven B cell heterogeneity during secondary influenza infection in vivo. Together, these results establish RNA fingerprinting as a versatile framework for interpreting single-cell datasets by linking cellular states to their underlying perturbations.

articles.title: Headless Compression Screws May Reduce Symptomatic Hardware After Medial Malleolus Fixation: A Comparative Cohort Study.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: To compare rates of medial-sided symptomatic hardware, hardware removal, and fracture union following medial malleolus fixation using partially threaded, headless compression screws versus traditional partially threaded, headed screws.

METHODS: Design: Retrospective cohort.

SETTING: Single, academic, Level I trauma center.

PATIENT SELECTION CRITERIA: Skeletally mature patients who underwent operative fixation of a medial malleolus fracture [OTA/AO 44A-C] between 2021 and 2025 and had a minimum of 3 months follow-up were included.

OUTCOME MEASURES AND COMPARISONS: Demographics, injury characteristics, and surgical management was collected for the headless and headed screw cohort. The primary outcome was medial-sided symptomatic hardware. Secondary outcomes included removal of hardware from the medial malleolus, medial malleolus fracture union, and infection of the medial aspect of the ankle. A comparison between the medial malleolus screw type used was undertaken.

RESULTS: Of 306 patients, 195 (63.7%) received headed screws (mean age 56.0 years, range 18-92; 72.3% female; mean follow-up 15.1 months) and 111 (36.3%) received headless compression screws (mean age 51.0 years, range 18-95; 58.6% female; mean follow-up 13.2 months). Symptomatic hardware occurred in 34.8% of patients in the headed screw group compared with 20.7% in the headless screw group (p = 0.01), corresponding to an absolute risk reduction of 14.1%. Hardware removal rates did not differ between groups (30.8% vs 23.4%, p = 0.17). There were no differences in nonunion (3.6% vs 3.6%, p = 0.99) or infection rates (4.6% vs 5.4%, p = 0.97). On multivariable analysis, headless screw fixation was independently associated with a decreased likelihood of symptomatic hardware (odds ratio 0.55, 95% CI 0.32-0.96, p = 0.04). No independent association was observed between screw type and hardware removal.

CONCLUSIONS: Headless compression screws may be associated with a lower rate of symptomatic hardware at a mean of one year following medial malleolus fixation without compromising fracture healing or increasing infection risk. The lower observed incidence of symptomatic implants may suggest a clinically meaningful benefit of implant selection in this subcutaneous anatomic region.

LEVEL OF EVIDENCE: Level III, retrospective cohort study.

articles.title: Left Ventricular Structural, Physiological, and Transcriptomic Abnormalities in a Novel Porcine Hypertrophic Cardiomyopathy Model.
articles.abstract: Hypertrophic cardiomyopathy (HCM) is a disease of heart muscle commonly caused by variants in genes encoding sarcomere-associated proteins. The mechanisms by which these variants lead to the phenotype are uncertain, partly because of the lack of model systems amenable to integrated translational studies. We generated Yucatan minipigs with heterozygous knockin of the human HCM R403Q variant in MYH7. MYH7 R403Q pigs exhibited hypertrophy similar to humans on cardiac imaging. Relative to wild-type, MYH7 R403Q pigs showed increased interstitial fibrosis, increased myocyte disarray, lower capillary density, and intimal hyperplasia of intramyocardial arterioles with decreased luminal diameters. Bulk RNA sequencing and single nuclear RNA sequencing analyses showed upregulation of profibrotic and proinflammatory pathways. MYH7 R403Q hearts showed hypercontractility, elevated end-diastolic pressures, blunted β-adrenergic enhancement of systolic and diastolic function, and increased Ca2+ sensitivity. The cardiac myosin inhibitor MYK-581 reduced hypercontractility and improved diastolic function. Data from this large animal genetic model of HCM strengthen the mechanistic link between genetic variants and in vivo phenotypes and elucidate the mechanisms of myofilament-targeted therapies.

articles.title: Identifying Cardiac Autoantibody Biomarkers that Predict the Severity of Chagas Cardiomyopathy.
articles.abstract: Chagas cardiomyopathy (ChCM) affects up to 30% of patients with chronic Chagas disease and lacks reliable biomarkers for severity and conduction abnormalities. We profiled cardiac autoantibodies using 2-dimensional gel electrophoresis and mass spectrometry, followed by enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay validation and machine learning analysis. Six autoantibodies linked to glycolysis, adenosine triphosphate metabolism, and sarcomere structure distinguished ChCM stages (area under the curve: 0.87; 95% CI: 0.777-0.977) and a mean classification accuracy (0.84; 95% CI: 0.705-0.935). These findings suggest that an antibody-based panel may enable cost-effective risk stratification and prognostication in ChCM, with prospective validation before clinical application.

articles.title: Identification of recycled PET fibers using TMAH-assisted reactive pyrolysis-GC/MS and machine learning.
articles.abstract: Recycled poly(ethylene terephthalate) (rPET) is increasingly used in polyester fibers, but reliable molecular-level identification remains challenging because chemical differences between virgin poly(ethylene terephthalate) (vPET) and rPET are often weak and distributed across multiple trace features. In this study, a tetramethylammonium hydroxide (TMAH)-assisted reactive pyrolysis-gas chromatography/mass spectrometry (Py-GC/MS) workflow coupled with machine learning was developed to distinguish rPET from vPET fibers. Poly(ethylene terephthalate) (PET) fiber samples were analyzed by full-scan TMAH-assisted Py-GC/MS, and peak-level features were extracted using MS-DIAL software. To reduce the influence of background peaks and unstable integrations, candidate variables were selected within the training set using partial least squares-discriminant analysis (PLS-DA) variable importance in projection (VIP) ranking and were further curated by manual inspection of peak shape, retention behavior, quantifier ions, and electron ionization (EI) mass spectra. Six classifiers, including LDA, RF, SVM, XGBoost, ElasticNet, and a lightweight neural network, were compared using repeated cross-validation.
