A pre-specified secondary analysis evaluated an expanded composite endpoint including all-cause death, heart failure hospitalisation, or tricuspid valve intervention (TVI). A subgroup of 50 patients underwent repeat CMR after TVI.

RESULTS: During follow-up, 106 patients (37%) reached the primary endpoint. Both the Vol RV-PA Coupling Index and effective RVEF were independently associated with the primary endpoint and significantly improved risk discrimination beyond conventional RVEF (Δ Harrell's C-index 0.056 and 0.043, respectively; both p < 0.01). Similar findings were observed for the expanded composite endpoint. Following TVI, both indices improved significantly and were associated with mortality during post-intervention follow-up.

CONCLUSIONS: Vol RV-PA Coupling Index and effective RVEF are complementary CMR-derived markers of RV performance that provide incremental prognostic information beyond conventional RVEF in patients with severe TR. Their improvement after TVI further supports their potential role for longitudinal assessment of RV performance.

articles.title: CS-MORT-6: A mortality score that refines risk within EHR-derived SCAI stages in cardiogenic shock.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Cardiogenic shock carries high in-hospital mortality, and the ordinal SCAI classification does not rank risk within a stage. Existing scores generally require imaging, procedural, or support-dependent data.

METHODS: We identified 3103 adults with documented cardiogenic shock in MIMIC-IV. Six predictors (lactate, urine output, cardiac arrest, age, blood urea nitrogen, red cell distribution width) were selected by bootstrap LASSO screening and clinical review. CS-MORT-6 was derived as two continuous ridge logistic models (lactate or anion gap) fitted at a 24-h landmark and a 0-to-15-point integer score. The primary outcome was subsequent in-hospital death among patients alive in the ICU at the landmark (n = 2694; 892 deaths). The models were externally validated in 1047 patients from 117 eICU hospitals.

RESULTS: The integer score's AUROC was 0.727 (95% CI, 0.706-0.747) on cross-validation and 0.759 (0.729-0.790) externally; corresponding values were 0.734 and 0.759 (lactate model) and 0.726 and 0.748 (anion-gap model). Externally, the integer score over-predicted on average (calibration-in-the-large -0.22, slope 1.15). Within EHR-derived SCAI stages, mortality differed by 20 to 47 percentage points between the lowest and highest score tertiles in MIMIC-IV, with a similar pattern in eICU. Adding the anion-gap model to stage increased apparent AUROC by 0.139 (0.116-0.162) in MIMIC-IV and 0.141 (0.101-0.178) in eICU. Compared with BOS,MA2 (654 eICU patients scorable by both), the anion-gap model's AUROC difference was 0.004 (-0.039 to 0.046).

CONCLUSIONS: At 24 h, CS-MORT-6 distinguished mortality risk within EHR-derived SCAI stages and retained moderate discrimination externally. Repeated scoring and real-time performance require prospective evaluation.

articles.title: Technology-Supported Solutions to Improve Guideline-Informed Care for Kidney Disease: Conclusions from a Kidney Disease: Improving Global Outcomes (KDIGO) Controversies Conference.
articles.abstract: Implementation of guideline-informed care for the prevention, detection, and management of kidney disease remains suboptimal throughout the world. In November 2025, Kidney Disease: Improving Global Outcomes (KDIGO) held a Controversies Conference on the role of technology-supported solutions to improve guideline-informed care for people with or at risk for kidney disease and to identify priorities for research. There have been rapid advances in various technologies for earlier identification of people with kidney disease; risk stratification for adverse kidney, cardiovascular, and other clinical and patient-centered outcomes; and promotion of guideline-informed therapies, monitoring, and patient self-management. Still, there remain important considerations for how to optimize the use of such technologies for achieving care that is integrated, personalized, safe, and guideline-informed. The conference identified a range of lived experience, clinician, health care system, health policy, and technology-level factors that can influence the effectiveness of technology-supported solutions in improving guideline-informed care. Research priorities included developing and maintaining living guidelines; harmonizing and integrating guideline recommendations into clinical decision support solutions; generating evidence on the effectiveness and safety of technology-supported solutions that reduce disparities and preserve trust; developing and evaluating efforts that promote interoperability, feasibility and scalability of technologies across health care systems; developing more effective public-private partnerships and systematic use of validated health technology assessments; and clarifying the incremental value of emerging technologies involving sensor-derived biomarkers and integrated multimodal data. Strategies to optimize digital health technologies for promoting guideline-informed care were also delineated.

articles.title: Back to the back wall: An issue with target, technique or patient selection?
Does it Fit? Testing a Novel Pediatric Surgical Risk Calculator in Africa.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Low- and middle-income countries (LMICs), particularly Sub-Saharan Africa, experience a high burden of surgical disease and a disproportionately high postoperative morbidity and mortality. Although machine learning based pediatric surgical risk calculators (SRCs) have been developed to support clinical decision making, most are derived from high-income settings and may not generalize well to LMIC populations. We previously developed a pediatric surgical risk calculator using multinational LMIC data; however, its performance in independent African cohorts remains unknown.

METHODS: We conducted an external validation study of a previously developed pediatric surgical risk calculator using prospective data from children undergoing surgery at four tertiary referral hospitals in Ethiopia and Nigeria between July 2024 and February 2025. Model performance was assessed by evaluating discrimination (area under the receiver operating characteristic curve) and calibration (slope and intercept). Predicted risk was stratified into low, intermediate, and high-risk categories to enhance clinical applicability. Model recalibration was performed to optimize performance in the external cohort.

RESULTS: A total of 1,670 pediatric surgical patients were included from the four hospitals. In-hospital mortality was 6.8%. Mortality varied significantly by site, age, weight, sex, prematurity, preoperative sepsis, transfusion, supplemental oxygen use, antibiotic use, ASA class, type of surgery (emergent vs elective), need of ICU postoperatively and reoperation. The risk prediction model had good discrimination overall with an area under the curve (AUC) of 0.84, outperforming ASA classification alone (AUC = 0.77). Discrimination remained high for general pediatric surgery cases (AUC=0.83) and was highest for emergency cases (AUC = 0.89), but was low in neonates (AUC = 0.64). The model demonstrated systematic miscalibration, which improved following logistic calibration. Patients were stratified into meaningful risk categories, which reliably distinguishes between low-and-hgih risk patients (LR=0.1 and LR=5.4 respectively). However, 66.5% fall in the intermediate risk group which is not useful in decision making (LR=1.0).

CONCLUSION: The pediatric surgical risk calculator demonstrated good performance in the African context, with improved clinical utility following recalibration and risk stratification. Reduced performance in neonates suggests the need to incorporate additional risk factors and potentially separate models for this subgroup. Future efforts should focus on supporting the use of the SRC in risk communication, clinical decision making, and resource prioritization.

articles.title: Single-Stage Versus Staged Repair of Rectovestibular Fistula in Girls: A Systematic Review and Meta-analysis.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: The optimal repair strategy for rectovestibular fistula remains uncertain. We compared single-stage with staged repair and estimated complication and functional-outcome rates across operative techniques.

METHODS: PubMed/MEDLINE, Scopus, and Web of Science were searched from inception through May 20, 2026. Studies of girls with congenital anorectal-malformation-associated rectovestibular fistula undergoing definitive repair were eligible. Random-effects models pooled logit-transformed single-arm proportions and risk ratios (RRs) for direct comparisons. Risk of bias was assessed with design-specific tools and certainty with GRADE. The protocol was prospectively registered in PROSPERO (CRD420261436081).

RESULTS: Twenty-six core studies were included; 25 contributed to meta-analysis. Pooled proportions were 10.1% for wound infection (95% confidence interval [CI], 5.2%-18.7%), 8.1% for anal stenosis/stricture (95% CI, 5.1%-12.5%), 7.4% for rectal or mucosal prolapse (95% CI, 4.7%-11.4%), 3.4% for fistula recurrence (95% CI, 1.4%-8.2%), and 23.0% for constipation among age-eligible children (95% CI, 14.0%-35.3%). Single-stage repair was associated with more wound infection than staged repair (RR, 1.86; 95% CI, 1.10-3.16) and suggested more wound dehiscence/disruption (RR, 2.41; 95% CI, 1.00-5.83). Both comparisons were unadjusted and nonrandomized. No clear differences were found for anal stenosis, constipation, soiling, or voluntary bowel movements. Sensitivity analyses gave consistent results.

CONCLUSIONS: Single-stage repair was associated with a higher reported risk of wound infection, but this unadjusted, nonrandomized association is susceptible to confounding by indication and cannot establish causality; certainty was low. Evidence was insufficient to determine whether staging affects anal stenosis or age-eligible bowel outcomes. Decisions regarding fecal diversion should therefore remain individualized pending prospective comparative evidence.

PROSPERO: CRD420261436081.

articles.title: Echocardiographic changes in hyperthyroid cats: comparison of subclinical disease and congestive heart failure.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Hyperthyroidism induces a wide spectrum of cardiovascular changes in cats, yet the factors distinguishing subclinical cardiac involvement from congestive heart failure (CHF) remain poorly defined. Previous studies have focused primarily on structural changes, with limited evaluation of atrial function or right-sided involvement.

OBJECTIVES: To compare echocardiographic variables between hyperthyroid cats with subclinical cardiac disease and those presenting in CHF, with emphasis on left atrial remodelling, left atrial function, and left ventricular dimensional changes, and right-sided involvement assessed by right atrial diameter. The comparison of clinical and biochemical variables was a secondary objective.

METHODS: A retrospective case-control study was performed using medical records of 51 hyperthyroid cats with subclinical cardiac disease and 47 hyperthyroid cats presenting in CHF. All cats underwent standard echocardiography, serum biochemistry including total thyroxine (TT4). Type of congestion was determined by thoracic radiography or point-of-care ultrasound, and CHF cats were classified as having pulmonary oedema only or pleural/mixed effusion.

RESULTS: Cats with CHF had significantly larger atrial dimensions and increased left ventricular internal diameter compared with subclinical cats. Left atrial dysfunction was the most robust discriminator between groups. Pleural or mixed effusion was the predominant CHF phenotype and, compared with pulmonary oedema alone, was associated with greater right-sided and global volume overload. TT4 concentrations did not differ significantly between cats with and without CHF. Similarly, biochemical variables showed no significant differences between subclinical or CHF cats or between CHF subtypes.

CONCLUSIONS: Atrial remodelling - particularly impaired atrial function and biatrial enlargement - represents the clearest echocardiographic marker of decompensation in hyperthyroid cats. The predominance of pleural or mixed effusion highlights the importance of assessing right-sided cardiac measurements. Comprehensive echocardiographic evaluation is essential for early identification of cats at risk of CHF, whereas TT4 concentration alone does not predict cardiac status.

articles.title: Seven years is not a lifetime: long-term TAVR outcomes in an era of expanding indications.
Chinese expert consensus on botulinum toxin injection for the treatment of disabling spasticity in adults.
articles.journal: Toxicon : official journal of the International Society on Toxinology
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: This expert consensus aims to update current knowledge and techniques and to provide recommendations for key aspects of botulinum toxin (BT) injection in adults with spasticity.

METHODS: A consensus advisory committee consisting of 6 rehabilitation medicine experts, 6 neurology experts, and 1 statistician from the Neurotoxin Branch of the Chinese Neuroscience Society (NTCNS) formulated recommendations, evidence levels, and recommendation strengths with reference to the GRADE approach and drafted a preliminary consensus. The draft was distributed online to members of the NTCNS with clinical experience in spasticity management (n = 38). Information on experts' clinical practice and their agreement with the proposed recommendations was used to form the final consensus. A recommendation was considered to have reached consensus when more than 75% of respondents with a definite opinion agreed or partially agreed; responses of "uncertain" were excluded from the denominator.

RESULTS: Among the 26 recommendations, 1 was supported by GRADE A evidence, 5 by GRADE B evidence, 8 by GRADE C evidence, and 12 by GRADE D evidence. Six recommendations were strong, 14 were weak, and 6 were neutral positions. Thirty-eight experts completed the survey.

CONCLUSIONS: This consensus supports the rational use of BT injection for adult disabling spasticity and provides a decision-making basis for primary care and specialist physicians regarding BT treatment for spasticity caused by different diseases, selection and attainment of treatment goals, common upper- and lower-limb manifestations and injection dose ranges, timing and repetition of BT injection, injection guidance techniques, combined treatment and other treatment options, diagnostic nerve blocks, and cost-effectiveness.

articles.title: Robust Approach to Measure Time-Resolved Septal Curvature in Pediatric Pulmonary Hypertension Patients Using Standard Short-Axis Ventricular Volume Contours: A Retrospective, Cross-Sectional Study.
articles.journal: Journal of cardiovascular magnetic resonance : official journal of the Society for Cardiovascular Magnetic Resonance
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Right heart catheterization is the gold standard for diagnosis and monitoring of pediatric pulmonary hypertension (PH). Noninvasive cardiovascular magnetic resonance (CMR) and echocardiography can additionally provide volumetric and functional assessment of the right ventricle and possibly serve as a non-invasive method for surveillance of PH severity using ventricular septal curvature (SC), interventricular septal (IVS) angle, or eccentricity index (EI). However, these septal wall measurements require manual interaction and can be observer dependent. This study presents the results of a robust, contour-based SC computation and assesses interobserver variability and performance as a candidate marker of RV afterload as compared to manually measured SC, IVS angle and EI.

METHODS: This cross-sectional, retrospective study enrolled PH patients with mixed etiology (idiopathic/heritable and congenital heart/connective tissue disease-associated PH) and similar-age controls who underwent clinical CMR and catheterization (catheterization only for patients). A standard short-axis CMR stack was processed on commercial image-processing software to semi-automatically extract the relevant contours for the endo- and epicardial ventricular walls. SC was computed based on the contours and the minimum value in the cardiac cycle was obtained (SCcontour). For comparison, SC (SCmanu), IVS angle and EI were manually obtained from the CMR images. The relationship between septal wall measurements and invasive pressure measurements by catheterization was evaluated via Spearman correlation. Association with adverse events (death, lung or heart and lung transplant, and Potts surgery) was evaluated via univariate Cox proportional hazard model. Interobserver agreement was analyzed using intraclass correlation coefficient (ICC).

RESULTS: Analysis was performed on 24 patients and 14 controls (median age 16.4 [12.3 - 18.9] and 15.9 [14.7 - 17.4] years respectively). SCcontour demonstrated moderate-strong correlations with RVSP (ρ=-0.79), RVSP/SBP (ρ =-0.65), and mPAP (ρ=-0.80) and had the strongest correlation in idiopathic/heritable PH patients (ρ = -0.74 - -0.83). SCcontour demonstrated a higher ICC (0.96 (95% CI 0.93 - 0.98; p<0.001) versus SCmanu (0.89 (95% CI 0.80 - 0.94; p<0.001)). In the exploratory prognostic analysis, significant associations with adverse events were not observed for any septal wall measurements.

CONCLUSIONS: The contour-based SC approach demonstrated strong correlation with invasive pressure measurements, with less manual interaction and observer dependency than manual measurements.

articles.title: Ion Channel Nano-Diagnostics for ER+ Breast Cancer.
articles.abstract: Ion channels are pore-forming transmembrane proteins that allow ions to move down an electrochemical gradient and across the channel pore and regulate many cell functions. Among them, are the G-protein-gated inwardly-rectifying K+ channels 1 (GIRK1) that are ubiquitously expressed with major functions in the brain and heart. Interestingly, significantly higher GIRK1 expression has been found in estrogen receptor positive (ER+) breast cancer patients compared to patients with HER2+ tumors or normal patients, and that was statistically correlated with shorter survival times and metastatic potential. Herein, we report the preparation of a ∼4 nm GAT1508-coated poly(ethylene glycol) gold nanoparticle (PEGylated AuNP) biomarker for ER+ breast cancer cell screening through an optical microscope. A urea-based small molecule, GAT1508, with an N-methylpyrazole benzyl group on its head and a bromo-thiophene on its tail, has been shown to predominantly bind GIRK1 subunits and specifically activate GIRK1/2 channels. Two derivatives of GAT1508 were synthesized and characterized: an ethylamine derivative (GAT1508-EA) with a chain extension from the benzyl ring, and a propylamine derivative (GAT1508-PA) with a chain extension from the pyrazole ring. Electrophysiology (TEVC and whole-cell patch-clump) experiments as well as fluorescence studies (Thallium assay) showed that only GAT1508-PA inhibited GIRK1/2-mediated K+ currents in transfected HEK293GIRK1 cells. Docking studies showed strong binding for the propylamine GAT1508 derivative, both in the amine form (GAT1508-PA) as well as in the amide form (GAT1508-PA-EG2; coupled with PEG as in the AuNPs). GAT1508-PEG-AuNPs (GAT1508-NPs) were synthesized subsequently with ∼65 wt% metal loading. UV-Vis studies revealed the presence of the conjugated ligand at 260 nm. Flow cytometry studies showed binding of Alexa 594-labeled GAT1508-NPs in ER+ MCF-7 breast cancer cells with a strong interaction, while incubation of fixed MCF-7 cells with a GAT1508-NP solution led to optical detection of ER+ breast cancer cells, without the need of fluorescent dyes and additional amplification steps. Detection was not feasible in MDA-MB-231 cells, a triple (-) breast cell line that does not express GIRK1. This, to our knowledge, is the first study that couples nanotechnology with small molecule drug design and electrophysiology to develop ion channel-tracing molecular probes for the detection/screening of ER+ breast cancer.

articles.title: Reading the Lipid Code: Cooperative Domain Functions in Perilipin Targeting to Lipid Droplets.
articles.abstract: Perilipins (PLINs) are the most abundant proteins coating the phospholipid monolayer of lipid droplets (LDs), regulating their biogenesis, stability, growth, and lipolysis. Most mammalian isoforms (PLIN1-3, PLIN5) share a modular architecture characterized by an N-terminal PAT domain (perilipin-adipophilin-TIP47), a central 11-mer repeat region forming amphipathic helices (hydrophobic and hydrophilic faces on opposite sides of the helix), and a C-terminal 4-helix bundle; PLIN4 is a notable exception that relies mainly on expanded amphipathic helices. In this review, we synthesize recent structural, biophysical, and cell-biological advances and present a working framework in which these domains function cooperatively to read a local lipid code composed of diacylglycerol (DAG) enrichment, phospholipid composition, packing defects, and surface tension. The PAT domain preferentially engages DAG-rich endoplasmic reticulum (ER) subdomains to initiate recruitment and support LD budding. The 11-mer amphipathic helices, often weakly hydrophobic and highly repetitive, especially in PLIN4, recognize lipid packing defects and enable dynamic, tension-responsive binding, with polar residues supporting multimeric assembly and exceptional stability on LD surfaces. The C-terminal 4-helix bundle contains a conserved hydrophobic cleft that can accommodate phosphatidylethanolamine (PE); isolated domains prefer PE-rich interfaces, and PE limitation reduces cellular recruitment. Isoform-specific variations, including PLIN1's integral membrane segment for ER insertion and high-affinity binding, contribute to hierarchical sorting and LD heterogeneity. Together, these cooperative domain functions integrate lipid cues to orchestrate LD assembly and remodeling, with implications for metabolic diseases such as metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease, obesity, and lipodystrophies.

articles.title: Endoscopic treatment of sacrococcygeal pilonidal sinus (EPSIT): results in 104 patients.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Sacrococcygeal pilonidal sinus (PS) is a common condition in young adults, characterised by an inflammatory response due to hair impaction in the gluteal cleft. Optimal treatment remains controversial because of the morbidity and recurrence associated with conventional techniques. The endoscopic EPSIT technique has emerged as a minimally invasive alternative.

OBJECTIVE: To evaluate the recurrence rate of EPSIT and, secondarily, postoperative complications, healing time, and return to daily activities.

MATERIALS AND METHODS: Observational study including 104 patients with primary or recurrent sacrococcygeal pilonidal sinus treated with EPSIT between April 2024 and April 2025. The procedure was performed on an outpatient basis under local anaesthesia and intravenous sedation. Demographic variables, operative time, postoperative pain (VAS), analgesic use, complications, healing time, return to activities, and recurrence were recorded.

RESULTS: Most patients were male (76.9%), with a mean age of 31 years. Primary disease was present in 83 cases and recurrent in 21. Mean operating time was 14.2 minutes, and all patients were discharged within 3 hours. Mild postoperative pain (VAS 1-3) was reported in 89.4% of patients. Mean return to activities was 5 days, and mean healing time was 24 days. One surgical site infection was recorded. The recurrence rate was 9.62%.

CONCLUSIONS: EPSIT is a minimally invasive, reproducible technique associated with low morbidity, minimal pain, and rapid recovery, with an acceptable recurrence rate in selected patients.

articles.title: Advances in precision medicine for the anterior segment: Therapeutic applications using CRISPR-Cas9.
articles.journal: Archivos de la Sociedad Espanola de Oftalmologia
articles.abstract: CRISPR-Cas9 gene editing has emerged as one of the most promising strategies in precision medicine applied to ophthalmology. Although its initial development focused on inherited retinal diseases, recent advances have increasingly targeted anterior segment disorders, including herpetic keratitis, hereditary corneal dystrophies, and genetically associated glaucoma. The ability to modify specific DNA or RNA sequences enables direct intervention in molecular pathways involved in inflammatory, degenerative, and infectious disease progression. This review summarizes the biological basis of CRISPR-Cas systems and discusses the main preclinical and translational findings related to corneal and glaucomatous diseases. Current limitations, including off-target effects, immunogenicity, and challenges associated with molecular delivery into ocular tissues, are also addressed. Available evidence suggests that CRISPR-Cas9 may significantly transform the future management of multiple anterior segment diseases.

articles.title: Optimal Control of an SIR Model with Noncompliance as a Social Contagion.
articles.abstract: We propose and study a compartmental model for epidemiology with human behavioral effects. Specifically, our model incorporates governmental prevention measures aimed at lowering the disease infection rate, but we split the population into those who comply with the measures and those who do not comply and therefore do not receive the reduction in infectivity. We then allow the attitude of noncompliance to spread as a social contagion parallel to the disease. We derive the reproductive ratio for our model and provide stability analysis for the disease-free equilibria. We then propose an optimal control scenario wherein a policy-maker with access to control variables representing disease prevention mandates, treatment efforts, and educational campaigns aimed at encouraging compliance minimizes a cost functional incorporating several cost concerns. Via careful analysis of the control-to-state map, we are able to prove existence of optimal controls. Our proof applies to dynamics which can be nonlinear in the control variables and general cost functionals including the case of L1 control costs. We numerically resolve optimal strategies using the sequential quadratic Hamiltonian method, a relatively new numerical method for optimal control which is easy to implement and admits sufficient-decrease guarantees, as we demonstrate. We test our model in several parameter regimes with specific interest in observing how the policy-maker's optimal strategies depend on their particular preferences which are expressed via design of different cost functionals.

articles.title: An MMP12-Enriched Kupffer Cell-Associated Programme Links ATF3-Associated Immunometabolic Remodeling to Hepatic Metabolic Dysfunction and Fibrotic Communication Networks.
articles.journal: Food and chemical toxicology : an international journal published for the British Industrial Biological Research Association
articles.abstract: Metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD) is a major cause of chronic liver injury, yet the cellular programmes linking metabolic stress with inflammation and fibrosis remain incompletely understood. Here, we integrated single-cell transcriptomics, regulatory network analysis, functional validation, and in vivo perturbation approaches to investigate macrophage-associated mechanisms during metabolic liver injury. We identified an MMP12-enriched Kupffer cell-associated programme that emerges under metabolic stress and exhibits distinct ATF3-associated immunometabolic characteristics. Functional modulation of ATF3 altered macrophage transcriptional states and mitochondrial metabolic properties, supporting its involvement in macrophage adaptation. Intercellular communication analysis combined with experimental validation identified CD93-associated hepatocyte responses and FLRT2-associated hepatic stellate cell activation as candidate pathways linking macrophage states with steatosis and fibrotic remodeling. Hepatic perturbation of these pathways improved metabolic and fibrosis-related phenotypes, while additional analyses defined the interpretation of AAV8-mediated effects at the hepatic pathway level rather than exclusive Kupffer cell specificity. Human liver datasets provided exploratory evidence for conservation of macrophage-associated regulatory programmes. Collectively, our findings reveal an immunometabolic framework connecting macrophage states with hepatic metabolic dysfunction and tissue remodeling, providing potential insights for precision therapeutic strategies in MASLD.

articles.title: Atmospheric Deposition Dominates Trifluoroacetic Acid Loading in a Large Urbanized River: Insights from Mass Balance and Causal Inference.
articles.abstract: Trifluoroacetic acid (TFA), an ultra-short-chain PFAS, is an increasingly widespread contaminant formed partly through atmospheric transformation of fluorinated replacement compounds. However, the relative roles of atmospheric deposition and hydrological transport in regulating TFA in large urbanized rivers remain poorly constrained. Here, TFA was investigated across environmental and drinking-water matrices in the Nanjing Reach of the Yangtze River under contrasting hydrological conditions. TFA was detected in all compartments, reaching 524,380 ng/L in surface water and persisting from source water to finished tap water. Watershed-scale mass balance showed an annualized net downstream TFA flux increase of 1,500 Mg/yr, of which direct atmospheric deposition accounted for 73.8%, making it the largest quantified local input source, whereas upstream transport remained the dominant regional background load (approximately 91.0% of the total input budget). Interpretable machine learning identified mainstream discharge as the strongest predictor of TFA variability, and double machine learning estimated the largest positive effect for atmospheric deposition, supporting coupled atmospheric loading and hydrological regulation of TFA concentrations and downstream export.

articles.title: Association between Long-term Exposure to Air Pollution and Incident Chronic Kidney Disease among Adults in Beijing, China.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Chronic kidney disease (CKD) has become an increasing global health concern. The research objective was to explore the relationship between long-term exposure to atmospheric pollutants and the development of CKD.

METHODS: A total of 15,580 participants were enrolled from the Beijing Air Pollution and Population Health Cohort. Incident CKD was identified by calculating estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR) based on biochemical measurements. Annual average concentrations of five ambient air pollutants (PM10, PM2.5, NO2, CO, and O3) in Beijing during the study period were collected. We applied time-varying Cox proportional hazards regression models to quantify the associations of individual air pollutants with incident CKD, reporting hazard ratios (HRs) and 95% confidence intervals (CIs). In addition, a composite air pollution score was constructed to evaluate the joint effect of multiple pollutants. Additionally, subgroup analyses were performed to examine potential modifying factors.

RESULTS: Over the follow-up period from 2019 to 2025, 664 incident CKD cases occurred. Per 10μg/m3 increase, PM10(HR=1.18, 95%CI: 1.06-1.31) and CO (HR=1.02, 95%CI:1.01-1.03) were significantly associated with increased CKD risk. Both PM2.5 and NO2 showed positive risk associations, with HRs of 1.22 (95% CI: 0.99-1.50) and 1.17 (95% CI: 0.96-1.43), respectively. Conversely, O3 was inversely associated (HR=0.77, 95% CI: 0.68-0.87). Furthermore, each IQR increase in the composite air pollution score was associated with a 51% higher risk of CKD (HR, 1.51; 95% CI, 1.07-2.12). Subgroup analyses revealed stronger positive associations for PM2.5, PM10, CO, and combined exposure among females and older adults, and for PM2.5, NO2, and CO in urban residents.

CONCLUSION: Sustained PM10 and CO exposure was linked to elevated CKD risk, with O3 showing a potentially inverse pattern. The detrimental effects of air pollutants on renal function appeared to be amplified in several susceptible populations.

articles.title: GLP-1 Receptor Biology and the Therapeutic Role of Incretin-Based Agonists in Metabolic Diseases.
articles.abstract: Type 2 diabetes (T2DM) and obesity represent a growing global health burden, sharing underlying pathophysiological mechanisms such as impaired insulin signalling and chronic low-grade inflammation. The discovery of the incretin effect opened the way for agonist therapies targeting the glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor (GLP-1R) as therapies capable of addressing the metabolic dysregulation common to both diseases simultaneously. This review examines the biology of GLP-1 and the incretin system, with a focus on the structure and signalling mechanisms of GLP-1R, including biased agonism and receptor trafficking. The clinical effectiveness of stable, long-acting GLP-1RAs is evaluated across three therapeutic domains: T2DM management, obesity treatment, and emerging cardiovascular protection. Current evidence demonstrates that GLP-1RAs, which induce insulin secretion and suppress appetite, achieve superior glycaemic control and significant weight reduction compared with conventional therapies, with emerging cardiovascular benefits now extending to non-diabetic patients as well. The shift towards dual and triple receptor agonists, such as tirzepatide and retatrutide, together with biased agonist design, is a promising development for further improvements in effectiveness. Progress in oral formulations of GLP-1RAs may also improve tolerability and patient adherence. Nevertheless, important challenges remain, including gastrointestinal side effects, weight regain upon discontinuation, loss of lean body mass, and unresolved questions regarding long-term safety. In conclusion, while GLP-1R-based therapies represent a major therapeutic advancement, particularly for T2DM patients, their broader application in obesity management requires careful patient selection, continued long-term safety monitoring, and integration with lifestyle interventions.

articles.title: Tirzepatide alleviates hepatic steatosis and inflammation in MASLD partly through suppression of macrophage Dectin-1/Syk/NF-κB signaling.
articles.abstract: Metabolic stress, hepatic lipid accumulation, and macrophage-associated sterile inflammation are closely involved in the development of metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD). Tirzepatide improves metabolic outcomes, but its effects on macrophage inflammatory signaling in MASLD remain unclear. This study investigated the protective effects of tirzepatide against high-fat, high-fructose diet (HFHFD)-induced MASLD and examined the potential involvement of macrophage Dectin-1/spleen tyrosine kinase (Syk)/nuclear factor-κB (NF-κB) signaling. After 7 weeks of HFHFD feeding to establish the MASLD model, male C57BL/6J mice received tirzepatide (10 nmol/kg, subcutaneously, every 3 days) for an additional 7 weeks. Biochemical assays, histology, hepatic RNA sequencing (RNA-seq), RT-qPCR, Western blotting, and immunofluorescence were performed. Palmitic acid (PA)-stimulated RAW264.7 cells, siRNA-mediated Dectin-1 knockdown, and a RAW264.7 cell-derived conditioned medium-based macrophage-hepatocyte indirect interaction model were used for mechanistic validation. Tirzepatide treatment improved HFHFD-induced metabolic dysfunction, liver injury, hepatic steatosis, and inflammatory responses in mice. RNA-seq revealed enrichment of C-type lectin receptor and NF-κB signaling pathways, while HFHFD-induced Clec7a upregulation was reversed by tirzepatide. Tirzepatide reduced hepatic macrophage accumulation, Dectin-1 expression, and Syk/p65 phosphorylation. In PA-stimulated RAW264.7 cells, tirzepatide suppressed pro-inflammatory cytokine expression and secretion and inhibited Dectin-1/Syk/NF-κB activation. Conditioned medium from tirzepatide-treated RAW264.7 cells attenuated lipid accumulation and abnormalities in lipid metabolism- and inflammation-related gene expression in HepG2 cells. Dectin-1 knockdown itself attenuated PA-induced inflammatory responses and was associated with a reduced additional response to tirzepatide. These findings suggest that tirzepatide alleviates HFHFD-induced MASLD, with suppression of macrophage Dectin-1/Syk/NF-κB signaling potentially contributing to these effects.

articles.title: Predicting drug-drug interaction and optimal dosing regimens of rivaroxaban combined with ceritinib using physiologically based pharmacokinetic and pharmacodynamic modeling.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Direct oral anticoagulants like rivaroxaban are globally recommended for cancer-associated thrombosis. However, co-administration with the targeted ALK inhibitor ceritinib in lung cancer patients poses a critical risk of drug-drug interactions (DDI) due to potent CYP3A4 inhibition, lacking quantitative clinical assessments.

OBJECTIVES: To develop and validate physiologically based pharmacokinetic and pharmacodynamic (PBPK/PD) models to quantitatively assess this specific DDI and provide model-predicted dosing strategies.

METHODS: A hybrid "bottom-up" and "top-down" modeling strategy was employed within PK-Sim®. The rivaroxaban model integrated complex hepatic metabolic pathways (CYP3A4, CYP2J2, non-CYP hydrolysis) and active transport (P-gp, BCRP). The ceritinib model incorporated competitive and time-dependent CYP3A4 inhibition parameters. DDI simulations were conducted in a virtual Chinese population. The established model was applied to an exploratory clinical case, comparing its predictions against steady-state plasma concentrations determined via highly specific UPLC-MS/MS from a real-world ALK-positive non-small-cell lung cancer patient.

RESULTS: Simulations demonstrated that concomitant administration of ceritinib (450 mg qd) increased rivaroxaban AUC by 52%-63% and Cmax by 49%-59%. Consequently, the exploratory risk of major bleeding elevated to 1.64- to 1.79-fold that of rivaroxaban monotherapy, aligning closely with observed clinical case data. However, reducing rivaroxaban from 20 mg qd to 12.5 mg qd (normal or mildly impaired renal function), and from 15 mg qd to 10 mg qd (moderate renal impairment), yielded exposure and bleeding risk comparable to standard monotherapy.

CONCLUSIONS: Our model predicts that ceritinib co-administration substantially elevates rivaroxaban exposure and exploratory major bleeding risk. Dose adjustment, alternative therapies, or close clinical monitoring are recommended to ensure patient safety.

articles.title: Cardiac Magnetic Resonance-derived Ablation Footprint after Sequential Unipolar Radiofrequency, Focal Pulsed Field, and Bipolar Radiofrequency Ablation of Resistant Left Ventricular Summit VT.
LongCAF: A longitudinal context-constructive agentic framework for LLM-supported hypertension self-management.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Long-term hypertension self-management requires patients to make daily decisions and be cautious of when to seek medical attention. Although large language model (LLM)-based systems provide new opportunities for conversational self-management support, conventional question-answering conversational paradigms may be insufficient for providing accurate and personalized responses under conditions of fragmented patient expression, incomplete contextual reporting, and changing interaction intents. Therefore, this study aims to address the current limitations by developing and evaluating a context-constructive agentic framework that integrates longitudinal memory, interaction coordination, proactive communication, and safety escalation.

METHODS: This study proposes the Longitudinal Context-constructive Agentic Framework (LongCAF) that structures longitudinal patient-LLM interaction as a unified workflow with five core modules: longitudinal context memory for constructing and maintaining patient-specific context, intent-aware interaction coordination for categorizing and routing heterogeneous interaction intents, interaction synthesis for organizing and generating context-grounded personalized responses, proactive communication for eliciting missing information and clarifying patient concerns when possible, and safety escalation for governing and escalating safety-critical interactions to clinicians. The framework was evaluated in a 6-month real-world deployment.

RESULTS: LongCAF supported longitudinal context construction and context-grounded patient-system interaction during deployment. Patient-level longitudinal context completeness increased from 42.9% (IQR 14.3%-57.1%) at baseline to 57.1% (IQR 57.1%-71.4%) at follow-up, in which 79,290 clinically relevant entries were added, and non-blood-pressure domains accounted for 49.3% of newly acquired entries. Patient-facing outputs supported by retrieved patient-specific context accounted for 69% of outputs, with retrieved domains spanning multiple domains. Candidate-question adoption reached 84.4% among eligible interactions, and intent-aware interaction coordination achieved a micro-F1 score of 0.911. End-to-end safety escalation achieved a precision of 0.915, recall of 0.977, and F1 score of 0.945. Clinician and patient evaluations suggested that LongCAF-supported responses were clinically relevant, contextually appropriate, and useful for continued self-management.

CONCLUSIONS: The real-world deployment demonstrates the feasibility of LongCAF, highlighting its potential as a practical framework for developing more personalized and clinically governed conversational systems for chronic disease self-management.

articles.title: Antibiotic Prescribing for Acute Respiratory Infections in Kentucky Medicaid: Opportunities for Stewardship.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Inappropriate antibiotic prescribing for acute respiratory infections (ARIs) is a major stewardship target. We examined antibiotic prescribing in Kentucky Medicaid from 2022 to 2024 and identified factors associated with inappropriate ARI prescribing to inform stewardship targeting.

METHODS: Retrospective analysis of linked pharmacy and medical claims in Kentucky Medicaid. Prescriptions for beneficiaries with an outpatient ARI diagnosis within seven days of dispensing were classified for appropriateness using a three-tiered diagnostic classification framework, with Tier 3 considered inappropriate. Multivariable logistic regression with prescriber-clustered standard errors assessed patient, provider, and contextual factors.

RESULTS: Of 2,386,291 ARI antibiotic prescriptions, 437,193 (18.3%) were inappropriate. Four conditions accounted for 87.0%: viral upper respiratory infection, bronchitis, non-suppurative otitis media, asthma and allergy. Azithromycin accounted for 38.3% of inappropriate prescriptions and was the most common antibiotic for both viral upper respiratory infection and bronchitis. Advanced practice providers accounted for 67% of antibiotic volume and 65% of inappropriate prescriptions despite lower adjusted odds than adult primary care physicians. Rural residence was associated with higher odds of inappropriate prescribing [Adjusted Odds Ratio (AOR): 1.25]. Inappropriate prescribing declined 21% overall, driven by a 26% reduction between 2022 and 2023 with a modest increase in 2024.

CONCLUSIONS: Inappropriate ARI antibiotic prescribing in Kentucky Medicaid is concentrated in a small set of conditions and antibiotics. Distinguishing prescribing volume from appropriateness has direct implications for stewardship targeting, and the longitudinal surveillance infrastructure developed here is replicable by other state health departments.

articles.title: Postural Intraocular Pressure Changes and the Trans-Lamina Cribrosa Pressure Difference: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
articles.abstract:
TOPIC: This systematic review and meta-analysis (PROSPERO: CRD42024556443) addresses the magnitude of intraocular pressure (IOP) changes when transitioning from sitting to supine and lateral decubitus positions. It investigates the interaction with intracranial pressure (ICP) to estimate the translaminar cribrosa pressure difference (TLPD). Participants included healthy individuals, glaucoma suspects, and patients with ocular hypertension or glaucoma.

CLINICAL RELEVANCE: Glaucoma management relies on IOP measurements taken upright during clinic hours. This paradigm overlooks nocturnal stressors occurring during recumbency, which occupies one-third of a patient's life. Postural IOP elevations, particularly when coupled with low ICP, may drive disease progression in patients who appear stable during diurnal visits, especially those with normal-tension glaucoma (NTG).

METHODS: We searched Ovid MEDLINE and Embase from inception to July 2024 for observational and interventional studies measuring IOP or ICP in at least two body positions. Eligibility criteria required quantitative reporting in mmHg; studies confounding posture with circadian rhythm were excluded. Risk of bias was assessed using Risk of Bias In Non-randomized Studies - of Interventions for observational studies and the Risk of Bias 2.0 tool for the randomized trial.

RESULTS: Thirty-two cohorts comprising 2,842 eyes and 2,385 patients (weighted mean age 61.5 years) were included; 27 studies contributed quantitative data, including 22 for the supine-versus-sitting analysis. Supine IOP increases were +2.49 mmHg (95% CI, 1.33-3.65) in healthy eyes, +2.89 mmHg (95% CI, 2.27-3.50) in the glaucoma spectrum, and +3.60 mmHg (95% CI, 3.24-3.96) in ocular hypertension (one study). The dependent lateral decubitus eye increased by +3.92 mmHg (95% CI, 3.08-4.75). Qualitative synthesis suggested lower ICP in several glaucoma cohorts, although most IOP and ICP measurements were asynchronous.

CONCLUSION: Recumbency induces significant IOP elevations, pronounced in the dependent eye during lateral decubitus positioning. Current evidence hypothesizes a potential double hit for patients with NTG who may lack cerebrospinal fluid counter-pressure, though this relies largely on inferred, asynchronous measurements. While limited by heterogeneity and reliance on ICP estimates, these findings highlight the necessity of future longitudinal research into nocturnal postural physiology to determine its role in glaucoma management.

articles.title: Impact of Intraoperative Hyperglycemia on Postoperative Complications in Adult Cardiac Surgery: A Multi-Institutional Analysis.
articles.journal: The Journal of thoracic and cardiovascular surgery
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Perioperative hyperglycemia is common in cardiac surgery and is associated with adverse outcomes; however, optimal intraoperative glucose targets remain incompletely defined. We evaluated the association between intraoperative glycemic control and postoperative outcomes and assessed the impact of a prospectively implemented statewide quality improvement (QI) initiative.

METHODS: Patients undergoing cardiac surgery with cardiopulmonary bypass from 2020 to 2024 within a statewide collaborative were retrospectively stratified by peak intraoperative glucose level (<180 mg/dL versus ≥180 mg/dL) for analysis. Primary outcomes included infectious complications, acute kidney injury (AKI), renal failure, stroke, and composite morbidity. Multivariable mixed-effects logistic regression models adjusted for patient, operative, and institutional factors. Interrupted time series analysis evaluated changes in glycemic control following QI implementation.

RESULTS: Among 22,747 patients, 74.2% achieved peak intraoperative glucose <180 mg/dL. Patients with peak glucose <180 mg/dL had lower rates of composite infection (4.75% vs 7.64%), AKI (23.46% vs 28.85%), and operative mortality (1.73% vs 3.31%) (all p<0.001). After adjustment, peak glucose <180 mg/dL remained associated with lower odds of surgical site infection (OR 0.81), sepsis (OR 0.61), pneumonia (OR 0.80), AKI (OR 0.86), renal failure (OR 0.79), and composite complications (OR 0.86); stroke was not associated. Following QI implementation, achievement of peak glucose <180 mg/dL increased from 66.9% to 88.2%, with a significant improvement in temporal trends (p<0.001).

CONCLUSIONS: Peak intraoperative glucose <180 mg/dL was independently associated with improved infectious and renal postoperative outcomes after cardiac surgery. A statewide QI initiative significantly improved glycemic control, supporting adoption of standardized intraoperative glucose management protocols.

articles.title: Machine learning-aided serum N-glycomic signatures reveal potential biomarkers for acute ischemic stroke and minocycline treatment response.
articles.journal: Clinica chimica acta; international journal of clinical chemistry
articles.abstract: The absence of molecular-level tools for diagnosing and monitoring acute ischemic stroke (AIS) underscores the need for novel biomarkers. Serum N-glycosylation represents a promising but remains underexplored source of such markers in AIS. Using hydrophilic interaction liquid chromatography with fluorescence detection (HILIC-FLD), serum N-glycome profiling from healthy controls (HC), AIS patients who had not received prior treatment (AIS) and administered minocycline (A_M) were conducted. A computational pipeline integrating multiple machine-learning (ML) models and feature-selection algorithms was employed to decode the glycomic data. AIS was associated with a distinct serum N-glycome signature characterized by increased branching and hypersialylation, which was partially reversed after the minocycline treatment. An optimized random forest model (Glyco_RFF) based on six glycome features (Glyco_F: GP14, GP32, GP33, GP34, S3, S4) discriminated both AIS from HC, and AIS from A_M with high accuracy (AUC values > 0.9). Longitudinal changes in two features (GP34, S4) correlated significantly with clinical improvement (NIHSS score reduction), suggesting their potential as dynamic biomarkers of treatment response. This study identifies a dynamic serum N-glycome signature in AIS and its modulation by minocycline. The Glyco_RFF model provides a novel, non-invasive tool for diagnosis and therapeutic monitoring.

articles.title: Effects of different gestational diabetes treatments on myo-inositol levels and placental insulin signalling.
articles.abstract: Myo-inositol (MI) is a precursor of inositol-3-phosphate, which participates in the insulin receptor pathway. Glucose enhances urinary MI excretion, which could affect gestational diabetes mellitus (GDM) management. The relationship between MI levels and GDM treatment remains unclear, raising questions about potential MI supplementation. The aim of this study was to evaluate MI levels in GDM women treated with either diet or insulin, and their associations with glycaemia and placental insulin signalling. MI was quantified in 23 women with GDM treated with diet (GDM-Diet), 20 GDM treated with insulin (GDM-Insulin) and 25 healthy non-GDM (control). Samples were collected at both the third trimester of pregnancy and at delivery in serum, urine, placenta and cord blood. Placental insulin cascade proteins were assessed by western blot. MI concentration in serum and placenta were decreased in GDM women at delivery, especially in the GDM-diet group. Furthermore, diabetic patients showed greater urinary excretion of MI already at third trimester. Nevertheless, cord MI was not affected by GDM. Placental p-Akt was strongly associated with placental MI (R=0.415, P=0.006), and its levels were lower in GDM-diet group (P=0.031). Insulin treatment tended to normalize maternal MI levels and insulin signalling, whereas GDM treated with diet had lower MI concentrations in both serum and placenta compared to controls. Women with GDM show reduced serum and placental MI concentrations than controls, linked to impaired insulin signalling. Women with GDM managed with diet show the greatest MI deficit and thus may therefore represent a target population for future supplementation trials.

articles.title: Dietary Zeaxanthin Attenuates Cigarette Smoke-Induced COPD by Suppressing ERK-Driven Apoptosis.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Dietary zeaxanthin's role in COPD remains underexplored.

METHODS: A multi-dimensional approach integrating NHANES epidemiological data, multi-omics analyses (network pharmacology, transcriptomics, molecular docking), and experimental validation in a CSE-induced mouse model and HBE cells.

RESULTS: NHANES analysis revealed an inverse association between zeaxanthin intake and COPD risk. Multi-omics identified MAPK1 (ERK2) as a core target, with molecular docking predicting favorable zeaxanthin-MAPK1/MAPK3 interactions. Zeaxanthin alleviated emphysema, improved lung function, and reduced apoptosis/inflammation in vivo, and protected HBE cells in vitro. Mechanistically, it dose-dependently inhibited ERK phosphorylation and downstream cleaved caspase-3 activation. PMA-mediated reactivation of ERK partially reversed the anti-apoptotic effect of zeaxanthin.

CONCLUSION: Dietary zeaxanthin protects against COPD by suppressing the ERK-mediated apoptotic pathway, supporting its potential as a nutritional intervention.

articles.title: Dietary iron supplementation attenuates doxorubicin-induced cardiotoxicity by improving myocardial iron homeostasis and reducing ferroptosis-associated injury in mice.
articles.abstract: Iron deficiency frequently accompanies chronic heart failure (CHF) and is linked to adverse clinical outcomes. Although intravenous iron replacement has shown clinical benefit in heart failure, whether increasing dietary iron intake can provide cardioprotective effects remains uncertain. In this study, we examined the effects of dietary iron supplementation in a murine model of doxorubicin (Dox)-induced cardiotoxicity. Mice were treated with Dox at 2.5 mg/kg by intraperitoneal injection once weekly for 6 weeks and received either standard chow containing 45 ppm iron or ferric citrate-enriched chow containing 5,000 ppm iron. We assessed cardiac function, myocardial injury, fibrosis, apoptosis, mitochondrial ultrastructure, oxidative stress, transcriptomic changes, and iron metabolism-related proteins through echocardiography, histological examination, biochemical assays, RNA sequencing, and Western blot analysis. In Dox-treated mice, the iron-enriched diet was associated with better survival and cardiac performance, together with less myocardial damage, fibrosis, apoptosis, mitochondrial injury, and oxidative stress. Transcriptomic analysis revealed enrichment of ferroptosis-related pathways in hearts exposed to Dox. Dox exposure also disturbed cardiac iron handling, as reflected by abnormal myocardial iron distribution, higher transferrin receptor 1 (TFR1) and nuclear receptor coactivator 4 (NCOA4) abundance, and lower ferritin heavy chain 1 (FTH1) expression. Most of these changes shifted toward control levels after dietary iron supplementation, while SLC7A11 abundance was unaffected. Taken together, our findings suggest that dietary iron supplementation mitigates Dox-induced cardiac injury, accompanied by improved myocardial iron homeostasis and attenuation of ferroptosis-related injury. Changes in NCOA4 and FTH1 abundance may reflect altered ferritin turnover and potentially contribute to the observed cardioprotective effects.

articles.title: Delirium after Aortic Arch Surgery with Hypothermic Circulatory Arrest: Clinical and Neuroimaging Insights from the GOT ICE Randomized Trial.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Postoperative delirium (POD) is a complication of arch surgery with hypothermic circulatory arrest (HCA) and may contribute to long-term cognitive decline, but prospective data are limited. We examined its incidence, predictors, and neurocognitive and neuroimaging correlates.

METHODS: The Cognitive Effects of Body Temperature During Hypothermic Circulatory Arrest trial compared deep versus moderate hypothermia during elective arch repair. Delirium was assessed preoperatively and on postoperative days 1-3 using the Confusion Assessment Method. Thirty-day outcomes, cognition, quality of life, and resting-state functional magnetic resonance imaging at 4 weeks and 1 year were compared by POD status.

RESULTS: Of 269 patients with complete assessments, POD occurred in 34.6% and did not differ significantly between hypothermia groups (p=0.45). Patients with POD had higher stroke rates (9.7% vs 0.6%; p<0.001), prolonged ventilation (3.2% vs. 0%; p=0.017), and longer hospitalization (8.5 vs. 5.9 days; p<0.001). Affected patients had worse cognition and quality of life (p<0.001) at 30 days, with partial recovery at 1 year. Baseline imaging demonstrated reduced thalamo-cerebellar connectivity in patients who developed POD (p<0.01, p-FWE<0.05), with persistent abnormalities at 1-year. Higher baseline cognition and ejection fraction were protective against POD (OR<1), whereas longer antegrade cerebral perfusion time increased risk (OR 1.03; 95% CI, 1.005-1.05; p=0.019).

CONCLUSIONS: POD affects >one-third of patients after arch surgery with HCA and is associated with worse 30-day and 1-year cognitive outcomes with enduring imaging abnormalities. Reduced preoperative thalamo-cerebellar connectivity suggests a preexisting neural vulnerability, indicating that delirium may unmask rather than cause long-term cognitive decline.

articles.title: Operative Details and Clinical Outcomes of Chordal Preservation in Mitral Valve Replacement Surgery.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Chordal preservation in mitral valve replacement (MVR) has been historically associated with favorable postoperative left ventricular remodeling. We evaluated the outcomes of chordal preservation in a contemporary MVR cohort.

METHODS: Consecutive MVR patients at a single institution (2015-2024) were divided into chordal preservation and non-preservation groups. Baseline differences were balanced by inverse probability of treatment weighting. Primary outcome was survival. Secondary outcomes included change in left ventricular ejection fraction and end-diastolic diameter between pre- and postoperative echocardiography. Subgroup analyses by mitral valve disease etiology were performed.

RESULTS: Of 320 patients, 244 (76.3%) underwent chordal preservation and 76 (23.7%) did not. Adjusted Kaplan-Meier analysis demonstrated similar postoperative four-year survival between chordal preservation and non-preservation patients (79.0% vs. 75.3%, p=0.31), confirmed by multivariable Cox regression adjusting for concomitant tricuspid surgery and prosthesis type (aHR 0.67 [0.33-1.35], p=0.26). Percent change in left ventricular ejection fraction (-1.2% vs. -1.5%, p=0.94) and end-diastolic diameter (-13.5% vs. -6.5%, p=0.12) were similar. In adjusted subgroup analyses, chordal preservation was associated with improved survival in myxomatous disease (aHR 0.23 [0.09-0.59], p=0.002) but not rheumatic disease (aHR 0.55 [0.20-1.52], p=0.25); however, formal interaction analysis showed no evidence that the effect of preservation differed by etiology (Wald p=0.44).

CONCLUSIONS: After adjustment, chordal preservation was not associated with differences in overall survival or early left ventricular function in contemporary MVR. We found no evidence that mitral valve disease etiology modifies this association.

articles.title: Timing of Surgery in Patients with Severe Degenerative Mitral Regurgitation Due to Bileaflet Prolapse.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The purpose of this study was to evaluate the impact of surgical timing on patients with bileaflet prolapse.

METHODS: From 1/1/2016 to 7/1/2020, 250 adults underwent primary mitral valve surgery for severe mitral regurgitation (MR) due to bileaflet prolapse at Cleveland Clinic and were divided into an early surgery group (asymptomatic patients, no history of atrial fibrillation, left ventricle end-systolic diameter ≤40 mm, ejection fraction ≥60%, and pulmonary arterial systolic pressure ≤50 mmHg) and a late surgery group with ≥1 of these criteria. Longitudinal analysis of postoperative echocardiographic data from 601 transthoracic echocardiograms were used to assess durability of repair between early surgery (n=50) and late surgery (n=200) groups.

RESULTS: All patients underwent successful mitral valve repair (n=250; 100%). Minimally invasive approaches were used in 48% (n=24) of the early surgery group and 41% (n=82) of the late surgery group (P=.37). Anterior neochordae were required in the majority of patients (66% (n=54) vs. 60% (n=119); P=.40). There was no operative morality in this series. Five-year prevalence of ≥ 2+ MR was estimated at 20% in the early surgery group and 16% in the late group (P=.69). Freedom from reoperation at 5 years was 100% after early surgery and 97% after late surgery (P=.30).

CONCLUSIONS: Most patients with severe MR due to bileaflet prolapse underwent late surgery. Repair was 100% with similar complexity regardless of surgical timing. In the absence of symptoms and adverse remodeling, early surgery for severe MR due to bileaflet prolapse may be recommended at an experienced center.

articles.title: Efficacy and safety of CO₂ laser ablation followed by 5-aminolevulinic acid photodynamic therapy for cervical high-grade squamous intraepithelial lesions in women of childbearing age: a retrospective single-arm study.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To evaluate the clinical efficacy and safety of CO2 laser ablation followed by 5-aminolevulinic acid photodynamic therapy in reproductive-age women with cervical high-grade squamous intraepithelial lesions (HSIL).

METHODS: This retrospective single-arm study included 57 reproductive-age women with biopsy-proven cervical HSIL and high-risk HPV infection who received CO2 laser ablation followed by 5-ALA-PDT between January 2022 and June 2025.

RESULTS: At 6 months, the overall response to the initial combined treatment was 92.98% (53/57), with cure in 84.21% (48/57), improvement in 8.77% (5/57), and persistent HSIL in 7.02% (4/57). The four patients with persistent HSIL received rescue LEEP. At 12 months, when the four rescue LEEP patients were counted as treatment failures for the initial combined regimen, cure was 84.21% (48/57) and overall response was 92.98% (53/57). After including rescue LEEP as a separate rescue-treatment outcome, all 57 patients had normal TCT and normal histopathology; 52/57 (91.23%) were cured and 5/57 (8.77%) had persistent HR-HPV and were classified as improved. Thus, the 100% (57/57) 12-month overall response includes four patients who achieved normal histology after rescue LEEP and cannot be attributed to CO2 laser ablation plus 5-ALA-PDT alone. HPV clearance for the initial combined treatment was 48/57 (84.21%) at 6 months and 48/57 (84.21%) at 12 months when the four rescue LEEP patients were counted as initial treatment failures; the final 12-month HPV clearance rate including rescue LEEP was 52/57 (91.23%).

CONCLUSION: CO2 laser ablation followed by 5-ALA-PDT is associated with high histological remission and HR-HPV clearance and a mild adverse-event profile in selected reproductive-age women with cervical HSIL. However, the 100% 12-month overall response includes four patients who received rescue LEEP and cannot be attributed to CO2 laser ablation plus 5-ALA-PDT alone. This single-arm study cannot establish the incremental benefit of laser ablation over PDT alone or of PDT over laser ablation. Cervical adhesions occurred in 7.02% (4/57), and cervical length, cervical function, fertility, and obstetric outcomes were not assessed; anatomical preservation cannot be equated with functional or fertility protection.

articles.title: PHD1/IKKβ/NF-κB signaling pathway regulates macrophage polarization and is involved in hypoxia-tolerant large yellow croaker (Larimichthys crocea) against Aeromonas hydrophila infection.
articles.abstract: The hypoxia-tolerant group (T group) large yellow croaker (Larimichthys crocea) exhibits high survival rates when infected with Aeromonas hydrophila. To elucidate the underlying mechanism, this study explored the potential new role of proline hydroxylase domain-containing protein 1 (PHD1) in immunity, and examined the differences in PHD1/IKKβ/NF-κB signaling pathway between the T group and normal group following A. hydrophila challenge. Our results found that LcPhd1 responds to LPS stimulation in head kidney macrophages of L. crocea and affects the phosphorylation of IKKβ and NF-κB nuclear translocation in the classical immune signaling pathway. Co-IP and site-directed mutagenesis further demonstrated that this effect may occur through the modulation of the proline residue in the LXXLAP sequence of LcIKKβ. Additionally, PHD1 inhibited macrophage polarization into the M1 type, including reducing the production of bactericidal substances, such as inflammatory factors, ROS, as well as diminishing the macrophage functions, such as migration, invasion, and phagocytosis. Following A. hydrophila infection, the PHD1 expression in the head kidney of T gorup L. crocea decreased, while IKKβ phosphorylation and p65 nuclear translocation increased. In conclusion, these results indicated that PHD1 may regulate macrophage polarization through the IKKβ/NF-κB signal cascade and contribute to the resistance of T gorup L. crocea to A. hydrophila infection.

articles.title: Vibrio infection compromises byssal attachment in the mussel Mytilus coruscus by modulating energy homeostasis and byssal protein gene expression.
articles.abstract: Mussels are important bivalve species that are cultured worldwide and attach to substrate by byssal threads. Mass detachment of mussels poses a significant threat to the sustainability of mussel aquaculture. It remains unclear whether biological factors such as infections caused by marine pathogenic bacteria affect byssal attachment in mussels. In this study, two strains each of Vibrio splendidus and V. anguillarum were isolated from seawater, and mussels were exposed to different concentrations (104, 105, 106, and 107 CFU/mL) of each bacterial strain for seven days. After exposure, we analyzed byssal thread number, detachment frequency, mechanical properties, adhesion strength, energy reserves (triglycerides, glycogen and proteins) in the gill and hepatopancreas, and the expression levels of byssal protein genes (mfp-1T, mfp-2, col-1, mfp-5 and mfp-6). The results showed that both Vibrio species caused a significant decrease in byssal thread number (P < 0.05), a significant increase in detachment frequency (P < 0.05), and a significant reduction in byssal diameter and breaking force (P < 0.05) compared with the control group after seven days of exposure. At 107 CFU/mL, both bacterial strains significantly decreased triglyceride levels in the hepatopancreas (P < 0.05), whereas protein and glycogen contents remained unchanged. qPCR analysis revealed that the byssal fiber structural gene col-1 was significantly downregulated at all bacterial concentrations (P < 0.05), and the adhesive plaque protein gene mfp-2 was significantly downregulated at 107 CFU/mL (P < 0.05). These findings demonstrate that Vibrio infection compromises byssal attachment by depleting hepatopancreatic triglyceride reserves and suppressing the expression of byssal protein genes col-1 and mfp-2. This study identifies Vibrio infection as a key biological factor underlying weakened byssal attachment in mussels and provides new insights into the ecological implications of host-pathogen interactions in bivalves.

articles.title: Immune responses in the olfactory organ and brain of Atlantic cod (Gadus morhua) following nasal vaccination against Francisella noatunensis.
articles.abstract: Bacterial infections caused by the intracellular bacterium Francisella noatunensis pose a major health challenge in Atlantic cod (Gadus morhua), largely due to the lack of effective prophylactic and therapeutic measures. Here we evaluated the immune and physiological responses of cod to two candidate live attenuated vaccines (i.e. clpB and iglC) against F. noatunensis delivered intranasally. These experimental vaccines were constructed by a single knockout mutation of a virulence gene in F. noatunensis. Cod was vaccinated intranasally and reared for 45 days until infection with the wild-type strain Francisella noatunenesis subp. noatunensis and further reared for 47 days until termination. Given the chosen delivery route, our analyses were focused on the olfactory organ and brain of cod. Infected cod presented classic gross pathologies of francisellosis, including multi-organ nodulations, splenomegaly, and hepatomegaly. Among the vaccine candidates, the clpB-vaccinated group demonstrated upregulated expression of immune response genes in both the olfactory organ and brain, exhibited the lowest nodulation score, and showed minimal histological alterations in the olfactory organ. To further explore the physiological consequences of the clpB mutant, shotgun proteomics was performed in selected olfactory organ and brain of vaccinated cod. We identified 404 differentially expressed proteins (DEPs) in the brain and 241 in the olfactory organ with 17 DEPs common to both organs. These DEPs were mostly involved in cellular signalling, transmembrane internalisation, enzymatic processes, and important immune response pathways, such as immune recruitment and activation, the respiratory burst reaction, and apoptosis. These findings suggest that the clpB-attenuated vaccine holds promise as a candidate vaccine against F. noatunensis and provides valuable insights into the mechanisms of immune modulation.

articles.title: Extracellular lactate enhances IL-10 transcription via H4K5 lactylation and promotes an A2-like reactive-astrocyte phenotype after ischemic stroke.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Ischemic stroke triggers a rapid rise in lactate levels in the brain tissue. The neuroprotective role of exogenous lactate administered during the reperfusion phase has recently garnered attention. A neuroprotective A2 phenotype of reactive astrocytes (RACs) is characterized by interleukin-10 (IL-10) upregulation, which mitigates neuroinflammation. However, whether exogenous lactate drives A2-like polarization of RACs remains unknown. This study aimed to elucidate the mechanism by which lactate regulates this process.

METHODS: Rat middle cerebral artery occlusion (MCAO) and in vitro primary RACs models were established. Western blotting, immunofluorescence staining, and RT-qPCR were used to assess A1/A2 polarization markers, IL-10 expression, histone lactylation, and related neuroimmune signaling molecules. Ubiquitination, chromatin immunoprecipitation, and dual-luciferase reporter assays were performed to clarify the mechanism by which lactate regulates IL-10 expression and A2-like polarization of RACs.

RESULTS: Our results demonstrated that increased lactate levels after ischemic stroke correlated with A2 polarization of RACs. Lactate treatment significantly enhanced A2 polarization and reduced infarct volume in the rat MCAO model. Mechanistically, lactate activated signal transducer and activator of transcription 3 (STAT3) signaling while suppressing sirtuin 1 (SIRT1) expression and synergistically enhancing H4K5 lactylation (H4K5la) and IL-10 expression, thereby driving RACs toward an anti-inflammatory phenotype.

CONCLUSIONS: This study revealed that elevated extracellular lactate in the acute phase of ischemic stroke drove RACs toward an A2-like phenotype through the Yes-associated protein 1 (YAP1)/STAT3/IL-10 and YAP1/SIRT1/H4K5la signaling axes. These findings provide a theoretical basis for targeting RAC lactylation as a potential therapeutic strategy to limit inflammatory damage after stroke.

articles.title: CMR-derived anatomical indices for arrhythmia risk stratification in Ebstein anomaly.
Loss to Follow-up in Randomized Controlled Trials on Elbow Pathology: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
articles.journal: Journal of shoulder and elbow surgery
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Loss to follow-up (LTFU) is a well-recognized source of bias in musculoskeletal research and may compromise the validity of randomized controlled trials (RCTs). Patients lost to follow-up may have different, often worse, outcomes, potentially leading to overestimation of treatment effects. Despite improved reporting guidelines, LTFU remains inconsistently reported in orthopaedic literature. This study aimed to assess the rate of LTFU in RCTs focusing on elbow pathology and to identify factors associated with LTFU.

METHODS: A systematic review was conducted according to PRISMA guidelines. PubMed, Embase, Cochrane Central, and Web of Science were searched for RCTs published between January 2020 and July 2025. Studies on elbow pathology with a minimum follow-up of six months, published in English or Dutch and in Q1 or Q2 journals, were included. Data extraction included study characteristics, follow-up-related variables, and patient characteristics. The primary outcome was the LTFU rate. Descriptive statistics and forest plots were used to explore potential associations.

RESULTS: A total of 44 RCTs including 3,012 patients were analyzed. The mean LTFU rate was 12.1% (range 0-35.6%), with follow-up durations ranging from 6 months to 2 years. No associations were found between LTFU and age, gender, type of intervention, type of pathology, traumatic vs. non-traumatic pathology, follow-up duration, study location, type of hospital, funding source, or journal ranking. A higher number of follow-up moments per month was associated with lower LTFU rates. Reporting of several variables, including factors related to trial conduct, patient characteristics, and reasons for LTFU, was often incomplete.

CONCLUSION: This systematic review found a mean LTFU rate of 12.1% in RCTs on elbow pathology, consistent with the commonly assumed 10% attrition rate. Most factors were not associated with LTFU, although more frequent follow-up was linked to fewer dropouts. Incomplete reporting remains a key limitation and should be improved to strengthen future research.

LEVEL OF EVIDENCE: Level II, Systematic Review, Research Methodology.

articles.title: Adoption of Patient-Reported Outcomes Measurement Information System (PROMIS) and Trends in PROM Use in Shoulder Literature: A Systematic Review.
articles.journal: Journal of shoulder and elbow surgery
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: To provide a systematic review on the current literature specific to the adoption of Patient-Reported Outcomes Measurement Information System (PROMIS) and trends in patient reported outcome measure (PROM) use in shoulder orthopedic literature.

METHODS: A review of all English language articles in PubMed, Web of Science, and Embase was conducted in January of 2026. All articles between 2015 and 2025 reporting on patient outcomes in shoulder specific orthopedic literature had their study characteristics extracted, including publication year, country of origin, level of evidence, journal of publication, shoulder topic, and which PROMs were reported on. Review papers or studies that were non-English, failed to include PROMs, or were not specific to shoulder literature were excluded.

RESULTS: A total of 7,416 studies were reviewed and 3,473 met the inclusion criteria. PROMIS instruments were used in 115 studies (3.3%), with utilization increasing from 0.0% in 2015 to 5.5% in 2025 (absolute increase, 5.5%; 95% CI, 3.0%-7.9%; p = 0.001). The majority of studies utilizing PROMIS were published in the Journal of Shoulder and Elbow Surgery and related journals (60.9%), rotator cuff disorders and shoulder arthroplasty were the most commonly reported topics. The most frequently reported PROMIS domains were Upper Extremity (60.0%), Pain Interference (47.8%), and Physical Function (33.9%). PROMIS instruments were used more commonly in conjunction with traditional outcome measures (69.6%), instead of as a stand-alone PROM; it was most commonly paired to the American Shoulder and Elbow Surgeon (ASES) outcome measure (60.0%). During the study period, there was no significant increase in the number of PROMs collected per study over time (β = 0.008 PROMs per year, P = 0.388, R2 = 0.08). Constant score (CS), Simple Shoulder Test (SST) and ASES score were the three most commonly reported outcome scores for shoulder condition. CS and SST utilization demonstrated a significant decline (p<0.01), while the increase in ASES utilization was not significant during the study period.

CONCLUSIONS: Although PROMIS enables a standardized, patient-centered assessment of orthopedic conditions, the current study demonstrates its limited adoption over the past decade as a primary outcome measure for shoulder conditions compared to traditional legacy scores.

LEVEL OF EVIDENCE: Research Methodology, Systematic Review.

articles.title: Accelerating returns in gene panel design: A completion theory for regulatory network identification.
articles.abstract: Measurement panel design for regulatory network inference requires choosing which genes to observe. We prove that under random gene selection, expected marginal identifiability is non-decreasing and strictly increasing for sufficiently large k (once nontrivial regulatory interactions can be completed)-a property we term acceleration, meaning that E[Δ(k+1)]>E[Δ(k)], rooted in order statistics of random permutations. Formally, the expected number of regulatory edges completed at step k equals ∑j(k-1sj-1)/(Nsj), which is strictly increasing in k for k≥maxjsj whenever any regulatory interaction involves two or more genes. From this theorem we motivate a lookahead panel selection strategy that achieves 10 percentage points more completed regulatory edges than greedy set cover at 50% panel size (Cohen's d=0.77, p=9.8×10-8, paired Wilcoxon, n=50 networks with N≤40), evaluated across all 285 published Boolean regulatory networks from the Biodivine Boolean Models database. Across 285 BBM networks, the mean minimum panel size for eliminating all observational blind spots is 26.4% of model nodes, while the median 50%-full-observability threshold is 65.2% (under two-phase greedy ordering), and 90% full observability requires a mean of 95.1% of model nodes (median 95.2%). With the lookahead strategy, 50% completion is reached at 61.2% panel size in the strategy-comparison cohort (n=50, N≤40). The theorem further establishes that, under random ordering, intrinsic identifiability potential depends solely on the in-degree distribution, while extractable identifiability under a topology-aware algorithm depends on the interaction between the selection algorithm and network topology. Biological wiring is significantly better exploited by topology-aware algorithms than degree-preserved random wiring (Cohen's d=0.29, p=2×10-7), a small but robust effect consistent with biological regulatory architecture being exploitable by systematic measurement design.

articles.title: miR-885-5p regulates fibrogenic phenotypes in TGF-β1-treated LX-2 cells via targeting NR5A2, with clinical association with MAFLD.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Metabolic-associated fatty liver disease (MAFLD) is a common chronic liver disease worldwide, with liver fibrosis serving as a major determinant of poor prognosis.
