Evidence from clinical, preclinical, and translational studies demonstrates that dietary interventions can enhance endogenous GLP-1 secretion, improve satiety, reduce postprandial glycaemia, and support modest weight reduction. However, responses remain variable and generally less potent than pharmacological GLP-1R agonism CONCLUSION: Collectively, current findings support natural dietary components as physiologically relevant indirect modulators of GLP-1R signaling that may complement pharmacological therapies and contribute to sustainable long-term weight management. Further well-controlled human studies are required to clarify receptor-specific mechanisms, optimize dietary strategies, and strengthen translational applicability.

articles.title: Selected risk factors for mortality in children with HUS - a single-center analysis.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: The aim of the study was to describe clinical and laboratory characteristics of hemolytic-uremic syndrome (HUS), and identify prognostic factors, including risk factors for mortality and complications.

MATERIALS AND METHODS: It is a retrospective study of 74 pediatric patients (69 survivors and 5 non-survivors) with the first episode of HUS who were hospitalized in our tertiary reference center during 10-year period.

RESULTS: Compared to survivors, non-survivors significantly more frequently developed neurological symptoms (100% vs. 31.9%), suffered from respiratory tract infections (80% vs. 27.5%), respiratory insufficiency (100% vs. 21.7%), circulatory failure (80% vs. 2.9%), and more often required renal replacement therapy (100% vs. 52.2%). In this group, there was a significant reduction in complement C3c and C4 components (0.67 vs. 0.97, 0.08 vs. 0.18, respectively). Elevated PCT, CRP, D-dimers, APTT, lipase, AST, GGTP and reduced C3c and C4 were associated with increased mortality risk. Severe neurological and ophthalmological complications, as well as circulatory insufficiency were the strongest predictors of death. Overall mortality rate was 6.8%.

CONCLUSIONS: Neurological (ischemic stroke, ophthalmological anomalies) and systemic (circulatory failure) complications may represent important determinants of outcome in pediatric HUS. Mortality also appears to be associated with systemic inflammatory activation and coagulopathy.

articles.title: Thrombospondin-1 and Thrombospondin-2 are associated with biatrial fibrotic remodeling in human valvular heart disease.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: Atrial fibrosis is a key structural substrate of atrial fibrillation and atrial cardiomyopathy. Thrombospondin-1 (TSP-1) and thrombospondin-2 (TSP-2) regulate TGF-β signaling and matrix organization, but their roles in human atrial remodeling remain incompletely understood. Therefore, this study aimed to compare atrial TSP-1 and TSP-2 expression in mitral and aortic valve disease and examine their associations with fibrosis, inflammation, and adhesion-related remodeling.

METHODS: This observational cross-sectional study included 67 cardiac surgery patients: 30 with mitral valve disease, 23 with aortic valve disease, and 14 undergoing coronary artery bypass grafting without significant valvular disease. Left and right atrial tissues were examined using RT-qPCR, ELISA, histology, and immunofluorescence. Molecular assays used pooled tissue preparations. Systemic inflammation was evaluated using the neutrophil-to-lymphocyte ratio.

RESULTS: TSP-1 and TSP-2 transcript levels were increased in both valve disease groups, alongside greater collagen deposition and increased inflammatory gene expression. Transcript changes were particularly marked in left atrial tissue from patients with mitral valve disease. TSP-1 protein was significantly increased in right atrial tissue from the mitral valve group, whereas TSP-2 protein did not differ significantly between groups. Cadherin transcript levels were also altered. The neutrophil-to-lymphocyte ratio was higher in both valve disease groups than in the surgical comparator group.

CONCLUSIONS: Atrial TSPs expression was associated with fibrotic and inflammatory remodeling in valvular heart disease. Differences between transcript and protein findings and the use of pooled preparations warrant cautious interpretation. These observational findings require validation in independent cohorts and do not establish causality.

articles.title: Parallel bioassay-guided discovery and mechanistic characterization of a dual DPP-IV and ACE inhibitory peptide from defatted Nigella sativa seed cake.
articles.abstract:
ETHNOPHARMACOLOGICAL RELEVANCE: Nigella sativa L. (black cumin) has long been used in traditional Islamic, Unani, and Ayurvedic medicine for managing metabolic disorders. Although its medicinal properties have been largely attributed to seed oil and phytochemicals, the protein-rich defatted seed cake generated during oil production remains an underutilized by-product with largely unexplored bioactive peptide potential.

AIM OF THE STUDY: This study aimed to identify and characterize multifunctional peptides from defatted N. sativa seed proteins with dual inhibitory activity against dipeptidyl peptidase-IV (DPP-IV) and angiotensin-I converting enzyme (ACE).

MATERIALS AND METHODS: Following protease screening, the thermolysin hydrolysate was subjected to parallel bioassay-guided fractionation by strong cation exchange chromatography and reversed-phase HPLC. Peptides were identified by LC-MS/MS and de novo sequencing, prioritized in silico, synthesized, and evaluated by enzyme inhibition, kinetics, docking, and pre-incubation assays.

RESULTS: Thermolysin generated the most potent DPP-IV inhibitory hydrolysate. Comparative LC-MS/MS analysis identified LYDGELRQGQL (LL-11) in both active fractions. LL-11 exhibited dual inhibitory activities against DPP-IV (IC50 = 1.15 ± 0.25 mM) and ACE (IC50 = 49.98 ± 4.04 μM), acting as a noncompetitive DPP-IV inhibitor and a competitive ACE inhibitor. Molecular docking and enzyme pre-incubation studies supported distinct enzyme-specific binding and stability profiles.

CONCLUSION: LL-11 is a dual-functional peptide identified from defatted N. sativa seed cake. The integrated workflow highlights this underutilized by-product as a sustainable source of bioactive ingredients with potential relevance to the dietary management of diabetes and hypertension. However, further cell-based and in vivo validation is warranted to establish the physiological relevance of LL-11.

articles.title: Mechanism of Buyang Huanwu Decoction in regulating arachidonic acid metabolism to mediate microglial polarization and alleviate cerebral ischemic injury.
articles.abstract:
ETHNOPHARMACOLOGICAL RELEVANCE: BYHWD, a classical prescription for post-stroke rehabilitation, protects against cerebral ischemia by modulating microglial polarization, oxidative stress, and lipid metabolism.

OBJECTIVE: To investigate the mechanism by which Buyang Huanwu Decoction regulates arachidonic acid metabolism to mediate microglial polarization and alleviate cerebral ischemic injury.

METHODS: The study employed a rat model of middle cerebral artery occlusion (MCAO) using SD rats, as well as oxygen-glucose deprivation/reoxygenation (OGD/R) models in bEnd.3 and BV.2 cells. The subjects received BYHWD treatment. The protective effects of BYHWD on brain tissue were evaluated using neurological function scoring, HE staining, immunofluorescence, ELISA, PCR, and biochemical assays. The effects of BYHWD on the function and morphology of microvascular endothelial cells were examined using immunofluorescence, tube formation assays, and cytoskeletal staining. Metabolomic profiling was performed to screen for differential metabolites and associated pathways involved in BYHWD-mediated improvement of lipid metabolism. The identified key targets were validated by a combination of Western blotting, immunofluorescence, and biochemical assays. Finally, Mendelian randomization analysis was employed to confirm the causal relationship.

RESULTS: In vivo and in vitro studies showed that BYHWD markedly improved neurological function and attenuated neuronal injury. The underlying mechanism involves the inhibition of arachidonic acid metabolism and the regulation of glycerophospholipid metabolism to restore lipid homeostasis, along with the attenuation of inflammatory responses and oxidative stress damage, as well as the promotion of cerebral microvascular repair. Mendelian randomization analysis further confirmed that lipid metabolic disturbances are a risk factor for large artery atherosclerosis stroke.

CONCLUSION: BYHWD protects against cerebral ischemia/reperfusion injury by blocking arachidonic acid metabolism, adjusting glycerophospholipid pathways to restore lipid homeostasis reducing inflammation and oxidative stress, and facilitating the restoration of injured blood vessels.

articles.title: Alpinia oxyphylla Miq. promotes angiogenesis and preserves neurons in subacute ischemic stroke in rats: possible involvement of the HIF-1α/Nrf2/VEGF-A-mediated signaling pathway.
articles.abstract:
ETHNOPHARMACOLOGICAL RELEVANCE: Alpinia oxyphylla Miq., referred to in Chinese as Yi Zhi Ren (YZR), is a traditional Chinese herbal medicine long used to treat stroke. However, the effects of YZR extract on angiogenesis in subacute ischemic stroke remain unclear.

AIM OF THE STUDY: The effects of YZR extract administered at different phases on angiogenesis were investigated to determine the involvement of the upregulation of potential targets through network pharmacology analysis.

MATERIALS AND METHODS: Liquid chromatography-tandem mass spectrometry profiling combined with network pharmacology predicted therapeutic targets and pathways. Male Sprague-Dawley rats received intracerebroventricular dimethyl sulfoxide 25 min before ischemic stroke induction, followed by intragastric YZR extract (0.8 g/kg) administered during the early subacute phase (D+E-YZR), delayed subacute phase (D+D-YZR), or both the early and delayed subacute phases (D+T-YZR).

RESULTS: Through network pharmacology-based prediction, hypoxia-inducible factor-1α (HIF-1α), vascular endothelial growth factor-A (VEGF-A), and matrix metalloproteinase-9 (MMP-9) signaling pathways are potential targets of YZR extract on angiogenesis in subacute ischemic stroke. D+T-YZR treatment ameliorated neurological deficits; significantly upregulated the expression of phospho-p38 mitogen-activated protein kinase (p-p38 MAPK)/p38 MAPK (1.9-fold), HIF-1α (1.8-fold), nuclear factor E2-related factor 2 (Nrf2) (2.5-fold), VEGF-A (2.3-fold), VEGF receptor 2 (2.7-fold), von Willebrand factor (1.9-fold), stromal cell derived factor-1 (SDF-1) (2.1-fold), C-X-C chemokine receptor type 4 (2.2-fold), angiopoietin-2 (Ang-2) (2.1-fold), Tie2 (2.6-fold), CD105 (1.7-fold), fibroblast growth factor 2 (FGF-2) (2.8-fold), MMP-9 (2.2-fold), nerve growth factor (NGF) (2.4-fold), synapsin 1 (5.4-fold), microtubule-associated protein 2 (3.3-fold), postsynaptic density 95 (1.7-fold), neuronal nuclei (NeuN) (2.3-fold), growth-associated protein 43 (1.8-fold), VEGF-A/CD105 (4.2-fold), and VEGF-A/NeuN (2.5-fold); and downregulated Ang-1 (0.5-fold) expression in the cortical ischemic boundary zone (IBZ). Treatment with the HIF-1α inhibitor 2-methoxyestradiol and the Nrf2 inhibitor ML385 tended to attenuate the effects of D+T-YZR treatment on angiogenesis and neuronal preservation.

CONCLUSION: YZR extract appeared to promote neurological recovery during both the early and delayed subacute phases of ischemic stroke. This treatment promoted angiogenesis and preserved neurons, with the possible involvement of the upregulation of p38 MAPK-associated HIF-1α/Nrf2/VEGF-A-mediated SDF-1/Ang-2/CD105 and FGF-2/MMP-9/NGF signaling in the cortical IBZ at 28 days post-stroke.

articles.title: Isodon rosthornii accelerates wound healing via dual antimicrobial activity and NF-κB/MAPK suppression.
articles.abstract:
ETHNOPHARMACOLOGICAL RELEVANCE: Isodon rosthornii (Diels) Kudo is a traditional medicinal plant used by the Yi, Miao and Hui peoples in southwestern China to treat traumatic injuries and bruises, conditions often complicated by microbial infection and inflammation. However, its wound-healing potential and mechanisms remain scientifically unvalidated.

AIM OF THE STUDY: To investigate the wound-healing activity of the bioactive fraction of I. rosthornii (IRE), identify and quantify its key bioactive constituents, and elucidate the underlying antimicrobial and anti-inflammatory mechanisms in non-infected and infected wound settings.

MATERIALS AND METHODS: IRE was characterized by UHPLC-Q-TOF-MS and standardized by HPLC-DAD. Network pharmacology and molecular docking were used to predict active compounds and targets. Antimicrobial activity against Staphylococcus aureus, Staphylococcus epidermidis and Cutibacterium acnes was evaluated. Anti-inflammatory mechanisms were investigated in LPS-stimulated RAW 264.7 macrophages. Wound healing efficacy was assessed in rat excisional and S. aureus-infected wound models, including early inflammatory time-point analysis.

RESULTS: UHPLC-Q-TOF-MS identified 150 compounds, predominantly kaurane diterpenoids and flavonoids; oridonin and nodosin were confirmed and quantified. Network pharmacology predicted enrichment in NF-κB and MAPK pathways. IRE exhibited bactericidal activity against all tested skin pathogens, inhibited biofilm formation, and disrupted membrane integrity. In macrophages, IRE suppressed NO production and pro-inflammatory cytokine release, and attenuated NF-κB and MAPK phosphorylation. In vivo, IRE accelerated wound closure, enhanced collagen deposition, and reduced macrophage infiltration. Notably, in S. aureus-infected wounds, IRE reduced bacterial burden and improved healing, with anti-inflammatory effects evident at an early stage. Head-to-head comparison confirmed that oridonin and nodosin contribute to but only partially account for the extract's activity.

CONCLUSION: Isodon rosthornii extract promotes wound healing through combined antimicrobial and anti-inflammatory actions associated with reduced NF-κB and MAPK activation. These findings provide scientific support for its traditional use and support its further development as a topical wound-healing agent.

articles.title: Morphological and Behavioural Predictors of Motor Laterality in Domestic Horses: A Cross-Sectional Field Study.
articles.abstract: Motor laterality in horses affects performance, training, and welfare. A simple morphological marker for laterality would help riders, trainers, and veterinarians identify likely locomotor asymmetries early. This study tested whether observable morphological and behavioural characteristics were associated with rider-perceived motor laterality in domestic horses, using a cross-sectional observational field study design conducted in the Blida and Algiers regions of Algeria. The study included 100 regularly ridden domestic horses. Mane orientation, facial whorl characteristics, standing curvature, masticatory laterality, mouth hardness side, spontaneous body bending, and preferred limb use were recorded. Experienced riders assessed two laterality outcomes: preferred forelimb at walk departure (dep1) and ease of canter departure (dep2). Univariable and multivariable analyses tested associations between recorded characteristics and laterality outcomes. Mane orientation was the strongest predictor of laterality (p < 0.001): right-maned horses were predominantly right-lateralised (dep1: 91.1%; dep2: 78.7%), and left-maned horses were mainly left-lateralised (dep1: 89.1%; dep2: 81.1%). In multivariable analysis, mane orientation was the sole independent predictor (dep1 OR = 83.71; dep2 OR = 15.91; GEE OR = 32.12, 95% CI 13.30-77.61). Model discrimination was excellent (AUC = 0.91). Masticatory laterality and mouth hardness side showed significant univariable associations but were not independent predictors. Facial whorl traits, age, breed, discipline, and sex showed no significant associations. The cross-sectional design prevents causal inference. Laterality outcomes relied on rider perception rather than objective kinematic measurements, which introduces possible observer bias. Longitudinal and biomechanical validation remains needed. Mane orientation is a robust, non-invasive indicator of inherent motor laterality in domestic horses and can be used by riders, trainers, and veterinarians to anticipate locomotor asymmetries without specialised equipment. Longitudinal and kinematic studies are required to confirm causality.

articles.title: Multimorbidity patterns and temporal trends of chronic diseases among community-dwelling older adults: Repeated cross-sectional surveys from 2022 to 2024.
articles.abstract: This study examined short-term trends in the prevalence of major chronic diseases, multimorbidity patterns, and of healthy aging levels among older adults participating in free health checkups in Longhua District, Shenzhen, from 2022 to 2024. Using random sampling, 10,000 participants were selected annually from the elderly health management information system, and both crude and age-standardized rates were calculated. Changes in prevalence were assessed using the Mantel-Haenszel test and multivariable logistic regression, while multimorbidity patterns were evaluated through network analysis and latent class analysis. After age standardization, the risks of hypertension (OR = 0.80, 95%CI: 0.75-0.85) and diabetes (OR = 0.88, 95%CI: 0.82-0.94) significantly decreased (both p < 0.001), whereas the risks of nonalcoholic fatty liver disease (OR = 1.11, 95%CI: 1.05-1.18) and stroke (OR = 2.67, 95%CI: 1.58-4.70) significantly increased (both p < 0.001). Subgroup analyses revealed that the oldest-old aged 70-79 years achieved the favorable control of hypertension and diabetes, while the prevalence of fatty liver disease rose significantly across normal-weight, overweight, and obese individuals. The centrality of diabetes and central obesity within the multimorbidity network increased in 2024, and the median healthy aging index improve compared with 2022 (p < 0.001). In conclusion, although notable progress were observed in hypertension and diabetes management among older adults in this district, the rising burdens of fatty liver disease and stroke underscore the urgent need for enhanced early screening and targeted intervention for metabolic diseases and stroke, with particular emphasis on metabolic health management in individuals aged under 70 years and those who are overweight.

articles.title: Cat Stress Score and hair cortisol concentrations are not associated with subclinical hypertrophic cardiomyopathy in cats.
articles.abstract: Hypertrophic cardiomyopathy (HCM) is a common heart disease in domestic cats, but most lack an identifiable cause. This prospective case-control study tested the hypothesis that chronic stress predisposes cats to HCM. Ten cats with echocardiographically confirmed subclinical HCM were compared with 10 healthy cats, HCM-negative cats matched for husbandry, age, sex, and neuter status. Stress was assessed via visual Cat-Stress-Score and hair cortisol concentrations, measured using an enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay from full-length hair samples collected from the lumbar region. Cat-Stress-Scores did not differ between groups across four time points (median 23.3 in the HCM group [range: 17.8-34.0] versus median 25.5 in the control group [range: 21.8-29.2], P = 0.241). Likewise, hair cortisol concentrations did not differ between groups (median 0.25ng/mL [range: 0.15-0.35] in the HCM group and median 0.19ng/mL [range: 0.09-0.29] in the control group, P = 0.267). In conclusion, cats with pre-existing subclinical HCM did not display greater stress than healthy controls on the measures of stress assessed.

articles.title: Changes in small airway function following Dupilumab initiation for type 2 COPD - a prospective multicenter study.
The impact of pretreatment HBs-Ag levels on response to interferon therapy in chronic hepatitis D patients.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Hepatitis D virus (HDV) infection is closely associated with hepatitis B virus (HBV) infection. Given the virological dependence of HDV on HBV for its replication, quantitative HBsAg levels have been considered as potential predictors of treatment outcomes. This study aims to investigate the actual role of pretreatment HBsAg levels as predictors of treatment response to Peg-IFNα therapy in chronic hepatitis D patients.

METHODS: A retrospective analysis was conducted on 42 patients with chronic hepatitis D who had received a 48-week course of Peg-IFNα therapy (180 μg weekly). All of these patients were positive for HBsAg, anti-HDV, and HDV-RNA. Sustained virological response (SVR) was defined as undetectable HDV-RNA (<100 copies/mL) at 24 weeks subsequent to treatment completion (week 72). End-of-treatment (EOT) response was defined as undetectable HDV-RNA at week 48. Baseline quantitative HBsAg levels were measured using the Architect HBsAg assay. Statistical analyses included t-tests, Mann-Whitney U tests, Chi-square tests, and ROC analysis.

RESULTS: Out of the 42 patients, 25 (59.5%) had available SVR data at week 72. Fourteen of them (56.0%) achieved SVR and 11 (44.0%) were non-responders. The mean baseline HBsAg level was 2972 IU/mL (±1208.8 SD). The t-test showed no significant difference in mean HBsAg levels between SVR responders (2789.4 IU/mL ±1421.8 SD) and non-responders (3185.2 IU/mL ±801.5 SD; p = 0.412). ROC analysis for SVR yielded an AUC of 0.589 (95% CI: 0.381-0.797). For EOT response, the AUC was 0.606 (95% CI: 0.421-0.791). Even though exploratory quartile analysis for EOT response revealed a significant association (p = 0.008), given the multiplicity of comparisons, this finding should be interpreted with caution.

CONCLUSION: Baseline HBsAg levels do not predict SVR at 24 weeks post-treatment. The predictive value for EOT response is limited (AUC 0.606). Quantitative HBsAg testing alone is unlikely to provide sufficient predictive accuracy for clinical decision-making in CHD. Sustained HBsAg decline during treatment may provide a perusasive rationale for personalized treatment duration.

articles.title: Culture-confirmed brucellosis presenting with acute kidney injury and multi-organ dysfunction.
articles.abstract: Brucellosis is a widespread zoonosis caused by Gram-negative Brucella coccobacilli. Renal involvement, particularly acute kidney injury (AKI), is uncommon. A 47-year-old construction worker with livestock exposure and raw milk consumption presented with intermittent fever, pedal edema, hematuria, and AKI. He subsequently developed presumed Brucella endocarditis, rapidly progressive glomerulonephritis, and multiorgan dysfunction. Brucella melitensis (B. melitensis), bacteremia was confirmed by prolonged blood culture and PCR, supported by positive Brucella serology. Despite targeted antimicrobial and supportive therapy, the patient died. This case highlights brucellosis as an important differential diagnosis for AKI in endemic regions and its potential to cause fatal multisystem disease.

articles.title: Ex vivo functional immune alterations in ICU patients with Legionnaires' Disease, a proof-of-concept study.
articles.journal: International journal of infectious diseases : IJID : official publication of the International Society for Infectious Diseases
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: Legionnaires' disease (LD), caused by Legionella pneumophila intracellular bacterium, leads to intensive care unit (ICU) admission in 20-40% of cases. While ICU-LD patients display lung injury or septic shock, their functional immune response remains poorly understood. This proof-of-concept study assessed ex vivo immune gene expression in ICU-LD and non-ICU-LD patients.

METHODS: Whole blood from ICU-LD (n=6), non-ICU-LD (n=8), LD-unrelated septic shock (n=14), and healthy volunteers (n=9) was stimulated with lipopolysaccharide (LPS). Expression of 93 immune-related genes was quantified using nCounter (NanoString Technologies) and expressed relative to healthy volunteers. Functional enrichment analyses were performed using the STRING database.

RESULTS: ICU-LD patients displayed a 1.6-fold higher number of less induced genes (35/93 vs 22/93) and lower gene expression (median log2(FC): -1.9 vs -1.2, p=0.0011) than non-ICU-LD. Top five pathways identified as enriched in ICU-LD but not in non-ICU-LD patients were cellular response to LPS, regulation of IFN-β production, I-κB/NF-κB complex, IFN regulatory factor complex, and TRAF6-mediated NF-κB activation.

CONCLUSIONS: Ex vivo immune gene expression alterations were found in LD patients, particularly in ICU-LD patients. ICU-LD patients displayed lower expression of genes involved in crucial pathways for Legionella replication control. These preliminary findings support further studies to evaluate the impact of LD patients' immune response on disease severity.

articles.title: Hazard Characterization and Dietary Risk Assessment of Pentachlorothiophenol in Food Using Health-Based Guidance Values Based on a Read-Across Approach.
articles.abstract: Pentachlorothiophenol is a persistent organic pollutant for which no health-based guidance values have been established. This study presents the first hazard characterization and dietary risk assessment of PCTP in food. A provisional reference dose (RfD) of 0.001 mg/kg-BW/day was derived using a read-across approach from hexachlorobenzene, incorporating quantitative human biomonitoring data and standard uncertainty factors. Dietary exposure was estimated by integrating PCTP occurrence data from 870 Korean food samples with consumption patterns from the Korea National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey (2019-2021, n=18,895). Owing to low detection frequency, non-detected concentrations were imputed using robust regression on order statistics (ROS), and exposure estimates were interpreted considering this uncertainty. Mean estimated daily intakes ranged from 6.59 ng/kg-BW/day in adults aged ≥65 years to 22.5 ng/kg-BW/day in children aged 1-2 years. The highest estimated exposure occurred in children aged 1-2 years at the 95th percentile, reaching 41.3 ng/kg-BW/day, approximately 24 times lower than the provisional RfD of 1000 ng/kg-BW/day. Hazard quotients were below 4.13% across age groups and scenarios. Agricultural products were primary contributors, followed by livestock and fishery products. Under the evaluated exposure scenarios, estimated dietary PCTP exposure in Korea remained below the provisional screening benchmark for all age groups. However, reliance on read-across methodology and extensive non-detects necessitate PCTP-specific toxicological studies and continued monitoring to refine risk conclusions.

articles.title: Prognostic Implications of Right Ventricular-Pulmonary Arterial Coupling Derived from Right Ventricular Strain in Secondary Tricuspid Regurgitation.
articles.journal: Journal of the American Society of Echocardiography : official publication of the American Society of Echocardiography
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Right ventricular (RV)-pulmonary arterial (PA) coupling is a key determinant of prognosis in moderate and severe secondary tricuspid regurgitation (TR), reflecting the complex interplay between RV contractility and afterload. RV free wall longitudinal strain (RVFWLS) provides a less angle- and load-dependent estimate of RV contractility than tricuspid annular plane systolic excursion (TAPSE). This study evaluated the prognostic utility of the RVFWLS/pulmonary artery systolic pressure (PASP) ratio in secondary TR, its association with excess mortality relative to a matched general population, and whether it provides incremental value beyond the established TAPSE/PASP ratio.

METHODS: A total of 1,007 patients (71 [IQR 62-78] years, 51% male) were followed up for the endpoint of all-cause mortality from the diagnosis of moderate or severe TR.

RESULTS: Over a median follow-up of 59 (IQR 19 to 100) months, 564 (56%) patients died. In a comprehensive multivariable model, the RVFWLS/PASP ratio remained independently associated with all-cause mortality (adjusted HR 1.13 per 0.10 decrease below 0.60, 95% CI 1.07 to 1.19, P<0.0001) and was associated with substantial excess mortality when compared to the matched general population, with spline curve analysis showing increased mortality beginning at values <0.60. The LR χ2 test for nested models demonstrated that the RVFWLS/PASP ratio added incremental prognostic value to models including the TAPSE/PASP ratio (P<0.0001).

CONCLUSION: The RVFWLS/PASP ratio is independently associated with mortality in patients with moderate and severe secondary TR, identifies patients with substantial excess mortality relative to the general population, and adds incremental prognostic value over the TAPSE/PASP ratio, highlighting its potential as a more precise non-invasive marker of RV-PA coupling.

articles.title: Scottish Airways Research Network (SARN) Delphi Consensus on pre-biologic assessment, clinical remission and post-remission management in severe asthma.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Scotland's severe asthma multidisciplinary teams and prescribing recommendations may contribute to variation in biologic decisions. We sought expert consensus on pre-biologic assessment, clinical remission and post-remission management through the Scottish Airways Research Network (SARN).

METHODS: A scientific committee developed 28 statements across these three domains. Thirty specialists from 15 centres rated statements using a five-point Likert scale. Consensus was predefined as >75% agreeing or strongly agreeing. Statements requiring revision were considered in Round 2.

RESULTS: Twenty-four panellists completed Round 1 (80% response), achieving consensus on 15/28 statements (53.6%); 23 completed Round 2 (76.7% response), achieving consensus on 10/13 revised statements (76.9%). Pre-biologic assessment should include treatment optimisation, comprehensive phenotyping, type 2 biomarkers, exacerbation history, comorbidities and patient characteristics. Clinical remission should generally be assessed after at least 12 months and comprise freedom from maintenance oral corticosteroids, absent or minimal symptoms, no severe exacerbations, stable lung function, normalised asthma-related quality of life, and patient-healthcare professional agreement. Improved lung function, reduced airway inflammation and treatment burden, and normalised airway hyperresponsiveness were desirable but not mandatory. No consensus was reached on a specific Asthma Control Questionnaire threshold for remission or restricting biologic access among current smokers not participating in smoking cessation. Dosing-interval extension or discontinuation should not be routine but may be considered for selected patients with sustained remission under specialist supervision, shared decision-making, close monitoring and a rapid restart plan.

CONCLUSION: This Scottish Delphi study provides a pragmatic framework to support equitable, consistent decisions on pre-biologic assessment, remission and treatment de-escalation.

articles.title: Ten years of experience with pediatric palliative extubation in a Brazilian pediatric hospital: a retrospective analysis.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To describe the clinical characteristics and outcomes of pediatric patients undergoing palliative extubation (PE) and identify factors associated with in-hospital death.

METHODS: This retrospective cohort study included pediatric patients who underwent PE between April 2014 and May 2023. Demographic and clinical variables were assessed, including diagnosis, duration of mechanical ventilation, time between decision-making and extubation, timing and location of extubation, medications used, catecholamine use before extubation, symptoms, treatments instituted, and hospital outcome. Descriptive and comparative analyses were performed according to hospital outcome. Time to outcome was evaluated using Kaplan-Meier survival analysis, with comparisons by the log-rank test.

RESULTS: Forty-one patients were included, with a median age of 2.67 years; 51.2% were male, and 90% had neurological impairment secondary to the underlying disease. Most patients underwent PE in the intensive care unit; 73.2% had endotracheal tubes, and 68.3% died in hospital. Median mechanical ventilation duration was 24 days; median time between decision-making and extubation was 1 day; and median time from PE to in-hospital death was 31.2 hours. Symptoms after extubation were less frequent among patients receiving opioids and/or benzodiazepines before extubation (p=0.07). The main symptoms were dyspnea and pain. Dyspnea and opioid use after extubation were associated with in-hospital death. Time to death was shorter among patients receiving catecholamines within 72 hours before PE or morphine and/or benzodiazepines after extubation.

CONCLUSIONS: This study provides clinical and epidemiological information on pediatric PE. Findings should be interpreted cautiously given the small sample size.

articles.title: Pulmonary arterial volume and mortality in smokers without chronic obstructive pulmonary disease.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Pulmonary vascular remodelling is a recognised consequence of chronic tobacco exposure and may have prognostic associations even without airway obstruction. The association between the extraparenchymal pulmonary artery (ePA) and all-cause mortality in current and ex-smokers without COPD has not been demonstrated and replicated in large cohort studies.

STUDY DESIGN AND METHODS: Retrospective analysis of prospective data from the COPDGene cohort, with validation in the SUMMIT lung cancer screening trial. ePA volume and lung volume were measured on chest CT using automated deep learning-based segmentation. All-cause mortality risk was estimated using Cox proportional hazards models, adjusted for age, gender, body mass index, smoking status, pack-years, emphysema extent, Charlson Comorbidity Index, ILA presence, and FEV1.

RESULTS: 4,719 participants without COPD were included in the discovery COPDGene cohort (median age 56 [51-63] years, 50% male) and 3,391 in the SUMMIT validation cohort (median age 64 [59-69] years, 61% male). There were 600 deaths (13%; 39,531 person-years) in COPDGene and 214 deaths (6.3%; 16,629 person-years) in SUMMIT. Each one-standard-deviation (∼25mL) increase in ePA volume was independently associated with all-cause mortality in COPDGene (aHR 1.42 [1.25-1.60], p<0.001) and SUMMIT (aHR 1.23 [1.07-1.42], p=0.003). A parsimonious, ridge-regularised multivariable model developed in COPDGene showed good discrimination (C-index 0.70 [0.65-0.74]) and calibration (integrated calibration index 2.1% [1.3-6.4]) when validated in SUMMIT.

INTERPRETATION: Increasing ePA volume in current and ex-smokers without COPD is associated with all-cause mortality and could represent a candidate imaging marker for cohort enrichment in studies of pulmonary vasculopathy, although this requires prospective validation.

TRIAL REGISTRATION: N/A.

articles.title: Infant wheeze phenotypes do not establish a preventable trajectory to childhood asthma.
Short and long-term outcomes of intermediate-high risk pulmonary embolism treated with catheter-directed reperfusion therapy versus anticoagulation.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Treatment of intermediate-high risk pulmonary embolism (PE) with catheter directed therapy remains a topic of controversy. It is unknown if long-term post-hospitalization outcomes of these patients are improved compared to anticoagulation.

RESEARCH QUESTION: What is the comparative effectiveness of catheter-directed reperfusion therapy versus conventional anticoagulation on both short- and long-term outcomes among patients with intermediate-high risk PE?

STUDY DESIGN AND METHODS: This was a retrospective cohort study of hospitalized patients in the United States with intermediate-high risk pulmonary embolism between 2010 and 2024 from a multi-institutional aggregated electronic health record database. Patients were categorized as receiving catheter-directed intervention (CDI) or conventional anticoagulation and followed for 30-day mortality, bleeding and procedural complications (short-term outcomes) and, among those who survived discharge, for readmission related to heart failure or respiratory failure, oxygen dependence, and pulmonary hypertension related diagnosis (long-term outcomes). Overlap weighting was used to balance characteristics between patients in both groups and weighted hazard ratios were calculated.

RESULTS: After application of a specific phenotype definition integrating diagnosis codes, vital signs, and laboratory biomarkers to identify patients with intermediate high-risk PE in a large-scale data set, a total of 50,614 patients were included in the analysis of short-term outcomes and 49,122 were included in the analysis of post-discharge outcomes. CDI was associated with a lower hazard of death in both crude (HR 0.56; 95% CI 0.53-0.59, p < 0.001) and adjusted comparisons (aHR 0.70; 95% CI 0.66-0.73, p < 0.001). Although there was no increase in CTEPH rates (aHR 1.05; 95% CI 1.00-1.10, p = 0.057), long-term outcomes favored CDI including lower rates of readmission for heart failure (aHR 0.79; 95% CI 0.75-0.83, p < 0.001), readmission for respiratory failure (aHR 0.85; 95% CI 0.81-0.90, p < 0.001), and lower chronic oxygen usage (aHR 0.69; 95% CI 0.65-0.74, p < 0.001).

INTERPRETATION: Among patients with intermediate-high risk pulmonary embolism, CDI was associated with improved short- and long-term survival compared to anticoagulation alone. These findings suggest a potential benefit of CDI in intermediate-high risk PE and support the need for randomized trials powered for long-term, patient-centered outcomes.

articles.title: Exercise to enhance antipsychotic effectiveness and mitigate metabolic harm: systematic review and meta-analysis.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Antipsychotics are first-line treatments for schizophrenia and related psychotic disorders but are frequently accompanied by cardiometabolic adverse effects (weight gain, hypertension, dyslipidaemia, hyperglycaemia). We assessed whether supervised exercise interventions enhance psychopathology outcomes and reduce antipsychotic-related metabolic harm in adults receiving antipsychotic treatment medication.

DESIGN: Systematic review and meta-analysis.

DATA SOURCES: We searched PubMed, Web of Science, and Scopus following PRISMA 2020 (PROSPERO CRD420251139904). Randomised controlled trials (RCTs) published since 2000 that tested supervised exercise in people receiving antipsychotics were eligible.

ELIGIBILITY CRITERIA FOR SELECTING STUDIES: Two reviewers selected studies using PICOS criteria, assessed methodological quality with the Revised Cochrane risk-of-bias tool for randomised trials (RoB 2), and pooled effects with random-effects models, expressed as mean differences (MD) with 95% CIs. The certainty of evidence was assessed with GRADE.

RESULTS: Twenty-eight studies (n = 1119) and four additional analyses met inclusion criteria. Exercise significantly improved negative symptoms (MD -3·078, 95% CI -4·457 to -1·699; p < 0·001), general psychopathology (-2·178, -4·140 to -0·216, p = 0·034), and PANSS total score (-7·069, -13·290 to -0·849; p = 0·030). Effects on positive symptoms were not significant (-1·220, -2·462 to 0·022; p = 0·053). Exercise reduced body weight (-1·620, -3·080 to -0·159; p = 0.034), body fat percentage (-1·250, -2·174 to -0·327; p = 0·020) and waist circumference (-1·420, -2·646 to -0·195; p = 0·032), with no material change in BMI. No significant effects were observed for systolic, diastolic blood pressure or fasting glucose. Lipid outcomes were largely null, with limited and inconsistent evidence, including a small increase in total cholesterol. Based on GRADE assessment, the certainty of evidence was moderate for negative symptoms, general psychopathology, body weight, body fat percentage, and waist circumference, with low to very low for the remaining outcomes.

CONCLUSION: Supervised exercise may be a beneficial adjunct to antipsychotic treatment, improving core psychopathology, particularly negative symptoms, and favourably shifting body composition by reducing adiposity and central fat, although the magnitude of change did not reach clinically meaningful thresholds. High-quality, adequately powered RCTs using multicomponent exercise and comprehensive metabolic endpoints are needed to determine effects on blood pressure, lipid profile, and glucose regulation.

FUNDING: None.

articles.title: Cognitive performance and self-reported physical exercise in bipolar disorder: A cross-sectional analysis of pre-randomization screening data from an ongoing randomized controlled trial.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Bipolar Disorder (BD) is frequently associated with persistent cognitive deficits that significantly impair functionality and quality of life. While physical exercise (PE) has shown promise in improving cognition in healthy individuals and those with other psychiatric conditions, most consistently in major depressive disorder and schizophrenia, its specific impact on individuals with BD remains under-investigated. This study aimed to investigate the association between self-reported regular physical exercise and cognitive performance in individuals with Bipolar Disorder.

METHODS: This study consists of a cross-sectional analysis of pre-randomization screening data from an ongoing randomized controlled trial. The analysis included 108 euthymic BD individuals (aged 18-55) recruited from the outpatient clinic at the University of São Paulo Medical School (PROMAN). Participants were allocated into either the Exercise Group (n = 48), defined by self-reported engagement in regular structured physical exercise at least twice a week, and the No-Exercise Group (n = 60); exercise status was ascertained with a brief in-house checklist. Cognitive performance was assessed using the Screen for Cognitive Impairment in Psychiatry (SCIP). Secondary measures included mood symptoms (MADRS and YMRS) and pharmacological treatment profiles. Effect sizes were estimated with Cohen's d, and a Bonferroni-corrected threshold of α = 0.0033 was applied to the 15 comparisons performed.

RESULTS: The Exercise group demonstrated significantly higher SCIP Total Scores compared to the No-Exercise group (64.63 ± 9.19 vs. 56.50 ± 7.84; p < 0.001, d = 0.95). Significant advantages for the exercise group were observed in sub-domains related to verbal learning (p = 0.010) and working memory (p = 0.002); the total score and working memory remained significant after Bonferroni correction, whereas verbal learning did not. Notably, the No-Exercise group had a significantly higher usage of stimulants (27.5% vs. 4.5%, p = 0.029), while the Exercise group had a higher prevalence of anticonvulsant use (45.5% vs. 20%, p = 0.035); neither medication difference survived correction.

LIMITATIONS: Exercise status was self-reported and dichotomous, with no data on intensity, duration or modality, and no demographic or clinical covariates were available for adjustment.

CONCLUSION: Regular physical exercise appears to be associated with superior global cognition, verbal learning, and working memory in individuals with BD. These findings, derived from the screening phase of an ongoing trial, suggest that PE may be a promising adjunctive strategy for neurocognitive rehabilitation, although the cross-sectional design precludes any causal inference.

articles.title: First-line durvalumab and tremelimumab in poor-prognosis unresectable hepatocellular carcinoma: Phase IIIb single-arm SIERRA study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND & AIMS: Clinical trials in unresectable hepatocellular carcinoma (uHCC) often exclude patients with poor prognostic factors, including impaired liver function, poor functional status or main trunk portal vein thrombosis (Vp4). The dual immune checkpoint inhibitor regimen STRIDE (Single Tremelimumab Regular Interval Durvalumab) is a standard-of-care treatment for first-line uHCC. The phase IIIb SIERRA (NCT05883644) study previously reported early safety of STRIDE in participants of poor prognosis. Here, we present safety and efficacy results from the primary analysis of the SIERRA study.

METHODS: Adults with uHCC with either Child-Pugh B7/B8 liver function (Child-Pugh B7/B8 cohort), Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group performance status 2 (ECOG PS 2 cohort) or Vp4 (Vp4 cohort) were enrolled. All participants received STRIDE (tremelimumab 300 mg plus durvalumab 1500 mg once, followed by durvalumab 1500 mg every 4 weeks) until disease progression, unacceptable toxicity or withdrawal. Primary endpoints were Grade 3 or 4 adverse events possibly related to study treatment within 6 months of treatment initiation (Grade 3/4 PRAEs ≤6 months) and objective response rate (ORR; data cut-off: 22 September 2025).

RESULTS: In total, 111 participants were included (Child-Pugh B7/B8 n = 44, ECOG PS 2 n = 47, Vp4 n = 20). The incidence of Grade 3/4 PRAEs ≤6 months (95% confidence interval [CI]) was 19.8% (12.9-28.5): Child-Pugh B7/B8, 18.2% (8.2-32.7); ECOG PS 2, 19.1% (9.1-33.3); and Vp4, 25.0% (8.7-49.1). ORR (95% CI) was 14.4% (8.5-22.4): Child-Pugh B7/B8, 6.8% (1.4-18.7); ECOG PS 2, 21.3% (10.7-35.7); and Vp4, 15.0% (3.2-37.9).

CONCLUSIONS: SIERRA safety and efficacy findings were indicative of a favourable risk-benefit profile for STRIDE in this participant population with a high unmet need.

IMPACT AND IMPLICATIONS: Participants with poor prognosis (e.g. Child-Pugh B/C, Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group performance status >1 or main trunk portal vein thrombosis [Vp4]) remain underrepresented in global, phase III trials despite comprising up to 65% of patients with unresectable hepatocellular carcinoma (uHCC) in clinical practice. To address this unmet need, the phase IIIb SIERRA study (NCT05883644) evaluated STRIDE (Single Tremelimumab Regular Interval Durvalumab) in participants with poor prognostic factors. Safety and efficacy findings as per the co-primary endpoints are indicative of a favourable risk-benefit profile for STRIDE in this participant population with a high unmet need, with an incidence of Grade 3 or 4 PRAEs within 6 months of 19.8% and ORR of 14.4% in the total population. This is the first prospective interventional study to provide data informing the safety and efficacy of STRIDE in patients with uHCC in a previously underrepresented population of poor prognosis that are excluded from other phase III trials.

CLINICAL TRIAL NUMBER: NCT05883644.

articles.title: Proceedings from the 2025 International Consensus Meeting on Orthopedic Infections: the definition of Shoulder Periprosthetic Joint infection.
articles.journal: Journal of shoulder and elbow surgery
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Periprosthetic joint infection (PJI) remains one of the greatest diagnostic and treatment challenges facing shoulder surgeons and their patients. A definition for shoulder PJI was established by the 2018 International Consensus Meeting (ICM) on Orthopedic Infections, but the selection and weighting of its minor criteria relied largely on expert opinion. The purpose of this study was to present an updated, evidence-based definition of shoulder PJI generated by the 2025 ICM Shoulder Group.

METHODS: The 2025 ICM Shoulder Group, an international panel of shoulder surgeons and infectious disease specialists, used a modified Delphi process informed by 86 systematic reviews and by a predictive statistical model derived from the American Shoulder and Elbow Surgeons (ASES) Multicenter Revision Arthroplasty and PJI Group dataset to reconsider the 2018 ICM definition of shoulder PJI, including its major criteria, minor criteria, and diagnostic categories.

RESULTS: The delegates voted to eliminate organism virulence from the definition and to retain gross intra-articular purulence and presence of a sinus tract as the two criteria defining Definite PJI. The Minor Criteria were revised to include erythema, unexpected wound drainage, elevated erythrocyte sedimentation rate (ESR) and C-reactive protein (CRP), elevated synovial neutrophil percentage, positive frozen section, radiographic humeral osteolysis, intraoperative humeral loosening, and positive culture, each statistically weighted using the predictive model. Non-definite PJI was categorized by summed minor criteria score as High likelihood (≥13 points), Moderate likelihood (7-12 points), Unknown (1-6 points), or No PJI (0 points). The final definition achieved unanimous delegate consensus (51 of 51 delegates; 100% agreement; super majority, strong consensus).

CONCLUSIONS: The 2025 ICM definition of shoulder PJI represents an evidence-informed evolution of the 2018 definition, combining statistical modeling of prospective multicenter data with structured expert consensus. The definition is expected to continue to evolve as further shoulder-specific data become available.

articles.title: Microplastics and Nanoplastics as a Novel Cardiovascular Risk Factor: A Narrative Review.
articles.abstract: Microplastics and nanoplastics (MNPs) are pervasive environmental contaminants now detected throughout the human cardiovascular system, including atherosclerotic plaques, coronary and carotid arteries, cardiac tissue, peripheral blood, and vascular thrombi. Against the backdrop of cardiovascular disease (CVD) accounting for approximately 17-20 million deaths annually, MNPs have emerged as a candidate modifiable cardiovascular risk factor. In the landmark prospective cohort by Marfella and colleagues (N Engl J Med 2024), MNP-laden carotid plaques conferred a 4.53-fold increased risk of major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE). MNPs were also detected in 80% of human thrombi from patients with myocardial infarction (MI), stroke, and deep vein thrombosis (DVT). Experimental studies link MNPs to cardiovascular toxicity through oxidative stress, NF-κB-mediated inflammation, endothelial senescence and dysfunction, macrophage foam cell formation, and Wnt/β-catenin-mediated cardiac fibrosis. This narrative review synthesizes current evidence linking MNPs to coronary artery disease, myocardial infarction, arrhythmias, heart failure, and thrombosis, and evaluates clinical and public health implications. Standardized detection protocols, large-scale prospective studies, and regulatory action are urgently warranted.

articles.title: Central GHSR inverse agonism by a LEAP2 analog regulates thermometabolic and behavioral responses via catecholamine signaling.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Liver-expressed antimicrobial peptide 2 (LEAP2) is an endogenous GHSR inverse agonist that antagonizes ghrelin-mediated signaling, thereby opposing several of the physiological actions elicited by ghrelin. Evidence indicates that GHSR participates in autonomic, cardiovascular, renal, and psychogenic regulation, interacts with dopaminergic signaling and interplays with adrenergic pathways during sympathetically driven hypertension. Here, we investigated whether catecholaminergic mechanisms mediate behavioral and thermometabolic effects evoked from central GHSR inverse agonism by a LEAP2 analog.

METHODS: Adult male Wistar rats were systemically pretreated with either the tyrosine hydroxylase inhibitor α-methyl-para-tyrosine (AMPT; 200 mg/kg) or the non-selective dopamine receptor antagonist chlorpromazine (CLP; 2 mg/kg) and then centrally pretreated with LEAP2[1-14] (6 nmol) or vehicle. Rats were evaluated across a range of paradigms, including anxiety- and panic-like behaviors, open-field exploration, ingestive activity, treadmill performance with VO₂ recorders and infrared thermography of caudal heat dissipation.

RESULTS: Central LEAP2 analog impaired the expression of anxiety- and panic-like responses and attenuated heat-conservation mechanisms triggered by aversion. Behavioral and food ingestive effects were largely dependent on dopaminergic receptor signaling, whereas thermoregulatory responses during exercise required the entire catecholaminergic pathways inhibited by AMPT.

CONCLUSION: LEAP2 analog regulates specific behavioral and thermometabolic responses through neurobiological mechanisms involving catecholaminergic pathways and dopamine receptors, highlighting central GHSR as a potential pharmacological target for neuroendocrine defense mechanisms.

articles.title: Pterostilbene attenuates cisplatin-induced acute kidney injury by suppressing TLR4/MyD88/NF-κB signaling.
articles.abstract: Cisplatin-induced acute kidney injury (Cis-AKI) is a common and severe dose-limiting complication of cisplatin-based chemotherapy, and effective preventive or therapeutic strategies remain limited. Pterostilbene (PTE), a naturally occurring polyphenolic compound, exhibits potent anti-inflammatory and antioxidant properties; however, its protective effects and underlying mechanisms in Cis-AKI are not fully understood. In this study, we investigated the renoprotective effects of PTE in cisplatin-induced injury using Human proximal tubular epithelial cells (HK-2 cells) and a mouse model of Cis-AKI. In vitro, PTE significantly alleviated cisplatin-induced cytotoxicity, improved cell viability, and attenuated tubular epithelial cell injury. In addition, PTE reduced oxidative stress, suppressed pro-inflammatory cytokine production, and inhibited apoptosis in cisplatin-treated HK-2 cells. In vivo, PTE improved renal function, alleviated tubular histopathological injury, and preserved renal tubular mitochondrial ultrastructure in cisplatin-treated mice. Exploratory transcriptomic screening highlighted TLR4/NF-κB-related signaling as a candidate pathway for further validation. Mechanistically, PTE inhibited TLR4/MyD88/NF-κB activation, whereas both pharmacological activation of TLR4 with Kdo2-Lipid A (KLA) and genetic restoration of TLR4 expression partially reversed the protective effects of PTE against cisplatin-induced inflammation, oxidative stress, apoptosis, and tubular epithelial damage. Collectively, these findings indicate that PTE protects against Cis-AKI, at least in part, through suppression of the TLR4/MyD88/NF-κB signaling cascade, thereby mitigating inflammation, oxidative stress, and apoptosis. These results suggest that PTE represents a promising therapeutic candidate for the prevention and treatment of Cis-AKI.

articles.title: Seladelpar improves liver stiffness in PBC: ASSURE interim analysis.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND & AIMS: Liver stiffness measurement (LSM) by transient elastography can predict clinical outcomes in patients with primary biliary cholangitis (PBC), with ongoing disease activity associated with progressive LSM increases. Seladelpar is a first-in-class approved delpar with demonstrable biochemical and symptom improvements in PBC. We assessed LSM changes, with up to 3 years of seladelpar treatment, in an interim analysis of the ongoing, open-label ASSURE study.

METHODS: Patients with PBC rolled over into ASSURE from the pivotal, placebo-controlled RESPONSE study or enrolled after participation in earlier legacy studies. Patients who received seladelpar 10 mg with ≥1 on-treatment LSM were evaluated (cutoff: January 31, 2025). Patients were grouped by baseline LSM (kPa) into low (<10.7), intermediate (≥10.7 to <16.9), and high (≥16.9) risk. LSM change from baseline (CfB) was evaluated overall and by baseline risk category, with category shifts assessed at Month (M)36. Multivariate analysis identified factors associated with stable/improved versus worsening LSM at M36.

RESULTS: A total of 307 patients were included, with baseline mean (SD) LSM (kPa) of 9.8 (7.4); 72.6% were low-, 16.6% were intermediate-, and 10.7% were high-risk. Among 113 patients with M36 LSMs, median CfB was -3.4% overall and -29.7% among high-risk patients. Most patients (89/113; 78.8%) had stable/improved LSM at M36. Biochemical response at M12 was significantly associated with LSM stability/improvement at M36 (odds ratio [95% CI]: 4.30 [1.35, 13.71] for alkaline phosphatase [ALP] normalization and 4.21 [1.27, 13.92] for ALP >ULN but <1.67× ULN, versus ALP ≥1.67× ULN).

CONCLUSIONS: Most patients with M36 LSMs available showed stable/improved liver stiffness with seladelpar treatment, with reductions observed among high-risk patients. Maintenance or improvement of liver stiffness was associated with biochemical response.

CLINICAL TRIAL NUMBER: NCT03301506 IMPACT AND IMPLICATIONS: Liver stiffness assessed by transient elastography is a prognostic tool reflecting risk of disease progression in patients with PBC. Among patients with baseline liver stiffness (FibroScan®) ≥10 kPa, those with cirrhosis, and those who do not receive adequate treatment, LSM has been observed to increase over time. This interim analysis suggests that long-term treatment with seladelpar, an approved second-line therapy, may lead to stable or improved LSM, with biochemical response associated with LSM stability and improvement. These results build on existing evidence of the efficacy of seladelpar, suggesting its potential to favorably impact disease progression. The results also highlight the importance of ALP reduction to reduce risk of disease progression in patients with PBC.

articles.title: Group B Streptococcus serotype-specific IgG immunity in mother-newborn dyads in South Asian and African countries: a multicountry study, 2016-2018.
articles.journal: Clinical microbiology and infection : the official publication of the European Society of Clinical Microbiology and Infectious Diseases
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To evaluate the sero-epidemiology of maternal and cord blood Group B Streptococcus (GBS) serotype-specific capsular polysaccharide (CPS) immunoglobulin G (IgG) concentrations and transplacental antibody transfer across diverse low-middle income country populations.

METHODS: We conducted a multi-country, cross-sectional study among pregnant women without HIV-1 infection and their newborns across six African (South Africa, Kenya, Mozambique, Ethiopia, Mali, Nigeria) and three South Asian countries (Bhutan, Bangladesh, India). Maternal and cord blood samples were collected at delivery and analyzed using a multiplex immunoassay for serotype-specific CPS GBS IgG.

RESULTS: We analyzed 2,293 mother-newborn dyads. Maternal serotype-specific CPS-IgG concentrations varied significantly by country and serotype. Most women had detectable serotype-specific IgG antibodies, with >95% of participants having detectable antibodies against serotypes II, III, and IV across most countries, whereas lower proportions were observed for serotypes Ib and V. Serotype II demonstrated the most efficient transplacental transfer ratios with GMRs ranging from 0.80 (95% CI 0.74-0.85) in South Africa to 1.16 (95% CI 1.07-1.27) in Bhutan. Transfer was generally lower for other serotypes, particularly in Kenya, where GMRs ranged from 0.51 (95% CI 0.46-0.58) for serotype IV to 0.81 (95% CI 0.73-0.91) for serotype II. The proportions of newborns above the serotype-specific serological thresholds of risk reduction (SToRR) varied widely across countries ranging from 10.0%-56.8% for serotype Ia and 13.5%-68.0% for serotype III. Bangladesh consistently had the highest maternal and cord blood antibody concentrations whereas Bhutan and Ethiopia had the lowest.

CONCLUSIONS: Marked geographic and serotype-specific variability in maternal and neonatal GBS IgG concentration was observed across South Asian and African countries. These findings provide important information on baseline naturally acquired immunity and transplacental antibody transfer, which may inform the evaluation and implementation of maternal GBS vaccines in diverse populations.

articles.title: Immunomodulatory polysaccharides from natural sources: A review focusing on plant, fungal, and algal polysaccharide origins, extraction, mechanisms, and structure-activity relationships.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The rising incidence of immune-related diseases has increased healthcare expenditures. Currently, conventional drugs are limited by high costs, increased infection risk, off-target effects, and other adverse effects. Natural polysaccharides offer an alternative due to their diverse sources, safety, and remarkable immunomodulatory activities. A systematic review of their sources, extraction methods, mechanisms, and structure-activity relationships is lacking.

SCOPE AND METHODS: This paper reviews the progress in research on natural polysaccharides with immunomodulatory properties, and summarizes their sources (plants, fungi, and algae), extraction technologies (conventional versus emerging green techniques), and immunoregulatory mechanisms (encompassing innate/adaptive immune cells, immune organs, and gut immunity, along with associated signaling networks). Moreover, this paper summarizes the structure-activity relationships of these polysaccharides (including molecular weight, monosaccharide composition, glycan chain structure, chemical modifications, and higher-order conformation). This review synthesizes the literature by searching Web of Science, PubMed, and Scopus (literature search last updated in August 2026), summarizes the progress, and discusses future trends.

CONCLUSIONS: Immunomodulatory polysaccharides are mainly derived from plants, algae, and fungi. They regulate immune cells and organs through multiple signaling pathways, thereby controlling immune responses. Although these polysaccharides are diverse, some exhibit specific structure-activity relationships. This review synthesizes structure and activity from various source polysaccharides, elucidates their complex regulatory mechanisms, and summarizes the structure-activity relationships. Despite significant advances in research on the structure and activity of polysaccharides, conformational analysis of polysaccharides in the physiological environment, the application of artificial intelligence in the optimization of green extraction processes, and clinical transformation still need to advance.

articles.title: Poly(lactic-co-glycolic acid) nanoparticle delivery enhances the immunogenicity and anticoccidial activity of recombinant multi-epitope 14EGT protein against multiple chicken Eimeria infections.
articles.abstract: Chicken coccidiosis is frequently caused by single or multiple Eimeria species, whereas protective immunity is largely species-specific. Recombinant multi-epitope proteins derived from conserved Eimeria antigens represent promising candidates for cross-protection against multiple chicken Eimeria species, but their efficacy is often limited by insufficient antigen delivery. In this study, r14EGT, a recombinant multi-epitope protein containing concentrated T-cell epitopes from four conserved Eimeria antigens, including 14-3-3, EF-2, GAPDH, and transhydrogenase, was encapsulated into poly(lactic-co-glycolic acid) (PLGA) nanoparticles to enhance its immunogenicity and anticoccidial activity. The resulting PLGA-r14EGT nanoparticles were approximately 105 nm in diameter with an encapsulation efficiency of 62.46%. In an Eimeria tenella challenge model, PLGA-r14EGT achieved the highest anticoccidial index (ACI) among the tested r14EGT-based formulations and produced the greatest reduction in intestinal lesion scores. Immunization with PLGA-r14EGT also enhanced both cellular and humoral immune responses, as evidenced by increased splenic CD4+ and CD8+ T-cell proportions, elevated IFN-γ, IL-4, and IL-17 A transcription, and higher serum antigen-specific IgY levels. Further optimization identified ocular-nasal immunization with 50 μg PLGA-r14EGT at 0, 7, and 14 days of age as the most effective regimen. Under this schedule, PLGA-r14EGT achieved ACI values of 174.95, 171.75, and 169.72 against Eimeria tenella, Eimeria maxima, and Eimeria acervulina single-species infections, respectively, and 161.13 against mixed infection. These findings indicate that PLGA nanoparticle delivery enhances the biological activity of r14EGT protein and supports its potential for controlling single and mixed Eimeria infections in chickens.

articles.title: A Schiff base-driven pH responsive dual release coating incorporated thyme essential oil nanoemulsion for strawberry preservation.
articles.abstract: Strawberries are susceptible to infection after harvest, resulting in significant losses every year. To address this issue, this paper prepared pH-responsive dual release coatings for preserving strawberries through Schiff base bond in carboxymethyl chitosan (CMCS)/pullulan matrix. The addition of thyme essential oil (TEO) could increase the antifungal activity of CMCS/pullulan composite coating by 94.45%. The addition of vanillin enabled the formation of Schiff base bond with CMCS and enhanced mechanical strength, UV resistance and water vapor resistance of CMCS/pullulan composite film. When strawberries were infected by fungus that gradually form a slightly acidic environment during storage, the Schiff base bond could break to release vanillin and TEO to inhibit fungus growth. Release tests showed that the release profiles of TEO and vanillin were sustained, and the release content of vanillin was 66.91% higher at pH = 5 than pH = 7. Strawberry storage experiment demonstrated that the CMCS/PUL/T/VA group had the best preservation effect, with the lowest decay rate, the highest firmness and better appearance. Soil degradation test confirmed that CMCS/PUL/T/VA films could be completely degraded within 60 d. This paper prepared natural, biodegradable, and antifungal pH-responsive dual release coatings and provided a strategy for the future development of multifunctional pH-responsive packaging.

articles.title: Synergistic construction of low-temperature-resistant, water-retaining, and cushioning hydrogels via 1-s UV curing and ethylene glycol annealing for postharvest fruit protection.
articles.abstract: Hydrogels are promising cushioning materials for fresh produce packaging because of their viscoelasticity, deformability, and energy-dissipation capability. In this study, a UV-curable hydrogel based on methacrylated hyaluronic acid (HAMA) was developed. Through ethylene glycol (EG) annealing, a cushioning material (HAMA-EG) with good low-temperature tolerance and high water retention was fabricated. Systematic characterizations indicated that the hydrogel achieved rapid 1 s UV curing, attributed to approximately 0.69 methacryloyl groups grafted per HA disaccharide unit, which provided sufficient photosensitive crosslinking sites on the HAMA chains. HAMA-EG also exhibited a regular porous structure, good mechanical properties (Young's modulus of 0.28 MPa and compressive strength of 3.85 MPa), and biocompatibility. The incorporation of EG enhanced the material's low-temperature resistance (no freezing at -40 °C) and environmental stability (cumulative weight loss of only 29.41% after 120 h). In addition, HAMA-EG Gel showed enhanced cyclic mechanical stability after environmental pretreatment; after -20 °C freezing, its cyclic mechanical retention remained at 72.52%, compared with 6.43% for HAMA Gel. In simulated vibration and drop transportation tests using peaches as a bruise-sensitive fruit model, HAMA-EG reduced mechanical damage and better maintained fruit quality than commercial cushioning materials. Overall, HAMA-EG enabled rapid curing and forming with good energy dissipation and water-retention properties, thus holding broad application in cushioning protection for fresh produce.

articles.title: Resveratrol protects primary hepatocytes against senescence induced by endogenous toxic metabolites.
articles.abstract: Liver dysfunction rates increase markedly with ageing causing the plasma concentrations of toxic endogenous metabolites to rise. We demonstrated that brief exposure of HepG2 cells in vitro to a liver-derived toxic metabolite cocktail triggers a distinct state of cellular senescence termed senescence induced by liver toxins (SILT). SILT combines classical features of senescence (loss of proliferative capacity, proinflammatory changes, senescence associated β- galactosidase reactivity and cyclin dependent kinase inhibitor upregulation) with a broader loss of essential hepatocyte functions. Immortalised cell lines are valuable models for primary hepatic function but also show important physiological differences. We have extended our analysis to primary hepatocytes and have found that both human and porcine liver cells undergo SILT in vitro when exposed to the concentrations of endogenous toxins typical of liver disease. As in HepG2 cells, SILT in primary hepatocytes was accompanied by loss of albumin production (as measured by ELISA) and urea synthesis (measured biochemically) but was reversible by 5µM resveratrol in a species- and function-dependent manner. Deeper transcriptomic profiling of SILT revealed the activation of stress and inflammatory pathways combined and repression of hepatocyte metabolic programmes. Gene Set Enrichment Analysis demonstrates that the SILT is present in vivo in multiple reference transcriptomic datasets derived from diseased, but not healthy liver. This is consistent with the presence of a population of SILT hepatocytes among the senescent cells found in the ageing organ in vivo. Thus, SILT may contribute to the ultimate failure of liver function which may potentially be delayed by resveratrol treatment.

articles.title: Application of lytic bacteriophages OM982647 and OM982646 individually and in combination for mitigating STEC Escherichia coli O157:H7 in milk, yoghurt, and white soft cheese.
articles.abstract: Shiga toxigenic Escherichia coli (STEC O157:H7), a significant foodborne pathogen linked to dairy products, cause severe hemorrhagic enteritis in human. Nonetheless, the growing demand for natural, clean label and sustainable biocontrol food safety interventions has highlighted bacteriophages as promising biocontrol agents. In this study, the biocontrol efficacy of two lytic bacteriophages (STEC P2 and STEC P4) individually and in cocktail was evaluated against STEC O157:H7 in various dairy matrices (pasteurized milk, yoghurt, and white soft cheese). Coupled with assessing phages stability in cheese manufacturing conditions, and their potential impact on the starter culture activity. The findings revealed that, the phage cocktail (multiplicity of infection; MOI 106) eliminated STEC in milk within 2 h at 25 °C; however, bacterial regrowth was observed after 12 h. In contrast, at refrigeration temperature (4 °C), STEC P2 and the phage cocktail (MOI 106) reduced STEC below the detection limit within 24 h. In yoghurt, individual phages and their cocktail effectively inhibited STEC by the end of processing, without significantly affecting starter culture activity (P > 0.05). Furthermore, in white soft cheese, the phage cocktail (MOI 106) STEC was not detected by the 7th day of storage at 4 °C. Moreover, both phages exhibited high stability under cheese processing conditions (NaCl (3,5,7%), 0.02% CaCl₂, and 0.04% rennet), nevertheless, reductions of 1.04 and 2.05 log₁₀ PFU were observed for P2 and P4, respectively, during the curd formation phase. These findings demonstrate that STEC P2 and P4 phages, particularly when applied as a cocktail, represent effective sustainable compatible biocontrol agents for mitigating STEC O157:H7 in dairy sector.

articles.title: Cytoaura vision: a quantitative imaging platform for real-time assessment of bacterial turbidity and culture dynamics.
articles.abstract: Bacterial growth quantification plays a critical role in antimicrobial susceptibility testing, environmental microbial monitoring, and antimicrobial drug discovery. Here, we describe Cytoaura Vision, a cost-effective label-free imaging platform for quantitative and spatial analysis of bacterial growth in standard 96-well microtiter plates. The system comprises controlled illumination, high-resolution imaging, computational image correction, and automated pixel-intensity analysis. The validation on serial bacterial dilution (P. aeruginosa PAO1) revealed that the image-derived pixel intensity increased in a concentration-dependent manner, supporting the use of the imaging signal as a quantitative readout of the growth-associated turbidity. Time-resolved imaging captured the growth trajectories over 0-270 min, while heatmap and pixel-intensity distribution analyses provided complementary data on the temporal and spatial trends in the image-derived signal. The growth trajectories were further fitted to the Logistic, Gompertz and Modified Gompertz models using goodness-of-fit statistics (R2 and RMSE). For the four experimental groups, the Logistic model achieved R2 values of 0.903, 0.955 and 0.979 respectively, and we compared it against Gompertz and Modified Gompertz models, which yielded R2 values across the corresponding groups. Model suitability was assessed according to goodness-of-fit statistics, whereas AUC offered a cumulative metric reflecting the overall signal exposure during the experiment. The platform was further benchmarked for antibiotic-induced modulation using gentamicin, where the treated cultures exhibited diminished signal accumulation relative to the bacterial control, thereby indirectly assessing the antimicrobial effect within 2-3 h of treatment. These results demonstrate the platform's prowess in resolving growth-associated transitions and antibiotic-mediated suppression through label-free time-resolved imaging. The platform offers a scalable and affordable solution for quantitative microbial growth analysis and has the potential to impact antimicrobial research, compound screening, and other plate-based biological assays.

articles.title: Early outcomes of the Octapro balloon-expandable transcatheter heart valve in an unrestricted cohort of patients with aortic valve stenosis: the MyPro registry.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Data on early outcomes of the novel balloon-expandable (BE) Octapro transcatheter heart valve (THV) in real-world practice are limited. We sought to assess procedural safety and early outcomes of the Octapro in patients with severe native aortic stenosis (AS) undergoing transcatheter aortic valve implantation (TAVI).

METHODS: Between November 2024 and October 2025, consecutive patients with severe AS undergoing TAVI with Octapro in European and Indian centres were enrolled. Primary endpoints were VARC-3 technical success, device success, and early safety at 30-day.

RESULTS: A total of 303 patients were included (age 78.9 ± 7.4 years; bicuspid 13%). VARC-3 technical success was 97%, peri-procedural mortality 0.3% while no procedural stroke or myocardial infarction were reported. In-hospital guidelines-indicated permanent pacemaker implantation (PPI) rate was 13.5%. At discharge mean gradient was 8.4 ± 4.5 mmHg, effective orifice area 1.8 ± 0.3 cm2, while moderate-to-severe paravalvular leak was reported in 3.3% of the patients. At 30-day, device success was 92.4% and early safety 80%. All-cause mortality was 2.6%, stroke 0.3%, and guidelines-indicated PPI 14.2%. Mean gradient remained low (9 ± 4 mmHg). Implantation depth and baseline right bundle branch block (RBBB) were independent predictors of PPI. ROC analysis identified an implantation depth threshold of 4.75 mm associated with increased PPI risk.

CONCLUSIONS: In this real-world registry, the Octapro THV demonstrated high procedural success, favourable early clinical outcomes, and excellent haemodynamic performance. Implantation depth and baseline RBBB were independent predictors of PPI, supporting optimization of implantation technique to mitigate conduction disturbances.

articles.title: Timing of revascularisation in patients undergoing high-risk percutaneous coronary intervention and Transcatheter aortic valve implantation: insights from the ASCoP registry.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Evidence on the management of complex and high-risk coronary artery disease (CAD) in patients undergoing transcatheter aortic valve implantation (TAVI) is still limited. In particular, the optimal timing of percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) relative to TAVI remains uncertain.

METHODS: The ASCop is an observational, multicenter registry that retrospectively enrolled patients with a clinical indication for both TAVI and high-risk PCI. For the purpose of this analysis, patients were divided into three groups according to the PCI timing strategy used: PCI concomitant to TAVI, PCI before TAVI, and PCI after TAVI. The primary endpoint was a composite of all-cause death and first unplanned hospitalisation. The secondary endpoint was a composite of major adverse cardiac and cerebrovascular events (MACCE). A propensity score methodology with inverse probability of treatment weighting (IPTW) was performed to account for selection bias between the three treatment groups.

RESULTS: Of the 519 patients included in the registry, 156 (30.1%) underwent high-risk PCI during the same TAVI procedure, 333 (64.1%) received PCI before TAVI, while in 30 cases (5.8%) PCI was performed after TAVI. At 1-year follow-up, adopting a strategy of staging PCI after TAVI was associated with a higher incidence of the primary endpoint (HR 2.31, 95%CI:1.24-4.32; p-value = 0.008), while staging PCI before TAVI was associated with a lower incidence of MACCE (HR 0.55, 95%CI:0.35-0.85; p-value = 0.008). Results were consistent after IPTW adjustment.

CONCLUSIONS: In this high-risk TAVI cohort, the strategy of staging high-risk PCI after TAVI was associated with an increased risk of adverse events at 1-year.

articles.title: Transcatheter mitral valve implantation in complex anatomies: Outcomes after prior repair or aborted interventions.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Patients with recurrent mitral valve disease after prior repair or persistent disease following an aborted edge-to-edge repair attempt face high risks with conventional surgery. The outcomes of transcatheter mitral valve implantation (TMVI) in these distinct cohorts remain unclear.

METHODS: This retrospective single-center study included all patients undergoing Tendyne-TMVI between June 2020 and December 2024 for recurrent mitral valve disease after TEER, SMA, balloon valvuloplasty, or persistent mitral valve disease after aborted TEER. Outcomes were assessed using MVARC criteria.

RESULTS: Of 85 TMVI procedures, 16 were included (median age 80 years (IQR 70-83); STS 6.9% (IQR 5.6-8.2)). Prior interventions were SMA (37.5%), TEER (12.5%), balloon valvuloplasty (6.2%) and aborted TEER (43.8%). Technical success was 93.8%. At discharge, all patients showed none/trace residual mitral or paravalvular regurgitation, with a mean gradient of 3.9 ± 1.1 mmHg. At 30 days, one patient presented with severe paravalvular regurgitation due to atrialization of the prosthetic valve; no stroke occurred. Acute renal failure requiring dialysis occurred in 18.8%, one major bleeding and rehospitalization for heart failure in 12.5%. Thirty-day mortality was 12.5%. NYHA class improved significantly from 3 to 2 (p = 0.042). MVARC device success at 30 days was 63%. Estimated 1- and 2-year survival was 67% and 56% with 50% of deaths being non-cardiovascular.

CONCLUSIONS: In carefully selected high-risk patients with recurrent or persistent mitral valve disease, Tendyne TMVI achieved durable prosthetic mitral valve function, leading to significant symptomatic improvement.
