Trajectories of Albuminuria and Non-Albumin Proteinuria After Sequential Addition of Finerenone for Residual Albuminuria Despite Established SGLT2 Inhibitor Therapy in Diabetic Kidney Disease: A Real-World Cohort Study.
articles.abstract:
AIMS: CONFIDENCE evaluated simultaneous initiation of finerenone and an SGLT2 inhibitor (SGLT2i). We examined 12-month trajectories of albuminuria and non-albumin proteinuria after finerenone was added to established SGLT2i therapy.

MATERIALS AND METHODS: This single-centre retrospective cohort study included 86 patients with type 2 diabetes treated with finerenone after SGLT2i therapy. Urinary albumin-to-creatinine ratio (UACR), protein-to-creatinine ratio (UPCR) and non-albumin protein-to-creatinine ratio (UNAPCR) were measured before SGLT2i initiation (T1) and finerenone initiation (T2), at the first post-finerenone assessment (median 1.6 months), and at 6 and 12 months. Covariate-adjusted linear mixed-effects models of log-transformed markers estimated geometric mean changes from T2, with Holm adjustment across 12 primary contrasts.

RESULTS: Urinary markers showed no significant net changes between T1 and T2. After finerenone initiation, UACR decreased by 46.2% at the first post-finerenone assessment and remained 35.2% lower at 12 months (95% confidence interval [CI], -47.1 to -20.7); corresponding reductions were 39.9% and 23.1% for UPCR and 33.7% and 13.6% for UNAPCR. All reductions were significant except for UNAPCR at 12 months (adjusted p = 0.16). At 12 months, 39 of 76 patients (51.3%) achieved a UACR reduction ≥ 30%. Mean serum potassium level increased from 4.6 to 4.8 mmol/L and plateaued; levels > 5.5 and > 6.0 mmol/L occurred in 17.4% and 4.7% of patients, respectively.

CONCLUSIONS: In patients with residual albuminuria despite established SGLT2i therapy, finerenone addition was associated with sustained 12-month reductions in albuminuria and total proteinuria and an early reduction in non-albumin proteinuria that attenuated by 12 months. Prospective confirmation is warranted.

articles.title: High-Content Screening Comparison of 1R6F Cigarette Smoke Extract and Selected Heated Tobacco and Electronic Vapour Product Aerosol Extracts in Endothelial and Bronchial Epithelial Cell Models.
articles.abstract: Cigarettes induce oxidative stress and DNA damage, processes that contribute to cardiovascular and pulmonary disease. High content screening (HCS) is an increasingly valuable tool for comparative toxicology because it enables simultaneous quantification of multiple mechanistic endpoints at single-cell resolution. In this study, HCS was used to compare the biological activity of extracts from reference cigarette 1R6F smoke and aerosol extracts from one heated tobacco product and two electronic vapour products in human coronary artery endothelial cells and bronchial epithelial cells. Endpoints included reactive oxygen species generation, glutathione depletion, γH2AX induction as a marker of DNA double-strand break signalling and NRF2 translocation as an indicator of oxidative stress signalling. 1R6F cigarette smoke extract showed the highest cytotoxic and genotoxic responses, whereas the selected HTP and EVP aerosol extracts generally showed lower potency, with higher minimum effective concentrations across several endpoints under the tested conditions. N-acetylcysteine (NAC) attenuated several responses, supporting oxidative stress as an important contributor to the observed cellular effects. Overall, under the tested in vitro conditions, extracts from the selected HTP and EVP products showed lower potency across several oxidative stress-, genotoxicity- and cytotoxicity-associated endpoints than 1R6F cigarette smoke extract. These findings support product-specific comparative in vitro bioactivity assessment but do not directly establish reduced human health risk, product safety or clinical harm reduction. The study extends previous HCS work by integrating potency-based comparisons, mechanistic interrogation using NAC and cross-tissue evaluation.

articles.title: Antimicrobial stewardship priorities and prescribing in Australian equine practice.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Antimicrobial resistance is a global health crisis that needs to be addressed by all areas of human and animal health sectors to safeguard effective antibiotics into the future. Understanding current antimicrobial prescribing patterns and veterinary antimicrobial stewardship (AMS) priorities is crucial for effective stewardship program design and sustainable uptake.

OBJECTIVE: To identify focus areas for stewardship interventions, implementation, resource allocation, and future campaign targets for equine practice.

STUDY DESIGN: Cross-sectional study of equine veterinarians in Australia.

METHODS: A cross-sectional study of equine veterinarians attending equine conferences and meetings in Australia was conducted. A combination of closed-ended questions and free-text responses were used to obtain perspectives, priorities and antimicrobial prescribing behaviours of equine veterinarians in Australia. Descriptive statistics were computed, with percentages reported as the proportion of respondents answering each question.

RESULTS: There were 103 responses, 85 of which were complete, from equine veterinarians across a broad range of sectors and levels of experience. Results indicate that equine veterinarians are overwhelmingly in favour of adopting AMS programs that have been developed for equine practice. Respondents consider unnecessary antimicrobial use and use of high importance antimicrobials when lower importance alternatives may be equally effective to be key targets. Mixed practice veterinarians showed an interest in client-facing resources, particularly those addressing wound management and reproduction. There was a lack of consensus among participants regarding when to stop antimicrobials in the treatment of equine pneumonia.

MAIN LIMITATIONS: The sample size of this study was small, consequently, the study was underpowered for formal inferential comparisons between subgroups. Selection and response bias need to be considered especially since participants were recruited during an equine conference.

CONCLUSIONS: This study serves to inform focus areas for stewardship interventions, including high-importance antimicrobial use, equine-specific antimicrobial prescribing guidelines, client-facing educational resources and guidance on antimicrobial duration for equine pneumonia, to improve stewardship efforts of equine veterinarians.

articles.title: Evaluation of a multiplex qPCR assay for rapid diagnosis of fungal pneumonia and tuberculosis in people with advanced HIV disease.
articles.abstract: Fungal pneumonias and tuberculosis (TB) remain major causes of mortality among people living with advanced HIV disease (PLWHA). Their overlapping clinical manifestations delay diagnosis in developed and resource-limited settings, with greater impact where access to rapid diagnostic tools is limited. This study evaluated the performance of a multiplex quantitative PCR (qPCR) assay for simultaneous detection of Histoplasma capsulatum, Cryptococcus neoformans, Pneumocystis jirovecii, and Mycobacterium tuberculosis complex in respiratory samples from PLWHA. A cross-sectional study was conducted at the Instituto Nacional de Infectologia Evandro Chagas (Rio de Janeiro, Brazil) between December 2023 and March 2025. Adults with HIV infection (CD4 < 200 cells/mm³) and clinical or radiological evidence of pulmonary infection were enrolled. Standard diagnostic methods included culture, microscopy, antigen detection (CrAg-LFA, urinary Histoplasma antigen, TB-LAM), GeneXpert® MTB/RIF, and commercial qPCR for P. jirovecii. The multiplex assay targeted the ITS region (H. capsulatum and C. neoformans), mtLSU (P. jirovecii), and IS6110 (M. tuberculosis). Among 198 screened participants, 88 met inclusion criteria (mean CD4 count: 56 cells/µL). Diagnosis included TB (56.8%), pneumocystosis (34.1%), histoplasmosis (10.2%), and cryptococcosis (11.4%); 25% presented coinfections. The multiplex qPCR showed 100% sensitivity for histoplasmosis, 80% for pneumocystosis, and 40% for both cryptococcosis and TB, with specificities ≥ 82% and 100% for TB. Overall accuracy ranged from 66% to 86%. Mortality was 12.5%, highest among cryptococcosis cases (20%). The assay provided accurate detection of H. capsulatum and P. jirovecii, although performance was limited for TB and cryptococcosis, supporting its use as a complementary molecular tool for differential diagnosis in PLWHA.

articles.title: Pass rates using the FEI noseband measurement device at British Dressage 2025 Championships.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Appropriate fitting of equipment provides horse comfort and avoids compromising equine welfare. In May 2025, the Fédération Equestre Internationale (FEI) introduced an evidence-based measuring device that is passed beneath the noseband to ensure sufficient laxity.

OBJECTIVES: To study the use of the FEI noseband device during mandatory tack and equipment checks at British Dressage Championships.

STUDY DESIGN: Observational.

METHODS: Noseband testing was observed for a total of 523 horses competing at the 2025 British Dressage National Championship, Middle Tour Championship and Area Festival Championship. During each inspection using the FEI noseband measurement device, five parameters were recorded: (1) measurement outcome (pass/fail), (2) noseband type, (3) bridle type, (4) horse compliance and (5) steward confidence. Frequency analyses and descriptive statistics were used to compare differences.

RESULTS: In the majority of horses (95%), the noseband had sufficient laxity to pass the noseband check. Horses ridden with nosebands most frequently used the Swedish (39%), followed by a flash (29%), cavesson (21%), drop (9%), and grackle (2%) nosebands. Horse compliance during insertion and passage of the FEI measurement device beneath the noseband was graded as 'compliant' by stewards in 96% of horses.

MAIN LIMITATIONS: No behavioural assessment carried out.

CONCLUSION: This study found that a high percentage of horses were ridden with a noseband with sufficient laxity to pass the noseband check. Previously published data from competition horses reported much larger proportions of horses wearing overtightened nosebands compared with the data presented here. These differences may relate to improved education relating to the impact of noseband tightness or may be a consequence of the introduction of mandatory testing of noseband tightness.

articles.title: Biochemical, structural, and functional characterization of the Nocardia asteroides dihydrofolate reductase: a primary target of anti-nocardiosis treatment.
articles.abstract: Nocardiosis is a human infectious disease caused by several species of Nocardia and primarily affecting the skin, lungs and central nervous system. The first-line treatment is based on cotrimoxazole, combining trimethoprim and sulfamethoxazole. These two drugs target respectively the dihydrofolate reductase (DHFR) and the dihydropteroate synthase (DHPS) involved in the essential folate synthesis pathway. The occurrence of drug resistance to these two drugs is however frequent. While the molecular mechanisms of trimethoprim resistance are well documented in other bacteria, they remain poorly explored and documented in Nocardia. This is partly because few biochemical structural or genetic studies have been conducted on DHFR from this genus. In this study, we report the biochemical and structural characterization of DHFR from Nocardia asteroides (DHFRNad). We show that overexpression of DHFRNad in N. asteroides confers strong resistance to trimethoprim. We recombinantly expressed and purified active DHFRNad and determined its inhibition constant for trimethoprim. We solved the crystal structure of DHFRNad bound to trimethoprim at high resolution. Further, biochemical studies of mutant DHFR variants pinpointed the role of important residues for trimethoprim binding and drug-resistance.

articles.title: An evaluation of technical assistance provided to infection prevention and control and antimicrobial resistance programs funded by the Global Fund's COVID-19 Response Mechanism.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Effective infection prevention and control (IPC) programs are essential for preventing healthcare-associated infections and combating antimicrobial resistance (AR), particularly in low- and middle-income countries (LMICs). The Global Fund's COVID-19 Response Mechanism (C19RM) created an opportunity for countries to receive funding to strengthen IPC and AR programs. In 2022, the United States Centers for Disease Control and Prevention, in partnership with the CDC Foundation, provided technical assistance (TA) to seven countries that received C19RM IPC and AR funds. This manuscript describes an evaluation of the TA program.

METHODS: TA was delivered by in-country consultants and US-based experts via virtual engagement and in-person visits. A mixed-methods evaluation was conducted, analyzing monitoring data, surveys, and key informant interviews. Guided by the CDC Framework for Program Evaluation and an adapted Kirkpatrick Model, the evaluation assessed TA delivery and recipient satisfaction and perceptions of TA.

RESULTS: All 12 survey respondents reported satisfaction, noting that TA increased C19RM funding awareness and supported proposal development, with approximately $14 million in C19RM IPC and AR funds awarded in their countries. Recipients perceived improved capacity to plan, implement, coordinate, and monitor IPC and AR activities.

CONCLUSIONS: These findings highlight the value of tailored TA for IPC and AR programs.

articles.title: Implementation of beta-lactam Therapeutic Drug Monitoring in clinical practice: a prospective, comparative, interventional study in intensive care unit patients.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: This study aimed to evaluate whether implementation of TDM of beta-lactams in clinical practice improved the achievement of PK/PD targets and clinical outcomes in a population of ICU patients receiving high doses by continuous infusion.

METHODS: It was a prospective, comparative, non-randomised, and interventional study conducted in two ICUs (11/2018 to 01/2021), in which TDM of beta-lactams was sequentially implemented. Eligible patients were aged 18 years or older, treated with one of the following five beta-lactams administered in continuous infusion: cefepime, ceftazidime, cefotaxime, piperacillin/tazobactam, and meropenem. The primary endpoint was the PK/PD target attainment at D4 and D7.

RESULTS: In the non-TDM group (n = 60), 54%, 46%, and 25% of patients reached the targets at D1, D4, and D7 vs. 51%, 57%, and 57% in the TDM group (n = 112), respectively. Target achievement at D4 or D7 was not correlated with TDM implementation (p = 0.89), unlike reaching the target concentrations at D1 (p < 0.001) and a documented infection (p = 0.008). There was no significant difference in electroencephalogram (EEG) neurotoxicity at D4 between the TDM and the non-TDM groups (10% vs. 18%, p = 0.34). A concentration at D1 and/or D4 above the toxicity threshold was reported in patients with acute kidney dysfunction (OR: 8.5 [2.1; 35.4], p = 0.002) and associated with neurotoxicity (OR: 6.0 [1.7; 21.7], p = 0.005).

CONCLUSIONS: In this study, the implementation of TDM did not significantly impact PK/PD target attainment, which underscores the importance of integrating a protocolised dose adaptation algorithm. Neurological adverse events were associated with drug overexposure and kidney function impairment.

REGISTRATION: ClinicalTrials.gov, under I.D. NCT03339869.

articles.title: Mitochondria-associated endoplasmic reticulum membranes facilitate gastric epithelial injury in hypoxia-induced gastric mucosal lesions.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Hypoxia following mucosal congestion in clinical practice causes a wide range of gastrointestinal symptoms and induces profound structural and functional perturbations in mitochondria-associated ER membranes (MAMs), which are subcellular compartments whose integrity and stability are regulated by FUN14 domain-containing protein 1 (FUNDC1).

OBJECTIVES: To investigate the effect of hypoxia-induced MAMs formation on gastric mucosal lesions in patients with severe hepatic disorders.

METHODS: Liver cirrhosis (LC) and hepatic failure (HF) were selected as representative severe hepatic diseases, and gastric mucosal tissues were collected. We applied the gastrointestinal symptom rating scale (GSRS) and endoscopic images to evaluate the possible relationship between gastrointestinal symptoms and mucosal lesions. Portal hypertension (PHT)-induced mouse models and hypoxia-induced cell models were also established. The roles of FUNDC1, hypoxia-induced MAMs formation and mitochondrial oxidative stress in mucosal epithelial injury were analyzed.

RESULTS: Patients with LC or HF frequently experienced gastrointestinal symptoms, which were correlated with the progression of gastric mucosal lesions. Hypoxia induced the upregulated expression of HIF-1α in gastric mucosal tissues, which was directly associated with the FUNDC1 promoter region, thereby increasing FUNDC1 gene transcription. Moreover, METTL3-mediated m6A methylation of FUNDC1 established a posttranscriptional regulatory layer to collectively drive upregulation of FUNDC1 expression. In addition, the increased level of FUNDC1 facilitated the formation of MAMs, drove a metabolic shift toward increased glycolysis, and elicited mitochondrial reactive oxygen species (mtROS) production. Ultimately, this increase in mtROS generation promoted NINJ1 oligomerization/activation to exacerbate gastric epithelial cell death and mucosal injury.

CONCLUSION: Under hypoxic conditions, FUNDC1-regulated MAMs formation and mitochondrial oxidative stress play pivotal roles in the development of gastric mucosal lesions.

articles.title: Expert Agreement on Palliative Reasoning and Monitoring in Heart Failure: International Delphi Study.
articles.journal: Journal of pain and symptom management
articles.abstract:
CONTEXT: Palliative reasoning aims to support the integration of palliative care (PC) into heart failure (HF) management and includes multidimensional monitoring of symptoms, wishes, and needs.

OBJECTIVES: This study aimed to establish expert agreement on palliative reasoning and the content of a PC monitoring instrument within the European context.

METHODS: A two-round modified Delphi study complemented by expert panel meetings after each round. Experts in HF and PC from nine European countries rated the relevance and wording of 57 items. Agreement was pre-defined as Individual item Content Validity Index (I-CVI) ≥0.80 on a 5-point Likert scale (score ≥4), with items between I-CVI 0.75-0.80 agreement reformulated by the panel and re-assessed in round two. Items with I-CVI<0.75 on relevance were removed.

RESULTS: Round one included 155 participants and round two 121 participants (78.1% retention). Agreement was reached in the first Delphi round on all steps of palliative reasoning (I-CVI range across steps: 0.82-0.95). Across the two Delphi rounds, 25 of the 33 symptoms (76%) achieved agreement on both relevance and formulation (I-CVI range for relevance: 0.81-0.99). Nineteen of the 20 items (95%) addressing wishes and needs reached agreement on both relevance and formulation (I-CVI range for relevance: 0.84-0.97).

CONCLUSION: This Delphi study established expert agreement on the steps of palliative reasoning and the content of a multidimensional monitoring instrument. These findings provide a shared foundation for earlier, more person-centred and coordinated PC, while allowing national adaptations.

articles.title: Kinetics of local C3 production orchestrates neutrophil recruitment in lung injury.
articles.abstract: Complement component 3 (C3) is crucial for host defense against bacteria. While the liver is the primary source of circulating C3, local C3 production at barrier surfaces such as the lung is key in early responses. Yet, how local complement-mediated responses are initiated at mucosal barriers-and how locally-derived C3 functions distinctly from its established cytoprotective role-is unknown. This study investigates the kinetics and necessity of lung-derived C3 during the initial hours of an infection. Leveraging models of bacterial pneumonia in ex vivo-perfused human lungs and mice deficient in liver-derived C3, we demonstrate that intrapulmonary C3 production and activation precedes the accumulation of circulating C3 into the bronchoalveolar space. Utilizing conditional knockout mice, we demonstrate that lung epithelial cell-derived C3 is required for early neutrophil recruitment in pneumonia. C3-mediated early neutrophil recruitment depends on a local C3a-C3aR axis that increases epithelial CXCL1 and CXCL2 production and occurs without any difference in epithelial injury, revealing that this activity is mechanistically different from its cytoprotective function. Collectively, our study demonstrates that an initial, entirely local phase of complement-mediated mucosal protection is critical for host defense during lung injury, before alveolar-capillary barrier disruption results in a subsequent, systemic response.

articles.title: Comparative Outcomes of Carotid Artery Stenting, Transcarotid Artery Revascularization, and Carotid Endarterectomy in Asymptomatic Carotid Stenosis: A Propensity-Matched Analysis.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: To compare myocardial infarction (MI), stroke, mortality, and major adverse events (MAE) after carotid artery stenting (CAS), transcarotid artery revascularization (TCAR), and carotid endarterectomy (CEA).

METHODS: Using TriNetX, adults undergoing CAS, TCAR, or CEA for asymptomatic carotid stenosis from 2015-2025 were identified using ICD-10-PCS codes. Asymptomatic status required no stroke or transient ischemic attack within 6 months before surgery. Propensity score matching was performed for CAS versus TCAR (5,558 pairs), TCAR versus CEA (9,666 pairs), and CAS versus CEA (13,707 pairs). Outcomes through 1 year were assessed using risk ratios and Kaplan-Meier analyses.

RESULTS: At 1 year, CAS was associated with higher stroke risk than TCAR (5.16% vs 3.74%; RR 1.31; p=0.002) and CEA (4.92% vs 3.47%; RR 1.44; p<0.001), whereas TCAR and CEA were similar (3.91% vs 3.79%; p=0.52). CAS had lower mortality than TCAR (3.78% vs 7.65%; RR 0.49; p<0.001), but mortality was similar in the other comparisons. MI was lower after CAS than TCAR (2.03% vs 2.95%; RR 0.63; p<0.001), with no differences otherwise. MAE was higher after CAS than CEA (7.66% vs 6.46%; RR 1.20; p<0.001), but similar between CAS and TCAR and between TCAR and CEA.

CONCLUSIONS: Among patients selected for revascularization, CAS was associated with higher stroke risk than TCAR and CEA, lower MI and mortality than TCAR, and higher MAE than CEA. These observational findings complement randomized evidence and require cautious interpretation given residual confounding and unavailable anatomic data.

articles.title: Inflammatory and Hemostatic Biomarker Response After Endovenous Laser Ablation Versus High Ligation and Stripping: A Randomized Controlled Trial.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: This randomized controlled trial aimed to evaluate and compare perioperative inflammatory response, primary hemostasis, and coagulation cascade activation between endovenous laser ablation (EVLA) and high ligation and stripping (HLS) in patients with great saphenous vein (GSV) incompetence.

METHODS: This prospective randomized trial included 39 patients with unilateral GSV incompetence (CEAP C2-C6), randomized to EVLA using a 1470-nm radial fiber (n=21) or conventional HLS (n=18). Blood samples were collected at baseline, 8 hours, 7 days, and 30 days postoperatively to assess inflammatory cytokines, adhesion molecules, and acute-phase markers. The primary endpoint was differences in biomarker levels between techniques over time.

RESULTS: The EVLA group demonstrated significantly earlier return to daily activities compared to HLS (17 vs 30 days, p<0.0001). Distinct inflammatory patterns were observed: EVLA showed increased P-selectin at 1 week and elevated IL-1, TNF-α, and IL-6 at 1 month, indicating a delayed inflammatory response. In contrast, HLS demonstrated higher von Willebrand factor levels at 1 week, suggesting earlier endothelial activation. No cases of deep vein thrombosis or endovenous heat-induced thrombosis were observed.

CONCLUSIONS: EVLA and HLS exhibit distinct temporal patterns of inflammatory and hemostatic activation. EVLA is associated with a delayed pro-inflammatory response, whereas HLS demonstrates earlier endothelial activation. Despite these differences, both techniques showed similar safety profiles. These findings may contribute to individualized thrombotic risk stratification and perioperative management strategies in venous surgery.

articles.title: Health-Related Quality of Life After Open and Endovascular Revascularization for Aortoiliac Occlusive Disease: A Prospective Cohort Study.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: To investigate the impact of open (OR) and endovascular repair (ER) on Health-Related Quality of Life (HRQOL) in patients treated for Aortoiliac Occlusive Disease (AIOD).

METHODS: We conducted a single-center prospective observational cohort study on consecutive patients treated by OR and ER for AIOD between January 2020 and July 2025. HRQOL was assessed using the 36-Item Short Form Health (SF-36) questionnaire at baseline, 1, 6, and 12 months. Physical (PCS) and Mental (MCS) Component Summary scores were compared between treatment groups using linear mixed-effects models with fixed effects for time, treatment, and their interaction. Linear regression models were used to assess factors associated with baseline HRQOL, while Firth's penalized logistic regression was used to evaluate factors associated with changes in HRQOL during follow-up.

RESULTS: Eighty-one patients were included: 20 (24.7%) underwent OR and 61 (75.3%) ER, for claudication (74.1%), rest pain (13.6%), or tissue loss (12.3%). No postoperative mortality occurred. Baseline PCS was associated with higher Rutherford class (p = .033) and TransAtlantic Inter-Society Consensus (TASC) lesion complexity (p = 0.02), while baseline MCS was associated with disease severity (p = .018) and comorbidities (p = .048). PCS improved significantly over time (p < 0.001), with a faster early improvement in the ER group (p for interaction= .005) especially within the first month from the procedure (p = .011). MCS also improved over time (p = .005), with no differences between groups. Early reintervention (p = .049 for PCS), late complications (p = .018 for PCS; p = .031 for MCS), chronic kidney disease (CKD) (p = .012 for PCS), coronary artery disease (CAD) (p = .014) and limb loss (p = .049 for PCS) were associated with reduced likelihood scores of HRQOL improvements at follow-up.

CONCLUSIONS: Both OR and ER were associated with significant improvements in HRQOL. ER provided faster early physical recovery, whereas mental health outcomes were comparable between treatment strategies. Patient characteristics and postoperative adverse events had a greater influence on HRQOL recovery than the revascularization strategy itself.

articles.title: Bridge Endovascular Aneurysm Repair Followed by Delayed Open Reconstruction for Infected Native Abdominal Aortic Aneurysm.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: Infected native abdominal aortic aneurysm (INAA) is a life-threatening condition for which emergency open repair may carry substantial physiologic risk. This study evaluated a staged strategy using endovascular aneurysm repair (EVAR) for initial aneurysm exclusion, followed by prolonged antimicrobial therapy and delayed definitive open reconstruction.

METHODS: We retrospectively reviewed consecutive patients with INAA treated at a single tertiary referral center between January 2020 and December 2025. Patients undergoing bridge EVAR followed by delayed EVAR explantation and open reconstruction after infection control were included. Clinical characteristics, operative details, postoperative complications, infection-related outcomes, and survival were assessed descriptively.

RESULTS: Nine patients were diagnosed with INAA, of whom eight underwent staged treatment. Mean age was 68.1 years, five patients (62.5%) were male, and blood cultures were positive in six (75.0%). The median interval from EVAR to definitive reconstruction was 79.5 days (range, 55-105 days). Seven patients underwent in situ prosthetic graft reconstruction after infection control; one patient with persistent infection underwent autologous femoral vein reconstruction. During a median follow-up of 20.5 months (range, 1-39 months), two patients died. Estimated overall survival was 87.5% at 1 year and 65.6% at 3 years. No recurrent infection, graft infection, or graft-related reintervention was observed among surviving patients.

CONCLUSIONS: In this small cohort managed with a staged institutional strategy, bridge EVAR followed by prolonged antimicrobial therapy and delayed open reconstruction was feasible and achieved durable infection control among survivors. This strategy may provide time for infection control and physiologic recovery before definitive reconstruction; larger comparative studies are required.

articles.title: Long-Term Mortality After Major Lower Extremity Amputation for Dysvascular or Infected Limbs.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Previous studies have reported poor survival rates after major amputation for dysvascular or infected limbs. In this study, we examined contemporary long-term survival rates and causes of death among patients undergoing major lower extremity amputation.

METHODS: Institutional medical records were queried for patients undergoing either above-knee (AKA) or below-knee amputation (BKA) for chronic limb-threatening ischemia (CLTI) or severe infection, from 2020-2023. Mortality rates were evaluated using Kaplan-Meier survival curves, and Cox proportional hazards models were constructed to identify risk factors.

RESULTS: A total of 747 patients underwent major amputation over the four-year period, with a median follow-up of 1.2 years. Median age was 65 years old and 62.7% were male sex. AKAs (n=371, 49.7%) and BKAs (n=376, 50.3%) were evenly distributed. The overall 30-day, one-year, and three-year survival rates were 91.9% (95% confidence interval [CI], 89.9-93.9%), 72.8% (95% CI, 69.4-76.2%), and 49.0% (44.3-53.7%), respectively. Amputation-related causes of death comprised 15.9% of all patient mortalities, with a median interval of 24 postoperative days (interquartile range, 8-64). Risk factors for overall mortality included patient age (hazard ratio [HR] 1.02 per year, 95% CI 1.01-1.03, p < .001), AKA (vs BKA; HR 1.76, 95% CI 1.39-2.25, p < .001), emergent amputation (versus elective; HR 8.59, 95% CI 3.12-17.84, p < .001), chronic kidney disease (HR 1.37, 95% CI 1.04-1.80, p = .026), end-stage renal disease (HR 1.41, 95% CI 1.00-1.98, p = .048), and coronary artery disease (HR 1.36, 95% CI 1.08-1.71, p = .010).

CONCLUSION: Long-term mortality rates remain substantial among patients undergoing major lower extremity amputation. However, only a small fraction of these deaths are attributable to the amputation procedure or postoperative complications. Risk factors for overall mortality include advanced patient age, emergent operation, and the presence of significant medical comorbidities. These findings highlight the importance of comprehensive risk assessment and may aid in prognostication and shared decision-making for patients with CLTI or severe infection considering major amputation.

articles.title: Contemporary Outcomes of Isolated Common Femoral Endarterectomy in the Endovascular Era.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Common femoral endarterectomy remains the reference treatment for common femoral artery occlusive disease, yet contemporary real-world data focused specifically on isolated common femoral endarterectomy remain limited. This study aimed to evaluate the clinical profile, operative characteristics and outcomes of isolated common femoral endarterectomy performed in a tertiary vascular surgery center, with particular emphasis on postoperative complications, reintervention and occlusion, as well as the possible influence of wound closure technique and hemostatic adjunct use on local morbidity.

METHODS: A retrospective observational study was conducted including consecutive patients who underwent isolated common femoral endarterectomy between January 2013 and December 2023. Baseline characteristics, clinical presentation, lesion complexity, operative details, postoperative complications, reinterventions and postoperative occlusion were analyzed. Lesions were classified according to TASC II. Kaplan-Meier analysis was used to assess freedom from occlusion, while Cox regression was performed to explore factors associated with postoperative occlusion. Fisher's exact test was used to assess associations between wound closure technique, hemostatic adjunct use and postoperative complications.

RESULTS: A total of 96 patients underwent 100 isolated common femoral endarterectomies. Mean age was 68.5 ± 9 years, 89% were male and 63% presented with chronic limb-threatening ischemia. Most lesions were classified as TASC A-B (68%). Median follow-up was 3.5 years (95% CI, 3.2-3.9). Early postoperative complications were predominantly local, including groin hematoma (4%), lymphatic leakage (4%), lymphocele (5%), pseudoaneurysm (2%) and infection (8%). Overall, 18% of procedures required reintervention, with 14% undergoing open and 4% endovascular reintervention. Nine occlusive events occurred during follow-up. Estimated freedom from occlusion was 100% at 30 days, 96% at 1 year and 86% at 5 years. TASC C-D lesions showed a numerically higher occlusion rate than TASC A-B lesions (12.5% vs. 7.4%; OR, 1.80), although this difference was not statistically significant (p = 0.462). In univariable Cox regression, aspirin therapy was the only variable significantly associated with lower risk of postoperative occlusion (HR, 0.20; p = 0.026). Neither intradermal wound closure nor hemostatic adjunct use was significantly associated with postoperative complications.

CONCLUSIONS: Isolated common femoral endarterectomy remains a safe and durable treatment for common femoral artery occlusive disease, with low rates of early local complications, acceptable reintervention rates and good freedom from occlusion during follow-up. These findings support the continued role of isolated common femoral endarterectomy as the reference treatment for common femoral artery disease in the endovascular era.

articles.title: HF STATS 2026: An Updated Report on Heart Failure Epidemiology and Outcomes from the Heart Failure Society of America.
The Comorbidity-Driven Interleukin-6-Mediated Systemic Inflammation Hypothesis of Heart Failure With Preserved Ejection Fraction: A Decade of Testing Ends in Disappointment.
articles.abstract: In 2013, Paulus and Tschöpe proposed that the multitude of comorbidities seen in patients with heart failure with preserved ejection fraction (HFpEF) was causally responsible for triggering an interleukin-6 (IL-6)-mediated systemic inflammatory state that might lead to HFpEF, postulating the intermediary contribution of coronary microvascular disease and deficient nitric oxide/cyclic guanosine monophosphate (NO-cGMP) signaling and cytokine-mediated cardiac hypertrophy and fibrosis. The comorbidity-driven IL-6-systemic inflammation hypothesis has been extensively evaluated in randomized controlled trials. However, in these trials, most comorbidities have not been shown to represent a causal mechanism for systemic inflammation, and the treatment of comorbidities (other than obesity) has not ameliorated HFpEF. Although coronary microvascular dysfunction is common in HFpEF, it is often not endothelium-dependent, and it is not a cause of defective NO-cGMP signaling. Numerous randomized clinical trials with NO-cGMP enhancing drugs (nitrates/nitrites, phosphodiesterase 5 inhibitors and soluble guanylyl cyclase stimulators) have not provided symptomatic or exercise benefits in HFpEF. Mendelian randomization studies link IL-6 to the development of HFpEF; serum levels of IL-6 precede the development and track the severity of HFpEF; and experimental models point to IL-6 as a causal mediator of HFpEF. However, the adipokine hypothesis partitioned IL-6 and other classical cytokines from pathogenic adipokines in identifying molecular mediators of HFpEF, based on the observations that systemic IL-6 does not reliably reflect visceral adipose tissue dysfunction, and it is cosecreted with neutralizing cytokine antagonists. These observations suggested systemic IL-6 represents a distal marker, and not a mediator, of adipose tissue inflammation, and thus, unlikely to play a role in HFpEF. In proteomics analyses, heightened natural endogenous cytokine antagonists are more prominent and consistent features of HFpEF than circulating levels of the cytokines themselves. The HERMES trial tested the efficacy of the IL-6 antibody, ziltivekimab, in patients with HFpEF who were enriched for cytokine-mediated systemic inflammation, but the trial has been stopped for futility. Therefore, as a result of rigorous testing of each of its mechanistic layers, it is now difficult to support the hypothesis that HFpEF is a comorbidity-driven IL-6-mediated systemic inflammatory disorder that acts through or independently of a NO-cGMP deficiency mechanism.

articles.title: Evolution of Stakeholder Involvement and Scope of Research Priority-Setting Studies in Kidney Disease: A Systematic Review.
articles.journal: American journal of kidney diseases : the official journal of the National Kidney Foundation
articles.abstract:
RATIONALE & OBJECTIVE: Kidney research that explicitly includes patient and caregiver perspectives has been identified as a priority. This study aimed to assess the evolution of research studies on priority-setting in kidney disease, including the clinical scope of priorities and the extent of stakeholder involvement.

STUDY DESIGN: Systematic review.

SETTING & STUDY POPULATIONS: Studies conducted to identify research priorities in kidney disease that elicited the perspectives of patients, caregivers, researchers, clinicians, or policymakers.

SELECTION CRITERIA FOR STUDIES: MEDLINE, EMBASE, PsycINFO, and CINAHL were searched from database inception to January 20, 2025.

DATA EXTRACTION: Full texts assessed independently by two reviewers.

ANALYTICAL APPROACH: Descriptive synthesis.

RESULTS: Thirty-four studies involving more than 3,709 stakeholders (clinicians (n=1976), patients (n=768), caregivers (n=114), researchers (n=232), and policymakers (n=63)) were included. Eight studies were multinational, with the remaining conducted in five countries (all high income). Almost all were published since 2000, with over half since 2015. Explicit patient and caregiver involvement increased from 25% (4/16) pre-2015 to 80% (16/18) in 2015 or later, with a priority-setting framework explicitly used in 38% (6/16) of studies pre-2015, and 50% (9/18) of studies in 2015 or later. REPRISE checklist reporting showed some increase in domain-level reporting over time with substantial gaps remaining (overall around 30%). Temporal trends demonstrated a broadening of research priorities from a common singular focus on medical treatments, towards inclusion of domains such as psychosocial and educational supports, health services, and equitable access to care across the spectrum of chronic kidney disease.

LIMITATIONS: Restricted to peer-reviewed, English-language publications.

CONCLUSIONS: Research priority-setting studies in kidney disease are becoming more common, are increasingly including patients/caregivers, and have become broader in scope over time. However, significant gaps remain, related to studies in low- and middle-income settings, the consistent inclusion end-users of research, and the completeness of reporting.

articles.title: Educational Impact of Hybrid and Remote Work: Attending and Trainee Perspectives on Preparing the Next Generation of Radiologists.
articles.journal: Journal of the American College of Radiology : JACR
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: To evaluate attending and trainee perspectives of hybrid and work from home (HYB-WFH) practice models and their implications for radiology education and preparedness for contemporary practice.

METHODS: A voluntary, anonymous 38-question electronic survey was distributed to musculoskeletal (MSK) attending radiologists and fellows, and radiology residents, through the Society of Skeletal Radiology (SSR). Descriptive statistics summarized respondent characteristics. Chi-square test compared attending and trainee responses. Thematic analysis identified recurring educational perspectives from free-text responses.

RESULTS: Most trainees (93%) supported HYB-WFH practice models, citing improved work-life balance, and no trainee preferred a fully in-person practice model. Most readouts remained in-person, although nearly all trainees reported experience with virtual readouts, and perceptions of virtual readouts were mixed. Trainees were more likely than attendings to report receiving formal preparation regarding HYB-WFH practice during training (68% vs 37%, p=0.0005) yet were significantly less likely to report feeling prepared for HYB-WFH practice (61% vs 83%, p=0.002). Nearly one-quarter of trainees (23%) indicated they would benefit from additional education, specifically regarding remote workflows and practical aspects of HYB-WFH practice. Thematic analysis identified that successful remote teaching requires intentional educational design for virtual readout and active engagement from faculty and trainees, while preserving opportunities for in-person mentorship, professional relationship-building, and learning to function as consultant physicians.

CONCLUSIONS: As HYB-WFH practice models become increasingly integrated into radiology practice, training programs should deliberately prepare trainees for contemporary practice by incorporating education on remote workflows, virtual readouts, and strategies for building professional relationships.

articles.title: Genomic and Pathogenic Characterization of Francisella salimarina Associated with Mortality in Fourfinger Threadfin (Eleutheronema tetradactylum) in Taiwan.
articles.abstract: In 2024, a mortality event affected farmed fourfinger threadfin (Eleutheronema tetradactylum) in Pingtung County, Taiwan, resulting in significant economic losses. Affected fish displayed anorexia and lethargy, with internal lesions characterized by multifocal white nodules. Histopathological examination confirmed systemic granulomatous disease. Two bacterial isolates, designated F5 and F69, were recovered from internal organs and identified as Francisella spp. by PCR. Experimental challenge demonstrated that strain F69 was less virulent than F5, exhibiting a higher LD50 (5.6 × 106 CFU/fish vs. 2.5 × 106 CFU/fish). Whole-genome average nucleotide identity analysis confirmed that both strains share >95% ANI with the Francisella salimarina group, classifying them within this species. Comparative genomic analysis identified two distinct polysaccharide-associated regions in strains F5 and F69. One region comprises a sugar biosynthetic gene cluster that is intact in F5 but contains several disrupted genes in strain F69. A second region encodes surface architecture characteristic of a KpsMT-dependent polysaccharide export system (kpsD, kpsE, kpsM, and kpsS), along with multiple glycosyltransferases and enzymes involved in the biosynthesis of UDP-activated amino sugars. Both strains contained a single copy of the Francisella pathogenicity island; however, key components such as pdpC were absent, and the pdpD gene was disrupted in F69. Genomic analysis identified a class A β-lactamase gene (blaOXY-2) in both strains, while F5 additionally harbored an FPH-family carbapenem-hydrolyzing class A β-lactamase. Consistent with these findings, both strains were phenotypically resistant to penicillins and cephalosporins, whereas only F5 exhibited resistance to imipenem. This study represents the first documented case of F. salimarina infection in Asia, affecting fourfinger threadfin in Taiwan, and provides important insights into its pathogenicity, antimicrobial resistance, and genomic features.

articles.title: Machine Learning for Predicting Long-Term Outcomes in Neurocritical Care: A sub-analysis from the SYNAPSE-ICU Study.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: Neurocritical conditions present significant challenges in the intensive care unit (ICU), especially during the initial hours. Accurate early risk assessment is essential for guiding acute care and influencing long-term outcomes. This study aims to evaluate the potential of machine learning (ML) models for risk prediction in neurocritical patients.

METHODS: This retrospective sub-analysis of the SYNAPSE-ICU Study applied machine learning to predict the 6-month outcome for patients with three different neurocritical conditions: subarachnoid hemorrhage (SAH), traumatic brain injury (TBI), or intracerebral hemorrhage (ICH). Models were trained at ICU admission, ICU day 3, ICU day 7, and Hospital discharge using the H2O framework, including GLM, DRF, GBM, XGBoost, and Stacked Ensembles. Predictive performance was evaluated using AUPRC and AUROC metrics.

RESULTS: 2,202 patients were included with a complete data set to predict the 6-month outcome. At 6 months, 836 patients had a favorable outcome (Glasgow Outcome Scale Extended (GOSE) ≥5) and had a significantly higher GOSE at Hospital discharge (p<0.001). Predictive performance (pooled across five multiply-imputed datasets) was highest at ICU admission (AUROC 0.841 [95% CI 0.804-0.878]) and Hospital discharge (AUROC 0.885 [0.845-0.925]), with a transient reduction during the ICU stay (Day 3: AUROC 0.830 [0.789-0.870]; Day 7: AUROC 0.821 [0.777-0.865]). Age was the most important parameter at the respective time points, except for Hospital discharge, where the GOSE at discharge had the highest impact on the 6-month outcome.

CONCLUSION: This sub-analysis demonstrates that machine learning models can effectively predict long-term outcomes for neurocritical patients, with accuracy improving from ICU admission to Hospital discharge. GOSE at discharge and age are critical parameters. The findings underscore the potential of ML models to improve prognostic assessments in neurocritical care.

articles.title: Sotatercept in Pediatric Pulmonary Hypertension: Experience from the Pediatric Pulmonary Hypertension Network.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Sotatercept, a ligand trap for TGF-β family members, has been shown to improve exercise capacity and decrease pulmonary vascular resistance (PVR) in adults with pulmonary arterial hypertension. Limited data exist describing the use of sotatercept in children with pulmonary hypertension (PH).

RESEARCH QUESTION: What is the safety and efficacy of sotatercept as add-on therapy in children with PH.

STUDY DESIGN AND METHODS: This is a multi-center, retrospective study of children and young adults ≤ 21 years of age with pediatric PH treated by programs in the Pediatric PH Network and institutional registries. Demographic data and clinical characteristics before and after sotatercept initiation were collected.

RESULTS: Sixty-six subjects received sotatercept as add-on therapy for a median duration of 323 days (Interquartile range 239, 500). Forty (60%) were female with median age 15.3 years (range 3.0 - 21.0) at initiation of sotatercept, and 61 with Group 1 (92%) PH. WHO functional class improved in 51% and did not worsen in any subjects (p < 0.0001). Subjects experienced significant improvement in six-minute walk distance (median 31 m, p=0.0003, n=40), NT-proBNP (median decrease 378 pg/ml, p< 0.0001, n=26), mean pulmonary artery pressure (median decrease 17 mmHg, p<0.0001, n=21), and PVR (median decrease 4.4 WUi, p=0.0011, n=21). Parenteral prostacyclin was weaned or discontinued in 13 of 38 patients. Adverse events occurred in 33 (50%) subjects with bleeding in 15 (23%). No patients had escalation of PH therapy, were hospitalized for clinical worsening, underwent lung transplant, or died.

INTERPRETATION: Pediatric PH patients treated with sotatercept as add-on therapy demonstrated improvement in functional class and other PH disease indicators and was generally well tolerated.

articles.title: From Menarche to Menopause: A Narrative Review of Female Reproductive Milestones and Risk of Chronic Airway Disease.
articles.abstract:
TOPIC IMPORTANCE: Female reproductive factors are underrecognized determinants of lifelong respiratory health. This narrative review examines relationships between reproductive milestones and chronic airway disease risk.

REVIEW FINDINGS: Early menarche is associated with reduced adult lung function and a higher incidence of asthma. Polyendocrine metabolic ovarian syndrome is also associated with increased asthma risk, particularly in obese individuals, through sex hormone dysregulation, metabolic dysfunction, and chronic low-grade inflammation. Adverse pregnancy outcomes are associated with lower lung function and heightened future asthma and chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) susceptibility, potentially from persistent systemic inflammation, endothelial injury, and oxidative stress beyond the perinatal period. Effects of exogenous sex hormones on the airways are complex and context-dependent. Hormonal contraception may reduce asthma risk in lean females by stabilizing estrogen and progesterone fluctuations, but increase risk in obesity, as exogenous estrogen can amplify airway inflammation. Similarly, effects of menopause hormone therapy (MHT) vary by formulation, timing of initiation, and use duration. Estrogen-only MHT - particularly when started at younger ages, before menopause, or used for longer duration - may increase asthma risk. Early menopause is linked to accelerated lung function decline, higher asthma incidence among those with obesity, and increased COPD risk.

SUMMARY: Female reproductive factors may influence susceptibility to chronic airway disease, although these relationships involve multiple pathways, with obesity as a major confounder. A dedicated life-course cohort with deep phenotyping and hormone profiling is needed to elucidate how reproductive exposures, sex hormones, metabolic determinants and other susceptibility factors interact to shape respiratory outcomes in females.

articles.title: Exacerbation trajectories in biologic-eligible severe asthma patients.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Asthma biologics are highly effective in reducing exacerbations. Improvement in exacerbations after biologic initiation is often attributed to treatment effect.

RESEARCH QUESTION: What proportion of biologic-eligible severe asthma patients improve without biologic therapy, and what characterises those who remain frequent exacerbators?

STUDY DESIGN AND METHODS: Biologic-naïve adults with severe asthma were identified in nationwide UK electronic medical records. Year 0 was defined as the first year patients met severe asthma criteria with ≥3 systemic corticosteroid-treated exacerbations (biologic-eligible). Post-eligibility exacerbation trajectories were identified using longitudinal k-means. Sensitivity analyses included alternative k and a lower exacerbation threshold (≥2/year). Covariates included the highest blood eosinophil count, inhaled corticosteroid (ICS) dose and comorbidities.

RESULTS: Among 10,078 biologic-eligible adults (median age 51 years; 71% female), we identified three exacerbation trajectories: (1) Remitting-stable (70%, n=7,091), with sustained improvement to <3 exacerbations/year even though ICS reduced after peak exacerbation year; (2) Chronic-frequent (20%, n=1,969), with persistently frequent exacerbations (median 5/year); (3) Refractory-frequent (10%, n=1,018), with high ongoing oral corticosteroid exposure (median >10 courses/year). Results were consistent across sensitivity analyses. Remitting-stable patients were least likely to have bronchiectasis but were otherwise similar in demographics and allergic comorbidities. Blood eosinophil count was higher in the chronic-frequent group (Year 0 median 0.30×109/L) compared with remitting-stable (0.23×109/L) and refractory-frequent groups (0.21×109/L, p<0.001); this was evident several years before meeting biologic exacerbation criteria.

INTERPRETATION: Over two-thirds of biologic-eligible patients improved with standard care alone. Chronic-frequent exacerbators had higher blood eosinophil counts, even years before meeting biologic criteria, suggesting a distinct disease phenotype.

articles.title: Magnetite-assisted enhancement of stability and resilience in anaerobic digesters against hydraulic overloading and volatile fatty acid shocks.
articles.abstract: Anaerobic digestion (AD) stability is often compromised under operational disturbances due to imbalances between acidogenesis and methanogenesis, where insufficient interspecies electron transfer (IET) can limit syntrophic oxidation of volatile fatty acids (VFAs). Conductive additives are widely recognized to enhance direct IET (DIET), yet the responses of electroactive microbial communities that support process resilience to operational disturbances remain unclear. Here, duplicate continuous AD reactors with and without submicron magnetite (Fe3O4) supplementation were operated under sequential VFA shocks and stepwise hydraulic retention time (HRT) reductions to examine process performance, sludge activity, and RNA-level microbial community dynamics. Following the second VFA shock of 4.5 g chemical oxygen demand (COD)/L, magnetite-amended reactors stabilized within three days, whereas controls required up to ten days, reflecting improved syntrophic VFA oxidation, especially of propionate. Under stepwise HRT reduction, magnetite-amended reactors sustained a methane yield of 0.19 L/g COD fed even at a 10-d HRT, whereas controls yielded only 0.01 L/g COD fed with VFA accumulation. Magnetite also reduced toxic H2S accumulation with concurrent S0 formation, suggesting an additional benefit for sulfide control. The improved performance coincided with higher electron transport and specific methanogenic activities, greater retention of putative electroactive microorganisms, and persistent dominance of Methanothrix. Potential bacterial partners of Methanothrix shifted with disturbance conditions, with Anaerolineaceae and Syntrophus retained during VFA shocks and Tolumonas, Syntrophus, and Geobacter becoming more prominent under short-HRT conditions. These findings suggest that magnetite contributes to AD resilience, potentially through electro-syntrophic interactions that support process stability during operational disturbances.

articles.title: Post-weaning threonine supplementation improves social memory in female offspring exposed to maternal sleep deprivation.
articles.abstract: Maternal sleep disturbances are common during late pregnancy and have been associated with long-term neurodevelopmental vulnerability in offspring, but the underlying gut-brain mechanisms remain unclear. Here, we found that late-gestational maternal sleep deprivation (SD) selectively impaired social memory without affecting sociability in adult female offspring. Integrated fecal 16S rRNA sequencing and serum metabolomics identified microbial differences and candidate metabolic changes, including reduced serum L-threonine (Thr). An exploratory cross-condition fecal-transfer experiment revealed parallel behavioral, colonic, and hippocampal patterns in recipient mice, although the design did not permit donor-origin or microbiota-specific causal inference. Given the reduction in circulating Thr and its established role in mucin synthesis, Thr was subsequently evaluated as a candidate intervention. Post-weaning Thr supplementation improved social memory and colonic mucus thickness, whereas these improvements were attenuated by DSS co-treatment. Thr supplementation was also accompanied by attenuation of hippocampal neuroinflammation and recovery of proteins involved in synaptic plasticity. Together, these findings demonstrate that post-weaning Thr supplementation improves social memory in adult female offspring following maternal SD.

articles.title: Plant-based food groups and cardiovascular disease: inverse associations with variable mechanistic support.
articles.abstract: This review integrates recent evidence on the associations between major plant-based food groups and cardiovascular disease (CVD), the biological plausibility of the proposed mechanisms, certainty-of-evidence assessments, and recurrent methodological limitations. PubMed and Web of Science were searched for English-language publications from 2020 to July 2026, with earlier studies included when evidence was sparse. Association evidence was derived primarily from umbrella reviews and systematic reviews of observational studies, supplemented by prospective cohort studies where review-level evidence was limited. Mechanistic evidence from human intervention studies, animal models, and in vitro investigations was synthesized using a three-tier framework. Higher intakes of whole grains, legumes or pulses, fruits and vegetables, and nuts and seeds were generally associated with lower risks of CVD outcomes. However, the magnitude and consistency of associations varied across food groups and outcomes. Human trials most consistently showed reductions in low-density lipoprotein cholesterol with cereal bran, oat β-glucan, legumes, and nuts relative to comparators, together with modest improvements in lipid profiles following fruit and vegetable interventions. Evidence for other proposed effects was more limited or heterogeneous and, for several pathways, derived mainly from preclinical models. Certainty-of-evidence assessments varied and several limitations recurred across the literature. Higher consumption of major plant-based food groups is generally associated with lower risks of several cardiovascular outcomes. However, the observational nature of the epidemiological evidence limits causal inference. Moreover, heterogeneity in findings and recurrent methodological limitations across the included sources warrant caution in drawing firm conclusions. Future research should standardize food-group definitions and dietary assessment methods and strengthen the integration of epidemiological and mechanistic evidence.

articles.title: Maternal immune activation influences social behavior development in a nonhuman primate model.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Women exposed to infection during pregnancy have an increased risk of giving birth to a child who will later be diagnosed with neurodevelopmental disorders (NDDs) characterized by changes in social development, such as autism and schizophrenia. Preclinical rodent models of maternal immune activation (MIA) have established causal links between elevated maternal cytokines and offspring social deficits indicative of human NDDs.

METHODS: Here, we use a unique nonhuman primate (NHP) MIA model to explore the longitudinal development of social behavior, given their phylogenetic similarity, social complexity, and translational potential for identifying the emergence of NDDs in humans. We explore social behavior (N=28 males) in pairs, social groups, and a dominance assessment.

RESULTS: MIA-exposed and control offspring developed a species-typical repertoire of social behavior and interacted with conspecifics. Yet, consistent with rodent and human studies, we found that MIA-exposed NHP offspring were, overall, less social towards familiar peers. We also found that MIA-exposed offspring were more likely to play with their treatment-matched pair mate during the weaning period, while controls did not exhibit a partner preference. There were also patterns suggesting that MIA exposure led to reduced contact with dams during infancy, greater withdrawals from pair-mates, and reduced positive social interactions with peers.

CONCLUSIONS: These results confirm that NHP models of MIA are consistent with evidence from rodent and human studies indicating that MIA exposure reduces overall sociality. They also suggest that social deficits may be specific to certain behaviors and more subtle or masked during observations in large social groups.

articles.title: A rapid visual detection method for Schistosoma japonicum in Oncomelania hupensis snails using recombinase-aided amplification and lateral flow dipsticks.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Effective surveillance of infected Oncomelania hupensis snails is pivotal for schistosomiasis elimination, yet traditional methods lack sensitivity and molecular assays require sophisticated equipment.

METHODS: We developed an RAA-LFD method targeting the SjG28 gene, using biotin-labeled primers and FAM-labeled probes, with isothermal amplification at 39°C for 15 min and visual readout on dipsticks.

RESULTS: The assay achieved a detection limit of 1 pg/μL genomic DNA and 10 copies/μL plasmid DNA, with no cross-reactivity against six other parasites. It detected as few as one infected snail among 50 and identified infections from day 7 post-infection.

CONCLUSION: This equipment-free, visual RAA-LFD method offers a practical solution for field-based surveillance, with potential to strengthen schistosomiasis elimination efforts in resource-limited settings.

articles.title: Antibiotic versus saline wound irrigation after appendectomy for prevention of incisional surgical site infection: a systematic review and meta-analysis of randomised controlled trials.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Incisional surgical site infection (SSI) remains a costly complication after appendectomy. Although saline wound irrigation is widely used, the added value of antibiotic irrigation remains uncertain, particularly in the context of antimicrobial stewardship.

AIM: To evaluate whether intraoperative incisional wound irrigation with an antibiotic solution reduces incisional SSI compared with saline irrigation after open appendectomy.

METHODS: We conducted a PRISMA 2020 systematic review and meta-analysis (PROSPERO-CRD420261323864) of randomised controlled trials comparing antibiotic solution versus normal saline wound irrigation during open appendectomy. PubMed/MEDLINE, EMBASE, Web of Science, Scopus, and the Cochrane Library were searched to February 28, 2026. The primary outcome was incisional SSI. Pooled risk ratios (RRs) with 95% confidence intervals (CIs) were estimated using a random-effects model. Subgroup analyses, meta-regression, publication bias assessment, GRADE assessment, and trial sequential analysis (TSA) were performed.

FINDINGS: Eight trials involving 2007 participants were included. Incisional SSI occurred in 40/994 patients in the antibiotic-irrigation group and 89/1013 patients in the saline-irrigation group. Antibiotic irrigation was associated with a lower risk of incisional SSI (RR 0.48, 95% CI 0.32-0.71; P=0.0002), with low statistical heterogeneity (I2=7.5%). Subgroup and meta-regression analyses did not identify significant effect modification. The certainty of evidence was low because of risk of bias and indirectness.

CONCLUSION: Low-certainty randomised evidence suggests that antibiotic-solution wound irrigation may reduce incisional SSI after open appendectomy. However, no reproducible regimen can currently be recommended, the benefit was not statistically significant in the small low-risk-of-bias subgroup, and high-quality trials are needed before routine implementation.

articles.title: Anti-receptor-binding domain IgG responses after SARS-CoV-2 infection in outpatients treated with ensitrelvir.
articles.journal: Journal of infection and chemotherapy : official journal of the Japan Society of Chemotherapy
articles.abstract: Ensitrelvir, a SARS-CoV-2 3C-like protease inhibitor, achieves rapid viral clearance. Whether early viral suppression attenuates humoral immune responses induced by SARS-CoV-2 infection remains unclear. During the KP.3 epidemic in Japan, we conducted a prospective study at 10 outpatient clinics comparing post-infection antibody responses in patients with mild COVID-19 treated with ensitrelvir and those untreated. KP.3-specific anti-spike receptor-binding domain (RBD) IgG titers were measured at baseline and 28 days. Data from 54 patients (30 treated and 24 untreated) were analyzed, with some baseline characteristics differing between groups. The post-treatment geometric mean titers (GMTs) were lower in the ensitrelvir group than in the untreated group (3,652 [95% CI, 2,849-4,682] vs. 5,816 [3,887-8,702] AU/mL; p = 0.040), although the difference was within twofold and the geometric mean fold increases were comparable between groups (12.51 [95% CI, 8.22-19.04] vs. 12.15 [7.33-20.17]; p = 0.928). In multivariable analysis, ensitrelvir use was independently associated with lower titers (β = -0.77; 95% CI, -1.33 to -0.22; p = 0.008), whereas in the propensity score-matched analysis, the between-group difference remained within twofold and was no longer statistically significant (p = 0.111). Substantial antibody increases were observed in both groups, with no statistically significant difference (9.61 vs. 14.8; p = 0.382), although a between-group difference cannot be excluded given the limited sample size. These results suggest that ensitrelvir may not meaningfully impair humoral immune responses to SARS-CoV-2 infection; however, the findings should be interpreted cautiously in light of baseline imbalances between treatment groups and potential residual confounding.

articles.title: Species distribution and clinical significance of filamentous fungi detected from respiratory specimens before and after matrix-assisted laser desorption/ionization time-of-flight mass spectrometry implementation.
articles.journal: Journal of infection and chemotherapy : official journal of the Japan Society of Chemotherapy
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The clinical significance of filamentous fungi detected from respiratory specimens uncertain in routine clinical practice, particularly for non-Aspergillus. We evaluated longitudinal species distribution and clinical correlates after implementation of MALDI-TOF MS.

METHODS: This single-center retrospective study included 585 patients with a filamentous-fungus-positive respiratory specimen from 2010 through 2024; the most recent positive specimen per patient was retained. Independent pre-implementation (2010-2018) and post-implementation (2019-2024) periods were compared. Medical records of 228 post-implementation patients were reviewed. Isolates were classified as Aspergillus or non-Aspergillus filamentous fungi. Cases treated with systemic antifungal agents were classified as clinically treated infection and untreated cases as colonization. Clinical characteristics were compared between the two groups.

RESULTS: Overall, 307 isolates (52.5 %) were Aspergillus, 130 (22.2 %) were identified non-Aspergillus filamentous fungi, and 148 (25.3 %) remained unidentified. From the pre-implementation to post-implementation period, identified non-Aspergillus filamentous fungi increased from 17.6 % to 29.4 % (p = 0.001), while unidentified isolates decreased from 28.6 % to 20.2 % (p = 0.023). In the post-implementation cohort, 58 patients had clinically treated infection and 170 had colonization. Multivariable analysis showed that non-Aspergillus detection was negatively associated with clinically treatable infection (OR 0.268, 95 % CI 0.121-0.565), whereas corticosteroid or other immunosuppressant use was positively associated (OR 3.300, 95 % CI 1.597-6.974).

CONCLUSIONS: MALDI-TOF MS implementation was associated with fewer unidentified isolates and greater recognition of non-Aspergillus filamentous fungi. When filamentous fungi are detected from respiratory specimens, infection should be assessed by considering fungal species, host factors, and clinical presentation.

articles.title: Early versus late escalation to extrafine BDP/FF/GB single-inhaler triple therapy in COPD: a real-world subgroup analysis by disease duration since diagnosis.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The optimal timing for escalation to triple therapy in chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) remains undefined, often resulting in delayed treatment. Consequently, evidence on the effectiveness of early initiation is limited.

METHODS: This subgroup analysis used pooled patient-level data from six observational studies to evaluate the real-world effectiveness of beclomethasone dipropionate/formoterol fumarate/glycopyrronium bromide single-inhaler triple therapy (SITT) in COPD according to disease duration. Patients were stratified into three subgroups: ≤48 months (short), 49-96 months (intermediate), and ≥97 months (long-standing). Outcomes assessed at 3, 6, and 12 months post-SITT initiation included mean number of exacerbations, proportion of patients experiencing ≥1 exacerbation, and proportion achieving disease stability and control.

RESULTS: Mean number of exacerbations decreased from the year prior to SITT initiation at all post-treatment time points across all subgroups, with the largest reductions observed in short disease patients, particularly at 12 months. Similarly, the proportion of patients experiencing ≥1 exacerbation decreased in all subgroups, with the lowest proportions observed in short disease patients. No differences between subgroups were observed at 3 and 6 months in the proportion of patients achieving disease stability and control; conversely, at 12 months the short disease subgroup showed significantly higher rates of disease stability and control compared with longer disease duration subgroups, suggesting that earlier SITT initiation may provide more sustained benefits.

CONCLUSION: Early escalation to SITT in COPD may result in more durable sustained clinical benefits compared with later intervention, reducing exacerbations and maintaining disease stability and control up to 12 months.

articles.title: The E3 ubiquitin ligase Fancl negatively regulates zebrafish antiviral immunity against spring viremia of carp virus.
articles.abstract: The innate immune response serves as the first line of host defense against pathogenic infections, and its precise regulation is critical for maintaining immune homeostasis. Fanconi Anemia complementation group L (Fancl) is an E3 ubiquitin ligase that plays an essential role in zebrafish ovarian differentiation, but whether it is involved in innate immunity remains elusive. Here, we investigate the function of fancl in antiviral innate immunity using zebrafish model. We found that fancl was induced upon spring viremia of carp virus (SVCV) infection. Overexpression of fancl in cells suppressed antiviral gene expression and promoted viral replication, whereas fancl-/- zebrafish exhibited enhanced antiviral resistance with increased survival rate, higher interferon-stimulated genes expression, and reduced viral loads. Mechanistically, fancl deficiency increased Tp53 protein abundance in zebrafish following SVCV infection. Consistently, tp53-/- zebrafish exhibited impaired antiviral immunity, with increased mortality and enhanced viral proliferation, indicating that Tp53 is required for the antiviral response. Together, our findings identify fancl as a critical negative regulator of antiviral innate immunity and reveal that fancl functions through Tp53 to orchestrate antiviral innate immunity. This study also provides potential genetic insights into disease-resistant breeding in aquaculture.

articles.title: TAILORD electronic intervention to improve therapy in a diverse cohort of patients with heart failure (TAILORD-HF): Study protocol.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Evidence-based guideline directed medical therapy (GDMT) for patients with heart failure with reduced ejection fraction (HFrEF) is under-prescribed. Decision support tools have been studied to help bridge the gap between clinical evidence and real-world use for GDMT with mixed success. This paper describes a trial of modified GDMT checklist that is distributed to both patients and clinicians with the aim of evaluating its impact on GDMT intensification and identifying modifiable barriers and facilitators for its use.

HYPOTHESIS: GDMT intensification will be increased by delivering an evidence-based checklist through the electronic medical record.

DESIGN: TAILORD-HF is a trial conducted within one academic health system using a two-phase clinic-level parallel cluster randomized design. In Phase 1, patients in intervention clinics will receive the modified GDMT checklist via portal message. In Phase 2, clinicians in intervention clinics will also see an analogous GDMT list via EMR display. The primary outcome is intensification of GDMT. Clinicians and patients are interviewed to assess their experience with the checklist.

DISCUSSION: TAILORD-HF will provide insights on the impact of a modified GDMT checklist on GDMT intensification in a real-world clinic population of patients with HFrEF. Additionally, the trial will provide novel information on patient and clinician perspectives regarding decision tools for GDMT intensification. Findings will enhance understanding of how to effectively deliver an EMR intervention for patients with HFrEF to address unmet needs around GDMT optimization, and in conjunction with other ongoing trials, deepen understanding of how to improve care of patients with heart failure.

articles.title: The Cardiac Calcium Handling Machinery is Remodeled in Friedreich's Ataxia.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Friedreich's ataxia (FA) is a progressive neurodegenerative disorder caused by an expansion of the GAA triplet repeat in the Frataxin (FXN) gene, leading to reduced frataxin expression. FA commonly affects the heart, causing hypertrophy, heart failure, and fibrosis. The mechanisms of FA-associated cardiac dysfunction may involve disrupted calcium handling and mitochondrial impairment.

OBJECTIVE: To investigate whether abnormalities in calcium handling machinery contributes to cardiac dysfunction in FA.

METHODS: Human left ventricular tissue from FA patients and unaffected donors, and an FXN knock-out (FXN-KO) mouse model, were analyzed. In mice, cardiac function was assessed by echocardiography and ECG. Calcium-handling protein expression was evaluated with Western blotting, RT-qPCR, and immunofluorescence. Single-cell contractility and calcium transients were measured in isolated ventricular myocytes. Mitochondrial function was assessed via confocal imaging to quantify mitochondrial membrane potential (Δψm) and reactive oxygen species (ROS).

RESULTS: FXN-KO mice exhibited significant reductions in ejection fraction, stroke volume, fractional shortening, and cardiac output, with increased LV mass and elevated end-diastolic and end-systolic volumes. Strain analysis revealed increased global and peak longitudinal strain. On ECG, the RR, PR, QRS, and QTc intervals were prolonged. Both human FA and FXN-KO hearts showed downregulation of SERCA2a and Ryr2, with reduced phospholamban phosphorylation. FXN-KO mice also showed upregulation of mitochondrial calcium-handling proteins, including MCU and VDAC, depolarized Δψm, and elevated ROS.

CONCLUSION: Cardiac dysfunction in FA is associated with impaired calcium handling, mitochondrial dysregulation, and systolic impairment, identifying potential molecular targets for therapy.

articles.title: Clinical and economic impact of central venous catheter-associated or catheter-related bloodstream infections in pediatric intensive care units: protocol for a systematic review and meta-analysis.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: Central venous catheter-associated and catheter-related bloodstream infections may increase mortality, length of stay, and hospital costs in critically ill children. This systematic review will estimate their clinical and economic impact in pediatric intensive care and examine how infection definitions, confounding, and the time-dependent nature of infection influence the evidence.

PATIENTS AND METHODS: Comparative longitudinal observational studies including patients aged 18 years or younger admitted to pediatric intensive care units and exposed to central venous catheters will be eligible. The exposure will be catheter-associated or catheter-related bloodstream infection, compared with patients from the same catheter-exposed source population who are infection-free at the relevant risk time. Mortality, length of stay, and hospital costs are co-primary outcomes. Multiple bibliographic databases, gray-literature sources, and study registries will be searched without date restrictions. Two reviewers will independently select studies, extract data, assess risk of bias, and evaluate certainty. Meta-analysis will be performed when studies are sufficiently comparable; otherwise, structured synthesis will be used.

RESULTS AND CONCLUSIONS: The review is expected to clarify the magnitude and methodological robustness of the clinical and economic consequences of these infections and identify priorities for future pediatric intensive care research.

articles.title: Dragnet.
articles.abstract: A 24-year-old previously healthy woman with a high body mass index presented with a several week history of poor vision in the left eye associated with non-positional headaches. Examination was notable for Frisén grade 2 bilateral optic disc swelling with a visual acuity of 20/20-1 in the right eye and 20/100+1 in the left eye and no relative afferent pupillary defect. Magnetic resonance (MR) imaging and MR venography of the brain were negative for a mass or venous sinus thrombosis. Lumbar puncture opening pressure was elevated, and the cerebrospinal fluid constituents were bland. A diagnosis of idiopathic intracranial hypertension was made; however, despite improvement in the papilledema with oral acetazolamide the vision continued to be reduced in the left eye. Macular optical coherence tomography confirmed a juxtapapillary choroidal neovascular membrane extending into the macula. The evaluation and various causes of visual loss in the setting of papilledema are discussed.

articles.title: Circulating levels of glucoselysine, a fructose-specific glycation product, are modulated by dietary fructose; post-hoc analysis of a case-control study and a randomized controlled trial.
articles.journal: The American journal of clinical nutrition
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Fructose consumption has been associated with cardiometabolic disease, including type 2 diabetes and cardiovascular disease. The formation of the fructose-specific glycation product glucoselysine (GL) may underlie the development of these complications. A previous study showed that endogenously produced fructose contributes to GL formation.

OBJECTIVE: Here, we aimed to investigate the effects of exogenous fructose on the formation of GL. Methods We first developed and validated an ultra-performance liquid chromatography tandem mass spectrometry (UPLC-MS/MS) stable isotope dilution method for the quantification of total GL in human serum samples.
