GL levels were subsequently measured in serum samples obtained from: 1) a case-control study, comparing patients with hereditary fructose intolerance (HFI) (n=15) on a fructose restricted diet with age-, sex- and BMI-matched healthy controls; and 2) a double-blind randomized control trial to study effects of dietary fructose restriction in adults with overweight and hepatic steatosis (n=35).

RESULTS: We successfully developed a UPLC-MS/MS method for the detection of total GL in serum, with inter- and intra-assay variability ranging from 1.1% to 6.0%. Serum GL concentrations were significantly lower in HFI patients compared to healthy controls (35.1 compared with 45.8 nmol/L, difference: -11.5; 95%CI: -14.3, -8.8). Similarly, dietary fructose restriction resulted in significantly lower serum GL levels in individuals with overweight and hepatic steatosis (38.8 pre- compared with 31.2 nmol/L post-intervention, change from baseline: -8.0; 95%CI: -12.0, -4.5).

CONCLUSIONS: Total serum GL can be analyzed accurately and precisely using UPLC-MS/MS. Our findings from two clinical studies demonstrate that GL formation is significantly influenced by dietary fructose intake. The observation that GL levels were not completely reduced after dietary fructose restriction suggests that additional factors such as an endogenous fructose pool contribute to GL formation. Further research is needed to elucidate the role of GL formation in fructose-induced cardiometabolic complications.

STUDY REGISTRATION: The FRUITLESS study was registered at https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT03067428, identifier: NCT03067428.

articles.title: The Use of Adjunctive Interferon-γ Therapy for Complex Mycobacterial Disease in Patients with Advanced HIV: A Case Series.
articles.journal: International journal of infectious diseases : IJID : official publication of the International Society for Infectious Diseases
articles.abstract: Management of mycobacterial opportunistic infection remains challenging in patients living with HIV, particularly when infection persists despite antiretroviral therapy (ART) and optimised antimycobacterial therapy (AMT). Interferon-γ is a key mediator of macrophage activation and intracellular pathogen killing, providing a rationale for its use as adjunctive host-directed therapy in selected patients. We describe three patients with advanced HIV and complex mycobacterial disease treated with adjunctive interferon-γ. One patient had disseminated tuberculosis with recurrent psoas abscesses after completion of AMT, while two had disseminated macrolide-resistant Mycobacterium avium complex (MAC) infection with persistent disease despite optimised therapy. Interferon-γ initiation was followed by improvement in all three cases, including radiological resolution of a recurrent psoas abscess and culture sterilisation in the two patients with disseminated MAC. Treatment was well tolerated, with only mild influenza-like symptoms. Concurrent ART-mediated immune reconstitution and AMT optimisation limit causal inference, but the temporal association between interferon-γ initiation and improvement supports further evaluation of interferon-γ as adjunctive therapy in refractory mycobacterial disease in patients with advanced HIV.

articles.title: Cardiac Deceleration Capacity Refines Sudden Cardiac Death Risk Stratification in Patients with Hypertrophic Cardiomyopathy for Primary Prevention.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Precise sudden cardiac death risk stratification in hypertrophic cardiomyopathy remains challenging. Parasympathetic dysfunction is closely related to malignant ventricular arrhythmias, and deceleration capacity is a robust parameter to quantify vagal tone. This study aims to elucidate the association between deceleration capacity and sudden cardiac death risk in hypertrophic cardiomyopathy.

METHODS: A total of 648 hypertrophic cardiomyopathy patients completing 24-hour ambulatory Holter monitoring were consecutively enrolled in this cohort study. Baseline deceleration capacity was calculated from the Holter recordings. The primary endpoint was a composite of sudden cardiac death or sudden-cardiac-death-equivalent events including sudden death, resuscitated cardiac arrest, and appropriate implantable cardioverter-defibrillator (ICD) therapies.

RESULTS: There were 464 patients included in final analysis. During mean follow-up of 827 days, 33 (7.1%) patients met primary composite endpoint. Deceleration capacity showed a significant linear inverse association with this composite endpoint (hazard ratio 0.660 [95% confidence interval, 0.546-0.799], P < 0.001). The derived cut-off value was 6.25 ms. Adding deceleration capacity to the traditional risk model significantly improved risk discrimination (C-statistic increased from 0.732 to 0.827, Delong P = 0.019) especially in the intermediate-risk subgroup (C-statistic increased from 0.565 to 0.849, Delong P = 0.011). Patients with lower deceleration capacity and elevated risk score suffered the worst outcome (Log-rank P < 0.001).

CONCLUSIONS: Deceleration capacity independently predicts sudden cardiac death risk in hypertrophic cardiomyopathy and provides significant prognostic value particularly in the clinically challenging intermediate-risk subgroup. Integration of deceleration capacity into risk evaluation warrants prospective validation before guiding ICD decision-making.

articles.title: CSN-associated c-Cbl control alternative NF-κB/RelB activity in Helicobacter pylori infection.
articles.journal: Biochimica et biophysica acta. Molecular cell research
articles.abstract: TheThe colonization of the gastric epithelium with Helicobacter pylori elicits a robust nuclear factor kappa-light chain enhancer of activated B cells (NF-κB)-dependent inflammatory response. The bacterial effector molecule adenosine diphosphate-glycero-β-D-manno-heptose (ADP-heptose) triggers both the classical and alternative NF-κB pathways almost simultaneously leading to activation of the transcription factor heterodimers p50/RelA and p52/RelB. Previous studies have demonstrated that the COP9 signalosome complex (CSN) plays an important role in regulating the classical NF-κB pathway through deneddylation of the E3 ligase Skp1-Cullin1-F-Box-β-TRCP (SCFβ-TRCP), while the influence of the CSN on the alternative NF-κB pathway remains unclear. Here, we show that CSN-dependent deneddylation of Cullin-1 controls via the classical NF-κB signaling pathway the upregulation of RelB mRNA and protein expression, enhancing the nuclear translocation of RelB. These findings are supported by the fact that ADP-heptose induces RelB expression in 2D mucosoids derived from 3D organoids from gastric antral glands of the stomach. Blocking neddylation and the activity of SCFβ-TRCP by treatment with the NEDD8-activating enzyme inhibitor MLN4924 prior to H. pylori infection, stabilized IκBα as well as p100 and suppressed RelA and RelB nuclear translocation. Therefore, our data show that CSN-dependent regulation of SCFβ-TRCP controls classical NF-κB signaling and consequently contributes to RelB nuclear translocation and alternative NF-κB activity. For the termination of alternative NF-κB activity, the CSN serves as a hub between constitutively associated c-Cbl and nuclear RelB, allowing c-Cbl-mediated ubiquitinylation of nuclear RelB following H. pylori infection.

articles.title: The Golgi-resident protein ACBD3 facilitates the interaction between enteroviral 3A proteins and Exportin-1.
articles.abstract: Enteroviruses are among the most common viral pathogens in humans, causing illnesses ranging from the common cold to severe and sometimes life-threatening diseases such as acute haemorrhagic conjunctivitis or poliomyelitis. To replicate efficiently within host cells, enteroviruses hijack several host factors, including the lipid kinase PI4KB and the adaptor protein ACBD3. During infection, ACBD3 is recruited to viral replication sites through a direct interaction between its C-terminal GOLD domain and viral non-structural 3A proteins. Here, we identify exportin 1 (XPO1) as a host factor involved in enteroviral replication. We demonstrate that 3A proteins of various enteroviruses recruit the host proteins ACBD3 and XPO1 to form a stable ternary complex. Chemical inhibition of XPO1 with selinexor, (originally developed as an anti-cancer medication), significantly attenuates coxsackievirus B3 replication in human cells. Consequently, our study identifies XPO1 as a host target for potential anti-enteroviral interventions, highlighting an immediate opportunity for drug repurposing.

articles.title: The Impact of Blood Gas Sample Waiting Time on Laboratory Parameters in Intensive Care Patients.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: This study aimed to investigate the impact of blood gas sample waiting time on laboratory parameters in intensive care patients, focusing on pH-related changes.

METHODS: This prospective longitudinal observational study was conducted in the pulmonary diseases intensive care unit of a training and research hospital in Turkey between July 1 and November 30, 2023. A total of 81 patients were included in the study. Blood gas samples were categorized into three groups based on initial pH levels: acidosis, normal, and alkalosis. The samples were stored at 22 °C and analyzed at 0, 30, and 60 minutes after collection. Statistical analyses were conducted using ANOVA and the Friedman test, and effect sizes were evaluated with Eta squared and Kendall's W.

RESULTS: Significant time-dependent changes were observed in PaO2 and SaO2 levels in the acidosis group. In the normal pH group, significant changes occurred in pH, PaCO2, PaO2, SaO2, glucose, and lactate levels. Similarly, in the alkalosis group, significant changes were detected in pH, PaCO2, SaO2, HCO3, glucose, and lactate levels. These findings suggested that slower metabolic activity in acidosis samples led to limited changes, whereas earlier changes were observed in normal and alkalosis samples.

CONCLUSIONS: To ensure accuracy in laboratory parameters, blood gas samples should be analyzed immediately after collection. Future studies with larger sample sizes and diverse methodologies are required to validate these findings and address the study's limitations, if unavoidable, aim for ≤30 min and document delay for interpretation.

articles.title: Assessment of the influence of beliefs about medicines on medication adherence among asthmatic patients who are on follow-up at a tertiary hospital in Ethiopia.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Patients' beliefs and perceptions about medications might influence their adherence to treatment regimens, which is particularly crucial for chronic diseases like asthma. This study investigates the relationship between medication beliefs and adherence among asthmatic patients in Ethiopia.

METHODS: A cross-sectional study was conducted at Tikur Anbessa Specialized Hospital (TASH) in Addis Ababa, Ethiopia, from April 1 to May 31, 2023. Adult asthmatic patients on follow-up at chest clinic of the hospital were included in the study. The study involved 207 asthmatic patients who were assessed using the Medication Adherence Reporting Scale for asthma (MARS-A) and the Beliefs about Medicines Questionnaire (BMQ).

RESULTS: The mean adherence score was 3.76 ± 0.50, with 63.8% of patients demonstrating poor adherence. The average scores for specific necessity, specific concern, general overuse, and general harm were 13.55, 13.73, 9.45, and 13.66, respectively. Analysis of mean ranks using Mann Whitney U test revealed that there was no significant difference between adherent and non-adherent patients regarding beliefs on necessity of asthma medications and beliefs on general harm of medicines (p > 0.05). In contrast, the mean ranks for specific concern score [114.1 (n = 207, p < 0.001)] and general overuse score [121.0 (n = 207, p < 0.001)] were significantly higher in non-adherent patients. In multivariable linear regression, higher specific concern (B = -0.027, p = 0.003) and stronger beliefs in general overuse (B = -0.106, p < 0.001) were independently associated with lower MARS adherence scores.

CONCLUSION: The findings of the study revealed low level of adherence among asthmatic patients. Skepticism on the importance of asthma medication was demonstrated by low specific necessity score and low agreement rate to necessity statements. Higher specific concern and general overuse scores were associated with non-adherence. By incorporating structured patient education programs, motivational interviewing, and community health worker support into the care continuum, clinicians can directly counteract the identified belief barriers.

articles.title: Moderating role of cognitive function in the relationship between stress and stroke recurrence: A Descriptive Study.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Psychological stress is a recognized risk factor for stroke recurrence and is common in post-stroke nursing care. Cognitive impairment may limit patients' ability to manage stress, yet its moderating role in stroke recurrence remains unclear. This study examined whether cognitive function moderates the relationship between stress and stroke recurrence among stroke survivors, with implications for nursing assessment and secondary prevention.

METHOD: A descriptive cross-sectional study was conducted among 84 stroke survivors with recurrent stroke recruited through convenience sampling. Sample size was estimated using G*Power assuming a medium effect size (Cohen's f² = 0.15), α = 0.05, and power = 0.90. Data were collected using a sociodemographic questionnaire, the International Stress Management Association (ISMA) questionnaire, and the Mini-Mental State Examination (MMSE). Data were analyzed using IBM SPSS Statistics version 30 with the PROCESS macro (version 4.2) and 5,000 bootstrap resamples.

RESULTS: Most participants had ischemic stroke (83.33%), mild cognitive impairment (35.71%), and moderate stress levels (72.62%). Psychological stress was positively associated with stroke recurrence (r = 0.240, p = 0.028), while cognitive function was negatively associated with recurrence (r = -0.270, p = 0.013). A significant interaction effect between stress and cognitive function was identified (β = -0.015, p = 0.040, 95% CI - 0.029 to -0.001), indicating that better cognitive function weakened the adverse effect of stress on stroke recurrence.

CONCLUSION: Cognitive function moderates the relationship between psychological stress and stroke recurrence. Routine assessment of stress and cognitive function may help nurses identify patients at higher risk and support targeted secondary prevention strategies.

articles.title: Vancomycin treatment outcomes and machine learning-based identification of heterogeneous vancomycin-intermediate Staphylococcus aureus infections.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: Heterogeneous vancomycin-intermediate Staphylococcus aureus (hVISA) infections remain underdiagnosed with unclear clinical impact. This multicenter study evaluated vancomycin treatment outcomes and developed a machine learning (ML)-based diagnostic model.

METHODS: We prospectively enrolled 200 patients with MRSA infections from 20 Chinese hospitals between February 2012 and July 2021. Population analysis profile-area under the curve (PAP-AUC) testing was performed on frozen isolates to confirm hVISA phenotype, and confirmed strains underwent whole-genome sequencing. Vancomycin therapeutic drug monitoring and pharmacokinetic/pharmacodynamic (PK/PD) analysis was performed. A ML model was developed for hVISA prediction.

RESULTS: Of 200 MRSA-infected patients, 117 (58.5%) were identified with hVISA infections, including 98 (98/175, 56.0%) adults and 19 (19/25, 76.0%) pediatric patients. Despite higher vancomycin doses, adult patients with hVISA infection achieved lower PK/PD indices than vancomycin-susceptible S. aureus (VSSA). In adults receiving vancomycin monotherapy, hVISA infection was associated with significantly higher treatment failure than VSSA infection (34.6% vs. 5.0%, P = 0.028). The predominant hVISA clones were ST5, ST239 and ST764, with ST5 and ST239 showing higher treatment failure rates than ST764. Among 10 ML models, LASSO-logistic regression performed best with AUC of 0.834 (95% CI 0.711-0.930) on test set, identifying vancomycin MIC, tracheal intubation, and prior penicillin use as key predictors.

CONCLUSIONS: High prevalence of hVISA among MRSA isolates and its impact on vancomycin monotherapy warrant early identification. The ML model enables identification of high-risk patients, supporting a shift toward phenotype- and sequence type-guided personalized dosing.

articles.title: TREATMENT OF PERISTOMAL VARICEAL BLEEDING BY SELECTIVE EMBOLISATION WITHOUT TIPS VIA A TRANSHEPATIC APPROACH.
Mathematical modeling and intelligent methods in systems biology and medicine applied to complex diseases: An overview.
articles.abstract: This article presents a comprehensive analysis of the intersection between mathematical models, classic algorithmic simulations as well as with machine learnig, alongside their applications, in biology, medicine and bioinformatics. From the first models on population growth and competition, we review the evolution of formalizations to present modeling of complex diseases such as diabetes, cancer, aging, and neurodegenerative disorders. Mathematical models are introduced and categorized, alongside the algorithms and computational methods from deterministic models on exponential and logistic growth, predator-prey dynamics, SIR framework, and cellular automata. The stochastic models on reaction-diffusion, Monte Carlo methods, Markov chains, and Bayesian networks. Thermodynamics-based models on phase transitions and cancer growth; as well the close related Ising Hamiltonian-based models on cancer immunoediting, joint to aspects on genetic and phenotype immune response. The role of classic and deep machine learning -hybrid- models for integrating multi-omic data in challenging scenario prediction. It is highlighted through relevant applications on systems and precision medicine.

articles.title: One-year outcomes in patients with persistent atrial fibrillation using CARTOFINDER mapping with OCTARAY: a Shinshu-AB registry study.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Persistent atrial fibrillation (PerAF) has no established method of catheter ablation. Although catheter ablation using CARTOFINDER has shown some therapeutic effects, the associated prolonged procedure time remains a challenge. The identification of focal or rotational activation sites by CARTOFINDER using OCTARAY™ Mapping Catheter (OCTARAY) suggests that it can more efficiently detect the activation sites owing to its greater coverage of the left atrium (LA). This study aimed to compare the outcomes of catheter ablation guided by CARTOFINDER versus BOX isolation (BOXI) in patients with PerAF.

METHODS: Using the Shinshu-AB registry, the study included 117 patients with PerAF who underwent catheter ablation between May 2021 and May 2024. The patients were matched at 1:1 ratio (n = 39 each): Group 1 underwent CARTOFINDER-guided catheter ablation, and Group 2 underwent BOXI-guided catheter ablation. CARTOFINDER detection was limited to four sites on the LA posterior wall, the LA appendage ostium, and the LA septum, for a total of six sites.

RESULTS: Procedure time was significantly shorter in Group 1 (140.2 ± 37.7 vs. 174.4 ± 74.1 min, p = 0.016). The 1-year AF recurrence rate was significantly lower in Group 1 (17.9% vs. 38.5%, p = 0.031). Based on Cox proportional hazards regression analysis, AF duration and CARTOFINDER-guided catheter ablation were both independent predictors of recurrent AF after catheter ablation for PerAF.

CONCLUSION: Compared to BOXI, CARTOFINDER-guided catheter ablation may lead to better outcomes in patients with PerAF.

articles.title: ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE AND REMOTE MONITORING OF CARDIAC DEVICES: A NARRATIVE REVIEW.
articles.abstract: Remote monitoring of Cardiac Implantable Electronic Devices (CIEDs) has evolved significantly from early trans-telephonic transmissions to now becoming a standard of care that improves survival and outcomes. However, the resulting exponential growth in data has resulted in alert fatigue and information overload, creating a need for advanced data interpretation. This narrative review examines the transformative role of Artificial Intelligence (AI) in reshaping remote monitoring and cardiac device management into an active, predictive, and personalised system. We examine the role of AI across all cardiac implantable electronic devices, including implantable loop recorders (ILRs), pacemakers, implantable cardioverter-defibrillators (ICDs) and cardiac resynchronisation therapy (CRT) devices. We address four questions: (1) the scale and nature of the remote monitoring burden; (2) the AI tools in current clinical use, particularly for ILRs, where alert burden is greatest; (3) AI applications evaluated but not yet widely implemented, including prediction of ventricular arrhythmias, heart failure events and device failure; and (4) future directions, including adaptive device programming and digital twins. While AI demonstrates significant potential to enhance clinical decision-making and patient outcomes, its widespread adoption remains constrained by barriers regarding data quality, algorithm transparency, regulatory compliance, and privacy protections. Realising the full potential of AI in electrophysiology will require sustained collaboration between clinical and technical stakeholders to ensure these tools are deployed effectively and safely.

articles.title: Explainable Machine Learning to Identify Clinical, Environmental, and Social Factors Associated with Diagnosed Pediatric Asthma.
articles.journal: Annals of allergy, asthma & immunology : official publication of the American College of Allergy, Asthma, & Immunology
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Pediatric asthma reflects clinical, physiologic, environmental, and social determinants, yet most classification models use clinical variables alone and are difficult to interpret.

OBJECTIVE: To use explainable machine learning on nationally representative data to identify and rank factors associated with a reported physician diagnosis of asthma in U.S. children, and to test whether fewer higher-ranked features retain full performance.

METHODS: We analyzed 6,567 children aged 6 to 17 years in NHANES 2007-2012 (weighted asthma prevalence 18.8%). Of 477 harmonized variables, 22 entered the primary CatBoost model after pre-specified eligibility screening, feature engineering, and correlation pruning. Data were split into training, validation, and held-out internal test sets (60/20/20), with the operating threshold locked on validation. SHAP ranked features; 95% confidence intervals used stratified bootstrap.

RESULTS: The primary model reached a test-set AUC of 0.78 (95% CI 0.74-0.81), sensitivity 0.75, specificity 0.63, and negative predictive value 0.92. The highest-ranked features included recent wheezing, family history of asthma, general health status, serum cotinine, household size, FEV₁/FVC ratio, race/Hispanic origin, insurance coverage, and U.S. birth. A reduced model of these ten plus two spirometry-availability indicators had more favorable point estimates on every metric (AUC 0.80; paired difference 0.023, 95% CI 0.007-0.041; sensitivity 0.79; specificity 0.67; negative predictive value 0.93).

CONCLUSION: Explainable machine learning recovers established clinical signals and ranks social and contextual factors associated with a reported pediatric asthma diagnosis; a parsimonious feature set retains this performance. Given the cross-sectional design and internal evaluation, external and prospective validation is required before clinical use.

articles.title: Complementary Antihypertensive Mechanisms of the Tianma-Gouteng Herb Pair Targeting the Endothelium and Smooth Muscle: Emphasizing Endothelial Protection by Tianma Involving the PGR-Associated PI3K/Akt/eNOS Pathway.
articles.abstract:
ETHNOPHARMACOLOGICAL RELEVANCE: The herb pair Tianma (Gastrodia elata Blume, TM) and Gouteng (Uncaria rhynchophylla (Miq.) Miq., GT) has long been used in traditional Chinese medicine to treat hypertension. However, their combined antihypertensive (anti-HTN) mechanisms remain unclear.

AIM OF THE STUDY: To elucidate the complementary anti-HTN mechanisms of TM-GT, with a particular focus on the endothelial protective effects of TM.

MATERIALS AND METHODS: The anti-HTN and vascular protective effects of TM-GT were evaluated in L-NAME-induced hypertensive mice, H2O2-injured EA.hy926 endothelial cells, and Ang II-stimulated primary vascular smooth muscle cells (VSMC). Vascular remodeling, endothelial integrity, smooth muscle phenotype, NO/redox balance, mitochondrial function, transcriptomic profiling, PI3K inhibition, and PGR knockdown were used to investigate the underlying mechanisms. The core chemical compounds of TM-GT were characterized using UHPLC-Q-TOF-MS/MS.

RESULTS: TM-GT reduced blood pressure, improved circulating NO-related bioavailability and SOD levels, and decreased Ang II and ET-1, accompanied by attenuated medial thickening. Furthermore, TM preferentially restored endothelial coverage and function, whereas GT preserved medial α-SMA and mitigated VSMC phenotypic switching, suggesting compartment-specific actions. Transcriptomic analysis implicated a PGR-associated PI3K/Akt/eNOS pathway in TM-mediated endothelial protection. Both PI3K inhibition and PGR knockdown significantly attenuated TM-induced improvements in endothelial viability, NO production, migration, mitochondrial integrity, and eNOS phosphorylation. Parishin A was identified as a candidate TM-derived constituent linked to this axis.

CONCLUSION: TM preferentially protects the endothelial compartment, at least partly in association with the PGR-associated PI3K/Akt/eNOS signaling axis. In contrast, GT stabilizes contractile vascular smooth muscle cells (VSMC) and mitigates medial remodeling. These effects support the traditional use of this herbal pair in treating hypertension-related vascular disorders.

articles.title: Dabushen decoction ameliorates diabetes-associated cognitive dysfunction in association with changes in PINK1/Parkin-related mitophagy.
articles.abstract:
ETHNOPHARMACOLOGICAL RELEVANCE: Diabetes-associated cognitive dysfunction (DCD) is a common and serious central nervous system complication of type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM). Dabushen Decoction (DBSD), first recorded in Fu Xing Jue Zang Fu Yong Yao Fa Yao, is a traditional Chinese herbal formula used to tonify the kidney and replenish essence. DBSD has shown potential pharmacological value in the intervention of cognitive dysfunction; however, its neuroprotective mechanisms remain to be systematically elucidated.

AIM OF THE STUDY: This study aimed to validate the mitigating effect of DBSD on DCD and to further investigate its mechanism.

MATERIALS AND METHODS: Ultra-high-performance liquid chromatography coupled with Q Exactive Orbitrap high-resolution mass spectrometry (UHPLC-QE/MS) was used to analyze the chemical constituents of DBSD. Network pharmacology analysis was subsequently performed by integrating the SwissTargetPrediction, GeneCards, and OMIM databases. A T2DM rat model was established using a high-fat diet combined with streptozotocin (HFD/STZ), followed by oral administration of DBSD for 8 weeks. The overall pharmacological effects of DBSD were evaluated using the Morris water maze, Y-maze, and glucose and lipid metabolism-related indicators. Nissl staining and immunohistochemistry were used to assess pathological changes in hippocampal neurons, while transmission electron microscopy, ATP measurement, and JC-1 staining were used to evaluate hippocampal mitochondrial ultrastructure and function. ELISA was used to measure oxidative stress and inflammatory markers, and hippocampal proteomics was performed to analyze the potential biological processes involved. Finally, immunofluorescence colocalization and Western blotting were used to evaluate changes in PINK1/Parkin-mediated mitophagy markers.

RESULTS: A total of 22 candidate circulating prototype compounds were putatively annotated by UHPLC-QE/MS. Network pharmacology identified 215 intersecting targets, and GO and KEGG enrichment analyses suggested that these targets were mainly involved in mitochondrial ATP synthesis, oxidative phosphorylation, and metabolic pathways. In vivo experiments showed that DBSD, particularly at the high dose, reduced FBG, FINS, OGTT-AUC, TC, TG, and LDL-C levels, increased HDL-C levels, and enhanced behavioral performance in the Morris water maze, as reflected by a greater number of platform crossings and longer time spent in the target quadrant. Histopathological results showed that DBSD increased the density of Nissl-positive neurons and the percentage of NeuN-positive cells in the hippocampal CA1 region and reduced Aβ immunoreactivity. In addition, DBSD ameliorated mitochondrial and synaptic ultrastructural damage, increased ATP levels, and improved mitochondrial membrane potential. DBSD reduced serum IL-1β, IL-18, and MDA levels as well as hippocampal NLRP3 protein expression, while increasing serum SOD and GSH levels. Proteomic analysis identified 82 shared differentially expressed proteins, which were mainly associated with mitochondrial energy metabolism, mitophagy, and synaptic function. Further validation showed that DBSD increased the percentage of LC3/TOMM20 colocalization-positive cells, significantly upregulated the expression of PINK1, Parkin, Beclin-1 and the LC3B-II/LC3B-I ratio, and downregulated p62, TOMM20, and COX IV protein expression in the hippocampus.

CONCLUSIONS: DBSD improved cognitive function in rats with DCD, and its neuroprotective effects may be associated with changes in markers of PINK1/Parkin-mediated mitophagy and improved mitochondrial function.

articles.title: Shema Zhichuan Liquid alleviates airway inflammation in Allergic Asthma by regulating autophagy pathways through DNA methylation.
articles.abstract:
ETHNOPHARMACOLOGICAL RELEVANCE: Shema Zhichuan Liquid (SMZCL) is a traditional Chinese medicine formulation used clinically as an adjunct therapy for asthma. Its therapeutic mechanism in allergic asthma (AA), however, remains poorly understood.

AIMS OF THE STUDY: This study aimed to evaluate the efficacy of SMZCL in treating AA and to elucidate its molecular mechanisms, with particular focus on the regulation of autophagy via DNMT1-mediated promoter demethylation of autophagy-related genes.

MATERIALS AND METHODS: The AA mouse model was established by ovalbumin (OVA)/Al(OH)3 sensitization and challenge. Lung histopathological, inflammatory cytokine levels, Th2 cell proportion, methylation status of autophagy-related genes, and the expression of autophagy-associated markers were assessed. Additionally, an in vitro inflammatory model was generated using lipopolysaccharide (LPS)-stimulated RAW264.7 macrophages to further investigate the mechanism by which SMZCL modulates autophagy through modulating DNA methylation.

RESULTS: In vivo, SMZCL attenuated airway inflammation in AA mice and reduced the proportion of Th2 cells in BALF. It significantly decreased serum levels of IgE, Th2 cytokines IL-4 and IL-13, and pro-inflammatory cytokines TNF-α and IL-6, while increasing the Th1 cytokine IFN-γ. Mechanistically, SMZCL inhibited DNMT1 mRNA and protein expression, decreased the relative methylation levels of the ATG5 and Beclin-1 promoters, upregulated mRNA and protein levels of ATG5, Beclin-1, and LC3, and downregulated p62 mRNA expression. In vitro, SMZCL treatment reduced pro-inflammatory cytokines (TNF-α, IL-6, and IL-1β), suppressed DNMT1 expression, induced demethylation of ATG5 and Beclin-1 promoters, and upregulated their expression. SMZCL restored autophagic flux, as evidenced by elevated absolute levels of LC3-II, enhanced p62 degradation, an upward trend in the LC3-II/I ratio, a concurrent increase in both autophagosome and autolysosome puncta in mCherry-GFP-LC3 dual-fluorescence analysis, and further LC3-II accumulation in the presence of chloroquine. Moreover, SMZCL inhibited the expression of mTOR and phosphorylated mTOR (p-mTOR).

CONCLUSION: SMZCL inhibited DNMT1, leading to demethylation of the ATG5 and Beclin-1 promoters, and concurrently suppressed the mTOR signaling pathway. Through these mechanisms, SMZCL restored autophagic flux, exerted anti-inflammatory effects, and thereby provided protection against AA.

articles.title: Depot-specific molecular remodelling of human adipose tissue and liver following bariatric surgery revealed by longitudinal multi-omic profiling.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Obesity and its complications, including metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease, remain significant global health challenges. Bariatric surgery has established clinical benefits, but the mechanisms driving metabolic improvements are not clearly defined.

METHODS: We undertook a randomised, prospective, longitudinal (1-year) study in women living with obesity to determine the impact of a low-calorie diet followed by bariatric surgery (individuals randomised to sleeve gastrectomy (SG) or Roux-en-Y gastric bypass (RYGB)) on metabolic phenotype, including MASLD. We combined repeated clinical assessments with state-of-the-art imaging, dynamic meal testing and a multi-omic analysis (proteomic, metabolomic) from tissue (multiple adipose depots, liver) and blood. A control group without obesity underwent identical phenotyping and molecular analysis with the exception of no low-calorie diet.

RESULTS: Obesity was associated with metabolic, proteomic and hepatic dysregulation. Bariatric surgery normalized non-invasive assessments of liver phenotype and was associated with reductions in body fat, notably in android as opposed to gynoid fat mass. This was paralleled by proteomic changes in abdominal, but not gluteal, adipose tissue. Proteomic and metabolomic analyses highlighted putative roles for all-trans-retinol dehydrogenase, lumican and androgenic steroids in the regulation of metabolic phenotype. Clinical or molecular outcomes were not significantly different between SG and RYGB.

CONCLUSIONS: These data highlight the differential impact of bariatric surgery on adipose tissue depots, and this is likely to be crucial in delivering metabolic benefit. Furthermore, the specific pathways and targets that have been identified offer the potential for therapeutic intervention.

articles.title: When channelrhodopsin goes off-target: biophysical signatures of ectopic expression in neurons.
articles.abstract: The Cre-lox system allows targeted expression of optogenetic proteins such as channelrhodopsin-2 (ChR2), but can also produce unintended expression in non-target cells. In a VGLUT1-Cre::ChR2(H134R)-eYFP mouse line, we bred mice that correctly expressed ChR2 in VGLUT1 positive neurons. This was corroborated with whole cell recordings of dopaminergic (DA) neurons of the substantia nigra (SN), which elicited blue light evoked AMPA currents with a delay of a few milliseconds following the onset of light stimulation. However, at some point during breeding we discovered recurring ectopic expression of ChR2 that crept into our line. ChR2, which previously did not express in SN DA neurons, were now expressing in those neurons. These ectopically expressing DA neurons generated ChR2 currents that almost immediately followed (∼200 μs) the onset of blue light stimulation followed by a few milliseconds later with AMPA synaptic currents. While DA neurons from non-ectopic mice exhibited only synaptically mediated AMPA currents with onset latencies of a few milliseconds. In ectopic mice, the ChR2 currents in DA neurons had smaller amplitudes, more depolarized reversal potentials, and faster decay kinetics compared to canonical ChR2 responses recorded from cortical pyramidal neurons as control. Confocal imaging confirmed ChR2-YFP fluorescence within DA neurons from ectopically expressing mice, which were absent from DA neurons of non-ectopic mice. Together, these findings demonstrate that ectopically expressed ChR2 retains light sensitivity but may display altered biophysical properties that can mislead data interpretation. This work highlights the need to verify both expression fidelity and photocurrent behavior in Cre-lox based optogenetic models.

articles.title: Rational design of a consensus bothropic metalloproteinase as an immunogen for broadly protective antivenom development.
articles.abstract: Antivenoms remain the only specific therapy for snakebite envenoming. In Bothrops venoms, Snake Venom Metalloproteinases (SVMPs) are abundant and highly diverse toxins responsible for the major local and hemotoxic effects induced by envenoming. However, currently available bothropic antivenoms fail to fully neutralize these effects, frequently resulting in permanent and disabling sequelae in affected patients. Here, we describe a rational approach to improve the SVMP neutralization potential of bothropic antivenoms using a consensus toxin. Forty SVMP sequences belonging to PI, P-II, and P-III classes from snakes of the Bothrops genus were analyzed, and a consensus amino acid sequence corresponding to the M12 metalloproteinase domain was determined through multiple sequence alignment. Based on the structural organization of SVMPs, we designed a recombinant construct containing an N-terminal hexahistidine tag, followed by a metalloproteinase pro-domain from Bothrops and a Tobacco Etch Virus (TEV) protease recognition site inserted between the pro-domain and the catalytic domain, enabling the expression of a consensus PI SVMP zymogen (pro_crSVMP-I) in the heterologous system Komagataella phaffii. Cleavage of the pro-domain and histidine tag by TEV protease yielded the mature form of the recombinant consensus PI SVMP (crSVMP-I). The consensus protein exhibited high immunogenicity in Swiss mice, whose anti-crSVMP-I immunoglobulins recognized in vitro, PI, P-II, and P-III SVMPs from 24 distinct Bothrops species. In addition, these antibodies were able to prevent or attenuate cutaneous hemorrhage induced by a bothropic venom mixture (B. jararaca, B. jararacussu, B. alternatus, B. neuwiedi, and B. moojeni) as well as by isolated venoms from B. atrox, B. asper, and B. leucurus in an in vivo experimental model. Together, these findings support the use of crSVMP-I as a rational immunogen with the potential to expand the efficacy and coverage of bothropic antivenoms.

articles.title: Anaplasma phagocytophilum Ats-1 modulates host ER translocation-coupled N-glycosylation through SDCBP and SEC61A2.
articles.abstract: Anaplasma phagocytophilum remodels host-cell processes through secreted effectors, but whether it targets ER translocation-coupled N-glycosylation remains unclear. Here, we investigated the role of the effector Ats-1 in this pathway. Ats-1 associated with SEC61A2 and modulated the SEC61A2-associated ER translocation-N-glycosylation pathway in an SDCBP-dependent manner. Ats-1 increased the abundance of the OST-associated components RPN2 and DDOST and altered the N-glycosylation status of representative membrane glycoproteins, including integrin β1, CD63, and transferrin receptor (TfR). Perturbation of the SDCBP-SEC61A2 axis attenuated these effects and was accompanied by changes in UPR- and autophagy-related markers. Together, these findings define an SDCBP-dependent Ats-1-SEC61A2 regulatory framework linking ER protein translocation to OST-associated glycoprotein processing and provide a basis for testing its relevance during authentic A. phagocytophilum infection.

articles.title: Effects of MASH risk genotypes on resmetirom efficacy in patients with MASH and fibrosis.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND & AIMS: Resmetirom, a thyroid hormone receptor beta agonist, improves metabolic dysfunction-associated steatohepatitis (MASH) and liver fibrosis in patients with non-cirrhotic MASH. Risk genotypes of PNPLA3, HSD17B13, TM6SF2, MTARC1, MBOAT7, and SERPINA1 have been associated with altered susceptibility to metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD), MASH, fibrosis, cirrhosis, and/or hepatocellular carcinoma. We evaluated the impact of MASLD risk genotypes on baseline characteristics and the response to resmetirom vs. placebo with respect to MASH, fibrosis, MRI-proton density fat fraction (MRI-PDFF), and other biomarkers.

METHODS: Testing the effects of MASLD risk genotypes or combinations of high-risk alleles on liver biopsy, MRI-PDFF, and biomarker responses to resmetirom was a pre-specified analysis in 738 patients enrolled in the MAESTRO-NASH phase III trial who consented to DNA collection, were genotyped for all genes, and had liver biopsies at baseline and Week 52.

RESULTS: At baseline, patients with high-risk genotypes of PNPLA3 or HSD17B13 had a lower frequency of metabolic risk factors, including type 2 diabetes mellitus and hypertension, than patients with low-risk genotypes. Interaction analyses and efficacy assessments indicated that resmetirom had similar positive effects on MASH resolution, fibrosis improvement on liver biopsy, MRI-PDFF response, and biomarkers at Week 52 in MAESTRO-NASH patients with high-risk genotypes of PNPLA3, HSD17B13, TM6SF2, MTARC1, and MBOAT7, either individually or as part of a composite genetic risk score. These effects were independent of sex, Hispanic ethnicity, and metabolic risk factors. Due to the limited sample size, the study was not powered to detect small effects of risk genotypes on resmetirom efficacy.

CONCLUSIONS: Resmetirom's effects on MASH, liver fibrosis, MRI-PDFF, and MASH biomarkers in the MAESTRO-NASH trial were not significantly impacted by the presence of common MASH risk genotypes, suggesting that resmetirom's mechanism of action may help mitigate the deleterious effects of MASH risk variants.

CLINICAL TRIAL: Number: NCT03900429 IMPACT AND IMPLICATIONS: Resmetirom has recently been approved for the treatment of metabolic dysfunction-associated steatohepatitis (MASH). It leads to MASH resolution and improvement of fibrosis in patients with non-cirrhotic MASH. Patients with MASH have higher prevalence of certain genetic variants which can be associated with more severe disease. In this study we evaluated the relationship between the presence of select MASH risk genotypes (e.g. PNPLA3, TM6SF2, or HSD17B13) or the combined total of MASH genetic risk alleles on the response to resmetirom and placebo in 738 patients with non-cirrhotic MASH with serial liver biopsies at baseline and week 52. Within the limitation of study sample size, resmetirom's benefits on MASH resolution, fibrosis improvement and hepatic steatosis were independent of the presence of MASH genetic risk genotypes either alone or in combination.

articles.title: Temporal assessment of spatial and single-cell transcriptomes identifies CD226-NECTIN2 T cell-cholangiocyte interaction in bile duct inflammation.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND AND AIMS: Primary sclerosing cholangitis (PSC) and primary biliary cholangitis (PBC) are inflammatory bile duct disorders affecting mostly young adults that often lead to liver cirrhosis and cancer. Especially for PSC, pathogenic mechanisms remain unclear and treatment options are lacking. To better understand biliary disease processes in bile duct inflammation, we analyzed livers of NOD.c3c4 mice by spatial and single-cell (scRNA-seq) transcriptomics, identifying key cell types, interactions and potential changes over time that were validated in human liver explants.

METHODS: Livers of 10, 20 and 40-week-old male NOD.c3c4 mice were used for spatial transcriptomics and scRNA-seq. Differentially-expressed genes at different time points were analyzed using the CellphoneDB database with a focus on T cell-related interactions. CD226-NECTIN2 interaction was validated using co-culture experiments and antibody treatment in NOD.c3c4 mice. CD226-NECTIN2 in PSC, PBC and alcohol-related liver disease (ALD) explants was analyzed by spatial transcriptomics and immunofluorescence.

RESULTS: Spatial transcriptomics consistently distinguished inflamed and non-inflamed liver areas in NOD.c3c4 mice at different ages. When combined with scRNA-seq enriched for immune cells and cholangiocytes, key inflammatory cell types were localized to biliary structures. Using differentially-expressed genes and a curated overview of biologically-validated interactions (CellphoneDB), the CD226-NECTIN2 T cell-cholangiocyte interaction was discovered. Knock-down of Nectin2 in vitro and anti-CD226 blocking in NOD.c3c4 mice specifically reduced T cell activation and diseased human liver showed consistent CD226-NECTIN2 co-localization at inflamed bile ducts.

CONCLUSIONS: By combining spatial transcriptomics and scRNA-seq in NOD.c3c4 mice, we generated a pipeline for in-depth identification of potential disease relevant genes and interaction partners. The T cell-cholangiocyte interaction CD226-NECTIN2 was identified, functionally validated and detected in human disease highlighting this interaction as a possible future treatment target.

IMPACT AND IMPLICATIONS: PSC is an intractable immune-mediated cholestatic liver disease that mainly affects young people and has a significant impact on families and the healthcare system due to treatment costs and sick leave. Our study aimed to find new ways of understanding PSC and highlight potential treatment targets by first identifying disease-relevant cell interactions in a mouse model, followed by confirmation in human PSC livers.

articles.title: Sex differences in MASLD and fitness improvement during a weight loss intervention for adolescents living with obesity.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND AND AIMS: The interplay between liver and muscle health is incompletely understood, especially in adolescents living with obesity. Cardiopulmonary exercise testing (CPET) evaluates cardiorespiratory fitness through peak oxygen uptake ( O2peak). The association of baseline cardiorespiratory fitness and metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD), and their longitudinal co-evolution during a lifestyle intervention, have not been studied in this population.

METHODS: Adolescents with obesity receiving a lifestyle intervention in a residential setting were prospectively followed for 9 - 12 months. At baseline and after 6 months, MASLD was defined as a controlled-attenuation parameter ≥ 248dB/m. Cardiorespiratory fitness and body composition were assessed at the start and throughout the trajectory.

RESULTS: 142 adolescents (69 boys) were included. Relative O2peak was 37.9 (33.5 - 42.3) vs. 43.4 (39.7 - 49.8 ; p=0.004) mL∙kg-1∙min-1 [LM] in boys with and without MASLD, and respectively 36.3 (31.7 - 43.2) vs. 41.3 (34.8 - 46.2 ; p=0.055) mL∙kg-1∙min-1 [LM] in girls. Oxygen uptake efficiency slope (OUES) was respectively 40.6 (35.8 - 46.3) vs. 46.7 (41.6 - 53.8; p=0.011) in boys and 39.1 (34.7 - 45.1) vs. 44.2 (39.1 - 50.8 ; p=0.011) in girls. For boys with MASLD, initial relative O2peak was the lowest for those with persistent MASLD during the lifestyle trajectory (33.5; 30.5 - 36.6 mL∙kg-1∙min-1 [LM]). During the lifestyle intervention, lean body mass (LM) was preserved in boys with MASLD resolution and girls without baseline MASLD, whereas boys with persistent MASLD and girls with baseline MASLD experienced LM losses of 7 - 9%.

CONCLUSION: Lower baseline cardiorespiratory fitness, independent from (fat) mass, is associated with (persistent) MASLD during a residential lifestyle intervention. LM preservation during weight loss trajectories, with concomitant improvement of maximal oxygen uptake, are important therapeutic targets.

IMPACT AND IMPLICATIONS: Metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD) has become the most common liver disease in children and adolescents worldwide. Although a better cardiorespiratory fitness at the start of a lifestyle intervention is linked with more weight loss, its association with cardiometabolic health and MASLD has not been assessed. A lower initial cardiorespiratory fitness was observed in adolescents with (persistent) MASLD, and in boys with an increased transient elastography. During the lifestyle intervention, boys and girls without MASLD or boys who experience MASLD resolution preserve their lean mass. Improvement of cardiorespiratory fitness and preservation of lean mass during a structured lifestyle intervention are important therapeutic targets, and sex-specific lifestyle interventions need to be developed and validated.

articles.title: Biologic Injection-Related Pain in Severe Asthma, Its Impact on Treatment Aversion, and Pain-Relief Approach: A Multicenter Observational Study.
articles.journal: The journal of allergy and clinical immunology. In practice
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Although biologic therapies are essential for managing severe asthma, injection-related pain may be a frequently overlooked barrier to treatment persistence.

OBJECTIVE: To quantify biologic injection-related pain in asthma cases, identify clinical factors associated with such pain and treatment aversion, and explore practical pain-relief approaches.

METHODS: This multicenter observational study enrolled patients with asthma receiving biologics between May 2025 and March 2026. Insertion pain, injection pain, and treatment aversion attributable to injection-related pain were assessed using 0 to 10 visual analog scales. Associations between clinical factors, pain scores, and treatment aversion scores and the effects of local pressure and cooling at the injection site were evaluated. Patients with diabetes mellitus receiving tirzepatide served as a reference group.

RESULTS: In total, 122 biologic-treated and 27 tirzepatide-treated patient responses were analyzed. Mean insertion and injection pain scores for biologics were 3.00 ± 2.60 and 3.28 ± 2.91, respectively. Adjusted pain scores did not differ significantly across biologics and tirzepatide. Insertion pain was associated with anxiety and arm injection, whereas injection pain was associated with younger age and female sex. Both insertion and injection pain showed independent associations with log-transformed treatment aversion score (unstandardized regression coefficient [B] = 0.08, 95% CI, 0.03-0.12, and B = 0.07, 95% CI, 0.03-0.11, respectively). Injection-site cooling significantly reduced both pain types.

CONCLUSIONS: Among patients receiving biologics for asthma, injection-related pain is common and independently associated with treatment aversion. Local cooling may offer a simple approach to reducing injection-related pain and addressing treatment aversion.

articles.title: Thermal Dose and Thermobiophysical Regulation of Skeletal Tissues: A Context-Dependent Framework from Molecular Thermosensing to Microenvironment Remodeling.
articles.journal: Progress in biophysics and molecular biology
articles.abstract: Temperature is a biologically active physical variable in skeletal tissues, but apparently contradictory findings often arise because thermal magnitude is reported without the accompanying time, spatial, mechanical, and pathological context. This critical review synthesizes evidence on temperature-dependent regulation of bone and cartilage using a thermal-dose framework that distinguishes local mild hypothermia, chronic systemic cold exposure, adaptive mild heating, and hyperthermic injury. Representative studies indicate that no universal boundary temperature exists: transient exposures of approximately 39-41 °C can support heat-shock-protein-dependent osteogenic or chondrogenic adaptation, whereas longer exposures at the same or slightly higher temperatures may inhibit proliferation; cartilage injury increases steeply around 50-55 °C, while sustained culture at 34-35.5 °C suppresses osteoblast differentiation and promotes osteoclastogenesis. We therefore interpret biological outcome as a function of temperature-time history, spatial gradients, delivery modality, tissue depth, mechanical/osmotic co-stimulation, and disease state rather than nominal temperature alone. At the molecular level, mild heat can be buffered by proteostasis networks and polymodal TRPV4-Ca2+ signaling, whereas excessive thermal load increases protein unfolding/aggregation, oxidative and mitochondrial stress, and remodeling signals from osteocytes and other microenvironmental cells. Evidence is strongest for cell- and tissue-specific response windows, but clinical dose-response relationships remain incompletely validated. We propose a testable multiscale framework that links bioheat transfer, molecular damage-versus-adaptation, and multicellular remodeling, together with a minimum reporting set for thermal interventions. NIR photothermal and magnetothermal biomaterials illustrate the promise of spatially controlled heating, but their translation requires direct target-tissue thermometry, modality-specific dosimetry, and patient-stratified validation.

articles.title: Heparin Management and Coagulation in Acute Aortic Dissection Surgery: A Randomised Controlled Trial.
articles.journal: Journal of thrombosis and haemostasis : JTH
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Acute type A aortic dissection remains a life-threatening condition characterised by profound consumptive coagulopathy and perioperative transfusion requirements. The optimal anticoagulation strategy during cardiopulmonary bypass remains uncertain.

OBJECTIVES: To assess baseline coagulation and compare the impact of two standard anticoagulation strategies on thrombin generation and clinical outcomes in patients undergoing emergent surgery for acute type A aortic dissection.

PATIENTS/METHODS: In this single-centre, partially blinded, randomised controlled trial, patients were allocated 1:1 to heparin-dose response (HDR) or activated clotting time (ACT) guided anticoagulation. Randomisation was stratified by organ dysfunction and preoperative anticoagulation. Primary endpoint was change in prothrombin fragment 1+2 (F1+2) from baseline to heparin reversal after cardiopulmonary bypass. Secondary endpoints included coagulation markers, bleeding, transfusion, and clinical outcomes up to 90 days.

RESULTS: Between December 2022 and September 2024, 26 patients were randomised (HDR= 14; ACT= 12). Both groups demonstrated marked baseline consumptive coagulopathy with ongoing intraoperative thrombin generation. Despite baseline differences in F1+2, the primary endpoint did not differ significantly (median change HDR: 333 [IQR 654] vs. ACT: -92 pmol/L [IQR 1984], p = 0.31). Post hoc baseline-adjusted ANCOVA sensitivity analysis of log-transformed change (n = 25) showed a 14% lower fold-increase in HDR compared with ACT (HDR/ACT ratio 0.86, 95% CI 0.63-1.17; p = 0.32). Secondary endpoints were comparable, except for a lower protamine-to-heparin ratio in HDR group (0.51 vs 0.75; p < 0.001).

CONCLUSIONS: Thrombin generation was insufficiently suppressed by either anticoagulation protocol. Exacerbation of preoperative consumptive coagulopathy highlights the insufficiency of current anticoagulation strategies in acute aortic dissection.

articles.title: Understanding the Needs of Spanish-Speaking First-Time Mothers in Nurse-Family Partnership: Quantitative Findings and Nurse Practice Insights.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To examine the characteristics and needs of Spanish-speaking first-time mothers enrolled in the Nurse-Family Partnership (NFP) and to contextualize quantitative findings with observations from a bilingual nurse key informant regarding barriers, challenges, and service-access needs among Spanish-speaking clients.

DESIGN: A cross-sectional observational study combining quantitative data from mothers via retrospective chart review with qualitative insights from a single key informant interview with a Spanish-speaking nurse home visitor.

SETTING: A Texas NFP program serving low-income, first-time mothers.

PARTICIPANTS: Quantitative data were collected from 305 first-time mothers enrolled in NFP, including 62 Spanish-speaking and 243 non-Spanish-speaking participants. Qualitative data were collected through a recorded 50-min semistructured interview in English with a bilingual NFP nurse who primarily serves Spanish-speaking mothers.

METHODS: Quantitative data from routine NFP home visits were analyzed using descriptive statistics, chi-square tests, and independent-samples t tests to compare Spanish-speaking and non-Spanish-speaking participants. Measures included demographics, insurance type, health behaviors, depression, anxiety, intimate partner violence, and referrals to services. The nurse interview was analyzed using thematic analysis to contextualize the quantitative findings.

RESULTS: Quantitative analyses showed that Spanish-speaking participants differed from non-Spanish-speaking participants across several sociodemographic, insurance, health behavior, mental health, and referral outcomes. Spanish-speaking participants reported lower depression, anxiety, and intimate partner violence. The nurse interview generated four themes: complex systems navigation; trust building as the foundation for engagement; language, cultural, and structural barriers; and resilience-based nursing practice.

CONCLUSION: This study highlights the distinct needs and contextual challenges of Spanish-speaking first-time mothers enrolled in NFP and underscores the value of bilingual, culturally responsive, and relationship-centered home-visiting practices to support system navigation, client engagement, and access to maternal health and community resources.

articles.title: Marinelli Equation vs. DIN 6861-1: Comparison of the Achieved Therapeutic Thyroid Dose after Radioiodine Therapy Using Different Pretherapeutic Dosimetry.
articles.abstract:
AIM: Pretherapeutic dosimetry is an essential component of individualized radioiodine therapy. This study aimed to compare radioiodine therapies planned according to the Marinelli equation or DIN 6861-1:2021-11 with regard to the deviation of the planned and achieved thyroid doses in patients with benign thyroid diseases.

METHODS: The relative deviation of the achieved thyroid dose during radioiodine therapy from the pretherapeutically planned dose was analyzed according to the applied dosimetric method. Patient cohorts with goiter, recurrent goiter, disseminated and focal thyroid autonomy and autoimmune thyroid disease were evaluated. The cohorts were compared using the Mann-Whitney U- test.

RESULTS: For goiter, recurrent goiter, disseminated thyroid autonomy and focal thyroid autonomy, radioiodine therapies planned according to DIN 6861-1:2021-11 were associated with significantly smaller deviations between the planned and achieved thyroid doses than therapies planned according to the Marinelli equation. Depending on the diagnostic group, the mean relative deviation was approximately 15 to 32 percentage points lower in the DIN cohorts. The DIN cohorts also showed less variability in dose deviations. In patients with autoimmune thyroid disease, no statistically significant differences of the mean relative deviation were observed between the dosimetric methods. However, variability was also lower in the DIN cohorts.

CONCLUSION: The use of DIN 6861-1:2021-11 is associated with improved prediction of the thyroid dose compared with the Marinelli equation and may contribute to more precise individualized planning of radioiodine therapy in patients with benign thyroid diseases.

articles.title: A wavelet-guided diffusion method for brain magnetic resonance parameter mapping using MOLED-based datasets: proof-of-principle.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Quantitative magnetic resonance imaging (qMRI) can noninvasively acquire parametric maps, providing quantitative biomarkers for clinical diagnosis. Owing to their distinct physical origins, various parametric maps have inherent differences in numerical scale. The existing deep learning methods primarily focus on end-to-end feature learning in the image domain without fully considering these inherent differences, which exhibit limited generalizability when processing diverse quantitative tasks. To improve the generalizability and robustness of the deep learning model for parameter mapping tasks and to deliver dependable quantitative references for clinical diagnosis, we propose a wavelet-guided diffusion model.

APPROACH: We extend the discrete convolution wavelet transform (DCWT) to two-dimension and combine it with a conditional denoising diffusion model to develop a diffusion-based discrete convolution wavelet transform (Diff-DCWT) for parameter mapping. Diff-DCWT achieves accurate parameter mapping under the guidance of wavelet coefficient maps, thereby reducing reliance on image domain learning. The performance of Diff-DCWT is evaluated through simulation and in vivo experiments across T2, T2 * , and ADC mapping tasks.

MAIN RESULTS: Both simulation and healthy volunteer experiments demonstrate that T2, T2 * , and ADC maps obtained from Diff-DCWT maintain excellent visual quality and quantitative accuracy. Clinical case studies validate the efficacy of T2 and ADC maps from Diff-DCWT for stroke staging. In glioma characterization, Diff-DCWT enables accurate T2 mapping, facilitating clear differentiation between lesional and normal brain regions.

SIGNIFICANCE: Diff-DCWT establishes a high-fidelity framework for parameter mapping, with its clinical efficacy validated in stroke staging and glioma characterization. Moreover, this work demonstrates the potential of wavelet-domain prior guidance for deep learning-based qMRI applications.

articles.title: Biodistribution and dosimetry of free118Te, anin vivogenerator of the positron emitter118Sb for long-term positron emission tomography.
articles.abstract: Objective. Tellurium-118 (118Te;t1/2= 6.00 ± 0.02 d) can act as anin vivogenerator of the positron emitter antimony-118 (118Sb;t1/2= 3.6 ± 0.3 min), enabling positron emission tomography (PET) over a week or longer. This work assessed absorbed doses associated with free118Te to establish a dosimetric safety basis for118Te radiopharmaceuticals.Approach. Injection solutions of free118Te were prepared by alpha-particle irradiation of an enriched tin-116 target followed by radiochemical isolation.Ex vivobiodistribution in healthy female Slc:ICR mice was acquired at seven time points from 2 h to 29 d postinjection (n= 6 per time point). Time-integrated activity coefficients were computed from the biodistribution profiles and extrapolated to a human model using relative mass scaling. Absorbed dose coefficients (ADCs) were calculated following the Medical Internal Radiation Dose formalism with computational phantoms implemented in the dosimetry software OLINDA. Dosimetric contributions from118Te and its coproduced radioisotopic impurity119mTe (t1/2= 4.69 ± 0.04 d), along with their equilibrium daughters118Sb and119Sb, were individually assessed.Main results. The kidneys exhibited the highest ADC in both mouse (2666.0 mGy MBq-1) and human (2.639 mGy MBq-1) models. Bone received the second-highest ADC in the mouse model, 1855.5 mGy MBq-1. Antimony-118 dominated absorbed doses across all organs examined, accounting for more than 82% of ADCs in both models. Contributions from118Te,119mTe, and119Sb were minor by comparison.Significance. The kidneys and bone were identified as the primary dosimetric targets of free118Te, with its daughter118Sb being the principal dose contributor. The limited dosimetric impact from118Te provides justification for its use as anin vivogenerator of118Sb for long-term PET. The ADCs reported here offer a quantitative basis for assessing the dosimetric safety of118Te radiopharmaceuticals.

articles.title: A generalized phenomenological model of oxygen depletion for FLASH particle radiotherapy: evidence fromin vitrodata.
articles.abstract: Ultra-high dose rate (uHDR: FLASH) radiotherapy reduces normal tissue toxicity while preserving tumour control. The oxygen depletion hypothesis posits that rapid oxygen consumption during FLASH irradiation transiently reduces radiosensitivity. However, experimental measurements suggest oxygen depletion may be limited, particularly under normoxia. This study quantitatively assesses the adequacy of this hypothesis in reproducing experimentally observed sparing effects by comparing mechanistic simulations with in vitro cell survival data across a wide range of irradiation conditions.Approach. We developed a phenomenological framework for radiolytic oxygen depletion incorporating temporal dose delivery, dose rate, and linear energy transfer (LET). LET dependence was included through oxygen consumption efficiency and the maximum oxygen enhancement ratio. For direct comparison, simulation results were linked to clonogenic cell survival using a damage reduction factor (DRF) derived from the linear-quadratic model. Simulated DRFs were compared with experimental DRFs from six independent in vitro studies involving electrons, protons, helium ions, and carbon ions over broad ranges of LET, oxygenation, and dose rates using parity plots, residual analyses, stratified weighted statistics, and correlation analyses.Main results. Under most irradiation conditions, simulated DRFs remained close to unity (minimum values approximately 0.96), indicating limited predicted protection from oxygen depletion. Conversely, experimental DRFs exhibited substantially larger deviations. Stratified analyses revealed systematic discrepancies between simulated and experimental DRFs across oxygenation, LET, and dose rate, with pronounced disagreement under normoxia, high LET, and ultra-high dose rates. Residual analyses demonstrated underestimation of the sparing effect by the model. Correlation analyses showed statistically insignificant associations between simulated and experimental metrics.Significance. The oxygen depletion model considered in this work insufficiently reproduces the observed sparing effect under the in vitro conditions considered. Additional biological and physicochemical mechanisms likely play a significant role. This framework provides a quantitative basis for evaluating alternative mechanisms and integrating future experimental data toward a more complete understanding of FLASH radiotherapy.

articles.title: AnF-DiffPET: anatomy- and frequency-guided diffusion for simulated low-dose PET/CT denoising.
articles.abstract: Positron emission tomography (PET) provides essential functional information for disease assessment. However, reducing injected activity or acquisition time produces low-dose (LD) PET with stronger count-dependent noise and less reliable uptake quantification. Diffusion models offer a promising solution for PET denoising by progressively recovering high-dose (HD) PET images from LD inputs. However, LD-to-HD PET denoising remains challenging because of limited anatomical guidance, unstable multi-scale feature propagation, and inaccurate recovery of uptake patterns in the frequency domain.Approach: We propose AnF-DiffPET, an anatomy- and frequency-guided diffusion framework for computed tomography (CT)-conditioned LD PET denoising. The framework integrates Anatomical-Frequency Guidance (AFG), Multi-Scale Cross-Transformer Reconstruction (MSCTR), and Frequency-Contrastive Hard Mining (FCHM) to enhance anatomy-aware feature modulation and frequency-domain consistency during denoising.Main results: Experimental results across four simulated low-dose PET/CT datasets show that the proposed method improves image fidelity, anatomical consistency, and quantitative fidelity over representative CNN-based, GAN-based, Transformer-based, Mamba-based, and diffusion-based methods.Significance: AnF-DiffPET provides a PET/CT-specific diffusion restoration framework that combines anatomical guidance, multi-scale feature reconstruction, and frequency-domain regularization for LD PET denoising. The code and trained models will be publicly released upon acceptance.

articles.title: CAR T cells for autoimmune diseases: 2026 update of the EBMT-ISCT-JACIE practice harmonisation and consensus recommendations.
authors: participants to the Cell Therapies for Autoimmune Diseases: CAR-T from Biology to Clinical Application course
articles.abstract: Autoimmune diseases are a heterogeneous group of chronic diseases characterised by loss of immune tolerance with substantial morbidity and mortality. Since 2021, chimeric antigen receptor (CAR) T cells have recently emerged as a promising treatment option for patients with severe, refractory autoimmune diseases. In 2024, an international expert panel from the European Society for Blood and Marrow Transplantation (EBMT), the International Society for Cell and Gene Therapy (ISCT), and the Joint Accreditation Committee of ISCT and EBMT (JACIE) released the first best-practice recommendations on CAR T cells for autoimmune diseases. Using the same consensus methodology, these living recommendations were updated thereafter. The 2026 consensus reviews current evidence and expert practices on CAR T cells for rheumatic, neurological, haematological, other autoimmune diseases, and paediatric indications, providing updated, expert-based recommendations on patient selection, diagnostic investigation, clinical management, follow up, and immune monitoring for each disease group. Unmet needs and future research priorities are also highlighted.

articles.title: Growth patterns of children with congenital Zika syndrome in Brazil: a matched-cohort study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Children born with congenital Zika syndrome typically present with structural abnormalities and neurological impairments that can disrupt postnatal growth. We aimed to evaluate longitudinal anthropometric trajectories of children with congenital Zika syndrome compared with children without congenital Zika syndrome in Brazil.

METHODS: In this matched-cohort study, we used Brazilian administrative data on singleton livebirths from Jan 1, 2015, to Dec 31, 2018, with follow-up routine primary care health data from birth to age 5 years. We excluded children with missing or inconsistent information about sex, type of pregnancy, birthweight, gestational age, date of birth, and anthropometric measurements. Cases of congenital Zika syndrome were obtained from the Brazilian Ministry of Health's Public Health Event Registry. For children classified with congenital Zika syndrome, we excluded those with a diagnosis of congenital syphilis or toxoplasmosis. An exactly matched comparison group of children with a similar likelihood of exposure to the Zika virus was selected. Descriptive statistics was used to compare anthropometric characteristics among children with congenital Zika syndrome and microcephaly, children with congenital Zika syndrome without microcephaly, and children without congenital Zika syndrome. Using mixed-effects models, we estimated mean trajectories of length or height (cm), weight (kg), and BMI (kg/m2) for these three groups. Multi-state models, stratified by microcephaly status and sex, were applied to compare transitions between nutritional status (based on WHO growth indicators) over time.

FINDINGS: We analysed growth measurements for 1268 children with congenital Zika syndrome and 6340 matched controls. Measurements indicative of stunting (length-for-age and height-for-age Z score <-2), underweight (weight-for-age Z score <-2), malnutrition (BMI-for-age Z score <-2), and wasting (weight-for-length and weight-for-height Z score <-2) were more frequent among children with congenital Zika syndrome and microcephaly (1676 [49·2%] of 3408, 1623 [39·3%] of 4126, 743 [21·8%] of 3408, and 839 [24·6%] of 3408, respectively) and children with congenital Zika syndrome but no microcephaly (924 [30·5%] of 3028, 857 [24·0%] of 3577, 566 [18·7%] of 3028, and 602 [19·9%] of 3028, respectively) than among children without congenital Zika syndrome (3489 [11·0%] of 31 836, 1355 [3·5%] of 38 172, 1490 [4·7%] of 31 836, and 1410 [4·4%] of 31 836, respectively; all p<0·0001). At age 5 years, adjusted mean height was 6·61 cm less in children with congenital Zika syndrome and microcephaly and 4·21 cm less in those without microcephaly than matched controls. In transition models, the 6-month probability of recovery from severe stunting (≥-6 SD to <-3 SD) among children with congenital Zika syndrome with microcephaly was 0·32 (95% CI 0·27-0·37) in males and 0·24 (0·20-0·29) in females. The transition probabilities increased among children with congenital Zika syndrome and no microcephaly (0·47 [95% CI 0·40-0·53] in males and 0·37 [0·30-0·44] in females). By contrast, the transition probabilities were at least 0·75 among all children without congenital Zika syndrome. Expected first passage times, representing the expected time to transition from one nutritional state to another, also indicated slower recovery in children with congenital Zika syndrome.

INTERPRETATION: A substantial and persistent burden of growth impairment in children with congenital Zika syndrome highlights the need for sustained growth monitoring and targeted nutritional interventions to support long-term health in this population.

FUNDING: Wellcome Trust, Brazilian Ministry of Health.

TRANSLATION: For the Portuguese translation of the abstract see Supplementary Materials section.

articles.title: Long-term immunogenicity and efficacy of the quadrivalent human papillomavirus vaccine in women with HIV: a longitudinal cohort study.
authors: CTN 236 HPV in HIV Study Team
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Understanding the impact of the human papillomavirus (HPV) vaccine in women with HIV, who have higher rates of HPV infection and associated disease, is vital to achieving cervical cancer elimination. We aimed to assess the immunogenicity and efficacy of the quadrivalent HPV (qHPV) vaccine up to 9 years in a cohort of women with HIV.

METHODS: This longitudinal multicentre cohort study recruited girls and women with HIV aged 9 years and older from 14 clinics providing HIV and gynaecological care across Canada. Participants were administered three doses of qHPV vaccine at 0, 2, and 6 months and followed up from July 1, 2008, to June 27, 2019. Clinical data, anti-HPV serology, liquid-based cervical cytology, and HPV DNA genotyping were conducted at baseline and every 6-12 months. Immunogenicity endpoints were anti-HPV geometric mean titres (GMTs) and seropositivity rates. We assessed the effect of time-varying HIV parameters on time to seroreversion with extended Cox regression models. GMTs for an age-restricted subset (24-45 years) were compared with a published cohort with one-sample t tests. Efficacy endpoints were the incidence of persistent qHPV, genital warts, and cervical intraepithelial neoplasia of grade two and higher (CIN2+).

FINDINGS: There were 228 participants in the per-protocol population, with a median age at baseline of 38·5 years (IQR 32·0-45·4), median CD4 count of 499·5 (IQR 380·8-700·0) cells per μL, and 160 (70·2%) participants had suppressed HIV viral loads (<50 copies per mL). Median follow-up was 5·9 years (IQR 2·3-7·7). In the per-protocol population, following very high seroconversion rates at month 7, during follow-up there were 18 (13·6%) of 132 seroreversions for HPV6, 22 (11·8%) of 186 for HPV11, 12 (8·5%) of 141 for HPV16, and 60 (36·4%) of 165 for HPV18. Peak antibody titres and serial HIV viral load were significant predictors of time to seroreversion. Anti-HPV GMTs were similar between women with and without HIV (historical comparator group) for up to 9 years. In the per-protocol population, the incidence of persistent qHPV was 0·52 (95% CI 0·22-1·10) per 100 person-years, the incidence of genital warts was 0·37 (0·12-0·87) per 100 person-years, and the incidence of CIN2+ was 0·00 (0·00-0·24) per 100 person-years.

INTERPRETATION: These data show low rates of infection and disease in this vaccinated cohort of women with HIV. Continual HIV viral load suppression after vaccination is important to ensure continued protection.

FUNDING: Canadian Institutes for Health Research (CIHR), CIHR Canadian HIV Trials Network, and in-kind contribution from Merck Canada.

articles.title: Fungal hyphae through the lens of microfluidic devices: From biological properties to novel therapeutic opportunities.
articles.abstract: Fungal diseases are increasingly being recognized as a major health problem worldwide. Advancing therapeutic approaches against fungal pathogens require comprehensive knowledge of their biological properties, which enable fungi to explore host environments, interact with host cells and coinhabiting microorganisms, adopt colonization and infective strategies. Thus, fungus intrinsic as well as extrinsic mechanisms functionally cooperate for successful host infection and disease development. In this regard, fungal hyphae, i.e. long, filamentous structures with polarized tip growth, represent a unique feature of multicellular fungi and play critical roles during the infectious process, calling for in-depth characterization of their functional and structural properties. In this context, reproducing hyphal growth in physiological conditions represents a fundamental prerequisite for disease modeling and therapeutic development. For their potential to accommodate and interconnect cells and miniature tissues, microfluidic devices stand as unique opportunities in this direction by overcoming acknowledged limits of animal models and traditional cell cultures. Based on these premises, we herein provide an overview of the use of microfluidic devices in the study of fungal hyphae, from the investigation of their biological properties to the analysis of inter-organismal networking, including the interaction between fungal hyphae and host cells. By dissecting hyphal strategies of environmental navigation as well as modalities of cell-cell interactions, resorting to microfluidics devices may provide novel opportunities for therapeutic targeting of fungal pathogens, in line with the objectives of the World Health Organization.

articles.title: Oncology Nurses' Educational Needs Regarding Genomic and Genetic Tests in the Era of Precision Oncology.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: We sought to assess oncology nurses' general knowledge of cancer genomics and genetics, evaluate oncology nurses' application of genomics and biomarkers in oncology nursing practice, and determine oncology nurses' educational needs and learning preferences related to cancer genomics and biomarkers.

METHODS: All the oncology nurses who care for cancer patients in an academic medical center (n=900) were sent an email to complete the Oncology Nursing Survey of Genomics and Biomarkers in the Era of Precision Cancer Care. The survey obtained information on general knowledge of cancer genomics/genetics and biomarkers, application of genomics and biomarkers in oncology clinical practice, and learning needs of oncology nurses. Descriptive statistics were calculated for responses to the survey items.

RESULTS: The survey response rate was 22.4%. The majority of the oncology nurses rated their understanding of the genetics of common diseases as poor. The majority of the nurses knew the difference between somatic and germline mutations, as well as various genetic variations. While only 9.4% of the nurses indicated that they had received formal education about genomics, greater than 50% had taken continuing education courses or "were learning on the job."
