The VR was associated with statistically significant reductions in procedural pain (SMD -0.68, 95% CI -1.25 to -0.11) and anxiety (SMD -1.39, 95% CI -2.64 to -0.14), although both estimates carried substantial heterogeneity (I² = 91.7% and 89%, respectively). Subgroup analysis of pain by procedure type revealed marked divergence: VR produced negligible benefit during cystoscopy (SMD -0.16, 95% CI -0.32 to 0.00) but a large reduction during TRUS-Bx (SMD -1.84, 95% CI -2.82 to -0.85), the latter based on only two studies with substantial heterogeneity. Narrative synthesis showed consistent improvements in patient satisfaction and procedural comfort and attenuation of physiological stress markers. No serious VR-related adverse events were identified across approximately 900 patients. The certainty of evidence was low for all outcomes. The HMD VR may offer meaningful reductions in procedural pain and anxiety during selected awake urological procedures, particularly those characterised by sustained nociceptive stimulation and high anticipatory distress, with a consistent safety profile. However, the very high between-study heterogeneity means these pooled averages should be interpreted cautiously, and the benefit appears procedure-specific rather than uniform. The benefit appears procedure-specific and is unlikely to exceed established pharmacological standards during routine cystoscopy. Adequately powered procedure-specific trials are needed before VR can be considered a standard adjunct.

articles.title: Neuropathic Pain: From Mechanisms to Therapeutic Interventions.
articles.abstract: Neuropathic pain is caused by injury or disease of the somatosensory system. It involves peripheral nerve injury, central sensitization, transmitter imbalance, glial activation, and large-scale network remodeling. Despite substantial advances in pain biology, clinical assessment continues to rely predominantly on patient-reported symptoms, sensory examination, and conventional neurophysiological testing, approaches that often fail to delineate the predominant biological mechanisms underlying pain in individual patients. Recent advances in sensory phenotyping and multimodal imaging have enabled in vivo characterization of abnormalities at the receptor, neuroinflammatory, and circuit levels, thereby providing a foundation for mechanism-based stratification and more individualized therapeutic decision-making. This review summarizes neuropathic pain from clinical stratification to mechanism-based imaging and therapeutic intervention. We describe key clinical dimensions, including sensory gain, sensory loss, peripheral and central pain generators, mixed nociceptive-neuropathic pain, central sensitization, and autonomic or small-fiber modifiers. These dimensions help explain why patients with the same diagnosis may show different symptoms and treatment responses. We also review major molecular mechanisms, including glutamatergic overactivity, GABAergic and glycinergic disinhibition, monoaminergic remodeling, and neuroimmune modulation. These changes reshape spinal, thalamocortical, limbic, salience, reward, cerebellar, and descending control circuits. Peripheral nerve ultrasound and MR neurography can help identify structural peripheral pain generators. PET, MRS, MRI, DTI, fMRI, EEG, and multimodal imaging can assess receptor availability, neurotransmitter balance, neuroinflammation, white matter integrity, and network connectivity. These imaging tools may link clinical phenotypes with biological mechanisms and help define mechanism-based subtypes. Imaging biomarkers may also support treatment selection, treatment monitoring, neuromodulation targeting, and translational trial design. This framework supports a shift from symptom-based assessment to mechanism-guided precision care for neuropathic pain.

articles.title: Clinical performance and practical limitations of large language models in respiratory medicine.
articles.abstract: This Journal club discusses three recent studies evaluating large language models (LLMs) in respiratory medicine and allergy. In COPD, ChatGPT-3.5 was rated higher than Bing Chat by respiratory specialists for accuracy, completeness, clarity and safety, although clinically important omissions remained. In asthma, 13 out of 14 models exceeded 85% accuracy on multiple-choice questions and five exceeded 95%, but performance was lower and more variable in objective structured clinical examinations. In allergen immunotherapy, ChatGPT-4 achieved fair overall DISCERN quality, but showed insufficient Journal of the American Medical Association (JAMA) benchmark reliability and produced responses that were often difficult to read. Together, these studies show that LLMs perform best on structured and familiar knowledge tasks, while weaknesses persist in completeness, transparency, readability and clinically nuanced application. Current evidence supports supervised educational use in respiratory medicine and allergy, but not unsupervised patient counselling or autonomous clinical deployment.

articles.title: Mechanical ventilation in acute brain injury.
articles.abstract: Acute brain injury (ABI) includes traumatic brain injury, subarachnoid and intracerebral haemorrhage, ischaemic stroke and global hypoxic-ischaemic injury, and patients often require admission to intensive care. Although pathologically heterogeneous, they share common mechanisms of primary injury followed by secondary brain injury. Systemic derangements such as hypoxaemia, dysregulated carbon dioxide tension and elevated intracranial pressure (ICP) may exacerbate secondary injury and should be avoided. Patients with ABI often require invasive mechanical ventilation (IMV), and of these up to 19-22% may develop acute respiratory distress syndrome. Lung-protective ventilation (LPV) strategies using low tidal volumes and moderate positive end-expiratory pressure to minimise ventilator-induced lung injury are established practices in patients requiring IMV. However, strict application of LPV principles may conflict with neuro-protective goals, particularly carbon dioxide control to optimise cerebral blood flow and avoid rises in ICP. This review examines the physiological tension between lung and brain protection, focusing on neuro-respiratory interactions and brain-lung crosstalk. We synthesise the evidence on ventilatory strategies in the context of patients with ABI, discuss the implications for neurological and pulmonary outcomes, and highlight the need for an integrated, individualised approach to ventilation in these patients.

articles.title: Advanced Glycation End Products: From Pathogenesis to Treatment.
articles.abstract: Advanced glycation end products (AGEs) are chemically heterogeneous modifications generated through nonenzymatic glycation, glycoxidation, and carbonyl stress. Their accumulation increases during aging and is accelerated by hyperglycemia, oxidative stress, inflammation, exogenous exposure, and impaired renal clearance. Although AGE biology has often been framed around the AGE-RAGE-oxidative stress axis, current evidence supports a broader systems-level model in which AGE burden reflects the balance among formation, detoxification, tissue retention, and clearance. This review summarizes AGE chemistry, endogenous and exogenous sources, detoxification pathways, receptor systems, and mechanisms of AGE-mediated tissue injury. We distinguish two complementary pathogenic routes: receptor-independent structural damage, including protein dysfunction, proteostatic stress, extracellular matrix crosslinking, and altered tissue mechanics; and receptor-dependent signaling, mainly through RAGE-mediated redox-inflammatory amplification. We then examine the clinical relevance of AGEs in diabetes, cardiovascular disease, chronic kidney disease, neurovascular and retinal dysfunction, fibrosis, and aging-related tissue decline. Particular attention is given to compartment-specific biomarker interpretation, because circulating free adducts, protein-bound AGEs, tissue autofluorescence, dietary AGE estimates, and dicarbonyl stress markers are not interchangeable. Finally, we evaluate therapeutic strategies and propose a framework that matches each intervention to the relevant mechanism and can be tested clinically. In doing so, the review clarifies major conceptual and methodological uncertainties in AGE research and provides a foundation for more rigorous biomarker interpretation, study design, and clinical translation.

articles.title: Acute Cor Pulmonale Caused by Pulmonary Tumor Thrombotic Microangiopathy as the Initial Presentation of Multiple Myeloma: A Case Report.
articles.abstract: Pulmonary tumor thrombotic microangiopathy (PTTM) is a rare cause of acute cor pulmonale, typically associated with advanced solid tumors; its occurrence as the initial presentation of multiple myeloma (MM) has not been described. A 45-year-old woman developed acute right heart failure on postoperative day 1 after uterine myomectomy. Echocardiography showed a pulmonary artery systolic pressure of 86 mmHg with a d-shaped left ventricle and right ventricular dysfunction (TAPSE 10 mm); CTPA excluded pulmonary embolism but revealed bilateral ground-glass opacities. Platelet count fell from 115 × 109/L preoperatively to 30 × 109/L. An overlooked preoperative globulin of 67 g/L prompted serum protein electrophoresis and immunofixation, which identified an IgG κ M-protein; bone marrow aspiration revealed 14% morphologically abnormal plasma cells. Presumed MM-associated PTTM was treated with heparin and sildenafil. The platelet count recovered, and a follow-up echocardiogram on day 7 showed normalized cardiac structure and function. The patient self-discontinued rivaroxaban 1 week after discharge and died 3 months later from progression of untreated MM. In CTPA-negative acute cor pulmonale with unexplained thrombocytopenia, an elevated globulin on routine biochemistry may be the only early clue to a plasma cell disorder, and timely anticoagulation with pulmonary vasodilation may buy time for definitive therapy.

articles.title: A Team-Based Patient Engagement Approach to Selexipag Initiation and Maintenance in Pulmonary Arterial Hypertension (TEAM PAH): Real-World Dosing Patterns and Persistence Among Patients With and Without a History of Methamphetamine Use.
articles.abstract: Selexipag is an oral prostacyclin receptor agonist approved for pulmonary arterial hypertension (PAH). This single-center, retrospective study described oral selexipag dosing patterns and persistence, overall and stratified by history of methamphetamine (meth) use, at an expert center in California, USA, using a multidisciplinary, nurse-directed protocol entailing frequent follow-up and individualized side effect management. Medical charts of patients with PAH initiating oral selexipag between January 2016 and March 2023 were abstracted. Patient characteristics and dosing patterns were described up to 14 months post-initiation. The individualized maintenance dose (IMD) was the first dose maintained for ≥ 14 days after reaching the maximum tolerated dose. Persistence was described using Kaplan-Meier analysis. A total of 200 patients initiated oral selexipag (median age 52 years; 69.5% female; 54.5% White; 70.5% on triple therapy; 41% with a history of meth use). Most patients (89.0%) achieved maintenance (median IMD: 900 μg twice daily; median time to maintenance: 2.5 months). Selexipag persistence at 1 year was 76.2%, with most discontinuations occurring within 2 months of initiation. Similar proportions of patients with and without a history of meth use achieved maintenance (85.4% vs. 91.5%; p = 0.3) and persisted on selexipag at 1 year (74.0% vs. 77.5%; p = 0.9). Using a multidisciplinary nurse-directed protocol, most patients with PAH were titrated to their IMD and persisted on oral selexipag, including those with a history of meth use. These findings highlight the importance of frequent patient contact for dose adjustment and side effect management, particularly earlier in the titration process.

articles.title: Patient Perceptions of a Video-Based Educational Platform for Pulmonary Arterial Hypertension: A Qualitative Study of the SMART-PAH Course.
articles.abstract: Pulmonary arterial hypertension (PAH) is a chronic and progressive disease with substantial physiological and psychosocial burden. Effective patient education is essential for self-management and improved outcomes, yet access to reliable information remains limited by brief clinic visits and variable-quality external resources. Although video-assisted learning has been used in other chronic diseases, patient perceptions of video education in PAH have not been studied. To address this gap, we developed the SMART-PAH Library, a web-based learning management platform featuring 12 concise, expert-developed videos on key aspects of PAH management. This qualitative pilot explored patient perceptions, feasibility, and perceived impact of the SMART-PAH library. After completing the SMART-PAH course, 13 PAH patients participated in semi-structured virtual interviews exploring user experience, unmet educational needs, and the impact of the content on knowledge and self-management. Transcripts were analyzed iteratively by multiple reviewers using an inductive grounded theory-informed approach until thematic saturation was reached. Transcript analysis identified four domains in which patients sought support from a PAH-focused educational platform: emotional, physical, educational, and structural. Patients valued credible, relatable content, practical disease-management guidance, and education on under-addressed topics such as sexual health and palliative care. The platform helped address barriers including limited specialist access, financial complexity, and provider trust through accessible, repeatable reinforcement of clinical guidance. The SMART-PAH video library was perceived as a feasible and impactful approach to PAH education. Video-assisted learning can complement traditional PAH care by addressing informational gaps and supporting self-management. Larger studies are needed to evaluate effects on mental health, patient knowledge, and outcomes.

articles.title: Suboptimal Response to Eculizumab in Renal-Limited Thrombotic Microangiopathy Associated With Malignant Hypertension and Monoclonal Gammopathy: A Case Report.
articles.abstract: Renal-limited thrombotic microangiopathy (TMA) is clinically milder but etiologically complex and is often underdiagnosed. This case presents as complement-mediated TMA with malignant hypertension and monoclonal gammopathy but showed suboptimal response to eculizumab treatment, suggesting heterogeneity in both etiology and treatment outcomes.

articles.title: Blocking Extracellular Cyclophilin A-Mediated Adhesion Protects Against Bacterial Infection.
articles.abstract: Bacterial pneumonia remains a leading cause of mortality and morbidity worldwide and is primarily managed through antibiotic therapy. However, the increasing threat of antimicrobial resistance underscores the urgent need for alternative strategies. In this study, we identify extracellular cyclophilin A (eCypA) as a key host factor that promotes the adherence of bacteria such as group A Streptococcus (GAS) and Streptococcus pneumoniae (S. P.). Using single-nucleus RNA sequencing of mouse lung tissue, we demonstrate that eCypA upregulates the expression of integrin/extracellular matrix adhesion receptors, including integrin α5, fibronectin, and mucin, an effect largely mediated by enhancing the transforming growth factor-β (TGF-β) signaling. Mechanistically, eCypA interacts with TGF-β receptor II, acting as a coactivator to increase its binding to TGF-β1 and amplify downstream signaling. Notably, administration of an anti-CypA monoclonal antibody yields both prophylactic and therapeutic effects against GAS-induced lung damage in mice by reducing bacterial adhesion and suppressing proinflammatory cytokine production. Collectively, these findings identify eCypA as a critical regulator of infection exploited by diverse bacteria that rely on integrin/extracellular matrix for adherence, highlighting eCypA as a promising target for host-directed therapies designed to mitigate bacterial attachment and subsequent inflammation.

articles.title: AI-augmented cardiopulmonary point-of-care ultrasound: a narrative review for pulmonary and critical care clinicians.
articles.abstract: Point-of-care ultrasound (POCUS) is an increasingly utilised tool in pulmonary and critical care medicine, yet its effectiveness remains limited by operator dependency and the required cognitive demands of real-time image acquisition and interpretation. Artificial intelligence (AI) has emerged as a promising approach to augment POCUS by supporting image acquisition, interpretation and quantitative analysis. Given the rapid evolution of this field, clinicians must understand both the capabilities and limitations of AI-enabled POCUS. However, prior reviews have largely catalogued applications without focusing on how these tools integrate into bedside workflows. This narrative review examines AI in cardiopulmonary POCUS through a workflow-based lens relevant to pulmonologists and intensivists. We discuss the role of AI as a bedside coach, interpreter and quantifier, highlighting applications in lung and focused cardiac ultrasound, including pneumothorax detection, B-line analysis, left ventricular function assessment, and identification of other cardiopulmonary pathologies. Across domains, AI demonstrates strong performance in controlled settings, although variability persists in real-world environments due to differences in image quality, patient factors and dataset limitations. Future directions include interactive, clinician-in-the-loop systems, protocol-driven integration, and multimodal data synthesis. A clear understanding of these developments will be essential for clinicians as AI becomes increasingly embedded within bedside patient care.

articles.title: Acute Kidney Injury Following Whole Cherry Consumption as a Sleep Aid in a Geriatric Patient With Chronic Kidney Disease.
articles.abstract: Cherries are consumed for their anti-inflammatory and sleep-promoting effects, but their potential adverse effects remain poorly characterized. A 95-year-old woman with stage 3A chronic kidney disease (CKD) presented with an increase in serum creatinine from a baseline of 0.8 to 1.3 mg/dL and a decrease in estimated glomerular filtration rate from 55.3 to 35.2 mL/min/1.73 m² following two weeks of consuming 15-20 fresh or frozen whole cherries nightly. Cherry consumption was discontinued, and her kidney function returned to baseline one month later. Cherries contain high amounts of anthocyanins, which may contribute to acute kidney injury (AKI) in CKD patients through cyclooxygenase (COX)-inhibitory mechanisms, similar to nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drugs (NSAIDs). Application of the Naranjo Adverse Drug Reaction Probability Scale yielded a score of 7, indicating a "probable" association between cherry consumption and AKI.

articles.title: MicroRNA-1246 regulates macrophage lipid metabolism and is involved in resistance to human Mycobacterium tuberculosis infection.
articles.abstract: We determined whether microRNAs (miRNAs) regulate resistance to Mycobacterium tuberculosis (Mtb) infection in healthy household contacts (HHCs) of patients with tuberculosis (TB). As shown in our previously published study, we recruited 460 HHCs from 443 index cases of active pulmonary TB, with 293 (64.8%) remaining IGRA-negative throughout a two-year follow-up. Whole-transcriptome sequencing at baseline (0 months) and follow-up (24 months) and confirmation studies identified miRNA-1246 (downregulated) and miRNA-125b (upregulated) as potential candidates for the development of resistance in nonconverters compared with converters and progressors. Mechanistic studies using proteomics and computational analysis revealed that miRNA-1246 inhibitor reduce Mtb growth in macrophages by regulating lipase activity, specifically through targeting alpha/beta hydrolase domain-containing protein 2 (ABHD2). Inhibition of miRNA-1246 increased glycolytic activity and promoted a metabolic shift in macrophages conducive to pathogen clearance, suggesting its critical role in metabolic regulation and resistance to tuberculosis. These findings highlight potential miRNA-based therapeutic strategies to enhance immunity against Mtb.

articles.title: Travel history and occupation among diagnosed Cutaneous Leishmaniasis cases in Guyana: A multi-site retrospective case series, 2017-2021.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Cutaneous Leishmaniasis (CL) in Guyana has not been systematically characterised in the peer-reviewed literature for several decades. This study aimed to describe the demographic, occupational, geographic, and clinical profile of diagnosed CL cases at Guyana's principal diagnostic sites, and to test, within this case series, whether field-based occupation is associated with reported interior travel and whether travel history is associated with time to presentation.

METHODOLOGY/PRINCIPAL FINDINGS: Retrospective case series (chart review) of CL diagnoses recorded at three facilities in Georgetown and the interior (2017-2021). Of 223 available case records, a random subsample of 170 was abstracted. Occupation and interior travel were patient-declared; their association was tested directly, then via adjusted logistic regression. Most patients (61.8%) reported interior travel, and 45.3% held field-based occupations, chiefly mining and military. Interior travel was more common among field-based than non-field workers (84.4% vs 43.0%; OR = 7.18 [95% CI, 3.42-15.04]; p < .001), and this association persisted after adjustment for age and sex (OR = 7.08 [3.07-16.30]). Younger age was associated with interior travel (OR = 0.96 [0.94-0.98]; p = .001), whereas sex was not. The sample was predominantly male (81.8%; median age 33 years). Patients with interior travel presented earlier than those without (Mdn = 61 vs 243 days; p < .001).

CONCLUSIONS/SIGNIFICANCE: Most diagnosed CL cases in this series occurred in people reporting interior travel, predominantly those in field-based occupations, and this travel history was associated with earlier presentation. All participants had CL and there was no comparison group, so these findings describe the case population and associations within it rather than risk factors for acquiring infection; they also rest on a single, retrospectively recorded travel variable. They nonetheless indicate where pre-deployment prevention, occupational screening, and traveller advisories could be focused, and they support a case-control study with validated exposure measurement.

articles.title: The Utility of Microbial Cell-Free DNA in the Rapid Diagnosis of Chagas Disease: Chagas Disease Case Series.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Chagas disease (CD) is a leading tropical disease and the most prevalent parasitic infection in Latin America, affecting >7 million people globally and ∼240 000-350 000 individuals within the United States. Though known to be endemic to Latin America, prevalence in the United States is also increasing with improved recognition of locally acquired cases, especially in Texas. Autochthonous cases occur throughout the Southern United States, but the geographic range is anticipated to shift northwards as a result of climate change. Chagas disease is referred to as a "silent and silenced disease" by the World Health Organization as most people show no signs or symptoms for years following acute infection, and it primarily affects individuals who are socioeconomically disadvantaged. Historically, Chagas disease has been underrecognized. In the absence of treatment, infected individuals progress to a clinically silent or "indeterminate form" of infection that persists for life. While most patients with indeterminate Chagas disease do not have long-term sequelae, ∼30%-40% will develop end-organ cardiac or gastrointestinal disease decades after infection. Due to its protean clinical presentations, diagnosis requires a high clinical index of suspicion and knowledge of the epidemiology. Traditionally, the diagnosis is based on serology, visualization of the parasite in blood, and polymerase chain reaction (PCR), all of which require suspecting the infection. Microbial cell-free DNA (mcfDNA) of blood can serve as a useful tool for detection of Trypanosoma cruzi even when Chagas disease is not suspected.

RESULTS: Here we present 7 cases, 3 children and 4 adults, who presented with nonspecific manifestations; CD was not in the initial differential diagnosis in 5 of them. Chagas disease was ultimately diagnosed by Karius Spectrum test. In 1 case, the test was sent to expedite diagnosis in the setting of suspected Chagas reactivation.

articles.title: Blood Eosinophil Count and Lund-Mackay Ethmoid Score as Predictors of Recurrence After Endoscopic Sinus Surgery in CRSwNP.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: To evaluate the incremental prognostic value of blood eosinophil count (BEC) and Lund-Mackay (LM) ethmoid score beyond age and asthma for recurrence after endoscopic sinus surgery (ESS) in adults with chronic rhinosinusitis with nasal polyps (CRSwNP).

METHODS: This retrospective cohort included adults with CRSwNP undergoing ESS from January 2022 to November 2024. The outcome was endoscopically confirmed recurrence. Cox models included age and asthma, then added BEC and LM ethmoid score. Performance was evaluated at 36 months and internally validated using 1000 bootstrap resamples.

RESULTS: Among 157 patients, 51 (32.5%) experienced recurrence; 36-month recurrence-free survival was 72.5% (95% confidence interval [CI], 64.7%-78.9%). Earlier recurrence was associated with age (adjusted hazard ratio [HR] per 10 years, 1.26; 95% CI, 1.03-1.53), asthma (HR, 2.00; 95% CI, 1.03-3.90), BEC (HR per 0.1 × 109/L, 1.23; 95% CI, 1.12-1.36), and LM ethmoid score (HR per point, 1.29; 95% CI, 1.13-1.47). Adding BEC and LM ethmoid score reduced the Akaike information criterion from 476.3 to 458.6 and 446.1. Apparent and optimism-corrected 36-month area under the curve values were 0.818 (bootstrap 95% interval, 0.747-0.896) and 0.804; corrected C-index and Brier score were 0.756 and 0.154.

CONCLUSION: BEC and LM ethmoid score provided complementary information beyond age and asthma. External validation and recalibration are required before clinical use.

articles.title: The Proteome of Plasma Extracellular Vesicles in Latent and Active Tuberculosis Reveals Phase-Specific Composition and Immunometabolic Insights.
articles.abstract: Tuberculosis (TB) is an infectious disease that affects millions of people worldwide. Extracellular vesicles (EVs) are mediators of intercellular communication that participate in the immunopathogenesis of TB. Here, we characterized plasma EVs from healthy individuals and from individuals with latent (LTB) or active TB (ATB). We found increased total protein concentrations in EVs from LTB and ATB individuals compared to healthy controls, without significant differences in EV concentrations, but reduced exosome abundance in LTB. Proteomic and bioinformatic analysis showed that LTB EVs were enriched in proteins associated with the regulation of inflammation, tissue remodeling, and lipid metabolism, including TGFβ and apolipoproteins (APO) A1 and E. In contrast, ATB EVs were enriched in mycobacterial antigens and host proteins associated with acute inflammation, including serum amyloid A1 and A2 (SAA1/A2) and the calgranulin complex proteins S100A8 and S100A9. These host proteins were central and/or cohesive nodes in the protein-protein interaction networks of these EVs. Dot blot analysis confirmed the increased levels of these EV proteins in a second group of individuals with LTB or ATB. The EV levels of mycobacterial antigens correlated positively with the EV levels of SAA1/A2 and S100A8/A9, but negatively with their levels of TGFβ and APOA1. Principal component analysis and hierarchical clustering suggested that the simultaneous analysis of mycobacterial antigens and these EV proteins could discriminate between healthy, LTB, and ATB individuals. Our findings confirm that plasma EVs provide insights into the host immunometabolic response to TB and may be a source of clinically useful biomarkers.

articles.title: Mini OPCAB in severe COPD-world's first report of three cases.
articles.abstract: Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) among patients requiring coronary artery bypass graft is common and is associated with worse outcomes. Although off pump coronary artery bypass (OPCAB) ameliorates cardiopulmonary bypass related derangements, COPD is still an independent risk factor for adverse outcomes. As minimally invasive direct coronary artery bypass is an absolute contraindication in COPD, an alternative minimally invasive approach is imperative to optimize outcomes. We present the world's first reported cases in the literature of Mini OPCAB performed successfully in three patients with severe COPD that received left internal mammary artery to left anterior descending artery (LAD) revascularization. All three patients were discharged on the first post-operative day with nil complications. All three patients were well at 3 months follow-up, having returned to their normal daily routine by 3 weeks with normal wound healing and without hospital readmission. Therefore, Mini OPCAB as a minimally invasive approach seems an attractive and feasible option in severe COPD, particularly those requiring revascularization to single vessel (LAD). This is the first documented report of Mini OPCAB performed successfully in patients with severe COPD.

articles.title: Pembrolizumab and reactivation of TB: is there a link?
Projected detection of active pulmonary TB through the Japan pre-entry TB screening programme.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: This study aimed to estimate the number of bacteriologically confirmed pulmonary TB (BC-PTB) cases expected to be detected and the number needed to screen (NNS) to detect one BC-PTB case by the Japan Pre-entry Tuberculosis Screening (JPETS) programme.

METHODS: This descriptive study estimated the number of cases with BC-PTB to be detected and the NNS required to detect one case using the JPETS programme, based on national TB prevalence survey data from the six JPETS target Asian countries and immigration statistics in Japan.

RESULTS: Among JPETS applicants, the estimated total number of BC-PTB cases diagnosed per year was 1,997 (95% confidence interval [CI]: 1,910-2,086) when adjusted for sex and 1,323 (95% CI: 1,253-1,396) when adjusted for age group. The estimated NNS to identify one BC-PTB case was 227 cases (95% CI: 217-237) when adjusted for sex and 319 cases (95% CI: 302-337) when adjusted for age.

CONCLUSION: The JPETS is projected to identify approximately 1,300 BC-PTB cases per year across six Asian countries. When selecting countries for JPETS, consideration of both the number of TB cases in Japan and the TB prevalence in target countries may enhance screening effectiveness.

articles.title: Managing TB infection among household contacts of patients with pulmonary TB.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: One third of India's population has TB infection (TBI) with 10% at risk of developing TB disease. A multi-centric TBI initiative for household contacts (HHCs) of people with pulmonary TB (PTB) was implemented.

METHODS: The project Joint Effort for Elimination of TB was implemented in collaboration with India's National TB Elimination Programme from April 2021 to March 2024. This included doorstep ruling out of TB disease, screening HHCs for TBI, provision of TB preventive treatment (TPT), and adverse events management.

RESULTS: Of the 151,890 notified patients with PTB, 138,812 (91%) could be contacted. Of these, 112,687 (74%) consented to home visits and 94,621 (63%) households were visited. During the visits, 403,923 HHCs were identified, of whom 398,822 (99%) were screened for TBI; 310,605 (77%) consented and 253,885 (63%) initiated on TPT. Adverse events were reported by 3% HHCs with no serious episodes. Of the eligible 148,715 HHCs on TPT, 130,304 (88%) completed with an increasing trend in the TPT completion.

CONCLUSION: This community-based model for TBI management is feasible and effective. High screening and treatment completion rates alongside minimal adverse events prove this strategy is scalable and replicable for other high-burden settings worldwide.

articles.title: Acute Pancreatitis Presenting With ST-Segment Elevation and Marked Troponin Elevation: A Diagnostic Dilemma in a Resource-Limited Setting-A Case Report.
articles.abstract: Acute pancreatitis can present with ST-segment elevation and marked troponin elevation, mimicking acute coronary syndrome. In resource-limited settings where coronary angiography, cardiac magnetic resonance imaging, and serial high-sensitivity troponin testing are unavailable, distinguishing acute myocardial injury associated with pancreatitis from Type 1 myocardial infarction can be challenging.

articles.title: Toxin-mediated tRNATrp depletion drives Trp-codon-dependent reprogramming in Mycobacterium tuberculosis while selectively enriching the PDIM biosynthetic machinery.
articles.abstract: Mycobacterium tuberculosis (Mtb) must adapt to host-imposed stresses that limit its growth and ability to establish an infection. One important immune-regulated host defense mechanism involves competition between host and pathogen for tryptophan (Trp). Although Mtb is a Trp prototroph capable of synthesizing its own Trp, it normally acquires this amino acid from host macrophages because of the high energetic cost of its synthesis. However, interferon-γ-activated macrophages attempt to restrict Mtb growth by inducing indoleamine 2,3-dioxygenase 1 (IDO1) that degrades Trp. In response, Mtb senses and adapts to limitation of this essential amino acid by inducing its own Trp biosynthetic pathway, although the mechanisms coupling Trp limitation and compensatory Trp biosynthesis remain unknown. Here, we studied the Mtb VapC37 toxin and demonstrate that it arrests growth and is a highly selective tRNase that exclusively depletes tRNATrp. Consequently, VapC37 triggers a state of perceived Trp starvation to upregulate production of Trp biosynthetic enzymes. Therefore, this toxin appears to link intracellular Trp availability-a well-established regulator of Mtb growth-to a codon-dependent adaptive response to increase the Trp concentration. VapC37 also broadly reprograms the Mtb transcriptome and translatome toward synthesis of mRNAs and proteins with low or no Trp codons. However, there is one striking exception: key enzymes in the phthiocerol dimycocerosate (PDIM) biosynthetic pathway were robustly synthesized despite being large and Trp-numerous, resulting in a > 2-fold increase in PDIM lipid production upon VapC37 expression. Thus, Mtb selectively preserves PDIM production under conditions of tRNATrp limitation. Finally, VapBC37 and PDIM transcripts are upregulated in Mtb cells subjected to nitrosative stress and upon Mtb infection of THP-1 macrophage-like cells. This might implicate early macrophage-associated stresses as activators of VapC37, possibly enabling this toxin to reallocate metabolic priorities toward Trp biosynthesis while selectively preserving PDIM production critical for Mtb early immune escape and virulence.

articles.title: A machine learning model for in-hospital mortality prediction in patients with sepsis-related myocardial injury.
articles.abstract: Sepsis-related myocardial injury (SRMI) is associated with high mortality, but the transportability of prediction models across heterogeneous cohorts remains uncertain. We developed and externally validated a machine learning model for in-hospital mortality prediction in SRMI and evaluated its discrimination, calibration, interpretability, and distributional shift across cohorts. Using MIMIC-IV for development and MIMIC-III and a local cohort for external validation (n = 1,226, 962, and 280, respectively), we compared eight classification algorithms. A two-stage feature-selection strategy, recursive feature accumulation and sequential elimination with incremental feature evaluation, ranked 31 candidate variables to derive a parsimonious predictor set. The selected model was evaluated for discrimination, precision-recall performance, calibration, clinical utility, and risk stratification. Logistic recalibration, population stability index (PSI) analysis, and SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) were used to assess probability alignment, cross-cohort distributional shift, and model interpretability. Feature selection reduced 31 candidate variables to 8 predictors with little loss of cross-validated performance (AUC, 0.819 with 31 variables versus 0.810 with 8 variables). The selected random forest model achieved an AUC of 0.819 (bootstrap 95% CI, 0.787-0.848) and a PR-AUC of 0.702 (0.657-0.751) in MIMIC-III, and an AUC of 0.758 (0.693-0.816) and a PR-AUC of 0.525 (0.435-0.630) in the local cohort. Recalibration reduced the Brier score from 0.162 to 0.147 in MIMIC-III and from 0.233 to 0.196 in the local cohort. PSI indicated minimal distributional shift between MIMIC-IV and MIMIC-III but substantial shift in the local cohort, particularly for SOFA score, respiratory rate, and prothrombin time. SHAP identified prothrombin time, invasive ventilation, lactate, temperature, and urine output as major contributors to model predictions. In two external cohorts, an 8-variable random forest model showed moderate discrimination for mortality prediction in SRMI. The evaluation of external performance, calibration, distributional shift, and SHAP-based explanations provides an assessment of model transportability. Prospective validation is needed before clinical deployment.

articles.title: Automating chart review for identification of infected patients using natural language processing.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Expert clinician chart review is the most accurate method to identify patients with infection but is laborious and costly. We aimed to develop and externally validate machine-learning models using structured and unstructured data to identify infection in hospitalized patients compared to chart review.

MATERIALS AND METHODS: Adult inpatient encounters at 2 health systems (2006-2016) were manually annotated for suspected infection on admission. Data from one site were used to develop gradient-boosted machine-learning models. Structured features included labs, vital signs, and nursing assessments. Unstructured clinical notes were converted to concept unique identifiers (CUIs) using the clinical Text Analysis and Knowledge Extraction System. Unimodal and multimodal models were tuned to maximize the area under the receiver operating curve (AUROC) in the derivation site through cross-validation. Model discrimination and calibration were assessed in the external validation site.

RESULTS: Of the 3014 included admissions, 677 (22.5%) were classified as having suspected infection on admission. A multimodal model combining n-gram TF-IDF and structured data demonstrated the best performance, significantly outperforming the structured data only model (AUROC 0.88 vs 0.82, P < .001, area under the precision-recall curve 0.71 vs 0.58, P < .001). The most important features came from unstructured data.

DISCUSSION AND CONCLUSION: Our results highlight the value of unstructured text data for developing models that accurately replicate chart reviews in identifying patients with infection. By expediting the annotation of infection cases, our models can facilitate epidemiological research and the curation of datasets necessary for developing clinical decision support systems for early sepsis detection.

articles.title: Multiple Neurological Complications and Multidrug-Resistant Bacterial Infections During Prolonged Intensive Care for Undocumented Meningoencephalitis in Côte d'Ivoire: A Case Report.
articles.abstract: Acute meningoencephalitis requiring intensive care may be complicated by severe neurological injury and nosocomial infections. Hydrocephalus is well recognized, whereas spinal cord ischemia, central diabetes insipidus, and flaccid tetraparesis are rarely reported. Their coexistence, together with successive infections involving multidrug-resistant organisms, presents substantial diagnostic and therapeutic challenges. A previously healthy 32-year-old man presented with neck and back pain following a road traffic accident, subsequently developing cerebellar signs, acute confusion, and meningeal signs without fever. Cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) analysis revealed neutrophilic pleocytosis, elevated protein, and marked hypoglycorrhachia. Microbiological investigations were negative, and no causative pathogen was identified. Empirical antimicrobial therapy was followed by normalization of the CSF leukocyte count by hospital day 6. Despite this initial response, the patient required mechanical ventilation and developed shunt-dependent tetraventricular hydrocephalus, probable central diabetes insipidus, imaging findings suggestive of thoracic spinal cord ischemia, and areflexic flaccid tetraparesis with diffuse axonal sensorimotor neuropathy. His prolonged intensive care course was further complicated by successive nosocomial infections involving multidrug-resistant bacteria. He died on hospital day 70 from septic shock associated with Enterobacter cloacae bacteremia and multiorgan failure. Negative microbiological findings do not exclude meningoencephalitis when clinical and CSF abnormalities support the diagnosis, although alternative etiologies require consideration. Improvement in CSF findings does not preclude subsequent neurological deterioration or nosocomial infection. Continued neurological assessment, rigorous infection-prevention measures, and prompt investigation of suspected nosocomial infections remain essential throughout prolonged intensive care, particularly in resource-limited settings.

articles.title: Bone missile injury with an intact host femur after high energy road traffic trauma: a case report.
articles.abstract: A 28 year old woman presented with local wound infection two weeks after sustaining an anterior thigh laceration in a high energy motorbike crash that killed the co-riding motorcyclist. X-ray revealed a non-identifiable radio-opaque fragment and computed tomography identified a bony foreign body deep in the thigh adjacent to the femoral vessels, with the host femur intact. A 6 x 3 cm fragment of cortical bone was removed at surgery. Histopathology and genetic studies to confirm its origin were not feasible in this resource-limited setting, but an intact host femur suggested it originated from the deceased rider. The wound healed by secondary intention, HIV and hepatitis serology were negative at 6 weeks. This case highlights the unusual occurrence of a bone missile and the importance of early advanced imaging and prompt post-exposure prophylaxis following high-energy, multi-victim trauma.

articles.title: Pregnancy Complicated by Citrin Deficiency and Gestational Diabetes Mellitus: Perioperative Metabolic Management and Postoperative Analgesic Challenges Following Caesarean Delivery.
articles.abstract: Citrin deficiency is a rare autosomal recessive metabolic disorder caused by pathogenic variants in the SLC25A13 gene. Pregnancy in affected women is uncommon and presents unique challenges because conventional obstetric management may conflict with metabolic requirements. The coexistence of gestational diabetes mellitus (GDM) introduces additional complexity. A 25-year-old, gravida 2 para 0+1 woman with genetically confirmed citrin deficiency (homozygous SLC25A13 c.1763G>A mutation) was managed jointly by obstetric and inherited metabolic disease (IMD) teams. Her pregnancy was complicated by severe nausea and vomiting during the first trimester and subsequent GDM diagnosed using capillary glucose monitoring rather than an oral glucose tolerance test. Representative fasting glucose values were 6.3-6.8 mmol/L, with postprandial values up to 10.7 mmol/L. Specialist dietary modification and insulin therapy were instituted following multidisciplinary review. A personalised metabolic plan emphasised avoidance of prolonged fasting, restriction of excessive carbohydrate intake, maintenance of adequate energy intake, and avoidance of routine glucose-containing intravenous fluids. At 38+5 weeks' gestation, she underwent emergency caesarean section for failure to progress in labour under spinal anaesthesia. A healthy infant weighing 3074 g was delivered with Apgar scores of 9, 10 and 10 at 1, 5 and 10 minutes, respectively. Postoperative pain management was challenging because the specialist metabolic plan advised caution with paracetamol. Following inadequate analgesia with ibuprofen and dihydrocodeine, paracetamol was cautiously introduced at reduced doses and subsequently increased to 500 mg four times daily, with additional opioid analgesia as required. Daily plasma ammonia and liver function monitoring was undertaken during the five-day postoperative admission; ammonia values remained within the laboratory reference range, with no hyperammonaemia (range <10-32 µmol/L) or significant hepatic biochemical deterioration. This case highlights the complexity of managing pregnancy in women with citrin deficiency, particularly when complicated by GDM. It also demonstrates a practical approach to postoperative analgesia following caesarean delivery using cautious dose escalation and biochemical surveillance.

articles.title: Necrotizing fasciitis secondary to Wohlfahrtiimonas chitiniclastica in the absence of myiasis.
articles.abstract: Wohlfahrtiimonas chitiniclastica is a rare Gram-negative bacillus associated with fly larvae, myiasis, chronic wounds, and severe polymicrobial infection. We report a 71-year-old woman with diabetes, peripheral neuropathy, severe peripheral vascular disease, and previous contralateral above-knee amputation who presented with septic shock secondary to an infected right hallux ulcer. Radiographs demonstrated soft-tissue gas extending into the distal calf. Emergency exploration revealed extensive necrosis and dishwater pus tracking proximally along the flexor hallucis longus tendon, consistent with necrotizing fasciitis. Radical debridement was performed, although major amputation was initially declined. Tissue and pus cultures grew W. chitiniclastica and Enterococcus faecalis; no larvae were identified. Despite temporary clinical stabilization with intensive care support and broad-spectrum antibiotics, the foot remained non-viable and definitive above-knee amputation was required. The patient improved rapidly following source control and was discharged to rehabilitation. This case highlights the importance of early recognition, aggressive debridement, and definitive source control for survival.

articles.title: Trends in Modifiable Risk Factors Contributing to Ischemic Heart Disease Mortality in Afghanistan: Estimates From the Global Burden of Disease Study 2023 (1999-2023).
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Ischemic heart disease (IHD) is the leading cause of death, and the majority of this burden can be attributed to modifiable risk factors. Although surveys show that these risk factors are prevalent in Afghanistan, no study has used Global Burden of Disease (GBD) methodology to describe their contribution to IHD mortality. The study examined trends (1999-2023) in 14 selected behavioral, dietary, and metabolic risk factors for IHD mortality using the GBD 2023 estimates.

METHODOLOGY: This retrospective analysis used GBD 2023 estimates of deaths from IHD in Afghanistan attributable to 14 selected behavioral, dietary, and metabolic risk factors and to the GBD "all risk factors" composite, which also includes exposures outside these 14 (e.g., air pollution), covering 1999-2023 (both sexes; all ages and age-standardized). The number (N) and percentage (%) attributable to each risk factor are reported. Trends in age-standardized death rates were examined with a segmented log-linear trend analysis written by the authors as a permutation-based approximation to the NCI Joinpoint approach; the NCI software was not used. The average annual percentage change (AAPC) and its 95% confidence interval (CI) are conditional on the selected model. A multiple linear regression was used only as a descriptive comparison of average rates by risk factor category, sex, and calendar year. A p-value of 0.05 or less was considered significant, with no adjustment for multiple comparisons, so the trend results are exploratory.

RESULTS: From 1999 to 2023, the age-standardized IHD death rate for all GBD risk factors combined (the GBD composite) went down from 275.94 to 230.49 per 100,000. This is a drop of 16.5% (AAPC: -0.77%, 95% CI: -0.90 to -0.63; p < 0.001). We found at least one joinpoint in 41 of the 45 series, and most of them were around 2009 and 2013. High systolic blood pressure (11,969.1 deaths, or 55.17% of all IHD deaths in 2023) and high low-density lipoprotein (LDL) cholesterol (5,875.8 deaths, or 27.12%) remained the leading factors among the 14, both of which were decreasing (AAPC: -0.95% and -1.14%; both p < 0.001). The rates associated with a diet high in sugar-sweetened beverages (AAPC: +1.28%, 95% CI: +0.94 to +1.63; p < 0.001) and with smoking (AAPC: +0.37%; p < 0.001) increased, whereas the increases linked to a diet high in processed meat, sodium, and secondhand smoke were not significant in the segmented model (all p > 0.05). The age-standardized rates were higher among females, while the smoking rates were higher among males (25.83 as compared with 5.09 per 100,000). In the descriptive regression model (N = 700; R² = 0.963), average rates differed by risk factor category, calendar year, and sex (all p < 0.05), with high systolic blood pressure having the largest coefficient (B = +140.92; p < 0.001).

CONCLUSIONS: In Afghanistan, metabolic risk factors, especially high systolic blood pressure and high LDL cholesterol, were the largest contributors to IHD deaths among the 14 selected risk factors. The composite age-standardized rate declined, with a common inflection around 2009-2013 that may reflect GBD modeling inputs. The rates attributable to sugar-sweetened beverages and to smoking increased, which points to an emerging threat that should be the subject of targeted prevention measures, with ongoing efforts to control hypertension and lipid levels. These exploratory trend estimates need confirmation with the NCI Joinpoint software.

articles.title: Body Composition Differences Across Ranks and Sexes of Competitive Swimmers: A Cross-Sectional Study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND AND AIMS: Body composition (BC) plays a key role in assessing athletes' health. However, many factors, including sex and performance rank, may influence BC and should be considered when assessing it. Moreover, BC is estimated indirectly, and body volume (BV) represents a key component of densitometric assessment. This investigation aimed to compare swimmers' BC across sexes and performance ranks, compare methods for BF estimation, and develop a model for predicting BV.

METHODS: This was a cross-sectional study. Participants underwent air-displacement plethysmography (ADP), anthropometric measurements, and bioimpedance analysis (BIA) according to standardized procedures. Sixty-four competitive (13.6 ± 1.9 training hours per week) swimmers (17.8 ± 4.4 years, 56.3% male; 13.6 ± 1.9 training hours per week) were enrolled from the national competitive list. They were stratified by sex and classified into three groups according to performance rank (Best World Aquatic score, BWA). A two-way ANCOVA (sex and rank), adjusted for age, was used to compare BC variables. A bootstrap model-averaging approach was used to select a linear regression model for predicting BV.

RESULTS: Males showed higher BV, total body water (TBW), and fat-free mass (FFM) than females. Most rank-related differences were attenuated after adjustment for age; however, BWA showed a strong positive correlation with limb girths and FFM (Pearson rho > 0.5). BF estimated using specific cut-offs exhibited the lowest error propagation (reduction of 6.42%). The best model was selected with a 18.81% frequency (adjusted R 2 = 0.981; RMSE = 1.541), and the variables that showed an adequate bootstrap inclusion frequency (> 60%) were stature (β = 0.342), stretched arm (β = 0.905), hip (β = 0.117), thigh (β = 0.659) and calf (β = 0.508) girths, with a mean relative conditional bias of 1.79%.

CONCLUSION: The proposed BF estimation method showed lower error propagation in this sample, while the anthropometric model provided an accurate internal prediction of BV. These findings support the use of predicted BV for subsequent BF estimation using specific cut-offs, although external validation of the BV prediction model is required.

articles.title: Work-Related Stress Among Neglected Work Forces in Tertiary Hospitals, Eastern Ethiopia: A Cross-Sectional Study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Hospital cleaners are an often-neglected workforce routinely exposed to hazardous working conditions that increase their risk of work-related stress (WRS). However, evidence on WRS among hospital cleaners in low- and middle-income countries, including Ethiopia is limited. This study aimed to determine the prevalence of WRS and identify associated factors among hospital cleaners working in eight tertiary hospitals in eastern Ethiopia.

METHODS: A hospital-based cross-sectional study was conducted among 741 cleaners from May to August 2023. Work-related stress (WRS) was assessed using modified items from the Copenhagen Psychosocial Questionnaire II (COPSOQ-II) and the National Health Survey. Severe and low WRS were classified using the mean cut-off score derived from the summed components of physical indicators of WRS. Data quality was ensured through training, pretesting, expert evaluation of the assessment tools, and internal consistency testing using Cronbach's alpha. Data were entered into EpiData version 3.1 and analyzed using Stata 17MP. Descriptive statistics summarized participant characteristics. Binary and multivariable logistic regression analyses identified factors associated with WRS. Variables with p < 0.20 were included in the multivariable model, and AORs with 95% CIs were reported.

RESULTS: Of 741 hospital cleaners, 679 participated (response rate: 91.63%). The prevalence of severe WRS was 29.16% (95% CI: 25.77%-32.74%). Multivariable analysis identified significant factors. Workload (AOR = 10.23, 95% CI: 6.16-16.98; p < 0.001), smoking (AOR = 6.64, 95% CI: 3.53-12.51; p < 0.001), khat chewing (AOR = 4.07, 95% CI: 2.34-7.09; p < 0.001), job dissatisfaction (AOR = 2.67, 95% CI: 1.24-5.76; p = 0.012), less-than-monthly supervision (AOR = 1.63, 95% CI: 1.01-3.06; p = 0.030), lack of social recognition (AOR = 3.11, 95% CI: 1.63-5.92; p < 0.001), sleeping difficulties (AOR = 2.18, 95% CI: 1.27-3.71; p = 0.004), and inadequate OHS services (AOR = 1.64, 95% CI: 1.16-2.83; p = 0.043) increased WRS. Experience > 6.72 years reduced stress (AOR = 0.44, 95% CI: 0.26-0.75; p = 0.003).

CONCLUSION: The study concludes that almost one-third of cleaners in tertiary hospitals had severe WRS. Higher levels of stress were substantially associated with smoking, chewing khat, job dissatisfaction, infrequent supervision, lack of social recognition, trouble sleeping, and inadequate workplace health and safety services, with workload being the most significant predictor. Conversely, higher levels of education and more work experience were protective factors. These findings highlight the necessity of comprehensive workplace interventions that reduce excessive workloads, support occupational health and safety services, improve supervision and recognition, promote healthy lives, and support cleaners' professional growth.

articles.title: Effect of Virtual Reality Relaxation on Alarm Fatigue and Professional Quality of Life Among Nurses in Intensive Care Units.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Intensive care unit nurses are faced with a large number of equipment alarms daily, which can increase the likelihood of errors and threaten their professional quality of life. Today, the use of virtual reality to create relaxing experiences in stressful environments has received attention. This study aimed to determine the effect of virtual reality relaxation on alarm fatigue and the professional quality of life among ICU nurses.

METHODS: This is an intervention study with a pretest-posttest design with a control group. ICU nurses who met the inclusion criteria were selected conveniently and were randomly assigned to two intervention and control groups (30 people in each group). The intervention was implemented as three 20-min virtual reality relaxation sessions over a week. The data collection tools included the Alarm Fatigue Scale (AFS) and the Professional Quality of Life (ProQOL) questionnaire. The questionnaires were completed before and immediately after the intervention.

RESULTS: The results showed that the mean AFS score improved significantly after the intervention (p < 0.001), and there was a significant difference between the intervention and control groups (p = 0.014). The mean dimensions of ProQOL also improved significantly in all three dimensions of compassion satisfaction, burnout, and secondary trauma stress after the intervention (p < 0.001). There was a significant difference between two groups in all dimensions after the intervention (p < 0.001).

CONCLUSION: The significant improvement in AFS and ProQOL scores indicates that the use of new technologies, such as virtual reality can be considered as a complementary tool in promoting the mental and professional health of nurses in stressful environments.

articles.title: External Iliac Arteriovenous Fistula Caused by Stab Wound.
articles.abstract: Major abdominal arteriovenous fistula (AVF), including external iliac vessels, is a rare condition. If untreated long term, AVFs may cause venous hypertension and heart failure. We report the case of a 47-year-old man who stabbed his left lower abdomen. His vital signs were stable. Computed tomography revealed hemoperitoneum and a left external iliac AVF. Prior to laparotomy, endovascular repair of AVF was performed. Subsequent laparotomy was performed, and omental injury and a small bowel injury were repaired. Exploration of the retroperitoneal hematoma showed no bleeding from the external iliac vessels. The patient was discharged on day 6. In the management of retroperitoneal hematoma after penetrating trauma, laparotomy has been recommended. Among hemodynamically stable patients with stab wounds and traumatic external iliac AVF, endovascular intervention may be considered prior to laparotomy. Further investigations are required to reveal the long-term safety and durability of a covered stent for traumatic AVFs.

articles.title: Aligning Antimicrobial Stewardship and Infection Prevention Through Repeated Assessment and Feedback: A Multisite Quality Improvement Initiative in Viet Nam.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Antimicrobial stewardship (AMS) and infection prevention and control (IPC) are complementary strategies to improve patient safety and address antimicrobial resistance (AMR). In low- and middle-income countries (LMICs), they are often implemented separately, limiting potential impact.

OBJECTIVE: To evaluate the feasibility of an aligned AMS-IPC improvement approach and describe changes in implementation in Vietnamese hospitals.

METHODS: We conducted a quality improvement initiative in 4 hospitals within the national AMR surveillance network in Viet Nam (March-September 2025). We used US-CDC's tools to guide implementation, including the Global Antibiotic Stewardship Evaluation Tool (G-ASET) and the Infection Control Assessment and Response (ICAR) tool. Baseline assessments were followed by feedback, multidisciplinary action planning, and targeted capacity building. Follow-up occurred 2-5 months later. Changes were analyzed descriptively using quantitative scores and qualitative synthesis and reported following the SQUIRE 2.0 guidelines.

RESULTS: All hospitals had established IPC programs at baseline, while AMS maturity varied. G-ASET scores increased across all sites, with larger absolute gains in hospitals starting from lower baselines. Improvements were seen in leadership and governance, education and training, stewardship actions, and monitoring and reporting. Selected IPC activities aligned with AMS priorities also improved, particularly transmission-based precautions, environmental cleaning, and cross-team coordination. Infrastructure-dependent areas, such as water safety, showed limited short-term progress.

CONCLUSIONS: This aligned AMS-IPC quality improvement strategy was feasible and associated with improvements in implementation capacity and program maturity over short follow-up. Further studies with longer follow-up, comparator designs, and outcome-level measures are needed to evaluate effectiveness, sustainability, and generalizability.

articles.title: Self-inflicted thoracoabdominal nail-gun injury presenting as STEMI: diagnostic challenges in a time-critical care pathway.
articles.abstract: A 60-year-old male with a history of depression and a prior nail-gun thoracic injury was found in shock at home, with inferior ST-segment elevation on the paramedic electrocardiogram prompting pre-hospital ST-elevation myocardial infarction pathway activation. Initial high-sensitivity troponin was elevated, consistent with the presumed diagnosis. Normal coronary angiography and preserved ventricular function were discordant with the patient's ongoing haemodynamic instability. Four small anterior chest puncture wounds and radiopaque foreign bodies demonstrated on chest radiograph and angiographic imaging did not initially prompt consideration of penetrating injury. Computed tomography pulmonary angiography, performed to exclude pulmonary embolism, identified four nail-gun projectiles penetrating the heart and stomach. The patient underwent sternotomy and laparotomy with repair of cardiac, diaphragmatic, and gastric injuries. The case illustrates the challenges of situation awareness and diagnostic reassessment within time-critical, protocol-driven care.

articles.title: Disseminated Blastomycosis With Pulmonary, Cutaneous, and Splenic Involvement in a Construction Worker: A Case Report.
articles.abstract: Blastomycosis is a systemic fungal infection that is caused by Blastomyces dermatitidis or Blastomyces gilchristii. Although the lungs are the primary site of infection, blastomycosis can disseminate to the skin, bones, genitourinary system, and, rarely, visceral organs such as the spleen. Occupational exposure to soil and decaying matter, particularly in construction workers, increases the risk of blastomycosis infection. A 40-year-old male presented with a progressively enlarging right facial lesion, which initially appeared as a small papule. The lesion had gradually increased in size and pain over several months and failed to respond to antibiotics. Notable symptoms include generalized fatigue, low mood, intermittent morning headaches, confusion, poor appetite with weight loss, intermittent night sweats, and joint pain. The diagnostic workup included imaging findings of an exophytic skin lesion arising from the right cheek, pulmonary micronodules and consolidation, and splenic changes. Serum Blastomyces antigen testing was positive, fungal culture of tissue from the facial lesion grew Blastomyces dermatitidis, and histopathologic examination demonstrated granulomatous inflammation with broad-based budding yeast within the dermis, supporting the diagnosis of disseminated blastomycosis. Liposomal amphotericin B induction therapy was initiated, and the facial lesion improved. The patient was discharged home with a transition to oral itraconazole. This report presents a case of disseminated blastomycosis involving the lungs, skin, and spleen in an immunocompetent individual. High index of suspicion and recognition of cutaneous lesions in the context of occupational and environmental risk factors for blastomycosis enable early diagnosis and treatment.

articles.title: Red Cell and Platelet Indices as Biomarkers of Poor Glycemic Control in Patients With Type 2 Diabetes: A Case-Control Study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND AND AIM: Type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) is associated with systemic inflammation and altered hematological function, including changes in red cell indices and platelet hyperreactivity. While glycosylated hemoglobin (HbA1c) is the gold standard for monitoring glycemic control, its cost and susceptibility to conditions like anemia highlight the need for accessible, reliable alternative biomarkers, particularly for identifying patients with poor glycemic control (HbA1c ≥ 7.0%). This case-control study, therefore, investigated the utility of red cell and platelet indices as potential biomarkers of poor glycemic control in Ghanaian T2DM patients.

METHODS: This study recruited 134 people living with T2DM and 134 nondiabetic controls. Cases were categorized into groups with poor glycemic control (HbA1c ≥ 7.0%) and good glycemic control (HbA1c < 7.0%). HbA1c was measured using an automated analyzer, and hematological indices were measured using a Sysmex XN 2000 analyzer. Statistical analyses were performed in R Language and SPSS version 26 at a significance level of 0.05% and 95% confidence interval employing a logistic prediction model.

RESULTS: Prevalence of poor glycemic control was 60.9%. Cases with poor glycemic control had significantly lower red cell indices such as hemoglobin, hematocrit, red blood cells count, and MCV, but a higher MPV compared to controls (p < 0.05). Multivariate logistics regression showed increasing hemoglobin levels (aOR: 0.40, 95% CI: [0.11-0.78]; p = 0.0130) and hematocrit (aOR: 0.03, 95% CI: [0.01-0.92]; p = 0.0140) were independently associated with decreased likelihood of poor glycemic control, whiles increasing MPV (aOR: 1.15, 95% CI: [1.02-3.09]; p = 0.0440) demonstrated an independent association with increased likelihood of poor glycemic control.

CONCLUSION: Hemoglobin level, hematocrit, and mean platelet volume are significantly associated with, and can potentially serve as independent predictors of poor glycemic control. These routine, cost-effective hematological parameters could be incorporated into risk assessment and management protocols for T2DM in resource-limited settings.

articles.title: Sleep-Disordered Breathing and Sleep Fragmentation in Relation to Atrial Fibrillation Risk: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Atrial fibrillation (AF) is one of the most prevalent cardiac arrhythmias worldwide. This study aimed to evaluate the association between sleep-disordered breathing (SDB), primarily assessed using the apnea-hypopnea index (AHI), and AF risk, with additional analysis of sleep fragmentation parameters such as wake after sleep onset (WASO) and arousal index (AI).

METHODS: This systematic review and meta-analysis followed Cochrane Handbook recommendations and PRISMA guidelines, with protocol registration in PROSPERO (No. 127490). Randomized controlled trials (RCTs) and observational cohort studies assessing sleep disturbances and AF were included. MEDLINE, Cochrane Library, and Scopus were searched from inception to February 2026. Extracted data included study characteristics, demographics, cardiovascular risk factors, and sleep metrics. Outcomes were incident and recurrent AF. A random-effects model was applied.

RESULTS: Twenty-one cohort studies (611,898 participants) were included. SDB was associated with increased incident AF risk (RR 1.67, 95% CI 1.41-1.97; I 2 = 66.5%), with consistent Bayesian estimates. A dose-response relationship showed a 2% increase in AF risk per unit rise in AHI. For AF recurrence, 11 studies (n = 1810) demonstrated a significant association (RR 1.55, 95% CI 1.40-1.72; I 2 = 0%), supported by Bayesian analysis.

CONCLUSION: Sleep disturbances are significantly associated with both incident and recurrent AF and may represent modifiable risk factors.

articles.title: Suspected Mesenteric Malperfusion in Acute Type A Aortic Dissection During Pregnancy: A Case Report and Review of Reperfusion-First Strategies.
articles.abstract: Aortic dissection during pregnancy is rare but potentially catastrophic. Acute Type A aortic dissection generally requires urgent surgical repair. When visceral malperfusion is present, however, the optimal sequence of interventions may be complex, particularly when pregnancy and recent cesarean delivery increase operative risk. Endovascular reperfusion followed by delayed aortic repair has been proposed in selected patients, although evidence supporting this strategy in pregnancy remains limited. A 37-year-old woman at 31 weeks' gestation presented with chest and back pain. Initial CT pulmonary angiography (CTPA) performed for suspected pulmonary embolism excluded pulmonary embolism but demonstrated marked aortic root dilatation measuring 6.7 × 5.4 cm. Before definitive aortic imaging could be obtained, she developed acute respiratory deterioration and fetal distress, prompting emergency cesarean delivery under general anesthesia. Postoperatively, transthoracic echocardiography demonstrated severe aortic root and ascending aortic dilatation, severe aortic regurgitation, reduced left ventricular ejection fraction, and a dissection flap consistent with Type A aortic dissection. Because of concern for catastrophic hemorrhage associated with cardiopulmonary bypass and hypothermic circulatory arrest shortly after cesarean delivery, definitive aortic repair was deferred for approximately 24 h while the patient underwent medical optimization. During this interval, she developed progressive metabolic acidosis and worsening renal function, raising clinical concern for visceral malperfusion. Dedicated abdominal vascular imaging was not obtained, and therefore the presence, distribution, and mechanism of mesenteric malperfusion could not be anatomically confirmed before surgery. At subsequent operative exploration, extensive small- and large-bowel necrosis and markedly hypoperfused adnexal tissue were identified, precluding definitive aortic repair. The patient subsequently died after transition to comfort-focused care. In an analysis from the International Registry of Acute Aortic Dissection, mesenteric malperfusion was associated with higher in-hospital mortality than dissection without malperfusion. This case highlights the diagnostic and management challenges of acute Type A aortic dissection during pregnancy. In a pregnant patient presenting with chest or back pain and marked aortic root dilatation on PE-protocol imaging, acute aortic syndrome should prompt urgent evaluation of the entire aorta. Progressive metabolic acidosis, renal dysfunction, or unexplained clinical deterioration should raise concern for visceral ischemia. Although reperfusion-first strategies have been described in selected patients with aortic dissection and mesenteric malperfusion, their applicability in pregnancy remains uncertain and depends on defined vascular anatomy and the mechanism of malperfusion.

articles.title: Does meniscal tear morphology independently predict repair failure? A context-adjusted analysis of 500 consecutive arthroscopic meniscal repairs.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: To determine whether meniscal tear morphology independently predicts repair failure following arthroscopic meniscal repair after adjustment for patient-, meniscal- and repair-related characteristics and to quantify the incremental prognostic value of tear morphology beyond established clinical predictors.

METHODS: A retrospective multicenter cohort study included 500 consecutive patients undergoing primary arthroscopic meniscal repair with a minimum follow-up of 24 months. Repairable tear morphologies included longitudinal vertical, bucket-handle, radial, horizontal cleavage, complex, ramp and root tears. Patients undergoing revision meniscal repair, previous ipsilateral meniscal repair or transplantation, treatment of discoid meniscus, repair of degenerative root tears associated with advanced osteoarthritis, concomitant corrective osteotomy or arthroplasty or with insufficient operative or follow-up data were excluded. Meniscal characteristics included tear morphology, laterality, vascular zone and intraoperatively assessed tissue quality based on structural integrity, macroscopic degeneration and suture-holding capacity. Repair-related variables included repair technique (all-inside, inside-out or hybrid), number of fixation sutures, suture density and concomitant anterior cruciate ligament reconstruction. Repair failure was defined as subsequent ipsilateral meniscal reoperation. Kaplan-Meier analysis and multivariable Cox proportional hazards regression were used to evaluate repair survival and independent predictors of failure.

RESULTS: During a median follow-up of 45 months, 81 patients (16.2%) underwent reoperation. Five-year repair survivorship was 82.6%. Although repair survival differed among tear morphologies in univariable analysis (log-rank p = 0.012), tear morphology was no longer independently associated with failure after multivariable adjustment. Independent predictors of failure included medial meniscal repair (hazard ratio [HR] 2.18), poor tissue quality (HR 2.74), avascular tear location (HR 1.89), lower suture density (HR 0.71 per additional suture/cm) and absence of concomitant anterior cruciate ligament reconstruction (HR 1.67). Addition of tear morphology to the clinical prediction model produced only a modest improvement in discrimination (Harrell's C-index 0.782 vs. 0.794) and minimal improvement in calibration.

CONCLUSION: Meniscal tear morphology demonstrated limited independent prognostic value after adjustment for patient-, lesion- and procedure-related characteristics. Prognosis after arthroscopic meniscal repair appears to depend more strongly on the biological and mechanical context of the reparable meniscus than on tear configuration alone. Clinical decision-making should therefore move beyond descriptive tear classification toward comprehensive contextual assessment integrating tissue quality, vascularity, meniscal laterality and repair-related factors.

LEVEL OF EVIDENCE: Level III.

articles.title: Rapid Radiological Disappearance of Pancreatic Duct Stones Following Oral Trimethadione.
articles.abstract: A 59-year-old man with chronic pancreatitis, surgically altered anatomy, and an implantable cardioverter-defibrillator presented with acute exacerbation caused by cast-like obstructive pancreatic duct stones. Endoscopic therapy was considered technically difficult, and extracorporeal shock wave lithotripsy was avoided. While delayed surgical drainage was being considered, off-label oral trimethadione was started after institutional ethics approval. Computed tomography 2 weeks later showed disappearance of the stones and improvement of ductal dilatation. No adverse events occurred, and surgery was deferred. This case suggests that trimethadione may be a potential salvage option when standard interventions are infeasible.

articles.title: Coexisting focal nodular hyperplasia and diffuse hepatic metastases from an ileal neuroendocrine tumor: a case report and literature review.
articles.journal: International journal of surgery case reports
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION AND IMPORTANCE: Focal nodular hyperplasia (FNH) is a benign liver lesion usually associated with vascular abnormalities. Neuroendocrine tumors (NETs), on the other hand, frequently metastasize to the liver and typically appear as hypervascular lesions. The coexistence of FNH and diffuse hepatic metastases from an ileal NET is exceptionally rare and represents a major diagnostic challenge because both entities may present as hypervascular liver lesions, potentially leading to misdiagnosis and inappropriate management.

CASE PRESENTATION: A 56-year-old woman with a history of epilepsy treated with sodium valproate presented with progressive right upper quadrant pain and abdominal distension. Imaging showed a large hepatic lesion suggestive of FNH along with multiple hypervascular liver nodules suspicious for metastases. A CT-guided liver biopsy demonstrated metastatic well-differentiated NET with a Ki-67 index below 2%. Laboratory tests revealed elevated chromogranin A and urinary 5-hydroxyindoleacetic acid levels. The patient also had chronic diarrhea and moderate tricuspid regurgitation consistent with carcinoid syndrome. A ^68 Ga-DOTANOC positron emission tomography/computed tomography localized the primary tumor to the ileum. The integration of radiological, functional, and histopathological findings enabled accurate diagnosis and appropriate therapeutic planning. Surgical resection of the primary tumor was performed, followed by long-acting octreotide therapy. The patient remained clinically stable, with no progression of the hepatic lesions during follow-up.

CLINICAL DISCUSSION: The presence of multiple hypervascular liver lesions in patients with NETs raises important diagnostic issues, especially when benign and malignant lesions coexist. This case demonstrates the value of integrating hepatobiliary magnetic resonance imaging (MRI), histopathological confirmation, and functional imaging to accurately distinguish FNH from metastatic disease and to guide appropriate therapeutic management.

CONCLUSION: The coexistence of FNH and diffuse liver metastases from an ileal NET is rare. This case highlights the pivotal role of a multimodal diagnostic approach combining hepatobiliary MRI, functional imaging, and targeted histopathological confirmation to distinguish benign from malignant hypervascular liver lesions, avoid diagnostic pitfalls, and optimize patient management.

articles.title: Cesarean Delivery after Abdominal Wall Reconstruction Using an Anterolateral Thigh Flap with Vascularized Fascia Lata.
articles.journal: Plastic and reconstructive surgery. Global open
articles.abstract: Techniques for abdominal wall reconstruction include the use of prosthetic materials (synthetic or biological meshes), component separation, autologous tissue reconstruction, or a combination thereof. Reconstruction using prosthetic materials avoids additional trauma to healthy tissues but carries risks such as infection, adhesion to surrounding structures, and bowel obstruction caused by intestinal adhesions. Therefore, abdominal wall reconstruction using autologous tissue may be considered as an option suitable for women of childbearing potential. Only a few cases of successful childbirth following abdominal wall reconstruction have been reported, and opportunities to reincise and directly observe the reconstructed wall are rare. No previous reports have described intraoperative findings during reincision of a previously reconstructed abdominal wall. We report the case of a 23-year-old woman who underwent abdominal wall resection for a rectus abdominis tumor secondary to an immature ovarian teratoma. We reconstructed the abdominal wall using an anterolateral thigh flap with vascularized fascia lata, including the perifascial areolar tissue.
